title: Beyond the Leaderboard: Rethinking Medical Benchmarks for Large Language Models
outcome: Clinical fidelity and safety-oriented dimensions of 53 medical LLM benchmarks audited with MedCheck checklist
effect: Benchmarks show a profound disconnect from clinical practice, unmitigated data contamination risks, and systematic neglect of robustness and uncertainty awareness (no numeric rates in abstract).
quote: Our analysis uncovers widespread, systemic issues, including a profound disconnect from clinical practice, a crisis of data integrity due to unmitigated contamination risks, and a systematic neglect of safety-critical evaluation dimensions like model robustness and uncertainty awareness.

title: Are Large Language Models Dynamic Treatment Planners? An In Silico Study from a Prior Knowledge Injection Angle
outcome: LLM insulin dosing failure modes including arithmetic errors in simulator
effect: LLMs showed arithmetic hallucination, temporal misinterpretation, inconsistent clinical logic, and overly aggressive insulin dosing with chain-of-thought prompting.
quote: However, LLMs exhibit notable limitations, such as overly aggressive insulin dosing when prompted with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, highlighting critical failure modes including arithmetic hallucination, temporal misinterpretation, and inconsistent clinical logic.

title: Are Large Language Models Dynamic Treatment Planners? An In Silico Study from a Prior Knowledge Injection Angle
outcome: Zero-shot LLM insulin dosing performance versus trained RL agents in simulator
effect: Carefully prompted smaller LLMs (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B) achieved comparable or superior clinical performance versus trained SRAs, particularly in stable cohorts; limitations in other settings.
quote: Our results indicate that carefully designed zero-shot prompts enable smaller LLMs (e.g., Qwen2.5-7B) to achieve comparable or superior clinical performance relative to extensively trained SRAs, particularly in stable patient cohorts.

title: PrinciplismQA: A Philosophy-Grounded Approach to Assessing LLM-Human Clinical Medical Ethics Alignment
outcome: Gap between LLM knowledge accuracy and clinical ethical reasoning performance
effect: Models showed significant ethical reasoning gaps despite high knowledge accuracy; no numeric results in the provided text.
quote: Evaluating recent models reveals significant ethical reasoning gaps despite high knowledge accuracy, demonstrating that knowledge-oriented training does not ensure clinical ethical alignment.

title: Trustworthy Medical Imaging with Large Language Models: A Study of Hallucinations Across Modalities
outcome: Hallucinations in LLM-generated radiology reports and synthetic medical images
effect: Common patterns of hallucination (factual inconsistencies, anatomical inaccuracies) found in both image-to-text and text-to-image tasks; no numeric results reported in abstract.
quote: Our findings reveal common patterns of hallucination in both interpretive and generative tasks, with implications for clinical reliability.

title: FEAT: A Multi-Agent Forensic AI System with Domain-Adapted Large Language Model for Automated Cause-of-Death Analysis
outcome: Cross-region generalization of cause-of-death analysis performance across six geographic regions
effect: Reported robust generalization across six geographic regions with high expert concordance in blinded validations; no numeric values given in abstract.
quote: It demonstrated robust generalization across six geographic regions and achieved high expert concordance in blinded validations.

title: DepressLLM: Interpretable domain-adapted language model for depression detection from real-world narratives
outcome: Classification AUC overall versus among high-confidence predictions from the SToPS confidence estimates
effect: AUC 0.789 overall, rising to 0.904 on samples with confidence ≥ 0.95.
quote: DepressLLM provides interpretable depression predictions and, via its Score-guided Token Probability Summation (SToPS) module, delivers both improved classification performance and reliable confidence estimates, achieving an AUC of 0.789, which rises to 0.904 on samples with confidence $\geq$ 0.95.

title: Out of the Box, into the Clinic? Evaluating State-of-the-Art ASR for Clinical Applications for Older Adults
outcome: ASR word error rate on older Dutch adults' speech, generic versus fine-tuned models
effect: Generic multilingual models outperformed models fine-tuned for older Dutch adults' speech, so they generalise well out of the box. Some inputs still caused a high word error rate.
quote: Our results show that generic multilingual models outperform fine-tuned models, which suggests recent ASR models can generalise well out of the box to real-world datasets.

title: The Knowledge-Reasoning Dissociation: Fundamental Limitations of LLMs in Clinical Natural Language Inference
outcome: LLM factual knowledge probe accuracy versus clinical trial reasoning task accuracy
effect: Mean GKMRV knowledge-probe accuracy was 0.918 while mean accuracy on main reasoning tasks was 0.25; output consistency across samples averaged 0.87.
quote: Models achieve near-ceiling GKMRV accuracy (mean accuracy 0.918) yet perform poorly on the main reasoning tasks (mean accuracy 0.25).

title: Is ChatGPT-5 Ready for Mammogram VQA?
outcome: GPT-5 mammogram performance compared with human experts and domain-specific fine-tuned models
effect: GPT-5 was best among GPT models but lagged human experts and fine-tuned models; sensitivity 63.5% and specificity 52.3% versus human expert estimates.
quote: Compared with human expert estimations, GPT-5 exhibited lower sensitivity (63.5%) and specificity (52.3%).
sample_unit: mammography images/questions across four public datasets (EMBED, InBreast, CMMD, CBIS-DDSM)

title: TracSum: A New Benchmark for Aspect-Based Summarization with Sentence-Level Traceability in Medical Domain
outcome: Summary accuracy and completeness with vs without prior sentence-level evidence tracking
effect: Explicit sentence-level tracking before summarization enhanced generation accuracy; adding full context further improved completeness. No numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: We also observe that explicitly performing sentence-level tracking prior to summarization enhances generation accuracy, while incorporating the full context further improves completeness.

title: Organ-Agents: Virtual Human Physiology Simulator via LLMs
outcome: Simulation accuracy under distribution shift on external ICU cohorts from two hospitals
effect: External validation on 22,689 ICU patients from two hospitals showed moderate degradation under distribution shifts, though simulation remained stable.
quote: External validation on 22,689 ICU patients from two hospitals showed moderate degradation under distribution shifts with stable simulation.

title: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation vs. Long-Context Input for Clinical Reasoning over EHRs
outcome: Effect of missing patient data (inter-hospital transfers) on LLM EHR task performance
effect: Error analysis showed missing information in clinical notes, often due to inter-hospital transfers, limited performance to some extent.
quote: Error analysis revealed that missing information in the clinical notes--often due to inter-hospital transfers--limited performance to some extent.

title: End-to-End Agentic RAG System Training for Traceable Diagnostic Reasoning
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of RL-trained agentic RAG versus prompt-engineering and training-free RAG methods
effect: End-to-end RL agentic RAG consistently outperformed prompt-engineering and training-free RAG; average accuracy gain of 22.7% over the second-best model on ID and OOD benchmarks.
quote: Experiments show our end-to-end RL framework consistently outperforms prompt-engineering and training-free RAG methods.

title: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Medical Question Answering in Romanian
outcome: Fine-tuned versus zero-shot LLM performance on Romanian cancer-patient medical QA, including cross-center and cross-cancer tests
effect: Fine-tuned models significantly outperformed zero-shot models; pretrained models failed to generalize on MedQARo (no numbers in abstract).
quote: Our results show that fine-tuned models significantly outperform zero-shot models, indicating that pretrained models fail to generalize on MedQARo.

title: PediatricsMQA: a Multi-modal Pediatrics Question Answering Benchmark
outcome: LLM/VLM performance on pediatric text and image questions, an underrepresented age group
effect: Dramatic performance drops in younger cohorts among evaluated open models; age bias described as reflecting pediatric underrepresentation in medical research.
quote: Evaluating state-of-the-art open models, we find dramatic performance drops in younger cohorts, highlighting the need for age-aware methods to ensure equitable AI support in pediatric care.

title: PediatricsMQA: a Multi-modal Pediatrics Question Answering Benchmark
outcome: Model accuracy across pediatric developmental-stage subgroups
effect: Dramatic performance drops in younger cohorts across seven developmental stages (prenatal to adolescent).
quote: Evaluating state-of-the-art open models, we find dramatic performance drops in younger cohorts, highlighting the need for age-aware methods to ensure equitable AI support in pediatric care.

title: Trustworthy Agents for Electronic Health Records through Confidence Estimation
outcome: Accuracy under hallucination-controlled confidence thresholds (HCAcc@k%) for EHR question answering agent
effect: TrustEHRAgent improved 44.23%p and 25.34%p at HCAcc@70% on MIMIC-III and eICU, while baseline methods fail at these thresholds.
quote: Experiments on MIMIC-III and eICU datasets show TrustEHRAgent outperforms baselines under strict reliability constraints, achieving improvements of 44.23%p and 25.34%p at HCAcc@70% while baseline methods fail at these thresholds.

title: AT-CXR: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Triage for Chest X-rays
outcome: Selective-prediction performance (AURC, error at high coverage) of an agent that abstains on uncertain cases for human review
effect: Both AT-CXR routers achieved lower AURC and lower error at high coverage than zero-shot VLMs and supervised classifiers, with higher full-coverage accuracy. No numeric values in the text.
quote: Across five-fold evaluation on a balanced subset of NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset, both variants outperform strong zero-shot vision-language models and state-of-the-art supervised classifiers, achieving higher full-coverage accuracy and superior selective-prediction performance, evidenced by a lower area under the risk-coverage curve (AURC) and a lower error rate at high coverage, while operating with lower latency that meets practical clinical constraints.
sample_unit: chest X-ray images (balanced subset of NIH ChestX-ray14, five-fold)

title: AT-CXR: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Triage for Chest X-rays
outcome: Whether the agent defers or abstains appropriately on uncertain cases, measured by risk-coverage tradeoffs
effect: Uncertainty-aware abstention policy gave lower risk-coverage AUC and lower error at high coverage than baselines. Two routers offer throughput-focused or accuracy-focused operating points. No numeric values in the text.
quote: The two routers provide complementary operating points, enabling deployments to prioritize maximal throughput or maximal accuracy.
sample_unit: chest X-ray images (balanced subset of NIH ChestX-ray14, five-fold)

title: DPF-CM: A Data Processing Framework with Privacy-Preserving Vector Databases for Chinese Medical LLMs Training and Deployment
outcome: Training data privacy leakage with the Privacy Preserving Vector Database approach
effect: The framework reduces training data privacy leakage by 27%.
quote: Moreover, the framework reduces training data privacy leakage by 27%.

title: mFARM: Towards Multi-Faceted Fairness Assessment based on HARMs in Clinical Decision Support
outcome: Fairness (mFARM score) across race x gender prompt variants under quantization and reduced context
effect: Most models kept robust mFARM scores across quantization levels but deteriorated significantly when context was reduced.
quote: We find that most models maintain robust performance in terms of $mFARM$ score across varying levels of quantization but deteriorate significantly when the context is reduced.

title: OpenAIs HealthBench in Action: Evaluating an LLM-Based Medical Assistant on Realistic Clinical Queries
outcome: Deployed agentic RAG assistant scored on rubric-based HealthBench Hard clinical competencies vs frontier LLMs
effect: DR. INFO scored 0.68 on HealthBench Hard vs GPT-5 0.46, GPT-5.2 0.42, GPT-5.1 0.40, Grok 3 0.23, Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.19, Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.02; 0.72 in a 100-sample comparison against OpenEvidence and Pathway.md.
quote: On the Hard subset of 1,000 challenging examples, DR. INFO achieves a HealthBench Hard score of 0.68, outperforming leading frontier LLMs including the GPT-5 model family (GPT-5: 0.46, GPT-5.2: 0.42, GPT-5.1: 0.40), Grok 3 (0.23), Gemini 2.5 Pro (0.19), and Claude 3.7 Sonnet (0.02) across all behavioral axes (accuracy, completeness, instruction following, etc.).

title: Facts Fade Fast: Evaluating Memorization of Outdated Medical Knowledge in Large Language Models
outcome: LLM reliance on outdated medical knowledge on questions where consensus changed
effect: Evaluation of eight LLMs on MedChangeQA (512 QA pairs) showed consistent reliance on outdated knowledge across all models.
quote: Our evaluation of eight prominent LLMs on the datasets reveals consistent reliance on outdated knowledge across all models.
sample_unit: questions (MedChangeQA QA pairs where medical consensus changed; MedRevQA has 16,501)

title: Facts Fade Fast: Evaluating Memorization of Outdated Medical Knowledge in Large Language Models
outcome: Obsolete pre-training knowledge leading to outdated recommendations
effect: All eight LLMs showed reliance on outdated knowledge; the study analyzes the influence of obsolete pre-training data and training strategies.
quote: Our evaluation of eight prominent LLMs on the datasets reveals consistent reliance on outdated knowledge across all models.
sample_unit: questions (MedChangeQA QA pairs where medical consensus changed; MedRevQA has 16,501)

title: ArGen: Auto-Regulation of Generative AI via GRPO and Policy-as-Code
outcome: Domain-scope adherence of medical AI assistant versus baseline model
effect: 70.9% improvement in domain-scope adherence over the baseline, implying the baseline model had substantial out-of-scope behavior.
quote: This challenging application demonstrates ArGen's adaptability, achieving a 70.9% improvement in domain-scope adherence over the baseline.

title: Preventing Another Tessa: Modular Safety Middleware For Health-Adjacent AI Assistants
outcome: Interception of unsafe prompts by lexical gate plus in-line LLM policy filter, cost and latency
effect: Hybrid middleware achieved perfect interception of unsafe prompts at baseline cost and latency, outperforming traditional multi-stage pipelines (synthetic evaluations; sample size not reported in text).
quote: Using synthetic evaluations, we show that this design achieves perfect interception of unsafe prompts at baseline cost and latency, outperforming traditional multi-stage pipelines.

title: Preventing Another Tessa: Modular Safety Middleware For Health-Adjacent AI Assistants
outcome: interception of unsafe prompts
effect: achieved perfect interception of unsafe prompts at baseline cost and latency, outperforming traditional multi-stage pipelines
quote: Using synthetic evaluations, we show that this design achieves perfect interception of unsafe prompts at baseline cost and latency, outperforming traditional multi-stage pipelines.

title: CancerGUIDE: Cancer Guideline Understanding via Internal Disagreement Estimation
outcome: Ability of a meta-classifier's calibrated confidence scores to verify correctness of LLM treatment recommendations
effect: Meta-classifier verifying prediction accuracy with calibrated confidence scores achieved AUROC=0.800; no comparison without the confidence scores.
quote: Third, we develop a hybrid approach combining expensive human annotations with model consistency information to create both the agent framework that predicts the relevant guidelines for a patient, as well as a meta-classifier that verifies prediction accuracy with calibrated confidence scores for treatment recommendations (AUROC=0.800), a critical capability for communicating the accuracy of outputs, custom-tailoring tradeoffs in performance, and supporting regulatory compliance.

title: Factuality Beyond Coherence: Evaluating LLM Watermarking Methods for Medical Texts
outcome: Effect of LLM watermarking (content provenance) on factual accuracy and coherence of medical text
effect: Current watermarking methods substantially compromise medical factuality, with entropy shifts degrading medical entity representation.
quote: Our evaluation shows current watermarking methods substantially compromise medical factuality, with entropy shifts degrading medical entity representation.

title: Compartmentalised Agentic Reasoning for Clinical NLI
outcome: Accuracy of clinical NLI against benchmark ground truth, agentic framework versus direct prompting
effect: CARENLI improves mean accuracy from about 23% with direct prompting to about 57%, a gain of roughly 34 points across four backbone models.
quote: Across four contemporary backbone models, CARENLI improves mean accuracy from about 23% with direct prompting to about 57%, a gain of roughly 34 points, with the largest benefits on structurally demanding reasoning types.

title: A Comparison and Evaluation of Fine-tuned Convolutional Neural Networks to Large Language Models for Image Classification and Segmentation of Brain Tumors on MRI
outcome: Glioma classification and segmentation performance of a general LLM versus custom 3D CNNs on the same BraTS data
effect: CNN reached 80% accuracy on LGG vs HGG; base LLM 76% accuracy with 18% specificity; fine-tuned LLM 72% accuracy and 55% specificity. LLM segmentation clustered near image center with no spatial accuracy.
quote: Overall, CNNs outperformed LLMs in both tasks.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Evidence-Based Clinical Question Answering
outcome: Accuracy on previously incorrect items with and without retrieved abstracts in the prompt
effect: Gold-source abstract raised accuracy on previously incorrect items to 0.79; top 3 PubMed abstracts improved it to 0.23; random abstracts reduced it to 0.10 (within temperature variation).
quote: When we incorporate retrieval-augmented prompting, providing the gold-source abstract raises accuracy on previously incorrect items to 0.79; providing top 3 PubMed abstracts (ranked by semantic relevance) improves accuracy to 0.23, while random abstracts reduce accuracy (0.10, within temperature variation).

title: The Psychogenic Machine: Simulating AI Psychosis, Delusion Reinforcement and Harm Enablement in Large Language Models
outcome: Safety interventions offered across simulated multi-turn delusion scenarios
effect: Models offered safety interventions in roughly a third of applicable turns (mean SIS 0.37 ± 0.48); 51/128 (39.8%) of scenarios had no safety interventions offered.
quote: Models frequently enabled harmful user requests (mean HES of 0.69 $\pm$0.84) and offered safety interventions in only roughly a third of applicable turns (mean SIS of 0.37 $\pm$0.48).

title: The Psychogenic Machine: Simulating AI Psychosis, Delusion Reinforcement and Harm Enablement in Large Language Models
outcome: Delusion confirmation and safety intervention across evolving multi-turn simulated conversations, explicit versus implicit
effect: Mean DCS 0.91 ± 0.88; implicit scenarios had more delusion confirmation, more harm enablement, and fewer interventions (p < .001).
quote: Performance was significantly worse in implicit scenarios, models were more likely to confirm delusions and enable harm while offering fewer interventions (p < .001).

title: Adapting and Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis Self-Management: A Divide and Conquer Framework
outcome: MLLM performance on the AIS knowledge assessment task with versus without retrieval augmented generation
effect: RAG substantially improved models' performance on the knowledge assessment task. No numeric effect sizes are given in the abstract.
quote: Results showed varying effectiveness of visual prompting across different architectures, while RAG substantially improved models' performances on the knowledge assessment task.
sample_unit: anteroposterior X-rays with diagnostic texts (approximate database size)

title: MedFact: Benchmarking the Fact-Checking Capabilities of Large Language Models on Chinese Medical Texts
outcome: LLM veracity classification and error localization on Chinese medical fact-checking benchmark
effect: Models often determine if text contains errors but struggle to localize them precisely; top performers fall short of human performance; over-criticism misidentifies correct information as erroneous.
quote: We evaluate 20 leading LLMs on veracity classification and error localization, and results show models often determine if text contains errors but struggle to localize them precisely, with top performers falling short of human performance.

title: Simulating Clinical AI Assistance using Multimodal LLMs: A Case Study in Diabetic Retinopathy
outcome: Model susceptibility to incorrect simulated AI inputs (overreliance analog) in diabetic retinopathy detection
effect: Both models adjusted predictions based on simulated AI inputs; GPT-4o's performance collapsed with incorrect inputs, whereas MedGemma remained more stable.
quote: Both models adjusted predictions based on simulated AI inputs, but GPT-4o's performance collapsed with incorrect ones, whereas MedGemma remained more stable.

title: Combating Biomedical Misinformation through Multi-modal Claim Detection and Evidence-based Verification
outcome: Hallucination mitigation and claim verification performance when LLM outputs are grounded in retrieved biomedical evidence
effect: Authors report CER, which grounds LLM reasoning in retrieved scientific evidence, mitigates hallucination risk and achieves state-of-the-art performance on HealthFC, BioASQ-7b, and SciFact; no numeric results in provided text.
quote: By integrating the text-generation capabilities of large language models with advanced retrieval techniques for high-quality biomedical scientific evidence, CER effectively mitigates the risk of hallucinations, ensuring that generated outputs are grounded in verifiable, evidence-based sources.
sample_unit: claims (benchmark datasets HealthFC, BioASQ-7b, SciFact; counts not reported in text)

title: Not What the Doctor Ordered: Surveying LLM-based De-identification and Quantifying Clinical Information Loss
outcome: Adequacy of evaluation metrics for detecting clinical information removal in LLM de-identification
effect: Traditional classification metrics are inadequate for LLM errors that alter clinical information; an existing metric was manually validated by clinical experts and showed poor performance.
quote: We highlight poor performance and describe the inherent limitations of such metrics in identifying clinically significant changes.

title: Not What the Doctor Ordered: Surveying LLM-based De-identification and Quantifying Clinical Information Loss
outcome: Consistency of reporting standards across LLM de-identification papers
effect: The survey found heterogeneous reporting standards and inconsistent metrics, hindering direct comparison and reproducibility.
quote: Although these approaches often report near-perfect results, significant challenges concerning reproducibility and utility of the research papers persist.

title: Can I Trust This Chatbot? Assessing User Privacy in AI-Healthcare Chatbot Applications
outcome: User control over personal data and ability to disable data sharing in AI healthcare chatbot apps
effect: Only two of 12 apps offered an option to disable data sharing at sign-up; users had minimal control over their personal data.
quote: Moreover, users had minimal control over their personal data.

title: Can I Trust This Chatbot? Assessing User Privacy in AI-Healthcare Chatbot Applications
outcome: Whether apps informed users of data use through a privacy policy at sign-up
effect: Half of the 12 apps did not present a privacy policy during sign-up; most policies failed to address data protection measures.
quote: Our findings reveal that half of the examined apps did not present a privacy policy during sign up, and only two provided an option to disable data sharing at that stage.

title: EHR-MCP: Real-world Evaluation of Clinical Information Retrieval by Large Language Models via Model Context Protocol
outcome: Agent errors from tool arguments and tool-result interpretation versus physician gold standard
effect: Correct tool selection and execution; near-perfect accuracy on all but two tasks; lower on the time-dependent task. Most errors were incorrect arguments or misinterpretation of tool results.
quote: Most errors arose from incorrect arguments or misinterpretation of tool results.

title: EHR-MCP: Real-world Evaluation of Clinical Information Retrieval by Large Language Models via Model Context Protocol
outcome: Risk of long EHR tool responses exceeding the LLM context window
effect: EHR-MCP responses were reliable, but long and repetitive data risked exceeding the context window; no numbers reported.
quote: Responses from EHR-MCP were reliable, though long and repetitive data risked exceeding the context window.

title: RephQA: Evaluating Readability of Large Language Models in Public Health Question Answering
outcome: Readability of LLM answers to public health questions for lay readers (Flesch-Kincaid grade level, professional score)
effect: Most of the 25 LLMs evaluated failed to meet readability standards; no numeric values are reported in the abstract.
quote: Evaluation of 25 LLMs reveals that most fail to meet readability standards, highlighting a gap between reasoning and effective communication.

title: Filling in the Clinical Gaps in Benchmark: Case for HealthBench for the Japanese medical system
outcome: LLM benchmark performance and rubric applicability when translated to the Japanese clinical context
effect: Modest performance drop in GPT-4.1 due to rubric mismatches; significant failure in the Japanese-native LLM-jp-3.1 for lacking clinical completeness; many rubric criteria need localisation.
quote: Our findings reveal a modest performance drop in GPT-4.1 due to rubric mismatches, as well as a significant failure in the Japanese-native model, which lacked the required clinical completeness.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Calibrated Clinical Text Classification with Large Language Models
outcome: Misclassification-detection AUROC of posterior-based uncertainty versus black-box confidence baselines
effect: On MultiCare, misclassification-detection AUROC was 0.923 for M-SMC versus 0.760 for softmax and 0.584 for a consistency baseline.
quote: Across three clinical benchmarks and six open LLMs, the inferred posterior separates correct predictions from errors more sharply than black-box confidence, with misclassification-detection AUROC on MultiCare of 0.923 for M-SMC against 0.760 for softmax and 0.584 for a consistency baseline.
sample_unit: clinical text cases across three benchmarks (MultiCare, OLB-300, and one other)

title: MACD: Multi-Agent Clinical Diagnosis with Self-Learned Knowledge for LLM
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of physicians with MACD-human collaboration versus physician-only diagnosis on text vignettes
effect: MACD-human workflow yielded an 18.3-percentage-point improvement over physician-only diagnosis on text-only vignettes.
quote: Furthermore, the MACD-human workflow yields an 18.3-percentage-point improvement over physician-only diagnosis on text-only vignettes, demonstrating the synergistic potential of human-AI collaboration.

title: An Automated Retrieval-Augmented Generation LLaMA-4 109B-based System for Evaluating Radiotherapy Treatment Plans
outcome: Agreement of LLM outputs with values computed by retrieval and constraint-checking modules
effect: RAG system achieved 100% agreement with standalone retrieval and constraint-checking values on percentile estimates and constraint identification; no comparison against a non-grounded LLM.
quote: When tested end-to-end, the RAG system achieved 100% agreement with the computed values by standalone retrieval and constraint-checking modules on both percentile estimates and constraint identification, confirming reliable execution of all retrieval, prediction and checking steps.

title: On the Robustness of Answer Formats in Medical Reasoning Models
outcome: Answer-format robustness (correctness across multiple-choice, open-ended, ranked list formats) across 15 models
effect: Substantial variation in format robustness across 15 models (35-100%); reinforcement fine-tuning often shows higher cross-format brittleness than supervised fine-tuning.
quote: Across 15 proprietary and open-weight models, we observe substantial variation in format robustness (35-100%).

title: Beyond Classification Accuracy: Neural-MedBench and the Need for Deeper Reasoning Benchmarks
outcome: VLM performance on reasoning-intensive neurology benchmark versus conventional datasets
effect: Sharp performance drop on Neural-MedBench compared with conventional datasets; reasoning failures rather than perceptual errors dominate model shortcomings. No numbers given in abstract.
quote: Through systematic evaluation of state-of-the-art VLMs, including GPT-4o, Claude-4, and MedGemma, we observe a sharp performance drop compared to conventional datasets.

title: Large language models management of medications: three performance analyses
outcome: Omissions and hallucinated formulations when matching generic drugs to available formulations
effect: 49% accuracy matching generic medications to all available formulations; 1.23 omissions and 1.14 hallucinations per medication.
quote: For the first task of drug-formulation matching, GPT-4o had 49% accuracy for generic medications being matched to all available formulations, with an average of 1.23 omissions per medication and 1.14 hallucinations per medication.

title: Large language models management of medications: three performance analyses
outcome: Accuracy of identifying drug-drug interaction pairs for a given medication regimen
effect: 54.7% accuracy for identifying the DDI pair.
quote: For the second task of drug-drug interaction identification, the accuracy was 54.7% for identifying the DDI pair.

title: From Conversation to Query Execution: Benchmarking User and Tool Interactions for EHR Database Agents
outcome: Consistency of agent success across five repeated trials (Pass^5 vs Pass@5)
effect: Best agents reach Pass@5 over 90% on IncreQA and 60-70% on AdaptQA, but Pass^5 is substantially lower, with gaps of up to about 60%.
quote: Experiments with state-of-the-art LLMs (e.g., o4-mini and Gemini-2.5-Flash) over five i.i.d. trials show that while the best-performing agents achieve Pass@5 of over 90% (at least one of five trials) on IncreQA and 60-70% on AdaptQA, their Pass^5 (consistent success across all five trials) is substantially lower, with gaps of up to about 60%.
sample_unit: benchmark conversations (five i.i.d. trials per agent)

title: MedMMV: A Controllable Multimodal Multi-Agent Framework for Reliable and Verifiable Clinical Reasoning
outcome: Reasoning truthfulness and accuracy when grounding intermediate steps in a structured evidence graph with a hallucination detector
effect: Accuracy improved by up to 12.7% on six medical benchmarks; blind physician evaluations showed substantially increased reasoning truthfulness without loss of informational content.
quote: Blind physician evaluations confirm that MedMMV substantially increases reasoning truthfulness without sacrificing informational content.

title: KnowGuard: Knowledge-Driven Abstention for Multi-Round Clinical Reasoning
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and number of interaction turns of abstention approaches in multi-round clinical benchmarks
effect: KnowGuard improved diagnostic accuracy by 3.93% and reduced unnecessary interaction by 7.27 turns on average versus state-of-the-art abstention approaches.
quote: Experimental evidences clearly demonstrate that KnowGuard outperforms state-of-the-art abstention approaches, improving diagnostic accuracy by 3.93\% while reducing unnecessary interaction by 7.27 turns on average.

title: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation of Mental Health Crisis Handling by LLMs
outcome: Appropriateness and safety of LLM responses to suicidal ideation and self-harm crisis inputs
effect: Many outputs, especially for self-harm and suicidal categories, were inappropriate or unsafe. gpt-4o-mini and grok-4-fast produced more unsafe responses; gpt-5-nano and deepseek-v3.2-exp had low harm rates.
quote: Many outputs, especially in self-harm and suicidal categories, are inappropriate or unsafe.

title: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation of Mental Health Crisis Handling by LLMs
outcome: LLM recognition of and appropriate response to indirect crisis signals
effect: Models were reliable for some explicit crises, but all struggled with indirect signals, default replies, and context misalignment.
quote: All models struggle with indirect signals, default replies, and context misalignment.

title: Radiology's Last Exam (RadLE): Benchmarking Frontier Multimodal AI Against Human Experts and a Taxonomy of Visual Reasoning Errors in Radiology
outcome: Reproducibility of model diagnoses across three independent runs
effect: Reliability substantial for GPT-5 and o3, moderate for Gemini 2.5 Pro and Grok-4, and poor for Claude Opus 4.1.
quote: Reliability was substantial for GPT-5 and o3, moderate for Gemini 2.5 Pro and Grok-4, and poor for Claude Opus 4.1.

title: Radiology's Last Exam (RadLE): Benchmarking Frontier Multimodal AI Against Human Experts and a Taxonomy of Visual Reasoning Errors in Radiology
outcome: Frontier model diagnostic accuracy on difficult radiology cases versus radiologists
effect: Radiologists 83%, trainees 45%, best AI model (GPT-5) 30%; models fall far short of radiologists on challenging cases.
quote: Board-certified radiologists achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (83%), outperforming trainees (45%) and all AI models (best performance shown by GPT-5: 30%).

title: Radiology's Last Exam (RadLE): Benchmarking Frontier Multimodal AI Against Human Experts and a Taxonomy of Visual Reasoning Errors in Radiology
outcome: Frontier AI diagnostic accuracy compared against radiologists and trainees on same cases
effect: Radiologists 83%, trainees 45%, all AI models lower (best GPT-5 30%).
quote: Board-certified radiologists achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (83%), outperforming trainees (45%) and all AI models (best performance shown by GPT-5: 30%).

title: Assessing Algorithmic Bias in Language-Based Depression Detection: A Comparison of DNN and LLM Approaches
outcome: Effect of fairness-aware losses and ethical-framing prompts on subgroup disparities and accuracy
effect: Worst-group loss gave a better performance-fairness balance than fairness-regularized loss. Ethical-framing prompts reduced gender bias in 1-shot only. Neither prompting strategy nor more shots reduced race/ethnicity disparities.
quote: Among fairness-aware techniques for mitigating bias in DNN-based embeddings, the worst-group loss, which is designed to minimize loss for the worst-performing demographic group, achieves a better balance between performance and fairness.

title: Assessing Algorithmic Bias in Language-Based Depression Detection: A Comparison of DNN and LLM Approaches
outcome: Depression detection performance and fairness across gender and race/ethnicity subgroups
effect: LLMs showed reduced gender bias compared with DNN embeddings, but racial disparities persisted. LLMs outperformed DNNs particularly for underrepresented groups such as Hispanic participants.
quote: LLMs also exhibit reduced gender bias compared to DNN-based embeddings, though racial disparities persist.

title: Adapting Large Language Models to Mitigate Skin Tone Biases in Clinical Dermatology Tasks: A Mixed-Methods Study
outcome: SkinGPT-4 performance and fairness metrics across Fitzpatrick skin tones
effect: Average demographic parity 0.10 across Fitzpatrick types, with differences of 0.10-0.15 between lightest and darkest tones; weaker performance on darker tones.
quote: Large language models such as SkinGPT-4 showed weaker performance on darker tones.

title: Adapting Large Language Models to Mitigate Skin Tone Biases in Clinical Dermatology Tasks: A Mixed-Methods Study
outcome: Performance for underrepresented darker skin tones given lighter-tone-dominated training data
effect: Training dataset predominantly lighter skin tones; SkinGPT-4 weaker on darker tones, with 0.10-0.15 differences between lightest and darkest tones.
quote: Large language models such as SkinGPT-4 showed weaker performance on darker tones.

title: Adapting Large Language Models to Mitigate Skin Tone Biases in Clinical Dermatology Tasks: A Mixed-Methods Study
outcome: Fairness (demographic parity) and accuracy of finetuned models after bias mitigation across skin tones
effect: Custom models had average F1 0.75, precision 0.78, AUROC 0.78; average demographic parity 0.75, max disparity 0.21; best model parity 0.76-0.90 across Fitzpatrick I-VI.
quote: The best model achieved parity scores of 0.83, 0.83, 0.76, 0.89, 0.90, and 0.90 for Fitzpatrick I-VI, indicating robust fairness.

title: Grounding Large Language Models in Clinical Evidence: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Querying UK NICE Clinical Guidelines
outcome: Faithfulness of answers to source text with versus without retrieval-augmented grounding in NICE guidelines
effect: RAG raised faithfulness by 64.7 percentage points to 99.5% for O4-Mini; Meditron3-8B without RAG scored 43%.
quote: Faithfulness, the measure of whether an answer is supported by the source text, was increased by 64.7 percentage points to 99.5% for the RAG-enhanced O4-Mini model and significantly outperformed the medical-focused Meditron3-8B LLM, which scored 43%.

title: MedPAO: A Protocol-Driven Agent for Structuring Medical Reports
outcome: Expert-rated quality of structured CXR report outputs, protocol-grounded agent versus LLM-only baselines
effect: Expert radiologists and clinicians rated outputs 4.52 out of 5 on average; concept categorization F1 was 0.96; reported as surpassing LLM-only foundation-model baselines.
quote: Notably, expert radiologists and clinicians rated the final structured outputs with an average score of 4.52 out of 5, indicating a level of reliability that surpasses baseline approaches relying solely on LLM-based foundation models.

title: Toward Reliable Clinical Coding with Language Models: Verification and Lightweight Adaptation
outcome: Effect of an automated code verification step on LLM clinical coding accuracy
effect: Verification is reported as an effective and reliable step for improving LLM-based medical coding, addressing hierarchically near-miss errors. No numbers are given in the abstract.
quote: Our results highlight verification as an effective and reliable step toward improving LLM-based medical coding.

title: YpathRAG:A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework and Benchmark for Pathology
outcome: LLM accuracy on hard pathology questions with vs without retrieval-augmented grounding
effect: YpathRAG increased accuracies of both general and medical LLMs by 9.0% on average and up to 15.6% on the 300 hardest YpathQA-M questions.
quote: on YpathQA-M, a set of the 300 most challenging questions, it increases the accuracies of both general and medical LLMs by 9.0% on average and up to 15.6%.

title: Gender Bias in Large Language Models for Healthcare: Assignment Consistency and Clinical Implications
outcome: Consistency of LLM diagnoses and patient-gender relevance/necessity judgments across assigned LLM genders
effect: Diagnoses were relatively consistent across LLM genders for most models. Judgments of patient gender relevance and necessity were substantially inconsistent across all models, especially relevance. Some models showed a systematic female-male disparity.
quote: In our findings, diagnoses were relatively consistent across LLM genders for most models.

title: The Model's Language Matters: A Comparative Privacy Analysis of LLMs
outcome: Privacy leakage via extraction, counterfactual memorization, and membership inference across four languages
effect: Privacy vulnerability scales with linguistic redundancy and tokenization granularity; Italian shows strongest leakage, English higher membership separability, French and Spanish more resilient.
quote: Results show that privacy vulnerability scales with linguistic redundancy and tokenization granularity: Italian exhibits the strongest leakage, while English shows higher membership separability.

title: Cross-Representation Benchmarking in Time-Series Electronic Health Records for Clinical Outcome Prediction
outcome: Comparative performance of complex pre-trained models versus simpler count-based baselines on same EHR data
effect: Pre-trained CLMBR was highly sample-efficient in few-shot settings, but simpler count-based models were competitive given sufficient data; event stream models performed best overall.
quote: Pre-trained models like CLMBR are highly sample-efficient in few-shot settings, though simpler count-based models can be competitive given sufficient data.
sample_unit: benchmark tasks (MIMIC-IV ICU tasks and EHRSHOT longitudinal tasks)

title: Dr. Bias: Social Disparities in AI-Powered Medical Guidance
outcome: Difference in LLM medical advice features across simulated patient sex, age range, and ethnicity
effect: Responses systematically differed between social groups when patient sex, age range, and ethnicity were varied; differences amplified for intersectional groups.
quote: By comparing natural language features of the generated responses, we show that, when LLMs are used for medical advice generation, they generate responses that systematically differ between social groups.
sample_unit: LLM responses to simulated patient-profile medical questions

title: Dr. Bias: Social Disparities in AI-Powered Medical Guidance
outcome: Readability and complexity of LLM medical advice by patient social group
effect: Indigenous and intersex patients received advice that was less readable and more complex; trends amplified for intersectional groups.
quote: In particular, Indigenous and intersex patients receive advice that is less readable and more complex.
sample_unit: LLM responses to simulated patient-profile medical questions

title: Auditing medical multi-agent AI reveals risks of false consensus
outcome: Unsupported observations from agents propagating downstream in multi-agent reasoning
effect: Unsupported observations affect 16.63% of cases and propagate downstream.
quote: Unsupported observations affect 16.63% of cases and propagate downstream.

title: Auditing medical multi-agent AI reveals risks of false consensus
outcome: Multi-agent final answers substituting authority or majority for evidence checking
effect: Authority bias in 28.76% of cases (rising from 35.30% to 68.75% across rounds), self-contradiction 18.53%, contradiction neglect 5.48%, minority suppression 5.11%.
quote: During synthesis, final answers often substitute authority or majority count for evidence checking, showing authority bias in 28.76% (rising from 35.30% to 68.75% across rounds), self-contradiction in 18.53%, contradiction neglect in 5.48% and minority suppression in 5.11%.

title: Simulating Viva Voce Examinations to Evaluate Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Models
outcome: LLM diagnostic performance in multi-turn interactive reasoning versus single-turn benchmark-style vignettes
effect: LLMs competent diagnosing from well-described presentations, but performance degrades significantly in iterative diagnostic reasoning under uncertainty on VivaBench (1762 vignettes).
quote: While current LLMs demonstrate competence in diagnosing conditions from well-described clinical presentations, their performance degrades significantly when required to navigate iterative diagnostic reasoning under uncertainty in our evaluation.

title: Simulating Viva Voce Examinations to Evaluate Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Models
outcome: Failure modes in LLM diagnostic reasoning, including failing to screen for critical conditions
effect: Identified failure modes: fixation on initial hypotheses, inappropriate investigation ordering, premature diagnostic closure, and failing to screen for critical conditions.
quote: Our analysis identified several failure modes that mirror common cognitive errors in clinical practice, including: (1) fixation on initial hypotheses, (2) inappropriate investigation ordering, (3) premature diagnostic closure, and (4) failing to screen for critical conditions.

title: An AI-Based Behavioral Health Safety Filter and Dataset for Identifying Mental Health Crises in Text-Based Conversations
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of safety filter detecting mental health crises in messages (missed vs unnecessary flags)
effect: On the Verily dataset, sensitivity was 0.990 and specificity 0.992 for any crisis; on Aegis, sensitivity was 0.982 and specificity 0.859.
quote: The VBHSF demonstrated, well-balanced performance on the Verily Mental Health Crisis Dataset v1.0, achieving high sensitivity (0.990) and specificity (0.992) in detecting any mental health crises.
sample_unit: messages (1,800 simulated plus 794 Aegis mental health-related)

title: An AI-Based Behavioral Health Safety Filter and Dataset for Identifying Mental Health Crises in Text-Based Conversations
outcome: Sensitivity of general content moderation guardrails for specific mental health crisis types
effect: NeMo and OpenAI Omni Moderation showed inconsistent performance across crisis types, with sensitivity below 0.10 for some categories, meaning missed crises.
quote: NVIDIA NeMo and OpenAI Omni Moderation Latest exhibited inconsistent performance across specific crisis types, with sensitivity for some categories falling below 0.10.
sample_unit: messages (1,800 simulated plus 794 Aegis mental health-related)

title: Shallow Robustness, Deep Vulnerabilities: Multi-Turn Evaluation of Medical LLMs
outcome: LLM accuracy under misleading context and challenged answers across multi-turn medical QA
effect: Accuracy dropped from 91.2% to as low as 13.5% for Claude Sonnet 4 in multi-turn settings. Models did reasonably well under shallow perturbations. Indirect, context-based interventions were often more harmful than direct suggestions.
quote: Using controlled interventions on the MedQA dataset, we evaluate five state-of-the-art LLMs and find that while models perform reasonably well under shallow perturbations, they exhibit severe vulnerabilities in multi-turn settings, with accuracy dropping from 91.2% to as low as 13.5% for Claude Sonnet 4.

title: MEDEQUALQA: Evaluating Biases in LLMs with Counterfactual Reasoning
outcome: Stability of GPT-4.1 reasoning traces across counterfactual pronoun variants (STS)
effect: Overall high similarity (mean STS >0.80), but consistent localized divergences in cited risk factors, guideline anchors, and differential ordering, even when final diagnoses remain unchanged.
quote: Our results show overall high similarity (mean STS >0.80), but reveal consistent localized divergences in cited risk factors, guideline anchors, and differential ordering, even when final diagnoses remain unchanged.
sample_unit: benchmark items (counterfactual vignette ablations, ~23,000 per pronoun variant)

title: GAPS: A Clinically Grounded, Automated Benchmark for Evaluating AI Clinicians
outcome: Model robustness to adversarial perturbations on the P-axis of the GAPS benchmark
effect: Models were reported as highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations (P-axis); performance also degraded sharply with reasoning depth (G-axis). No numeric effect sizes were given in the abstract.
quote: Evaluating state-of-the-art models on the benchmark revealed key failure modes: performance degrades sharply with increased reasoning depth (G-axis), models struggle with answer completeness (A-axis), and they are highly vulnerable to adversarial perturbations (P-axis) as well as certain safety issues (S-axis).

title: Robust or Suggestible? Exploring Non-Clinical Induction in LLM Drug-Safety Decisions
outcome: Change in LLM adverse event predictions when persona socio-demographic attributes varied
effect: Systematic disparities in AE prediction accuracy; disadvantaged groups (low education, unstable housing) were frequently assigned higher predicted AE likelihoods than privileged groups (postgraduate-educated, privately insured).
quote: Disadvantaged groups (e.g., low education, unstable housing) were frequently assigned higher predicted AE likelihoods than more privileged groups (e.g., postgraduate-educated, privately insured).

title: Stable Prediction of Adverse Events in Medical Time-Series Data
outcome: Accuracy and temporal stability of per-patient risk trajectories across six early event prediction tasks
effect: Existing methods, especially LLMs, struggle to jointly optimize accuracy and stability, with notably poor recall at high-precision operating points.
quote: Across tasks, existing methods, especially LLMs, struggle to jointly optimize accuracy and stability, with notably poor recall at high-precision operating points.

title: Telling Speculative Stories to Help Humans Imagine the Harms of Healthcare AI
outcome: Range of harm types identified by participants with vs without AI-generated stories
effect: Story readers distributed responses more evenly across all 17 harm types; those without stories focused primarily on privacy and well-being (79.1%).
quote: In a user study, participants who read stories recognized a broader range of harms, distributing their responses more evenly across all 17 harm types.

title: Demo: Guide-RAG: Evidence-Driven Corpus Curation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Long COVID
outcome: LLM-judged faithfulness, relevance, comprehensiveness across six RAG corpus configurations for Long COVID questions
effect: Corpus combining clinical guidelines with high-quality systematic reviews consistently outperformed narrow single-guideline corpora and large-scale literature databases; no numeric results are given in the text.
quote: Our RAG corpus configuration combining clinical guidelines with high-quality systematic reviews consistently outperformed both narrow single-guideline approaches and large-scale literature databases.

title: Reliability of Large Language Model Generated Clinical Reasoning in Assisted Reproductive Technology: Blinded Comparative Evaluation Study
outcome: Agreement between AI evaluator (GPT-4o) and senior clinician ratings of CoT quality differences
effect: The AI evaluator failed to discern performance differences between prompting strategies that senior clinicians found significant (p < .001).
quote: Notably, the AI evaluator failed to discern these critical performance differences.

title: Reliability of Large Language Model Generated Clinical Reasoning in Assisted Reproductive Technology: Blinded Comparative Evaluation Study
outcome: prompt strategy effect on CoT quality
effect: Random Few-shot offered no significant improvement over Zero-shot; Selective Few-shot outperformed all human metrics (p < .001).
quote: Critically, the Random Few-shot strategy offered no significant improvement over the Zero-shot baseline, demonstrating that low-quality examples are as ineffective as no examples.

title: Who's Asking? Simulating Role-Based Questions for Conversational AI Evaluation
outcome: LLM response supportiveness and knowledge content for the same question framed by different asker roles
effect: Patient and caregiver roles elicited more supportive responses (+17%) and reduced knowledge content (-19%) than practitioner roles, across five LLMs.
quote: When used to evaluate five LLMs, for the same question but differing roles, we find systematic differences: vulnerable roles, such as patients and caregivers, elicit more supportive responses (+17%) and reduced knowledge content (-19%) in comparison to practitioners.

title: ReclAIm: A Multi-Agent Framework for Monitoring and Correcting Performance Decline in Medical Imaging AI
outcome: Detection of performance decline between test and inference data by automated monitoring
effect: Performance discrepancies between test and inference data were detected in 8 of 18 models, prompting fine-tuning.
quote: Performance discrepancies between test and inference data were detected in 8 of 18 models, prompting fine-tuning workflows that reduced performance gaps.

title: ReclAIm: A Multi-Agent Framework for Monitoring and Correcting Performance Decline in Medical Imaging AI
outcome: Recovery of performance metrics after fine-tuning models that had declined
effect: With declines of up to 40.6% (cardiomegaly, InceptionV3), fine-tuning restored performance metrics to within 2% of baseline.
quote: In cases with declines of up to 40.6% (cardiomegaly dataset, InceptionV3), fine-tuning restored performance metrics to within 2% of baseline values.

title: ECG-LLM -- training and evaluation of domain-specific large language models for electrocardiography
outcome: Consistency of model rankings across benchmark, automatic, LLM-judge and human expert evaluations
effect: Finetuned Llama 3.1 70B led on multiple-choice and automatic metrics, ranked second to Claude 3.7 in LLM-as-a-judge, while human experts favored Claude 3.7 and RAG for complex queries.
quote: Our findings reveal substantial performance heterogeneity across evaluation methodologies, underscoring assessment complexity.

title: ECG-LLM -- training and evaluation of domain-specific large language models for electrocardiography
outcome: Human expert preference for RAG-grounded outputs versus finetuned models on complex queries
effect: Human expert evaluation favored Claude 3.7 and RAG approaches for complex queries; no numeric effect reported in the abstract.
quote: Human expert evaluation favored Claude 3.7 and RAG approaches for complex queries.

title: Exploring Membership Inference Vulnerabilities in Clinical Large Language Models
outcome: Membership inference leakage of patient records from fine-tuned clinical LLM using loss-based and paraphrase-based attacks
effect: Limited but measurable membership leakage; the clinical LLM showed partial resistance but remained susceptible to subtle privacy risks. No numeric results reported in the text.
quote: Our preliminary findings reveal limited but measurable membership leakage, suggesting that current clinical LLMs provide partial resistance yet remain susceptible to subtle privacy risks that could undermine trust in clinical AI adoption.

title: Investigating LLM Capabilities on Long Context Comprehension for Medical Question Answering
outcome: Effect of retrieval augmentation on long-context medical QA comprehension across single- and multi-document datasets
effect: RAG excels in challenging cases and has best settings differing between single- and multi-document QA datasets, but shows limitations in cases requiring temporal reasoning. No numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: Our quantitative analysis reveals challenging cases where RAG excels while still showing limitations in cases requiring temporal reasoning.

title: Local Obfuscation by GLINER for Impartial Context Aware Lineage: Development and evaluation of PII Removal system
outcome: Character-level precision, recall and F1 of PII removal versus alternative de-identification systems
effect: Fine-tuned GLiNER micro-average F1 0.980 vs Gemini-Pro-2.5 0.845; 95% of documents fully sanitised vs 64% for next-best; 2% entity-level false negative rate remained.
quote: The fine-tuned GLiNER model achieved superior performance, with an overall micro-average F1-score of 0.980, significantly outperforming Gemini-Pro-2.5 (F1-score: 0.845).
sample_unit: test text instances from psychiatric hospital clinical notes

title: Towards Transparent Reasoning: What Drives Faithfulness in Large Language Models?
outcome: Faithfulness of LLM explanations under varied few-shot, prompting, and training settings on BBQ and MedQA
effect: Faithfulness varied significantly with number and quality of few-shot examples and with prompt design; instruction tuning improved measured faithfulness on MedQA.
quote: Our results show: (i) both the quantity and quality of few-shot examples significantly impact model faithfulness; (ii) faithfulness is sensitive to prompting design; (iii) the instruction-tuning phase improves measured faithfulness on MedQA.

title: Can SAEs reveal and mitigate racial biases of LLMs in healthcare?
outcome: Stigmatizing associations in LLM outputs when a Black-associated SAE latent is activated
effect: The Black latent activates on terms like "incarceration", and activating it increases the risk assigned to a patient becoming "belligerent".
quote: For example, activating the Black latent increases the risk assigned to the probability that a patient will become "belligerent".

title: Can SAEs reveal and mitigate racial biases of LLMs in healthcare?
outcome: Effectiveness of SAE latent steering for mitigating racial bias in LLM outputs
effect: Steering improved bias in simple settings but was less successful for realistic, complex clinical tasks; described as of marginal utility for realistic tasks.
quote: We find that this offers improvements in simple settings, but is less successful for more realistic and complex clinical tasks.

title: Can SAEs reveal and mitigate racial biases of LLMs in healthcare?
outcome: risk prediction under race latent activation
effect: Activating the Black latent increased assigned probability a patient will become “belligerent”.
quote: For example, activating the Black latent increases the risk assigned to the probability that a patient will become "belligerent".

title: MedRECT: A Medical Reasoning Benchmark for Error Correction in Clinical Texts
outcome: Error detection/correction performance gap between English and Japanese clinical texts
effect: Cross-lingual evaluation reveals 5-10% performance gaps from English to Japanese, with smaller disparities for reasoning models.
quote: (ii) cross-lingual evaluation reveals 5-10% performance gaps from English to Japanese, with smaller disparities for reasoning models;

title: Diagnosing Hallucination Risk in AI Surgical Decision-Support: A Sequential Framework for Sequential Validation
outcome: Recommendation quality under amplified case complexity stress-testing
effect: Recommendation quality degraded by 7.4% under amplified complexity, while rationality (+2.0%), readability (+1.7%) and diagnosis (+4.7%) marginally improved.
quote: Multidimensional stress-testing exposed model-specific vulnerabilities, with recommendation quality degrading by 7.4% under amplified complexity.

title: The Biased Oracle: Assessing LLMs' Understandability and Empathy in Medical Diagnoses
outcome: Readability of LLM diagnostic explanations for patients
effect: LLMs generated overly complex content as measured by readability metrics, leading to uneven accessibility; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: However, they also generate overly complex content and display biased affective empathy, leading to uneven accessibility and support.

title: The Biased Oracle: Assessing LLMs' Understandability and Empathy in Medical Diagnoses
outcome: Change in LLM explanation and empathy when patient socio-demographic attributes vary
effect: LLMs adapted explanations to socio-demographic variables and patient conditions and showed biased affective empathy, producing uneven accessibility and support; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: However, they also generate overly complex content and display biased affective empathy, leading to uneven accessibility and support.

title: Between Myths and Metaphors: Rethinking LLMs for SRH in Conservative Contexts
outcome: LLM interpretation of indirect, colloquial sexual and reproductive health language in clinical interactions
effect: LLMs struggled with semantic drift, myths, and polysemy when interpreting indirect communication in clinical interactions; no numeric results are reported in the abstract.
quote: Our analysis identifies two axes of communication (referential domain and expression approach) and shows LLMs struggle with semantic drift, myths, and polysemy in clinical interactions.
sample_unit: not reported (clinical observations, interviews, and focus groups with clinicians and patients)

title: Demo: Statistically Significant Results On Biases and Errors of LLMs Do Not Guarantee Generalizable Results
outcome: LLM answer differences across patient gender, race, and writing style in synthetic medical queries
effect: Only specific (answering, evaluation) LLM pairs yielded statistically significant differences across writing styles, genders, and races; results did not generalize across LLM pairs.
quote: We find that LLM annotators exhibit low agreement scores (average Cohen's Kappa $κ=0.118$), and only specific (answering, evaluation) LLM pairs yield statistically significant differences across writing styles, genders, and races.

title: Demo: Statistically Significant Results On Biases and Errors of LLMs Do Not Guarantee Generalizable Results
outcome: Inter-annotator agreement among LLM judges in the absence of ground truth
effect: LLM annotators showed low agreement (average Cohen's Kappa 0.118), so single-evaluator results may be statistically significant but non-generalizable.
quote: We find that LLM annotators exhibit low agreement scores (average Cohen's Kappa $κ=0.118$), and only specific (answering, evaluation) LLM pairs yield statistically significant differences across writing styles, genders, and races.

title: RxSafeBench: Identifying Medication Safety Issues of Large Language Models in Simulated Consultation
outcome: LLM ability to choose safe medications given contraindications and drug interactions in simulated consultations
effect: Current LLMs struggle to integrate contraindication and interaction knowledge, especially when risks are implied rather than explicit; no numeric results in the abstract.
quote: Results show that current LLMs struggle to integrate contraindication and interaction knowledge, especially when risks are implied rather than explicit.

title: LLMs Do Not See Age: Assessing Demographic Bias in Automated Systematic Review Synthesis
outcome: Age-related entity retention and hallucination in LLM summaries across child, adult, and older adult groups
effect: Systematic disparities across models and age groups. Demographic fidelity was lowest for adult-focused summaries, and under-represented populations were more prone to hallucinations. No numeric values are given in the abstract.
quote: Our results reveal systematic disparities across models and age groups: demographic fidelity is lowest for adult-focused summaries, and under-represented populations are more prone to hallucinations.

title: MedVoiceBias: A Controlled Study of Audio LLM Behavior in Clinical Decision-Making
outcome: Clinical recommendation shifts under audio input variation versus text
effect: Surgical recommendations for audio inputs varied by as much as 35% compared to identical text-based inputs, with one model providing 80% fewer recommendations.
quote: Our findings reveal a severe modality bias: surgical recommendations for audio inputs varied by as much as 35% compared to identical text-based inputs, with one model providing 80% fewer recommendations.
sample_unit: clinical cases (each synthesized with 36 voice profiles)

title: MedVoiceBias: A Controlled Study of Audio LLM Behavior in Clinical Decision-Making
outcome: age-based voice disparity
effect: Age disparities of up to 12% occurred between young and elderly voices and persisted in most models despite chain-of-thought prompting.
quote: Further analysis uncovered age disparities of up to 12% between young and elderly voices, which persisted in most models despite chain-of-thought prompting.
sample_unit: clinical cases (each synthesized with 36 voice profiles)

title: MedVoiceBias: A Controlled Study of Audio LLM Behavior in Clinical Decision-Making
outcome: Audio LLM surgical recommendations varying by voice age, gender, emotion versus identical text inputs
effect: Surgical recommendations for audio varied by up to 35% versus text; age disparities up to 12% between young and elderly voices, persisting in most models despite chain-of-thought prompting.
quote: Further analysis uncovered age disparities of up to 12% between young and elderly voices, which persisted in most models despite chain-of-thought prompting.
sample_unit: clinical cases (each synthesized with 36 voice profiles)

title: Contradictions in Context: Challenges for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Healthcare
outcome: Effect of outdated or contradictory retrieved PubMed abstracts on RAG answer accuracy and consistency
effect: Contradictions between highly similar retrieved abstracts degraded performance, causing inconsistencies and reduced factual accuracy in model answers. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
quote: Our findings show that contradictions between highly similar abstracts do, in fact, degrade performance, leading to inconsistencies and reduced factual accuracy in model answers.

title: Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine: A Large-Scale, Systematic Expert Evaluation and Practical Insights
outcome: Factuality and completeness of RAG vs non-RAG LLM responses, expert-rated
effect: Standard RAG often degraded performance: factuality and completeness dropped by up to 6% and 5% versus non-RAG; only 22% of top-16 passages relevant; evidence selection precision 41-43%, recall 27-49%.
quote: Contrary to expectation, standard RAG often degraded performance: only 22% of top-16 passages were relevant, evidence selection remained weak (precision 41-43%, recall 27-49%), and factuality and completeness dropped by up to 6% and 5%, respectively, compared with non-RAG variants.
sample_unit: model outputs annotated by 18 medical experts (80,502 annotations; 200 queries)

title: Rethinking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine: A Large-Scale, Systematic Expert Evaluation and Practical Insights
outcome: retrieved passage relevance
effect: Only 22% of top-16 passages were relevant.
quote: Contrary to expectation, standard RAG often degraded performance: only 22% of top-16 passages were relevant, evidence selection remained weak (precision 41-43%, recall 27-49%), and factuality and completeness dropped by up to 6% and 5%, respectively, compared with non-RAG variants.
sample_unit: model outputs annotated by 18 medical experts (80,502 annotations; 200 queries)

title: Simulating Psychological Risks in Human-AI Interactions: Real-Case Informed Modeling of AI-Induced Addiction, Anorexia, Depression, Homicide, Psychosis, and Suicide
outcome: LLM detection of distress and prevention of harm escalation in multi-turn simulated conversations
effect: Critical gaps found in detecting psychological distress, responding appropriately to vulnerable users, and preventing harm escalation across 157,054 simulated turns and 2,160 scenarios.
quote: Through the analysis of 157,054 simulated conversation turns, we identify critical gaps in detecting psychological distress, responding appropriately to vulnerable users, and preventing harm escalation.

title: Simulating Psychological Risks in Human-AI Interactions: Real-Case Informed Modeling of AI-Induced Addiction, Anorexia, Depression, Homicide, Psychosis, and Suicide
outcome: LLM response performance varying by simulated persona demographics such as age and income
effect: LLMs performed worse with elderly users but better with low- and middle-income groups compared to high-income groups.
quote: Regression analysis reveals variability across persona types: LLMs tend to perform worse with elderly users but better with low- and middle-income groups compared to high-income groups.

title: Data Poisoning Vulnerabilities Across Healthcare AI Architectures: A Security Threat Analysis
outcome: Success rate and detection time of data poisoning attacks on healthcare AI
effect: Attackers with 100-500 poisoned samples compromised healthcare AI regardless of dataset size, often over 60 percent success; detection estimated at 6 to 12 months or not at all.
quote: Our findings indicate that attackers with access to only 100-500 samples can compromise healthcare AI regardless of dataset size, often achieving over 60 percent success, with detection taking an estimated 6 to 12 months or sometimes not occurring at all.

title: CrossMed: A Multimodal Cross-Task Benchmark for Compositional Generalization in Medical Imaging
outcome: Performance on unseen modality-anatomy-task combinations versus seen combinations
effect: Related-split models reached 83.2% classification accuracy and 0.75 segmentation cIoU; performance dropped significantly under Unrelated and zero-overlap conditions.
quote: Models trained on Related splits achieve 83.2 percent classification accuracy and 0.75 segmentation cIoU, while performance drops significantly under Unrelated and zero-overlap conditions, demonstrating the benchmark difficulty.

title: Identifying Imaging Follow-Up in Radiology Reports: A Comparative Analysis of Traditional ML and LLM Approaches
outcome: Compared LLMs against simpler traditional ML baselines on same follow-up imaging classification data
effect: GPT-4o (Advanced) F1 = 0.832 and GPT-OSS-20B (Advanced) F1 = 0.828; LR and SVM performed strongly (F1 = 0.776 and 0.775), so simpler models remain valuable baselines.
quote: LR and SVM also performed strongly (F1 = 0.776 and 0.775), underscoring that while LLMs approach human-level agreement through prompt optimization, interpretable and resource-efficient models remain valuable baselines.

title: TCM-5CEval: Extended Deep Evaluation Benchmark for LLM's Comprehensive Clinical Research Competence in Traditional Chinese Medicine
outcome: LLM accuracy under permuted answer-option order in TCM benchmark questions
effect: All 15 evaluated models, including top scorers, showed substantial performance degradation when option ordering was varied, indicating positional bias and fragile inference. No numbers given in the abstract.
quote: All evaluated models, including the highest-scoring ones, displayed a substantial performance degradation when faced with varied question option ordering, indicating a pervasive sensitivity to positional bias and a lack of robust understanding.

title: Can Large Language Models Function as Qualified Pediatricians? A Systematic Evaluation in Real-World Clinical Contexts
outcome: LLM performance on licensing-level exam questions versus more complex tasks
effect: Qwen3-235B-A22B achieved over 90% accuracy on licensing-level questions, but performance declined ~15% as task complexity increased, revealing limitations in complex reasoning.
quote: State-of-the-art models performed well on foundational knowledge, with Qwen3-235B-A22B achieving over 90% accuracy on licensing-level questions, but performance declined ~15% as task complexity increased, revealing limitations in complex reasoning.

title: Generalist Foundation Models Are Not Clinical Enough for Hospital Operations
outcome: Zero-shot foundation model AUROC on real EHR-derived hospital operations tasks versus benchmark strength
effect: Zero-shot general-purpose and specialized models underperformed on four of five tasks (36.6%-71.7% AUROC); mortality prediction was the exception.
quote: In zero-shot settings, both general-purpose and specialized models underperform on four of five tasks (36.6%-71.7% AUROC), with mortality prediction being an exception.

title: How to Train Private Clinical Language Models: A Comparative Study of Privacy-Preserving Pipelines for ICD-9 Coding
outcome: Membership-inference AUC and ICD-9 coding utility across differentially private training pipelines
effect: Knowledge distillation from DP-trained teachers recovered up to 63% of non-private performance at epsilon 4 and 6 with membership-inference AUC approximately 0.5, outperforming direct DP-SGD and DP-synthetic data.
quote: At moderate and relaxed privacy budgets ($\varepsilon \in \{4, 6\}$), knowledge distillation from DP-trained teachers outperforms both direct DP-SGD and DP-synthetic data training, recovering up to 63\% of the non-private performance whilst maintaining strong empirical privacy (membership-inference AUC $\approx$ 0.5).

title: Cost-Aware Prediction (CAP): An LLM-Enhanced Machine Learning Pipeline and Decision Support System for Heart Failure Mortality Prediction
outcome: Clinician evaluation of cost-benefit threshold visualization and LLM patient-level analysis for decision support
effect: System was well received by clinicians, but feedback stressed the need to improve technical accuracy for speculative tasks. No comparator; clinician evaluation was qualitative and no numbers were reported in the abstract.
quote: The system was well received according to the evaluation by clinicians.

title: Balancing Natural Language Processing Accuracy and Normalisation in Extracting Medical Insights
outcome: accuracy versus simpler rule-based methods
effect: Rule-based methods had higher accuracy for information retrieval, especially age and sex; LLMs excelled in drug name recognition.
quote: Results demonstrate that rule-based methods provide higher accuracy in information retrieval tasks, particularly for age and sex extraction.

title: Balancing Natural Language Processing Accuracy and Normalisation in Extracting Medical Insights
outcome: accuracy of rule-based methods versus LLMs in information retrieval
effect: Rule-based methods provided higher accuracy than LLMs in information retrieval tasks, particularly for age and sex extraction
quote: Results demonstrate that rule-based methods provide higher accuracy in information retrieval tasks, particularly for age and sex extraction.

title: CARE-RAG - Clinical Assessment and Reasoning in RAG
outcome: LLM reasoning accuracy on Written Exposure Therapy questions when authoritative guideline passages are provided via RAG
effect: Errors persisted even when authoritative passages were provided; RAG can constrain outputs, but reasoning must be assessed as rigorously as retrieval. No numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: Our results highlight both the potential and the risks: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) can constrain outputs, but safe deployment requires assessing reasoning as rigorously as retrieval.

title: WER is Unaware: Assessing How ASR Errors Distort Clinical Understanding in Patient Facing Dialogue
outcome: Correlation of WER and other ASR metrics with clinician-assigned clinical risk labels
effect: WER and a comprehensive suite of existing metrics correlated poorly with clinician-assigned risk labels (No, Minimal, Significant Impact); the optimized LLM judge reached 90% accuracy and Cohen's kappa 0.816.
quote: Our analysis reveals that WER and a comprehensive suite of existing metrics correlate poorly with the clinician-assigned risk labels (No, Minimal, or Significant Impact).

title: Auditing Sex/Gender Disparities in Emergency Triage with LLM-based Paired Comparisons
outcome: Change in predicted triage severity when only patient sex is flipped in otherwise identical records
effect: Sex-swapped pairs were more likely to get a lower-severity score as female than male: 1.1% (95% CI 0.9-1.3) in the French cohort, 2.2% (1.7-2.7) in MIMIC-IV.
quote: Fine-tuning Mistral NeMo 12B for triage prediction and using Mistral Small 24B for pair generation, we find otherwise identical presentations were more likely to receive a lower-severity predicted score as female than male: 1.1% (95% CI 0.9-1.3) in the French cohort, 2.2% (1.7-2.7) in MIMIC-IV.
sample_unit: emergency department admissions (French cohort, more than 140,000)

title: Auditing Sex/Gender Disparities in Emergency Triage with LLM-based Paired Comparisons
outcome: Between-sex prediction gap after retraining on sex-neutralized inputs
effect: Retraining on sex-neutralized inputs eliminated the between-sex prediction gap, indicating the asymmetry is mediated by explicit sex markers. Effect on overall accuracy not reported in the abstract.
quote: A model retrained on sex-neutralized inputs eliminated the between-sex prediction gap, indicating the asymmetry is mediated by explicit sex markers.
sample_unit: emergency department admissions (French cohort, more than 140,000)

title: SCARE: A Benchmark for SQL Correction and Question Answerability Classification for Reliable EHR Question Answering
outcome: Post-hoc verification of generated SQL: answerability classification versus SQL error correction
effect: Benchmarked post-hoc verification methods, from two-stage to agentic, showed a critical trade-off between question classification and SQL error correction. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
quote: Our experiments reveal a critical trade-off between question classification and SQL error correction, highlighting key challenges and outlining directions for future research.
sample_unit: triples of question, candidate SQL query, and expected output

title: Leveraging Evidence-Guided LLMs to Enhance Trustworthy Depression Diagnosis
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and confidence score of DSM-5-grounded evidence-guided prompting versus direct and CoT prompting
effect: On OpenBioLLM, EGDR raised accuracy from 0.31 (Direct) to 0.76 and DCS from 0.50 to 0.67. On MedLlama, DCS rose from 0.58 (CoT) to 0.77. Overall gains were up to +45% accuracy and +36% DCS.
quote: For instance, on OpenBioLLM, EGDR improves accuracy from 0.31 (Direct) to 0.76 and increases DCS from 0.50 to 0.67.

title: MindEval: Benchmarking Language Models on Multi-turn Mental Health Support
outcome: LLM therapeutic communication quality in simulated multi-turn mental health conversations, including AI-specific problematic patterns
effect: All 12 LLMs scored below 4 out of 6 on average, with particular weaknesses in problematic AI-specific communication patterns; performance worsened with longer interactions and severe symptoms.
quote: Then, we evaluate 12 state-of-the-art LLMs and show that all models struggle, scoring below 4 out of 6, on average, with particular weaknesses in problematic AI-specific patterns of communication.

title: Cognitive bias in LLM reasoning compromises interpretation of clinical oncology notes
outcome: Guideline-discordant and potentially harmful recommendations associated with reasoning errors in oncology
effect: Reasoning errors occurred in 23 percent of interpretations; reasoning failures were associated with guideline-discordant and potentially harmful recommendations, particularly in advanced disease management.
quote: Reasoning failures were associated with guideline-discordant and potentially harmful recommendations, particularly in advanced disease management.
sample_unit: LLM responses to prostate cancer consult notes

title: Generalist Large Language Models Outperform Clinical Tools on Medical Benchmarks
