outcome: Comparative benchmark performance of clinical AI tools versus generalist LLMs on the same items
effect: Generalist LLMs consistently outperformed OpenEvidence and UpToDate Expert AI, with GPT-5 highest. Clinical tools showed deficits in completeness, communication quality, context awareness, and systems-based safety reasoning.
quote: Generalist models consistently outperformed clinical tools, with GPT-5 achieving the highest scores, while OpenEvidence and UpToDate demonstrated deficits in completeness, communication quality, context awareness, and systems-based safety reasoning.

title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
outcome: Physician performance with AI assistance versus conventional resources; omission of AI-generated recommendations
effect: In a randomized study of 101 physicians, AI assistance improved performance compared to conventional resources, but AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable AI recommendations and still scored lower than many AI systems alone.
quote: In a randomized study of 101 U.S.-licensed generalist physicians, AI assistance improved physician performance compared to conventional resources.

title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
outcome: Whether medical knowledge benchmark performance predicts clinical safety of deployed AI tools
effect: Despite strong performance on medical knowledge benchmarks, widely used AI tools can produce consultation advice with potential for severe harm.
quote: Collectively, these results show that despite strong performance on medical knowledge benchmarks, widely used AI tools can produce medical consultation advice with the potential for severe harm, and highlight the need for explicit measurement of clinical safety.

title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
outcome: Frequency and severity of harmful errors, especially omissions, in LLM consultation recommendations
effect: Direct application of recommendations carried potential for severe harm in up to 24.6% of cases, with errors of omission accounting for more than 80% of severe errors.
quote: Across 20 notable LLMs and 4 widely used retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) clinical AI tools, direct application of recommendations carried potential for severe harm in up to 24.6% of cases, with errors of omission accounting for more than 80% of severe errors.

title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
outcome: severe-harm potential in AI recommendations
effect: Severe-harm potential in up to 24.6% of cases; omission errors were more than 80% of severe errors.
quote: Across 20 notable LLMs and 4 widely used retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) clinical AI tools, direct application of recommendations carried potential for severe harm in up to 24.6% of cases, with errors of omission accounting for more than 80% of severe errors.

title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
outcome: comparative harm potential across systems
effect: Harm potential was not uniform; clinical AI tools outperformed generalist LLMs; multi-agent teaming improved generalist models.
quote: Harm potential was not uniform across systems, with clinical AI tools outperforming generalist LLMs, and multi-agent AI teaming further improving performance in generalist models.

title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
outcome: human-AI team versus standalone performance
effect: AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable AI-generated recommendations and scored lower than many AI systems alone.
quote: However, AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable AI-generated recommendations and still scored lower than many AI systems alone.

title: First, do NOHARM: a medical safety benchmark and randomized study of physician and AI teaming on clinical consultations
outcome: human-AI team performance compared to standalone AI
effect: AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable recommendations and scored lower than many standalone AI systems
quote: However, AI-assisted physicians frequently omitted valuable AI-generated recommendations and still scored lower than many AI systems alone.

title: Many-to-One Adversarial Consensus: Exposing Multi-Agent Collusion Risks in AI-Based Healthcare
outcome: Attack success and harmful recommendation rates under colluding adversarial assistant agents
effect: Collusion drives Attack Success Rate (ASR) and Harmful Recommendation Rates (HRR) up to 100% in unprotected systems.
quote: Using 50 representative clinical questions, we find that collusion drives the Attack Success Rate (ASR) and Harmful Recommendation Rates (HRR) up to 100% in unprotected systems.

title: Many-to-One Adversarial Consensus: Exposing Multi-Agent Collusion Risks in AI-Based Healthcare
outcome: Accuracy of decisions with a guideline-checking verifier agent versus unprotected systems
effect: The verifier agent restored 100% accuracy by blocking adversarial consensus, versus up to 100% ASR/HRR in unprotected systems.
quote: In contrast, the verifier agent restores 100% accuracy by blocking adversarial consensus.

title: Balancing Safety and Helpfulness in Healthcare AI Assistants through Iterative Preference Alignment
outcome: Harmful query detection under adversarial prompts versus erroneous refusals of benign queries after preference alignment
effect: Up to 42% improvement in safety-related metrics for harmful query detection, with trade-offs against erroneous refusals and architecture-dependent calibration biases.
quote: Our results show up to 42% improvement in safety-related metrics for harmful query detection, alongside interesting trade-offs against erroneous refusals, thereby exposing architecture-dependent calibration biases.

title: Optimizing Medical Question-Answering Systems: A Comparative Study of Fine-Tuned and Zero-Shot Large Language Models with RAG Framework
outcome: Answer accuracy and unsupported content with versus without retrieval grounding on medical QA benchmarks
effect: Fine-tuned LLaMA 2 with RAG reached 71.8% accuracy on PubMedQA vs 55.4% zero-shot baseline; grounding reduced unsupported content by approximately 60%.
quote: We also detail the system design and fine-tuning methodology, demonstrating that grounding answers in retrieved evidence reduces unsupported content by approximately 60%.

title: NeuroABench: A Multimodal Evaluation Benchmark for Neurosurgical Anatomy Identification
outcome: MLLM accuracy on neurosurgical anatomical structure identification benchmark
effect: Best-performing MLLM achieved only 40.87% accuracy in anatomical identification; best of four trainees scored 56%, lowest 28%, average 46.5%.
quote: Experiments on over 10 state-of-the-art MLLMs reveal significant limitations, with the best-performing model achieving only 40.87% accuracy in anatomical identification tasks.
sample_unit: annotated neurosurgical video clips/questions (9 hours of video, 89 procedures, 68 anatomical structures)

title: ContextualSHAP : Enhancing SHAP Explanations Through Contextual Language Generation
outcome: Perceived understandability of SHAP explanations with LLM text plus visuals versus visual-only
effect: Generated contextual text explanations were perceived as more understandable and contextually appropriate than visual-only outputs (Likert surveys and interviews; preliminary findings).
quote: The results, based on Likert-scale surveys and follow-up interviews, indicate that the generated explanations were perceived as more understandable and contextually appropriate compared to visual-only outputs.

title: Motion2Meaning: A Clinician-Centered Framework for Contestable LLM in Parkinson's Disease Gait Interpretation
outcome: Whether clinicians can validate correct predictions and contest erroneous AI outputs via the contestable interface
effect: The interface let clinicians validate correct predictions and successfully contest a portion of the model's errors. XMED found explanation discrepancies in 7.45% of incorrect vs 1.56% of correct predictions.
quote: XMED successfully identifies model unreliability by detecting a five-fold increase in explanation discrepancies in incorrect predictions (7.45%) compared to correct ones (1.56%), while our LLM-powered interface enables clinicians to validate correct predictions and successfully contest a portion of the model's errors.

title: A Principle-based Framework for the Development and Evaluation of Large Language Models for Health and Wellness
outcome: Whether a staged deployment with consented users surfaced problems missed in initial testing
effect: Staged deployment with over 13,000 consented users systematically identified challenges not apparent during initial testing, guiding targeted system improvements.
quote: Through the application of this framework to the Fitbit Insights explorer in a staged deployment involving over 13,000 consented users, challenges not apparent during initial testing were systematically identified.

title: A Principle-based Framework for the Development and Evaluation of Large Language Models for Health and Wellness
outcome: Whether real-world user feedback adds to isolated technical evaluations
effect: Real-world feedback led to targeted improvements and showed the need to combine isolated technical evaluations with real-world user feedback; no numeric results reported.
quote: This process guided targeted improvements to the system and demonstrated the necessity of combining isolated technical evaluations with real-world user feedback.

title: Knowledge-Guided Large Language Model for Automatic Pediatric Dental Record Understanding and Safe Antibiotic Recommendation
outcome: Effect of knowledge graph and RAG grounding on record understanding, antibiotic recommendation accuracy, and safety
effect: KG-LLM vs Llama-2 baseline: F1 0.914 vs 0.867, Top-1 dose-drug-duration accuracy 0.782 vs 0.716, unsafe antibiotic suggestions reduced by 50%; ablation shows KG and RAG each contribute substantially.
quote: Ablation analyses indicate that the knowledge graph, RAG, and safety modules each contribute substantially to clinical reliability and interpretability.

title: Knowledge-Guided Large Language Model for Automatic Pediatric Dental Record Understanding and Safe Antibiotic Recommendation
outcome: Contribution of deterministic rule plus learned-classifier safety validation to catching allergy, contraindication, and dosing errors
effect: Unsafe antibiotic suggestions reduced by 50% versus baseline; ablation indicates safety module contributes substantially to clinical reliability.
quote: Ablation analyses indicate that the knowledge graph, RAG, and safety modules each contribute substantially to clinical reliability and interpretability.

title: Black-Box Behavioral Distillation Breaks Safety Alignment in Medical LLMs
outcome: Rate of unsafe completions under adversarial prompts across surrogate, Meditron-7B, and base model
effect: Distilled surrogate produced unsafe completions for 86% of adversarial prompts, versus Meditron-7B 66% and untuned base model 46%; distillation cost $12.
quote: With a cost of $12, the surrogate achieves strong fidelity on benign inputs while producing unsafe completions for 86% of adversarial prompts, far exceeding both Meditron-7B (66%) and the untuned base model (46%).

title: MiraMind: Benchmarking Reliable Mental Health Reasoning beyond Answer Accuracy
outcome: Whether LLM judgments' certainty and specificity exceed what limited mental-health evidence supports
effect: Across 20 LLMs, a 'restraint gap' was found: the specificity or certainty of model judgments exceeds what limited evidence supports. No numbers are given in the abstract.
quote: Evaluating 20 LLMs reveals a restraint gap, in which the specificity or certainty of model judgments exceeds what limited evidence supports.

title: COMPARE: Clinical Optimization with Modular Planning and Assessment via RAG-Enhanced AI-OCT: Superior Decision Support for Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Compared to ChatGPT-5 and Junior Operators
outcome: Agreement of PCI planning decisions with expert record, RAG-enhanced CA-GPT versus general ChatGPT-5
effect: Pre-PCI median agreement score 5 (IQR 3.75-5) for CA-GPT vs 3 (2-4) for ChatGPT-5 (P<0.001); post-PCI 5 (4.75-5) vs 4 (4-5) (P<0.001).
quote: For pre-PCI planning, CA-GPT demonstrated significantly higher median agreement scores (5[IQR 3.75-5]) compared to both ChatGPT-5 (3[2-4], P<0.001) and junior physicians (4[3-4], P<0.001).

title: Script Gap: Evaluating LLM Triage on Indian Languages in Native vs Romanized Scripts in a Real World Setting
outcome: LLM triage performance on romanized versus native-script health queries
effect: Consistent degradation for romanized messages, with gaps reaching up to 24 points across languages and models; nearly 2 million excess triage errors estimated at the partner organization.
quote: Our results reveal consistent degradation in performance for romanized messages, with gap reaching up to 24 points across languages and models.
languages: Indian languages (five, not named in abstract)

title: Script Gap: Evaluating LLM Triage on Indian Languages in Native vs Romanized Scripts in a Real World Setting
outcome: LLM triage robustness to real-world orthographic input variation (romanization)
effect: Performance degrades consistently on romanized input, with gaps of up to 24 points across languages and models.
quote: Our results reveal consistent degradation in performance for romanized messages, with gap reaching up to 24 points across languages and models.
languages: Indian languages (five, not named in abstract)

title: AI-MASLD Metabolic Dysfunction and Information Steatosis of Large Language Models in Unstructured Clinical Narratives
outcome: LLM information extraction from noisy, redundant patient chief complaints across 20 probes
effect: All four models showed functional defects; most collapsed under extreme noise. Qwen3-Max performed best and Gemini 2.5 worst. GPT-4o severely misjudged pulmonary embolism risk secondary to DVT.
quote: Under conditions of extreme noise, most models experienced a functional collapse.

title: Leveraging LLMs for Structured Data Extraction from Unstructured Patient Records
outcome: Errors in expert-annotated reference standard identified by LLM framework
effect: Framework achieved high accuracy against the expert-annotated dataset and identified several annotation errors missed in manual review (no counts reported).
quote: In evaluation, the framework achieved high accuracy across multiple medical characteristics present in large bodies of patient notes when compared against an expert-annotated dataset and identified several annotation errors missed in manual review.

title: DL$^3$M: A Vision-to-Language Framework for Expert-Level Medical Reasoning through Deep Learning and Large Language Models
outcome: Stability of LLM clinical reasoning when prompts vary
effect: None of the 32 LLMs reached human-level stability; even the best LLMs changed their reasoning when prompts varied.
quote: Even the best LLMs change their reasoning when prompts vary.

title: PediatricAnxietyBench: Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Under Parental Anxiety and Pressure in Pediatric Consultations
outcome: Emergency recognition and safety under adversarial parental pressure in pediatric queries
effect: Emergency recognition was absent; adversarial queries reduced safety by 8% (p=0.03), urgency causing largest drop (-1.40); critical failures 4.8% (70B) vs 12.0% (8B).
quote: Hedging strongly correlated with safety (r=0.68, p<0.001), while emergency recognition was absent.

title: PediatricAnxietyBench: Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Under Parental Anxiety and Pressure in Pediatric Consultations
outcome: Diagnostic restraint and disclaimer maintenance under adversarial parental pressure
effect: Adversarial queries reduced safety by 8% (p=0.03); seizure queries showed 33.3% inappropriate diagnosis.
quote: Vulnerabilities appeared in seizures (33.3% inappropriate diagnosis) and post-vaccination queries.

title: Automated Healthcare Thematic Analysis using Multi-Agent Large Language Model: Algorithm Development and Evaluation
outcome: Junior investigators working with CoTI versus CoTI alone; possible overreliance
effect: Human-AI collaboration between CoTI and junior investigators gave only marginal gains compared to CoTI alone; junior investigators may over-rely on CoTI (hypothesis).
quote: In an exploratory human-AI collaboration experiment, we found that the collaboration between CoTI and junior investigators provided only marginal gains compared to CoTI alone.

title: Mitigating hallucinations in healthcare LLMs with granular fact-checking and domain-specific adaptation
outcome: Fact-checking module accuracy against EHR ground-truth propositions
effect: Precision 0.8904, recall 0.8234, F1-score 0.8556 on 3786 propositions extracted from 104 summaries.
quote: The fact-checking module achieves a precision of 0.8904, a recall of 0.8234, and an F1-score of 0.8556.

title: A Women's Health Benchmark for Large Language Models
outcome: LLM failure on missed urgency indicators in women's health queries
effect: Models universally struggle with missed urgency indicators; overall failure rate approximately 60% across the benchmark.
quote: Notably, models universally struggle with "missed urgency" indicators, while newer models like GPT-5 show significant improvements in avoiding inappropriate recommendations.

title: Biosecurity-Aware AI: Agentic Risk Auditing of Soft Prompt Attacks on ESM-Based Variant Predictors
outcome: ESM2 variant predictor performance (AUROC, AUPR) under targeted soft prompt adversarial attacks
effect: ESM2 is sensitive to targeted soft prompt attacks, with measurable performance degradation; exact figures are not given in the abstract.
quote: Using SAGE, we find that even state-of-the-art GFMs like ESM2 are sensitive to targeted soft prompt attacks, resulting in measurable performance degradation.

title: Scalable Stewardship of an LLM-Assisted Clinical Benchmark with Physician Oversight
outcome: Reliability of LLM-assisted reference labels in MedCalc-Bench versus physician ground truth
effect: At least 27% of test labels likely erroneous or incomputable; on 50 physician-validated instances, original labels agreed with physicians 20% (95% CI 11-33%) vs 74% (60-84%) for recomputed labels; original labels underestimate LLM accuracy by 16-23 points.
quote: At least 27% of test labels are likely erroneous or incomputable.

title: Improving Fairness of Large Language Model-Based ICU Mortality Prediction via Case-Based Prompting
outcome: Subgroup prediction disparities and overall AUROC/AUPRC after applying case-based prompting debiasing
effect: AUROC rose from 0.806 to 0.873 and AUPRC from 0.497 to 0.694. Disparities fell by more than 90% in sex and certain White-Black comparisons.
quote: Meanwhile, prediction disparities are substantially reduced across demographic groups, with reductions exceeding 90% in sex and certain White-Black comparisons.

title: MediEval: A Unified Medical Benchmark for Patient-Contextual and Knowledge-Grounded Reasoning in LLMs
outcome: LLM failure modes (hallucinated support, truth inversion) on patient-contextual factual and counterfactual statements
effect: Current proprietary, open-source, and domain-specific LLMs frequently exhibit hallucinated support and truth inversion; CoRFu fine-tuning eliminated truth inversion errors and improved macro-F1 by 16.4 points.
quote: Using this framework, we identify critical failure modes, including hallucinated support and truth inversion, that current proprietary, open-source, and domain-specific LLMs frequently exhibit.
sample_unit: medical statements linked to MIMIC-IV patient contexts

title: A Real-World Evaluation of LLM Medication Safety Reviews in NHS Primary Care
outcome: Whether LLM medication review correct in real-world NHS data beyond benchmark performance
effect: Sensitivity 100% and specificity 83.1% for recognising issues, but all issues and interventions correctly identified in only 46.9% [95% CI 41.1-52.8] of patients.
quote: Our primary LLM system showed strong performance in recognising when a clinical issue is present (sensitivity 100\% [95\% CI 98.2--100], specificity 83.1\% [95\% CI 72.7--90.1]), yet correctly identified all issues and interventions in only 46.9\% [95\% CI 41.1--52.8] of patients.

title: A Real-World Evaluation of LLM Medication Safety Reviews in NHS Primary Care
outcome: Persistence of failure patterns across patient demographic strata
effect: Failure patterns persisted across patient complexity and demographic strata, i.e., no subgroup was spared; not a subgroup-specific disparity.
quote: These patterns persisted across patient complexity and demographic strata, and across a range of state-of-the-art models and configurations.

title: A Real-World Evaluation of LLM Medication Safety Reviews in NHS Primary Care
outcome: LLM overconfidence under uncertainty in medication safety review
effect: Overconfidence in uncertainty was identified as one of five primary failure patterns.
quote: Failure analysis reveals that, in this setting, the dominant failure mechanism is contextual reasoning rather than missing medication knowledge, with five primary patterns: overconfidence in uncertainty, applying standard guidelines without adjusting for patient context, misunderstanding how healthcare is delivered in practice, factual errors, and process blindness.

title: The Illusion of Clinical Reasoning: A Benchmark Reveals the Pervasive Gap in Vision-Language Models for Clinical Competency
outcome: Gap between structured multiple-choice exam-style accuracy and open-ended multimodal clinical task accuracy
effect: Accuracy exceeded 90% on structured multiple-choice questions but scarcely reached 60% on open-ended tasks requiring multimodal integration.
quote: While state-of-the-art models achieved high accuracy, exceeding 90%, on structured multiple-choice questions, their performance markedly declined on open-ended tasks requiring multimodal integration, with accuracy scarcely reaching 60%.

title: Prompt engineering does not universally improve Large Language Model performance across clinical decision-making tasks
outcome: LLM performance on real-world clinical decision tasks versus knowledge assessments
effect: Near-perfect accuracy in final diagnosis, poor performance in relevant diagnostic testing, and moderate performance in remaining tasks across three LLMs.
quote: All models showed high variability by task, achieving near-perfect accuracy in final diagnosis, poor performance in relevant diagnostic testing, and moderate performance in remaining tasks.

title: Prompt engineering does not universally improve Large Language Model performance across clinical decision-making tasks
outcome: accuracy across clinical decision-making tasks
effect: Across 36 case studies: near-perfect final diagnosis, poor relevant diagnostic testing, moderate remaining tasks.
quote: All models showed high variability by task, achieving near-perfect accuracy in final diagnosis, poor performance in relevant diagnostic testing, and moderate performance in remaining tasks.

title: Prompt engineering does not universally improve Large Language Model performance across clinical decision-making tasks
outcome: clinical decision-making performance across sequential tasks
effect: Prompt engineering significantly improved performance on relevant diagnostic testing but was counterproductive for other tasks.
quote: While it significantly improved the performance on the task with lowest baseline accuracy (relevant diagnostic testing), it was counterproductive for others.

title: Benchmark Success, Clinical Failure: When Reinforcement Learning Optimizes for Benchmarks, Not Patients
outcome: Cross-dataset performance change after GRPO training (CheXpert vs NIH)
effect: GRPO improved CheXpert performance by 23% (macro-F1 = 0.346) but degraded NIH cross-dataset performance by 19%.
quote: Evaluations on CheXpert and NIH benchmarks reveal a fundamental tension: GRPO recovers in-distribution performance (23% improvement on CheXpert, macro-F1 = 0.346) but degrades cross-dataset transferability (19% drop on NIH).

title: Reasoning Over Recall: Evaluating the Efficacy of Generalist Architectures vs. Specialized Fine-Tunes in RAG-Based Mental Health Dialogue Systems
outcome: LLM-judged empathy, safety and contextual understanding of RAG mental health chatbot responses
effect: Generalist models scored higher on empathy than domain-specific fine-tunes (3.72 vs. 3.26, p < 0.001); all models performed well on safety; generalists showed better contextual understanding.
quote: We find a clear trend: the generalist models outperform the domain-specific ones in empathy (3.72 vs. 3.26, $p < 0.001$) in spite of being much smaller (3B vs. 7B), and all models perform well in terms of safety, but the generalist models show better contextual understanding and are less prone to overfitting as we observe in the domain-specific models.

title: JMedEthicBench: A Multi-Turn Conversational Benchmark for Evaluating Medical Safety in Japanese Large Language Models
outcome: Model safety under adversarial jailbreak conversations, commercial versus medical-specialized models
effect: Commercial models maintained robust safety; medical-specialized models showed increased vulnerability, which persisted across Japanese and English versions.
quote: we find that commercial models maintain robust safety while medical-specialized models exhibit increased vulnerability.

title: JMedEthicBench: A Multi-Turn Conversational Benchmark for Evaluating Medical Safety in Japanese Large Language Models
outcome: Safety score change across turns of adversarial multi-turn conversations
effect: Safety scores declined significantly across conversation turns (median 9.5 to 5.0, p < 0.001).
quote: Furthermore, safety scores decline significantly across conversation turns (median: 9.5 to 5.0, $p < 0.001$).

title: Clinical Knowledge Graph Construction and Evaluation with Multi-LLMs via Retrieval-Augmented Generation
outcome: Precision, relevance, and ontology compliance of KGs built with schema-constrained RAG vs baseline methods
effect: Reported consistent gains in precision, relevance, and ontology compliance over baseline methods; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: Experimental results demonstrate consistent gains in precision, relevance, and ontology compliance over baseline methods.
sample_unit: oncology cohorts (PDAC and BRCA) of clinical narratives

title: Evaluating the Diagnostic Classification Ability of Multimodal Large Language Models: Insights from the Osteoarthritis Initiative
outcome: Classification accuracy of full MLLM pipelines versus a trained vision encoder alone for knee OA
effect: A trained vision encoder alone outperformed full MLLM pipelines in classification accuracy. Fine-tuning the LLM gave no meaningful improvement over prompt-based guidance.
quote: In our classification task, a trained vision encoder alone could outperform full MLLM pipelines in classification accuracy and fine-tuning the LLM provided no meaningful improvement over prompt-based guidance.

title: CPGPrompt: Translating Clinical Guidelines into LLM-Executable Decision Support
outcome: Binary specialty-referral classification versus fine-grained pathway assignment on synthetic vignettes
effect: Binary referral F1 0.85-1.00 with recall 1.00 ± 0.00 across domains; multi-class pathway F1 was headache 0.47, lower back pain 0.72, prostate cancer 0.77.
quote: The binary specialty referral classification achieved consistently strong performance across all domains (F1: 0.85-1.00), with high recall (1.00 $\pm$ 0.00).

title: PsychEthicsBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Against Australian Mental Health Ethics
outcome: Ethical alignment of domain-specific fine-tuned mental health models versus their base backbone models
effect: Several specialized (fine-tuned) models underperformed their base backbones in ethical alignment across 14 models, so fine-tuning can degrade ethical robustness.
quote: Notably, we find that domain-specific fine-tuning can degrade ethical robustness, as several specialized models underperform their base backbones in ethical alignment.

title: The Forgotten Shield: Safety Grafting in Parameter-Space for Medical MLLMs
outcome: Retention of original safety alignment after medical fine-tuning of MLLMs
effect: Medical fine-tuning frequently induced catastrophic forgetting of the base model's safety alignment (no numbers in abstract).
quote: Furthermore, we find that the medical fine-tuning process frequently induces catastrophic forgetting of the model's original safety alignment.

title: The Forgotten Shield: Safety Grafting in Parameter-Space for Medical MLLMs
outcome: Vulnerability of Medical MLLMs to adversarial and jailbreak inputs
effect: Pervasive safety vulnerabilities across general and medical dimensions, with particular fragility to cross-modality jailbreak attacks (no numbers in abstract).
quote: Our empirical analysis reveals pervasive vulnerabilities across both general and medical-specific safety dimensions in existing models, particularly highlighting their fragility against cross-modality jailbreak attacks.

title: Accommodation and Epistemic Vigilance: A Pragmatic Account of Why LLMs Fail to Challenge Harmful Beliefs
outcome: LLM accommodation of harmful beliefs varying with linguistic encoding of the same premise
effect: Social and linguistic factors (at-issueness, linguistic encoding, source reliability) affect LLM accommodation and explain performance differences across three safety benchmarks (Cancer-Myth, SAGE-Eval, ELEPHANT).
quote: We show that social and linguistic factors known to influence accommodation in humans (at-issueness, linguistic encoding, and source reliability) similarly affect accommodation in LLMs, explaining performance differences across three safety benchmarks that test models' ability to challenge harmful beliefs, spanning misinformation (Cancer-Myth, SAGE-Eval) and sycophancy (ELEPHANT).

title: Self-MedRAG: a Self-Reflective Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Reliable Medical Question Answering
outcome: Benchmark QA accuracy with and without self-reflective evidence-verification loop over retrieval-grounded generation
effect: Self-reflective loop raised MedQA accuracy from 80.00% to 83.33% and PubMedQA accuracy from 69.10% to 79.82%; hybrid retrieval outperformed single-retriever baselines.
quote: Furthermore, the inclusion of the self-reflective loop yielded substantial gains, increasing accuracy on MedQA from 80.00% to 83.33% and on PubMedQA from 69.10% to 79.82%.

title: MLB: A Scenario-Driven Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Clinical Applications
outcome: LLM accuracy on scenario-based clinical tasks versus structured knowledge tasks
effect: Top model Kimi-K2-Instruct scored 77.3% overall and 87.8% on MedRU but only 61.3% in patient-facing SmartServ, showing a translational gap.
quote: Our comprehensive evaluation of 10 leading models reveals a critical translational gap: while the top-ranked model, Kimi-K2-Instruct (77.3% accuracy overall), excels in structured tasks like information extraction (87.8% accuracy in MedRU), performance plummets in patient-facing scenarios (61.3% in SmartServ).

title: MedEinst: Benchmarking the Einstellung Effect in Medical LLMs through Counterfactual Differential Diagnosis
outcome: LLM baseline accuracy versus Bias Trap Rate on counterfactual diagnosis cases
effect: Frontier models achieved high baseline accuracy but severe bias trap rates across 17 LLMs, so accuracy on standard medical benchmarks overstated clinical competence. No numbers in abstract.
quote: Extensive Evaluation of 17 LLMs shows frontier models achieve high baseline accuracy but severe bias trap rates.

title: Benchmarking Egocentric Clinical Intent Understanding Capability for Medical Multimodal Large Language Models
outcome: MLLM performance on egocentric clinical intent understanding benchmark incl. hallucination and sycophancy traps
effect: Current MLLMs struggle with egocentric intent due to over-reliance on global features, producing fabricated observations and uncritical acceptance of invalid instructions. No numeric results in the abstract.
quote: Experiments reveal current MLLMs struggle with egocentric intent due to over-reliance on global features, leading to fabricated observations and uncritical acceptance of invalid instructions.

title: GI-Bench: A Panoramic Benchmark Revealing the Knowledge-Experience Dissociation of Multimodal Large Language Models in Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Against Clinical Standards
outcome: Factual correctness of MLLM-generated endoscopy findings reports versus human endoscopists
effect: Models had superior readability versus humans (p<0.05) but significantly lower factual correctness (p<0.05), driven by over-interpretation and hallucination of visual features.
quote: Furthermore, qualitative analysis revealed a "fluency-accuracy paradox": models generated reports with superior linguistic readability compared with humans (p<0.05) but exhibited significantly lower factual correctness (p<0.05) due to "over-interpretation" and hallucination of visual features.
sample_unit: benchmark images/questions across 20 lesion categories (count not reported)

title: Who Fails Where? LLM and Human Error Patterns in Endometriosis Ultrasound Report Extraction
outcome: LLM extraction accuracy compared with expert human extraction on the same reports
effect: The 20B model reached mean accuracy of 86.02%, beating smaller models. Error profiles were complementary: the LLM was better on syntactic consistency, humans on semantic and contextual interpretation.
quote: Crucially, we identified a highly complementary error profile: the LLM excelled at syntactic consistency (e.g., date/numeric formatting) where humans faltered, while human experts provided superior semantic and contextual interpretation.

title: MedRedFlag: Investigating how LLMs Redirect Misconceptions in Real-World Health Communication
outcome: LLM redirection of false-premise patient health questions compared with clinician responses
effect: LLMs often fail to redirect problematic questions, even when the problematic premise is detected, and give answers that could lead to suboptimal medical decision making.
quote: Our analysis reveals that LLMs often fail to redirect problematic questions, even when the problematic premise is detected, and provide answers that could lead to suboptimal medical decision making.

title: CTest-Metric: A Unified Framework to Assess Clinical Validity of Metrics for CT Report Generation
outcome: Validity of report-generation evaluation metrics against expert ratings and under style or error perturbation
effect: Lexical NLG metrics highly sensitive to stylistic variation; GREEN Score best aligned with experts (Spearman~0.70); CRG negatively correlated; BERTScore-F1 least sensitive to factual error injection.
quote: Using our novel framework, we found that lexical NLG metrics are highly sensitive to stylistic variations; GREEN Score aligns best with expert judgments (Spearman~0.70), while CRG shows negative correlation; and BERTScore-F1 is least sensitive to factual error injection.
sample_unit: CT report cases rated by clinicians (disagreement cases)

title: Measuring Stability Beyond Accuracy in Small Open-Source Medical Large Language Models for Pediatric Endocrinology
outcome: Output divergence under semantically negligible prompt perturbations and system-level differences such as CUDA builds
effect: Small, semantically negligible prompt perturbations led to divergent outputs; CUDA build differences produced statistically significant shifts in model output despite stable accuracy.
quote: This work demonstrates that small, semantically negligible prompt perturbations lead to divergent outputs, raising concerns about reproducibility of LLM-based evaluations and highlights the output variability under different stochastic regimes, emphasizing the need of a broader diagnostic framework to understand potential pitfalls in real-world clinical decision support scenarios.

title: Faithfulness vs. Safety: Evaluating LLM Behavior Under Counterfactual Medical Evidence
outcome: LLM responses to counterfactual, dangerous or implausible medical evidence supplied as context
effect: Models overwhelmingly accepted counterfactual evidence at face value, even when dangerous or implausible, rather than rejecting it. Exact rates not given in the abstract.
quote: Our evaluation across multiple frontier LLMs on MedCounterFact reveals that in the presence of counterfactual evidence, existing models overwhelmingly accept such "evidence" at face value even when it is dangerous or implausible, and provide confident and uncaveated answers.

title: Faithfulness vs. Safety: Evaluating LLM Behavior Under Counterfactual Medical Evidence
outcome: Confidence and caveats in LLM answers given counterfactual medical evidence
effect: Models gave confident, uncaveated answers when the evidence was counterfactual, dangerous or implausible. Exact rates not given in the abstract.
quote: Our evaluation across multiple frontier LLMs on MedCounterFact reveals that in the presence of counterfactual evidence, existing models overwhelmingly accept such "evidence" at face value even when it is dangerous or implausible, and provide confident and uncaveated answers.

title: Knowing When to Abstain: Medical LLMs Under Clinical Uncertainty
outcome: LLM abstention when uncertain on medical multiple-choice questions
effect: Even state-of-the-art, high-accuracy open- and closed-source LLMs often fail to abstain when uncertain; explicit abstention options increased uncertainty and safer abstention; scaling and advanced prompting gave little improvement.
quote: Our systematic evaluation of both open- and closed-source LLMs reveals that even state-of-the-art, high-accuracy models often fail to abstain with uncertain.

title: BioPulse-QA: A Dynamic Biomedical Question-Answering Benchmark for Evaluating Factuality, Robustness, and Bias in Large Language Models
outcome: LLM performance under paraphrased and typographical-error perturbations of biomedical questions
effect: Performance differences were larger for paraphrasing than for typographical errors, showing that input perturbations change model performance.
quote: Performance differences are larger for paraphrasing than for typographical errors, while bias testing shows negligible differences.
sample_unit: expert-verified question-answer pairs and perturbed variants

title: BioPulse-QA: A Dynamic Biomedical Question-Answering Benchmark for Evaluating Factuality, Robustness, and Bias in Large Language Models
outcome: LLM output differences when demographic attributes are varied in questions
effect: Bias testing showed negligible differences across demographic variants.
quote: Performance differences are larger for paraphrasing than for typographical errors, while bias testing shows negligible differences.
sample_unit: expert-verified question-answer pairs and perturbed variants

title: Ethical Risks in Deploying Large Language Models: An Evaluation of Medical Ethics Jailbreaking
outcome: Jailbreak attack success rate of LLMs on Chinese medical ethics themes
effect: Jailbreak ASR reached 82.1%, an ASR Gain of over 80 percentage points; five models including Gemini-2.5-Pro and GPT-4.1 had ASRs of 96% to 100%; Claude-Sonnet-4-Reasoning was most robust.
quote: A systemic collapse of defenses was observed, whereas models demonstrated high baseline compliance, the jailbreak ASR reached 82.1%, representing an ASR Gain of over 80 percentage points.

title: Ethical Risks in Deploying Large Language Models: An Evaluation of Medical Ethics Jailbreaking
outcome: Maintenance of safety boundaries under adversarial multi-turn role-play prompting
effect: Under role-playing, scenario simulation and multi-turn dialogue, jailbreak ASR reached 82.1% (ASR Gain over 80 points), with five models at 96-100% ASR despite high baseline compliance.
quote: A systemic collapse of defenses was observed, whereas models demonstrated high baseline compliance, the jailbreak ASR reached 82.1%, representing an ASR Gain of over 80 percentage points.

title: MedConsultBench: A Full-Cycle, Fine-Grained, Process-Aware Benchmark for Medical Consultation Agents
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy versus information-gathering efficiency and medication safety in consultation agents
effect: Across 19 LLMs, high diagnostic accuracy often masks significant deficiencies in information-gathering efficiency and medication safety, indicating a gap between medical knowledge and clinical practice ability.
quote: Systematic evaluation of 19 large language models reveals that high diagnostic accuracy often masks significant deficiencies in information-gathering efficiency and medication safety.

title: PAIR-SAFE: A Paired-Agent Approach for Runtime Auditing and Refining AI-Mediated Mental Health Support
outcome: MITI-4 dimension scores with vs without Judge-agent runtime auditing (ALLOW/REVISE) of mental health responses
effect: Judge-supervised interactions showed significant improvements in Partnership, Seek Collaboration, and overall Relational quality; specific numbers not given in the abstract.
quote: We find that Judge-supervised interactions show significant improvements in key MITI dimensions, including Partnership, Seek Collaboration, and overall Relational quality.

title: PAIR-SAFE: A Paired-Agent Approach for Runtime Auditing and Refining AI-Mediated Mental Health Support
outcome: MITI therapeutic communication dimensions
effect: Judge-supervised interactions showed significant improvements in Partnership, Seek Collaboration, and overall Relational quality.
quote: We find that Judge-supervised interactions show significant improvements in key MITI dimensions, including Partnership, Seek Collaboration, and overall Relational quality.

title: PAIR-SAFE: A Paired-Agent Approach for Runtime Auditing and Refining AI-Mediated Mental Health Support
outcome: therapeutic relational quality and collaboration
effect: Judge-supervised interactions showed significant improvements in key MITI dimensions, including Partnership, Seek Collaboration, and overall Relational quality
quote: We find that Judge-supervised interactions show significant improvements in key MITI dimensions, including Partnership, Seek Collaboration, and overall Relational quality.

title: Bridging the Knowledge-Action Gap by Evaluating LLMs in Dynamic Dental Clinical Scenarios
outcome: Effect of retrieval-augmented generation on hallucinations in static tasks and dynamic dental workflows
effect: RAG mitigates hallucinations in static tasks, but its efficacy in dynamic workflows is limited and heterogeneous, sometimes causing degradation.
quote: While RAG mitigates hallucinations in static tasks, its efficacy in dynamic workflows is limited and heterogeneous, sometimes causing degradation.

title: Bridging the Knowledge-Action Gap by Evaluating LLMs in Dynamic Dental Clinical Scenarios
outcome: Gap between static knowledge-task performance and dynamic simulated clinical dialogue performance
effect: Models show high proficiency in static objective tasks, but performance drops in dynamic multi-turn clinical dialogues. The bottleneck is active information gathering and dynamic state tracking.
quote: Our analysis reveals that while models demonstrate high proficiency in static objective tasks, their performance precipitates in dynamic clinical dialogues, identifying that the primary bottleneck lies not in knowledge retention, but in the critical challenges of active information gathering and dynamic state tracking.

title: Improving the Safety and Trustworthiness of Medical AI via Multi-Agent Evaluation Loops
outcome: Ethical violations and risk level of LLM responses after iterative automated evaluator-agent review
effect: Iterative multi-agent loop achieved an 89% reduction in ethical violations and a 92% risk downgrade rate across 900 queries.
quote: The iterative multi-agent loop achieved an 89% reduction in ethical violations and a 92% risk downgrade rate, underscoring the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Anonpsy: A Graph-Based Framework for Structure-Preserving De-identification of Psychiatric Narratives
outcome: Re-identification risk and semantic similarity of de-identified psychiatric narratives versus an LLM-only rewriting baseline
effect: Anonpsy achieved consistently low re-identification risk under expert, semantic, and GPT-5 evaluations, with substantially lower semantic similarity and identifiability than the LLM-only baseline. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
quote: Compared with a strong LLM-only rewriting baseline, Anonpsy yields substantially lower semantic similarity and identifiability.

title: The Slow Drift of Support: Boundary Failures in Multi-Turn Mental Health LLM Dialogues
outcome: Boundary violations (guarantees, assuming responsibility, professional roles) by mental health LLMs over multi-turn dialogues
effect: Violations were common under both static progression and adaptive probing with similar rates. Adaptive probing cut mean turns to first boundary crossing from 9.21 to 4.64. Definitive or zero-risk promises were the main breach.
quote: The experimental results show that violations are common, and both pressure modes produced similar violation rates.

title: Uncovering Latent Bias in LLM-Based Emergency Department Triage Through Proxy Variables
outcome: LLM triage severity changes when patient proxy variable qualifiers (32 paired positive/negative) are varied
effect: Discriminatory behavior mediated through proxy variables in ED triage. LLMs systematically shifted perceived patient severity when specific tokens appeared, whether framed positively or negatively. No numeric results in abstract.
quote: Our results reveal discriminatory behavior mediated through proxy variables in ED triage scenarios, as well as a systematic tendency for LLMs to modify perceived patient severity when specific tokens appear in the input context, regardless of whether they are framed positively or negatively.
sample_unit: ED triage cases with paired proxy-variable qualifiers

title: Domain-Specific Knowledge Graphs in RAG-Enhanced Healthcare LLMs
outcome: Accuracy of LLMs with knowledge-graph RAG versus No-RAG across graph sources, probes and temperatures
effect: Scope-matched retrieval (notably G2) gave the most consistent gains; indiscriminate graph unions often reduced accuracy; larger models matched or exceeded KG-RAG with No-RAG on Probe 1.
quote: Results show that scope alignment between probe and KG is decisive: precise, scope-matched retrieval (notably $\mathbb{G}_2$) yields the most consistent gains, whereas indiscriminate graph unions often introduce distractors that reduce accuracy.

title: Towards Reliable Medical LLMs: Benchmarking and Enhancing Confidence Estimation of Large Language Models in Medical Consultation
outcome: Reliability of LLM confidence estimates in multi-turn medical consultation as information accumulates
effect: Medical data amplifies the limitations of token-level and consistency-level confidence methods across 27 methods. The proposed MedConf outperformed state-of-the-art methods on AUROC and Pearson correlation across two LLMs and three datasets, including under information insufficiency.
quote: We implement and compare 27 representative methods on this benchmark; two key insights emerge: (1) medical data amplifies the inherent limitations of token-level and consistency-level confidence methods, and (2) medical reasoning must be evaluated for both diagnostic accuracy and information completeness.
sample_unit: consultation cases (three medical datasets; count not reported)

title: From Attribution to Abstention: Training-Free Attention-Based Auditing for Clinical Summarization
outcome: Accuracy of sentence-level source attribution to supporting text spans or images
effect: Text F1 over 92% on radiology and 88% on dialogue summarization, substantially outperforming embedding-based and self-attribution baselines.
quote: For source attribution, ClinTrace achieves over 92% text F1 on radiology and 88% on dialogue summarization, substantially outperforming embedding-based and self-attribution baselines.

title: From Attribution to Abstention: Training-Free Attention-Based Auditing for Clinical Summarization
outcome: Faithfulness improvement from groundedness-based abstention on summary output
effect: Abstaining on the least-grounded 20% of output raised faithfulness from 61.7% to 72.6%; groundedness AUROC 0.77 with the medical-finetuned model.
quote: For hallucination detection, groundedness scores achieve 0.77 AUROC with the medical-finetuned model: competitive with embedding-based confidence at zero additional cost, and enable an abstention mechanism that improves faithfulness from 61.7% to 72.6% by withholding the least: grounded 20% of output for clinician review.

title: MRAG: Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Bio-medicine
outcome: LLM reliability with versus without retrieval augmentation on medical QA benchmark tasks
effect: RAG enhanced LLM reliability across MRAG tasks; performance varied with retrieval approach, model size, and prompting strategy; long-form responses became slightly less readable.
quote: RAG enhances LLM reliability across MRAG tasks.

title: SycoEval-EM: Sycophancy Evaluation of Large Language Models in Simulated Clinical Encounters for Emergency Care
outcome: Rate of LLM acquiescence to inappropriate patient requests under multi-turn adversarial persuasion
effect: Acquiescence ranged 0% to 100% across 19 LLMs (bimodal); seven models held near-perfect guideline adherence, six acquiesced in most encounters; highest for CT requests, lowest for opioids.
quote: Across 19 contemporary LLMs and 1,425 simulated clinical encounters spanning three Choosing Wisely scenarios, acquiescence rates ranged from 0% to 100%, revealing a bimodal distribution.

title: SycoEval-EM: Sycophancy Evaluation of Large Language Models in Simulated Clinical Encounters for Emergency Care
outcome: Whether static medical benchmark performance, scale, or recency predicted robustness to patient pressure
effect: Model scale, recency, and static benchmark performance did not consistently predict robustness; static benchmarks judged insufficient to predict safety under sustained social pressure.
quote: Model scale, recency, and performance on static medical benchmarks did not consistently predict robustness.

title: LLM is Not All You Need: A Systematic Evaluation of ML vs. Foundation Models for text and image based Medical Classification
outcome: Performance of classical ML versus prompt-based and fine-tuned foundation models on medical classification
effect: Classical ML (LR, LightGBM, ResNet-50) achieved best overall performance across most tasks; Gemini 2.5 zero-shot performed poorly on text tasks, and LoRA-tuned Gemma performed worst across all experiments.
quote: According to our results, traditional machine learning (ML) models set a high standard by consistently achieving the best overall performance across most medical categorization tasks.

title: Mind the Ambiguity: Aleatoric Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs for Safe Medical Question Answering
outcome: Medical QA accuracy with ambiguity detection and clarification requests versus baselines
effect: AU-Probe flags ambiguous input from hidden states and prompts the user to clarify; average accuracy improved 9.48% over baselines across four open LLMs.
quote: Extensive experiments across four open LLMs demonstrate the effectiveness of our QA framework, with an average accuracy improvement of 9.48% over baselines.

title: Health-ORSC-Bench: A Benchmark for Measuring Over-Refusal and Safety Completion in Health Context
outcome: Over-refusal of benign in-scope health prompts across 30 LLMs
effect: Safety-optimised models frequently refuse up to 80% of "Hard" benign prompts; larger frontier models show higher over-refusal than smaller or MoE-based models.
quote: We evaluate 30 state-of-the-art LLMs, including GPT-5 and Claude-4, revealing a significant tension: safety-optimised models frequently refuse up to 80% of "Hard" benign prompts, while domain-specific models often sacrifice safety for utility.

title: Expert Evaluation and the Limits of Human Feedback in Mental Health AI Safety Testing
outcome: Inter-rater reliability among psychiatrists rating LLM mental health responses
effect: Inter-rater reliability was consistently poor (ICC 0.087-0.295), below acceptable thresholds; one factor had Krippendorff's alpha -0.203; disagreement highest on suicide and self-harm items.
quote: Despite similar training and shared instructions, inter-rater reliability was consistently poor ($ICC$ $0.087$--$0.295$), falling below thresholds considered acceptable for consequential assessment.

title: CHiRPE: A Step Towards Real-World Clinical NLP with Clinician-Oriented Model Explanations
outcome: Clinician expert preference among AI explanation formats
effect: 28 clinical experts indicated a strong preference for novel concept-guided explanations, especially hybrid graph-and-text summary formats.
quote: Explanation formats were evaluated by 28 clinical experts who indicated a strong preference for our novel concept-guided explanations, especially hybrid graph-and-text summary formats.

title: Overalignment in Frontier LLMs: An Empirical Study of Sycophantic Behaviour in Healthcare
outcome: Whether benchmark accuracy predicts clinical reliability under sycophancy pressure
effect: Reasoning-optimized Thinking models show high vanilla accuracy but rationalize incorrect user suggestions under authoritative pressure; benchmark performance is not a proxy for clinical reliability.
quote: Our results across frontier models suggest that benchmark performance is not a proxy for clinical reliability, and that simplified reasoning structures may offer superior robustness against expert-driven sycophancy.

title: Counterfactual Cultural Cues Reduce Medical QA Accuracy in LLMs: Identifier vs Context Effects
outcome: Accuracy change when culture-related identifiers/context are inserted into otherwise invariant medical questions
effect: Cultural cues significantly affect accuracy (Cochran's Q, p<10^-14), with largest degradation when identifier and context co-occur (up to 3-7 percentage points under option-only prompting); neutral edits produce smaller, non-systematic changes.
quote: Across models, cultural cues significantly affect accuracy (Cochran's Q, $p<10^-14$), with the largest degradation when identifier and context co-occur (up to 3-7 percentage points under option-only prompting), while neutral edits produce smaller, non-systematic changes.

title: Planner-Auditor Twin: Agentic Discharge Planning with FHIR-Based LLM Planning, Guideline Recall, Optional Caching and Self-Improvement
outcome: Discharge-plan task coverage with vs without deterministic auditor-driven regeneration
effect: Self-improvement loop was the primary driver of gains, raising task coverage from 32% to 86%; context caching gave smaller gains over baseline.
quote: While context caching improved performance over baseline, the self-improvement loop was the primary driver of gains, increasing task coverage from 32% to 86%.

title: Planner-Auditor Twin: Agentic Discharge Planning with FHIR-Based LLM Planning, Guideline Recall, Optional Caching and Self-Improvement
outcome: Calibration of LLM confidence estimates (Brier, ECE) and high-confidence misses
effect: Calibration improved substantially with the auditor loop, with reduced Brier/ECE and fewer high-confidence misses, implying miscalibrated confidence at baseline.
quote: Calibration improved substantially, with reduced Brier/ECE and fewer high-confidence misses.

title: The Paradox of Robustness: Decoupling Rule-Based Logic from Affective Noise in High-Stakes Decision-Making
outcome: Decision shift under emotional framing perturbations of rule-bound prompts across eight LLMs
effect: Negligible effect size (Cohen's h = 0.003) versus human biases (h in [0.3, 0.8]); immigration extension +0.8 percentage point shift within +/-3 pp ROPE; adversarial narrative pilot found no meaningful decision shift.
quote: we find a negligible effect size (Cohen's h = 0.003) compared to the substantial biases observed in analogous human contexts (h in [0.3, 0.8]), approximately two orders of magnitude smaller.
sample_unit: unique prompts (9 base scenarios x 18 condition variants)

title: Adoption and Use of LLMs at an Academic Medical Center
outcome: Hallucinations and inaccuracies per LLM-generated summary in the deployed EHR interface
effect: Estimated 0.73 hallucinations and 1.60 inaccuracies per generation for summaries, the most frequent UI task.
quote: Generation of summaries was the most frequent task in the UI, with an estimated 0.73 hallucinations and 1.60 inaccuracies per generation.

title: Adoption and Use of LLMs at an Academic Medical Center
outcome: Adequacy of benchmark-based evaluation for monitoring the deployed LLM interface
effect: Benchmark-based evaluations were insufficient for monitoring and evaluating the UI, so new monitoring methods were required.
quote: Benchmark-based evaluations proved insufficient for monitoring and evaluation of the UI, requiring new methods to monitor performance.

title: Augmenting Clinical Decision-Making with an Interactive and Interpretable AI Copilot: A Real-World User Study with Clinicians in Nephrology and Obstetrics
outcome: Clinician cognitive workload (NASA-TLX) with interpretable AI copilot versus comparator condition
effect: Reduced cognitive workload reported with AICare; qualitative analysis showed trust built through verification. No numeric results in the abstract.
quote: Our findings indicate AICare's reduced cognitive workload.

title: MindGuard: Guardrail Classifiers for Multi-Turn Mental Health Support
outcome: False positives at high-recall operating points when detecting clinical crises versus general-purpose safeguards
effect: MindGuard classifiers reduce false positives at high-recall operating points compared with general-purpose safeguards (no numbers given in the abstract).
quote: Our classifiers reduce false positives at high-recall operating points and, when paired with clinician language models, help achieve lower attack success and harmful engagement rates in adversarial multi-turn interactions compared to general-purpose safeguards.

title: MindGuard: Guardrail Classifiers for Multi-Turn Mental Health Support
outcome: Attack success and harmful engagement
effect: Lower attack success and harmful engagement rates in adversarial multi-turn interactions than general-purpose safeguards.
quote: Our classifiers reduce false positives at high-recall operating points and, when paired with clinician language models, help achieve lower attack success and harmful engagement rates in adversarial multi-turn interactions compared to general-purpose safeguards.

title: MindGuard: Guardrail Classifiers for Multi-Turn Mental Health Support
outcome: Attack success and harmful engagement rates in adversarial multi-turn interactions with classifier safeguard
effect: Paired with clinician language models, MindGuard yields lower attack success and harmful engagement rates than general-purpose safeguards (no numbers given in the abstract).
quote: Our classifiers reduce false positives at high-recall operating points and, when paired with clinician language models, help achieve lower attack success and harmful engagement rates in adversarial multi-turn interactions compared to general-purpose safeguards.

title: A clinically validated framework for auditing AI chatbot behavior in mental health interactions
outcome: Concerning chatbot behavior across 13 clinical risk dimensions in multi-turn simulated mental-health conversations
effect: Concerning behavior was widespread across 9 target chatbots and 30 simulated user profiles in 810 conversations, though reduced in newer models; it accumulated over turns and was highest when supportive behaviors reinforced user vulnerability.
quote: Across 810 conversations, spanning 9 target chatbots and 30 simulated user profiles, concerning behavior in target chatbots was widespread, albeit reduced in newer models.

title: ECG-R1: Protocol-Guided and Modality-Agnostic MLLM for Reliable ECG Interpretation
outcome: Prevalence of hallucinations in MLLM ECG interpretation outputs
effect: Reported first quantitative evidence that severe hallucinations are widespread across proprietary, open-source, and medical MLLMs; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: Additionally, we systematically evaluate the ECG interpretation capabilities of proprietary, open-source, and medical MLLMs, and provide the first quantitative evidence that severe hallucinations are widespread, suggesting that the public should not directly trust these outputs without independent verification.

title: Cross-Lingual Empirical Evaluation of Large Language Models for Arabic Medical Tasks
outcome: Correlation between model-reported confidence/explanations and answer correctness in Arabic and English medical QA
effect: Model-reported confidence and explanations showed limited correlation with correctness, so stated confidence is an unreliable signal of accuracy.
quote: Tokenization analysis exposes structural fragmentation in Arabic medical text, while reliability analysis suggests that model-reported confidence and explanations exhibit limited correlation with correctness.

title: Clinical Validation of Medical-based Large Language Model Chatbots on Ophthalmic Patient Queries with LLM-based Evaluation
outcome: Rate of hallucinations or clinically misleading content in medical LLM ophthalmic answers
effect: MedLLaMA3-v20 had 25.5 percent of responses containing hallucinations or clinically misleading content, including fabricated terminology; gaps remained in clinical depth and consensus.
quote: MedLLaMA3-v20 performed poorest, with 25.5 percent of responses containing hallucinations or clinically misleading content, including fabricated terminology.
sample_unit: model responses to ophthalmology patient queries

title: Clinical Validation of Medical-based Large Language Model Chatbots on Ophthalmic Patient Queries with LLM-based Evaluation
outcome: Agreement between GPT-4-Turbo grading and ophthalmologist grading of LLM responses
effect: GPT-4-Turbo grading aligned strongly with clinicians (Spearman rho 0.80, Kendall tau 0.67); Senior Consultants graded more conservatively, supporting hybrid automated and clinician review.
quote: GPT-4-Turbo grading showed strong alignment with clinician assessments overall, with Spearman rho of 0.80 and Kendall tau of 0.67, though Senior Consultants graded more conservatively.
sample_unit: model responses to ophthalmology patient queries

title: MPIB: A Benchmark for Medical Prompt Injection Attacks and Clinical Safety in LLMs
outcome: Clinical harm and attack success rates under direct and RAG-mediated prompt injection
effect: ASR2 and CHER3 can diverge substantially; observed rates vary depending on whether adversarial instructions appear in the user query or in retrieved context. Numeric rates not given in the abstract.
quote: Evaluating MPIB across a diverse set of baseline LLMs and defense configurations, we find that ASR$_2$ and CHER$_3$ can diverge substantially, and that observed rates vary depending on whether adversarial instructions appear in the user query or in retrieved context.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Risk-Sensitive Evaluation of Hallucinated Medical Advice
outcome: risk-bearing language in hallucinated, weakly grounded LLM patient-facing medical answers across three models
effect: Models with similar surface-level behavior showed substantially different risk profiles; standard metrics did not capture these differences. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
quote: Our results show that models with similar surface-level behavior exhibit substantially different risk profiles and that standard evaluation metrics fail to capture these distinctions.

title: LiveMedBench: A Contamination-Free Medical Benchmark for LLMs with Automated Rubric Evaluation
outcome: LLM performance on contamination-free, real-world open-ended clinical cases versus inflated static benchmarks
effect: Best model achieved only 39.2%; 84% of models showed performance degradation on post-cutoff cases, indicating data contamination inflating static benchmark estimates.
quote: Extensive evaluation of 38 LLMs reveals that even the best-performing model achieves only 39.2%, and 84% of models exhibit performance degradation on post-cutoff cases, confirming pervasive data contamination risks.

title: A Patient Simulation Framework for Risk Assessment of Conversational Healthcare AI: Evaluation of an Antidepressant Decision Aid
outcome: Decision aid concept retrieval and recommendation accuracy across health literacy levels
effect: Rank-1 concept retrieval rose from 47.6% (limited health literacy) to 81.9% (proficient), with corresponding declines in antidepressant recommendation accuracy.
quote: Rank-1 concept retrieval increased from 47.6% for limited health literacy to 81.9% for proficient health literacy, with corresponding declines in antidepressant recommendation accuracy.

title: ADRD-Bench: A Preliminary LLM Benchmark for Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias
outcome: Gap between high benchmark accuracy and reasoning quality/stability in caregiving case studies
effect: Top-tier models exceeded 0.9 accuracy, yet case studies showed inconsistent reasoning quality and stability, indicating benchmark accuracy overstates domain competence.
quote: While top-tier models achieved high accuracies (>0.9), case studies revealed inconsistent reasoning quality and stability, highlighting a critical need for domain-specific improvement to enhance LLMs' knowledge and reasoning grounded in daily caregiving data.

title: MentalBench: A DSM-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating Psychiatric Diagnostic Capability of Large Language Models
outcome: LLM confidence calibration when distinguishing psychiatric disorders with overlapping symptoms
effect: State-of-the-art LLMs performed well on noise-free DSM-5 knowledge queries but struggled to calibrate confidence when distinguishing disorders with overlapping symptoms (no numbers in the abstract).
quote: Our experiments show that although state-of-the-art LLMs perform well on noise-free queries that probe DSM-5 knowledge, they struggle to calibrate their confidence when distinguishing between disorders with overlapping symptoms.

title: Implicit Bias in LLMs for Transgender Populations
outcome: LLM output changes when patient gender identity (transgender vs cisgender) is varied in word association and appointment allocation
effect: Consistent bias in appearance, risk, and veracity categories with stronger negative associations for transgender people; in allocation, transgender candidates favored for STI and mental health, cisgender for gynecology and breast care.
quote: Our results show consistent bias in categories such as appearance, risk, and veracity, indicating stronger negative associations with transgender individuals.

title: Detecting Jailbreak Attempts in Clinical Training LLMs Through Automated Linguistic Feature Extraction
outcome: Jailbreak detection performance of a feature-based classifier layer on clinical simulation dialogue
effect: Strong overall performance reported across cross-validation and held-out evaluations; no numeric values in the abstract.
quote: Across cross-validation and held-out evaluations, the system achieves strong overall performance, indicating that LLM-derived linguistic features provide an effective basis for automated jailbreak detection.

title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Medical AI: Leveraging Fine-Tuned GPT, LLaMA, and DeepSeek R1 for Evidence-Based and Bias-Aware Clinical Query Processing
outcome: Model uncertainty (perplexity) with vs without PubMed evidence augmentation
effect: Evidence augmentation reduced uncertainty (perplexity 4.13) compared to base responses; full system 87% accuracy, relevance around 0.80.
quote: In evaluation, the full system achieves 87% accuracy with relevance around 0.80, and evidence augmentation reduces uncertainty (perplexity 4.13) compared to base responses, with mean end-to-end latency of 36.5 seconds under the reported configuration.

title: Evidence-Grounded Subspecialty Reasoning: Evaluating a Curated Clinical Intelligence Layer on the 2025 Endocrinology Board-Style Examination
outcome: Board-exam accuracy of curated-evidence-grounded system vs web-retrieval frontier LLMs
effect: Mirror 87.5% (105/120) vs GPT-5.2 74.6%, GPT-5 74.0%, Gemini-3-Pro 69.8%; human reference 62.3%.
quote: Curated evidence with explicit provenance can outperform unconstrained web retrieval for subspecialty clinical reasoning and supports auditability for clinical deployment.

title: Evidence-Grounded Subspecialty Reasoning: Evaluating a Curated Clinical Intelligence Layer on the 2025 Endocrinology Board-Style Examination
outcome: Citation accuracy and guideline-tier source citation rate in outputs on manual verification
effect: 74.2% of outputs cited at least one guideline-tier source, with 100% citation accuracy on manual verification.
quote: Mirror provided evidence traceability: 74.2% of outputs cited at least one guideline-tier source, with 100% citation accuracy on manual verification.

title: Multi-Objective Alignment of Language Models for Personalized Psychotherapy
outcome: Empathy and safety of aligned therapy chatbot responses under single- versus multi-objective optimization
effect: Single-objective optimization gave 93.6% empathy but 47.8% safety; MODPO gave 77.6% empathy and 62.6% safety, a better balance.
quote: Multi-objective DPO (MODPO) achieves superior balance (77.6% empathy, 62.6% safety) compared to single-objective optimization (93.6% empathy, 47.8% safety), and therapeutic criteria outperform general communication principles by 17.2%.
sample_unit: survey respondents with lived mental health experience

title: LiveClin: A Live Clinical Benchmark without Leakage
outcome: LLM performance on realistic clinical-pathway cases versus inflated static benchmark scores
effect: Top-performing model reached Case Accuracy of just 35.7% on 1,407 real case reports, and static benchmarks are described as giving inflated scores.
quote: Our evaluation of 26 models on LiveClin reveals the profound difficulty of these real-world scenarios, with the top-performing model achieving a Case Accuracy of just 35.7%.

title: Bridging the Domain Divide: Supervised vs. Zero-Shot Clinical Section Segmentation from MIMIC-III to Obstetrics
outcome: Section segmentation performance drop from in-domain MIMIC-III to out-of-domain obstetrics notes
effect: Supervised models performed strongly in-domain but their performance dropped substantially out-of-domain; zero-shot LLMs adapted robustly once hallucinated section headers were corrected.
quote: Our results show that while supervised models perform strongly in-domain, their performance drops substantially out-of-domain.

title: Assessing Risks of Large Language Models in Mental Health Support: A Framework for Automated Clinical AI Red Teaming
outcome: Safety of AI psychotherapists in simulated multi-turn sessions, including suicide risk de-escalation
effect: Simulation of 369 sessions with six AI agents revealed critical safety gaps, including failure to de-escalate suicide risk and validation of patient delusions.
quote: We identify specific iatrogenic risks, including the validation of patient delusions ("AI Psychosis") and failure to de-escalate suicide risk.

title: Assessing Risks of Large Language Models in Mental Health Support: A Framework for Automated Clinical AI Red Teaming
outcome: Chatbot handling of suicide risk in simulated therapy dialogue
effect: AI agents failed to de-escalate suicide risk across N=369 simulated sessions; no rate reported in the abstract.
quote: We identify specific iatrogenic risks, including the validation of patient delusions ("AI Psychosis") and failure to de-escalate suicide risk.

title: AgenticSum: An Agentic Inference-Time Framework for Faithful Clinical Text Summarization
outcome: Faithfulness of clinical summaries with automated verification and targeted correction versus vanilla LLMs and baselines
effect: Reported consistent improvements over vanilla LLMs and other strong baselines across reference-based metrics, LLM-as-a-judge, and human evaluation; no numeric values in the provided text.
quote: Across various measures, AgenticSum demonstrates consistent improvements compared to vanilla LLMs and other strong baselines.

title: An artificial intelligence framework for end-to-end rare disease phenotyping from clinical notes using large language models
outcome: Ablation of extraction, ontology standardization, and prioritization modules on phenotyping performance
effect: Performance improved with the addition of each module, including ontology-grounded standardization to HPO terms; end-to-end ontology-based similarity 0.70 vs 0.58 for PhenoBERT.
quote: Ablation analyses demonstrated performance improvements with the addition of each module in RARE-PHENIX (extraction, standardization, and prioritization), supporting the value of modeling the full clinical phenotyping workflow.

title: PSF-Med: Measuring and Explaining Paraphrase Sensitivity in Medical Vision Language Models
outcome: Answer flip rate under meaning-preserving paraphrases of chest X-ray questions across nine VLMs
effect: Flip rates from 3% to 37% across nine VLMs; some low-flip models stay consistent even with image removed, suggesting reliance on language priors.
quote: Across nine VLMs, including general-purpose models, we find flip rates from 3% to 37%.

title: PSF-Med: Measuring and Explaining Paraphrase Sensitivity in Medical Vision Language Models
outcome: Consistency of VLM responses across equivalent paraphrased questions
effect: Flip rates of 3% to 37% across nine VLMs on meaning-preserving paraphrases; clamping a framing-related feature reduced flip rates by 31% relative.
quote: Medical Vision Language Models (VLMs) can change their answers when clinicians rephrase the same question, a failure mode that threatens deployment safety.

title: MEDSYN: Benchmarking Multi-EviDence SYNthesis in Complex Clinical Cases for Multimodal Large Language Models
outcome: MLLM versus expert clinician performance on differential diagnosis generation and final diagnosis selection
effect: Top models often match or outperform human experts on DDx generation, but all MLLMs show a much larger DDx-FDx performance gap than expert clinicians.
quote: While top models often match or even outperform human experts on DDx generation, all MLLMs exhibit a much larger DDx--FDx performance gap compared to expert clinicians, indicating a failure mode in synthesis of heterogeneous CE types.

title: CXReasonAgent: Evidence-Grounded Diagnostic Reasoning Agent for Chest X-rays
outcome: Faithful grounding and verifiability of diagnostic responses, tool-grounded agent versus LVLMs on multi-turn benchmark
effect: CXReasonAgent, which uses clinically grounded diagnostic tools, produced faithfully grounded responses and more reliable, verifiable diagnostic reasoning than LVLMs; no numeric results in the provided text.
quote: and show that CXReasonAgent produces faithfully grounded responses, enabling more reliable and verifiable diagnostic reasoning than LVLMs.

title: MED-COPILOT: A Medical Assistant Powered by GraphRAG and Similar Patient Case Retrieval
outcome: Note completion fidelity and medical QA accuracy with guideline-grounded GraphRAG versus parametric LLM and standard RAG
effect: GraphRAG with similar-patient retrieval consistently outperformed parametric LLM baselines and standard RAG, improving generation fidelity and clinical reasoning accuracy (no numbers in abstract).
quote: We evaluate our framework on clinical note completion and medical question answering, and demonstrate that it consistently outperforms parametric LLM baselines and standard RAG, improving both generation fidelity and clinical reasoning accuracy.

title: Conformal Prediction for Risk-Controlled Medical Entity Extraction Across Clinical Domains
outcome: Whether conformal calibration of LLM extraction confidence achieves target coverage with acceptable rejection rates
effect: Conformal prediction reached at least 90% target coverage in both FDA label and radiology settings, with 9-13% rejection rates; models were underconfident on FDA labels (tau about 0.06) and overconfident on radiology (tau up to 0.99).
quote: Despite this heterogeneity, conformal prediction achieves target coverage ($\geq 90\%$) in both settings with manageable rejection rates (9--13\%).
sample_unit: FDA drug labels (128,906 entities extracted); MIMIC-CXR reports also evaluated

title: PanCanBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Pancreatic Oncology
outcome: Rubric-based completeness of LLMs on real patient pancreatic cancer questions versus exam-style performance
effect: Rubric completeness ranged from 46.5% to 82.3% across 22 LLMs despite expert-level exam performance; newer reasoning models did not consistently improve factuality.
quote: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved expert-level performance on standardized examinations, yet multiple-choice accuracy poorly reflects real-world clinical utility and safety.
sample_unit: authentic patient questions (3,130 expert rubric criteria)

title: PanCanBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Pancreatic Oncology
outcome: Hallucination rate (responses with at least one factual error) across LLMs
effect: Hallucination rates ranged from 6.0% for Gemini-2.5 Pro and GPT-4o to 53.8% for Llama-3.1-8B; o3 produced inaccuracies more often than other GPT-family models.
quote: Factual errors were common, with hallucination rates (the percentages of responses containing at least one factual error) ranging from 6.0% for Gemini-2.5 Pro and GPT-4o to 53.8% for Llama-3.1-8B.
sample_unit: authentic patient questions (3,130 expert rubric criteria)

title: PanCanBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Pancreatic Oncology
outcome: Rubric score with versus without web-search grounding
effect: Web search did not improve scores: Gemini-2.5 Pro 66.8% to 63.9%; GPT-5 73.8% to 72.8% when web search was enabled.
quote: The average score changed from 66.8% to 63.9% for Gemini-2.5 Pro and from 73.8% to 72.8% for GPT-5 when web search was enabled.
sample_unit: authentic patient questions (3,130 expert rubric criteria)

title: Benchmarking LLM Summaries of Multimodal Clinical Time Series for Remote Monitoring
outcome: Event-level fidelity of LLM summaries: abnormality recall, duration recall, hallucinated event mentions
effect: Models with high semantic similarity often show near-zero abnormality recall; the vision-based approach reached 45.7% abnormality recall and 100% duration recall.
