quote: Models that achieve high semantic similarity scores often exhibit near-zero abnormality recall.
sample_unit: daily summaries of remote monitoring time series

title: MedCalc-Bench Doesn't Measure What You Think: A Benchmark Audit and the Case for Open-Book Evaluation
outcome: Errors in benchmark calculator implementations and ground truth
effect: Audit identified and fixed over 20 errors, from critical formula inaccuracies to runtime bugs; residual model errors attributed mainly to ground-truth issues and dataset ambiguities.
quote: First, we conduct a systematic audit of the benchmark's calculator implementations, identifying and fixing over 20 errors ranging from critical formula inaccuracies to runtime bugs in a NeurIPS-published dataset.

title: MedCalc-Bench Doesn't Measure What You Think: A Benchmark Audit and the Case for Open-Book Evaluation
outcome: Accuracy on clinical calculator tasks with vs without calculator specification in prompt
effect: Providing the calculator specification at inference (open-book) raised accuracy from ~52% to 81-85% on GLM-4.6V and GLM-4.7, without fine-tuning.
quote: Second, we show that a simple intervention-providing the model with the calculator specification at inference time ("open-book" prompting)-raises accuracy from ~52% to 81-85% on GLM-4.6V and GLM-4.7, surpassing all published results including RL-trained systems, without any fine-tuning.

title: MedCalc-Bench Doesn't Measure What You Think: A Benchmark Audit and the Case for Open-Book Evaluation
outcome: LLM accuracy on clinical calculation tasks under direct prompting
effect: State-of-the-art direct prompting scores plateau around 35% on the Verified split; the study concludes the benchmark measures formula memorization and arithmetic precision.
quote: MedCalc-Bench is a widely used benchmark for evaluating LLM performance on clinical calculator tasks, with state-of-the-art direct prompting scores plateauing around 35% on the Verified split (HELM MedHELM leaderboard) and the best published approach-RL with verifiable rewards-reaching 74%.

title: ExpGuard: LLM Content Moderation in Specialized Domains
outcome: Guardrail model classification of harmful prompts and responses in finance, medical, legal domains under adversarial attack
effect: ExpGuard surpassed WildGuard by up to 8.9% in prompt classification and 15.3% in response classification, with competitive performance on eight public benchmarks and resilience to domain-specific adversarial attacks.
quote: Comprehensive evaluations conducted on ExpGuardTest and eight established public benchmarks reveal that ExpGuard delivers competitive performance across the board while demonstrating exceptional resilience to domain-specific adversarial attacks, surpassing state-of-the-art models such as WildGuard by up to 8.9% in prompt classification and 15.3% in response classification.
sample_unit: labeled prompts (with paired refusal and compliant responses) in ExpGuardMix

title: From Conflict to Consensus: Boosting Medical Reasoning via Multi-Round Agentic RAG
outcome: Medical Q&A accuracy of retrieval-grounded multi-round agentic RAG versus backbone and RAG baselines
effect: MA-RAG consistently surpassed inference-time scaling and RAG baselines across 7 medical Q&A benchmarks, with +6.8 points average accuracy over the backbone model.
quote: Extensive evaluations across 7 medical Q&A benchmarks show that MA-RAG consistently surpasses competitive inference-time scaling and RAG baselines, delivering substantial +6.8 points on average accuracy over the backbone model.

title: RAG-X: Systematic Diagnosis of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Question Answering
outcome: Gap between perceived accuracy and evidence-based grounding in medical RAG QA benchmarks
effect: Reveals an 'Accuracy Fallacy' in which a 14% gap separates perceived system success from evidence-based grounding.
quote: Our experiments reveal an ``Accuracy Fallacy", where a 14\% gap separates perceived system success from evidence-based grounding.

title: Agentic retrieval-augmented reasoning reshapes collective reliability under model variability in radiology question answering
outcome: Cross-model robustness of correctness and consensus with vs without evidence-grounded agentic retrieval
effect: Agentic retrieval reduced inter-model decision dispersion (median entropy 0.48 vs. 0.13) and increased robustness of correctness across models (mean 0.74 vs. 0.81); majority consensus increased (P<0.001).
quote: Agentic inference reduced inter-model decision dispersion (median entropy 0.48 vs. 0.13) and increased robustness of correctness across models (mean 0.74 vs. 0.81).

title: Agentic retrieval-augmented reasoning reshapes collective reliability under model variability in radiology question answering
outcome: Correctness and agreement across heterogeneous models on radiology questions
effect: High agreement did not guarantee correctness; consensus strength and robust correctness correlated (rho=0.88 zero-shot; 0.87 agentic).
quote: Consensus strength and robust correctness remained correlated under both strategies (\r{ho}=0.88 for zero-shot; \r{ho}=0.87 for agentic), although high agreement did not guarantee correctness.

title: Agentic retrieval-augmented reasoning reshapes collective reliability under model variability in radiology question answering
outcome: Clinically assessed severity of incorrect LLM outputs
effect: Among 572 incorrect outputs, 72% were associated with moderate or high clinically assessed severity; inter-rater agreement was low (kappa=0.02).
quote: Among 572 incorrect outputs, 72% were associated with moderate or high clinically assessed severity, although inter-rater agreement was low (\k{appa}=0.02).

title: CORE-Acu: Structured Reasoning Traces and Knowledge Graph Safety Verification for Acupuncture Clinical Decision Support
outcome: Safety violation rate with knowledge-graph verification versus GPT-4o under identical rules
effect: CORE-Acu achieved 0/1,000 observed safety violations (95% CI: 0--0.37%), whereas GPT-4o exhibited an 8.5% violation rate under identical rules.
quote: Crucially, CORE-Acu achieved 0/1,000 observed safety violations (95\% CI: 0--0.37\%), whereas GPT-4o exhibited an 8.5\% violation rate under identical rules.

title: CORE-Acu: Structured Reasoning Traces and Knowledge Graph Safety Verification for Acupuncture Clinical Decision Support
outcome: Safety violations after deterministic rule-based veto and revise loop on LLM outputs
effect: CORE-Acu with Symbolic Veto Mechanism had 0/1,000 safety violations (95% CI: 0--0.37%); GPT-4o had 8.5% violations under identical rules.
quote: Crucially, CORE-Acu achieved 0/1,000 observed safety violations (95\% CI: 0--0.37\%), whereas GPT-4o exhibited an 8.5\% violation rate under identical rules.

title: A prospective clinical feasibility study of a conversational diagnostic AI in an ambulatory primary care clinic
outcome: Safety, patient and clinician experience of AI in a limited prospective real-world pilot with real-time supervision
effect: Safety supervisors monitored all interactions in real time and did not need to stop any consultation; patients reported high satisfaction; PCPs found output useful.
quote: Human safety supervisors monitored all patient-AMIE interactions in real time and did not need to intervene to stop any consultations based on pre-defined criteria.

title: Real-Time Trust Verification for Safe Agentic Actions using TrustBench
outcome: Reduction in harmful agent actions when a pre-execution verification toolkit is used
effect: TrustBench reduced harmful actions by 87% across multiple agentic tasks. Domain-specific plugins gave 35% greater harm reduction than generic verification.
quote: Across multiple agentic tasks, TrustBench reduced harmful actions by 87%.

title: Investigating Gender Stereotypes in Large Language Models via Social Determinants of Health
outcome: LLM gendered decisions and stereotypes probed via social determinants of health inputs in French patient records
effect: Embedded stereotypes could be probed using SDoH input, and LLMs relied on embedded stereotypes to make gendered decisions. No numeric results reported in the abstract.
quote: Through a series of experiments, we found that embedded stereotypes can be probed using SDoH input and that LLMs rely on embedded stereotypes to make gendered decisions, suggesting that evaluating interactions among SDoH factors could usefully complement existing approaches to assessing LLM performance and bias.

title: Quantifying Hallucinations in Language Language Models on Medical Textbooks
outcome: Hallucination rate of LLM answers on textbook-grounded medical QA with passages provided
effect: LLaMA-70B-Instruct hallucinated in 19.7% of answers (95% CI 18.6 to 20.7) with passages provided, while 98.8% of responses received maximal plausibility; lower hallucination rates aligned with higher usefulness across models (rho=-0.71, p=0.058).
quote: Our findings indicate that, across all scales and architectures tested, current large language models remain unfit for unsupervised clinical deployment, and that human expert oversight is both necessary and the dominant cost driver.

title: Fine-Tune, Don't Prompt, Your Language Model to Identify Biased Language in Clinical Notes
outcome: Classifier F1 when fine-tuned on in-domain versus other-specialty data
effect: GatorTron fine-tuned on OB-GYN reached F1 0.96 in-domain; tested on MIMIC-IV, F1 fell below 0.70 (44% drop). Training on MIMIC-IV then testing on OB-GYN gave F1 0.71 (11% drop) with reduced precision.
quote: Our findings demonstrate that fine-tuning outperforms prompting for emotional valence classification and that models must be adapted to specific medical specialties to achieve clinically appropriate performance.
sample_unit: annotated text chunks from clinical notes

title: Fine-Tune, Don't Prompt, Your Language Model to Identify Biased Language in Clinical Notes
outcome: Performance drop when model applied to a different specialty and health system
effect: External validation on MIMIC-IV showed F1 below 0.70, a 44% drop from the OB-GYN test set.
quote: External validation on MIMIC-IV revealed limited cross-domain generalizability (F1 < 0.70, 44% drop).
sample_unit: annotated text chunks from clinical notes

title: Human-AI Co-reasoning for Clinical Diagnosis with Evidence-Integrated Language Agent
outcome: Physician diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance, including automation bias
effect: PULSE assistance enabled physicians to correct initial errors and broaden diagnostic hypotheses, but also introduced risks of automation bias; serial and concurrent workflows were explored.
quote: When used collaboratively, PULSE enabled physicians to correct initial errors and broaden diagnostic hypotheses, but also introduced risks of automation bias.

title: Human-AI Co-reasoning for Clinical Diagnosis with Evidence-Integrated Language Agent
outcome: Comparison of AI diagnostic accuracy against physicians of varying expertise on same cases
effect: PULSE outperformed residents and junior specialists and matched senior specialists at Top@1 and Top@4.
quote: PULSE attained expert-competitive accuracy, outperforming residents and junior specialists while matching senior specialist performance at both Top@1 and Top@4 thresholds.

title: Human-AI Co-reasoning for Clinical Diagnosis with Evidence-Integrated Language Agent
outcome: Automation bias when physicians use AI assistance in diagnosis
effect: Collaborative use introduced risks of automation bias, despite helping correct initial errors.
quote: When used collaboratively, PULSE enabled physicians to correct initial errors and broaden diagnostic hypotheses, but also introduced risks of automation bias.

title: ThReadMed-QA: A Multi-Turn Medical Dialogue Benchmark from Real Patient Questions
outcome: Fully-correct response rate of LLMs on real patient multi-turn questions versus physician ground truth
effect: Even the strongest model, GPT-5, achieved only 41.2% fully-correct responses; all five models degraded significantly from turn 0 to turn 2 (p < 0.001).
quote: Even the strongest model, GPT-5, achieves only 41.2% fully-correct responses.

title: ThReadMed-QA: A Multi-Turn Medical Dialogue Benchmark from Real Patient Questions
outcome: Multi-turn consistency and error propagation across conversation turns
effect: Wrong-answer rates roughly tripled by turn 2; a single wrong turn raised the probability of a subsequent wrong turn by 1.9-6.1x; nearly one in three Claude Haiku conversations swung between fully correct and completely wrong.
quote: EPR shows that a single wrong turn raises the probability of a subsequent wrong turn by 1.9-6.1x across all models.

title: Stop Listening to Me! How Multi-turn Conversations Can Degrade LLM Reliability
outcome: Accuracy and abstention of LLMs in multi-turn conversations versus static clinical benchmarks
effect: Partitioning the answer space into sequential presentations reduced end-to-end accuracy and abstention against incorrect suggestions by an average of up to 30%, reaching 65% in certain models.
quote: Together our findings demonstrate that the general proficiency captured by static benchmarks do not translate over multi-turn dialogues.
sample_unit: LLMs evaluated across three clinical benchmarks

title: Stop Listening to Me! How Multi-turn Conversations Can Degrade LLM Reliability
outcome: Whether static benchmark performance carries over to multi-turn conversational use
effect: Pervasive 'conversation tax' of up to 30% average (65% in some models) and blind switching from abstention to incorrect and correct suggestions at near-identical rates reaching 50%.
quote: Together our findings demonstrate that the general proficiency captured by static benchmarks do not translate over multi-turn dialogues.
sample_unit: LLMs evaluated across three clinical benchmarks

title: Evaluation format, not model capability, drives triage failure in the assessment of consumer health AI
outcome: Triage accuracy under exam-style versus naturalistic patient-style evaluation of the same LLMs
effect: Naturalistic interaction improved triage accuracy by 6.4 percentage points (p = 0.015); asthma triage improved from 48% to 80%; three models scored 0-24% with forced choice but 100% with free text.
quote: Naturalistic interaction improved triage accuracy by 6.4 percentage points ($p = 0.015$).

title: Evaluation format, not model capability, drives triage failure in the assessment of consumer health AI
outcome: Emergency recognition and escalation by consumer LLM chatbots across triage scenarios
effect: DKA was triaged correctly in 100% of trials across all models and conditions. Forced-choice format registered under-triage (0-24% for three models) although free text recommended emergency care in 100%.
quote: The forced A/B/C/D format was the dominant failure mechanism: three models scored 0--24% with forced choice but 100% with free text (all $p < 10^{-8}$), consistently recommending emergency care in their own words while the forced-choice format registered under-triage.

title: Developing and evaluating a chatbot to support maternal health care
outcome: Emergency recall of stage-aware triage on labeled benchmark, with missed-emergency vs over-escalation trade-off
effect: Triage benchmark (N=150) achieved 86.7% emergency recall, so some emergencies were missed; the missed-emergency vs. over-escalation trade-off was explicitly reported.
quote: (i) a labeled triage benchmark (N=150) achieving 86.7% emergency recall, explicitly reporting the missed-emergency vs. over-escalation trade-off

title: PREBA: Surgical Duration Prediction via PCA-Weighted Retrieval-Augmented LLMs and Bayesian Averaging Aggregation
outcome: Surgical duration prediction error (MAE, R^2) with retrieval-grounded prompts versus zero-shot LLM inference
effect: Reduced MAE by up to 40% and raised R^2 from -0.13 to 0.62 over zero-shot inference; accuracy competitive with supervised ML methods.
quote: PREBA significantly improves performance-for instance, reducing MAE by up to 40% and raising R^2 from -0.13 to 0.62 over zero-shot inference-and it achieves accuracy competitive with supervised ML methods, demonstrating strong effectiveness and generalization.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Gait Classification Using Text-Encoded Kinematic Waveforms
outcome: LLM gait classification with vs without explicit reference gait statistics (grounding)
effect: Performance was highly dependent on explicit reference information; GPT-5 with reference grounding achieved multiclass MCC 0.70 and binary MCC 0.68.
quote: Performance of the LLM was highly dependent on explicit reference information and self-rated confidence; when restricted to high-confidence predictions, multiclass MCC increased to 0.83 on the filtered subset.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Gait Classification Using Text-Encoded Kinematic Waveforms
outcome: LLM versus conventional gait classifiers
effect: Supervised KNN MCC = 0.88; best LLM GPT-5 with reference grounding multiclass MCC = 0.70.
quote: The supervised KNN achieved the highest performance (multiclass Matthews Correlation Coefficient, MCC = 0.88).

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Gait Classification Using Text-Encoded Kinematic Waveforms
outcome: Self-rated confidence for LLM predictions
effect: When restricted to high-confidence predictions, multiclass MCC increased to 0.83 on the filtered subset.
quote: Performance of the LLM was highly dependent on explicit reference information and self-rated confidence; when restricted to high-confidence predictions, multiclass MCC increased to 0.83 on the filtered subset.

title: QuarkMedBench: A Real-World Scenario Driven Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models
outcome: Gap between exam-based scores and performance on real-world medical queries
effect: Baseline evaluations reveal significant performance disparities among state-of-the-art models on real-world clinical nuances; no numeric gap is reported in the abstract.
quote: Crucially, baseline evaluations on this benchmark reveal significant performance disparities among state-of-the-art models when navigating real-world clinical nuances, highlighting the limitations of conventional exam-based metrics.

title: Faithful or Just Plausible? Evaluating the Faithfulness of Closed-Source LLMs in Medical Reasoning
outcome: Faithfulness of LLM chain-of-thought explanations under causal ablation, positional bias and hint injection
effect: CoT reasoning steps often did not causally drive predictions, and models readily incorporated external hints without acknowledgment; positional biases had minimal impact. No numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: We find that CoT reasoning steps often do not causally drive predictions, and models readily incorporate external hints without acknowledgment.

title: Clinician input steers AI toward accurate and harmful recommendations
outcome: Model behavior under multi-turn disagreement challenges and adversarial arguments
effect: Multi-turn disagreement challenges revealed distinct model phenotypes from highly conformist to dogmatic, with adversarial arguments remaining a vulnerability even in otherwise resilient models.
quote: Multi-turn disagreement challenges revealed distinct model phenotypes, from highly conformist to dogmatic, with adversarial arguments remaining a vulnerability even in otherwise resilient models.

title: Clinician input steers AI toward accurate and harmful recommendations
outcome: Interactive clinician context changed diagnosis performance
effect: Expert context improved all 21 models (+20.4 pp); adversarial context degraded 14 models (mean -5.4 pp).
quote: Expert context significantly improved correct final-diagnosis inclusion in all 21 models (mean +20.4 pp), reflecting both improved reasoning and passive content echoing, while adversarial context significantly degraded performance in 14 models (mean -5.4 pp).

title: MedPriv-Bench: Benchmarking the Privacy-Utility Trade-off of Large Language Models in Medical Open-Ended Question Answering
outcome: Privacy leakage and clinical utility of LLMs with vs without privacy-preserving methods
effect: Unprotected Med42-v2-8B: utility 3.87/5, leakage 72.8%. Supervised fine-tuning: utility 4.25, leakage 38.9%. Local differential privacy: leakage 20.5%, utility 3.03.
quote: Relative to unprotected Med42-v2-8B (utility 3.87/5; leakage 72.8%), supervised fine-tuning improved utility to 4.25 and reduced leakage to 38.9%, whereas local differential privacy reduced leakage to 20.5% but lowered utility to 3.03.

title: ECG-Reasoning-Benchmark: A Benchmark for Evaluating Clinical Reasoning Capabilities in ECG Interpretation
outcome: Whether MLLM step-by-step ECG reasoning is grounded in visual evidence
effect: Models retrieve clinical criteria but show near-zero success (6% Completion) in maintaining a complete reasoning chain, mainly failing to ground ECG findings in the visual signal.
quote: Although models possess the medical knowledge to retrieve clinical criteria for a diagnosis, they exhibit near-zero success rates (6% Completion) in maintaining a complete reasoning chain, primarily failing to ground the corresponding ECG findings to the actual visual evidence in the ECG signal.

title: PathGLS: Evaluating Pathology Vision-Language Models without Ground Truth through Multi-Dimensional Consistency
outcome: Pathology VLM output stability under adversarial visual-semantic perturbations
effect: PathGLS Stability dimension measures output variance under adversarial perturbations; PathGLS sensitivity dropped 40.2% for hallucinated reports versus 2.1% for BERTScore.
quote: Specifically, on the Quilt-1M dataset, PathGLS reveals a steep sensitivity drop of 40.2% for hallucinated reports compared to only 2.1% for BERTScore.

title: Caging the Agents: A Zero Trust Security Architecture for Autonomous AI in Healthcare
outcome: Vulnerabilities found by automated security audit agent during 90-day deployment
effect: Automated security audit agent discovered four HIGH severity findings over 90 days, all remediated; fleet hardened across three VM image generations.
quote: We report results from 90 days of deployment including four HIGH severity findings discovered and remediated by an automated security audit agent, progressive fleet hardening across three VM image generations, and defense coverage mapped to all eleven attack patterns from recent literature.

title: The Validity Gap in Health AI Evaluation: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Benchmark Composition
outcome: Clinical composition of health LLM benchmarks versus real-world needs
effect: Benchmarks lack raw clinical artifacts: laboratory values 5.2%, imaging 3.8%, raw medical records 0.6%; chronic disease management only 5.5%; benchmark composition misaligned with real-world clinical needs.
quote: Evaluation benchmarks remain misaligned with real-world clinical needs, lacking raw clinical artifacts, adequate representation of vulnerable populations, and longitudinal chronic care scenarios.

title: The Validity Gap in Health AI Evaluation: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Benchmark Composition
outcome: Representation of safety-critical scenarios in benchmarks
effect: Suicide/self-harm queries comprised <0.7% of the corpus; safety-critical scenarios effectively absent.
quote: Safety-critical scenarios were effectively absent: suicide/self-harm queries comprised <0.7% of the corpus and chronic disease management only 5.5%.

title: The Validity Gap in Health AI Evaluation: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Benchmark Composition
outcome: Representation of vulnerable populations in benchmark queries
effect: Pediatrics and older adults each below 11% of the corpus; global health needs neglected.
quote: Benchmarks also neglected vulnerable populations (pediatrics/older adults <11%) and global health needs.

title: CoDA: Exploring Chain-of-Distribution Attacks and Post-Hoc Token-Space Repair for Medical Vision-Language Models
outcome: Zero-shot MVLM performance under clinically plausible pipeline shifts (acquisition, reconstruction, display, delivery) on MRI, chest X-ray, CT
effect: CoDA substantially degrades zero-shot performance of CLIP-style MVLMs; chained compositions were consistently more damaging than any single stage. Numbers not reported in the abstract.
quote: Across brain MRI, chest X-ray, and abdominal CT, CoDA substantially degrades the zero-shot performance of CLIP-style MVLMs, with chained compositions consistently more damaging than any single stage.

title: CURE: A Multimodal Benchmark for Clinical Understanding and Retrieval Evaluation
outcome: Differential diagnosis accuracy with physician reference evidence versus independent retrieval
effect: Up to 73.4% accuracy on differential diagnosis with physician reference evidence; as low as 25.4% when models relied on independent retrieval.
quote: Evaluations reveal a stark dichotomy: while advanced models demonstrate clinical reasoning proficiency when supplied with physician reference evidence (achieving up to $73.4\%$ accuracy on differential diagnosis), their performance substantially declines (as low as $25.4\%$) when reliant on independent retrieval mechanisms.

title: FDARxBench: Benchmarking Regulatory and Clinical Reasoning on FDA Generic Drug Assessment
outcome: LLM refusal behavior on unanswerable drug-label questions in document-grounded QA benchmark
effect: Experiments across proprietary and open-weight models revealed substantial gaps in safe refusal behavior, alongside gaps in factual grounding and long-context retrieval. No numbers in the abstract.
quote: Experiments across proprietary and open-weight models reveal substantial gaps in factual grounding, long-context retrieval, and safe refusal behavior.

title: TimeTox: An LLM-Based Pipeline for Automated Extraction of Time Toxicity from Clinical Trial Protocols
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM time toxicity extraction across 3 repeated runs on real-world protocols
effect: Vanilla pipeline: 95.3% clinically acceptable (IQR ≤ 3 days) across 3 runs on 644 protocols; 82.0% perfect stability (IQR = 0), so about 18% of protocols showed run-to-run variation.
quote: However, on real-world protocols, the vanilla pipeline showed superior reproducibility: 95.3% clinically acceptable accuracy (IQR $\leq$ 3 days) across 3 runs on 644 protocols, with 82.0% perfect stability (IQR = 0).
sample_unit: real-world oncology protocols (plus 20 synthetic schedules, 240 comparisons)

title: Deliberative multi-agent large language models improve clinical reasoning in ophthalmology
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of multi-agent councils vs pooled individual LLMs on ophthalmology vignettes
effect: Councils outperformed pooled individual models in all tiers. Accuracy was 95.0% vs 90.8% (flagship), 96.0% vs 86.5% (fast), and 91.0% vs 83.2% (open-source).
quote: Accuracy improved for proprietary flagship (95.0% vs 90.8%; risk difference [RD]: 4.25 [95% CI: 0.45, 8.05]), proprietary fast (96.0% vs 86.5%; RD: 9.50 [5.31, 13.59]), and open-source councils (91.0% vs 83.2%; RD: 7.75 [4.17, 11.33]).

title: Agentic Automation of BT-RADS Scoring: End-to-End Multi-Agent System for Standardized Brain Tumor Follow-up Assessment
outcome: BT-RADS classification accuracy versus expert reference standard, AI system compared with initial clinical assessments
effect: AI system 374/492 (76.0%; 95% CI 72.1%-79.6%) versus 283/492 (57.5%; 95% CI 53.1%-61.8%) for initial clinical assessments, +18.5 percentage points, P<.001
quote: The system achieved 374/492 (76.0%; 95% CI, 72.1%-79.6%) accuracy versus 283/492 (57.5%; 95% CI, 53.1%-61.8%) for initial clinical assessments (+18.5 percentage points; P<.001).

title: Errors in AI-Assisted Retrieval of Medical Literature: A Comparative Study
outcome: Validity and relevance of references retrieved by LLMs (DOI, PubMed ID, Google Scholar link, relevance)
effect: Complete miss rate 47.8%; mean score ratio 0.29 (SD 0.35); highest Grok 0.57, lowest Gemini 0.11; NEJM articles had lower scores than BMJ.
quote: LLM platforms completely failed to retrieve correct reference data 47.8% of the time.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Extract and Translate Medical Information in Doctors' Notes for Health Records and Diagnostic Billing Codes
outcome: ICD-10-CM code accuracy with retrieval-augmented generation versus zero-shot and few-shot prompting
effect: RAG enabled limited discovery of unseen codes, but it frequently saturated context windows, reducing overall accuracy.
quote: While RAG enabled limited discovery of unseen codes, it frequently saturated context windows, reducing overall accuracy.

title: MedMT-Bench: Can LLMs Memorize and Understand Long Multi-Turn Conversations in Medical Scenarios?
outcome: Accuracy on long multi-turn medical instruction following, including interference robustness and safety defense
effect: All 17 frontier models scored below 60.00% overall accuracy; the best model reached 59.75%.
quote: We test 17 frontier models, all of which underperform on MedMT-Bench (overall accuracy below 60.00\%), with the best model reaching 59.75\%.

title: From Physician Expertise to Clinical Agents: Preserving, Standardizing, and Scaling Physicians' Medical Expertise with Lightweight LLM
outcome: Reliability of LLM-as-a-judge versus physician evaluation of model outputs
effect: Automated judging tracks overall trends but shows bias on fine-grained individualized distinctions, highlighting need for physician involvement when ground truth is unavailable.
quote: We also examine the reliability of LLM-as-a-judge versus physician evaluation: automated judging tracks overall trends but shows bias on fine-grained individualized distinctions, highlighting the need for physician involvement when ground truth is unavailable and for domain-adapted judge models.

title: Can we generate portable representations for clinical time series data using LLMs?
outcome: Cross-hospital transfer performance drop of ICU prediction models using LLM-based portable embeddings versus baselines
effect: LLM-summary embeddings were competitive in-distribution and showed smaller relative performance drops when transferring to new hospitals, so performance degradation at new sites still occurs but is reduced.
quote: Across three cohorts (MIMIC-IV, HIRID, PPICU), on multiple clinically grounded forecasting and classification tasks, we find that our approach is simple, easy to use and competitive with in-distribution with grid imputation, self-supervised representation learning, and time series foundation models, while exhibiting smaller relative performance drops when transferring to new hospitals.
country: multiple (three ICU cohorts: MIMIC-IV, HIRID, PPICU)

title: Multi-Agent Reasoning with Consistency Verification Improves Uncertainty Calibration in Medical MCQA
outcome: Calibration (ECE) and discrimination (AUROC) of LLM confidence with verification and multi-agent fusion versus single-specialist baseline
effect: On MedQA-250, ECE 0.091 (74.4% reduction vs baseline), AUROC 0.630 (+0.056) at 59.2% accuracy; calibration gains of 49-74% across four settings; Two-Phase Verification drove ECE reduction.
quote: On MedQA-250, the full system achieves ECE = 0.091 (74.4% reduction over the single-specialist baseline) and AUROC = 0.630 (+0.056) at 59.2% accuracy.

title: Knowledge-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Zero-Shot Psychiatric Data: Privacy Preserving Synthetic Data Generation
outcome: Fidelity of synthetic psychiatric data with vs without clinical knowledge retrieval
effect: Ablation showed clinical retrieval reliably improved univariate and pairwise fidelity over a no-retrieval LLM.
quote: An ablation study shows that clinical retrieval reliably improves univariate and pairwise fidelity over a no-retrieval LLM.

title: A Decade-Scale Benchmark Evaluating LLMs' Clinical Practice Guidelines Detection and Adherence in Multi-turn Conversations
outcome: LLM adherence to clinical practice guideline recommendations in multi-turn conversations
effect: Adherence rates ranged from 21.8% to 63.2% across 8 LLMs; guideline recommendations were detected correctly in 71.1%-89.6%.
quote: The adherence rates range from 21.8% to 63.2% in different models, indicating a large gap between knowing the guidelines and being able to apply them.

title: A Decade-Scale Benchmark Evaluating LLMs' Clinical Practice Guidelines Detection and Adherence in Multi-turn Conversations
outcome: Correct referencing of guideline source titles by LLMs
effect: Only 3.6%-29.7% of corresponding guideline titles were correctly referenced, versus 71.1%-89.6% of recommendations detected.
quote: We find that the 71.1%-89.6% recommendations can be correctly detected, while only 3.6%-29.7% corresponding titles can be correctly referenced, revealing the gap between knowing the guideline contents and where they come from.

title: AD-CARE: A Guideline-grounded, Modality-agnostic LLM Agent for Real-world Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis with Multi-cohort Assessment, Fairness Analysis, and Reader Study
outcome: Neurologist and radiologist diagnostic accuracy and decision time with versus without the AI agent
effect: Agent improved neurologist and radiologist accuracy by 6%-11% and more than halved decision time in a controlled reader study; overreliance not reported in the abstract.
quote: In a controlled reader study, the agent improved neurologist and radiologist accuracy by 6%-11% and more than halved decision time.

title: AD-CARE: A Guideline-grounded, Modality-agnostic LLM Agent for Real-world Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis with Multi-cohort Assessment, Fairness Analysis, and Reader Study
outcome: Performance disparities across racial and age subgroups
effect: AD-CARE decreased average dispersion of four metrics by 21%-68% across racial subgroups and 28%-51% across age subgroups, so disparities were reduced but not eliminated.
quote: AD-CARE reduced performance disparities across racial and age subgroups, decreasing the average dispersion of four metrics by 21%-68% and 28%-51%, respectively.

title: When Chain-of-Thought Backfires: Evaluating Prompt Sensitivity in Medical Language Models
outcome: Prediction stability and accuracy under answer-option shuffling, few-shot, CoT, and context truncation perturbations
effect: Shuffling options changed predictions 59.1% of the time, accuracy dropping up to 27.4 points; few-shot lowered performance 11.9% and raised position bias from 0.14 to 0.47; CoT lowered accuracy 5.7%.
quote: Shuffling answer options causes the model to change predictions 59.1% of the time, with accuracy dropping up to 27.4 percentage points.

title: FairLLaVA: Fairness-Aware Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Large Vision-Language Assistants
outcome: Inter-group disparities and overall clinical and language generation performance after bias mitigation fine-tuning
effect: FairLLaVA consistently reduced inter-group disparities while improving equity-scaled clinical performance and natural language generation quality across chest radiology and dermoscopy benchmarks (no numbers in abstract).
quote: Extensive experiments on large-scale chest radiology report generation and dermoscopy visual question answering benchmarks show that FairLLaVA consistently reduces inter-group disparities while improving both equity-scaled clinical performance and natural language generation quality across diverse medical imaging modalities.
sample_unit: benchmark datasets (chest radiology report generation, dermoscopy VQA)

title: Automating Clinical Information Retrieval from Finnish Electronic Health Records Using Large Language Models
outcome: Consistency of LLM answers across semantically equivalent question variants
effect: Llama-3.1-70B had 97.3% consistency, but equivalent questions occasionally gave discordant responses; one correct and one clinically significant error in 0.96% of cases.
quote: semantically equivalent questions occasionally yielded discordant responses, including instances where one formulation was correct and the other contained a clinically significant error (0.96% of cases).

title: Automating Clinical Information Retrieval from Finnish Electronic Health Records Using Large Language Models
outcome: Rate of clinically significant errors in LLM outputs retrieving patient information from EHRs
effect: Clinical evaluation identified clinically significant errors in 2.9% of outputs; Llama-3.1-70B free-text accuracy was 95.3%.
quote: Clinical evaluation identified clinically significant errors in 2.9% of outputs

title: Automating Clinical Information Retrieval from Finnish Electronic Health Records Using Large Language Models
outcome: Response consistency across equivalent question paraphrases
effect: 97.3% consistency for Llama-3.1-70B across semantically equivalent variants; occasional discordant responses, including 0.96% with one correct and one clinically significantly erroneous.
quote: semantically equivalent questions occasionally yielded discordant responses, including instances where one formulation was correct and the other contained a clinically significant error (0.96% of cases).

title: PubMed Reasoner: Dynamic Reasoning-based Retrieval for Evidence-Grounded Biomedical Question Answering
outcome: Biomedical QA accuracy and judged evidence grounding of retrieval-grounded answers with citations
effect: 78.32% accuracy on PubMedQA with GPT-4o, slightly above human experts; consistent gains on MMLU Clinical Knowledge; LLM judges preferred responses for evidence grounding.
quote: PubMed Reasoner with a GPT-4o backbone achieves 78.32% accuracy on PubMedQA, slightly surpassing human experts, and showing consistent gains on MMLU Clinical Knowledge.

title: Beyond Idealized Patients: Evaluating LLMs under Challenging Patient Behaviors in Medical Consultations
outcome: LLM response safety to contradictory, inaccurate, self-diagnosing, or care-resistant patient utterances
effect: Models performed well overall but showed consistent behavior-specific failure patterns, with particular difficulty on contradictory or medically implausible patient information.
quote: While models perform well overall, we identify consistent, behavior-specific failure patterns, with particular difficulty in handling contradictory or medically implausible patient information.

title: Disentangling Prompt Element Level Risk Factors for Hallucinations and Omissions in Mental Health LLM Responses
outcome: Omission of safety-critical guidance in crisis and suicidal ideation prompts
effect: Omissions occurred in 13.2% of responses, concentrated in crisis and suicidal ideation prompts; hallucinations in 6.5%.
quote: Hallucinations occurred in 6.5% of responses and omissions in 13.2%, with omissions concentrated in crisis and suicidal ideation prompts.

title: Disentangling Prompt Element Level Risk Factors for Hallucinations and Omissions in Mental Health LLM Responses
outcome: Response failures across equivalent prompt variations in context and tone
effect: Failures were most consistently associated with context and tone, while user-background indicators showed no systematic differences after balancing.
quote: Across regression, element-specific matching, and similarity-matched comparisons, failures were most consistently associated with context and tone, while user-background indicators showed no systematic differences after balancing.

title: WHBench: Evaluating Frontier LLMs with Expert-in-the-Loop Validation on Women's Health Topics
outcome: LLM clinical accuracy and guideline adherence on women's health scenarios, including outdated guidelines and unsafe omissions
effect: No model mean performance exceeded 75 percent; best model reached 72.1 percent. Top models showed low fully correct rates and substantial variation in harm rates.
quote: Across 3,102 attempted responses (3,100 scored), no model mean performance exceeds 75 percent; the best model reaches 72.1 percent.

title: WHBench: Evaluating Frontier LLMs with Expert-in-the-Loop Validation on Women's Health Topics
outcome: Dosing errors in LLM responses to women's health scenarios
effect: Benchmark designed to expose dosing errors; no model exceeded 75% mean, and harm rates varied substantially. Dosing-specific rates are not reported in the provided text.
quote: We present the Women's Health Benchmark (WHBench), a targeted evaluation suite of 47 expert-crafted scenarios across 10 women's health topics, designed to expose clinically meaningful failure modes including outdated guidelines, unsafe omissions, dosing errors, and equity-related blind spots.

title: Development and multi-center evaluation of domain-adapted speech recognition for human-AI teaming in real-world gastrointestinal endoscopy
outcome: ASR accuracy generalization across five independent endoscopy centers
effect: Prospective multi-center CER 14.97% vs 16.20% for baseline Paraformer; medical term accuracy 84.16% vs 61.63%; described as consistent generalization across centers.
quote: In a prospective multi-center study spanning five independent endoscopy centers, EndoASR demonstrates consistent generalization under heterogeneous real-world conditions.

title: Blinded Radiologist and LLM-Based Evaluation of LLM-Generated Japanese Translations of Chest CT Reports: Comparative Study
outcome: Inter-rater agreement between radiologists, and between radiologists and LLM judges (QWK)
effect: Radiologist-LLM judge QWK -0.04 to 0.15; between the 2 radiologists QWK 0.01 to 0.06, indicating poor agreement in reference ratings.
quote: Agreement between the 2 radiologists was also poor (QWK=0.01 to 0.06).

title: Blinded Radiologist and LLM-Based Evaluation of LLM-Generated Japanese Translations of Chest CT Reports: Comparative Study
outcome: Agreement of LLM-as-a-judge with expert radiologist evaluation of translations
effect: LLM judges favored the LLM translation in 70%-99% of cases with near-zero agreement with radiologists (QWK -0.04 to 0.15); expert radiologist review remains important.
quote: For educational use of translated radiology reports, automated LLM-based evaluation alone is insufficient; expert radiologist review remains important.

title: Benchmarking Multi-turn Medical Diagnosis: Hold, Lure, and Self-Correction
outcome: LLM diagnostic behavior when clinical evidence is released incrementally across turns rather than in a single turn
effect: Over 55% of answers were committed within the first two turns. Salient evidence such as lab results triggered premature answering even when models were told to wait. Premature commitment caused accuracy drops of up to 23.3%.
quote: We translate these findings into clinically actionable guidance: deferring the diagnostic question to later turns reduces premature answering and improves accuracy at the first point of commitment by up to 62.6%, while reserving salient clinical evidence for later turns prevents a catastrophic accuracy drop of up to 23.3% caused by premature commitment.

title: Do No Harm: Exposing Hidden Vulnerabilities of LLMs via Persona-based Client Simulation Attack in Psychological Counseling
outcome: LLM safety failures (unauthorized medical advice, reinforcing delusions) under persona-driven multi-turn counseling attacks
effect: PCSA substantially outperformed four baselines on seven LLMs. Models gave unauthorized medical advice, reinforced delusions, and implicitly encouraged risky actions. No numbers in the abstract.
quote: Our results reveal that current LLMs remain vulnerable to domain-specific adversarial tactics, providing unauthorized medical advice, reinforcing delusions, and implicitly encouraging risky actions.

title: This Treatment Works, Right? Evaluating LLM Sensitivity to Patient Question Framing in Medical QA
outcome: Consistency of LLM conclusions across equivalent questions differing in framing and language style
effect: Positive vs negative framed pairs significantly more likely to yield contradictory conclusions than same-framing pairs; amplified in multi-turn conversations; no significant framing by language-style interaction.
quote: Our findings show that positively- and negatively-framed pairs are significantly more likely to produce contradictory conclusions than same-framing pairs.

title: This Treatment Works, Right? Evaluating LLM Sensitivity to Patient Question Framing in Medical QA
outcome: Response consistency under paraphrased or reframed medical questions with identical evidence
effect: Opposite-framing query pairs were significantly more likely to produce contradictory conclusions across eight LLMs; inconsistency increased with sustained persuasion in multi-turn conversations.
quote: Our findings show that positively- and negatively-framed pairs are significantly more likely to produce contradictory conclusions than same-framing pairs.

title: OGA-AID: Clinician-in-the-loop AI Report Drafting Assistant for Multimodal Observational Gait Analysis in Post-Stroke Rehabilitation
outcome: Error versus multimodal baselines
effect: OGA-AID outperformed single-pass multimodal baselines with low error; no numeric effect reported.
quote: Evaluated with expert physiotherapists on real patient data, OGA-AID consistently outperforms single-pass multimodal baselines with low error.

title: A Multi-Stage Validation Framework for Trustworthy Large-scale Clinical Information Extraction using Large Language Models
outcome: Agreement of judge-LLM assessments with subject matter expert review on high-uncertainty extractions
effect: Judge LLM assessments showed substantial agreement with subject matter expert review (Gwet's AC1=0.80); primary LLM F1 0.80 under relaxed matching against judge-evaluated references.
quote: For high-uncertainty cases, the judge LLM's assessments showed substantial agreement with subject matter expert review (Gwet's AC1=0.80).

title: A Multi-Stage Validation Framework for Trustworthy Large-scale Clinical Information Extraction using Large Language Models
outcome: Share of LLM-positive extractions removed by rule-based plausibility filtering and semantic grounding
effect: Rule-based filtering and semantic grounding removed 14.59% of LLM-positive extractions that were unsupported, irrelevant, or structurally implausible.
quote: Rule-based filtering and semantic grounding removed 14.59% of LLM-positive extractions that were unsupported, irrelevant, or structurally implausible.

title: A Multi-Stage Validation Framework for Trustworthy Large-scale Clinical Information Extraction using Large Language Models
outcome: specialty-care engagement prediction
effect: LLM-extracted SUD diagnoses were more accurate than structured-data baselines (AUC=0.80).
quote: LLM-extracted SUD diagnoses also predicted subsequent engagement in SUD specialty care more accurately than structured-data baselines (AUC=0.80).

title: Blending Human and LLM Expertise to Detect Hallucinations and Omissions in Mental Health Chatbot Responses
outcome: Accuracy of automated hallucination and omission detection in mental health chatbot responses, LLM judges versus expert-informed features
effect: LLM judges reached only 52% accuracy, with some near-zero recall. Expert-informed feature models reached 0.717 F1 (custom dataset) and 0.849 F1 (public benchmark) for hallucinations, and 0.59-0.64 F1 for omissions.
quote: We show that leading LLM judges achieve only 52% accuracy on mental health counseling data, with some hallucination detection approaches exhibiting near-zero recall.

title: MedDialBench: Benchmarking LLM Diagnostic Robustness under Parametric Adversarial Patient Behaviors
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy under perturbed patient inputs (fabricated or withheld information)
effect: Fabricating symptoms produced 1.7-3.4x larger accuracy drops than withholding information. Fabricating was significant across all five models (McNemar p<0.05). Worst-case drops ranged from 38.8 to 54.1 percentage points.
quote: we find a fundamental asymmetry: information pollution (fabricating symptoms) produces 1.7-3.4x larger accuracy drops than information deficit (withholding information), and fabricating is the only configuration achieving statistical significance across all five models (McNemar p < 0.05).
sample_unit: dialogues (85 cases x 17 configurations x 5 models)

title: To Adapt or not to Adapt, Rethinking the Value of Medical Knowledge-Aware Large Language Models
outcome: Model robustness to perturbed questions, instruction following, and strict output formatting
effect: Both general and clinical models showed substantial limitations in instruction following and strict output formatting; clinical models did not consistently beat general models even under the perturbation benchmark. No numbers in abstract.
quote: We further find that both general and clinical models exhibit substantial limitations in instruction following and strict output formatting.
sample_unit: multiple-choice clinical questions (English and Spanish benchmark subsets)

title: Self-Preference Bias in Rubric-Based Evaluation of Large Language Models
outcome: Self-preference bias of LLM judges when scoring HealthBench medical chat rubrics
effect: SPB skews model scores by up to 10 points on HealthBench; judges can be over 50% more likely to wrongly mark failed rubrics as satisfied for their own outputs on IFEval and LiveCodeBench.
quote: On HealthBench, a medical chat benchmark with subjective rubrics, we observe that SPB skews model scores by up to 10 points, a potentially decisive margin when ranking frontier models.

title: A Systematic Study of Retrieval Pipeline Design for Retrieval-Augmented Medical Question Answering
outcome: Zero-shot medical QA accuracy with versus without retrieval augmentation on MedQA USMLE
effect: Retrieval augmentation significantly improved zero-shot accuracy; best configuration (dense retrieval with query reformulation and reranking) reached 60.49% accuracy.
quote: Results show that retrieval augmentation significantly improves zero-shot medical question answering performance.

title: IatroBench: A Pre-Registered Benchmark of Clinical Omission in Language Models
outcome: Consistency of model responses across patient versus doctor framings of the same clinical case
effect: Mean decoupling gap of +0.38 across models (p = 0.003), and +0.22 under an independent LLM judge (95% CI 0.10-0.36, p = 0.0014); models shared more information in the doctor framing.
quote: We find that when the same case is presented as a patient query and a doctor consultation (the variants also differ in register, request and the supervision a treating physician implies), all five models we test share more information with the doctor than the patient.

title: IatroBench: A Pre-Registered Benchmark of Clinical Omission in Language Models
outcome: Agreement of LLM judge with a physician-written rubric, versus a standard LLM judge, in detecting omission harm
effect: Judge scores against the physician rubric aligned with the physician's scores as well as a second physician's did, while a standard LLM judge rated zero omission harm in 86.6% of cases the structured evaluation scored as omission harms.
quote: A standard LLM judge rates responses as having zero omission harm in 86.6% of cases where our structured evaluations score them as omission harms.

title: Automatic Generation of Executable BPMN Models from Medical Guidelines
outcome: Whether entropy-based uncertainty detection separates unambiguous policies from ambiguous ones needing human clarification
effect: Entropy scores increased monotonically with document complexity, reliably separating unambiguous policies from those requiring targeted human clarification; raw per-patient decision agreement exceeded 92% across all conditions.
quote: Across all conditions, raw per-patient decision agreement exceeds 92%, and entropy scores increase monotonically with document complexity, confirming that the detector reliably separates unambiguous policies from those requiring targeted human clarification.

title: Facet-Level Tracing of Evidence Uncertainty and Hallucination in RAG
outcome: Hallucination under Strict RAG, Soft RAG, and LLM-only modes in medical QA and HotpotQA
effect: Hallucinated answers remain common even when relevant documents are retrieved. Errors are driven less by retrieval accuracy and more by how retrieved evidence is integrated during generation. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
quote: Our results demonstrate that hallucinations in RAG systems are driven less by retrieval accuracy and more by how retrieved evidence is integrated during generation, with facet-level analysis exposing systematic evidence override and misalignment patterns that remain hidden under answer-level evaluation.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Evidence-Informed Guidance on Cannabidiol Use in Older Adults
outcome: Caution and guideline alignment of cannabidiol advice from retrieval-augmented versus standalone LLMs, judged by automated evaluation
effect: Across three automated evaluation strategies, retrieval-augmented models produced more cautious and guideline-aligned recommendations than standalone models; the ensemble retrieval approach performed best.
quote: Across three automated evaluation strategies, retrieval-augmented models consistently produced more cautious and guideline-aligned recommendations than standalone models, with the ensemble approach performing best.

title: VeriSim: A Configurable Framework for Stress-Testing Medical AI Under Patient Communication Noise
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and conversation length under simulated patient communication noise versus clean cases
effect: Realistic noise reduced diagnostic accuracy by 15-25 percentage points and increased conversation length by 34-55%; 7-8B models degraded 1.4x more than 70B+ models.
quote: Across seven open-weight LLMs, realistic noise reduces diagnostic accuracy by 15-25 percentage points and increases conversation length by 34-55%; the 7-8B models degrade 1.4x more than 70B+ models.

title: Evaluating Small Open LLMs for Medical Question Answering: A Practical Framework
outcome: Output reproducibility across 10 repeated runs per question at low temperature
effect: Self-agreement across runs reaches at most 0.20 despite T=0.2, while 87-97% of all outputs per model are unique.
quote: Evaluating three models (Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma 3 12B, MedGemma 1.5 4B) on 50 MedQuAD questions (N=1,500 total responses) reveals that despite low-temperature generation (T=0.2), self-agreement across runs reaches at most 0.20, while 87-97% of all outputs per model are unique -- a safety gap that single-pass benchmarks entirely miss.
sample_unit: responses (50 MedQuAD questions x 10 runs x 3 models)

title: How Robust Are Large Language Models for Clinical Numeracy? An Empirical Study on Numerical Reasoning Abilities in Clinical Contexts
outcome: LLM numeracy accuracy across semantically equivalent clinical note formats
effect: Performance dropped under note-style variation, indicating format sensitivity. Value retrieval was mostly above 85% accuracy; relational comparison and aggregation were weak, with some models below 15%.
quote: Fine-tuning on medical data can reduce numeracy relative to base models by over 30%, and performance drops under note-style variation indicate LLM sensitivity to format.

title: How Robust Are Large Language Models for Clinical Numeracy? An Empirical Study on Numerical Reasoning Abilities in Clinical Contexts
outcome: Numeracy of medically fine-tuned LLMs versus their base models
effect: Fine-tuning on medical data reduced numeracy relative to base models by over 30%.
quote: Fine-tuning on medical data can reduce numeracy relative to base models by over 30%, and performance drops under note-style variation indicate LLM sensitivity to format.

title: Consistency of AI-Generated Exercise Prescriptions: A Repeated Generation Study Using a Large Language Model
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM exercise prescriptions across repeated identical generations (semantic, structural, safety consistency)
effect: Mean cosine similarity 0.879-0.939; frequency consistent, but intensity varied, with 10-25% of resistance training intensity expressions unclassifiable; safety sentence counts varied significantly across scenarios (H=86.18, p<0.001).
quote: LLM-generated exercise prescriptions demonstrated high semantic consistency but showed variability in key quantitative components.
sample_unit: LLM-generated exercise prescriptions (20 per scenario, 6 scenarios)

title: Can Large Language Models Reliably Extract Physiology Index Values from Coronary Angiography Reports?
outcome: Robustness of extraction performance to prompt changes and few-shot prompting with implausible examples
effect: GPT-OSS showed highest robustness to prompt changes; changing prompt technique and adding a RegEx layer showed no significant improvement across models.
quote: Non-medical models performed similarly, the best results were obtained with Llama with a zero-shot prompting, while GPT-OSS demonstrated the highest robustness to changes in the prompts.

title: Can Large Language Models Reliably Extract Physiology Index Values from Coronary Angiography Reports?
outcome: RegEx post-processing
effect: Adding a RegEx layer showed no significant improvement across models.
quote: Changes in the prompt techinique and adding a RegEx layer showed no significant improvement across models, while using constrained generation decreased performance, although having the benefit of allowing the usage of specific models that are not able to conform with the templates.

title: Beyond Arrow's Impossibility: Fairness as an Emergent Property of Multi-Agent Collaboration
outcome: Fairness of resource allocation actions by LLM triage agents across demographic groups
effect: Neither agent's allocation was ethically adequate in isolation; an adversarially prompted agent favored demographic groups over clinical need. Joint final allocations could satisfy fairness criteria.
quote: We find that alignment systematically shapes negotiation strategies and allocation patterns, and that neither agent's allocation is ethically adequate in isolation, yet their joint final allocation can satisfy fairness criteria that neither would have reached alone.

title: Beyond Arrow's Impossibility: Fairness as an Emergent Property of Multi-Agent Collaboration
outcome: Whether an ethically aligned agent moderates a biased counterpart's allocation bias
effect: Aligned agents partially moderated bias and restored access for marginalized groups, without fully converting the biased counterpart. Aligned agents also showed intrinsic framework biases.
quote: Aligned agents partially moderate bias through contestation rather than override, acting as corrective patches that restore access for marginalized groups without fully converting a biased counterpart.

title: "AI Psychosis" in Context: How Conversation History Shapes LLM Responses to Delusional Beliefs
outcome: Risk and safety of LLM responses to escalating delusional multi-turn conversation, including directing user to external support
effect: GPT-4o, Grok 4.1 Fast and Gemini 3 Pro showed high-risk, low-safety profiles that degraded with accumulated context; Claude Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.2 Instant showed stronger safety interventions as context accumulated.
quote: As context accumulated, performance degraded in the unsafe group, while the same material activated stronger safety interventions among safer models.
sample_unit: LLMs tested across three levels of accumulated context

title: "AI Psychosis" in Context: How Conversation History Shapes LLM Responses to Delusional Beliefs
outcome: Model validation of delusional beliefs versus challenge and referral across increasing conversation context
effect: Unsafe-tier models validated or elaborated delusional premises and attempted harm reduction inside the delusional frame; safer models challenged beliefs and directed the user to external support, using the established relationship.
quote: Safer models, however, often used the established relationship to support intervention, challenging delusional beliefs and directing the user to external support.
sample_unit: LLMs tested across three levels of accumulated context

title: Enhancing Mental Health Counseling Support in Bangladesh using Culturally-Grounded Knowledge
outcome: Counseling response quality with clinically validated knowledge graph grounding versus RAG alone
effect: KG-based approaches consistently improved contextual relevance, clinical appropriateness, and practical usability compared to RAG alone (no numbers in abstract).
quote: The results show that KG-based approaches consistently improve contextual relevance, clinical appropriateness, and practical usability compared to RAG alone, demonstrating that structured, expert-validated knowledge plays a critical role in addressing LLMs limitations in counseling tasks.

title: Blinded Multi-Rater Comparative Evaluation of a Large Language Model and Clinician-Authored Responses in CGM-Informed Diabetes Counseling
outcome: LLM agent vs clinician-authored responses on six quality dimensions rated by blinded clinicians
effect: CA scored higher than clinicians (mean 4.37 vs 3.58); estimated difference 0.782 points (95% CI 0.692-0.872; P<.001); largest for empathy (1.062) and actionability (0.992).
quote: The CA received higher quality scores than clinician responses (mean 4.37 vs 3.58), with an estimated mean difference of 0.782 points (95% CI 0.692-0.872; P<.001).

title: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs for Inpatient Diagnosis: Real-World Performance, Safety, and Cost Across Ten Frontier Models
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy and safety scores versus routine ward diagnoses and versus other LLMs on same cases
effect: All ten LLMs significantly outperformed routine ward diagnoses on average diagnostic and safety scores. LLM performance was tightly clustered (<15% variation) despite large cost differences.
quote: (ii) All LLMs significantly outperformed routine ward diagnoses on average diagnostic and safety scores.

title: The Provenance Gap in Clinical AI: Evidence-Traceable Temporal Knowledge Graphs for Rare Disease Reasoning
outcome: Clinically relevant PubMed identifiers produced by frontier LLMs in citations
effect: No model produced a clinically relevant PMID without prompting; when asked to cite, best model achieved 15.3% relevant PMIDs; majority resolved to unrelated publications.
quote: No model produced a clinically relevant PubMed identifier without prompting.

title: The Provenance Gap in Clinical AI: Evidence-Traceable Temporal Knowledge Graphs for Rare Disease Reasoning
outcome: Evidence verifiability and clinical coverage of grounded knowledge graph versus ungrounded/RAG baselines
effect: HEG-TKG matched baseline clinical feature coverage with 100% evidence verifiability (203 inline citations); Guideline-RAG produced zero verifiable citations; clinician evaluation d = 1.81, p < 0.001, no degradation on safety or completeness.
quote: In a controlled three-arm comparison using the same synthesis model, HEG-TKG matches baseline clinical feature coverage while achieving 100% evidence verifiability with 203 inline citations.

title: The Provenance Gap in Clinical AI: Evidence-Traceable Temporal Knowledge Graphs for Rare Disease Reasoning
outcome: Traceability of claims to source via citation trace and detectability of injected errors
effect: 80% resistance to injected clinical errors with 100% detectability via citation trace; clinician-rated verifiability advantage d = 1.81.
quote: A counterfactual experiment shows 80% resistance to injected clinical errors with 100% detectability via citation trace.

title: Calibrated? Not for Everyone: How Sexual Orientation and Religious Markers Distort LLM Accuracy and Confidence in Medical QA
outcome: Change in LLM accuracy and confidence when sexual orientation or religion markers are added to questions
effect: Identity markers caused a "calibration crisis"; "Homosexual" markers consistently triggered performance drops; intersectional identities produced non-additive harms to calibration. Confirmed in an open-ended generation case study.
quote: "Homosexual" markers consistently trigger performance drops, and intersectional identities produce idiosyncratic, non-additive harms to calibration.

title: Calibrated? Not for Everyone: How Sexual Orientation and Religious Markers Distort LLM Accuracy and Confidence in Medical QA
outcome: Reliability of LLM confidence signals under social identity cues
effect: Social identity cues affect the reliability of confidence signals, not only predictions, posing a risk in confidence-based clinical workflows.
quote: Our results demonstrate that the presence of social identity cues does not merely shift predictions; it affects the reliability of confidence signals, posing a significant risk to equitable care and safe deployment in confidence-based clinical workflows.

title: MHSafeEval: Role-Aware Interaction-Level Evaluation of Mental Health Safety in Large Language Models
outcome: Harm discovery by adversarial multi-turn evaluation versus static benchmarks for mental health LLMs
effect: Adversarial multi-turn agent-based evaluation revealed substantial role-dependent and cumulative safety failures missed by static benchmarks, and improved failure-mode coverage and diagnostic granularity. No numbers are available in the text provided.
quote: Our results reveal substantial role-dependent and cumulative safety failures that are systematically missed by existing static benchmarks, and show that our framework significantly improves failure-mode coverage and diagnostic granularity.

title: First, Do No Harm (With LLMs): Mitigating Racial Bias via Agentic Workflows
outcome: Racial bias in differential diagnosis ranking across race-varied prompts, standalone vs agentic workflow
effect: DeepSeek V3 in an agentic workflow improved 0.0348 in mean p-value, 0.1166 in median p-value, and 0.0949 in mean difference versus standalone, though not uniform across every metric.
quote: When embedded in an agentic workflow, DeepSeek V3 showed an improvement of 0.0348 in mean p-value, 0.1166 in median p-value, and 0.0949 in mean difference relative to the standalone model, although improvement was not uniform across every metric.
sample_unit: LLM-generated synthetic cases and differential diagnosis lists

title: First, Do No Harm (With LLMs): Mitigating Racial Bias via Agentic Workflows
outcome: Deviation of LLM-generated synthetic patient cases from observed US race-stratified epidemiological distributions
effect: All five models deviated from observed racial distributions in synthetic case generation; GPT-4.1 showed the smallest overall deviation.
quote: All models deviated from observed racial distributions in the synthetic case generation task, with GPT-4.1 showing the smallest overall deviation.
sample_unit: LLM-generated synthetic cases and differential diagnosis lists

title: Beyond Semantic Similarity: A Component-Wise Evaluation Framework for Medical Question Answering Systems with Health Equity Implications
outcome: LLM performance disparities across public health topics, including chronic conditions common in older and minority populations
effect: Most models scored 13.8% lower than their overall average on topics about chronic conditions occurring in older and minority populations, which the authors interpret as condition-based algorithmic discrimination.
quote: Our findings indicate alarming performance disparities across various public health topics, with most of the models exhibiting 13.8% lower performance (compared to an overall average) for all the public health topics that relate to chronic conditions that occur in older and minority populations, which indicates the existence of what's known as condition-based algorithmic discrimination.

title: Effects of Cross-lingual Evidence in Multilingual Medical Question Answering
outcome: Medical QA accuracy with versus without retrieved or curated external evidence across languages and model sizes
effect: External knowledge did not systematically improve performance. English web retrieval helped most for high-resource languages. English plus target-language retrieval helped low-resource languages. PubMed lacked multilingual coverage.
quote: These findings challenge the assumption that external knowledge systematically improves performance and reveal that effective strategies depend on both the source of language resources and on model scale.

title: Can "AI" Be a Doctor? A Study of Empathy, Readability, and Alignment in Clinical LLMs
outcome: Readability (FKGL) of LLM responses versus physician-authored responses
effect: Larger models (GPT-5, Claude) reached FKGL up to 16.91-17.60 versus 11.47-12.50 for physician responses. Empathy prompting lowered FKGL by up to 6.87 points for GPT-5.
quote: Baseline models amplify affective polarity relative to physicians (Very Negative: 43.14-45.10% vs. 37.25%) and, in larger architectures such as GPT-5 and Claude, produce substantially higher linguistic complexity (FKGL up to 16.91-17.60 vs. 11.47-12.50 in physician-authored responses).

title: Can "AI" Be a Doctor? A Study of Empathy, Readability, and Alignment in Clinical LLMs
outcome: Affective polarity and empathy of LLM responses compared with physicians
effect: Baseline LLMs had more Very Negative affect (43.14-45.10% vs. 37.25% for physicians). Empathy-oriented prompting reduced extreme negativity without significantly raising semantic fidelity.
quote: Baseline models amplify affective polarity relative to physicians (Very Negative: 43.14-45.10% vs. 37.25%) and, in larger architectures such as GPT-5 and Claude, produce substantially higher linguistic complexity (FKGL up to 16.91-17.60 vs. 11.47-12.50 in physician-authored responses).

title: Serialisation Strategy Matters: How FHIR Data Format Affects LLM Medication Reconciliation
outcome: Medication reconciliation F1 across four input serialisation formats and five models
effect: Serialisation strategy had a large significant effect for models up to 8B; Clinical Narrative outperformed Raw JSON by up to 19 F1 points for Mistral-7B (r = 0.617, p < 10^-10); reversed at 70B.
quote: Clinical Narrative outperforms Raw JSON by up to 19 F1 points for Mistral-7B (r = 0.617, p < 10^{-10}).

title: Reliability Auditing for Downstream LLM tasks in Psychiatry: LLM-Generated Hospitalization Risk Scores
outcome: Change in predicted hospitalization risk when medically insignificant inputs and prompt reframings were added
effect: Adding medically insignificant variables produced a statistically significant increase in absolute mean predicted hospitalization risk and output variability across all four models and prompts, indicating reduced predictive stability.
quote: our results show that including medically insignificant variables resulted in a statistically significant increase in the absolute mean predicted hospitalization risk and output variability across all models and prompts, indicating reduced predictive stability as contextual noise increased.

title: Secure On-Premise Deployment of Open-Weights Large Language Models in Radiology: An Isolation-First Architecture with Prospective Pilot Evaluation
outcome: Frequency of critical errors (hallucinations, omissions) in LLM output by prompt task type
effect: Open-ended conclusion generation from findings produced the highest frequency of critical errors, such as clinically relevant hallucinations or omissions; source text-anchored tasks received the highest utility ratings.
quote: Source text-anchored tasks, such as report corrections or simplifications, and radiology guideline recommendations received the highest utility ratings, whereas open-ended conclusion generation based on findings resulted in the highest frequency of critical errors, such as clinically relevant hallucinations or omissions.

title: Domain Fine-Tuning vs. Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Multiple-Choice Question Answering: A Controlled Comparison at the 4B-Parameter Scale
outcome: MedQA-USMLE majority-vote accuracy with versus without retrieved passages inserted into the prompt
effect: RAG over MedMCQA explanations gave no statistically significant gain in either model; in MedGemma the point estimate was -1.9 pp (p = 0.16).
quote: RAG over MedMCQA explanations does not produce a statistically significant gain in either model, and in the domain-tuned model the point estimate is slightly negative (-1.9 pp, p = 0.16).

title: Quantum Knowledge Graph: Modeling Context-Dependent Triplet Validity
outcome: Medical QA accuracy with vs without knowledge-graph-backed validation of LLM reasoner outputs
effect: With Haiku-4.5, KG validation gave +0.61 pp over no validator; QKG with context matching gave +1.40 pp over no validator and +0.79 pp over KG without context matching (all p<0.05). With Qwen-3.6-Plus, QKG gain over no validator was +5.96 pp.
quote: With Haiku-4.5 as both the Reasoner and the Validator, KG-backed validation significantly improves over a no-validator baseline ($+0.61$ pp), and QKG with context matching yields the largest gain, outperforming both KG validation without context matching ($+0.79$ pp) and the no-validator baseline ($+1.40$ pp; paired McNemar, all $p<0.05$).

title: Agentic clinical reasoning over longitudinal myeloma records: a retrospective evaluation against expert consensus
outcome: Concordance with expert consensus, agentic system vs simpler RAG and full-context baselines on same data
effect: Agentic 79.6% concordance vs iterative RAG 75.4% and full-context 75.8% (+3.8 and +4.2 pp; p = 0.006 and 0.007); iterative RAG and full-context did not differ (p = 1.00).
quote: The agentic system reached 79.6% concordance (95% CI 76.4-82.8), exceeding both baselines (+3.8 and +4.2 pp; p = 0.006 and 0.007).

title: Agentic clinical reasoning over longitudinal myeloma records: a retrospective evaluation against expert consensus
outcome: Rate and clinical severity of system errors versus expert disagreement
effect: System error rate 12.2% vs expert disagreement 13.6%; 57.8% of system errors clinically significant vs 18.8% of expert disagreements.
quote: The system error rate (12.2%) was comparable to expert disagreement (13.6%), but severity was inverted: 57.8% of system errors were clinically significant versus 18.8% of expert disagreements.

title: FastOMOP: A Foundational Architecture for Reliable Agentic Real-World Evidence Generation on OMOP CDM data
outcome: Adversarial and out-of-scope request block rates of NL-to-SQL agent team with process-boundary governance
effect: Reliability scores 0.84-0.94 across three OMOP datasets, with perfect adversarial and out-of-scope block rates, independent of model choice.
quote: FastOMOP achieved reliability scores of 0.84-0.94 with perfect adversarial and out-of-scope block rates, demonstrating process-boundary governance delivers safety guarantees independent of model choice.

title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
outcome: Consistency of LLM differential diagnoses across benign rephrasings of patient queries
effect: Prompt-level factors shifted model behavior along clinically meaningful dimensions. Neutralization increased plausibility and conciseness but reduced coverage of highly likely and safety-critical conditions. No numbers in the abstract.
quote: We also study perturbation regimes that capture routine input variation and show that prompt-level factors shift model behavior along clinically meaningful dimensions.

title: Green Shielding: A User-Centric Approach Towards Trustworthy AI
outcome: LLM diagnostic output sensitivity to realistic non-adversarial input variation
effect: Benign input variation shifted outputs, tracing Pareto-like tradeoffs across multiple frontier LLMs. Neutralization reduced coverage of highly likely and safety-critical conditions.
quote: Across multiple frontier LLMs, these shifts trace out Pareto-like tradeoffs.

title: Case-Specific Rubrics for Clinical AI Evaluation: Methodology, Validation, and LLM-Clinician Agreement Across 823 Encounters
outcome: Whether clinician-authored case-specific rubrics discriminate high- from low-quality AI outputs, and stability of scoring
effect: Median score gap between preferred and rejected outputs was 82.9%, with median scoring range of 0.00%. Clinician-LLM ranking agreement (tau 0.42-0.46) matched or exceeded clinician-clinician agreement (tau 0.38-0.43).
quote: Clinician-authored rubrics discriminated effectively between high- and low-quality outputs (median score gap: 82.9%) with high scoring stability (median range: 0.00%).

title: Analyzing LLM Reasoning to Uncover Mental Health Stigma
outcome: Stigmatizing language toward people with psychological conditions in LLM reasoning versus multiple-choice answers
effect: Evaluating LLM reasoning exposes substantially more stigma than traditional MCQ-based methods; stigmatizing statements were tagged and rated by severity (no numbers in the abstract).
quote: Our findings demonstrate that evaluating model reasoning not only exposes substantially more stigma than traditional MCQ-based methods but also helps identify the flaws in the LLMs' logic and their understanding of mental health conditions.

title: One-shot emergency psychiatric triage across 15 frontier AI chatbots
outcome: Emergency under-triage rate of psychiatric emergencies (level D) from single-message disclosures
effect: Emergency under-triage in 23 of 410 level D trials (5.6%); all reassigned to level C. Accuracy highest for level D (94.3%), with marked over-triage of low and intermediate risk presentations.
quote: Emergency under-triage occurred in 23 of 410 level D trials (5.6%), and all under-triaged emergencies were reassigned to level C urgency.

title: One-shot emergency psychiatric triage across 15 frontier AI chatbots
outcome: Missed and unnecessary escalation in psychiatric triage by chatbots
effect: Emergency under-triage 5.6% (23/410 level D trials); mean signed ordinal error +0.47 levels indicating net over-triage; level B accuracy 19.7%.
quote: Mean signed ordinal error was positive (+0.47 triage levels), indicating net over-triage.

title: Benchmarking the Safety of Large Language Models for Robotic Health Attendant Control
outcome: Rate of LLMs following harmful or prohibited instructions (violation rate) in robotic health attendant simulation
effect: Mean violation rate across 72 LLMs was 54.4%, with more than half of models exceeding 50%; proprietary median 23.7% vs open-weight 72.8%.
quote: The mean violation rate across all models was 54.4\%, with more than half exceeding 50\%, and violation rates varied substantially across behavior categories, with superficially plausible instructions such as device manipulation and emergency delay proving harder to refuse than overtly destructive ones.

title: Benchmarking the Safety of Large Language Models for Robotic Health Attendant Control
outcome: Agent LLM execution of harmful actions outside its safe envelope in simulated robot control
effect: Mean violation rate 54.4% across 72 LLMs; device manipulation and emergency delay instructions harder to refuse than overtly destructive ones.
quote: The mean violation rate across all models was 54.4\%, with more than half exceeding 50\%, and violation rates varied substantially across behavior categories, with superficially plausible instructions such as device manipulation and emergency delay proving harder to refuse than overtly destructive ones.

title: Domain-Adapted Small Language Models for Reliable Clinical Triage
