outcome: ESI discordance and clinically significant errors after fine-tuning on institutional pediatric triage data vs baseline models
effect: Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B substantially reduced discordance and clinically significant errors, outperforming all baseline SLMs and GPT-4o (no numbers in abstract).
quote: Through large-scale domain adaptation using expert-curated and silver-standard pediatric triage data, fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B models substantially reduced discordance and clinically significant errors, outperforming all baseline SLMs and advanced proprietary large language models (LLMs, e.g., GPT-4o).

title: A Randomized Controlled Trial and Pilot of Scout: an LLM-Based EHR Search and Synthesis Platform
outcome: Whether manual review of sampled outputs corrects the automated LLM-as-judge error flags
effect: Manual review of a subset found that most claims the automated judge flagged as errors were supported by the patient chart, so human validation was needed to estimate real error rates.
quote: Subsequent manual review of a subset of outputs revealed that most claims flagged by the automated judge as errors were in fact supported by the patient chart, demonstrating the importance of human validation.

title: CareGuardAI: Context-Aware Multi-Agent Guardrails for Clinical Safety & Hallucination Mitigation in Patient-Facing LLMs
outcome: Safety and hallucination detection on PatientSafeBench, MedSafetyBench, and MedHallu with a pre-release risk gate versus baselines
effect: Framework releasing responses only when SRA and HRA are <=2 consistently outperformed strong baseline models including GPT-4o-mini; no numeric results in the abstract.
quote: Across these benchmarks, the framework consistently outperforms strong baseline models, including GPT-4o-mini, demonstrating the importance of context-aware, risk-based, inference-time safety mechanisms for reliable deployment in healthcare.

title: Fidelity, Diversity, and Privacy: A Multi-Dimensional LLM Evaluation for Clinical Data Augmentation
outcome: Privacy/plagiarism (memorization) of LLM-generated synthetic mental health reports
effect: All three models reportedly generated privacy-safe synthetic reports, with no compromise of patient confidentiality; no numeric results given in the abstract.
quote: The results demonstrate that all models can generate clinically coherent, diverse, and privacy-safe synthetic reports, significantly expanding the available training data for clinical natural language processing tasks without compromising patient confidentiality.

title: Persona-Grounded Safety Evaluation of AI Companions in Multi-Turn Conversations
outcome: Companion chatbot responses to high-risk personas in multi-turn scenarios (self-harm, disordered eating, violent fantasy)
effect: Replika frequently mirrored or normalized unsafe content such as self-harm, disordered eating, and violent-fantasy narratives across 1,674 dialogue pairs in 25 high-risk scenarios.
quote: Results show that Replika exhibits a narrow emotional range dominated by curiosity and care, while frequently mirroring or normalizing unsafe content such as self-harm, disordered eating, and violent-fantasy narratives.

title: When RAG Chatbots Expose Their Backend: An Anonymized Case Study of Privacy and Security Risks in Patient-Facing Medical AI
outcome: Unauthenticated access to chatbot backend configuration and patient conversation records
effect: Ordinary browser inspection exposed the system prompt, RAG configuration, API schema, knowledge base, and the 1,000 most recent patient-chatbot conversations, all retrievable without authentication.
quote: The deployment also contradicted its privacy assurances: full conversation records, including health-related queries, were retrievable without authentication.
sample_unit: publicly accessible patient-facing RAG chatbot deployments

title: When RAG Chatbots Expose Their Backend: An Anonymized Case Study of Privacy and Security Risks in Patient-Facing Medical AI
outcome: Privacy and security failures in a deployed patient-facing chatbot that went unidentified before deployment
effect: Serious privacy and security failures were identified with standard browser tools, without specialist skills or authentication; the authors conclude independent review should be a prerequisite for deployment.
quote: Serious privacy and security failures in patient-facing RAG chatbots can be identified with standard browser tools, without specialist skills or authentication; independent review should be a prerequisite for deployment.
sample_unit: publicly accessible patient-facing RAG chatbot deployments

title: CLEAR: Revealing How Noise and Ambiguity Degrade Reliability in LLMs for Medicine
outcome: LLM ability to abstain on incorrect answer options as answer space and abstention framing vary
effect: More plausible answers degraded correct-answer identification and abstention. Abstention worsened when framed as "I don't know". Including IDK alone increased incorrect selections. The humility deficit worsens with model scale.
quote: First, increasing the number of plausible answers degrades a model's ability to identify the correct answer and abstain against incorrect ones.
sample_unit: LLMs evaluated across three medical benchmarks

title: CLEAR: Revealing How Noise and Ambiguity Degrade Reliability in LLMs for Medicine
outcome: LLM reliability under perturbed answer-option count, abstention option presence, and semantic framing
effect: Perturbing the decision space degraded reliability. Adding an IDK option increased incorrect answer selections. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
quote: Notably, just including IDK in the answer space increases incorrect answer selections.
sample_unit: LLMs evaluated across three medical benchmarks

title: Compared to What? Baselines and Metrics for Counterfactual Prompting
outcome: LLM output changes under counterfactual patient demographic edits versus a paraphrase baseline
effect: MedQA gender-swap flip rate 14.9% vs paraphrase flip rate 14.1% (indistinguishable); MedPerturb demographic and style effects mostly vanish, with 5 of 120 tests significant after baseline correction.
quote: We find that these effects largely dissipate when we account for general model sensitivity, with only 5 of 120 tests reaching statistical significance.

title: Compared to What? Baselines and Metrics for Counterfactual Prompting
outcome: Prediction flips on medical QA under meaning-preserving paraphrase of inputs
effect: Paraphrasing inputs alone induced prediction flip rates of 14.1% on MedQA, similar to the 14.9% from changing patient gender.
quote: However, this is statistically indistinguishable from the flip rates induced by simply paraphrasing inputs (14.1%).

title: Teaching LLMs Brazilian Healthcare: Injecting Knowledge from Official Clinical Guidelines
outcome: LLM knowledge of official Brazilian clinical guideline content on true/false and open-ended questions
effect: Current LLMs perform poorly on guideline-specific knowledge; the adapted 14B model reached 83.9% on HealthBench-BR and 85.4% on PCDT-QA, outperforming GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and Google AI Overview.
quote: Yet current LLMs perform poorly on this guideline-specific knowledge, and no benchmark evaluates clinical recall grounded in Brazilian Portuguese protocols.
sample_unit: true/false clinical assertions (HealthBench-BR); plus 890 open-ended questions (PCDT-QA)

title: PhysicianBench: Evaluating LLM Agents in Real-World EHR Environments
outcome: Agent success rate on long-horizon EHR tasks requiring tool use, multi-step planning, and consequential actions
effect: Best model reached 46% pass@1; open-source models reached at most 19%, across 100 tasks averaging 27 tool calls.
quote: Across 13 proprietary and open-source LLM agents, the best-performing model achieves only 46% success rate (pass@1), while open-source models reach at most 19%, revealing a substantial gap between current agent capabilities and the demands of real-world clinical workflows.

title: SHIELD: A Diverse Clinical Note Dataset and Distilled Small Language Models for Enterprise-Scale De-identification
outcome: Span-level precision and recall of PHI de-identification against gold-standard annotations
effect: Best distilled model reached micro-averaged precision 0.89 and recall 0.88; macro-averaged per-category recall 0.81 vs 0.90 for the cloud teacher, so some PHI is missed.
quote: Our best distilled model reaches micro-averaged span-level precision of 0.89 and recall of 0.88 while running on standard workstation hardware.

title: SHIELD: A Diverse Clinical Note Dataset and Distilled Small Language Models for Enterprise-Scale De-identification
outcome: Cross-dataset generalization of de-identification models across institutions and PHI categories
effect: Diversity-trained models generalized well on universal structured PHI categories, but institution-specific entities remained hard to transfer in both directions.
quote: Cross-dataset evaluation shows that diversity-trained models generalize well on universal structured PHI categories, while institution-specific entities remain hard to transfer in both directions, which suggests pairing broad-coverage models with specialized models for high-volume, semi-structured note types.

title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Understand Pathologic Movements? A Pilot Study on Seizure Semiology
outcome: Zero-shot MLLM feature recognition versus fine-tuned CNN and ViT baselines on seizure videos
effect: MLLMs outperformed fine-tuned CNN and ViT baseline models on 13 of 18 features without task-specific training.
quote: MLLMs outperformed fine-tuned Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) baseline models on 13 of 18 features without task-specific training, demonstrating particular strength in recognizing salient postural and contextual features while struggling with subtle, high-frequency movements.

title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Understand Pathologic Movements? A Pilot Study on Seizure Semiology
outcome: Expert-rated faithfulness of MLLM-generated explanations for correctly predicted cases
effect: 94.3 percent of MLLM explanations for correctly predicted cases achieved at least 60 percent faithfulness scores, aligning with epileptologist reasoning.
quote: Expert evaluation showed that 94.3 percent of MLLM-generated explanations for correctly predicted cases achieved at least 60 percent faithfulness scores, aligning with epileptologist reasoning.

title: CuraView: A Multi-Agent Framework for Medical Hallucination Detection with GraphRAG-Enhanced Knowledge Verification
outcome: Sentence-level detection of faithfulness hallucinations in LLM-generated discharge summaries (F1, recall, precision)
effect: Fine-tuned Qwen3-14B detector: E4 F1 0.831 (90.9% recall, 76.5% precision); E3+E4 F1 0.823, a 50.0% relative improvement over base model and better than RAGTruth-style and QAGS-style baselines.
quote: Our fine-tuned Qwen3-14B detection model achieves an F1 of 0.831 on the safety-critical E4 metric (90.9% recall, 76.5% precision) and an F1 of 0.823 on E3+E4, representing a 50.0% relative improvement over the base model and outperforming RAGTruth-style and QAGS-style baselines.
sample_unit: patients (held-out test set from 250 patients in the Discharge-Me benchmark)

title: EQUITRIAGE: A Fairness Audit of Gender Bias in LLM-Based Emergency Department Triage
outcome: Change in ESI assignment under gender-swapped counterfactual vignettes (flip rate, F/M undertriage ratio)
effect: All five models exceeded the pre-registered 5% flip threshold (9.9% to 43.8%); DeepSeek F/M 2.15:1 and Gemini 1.34:1 directional female undertriage.
quote: All five models produced flip rates above a pre-registered 5% threshold (9.9% to 43.8%).

title: EQUITRIAGE: A Fairness Audit of Gender Bias in LLM-Based Emergency Department Triage
outcome: Subgroup-specific bias hidden from aggregate performance in LLM triage
effect: DeepSeek's directional bias coexisted with a low outcome-linked calibration gap (0.013), showing group calibration can mask counterfactual non-invariance.
quote: DeepSeek's directional bias coexisted with a low outcome-linked calibration gap (0.013 against MIMIC-IV admission), a Chouldechova-style dissociation between within-group calibration and between-pair counterfactual invariance.

title: EQUITRIAGE: A Fairness Audit of Gender Bias in LLM-Based Emergency Department Triage
outcome: Effect of demographic blinding on flip rate and directional bias
effect: Blinding reduced Gemini's flip rate to 0.5%; age-preserving blind variant left DeepSeek with residual F/M 1.25, so effectiveness was model-dependent.
quote: Demographic blinding reduced Gemini's flip rate to 0.5%; an age-preserving blind variant left DeepSeek with residual F/M 1.25, implicating age as a residual channel.

title: EQUITRIAGE: A Fairness Audit of Gender Bias in LLM-Based Emergency Department Triage
outcome: Accuracy of ESI assignment under chain-of-thought prompting versus other prompt strategies
effect: Chain-of-thought prompting degraded accuracy for all five models.
quote: Chain-of-thought prompting degraded accuracy for all five models.

title: Safety and accuracy follow different scaling laws in clinical large language models
outcome: Accuracy and safety errors with clean clinician-defined evidence versus closed-book prompting across 34 LLMs
effect: Mean accuracy rose from 73.5% to 94.1%; high-risk error fell from 12.0% to 2.6%; contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%; dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.
quote: Clean evidence produced the strongest improvement, increasing mean accuracy from 73.5% to 94.1%, while reducing high-risk error from 12.0% to 2.6%, contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%, and dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.

title: Safety and accuracy follow different scaling laws in clinical large language models
outcome: Safety of standard and agentic RAG retrieval grounding versus clean evidence
effect: Standard and agentic RAG did not reproduce clean-evidence safety; agentic RAG improved accuracy and reduced contradiction, but high-risk error and dangerous overconfidence remained elevated.
quote: Standard RAG and agentic RAG did not reproduce this safety profile: agentic RAG improved accuracy over standard RAG and reduced contradiction, but high-risk error and dangerous overconfidence remained elevated.

title: Safety and accuracy follow different scaling laws in clinical large language models
outcome: Rate of dangerous overconfidence in LLM answers across deployment conditions
effect: Dangerous overconfidence was 8.0% closed-book, falling to 1.6% with clean evidence, and remained elevated under standard and agentic RAG.
quote: Clean evidence produced the strongest improvement, increasing mean accuracy from 73.5% to 94.1%, while reducing high-risk error from 12.0% to 2.6%, contradiction from 12.7% to 2.3%, and dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%.

title: Are Multimodal LLMs Ready for Clinical Dermatology? A Real-World Evaluation in Dermatology
outcome: Top-3 diagnostic accuracy on public benchmarks versus real-world consultation cases
effect: Public benchmarks: top-3 accuracy 26.55% best open-weight, 42.25% GPT-4.1. Real-world images alone: 1.50%-13.35% open-weight, 24.65% GPT-4.1.
quote: These findings demonstrate that benchmark performance substantially overestimates the real-world clinical capability of current dermatology MLLMs.

title: Are Multimodal LLMs Ready for Clinical Dermatology? A Real-World Evaluation in Dermatology
outcome: Model output sensitivity to incomplete or erroneous consultation context
effect: Model outputs were highly sensitive to incomplete or erroneous consultation context, although adding clinical context raised top-3 accuracy up to 28.75% (open-weight) and 38.93% (GPT-4.1).
quote: However, model outputs were highly sensitive to incomplete or erroneous consultation context.

title: MedFabric: Gold Evidence Hides the Difficulty of Word-Level Medical Fabrication Detection
outcome: Accuracy of fabrication detectors (macro F1) across evidence conditions, including expert clinicians
effect: Expert clinicians reached 53.3% macro F1 and no detector family cleared about 60% without gold evidence. A strong LLM scored 91% with gold evidence and 35% with wrong evidence.
quote: On MedFabric the task is unsolved: expert clinicians reach only 53.3% macro F1 and no detector family clears about 60% without gold evidence.

title: MedFabric: Gold Evidence Hides the Difficulty of Word-Level Medical Fabrication Detection
outcome: Expert clinicians' ability to detect word-level medical fabrications (macro F1)
effect: Expert clinicians reached only 53.3% macro F1 detecting fabrications, so unverified fluent but wrong LLM statements may not be caught.
quote: On MedFabric the task is unsolved: expert clinicians reach only 53.3% macro F1 and no detector family clears about 60% without gold evidence.

title: Resolving the bias-precision paradox with stochastic causal representation learning for personalized medicine
outcome: Clinician decision accuracy and decision time with versus without AI support
effect: Clinician accuracy improved by 14.7% while decision time was reduced with the AI method.
quote: In human-AI evaluation, our method outperforms clinicians-in-training and large language models, and improves clinician accuracy by 14.7% while reducing decision time, enabling interpretable, real-time clinical decision support.

title: Resolving the bias-precision paradox with stochastic causal representation learning for personalized medicine
outcome: AI performance compared against clinicians-in-training and large language models
effect: The method outperformed clinicians-in-training and large language models in the human-AI evaluation.
quote: In human-AI evaluation, our method outperforms clinicians-in-training and large language models, and improves clinician accuracy by 14.7% while reducing decision time, enabling interpretable, real-time clinical decision support.

title: Systematic Evaluation of Large Language Models for Post-Discharge Clinical Action Extraction
outcome: Annotation inconsistencies in reference labels confounding interpretation of LLM errors
effect: Many failures stem from misalignment between model reasoning and dataset annotation conventions; labels without rationales cannot separate model reasoning failures from annotation mismatches.
quote: Labels without rationales make it impossible to distinguish clinical reasoning failures from annotation convention mismatches.

title: Research on Security Enhancement Methods for Adversarial Robust Large Language Model Intelligent Agents for Medical Decision-Making Tasks
outcome: Effect of removing evidence retrieval module on accuracy and attack success rate
effect: Removing evidence retrieval reduced accuracy by 9.1% and increased attack success rate by 11.1% in ablation.
quote: Ablation experiments quantify each module's contribution: removing risk perception, evidence retrieval, consistency verification, and confidence reweighting reduces accuracy by 6.7%, 9.1%, 7.6%, and 4.4%, respectively, and increases attack success rate by 13.8%, 11.1%, 8.6%, and 6.9%.

title: Research on Security Enhancement Methods for Adversarial Robust Large Language Model Intelligent Agents for Medical Decision-Making Tasks
outcome: Effect of removing input risk perception module on accuracy and attack success rate
effect: Removing risk perception reduced accuracy by 6.7% and increased attack success rate by 13.8% in ablation.
quote: Ablation experiments quantify each module's contribution: removing risk perception, evidence retrieval, consistency verification, and confidence reweighting reduces accuracy by 6.7%, 9.1%, 7.6%, and 4.4%, respectively, and increases attack success rate by 13.8%, 11.1%, 8.6%, and 6.9%.

title: Research on Security Enhancement Methods for Adversarial Robust Large Language Model Intelligent Agents for Medical Decision-Making Tasks
outcome: Attack success rate under prompt injection and other attacks versus baseline agents
effect: ARSM-Agent reduced overall attack success rate to 8.7% under semantic perturbation, prompt injection, drug-name confusion, and false-evidence attacks; knowledge consistency 0.91.
quote: Under semantic perturbation, prompt injection, drug-name confusion, and false-evidence attacks, ARSM-Agent reduces the overall attack success rate to 8.7% and achieves a knowledge consistency score of 0.91.

title: Can Language Models Identify Side Effects of Breast Cancer Radiation Treatments?
outcome: LLM side-effect list sensitivity to minor documentation changes in paired scenarios
effect: Across models, LLM outputs were sensitive to minor documentation changes, with precision-recall trade-offs and systematic under-recall of rare and long-term side effects.
quote: Across models, we reveal sensitivity to minor documentation changes, trade-offs between precision and recall, and systematic under-recall of rare and long-term side effects.
sample_unit: breast cancer patient profiles (paired scenarios differing in radiotherapy regimen)

title: Can Language Models Identify Side Effects of Breast Cancer Radiation Treatments?
outcome: Reliability and robustness of LLM side effect lists with grounding in clinician-curated lists
effect: Grounding outputs in clinician-curated side effect lists substantially improved reliability and robustness; numeric constraints alone reduced precision (no numbers in abstract).
quote: When used alone, constraints on the number of side effects generated reduce precision, and grounding outputs in clinician-curated side effect lists substantially improves reliability and robustness.
sample_unit: breast cancer patient profiles (paired scenarios differing in radiotherapy regimen)

title: EpiGraph: Building Generalists for Evidence-Intensive Epilepsy Reasoning in the Wild
outcome: LLM performance on five epilepsy tasks with vs without Graph-RAG grounding in the knowledge graph
effect: Graph-RAG consistently improved performance across all tasks for six LLMs, with the largest gains in pharmacogenomic reasoning (+30-41%).
quote: Results show that integrating \textsc{EpiGraph} consistently improves performance across all tasks, with the largest gains observed in pharmacogenomic reasoning (+30--41\%).

title: Can We Trust LLMs for Mental Health Screening? Consistency, ASR Robustness, and Evidence Faithfulness
outcome: Intra-model score consistency across repeated runs and under ASR transcription noise
effect: Phi-4 and Gemma-2-9B ICC > 0.89 with minimal degradation under ASR; Llama-3.1-8B ICC dropped from 0.82 to 0.36 at 10% WER.
quote: Llama-3.1-8B shows ASR-fragile consistency, with ICC dropping from 0.82 to 0.36 at 10% WER

title: MedMeta: A Benchmark for LLMs in Synthesizing Meta-Analysis Conclusion from Medical Studies
outcome: Meta-analysis conclusion quality with ground-truth retrieved abstracts (Golden-RAG) versus parametric-only generation
effect: Golden-RAG consistently and significantly outperformed Parametric-only across models; domain-specific fine-tuning benefits were marginal and neutralized when external material was provided. Best scores were only ~2.7/5.0.
quote: Our findings underscore the critical importance of information grounding: the Golden-RAG workflow consistently and significantly outperforms the Parametric-only approach across models.

title: MedMeta: A Benchmark for LLMs in Synthesizing Meta-Analysis Conclusion from Medical Studies
outcome: Whether models identify and reject negated evidence in stress tests
effect: All models, regardless of architecture, failed to identify and reject negated evidence, described as a critical vulnerability in current RAG systems.
quote: Furthermore, stress tests show that all models, regardless of architecture, fail to identify and reject negated evidence, highlighting a critical vulnerability in current RAG systems.

title: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Medical Multi-Modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
outcome: Vulnerability of medical multimodal RAG to knowledge poisoning attacks producing incorrect diagnostic outputs
effect: The M3Att attack, using imperceptible image perturbations and covert misinformation, consistently produced clinically plausible but incorrect generations across five LLMs and datasets. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
quote: Experiments on five LLMs and datasets demonstrate that M\textsuperscript{3}Att consistently produces clinically plausible yet incorrect generations.

title: ClinicalBench: Stress-Testing Assertion-Aware Retrieval for Cross-Admission Clinical QA on MIMIC-IV
outcome: Share of auto-generated reference answers judged defective by physician adjudication
effect: Physicians identified 56 percent of auto-generated reference answers as defective; NLP-pipeline clinical-QA benchmarks need physician adjudication to be usable.
quote: Physician adjudication identified 56 percent of auto-generated reference answers as defective, a methodological finding indicating that NLP-pipeline clinical-QA benchmarks require physician adjudication to be usable.

title: ClinicalBench: Stress-Testing Assertion-Aware Retrieval for Cross-Admission Clinical QA on MIMIC-IV
outcome: Accuracy of assertion-aware knowledge-graph retrieval grounding versus LLM-alone baseline on clinical QA
effect: Author-blind primary endpoint +22.0 percentage points (95% Newcombe CI +5.1 to +31.5, p=0.0192); intent-aware KG-RAG over dense-RAG baseline +8.84 pp (p=1.79e-3).
quote: The author-blind primary endpoint, leave-author-out paired exact McNemar on 50 unanimous-strict items rated by two external physicians, yields +22.0 percentage points (95 percent Newcombe CI [+5.1, +31.5], p=0.0192).

title: Checkup2Action: A Multimodal Clinical Check-up Report Dataset for Patient-Oriented Action Card Generation
outcome: Problem recall and diagnostic overstatement with versus without safety constraints
effect: Removing safety constraints raised problem recall from 0.527 to 0.825 but produced more diagnostic overstatement, so the constraints trade coverage for safer patient communication.
quote: Removing safety constraints increased problem recall from 0.527 to 0.825, but produced more diagnostic overstatement.

title: Reconstruction of Personally Identifiable Information from Proprietary Data in Supervised Fine-Tuned Models
outcome: Targeted PII reconstruction from LLMs fine-tuned on small proprietary medical and legal SFT data
effect: COVA consistently improves PII reconstruction over baseline decoding methods across datasets. Even limited contextual knowledge about a target user substantially increases adversary success.
quote: Our findings demonstrate that small, proprietary SFT datasets can induce meaningful privacy leakage through the reconstruction of target-PII associations learned during fine-tuning.
sample_unit: synthetic multi-turn Q&A datasets (medical and legal)

title: Large Language Models Lack Temporal Awareness of Medical Knowledge
outcome: LLM accuracy on time-specific guideline knowledge, current versus historical recommendations
effect: Accuracy on up-to-date knowledge declines linearly over time. Historical knowledge accuracy is only 25.37%-53.89% of up-to-date knowledge. Predictions fluctuate across neighboring years.
quote: LLMs consistently struggle more with recalling outdated historical medical knowledge than with up-to-date recommendations: accuracy of historical knowledge is only 25.37%-53.89% of up-to-date knowledge

title: Large Language Models Lack Temporal Awareness of Medical Knowledge
outcome: Effect of agentic search tool integration on temporal awareness accuracy
effect: Agentic search did not easily solve the temporal awareness problem; accuracy changes ranged from -3.15% to 14.14%.
quote: We also show that the temporal awareness problem is a challenge that cannot be easily solved when integrated with agentic search tools (-3.15%-14.14%).

title: ProtoMedAgent: Multimodal Clinical Interpretability via Privacy-Aware Agentic Workflows
outcome: Comparison Set Faithfulness of generated reports, constrained framework versus standard RAG
effect: ProtoMedAgent achieved 91.2% Comparison Set Faithfulness versus 46.2% for standard RAG.
quote: Evaluated on a 4,160-patient clinical cohort, ProtoMedAgent achieves 91.2% Comparison Set Faithfulness where it fundamentally outperforms standard RAG (46.2%).

title: ProtoMedAgent: Multimodal Clinical Interpretability via Privacy-Aware Agentic Workflows
outcome: Artifact-level membership inference risk with the semantic privacy gate
effect: The l-diversity phase transition reduced artifact-level membership inference risk by an absolute 9.8%.
quote: ProtoMedAgent additionally leverages a binding $\ell$-diversity phase transition to systematically reduce artifact-level membership inference risks by an absolute 9.8%.

title: Quantifying and Mitigating Premature Closure in Frontier LLMs
outcome: Rate of selecting an answer when the correct choice was removed (false-action rate)
effect: Baseline false-action rates were 55-81% on MedQA (n=500) and 53-82% on AfriMed-QA (n=490). Open-ended inappropriate answers averaged 30% of 861 HealthBench questions and 78% of 191 adversarial queries.
quote: In MedQA (n = 500) and AfriMed-QA (n = 490) questions where the correct choice had been removed, models still selected an answer at high rates, with baseline false-action rates of 55-81% and 53-82%, respectively.
sample_unit: questions (MedQA n=500; AfriMed-QA n=490; HealthBench n=861; adversarial queries n=191)

title: Quantifying and Mitigating Premature Closure in Frontier LLMs
outcome: Inappropriate commitment when the safer response was clarification, abstention, escalation, or refusal
effect: Models gave inappropriate answers on an average of 30% of 861 HealthBench questions and 78% of 191 physician-authored adversarial queries; residual failure persisted after safety prompting.
quote: In open-ended evaluation, models gave inappropriate answers on an average of 30% of 861 HealthBench questions and 78% of 191 physician-authored adversarial queries.
sample_unit: questions (MedQA n=500; AfriMed-QA n=490; HealthBench n=861; adversarial queries n=191)

title: When AI Tells You What You Want to Hear: Sycophantic Behavior of Large Language Models in Dementia Care Settings
outcome: Response quality change across prompts with increasing confirmatory and authority framing in dementia care
effect: All four LLMs showed negative Spearman correlations between prompt level and quality (rho -0.543 to -0.734, all p<0.01); Mistral Large mean score fell from 6.0/7 at P1 to 0.2/7 at P5.
quote: All models showed significant negative Spearman correlations between prompt level and response quality (rho ranging from -0.543 to -0.734, all p < 0.01).

title: Artificial Intolerance: Stigmatizing Language in Clinical Documentation Skews Large Language Model Decision-Making
outcome: Model output sensitivity to subtle linguistic variation in clinical text
effect: A single stigmatizing sentence was sufficient to alter model outputs, showing a clear dose-response relationship.
quote: Notably, we observe a high sensitivity to linguistic framing, where a single SL sentence is sufficient to alter model outputs, revealing a clear dose-response relationship.

title: Artificial Intolerance: Stigmatizing Language in Clinical Documentation Skews Large Language Model Decision-Making
outcome: Bias in clinical management decisions
effect: Across nine frontier LLMs and four stigmatized medical conditions, all evaluated models showed substantial bias toward less aggressive patient management.
quote: Our results demonstrate that all evaluated models exhibit substantial bias, with clinical decision-making significantly skewed towards less aggressive patient management.

title: What Does the AI Doctor Value? Auditing Pluralism in the Clinical Ethics of Language Models
outcome: Decision consistency across repeated sampling and semantic variations of dilemma prompts
effect: Individual model decisions were near-deterministic across repeated sampling and semantic variations, so no brittleness or nondeterminism. The consistency failed to reproduce the physician panel's distributional pluralism.
quote: However, individual model decisions are near-deterministic across repeated sampling and semantic variations, failing to reproduce the distributional pluralism of the physician panel.

title: Evaluating the Utility of Personal Health Records in Personalized Health AI
outcome: Answer helpfulness with vs without PHR context provided to the LLM
effect: Significant improvements in helpfulness for all question types with PHR data (p < 0.001, paired t-test); potential gains in safety, accuracy, relevance and personalization.
quote: We see significant improvements in the helpfulness of answers to all question types with PHR data (p < 0.001, paired t-test).

title: Prompting language influences diagnostic reasoning and accuracy of large language models
outcome: Diagnostic reasoning and accuracy of LLMs compared between English and French prompts
effect: Four of five models performed better in English (mean difference 0.37-0.91, adjusted p < 0.05); o3 showed no overall language effect.
quote: Four of the five models performed better in English (mean difference 0.37-0.91, adjusted p < 0.05), with the gap spanning multiple aspects of reasoning, including differential diagnosis, logical structure, and internal validity.

title: GrandGuard: Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Safeguards for Elderly-Chatbot Interaction Safety
outcome: Unsafe-prompt detection accuracy of safeguard models for elderly-specific risks
effect: Fine-tuned Llama-Guard-3 reached up to 96.2% and policy-enhanced gpt-oss-safeguard-20b up to 90.9% unsafe-prompt detection accuracy.
quote: We mitigate these failures with two safeguards: a fine-tuned Llama-Guard-3 and a policy-enhanced gpt-oss-safeguard-20b, achieving up to 96.2% and 90.9% unsafe-prompt detection accuracy, respectively.

title: Do No Harm? Hallucination and Actor-Level Abuse in Web-Deployed Medical Large Language Models
outcome: Factual accuracy and hallucination of web-deployed medical GPTs
effect: 25-30% of MedGPTs exhibit low factual accuracy, with bottom- and middle-tier models at highest risk; 33.6-54.3% violate operational thresholds.
quote: Our results show that 25-30% of MedGPTs exhibit low factual accuracy, with bottom- and middle-tier models at highest risk; 33.6-54.3% violate operational thresholds, and 57.06% of Action-enabled models lack adequate privacy disclosures.
sample_unit: MedGPTs (custom medical GPTs, stratified sample from 6,233)

title: Do No Harm? Hallucination and Actor-Level Abuse in Web-Deployed Medical Large Language Models
outcome: Adequacy of privacy disclosures among Action-enabled MedGPTs
effect: 57.06% of Action-enabled models lack adequate privacy disclosures.
quote: Our results show that 25-30% of MedGPTs exhibit low factual accuracy, with bottom- and middle-tier models at highest risk; 33.6-54.3% violate operational thresholds, and 57.06% of Action-enabled models lack adequate privacy disclosures.
sample_unit: MedGPTs (custom medical GPTs, stratified sample from 6,233)

title: GraphRAG on Consumer Hardware: Benchmarking Local LLMs for Healthcare EHR Schema Retrieval
outcome: Hallucination and factual grounding under global versus local GraphRAG retrieval modes
effect: Local retrieval outperformed global summarization in latency and factual grounding with reduced hallucination; best answer quality was 3.3/5 (Qwen 2.5); Mistral showed degenerate repetition.
quote: In addition, indexing and answer quality are decoupled across models, and local retrieval consistently outperforms global summarization in both latency and factual grounding, with reduced hallucination.

title: HealthCraft: A Reinforcement Learning Safety Environment for Emergency Medicine
outcome: Agent performance on multi-step emergency medicine workflows with tool use
effect: Multi-step workflow performance collapsed to near zero (Claude 1.0%, GPT-5.4 0.0%) despite partial competence on individual steps; safety-failure rates were 27.5% and 34.0% overall.
quote: On multi-step workflows - the closest proxy to real emergency care - performance collapses to near zero (Claude 1.0%, GPT-5.4 0.0%) despite partial competence on individual steps.

title: What Users Cannot See: Evaluating LLM Emotional Support Beyond User Preference
outcome: Language/appraisal appropriateness of LLM emotional-support responses by persona (Soothe, Reframe, Endorse)
effect: Friend prompting increased Endorse and reduced Reframe; therapist prompting did the reverse; both increased Soothe relative to default. Lay raters detected only 60% of expert-confirmed Endorse instances.
quote: friend prompting increased Endorse and reduced Reframe, a pattern that could reinforce users' existing appraisals and plausibly contribute to escalation risk, whereas therapist prompting did the reverse.

title: What Users Cannot See: Evaluating LLM Emotional Support Beyond User Preference
outcome: lay detection of problematic endorsement
effect: Lay raters detected only 60% of expert-confirmed Endorse instances and rated personas similarly helpful and desirable.
quote: Two independent LLM judges substantially agreed with clinically trained raters, yet lay raters detected only 60% of expert-confirmed Endorse instances and rated the personas similarly helpful and desirable.

title: When Cases Get Rare: A Retrieval Benchmark for Off-Guideline Clinical Question Answering
outcome: Correct answer rate on off-guideline clinical questions with vs without retrieved medical articles
effect: Best baseline GPT-5.2 answered 56% correctly and specialized models reached 42%; retrieval augmentation improved performance to up to 82% (GPT-5.2).
quote: Augmenting models with retrieved medical articles improves this performance to up to 82% (using GPT-5.2) highlighting the importance of evidence-grounding for real-world medical reasoning tasks.

title: Active Evidence-Seeking and Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models for Clinical Decision Support
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and evidence quality, multi-turn evidence seeking versus static full-context evaluation
effect: Multi-turn evidence seeking reduced diagnostic accuracy by 12.75% and supporting-evidence quality by 24.36% relative to full-context evaluation across 468 cases and 15 models.
quote: Together, these results suggest that static full-context benchmarks may overestimate performance in interactive evidence-seeking settings, motivating complementary interactive assessment for safer clinical decision support.

title: Active Evidence-Seeking and Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models for Clinical Decision Support
outcome: Gap between static benchmark performance and interactive diagnostic inquiry performance
effect: Diagnostic accuracy fell 12.75% and supporting-evidence quality fell 24.36% under multi-turn evidence seeking versus full-context evaluation; errors linked to premature diagnostic closure and inefficient questioning.
quote: Across 468 cases and 15 models in our protocol, we observe that multi-turn evidence seeking reduces diagnostic accuracy by 12.75% and lowers supporting-evidence quality by 24.36% relative to full-context evaluation; error analyses associate these drops with premature diagnostic closure and inefficient questioning.

title: When Symptoms Are Not Enough: Evidence-Weighting Patterns in Large Language Model Psychiatric Screening
outcome: LLM psychiatric classification accuracy across sex, age, and race subgroups
effect: Higher depression-classification accuracy among male than female participants, no consistent age-related pattern, and modest non-uniform variation across race strata.
quote: Subgroup analyses found higher depression-classification accuracy among male than female participants, no consistent age-related pattern, and modest non-uniform variation across race strata.

title: IyàwóBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Model Clinical Triage Accuracy on Undifferentiated Febrile Illness in Nigerian Primary Health Settings
outcome: Missed escalation: critical REFER NOW cases downgraded to TREAT HERE (safety score)
effect: All six models achieved 100% safety scores (95% CI 96.4-100.0%); no critical REFER NOW case was downgraded to TREAT HERE.
quote: All six models achieved 100% safety scores (95% CI: 96.4-100.0%), never downgrading a critical REFER NOW case to TREAT HERE.

title: IyàwóBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Model Clinical Triage Accuracy on Undifferentiated Febrile Illness in Nigerian Primary Health Settings
outcome: Triage accuracy of guideline-embedded systems versus general-purpose models
effect: Clinically engineered systems with embedded WHO guidelines outperformed general-purpose models by up to 28.5 percentage points in triage accuracy.
quote: Clinically engineered systems with embedded WHO guidelines outperform general-purpose models by up to 28.5 percentage points.

title: When Correct Beliefs Collapse: Epistemic Resilience of LLMs under Clinical Pressure
outcome: Belief stability of correct diagnoses under escalating multi-turn pressure across nine LLMs
effect: High initial diagnostic capability did not imply high belief stability, yielding large knowledge-robustness gaps for several LLMs.
quote: Across nine frontier large language models (LLMs), we find a clear dissociation between medical knowledge and robustness: high initial diagnostic capability does not imply high belief stability, yielding large knowledge-robustness gaps for several LLMs.

title: When Correct Beliefs Collapse: Epistemic Resilience of LLMs under Clinical Pressure
outcome: Gap between medical benchmark accuracy and belief robustness in clinical dialogue
effect: Despite strong medical benchmark accuracy, LLMs showed severe multi-turn sycophancy, abandoning initially correct diagnoses under escalating pressure.
quote: Despite strong medical benchmark accuracy, LLMs can exhibit severe multi-turn sycophancy in clinical dialogue, abandoning initial correct diagnosis under escalating pressure.

title: A Multi-Probe Audit of Clinical-Interview Depression Detection Benchmarks
outcome: Performance of near-ceiling in-domain baselines on external corpora
effect: CMDC and ANDROIDS baselines with near-ceiling in-domain performance showed substantially weaker zero-shot transfer to external corpora; E-DAIC CV and official-test rankings aligned only moderately.
quote: Zero-shot transfer to external corpora is substantially weaker.

title: GlobalDentBench: A Multinational Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Clinical Reasoning in Dentistry with Expert Calibration
outcome: LLM accuracy across question formats and reasoning levels on a dental benchmark
effect: Accuracy fell from 81.34% on multiple-choice to 64.53% on short-answer and 22.34% on case-based questions; from 74.01% at L1 to 55.64% at L2 and 35.71% at L3.
quote: Specifically, accuracy plummeted from 81.34% on multiple-choice to 64.53% on short-answer and 22.34% on case-based questions, while declining markedly from 74.01% at L1 to 55.64% at L2 and 35.71% at L3.

title: GlobalDentBench: A Multinational Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Clinical Reasoning in Dentistry with Expert Calibration
outcome: Safety of LLM-generated clinical recommendations in real-world dental cases
effect: Overall unsafe rate of 31.01% in LLM-generated clinical recommendations, with 4.51% posing risks of irreversible patient harm, particularly in orthodontics.
quote: More critically, risk analysis of real-world dental cases demonstrated an alarming overall unsafe rate of 31.01% in LLM-generated clinical recommendations, with 4.51% posing risks of irreversible patient harm and risks particularly pronounced in specialties such as orthodontics.

title: When Reasoning Hurts: Source-Aware Evaluation of Frontier LLMs for Clinical SOAP Note Generation
outcome: Whether reasoning benchmark gains transfer to SOAP note generation quality across three datasets
effect: Enabling reasoning significantly degraded GPT-5.4 performance across all three datasets; non-reasoning GPT-5.4 scored highest overall, so benchmark reasoning strength did not predict task quality.
quote: Overall, the findings indicate that stronger reasoning capability should not be assumed to improve fidelity-sensitive SOAP note generation without dedicated, task-specific evaluation.

title: A Dataset of Robot-Patient and Doctor-Patient Medical Dialogues for Spoken Language Processing Tasks
outcome: LLM confidence calibration when selecting sentences in medical dialogues
effect: All three LLMs were highly overconfident in probabilistic predictions whether correct or incorrect; best accuracy was Claude Sonnet 4 at 71.1% (manual transcripts) and 74.7% (automatic transcripts).
quote: Experimental results reveal that Claude Sonnet 4 is the best in sentence selection, with 71.1% accuracy using manual transcriptions and 74.7% using automatic transcriptions, and that all LLMs are highly overconfident in their probabilistic predictions, regardless of selecting correct or incorrect sentences in medical dialogues.
sample_unit: hours of speech data (robot-patient and doctor-patient dialogues)

title: Neuro-Symbolic Verification of LLM Outputs for Data-Sensitive Domains (extended preprint)
outcome: Hallucination detection rates of automated verification on LLM-generated report outputs
effect: Hallucination detection rates over 83% for structured entities and 72% for semantic fabrications; 30% reduction in report creation time
quote: Evaluation shows hallucination detection rates of over 83% for structured entities and 72% for semantic fabrications, with a 30% reduction in report creation time, demonstrating that neuro-symbolic architectures can provide principled safeguards for LLM deployment in data-sensitive domains.

title: MIRA: A Bilingual Benchmark for Medical Information Response Audit
outcome: Consistency of LLM responses across equivalent prompts varying in health literacy signals
effect: Responses to low health-literacy signals consistently omitted more key information, gave fewer concrete next steps, and offered less support for independent judgment across five LLMs.
quote: Across five mainstream LLMs, models answered all medical questions, but responses to low health-literacy signals consistently omitted more key information, provided fewer concrete next steps, and offered less support for independent judgment.

title: MIRA: A Bilingual Benchmark for Medical Information Response Audit
outcome: Information completeness of generative AI responses for users with low health literacy signals
effect: Low health-literacy signals led to more omitted key information and fewer concrete next steps, termed Differential Information Dilution (DID).
quote: We term this pattern Differential Information Dilution (DID).

title: Better Accuracies, Worse Reasoning: A Step-Level Audit of Medical Chain-of-Thought Distillation
outcome: Medical QA benchmark answer metrics versus step-level factuality of reasoning traces after CoT distillation
effect: MedQA-USMLE SC@64 rose 74.7% to 84.4% and ECE fell 0.096 to 0.034, while step error rate rose from 30.6% to 50.3% under an LLM-judge audit.
quote: Yet under a Kimi-K2.6 style-blind LLM-judge audit, its error rate over non-abstained steps rises from 30.6% to 50.3%.
sample_unit: reasoning steps (plus 150 steps in clinical expert audit)

title: Not All Uncertainty Is Equal: How Uncertainty Granularity Shapes Human Verification in LLM-Assisted Decision Making
outcome: User agreement, confidence, and verification behavior under output-, relation-, and token-level uncertainty displays
effect: Token-level uncertainty increased agreement with the AI; output- and relation-level did not increase agreement but reduced users' confidence in own answers; relation-level also reduced external verification.
quote: Token-level uncertainty increased users' agreement with the AI, whereas output- and relation-level uncertainty did not increase agreement but instead reduced users' confidence in their own answers.

title: Not All Uncertainty Is Equal: How Uncertainty Granularity Shapes Human Verification in LLM-Assisted Decision Making
outcome: Effect of displayed uncertainty at different granularities on user reliance and verification
effect: Relation-level uncertainty reduced external verification (internet searches, checking URLs), steering users toward reliance on the LLM and its uncertainty cues; token-level increased agreement.
quote: Notably, relation-level uncertainty also reduced external verification (i.e., internet searches, checking provided URLs), steering users away from independent fact-checking and toward reliance on the LLM and its accompanying uncertainty cues.

title: Not All Uncertainty Is Equal: How Uncertainty Granularity Shapes Human Verification in LLM-Assisted Decision Making
outcome: Whether uncertainty display design promotes user verification of LLM outputs
effect: Uncertainty granularity shaped verification: relation-level reduced external verification, token-level increased agreement, output-level reduced self-confidence without more agreement.
quote: Our findings demonstrate that uncertainty granularity significantly shapes how users interact with and verify LLM outputs, providing concrete design guidance for building responsible LLM applications that encourage appropriate skepticism and verification behaviors.

title: Not All Uncertainty Is Equal: How Uncertainty Granularity Shapes Human Verification in LLM-Assisted Decision Making
outcome: external verification
effect: No effect sizes reported; relation-level uncertainty reduced internet searches and URL checking, shifting users toward LLM reliance.
quote: Notably, relation-level uncertainty also reduced external verification (i.e., internet searches, checking provided URLs), steering users away from independent fact-checking and toward reliance on the LLM and its accompanying uncertainty cues.

title: GRASP: Gated Regression-Aware Skill Proposer for Self-Improving LLM Agents
outcome: Agent success when each skill-library update is validated by a gate versus unvalidated skill writing
effect: On MedAgentBench GRASP lifted gpt-oss-120b from 40.6% to 88.8%. Skill writing without validation was no better than using no skills. Adding the same gate to five baselines lifted each in-domain.
quote: Ablations attribute the gain to comparative proposal generation, the acceptance gate, and the hard regression budget rather than to skill writing itself, which without validation is no better than using no skills.

title: MedCase-Structured: A Text-to-FHIR Dataset for Benchmarking Diagnostic Reasoning in Clinically Realistic EHR Settings
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy on structured FHIR inputs versus plain-text inputs
effect: LLMs showed consistently lower diagnostic accuracy on structured FHIR inputs than on plain text. Specific accuracy numbers are not given in the abstract.
quote: Evaluation on MedCase-Structured reveals consistently lower diagnostic accuracy for LLMs on structured FHIR inputs than with plain text, highlighting the importance of deployment-aligned benchmarking.
sample_unit: synthetic FHIR bundles derived from clinician-authored diagnostic cases

title: Same Patient, Different Words, Different Diagnosis? Evaluating Semantic Stability in Clinical LLMs
outcome: Robustness of general-purpose vs medical LLMs to meaning-preserving prompt reformulations on DiagnosisQA and MedQA
effect: Robustness differences between domain-specific and general-purpose models were mixed and model-dependent; some DS models were among the most robust, and strong GP baselines stayed competitive. Sensitivity to rephrasing is described as a risk.
quote: Our results demonstrate that robustness differences between domain-specific (DS) models are mixed and highly model-dependent, i.e., domain specialization does not consistently improve or reduce robustness to meaning-preserving prompt reformulations.

title: Reliable Multilingual Orthopedic Decision Support from Clinical Narratives: Language-Aware Adaptation and Verification-Guided Deferral
outcome: Selective accuracy and Macro-F1 with deferral versus accept-all prediction
effect: Selective verification achieved 84.4% selective accuracy and 0.76 Macro-F1 at 72.3% coverage, versus 71.5% accuracy and 0.65 Macro-F1 for accept-all.
quote: On a randomly selected held-out 5,000-record subset, it achieves 84.4% selective accuracy and 0.76 selective Macro-F1 at 72.3% coverage, compared with 71.5% accuracy and 0.65 Macro-F1 for accept-all prediction.

title: Reliable Multilingual Orthopedic Decision Support from Clinical Narratives: Language-Aware Adaptation and Verification-Guided Deferral
outcome: Comparison of zero-shot LLMs against task-adapted encoders on same data
effect: Zero-shot LLMs were substantially less effective than task-adapted encoders for closed-set classification, with language-dependent instability; IndicBERT-HPA Macro-F1 0.8792.
quote: The evaluated zero-shot LLMs remain substantially less effective than task-adapted encoders for closed-set classification, with language-dependent instability.

title: A Multi-Domain Red Teaming Framework for Safety, Robustness, and Fairness Evaluation of Medical Large Language Models
outcome: Change in LLM error rates on equity tasks when demographic attributes were modified
effect: Equity-related tasks showed 10-20% error amplification with demographic modifications.
quote: Equity-related tasks showed 10-20% error amplification with demographic modifications, and human reviewers identified clinically relevant failures missed by automated evaluation.

title: A Multi-Domain Red Teaming Framework for Safety, Robustness, and Fairness Evaluation of Medical Large Language Models
outcome: Whether human clinician review catches failures missed by automated evaluation of LLM outputs
effect: Human reviewers identified clinically relevant failures missed by automated evaluation; hybrid evaluation combining automation with clinician oversight is described as essential.
quote: Equity-related tasks showed 10-20% error amplification with demographic modifications, and human reviewers identified clinically relevant failures missed by automated evaluation.

title: Structured Visual Evidence Decomposition for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Screening of Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome
outcome: Effect of seven-question visual decomposition and balanced adjudication ablations on screening performance
effect: Ablations showed that seven-question visual decomposition and balanced final adjudication were critical to the high-sensitivity operating point; the full framework outperformed clinical-only, direct multimodal, and naive two-stage pipelines.
quote: Ablations showed that seven-question visual decomposition and balanced final adjudication were critical to the high-sensitivity operating point.

title: Structured Visual Evidence Decomposition for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Screening of Obstructive Sleep Apnea-Hypopnea Syndrome
outcome: Comparison of EviOSAHS against alternative prompting pipelines on same cohort and protocol
effect: EviOSAHS achieved 88.47% accuracy, 94.86% sensitivity, 93.74% F1-score, and 5.14% false-negative rate, outperforming clinical-only prompting, direct multimodal prompting, and naive two-stage pipelines under a unified protocol.
quote: EviOSAHS achieved 88.47% accuracy, 94.86% sensitivity, 93.74% F1-score, and a 5.14% false-negative rate, outperforming clinical-only prompting, direct multimodal prompting, and naive two-stage pipelines under a unified protocol.

title: CardioLens: Revealing the Clinical Reality Gap of MLLMs via Multi-Sequence Cardiac MRI Evaluations
outcome: MLLM performance on multi-sequence CMR image understanding, report generation, and diagnosis versus public benchmark performance
effect: Models perform poorly overall, with performance degrading along the real CMR workflow, despite strong performance on public medical benchmarks.
quote: Across 24 state-of-the-art MLLMs, CardioLens reveals a substantial clinical reality gap: models perform poorly overall, with performance degrading along the real CMR workflow.

title: CardioLens: Revealing the Clinical Reality Gap of MLLMs via Multi-Sequence Cardiac MRI Evaluations
outcome: Sensitivity of MLLM performance to input slice selection protocols and slice budgets
effect: Comparing random, clinically motivated, and data-driven slice selection under different slice budgets, performance changed only marginally, typically by about 1%.
quote: To rule out MLLM-compatible input construction as the primary cause, we compare random, clinically motivated, and data-driven slice selection protocols under different slice budgets; performance changes only marginally, typically by about 1%.

title: Lost in Delusion: Examining LLM Safety Under User Delusions and Distress
outcome: Timely escalation of safety-critical distress in multi-turn conversations
effect: Safety interventions were suppressed by up to 4.5x under delusional framing despite comparable distress detection.
quote: This reveals a recognition-intervention gap: models detect distress at comparable rates regardless of framing, yet sharply fail to act on it once distress is embedded in delusion, with safety interventions suppressed by up to 4.5x.

title: Lost in Delusion: Examining LLM Safety Under User Delusions and Distress
outcome: Failure to act on user distress in chatbot conversations with delusional framing
effect: Models fail to act on recognized distress when it is embedded in delusion, with safety interventions suppressed by up to 4.5x.
quote: This reveals a recognition-intervention gap: models detect distress at comparable rates regardless of framing, yet sharply fail to act on it once distress is embedded in delusion, with safety interventions suppressed by up to 4.5x.

title: Lost in Delusion: Examining LLM Safety Under User Delusions and Distress
outcome: distress recognition and action under delusional framing
effect: Models detected distress at comparable rates but failed to act; safety interventions were suppressed by up to 4.5x.
quote: This reveals a recognition-intervention gap: models detect distress at comparable rates regardless of framing, yet sharply fail to act on it once distress is embedded in delusion, with safety interventions suppressed by up to 4.5x.

title: Lost in Delusion: Examining LLM Safety Under User Delusions and Distress
outcome: therapeutic appropriateness with delusional premises
effect: Failure tracked accumulated acceptance of users' premises rather than emotional validation.
quote: The failure tracks accumulated acceptance of the user's premises rather than emotional validation.

title: Implicit Geographic Inference in LLM Medical Triage: Language-Driven Disparities in Emergency Recommendations
outcome: Rate of ER recommendations for identical neurological symptoms across prompt languages
effect: ER recommendation rates ranged from 0% (Japanese, Hindi) to 30% (English, Arabic) despite near-identical severity scores (7.7-8.0/10).
quote: We find that the model recommends emergency room visits at rates ranging from 0% (Japanese, Hindi) to 30% (English, Arabic), despite assigning nearly identical severity scores (7.7-8.0/10) across all languages.
country: Not applicable (simulated prompts in six languages; US and Tokyo locations tested)

title: Implicit Geographic Inference in LLM Medical Triage: Language-Driven Disparities in Emergency Recommendations
outcome: Change in ER recommendations when only prompt language or location attribute varied
effect: A US location sentence raised ER recommendations by up to 76.7 percentage points for non-English prompts; English prompt with Tokyo location cut ER rate from 30% to 6.7%.
quote: Adding a single sentence specifying the patient's US location increases ER recommendations by up to 76.7 percentage points for non-English prompts, while the reverse anchor (English prompt with a Tokyo location) reduces the ER rate from 30% to 6.7%.
country: Not applicable (simulated prompts in six languages; US and Tokyo locations tested)

title: Med-HEAL: Analyzing and Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical LLMs with Hallucination-Aware In-Context Learning
outcome: Accuracy change from model self-critique and regeneration of flagged answers on clinical QA
effect: Self-critique pipeline improved accuracy for three of five open-source LLMs (p < 0.05) without parameter updates; no significant improvement for the other two.
quote: Experiments across five open-source LLMs-BioMistral, Llama-3.1, DeepSeek, Qwen2.5, and Qwen3, show that the self-critique strategy improves accuracy for three of five models (p < 0.05) without requiring parameter updates.
sample_unit: open-ended clinical questions (EHRNoteQA, MIMIC-IV discharge summaries)

title: DrugClaw and DrugAudit: A Primary-Source-Grounded Agent and Authority-Aware Benchmark for Drug-Information Question Answering
outcome: Primary-source rate and citation faithfulness of a retrieval-grounded drug QA agent versus next-best baselines
effect: DrugClaw primary-source rate 0.918 (+10.1 pp over next-best); faithfulness 0.887 (+5.9 pp); MedQA 0.920; PubMedQA 0.693.
quote: Across DrugAudit plus drug-related subsets of MedQA (751) and PubMedQA (512), DrugClaw is top-1 on every column of the headline table: composite Evidence Index under both judges, judge-mediated answer correctness, primary-source rate (0.918, +10.1 pp over next-best), faithfulness (0.887, +5.9 pp), MedQA (0.920), and PubMedQA (0.693).

title: Food Noise & False Safety: A Systematic Evaluation of How LLMs Fail to Adapt to Eating Disorder Queries with Clinician Feedback
outcome: Unsafe LLM responses to eating disorder prompts with varying risk levels
effect: Specific linguistic cues in prompts increased the likelihood of unsafe responses. LLMs uncritically adapted to problematic and potentially dangerous user inputs. No numeric results reported in the abstract.
quote: We find, in consultation with clinical ED experts, that specific linguistic cues in prompts increase the likelihood of unsafe responses

title: MultiTurnPSB: Evaluating Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks an dClassifier-Based Defenses for Medical AI Safety
outcome: Unsafe response rate across four adversarial turns under live attack
effect: Unsafe responses rose from 35% to nearly 80% by Turn 4 under live attack; GPT-4.1-mini and Claude Sonnet 4.5 diverged to a 19x gap by Turn 4.
quote: Unsafe responses rise from 35% to nearly 80% by Turn 4 under live attack.

title: MultiTurnPSB: Evaluating Multi-Turn Jailbreak Attacks an dClassifier-Based Defenses for Medical AI Safety
outcome: Turn 4 unsafe responses with input-side classifier, and false alarm rate on benign queries
effect: The classifier reduced Turn 4 unsafe responses by 52 percentage points despite severe accuracy degradation, but produced a 45% false alarm rate on benign queries.
quote: A lightweight input-side classifier reduces Turn 4 unsafe responses by 52 percentage points despite severe accuracy degradation, but the 45% false alarm rate on benign queries is the primary deployment constraint.

title: AI Rater Discrimination Depends on Scoring Protocol in Complex Clinical Decision-Making
outcome: AI rater scoring discrimination under rubric-anchored (Gold Rubric) vs rubric-free protocol
effect: Non-GR scores 74–78 on average, 7.69 to 49.64 points higher than GR; GR amplified discrimination between DRG and Baseline outputs by factors of 1.76 to 5.10.
quote: Within each question, GR amplified the AI rater's discrimination between DRG and Baseline CDSS outputs by factors of 1.76 to 5.10, while also revealing substantial behavioral variation across rater models that Non-GR suppressed.
sample_unit: CDSS outputs scored by AI raters

title: Can I Take Another Dose? Evaluating LLM Decision-Making Under Temporal Uncertainty in OTC Dosing QA
outcome: LLM dosing correctness on rolling 24-hour OTC dosing scenarios
effect: Models frequently struggle with rolling-window reasoning and ambiguity-sensitive cases; stable or confident-looking responses can still violate dosing constraints.
quote: Our results show that models frequently struggle with rolling-window reasoning and ambiguity-sensitive cases and that stable or confident-looking responses can still violate dosing constraints.
sample_unit: model responses (81 scenarios, 4 LLMs, repeated runs)

title: Can I Take Another Dose? Evaluating LLM Decision-Making Under Temporal Uncertainty in OTC Dosing QA
outcome: Consistency of LLM dosing answers across repeated runs
effect: Stable or confident-looking responses can still violate dosing constraints; consistency assessed across repeated runs, with 1,620 responses evaluated.
quote: Our results show that models frequently struggle with rolling-window reasoning and ambiguity-sensitive cases and that stable or confident-looking responses can still violate dosing constraints.
sample_unit: model responses (81 scenarios, 4 LLMs, repeated runs)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Dynamic Clinical Decision-Making with Standardized Patient Cases
outcome: Correlation of static benchmark performance with performance in interactive standardized patient scenarios
effect: Performance on static benchmarks does not reliably translate to SP scenarios; best model GPT-5.5 completes 60.4% of rubric items, best medical model 40.0%.
quote: Applying MedSP1000 to a range of general-purpose and medically specialized LLMs, we find that performance on static benchmarks does not reliably translate to such educational scenarios.

title: Ten Headache Specialists versus Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Literature Summarization: A Critical Evaluation and Comparison
outcome: Blinded specialist ratings and preference ranking of RAG LLM summaries versus expert-written summaries
effect: Expert-written summaries were preferred over LLM summaries, though experts sometimes could not distinguish human from AI-generated summaries. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
quote: Our study, comparing LLM- and expert-written literature summaries evaluated by headache specialists, showed that expert-written summaries were preferred, although experts sometimes found it challenging to distinguish between human- and AI-generated summaries.
sample_unit: headache specialist evaluators (each rating summaries for 9 of 10 questions)

title: Measuring the sensitivity of LLM-based structured extraction to prompt, model, and schema choices in clinical discharge summaries
outcome: Output agreement across prompt paraphrases and model choices in structured extraction
effect: Median cross-prompt kappa 0.69 and 0.68 on three-way flags; model change reassigns dominant admission tag on close to half of notes, prompt phrasing on roughly one in eight.
quote: On the multi-class admission categorization, changing the model reassigns the dominant tag on close to half of all notes while changing the prompt phrasing reassigns it on roughly one in eight, and the larger model places far less mass on residual catch-all categories (44% to 26%).

title: Evidence-Based Intelligent Diagnostic and Therapeutic Visualization System with Large Language Models: Multi-Turn Interaction and Multimodal Treatment Plan Generation
outcome: Non-standard outputs with versus without knowledge graph constraints
effect: Knowledge graph constraints reduced non-standard outputs by 32%.
quote: Knowledge graph constraints reduced non-standard outputs by 32%.

title: When Large Language Models Fail in Healthcare: Evaluating Sensitivity to Prompt Variations
outcome: LLM robustness to lexical, syntactic, and adversarial prompt perturbations on MedMCQA
effect: Models resilient to simple lexical substitutions or paraphrasing but break down under syntactic reordering or misleading contextual cues; fragility across general-purpose and medical LLMs. No numbers in abstract.
quote: While models tend to show resilience to simple lexical substitutions or paraphrasing, they often break down under syntactic reordering or misleading contextual cues.

title: When Large Language Models Fail in Healthcare: Evaluating Sensitivity to Prompt Variations
outcome: Consistency of LLM responses across equivalent reworded prompts
effect: Even minor variations in phrasing can alter clinical advice; models can change diagnoses due to reworded inputs. No numbers in abstract.
quote: Even minor variations in phrasing can alter clinical advice, and targeted adversarial prompts can provoke harmful outputs.

title: LLM-Guided Evolution for Medical Decision Pipelines
outcome: Emergency recall in urgency triage, baseline versus evolved programs
effect: Baseline emergency recall was 0.60, so emergencies were missed. Evolved programs raised it to 0.97, and Semigran accuracy rose from 77.3% to 87.1%.
quote: In triage, evolved programs increase Semigran accuracy from $77.3\%$ to $87.1\%$ and emergency recall from $0.60$ to $0.97$, while improving safety-weighted held-out MIMIC-ESI performance.

title: Beyond English benchmarks: clinical llm evaluation in Brazilian Portuguese
outcome: LLM clinical task performance gap between Portuguese and English
effect: English advantage in diagnosis retrieval (+7.5-12.1 accuracy points across all models); advantage disappears in differential diagnosis, exam recommendation, and treatment planning, where CIs cross zero for most models.
quote: In diagnosis retrieval, English yields a consistent advantage across all models, with +7.5-12.1 accuracy points.

title: Stress-testing medical large language models reveals latent safety pathology beyond benchmark accuracy
outcome: LLM performance under narrative perturbation probes versus clean baseline
effect: All models performed uniformly well at baseline; under narrative stress performance diverged sharply, with two stress-response phenotypes. Quantized models showed pseudonormalization (low flip rates hiding functional collapse).
quote: Under realistic narrative stress, performance diverged sharply, revealing two distinct stress-response phenotypes.

title: Stress-testing medical large language models reveals latent safety pathology beyond benchmark accuracy
outcome: Whether clean benchmark accuracy reflects safety under realistic stress
effect: Models were uniformly good on clean baseline but diverged sharply under narrative stress, so benchmark accuracy did not reveal safety-relevant failures.
quote: Under clean baseline conditions, all models performed uniformly well.

title: Stress-testing medical large language models reveals latent safety pathology beyond benchmark accuracy
outcome: Counterfactual fairness index across models, including effect of medical fine-tuning
effect: Medical supervised fine-tuning systematically degraded logical stability, fairness, and information extraction; fairness measured by counterfactual fairness index (CFI).
quote: Medical supervised fine-tuning systematically degraded logical stability, fairness, and information extraction.

title: SurgiQ: A Large-Scale Multi-Domain Benchmark for Evaluating Surgical Understanding in Large Language Models
outcome: Model calibration and confident errors on plausible distractors in surgical multiple-choice questions
effect: Best model reached 68.1% accuracy; smaller models often near 25% random baseline; even strong models made confident mistakes on clinically plausible distractors.
quote: Calibration and error analysis further show that even strong models make confident mistakes on clinically plausible distractors, motivating more reliable and broader surgical LLM evaluation.

title: Testing the Black Box: Structural Barriers to Independent Evaluation of Consumer-Facing Health LLMs
outcome: Traceability of consumer LLM model versions for replication
effect: Models changed without traceable version identifiers, preventing reliable replication of evaluations.
quote: Models changed without traceable version identifiers, preventing reliable replication.

title: Testing the Black Box: Structural Barriers to Independent Evaluation of Consumer-Facing Health LLMs
outcome: Feasibility of independent context-specific evaluation of consumer health LLM risks
effect: Five linked barriers found, including terms-of-service and rate limits, non-resettable interfaces, and unsuitable accuracy criteria. No reliable independent evaluation framework exists.
quote: No reliable independent evaluation framework yet exists for examining how consumer-facing health LLMs behave in ordinary use.

title: CARE: A Conformal Safety Layer for Medical Summarization
outcome: Clinician omission detection with versus without calibrated flags in summary review
effect: Calibrated flags improved omission detection by 28.6 percentage points on average in a preliminary clinician study (75 document reviews).
quote: In a preliminary clinician study (75 document reviews), calibrated flags improved omission detection by 28.6 percentage points on average.

title: CARE: A Conformal Safety Layer for Medical Summarization
outcome: Calibrated risk control
effect: CARE satisfied the target risk bound at $α= 0.15$ with 95% confidence across 100 resplits.
quote: Across five medical summarization tasks, CARE satisfies the target risk bound at $α= 0.15$ with 95% confidence across 100 calibration/test resplits, using only ~100 labeled documents per domain.

title: CARE: A Conformal Safety Layer for Medical Summarization
outcome: Hallucination and omission flagging
effect: CARE preserved formal guarantees while surfacing up to 5$\times$ fewer sentences than alternative calibrated baselines.
quote: By jointly calibrating over the full $(τ,γ)$ threshold space, CARE preserves formal guarantees while surfacing up to 5$\times$ fewer sentences than alternative calibrated baselines.

title: MetaPlate: Counterfactual-Guided RAG-LLM Tool for Personalized Food Recommendation and Hyperglycemia Prevention
outcome: Registered dietitian review of LLM meal recommendations for realism and suitability, before vs after prompt refinement
effect: Improvements in meal realism, portion suitability, and recommendation likelihood; expert feedback showed a shift from clinically implausible outputs to actionable, contextually appropriate recommendations.
quote: Results show improvements in meal realism, portion suitability, and recommendation likelihood, with expert feedback indicating a shift from clinically implausible outputs to actionable, contextually appropriate recommendations.
sample_unit: meal recommendations rated by registered dietitians

title: Reassessing High-Performing LLMs on Polish Medical Exams: True Competence or Bias-Driven Performance?
outcome: LLM accuracy drop from standard MCQA to harder benchmark on Polish medical exams
effect: Best model (Qwen3.5-122B) drops 28.4 pp on English and 31 pp on Polish exams under the harder setup; standard MCQA scores do not reliably reflect true medical competence.
quote: Under our harder setup, the best model (Qwen3.5-122B) drops by 28.4 and 31 pp on English and Polish exams, respectively.

title: Measuring Epistemic Resilience of LLMs Under Misleading Medical Context
outcome: LLM accuracy and attack success under injected misleading context versus original questions
effect: Mean accuracy fell from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success across 11 model configurations.
quote: Across 11 model configurations, mean accuracy falls from 71.1% on original questions to 38.0% under focused misleading context, with 51.5% attack success.

title: Measuring Epistemic Resilience of LLMs Under Misleading Medical Context
outcome: Whether licensing-exam-level scores predict safe medical judgment under misleading context
effect: Models abandon originally correct answers when misleading context is injected; accuracy drops from 71.1% to 38.0%, showing exam-style benchmark performance overstates robustness.
quote: We show this assumption is fragile: when misleading context is injected into questions that LLMs originally answer correctly, they abandon the correct answer.

title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
outcome: Rate of recommending banned or withdrawn drugs in default LLM configurations
effect: All models showed high hallucination rates in default configurations, consistently selecting banned drugs that matched training data patterns (no numeric default rate given in abstract).
quote: In default configurations, all models showed high hallucination rates, consistently selecting banned drugs that matched training data patterns.

title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
outcome: Hallucination Error Rate with vs without agentic pipeline using real-time regulatory data
effect: The agentic architecture reduced HER by approximately 53% across models compared with vanilla conditions. Pointwise scores shifted from -0.25 toward 0.0.
quote: Our proposed agentic architecture reduced HER by approximately 53% across models.

title: Trust but Verify: Mitigating Medical Hallucinations via Post-Hoc Adversarial Auditing and Multi-Agent Feedback Loops
outcome: Whether a post-hoc automated safety audit intercepts dangerous LLM outputs
effect: The safety audit intercepted dangerous outputs even when the models' parametric knowledge favored the banned substance. HER fell by about 53%.
quote: The safety audit intercepted dangerous outputs even when models' parametric knowledge favored the banned substance.

title: EHRNote-ChatQA: A Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Multi-Turn Clinical Question Answering over Longitudinal Discharge Summaries
outcome: Whether single-turn clinical QA performance transfers to multi-turn, evidence-grounded discharge-summary QA
effect: Across 22 LLMs, single-turn clinical QA performance did not reliably transfer to the multi-turn setting; evidence grounding was harder than content answering, and multi-turn errors compounded. No numbers in abstract.
quote: Benchmarking 22 open- and closed-source LLMs reveals several challenges, including that LLMs struggle more with evidence grounding than content answering, multi-turn errors compound across turns, and single-turn clinical QA performance does not reliably transfer to this setting.

title: AgentFairBench: Do LLM Agents Discriminate When They Act?
outcome: Counterfactual changes in agent actions when only name-coded race x gender varied (hiring, lending, triage)
effect: No demographic effect above sampling noise for claude haiku 4.5: 0 of 120 pairwise and 0 of 9 omnibus contrasts survived correction; planted-bias test showed the instrument detects disparity.
quote: Against an arity matched noise floor and an omnibus group test, claude haiku 4 5 shows no demographic effect above sampling noise (0 of 120 pairwise and 0 of 9 omnibus contrasts survive correction); a planted-bias test confirms the instrument detects disparity when present.

title: AgentFairBench: Do LLM Agents Discriminate When They Act?
outcome: Demographic disparity in actions and tool invocations of LLM agents across scaffolds, including medical triage
effect: No demographic disparity in agent actions above sampling noise for claude haiku 4.5 (0 of 120 pairwise, 0 of 9 omnibus contrasts significant after correction).
quote: Against an arity matched noise floor and an omnibus group test, claude haiku 4 5 shows no demographic effect above sampling noise (0 of 120 pairwise and 0 of 9 omnibus contrasts survive correction); a planted-bias test confirms the instrument detects disparity when present.
