title: Compositional Reasoning Depth Predicts Clinical AI Failure: Empirical Evidence Consistent with Transformer Compositionality Limits in Electronic Health Record Question Answering
outcome: LLM accuracy on clinician-generated EHR questions by reasoning hop count
effect: Accuracy declined monotonically with hop count across all three models: Claude Sonnet 30.6% to 17.6%, GPT-4o 37.8% to 14.7%, GPT-5.4 37.8% to 23.5%.
quote: All three models, spanning two providers and two OpenAI generations (GPT-4 and GPT-5), show monotone accuracy decline with hop count: Claude Sonnet zero-shot falls from 30.6% (hop=1) to 17.6% (hop=4) (Cochran-Armitage z=-2.30, p=0.011; OR per hop 0.72, 95% CI [0.56,0.92], p=0.008); GPT-4o replicates this (37.8% to 14.7%; OR 0.58 [0.45,0.75], p<0.001); and gpt-5.4-2026-03-05 confirms it (37.8% to 23.5%; OR 0.80 [0.66,0.98], p=0.027).

title: ProvenanceGuard: Source-Aware Factuality Verification for MCP-Based LLM Agents
outcome: Block F1 and source accuracy of automated claim-level verifier on held-out medical agent traces
effect: Block F1 0.802 and source accuracy 0.858 over 260 source-eligible claims on the 40-trace held-out split; outperformed source-blind baselines. Harder multi-source benchmark: block F1 0.846.
quote: On the 40-trace held-out split, ProvenanceGuard achieves block F1 0.802 and source accuracy 0.858 over 260 source-eligible claims, outperforming source-blind baselines that do not emit claim-to-source IDs.

title: ProvenanceGuard: Source-Aware Factuality Verification for MCP-Based LLM Agents
outcome: Detection of wrong source attribution (cross-source conflation) in clinical agent answers
effect: Detected all injected attribution swaps in 50 clinical conflation probes with no retained wrong attribution; on a harder multi-source benchmark, source-plus-relation accuracy dropped to 0.229.
quote: In 50 controlled clinical conflation probes, ProvenanceGuard detects all injected attribution swaps with no retained wrong attribution.

title: Agentic AI-based Framework for Mitigating Premature Diagnostic Handoff and Silent Hallucination in Healthcare Applications
outcome: diagnostic precision
effect: Full architecture achieved 49.3% diagnostic precision, an absolute improvement of 11.3 percentage points over an unconstrained baseline.
quote: The full architecture achieves 49.3% diagnostic precision, representing an absolute improvement of 11.3 percentage points over an unconstrained baseline.

title: Towards Understanding and Measuring COGNITIVE ATROPHY in LLM Behaviour
outcome: Atrophy-aligned behaviour (directive advice, validation reinforcing dependence) in LLM mental-health counseling responses
effect: Five LLMs showed a consistent moderate-to-high level of atrophy-aligned behaviour across single and multi-turn settings; dominant patterns were directive advice, problem-solving, recommendations, topic shifts and dependence-reinforcing validation.
quote: Across five LLMs, models show a consistent moderate-to-high level of atrophy-aligned behaviour across single and multi-turn settings.
sample_unit: human-generated counseling conversations (15,680 turns; 42,230 LLM responses; 5,324 reviewer judgments)

title: When Prompts Mislead: Textual Dominance and Diagnostic Bias in MLLMs
outcome: Model accuracy when text prompts conflict with the visual cue, and effect of Chain-of-Thought
effect: Overall accuracy dropped from 75% to 46% versus the visual-only condition when an inconsistent textual claim was paired with the lesion contour. CoT was associated with further degradation.
quote: (iii) When an overlaid lesion contour is paired with an inconsistent textual claim, the textual prompt overrides the correct visual cue: overall accuracy drops from 75% to 46% relative to the visual-only condition, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning is associated with further degradation rather than self-correction.

title: Possible or Definite? A Benchmark for Evaluating Diagnostic Uncertainty Preservation in Clinical Text
outcome: LLM preservation of diagnostic uncertainty cues across five levels in clinical text revision
effect: LLMs preserved original uncertainty cues poorly, often less than half the time, and struggled to distinguish adjacent uncertainty levels.
quote: Our results show that (1) LLMs preserve the original uncertainty cues poorly, often less than half the time; (2) LLMs struggle with nuanced distinctions between adjacent levels.

title: Language Models as Interfaces, Not Oracles: A Hybrid LLM-ML System for Pediatric Appendicitis
outcome: Robustness of end-to-end LLM diagnostic performance to sentence-order permutation of narratives
effect: End-to-end LLMs showed unstable sensitivity-specificity trade-offs and greater degradation under narrative reordering than the hybrid ClaMPAPP system.
quote: End-to-end LLMs showed unstable sensitivity-specificity trade-offs and greater degradation under narrative reordering.

title: DrugBench: Evaluating AI Control Protocols for Medication Harm Mitigation
outcome: Whether AI control protocols mitigate medication-harm outputs and resist subversion
effect: Existing control protocols can be subverted under a severity-based safety definition; severity-based monitoring is proposed to address this. No numbers in abstract.
quote: Under this revised definition, we show that existing control protocols can be subverted and propose severity-based monitoring to address this limitation.

title: A Multi-Agent Audit Framework for High-Stakes Reasoning: Evaluation and Interpretability in Clinical Mental Health Screening
outcome: PHQ-8 severity prediction MAE, multi-agent pipeline with audit stage vs single-agent baseline
effect: MAE fell from 5.35 (single-agent) to 5.02 (multi-agent pipeline with audit verification stage) on DAIC-WOZ.
quote: Experimental results demonstrate that our multi-agent pipeline significantly outperforms single-agent baselines, reducing the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for PHQ-8 depression severity prediction from 5.35 to 5.02.

title: MEDLAYXPLAIN: Benchmarking the Expert-Lay Gap in Medical Vision-Language Models
outcome: Lay-register quality versus expert-register quality of VLM-generated image descriptions
effect: Medical VLMs achieve strong expert captioning but suffer significant lay-register degradation. General-purpose VLMs produce more accessible language but lack clinical precision. Neither paradigm adequately serves patient-facing communication.
quote: Benchmarking 33 VLMs on MedLayXPlain-122K reveals a systematic Expert-Lay Gap: medical VLMs achieve strong expert captioning but suffer significant lay-register degradation, while general-purpose VLMs produce more accessible language yet lack clinical precision, confirming that neither current paradigm adequately serves patient-facing communication.

title: Old Fictions, New Skins: Evaluating the Manipulative Capabilities of LLMs in Healthcare
outcome: Manipulation success in steering participants to an incorrect treatment choice, manipulative vs control LLM
effect: Manipulation success was 59.5% in the manipulative condition vs 44.0% in control (OR = 2.11, 95% CI [1.12, 4.00], p = .021).
quote: Manipulation success rates were higher in the manipulative condition (59.5%) than in the control condition (44.0%), with the effect reaching significance (OR = 2.11, 95% CI [1.12, 4.00], p = .021).

title: Large Language Model-Assisted Cleaning of Report-Derived Labels in a Large-Scale Chest CT Dataset
outcome: Radiologist adjudication of label-report discordance between CT-RATE labels and GPT-5.4 labels
effect: Adjudication supported GPT-5.4-derived labels in 72 of 97 (74.2%) general discordant instances and 91 of 99 (91.9%) targeted lymphadenopathy discordant instances; overall agreement 96.4%, kappa 0.884.
quote: In discordance review, radiologist adjudication supported GPT-5.4-derived labels in 72 of 97 (74.2%) general discordant instances and 91 of 99 (91.9%) targeted lymphadenopathy discordant instances.

title: Physiology-Aware CNN and Zero-Shot Multimodal LLMs for ECG Image Classification: A Comparative Study
outcome: Comparison of zero-shot multimodal LLMs against CNN baselines on the same ECG normal/abnormal task
effect: CNN models reached average internal ROC-AUC 0.92-0.94 and external 0.85-0.86, while zero-shot LLMs were near chance (ROC-AUC around 0.5).
quote: In contrast, zero-shot LLM discrimination remained near-chance (ROC-AUC around 0.5).

title: Physiology-Aware CNN and Zero-Shot Multimodal LLMs for ECG Image Classification: A Comparative Study
outcome: Performance drop from internal test set to external PTB-XL dataset
effect: CNN average ROC-AUC fell from 0.92-0.94 internally to 0.85-0.86 externally, a moderate drop; stable discrimination across seeds.
quote: Across seeds, CNN-based models demonstrated stable discrimination, with average internal ROC-AUC of 0.92-0.94, and external ROC-AUC of 0.85-0.86.

title: Physiology-Aware CNN and Zero-Shot Multimodal LLMs for ECG Image Classification: A Comparative Study
outcome: LLM sensitivity to ECG image rendering (grid vs grid-free) across repeated runs
effect: PR-AUC improved slightly with a grid-based calibration background compared with grid-free ECGs; discrimination remained near chance overall.
quote: The PR-AUC improved slightly when ECGs used a grid-based calibration background compared with the grid-free ECGs.

title: TTFT-Aware Graph Chain-of-Thought:Distance-Indexed Neural A* for Low-Hallucination Multi-Hop Medical Reasoning
outcome: Clinician-audited hallucinations, latency, and recall for graph-path-grounded generation versus text-only RAG
effect: Hybrid PLL+AStarNet graph-grounded generation gave a better latency/recall Pareto frontier than text-only RAG, lowered TTFT, and reduced clinician-audited hallucinations; no numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: On fertility-focused queries, the hybrid (PLL+AStarNet) establishes a better latency/recall Pareto frontier than text-only RAG and single-component baselines, lowers TTFT, and reduces clinician-audited hallucinations while preserving explanation clarity.

title: EHR-Complex: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Complex Clinical Reasoning
outcome: Output consistency across repeated runs (Pass^k) of LLM agents on EHR tasks
effect: Pass^k consistency drops below 50% for nearly all evaluated models at k=4; top model reached only 62.3% exact-match accuracy.
quote: Pass^k consistency drops below 50% for nearly all evaluated models at k=4, exposing broad stochastic fragility.

title: One Year Later...The Harms Persist, But So Do We!
outcome: LLM safeguard failure rates across 16 DSM-5 conditions under adversarial attack
effect: Safeguards held reliably only for suicide and self-harm; eating disorders, substance use disorder, and major depressive disorder showed failure rates of up to 100%.
quote: Results show that safeguards hold reliably only for suicide and self-harm, while conditions such as eating disorders, substance use disorder, and major depressive disorder exhibit failure rates of up to 100%.

title: One Year Later...The Harms Persist, But So Do We!
outcome: Whether LLM safeguards block harmful mental health outputs across conditions and adversarial prompts
effect: Safeguards are inadequate and inconsistent across clinical conditions; failure rates reach up to 100% for several conditions.
quote: General-purpose large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for mental health-related conversations, yet safety guardrails remain inadequate and inconsistent across clinical conditions.

title: RASC+: Retrieval-Constrained LLM Adjudication for Clinical Value Set Authoring
outcome: Value set completion macro F1 with retrieval-constrained LLM adjudication versus SAPBert selector over same pool
effect: Full-test macro F1 rose from 0.287 (SAPBert) to 0.549 (GPT-5); held-out-publisher macro F1 rose from 0.233 to 0.533, with all codes drawn from an auditable candidate pool.
quote: These results show that retrieval-constrained LLM adjudication can substantially improve value set completion while preserving the safety constraint that all returned codes must come from an auditable candidate pool.

title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
outcome: Compliance with graph-checkable evidence requirements after constrained revision of LLM outputs
effect: Baseline outputs failed evidence-path checks in 35% (GPT-4o-mini) and 33% (GPT-4o) of 100 vignettes; constrained revision brought outputs into verifier-level compliance.
quote: The evidence gate detects unsupported omissions and uses constrained revision to bring outputs into verifier-level compliance with benchmark-defined evidence requirements.

title: T2D-Bench: Evidence-Gated Evaluation of LLM Outputs for Type 2 Diabetes Using a Multi-Layer Clinical-Lifestyle Knowledge Graph
outcome: LLM outputs failing guideline constraints and evidence-path checks in type 2 diabetes vignettes
effect: Baseline outputs failed benchmark-defined evidence-path checks in 35% of cases for GPT-4o-mini and 33% for GPT-4o.
quote: Across 100 structured vignettes spanning diagnosis, medication safety, and adversarial lifestyle conflicts, baseline outputs failed benchmark-defined evidence-path checks in 35% of cases for GPT-4o-mini and 33% for GPT-4o.

title: A specialized reasoning large language model for accelerating rare disease diagnosis: a randomized AI physician assistance trial
outcome: Physician rare-disease diagnostic accuracy with LLM assistance versus internet search alone
effect: RaDaR assistance improved physicians' rare-disease diagnostic accuracy by 21.44 percentage points compared with internet search alone.
quote: In a randomized physician-assistance trial, RaDaR assistance improved physicians' rare-disease diagnostic accuracy by 21.44 percentage points compared with internet search alone.

title: MedGuards: Multi-Agent System for Reliable Medical Error Detection and Correction
outcome: Automated multi-agent detection and correction of medical errors in clinical notes across four datasets
effect: Reported significant improvements across several metrics and models on four multilingual clinical note datasets; no numeric values given in the abstract.
quote: Experiments across four multilingual medical datasets consisting of clinical notes demonstrate significant improvements by the proposed framework across several metrics and models.

title: From Black-Box to Clinical Insight: A Multi-Stage Explainable Framework for Speech-Based Cognitive Impairment Detection
outcome: Physician-rated clinical meaningfulness and alignment of AI-generated explanations with patient cognitive profiles
effect: Physician evaluation on 70 samples showed strong alignment with patient-level cognitive profiles; System Usability Scale score of 82/100.
quote: Physician evaluation on 70 stratified English samples demonstrated strong alignment with patient-level cognitive profiles, and a System Usability Scale score of 82/100 indicated high potential for clinical workflow integration.
sample_unit: stratified English speech samples rated by physicians

title: From Black-Box to Clinical Insight: A Multi-Stage Explainable Framework for Speech-Based Cognitive Impairment Detection
outcome: Physician assessment of AI explanations' correctness and usability
effect: Physician evaluation on 70 samples showed strong alignment with cognitive profiles; SUS 82/100 indicated high potential for workflow integration.
quote: Physician evaluation on 70 stratified English samples demonstrated strong alignment with patient-level cognitive profiles, and a System Usability Scale score of 82/100 indicated high potential for clinical workflow integration.
sample_unit: stratified English speech samples rated by physicians

title: When Medical Safety Alignment Fails: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on High-Risk Medical Queries
outcome: Effect of external guardrail models on blocking unsafe high-risk medical queries and outputs
effect: External guardrails reduced some failures but introduced brittle blocking and weak safe helpfulness; no numbers in the abstract.
quote: Results reveal a substantial gap between apparent alignment and medical safety: aligned models can still produce unsafe or actionable responses, medical fine-tuning can amplify harmful specificity, and external guardrails reduce some failures while introducing brittle blocking and weak safe helpfulness.

title: IMCBench: A benchmark for multimodal LLMs in Image-grounded Medical Conversations
outcome: Change in safety score when EHR context or visual input removed
effect: Safety dropped by 0.23 on average when EHR context was removed and by 0.18 when visual input was removed; stronger models used visual features more effectively.
quote: Ablation studies further reveal that both visual input and EHR context contribute to safe guidance (safety drops of 0.18 and 0.23 on average when each is removed), with stronger models leveraging visual features more effectively.

title: Why Trust Your Agent? Empirical Security Gains from TRiSM-Guided Agentic Workflows in Healthcare
outcome: Attack success rates for RAG poisoning, data-field injection, and network injection, TRiSM-guided vs insecure workflow
effect: RAG poisoning ASR fell from 31% to 10%; data-field injection from 42% to 25%; network injection eliminated via server-side prompt construction.
quote: The TRiSM-guided agentic workflow reduced mean attack success rates from 31% to 10% for RAG poisoning and from 42% to 25% for data-field injection, while eliminating the network injection vector entirely through server-side prompt construction.

title: Why Trust Your Agent? Empirical Security Gains from TRiSM-Guided Agentic Workflows in Healthcare
outcome: Attack success rates under adversarial testing, secured vs insecure agent workflow
effect: Across 500 attack scenarios, mean ASR dropped for RAG poisoning (31% to 10%) and data-field injection (42% to 25%); network injection eliminated.
quote: The TRiSM-guided agentic workflow reduced mean attack success rates from 31% to 10% for RAG poisoning and from 42% to 25% for data-field injection, while eliminating the network injection vector entirely through server-side prompt construction.

title: Why Trust Your Agent? Empirical Security Gains from TRiSM-Guided Agentic Workflows in Healthcare
outcome: agentic workflow security and accuracy
effect: Least-privilege, defence-in-depth workflows improved security and accuracy; attack success fell 31% to 10% and 42% to 25%, and accuracy rose 72.5% to 86.5%.
quote: This paper contributes to knowledge by demonstrating least-privilege, defence in depth agentic workflows improving security and accuracy, while also highlighting model choice is a necessary architectural consideration.

title: Bad company corrupts good morals: Understanding and Measuring Narrative-Induced Moral Reasoning Degradation in LLMs
outcome: Moral reasoning accuracy of LLMs after prolonged negative narrative exposure versus baseline
effect: Negative narrative exposure degraded moral accuracy across multiple LLMs, with average drops of 12%-31%, worse in ambiguous scenarios and those involving vulnerable individuals; first-person narratives had stronger effects.
quote: First, negative narrative exposure degrades moral accuracy across multiple LLMs, with average drops of 12%-31%, especially in ambiguous scenarios and those involving vulnerable individuals.

title: MAM-AI: An On-Device Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Nurses and Midwives in Zanzibar
outcome: Effect of retrieved guideline context on small generator answer quality and faithfulness
effect: Adding retrieved context did not improve the 4B generator's answers. Where the corpus held the right passage, answers were specific and actionable; otherwise they were vague. The chosen generator was about twice as faithful to its sources.
quote: The small generator is what remains in doubt: adding retrieved context does not improve its answers, and at 4B it cannot be both helpful and safe at once -- of two same-size candidates, the more helpful one commits genuine dangerous errors, so we deploy the other, which is about twice as faithful to its sources (as faithful as a frontier model), and recover its helpfulness with a redesigned prompt that cuts deflection from 33% to 3%.

title: MAM-AI: An On-Device Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Nurses and Midwives in Zanzibar
outcome: answer quality when corpus lacks passage
effect: Answers were specific/actionable when corpus held the right passage, vague when it did not.
quote: Corpus quality is decisive for the same reason: where the corpus holds the right passage the answer is specific and actionable, and where it does not it goes vague.

title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy under progressive information masking and reasoning-to-output mismatch versus expert annotations
effect: GPT-4o-mini accuracy dropped from 95.0% to 32.5% under information scarcity; 68.6% reasoning-to-output mismatch; standalone automated evaluations can substantially overestimate clinical reliability.
quote: These results suggest that standalone automated clinical evaluations can substantially overestimate clinical reliability without expert-grounded validation.
sample_unit: rare diagnostic cases (200 reasoning traces; 5,600 expert-physician annotations)

title: CLExEval: A Human-in-the-Loop Framework for Qualitative Evaluation of LLM Clinical Reasoning
outcome: Whether LLM-as-a-Judge approvals agree with human-verified clinically incorrect outputs
effect: On a human-verified failure set (n=142), GPT-4o-mini approved 47.9% of clinically incorrect outputs; HuatuoGPT-o1 approved all validly scored failures and showed positive self-preference bias.
quote: GPT-4o-mini approved 47.9% of clinically incorrect outputs, while HuatuoGPT-o1 approved all validly scored failures and showed a positive self-preference bias.
sample_unit: rare diagnostic cases (200 reasoning traces; 5,600 expert-physician annotations)

title: Clinician-Level Agreement Without Clinical Caution: LLM Evaluator Limits in Medical AI Benchmarking
outcome: Whether LLM evaluators abstain or defer on difficult items, compared with physicians
effect: Physicians scaled abstention with item difficulty, while frontier LLM evaluators assigned definitive scores in every case, showing near-absent clinical metacognition.
quote: Despite this statistical alignment, automated evaluators exhibited near-absent clinical metacognition: physicians scaled abstention with item difficulty, while frontier models assigned definitive scores in every case.

title: Clinician-Level Agreement Without Clinical Caution: LLM Evaluator Limits in Medical AI Benchmarking
outcome: Lineage-dependent self-preference bias in LLM evaluators scoring outputs of related models
effect: LLM evaluators preferentially scored architectural siblings, systematic lineage-dependent bias independent of language; evaluator independence requires explicit verification.
quote: We additionally quantified systematic lineage-dependent biases, where models preferentially scored architectural siblings, an effect independent of language.

title: A rubric-based controlled comparison of frontier language models on expert-authored clinical reasoning tasks
outcome: Rubric pass rates on expert-authored clinical reasoning tasks, by criterion weight
effect: Mean rubric pass rates were 0.47 (Claude), 0.38 (GPT), 0.37 (Gemini); critical weight-5 criteria passed at only 32.4-41.7% versus 80-90% for weight-1 criteria; 55 of 108 critical criteria satisfied by no model.
quote: The central finding is an inversion of clinical priority: the highest-weighted (weight-5, critical) criteria passed at only 32.4-41.7%, while low-stakes weight-1 criteria passed at 80-90%.
sample_unit: clinician-authored clinical scenarios (184 rubric criteria; 552 graded criteria)

title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Causality Assessment in Pharmacovigilance: Developing a Performance Metric as Objective for Bayesian Hyperparameter Optimization
outcome: Effect of temperature (output variability) on LLM-expert agreement in Naranjo causality assessment
effect: Temperature showed no systematic population-level effect (beta = 0.002, p = 0.959); case-specific EWACS-guided temperature optimization improved classification agreement from 45.0% to 72.0% (+27 pp).
quote: Temperature showed no systematic population-level effect (\b{eta} = 0.002, p = 0.959).

title: Medi-Gemma: A Hybrid Clinical Decision Support System Integrating Deterministic EMR Analytics and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
outcome: Factual adherence and context drift of LLM outputs when grounded in structured EMR data and RAG
effect: Abstract reports the architecture eliminates semantic context drift, prevents database compilation crashes, and improves factual adherence to backend clinical repositories. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
quote: Validation shows that this architecture eliminates semantic context drift, prevents database compilation crashes, and improves factual adherence to backend clinical repositories.

title: Toward Trustworthy Large Language Model Agents in Healthcare
outcome: Safety compliance of scheduling agent with scope constraints refusing medical advice or diagnosis
effect: 96.0% safety compliance on the dedicated safety-critical evaluation subset; 91.8% task completion
quote: Experimental results demonstrate a 91.8% task completion rate with a median per-request latency of 2.2 seconds, 96.0% safety compliance on the dedicated safety-critical evaluation subset, and an average operational cost of $0.0324 per appointment, yielding a significant cost reduction compared to manual human scheduling.

title: Toward Trustworthy Large Language Model Agents in Healthcare
outcome: Recognition of emergencies and medical-intent requests via deterministic short-circuit guardrails
effect: 96.0% safety compliance on the safety-critical evaluation subset
quote: Experimental results demonstrate a 91.8% task completion rate with a median per-request latency of 2.2 seconds, 96.0% safety compliance on the dedicated safety-critical evaluation subset, and an average operational cost of $0.0324 per appointment, yielding a significant cost reduction compared to manual human scheduling.

title: CCBENCH: Assessing LLM Cultural Competence via Implicitly Signaled Norms using Health Queries
outcome: Culturally appropriate LLM responses to health questions from personas signaling cultural norms
effect: Even the best of five models gave culturally appropriate responses only 20-30% of the time. Afghan context averaged 8.8%. Explicit cultural-cue (CoT) prompting improved results by only 3-5% on average.
quote: Benchmarking five leading models reveals that even the best achieve culturally appropriate responses only 20-30% of the time.

title: Healthier LLMs: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Public Health Question Answering
outcome: Multiple-choice accuracy of LLMs with versus without retrieved context from UK public health guidance
effect: Retrieved context substantially increased multiple-choice accuracy across diverse LLMs; smaller open-weight models with retrieval matched or outperformed larger models without retrieval. Gains were driven by retrieval quality and context selection.
quote: Providing retrieved context substantially increases multiple-choice accuracy across a diverse set of LLMs, enabling smaller open-weight models to match or outperform larger models used without retrieval, with gains primarily driven by retrieval quality and careful context selection.

title: Evaluating LLM Robustness Under Domain-Specific Prompt Perturbations in Public Health Applications
outcome: LLM accuracy and prediction flips under misinformation framing and layperson rewriting perturbations
effect: MF degrades accuracy by 7.2 pp on average with prediction flip rates of 9-38 percent, even when claims are labelled unsupported; LR causes only 1.4 pp degradation.
quote: Experiments show that MF degrades accuracy by 7.2 pp on average with prediction flip rates of 9-38 percent, even when claims are explicitly labelled as unsupported; LR causes only 1.4 pp degradation.

title: Evaluating LLM Robustness Under Domain-Specific Prompt Perturbations in Public Health Applications
outcome: Consistency of LLM answers when patients rephrase symptoms in everyday language
effect: Layperson rewriting caused only 1.4 pp accuracy degradation, while misinformation framing caused 7.2 pp degradation on average.
quote: Experiments show that MF degrades accuracy by 7.2 pp on average with prediction flip rates of 9-38 percent, even when claims are explicitly labelled as unsupported; LR causes only 1.4 pp degradation.

title: A safety-oriented hypothetico-deductive framework for AI-assisted differential diagnosis
outcome: Top-3 diagnostic accuracy with evidence-grounded verification framework versus standalone LLM on case reports
effect: Top-3 accuracy 59.9% vs 52.1% (JAMA) and 62.7% vs 51.4% (NEJM); Annals of Emergency Medicine 85.7% vs 68.6%.
quote: On literature-derived case reports from NEJM and JAMA, with GPT-oss-120B as the shared backbone, Top-3 diagnostic accuracy was 59.9% versus 52.1% for the standalone LLM on JAMA cases and 62.7% versus 51.4% on NEJM cases.
sample_unit: real-world emergency department notes (blinded physician evaluation)

title: A safety-oriented hypothetico-deductive framework for AI-assisted differential diagnosis
outcome: Capture of physician-consensus must-not-miss diagnoses in top three differential
effect: AegisDx captured at least one must-not-miss condition in top three in 78.0% of cases versus 52.0% for standalone LLM.
quote: against physician-consensus must-not-miss diagnosis sets, AegisDx captured at least one such condition among its top three diagnoses in 78.0% of cases versus 52.0%.
sample_unit: real-world emergency department notes (blinded physician evaluation)

title: Towards Precision Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Clinical-Reasoning LLM for Risk Stratification and Treatment Guidance
outcome: Physician decision accuracy and speed with versus without the LLM assistant
effect: Physicians using HCC-STAR as an assistant made more accurate decisions faster; the model also surpassed resident and attending physicians in treatment accuracy. No numbers in abstract.
quote: The model surpassed resident and attending physicians in treatment accuracy and helped physicians make more accurate decisions faster when used as an assistant.

title: Towards Precision Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Clinical-Reasoning LLM for Risk Stratification and Treatment Guidance
outcome: Treatment recommendation and risk stratification versus guidelines and competing models
effect: HCC-STAR achieved state-of-the-art performance versus clinical guidelines (BCLC, CNLC) and competitive models including GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5 Pro in 6,668 patients from 12 hospitals.
quote: In a multi-center cohort of 6,668 patients from 12 hospitals in China, HCC-STAR achieved state-of-the-art performance in treatment recommendation and risk stratification compared with clinical guidelines and competitive models, including GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5 Pro.

title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
outcome: Change in LLM urgency triage across patient personae differing in communication style and emotion
effect: Communication style significantly altered triage outcomes across five patient personae and four LLMs (1,164 clinician-graded cases); specific effect sizes not reported in the abstract.
quote: We found that communication style can significantly alter triage outcomes.

title: MedRealMM: A Real-World Multimodal Benchmark for Chinese Online Medical Consultation
outcome: LLM next-response quality versus online physician responses on rubric criteria
effect: Frontier models remain below the online physician response. Some meet as many or more positive criteria than physicians but trigger more negative criteria.
quote: Our results show that image information is critical for reliable clinical performance and that current frontier models remain below the online physician response.

title: Trivial Prompt Reframing Bypasses Safety Guardrails in Googleś MedGemma-4B
outcome: Attack success rate: model complying with guarded out-of-scope requests under adversarial reframing
effect: Overall ASR 38.0%; medical board exam framing raised ASR from 29.0% to 53.1% (+24.0 points); doctor authority framing 43.7% (+14.7); instruction-override prefixes had no significant effect.
quote: recasting a question as a "medical board exam" item raises ASR from a 29.0% baseline to 53.1% (+24.0 points), and an appeal to an alleged doctor's authority raises it to 43.7% (+14.7); crude instruction-override prefixes have no significant effect.

title: Trivial Prompt Reframing Bypasses Safety Guardrails in Googleś MedGemma-4B
outcome: Model advising that emergency care can be skipped under attack framings
effect: Emergency-deferral guardrail strong at 4.7% ASR, but the authority framing was the only attack that breached it.
quote: the drug-interaction guardrail is nearly absent (83.2% ASR) while the emergency-deferral guardrail is strong (4.7%) -- and the authority framing is the only attack that breaches it.

title: Trivial Prompt Reframing Bypasses Safety Guardrails in Googleś MedGemma-4B
outcome: Model providing dosages, diagnoses, treatments, and drug interaction judgments despite prohibited behaviors
effect: Overall ASR 38.0% across guarded concepts; drug-interaction guardrail nearly absent at 83.2% ASR.
quote: Under the primary LLM judge the overall Attack Success Rate (ASR, the fraction coded comply) is 38.0%.

title: Trivial Prompt Reframing Bypasses Safety Guardrails in Googleś MedGemma-4B
outcome: Robustness of model behavior under paraphrased/reframed inputs and repeated runs
effect: ASR shifted substantially by reframing (29.0% baseline to 53.1% under exam framing); topic drove robustness (drug-interaction 83.2% vs emergency 4.7%).
quote: Robustness is dominated by topic: the drug-interaction guardrail is nearly absent (83.2% ASR) while the emergency-deferral guardrail is strong (4.7%) -- and the authority framing is the only attack that breaches it.

title: Faithful by Design: Evaluating and Improving LLM-Generated Clinical Trial Summaries for Multi-Stakeholder Audiences
outcome: NLI-based faithfulness of trial summaries with vs without knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval
effect: Knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval produced statistically significant improvements in NLI faithfulness scores (entailment +0.0125, faithfulness +0.0130, p < 0.0001) versus baseline; effects were small and model-dependent.
quote: A knowledge-graph-augmented retrieval system was developed and evaluated against the baseline, producing statistically significant improvements in NLI-based faithfulness scores (entailment +0.0125, faithfulness +0.0130, p < 0.0001).
sample_unit: generated summaries (200 trials x 3 audiences x 3 models)

title: Faithful by Design: Evaluating and Improving LLM-Generated Clinical Trial Summaries for Multi-Stakeholder Audiences
outcome: Unsupported claims (hallucination) in LLM-generated clinical trial summaries
effect: Unsupported Claims was the dominant failure mode across all three models, mean annotation score 1.55 out of three.
quote: Unsupported Claims was identified as the dominant failure mode across all three models, with a mean annotation score of 1.55 out of three.
sample_unit: generated summaries (200 trials x 3 audiences x 3 models)

title: Information-seeking failures of large language models in agentic clinical reasoning
outcome: Overall accuracy of frontier LLMs on agentic hematologic oncology reasoning benchmark
effect: Across 32 frontier models, the best achieved only 68% overall accuracy despite high scores on medical knowledge assessments.
quote: Across 32 frontier models, the best achieved only 68% overall accuracy.

title: Information-seeking failures of large language models in agentic clinical reasoning
outcome: Reasoning trace quality versus accuracy in agentic reasoning
effect: Reasoning traces scored high on a rubric (91% above threshold) but decorrelated from accuracy, showing locally coherent rationales with globally incorrect conclusions.
quote: Reasoning traces scored high on a clinical reasoning rubric (91% above threshold) but decorrelated from accuracy, revealing a gap between locally coherent rationales and globally correct conclusions.

title: Agentic systems for breast cancer treatment recommendations
outcome: Citation errors in agentic LLM breast cancer treatment recommendations, found by oncologist error analysis
effect: Oncologist-led error analysis revealed persistent clinically relevant failures including citation errors, outdated claims, and flawed justifications.
quote: oncologist-led error analysis revealed persistent clinically relevant failures, including incorrect or missing recommendations, flawed justifications, citation errors, outdated claims, and overconfidence.

title: Agentic systems for breast cancer treatment recommendations
outcome: Overconfidence in LLM breast cancer treatment recommendations found in oncologist error analysis
effect: Overconfidence was among the persistent clinically relevant failures identified; systems judged insufficient for unsupervised clinical use.
quote: oncologist-led error analysis revealed persistent clinically relevant failures, including incorrect or missing recommendations, flawed justifications, citation errors, outdated claims, and overconfidence.

title: Evidence-Grounded AI for Musculoskeletal Care
outcome: Cumulative cases per bed and patient-reported access to health information in randomised deployment
effect: Routine-care integration increased cumulative cases per bed by 9.7% and improved patient-reported access to health information among 8,240 inpatients.
quote: In a randomised deployment involving 8,240 inpatients, integration into routine care increased cumulative cases per bed by 9.7% and improved patient-reported access to health information.

title: Ask Before You Diagnose: Safe-Psych, a Sequential Evaluation Benchmark for LLMs in Psychiatry
outcome: LLM under-abstention and over-abstention when clinical information is incomplete (DIAGNOSE/CLARIFY/ABSTAIN)
effect: Under-abstention exceeded 60% for most models; safety-aware prompting reduced premature commitment only by shifting errors toward excessive abstention; models rarely sought clarification unless explicitly prompted.
quote: Our findings show that capability does not ensure calibration: even strong models struggle under incomplete clinical information, with under-abstention exceeding 60% for most models and safety-aware prompting reducing premature commitment only by shifting errors toward excessive abstention.
sample_unit: psychiatric clinical notes (over 1,000, segmented into sequential stages)

title: Designing Safety-Constrained LLM Systems for Public Health Information Access
outcome: Enforcement of scope boundaries on in-scope, out-of-scope, and emergency scenario queries
effect: Scenario-based validation showed consistent enforcement of safety constraints (no medical advice); no numeric rates reported in abstract; average response time 5.3 seconds.
quote: Results show consistent enforcement of safety constraints, reliable resource grounding, and stable system performance, with an average response time of 5.3 seconds.

title: Designing Safety-Constrained LLM Systems for Public Health Information Access
outcome: Grounding of responses in curated public health resources via domain-restricted RAG
effect: Scenario validation reported reliable resource grounding; no quantitative grounding metric or comparison reported in abstract.
quote: Results show consistent enforcement of safety constraints, reliable resource grounding, and stable system performance, with an average response time of 5.3 seconds.

title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation
outcome: Gap between base accuracy and robust accuracy under counterfactual clinical perturbation
effect: Base accuracy overstates robust accuracy by 16-28 percentage points in every model; residual BTR of 20% with EA-RAG.
quote: Across eight configurations of four frontier LLMs, base accuracy overstates robust accuracy by 16-28 percentage points in every model.

title: MamaBench: Benchmarking LLM Robustness in Maternal and Child Health Diagnosis through Counterfactual Clinical Perturbation
outcome: Bias Trap Rate and base accuracy with retrieval-grounded method (EA-RAG) on Claude Sonnet 4.6
effect: EA-RAG achieved 20.3% BTR and 65.0% robust accuracy, a 5.5 percentage point BTR reduction without degrading base accuracy.
quote: EA-RAG achieves 20.3% BTR and 65.0% robust accuracy on Claude Sonnet 4.6, a 5.5 percentage point BTR reduction without degrading base accuracy.

title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Understand OCT?
outcome: MLLM performance on OCT understanding benchmark across perception, cognition, reasoning
effect: Current models remain substantially short of reliable OCT understanding; neither medical-domain adaptation nor increased model scale consistently improves performance across capability levels.
quote: Experimental results demonstrate that current models remain substantially short of reliable OCT understanding.

title: Robust Summarization of Doctor-Patient Conversations: TalTech Systems for the Beyond Transcription Challenge
outcome: Hallucination rate of ambient SOAP notes by independent LLM-as-a-judge, compared with other submissions
effect: Lowest hallucination rate among all submissions; no absolute rate reported in the abstract, so hallucination is not shown to be absent.
quote: Our systems ranked first in both tracks, and an independent LLM-as-a-judge evaluation showed the lowest hallucination rate among all submissions, indicating that reinforcement learning against a concept-matching metric need not compromise factual reliability.
sample_unit: submissions to challenge (SOAP notes from long doctor-patient recordings)

title: Safety That Does Not Transfer: Cross-Lingual Clinical Correctness Drift in Deployable Medical Language Models
outcome: Clinical correctness of LLM responses in English versus Hausa, by model tier
effect: Locally deployable models' mean clinical correctness fell from 1.57 in English to -0.03 in Hausa; the frontier model moved from 2.00 to 1.75 with no harmful responses in either language.
quote: Among locally deployable models, mean clinical correctness fell from 1.57 in English to -0.03 in Hausa, on a scale where 2 denotes a correct answer and -1 an actively harmful one.

title: Judge-dependent safety gains and model-specific helpfulness costs of evidence-sufficiency prompting in clinical LLMs
outcome: Unsafe overconfidence reduction and correct-diagnosis cost with evidence-sufficiency prompt that induces deferral/uncertainty
effect: Unsafe overconfidence fell from 49.3% to 24.7% (paired reduction 24.7 points, 95% CI 21.8-27.7); correct diagnosis fell from 80.3% to 50.3%; near-free for GPT-5.5, near-total for Gemini (-58 points).
quote: The gain carried a model-specific helpfulness cost (correct diagnosis 80.3% to 50.3%): near-free for GPT-5.5, near-total for Gemini (-58 points).
sample_unit: paired model-response cells (4 models x common panel of questions, standard vs wrapper prompt)

title: Judge-dependent safety gains and model-specific helpfulness costs of evidence-sufficiency prompting in clinical LLMs
outcome: Reduction in unsafe overconfident answers under incomplete evidence with structured prompt
effect: Unsafe overconfidence fell from 49.3% to 24.7%, a paired reduction of 24.7 points (95% CI 21.8-27.7; p<0.001); a different-family judge showed a smaller effect (+13.1 points).
quote: Unsafe overconfidence fell from 49.3% to 24.7%, a paired reduction of 24.7 points (95% CI 21.8-27.7; p<0.001), robust in direction across models and paraphrases.
sample_unit: paired model-response cells (4 models x common panel of questions, standard vs wrapper prompt)

title: Judge-dependent safety gains and model-specific helpfulness costs of evidence-sufficiency prompting in clinical LLMs
outcome: Dependence of LLM-judged safety effect on judge choice; judge specificity against blinded clinicians
effect: Sonnet judge nearly halved the effect (+13.1 points); primary judge had sensitivity 1.00 and specificity 0.55 versus blinded clinicians.
quote: Blinded clinicians characterized the primary judge as a high-sensitivity (1.00), low-specificity (0.55) screen, not a calibrated rate.
sample_unit: paired model-response cells (4 models x common panel of questions, standard vs wrapper prompt)

title: Evaluating medical AI under missing information: same-provider judges and human raters change apparent safety
outcome: Same-provider LLM judge leniency effect on apparent model safety ranking
effect: Positive same-provider association remained after leniency adjustment (exact permutation p = 0.04; GPT-5.5 ~ +0.10 probability); excluding own-provider judge changed which model over-commits least; Fleiss' kappa 0.65.
quote: First, judge choice materially changes apparent safety: inter-judge agreement is only moderate (Fleiss' kappa = 0.65), and after adjusting for each judge's general leniency (vote-level logistic regression), a positive same-provider association remains (exact permutation p = 0.04; GPT-5.5 ~ +0.10 on the probability scale) - large enough to change which model appears to over-commit least once its own-provider judge is excluded.
sample_unit: HealthBench conversations (50-item subsample for clinician rating)

title: Evaluating medical AI under missing information: same-provider judges and human raters change apparent safety
outcome: Agreement of LLM judges with blinded clinician reference on crediting appropriate uncertainty
effect: All four LLM judges significantly more lenient than the stricter clinician (credited uncertainty on 66-84% of items vs 52%); judge-vs-consensus kappa 0.20-0.43.
quote: Second, LLM judges are more permissive than clinicians on a blinded 50-item subsample: all four are significantly more lenient than the stricter independent clinician (crediting appropriate uncertainty on 66-84% of items vs 52%), and three of four than the author-influenced consensus (Grok directional only; judge-vs-consensus kappa = 0.20-0.43).
sample_unit: HealthBench conversations (50-item subsample for clinician rating)

title: Evaluating medical AI under missing information: same-provider judges and human raters change apparent safety
outcome: Model safety when final user turn is truncated (missing information), knowledge versus calibration
effect: MedQA accuracy high with option-order effects within +/-5-point equivalence for three of four models, indicating the safety gap under missing information is calibration, not knowledge.
quote: A closed-ended MedQA anchor confirms accuracy is high and option-order effects are within a +/-5-point equivalence region for three of four models, so the safety gap is about calibration, not knowledge.
sample_unit: HealthBench conversations (50-item subsample for clinician rating)

title: Human-in-the-Loop Large Language Model Framework for Identification of Cutaneous Immune-Related Adverse Events
outcome: Reviewer accuracy, agreement and review time with versus without LLM assistance
effect: LLM-assisted workflow improved accuracy (F1 = 0.88 vs 0.77), Cohen's kappa (0.82 vs 0.50), and reduced average review time by approximately half.
quote: Compared with unassisted manual review, the LLM-assisted workflow improved accuracy (F1 = 0.88 vs 0.77), inter-rater agreement measured by Cohen's kappa (kappa = 0.82 vs 0.50), and reduced average review time by approximately half.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Large Language Model Framework for Identification of Cutaneous Immune-Related Adverse Events
outcome: Performance versus unassisted manual review
effect: F1 = 0.88 vs 0.77; kappa = 0.82 vs 0.50; review time reduced by approximately half.
quote: Compared with unassisted manual review, the LLM-assisted workflow improved accuracy (F1 = 0.88 vs 0.77), inter-rater agreement measured by Cohen's kappa (kappa = 0.82 vs 0.50), and reduced average review time by approximately half.

title: A Knowledge-Injection Framework for Zero-Shot Adaptation of LLMs to Delirium Prediction
outcome: Delirium prediction AUROC with vs without injected clinical knowledge report, and with random control reports
effect: Clinically meaningful knowledge report improved AUROC by 8.57 points (8B) and 1.99 points (70B); random control reports did not improve and often degraded performance.
quote: Adding a clinically meaningful external knowledge report improves AUROC by 8.57 percentage points for the 8B model and 1.99 percentage points for the 70B model compared to no external knowledge.

title: Marking the Wrong Symptoms: Evaluating LLM Watermarks in Medical Texts
outcome: Effect of watermarking (content provenance) on medical reasoning quality, terminology, hallucinations
effect: Watermarking can induce substantial degradation across failure modes, including lexical corruption, hallucinated terminology, and amplified misattribution or omission of image findings.
quote: Our results reveal that watermarking can induce substantial degradation across multiple failure modes, including lexical corruption, hallucinated terminology, and amplified misattribution or omission of image findings.
sample_unit: not reported (5 watermarking schemes across 11 LLMs and 7 VLMs on medical tasks)

title: Marking the Wrong Symptoms: Evaluating LLM Watermarks in Medical Texts
outcome: Whether general aggregate benchmarks mask clinically consequential failures without domain-specific evaluation
effect: Absence of domain-specific analyses plus aggregate metrics systematically obscures watermark-induced degradations in clinical text; domain-specific evaluation is called a prerequisite for safe deployment.
quote: Notably, we find that the absence of domain-specific analyses, combined with aggregate metrics that miss failures inherent to clinical text, can systematically obscure practical watermark-induced degradations.
sample_unit: not reported (5 watermarking schemes across 11 LLMs and 7 VLMs on medical tasks)

title: Enhancing Explainable Cardiac Diagnosis with Guide-Grounded Multimodal LLMs
outcome: Semantic similarity (BERTScore) of generated ECG impressions to reference reports, with vs without guide grounding
effect: Average BERTScore rose from 0.818 to 0.953 versus the CNN+Grad-CAM+MLLM baseline without the guide, while classification performance stayed competitive.
quote: In particular, our method increases the average BERTScore of generated impressions from 0.818 to 0.953 relative to a strong CNN+Grad-CAM+MLLM baseline, indicat- ing closer alignment with reference reports.

title: Socioeconomic Inference in LLM Medical Triage: Same Symptoms, Different ZIP Code
outcome: ER referral rate changes when only patient SES signal varied in prompts
effect: All three models raised ER referral for lower-SES patients given explicit signal (spreads 13-50 points); Gemini shifted 11.4 points pooled from ZIP code alone (p=1.4e-7); Claude -0.1; GPT-5.4-mini 2.0.
quote: All three models raise their emergency-room (ER) referral rate for lower-SES patients given the explicit signal (spreads of 13-50 percentage points).
sample_unit: simulated triage queries (single fixed symptom vignette with varied SES signals)

title: Socioeconomic Inference in LLM Medical Triage: Same Symptoms, Different ZIP Code
outcome: system-prompt mitigation of ZIP SES gap
effect: Gemini gap between low- and high-income ZIPs fell from 11.4 to 5.8 points, reduced but not eliminated.
quote: A single-sentence system-prompt instruction reduces but does not eliminate the effect (Gemini's gap between low- and high-income ZIPs falls from 11.4 to 5.8 points).
sample_unit: simulated triage queries (single fixed symptom vignette with varied SES signals)

title: Socioeconomic Inference in LLM Medical Triage: Same Symptoms, Different ZIP Code
outcome: ER referral rate variation by socioeconomic status
effect: All three models raised ER referral rates by 13-50 percentage points for lower-SES patients given explicit signals; Gemini shifted ER rates by 11.4 points based on ZIP code alone (p = 1.4e-7).
quote: All three models raise their emergency-room (ER) referral rate for lower-SES patients given the explicit signal (spreads of 13-50 percentage points).
sample_unit: simulated triage queries (single fixed symptom vignette with varied SES signals)

title: Spectral Dynamics of Semantic Drift in Clinical Multi-Agent Language Model Networks
outcome: semantic drift and hallucination amplification
effect: Terminal cosine similarity degradation 53.29%; variance amplification 51.81% (ρ= 1.5181) versus ER ρ= 1.0766.
quote: Moreover, the terminal semantic drift reveals a catastrophic variance amplification of 51.81% ($ρ= 1.5181$) in highly clustered architectures, proving total system unpredictability when compared to Erdős--R'enyi configurations ($ρ= 1.0766$).

title: RareLens: Towards End-to-End Rare Disease Care via Aligning Divergent Large Language Model Reasoning
outcome: Physician performance with versus without AI assistance, compared with autonomous AI
effect: Autonomous RareLens and physicians assisted by RareLens both outperformed unaided physicians; effective human-AI collaboration required more than simply providing model outputs.
quote: In an external evaluation involving 1,287 cases and 23 physicians, autonomous RareLens and physicians assisted by RareLens both outperformed unaided physicians, while demonstrating that effective human-AI collaboration requires more than simply providing model outputs.

title: Closed-Loop Validation-Repair for Healthcare Interoperability: A Multi-Model Study of Schema Compliance in Clinical LLMs
outcome: Compliance of AI outputs with schema under automated post-processing validation and repair
effect: Automated validation-repair raised compliance to 99.0% from baseline 85.9 to 91.6%; absolute gains of 7.8 to 12.5 percentage points, exact McNemar p<0.001.
quote: Exact McNemar p-values below 0.001 and absolute improvements of 7.8 to 12.5 percentage points across model sizes confirm statistical significance.

title: Aletheia: An Offline-First Clinical Decision Support System for Differential Diagnosis in Low-Resource Healthcare Settings
outcome: Expected Calibration Error of model confidence in diagnostic outputs
effect: ECE of 0.275 reported for the fine-tuned model, indicating miscalibrated confidence; Top-1 accuracy 80% (8/10) and Top-3 100% on ten cases.
quote: The system achieves an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.275 and passes the Africa Deep Tech Challenge 2026 (ADTC 2026) memory budget constraint of 7168 MB, achieving a peak inference RAM of approximately 3630 MB on the standardised benchmark laptop.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs for Mental Health: Quantifying the Incremental Contribution of Retrieval Within a Layered Safety Architecture
outcome: Intent classification accuracy/recall for RAG-enabled versus RAG-disabled LLM modes in mental health chatbot
effect: RAG improved accuracy, consistency and safety of intent detection, with a rise in false alarms; routed to additional review.
quote: While RAG caused a rise in false alarms, the trade-off is consistent with safety-critical design principles that prioritize sensitivity, where flagged cases are routed to additional review rather than acted on directly.

title: PatientAgentBench: A Benchmark Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Health AI Agents
outcome: Triage quality pass rates, including clinical screening of administrative requests, across 10 models
effect: Triage pass rates rose from 32% for weakest models to 88% for strongest; agents often acted on administrative requests without clinical screening.
quote: Triage quality is the most discriminating dimension: pass rates rise from 32% for the weakest models to 88% for the strongest, with agents often acting on administrative requests without clinical screening.

title: PatientAgentBench: A Benchmark Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Health AI Agents
outcome: Omitted crisis resources in emergency scenarios during multi-turn agent conversations
effect: Frontier models fail on only 1-3% of cases, from unverified tool outputs and omitted crisis resources in an emergency.
quote: Clinical safety and workflow accuracy follow the same pattern: the weakest models fail often, fabricating unexecuted actions, while frontier models fail on only 1-3% of cases, from unverified tool outputs and omitted crisis resources in an emergency.

title: PatientAgentBench: A Benchmark Framework for Evaluating Patient-Facing Health AI Agents
outcome: Agents' use of tool outputs without verification
effect: Frontier-model failures (1-3% of cases) arose from unverified tool outputs; weakest models fabricated unexecuted actions.
quote: Clinical safety and workflow accuracy follow the same pattern: the weakest models fail often, fabricating unexecuted actions, while frontier models fail on only 1-3% of cases, from unverified tool outputs and omitted crisis resources in an emergency.

title: Evaluating Multi-Turn Multimodal Diagnostic Reasoning on Challenging Real-World Clinical Cases
outcome: Multi-turn multimodal diagnostic accuracy and reasoning quality of MLLMs on real-world cases
effect: Proprietary models had highest overall diagnostic accuracy, but the proportion of completely correct diagnoses remained limited across all models; reasoning quality showed considerable limitations.
quote: Results showed that proprietary models achieved the highest overall diagnostic accuracy, but the proportion of completely correct diagnoses remained limited across all models.

title: When Derived Measurements Mislead: Quantifying and Mitigating LLM Over-Trust with Privileged-Modality Reliability Evidence
outcome: Over-trust repair, specificity, and unnecessary verification
effect: Baseline improved four repair/specificity endpoints by 1.82-6.69 percentage points; UHR increased 0.67 percentage points (95% CI: -0.4 to +1.7).
quote: On a protocol-locked 187-patient test, the baseline improves four repair and specificity endpoints by 1.82-6.69 percentage points, with all paired confidence intervals excluding zero; UHR increases by 0.67 percentage points (95% CI: -0.4 to +1.7).

title: EarlyDx: An Admission-Anchored Benchmark for Open-Ended Generation of Evidence-Supported ED-Encounter Diagnoses
outcome: LLM diagnostic recall on admission-time evidence, especially inference-dependent diagnoses
effect: Zero-shot models recover only 3-31% of diagnoses that must be inferred; post-training raises inference-dependent recall to 56%; no system attains a clinician's balance of sensitivity and precision on time-critical conditions.
quote: Zero-shot models score largely by extraction, recovering only 3-31% of diagnoses that must be inferred rather than read from the record; post-training raises inference-dependent recall to 56%, but a sizeable margin remains, and on time-critical conditions no system attains a clinician's balance of sensitivity and precision.

title: Can Zero-Shot LLMs Predict Child Malnutrition? A Fairness and Temporal Robustness Study
outcome: Zero-shot LLM stunting prediction performance and fairness across sex, residence, and wealth subgroups
effect: Performance was relatively consistent across child sex groups, but important fairness disparities were observed across residence and household wealth categories.
quote: however, important fairness disparities were observed across residence and household wealth categories, highlighting the need for further investigation before deployment of foundation models in public health prediction settings.

title: IyawoBench v2.0: Extended Diagnostic Evaluation of Large Language Model Clinical Triage in Nigerian Primary Care
outcome: Under-triage and over-escalation failure modes in LLM triage of safety-critical cases
effect: All three models exhibit at least one formal failure mode; conventional sensitivity conceals a 77 percentage point under-triage gap in Llama 3.1 8B.
quote: (1) all three models exhibit at least one formal failure mode; (2) traditional sensitivity metrics conceal a 77 percentage point under-triage gap in Llama 3.1 8B;

title: IyawoBench v2.0: Extended Diagnostic Evaluation of Large Language Model Clinical Triage in Nigerian Primary Care
outcome: Whether conventional safety metrics conceal triage failure modes
effect: Models scoring 100% on binary 'did not send an emergency home' safety measures may still show systematic failure modes; sensitivity metrics conceal a 77 percentage point under-triage gap in Llama 3.1 8B.
quote: Existing safety metrics, however, produce misleading confidence: models scoring 100% on binary "did not send an emergency home" safety measures may nevertheless exhibit systematic failure modes that render them undeployable at scale.

title: TreeProbe : A Tibetan Medicine Benchmark for Cultural Bias in LLMs
outcome: LLM knowledge gaps and ontology drift on Tibetan medicine benchmark
effect: Current models remain limited in native Tibetan medical contexts and show systematic external ontology drift toward biomedical or TCM reasoning. Benchmark covers 4,719 items, 467 diseases, and 10 subtasks.
quote: Experiments on representative LLMs show that current models remain limited in native Tibetan medical contexts and exhibit systematic external ontology drift.

title: Large language models improve physician accuracy but lead to false reliance
outcome: Physician accuracy with versus without LLM assistance and reliance on the AI
effect: Physician accuracy increased from 70.8% unaided to 82.6% with CORA; resistance to incorrect LLM answers fell from 92% to 34.8% when the answer appeared citation-supported.
quote: In a study of 46 physicians, accuracy increased from 70.8% unaided to 82.6% with CORA.

title: Large language models improve physician accuracy but lead to false reliance
outcome: Physician resistance to incorrect LLM answers when citation-supported
effect: When an incorrect LLM answer appeared citation-supported, physician resistance fell from 92% to 34.8%; adoption of correct advice rose from 34% to 76.9%.
quote: perceived support increased adoption of correct advice from 34% to 76.9% but when an incorrect LLM answer appeared citation-supported, physician resistance to it fell from 92% to 34.8%.

title: Large language models improve physician accuracy but lead to false reliance
outcome: Effect of displayed supporting citations on physician reliance and correctness
effect: Supporting citations predicted correct answers (87.7% vs 65.5%), but citation-supported incorrect answers were resisted less (92% to 34.8%).
quote: Supporting citations predicted correct answers (87.7% vs 65.5%), but citations created an important asymmetry

title: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy
outcome: Sycophancy rate with versus without grounding in retrieved or curated context
effect: Grounding reduced sycophancy but did not eliminate it (no numbers in abstract).
quote: Grounding helps, but does not eliminate the behavior.

title: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy
outcome: Model susceptibility to user pushback and framing variations (role, evidence, structure)
effect: Sycophancy nearly three times more common when users challenge an answer already given than when the false claim is in the initial query; higher for users presented as physicians or medical students.
quote: Medical sycophancy is nearly three times more common when users challenge an answer the model has already given than when the false claim appears in the initial query.

title: MedPRESS: A Multi-turn Benchmark for Patient-Pressure-Induced Medical Sycophancy in LLMs
outcome: Model shift to unsafe agreement under escalating patient pressure in five-turn dialogues, including symptom triage and care resistance
effect: Models frequently shift toward unsafe agreement under repeated patient pressure, varying by family, scale and prompt type; anti-sycophancy prompting improves several models but does not eliminate unsafe agreement.
quote: Results show that models frequently shift toward unsafe agreement under repeated patient pressure, with substantial variation across model families, model scale, and prompt type.

title: Preferred, Not Safer: Pairwise Preference Is a Poor Proxy for Clinical Safety
outcome: Distribution of clinically unsafe failure rates across medical specialties versus aggregate rankings
effect: Failures (<= -1 on Harmlessness and Accuracy) were unevenly distributed across specialties, creating domain-specific no-go zones hidden in aggregate rankings, even for highly ranked models.
quote: These failures are unevenly distributed across specialties, creating domain-specific ``no-go zones'' not visible in aggregate rankings or single-number leaderboards.

title: Preferred, Not Safer: Pairwise Preference Is a Poor Proxy for Clinical Safety
outcome: Whether pairwise preference metric reflects clinical safety performance of LLMs
effect: Preference is a poor proxy for safety; highly ranked models still had substantial rates of clinically meaningful failures (<= -1), and surface features explained slightly more preference variation than safety rubric differences.
quote: we find that clinician preference is a poor proxy for safety-critical performance.

title: Evaluating Counterfactual Sensitivity to Patient Information in Medication-Safety Reasoning
outcome: LLM accuracy on medication-safety questions when patient information is counterfactually changed
effect: All 28 models performed worse on counterfactual questions; mean accuracy fell from 63.6% to 45.1%. Rationales often acknowledged the change, but final answers kept the prior safety judgment.
quote: Across 28 medical-specific, general, and proprietary LLMs, every model performs worse on counterfactual questions, with mean accuracy falling from 63.6\% to 45.1\%.

title: Evaluating Counterfactual Sensitivity to Patient Information in Medication-Safety Reasoning
outcome: Whether static medication-safety accuracy reflects patient-specific reliability
effect: Models scored well on fixed guideline-following questions (mean 63.6%) but fell to 45.1% on paired counterfactual questions. The authors conclude static accuracy is limited for assessing patient-specific reliability.
quote: MedPIC-Bench therefore makes conditional rule application measurable and highlights the limitations of static medication-safety accuracy for assessing patient-specific reliability.

title: CARE-Bench: Benchmarking Patient-Facing LLM Triage
outcome: Per-turn triage action accuracy, including preserving the ask-for-more-information step
effect: Unprompted macro-F1 31.2 to 50.4; prompted 46.9 to 63.4. When correct action was to ask for more information, only 33.5% of prompted outputs preserved the step.
quote: Prompted models often recommend care before needed clarification is obtained; when the correct action was to ask for more information, only 33.5% of prompted outputs preserved the step.

title: CARE-Bench: Benchmarking Patient-Facing LLM Triage
outcome: LLM triage macro-F1 on a source-grounded benchmark of intended-use action selection
effect: Unprompted macro-F1 ranged from 31.2 to 50.4; prompted 46.9 to 63.4, with substantial threshold errors remaining.
quote: Unprompted macro-F1 remains low, ranging from 31.2 to 50.4.

title: When Calibration Depends on the Scoring Rule: Quantized Biomedical LLM Classification
outcome: Accuracy sensitivity to prompt template choice across precisions
effect: Prompt choice changed mean accuracy across precisions by 2.9 to 17.8 percentage points between the two primary templates.
quote: Between them, prompt choice changes mean accuracy across precisions by 2.9 to 17.8 percentage points.
sample_unit: test sentences (medical abstract sentences, five-class classification)

title: When Calibration Depends on the Scoring Rule: Quantized Biomedical LLM Classification
outcome: Accuracy change after quantization (INT8, INT4) versus FP16
effect: INT8 changed accuracy by at most 1.1 percentage points for adapted checkpoints; INT4 showed mixed but non-catastrophic effects.
quote: Eight-bit quantization changes accuracy by at most 1.1 percentage points for the adapted checkpoints; four-bit quantization shows mixed but non-catastrophic effects.
sample_unit: test sentences (medical abstract sentences, five-class classification)

title: RESPClinBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Clinical Decision-Making and Longitudinal Disease Management in Respiratory Specialty Care
outcome: Medication-safety risk flags in LLM responses to COPD management cases
effect: Medication-safety risk occurred in 26.93% and serious medical risk in 1.44% of AECOPD-PIM responses.
quote: medication-safety risk and serious medical risk occurred in 26.93% and 1.44% of AECOPD-PIM responses.

title: RESPClinBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Clinical Decision-Making and Longitudinal Disease Management in Respiratory Specialty Care
outcome: Output accuracy and safety of LLMs against physician-adjudicated reference answers and rubrics
effect: Mean final score across 623 cases was 68.58; imaging hallucination in 31.85% and serious medical risk in 8.16% of PNBIM responses.
quote: Imaging hallucination and serious medical risk occurred in 31.85% and 8.16% of PNBIM responses;

title: ECHO: A Locally-Deployable Agentic Health Assistant with Temporal Memory, Safety Guardrails, and Speech Assessment
outcome: Accuracy and unsafe recall of a hybrid safety layer classifying and blocking unsafe health queries
effect: Signed GNN safety classifier reached 88.8% accuracy and 90.6% unsafe recall on 2,537 Turkish queries, outperforming zero-shot LLM baselines including Llama 3.3 70B.
quote: a signed graph neural network (GNN) with APPNP-style propagation classifies boundary cases by clinical intent, achieving 88.8% accuracy and 90.6% unsafe recall on a 2,537-query annotated Turkish health dataset while outperforming zero-shot LLM baselines including Llama 3.3 70B.

title: Preventive Care Recommendations by Large Language Models
outcome: LLM preventive care prioritization compared with historical physicians on the same survey (LYGPC, consistency, selectiveness)
effect: LLMs closely mirrored physicians (mean Spearman 0.83); several models exceeded physicians in LYGPC and consistency; lifestyle services underprioritized (8.8% vs 38% rated 4 or higher); augmentation effects varied by model.
quote: Several models exceeded physicians in LYGPC and consistency while being more selective.

title: Does Splitting a Triage Decision Across Agents Hide Bias or Help Catch It? A Multi-Agent Simulation Study of LLM-Based Resource Allocation Under Audit Capacity Constraints
outcome: Rate of biased outcomes in paired cases differing only in one demographic attribute
effect: Biased outcomes occurred in 6.9% (single-agent) vs. 6.1% (nine-agent pipeline) of paired cases, p = 0.498; no measurable difference between conditions.
quote: We find no measurable difference in how often biased outcomes occur between the two conditions (6.9% vs. 6.1%, p = 0.498).

title: Does Splitting a Triage Decision Across Agents Hide Bias or Help Catch It? A Multi-Agent Simulation Study of LLM-Based Resource Allocation Under Audit Capacity Constraints
outcome: Audit coverage under capacity constraint with risk-ordered queue vs first-come-first-served
effect: Risk-ordered audit queue raised coverage from 65.6% to 91.7% (p = 0.028) under the same capacity constraint.
quote: A follow-up experiment shows that reordering the audit queue by estimated risk, rather than first-come-first-served, recovers most of the lost coverage under the same capacity constraint (65.6% to 91.7%, p = 0.028).

title: ResidencyRL: Reinforcement Learning in Simulated Clinical Environments
outcome: Missed red flag rate and diagnostic accuracy in adversarial simulated multi-turn encounters
effect: Trained agent improved diagnostic accuracy under adversarial conditions (88.0% vs. 81.0%) and reduced missed red flag rates by 31% relative to the base model.
quote: On held-out evaluations, the ResidencyRL agent improves diagnostic accuracy by 7.0% under adversarial conditions (88.0% vs. 81.0%) and reduces missed red flag rates by 31%, demonstrating rigorous mitigation of premature closure.

title: An Agentic AI Framework Overcomes Fundamental Limitations of Large Language Models for Glaucoma Detection from Fundus Photography
outcome: Run-to-run reproducibility of LLM glaucoma classification, measured by kappa across repeated runs
effect: LLM-alone Gemini 2.5 Flash varied stochastically between runs (kappa as low as -0.01); the agentic workflow raised consistency to kappa up to 0.96.
quote: Run-to-run consistency rose from near-random (kappa as low as -0.01) to near-perfect (kappa up to 0.96).

title: CliniCARE-Bench: Clinical Calibrated Audit of Medical Reasoning in EHR
outcome: Raw verdict accuracy versus defect-free accuracy (correct verdict without prohibited shortcuts) across agentic systems
effect: Four-way accuracy spans 65.3-76.1%, but defect-free accuracy is 4.8-14.8 points lower and reorders the leaderboard, so raw accuracy overstates investigation quality.
quote: Defect-free accuracy, which credits a verdict only when correct and free of prohibited shortcuts, is 4.8-14.8 points lower and reorders the leaderboard.

title: Same Question, Different Answer? Measuring and Mitigating Prompt Privilege for Equitable AI Access
outcome: Performance consistency across semantically equivalent prompts varying in literacy and prompting expertise
effect: Statistically significant performance disparities between low-literacy and expert-prompting cohorts on MedQA; applying PET eliminated the disparities while preserving semantic fidelity.
quote: Experiments on the MedQA benchmark demonstrate measurable prompt privilege, with statistically significant performance disparities between low-literacy and expert-prompting cohorts.

title: Same Question, Different Answer? Measuring and Mitigating Prompt Privilege for Equitable AI Access
outcome: LLM accuracy on medical questions for low-literacy versus expert-prompting users
effect: Statistically significant performance disparities between low-literacy and expert-prompting cohorts on MedQA (numbers not given in the abstract).
quote: Experiments on the MedQA benchmark demonstrate measurable prompt privilege, with statistically significant performance disparities between low-literacy and expert-prompting cohorts.

title: When Confidence Fails: Overconfidence in LLMs under Uncertainty and Missing Clinical Information
outcome: Alignment of LLM confidence with accuracy under linguistic uncertainty and missing information
effect: Accuracy degraded with increasing uncertainty while confidence stayed misaligned with accuracy, causing a substantial increase in unsafe confident errors (UCER).
quote: Our results reveal a consistent failure mode, i.e., although accuracy degrades under increasing uncertainty, model confidence remains misaligned with accuracy.

title: When Confidence Fails: Overconfidence in LLMs under Uncertainty and Missing Clinical Information
outcome: Ability of LLMs to abstain when the correct answer option was removed
effect: Significant variation across models in abstaining when the correct answer is unavailable; some models persistently produced high-confidence hallucinated answers.
quote: Furthermore, we observe significant variation across models in their ability to abstain when the correct answer is unavailable, with some models persistently producing high confidence hallucinated answers.

title: Coupled Graph--Policy Distillation for Personalized Medication Safety in Older Adults with Multimorbidity
outcome: Strict Success Rate and safety reasoning of guideline-graph-grounded agent versus baseline LLMs
effect: Exceeds strongest proprietary LLM baseline by 53.73 points in Strict Success Rate and 14.63 points in OSRS, with no unsafe recommendations under the automated evaluator.
quote: On the European non-interactive multimorbidity benchmark, it exceeds the strongest proprietary LLM baseline by 53.73 points in Strict Success Rate and 14.63 points in overall safety reasoning score (OSRS), with no unsafe recommendations under the automated evaluator.

title: TAF-MED: Multi-Turn Safety Refusal Collapse in LLMs Under Declared Self-Treatment Intent
outcome: Medication-safety boundary persistence across multi-turn conversations after declared self-treatment intent
effect: 71.6% of conversations contained an UNSAFE response; 61.4% of those beginning with a strictly SAFE response later collapsed to UNSAFE; model-level collapse rates ranged from 24.4% to 96.2%.
quote: Overall, 71.6% of conversations contained an UNSAFE response, and 61.4% of those beginning with a strictly SAFE response later collapsed to UNSAFE; model-level collapse rates ranged from 24.4% to 96.2%.

title: TAF-MED: Multi-Turn Safety Refusal Collapse in LLMs Under Declared Self-Treatment Intent
outcome: Refusal persistence across multi-turn follow-ups after self-treatment intent
effect: 61.4% of conversations beginning with a strictly SAFE response later collapsed to UNSAFE; model collapse rates 24.4% to 96.2%.
quote: Overall, 71.6% of conversations contained an UNSAFE response, and 61.4% of those beginning with a strictly SAFE response later collapsed to UNSAFE; model-level collapse rates ranged from 24.4% to 96.2%.

title: TAF-MED: Multi-Turn Safety Refusal Collapse in LLMs Under Declared Self-Treatment Intent
outcome: Model-ranking stability between first-turn unsafe rate and multi-turn collapse rate
effect: Four of 28 model pairs reversed order between initial unsafe and collapse rates.
quote: Four of 28 model pairs reversed order between initial unsafe and collapse rates.

title: Locally Deployable Small Language Models for Emergency Department Decision Support: A Systematic Benchmark of Fine-Tuning Strategies
outcome: Comparison of fine-tuned open-source SLMs against commercial LLM baselines on ED triage, referral, and diagnosis tasks
effect: LoRA fine-tuned open-source SLMs outperformed Claude Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 baselines on triage level and specialist referral; diagnosis prediction remained challenging for open-source SLMs.
quote: Using 2,083 MIMIC-IV-ED cases and Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 as baselines, we found that LoRA fine-tuned open-source SLMs outperform commercial baselines on triage level prediction and specialist referral recommendation, while diagnosis prediction remains challenging for open-source SLMs.

title: Quantifying the Relationship Between Clinical Safety and Environmental Impact in Therapeutic LLMs
outcome: Environmental cost (energy, carbon, water, abiotic depletion) versus clinical safety score across LLM configurations
effect: 2.61 percentage-point increase in clinical safety score corresponded to about 60-fold increase in estimated energy use per million output tokens; extra test-time compute did not consistently improve safety.
quote: The results indicate a non-linear trade-off at the upper end of the safety distribution: a 2.61 percentage-point increase in clinical safety score corresponded to an approximately 60-fold increase in estimated energy use per million output tokens.
