title: A corpus-specific clinical RAG system matches or outperforms newer frontier LLMs on HealthBench
outcome: HealthBench rubric score of corpus-grounded RAG system versus frontier LLMs without that corpus
effect: VITA ranked first (51.9% vs GPT-5.4 46.1%) on 4,023 questions. On the 500-question subset with newer models and a neutral judge, VITA and GPT-5.5 were statistically indistinguishable; VITA's communication scores were lower.
quote: Here the gap narrowed to parity: VITA and GPT-5.5 were statistically indistinguishable on mean per-question score, while VITA led on points-weighted score and won the most questions.

title: How LLMs Respond to Escalating Delusions: Four Longitudinal Trajectories of Model Behavior
outcome: Recognition and appropriate response to escalating psychosis across a 30-day multi-turn simulated conversation
effect: Four trajectories found: premature medicalization, recognition without safeguarding, delayed and unstable recognition, and delusion co-construction (Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Claude Sonnet 4). Most models failed to recognize or safeguard reliably.
quote: Across model generations and vendors, we identified four response trajectories: (1) premature medicalization and disengagement (Claude Haiku 4.5); (2) recognition without safeguarding, marked by LLM self-sufficiency in offering help (GPT Instant/Thinking); (3) delayed and unstable recognition, marked by late, non-progressive conceptualization (Claude Opus 3/4/4.1, Claude Haiku 3.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 3.1 Pro); and (4) delusion co-construction through active engagement with delusional content (Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Claude Sonnet 4).

title: Do AI chatbots find what experts would? Effects of model, user role, and sample size on study retrieval for medical questions
outcome: Recall of Cochrane included studies by simulated user role (patient, clinician, researcher)
effect: Recall was lowest for the patient role (36.1% ± 29.3%) vs clinician (38.6% ± 28.9%) and researcher (42.8% ± 30.8%), p=2.0e-5; differences were small relative to variability.
quote: The researcher role yielded higher recall than the clinician or patient roles (42.8% $\pm$ 30.8% vs. 38.6% $\pm$ 28.9% vs. 36.1% $\pm$ 29.3%; $p=2.0\times10^{-5}$).

title: Large Language Models Show Metacognitive Sensitivity in Medical Reasoning
outcome: Calibration of LLM confidence against accuracy and evidence strength in diagnostic vignettes
effect: Accuracy 93.5%, mean confidence 78.4%, AUROC2 0.876. Confidence tracked evidence strength and missing information, but errors in moderate, conflicting AT-NCD cases retained more confidence than accuracy justified.
quote: However, errors clustered in moderate, conflicting AT-NCD cases, where the model shifted toward DRCI and retained more confidence than empirical accuracy justified.
sample_unit: trials (45 synthetic vignettes x 3 prompt variants)

title: Characterizing Rhetorical Misalignment in Decision-Making with Language Models
outcome: Rate of harmful decision flips from correct to incorrect after LLM-generated information
effect: LLMs induce an average 2.81% rate of harmful decision flips across different models, where clinician participants change from a correct to an incorrect answer.
quote: By measuring how LLM-generated information affects decisions, we observe that LLMs induce an average 2.81% rate of harmful decision flips across different models, where clinician participants change from a correct to an incorrect answer.

title: Prompting is not enough: supervised baselines and leakage control for measuring shared decision-making with LLMs in pediatric encounters
outcome: Macro kappa of zero-shot LLM versus simpler supervised classifier on the same data
effect: Zero-shot LLM macro kappa 0.139 (95% CI 0.111-0.164) vs supervised classifier 0.227 (0.186-0.262); paired improvement 0.088 (0.051-0.119); stack 0.242.
quote: The supervised classifier reached kappa = 0.227 (0.186-0.262), a paired improvement of 0.088 (0.051-0.119).

title: Prompting is not enough: supervised baselines and leakage control for measuring shared decision-making with LLMs in pediatric encounters
outcome: Sensitivity of reported performance to data splitting unit and leakage of labeled exemplars
effect: Multiple leakage paths identified (sibling recordings split separately, held-out patient labels entering few-shot exemplars); performance sensitive to splitting unit and exemplar placement. No leakage effect numbers reported in abstract.
quote: Reported performance is sensitive to the unit of data splitting and to where labeled exemplars enter the pipeline.

title: Framework for Grounding Healthcare LLMs in a Causal Knowledge Graph: A Cardiovascular Example Pilot
outcome: Effect of knowledge-graph and causal-graph grounding on LLM causal, evidence, unsupported-claim, and intervention accuracy metrics
effect: Integrated grounding (C4) had the best causal edge F1 (0.838), adverse-effect F1 (0.833), evidence accuracy (0.738) and unsupported claim rate (0.114); ungrounded C1 had the highest raw intervention accuracy (0.948).
quote: The metric panel discriminates conditions along interpretable, non-redundant axes: C4 obtains the strongest causal edge F1 (0.838), adverse-effect F1 (0.833), evidence accuracy (0.738), and unsupported claim rate (0.114), while C1 obtains the highest raw intervention accuracy (0.948) with no measurable causal or evidential grounding.

title: ETHOS: Towards a Modular Ethics Framework for Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
outcome: Appropriate abstention by agentic system when safe recommendations cannot be supported
effect: ETHOS appropriately increased abstention when safe recommendations could not be supported; no numbers in abstract.
quote: Results show that ETHOS improves decision reliability by detecting incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and appropriately increasing abstention when safe recommendations cannot be supported.

title: ETHOS: Towards a Modular Ethics Framework for Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
outcome: Automated runtime quality checks
effect: No numerical results reported; ETHOS improved decision reliability by detecting incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence.
quote: Results show that ETHOS improves decision reliability by detecting incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and appropriately increasing abstention when safe recommendations cannot be supported.

title: ETHOS: Towards a Modular Ethics Framework for Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
outcome: Decision reliability of hepatology multi-agent system with runtime ethics oversight suppressing or revising failing outputs
effect: ETHOS improved decision reliability by detecting incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and increasing abstention when safe recommendations could not be supported; no numbers in abstract.
quote: Results show that ETHOS improves decision reliability by detecting incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and appropriately increasing abstention when safe recommendations cannot be supported.

title: ETHOS: Towards a Modular Ethics Framework for Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
outcome: Out-of-scope detection and abstention
effect: No numerical results reported; ETHOS detected incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and increased abstention when recommendations lacked support.
quote: Results show that ETHOS improves decision reliability by detecting incomplete, inconsistent, or out-of-scope evidence and appropriately increasing abstention when safe recommendations cannot be supported.

title: Toward Better Assessment of LLMs' Performance in Clinical Error Detection
outcome: Pairwise discrimination versus aggregate F1 for LLM clinical error detection across 4 test sets and 3 languages
effect: 13 of 15 models fell below random pairwise discrimination despite moderate-looking F1 scores; F1 and pairwise accuracy move in opposite directions under the same bias, so F1 ranking may favor the weakest discriminators.
quote: In particular, evaluating 15 diverse LLMs on 4 standardized clinical error-detection test sets across 3 languages, we find that 13 of 15 models fall below the level of random pairwise discrimination, even while achieving F1 scores that standard practice would read as moderate.
sample_unit: LLMs evaluated on 4 clinical error-detection test sets

title: Institution-Specific LLM Prompting Recovers PHI That De-identification Systems and Their Gold Standards Both Miss
outcome: Reference standard annotation gaps found by LLM outputs and re-annotation
effect: LLM outputs surfaced 414 candidate annotation gaps; re-annotation confirmed 227 PHI spans missing from the gold standard; recall against corrected standard 0.981.
quote: LLM outputs surfaced 414~candidate annotation gaps; re-annotation confirmed 227~PHI spans, against which the final prompt reached recall=0.981 (F1=0.907$\pm$0.002).
sample_unit: annotated pediatric oncology notes (5,322 PHI spans)

title: Institution-Specific LLM Prompting Recovers PHI That De-identification Systems and Their Gold Standards Both Miss
outcome: LLM F1 for de-identification compared with purpose-built systems on same notes
effect: Best LLM F1=0.918±0.001 vs. Stanford TiDE 0.779; advantages concentrated in contextual categories.
quote: LLMs outperformed the purpose-built systems (best F1=0.918$\pm$0.001 vs.\ TiDE 0.779), with advantages concentrated in contextual categories.
sample_unit: annotated pediatric oncology notes (5,322 PHI spans)

title: Institution-Specific LLM Prompting Recovers PHI That De-identification Systems and Their Gold Standards Both Miss
outcome: Recovery of missed institutional PHI after institution-specific prompt adaptation
effect: Naming the missed categories recovered 79% (48/61) of them; discouraging over-redaction restored precision.
quote: Naming the missed categories recovered 79\% (48/61) of them, and discouraging over-redaction restored precision.
sample_unit: annotated pediatric oncology notes (5,322 PHI spans)

title: LLMs for Medical Consultation Are Evaluated Too Late: The Preformulation Gap
outcome: Self-care advice given before any patient answer in multi-turn vignettes with vague or minimized concerns
effect: Self-care or home-management advice before any patient answer appeared in 9 of 12 baseline case-model cells and 0 of 12 instruction cells.
quote: Self-care or home-management advice before any patient answer appeared in 9 of 12 baseline case-model cells and 0 of 12 instruction cells, while structured handoff summaries appeared in 0 of 12 and 10 of 12 cells, respectively.

title: Same Facts, Different Updates: Inference Setup Shapes LLM Behavior in Medical Allocation
outcome: Change in allocation probabilities between paired-context and independent inference after one added patient sentence
effect: Across three of four models, paired-context and independent-inference runs showed different probability shifts, often in opposite directions, when new information was provided.
quote: Across three of four tested models, the paired-context and independent-inference experiments have different probability shifts, often in opposite directions (in favor of Person B vs. in favor of Person A) when new information is provided.

title: FairGlucose: A CGM Fairness Benchmark Reveals Subgroup Disparities Hidden in Population-Level Validation
outcome: Whether aggregate external validation conceals subgroup performance disparities in CGM glucose forecasting
effect: Aggregate OOD metrics appeared stable (~1.0) while subgroup ratios ranged 0.8 to 1.4; T1D showed 6 mg/dL higher error than T2D (p<0.001), across all 33 models.
quote: Aggregate out-of-distribution metrics appear stable (approximately 1.0), yet subgroup-level ratios range from 0.8 to 1.4, with T1D patients showing 6 mg/dL higher prediction error than T2D (p < 0.001).

title: FairGlucose: A CGM Fairness Benchmark Reveals Subgroup Disparities Hidden in Population-Level Validation
outcome: Whether population-level validation reveals subgroup performance gaps versus subgroup-disaggregated analysis
effect: Population-level external validation concealed subgroup disparities (ratios 0.8 to 1.4; T1D vs T2D gap of 6 mg/dL, p<0.001) persisting across all 33 models.
quote: These findings establish that population-level validation alone is insufficient for equity assessment of digital health AI, motivating subgroup-disaggregated reporting as a default standard.

title: A knowledge-guided agentic framework for mitigating patient-context ambiguity in health queries
outcome: Diagnosis retrieval accuracy with vs without acquiring missing patient context before answering
effect: Framework increased exact Top-1 accuracy by at least 57.1 percentage points and selective exact Recall@5 by at least 77.7 points across five models versus direct prompting.
quote: In diagnosis retrieval, it increased overall exact Top-1 accuracy by at least 57.1 percentage points and selective exact Recall@5 by at least 77.7 percentage points across the five evaluated models compared with direct prompting.
sample_unit: queries (1,034 symptom queries plus 487 dietary-safety queries)

title: When Vocabulary Comprehension Fails Clinical Reasoning: Evaluating Therapy Bots' Safety Risks for Generation Alpha
outcome: Clinical risk calibration and crisis recognition in multi-turn Gen Alpha mental health conversations
effect: Models understand 76-82% of vocabulary but correctly calibrate only 64-72% of clinical risk; 34% baseline miss rate; three or more failure patterns yield 94% miss rates.
quote: Across evaluations of LLM architectures underlying therapy apps and general chatbots - Claude, GPT-4o, Llama-3.1 - models understand 76-82% of vocabulary but correctly calibrate only 64-72% of clinical risk, creating a 10-14 percentage point (pp) vocabulary-comprehension gap (p<.001, d>0.48) absent in human therapists (3pp, p=.22).

title: When Vocabulary Comprehension Fails Clinical Reasoning: Evaluating Therapy Bots' Safety Risks for Generation Alpha
outcome: Acceptance of symptom minimization by AI across conversation turns
effect: Minimization acceptance failure pattern produced a 43pp gap, the largest of six identified failure patterns.
quote: We identify six failure patterns: sarcasm masking (29pp), minimization acceptance (43pp), informal style bias (24pp), risk-stratified ambiguity (19pp), semantic drift (19pp), context-dependent violence (7pp).

title: When Vocabulary Comprehension Fails Clinical Reasoning: Evaluating Therapy Bots' Safety Risks for Generation Alpha
outcome: Model performance on non-standard youth slang, colloquialisms, and informal style
effect: Vocabulary-comprehension gap of 10-14pp, widening with ambiguity (7pp to 18pp); informal style bias 24pp.
quote: The gap is architecturally consistent and widens with ambiguity (7pp -> 18pp).

title: When Vocabulary Comprehension Fails Clinical Reasoning: Evaluating Therapy Bots' Safety Risks for Generation Alpha
outcome: Comparison of LLM performance with human therapists on risk calibration gap
effect: Human therapists showed a 3pp gap (p=.22) versus 10-14pp for LLMs (p<.001); only heavy scaffolding achieved human performance at 6.4x cost.
quote: Lightweight mitigations fail; only heavy scaffolding achieves human performance (6.4x cost).

title: Inhibitory Attention for Clinical Long-Context Reasoning: Characterizing and Mitigating Lost-in-the-Middle Effects in EHR Processing
outcome: LLM accuracy on EHR instructions by position of relevant information within long context
effect: 21.9 percentage-point gap between peak accuracy (59.5%) and trough accuracy (37.6%); 67.8% of reference answers fall inside the trough (10th-90th percentile of the EHR timeline).
quote: Across 2,196 instruction-response pairs and six language models, we observe a 21.9 percentage-point gap between peak accuracy (59.5%, 95% CI [46.3, 71.0], 20-30% decile) and trough accuracy (37.6% [23.2, 52.5] at 70-80%); 67.8% of reference answers fall between the 10th and 90th percentiles of the EHR timeline, inside the CLitM trough.

title: An ambiguity taxonomy for evaluating large language model performance on clinical registry abstraction: a multi-site prospective study
outcome: LLM answer accuracy against abstractor consensus on local EMR data for registry questions
effect: 87% of LLM answers exactly matched consensus, 2% partially, 9% did not; mean question-level accuracy 91.5% (SD 13.4%); human inter-rater agreement about 98%.
quote: In validation, human inter-rater agreement was approximately 98\% while 87\% of LLM answers exactly matched consensus, 2\% partially, and 9\% did not.

title: Dissecting Neuro-Symbolic Quality Assurance for Synthetic Oncology Data Generation
outcome: Rejection of invalid synthetic records by automated symbolic gate versus ungated generation
effect: Ungated, 29.9% of records contain schema failures and 20.1% contain clinically invalid staging. Schema validation rejects 148 of 512 records, ontology grounding a further 24, staging-logic none.
quote: Ungated, 29.9% of records contain schema failures and 20.1% contain clinically invalid staging.

title: Dissecting Neuro-Symbolic Quality Assurance for Synthetic Oncology Data Generation
outcome: Effect of retrieval augmentation on gate compliance across generators
effect: Retrieval improves gate compliance for one generator by 12.5 percentage points, has no measurable effect for a second, and collapses output in a third.
quote: Retrieval augmentation is strongly model-dependent: it improves gate compliance for one generator by 12.5 percentage points, has no measurable effect for a second, and collapses output in a third.

title: Development and Feasibility Evaluation of an Edge AI as Medical Device System for Breast Cancer Multidisciplinary Team Meetings
outcome: Treatment recommendation accuracy and concordant interventions versus proprietary cloud comparator
effect: MedGemma-RAG identified 2.3 times more MDT-concordant interventions than the proprietary cloud comparator (p = 0.020), with no significant difference in overall accuracy.
quote: MedGemma-RAG identified 2.3 times more MDT-concordant interventions than a proprietary cloud comparator (p = 0.020), with no significant difference in overall accuracy.

title: SDoH-Aware Narrative Anchoring Bias in Medical LLMs for Trustworthy Clinical Decision Support
outcome: Answer stability across medically equivalent SDoH-aware patient persona narratives with fixed answer key
effect: Narrative sensitivity error persisted in all models; the lowest error (Qwen2.5 7B) was still 31.67 percent. Best accuracy 56.33 percent; best correct consistency 40.33 percent.
quote: Even so, narrative sensitivity remains, with the lowest error still at 31.67 percent.
sample_unit: clinical cases (8,100 model responses across three prompting conditions)

title: Proxy reliance in large language model decisions is uncalibrated to predictive evidence
outcome: Causal effect of proxy attributes on LLM clinical-ranking decisions versus warranted reliance
effect: Under neutral labels every model relies on proxies with no information. Informative proxies draw over-reliance, warranted and under-reliance. Reliance severely undertracks the evidence.
quote: Under neutral labels every model relies on proxies with no information.

title: Proxy reliance in large language model decisions is uncalibrated to predictive evidence
outcome: Whether LLMs rely on proxy features in line with their predictive evidence
effect: Reliance on proxies is uncalibrated to predictive evidence; social-label suppression is fragile, since in-context examples raise reliance above zero in every model. Accuracy-based evaluation detects none of this.
quote: Two findings explain this.

title: TSWAP: A Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Thai Wellness Advisor
outcome: Out-of-scope and drug-dosing responses with vs without safety prompt
effect: Without the safety prompt, the backend model family produced a full drug-dosing schedule and complied with out-of-scope requests (71-question no-retrieval probe).
quote: We release the first Thai traditional-medicine/wellness retrieval benchmark (50 questions with gold document IDs; Recall@5 = 0.88), production QA logs (91.1% test-retest pass over 259 cases), and a 71-question frontier no-retrieval probe showing what each grounding pillar contributes: without the safety prompt the backend model family produced a full drug-dosing schedule and complied with out-of-scope requests, and without the knowledge base it produced zero verifiable provider recommendations.

title: TSWAP: A Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Thai Wellness Advisor
outcome: Verifiable provider recommendations with vs without knowledge-base grounding
effect: Without the knowledge base, the model produced zero verifiable provider recommendations; forced-retrieval routing was necessary for reliable grounding.
quote: We further report two transferable deployment findings: English-calibrated 4-bit AWQ quantization corrupts Thai tone marks, and forced-retrieval routing is necessary for reliable grounding.

title: TSWAP: A Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Thai Wellness Advisor
outcome: Test-retest reproducibility of production QA cases
effect: 91.1% test-retest pass over 259 cases.
quote: We release the first Thai traditional-medicine/wellness retrieval benchmark (50 questions with gold document IDs; Recall@5 = 0.88), production QA logs (91.1% test-retest pass over 259 cases), and a 71-question frontier no-retrieval probe showing what each grounding pillar contributes: without the safety prompt the backend model family produced a full drug-dosing schedule and complied with out-of-scope requests, and without the knowledge base it produced zero verifiable provider recommendations.

title: TSWAP: A Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Thai Wellness Advisor
outcome: Compliance with out-of-scope requests after removing the safety prompt
effect: In the 71-question frontier no-retrieval probe, removing the safety prompt led the backend model family to produce a full drug-dosing schedule and comply with out-of-scope requests.
quote: We release the first Thai traditional-medicine/wellness retrieval benchmark (50 questions with gold document IDs; Recall@5 = 0.88), production QA logs (91.1% test-retest pass over 259 cases), and a 71-question frontier no-retrieval probe showing what each grounding pillar contributes: without the safety prompt the backend model family produced a full drug-dosing schedule and complied with out-of-scope requests, and without the knowledge base it produced zero verifiable provider recommendations.

title: Improving O-RADS Risk Stratification from Ultrasound Reports: A Comparative Evaluation of Hybrid versus End-to-End LLM Reasoning Strategies
outcome: O-RADS classification accuracy of LLM strategies versus original clinical reports against expert consensus
effect: Hybrid Gemini 3.6 Flash accuracy 99.2% (387/390) vs original clinical reports 87.7% (342/390) and end-to-end LLM strategies 65.6% to 95.9%.
quote: Its performance surpassed that of original clinical reports (accuracy, 87.7% [342 of 390]; weighted kappa = 0.94; 95% CI: 0.91-0.96) and end-to-end LLM strategies (accuracy range, 65.6% [256 of 390] to 95.9% [374 of 390]).

title: Gated Activation Steering for Reducing Sycophancy & Hallucination in Medical Question Answering
outcome: Unsupported claims (hallucination) in clinical QA grounded in EHR context
effect: Hallucination described as introducing information unsupported by context; the gated steering component was designed to mitigate it. No hallucination rates given in the abstract.
quote: Hallucination can introduce information that is unsupported by the context, while sycophancy can cause a model to abandon a previously correct answer when challenged by the user.

title: Neurosymbolic Alignment for Physiologically-Safe Clinical Language Models
outcome: Safety score (CSS) under synthetic EHR-style input noise
effect: 84.2% CSS retained under synthetic EHR-style noise, versus 90.8% CSS on clean benchmark inputs (a drop of about 6.6 pp).
quote: Under synthetic EHR-style noise, 84.2% CSS is retained.

title: Right Diagnoses, Decorative Reasoning:A Perturbation Audit of Medical Chain-of-Thought
outcome: Chain-of-thought response to clinically motivated input and chain perturbations
effect: Chain-Decoupling Rate 72.9% panel-wide on clinically meaningful destructive edits; chain corruption leaves accuracy unchanged; removing CoT prompting does not reduce accuracy.
quote: the Chain-Decoupling Rate (CDR; chain does not register the edit and the answer does not flip) is 72.9% panel-wide on clinically meaningful destructive edits, chain corruption leaves accuracy unchanged, and removing CoT prompting does not reduce accuracy.
sample_unit: LLMs evaluated on four medical QA benchmarks

title: Standalone LLM and a Pre-specified Agentic Pipeline for Explaining ICU Mortality Predictions: a Feasibility Study on the eICU Demo Dataset
outcome: Guideline grounding of LLM ICU mortality explanations, agentic guideline-checking pipeline vs standalone LLM
effect: Among 14 overlapping cases, guideline grounding was 0.762 (agentic) vs 0.143 (standalone); 1 standalone explanation had outcome leakage vs none for agentic. Standalone had higher SHAP alignment (Jaccard 0.171 vs 0.077).
quote: Clinically, the results suggest that agentic decomposition may improve safety-relevant grounding and patient-specific detail, but it should be paired with attribution-based checks before use in high-stakes risk explanation.

title: Evaluating AI Generated Summaries for Cancer Patients
outcome: Whether expert clinician review of AI cancer summaries identifies inaccuracies and omissions
effect: Expert review identified limitations in generated summaries, such as occasional omissions and minor inaccuracies, which were used to improve prompts, grounding, and guardrails.
quote: Some limitations were identified in the generated summaries e.g., occasional omissions and minor inaccuracies.

title: MA-RAG: Multi-Agent Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Query-Driven Summarization of Longitudinal Parkinson's Disease Assessments
outcome: Fact precision and hallucination rate of grounded multi-agent RAG versus non-grounded baselines
effect: MA-RAG increased Fact Precision up to 122% (0.436 to 0.990) and reduced Hallucination Rate by up to 98% (0.564 to 0.010) versus Traditional, RAG-only, and Single-agent RAG baselines.
quote: Compared to Traditional, RAG-only, and Single-agent RAG baselines, MA-RAG substantially improves factual correctness, achieving up to a 122% relative increase in Fact Precision (from 0.436 to 0.990) and reducing the Hallucination Rate by up to 98% (from 0.564 to 0.010), while consistently receiving top ratings from clinical experts for organization and clinical usefulness.

title: When Patients Cut In: Extending Clinical Conversational AI Safety to Interruptions
outcome: Preservation of clinically required content after simulated patient interruptions in voice-agent transcripts
effect: Competitive FAQ interruption produced 30/30 provision-coverage failures for all four models (Wilson 95% CI 88.6-100.0%); baseline 0/30 for three models, 4/30 for Llama.
quote: Rankings differ across cells, and competitive FAQ interruption produced 30/30 provision-coverage failures for all four models (Wilson 95% CI: 88.6-100.0%; baseline 0/30 for three, 4/30 for Llama).
sample_unit: simulated interruption conversation transcripts (30 per condition in reported cells)

title: Review Before Trust: Source-Grounded Integrity Gates for AI-Assisted Personal Health Records
outcome: Share of LLM-extracted lab candidates admitted by schema, packet-level, and quotation/row-level automated checks
effect: Of 97 numeric candidates, schema validation accepted 97, the earlier packet-level check accepted 94, and the hardened policy admitted 72 and retained 25 for review. Correctness of the admitted candidates was not evaluated.
quote: The reports produce 97 numeric candidates: schema validation accepts all 97, an earlier packet-level evidence check accepts 94, and the hardened quotation- and row-level policy admits 72 while retaining 25 for review.
sample_unit: numeric candidates extracted from laboratory PDF reports

title: Review Before Trust: Source-Grounded Integrity Gates for AI-Assisted Personal Health Records
outcome: Source-grounded admission of generated candidates
effect: Hardened quotation- and row-level policy admitted 72 of 97 numeric candidates and retained 25 for review; schema validation accepted all 97.
quote: The reports produce 97 numeric candidates: schema validation accepts all 97, an earlier packet-level evidence check accepts 94, and the hardened quotation- and row-level policy admits 72 while retaining 25 for review.
sample_unit: numeric candidates extracted from laboratory PDF reports

title: GPAgentBench-2K: Benchmarking Large Language Model Agents in Complex Clinical Action Space
outcome: Safety constraint violations by LLM agents in high-risk primary-care cases
effect: Even frontier models with the highest diagnosis accuracy violate safety constraints in over half of high-risk cases; performance degrades as action space scales.
quote: Crucially, we uncover a clinical quality-safety gap: even frontier models with the highest diagnosis accuracy violate safety constraints in over half of high-risk cases.

title: Medical Causal Hypothesis Verification with Large Language Models
outcome: Validity of scientific articles and evidence cited by LLMs when verifying medical causal hypotheses
effect: Eight LLMs showed strong recall but often performed poorly at providing valid scientific articles and evidence for support and at rejecting unsupported hypotheses (1,067 annotation points, 17 hypotheses).
quote: Our analysis shows that while LLMs exhibit strong recall, they often perform poorly at providing valid scientific articles and evidence for support and at rejecting unsupported hypotheses.

title: NSIDDx: A Design Framework for Neuro-Symbolic, Practitioner-First Differential Diagnosis in Low-Resource Settings
outcome: Confidence and verifiability of LLM+RAG differential diagnosis outputs on uncommon presentations
effect: LLM+RAG pipeline produced confident outputs that were frequently unverifiable and resistant to clinician interrogation; no numbers in abstract.
quote: We evaluate an LLM+rare-disease-RAG pipeline across two cohorts and show that the paradigm produces confident outputs that are frequently unverifiable and systematically resistant to clinician interrogation.
sample_unit: cases (two cohorts, size not reported in abstract)

title: NSIDDx: A Design Framework for Neuro-Symbolic, Practitioner-First Differential Diagnosis in Low-Resource Settings
outcome: Traceability and verifiability of LLM+RAG diagnostic outputs by clinicians
effect: Outputs were frequently unverifiable and resistant to clinician interrogation; no numbers in abstract.
quote: We evaluate an LLM+rare-disease-RAG pipeline across two cohorts and show that the paradigm produces confident outputs that are frequently unverifiable and systematically resistant to clinician interrogation.
sample_unit: cases (two cohorts, size not reported in abstract)

title: How Does LGBTQIA+ Identity Affect LLM Behavior? Implications for Requirements Engineering of Mental Health AI Systems
outcome: Change in ChatGPT mental health responses when patient LGBTQIA+ or straight identity is disclosed
effect: Identity disclosure did not substantially affect completeness or supportive guidance. LGBTQIA+ responses had substantially more identity acknowledgment, contextual expansion, unsupported assumptions and occasional stereotypical reasoning than the other two conditions.
quote: Our findings indicate that LGBTQIA+ identity disclosure did not substantially affect response completeness or supportive guidance.

title: How Does LGBTQIA+ Identity Affect LLM Behavior? Implications for Requirements Engineering of Mental Health AI Systems
outcome: Stereotypical reasoning and unsupported assumptions in responses to LGBTQIA+-identified users
effect: LGBTQIA+-explicit responses showed substantially more unsupported assumptions and occasional stereotypical reasoning than the no-disclosure and straight-disclosure conditions.
quote: However, responses in the LGBTQIA+-explicit condition presented substantially more identity acknowledgment, contextual expansion, unsupported assumptions, and occasional stereotypical reasoning compared to both other conditions.

title: Investigating Linear Probe Robustness to Linguistic Register, Medical Specialty, and Corpus Shifts in Medical QA
outcome: Linear probe AUROC change under register, specialty, and corpus shifts
effect: Truth direction largely robust to writing style (mean Δ_register ≈ 0.10 AUROC) and specialty (Δ ≈ 0.03), but degrades by 0.12 AUROC on MMLU-medical and 0.21 on MedMCQA.
quote: Probing four open-weight LLMs (2--8B), we find that the truth direction is largely robust to writing style (mean $Δ_\text{register} \approx 0.10$ AUROC on held-out facts) and to medical specialty ($Δ_\text{specialty} \approx 0.03$), but degrades unevenly across corpora: by $0.12$ AUROC on MMLU-medical and by $0.21$ on MedMCQA, roughly twice the register gap.
sample_unit: MedQA entries (each rewritten into four styles)

title: Improving Health Literacy through Lay Summarization of Radiological Reports: An Evaluation of BioNER and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
outcome: Quality, factual consistency and readability of lay summaries with versus without retrieval grounding
effect: RAG alone offered no benefit and could introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms; RAG plus NER degraded few-shot performance but improved readability when fine-tuned.
quote: Results show that NER consistently improves readability and overall quality, while RAG alone offers no benefit and can introduce hallucinations from irrelevant retrieved terms.

title: Counterfactual Fairness Audits of Multi-Step Clinical LLM Agents Require a Measured Per-Action Instability Floor
outcome: Action instability when identical condition re-run ten times across vignettes
effect: Identical re-runs moved agent action in 8.7% of outcome-vignette cells; instability varied eightfold from 0.022 (ICU escalation) to 0.179 (controlled-substance caution); second model pooled floor 6.7%.
quote: Re-running an identical condition ten times over sixteen vignettes (same narrative, same descriptor string, nothing varied) moved a clinical agent's action in 8.7% of outcome-vignette cells, and instability was heterogeneous across actions by a factor of eight, from 0.022 for ICU escalation to 0.179 for controlled-substance caution.

title: Counterfactual Fairness Audits of Multi-Step Clinical LLM Agents Require a Measured Per-Action Instability Floor
outcome: Counterfactual demographic flip rates versus run-to-run instability floor
effect: No demographic contrast was distinguishable from the 8.7% instability floor; counterfactual flip rates uninterpretable without a per-action floor. Majority vote over five draws removed 39% of the floor.
quote: No demographic contrast in our data was distinguishable from that floor.

title: Beyond Majority Vote: Multi-Perspective Adjudication for Medical Hallucination Detection
outcome: Factual errors found by first-pass annotation versus multi-perspective adjudication in chatbot responses
effect: First-pass annotators frequently missed factual errors later validated by adjudicators; adjudicators also disagreed with each other, so multi-pass adjudication improves benchmark completeness but still needs judgment and expertise.
quote: First-pass annotators frequently miss factual errors later validated by adjudicators.

title: Will My Assistant Remember My Allergy? What Personal LLM Assistants Forget When Conversation Memory Is Compressed
outcome: Retention of a passing-mentioned allergy under KV-cache compression, with question hidden versus known
effect: When the question is hidden until after compression, a passing allergy mention survives 0-1% of the time versus 97% with full memory; prior benchmarks report retention at a 20% budget.
quote: Hide the question until after compression and the advantage vanishes: on PA-Bench, 100 assistant conversations we construct, an allergy mentioned in passing survives to the question that needs it 0--1% of the time, against 97% with full memory.

title: Will My Assistant Remember My Allergy? What Personal LLM Assistants Forget When Conversation Memory Is Compressed
outcome: Loss of safety-critical facts when conversation memory is compressed or truncated
effect: Training-free eviction policies fail to rank the allergy fact highly enough; allergy survives 0-1% of the time versus 97% with full memory, and the budget needed to keep it is too large to be worth compressing.
quote: Hide the question until after compression and the advantage vanishes: on PA-Bench, 100 assistant conversations we construct, an allergy mentioned in passing survives to the question that needs it 0--1% of the time, against 97% with full memory.

title: Beyond the Flag: Clinical Framing Closes the Moderation Gap in Suicide Risk Measurement
outcome: Moderation API recovery of graded suicide risk severity versus high/low risk separation
effect: Moderation APIs reached 0.860 high-risk F1 but only 0.395 macro F1 for severity, and over-predicted the most severe category.
quote: Vendor moderation APIs separate low- from high-severity posts well (0.860 high-risk F1) but measure severity poorly (0.395 macro F1), systematically over-predicting the most severe category.

title: Beyond the Flag: Clinical Framing Closes the Moderation Gap in Suicide Risk Measurement
outcome: Effect of expert-authored clinical framing on LLM suicide severity classification
effect: Clinically grounded zero-shot prompting reached 0.562 macro F1 versus 0.395 for moderation APIs; expert-authored framing was the effective lever, not fine-tuning, reasoning, or multi-agent aggregation.
quote: Clinically grounded zero-shot prompting recovers much of that gap (0.562 macro F1), and expert-authored framing (not fine-tuning, added reasoning, or naive multi-agent aggregation) is the effective lever.

title: SIFTING: A Novel LLM-Based Framework for Structured and Transparent Information Extraction from Clinical Free-Text Reports, with Application to Tumor Staging in Lung Cancer
outcome: Extraction accuracy against expert-created reference standard
effect: SIFTING-T-stage achieved an accuracy of 90% (95% CI: 84-95) against the reference standard, comparable to the largest reasoning LLMs.
quote: SIFTING-T-stage achieved an accuracy of 90% (95% CI: 84-95) against the reference standard.

title: Automated Chest CT Protocol Selection via Large Language Model Derived Text Embeddings from Imaging Request Text
outcome: LLM protocol accuracy versus radiologists on 300 cases with expert consensus
effect: LLM overall accuracy 80% versus 83% for radiologists, no significant difference (p = 0.263); LLM exceeded radiologists for some challenging categories.
quote: On 300 independent cases with expert consensus, the LLM reached an overall accuracy of 80% versus 83% for radiologists, with no significant difference (p = 0.263).

title: Delusions and Harms Associated with AI Chatbot Use: Early Evidence from 185 Real-World Reports
outcome: Chatbot validation of delusions and suicide outcomes in self-reported chatbot-associated mental health harms
effect: Delusional beliefs in 102 of 185 reports (55.1%); chatbot validation of beliefs in 50/102 (49.0%); four second-hand reports described death by suicide.
quote: Four second-hand reports described death by suicide.

title: Auditable Emergency Triage for Maternal and Newborn Care in India
outcome: Emergency recall, missed emergencies, and over-escalation rate of LLM triage
effect: Recall rose from 0.565 to 0.810 and F1 from 0.606 to 0.702 with the new system; in deployment, over-escalation rate was 17.8%, with no increase in missed emergencies.
quote: The over-escalation rate has been 17.8%, without any increase in missed emergencies.

title: Auditable Emergency Triage for Maternal and Newborn Care in India
outcome: Emergency-triage recall and F1 with an interpretable, rule-based pipeline
effect: Recall increased from 0.565 to 0.810 and F1 from 0.606 to 0.702; structured rules drove most accuracy gains.
quote: We show that the new system raised recall from 0.565 to 0.810 and F1 from 0.606 to 0.702, with structured rules driving most of the accuracy gains while the decomposition provides auditability: clinical experts can inspect each stage of the new system to see whether the query was mistranslated, symptoms were incorrectly extracted, patient context was wrongly inferred, or the necessary rules were missing.

title: Auditable Emergency Triage for Maternal and Newborn Care in India
outcome: over-escalation and missed emergencies
effect: The over-escalation rate was 17.8%, with no increase in missed emergencies.
quote: The over-escalation rate has been 17.8%, without any increase in missed emergencies.

title: Towards a Deterministic Math Solver for Clinical Language Models
outcome: Accuracy of clinical calculator results from direct model arithmetic versus solver hand-off
effect: Direct model arithmetic reached 72.02% (7B) and 83.47% (32B); solver hand-off gave 75.31% (7B, not reliably better) and 90.53% (32B, +7.05 points).
quote: With formulas and gold variables supplied and both routes reading the whole note, handing off to the solver is not a reliable advantage at 7B (75.31% against 72.02%, a paired +3.29 points with a 95% calculator-cluster interval of [-3.49, 10.38]) but is one at 32B (90.53% against 83.47%, +7.05 [0.47, 14.60], clear of zero).

title: Can LLMs Follow Medical Expert Logic? A Benchmark for Hierarchical Logical Consistency in Risk-of-Bias Assessment
outcome: Benchmark versus end-to-end logical consistency of LLMs in risk-of-bias assessment
effect: Top model reached 98.88% Atomic Consistency but end-to-end consistency collapsed to 45.13%; several open-weight models fell to nearly 0%.
quote: Experiments on 10 state-of-the-art LLMs reveal a catastrophic Error Compounding Effect: despite the top model reaching 98.88% Atomic Consistency, its end-to-end consistency collapses to 45.13%, with several open-weight architectures plummeting to nearly 0%.

title: Can LLMs Follow Medical Expert Logic? A Benchmark for Hierarchical Logical Consistency in Risk-of-Bias Assessment
outcome: Failure to deduce correct outcomes from retrieved evidence and blind guess rates
effect: Even with high-quality evidence retrieved, models failed to deduce correct outcomes in 18.63-40.05% of cases; Blind Guess Rates reached 48.28%.
quote: We further uncover a systematic evidence-reasoning gap: even when models retrieve high-quality evidence, they fail to deduce correct outcomes in 18.63-40.05% of cases, while Blind Guess Rates reach 48.28%.

title: A decision-basis contract for auditable LLM-assisted medical billing verification: deterministic rules, verbatim evidence, and fail-closed abstention
outcome: Outcome agreement versus baseline
effect: Outcome agreement varied across models and showed no consistent advantage over the baseline.
quote: Outcome agreement varied across models and showed no consistent advantage over the baseline.

title: A decision-basis contract for auditable LLM-assisted medical billing verification: deterministic rules, verbatim evidence, and fail-closed abstention
outcome: Missing information identification
effect: Explicit documentation requirements improved identification of missing information for all four models.
quote: Explicit documentation requirements improved identification of missing information for all four models.

title: A decision-basis contract for auditable LLM-assisted medical billing verification: deterministic rules, verbatim evidence, and fail-closed abstention
outcome: Unsupported judgments detected
effect: Correct raw judgments lacking valid evidence were converted to incomplete decision-basis entries.
quote: The evidence gate also exposed cases in which correct raw judgments lacked valid evidence and were converted to incomplete decision-basis entries.

title: MedRoundsQA: A Persona and Difficulty Aware Evaluation for Multi-Turn Medical Consultations
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLM doctor agents across simulated patient personas by education level
effect: Patient persona differences shifted diagnosis accuracy by about 7-8 points from lowest to highest education, indicating equity risks.
quote: (iii) patient persona differences can shift diagnosis accuracy by about 7-8 points (lowest to highest education), highlighting equity risks that single-turn benchmarks miss.

title: MedRoundsQA: A Persona and Difficulty Aware Evaluation for Multi-Turn Medical Consultations
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy drop from single-turn benchmark to multi-turn consultation
effect: Moving from single-turn diagnosis to multi-turn consultations caused degradations of roughly 13-39 points, showing single-turn benchmarks overstate competence.
quote: (i) moving from a single-turn diagnosis on the standardized records to multi-turn consultations causes large degradations of roughly 13-39 points
sample_unit: board-exam cases (converted to 24-slot records and simulated dialogues)

title: Tasks over Application Manuals: Revealing Gaps in Long-Horizon Procedural Reasoning for Language Models
outcome: Exact-match accuracy on long-horizon ICD-10-CM coding and sentencing tasks versus existing short-horizon benchmarks
effect: Best exact-match performance with GPT-5 was 1% on ICD-10-CM coding and 15.5% on sentencing tasks, suggesting existing benchmarks overestimate LLM ability.
quote: These results show that current benchmarks may overestimate LLM reasoning ability and miss a key challenge: reliably following long, rule-based procedures.

title: Anchoring Clinical Events in Time: UID-Preserving Multimodal Reconstruction and Source-Grounded Adjudication
outcome: Temporal agreement and event recovery with versus without structured-evidence source-row grounding
effect: GLM 5.2 multimodal revision improved temporal agreement over text-only without reducing event recovery; adjudication favored multimodal for GLM 5.2 but not DeepSeek V3.2; other models showed smaller gains.
quote: Ablations showed that UIDs primarily preserve event retention, whereas source-row linkage supports temporal placement.

title: Hindsight Bias in Clinical Temporal Reasoning: How Future Data Exposure Affects Large Language Model Judgment
outcome: Hindsight-bias metrics and accuracy with future data truncated versus full timeline exposure
effect: Full timeline exposure produced consistent hindsight-sensitive shifts across four LLMs; temporal masking reduced bias without lowering accuracy. Numeric results not reported in the abstract.
quote: Across GPT 5.6 Sol, Gemma 4, GLM 5.2, and Opus 5, full timeline exposure produces consistent hindsight-sensitive shifts, while temporal masking reduces bias without lowering accuracy.

title: Asclepius: An Adaptive Harness for Long-Horizon Clinical Agents
outcome: Agent completeness and timeliness of critical actions in simulated ED shift
effect: Current agents reach correct diagnosis in most cases yet fail to deliver complete and timely critical actions, revealing an execution gap.
quote: On CES, current agents reach the correct diagnosis in most cases yet fail to deliver complete and timely critical actions, revealing an execution gap.

title: Four Ledgers, Not One Score: Responsible Communication of LLM-Judge Calibration in Biomedical ML
outcome: Validity of reference standard: planted keys versus human dispositions and detector outputs
effect: Scoring imported plant keys yields 22/(22+9)=0.710 and 22/(22+79)=0.218, which are proposal-confirmation yield and ledger composition, not judge precision and recall; only 3 reviewed targets double annotated.
quote: A direct audit identity shows that these values are proposal-confirmation yield and submitted-ledger composition, not judge precision and recall, because no independent detector realization was preserved for the audited proposals in the available records.
sample_unit: targets (synthetic care-handoff documents with planted error cards)

title: Medical Knowledge Simplification for Patients in the Era of LLMs: A Case Study on Diabetes
outcome: Reading level (FKGL) of LLM-simplified diabetes responses and user satisfaction
effect: MediClear consistently reduced reading level of generated responses to the recommended patient literacy range, with high user satisfaction and willingness for future use (10 participants).
quote: Results show that MediClear consistently reduces the reading level of generated responses to the recommended patient literacy range while achieving high user satisfaction and willingness for future use.

title: Rethinking Correctness for Uncertainty Estimation in Clinical Prediction with Vision-Language Models
outcome: Agreement of eight correctness criteria with two-reviewer human annotation; effect on UE ranking
effect: Criterion choice changed error-detection AUROC by up to 0.146 and reversed UE method rankings; exact matching had highest human agreement and lowest UE distortion; LLM-judge accepted 16 of 30 human-identified errors.
quote: Across four UE methods and 23,254 clinical predictions, criterion choice changed error-detection AUROC by up to 0.146 and reversed the relative ranking of UE methods.

title: K-Bench: a clinically calibrated benchmark for evaluating large language models in high-risk mental health conversations
outcome: Risk exploration and supportive conversation in multi-turn high-risk mental health vignettes
effect: Leading models had combined-risk scores above 95, while risk exploration varied substantially among lower-performing configurations.
quote: Leading models combined strong supportive conversation with combined-risk scores above 95, whereas risk exploration exposed substantial variation among lower-performing configurations.

title: Verifiable by Construction: Claim-Level Evaluation of Verbatim Citation in Clinical Question Answering
outcome: Whether verbatim source quotes attached to LLM claims fully substantiate those claims
effect: Most models attach verbatim quotes to over 90% of claims, but quotes often fail to fully substantiate them; claude-opus-5 gives quotes for 98.0% of claims but fully substantiates only 37.1%.
quote: For instance, claude-opus-5 produces verbatim quotes for 98.0% of its claims, but fully substantiates only 37.1%.

title: Are We Grading Properly? Understanding Failure Modes in Medical Benchmarks
outcome: Share of benchmark rubric criteria with failure modes and effect on scores when regraded
effect: On HealthBench Professional an LLM judge flags 29.6% of criteria as non-atomic and 65.4% as misaligned/rigid; rewriting bundled criteria shifts scores by up to 15.9 percentage points on affected conversations.
quote: We apply RIFT, a global rubric failure taxonomy, to two clinical benchmarks (HealthBench Professional and LiveMedBench), and find failure modes are meaningful: on HealthBench Professional an LLM judge flags 29.6% of criteria as non-atomic and 65.4% as misaligned/rigid.

title: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation: A Conversational Benchmark for Safe Stroke Care in Japanese Using Large Language Models
outcome: Deployed LLM performance on multi-turn stroke history-taking, urgency, and safety versus exam-style benchmarks
effect: Eighteen models evaluated; top model scored 87.4% with zero critical mistakes, only two met safety threshold (≥80%, zero critical mistakes); eleven models made 17 critical mistakes despite strong exam-level knowledge.
quote: Two leaders met the safety threshold.

title: Japanese Stroke LLM Evaluation: A Conversational Benchmark for Safe Stroke Care in Japanese Using Large Language Models
outcome: Critical mistakes in emergency stroke management by LLMs in multi-turn conversations
effect: Eleven models made 17 critical mistakes, including failure to confirm labs or blood glucose before t-PA, surgery before airway stabilization, omission of cervical vascular evaluation, and t-PA outside indication.
quote: Eleven models made 17 critical mistakes, including failure to confirm laboratory results or blood glucose before t-PA, surgery before airway stabilization, omission of cervical vascular evaluation, and t-PA outside its indication.

title: Large Language Models Versus Physicians in Traditional Chinese Medicine: A Real-World Clinical Case Evaluation
outcome: Expert scores of LLMs versus TCM physicians on same outpatient cases
effect: Cutting-edge general-purpose LLMs achieved higher expert scores than the 60 physician comparators, especially for medical advice, treatment principles and selected diagnostic tasks.
quote: Cutting-edge general-purpose LLMs achieved higher expert scores than the physician comparators, particularly for medical advice, treatment principles and selected diagnostic tasks.
sample_unit: cases (de-identified outpatient TCM cases; 16 LLMs and 60 physicians compared)

title: Large Language Models Versus Physicians in Traditional Chinese Medicine: A Real-World Clinical Case Evaluation
outcome: Hallucinations in LLM TCM outputs identified in qualitative safety review
effect: Qualitative safety review identified hallucinations and undesirable template-driven outputs; prescription-level analyses showed discrepancies in herb selection, dosage and treatment strategy.
quote: However, prescription-level analyses revealed discrepancies in herb selection, dosage, and treatment strategy, and qualitative safety review identified hallucinations and undesirable template-driven outputs.
sample_unit: cases (de-identified outpatient TCM cases; 16 LLMs and 60 physicians compared)

title: EviGen: Predictive Evidence Scaffolding for Verifiable Clinical Rationale Generation
outcome: Rationale faithfulness and prediction performance of evidence-grounded generation versus full-context LLM and RAG baselines
effect: EviGen improves prediction performance and rationale faithfulness over full-context LLM and RAG baselines across three medical prediction datasets; clinical reviewers preferred it in a usability evaluation.
quote: Across three medical prediction datasets, EviGen improves prediction performance and rationale faithfulness over full-context LLM and RAG baselines, and is preferred by clinical reviewers in a usability evaluation.

title: HerHealthEval: Evaluating Multilingual and Register-Sensitive Understanding of Women's Health Communication
outcome: under-triage rate of risk calibration in French and Arabic

quote: A multilingual adaptation model reaches 0.994 under-triage in French and Arabic under language-asymmetric risk supervision.

title: HerHealthEval: Evaluating Multilingual and Register-Sensitive Understanding of Women's Health Communication
outcome: cross-form consistency across paraphrases varying in register, layperson and emotional framing

quote: Results reveal that aggregate accuracy and consistency can conceal safety-relevant failures.

title: From Discharge Notes to Patient Understanding: Persona-Grounded, Open-Ended Simulation of LLMs as Discharge Educators
outcome: LLM discharge educator performance across patient personas including health literacy and education level
effect: Aggregate scores concealed variation across ICD chapters and personas; difficult personas exposed coverage failures, comprehension gaps, and reduced source-answer agreement. No numbers in abstract.
quote: Across closed- and open-source LLMs, aggregate scores conceal clinically relevant variation across ICD chapters and patient personas; difficult personas expose coverage failures, comprehension gaps, and reduced source-answer agreement.

title: PhysioBench: A Unified Benchmark for Physiological Signal Question Answering
outcome: Sensitivity of model performance to question formulation (input wording variation)

outcome: Clinical inferences not based on the interview (ungrounded content) by LLM vs clinicians

outcome: Safety and performance change after fine-tuning a model on vaccination data

title: The Effect of Quantization on Clinical Benchmarks: Accuracy and Safety Across Model Families

title: The Effect of Quantization on Clinical Benchmarks: Accuracy and Safety Across Model Families

title: LLMs Anchor on Chief Complaint and Fail to Integrate Evidence in Sequential Clinical Triage

title: LLMs Anchor on Chief Complaint and Fail to Integrate Evidence in Sequential Clinical Triage
outcome: Standalone LLM triage performance compared with clinician performance on the same conversations

title: LLMs Anchor on Chief Complaint and Fail to Integrate Evidence in Sequential Clinical Triage
outcome: LLM triage sensitivity to input variation via controlled perturbations and prompting interventions

title: LLMs Anchor on Chief Complaint and Fail to Integrate Evidence in Sequential Clinical Triage
outcome: LLM ESI acuity prediction distribution and agreement with ground truth

title: Misaligned Clinical Risk Classification and Cost Asymmetry in Open-Weight Large Language Models

title: SkinAgent AI: A Safety-Grounded Multimodal Agentic Framework for Non-Diagnostic Skincare Support
outcome: Agent tool selection, task completion, and failure fallback on a locked benchmark
effect: Exact tool-set match 62.92%, strict task completion 47.08%, intent accuracy 80.00%; tool-selection errors and unreliable failure fallback remained.
quote: Tool-selection errors, incomplete grounding of product attributes, and unreliable failure fallback nevertheless remained.

title: SkinAgent AI: A Safety-Grounded Multimodal Agentic Framework for Non-Diagnostic Skincare Support

title: ChestPheNoT: Deployable, Auditable Label-Status-Evidence Extraction from Radiology Reports

title: Beyond Accuracy: Counterfactual Fragility and Demographic Bias in Clinical Evaluation of LLMs
outcome: Answer changes when demographic prefixes added to identical vignettes versus no-demographic baseline

quote: Across 5,400 demographic comparisons, 1,097 answers were changed (20.3%).

title: Beyond Accuracy: Counterfactual Fragility and Demographic Bias in Clinical Evaluation of LLMs
outcome: Stereotype evidence flags in model explanations under demographic prefixes, judged automatically
effect: 3,128 stereotype evidence flags, including 1,932 in the broad Other category; GLM had the highest stereotype flag rate.
quote: Automated judging identified 3,128 stereotype evidence flags, including 1,932 in the broad Other category.

outcome: Explanation robustness to paraphrases and consistency across repeated queries (ESI, PSS) in LLM clinical answers

title: Right Answer, Wrong Reason: Accuracy, Consistency, and Consensus Are Misleading Indicators of LLM Faithfulness in Clinical Decision Support
outcome: Whether exam-style accuracy reflects faithful reasoning in LLMs

title: Medical Knowledge Is Not All You Need: When Medical Q&A Becomes Situated Patient Assistance
outcome: effect of procedural grounding

title: Medical Knowledge Is Not All You Need: When Medical Q&A Becomes Situated Patient Assistance

title: Jev in Medicine: A Benchmark Evaluation. Preliminary Results

title: Explainable and Generalisable LLM-based Cognitive Decline Detection with Spontaneous Speech

title: Multi-Site Real-World Performance of Commercial AI for Pulmonary and Incidental Pulmonary Embolism Detection
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of FDA-cleared PE AI on local historical data versus clearance benchmarks

quote: Both models demonstrated lower sensitivity than FDA-clearance benchmarks while exceeding cleared specificity, with diminishing performance for peripheral and non-acute emboli mirroring known human reader limitations and underscoring the need for standardized post-market surveillance of AI-enabled medical devices.

title: Multi-Site Real-World Performance of Commercial AI for Pulmonary and Incidental Pulmonary Embolism Detection
outcome: AI performance across a 17-facility health system

quote: We retrospectively evaluated two FDA-cleared AI algorithms from a single commercial platform (Aidoc Medical BriefCase), one for PE triage on dedicated CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA; n = 30,678) and one for incidental PE (iPE) detection on routine contrast-enhanced CTs (n = 37,191), across a 17-facility academic health system.
sample_unit: CT examinations (30,678 CTPA and 37,191 routine contrast-enhanced CTs)

title: PrivMeSA: Privacy-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Medicine via Local-Remote LLM Collaboration
outcome: Disclosure of personal details and re-identifiability when a local agent consults remote LLMs

title: PrivMeSA: Privacy-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Medicine via Local-Remote LLM Collaboration
outcome: Leakage of identifying information in outbound transcripts to remote LLMs, with and without learned disclosure control

quote: In the same setting, PrivMeSA reduces the disclosure of personal details from 98.0% to 0.2% of cases and the share of cases in which the patient can be narrowed to ten or fewer registry patients from 74% to 0%.

title: Sense and Sensitivity: Benchmarking LLM Clinical Triage Recommendations with Physician Experts
outcome: LLM triage recommendation stability under clinically irrelevant text perturbations versus physicians

quote: First, LLMs are more likely than physicians to recommend unnecessary care at baseline, and this tendency increases under perturbed inputs.

title: Sense and Sensitivity: Benchmarking LLM Clinical Triage Recommendations with Physician Experts
outcome: Sensitivity of LLM triage recommendations to gender perturbations compared with physicians

quote: Further, we find that LLM recommendations are more sensitive to gender and tone perturbations than human recommendations.

title: Sense and Sensitivity: Benchmarking LLM Clinical Triage Recommendations with Physician Experts
outcome: Rate of unnecessary care (over-escalation) recommended by LLMs versus physicians
effect: LLMs were more likely than physicians to recommend unnecessary care at baseline, increasing under perturbed inputs.

title: EHR-RobustGym: Benchmarking and Training Agents for Robust Clinical Reasoning
outcome: LLM agent task success on clean versus noisy EHR queries

quote: Evaluating multiple LLMs reveals substantial robustness gaps: average task success across proprietary and large-scale open-weight models drops from 62.2% on Clean questions to 37.9% on Noise questions.

title: QoQ-Med3: a multimodal reasoning foundation model for clinical analysis
outcome: Model performance on held-out datasets from different clinical sites (MIMIC-IV, JHU PMAP)

quote: The model trained on public clinical data only generalized to both the held-out MIMIC-IV and the private JHU PMAP dataset collected at Johns Hopkins University hospital.

title: External validation of AI assisted colposcopy using WHO dataset for cervical precancer and cancer detection
outcome: Colposcopist CIN2+ sensitivity with versus without AI assistance
effect: With AI assistance, colposcopists sensitivity increased from 84.8% (95% CI, 82.7–86.9%) to 90.6% (95% CI, 88.7–92.1%); low-experience readers' AUC rose from 0.72 to 0.76 (p = 0.043).
quote: With AI assistance, colposcopists sensitivity increased from 84.8% (95% CI, 82.7–86.9%) to 90.6% (95% CI, 88.7–92.1%).

title: External validation of AI assisted colposcopy using WHO dataset for cervical precancer and cancer detection
outcome: AI performance on independent external WHO dataset versus internal testing
effect: Validated on independent WHO open-source set of 187 patients; standalone CIN2+ sensitivity 84.2% (95%CI 74.4–90.7%), described as robust performance on an external dataset.
quote: internal testing of the AI model could overestimate diagnostic performance

title: An interpretable artificial intelligence model for real-time leukemia screening via routine blood tests across multicenter cohorts
outcome: Discrimination across independent centers and prospective real-world evaluation
effect: AUC up to 0.996 in multicenter validation; AUC 0.969 in prospective evaluation of 58,481 unselected records, maintaining robust accuracy.
quote: In a prospective real‑world evaluation of 58,481 unselected records, it maintained robust accuracy (AUC = 0.969), identifying occult leukemia and early relapse in non‑hematology departments.

title: AI assistance for fetal ultrasound interpretation in a multi-reader study
outcome: Reader AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and interpretation time with versus without AI assistance
effect: AUC rose 68.9% to 90.9% (p<0.001); sensitivity 88.5% vs 54.2%; specificity 87.9% vs 80.7%; inter-reader agreement 72% vs 26%; time 23 vs 40 s per image.
quote: With AI assistance, AUC presented a mean improvement of 21.9 percentage points (68.9% to 90.9%, p < 0.001).

title: AI assistance for fetal ultrasound interpretation in a multi-reader study
outcome: Clinician performance with AI assistance versus unassisted reading in a multi-reader study
effect: Sensitivity improved 88.5% vs 54.2% (p<0.01) and specificity 87.9% vs 80.7% (p<0.01) with AI assistance.
quote: With AI, sensitivity was overall improved (88.5% vs. 54.2%, p < 0.01), as was specificity (87.9% vs. 80.7%, p < 0.01), inter-reader agreement (72% vs 26%) and interpretation time (23 vs 40 s per image).

title: Patient engagement, acceptability, and preference of artificial intelligence versus human coaching for diabetes prevention
outcome: Patient preference for human coach versus fully automated AI program
effect: 46.5% of AI-assigned participants would have preferred a human coach vs 31.5% preferring a fully automated program in the human-led group (p = 0.012).
quote: Preference responses also favored human coaching, with 46.5% of AI-assigned participants indicating they would have preferred a human coach compared with 31.5% preferring a fully automated program in the human-led group ( p = 0.012).

title: A multi-class gastric biopsy artificial intelligence model developed from whole slide histopathological images
outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy and time with versus without AI assistance
effect: GBAIM raised accuracy of all nine pathologists by 1.7%–39.0% and reduced diagnostic time by 29.4%–50.5%.
quote: GBAIM enhanced the performance of all nine pathologists in auxiliary diagnostic experiments, raising their accuracy by 1.7%–39.0%, while reducing diagnostic time by 29.4%–50.5%.

title: A multi-class gastric biopsy artificial intelligence model developed from whole slide histopathological images
outcome: Model sensitivity and specificity on external multicenter and prospective cohorts
effect: Sensitivity 96.1% and specificity 95.0% in external cohorts; 93.4% and 99.0% in the prospective cohort.
quote: GBAIM achieved 96.1% sensitivity and 95.0% specificity in external cohorts, and 93.4% and 99.0% in the prospective cohort, respectively, demonstrating excellent performance and strong generalization ability.

title: A Multimodal large language model-based triage tool for osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures using posture and movement videos
outcome: Internal-to-external AUC degradation on geographically independent validation cohort
effect: External validation (n=56) Gradient Boosting AUC 0.838 (95% CI 0.712–0.940), sensitivity 89.3%, specificity 71.4%, with negligible internal-to-external AUC degradation (ΔAUC < 0.001).
quote: On geographically independent external validation ( n = 56), the Gradient Boosting model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.838 (95% CI: 0.712–0.940), sensitivity of 89.3%, and specificity of 71.4%, with negligible internal-to-external AUC degradation (ΔAUC < 0.001).
sample_unit: participants (102 OVCF, 102 controls); external validation n=56

title: Impact of LLM assistance on physician decision-making: a multi-country randomized controlled trial
outcome: Physician vignette performance with versus without LLM access, and usage-related gains
effect: LLM access improved performance: Kenya 18% (95% CI 12.7-23.2), Indonesia 10.7% (5.7-15.7), Netherlands 7.2% (3.7-10.7); some control physicians outperformed those with access.
quote: Higher LLM usage was associated with greater performance gains, though some physicians without access outperformed those with access, suggesting that effective use depends on individual engagement.

title: Impact of LLM assistance on physician decision-making: a multi-country randomized controlled trial
outcome: Distribution of LLM performance benefits across countries and within-country score dispersion
effect: LLM access reduced cross-country performance disparities, particularly Kenya vs Netherlands; score dispersion increased in Indonesia and decreased in Kenya.
quote: However, distributional effects varied, with increased score dispersion in Indonesia and reduced variation in Kenya.

title: Cost-effectiveness of an AI-based app compared to usual care for early skin cancer detection in Belgium
outcome: Skin cancer detection rate and cost of AI app versus usual care
effect: App detection rate lower than usual care: melanoma 0.601 vs 0.874, BCC 0.585 vs 0.912, SCC 0.706 vs 0.922, benign 0.820 vs 0.937; costs were lower or similar; unnecessary benign referrals.
quote: In its current diagnostic performance the AI-based app was associated with lower skin cancer detection rates and as a consequence, lower costs.
sample_unit: decision-tree model simulation (no patient sample reported)

title: Beyond expertise: exploring behavioral personas in AI-assisted rare renal cancer diagnosis
outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance, and overreliance on incorrect AI output
effect: AI assistance improved accuracy (60.0–73.3%, P = 0.012) and inter-rater reliability (Fleiss' kappa 0.311–0.482); Receptive group had higher susceptibility to incorrect AI outputs (median CORR 0.800 vs 0.600).
quote: AI assistance significantly improved overall diagnostic accuracy (60.0–73.3%, P = 0.012) and inter-rater reliability (Fleiss’ kappa 0.311–0.482).

title: Beyond expertise: exploring behavioral personas in AI-assisted rare renal cancer diagnosis
outcome: Clinical overreliance on incorrect AI outputs among pathologists
effect: Receptive group (n=14) benefited more from correct AI advice (median RAIR 0.732 vs 0.444) but was more susceptible to incorrect outputs (median CORR 0.800 vs 0.600).
quote: The Receptive group derived greater diagnostic benefit from correct AI advice (median RAIR, 0.732 vs. 0.444) but exhibited higher susceptibility to incorrect outputs (median CORR, 0.800 vs. 0.600).

title: Lightweight non-contrast CT-based multimodal artificial intelligence for subtype classification of hepatic cystic echinococcosis in resource-limited clinical settings
outcome: Physician macro-AUC with versus without AI assistance in reader study
effect: AI-assisted macro-AUC 0.970 vs 0.905 physician-only (tertiary cohort); 0.963 vs 0.902 (county-hospital cohort)
quote: In the reader study, AI-assisted interpretation yielded higher observed macro-AUCs than physician-only interpretation in the tertiary cohort (0.970 vs. 0.905) and the county-hospital cohort (0.963 vs. 0.902).

title: Lightweight non-contrast CT-based multimodal artificial intelligence for subtype classification of hepatic cystic echinococcosis in resource-limited clinical settings
outcome: Macro-AUC internal versus external multi-site validation
effect: Macro-AUC 0.942 (95% CI 0.910–0.964) internally and 0.931 (95% CI 0.898–0.956) externally; small drop at county hospitals
quote: The multimodal model achieved the highest observed macro-AUC, with macro-AUC of 0.942 (95% CI: 0.910–0.964) internally and 0.931 (95% CI: 0.898–0.956) externally; subtype–level AUCs were consistent across CE1–CE5, with most errors occurring between adjacent transitional stages.

title: Full end-to-end diagnostic workflow automation of 3D OCT via foundation model-driven AI for retinal diseases
outcome: Model performance across four centers and diverse OCT devices in external and real-world validation

title: Full end-to-end diagnostic workflow automation of 3D OCT via foundation model-driven AI for retinal diseases
outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with expert ophthalmologists on abnormality detection and multi-disease diagnosis
effect: FOCUS matched expert performance in abnormality detection (F1: 95.47% vs 90.91%) and multi-disease diagnosis (F1: 93.49% vs 91.35%), with better efficiency.
quote: In human-machine comparisons, FOCUS matched expert performance in abnormality detection (F1: 95.47% vs 90.91%) and multi-disease diagnosis (F1: 93.49% vs 91.35%), while demonstrating better efficiency.

title: Differences in tone of AI and care team responses to patient messages by patient demographics
outcome: Demographic differences in tone of AI-drafted patient message replies

title: Differences in tone of AI and care team responses to patient messages by patient demographics
outcome: Population-specific differences in tone of generated patient message replies

quote: AI-GDRs had lower odds of including polite language in responses to Hispanic patients, compared to White patients.
sample_unit: message triads (patient message, AI-generated draft reply, care team response)

title: Prospective validation of machine learning models predicting Gram negative bacteremia in ICU versus clinical scores
outcome: ML model discrimination for Gram-negative bacteremia compared with established clinical scores in ICU
effect: Several clinical scores were significantly associated with bacteremia. ML models showed modest discrimination overall, improving to AUROC ≈ 0.70 with higher sensitivity in a post-hoc subgroup of cultures from ICU days 4-10.

title: Large language models as judges for clinical generative AI evaluation
outcome: Agreement between clinicians and LLM judges across seven rubrics

quote: LLM judges showed high concordance on text-comparison rubrics such as faithfulness and completeness, but weaker agreement for interpretive dimensions like reasoning and safety.

title: Large language models as judges for clinical generative AI evaluation
outcome: misalignment by rating scale
effect: Binary pass/fail exposed misalignments not apparent on ordinal scales.
quote: Repeated runs and multi-model panels did not systematically improve alignment beyond the best single model, while binary pass/fail evaluation exposed misalignments not apparent on ordinal scales.

title: Prospective multicenter evaluation of an autonomous robotic ultrasound system integrated with AI-assisted thyroid nodule assessment
outcome: Agreement with conventional ultrasound-based ACR TI-RADS assessment after sonologist revision

quote: Aitrox-USIP reduced analysis time (183 s vs. 254 s; p < 0.001), and sonologist revision improved agreement with conventional US-based ACR TI-RADS assessment ( κ , 0.754–0.879).

title: Prospective multicenter evaluation of an autonomous robotic ultrasound system integrated with AI-assisted thyroid nodule assessment
outcome: Missed fine-needle aspiration biopsy recommendations under FARUSS-based screening

title: Prospective multicenter evaluation of an autonomous robotic ultrasound system integrated with AI-assisted thyroid nodule assessment
outcome: Agreement of AI TI-RADS categories with conventional US after sonologist revision
effect: Sonologist revision of AI-assisted assessment improved agreement with conventional US-based ACR TI-RADS (κ 0.754–0.879); AI also reduced analysis time 183 s vs 254 s.
quote: Aitrox-USIP reduced analysis time (183 s vs. 254 s; p < 0.001), and sonologist revision improved agreement with conventional US-based ACR TI-RADS assessment ( κ , 0.754–0.879).

title: Prospective multicenter evaluation of an autonomous robotic ultrasound system integrated with AI-assisted thyroid nodule assessment
outcome: Missed FNAB recommendations when autonomous screening replaces on-site US
effect: FARUSS-based screening avoided 74.8% of unnecessary on-site exams but missed 19.2% of FNAB recommendations.

title: Blind spots in AI-assisted healthcare evidence search: multiplatform evaluation of clinical retrieval gaps and risk-of-bias
outcome: Evidence recall across 15 query formulations on five RAG-LLM platforms
