title: AI adoption and workflow optimization following orchestration platform implementation and structured change management
outcome: Radiologist user-verification rate of AI outputs
effect: Verification rose from 13.9% (318/2287) at baseline to 61.1% (1778/2910) after orchestration platform plus change management; full verification of multi-task exams 62.6%; 9480 AI tasks across 12 applications.
quote: The overall user-verification rate increased from 13.9% (318/2287) at baseline to 61.1% (1778/2910) after implementation, while full verification of examinations containing multiple AI tasks increased to 62.6%.

title: AI adoption and workflow optimization following orchestration platform implementation and structured change management
outcome: Radiologist user-verification rate of AI outputs
effect: Combined structured change management (education, standardization, feedback, governance) and platform associated with verification increasing from 13.9% to 61.1%; uncontrolled pre-post, bundled intervention.
quote: In conclusion, a combined orchestration platform and change management strategy was associated with substantially increased AI adoption and integration into routine neuroradiology workflow.

title: A multicenter assessment of human oversight of generative AI outputs in simulated clinical decision making
outcome: Junior clinicians' identification of GPT-4o hallucinations in simulated clinical scenarios
effect: Only 15.8% of hallucinations were identified, and 13.1% of clinicians failed to detect any hallucinations across all scenarios.
quote: Our results revealed that only 15.8% of hallucinations were identified, and 13.1% of clinicians failed to detect any hallucinations across all scenarios.

title: A multicenter assessment of human oversight of generative AI outputs in simulated clinical decision making
outcome: Whether users detect incorrect AI outputs (hallucinations)
effect: Only 15.8% of hallucinations identified; detection did not improve with increasing clinical risk.
quote: Notably, detection rates did not improve with increasing clinical risk, and variability in hallucination detection arose primarily from between-clinician rather than between-scenario differences.

title: Large language model–assisted preoperative communication reduces patient anxiety and physician workload in prostate cancer: a prospective randomized phase II trial
outcome: Patient anxiety (GAD-7), emotion, illness perception, satisfaction, physician workload (NASA-TLX), and communication time, AI-assisted vs standard communication
quote: AI-assisted patients reported significantly lower post-communication anxiety (GAD-7, 3.2 [2.7] vs. 5.7 [3.1]; P = 0.001) and better emotion, illness perceptions, and satisfaction.

title: When the Model Trains You: Induced Belief Revision and Its Implications on Artificial Intelligence Research and Patient Care — A Case Study on Predicting Obstructive Hydronephrosis in Children
outcome: Change in nuclear scan use after clinicians' exposure to model development and silent trial
effect: Nuclear scans fell from 80 to 58% (P=0.005) after the silent trial, with no identifiable change in workflow, personnel, guidelines, or patient characteristics. Authors propose separating clinical end-users in development from those in validation.
quote: Model-induced belief revision may threaten the scientific integrity of AI research, because it can lead to underestimated differences between AI predictions and clinical judgment, which may unconsciously be influenced by this phenomenon.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Machine Learning for Public Health Screening: Identifying Unknown Hepatitis C Carriers
outcome: HCV carriers identified per number screened, ML-targeted outreach versus concurrent USPSTF-eligible testing
effect: ML outreach: 477 screened, 38 active carriers, NNS 10. USPSTF-eligible testing: 53,403 tested, 38 carriers, NNS 1029. Over 100-fold greater efficiency.
quote: Among the 53,403 USPSTF screening–eligible members who were tested over the same period, 38 were found to be active HCV carriers, yielding an NNS of 1029.
sample_unit: members screened for HCV antibodies in prospective outreach

title: Advancing Diabetic Macular Edema Detection from 3D Optical Coherence Tomography Scans: Integrating Privacy-Preserving AI and Generalizability Techniques — A Prospective Validation in Vietnam
outcome: Prospective real-time performance of DME detection model in DR screening program
effect: Accuracy 93.70%, sensitivity 91.78%, specificity 93.06% for DME detection; performance similar to human experts.
quote: Our DL model was effective in detecting DME from three-dimensional OCT scans in a prospective, real-time clinical setting, suggesting that successful deployment of DL to improve DR screening programs in lower- and middle-income countries can be achieved.

title: Advancing Diabetic Macular Edema Detection from 3D Optical Coherence Tomography Scans: Integrating Privacy-Preserving AI and Generalizability Techniques — A Prospective Validation in Vietnam
outcome: Flagging uncertain cases for ophthalmologist re-evaluation via dual-threshold uncertainty range
effect: Model identified 64 cases as uncertain, indicating a need for re-evaluation by an ophthalmologist.

title: Artificial Intelligence–Powered Rapid Identification of ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction via Electrocardiogram (ARISE) — A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial
outcome: Door-to-balloon time, ECG-to-balloon time, and mortality with AI-ECG versus standard care in randomized trial
effect: ED median door-to-balloon 82.0 vs 96.0 min (P=0.002); ECG-to-balloon 78.0 vs 83.6 min (P=0.011); cardiac death OR 0.73 (P=0.029); all-cause mortality OR 1.02 (P=0.568).
quote: In patients with STEMI, AI-ECG–assisted triage of STEMI decreased the door-to-balloon time for patients presenting to the emergency department and decreased the ECG-to-balloon time for patients in the emergency room and inpatients.

title: AI-Assisted Spirometry Interpretation in Primary Care: A Randomized Controlled Trial
outcome: clinician performance with versus without AI
quote: Compared with the control group, the addition of AI decision support software led to improvements in preferred diagnosis prediction performance in all cases (mean difference, 9.0; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.5 to 13.3%; P=0.001) and in COPD cases (15.9; 95% CI, 9.0 to 22.7%; P<0.001).

title: AI-Assisted Spirometry Interpretation in Primary Care: A Randomized Controlled Trial
outcome: Clinician diagnostic performance with AI in intended workflow versus without AI
effect: AI adjunct improved clinician preferred diagnosis performance (mean difference 9.0%; COPD 15.9%); differential diagnosis and technical quality assessment also improved, not pattern interpretation or confidence.
quote: Differential diagnosis prediction and technical quality assessment performance also improved with intervention, but not pattern interpretation or clinician confidence levels.

title: AI-Assisted Spirometry Interpretation in Primary Care: A Randomized Controlled Trial
outcome: preferred diagnosis agreement with reference diagnosis
quote: Compared with the control group, the addition of AI decision support software led to improvements in preferred diagnosis prediction performance in all cases (mean difference, 9.0; 95% confidence interval [CI], 4.5 to 13.3%; P=0.001) and in COPD cases (15.9; 95% CI, 9.0 to 22.7%; P<0.001).

title: PROTEUS: A Prospective RCT Evaluating Use of AI in Stress Echocardiography
outcome: Appropriate referral for coronary angiography, AI-augmented vs standard decision-making, in randomized trial
effect: AUROC 0.63 intervention vs 0.55 control; difference 0.09 (95% CI -0.22 to 0.39); did not meet non-inferiority margin of -0.05. Sensitivity 64.2% vs 55.1%; specificity 98.6% vs 99.2%.
quote: AI–augmented decision-making in stress echocardiography did not meet the non-inferiority end point when evaluated in a large, prospective randomized controlled trial, but may be beneficial in low-volume centers.

title: PROTEUS: A Prospective RCT Evaluating Use of AI in Stress Echocardiography
outcome: Clinician decision-making with versus without AI assistance in intended deployment mode
effect: AI-augmented clinicians had AUROC 0.63 vs 0.55 for control, difference 0.09 (95% CI -0.22 to 0.39); non-inferiority not met; potential benefit in low-volume centers.
quote: The difference between the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) for the intervention (0.63; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.43 to 0.83) and control (0.55; 95% CI, 0.33 to 0.80), did not meet the prespecified non-inferiority margin of −0.05 (difference, 0.09; 95% CI, −0.22 to 0. 39).

title: How Academic Medical Centers Govern AI Prediction Tools in the Context of Uncertainty and Evolving Regulation
outcome: Presence of coordinated, accountable AI governance structures at academic medical centers
effect: Three governance phenotypes found (well-defined, emerging, interpersonal); in interpersonal systems an individual decides on model implementation without consistent evaluation requirements; even well-resourced AMCs struggled to manage pitfalls.
quote: In health systems using interpersonal or individual-driven governance approaches, an individual is tasked with making decisions about model implementation without consistent evaluation requirements.

title: Securing Collaborative Medical AI by Using Differential Privacy: Domain Transfer for Classification of Chest Radiographs
outcome: AUC drop from single-institution to cross-institution performance across five chest radiograph datasets
effect: Cross-institutional AUC decreased by 0.07 (VinDr-CXR), 0.07 (ChestX-ray14), 0.07 (CheXpert), 0.18 (UKA-CXR), and 0.07 (PadChest) for DP-DT, with similar drops for non-DP models.

title: Securing Collaborative Medical AI by Using Differential Privacy: Domain Transfer for Classification of Chest Radiographs
outcome: Effect of differential privacy on cross-institutional diagnostic AUC and subgroup performance versus non-DP models
effect: At ε≈1, no evidence of AUC differences between DP-DT and non-DP-DT; subgroup AUC differences under 1% for sex subgroups and nearly all age subgroups. Privacy protection itself was not measured.
quote: Cross-institutional performance of artificial intelligence models was not affected by DP.

title: Human Factors Validation Study of an Artificial Neural Network‑based Preoperative Decision‑support Tool for Noninvasive Lymph Node Staging (NILS) in Women with Primary Breast Cancer (ISRCTN99301435)

quote: Several interface challenges were identified, including difficulty in locating the reset and information buttons, the ability to enter values outside valid ranges (age and tumor size), and the risk of unintentionally modifying the entered values while scrolling.

title: Human Factors Validation Study of an Artificial Neural Network‑based Preoperative Decision‑support Tool for Noninvasive Lymph Node Staging (NILS) in Women with Primary Breast Cancer (ISRCTN99301435)
outcome: Whether the tool blocks invalid inputs (age, tumor size)

title: TOWARDS AN AI-DRIVEN REGISTRY FOR POSTOPERATIVE COMPLICA-TIONS: A PROOF-OF-CONCEPT STUDY EVALUATING THE OPPORTUNITIES AND CHALLENGES OF AI-MODELS

title: Evaluating ChatGPT for Disease Prediction: A Comparative Study on Heart Disease and Diabetes

quote: Even though ChatGPT does not outperform traditional machine learning and deep learning models, these findings highlight its potential as a complementary tool in disease prediction.
sample_unit: records from public datasets (Pima Indian Diabetes, Frankfurt Hospital Diabetes, heart disease)

title: RiskAgent: Autonomous Medical AI Copilot for Generalist Risk Prediction
outcome: Risk-prediction accuracy of LLM agent using evidence-based clinical tools versus commercial LLMs without them
effect: RiskAgent (8B) reached 76.33% accuracy on MedRisk, outperforming o1, o3-mini and GPT-4.5 and doubling GPT-4o's 38.39%.
quote: The results show that our RiskAgent, with 8 billion model parameters, achieves 76.33% accuracy, outperforming the most recent commercial LLMs, o1, o3-mini, and GPT-4.5, and doubling the 38.39% accuracy of GPT-4o.

title: Implementing a Resource-Light and Low-Code Large Language Model System for Information Extraction from Mammography Reports: A Case Study
outcome: Accuracy and coverage of LLM extractions when applying certainty thresholds to classification probabilities
effect: Certainty thresholds raised accuracies to >90% but reduced coverage rate to <50%.
quote: Setting certainty thresholds further improved accuracies to >90% but reduced the coverage rate to <50%.

title: Optimizing the Clinical Application of Rheumatology Guidelines Using Large Language Models: A Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework Integrating EULAR and ACR Recommendations
outcome: Answer quality (accuracy, safety, completeness) of RAG-grounded versus baseline LLM answers to guideline questions
effect: RAG significantly outperformed baseline across all criteria (p<0.001) per LLM judge; rheumatologists confirmed for accuracy, safety, completeness (p<0.001); RAG preferred in 92.8% of LLM-judge and 71.2%-74.8% of human comparisons.
quote: Analysis revealed that the RAG system significantly outperformed the baseline system across all criteria (p<0.001) in the LLM-as-a-judge evaluation.

title: The I-KAPCAM-AI-Q: A Novel Instrument for Evaluating Health Care Providers’ AI Awareness in Italy
outcome: Proportion of physicians who received digital technology training in medical education
effect: Only 17% of pilot participants (n=203) had received digital technology training during medical education; knowledge of AI in diagnostics was highest among applications at 48%.
quote: Pilot testing revealed only 17% of participants had received digital technology training during medical education, while 91% showed clinical agreement with AI-proposed diagnoses.
sample_unit: physicians (residents and specialists) in pilot testing

title: Grounding Large Language Model in Clinical Diagnostics
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and efficiency of ClinDiag-GPT plus physicians versus physicians alone
effect: Collaboration between ClinDiag-GPT and physicians enhanced both diagnostic accuracy and efficiency compared with physicians alone and the model alone.
quote: Collaboration between ClinDiag-GPT and physicians enhanced both diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, demonstrating ClinDiag-GPT's potential as a valuable clinical assistant.

title: Grounding Large Language Model in Clinical Diagnostics
outcome: LLM performance on diagnostic questions versus full clinical diagnostic procedures
effect: Models performed well answering diagnostic questions but consistently underperformed in clinical diagnostic procedures and exhibited a significant number of clinical errors.
quote: Although these models performed well in answering diagnostic questions, they consistently underperformed in clinical diagnostic procedures and exhibited a significant number of clinical errors.

title: Grounding Large Language Model in Clinical Diagnostics
outcome: diagnostic-question versus clinical-procedure performance
effect: Models performed well on diagnostic questions but underperformed in clinical procedures; no numeric effect reported.
quote: Although these models performed well in answering diagnostic questions, they consistently underperformed in clinical diagnostic procedures and exhibited a significant number of clinical errors.

title: Grounding Large Language Model in Clinical Diagnostics
outcome: diagnostic accuracy and efficiency
effect: Collaboration between ClinDiag-GPT and physicians enhanced both diagnostic accuracy and efficiency compared to ClinDiag-GPT alone and physicians alone.
quote: Collaboration between ClinDiag-GPT and physicians enhanced both diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, demonstrating ClinDiag-GPT's potential as a valuable clinical assistant.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Neuro-Oncology: Assessing ChatGPT’s Accuracy in MRI Interpretation and Treatment Advice
outcome: Differential diagnosis inclusion of correct tumor type on MRI interpretation by ChatGPT-4o
effect: Meningioma in differential for 73.3% of meningioma cases; glioma in 83.3% of glioblastoma cases; tumor localized correctly in 66.7% of cases.
quote: ChatGPT included meningioma in the differential diagnosis for 73.3% of meningioma cases and glioma in 83.3% of glioblastoma cases.
sample_unit: cases (90 MRI images, three planes per case)

title: ARE LLMS READY FOR PEDIATRICS? A COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF MODEL ACCURACY ACROSS CLINICAL DOMAINS
outcome: LLM accuracy on pediatric versus adult MedQA questions, by model
effect: Five of eight models scored significantly lower on pediatric questions, with drops of up to more than 10 percentage points; ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Claude 3.5 Sonnet showed comparable performance (ChatGPT-4o 83.57% adult, 83.18% pediatric; p = 0.80).
quote: Five models (Amazon Nova Pro 1.0, GPT 3.5-turbo-0125, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Grok 2, and Claude 3 Sonnet) demonstrated significantly lower performance on pediatric questions, with accuracy drops of up to more than 10 percentage points.

title: ARE LLMS READY FOR PEDIATRICS? A COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF MODEL ACCURACY ACROSS CLINICAL DOMAINS
outcome: Performance of general-purpose LLMs on pediatric content, a specialized population not specifically validated
effect: Five of eight LLMs performed significantly worse on pediatric than adult questions (up to more than 10 percentage points lower); three newer models performed comparably across domains.
quote: Five models (Amazon Nova Pro 1.0, GPT 3.5-turbo-0125, Gemini 2.0 Flash, Grok 2, and Claude 3 Sonnet) demonstrated significantly lower performance on pediatric questions, with accuracy drops of up to more than 10 percentage points.

title: Can co-designed educational interventions help consumers think critically about asking ChatGPT health questions? Results from a randomised-controlled trial
outcome: Intention to ask ChatGPT higher-risk health questions, ChatGPT knowledge, and trust after brief AI health literacy interventions vs control
effect: Both intervention groups had lower intention for higher-risk scenarios vs control (animation M=2.42, images M=2.69, control M=3.12; p<0.001), higher ChatGPT knowledge (p<0.001), and lower trust (p<0.001). No effect on lower-risk intentions (p=0.800).
quote: Participants in both intervention groups reported lower intentions to use ChatGPT for higher risk scenarios compared to control (n=205, M=3.12/5, 95%CI: 2.98 to 3.27, p<0.001).

title: Can co-designed educational interventions help consumers think critically about asking ChatGPT health questions? Results from a randomised-controlled trial
outcome: Intention to ask ChatGPT higher-risk questions and knowledge after AI literacy education for consumers
effect: Animation and image interventions reduced intention to use ChatGPT for higher-risk scenarios versus control (M=2.42 and 2.69 vs 3.12, p<0.001) and increased knowledge (p<0.001); trust was lower (p<0.001).
quote: Participants in the intervention groups had higher knowledge of ChatGPT (p<0.001) and reported lower trust (p<0.001), compared to those in the control group.

title: Facilitating User Interaction with the Tuberculosis Mutation Catalogue using AI Tools
outcome: Hallucination frequency of LLMs answering questions about the WHO TB mutation catalogue
effect: DeepSeek R1 exhibited some hallucinations despite high accuracy on focused datasets; Perplexity AI had a higher frequency of hallucinations; Gemini 2.5 Pro avoided hallucinations most often.
quote: DeepSeek R1 excelled in applying grading rules to novel mutations and showed high accuracy in focused datasets, but exhibited some hallucinations.

title: How Can I Stay Healthy? – Benchmarking Large Language Models for Personalized and Biomarker-Based Intervention Recommendations
outcome: LLM response robustness to prompt variability across combinatorial test cases
effect: LLMs responded positively to more concrete system-prompt instructions but remained vulnerable to overall prompt variability (1,000 test cases built combinatorially).
quote: LLMs respond positively to more concrete instructions in the system prompt but remain vulnerable to overall prompt variability.

title: How Can I Stay Healthy? – Benchmarking Large Language Models for Personalized and Biomarker-Based Intervention Recommendations
outcome: LLM performance differences across age groups
effect: Performance was heterogeneous across three age groups, displaying age-related biases, possibly due to differential disease prevalence.
quote: Moreover, LLM performance is heterogeneous across different age groups, displaying age-related biases, which may, however, be due to differential disease prevalence.

title: Benchmarking transformer-based models for medical record deidentification: A single centre, multi-specialty evaluation
outcome: Change in AnonCAT performance after local fine-tuning with site-specific data
effect: AnonCAT F1 rose from 0.851 (0.843-0.859) to 0.910 (0.905-0.914) after fine-tuning; fine-tuned model showed least performance shift across datasets.
quote: AnonCAT showed significant improvement in performance on fine-tuning (F1 increase from 0.851; 0.843-0.859 to 0.910; 0.905-0.914).

title: Benchmarking transformer-based models for medical record deidentification: A single centre, multi-specialty evaluation
outcome: De-identification performance (F1, precision, recall) of automated models for PII redaction in medical records
effect: Best tool Azure DeID F1 0.939 (precision 0.928, recall 0.950); fine-tuned AnonCAT F1 0.910 with recall 0.850; names/dates consistently redacted but variable performance for other PII categories.
quote: Names/dates were consistently redacted by all comparators; there was variable performance for other categories.

title: Benchmarking transformer-based models for medical record deidentification: A single centre, multi-specialty evaluation
outcome: PII redaction model selection
quote: The best performing redaction tool was the Microsoft Azure de-identification service: F1 0.939 (0.934-0.944), precision 0.928 (0.922-0.934), recall 0.950 (0.943-0.958).

title: Interpretable MRI-Based Deep Learning for Alzheimer’s Risk and Progression
outcome: External performance of North American-trained AD model on Chinese SILCODE cohort without retraining
effect: AUC 91.3% for AD classification with sensitivity 95.2%; identified 86.7% of individuals at risk of progression more than 5 years in advance, without retraining or fine-tuning.
quote: The model — initially trained on North American data — demonstrated robust cross-ethnic generalization, without any retraining or fine-tuning, achieving an AUC of 91.3% in AD classification with a sensitivity of 95.2%.

title: Enhanced Language Models for Predicting and Understanding HIV Care Disengagement: A Case Study in Tanzania
outcome: Fine-tuned LLM performance versus supervised ML and zero-shot LLMs on same data
effect: Enhanced LLMs outperformed the supervised ML model and zero-shot LLMs across all outcomes in both internal and external validation datasets.
quote: The enhanced LLMs consistently outperformed the supervised ML model and zero-shot LLMs across all outcomes in both internal and external validation datasets.
sample_unit: people living with HIV (4,809,765 EMR records)

title: Implementing a context-augmented large language model to guide precision cancer medicine
outcome: Accuracy of biomarker-driven treatment recommendations with vs without retrieval grounding in curated knowledge base
effect: LLM-only achieved 62–75% accuracy; RAG-LLM achieved 79–91% with an unstructured database and 94–95% with a structured database.
quote: While LLM-only achieved 62–75% accuracy in biomarker-driven treatment recommendations, RAG-LLM achieved 79–91% accuracy with an unstructured database and 94–95% accuracy with a structured database.

title: Automated Suicide Risk Factor Monitoring in Crisis Text Line Users: Comparative Study of AI and Human Ratings Using Large Language Models
outcome: LLM rating reliability across repeated runs, temperature settings and prompting styles
effect: Zero-shot prompting at temperature 0 yielded perfect inter-rating reliability (α=1.00, 95% CI: [1-1] for high & very high risk); lower temperatures consistently improved reliability and accuracy.
quote: Zero-shot prompting at temperature 0 yielded perfect inter-rating reliability (α=1.00, 95% CI: [1-1] for high & very high risk), while few-shot prompting showed best human-AI agreement for very high risk (α=0.78, 95% CI: [0.67-0.89]) and strongest classification performance (balanced accuracy 0.54-0.71).

title: Automated Suicide Risk Factor Monitoring in Crisis Text Line Users: Comparative Study of AI and Human Ratings Using Large Language Models
outcome: reliability across temperature and prompt configurations
effect: Configuration strongly influenced reliability; zero-shot temperature 0 had α=1.00 for high and very high risk.
quote: Zero-shot prompting at temperature 0 yielded perfect inter-rating reliability (α=1.00, 95% CI: [1-1] for high & very high risk), while few-shot prompting showed best human-AI agreement for very high risk (α=0.78, 95% CI: [0.67-0.89]) and strongest classification performance (balanced accuracy 0.54-0.71).

title: Changes in psychiatric documentation and treatment in primary care with artificial intelligence scribe use
outcome: Likelihood of psychiatric intervention (referral, new diagnosis, antidepressant) in ambient-scribed vs unscribed visits
effect: Psychiatric intervention was less likely with ambient scribes than with no scribe (aOR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72-0.95). Human scribes showed no difference (aOR 1.01, 95% CI 0.87-1.17). Documented symptoms were greater in ambient-scribed notes.
quote: In a logistic regression model, likelihood of a psychiatric intervention (referral, new diagnosis, or antidepressant prescription) was significantly lower among ambient-scribed visits compared to unscribed (aOR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72-0.95), but not for human-scribed compared to unscribed (aOR 1.01, 95% CI 0.87-1.17).

title: Unmasking True Clinical Competence: The Importance of Adaptive and Open-Ended Evaluation for Large Language Models in Cardiology
outcome: Accuracy on multiple-choice exam vs open-ended and clinically modified questions
effect: MC answers 93.0%, reasoning 92.4%; open-ended answers 80.0%, reasoning 80.5% (p<0.001); modified MC answers 93.9% to 66.7%, reasoning 93.9% to 71.2% (both p<0.001).
quote: Using existing MC question formats substantially overestimates the performance and clinical reasoning capabilities of GPT o1-preview.

title: Unmasking True Clinical Competence: The Importance of Adaptive and Open-Ended Evaluation for Large Language Models in Cardiology
outcome: Accuracy after modifying critical clinical parameters in questions
effect: Modified MC accuracy fell from 93.9% to 66.7% for answers and to 71.2% for reasoning (both p<0.001); answer-reasoning concordance fell from 93.9% to 66.7% (p<0.001).
quote: For modified MC questions, accuracy decreased significantly (answers: 93.9% to 66.7%; reasoning: 93.9% to 71.2%; both p<0.001), as well as answer-reasoning concordance (93.9% to 66.7%, p<0.001).

title: Internal Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Antimicrobial Stewardship: Evaluating Trainability of Data and the Accuracy of Clinical Recommendations Within a Clinical Decision Support System
outcome: Independent clinician review of ML recommendations against standard guidelines for discrepancies
effect: Among 644 clinician-trained reports, no major discrepancies in recommendations, with only 100 showing minor differences.
quote: Among 644 clinician-trained reports, there were no major discrepancies in recommendations, with only 100 showing minor differences.

title: GPT-4 Enhances Readability of Online Patient Materials for Cardiac Amyloidosis
outcome: Reading level of institutional cardiac amyloidosis patient materials versus 6th-grade recommendation
effect: None of the institutional PEMs met the 6th-grade level; median FKGL 10.9 (IQR 9.2, 12.6).
quote: None of the institutional PEMs met the recommended 6th-grade reading level and had a median Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) of 10.9 (high school freshman; IQR: 9.2, 12.6, p<0.001).

title: GPT-4 Enhances Readability of Online Patient Materials for Cardiac Amyloidosis
outcome: Readability of GPT-4 revised patient education materials versus institutional originals
effect: GPT-4 reduced median FKGL from 10.9 to 7.8 (IQR 7.0, 8.8); only 14/86 (16.3%) reached at least 6th-grade level.
quote: In comparison, GPT-4 revised PEMs reduced the median FKGL to 7.8 (seventh grade; IQR: 7.0, 8.8, p<0.001), with 14/86 (16.3%) achieving at least a 6th-grade reading level.

title: GPT-4 Enhances Readability of Online Patient Materials for Cardiac Amyloidosis
outcome: Readability of simplified patient education materials
effect: Median FKGL decreased from 10.9 to 7.8; 14/86 (16.3%) reached 6th-grade level.
quote: In comparison, GPT-4 revised PEMs reduced the median FKGL to 7.8 (seventh grade; IQR: 7.0, 8.8, p<0.001), with 14/86 (16.3%) achieving at least a 6th-grade reading level.

title: AUPA: weakly supervised approach for streamlining breast cancer diagnostic workflow by WSI histological type classification for efficient IHC triage
outcome: External validation performance across sites
effect: Over 91% sensitivity and specificity across histological types in internal validation and strong generalizability in two external pilot studies.
quote: It achieves over 91% sensitivity and specificity across histological types in internal validation and shows strong generalizability in two external pilot studies.

title: AUPA: weakly supervised approach for streamlining breast cancer diagnostic workflow by WSI histological type classification for efficient IHC triage
outcome: AUPA performance compared with expert pathologists and state-of-the-art models
effect: AUPA performs competitively against expert pathologists and state-of-the-art models, especially in distinguishing in situ from benign cases.
quote: Compared to expert pathologists and state-of-the-art models, AUPA performs competitively, especially distinguishing in situ from benign cases.

title: Large-Language-Model Mortality Risk Stratification in the Intensive Care Unit: A Benchmark Against APACHE II
outcome: Consistency of LLM risk stratification across repeated evaluations
effect: Gemini, GPT-4, and R1 showed highest consistency across repeated evaluations; Llama showed greater variability that improved with added context.
quote: Gemini, GPT-4, and R1 exhibited the highest consistency across repeated evaluations, while Llama showed greater variability that improved with context.

title: Large-Language-Model Mortality Risk Stratification in the Intensive Care Unit: A Benchmark Against APACHE II
outcome: Calibration of LLM mortality risk categories versus APACHE II predictions
effect: LLMs overestimated risk, classifying more patients as high risk than APACHE II; mortality in high-risk groups was lower than APACHE-predicted rates, indicating calibration mismatch.
quote: Mortality rates within high-risk groups were lower than APACHE-predicted rates, suggesting calibration mismatch.

title: Large-Language-Model Mortality Risk Stratification in the Intensive Care Unit: A Benchmark Against APACHE II
outcome: LLM mortality risk stratification compared with APACHE II
effect: LLMs classified more patients as high risk than APACHE II, with calibration mismatch; Gemini with added context uniquely identified a low-risk group.
quote: LLMs demonstrated a general tendency toward risk overestimation, classifying more patients as high risk compared to APACHE II.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Assisted Decision Making in Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma: A Comparative Study of AI Responses
outcome: Likert-scored LLM treatment recommendations versus multidisciplinary tumor board decisions across three LLMs
effect: ChatGPT mean 4.50 ± 0.57 vs Gemini 3.77 ± 0.43 and Copilot 3.85 ± 0.52 (p < 0.001); performance differed substantially between candidate tools.
quote: ChatGPT demonstrated superior performance with the highest mean score (4.50 ± 0.57) and a median score of 5, significantly outperforming Gemini (mean 3.77 ± 0.43, median 4) and Copilot (mean 3.85 ± 0.52, median 4) (p < 0.001).
sample_unit: questions (12 cases x 5 questions per LLM)

title: An Unsupervised XAI Framework for Dementia Detection with Context Enrichment
outcome: Clinical validity of XAI explanations assessed by clustering against morphology and qualitative clinician review
effect: Clustering homogeneity and completeness improved in morphology-enriched explanation spaces; clinicians (N=6) reported both challenges and opportunities of XAI for different clinical applications.
quote: Clinicians’ qualitative evaluation highlighted challenges and opportunities of XAI for different clinical applications.
sample_unit: participants (brain MRI scans); plus 6 clinicians for qualitative evaluation
country: multiple (ADNI, AIBL, DELCODE, DESCRIBE, EDSD, NIFD cohorts)

title: Verifiable Summarization of Electronic Health Records Using Large Language Models to Support Chart Review
outcome: Physician question-answering accuracy and completion time with vs without LLM summaries
effect: Accuracy 88.0% with summaries vs 86.4% without; overall completion time not significantly reduced, though frequent summary use significantly sped completion (p = 0.002).
quote: Importantly, summary use maintained accuracy in answering clinical questions (88.0% with summaries vs. 86.4% without).

title: Across Generations, Sizes, and Types, Large Language Models Poorly Report Self-Confidence in Gastroenterology Clinical Reasoning Tasks
outcome: Confidence calibration of LLM self-reported certainty on gastroenterology board-style questions (Brier score, AUROC)
effect: All 48 models showed poor certainty estimation. Even the best-calibrated models had substantial overconfidence (Brier 0.15-0.2, AUROC ~0.6). Models stayed highly certain regardless of question difficulty.
quote: Even the best-calibrated systems (o1 preview, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet) showed substantial overconfidence (Brier scores 0.15-0.2, AUROC ~0.6).

title: Empirical Review of LLM-driven Classification of Multidimensional Sleep Health Mentions from Free-Text Clinical Notes
outcome: Classification accuracy, latency and span identification of fine-tuned discriminative vs generative LLMs
effect: Fine-tuned discriminative models consistently gave higher classification accuracy, lower inference latency, and more robust span-level identification than prompted or fine-tuned generative LLMs, given adequate training data.
quote: Our experiments demonstrate that fine-tuned discriminative models consistently provide higher classification accuracy, lower inference latency, and more robust span-level identification than either prompted or fine-tuned generative LLMs, given adequate training data.

title: Empirical Review of LLM-driven Classification of Multidimensional Sleep Health Mentions from Free-Text Clinical Notes
outcome: Model performance differences across patient demographics and clinical departments
effect: Biases associated with patient demographics and clinical departments were reported as persistent challenges; no numbers given in abstract.
quote: Importantly, our results highlight persistent challenges, including difficulty extracting subtle sleep constructs such as sleep efficiency and daytime sleepiness, and biases associated with patient demographics and clinical departments.

title: Enhancing Fairness in Diabetes Prediction Systems through Smart User Interface Design
outcome: Fairness and prediction performance after Smart UI
quote: The Smart UI significantly reduced disparities: for age, the equal opportunity difference (EOD) improved from 0.35 to 0.25, with accuracy rising from 90.52% to 91.83%; for BMI, EOD decreased from 0.56 to 0.38, with the F1-score increasing from 83.89% to 86.37%.

title: AI-literacy training enhances physician-LLM diagnostic collaboration in a resource-limited setting: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: Diagnostic reasoning score for physicians with vs without LLM access, plus LLM alone comparison
effect: Physician+LLM 71.4% vs 42.6% conventional resources; adjusted difference 27.5 pp (95% CI 22.8 to 32.2). LLM alone outperformed physician+LLM by 11.5 pp.
quote: Of 58 physicians completing the study, those with LLM access achieved mean diagnostic reasoning scores of 71.4% versus 42.6% with conventional medical resources alone, yielding an adjusted difference of 27.5 percentage points (95% CI, 22.8 to 32.2; P < 0.001).

title: AI-literacy training enhances physician-LLM diagnostic collaboration in a resource-limited setting: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: standalone LLM versus physician-LLM performance
effect: LLM alone outperformed physician plus LLM by 11.5 percentage points (95% CI, 5.5 to 17.5; P < 0.001).
quote: While LLM alone outperformed the trained physician group by 11.5 percentage points (95% CI, 5.5 to 17.5; P < 0.001), in 38% of cases the physician plus LLM group surpassed the median LLM-alone performance, highlighting physician-AI complementarities.

title: AI-literacy training enhances physician-LLM diagnostic collaboration in a resource-limited setting: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: Human-AI team diagnostic reasoning versus physicians alone and LLM alone
effect: Physician+LLM 71.4% vs 42.6% without LLM; LLM alone exceeded trained physicians by 11.5 pp; in 38% of cases physician+LLM surpassed median LLM-alone.
quote: While LLM alone outperformed the trained physician group by 11.5 percentage points (95% CI, 5.5 to 17.5; P < 0.001), in 38% of cases the physician plus LLM group surpassed the median LLM-alone performance, highlighting physician-AI complementarities.

title: AI-literacy training enhances physician-LLM diagnostic collaboration in a resource-limited setting: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: diagnostic reasoning score of LLM alone versus physician plus LLM
effect: LLM alone outperformed trained physician group by 11.5 percentage points (95% CI, 5.5 to 17.5; P < 0.001)
quote: While LLM alone outperformed the trained physician group by 11.5 percentage points (95% CI, 5.5 to 17.5; P < 0.001), in 38% of cases the physician plus LLM group surpassed the median LLM-alone performance, highlighting physician-AI complementarities.

title: Clinically Interpretable Deep Learning via Sparse BagNets for Epiretinal Membrane and Related Pathology Detection
outcome: Detection performance of inherently interpretable sparse BagNet versus comparable black-box model
effect: Sparse BagNet performed on par with a comparable black-box model and generalised well to external data.
quote: It performed on par with a comparable black-box model and generalised well to external data.

title: Clinically Interpretable Deep Learning via Sparse BagNets for Epiretinal Membrane and Related Pathology Detection
outcome: Alignment of model visual explanations with clinical expertise in ophthalmologist user study
effect: User study with ophthalmologists showed the visual explanations from sparse BagNet were well-aligned with clinical expertise; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: Through a user study with ophthalmologists, we showed that the visual explanations readily provided by the sparse BagNet model for its decisions are well-aligned with clinical expertise.

title: Knowing When Not to Decide: Multi-Pathology Chest X-Ray Classification with Rejection Mechanisms
outcome: Accuracy-coverage trade-off when model abstains on uncertain chest X-ray predictions and defers to experts
effect: Selective rejection improved the trade-off between diagnostic accuracy and coverage; entropy-based rejection gave the highest average AuC across all pathologies. No numeric values reported in the abstract.
quote: Experiments conducted on three large public datasets (PadChest, NIH ChestX-ray14, and MIMIC-CXR) demonstrate that selective rejection improves the trade-off between diagnostic accuracy and coverage, with entropy-based rejection yielding the highest average AuC across all pathologies.
sample_unit: chest X-ray images (three public datasets: PadChest, NIH ChestX-ray14, MIMIC-CXR)

title: From Tool to Teammate: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Clinician-AI Collaborative Workflows for Diagnosis
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of clinicians with collaborative AI workflows versus traditional resources
effect: Clinicians using collaborative workflows achieved 85% (AI-first) and 82% (AI-second) accuracy versus 75% with traditional resources (p < 0.0004 and p < 0.00001); no significant difference from AI-alone at 90%.
quote: Clinicians using either collaborative workflow outperformed those using traditional tools, achieving average accuracies of 85% (AI-first) and 82% (AI-second), compared to 75% with traditional resources (p < 0.0004 and p < 0.00001; mean differences = 9.8% and 6.8%; 95% CI = 4.6%–15% and 4.0%–9.6%).

title: From Tool to Teammate: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Clinician-AI Collaborative Workflows for Diagnosis
outcome: diagnostic accuracy versus traditional resources
quote: Clinicians using either collaborative workflow outperformed those using traditional tools, achieving average accuracies of 85% (AI-first) and 82% (AI-second), compared to 75% with traditional resources (p < 0.0004 and p < 0.00001; mean differences = 9.8% and 6.8%; 95% CI = 4.6%–15% and 4.0%–9.6%).

title: External Validation of a Web- and Artificial Intelligence-Based HIV/STI Risk Assessment Tool: Performance Evaluation Using Data from Sydney Sexual Health Centre
outcome: External validation AUC at a new site versus original validation, pretrained models unmodified
effect: AUCs at SSHC were 0.67 (HIV), 0.70 (syphilis), 0.73 (gonorrhoea), 0.65 (chlamydia), lower than original MSHC validation metrics (0.74-0.87, all p<0.001).
quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values using data from SSHC were 0.67 (95% CI: 0.65–0.68) for HIV, 0.70 (95% CI: 0.69–0.71) for syphilis, 0.73 (95% CI: 0.73–0.74) for gonorrhoea, and 0.65 (95% CI: 0.65–0.66) for chlamydia, which were lower than the original MSHC validation metrics (0.74–0.87, all p < 0.001).

title: External Validation of a Web- and Artificial Intelligence-Based HIV/STI Risk Assessment Tool: Performance Evaluation Using Data from Sydney Sexual Health Centre
outcome: Model performance across demographic subgroups (MSM, age)
effect: Performance varied across subgroups: HIV AUC 0.78 among men who have sex with men; gonorrhoea AUC 0.79 among attendees <25 years.
quote: Notably, model performance varied across demographic subgroups, with stronger HIV prediction among men who have sex with men with an AUC of 0.78 and better gonorrhoea prediction among younger attendees < 25 years with an AUC value of 0.79.

title: Benchmarking Artificial Intelligence vs General Practitioners Decision-Making in Same-Day Appointments Triage: A Mixed-Methods Study in UK Primary Care
outcome: AI urgency triage under-triage and over-triage versus GP ratings
effect: 83.7% categorical agreement (κ 0.69); greater likelihood of over-triage, rarely under-triaging; no cases deemed non-urgent by AI later reclassified as emergencies by GPs.
quote: No cases deemed non-urgent by AI were later reclassified as emergencies by GPs.

title: Benchmarking Artificial Intelligence vs General Practitioners Decision-Making in Same-Day Appointments Triage: A Mixed-Methods Study in UK Primary Care
outcome: Agreement of AI triage urgency scores with GP urgency ratings
effect: Spearman ρ=0.796; 83.7% categorical agreement across eight urgency levels (κ 0.69).
quote: There was a strong correlation between AI and GP urgency ratings (ρ=0.796,  p 0.001), with 83.7% categorical agreement across eight urgency levels (κ 0.69,  p 0.001).

title: Enhancing Privacy-Preserving Deployable Large Language Models for Perioperative Complication Detection: A Targeted Strategy with LoRA Fine-tuning
outcome: AI model performance for perioperative complication detection compared with human experts on same records
effect: State-of-the-art models consistently outperformed human experts; fine-tuned 4B model F1 rose from 0.18 to 0.55 versus human experts' F1=0.526; 8B model F1>0.61.
quote: Initial evaluations revealed that state-of-the-art models consistently outperformed human experts, particularly reasoning models.

title: Completeness and Quality of Neurology Referral Letters Generated by a Large Language Model for Standardized Scenarios
outcome: Content gaps and management variability in LLM-generated neurology referral letters
effect: Noticeable gaps in history of present illness and physical findings in 72% (36/50) of letters; case management score varied (mean 2.18, SD 0.85).
quote: Noticeable gaps in content, particularly in history of present illness and physical findings, were identified in 72% (36/50) of the letters.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Towards Robust Artificial Intelligence Bone Segmentation in Socio-Technical Systems
outcome: Segmentation accuracy variation across voxel size, orientation, and osteosynthesis or pathology
effect: Segmentation accuracy varied by up to 25% depending on voxel size, bone orientation, and patient conditions such as osteosynthesis or pathology; metallic osteosynthesis and anatomical complexity significantly degraded results.
quote: We show that segmentation accuracy varies by up to 25% depending on socio-technical factors such as voxel size, bone orientation, and patient conditions such as osteosynthesis or pathology.

title: Evaluating User Experiences with an AI Chatbot for Health-Related Social Needs: A Cross-Sectional Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Intent accuracy of a RAG-grounded chatbot across message turns
effect: DAPHNE, using retrieval-augmented generation to ground every recommendation in a live social-care API, achieved 99% intent accuracy in 1,523 message turns.
quote: Furthermore, DAPHNE (using retrieval-augmented generation to ground every recommendation in a live social-care API) achieved 99 % intent accuracy in 1,523 message turns.

title: Evaluating User Experiences with an AI Chatbot for Health-Related Social Needs: A Cross-Sectional Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Usability and trust differences across demographic subgroups
effect: Usability and trust were broadly consistent across most demographic groups, though participants with higher education and lower income showed modest decrements in usability.
quote: Regression analysis showed usability and trust were broadly consistent across most demographic groups, though participants with higher education and lower income showed modest decrements in usability.

title: Rural Medical Centers Struggle to Produce Well-Calibrated Clinical Prediction Models: Data Augmentation Can Help
outcome: Model calibration variation across hospital sites by rurality
effect: Several factors associated with rurality were correlated with model miscalibration across sites.
quote: Several factors associated with rurality were correlated with model miscalibration and rural sites failed to meet sample size requirements for local recalibration.

title: Rural Medical Centers Struggle to Produce Well-Calibrated Clinical Prediction Models: Data Augmentation Can Help
outcome: Local recalibration sample size feasibility
effect: Rural sites failed sample size requirements for local recalibration; no counts or thresholds reported.
quote: Several factors associated with rurality were correlated with model miscalibration and rural sites failed to meet sample size requirements for local recalibration.

title: Rural Medical Centers Struggle to Produce Well-Calibrated Clinical Prediction Models: Data Augmentation Can Help
outcome: model calibration and sample size sufficiency for local recalibration
effect: Factors associated with rurality correlated with model miscalibration, and rural sites failed to meet sample size requirements for local recalibration.
quote: Several factors associated with rurality were correlated with model miscalibration and rural sites failed to meet sample size requirements for local recalibration.

title: Evaluating Language Models for Simplifying Health Literacy Materials
outcome: Readability and semantic fidelity of LLM-simplified health texts across general-purpose and domain-adapted models
effect: General-purpose LLMs reduced sentence complexity and improved fluency but occasionally introduced semantic shifts or omitted critical health information; domain-adapted models were more faithful but less readable due to retained jargon.
quote: Our findings reveal that while general-purpose LLMs excel at reducing sentence complexity and improving fluency, they occasionally introduce semantic shifts or omit critical health information.

title: Real-World Impact of an AI-Driven Teleradiology Workflow for Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection: Reducing Diagnostic Delays Across a Multicenter Emergency Network
outcome: PACS-to-assessment time and report turnaround time before vs after AI triage prioritization
effect: Mean PTAT reduced by 13.72 min (p=0.002) and RTAT by 26.62 min (p=0.001); overnight reduction of 26 min (p=0.001); ICH-positive PTAT drop of 31.43 min not significant.
quote: Integrating an AI-driven tool for the detection of ICH into a teleradiology workflow significantly reduced PTAT and RTAT without compromising diagnostic accuracy.

title: An interdisciplinary, randomized, single-blind evaluation of state-of-the-art large language models for their implications and risks in medical diagnosis and management
outcome: Hallucination severity and incompetence in general-purpose LLM clinical responses rated by specialists
effect: 40 hallucination instances (fabricated conditions, medications, classification errors) and incompetence (scores ≤4) across specialties; top models scored about 6.0 of 10.
quote: Instances of incompetence (scores ≤4) were detected across specialties, and 40 hallucination instances involving fabricated conditions, medications, and classification errors.

title: LLM Reasoning Does Not Protect Against Clinical Cognitive Biases - An Evaluation Using BiasMedQA
outcome: LLM accuracy on clinical vignettes with cognitive-bias-inducing input framing, base versus reasoning models
effect: Reasoning did not consistently prevent cognitive bias; reasoning models had better overall performance (OR 4.0 Llama, OR 3.6 Qwen), but Llama reasoning increased vulnerability to frequency bias (OR 0.6) and recency bias (OR 0.5).
quote: In neither of the two models, reasoning capabilities were able to consistently prevent cognitive bias, although both reasoning models achieved better overall performance compared to their respective base model (OR 4.0 for Llama-3.3-70B, OR 3.6 for Qwen3-32B).

title: Comparative Analysis of Multimodal Large Language Models GPT-4o and o1 vs Clinicians in Clinical Case Challenge Questions
outcome: Reproducibility of correct answers across five repeated trials
effect: Across five trials, GPT-4o and o1 provided the correct answer 5/5 times in 86.2% and 90.7% of cases, respectively, indicating some run-to-run inconsistency.
quote: Across five trials, GPT-4o and o1 provided the correct answer 5/5 times in 86.2% and 90.7% of the cases, respectively.

title: Bridging the Semantic Gaps: Improving MVQA Consistency with LLM-Augmented Question Sets
outcome: Answer consistency of medical VQA models across paraphrased versions of the same question
effect: Models flip answers when the same query is rephrased. Fine-tuning on LLM-augmented paraphrases raised mean answer accuracy by 19.4% and TAR-SC (accuracy plus across-paraphrase agreement) by 11.6%.
quote: We confront a critical yet under-studied weakness of Medical Visual Question Answering (MVQA): models often flip their answers when clinicians phrase the same diagnostic query differently.

title: Assessing Large Language Model Utility and Limitations in Diabetes Education: A Cross-Sectional Study of Patient Interactions and Specialist Evaluations
outcome: Specialist-rated accuracy and hallucinations in ChatGPT answers to patient diabetes questions
effect: Reviewers detected occasional inaccuracies and hallucinations; 98% of answers judged informative and empathetic; ophthalmologists rated clarity 3.09/5 and completeness 2.94/5.
quote: Reviewers detected occasional inaccuracies and hallucinations.

title: Early Stage Melanoma Benchmark Dataset
outcome: Performance of melanoma models on new early-stage dataset versus ISIC training-domain datasets
effect: Significant performance drop on the new early-stage melanoma dataset compared with results on ISIC Challenge datasets; limited capability to detect early-stage melanoma. No numbers in abstract.
quote: We evaluated several state-of-the-art deep learning models on this dataset and observed a significant drop in performance compared to their results on the ISIC Challenge datasets.

title: Assessment of the credibility of generative artificial intelligence large language models on nutritional guidelines for orthodontic patients
outcome: Readability of LLM nutrition guidance for orthodontic patients (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level)
effect: BOS and AAO sources were more readable than the LLMs. ChatGPT 4.0 was the most readable LLM but was still difficult for readers.
quote: The readability of the responses from LLMs was difficult.

title: Preserving Privacy, Increasing Accessibility, and Reducing Cost: An On-Device Artificial Intelligence Model for Medical Transcription and Note Generation
outcome: Major hallucinations and factual correctness in AI-generated notes on ACI benchmark, base vs fine-tuned model
effect: Major hallucinations fell from 85 to 35 cases after fine-tuning, so the base model hallucinated often and the tuned model still did; factual correctness rose from 2.81 to 3.54 on a 5-point scale.
quote: Clinical quality assessments showed marked reduction in major hallucinations (from 85 to 35 cases) and enhanced factual correctness (2.81 to 3.54 on 5-point scale).
sample_unit: transcripts (100 endocrinology transcripts and 140 modified ACI benchmark cases)

title: Introducing Answered with Evidence - a framework for evaluating whether LLM responses to biomedical questions are founded in evidence
outcome: reliable evidence-grounded answers
effect: Public-information LLMs varied greatly; ensemble agreement was 49%; ensemble plus Alexandria reliable for over 64% of queries.
quote: Combined, the ensemble approach and the Alexandria custom built source enabled reliable answers to over 64% of biomedical queries.

title: MedReadCtrl: Personalizing medical text generation with readability-controlled instruction learning
outcome: Readability instruction-following error and expert preference for readability-controlled versus GPT-4 outputs
effect: MedReadCtrl had lower readability instruction-following error than GPT-4 (1.39 vs. 1.59 on ReadMe, p<0.001). Experts preferred MedReadCtrl 71.7% vs. 23.3%, especially at low literacy levels.
quote: MedReadCtrl achieves significantly lower readability instruction-following errors than GPT-4 (e.g., 1.39 vs. 1.59 on ReadMe, p<0.001)

title: A Randomized-Clinical Trial of Two Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribes: Measuring Documentation Efficiency and Physician Burnout
outcome: Time-in-note change comparing two ambient scribe products head-to-head and versus control
effect: Nabla: -9.5% [-17.2,-1.8] vs control and -7.8% [-15.5,-0.1] vs DAX; DAX vs control -1.7% [-9.4,+5.9], p=.66. Burnout gains were similar across vendors.
quote: Nabla users experienced a 9.5% [95% CI:-17.2%,-1.8%] (p=.02) decrease in time-in-note versus the control group and a 7.8% [-15.5%,-0.1%] (p=.05) decrease versus DAX users, while DAX users exhibited no significant change versus control (-1.7% [-9.4%,+5.9%]; p=.66).

title: A Randomized-Clinical Trial of Two Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribes: Measuring Documentation Efficiency and Physician Burnout
outcome: Documentation time and burnout measures after ambient scribe use
effect: Time-in-note fell only with Nabla. Any scribe reduced task load (-35.8) and work exhaustion (-0.27) and raised Mini-Z (+2.76).
quote: Reductions in TL (scale 0-400, TL=-35.8 [-63.7,-7.9]; p=.01) and work exhaustion (scale 0-4, PFI-WE=-0.27 [-0.48,-0.07]; p=.01) were seen with users of any scribe.

title: A Randomized-Clinical Trial of Two Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribes: Measuring Documentation Efficiency and Physician Burnout
outcome: Physician-reported clinically significant inaccuracies in scribe-generated notes
effect: Clinically significant inaccuracies noted 'occasionally' (Likert DAX 2.7 vs Nabla 2.8; p=.68). One Grade 1 adverse event was reported.
quote: One Grade 1 (mild) adverse event was reported, while clinically-significant inaccuracies were noted “occasionally” on 5-point Likert questions (DAX 2.7 [2.4-3.0] vs. Nabla 2.8 [2.6-3.0]; p=.68).

title: Evaluating the Influence of Demographic Identity in the Medical Use of Large Language Models
outcome: LLM accuracy on diagnosis, medication and treatment tasks when patient and doctor race and gender were varied
effect: Significant disparities in accuracy and bias across models and tasks. Llama 3.1-8B was more sensitive to demographics, especially in diagnosis. Largest accuracy drop for Hispanic patients treated by White male doctors.
quote: Notably, we observe the largest accuracy drop when Hispanic patients are treated by White male doctors, underscoring potential risks of bias amplification.

title: From Rule-Based to DeepSeek R1 – A Robust Comparative Evaluation of Fifty Years of Natural Language Processing (NLP) Models To Identify Inflammatory Bowel Disease Cohorts
outcome: F1 and compute cost of simple vs. complex NLP models for IBD cohort identification on the same data
effect: Fine-tuned DistilBERT F1 94.06%; BOW F1 93.38% at 1.63g CO2; LLMs F1 86.65% to 91.58% with higher compute cost (938.5 to 33884.4g CO2) and more bias.
quote: Older NLP approaches, such as BOW, can outperform modern LLMs in clinical cohort detection when properly trained.

title: AI-generated patient-friendly discharge summaries to empower patients
outcome: Patient self-reported understanding after reading AI-generated plain-language discharge summary
effect: 90% (18/20) reported better understanding after reading the summary, including those who initially felt well-informed; 90% found it more helpful than discharge consultations.
quote: Among hospitalized patients recruited at two departments in our tertiary care hospital (n=20), most (90%) reported better understanding after reading the AI-generated summary, including those who initially felt well-informed.

title: Performance of Large Language Artificial Intelligence Models on Clear Aligner Treatment: Evaluation of Accuracy and Readibility in Answering Questions for Patients
outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRES) of ChatGPT 4o answers to patient clear aligner questions
effect: Highest FKGL 14.53 ± 8.88 (usage questions). For the top 10 questions, mean FKGL was 13.37 ± 4.37 and mean FRES was 47.18 ± 23.69, i.e., difficult, college-level text.
quote: For the top 10 questions, the average FKGL was 13.37 ± 4.37, and the average FRES was 47.18 ± 23.69.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT Responses to Frequently Asked Questions on Total Knee Arthroplasty
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of ChatGPT-3.5 answers to patient questions about total knee arthroplasty
effect: FKGL readability scores were high, meaning responses require a high level of education; the abstract reports no numeric FKGL values and says this level can be reduced.
quote: The readability scores for FKGL were high.

title: Evaluation of Large Language Model-Generated Patient Information for Communicating Radiation Risk
outcome: Professional ratings of readability, language suitability and tone of LLM-generated radiation risk patient information
effect: Professional groups differed significantly in scoring readability, language suitability and tone, especially for higher-risk procedures; qualitative feedback showed variable balance of technical accuracy and accessible language.
quote: Significant differences were identified among professional groups in their scoring of readability, language suitability, and tone, particularly for higher-risk procedures.
sample_unit: healthcare professionals rating LLM-generated patient information

title: Large Language Models Improve Coding Accuracy and Reimbursement in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of candidate LLMs versus human coders on the same NICU notes, physician-adjudicated
effect: GPT-o3-mini 79.1% vs human coders 76.3% (P=.52); GPT-4o 58.6% (P<.001 vs both), so the comparison separated a comparable model from an underperforming one.
quote: GPT-4o underperformed at 58.6% (95% CI, 52.5%-64.7%; P < .001 vs both).

title: Evaluating Deep Learning Sepsis Prediction Models in ICUs Under Distribution Shift: A Multi-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: target-data adaptation strategies
effect: DA MMD AUROC = 0.720, nAUPRC = 2.352 vs fusion AUROC = 0.712, nAUPRC = 2.215; p = 0.02, adjusted p = 0.07.
quote: For example, DA with maximum mean discrepancy (DA MMD) achieves superior performance in both area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC = 0.720) and normalized area under the precision-recall curve (nAUPRC = 2.352) compared to fusion training (AUROC = 0.712, nAUPRC = 2.215; p = 0.02, adjusted p = 0.07).

title: Evaluating Deep Learning Sepsis Prediction Models in ICUs Under Distribution Shift: A Multi-Centre Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: Distribution shifts between ICU cohorts and their effect on generalization
effect: Distribution shifts across HiRID, MIMIC-IV and eICU were quantified; poor generalization under external validation is attributed largely to distribution shift arising from heterogeneity in data.
quote: While artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on ICU data show promise for sepsis prediction, their clinical utility is frequently hampered by poor generalization under external validation, largely attributable to distribution shifts arising from heterogeneity in data.

title: Close, But no Cigar: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o and OpenAI o1-preview in Answering Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma-Related Questions
outcome: LLM accuracy, comprehensiveness and safety on NCCN-guideline PDAC clinical questions, including critical errors
effect: o1-preview accuracy 75% vs 60% for ChatGPT-4o; both made critical errors in complex scenarios and caused some potential harm to patients.
quote: However, both models made critical errors in some complex clinical scenarios.

title: Evaluating the Impact of Authoritative and Subjective Cues on Large Language Model Reliability for Clinical Inquiries: An Experimental Study
outcome: LLM accuracy on a clinical question under neutral versus misleading prompt framings
effect: Baseline accuracy 100% for all models; fell to 45% with incorrect self-recall prompts and 1% with authoritative prompts; Cramér's V = 0.75, P < .001.
quote: However, accuracy significantly decreased in conditions with misleading cues, dropping to 45% with self-recall prompts and 1% with authoritative prompts.
sample_unit: test runs (5 models x 5 scenarios x 10 repetitions)

title: Evaluating the Impact of Authoritative and Subjective Cues on Large Language Model Reliability for Clinical Inquiries: An Experimental Study
outcome: Self-rated LLM confidence when accuracy collapsed under authoritative cue
effect: Accuracy collapsed in the authoritative condition, but self-rated confidence stayed high with no statistical difference from baseline.
quote: Notably, while accuracy collapsed in the authoritative condition, the models' self-rated confidence remained high, showing no statistical difference from the baseline condition.
sample_unit: test runs (5 models x 5 scenarios x 10 repetitions)

title: Toward the Autonomous AI Doctor: Quantitative Benchmarking of an Autonomous Agentic AI Versus Board-Certified Clinicians in a Real World Setting
outcome: AI diagnostic and treatment concordance versus board-certified clinicians on same encounters
effect: Top diagnosis matched in 81% of cases; treatment plan aligned in 99.2%; in discordant cases AI superior in 36.1%, human superior in 9.3%.
quote: The top diagnosis of Doctronic and clinician matched in 81% of cases, and the treatment plan aligned in 99.2% of cases.

title: Toward the Autonomous AI Doctor: Quantitative Benchmarking of an Autonomous Agentic AI Versus Board-Certified Clinicians in a Real World Setting
outcome: Agent performance on historical telehealth encounters against clinician reference
effect: 81% top-diagnosis concordance and 99.2% treatment plan alignment across 500 consecutive encounters; no clinical hallucinations.
quote: No clinical hallucinations occurred (e.g., diagnosis or treatment not supported by clinical findings).

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Binary Classification of Pediatric Chest X-Rays: A Comparative Evaluation Using a Public Pneumonia Dataset
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of five multimodal LLMs compared on the same pediatric chest X-ray dataset
effect: GPT-4.1 had 84% sensitivity and 76% specificity; GPT-4o 99%/18%; Gemini 2.5 Pro 97%/25%; Claude 4 Sonnet 100%/0%; Grok 2 Vision 82%/56%.
quote: GPT-4.1 demonstrated the most balanced performance with 84% sensitivity and 76% specificity.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models for Binary Classification of Pediatric Chest X-Rays: A Comparative Evaluation Using a Public Pneumonia Dataset
outcome: Binary pneumonia classification performance of general-purpose multimodal LLMs on pediatric chest X-rays
effect: Most models showed high sensitivity but poor specificity (GPT-4o 18%, Gemini 25%, Claude 0%), indicating a strong false-positive tendency.
quote: Claude 4 Sonnet classified all images as pneumonia (100% sensitivity, 0% specificity).

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Automatic Detection of In-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Multi-Site Analysis of Clinical Notes
outcome: Variation in LLM performance and inter-site agreement across five hospitals
effect: Performance strongly influenced by site-specific documentation practices, with inter-site agreement rates varying by over 20%.
quote: Our systematic analysis of model outputs revealed that performance was strongly influenced by site-specific documentation practices, with inter-site agreement rates varying by over 20%.

title: Impact of LLM Assistance on Physician Decision-Making: A Multi-Country Randomized Controlled Trial  ∗
outcome: Physician clinical vignette performance with vs without GPT-4o access
effect: LLM access improved performance: Kenya 18% (95% CI 12.7 to 23.2), Indonesia 10.7% (5.7 to 15.7), Netherlands 7.2% (3.7 to 10.7), all p<0.001; some physicians without access outperformed those with access.
quote: Results showed that LLM access significantly improved clinical performance, with the largest effect in Kenya (18%, 95% CI: 12.7 to 23.2, p  < 0.001), followed by Indonesia (10.7%, 95% CI: 5.7 to 15.7, p  < 0.001) and the Netherlands (7.2%, 95% CI: 3.7 to 10.7, p  < 0.001).

title: AI-Powered Triage of Suicidal Ideation in Adolescents: A Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models Using Synthetic Clinical Vignettes
outcome: LLM suicide risk classification accuracy against psychiatrist gold standard, especially higher-risk categories
effect: Accuracy GPT-4o 82.5%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 75.0%, Llama-3.1-70B 67.5%; F1-scores showed challenges identifying higher-risk categories, particularly nuanced intent. Emergency evaluation was recommended consistently for high-risk cases.
quote: GPT-4o achieved the highest accuracy (82.5%), followed by Claude 3.5 Sonnet (75.0%) and Llama-3.1-70B (67.5%).

title: AI-Powered Triage of Suicidal Ideation in Adolescents: A Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models Using Synthetic Clinical Vignettes
outcome: Recognition of safety-critical suicide risk and appropriateness of action plans in vignettes
effect: Consistent adherence to basic safety protocols such as emergency evaluation for high-risk cases, but pervasive critical failures: omitted lethal means inquiry, no protective factors, inappropriate reassurance.
quote: Qualitative thematic analysis of the action plans identified consistent adherence to basic safety protocols (e.g., recommending emergency evaluation for high-risk cases).

title: AI-Powered Triage of Suicidal Ideation in Adolescents: A Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models Using Synthetic Clinical Vignettes
outcome: Inappropriate therapeutic reassurance in triage action plans
effect: Models generated clinically inappropriate therapeutic reassurance in a triage context, among pervasive critical failures.
quote: However, significant and critical failures were pervasive, including the omission of crucial inquiries about access to lethal means, failure to incorporate protective factors into planning, and the generation of clinically inappropriate therapeutic reassurance in a triage context.

title: Responsible AI in Action: Planning through Implementation of a Mortality Model for Palliative Care
outcome: 12-month mortality discrimination (AUC) of locally augmented model versus unmodified commercial model
effect: Augmenting the commercial EOLCI with local predictors raised AUC from 0.81 (95% CI 0.80, 0.81) to 0.87 (95% CI 0.86, 0.87); SICLI was very well calibrated.
quote: SICLI was very well calibrated and outperformed the EOLCI (AUC of 0.87 (95% CI:0.86, 0.87) vs. 0.81, (95% CI: (0.80, 0.81)).

title: Responsible AI in Action: Planning through Implementation of a Mortality Model for Palliative Care
outcome: Comparison of new model against existing commercial model on the same data
effect: SICLI outperformed the commercial EOLCI on the same cohort: AUC 0.87 vs 0.81.
quote: SICLI was very well calibrated and outperformed the EOLCI (AUC of 0.87 (95% CI:0.86, 0.87) vs. 0.81, (95% CI: (0.80, 0.81)).

title: Accelerating Insight Discovery in Large Biomedical Text with Scalable Processing Framework
outcome: Accuracy, efficiency, and misinformation risk when LLM answers are grounded in a curated document corpus
effect: Reported improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and computational cost on benchmark datasets; the curated document approach enhanced reliability and reduced misinformation risk. No numbers given in the abstract.
quote: Comparative evaluations on benchmark datasets demonstrate improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and computational cost, with the curated document approach enhancing reliability and reducing misinformation risk.

title: Physician- versus Large Language Model-Generated Clinical Summaries in the Emergency Department
outcome: Comparison of LLM-generated versus physician-authored ED one-liner summaries on accuracy, completeness, utility
effect: LLM summaries rated higher: accuracy 4.18 vs 3.40 (β=0.78, p<.001); completeness 3.69 vs 3.25 (p=.005); utility 3.88 vs 3.21 (p<.001). LLM preferred in 50.5% of encounters, physician in 38.4%.
quote: Across all dimensions, LLM-generated summaries received higher ratings than physician-authored summaries.

title: SROTAS IQ: An AI-Based Clinical Trial Matching Platform: A Validation Study in Breast Cancer
outcome: Accuracy of LLM trial eligibility decisions versus two-oncologist consensus on synthetic patients
effect: 88% of 150 patient-trial eligibility decisions correct; 90% or greater accuracy in 5 of 10 trials; lower accuracy in more intricate protocols.
quote: Across 150 patient-trial evaluations, the model correctly classified 88% of overall eligibility decisions.

title: Evaluation of Gender Bias in the Evaluation of Synthetic Cardiovascular Disease Cases with Open Source LLMs
outcome: Change in LLM cardiovascular ratings when only patient gender varied in identical vignettes
effect: Minimal gender differences; only Gemma-2b diagnostic certainty differed for female patients (58% vs 48%, p=0.031, adjusted p=0.092). Effect sizes small (Cohen's h 0.01-0.18).
quote: Only one statistically significant finding emerged: Gemma-2b assigned higher diagnostic certainty to female patients in initial presentations (58% vs. 48%, p=0.031, adjusted p=0.092).
sample_unit: model responses (500 synthetic cases x 3 models)

title: Evaluation of Gender Bias in the Evaluation of Synthetic Cardiovascular Disease Cases with Open Source LLMs
outcome: Gender subgroup differences in LLM CAD likelihood, certainty, and test usefulness
effect: No gender-based differences reached significance after multiple-comparison adjustment; Cliff's delta -0.11 to 0.12.
quote: No other gender-based differences reached significance after multiple-comparison adjustment.
sample_unit: model responses (500 synthetic cases x 3 models)

title: Evaluation of Gender Bias in the Evaluation of Synthetic Cardiovascular Disease Cases with Open Source LLMs
outcome: Variability between candidate LLMs in diagnostic confidence and test recommendations
effect: Substantial inter-model variability: Gemma-2b and Phi assertive, TinyLLaMA conservative.
quote: Substantial inter-model variability was observed, with Gemma-2b and Phi demonstrating assertive diagnostic patterns while TinyLLaMA showed conservative tendencies.
sample_unit: model responses (500 synthetic cases x 3 models)

title: A Mixed-Methods Evaluation of Clinician Experiences and Adoption Patterns of an EHR-integrated Generative AI-based Clinical Decision Support in Kenya
outcome: Clinician adoption of LLM decision support under structured change management
effect: AI Consult use across 16 facilities rose from 4% to 47% over 8 months; 21.7% of 258,106 episodes used it. No comparator without change management.
quote: It is possible to achieve non-trivial adoption of GenAI-based CDSS (4% to 47% over 8 months) when supported by structured change management.

title: Algorithmic Opacity in Opioid Risk Scoring: Need for Transparent AI Regulation in HealthcareSherry
outcome: Independent reproduction of a proprietary opioid risk score's reported performance on real-world datasets
effect: Models built from the documented feature set, with added socioeconomic covariates and multiple ML architectures, all performed well below reported benchmarks on California PDMP and IQVIA PharMetrics Plus data.
quote: Despite reconstructing the documented feature set, adding socioeconomic covariates, and rigorously evaluating multiple supervised machine learning architectures, all models performed well below reported benchmarks.
sample_unit: not reported in abstract (PDMP and claims records)

title: Expert-level validation of AI-generated medical text with scalable language models
outcome: Agreement of automated LM evaluators with physicians in detecting errors in LM-generated medical text
effect: MedVAL fine-tuning raised average F1 from 66% to 83% (p < 0.001), with per-sample safety classification scores up to 86%; GPT-4o improved by 8%.
quote: MedVAL fine-tuning significantly improves (p < 0.001) alignment with physicians on both seen and unseen tasks, increasing average F1 scores from 66% to 83%, with per-sample safety classification scores up to 86%.

title: Expert-level validation of AI-generated medical text with scalable language models
outcome: Automated LM validator detection of factual inconsistencies in generated medical outputs versus physician review
effect: Average F1 rose from 66% to 83% after MedVAL fine-tuning (p < 0.001); safety classification up to 86%.
quote: MedVAL fine-tuning significantly improves (p < 0.001) alignment with physicians on both seen and unseen tasks, increasing average F1 scores from 66% to 83%, with per-sample safety classification scores up to 86%.

title: Exploring ChatGPT’s capabilities, stability, potential and risks in conducting psychological counseling through simulations in school counseling
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT-4 empathy labels and sentiment scores across three repeated runs
effect: Moderate reliability across repeated replies (Fleiss' kappa = 0.59; ICC = 0.62). Confusing or realization labels in 2.5% of outputs, with minor sentiment drift.
quote: Stability metrics indicated moderate reliability (κ = 0.59; ICC = 0.62), while occasional confusing or realization labels (2.5% of outputs) and minor sentiment drift underscored randomness as a risk.

title: Exploring ChatGPT’s capabilities, stability, potential and risks in conducting psychological counseling through simulations in school counseling
outcome: Warmth, empathy and sentiment of ChatGPT-4 counseling replies, measured with NLP classifiers
effect: 97.5% warm responses, 94.2% empathy classification, mean compound sentiment 0.93 ± 0.19; automated proxies only, no clinician ratings.
quote: ChatGPT-4 achieved 97.5% warm responses, 94.2% empathy classification and a mean compound sentiment score of 0.93 ± 0.19.

title: Comparative Evaluation of State‑of‑the‑Art Large Language Models for Patient Education Prior to Interventional Radiology procedures
outcome: Radiologist-rated accuracy (5-point Likert) of LLM answers to IR procedure patient questions
effect: OpenBioLLM-8b (BEST 3.51, CT-HDR 3.32, TAPE 3.34) and BioMistral-7b (BEST 2.92, CT-HDR 3.03, TAPE 3.33) scored significantly worse than DeepSeek-V3 and ChatGPT-4o (DeepSeek BEST 4.49, CT-HDR 4.24).
quote: In contrast, OpenBioLLM-8b (BEST 3.51 (± 1.15), CT-HDR 3.32 (± 1.13), TAPE 3.34 (± 1.16)) and BioMistral-7b (BEST 2.92 (± 1.35), CT-HDR 3.03 (± 1.06), TAPE 3.33 (± 1.28)) performed significantly worse than DeepSeek-V3 and ChatGPT-4o across all procedures.

title: Algorithmic Fairness of QPrediction Cardiometabolic Risk Prediction Models
outcome: Subgroup discrimination parity (FNR, TNR) across ethnicity, education, income, deprivation
effect: Prediction parity was not reached in FNR and TNR by ethnicity, education level, household income and Townsend deprivation score; parity was achieved for immigration status.
quote: Prediction parity was not reached in FNR and TNR in terms of ethnicity, education level, average household income before taxation, and Townsend deprivation score.

title: Algorithmic Fairness of QPrediction Cardiometabolic Risk Prediction Models
outcome: Calibration of predicted versus observed risk in an external validation cohort
effect: All three models systematically overpredicted risk in the UK Biobank validation cohorts, with the degree of overprediction varying between models.
quote: Overall, all models showed systematic overprediction of risks for the UK Biobank validation cohorts, with the degree of overprediction varying between the models.

title: External Validation of a Machine Learning Model to Predict Postpartum Hemorrhage in a US Northeastern Healthcare System

quote: Additionally, in an adversarial re-run that inserted one fabricated medical detail into otherwise standard clinical cases, GPT-5 adopted or elaborated on the fabrication in 65% of runs (vs 53% for GPT-4o).
sample_unit: physician-validated emergency vignettes (each replayed across 32 sociodemographic labels plus control)

title: AI-driven quality assurance for emergency department documentation: Pilot comparison with physician peer review of chest pain cases
outcome: Inter-rater agreement among human physician reviewers used as reference for documentation quality
effect: Human reviewer overall score CCCs ranged from 0.28 to 0.86; inter-human pass/fail Kappa ranged from -0.12 to 0.68.
