quote: Inter-rater agreement among human reviewers showed substantial variability, with overall score CCCs ranging from 0.28 to 0.86.

title: Development and Application of a Machine Learning-Based Screening Model for Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease and Economic Benefit Evaluation: A Real-World Study
outcome: Prospective accuracy of the RF model on a second-batch cohort, evaluated by AUROC
effect: Prospective cohort of 74 individuals gave AUROC 0.82, 0.59, and 0.84 for no, mild, and moderate-to-severe NAFLD.
quote: The 295 cases collected in the first batch were used for model development and software creation, and the developed model was then evaluated in a prospective cohort of 74 individuals in the second batch, achieving AUROC values of 0.82, 0.59, and 0.84 for predicting no, mild, and moderate-to-severe NAFLD, respectively.

title: Detecting and Preventing Harmful Behaviors in AI Companions: Development and Evaluation of the SHIELD Supervisory System
outcome: Rate of concerning content (manipulative engagement, boundary violations) in AI companion outputs with vs without SHIELD supervisor
effect: Baseline concerning content 10–16% reduced to 3–8% with SHIELD (50–79% relative reduction), preserving 95% of appropriate interactions; sensitivity 59%, specificity 95%.
quote: Testing across five prominent LLMs (GPT-4.1, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemma 3 1B, Kimi K2, Llama Scout 4 17B) showed that the baseline rate of concerning content (10–16%) was significantly reduced with SHIELD (to 3–8%), a 50–79% relative reduction, while preserving 95% of appropriate interactions.

title: Postprocessing-Enhanced Machine Learning for Reliable Real-Time Sleep Staging in Closed-Loop Neuromodulation
outcome: Precision and recall of sleep staging under synthetic input noise, with vs without smoothing
effect: Under low and high synthetic noise (σ > 0.2), smoothed outputs retain 10–15% higher precision and recall across all stages.
quote: Smoothing improves generalization and robustness: under both low and high synthetic noise (  σ > 0.2), smoothed outputs retain 10–15% higher precision and recall across all stages.

title: Postprocessing-Enhanced Machine Learning for Reliable Real-Time Sleep Staging in Closed-Loop Neuromodulation
outcome: stage-trigger precision
effect: Hybrid high-confidence/low-uncertainty control achieved 80% Wake, 96% N2, 98% N3, and 86% REM precision.
quote: Control logic further enhances reliability: our hybrid method achieves 80% (Wake), 96% (N2), 98% (N3), and 86% (REM) precision.

title: Evaluating the Ethical and Clinical Implications of Generative AI in Patient-Centric Medical Applications
outcome: Change in model responses when patient demographic attributes were varied in queries
effect: Both GPT-4 and Med-PaLM 2 showed significant bias when demographic variations were introduced, especially race and immigration differences. No numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: It is also noticeable that both systems exhibited significant degree of bias in the same when demographical variations were introduced, especially in the case of race and immigration differences.

title: Evaluating the Ethical and Clinical Implications of Generative AI in Patient-Centric Medical Applications
outcome: Whether responses cited credible sources and disclosed limitations/AI disclaimers
effect: Both models disclaimed in fewer than 20% of cases and did not reference credible sources; GPT-4 accuracy 83% vs Med-PaLM 2 72%.
quote: The findings indicate that GPT-4 compared more favorably to Med-PaLM 2 in their clinical accuracy (83% vs. 72%), empathy (3.9 vs. 3.1) and trust (4.2 vs. 3.6), though both generative AI models showed great weaknesses in transparency where they were disclaiming in less than 20 percent of cases, and do not reference credible sources.

title: OOD Detectors Are Best Used Runtime Verifiers, Not Semantic Shift Classifiers
outcome: Expected lifetime cost per patient with OOD runtime verifiers versus conventional system in polyp segmentation
effect: Implementing OOD detectors as runtime verifiers reduced expected costs per patient by upwards of 40% versus a conventionally implemented system.
quote: Our results show that implementing OOD detectors as runtime verifiers reduces the expected costs per patient by upwards of 40%.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-5 Responses in Obstetric and Gynecological Emergencies: Concordance, Readability, and Clinical Reliability
outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-5 emergency management responses with guidelines and specialist gold standard
effect: High agreement (5/5) in 5 scenarios (33.3%), moderate (4/5) in 7 (46.7%), low (≤3/5) in 3 (20.0%); omissions of scoring systems and mortality risk emphasis.
quote: High agreement (5/5) was observed in 5 scenarios (33.3%), moderate agreement (4/5) in 7 scenarios (46.7%), and low agreement (≤ 3/5) in 3 scenarios (20.0%).

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-5 Responses in Obstetric and Gynecological Emergencies: Concordance, Readability, and Clinical Reliability
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-5 responses (FRES, FKGL, SMOG, CLI)
effect: FRES 40.5 ± 2.5; FKGL 11.6 ± 1.2; SMOG 10.9 ± 0.8; CLI 10.9 ± 0.8, indicating moderately technical language.
quote: Readability analyses showed that responses contained a moderate amount of technical language (FRES score = 40.5 ± 2.5; FKGL score = 11.6 ± 1.2; SMOG score = 10.9 ± 0.8; and CLI score = 10.9 ± 0.8).

title: Arkangel AI, OpenEvidence, ChatGPT, Medisearch: are they objectively up to medical standards? A real-life assessment of LLMs in healthcare
outcome: Clinician-rated dissatisfaction that cited references are real sources
effect: Dissatisfaction with real source of references was GPT-Personalized 75% and GPT-Regular 97%; ArkangelAI-Deep, ChatGPT-Deep, and OpenEvidence obtained 100% satisfaction.
quote: The most Dissatisfaction was for the real source of references: GPT-Personalized 75%, GPT-Regular 97%.

title: Safety Evaluation of a Clinical-Grade Generative AI Agent for Anxiety and Depression Symptoms
outcome: Harmful outputs in simulated high-risk synthetic patient conversations, including safety-critical scenarios
effect: Potentially harmful outputs occurred in <1 in 10,000 responses (0.01%, 95% CI [0.01%, 0.03%]) across 43,325 simulated responses; none encouraged harm to self or others.
quote: In simulation experiments, potentially harmful outputs occurred in <1 in 10,000 responses (0.01%, 95% CI [0.01%, 0.03%]); none encouraged harm to self or others, judged or actively invalidated the user, or used offensive language.
sample_unit: US adults with moderate-to-severe anxiety and depression symptoms (real-world study); 43,325 simulated responses in simulation

title: Safety Evaluation of a Clinical-Grade Generative AI Agent for Anxiety and Depression Symptoms
outcome: Offensive, invalidating or judgmental language in generative AI outputs during simulation
effect: No simulated outputs judged or actively invalidated the user or used offensive language.
quote: In simulation experiments, potentially harmful outputs occurred in <1 in 10,000 responses (0.01%, 95% CI [0.01%, 0.03%]); none encouraged harm to self or others, judged or actively invalidated the user, or used offensive language.
sample_unit: US adults with moderate-to-severe anxiety and depression symptoms (real-world study); 43,325 simulated responses in simulation

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Automated Triage of Breast Cancer Biopsies in Malaysia: A Pragmatic Trial to Reduce Resource Consumption and Diagnostic Turnaround Time
outcome: Suspicious-case diagnostic turnaround time
effect: Average TAT for suspicious cases reduced 38.2%, from 7.2 to 4.5 days; benign TAT slightly increased.
quote: The simulation demonstrated that the triage system reduced the average TAT for suspicious cases by 38.2% (from 7.2 to 4.5 days) while slightly increasing the TAT for benign cases.

title: Performance of a Large Language Model in BI-RADS Classification of Ultrasound Based Breast Lesions
outcome: Accuracy of general-purpose LLM in BI-RADS classification of breast ultrasound versus radiologist ground truth
effect: Overall accuracy 19.01%; ROC-AUC 0.5-0.6 across categories; malignancy-probable categories (4b-5) akin to random chance; predictions typically 1-2 categories off.
quote: We found that the overall accuracy of Gemini 2.0 was 19.01% in predicting the BI-RADS classification of the breast lesions, and those of each category did not significantly differ from one another.

title: Benchmarking generative AI tools for literature retrieval and summarization in genomic variant interpretation
outcome: Citation relevance and hallucination robustness of AI literature summaries across five tools
effect: VarChat ranked highest on accuracy, citation relevance and hallucination robustness; GPT-4o second; Perplexity and ScholarAI, despite being literature-focused, ranked lowest across most metrics.
quote: VarChat emerged as the top-ranked tool, showing the highest summarization accuracy, citation relevance, and robustness against hallucinations.

title: Benchmarking generative AI tools for literature retrieval and summarization in genomic variant interpretation
outcome: Reliability of AI-generated genomic variant literature summaries as judged by blinded domain experts
effect: Tool performance varied widely and was sensitive to literature scarcity; authors conclude reliable integration requires expert validation and domain-related fine-tuning.
quote: While some platforms already provide useful outputs, reliable integration into basic and clinical research requires expert validation and domain-related fine-tuning.

title: Prospective Validation of the EAC+ Algorithm for Surgical Timing in Multi-System Trauma: A Multicentre Pragmatic Trial
outcome: Accuracy, AUROC, precision and recall of EAC+ versus standard practice, EAC thresholds, logistic regression, decision tree
effect: EAC+ achieved the highest accuracy (91.4%), AUROC (0.94), precision (0.89), and recall (0.92) versus comparators; also shortened ICU stay by 1.6 days and lowered 30-day mortality.
quote: EAC+ achieved the highest accuracy (91.4%), AUROC (0.94), precision (0.89), and recall (0.92), while reducing unnecessary surgical delays, shortening ICU stay by an average of 1.6 days, and lowering 30-day mortality.

title: Prospective Validation of the EAC+ Algorithm for Surgical Timing in Multi-System Trauma: A Multicentre Pragmatic Trial
outcome: Multisite prospective validation across five Level 1 trauma centres
effect: Prospective multicentre evaluation in 3,512 patients across five Level 1 trauma centres; results reported as validated across centres, without per-site breakdown in the text.
quote: Involving 3,512 patients across five Level 1 trauma centres, the algorithm was benchmarked against standard practice, original EAC thresholds, logistic regression, and decision tree models.

title: Probing the Surgical Competence of LLMs: A global health study leveraging AfriMedQA benchmarks
outcome: LLM accuracy on specialty-specific benchmark questions, including surgery, pathology, and obstetrics
effect: Top models (o1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) exceeded 82% mean accuracy but consistently underperformed in surgery, pathology, and obstetrics compared with medical disciplines.
quote: Top models (o1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5) achieved mean accuracies exceeding 82%, showing strong diagnostic reasoning, yet consistently underperformed in surgery, pathology, and obstetrics compared with medical disciplines.
country: Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and other African countries (AfriMed-QA benchmark; authored by African medical professors)

title: Probing the Surgical Competence of LLMs: A global health study leveraging AfriMedQA benchmarks
outcome: Overconfident but incorrect answers from LLMs
effect: Error analyses revealed overconfident but incorrect answers, along with procedural reasoning failures and omission of local clinical guidelines.
quote: Error analyses revealed frequent procedural reasoning failures, omission of local clinical guidelines, and overconfident but incorrect answers.
country: Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and other African countries (AfriMed-QA benchmark; authored by African medical professors)

title: Probing the Surgical Competence of LLMs: A global health study leveraging AfriMedQA benchmarks
outcome: Omission of local clinical guidelines and procedural reasoning failures in LLM answers
effect: Error analyses revealed frequent procedural reasoning failures and omission of local clinical guidelines.
quote: Error analyses revealed frequent procedural reasoning failures, omission of local clinical guidelines, and overconfident but incorrect answers.
country: Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya and other African countries (AfriMed-QA benchmark; authored by African medical professors)

title: When Artificial İntelligence Speaks For The Obstetrician: Multilingual Accuracy On Real Patient Questions
outcome: LLM answer accuracy in Turkish versus English for pregnancy questions
effect: Gemini and DeepSeek answers to English questions had statistically higher accuracy than Turkish (p < 0.05); ChatGPT showed no general accuracy difference between languages.
quote: It was found that Google Gemini and DeepSeek's answers to English questions achieved statistically higher accuracy scores than their answers to Turkish questions (p < 0.05).

title: When Artificial İntelligence Speaks For The Obstetrician: Multilingual Accuracy On Real Patient Questions
outcome: Reliability, validity and accessibility of references cited by LLM answers
effect: ChatGPT had the highest 'perfect reference' rate (78.5% Turkish, 71.4% English), implying the other models' references were less reliable; references may not always be reliable.
quote: In particular, it was found that the response quality of LLMs may suffer for non-native English speakers and that the references provided may not always be reliable.

title: Evaluating an LLM-Assisted Workflow for Clinical Documentation:  A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial on Time and Quality
outcome: Document quality and creation time: clinician review/editing of LLM drafts vs clinician-only vs unedited LLM drafts
effect: Clinician-in-the-loop outperformed clinician-only in most quality domains; LLM-only drafts fastest but lowest quality. Summaries faster (β = −59.4 s, P = .047); referrals slower (β = 94.8 s, P<.001).
quote: LLM-only drafts were fastest but had the lowest quality.

title: Evaluating an LLM-Assisted Workflow for Clinical Documentation:  A Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial on Time and Quality
outcome: document creation time
effect: Summaries were shorter with clinician-in-loop (β = −59.4 seconds; 95% CI, −118.1 to −0.8; P = .047), but referrals took longer (β = 94.8 seconds; 95% CI, 40.4 to 149.3; P<.001).
quote: For referrals, clinician-in-the-loop required more time (β = 94.8 seconds; 95% CI, 40.4 to 149.3; P<.001).

title: Readability Optimization of Layperson Summaries in Urological Oncology Clinical Trials: Outcomes from the BRIDGE-AI 8 Study
outcome: Reading level (FRES) of publicly available ClinicalTrials.gov brief summaries for lay readers
effect: Original human-written summaries had mean FRES 17.0 ± 13.1, far below the recommended middle-school level, versus 73.3 ± 3.5 for GAI summaries (p < 0.0001).
quote: Brief summaries on ClinicalTrials.gov are indented for lay people, however are often written at a reading level that is too advanced for the public.

title: Readability Optimization of Layperson Summaries in Urological Oncology Clinical Trials: Outcomes from the BRIDGE-AI 8 Study
outcome: Readability and content completeness of GAI-generated layperson trial summaries
effect: GAI summaries had mean FRES 73.3 ± 3.5 (middle-school level), simpler syntax and reduced lexical complexity, and 100% inclusion of guideline-defined content elements.
quote: These findings suggest that GAI tools such as Pub2Post can generate patient-facing summaries that are both accessible and comprehensive.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Dental Professionals’ Performance in the Identification of Dental Implant Systems: The Impact of Deep Learning Algorithms – A Diagnostic Accuracy Study
outcome: Dental professionals' implant identification performance with versus without AI assistance, compared with standalone AI
effect: AI assistance significantly improved all metrics across all implant groups (p<0.05) except recall of NucleOSS T4, but assisted performance stayed below standalone AI, indicating automation bias.
quote: AI assistance improved participants’ diagnostic performance across all implant categories but did not exceed the standalone AI model, underscoring the impact of human–AI interaction and automation bias.

title: “Complex models, marginal benefits--a multi-centre development and validation study of early warning scores across 2·16 million patient admissions addressing intercurrent medical interventions”
outcome: Comparison of ML early warning model against NEWS and simpler scores on discrimination and net benefit
effect: XGB-EWS AUC 0.932 vs DEWS 0.908, NEWS 0.902, NEWS-Light 0.879; max net benefit difference 1.8 additional correct mortality identifications per 10,000 patients between XGB-EWS and NEWS.
quote: Decision curve analysis showed maximum net benefit differences of 1·8 additional correct mortality identifications per 10 000 patients between XGB-EWS and NEWS, and 1·7 per 10 000 between NEWS and NEWS-Light, across the evaluated risk thresholds.

title: OpenPFx: Evaluating the Ability of LLMs to Create Patient-Friendly Explanations of Radiological Incidental Findings
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) and ICD-10 alignment of LLM patient-friendly explanations across four workflows
effect: Across 407 outputs per workflow, the agentic workflow achieved a sixth-grade reading level and the highest accuracy; results for the other workflows are not given in the abstract.
quote: Across 407 outputs per workflow, the agentic method demonstrated the strongest overall performance, achieving a sixth-grade reading level and the highest accuracy.
sample_unit: outputs per workflow (patient-friendly explanations of incidental MRI findings)

title: Patient friendly summaries of oncology consultations generated by large language models - A pilot study of patient and provider satisfaction
outcome: Patient and provider ratings of clarity of LLM patient-friendly consultation summaries
effect: Patients agreed on clarity 100%; providers agreed on clarity 91%. Some summaries retained jargon; prompt to be optimized.
quote: Some of the summaries retained jargon and results from this study will be used to optimize the prompt for an expanded study.

title: A clinical-grade universal foundation model for intraoperative pathology
outcome: Human-AI collaboration effect on pathologist diagnostic workload and micrometastasis detection
effect: Human-AI collaboration reduced diagnostic workload by 35%, avoided 105 ancillary tests, and enhanced micrometastasis detection with 87.5% accuracy.
quote: Human-AI collaboration further reduced diagnostic workload by 35%, avoided 105 ancillary tests and enhanced detection of micrometastases with 87.5% accuracy.

title: A clinical-grade universal foundation model for intraoperative pathology
outcome: Model generalization across institutions, tumor types, and anatomical sites, including unseen sites
effect: Robust generalization across diverse institutions, tumor types, and anatomical sites, including previously unseen sites and rare cancers, evaluated on more than 15,000 slides from eight centers.
quote: The model demonstrated robust generalization across diverse institutions, tumor types, and anatomical sites-including previously unseen sites and rare cancers.

title: Technology-mediated screening interviews for youth mental health: content validation, randomized controlled trial, and expert evaluation
outcome: Patient satisfaction and expert ratings of chatbot and robot interviews versus psychiatrist-led interviews
effect: Psychiatrist-led interviews had higher satisfaction, especially communication quality; willingness to repeat did not differ; expert ratings comparable across modalities except alignment with other assessment methods favoring psychiatrists over robot.
quote: Psychiatrist-led interviews achieved higher satisfaction scores, particularly for communication quality, while willingness to repeat screening did not differ significantly across modalities.

title: The Clinical Impact of AI-Enhanced Imaging: Improving Outcomes Through Visual Data
outcome: Gender bias and anatomical inaccuracies in AI-generated medical illustrations of chronic heart failure
effect: AI failed to reliably generate female-specific medical images; critical anatomical errors observed, such as a patient depicted with three kidneys and incorrect organ positioning.
quote: Additionally, gender bias emerged, as the AI failed to reliably generate female-specific medical images.
sample_unit: AI-generated images of chronic heart failure (number not reported)

title: Validation of several TB-CAD chest-X-ray applications in individuals with presumptive TB visiting peripheral health institutes in Delhi State
outcome: Head-to-head accuracy of seven TB-CAD products and radiologist on same data
effect: qXR performed as good as the radiologist; CAD4TB, Insight CXR, DrAid, Genki AUCROC adults ≥0.80, children ≥0.90; InferRead DR Chest and Radify Chest performed less well
quote: CAD4TB, Insight CXR, DrAid, and Genki also demonstrated high accuracy (AUCROC: adults ≥0.80, AUCROCs children ≥0.90), while InferRead DR Chest and Radify Chest performed less well.

title: Clinical Usability of Generative Artificial Intelligence for MR Safety Advice
outcome: Clinical usability of generative AI answers to MR safety requests versus human expert, by expert panel
effect: 93% (28/30) human, 50% (15/30) GAIO and 43% (13/30) ChatGPT responses deemed acceptable for clinical use; AIs significantly lower than human MRSE.
quote: Overall, 93% (28/30) of the human responses, 50% (15/30) of the GAIO responses and 43% (13/30) of the ChatGPT responses were deemed acceptable for clinical use.

title: Artificial Intelligence-assisted reader evaluation in acute CT head interpretation (AI-REACT): a multireader multicase study
outcome: Reader sensitivity and specificity with versus without AI assistance for critical CT head abnormalities
effect: Pooled reader sensitivity rose from 82.8% to 89.7% (+6.9%, p<0.001) with AI; specificity fell from 84.5% to 78.9% (-5.5%, p=0.046). ED clinicians with AI matched unaided radiologists' sensitivity.
quote: With AI assistance, pooled reader sensitivity for critically abnormal scans increased from 82.8% to 89.7% (+6.9%, 95% CI +1.4% to +10.6%, p<0.001), and for intracranial haemorrhage from 84.6% to 91.6% (+7.0%, 95% CI +3.2% to +10.8%, p<0.001), but specificity decreased from 84.5% to 78.9% (–5.5%, 95% CI –11.0% to –0.09%, p=0.046).
sample_unit: readers (each interpreting 150 NCCTH scans unaided and with AI)

title: Artificial Intelligence-assisted reader evaluation in acute CT head interpretation (AI-REACT): a multireader multicase study
outcome: Clinician performance with AI in the reading workflow versus unaided, rather than standalone model metrics
effect: AI assistance raised pooled reader sensitivity from 82.8% to 89.7% but lowered specificity from 84.5% to 78.9%; reader confidence AUC did not change significantly.
quote: AI-assisted interpretation increased reader sensitivity for critical abnormalities but reduced specificity.
sample_unit: readers (each interpreting 150 NCCTH scans unaided and with AI)

title: Prompt Engineering Enables Open-Source LLMs to Match Proprietary Models in Diagnostic Accuracy for Annotation of Radiology Reports
outcome: Comparison of open-source Llama3 models against proprietary GPT-4o models on same annotation data
effect: GPT-4o highest accuracy 97.9%; Llama3.1-405b 97.1%, GPT-4o-mini 96.9%, Llama3-8b 96.9%, Llama3.1-70b 96.0%; open-source rivals proprietary
quote: Small, open-source LLMs can accurately annotate Danish trauma radiology reports when supported by effective prompt engineering, achieving accuracy levels that rival proprietary competitors.

title: Beyond Accuracy: An Efficiency- and Safety-Aware Framework for Evaluating Clinical AI with Large Language Models
outcome: Whether traditional metrics and benchmarks reflect clinical utility of LLM responses to pharmacology scenarios
effect: BLEU 0.003–0.024 and ROUGE-L 0.079–0.166 failed to reflect clinical utility; CVD framework exposed efficiency–safety trade-offs; GPT-4o safety 0.437 (moderate).
quote: Traditional metrics (BLEU: 0.003–0.024; ROUGE-L: 0.079–0.166) failed to reflect clinical utility, while the CVD framework exposed critical efficiency–safety trade-offs.

title: Fairness-Aware Machine Learning for Heart Failure Prediction: Performance, Bias, and Clinical Deployment Insights
outcome: Sex-specific discrimination (AUC-ROC) of heart failure prediction models
effect: SVM AUC-ROC 0.869 for females vs 0.796 for males; XGBoost favored males, showing subgroup gaps.
quote: Interestingly, we found contrasting gender preferences: SVM better detected females (AUC-ROC = 0.869 vs 0.796 for males), while XGBoost favored males.

title: Fairness-Aware Machine Learning for Heart Failure Prediction: Performance, Bias, and Clinical Deployment Insights
outcome: Transformer AUC-ROC on UCI versus external MIMIC data
effect: Transformer AUC-ROC 0.986 on UCI, with considerable performance degradation on MIMIC, indicating poor generalizability.
quote: Although the Transformer models depicted notable AUC-ROC in the UCI data (0.986), they suffered a considerable performance degradation in the MIMIC data, suggesting their generalizability issue.

title: Clinical Agents Don’t Care
outcome: Agent detection of tampered patient-identity fields (erroneous inputs) rather than propagating them
effect: GPT-4.1 flagged mismatched headers as UNKNOWN in 17.4% of runs but never detected subtle faults; GPT-4.1-nano detected 4.4% of header swaps and <1% of MRN or age changes; GPT-5-chat never identified mismatches.
quote: GPT-4.1 flagged mismatched headers as UNKNOWN in 17.4% of runs but never detected subtle faults.

title: Clinical Agents Don’t Care
outcome: Agents validating inputs before writing into records; copying codes into tampered charts
effect: Agents frequently failed, copying codes into tampered charts; subtle tampering (MRN or age changes) passed almost entirely without detection.
quote: Agents frequently failed, copying codes into tampered charts.

title: Clinical Agents Don’t Care
outcome: Agents noticing inconsistent or anomalous inputs and abstaining/notifying
effect: Other models rarely abstained; GPT-5-chat never identified mismatches but omitted responses in 12.6% of cases; subtle tampering passed almost entirely without detection.
quote: Subtle tampering passed almost entirely without detection.

title: Performance of Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models (LLMs) on Neurosurgical Board Examinations Across Text and Visual Modalities
outcome: Accuracy change when withholding history, physical exam, or lab components of clinical vignettes
effect: Removing history reduced accuracy by 19.3%; withholding physical exam or lab data reduced it by 6.0% and 5.9%.
quote: Ablation experiments showed that removal of history produced the largest decline in accuracy (19.3% reduction), while withholding physical exam or lab data produced smaller effects (6.0% and 5.9%).

title: Impact of Imaging Protocols on Convolutional Neural Network-Based Pressure Injury Detection
outcome: Model accuracy across variations in lighting, camera distance, positioning, and camera type
effect: Thermal imaging achieved >90% accuracy across models with minimal sensitivity to protocol variations; optical performance varied substantially across protocols (32-55% accuracy).
quote: In contrast, optical performance varied substantially across protocols (32-55% accuracy), demonstrating significant protocol dependency that could impact clinical implementation.

title: Impact of Imaging Protocols on Convolutional Neural Network-Based Pressure Injury Detection
outcome: Input protocol sensitivity
effect: Optical performance varied substantially across imaging protocols, 32-55% accuracy, indicating protocol-dependent reliability.
quote: In contrast, optical performance varied substantially across protocols (32-55% accuracy), demonstrating significant protocol dependency that could impact clinical implementation.

title: On the trade-off between fairness and performance in glioma grade prediction using pre-processing and post-processing techniques to mitigate bias
outcome: Effect of reweighting and equalized-odds mitigation on fairness metrics and prediction performance by race
effect: For race, reweighting worsened outcomes for the under-represented group and increased unfairness; equalized-odds post-processing improved results for the under-represented group with significant fairness gains.
quote: In the case of the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant fairness gains.

title: On the trade-off between fairness and performance in glioma grade prediction using pre-processing and post-processing techniques to mitigate bias
outcome: Subgroup performance and fairness gaps by race and gender in glioma grading models
effect: Demographic bias was found in glioma grading classifiers, with race showing the most severe bias.
quote: In the case of the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant fairness gains.

title: Learning the Phenotype of Medical Hallucinations
outcome: Detection of hallucinated LLM outputs by an automated classifier layer across medical tasks and models
effect: CHECK reduced Llama-3-70B hallucinations from 31% to 0.3% in oncology trial QA; detection AUCs 0.95–0.98 across tasks and models.
quote: This capability to discern hallucination generalized across diverse medical tasks (reasoning and education, patient and physician dialogue, radiology report summarization) and a suite of leading open-weight and commercial models (e.g., GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, GPT-o3, GPT-5), achieving detection AUCs of 0.95–0.98.

title: Learning the Phenotype of Medical Hallucinations
outcome: Hallucination rate when outputs are integrated with structured open clinical knowledge plus a classifier
effect: Hallucinations fell from 31% to 0.3% in Llama-3-70B on oncology trial physician QA; risk driven below accepted clinical error thresholds.
quote: By systematically driving hallucination risk below accepted clinical error thresholds, CHECK provides a scalable and plug-and-play solution to enable the reliable deployment of LLMs in medicine and other mission-critical domains.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models and Clinicians Using Locally Generated Primary Healthcare Vignettes in Kenya
outcome: Blinded physician ratings of LLM versus clinician responses across 11 quality domains
effect: Clinician mean ratings were lower than LLMs in 9/11 domains, e.g. guideline alignment 2.86 vs 4.25-4.72; expert knowledge 2.76 vs 4.25-4.73; harm extent 3.16 vs 4.29-4.68.
quote: Clinician mean ratings were lower than those for LLMs in 9/11 domains: 2.86 vs 4.25-4.72 (guideline alignment), 2.76 vs 4.25-4.73 (expert knowledge), 2.96 vs 4.30-4.73 (logical coherence), and 2.58 vs 4.16-4.68 (low omission of critical information).

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models and Clinicians Using Locally Generated Primary Healthcare Vignettes in Kenya
outcome: Rated avoidance of demographic and socio-economic bias in LLM responses versus clinicians
effect: Avoidance of demographic bias rated 4.86 for clinicians vs 4.91-4.94 for LLMs; clinicians and LLMs similar, LLMs had >90% probability of high rating.
quote: Performance was similar for low inclusion of irrelevant content (4.28 vs 4.25-4.35) and for avoidance of demographic bias (4.86 vs 4.91-4.94).

title: Measuring Reliability in Locally-deployed Language Model Dysarthric Speech Assessments
outcome: Reproducibility of locally deployed LLM intelligibility score across repeated runs
effect: LLM intelligibility score showed excellent repeatability across five runs (ICC = 0.97, Cronbach's α = 0.98) and strong correlations with ASR error metrics.
quote: Importantly, the LLM-derived intelligibility score demonstrated excellent repeatability across five runs (intra-class correlation; ICC = 0.97, Cronbach’s α = 0.98) and showed strong correlations with ASR error metrics.

title: Mixed Methods Assessment of ChatGPT Accuracy and Reliability in Healthcare Queries by Medical Residents
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT accuracy ratings when queries repeated after 10-15 days
effect: Reliability was strong, with intra-rater ICC 0.82 and inter-rater ICC 0.79.
quote: Reliability was strong, with Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC) at 0.82 and inter-rater ICC at 0.79.

title: Comparative analysis of privacy-preserving open-source LLMs regarding extraction of diagnosticinformation from clinical CMR imaging reports
outcome: LLM diagnostic classification F1 versus board-certified cardiologist on same CMR reports
effect: Top four LLMs outperformed the cardiologist (F1 0.94) across all metrics; Gemma 2 achieved F1 0.98, Qwen2.5:32B 0.96, DeepseekR1-32B 0.95.
quote: The top four LLMs outperformed our board-certified cardiologist (F1 scoreof 0.94) across all evaluation metrics in analyzing CMR reports.

title: Clinical Validation of AI/ML Based Model for Down Syndrome Detection Through Graphical Analysis of Facial Dysmorphic Features
outcome: Effect of adjusting confidence threshold on Down Syndrome detection sensitivity
effect: Adjusting the confidence threshold gave 100% sensitivity at the cost of more false positives; default threshold 0.5 gave precision 86.67%, recall 92.86%.
quote: On adjustment of software parameters (the confidence threshold of prediction), the technique can deliver highly accurate Down Syndrome diagnosis with a 100% Sensitivity, at the expense of false positives that may be ruled out through further confirmatory testing.

title: Clinical Validation of AI/ML Based Model for Down Syndrome Detection Through Graphical Analysis of Facial Dysmorphic Features
outcome: Local performance of the model on Indian children versus 98%+ controlled-experiment accuracy
effect: Sensitivity 100%, specificity 80%, average precision 96.6%, precision 86.67%, recall 92.86% at threshold 0.5, versus 98%+ accuracy in the controlled experiment.
quote: The CloudML model trained with 104 images initially achieved: Sensitivity - 100%, specificity - 80%, Average Precision - 96.6%, precision - 86.67%, and Recall - 92.86% (Precision and Recall are calculated at a confidence threshold of 0.5)

title: Human Evaluators vs. LLM-as-a-Judge: Toward Scalable, Real-Time Evaluation of GenAI in Global Health
outcome: Consistency and agreement of expert clinician raters used as reference standard
effect: Expert clinician ratings described as highly inconsistent; best LLM-judge matched human-equivalent evaluation on only four of eleven criteria.
quote: These findings underscore the need for further investment in scalable evaluation solutions, as well as potentially a fundamental rethink of how we approach the concept of “correctness” in clinical AI assessment (which is currently based on highly inconsistent expert clinician raters).
sample_unit: community health worker questions with responses rated

title: Clinical acceptance of a digital health clinical decision support algorithm for children in Tanzania and Rwanda: A mixed-method and before-after analysis from the DYNAMIC study
outcome: Diagnosis acceptance after algorithm adaptations informed by logged rejections and interviews
effect: Rejections were logged (acceptance 94.1% Tanzania vs 67.2% Rwanda for 2 months–14 years); adaptations based on rejection reasons improved acceptance for some diagnoses.
quote: A before–after analysis showed improved acceptance for some diagnoses following adaptations.

title: Clinical acceptance of a digital health clinical decision support algorithm for children in Tanzania and Rwanda: A mixed-method and before-after analysis from the DYNAMIC study
outcome: Clinician acceptance of proposed diagnoses after feedback-informed algorithm adaptations
effect: Acceptance improved for some diagnoses after adaptations informed by clinician feedback and expert input; numerical before–after effects were not reported.
quote: A before–after analysis showed improved acceptance for some diagnoses following adaptations.

title: Clinical acceptance of a digital health clinical decision support algorithm for children in Tanzania and Rwanda: A mixed-method and before-after analysis from the DYNAMIC study
outcome: acceptance for some diagnoses
effect: Adapting algorithms based on findings from overridden or rejected diagnoses led to improved acceptance for some diagnoses.
quote: A before–after analysis showed improved acceptance for some diagnoses following adaptations.

title: Nonfasting, Telehealth-Ready LDL-C Testing With Machine Learning to Improve Cardiovascular Access and Equity
outcome: Black-White gap in LDL-C estimation error (MAE) for race-free ML model
effect: Black-White gap −0.19 mg/dL with CI including zero; ML improvement over Friedewald was 19% for Black patients vs 11% for White patients.
quote: The system achieved racial equity without race input (Black-White gap −0.19 mg dL  −1 , CI includes zero) while providing greatest improvement for Black patients (19% vs 11% for White).
sample_unit: patients (All of Us Research Program participants; test set n=696)

title: Ambient scribe in general practice: a multi-perspective before-after longitudinal mixed-methods study
outcome: Clinical documentation time, consultation time, documentation quality, GP and patient experience after ambient scribe
effect: Documentation time decreased by 42.7 seconds (95% CI -56.29 to -30.78, p<0.0001); total consultation time not different (-61.4 s, p=0.069); GPs reported reduced workload; inaccurate summaries noted.
quote: Clinical documentation time decreased by 42.7 seconds (95% CI [-56.29; - 30.78], p<0.0001).

title: Does LLM Assistance Improve Healthcare Delivery? An Evaluation Using On-site Physicians and Laboratory Tests∗
outcome: Diagnostic alignment and treatment decisions in health-worker plans with versus without LLM feedback, judged by on-site physicians
effect: Health workers changed prescribing for more than half of patients, but on-site physicians saw little to no improvement; lab tests showed mixed effects with no significant increase in detection rates.
quote: However, on-site physicians observed little to no improvement in diagnostic alignment or treatment decisions.

title: Does LLM Assistance Improve Healthcare Delivery? An Evaluation Using On-site Physicians and Laboratory Tests∗
outcome: Agreement between chart-based retrospective review and on-site real-world clinical evaluation of LLM-assisted plans
effect: Retrospective academic reviewers rated LLM-assisted plans more favorably, while on-site physicians and laboratory tests showed little to no improvement, revealing a gap between chart review and real-world relevance.
quote: This highlights a gap between chart-based reviews and real-world clinical relevance that may be especially important in evaluating the effectiveness of LLM-based interventions.

title: Assessing the Capability of Large Language Models in Answering Pediatric Critical Care Board-Style Questions
outcome: LLM accuracy on pediatric critical care calculation questions versus other categories
effect: LLMs excelled in ethics but struggled with calculations. Overall accuracy was 78% for Llama-3.3-70B and 75% for Phi-4; calculation-category figures are not given in the abstract.
quote: The LLMs excelled in ethics but struggled with calculations.

title: Improving Doctor-Patient Communication Using Large Language Models - Results from an Experimental Study
outcome: Comprehension and subjective understanding of original vs GPT-4 plain-language translated medical notes
effect: Translated notes yielded higher objective comprehension scores, greater subjective understanding, higher perceived empathy, and reduced mental effort and negative emotions; reading times did not differ.
quote: LLM translation of medical notes significantly improved both objective and subjective patient understanding.

title: Test-Retest Reliability of Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Electrocardiography: A Multi-Center Study
outcome: Test-retest reliability of AI-ECG outputs across repeated ECGs 1-30 days apart
effect: Composite CCCs 0.90 (signal), 0.90 (image), 0.81 (EchoNext-Mini); disease-specific CCCs 0.77-0.86 and 0.50-0.97 for EchoNext-Mini nodes; image ensemble categorical concordance 87-89% versus 80-84% for disease-specific models.
quote: The image-based ensemble model achieved categorical screen-status concordance of 87-89% across 3 health systems (versus 80-84% for disease-specific models).

title: Ambient Only vs. Longitudinal Data-Enhanced AI Documentation: A Pilot Study Quantifying the Value of Historical Clinical Context in Primary Care
outcome: QNOTE assessment composite score for ambient-only vs ambient plus historical EHR data
effect: Consolidated documentation scored higher than ambient-only (94.8 vs. 80.1; difference 14.6 points; 95% CI 13.4-15.8; P<0.001); completeness difference 42.5 points.
quote: Consolidated documentation achieved significantly higher mean total assessment composite score compared to ambient-only (94.8 vs. 80.1 on a scale of 0-100; difference 14.6 points; 95% CI 13.4-15.8; P<0.001).

title: Ambient Only vs. Longitudinal Data-Enhanced AI Documentation: A Pilot Study Quantifying the Value of Historical Clinical Context in Primary Care
outcome: Ambient documentation completeness
effect: Completeness domain improvement with history was 42.5 points; P<0.001.
quote: The largest improvements was observed in the completeness domain (difference 42.5 points; P<0.001).

title: OncoGPT: A Modular AI Assistant Orchestrating LLMs in Molecular Oncology
outcome: Expert acceptance of context-grounded LLM outputs on oncology report prompts
effect: Automatic model selection with context achieved expert acceptance across all 19 prompts; a fixed high-end model had higher cost and lower expert-rated quality. No comparison without context was reported.
quote: Evaluated on 19 representative clinical prompts derived from real-world oncology reports, automatic model selection with context achieved expert acceptance across all prompts while reducing inference cost by an order of magnitude; by contrast, a fixed high-end model produced higher cost and lower expert-rated quality.

title: Exploring the Generalizability and Explainability of LLMs in Detecting Suicidal Ideation: The Impact of Data Heterogeneity
outcome: Subgroup disparity in suicidal ideation detection between alexithymia and non-alexithymia groups
effect: Alexithymia group had decreased likelihood of true detection of suicidal ideation (OR = 0.31, p < .001) with the topic-general classifier; family-related words (p = .02) mediated the disparity.
quote: Results showed subgroup disparity in topic-general classifier between alexithymia and non-alexithymia groups at which alexithymia group was associated with a decreased likelihood of true detection of suicidal ideation (OR = 0.31, p < .001) and unique language features, such as family-related words (p = .02), played a mediating/explanatory role.

title: Exploring the Generalizability and Explainability of LLMs in Detecting Suicidal Ideation: The Impact of Data Heterogeneity
outcome: Effect of topic-specific classifiers on subgroup disparity and overall AUC
effect: Topic-specific classifiers achieved AUC = 0.96 versus 0.83 for the topic-general classifier, and the subgroup disparity was largely reduced.
quote: Furthermore, topic-specific classifiers demonstrated superior performance (AUC = 0.96) compared to topic-general classifier (AUC = 0.83) and the subgroup disparity was largely reduced.

title: Leveraging simulation to provide a practical framework for assessing the novel scope of risk of LLMs in healthcare
outcome: False-negative rates of LLMs detecting suicidal ideation, therapy requests, and therapy-like interactions in synthetic chatbot conversations
effect: Frequent errors in suicidal-ideation and therapy-like interactions; estimated P1 ranged 2.0×10-8 to 2.6×10-4 and P2 from 7.1×10-5 to 9.6×10-3, spanning up to four orders of magnitude across 14 models.
quote: LLM success at generating synthetic safety datasets varied substantially by task, with strong performance for neutral and non-therapeutic content but frequent errors in suicidal-ideation and therapy-like interactions.
sample_unit: open-source LLMs evaluated on synthetic safety-classification tasks

title: Development of an LLM Pipeline Surpassing Physicians in Cardiovascular Risk Score Calculation
outcome: Agreement with expert-adjudicated scores for pipeline vs standalone LLMs vs treating clinicians
effect: Mean Krippendorff's alpha 0.79 (pipeline) vs 0.32 (standalone LLMs) vs 0.31 (clinicians); Qwen3 pipeline had lower RMSE than clinicians for HAS-BLED (0.20 vs 0.87), CHA2DS2-VASc (0.53 vs 1.08), EuroSCORE II (1.99 vs 2.05).
quote: Pipeline-generated scores showed substantially higher agreement with expert adjudication than standalone LLMs and treating clinicians (mean Krippendorff’s alpha: 0.79 vs 0.32 vs 0.31) and demonstrated superior calibration.

title: Domain shifts decrease the accuracy of machine learning algorithms to detect myocardial ischemia in ECG recordings: A multi-database analysis
outcome: Model performance across datasets (sites) in leave-one-dataset-out validation for ischemia detection
effect: AUC exceeded 0.90 within the same dataset, but performance dropped notably on data from different sources; sensitivity decreased substantially while specificity remained relatively stable.
quote: However, performance dropped notably when the models were tested on data from different sources.

title: Domain shifts decrease the accuracy of machine learning algorithms to detect myocardial ischemia in ECG recordings: A multi-database analysis
outcome: Effect of dataset shift between development and external datasets on model performance
effect: Variations in ECG patterns across datasets contributed to performance drops; sensitivity decreased substantially when tested on different datasets.
quote: Further analysis showed that variations in ECG patterns across datasets contributed to these differences in performance.

title: Evaluating the acceptability, usability and clinical appropriateness of  Your Path  , an AI-powered tool facilitating relevant access to HIV services post-HIV self-testing in South Africa
outcome: Clinician appraisal of appropriateness of AI conversation summaries from real user interaction transcripts
effect: HCPs reviewed transcripts of CM tool interactions and found the conversational summaries clinically appropriate, informative and beneficial for supporting linkage to HIV care.
quote: HCPs found the conversational summaries clinically appropriate, and cited the tool as informative and beneficial for supporting linkage to HIV care.

title: Evaluating the acceptability, usability and clinical appropriateness of  Your Path  , an AI-powered tool facilitating relevant access to HIV services post-HIV self-testing in South Africa
outcome: Usability (SUS) and acceptability among representative end users during simulated pilot use
effect: Mean SUS 81.6 (SD 17.5); 83.7% found it easy to use; 94.9% willing to use again; 91.0% reported positive influence on intention to access HIV services.
quote: The tool demonstrated high usability, with a mean SUS score of 81.6 (SD 17.5).

title: Multi-Modal Large Language Model for Medical Auxiliary Diagnosis
outcome: Ablation of retrieval and knowledge modules on expert-rated accuracy, treatment relevance, and reliability
effect: Abstract reports superior accuracy, treatment relevance, and information reliability versus general-purpose models, and that ablations show each module is essential. No numbers reported in the text.
quote: Ablation studies highlight the essential role of each module, particularly in managing multi-modal information.

title: Solace, a Therapeutic Conversational Agent for Management of Chronic Pain: Acceptability and Usability Study
outcome: Whether safety guardrails identified and managed suicidal ideation, injury, and medication recommendation requests
effect: Guardrails for suicidal ideation, injury, and medication recommendation requests reported as performing appropriately during the study; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: Safety guardrails designed to identify and manage instances of suicidal ideation, injury, or requests for medication recommendations performed appropriately during the study.

title: Solace, a Therapeutic Conversational Agent for Management of Chronic Pain: Acceptability and Usability Study
outcome: Whether chatbot safety guardrails handled suicidal ideation and injury risk in conversations
effect: Guardrails designed to identify and manage suicidal ideation and injury reported as performing appropriately during the study; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: Safety guardrails designed to identify and manage instances of suicidal ideation, injury, or requests for medication recommendations performed appropriately during the study.

title: Detecting Algorithmic Bias in ICU Clinical Decision: A Doubly-Robust Framework for Auditing Treatment Recommendation Disparities
outcome: Subgroup disparities in ICU outcomes and predicted treatment effects by age and race
effect: Age: 5.1pp mortality disparity; predicted treatment effects 3.2pp younger vs 1.8pp older. Race: severity-adjusted disparities averaged 2.2pp, reaching 5.6pp at high severity, despite similar aggregate outcomes.
quote: For race-based analysis, severity-adjusted outcome disparities (average 2.2pp, reaching 5.6pp at high severity) suggest potential differences in care quality or algorithmic recommendations despite similar aggregate outcomes.

title: Cloud vs. On-Premise Large Language Models for Urgent Patient- Portal Message Screening: A Comparative Evaluation
outcome: Sensitivity and NPV of urgency classification of epilepsy portal messages versus neurologist consensus
effect: Unanimous standard: 5 of 6 models had perfect sensitivity and NPV. Majority standard: GPT-5 sensitivity 0.98, NPV 1.00; GPT-OSS 20B sensitivity only 0.57 (specificity 0.95).
quote: Under the Unanimous reference standard, five of six models achieved perfect sensitivity and NPV, indicating safe rule-out performance.

title: Clinician Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Summaries of Pediatric CVICU Progress Notes
outcome: Readability of AI summaries versus original notes (Flesch Reading Ease, grade level)
effect: AI summaries had Flesch Reading Ease 29.25 vs 56.89 for original notes and Grade 15.24 vs Grade 8.98; cosine similarity 0.6 showed moderate alignment.
quote: The AI summaries were harder to read, with a Flesch Reading Ease score of 29.25 compared to 56.89 for the original notes, and required a higher reading level—Grade 15.24 for the summaries versus Grade 8.98 for the original notes.

title: Accuracy of AI-Driven Cephalometric Tracing Systems in Orthodontic Analysis Including Patients With Cleft Lip/Palate
outcome: Differences in AI tracing accuracy across Angle class, growth pattern, and cleft lip/palate subgroups
effect: Mthd*Class and Mthd*Growth interactions not significant for any measurements; Mthd*Clp interaction significant for 6 measurements.
quote: Two-way interactions between Mthd*Class and Mthd*Growth were not statistically significant for any measurements, however Mthd*Clp interaction was significant for 6 measurements.

title: Accuracy of AI-Driven Cephalometric Tracing Systems in Orthodontic Analysis Including Patients With Cleft Lip/Palate
outcome: Reliability of AI cephalometric tracing for clinical use without human oversight
effect: High concordance with computer-assisted manual tracing overall, but not sufficiently reliable in clinical practice without human oversight; Mthd significantly affected 62 of 85 measurements.
quote: Conclusion Although cephalometric landmark detection and measurements from AudaxCeph, OrthoDx, and WebCeph show high concordance with computer-assisted manual tracing, their use in clinical practice is not sufficiently reliable without human oversight.

title: Accuracy of AI-Driven Cephalometric Tracing Systems in Orthodontic Analysis Including Patients With Cleft Lip/Palate
outcome: Whether manual correction of automated tracings removes clinically unacceptable differences
effect: Semi-automated (manually corrected) modes compared with fully automated; U1-NA° and U1-L1° remained clinically unacceptable across all AI programs even after researcher intervention.
quote: U1-NA° and U1-L1° showed clinically unacceptable differences from RV across all AI programs, even after researcher intervention.

title: Accuracy of AI-Driven Cephalometric Tracing Systems in Orthodontic Analysis Including Patients With Cleft Lip/Palate
outcome: cephalometric measurement accuracy
effect: U1-NA° and U1-L1° showed clinically unacceptable differences from RV across all AI programs, even after researcher intervention.
quote: U1-NA° and U1-L1° showed clinically unacceptable differences from RV across all AI programs, even after researcher intervention.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy for Gastric Cancer, Adenoma, and Intestinal Metaplasia With vs Without AI Assistance: an observer-based, reader-blinded, randomized case-order exploratory validation study
outcome: Standalone AI accuracy versus endoscopist accuracy with AI assistance
effect: Standalone AI accuracy for focal lesions was 91.31% (M1) and 92.51% (M2), but AI-assisted readers reached 86.84% overall (from 74.80%). Standalone performance overstated the human-AI team's performance.
quote: As a stand-alone model, AI achieved 91.31% (M1) and 92.51% (M2) accuracy for focal lesions (sensitivities 91.02% and 91.91%; specificities 95.50% and 96.12%).
sample_unit: cases (still images and video clips read by 6 endoscopists)

title: KOM: A Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence System for Precision Management of Knee Osteoarthritis (KOA)
outcome: Time and treatment quality for clinician+AI versus clinician alone versus AI alone in randomized simulation
effect: Clinician-KOM collaboration reduced total diagnostic and planning time by 38.5% and improved treatment quality compared with each approach used independently.
quote: A randomized three-arm simulation study further revealed that collaboration between KOM and clinicians reduced total diagnostic and planning time by 38.5% and resulted in improved treatment quality compared to each approach used independently.

title: When Digital Health Falls Short: Limited Validity of an AI-Powered App for Dietary Assessment in Females with Obesity
outcome: Agreement of AI app energy intake estimates with doubly labelled water in free-living use
effect: SNAQ underestimated energy intake by 25% (2187 ± 1401 vs 3004 ± 481 kcal/day; p = 0.01). Limits of agreement were -3707 to 2073 kcal/day and within-subject ICC was 0.00.
quote: Despite its advanced AI architecture, SNAQ showed poor accuracy and reproducibility in free-living adults with obesity.

title: Test-Time Neural Style Transfer Harmonizes Domains and Improves Cone Detection in AOSLO Images
outcome: Cone detector Dice on out-of-domain low-quality AOSLO images versus in-domain images
effect: Out-of-domain LQ mean Dice was 0.47 (recall 0.37) without NST versus 0.88 on the in-domain dataset; NST raised LQ Dice to 0.84 (recall 0.92, precision 0.83).
quote: Our NST approach substantially improved mean Dice on the LQ dataset from 0.47 to 0.84, primarily by increasing recall (from 0.37 to 0.92) with a limited reduction in precision (from 0.95 to 0.83).
sample_unit: AOSLO images (three datasets: low-quality out-of-domain, high-quality out-of-domain, in-domain)

title: GenAI in Occupational Therapy: A Survey of Adoption, Ethical Concerns, and Training Needs
outcome: Proportion of practitioners reporting formal institutional GenAI policies
effect: Only 6.2% reported formal institutional GenAI policies.
quote: Only 6.2% reported formal institutional GenAI policies, and 94.8% never entered personally identifiable information into GenAI systems; only 12.2% obtained informed consent from stakeholders to use GenAI.

title: GenAI in Occupational Therapy: A Survey of Adoption, Ethical Concerns, and Training Needs
outcome: Proportion of practitioners who received GenAI training and desire for training
effect: 42.2% reported receiving no training; 68.3% believed practitioners should receive GenAI training; 73.2% desired formal webinar-based instruction.
quote: While 68.3% believed practitioners should receive GenAI training, 42.2% reported receiving no training, with most (73.2%) desiring formal webinar-based instruction.

title: Clinical Implementation of an AI Algorithm for Substance Misuse Screening in Hospitalized Adults
outcome: Addiction-related service receipt, 6-month readmission, and costs, AI-assisted vs manual screening
effect: Services 3.8% manual vs 3.4% SMART-AI (difference -0.4 pp; 95% CI -0.7 to -0.1); noninferiority not achieved. Readmissions unchanged (30.5% vs 30.5%); costs $6,166.71 lower.
quote: The lower limit of the confidence interval was below the noninferiority margin, so noninferiority was not achieved.

title: Large language models for automatable real-world performance monitoring of diagnostic decision support systems: a comparison to manual doctor panel review in a prospective clinical study
outcome: Agreement of LLM-automated vs clinician-review reference for estimating deployed DDSS accuracy
effect: GPT-5 eligibility accuracy 84.7% (κ = 0.57); exact diagnosis match 93.6% of 347 encounters; DDSS accuracy estimates indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3, one significant difference at Top-5.
quote: Diagnostic accuracy estimates based on manual versus GPT-5 mappings were statistically indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3 across the full analyzable sets, with one significant difference at Top-5.

title: Large language models for automatable real-world performance monitoring of diagnostic decision support systems: a comparison to manual doctor panel review in a prospective clinical study
outcome: Differences in DDSS accuracy estimates using clinician versus LLM-derived reference standards
effect: Manual versus GPT-5 mappings produced statistically indistinguishable Top-1 and Top-3 estimates, but one significant Top-5 difference. No statistical differences occurred in the overlapping 346 cases.
quote: Diagnostic accuracy estimates based on manual versus GPT-5 mappings were statistically indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3 across the full analyzable sets, with one significant difference at Top-5.

title: Large language models for automatable real-world performance monitoring of diagnostic decision support systems: a comparison to manual doctor panel review in a prospective clinical study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of DDSS versions
effect: The experimental DDSS version outperformed the original only at the Top-5 threshold across both reference sets.
quote: Across both reference sets, the experimental DDSS version outperformed the original only at the Top-5 threshold.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
outcome: Correctness and harmfulness of LLM responses to colonoscopy prep questions versus expert ratings
effect: Leading models approached but did not achieve adequate performance; all models produced harmful errors, mainly omissions or misinterpretations of prep instructions.
quote: All models produced harmful errors, primarily due to omissions or misinterpretations of prep instructions.
sample_unit: synthetic patient-AI Coach dialogues (250 per model x 5 models)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
outcome: Error and harmful response rates after automated safety filter replacing incorrect responses with deferral message
effect: Applying an automated safety filter reduced overall error rates but failed to eliminate harmful responses.
quote: Applying an automated safety filter reduced overall error rates but failed to eliminate harmful responses.
sample_unit: synthetic patient-AI Coach dialogues (250 per model x 5 models)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
outcome: error rates after automated filtering
effect: Reduced overall error rates but failed to eliminate harmful responses.
quote: Applying an automated safety filter reduced overall error rates but failed to eliminate harmful responses.
sample_unit: synthetic patient-AI Coach dialogues (250 per model x 5 models)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Correctness and Diversity in Synthetic Dialogues
outcome: error rates and harmful responses with automated safety filtering
effect: safety filter reduced overall error rates but failed to eliminate harmful responses
quote: Applying an automated safety filter reduced overall error rates but failed to eliminate harmful responses.
sample_unit: synthetic patient-AI Coach dialogues (250 per model x 5 models)

title: The Promise and Peril of Large Language Models in Digital Health: GPT-4 Personalizes Cardiovascular Patient Education but Amplifies Gender Biases
outcome: Stereotyping and linguistic bias in GPT-4 gender-tailored patient education content
effect: Revisions occasionally relied on social stereotypes (e.g., 'bottling up emotions'); both versions framed female symptoms as 'atypical' and showed gendered assumptions in recommended activities; 4 of 7 male-tailored revisions omitted erectile dysfunction.
quote: Revisions also occasionally relied on social stereotypes (e.g., “bottling up emotions”).

title: The Promise and Peril of Large Language Models in Digital Health: GPT-4 Personalizes Cardiovascular Patient Education but Amplifies Gender Biases
outcome: Completeness of clinical content in GPT-4 sex-specific CVD education revisions
effect: Male-tailored versions often missed key clinical factors; 4 of 7 revisions failed to mention erectile dysfunction as a CVD risk marker, while female-tailored versions incorporated biological facts such as menopause.
quote: For instance, 4 of 7 revisions failed to mention erectile dysfunction as a CVD risk marker.

title: The Promise and Peril of Large Language Models in Digital Health: GPT-4 Personalizes Cardiovascular Patient Education but Amplifies Gender Biases
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease) of GPT-4 revised patient education materials
effect: Readability was maintained after GPT-4 revision; the gender-inclusivity checklist median rose from 3.0/10 (original) to 8.0 (male-tailored) and 10.0 (female-tailored).
quote: Readability was maintained.

title: Physician Consensus Stratification Reveals Performance Limits of Deep Learning for Smartphone-Based Pharyngitis Diagnosis
outcome: Sensitivity for bacterial pharyngitis across models
effect: All models had high specificity (96-98%) but low sensitivity (2-15%) for bacterial pharyngitis, so negative results miss most bacterial cases and physician review is needed.
quote: The high specificity (96–98%) suggests strong potential for reducing unnecessary antibiotic prescriptions through AI-assisted triage, while the low sensitivity (2–15%) necessitates physician review for suspected bacterial infections.

title: Improving Performance, Robustness, and Fairness of Radiographic AI Models with Finely-Controllable Synthetic Data
outcome: Underdiagnosis fairness gap and accuracy after synthetic pretraining as bias mitigation
effect: Synthetic pretraining gave a 6.5% accuracy increase (vs 2.7% for naive real+synthetic mixing) and reduced the underdiagnosis fairness gap by 19.3%, with improvements across intersectional subgroups.
quote: We observe this performance improvement simultaneously with the reduction of the underdiagnosis fairness gap by 19.3%, with marked improvements across intersectional subgroups of sex, age, and race/ethnicity.

title: Improving Performance, Robustness, and Fairness of Radiographic AI Models with Finely-Controllable Synthetic Data
outcome: Performance and fairness when training with demographically balanced synthetic data
effect: Pretraining on a demographically balanced synthetic dataset (>565,000 images) improved performance, out-of-distribution generalization, and fairness across demographic subgroups on held-out data from five institutions.
quote: Through extensive evaluation on over 137,000 held-out chest radiographs from five institutions, we demonstrate that synthetic pretraining consistently improves model performance, generalization to out-of-distribution settings, and fairness across demographic subgroups defined across varying fairness metrics.

title: Large scale analysis and prediction of adverse maternal health events across heterogeneous populations from the All of Us dataset
outcome: Model performance and fairness across SDoH, age, and race subgroups
effect: Disparities in model performance across SDoH subgroups, but minimal disparities across age or race subgroups.
quote: Fairness evaluations revealed disparities in model performance across SDoH subgroups, but minimal disparities across age or race subgroups.

title: Opened Mind: A Cross-Modal, Multilingual Analysis of Empathetic AI  Evaluating the Impact of Emotion Acknowledgment Strategies (EAS) on Therapeutic and Empathetic Outcomes Across 12 Diverse Linguistic Contexts
outcome: Accuracy of emergency detection in mental health support AI
effect: Emergency detection system achieved 98% accuracy; missed versus unnecessary escalations not separately reported in the abstract.
quote: The emergency detection system also achieved 98% accuracy.

title: Opened Mind: A Cross-Modal, Multilingual Analysis of Empathetic AI  Evaluating the Impact of Emotion Acknowledgment Strategies (EAS) on Therapeutic and Empathetic Outcomes Across 12 Diverse Linguistic Contexts
outcome: Differences in therapeutic effectiveness across languages and interaction modes
effect: ANOVA and Chi-Squared tests found no bias in effectiveness by language or interaction mode (p > 0.05).
quote: Statistical checks, including ANOVA and Chi-Squared tests, found no bias in effectiveness by language or interaction mode (p > 0.05).

title: Recognizing "Conformity Bias" in Large Language Models: A New Risk for Clinical Use
outcome: Correct response rate after successive probing questions suggesting incorrect treatments (conformity bias)
effect: Correct rates after repeated probing: 25% GPT-4o, 10% Gemini-1.5 Flash, 0% Claude-3 Haiku, 25% GPT-o1 (P < 0.001); conformity to incorrect suggestions increased with repeated probing.
quote: Correct response rates after successive probing questions were alarmingly low: 25% (GPT-4o), 10% (Gemini-1.5 Flash), 0% (Claude-3 Haiku), and 25% (GPT-o1) (P < 0.001).

title: LLMs Can Do Medical Harm: Stress-Testing Clinical Decisions Under Social Pressure
outcome: Harmful decision rate across social-pressure prompt variations versus neutral control
effect: Authority or responsibility-transfer framings produced the most harmful responses; control prompts the fewest (mitigated 8.3–9.6%; unmitigated 14.3–16.0%; p<0.001).
quote: When exposed to social pressure, models behaved predictably but unevenly: prompts framed as authority or responsibility transfer generated the most harmful responses, whereas control prompts, neutral and pressure-free, produced the fewest (mitigated 8.3–9.6%; unmitigated 14.3–16.0%; χ  2 p < 0.001).

title: LLMs Can Do Medical Harm: Stress-Testing Clinical Decisions Under Social Pressure
outcome: Proportion of potentially harmful responses with versus without brief safety mitigation cue
effect: Mitigation cue reduced harmful decisions from 16.6% to 10.1% (p<0.001), but did not eliminate harm.
quote: Mitigation reduced harmful decisions from 16.6% to 10.1% (p < 0.001).

title: Development and validation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and GraphRAG for complex clinical cases
outcome: Clinical correctness and guideline adherence of RAG versus baseline LLM
effect: RAG-based methods outperformed the baseline LLM in clinical correctness and guideline adherence; GraphRAG achieved highest patient-specificity but lower clarity.
quote: RAG-based methods outperformed the baseline LLM in clinical correctness and guideline adherence.

title: Development and validation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and GraphRAG for complex clinical cases
outcome: performance with missing information
effect: All RAG systems performed poorly when essential information was missing.
quote: All RAG systems were limited by the scope of the indexed guideline and performed poorly when essential information was missing.

title: Development and validation of Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) and GraphRAG for complex clinical cases
outcome: clarity of GraphRAG outputs
effect: GraphRAG scored lower in clarity because long guideline excerpts obscured key recommendations.
quote: However, GraphRAG scored lower in clarity, as its graph walks often returned long guideline excerpts that obscured key recommendations.

title: A mixed-methods evaluation of the implementation of IOTA-ADNEX ultrasound triage in NHS secondary care ovarian diagnostic one-stop clinics
outcome: Surgery rates under IOTA-ADNEX-guided vs retrospectively calculated RMI-based triage
effect: 10% (32/334) underwent surgery under general gynaecology and cancer unit team using IOTA-ADNEX at 10% threshold vs 30% (94/334) would have under RMI triage.
quote: In comparison, 30% (94/334) would have undergone surgery under the same teams if RMI-based triage had been used.

title: Evaluation of Large Language Models on the Chinese Dental Licensing Examination
outcome: Effect of adding an 'unknown' option (with or without penalty) on LLM accuracy and hallucination
effect: Prompts with an 'unknown' option, alone or combined with a penalty for incorrect answers, did not improve model accuracy on the Chinese Dental Licensing Examination.
quote: Prompts that included an ‘unknown’ option—or combined it with a penalty for incorrect answers—did not improve model accuracy.

title: A Comparative Analysis of Five AI Chatbots in Providing Patient Education on Smile Design
outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of chatbot patient-education responses versus recommended patient reading level
effect: Readability differed significantly across chatbots (FRE p=0.004; FKGL p<0.001); ChatGPT-5 required the highest reading level; most responses were above eighth-grade level.
quote: Most chatbot responses were above an eighth-grade reading level, which may challenge general patient comprehension.

title: Assessing Pediatricians' Readiness for Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Pediatricians' AI readiness and attitudes (MAIRS-MS, GAAIS) by age and experience
effect: Total MAIRS 74.97 ± 13.01 (moderate-to-high readiness); age negatively correlated with readiness; those with ≥21 years' experience had significantly lower readiness and positive attitude (p < 0.05).
quote: The total MAIRS score was 74.97 ± 13.01, indicating a moderate-to-high level of AI readiness.

title: The Clinician in the Loop: How Multimodal AI Affects Clinical Decision-Making in Mental Healthcare
outcome: Effect of low explainability of multimodal AI data on clinician responses and errors
effect: Low explainability of multimodal data was a significant factor in clinician responses and led to clinical errors; no numeric estimates in the abstract.
quote: The low explainability of multimodal data was a significant factor in clinician responses and actually led to clinical errors.

title: Poetic or Prosaic? Evaluating the Linguistic Quality of AI-Generated Draft Replies to Patient Portal Messages
outcome: Token retention of AI drafts across prompt refinement phases
effect: Prompt refinements (Phases 2–4 vs Phase 1) increased token retention of drafts in final physician messages.
quote: Prompt refinements increased token retention.

title: Poetic or Prosaic? Evaluating the Linguistic Quality of AI-Generated Draft Replies to Patient Portal Messages
outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of AI drafts vs final physician-sent messages
effect: Final physician messages were longer and more readable than GPT drafts; authors cite readability challenges.
quote: Final messages were longer and more readable.

title: Poetic or Prosaic? Evaluating the Linguistic Quality of AI-Generated Draft Replies to Patient Portal Messages
outcome: Clinician uptake of AI-generated patient-message drafts
effect: Of 66,200 generated drafts, 21,073 were presented and 2,264 (11%) were used, documenting low uptake without establishing its cause.
quote: Of 66,200 GDRs generated, 21,073 were presented, and 2,264 (11%) were used.

title: A hybrid-reasoner LLM framework toward real-world clinical decision- making support in acute ischemic stroke
outcome: Physician performance with versus without LLM support, by experience level
effect: Junior and non-specialist physicians benefited most from LLM support, narrowing expertise gaps; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: Notably, human–AI interaction experiments revealed that junior and non-specialist physicians benefited most, narrowing expertise gaps.

title: A Comparative Performance Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in Gynecologic Oncology
outcome: Expert-graded response quality of RAG architectures versus non-RAG baseline on gynecologic oncology questions
effect: RAG systems generally outperformed non-RAG baseline; largest gains for complex surgical questions, modest and heterogeneous improvements for cervical cancer guideline questions.
quote: Across domains, RAG systems generally outperformed the non-RAG baseline.

title: A Comparative Performance Study of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in Gynecologic Oncology
outcome: Head-to-head model performance
effect: Thirteen RAG architectures were compared with a non-RAG baseline; RAG systems generally outperformed baseline, with domain-dependent gains.
quote: Across domains, RAG systems generally outperformed the non-RAG baseline.

title: Real-time Inflammation Panel for inpatient care: a before-after evaluation of post-analytic timeliness and outcomes at a tertiary center
outcome: Alert burden per patient-day after deployment of rule-based alerts
effect: Alert burden averaged 0.23 alerts/patient-day with around 4% duplicate suppression; sensitivity 0.88 and PPV 0.83 against an operational composite.
quote: Alert burden averaged 0.23 alerts/patient-day with around 4% duplicate suppression.

title: Atlas-Assisted Bone Age Estimation from Hand–Wrist Radiographs Using Multimodal Large Language Models: A Comparative Study
outcome: Bone age error of four multimodal LLMs versus an experienced radiologist reference standard
effect: ChatGPT-5 MAE 1.46 years, ICC 0.849; Gemini 2.5 Pro MAE 2.24; Grok-3 MAE 3.14; Claude 4 Sonnet MAE 4.29 years. Only ChatGPT-5 deemed clinically useful.
quote: ChatGPT-5 demonstrated statistically superior performance with MAE of 1.46 years and ICC of 0.849, showing highest alignment with the reference standard.

title: Companions Made of Code: Why Emotional AI Must Not Be Introduced into Mental Healthcare Without Regulation
outcome: Chatbot recognition of suicide-risk cues and guidance toward human help
effect: Exploratory test of eight widely available chatbots found systems frequently simulate empathy but fail to recognise suicide-risk cues or guide users toward human help. No numeric rates reported in the abstract.
quote: It combines theoretical analysis with an exploratory examination of eight widely available chatbots, demonstrating that current systems frequently simulate empathy while failing to recognise suicide-risk cues or guide users toward human help.

title: Companions Made of Code: Why Emotional AI Must Not Be Introduced into Mental Healthcare Without Regulation
outcome: Chatbot escalation to human help when suicide-risk cues appear
effect: Chatbots frequently failed to recognise suicide-risk cues or direct users to human help across eight tested systems. No numeric rates reported in the abstract.
quote: It combines theoretical analysis with an exploratory examination of eight widely available chatbots, demonstrating that current systems frequently simulate empathy while failing to recognise suicide-risk cues or guide users toward human help.

title: QoQ-Med3: Robust Multimodal Clinical Analysis Foundation Model with Reasoning
outcome: Generalization to held-out datasets from different clinical sites (MIMIC-IV and JHU PMAP)
effect: Model trained on public data generalized to held-out MIMIC-IV and the private JHU PMAP dataset; overall balanced accuracy 71.3% and F1 0.349 across benchmark.
quote: The model trained on public clinical dataonly generalized to the both the held-out MIMIC-IV and the private JHU PMAP dataset collected at Johns Hopkins Universityhospital.

title: Benchmarking large language models for cardiovascular risk stratification using clinical vignettes
outcome: Accuracy of LLM SCORE2 numeric risk computation versus guideline calculation
effect: Mean absolute error exceeded 5 percentage points in all but one of eleven LLMs; ten of eleven systematically underestimated risk.
quote: LLMs struggled with SCORE2 numeric computation, with mean absolute error exceeding 5 percentage points in all but one.

title: Failure-Aware Robustness Evaluation of Deep Learning Models for Tuberculosis Detection Under Real-World Chest X-Ray Degradation
outcome: Model performance and calibration under synthetically degraded chest X-ray inputs
effect: All models showed statistically significant degradation; motion blur reduced sensitivity by up to 21%; expected calibration error rose from about 0.04 to over 0.10 under degradation.
quote: Motion blur was the most detrimental artifacts, causing sensitivity reductions of up to 21%.

title: Comparative Accuracy of Large Language Models for CPT Coding Assignments from Surgical Procedure Notes
outcome: Run-to-run consistency of LLM CPT code outputs across three repeated queries
effect: Gemini had highest consistency (72.7% identical outputs across runs); Claude 63.6%; complex multi-component procedures showed greater inter-run variance.
quote: Consistency did not correlate with accuracy: Gemini demonstrated the highest run-to-run consistency (72.7% identical outputs across runs) despite lower benchmark alignment, while Claude showed greater variance (63.6%) yet superior accuracy.
sample_unit: orthopedic procedure notes with surgeon-labeled benchmark CPT codes

title: Comparative Accuracy of Large Language Models for CPT Coding Assignments from Surgical Procedure Notes
outcome: LLM CPT code accuracy against surgeon-labeled ground-truth reference standard
