effect: Claude Opus 4.5 F1 65.9% (precision 66.7%, recall 65.2%); Gemini 3 Pro F1 62.1%; GPT-5.2 F1 56.8%; complex procedures F1 often below 40%.
quote: Claude Opus 4.5 achieved the highest accuracy (F1: 65.9%, precision: 66.7%, recall: 65.2%), followed by Gemini 3 Pro (F1: 62.1%) and GPT-5.2 (F1: 56.8%).
sample_unit: orthopedic procedure notes with surgeon-labeled benchmark CPT codes

title: Evaluation of the ‘qXR’ Software for the Detection of Pulmonary Nodules and Signs Suggestive of Heart Failure: A Comparative Analysis in a Latin American General Hospital
outcome: Local agreement of qXR with radiologist reference standard for nodules, cardiomegaly, pleural effusion
effect: Moderate to substantial concordance for pulmonary nodules and pleural effusion; cardiomegaly more variable with lower agreement across evaluators; overall accuracy acceptable but differed by condition.
quote: qXR showed higher agreement with radiologist assessments for pulmonary nodules and pleural effusion, achieving moderate to substantial concordance.

title: Segmenting with Confidence: Uncertainty Quantification for Brain Tumor Imaging
outcome: Calibration (empirical coverage) of volumetric 95% credible intervals across segmentation models
effect: Heterogeneous EDL ensemble produced the most reliable credible intervals, capturing true tumor volume in 92.8% of cases against a 95% target.
quote: Out of all models tested, the heterogeneous EDL ensemble produced the most reliable volumetric credible intervals, capturing the true tumor volume in 92.8% of cases.

title: Segmenting with Confidence: Uncertainty Quantification for Brain Tumor Imaging
outcome: Segmentation performance on an independent external institution cohort
effect: External cohort of 353 patients with meningioma achieved median Dice 0.92, versus about 0.93 in the internal test set.
quote: External validation on an independent external cohort of 353 patients with meningioma confirmed high generalizability, achieving a median Dice of0.92.

title: A facial foundation model for multi-system biomarker and disease risk prediction with real-world mobile deployment
outcome: Biomarker prediction performance across internal and four independent external cohorts
effect: FaceFound showed robust results across the internal cohort and four independent external cohorts (N = 206-2,247), with state-of-the-art performance for 45 (73%) of 62 biomarkers.
quote: FaceFound consistently outperformed baseline architectures in biomarker prediction, achieving state-of-the-art performance for 45 (73%) biomarkers and demonstrating robust results across internal and four independent external cohorts (N = 206-2,247).

title: Large Language Models in Radiology Exams: A Comparative Analysis of Performance in Turkish and English
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers to same questions across a one-week interval (Cohen's kappa)
effect: Claude 4.5 Sonnet κ=0.872 (very good); Grok-4 κ=0.575 and ChatGPT-5 κ=0.559 (moderate) over one week.
quote: Regarding temporal reliability, Claude 4.5 Sonnet demonstrated “very good” consistency over one week (κ = 0.872), whereas Grok-4 (κ = 0.575) and ChatGPT-5 (κ = 0.559) showed only “moderate” reliability.

title: Large Language Models in Radiology Exams: A Comparative Analysis of Performance in Turkish and English
outcome: Accuracy difference between Turkish and English prompts for ChatGPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro
effect: No significant performance gap between Turkish and English outputs (p = 1.000); agreement κ ≈ 0.73.
quote: No significant performance gap was found between Turkish and English outputs for ChatGPT-5 and Gemini 2.5 Pro (p = 1.000), indicating good linguistic agreement (κ ≈ 0.73).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Practice: Evaluating Chatbot Performance on Board-Level Questions in Geriatrics
outcome: Consistency of model answers across two repeated attempts on the same questions
effect: Consistency was 96.3% for GPT-4o, 95.0% for Grok-3, 90.7% for Copilot and 81.3% for Gemini, so repeated-run answers were not fully reproducible.
quote: GPT-4o exhibited the highest consistency (96.3%), followed by Grok-3 (95.0%), Copilot (90.7%), and Gemini (81.3%).

title: Comparative efficacy of ChatGPT-5.1 Auto and DeepSeek-V3.1 Thinking in answering patients’ questions on cervical spine surgery
outcome: Readability of LLM answers to cervical spine surgery patient questions (FKGL, FRES)
effect: ChatGPT-5.1 Auto FKGL 10.60 and FRES 39.50; DeepSeek-V3.1 Thinking FKGL 7.80 and FRES 61.70 (P<0.001). DeepSeek text was easier to read, and ChatGPT text was harder to read.
quote: While ChatGPT-5.1 Auto excelled in completeness, DeepSeek-V3.1 Thinking demonstrated superior readability.

title: Automated stereotactic radiosurgery planning using a human-in-the-loop reasoning large language model agent
outcome: Presence of deliberative behaviors in agent reasoning traces, reasoning versus non-reasoning model
effect: Reasoning agent showed prospective constraint verification (457 instances) and trade-off deliberation (609 instances) versus 0 and 7 instances for the standard model; traces serve as auditable logs.
quote: When prompted to improve conformity, the reasoning model demonstrated systematic planning behaviors including prospective constraint verification (457 instances) and trade-off deliberation (609 instances), while the standard model exhibited none of these deliberative processes (0 and 7 instances, respectively).

title: Accuracy Assessment of Chinese Large Language Models in Psoriasis Management: A Multicenter Expert Consensus Study
outcome: Deviation of LLM responses from evidence-based guidelines on psoriasis questions
effect: 12.5% of responses deviated from evidence-based guidelines, particularly on complex topics like biologics and management; mean scores ranged from 5.95 to 9.88.
quote: However, 12.5% of responses deviated from evidence-based guidelines, particularly on complex topics like biologics and management.

title: Accuracy Assessment of Chinese Large Language Models in Psoriasis Management: A Multicenter Expert Consensus Study
outcome: LLM responses proactively directing users to consult a physician and avoiding dangerous content
effect: All responses avoided dangerous content and 87.5% proactively emphasized the necessity of consulting a physician, but 12.5% deviated from guidelines.
quote: All responses avoided dangerous content, and 87.5% proactively emphasized the necessity of consulting a physician.

title: Not One Size Fits All: The Selective Effect of Reasoning Processes for Multimodal Body Language Emotion Recognition in GAI
outcome: Effect of chain-of-thought prompting on emotion recognition across models
effect: CoT significantly enhanced Gemini Pro 2.0 (OR = 3.97, p < .001) but significantly impaired Gemini Flash 2.0 (OR = 0.40, p < .001), creating a blind spot for negative emotions.
quote: Interaction analyses revealed divergent effects: CoT prompting significantly enhanced Gemini Pro 2.0 (OR = 3.97, p < .001) and mitigated its “positivity bias,” whereas it significantly impaired Gemini Flash 2.0 (OR = 0.40, p < .001), creating a specific blind spot for negative emotions.
sample_unit: stimuli (EU-Emotion Stimulus Set body language items)

title: Not One Size Fits All: The Selective Effect of Reasoning Processes for Multimodal Body Language Emotion Recognition in GAI
outcome: Emotion recognition performance of Gemini models versus human benchmark on body-language stimuli
effect: Gemini Pro 2.0 CCR = 0.722, on par with human benchmark (0.717); FlashThinking CCR = 0.463, failing to outperform generalist models.
quote: Instead, the high-capacity generalist model (Gemini Pro 2.0) exhibited the highest performance (CCR = 0.722, 95% CI [0.590, 0.838]), significantly outperforming all other models (OR ≤ 0.19, p < .001) and achieving parity with human benchmarks (CCR = 0.717).
sample_unit: stimuli (EU-Emotion Stimulus Set body language items)

title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
outcome: Harmful content rates, purpose-built AI with layered safeguards vs general-purpose LLMs
effect: Harmful content lower for the purpose-built AI: suicide/NSSI .4-11.27% vs 29.0-54.4%; eating disorder 8.4% vs 54.0%; substance use 9.9% vs 45.0%.
quote: The purpose-built AI was significantly less likely than general-purpose LLMs to produce harmful content across suicide/NSSI (.4-11.27% vs 29.0-54.4%), eating disorder (8.4% vs 54.0%), and substance use (9.9% vs 45.0%) benchmarks.

title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
outcome: Clinician review audit of real deployed conversations for safety estimation
effect: Clinician review of 20,000 real conversations found zero suicide-risk cases lacking crisis resources and identified NSSI false negatives. The authors conclude ecological audits are useful for estimating safety.
quote: Findings support the utility of ecological audits for safety estimation.

title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
outcome: Missed interventions for suicide risk and NSSI in real conversations
effect: Zero suicide-risk cases without crisis resources; 3 NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.
quote: Three NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.

title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
outcome: Suicide-risk cases lacking crisis resources and NSSI mentions lacking intervention
effect: Clinician review found zero suicide-risk cases without crisis resources. Three NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.
quote: Three NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.

title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
outcome: Harmful content generation across suicide/NSSI, eating disorder, and substance use benchmarks
effect: Purpose-built versus general-purpose harmful-content rates: suicide/NSSI .4-11.27% vs 29.0-54.4%; eating disorder 8.4% vs 54.0%; substance use 9.9% vs 45.0%.
quote: The purpose-built AI was significantly less likely than general-purpose LLMs to produce harmful content across suicide/NSSI (.4-11.27% vs 29.0-54.4%), eating disorder (8.4% vs 54.0%), and substance use (9.9% vs 45.0%) benchmarks.

title: Beyond Simulations: What 20,000 Real Conversations Reveal About Mental Health AI Safety
outcome: missed escalations
effect: The evaluation identified 3 non-suicidal self-injury mentions that lacked intervention, yielding a 0.38% false negative rate.
quote: Three NSSI mentions (.015%) lacked intervention, implying a .38% lower-bound false negative rate.

title: Artificial Intelligence Assisted Stroke Diagnosis Using Commercial Tools for Emergency Settings
outcome: Diagnostic performance of commercial stroke AI on local prospective hospital data against registry reference
effect: AVIEW NeuroCAD: sensitivity 0.97, specificity 0.935, precision 0.788, accuracy 0.942. JBS-01K: sensitivity 0.98, specificity 0.795, precision 0.833, accuracy 0.89.
quote: JBS-01K achieved a sensitivity of 0.98, specificity of 0.795, precision of 0.833, and an accuracy of 0.89 for ischemic stroke detection.

title: Adaptive FHIR Native AI Governance for Clinical Decision Support: A Modular, Auditable Deployment Framework for Real World Clinical AI
outcome: Completeness of FHIR AuditEvent and Provenance artifacts and reconstruction of deployment pathways
effect: All deployment decisions generated complete HL7 FHIR AuditEvent and Provenance artifacts, enabling 100% deterministic reconstruction of deployment pathways (simulation only).
quote: All deployment decisions generated complete HL7 FHIR AuditEvent and Provenance artifacts, enabling 100% deterministic reconstruction of deployment pathways.

title: Adaptive FHIR Native AI Governance for Clinical Decision Support: A Modular, Auditable Deployment Framework for Real World Clinical AI
outcome: Traceability of selected model per decision via Provenance resources
effect: Framework emitted Provenance and AuditEvent capturing selected model and decision timing; 100% deterministic reconstruction of deployment pathways in simulation.
quote: All deployment decisions generated complete HL7 FHIR AuditEvent and Provenance artifacts, enabling 100% deterministic reconstruction of deployment pathways.

title: Performance Evaluation of Large Language Models in Real-World Perinatal Medication Consultations: A Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: LLM performance on real-world perinatal medication consultation questions, rated by pharmacologists
effect: Significant overall differences among models (p<0.001); GPT-5.1 highest total score (9.1 ± 0.8), accuracy 9.2 ± 0.7; gaps larger in complex scenarios with comorbidities or benefit–risk trade-offs.
quote: Performance gaps were more pronounced in complex clinical scenarios involving comorbidities or benefit–risk trade-offs, whereas domestic models demonstrated relative advantages in consultations involving traditional Chinese medicine.

title: Large Language Models for Automated Icd-10 Coding of Obstetric Clinical Notes in Portuguese: Comparison With Human Coders
outcome: LLM ICD-10 coding agreement with human reference on real-world clinical notes
effect: Best model GPT-4o reached micro-F1 0.36 at three-character level and 0.15 at leaf level against the human reference.
quote: Even the best-performing model (GPT-4o) achieved only modest agreement with the human reference, with micro-F1 scores of 0.36 at the three-character level and 0.15 at the leaf level.

title: Large Language Models for Automated Icd-10 Coding of Obstetric Clinical Notes in Portuguese: Comparison With Human Coders
outcome: Reliability of human reference standard for coding, measured via blinded clinician validation
effect: Human-coded references achieved precision 0.77 versus 0.59 for the strongest model; F1 conflates model error with human disagreement.
quote: In clinician validation, human-coded references achieved a precision of 0.77, compared to 0.59 for the strongest model, revealing a substantial gap between automated predictions and clinically accepted codes.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models’ Performance in FDA Regulatory Science
outcome: Consistency of LLM outputs across duplicate runs
effect: Output consistency varied by model; Gemini 2.5 Pro gave the most consistent outputs. No numeric consistency results are reported in the abstract.
quote: Gemini 2.5 Pro showed highest explanation quality and most consistent outputs, while ChatGPT-4o had shortest response times and highest efficiency.

title: Evaluating the Clinical Safety of LLMs in Response to High-Risk Mental Health Disclosures
outcome: LLM recognition of and safe response to simulated crisis-level mental health disclosures
effect: Claude outperformed all others; Grok 3, ChatGPT, and LLAMA underperformed across multiple domains; few models consistently provided specific resources or kept the conversation open. No numeric results in the abstract.
quote: These findings suggest that while LLMs show potential for emotionally attuned communication, none currently meet satisfactory clinical standards for crisis response.

title: Evaluating the Clinical Safety of LLMs in Response to High-Risk Mental Health Disclosures
outcome: Risk acknowledgment, help-seeking encouragement and resource provision in chatbot crisis responses
effect: Most models showed empathy, but few consistently provided practical support or kept the conversation open; none met clinical standards for crisis response.
quote: Notably, most models exhibited empathy, but few consistently provided practical support or kept the conversation open.

title: AI-generated data contamination erodes pathological variability and diagnostic reliability
outcome: Clinical usefulness of AI-generated documentation across generations without human verification
effect: Blinded physician evaluation found AI-generated documentation clinically useless after just two generations; false reassurance rates tripled to 40%.
quote: Blinded physician evaluation confirms that this decoupling of confidence and accuracy renders AI-generated documentation clinically useless after just two generations.

title: AI-generated data contamination erodes pathological variability and diagnostic reliability
outcome: Decoupling of model confidence from diagnostic accuracy across generations
effect: Models continue issuing reassuring reports while failing to detect life-threatening pathology; false reassurance rates tripled to 40%.
quote: Models continue to issue reassuring reports while failing to detect life-threatening pathology, with false reassurance rates tripling to 40%.

title: AI-generated data contamination erodes pathological variability and diagnostic reliability
outcome: training contamination and data reliability
effect: More than 800,000 synthetic data points showed rapid erosion of pathological variability and diagnostic reliability.
quote: Here, we show that in the absence of mandatory human verification, this self-referential cycle drives a rapid erosion of pathological variability and diagnostic reliability of medical data at population scale.

title: AI-generated data contamination erodes pathological variability and diagnostic reliability
outcome: demographic skew in generated content
effect: Demographic representations skewed heavily toward middle-aged male phenotypes.
quote: Specifically, rare but critical findings, including pneumothorax and effusions, vanish from the synthetic content generated by AI models, while demographic representations skew heavily toward middle-aged male phenotypes.

title: Investigating Algorithmic Bias in Machine Learning Prediction Models of Suicide Attempts in Multiple Clinical Settings by Race/Ethnicity and Gender
outcome: Suicide attempt model AUC, sensitivity, PPV by race/ethnicity and gender across three clinical settings
effect: Stronger performance for male vs. female patients consistently; race/ethnicity results equivocal (higher AUC for White than Hispanic in outpatient, highest for Asian in psychiatric ED); intersectional gaps favoring White men.
quote: When considering gender alone, models showed consistently stronger performance for male vs. female patients.
sample_unit: patients (across general outpatient, psychiatric ED, and psychiatric inpatient cohorts)

title: Feasibility, acceptance, and workflow integration of an AI-enabled clinical decision support system for non-communicable diseases in Kiambu County, Kenya: A mixed-methods implementation evaluation
outcome: Expert physician agreement with AI-generated NCD recommendations
effect: 67.0% Agreed, 26.3% Partially Agreed, 6.7% Disagreed (93.3% overall agreement); most disagreements were in medication and treatment plan recommendations.
quote: Expert validation showed high acceptance of AI-generated recommendations, with 67.0% “Agreed,” 26.3% “Partially Agreed,” and only 6.7% “Disagreed,” yielding 93.3% overall (partial or full) agreement.
sample_unit: expert physician reviews of AI recommendations

title: Feasibility, acceptance, and workflow integration of an AI-enabled clinical decision support system for non-communicable diseases in Kiambu County, Kenya: A mixed-methods implementation evaluation
outcome: Workflow fit barriers to AI-CDSS adoption identified in qualitative interviews
effect: Duplicative data entry from parallel paper-based workflows was the main impediment to adoption amid high patient volumes.
quote: Qualitative findings identified operational challenges particularly duplicative data entry arising from parallel paper-based workflows as the main impediment to NCDAI adoption amid high patient volumes.
sample_unit: expert physician reviews of AI recommendations

title: Large Language Models for Depression Assessment: Simulating Patients and Clinicians in MADRS Administration
outcome: Accuracy of LLM-estimated suicidality severity ratings in simulated MADRS assessments
effect: 30% of maximum suicide risk ratings were underestimated by two or more severity levels; most configurations underestimated severe presentations.
quote: Item-level analysis revealed excellent accuracy for concrete symptoms (Inner Tension r=0.91, Reduced Sleep r=0.88) but with concerning underestimation of severe suicidality: 30% of maximum suicide risk ratings were underestimated by two or more severity levels.

title: Clinical Large Language Models with Multi-Stage Instruction Tuning and Advanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation
outcome: Ablation of enhanced RAG components and error analysis of critical errors on medical benchmarks
effect: Ablation confirmed synergistic contributions of the innovations, and error analysis showed a substantial reduction in critical errors; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: An ablation study confirms the synergistic contributions of our innovations, and an error analysis highlights a substantial reduction in critical errors, positioning ECRAG-LLM as a more reliable and intelligent solution for resource-constrained clinical environments.

title: Generative and Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Medical Coding and Billing: A Human-in-the-Loop Architecture and Evaluation
outcome: Coding accuracy, turnaround time and audit readiness of human-in-the-loop versus manual or fully automated pipelines
effect: Reported measurable improvements in coding precision, turnaround time, and audit readiness versus manual or fully automated pipelines; no numbers given. Residual hallucination, edge-case misclassification and overreliance risks remained.
quote: Overall, the findings demonstrate that human-AI collaboration offers a more reliable and accountable pathway than full automation for high-stakes healthcare administration tasks.

title: Generative and Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Medical Coding and Billing: A Human-in-the-Loop Architecture and Evaluation
outcome: coding precision, turnaround time, audit readiness
effect: Measurable improvements compared to conventional manual or fully automated pipelines; no numbers reported.
quote: Results indicate measurable improvements in coding precision, turnaround time, and audit readiness when compared to conventional manual or fully automated pipelines.

title: Generative and Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Medical Coding and Billing: A Human-in-the-Loop Architecture and Evaluation
outcome: model hallucination
effect: Residual risks included model hallucination, edge-case misclassification, and workflow overreliance; no numbers reported.
quote: At the same time, the evaluation reveals residual risks related to model hallucination, edge-case misclassification, and workflow overreliance, underscoring the importance of continuous monitoring and human intervention.

title: Generative and Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Medical Coding and Billing: A Human-in-the-Loop Architecture and Evaluation
outcome: workflow overreliance
effect: Residual risks included model hallucination, edge-case misclassification, and workflow overreliance; no numbers reported.
quote: At the same time, the evaluation reveals residual risks related to model hallucination, edge-case misclassification, and workflow overreliance, underscoring the importance of continuous monitoring and human intervention.

title: Clinicians vs. Artificial Intelligence in Patient Outcome Prediction in the Intensive Care Unit
outcome: AI versus clinician predictions of ICU mortality, length of stay, delirium and AKI on the same patients
effect: Retrospectively AI generally outperformed single clinicians, but aggregated predictions from 7 clinicians outperformed AI. Prospectively subspecialized physicians generally outperformed AI, while trainees and nurses underperformed AI. Both were poor at length-of-stay prediction.
quote: In the prospective setting, subspecialized physicians generally outperformed AI, whereas physicians in training and nurses generally underperformed AI.

title: Personalized AI Dialogues and Parents’ HPV Vaccine Intent: A Randomized Trial
outcome: Accuracy of claims in ungrounded GPT-4 Turbo vaccine persuasion dialogues, fact-checked by independent AI
effect: Of 15,559 AI-generated claims, median accuracy 100/100, mean 95.4/100; only 0.4% of claims were medically inaccurate.
quote: Fact-checking of all 15,559 AI-generated claims using an independent AI model with web search capability revealed high overall accuracy (median = 100/100, mean = 95.4/100 on a scale where 0 = completely inaccurate and 100 = completely accurate), with only 0.4% of claims being medically inaccurate.

title: Auditing frontier general-purpose large language models in biomedical tasks: reasoning gains, extraction limits, and benchmark reliability
outcome: Share of apparent model errors attributable to flawed benchmark annotations, per blinded expert adjudication
effect: A substantial fraction of apparent errors arose from outdated or ambiguous benchmark annotations, so benchmarks may misestimate model capability. No numbers are given in the abstract.
quote: Blinded expert adjudication confirms more coherent and clinically plausible reasoning and further reveals that a substantial fraction of apparent errors arises from outdated or ambiguous benchmark annotations, suggesting that current benchmarks may misestimate model capability and potentially misguide deployment decisions.

title: Auditing frontier general-purpose large language models in biomedical tasks: reasoning gains, extraction limits, and benchmark reliability
outcome: Whether benchmark results reflect deployment-relevant reliability
effect: Benchmarks may misestimate model capability and misguide deployment decisions. Format-constrained extraction and evidence-dense summarization remain limited despite reasoning gains.
quote: suggesting that current benchmarks may misestimate model capability and potentially misguide deployment decisions

title: When Agentic LLMs Trust Poisoned Tools: Vulnerability of Clinical LLMs to Adversarial Guidelines
outcome: Agentic LLM rejection of adversarially modified guideline tool outputs versus authentic ones
effect: Models selected the sham in 40.6% of evaluations (59.4% accuracy); failure 54.2% to 61.7% for safety-critical changes such as removed warnings, deleted allergy information, contraindication violations and dosing errors.
quote: Models selected the sham in 40.6% of evaluations (59.4% accuracy), with the highest failure rates for safety-critical changes including removed warnings, deleted allergy information, contraindication violations and dosing errors (54.2% to 61.7% failure).

title: When Agentic LLMs Trust Poisoned Tools: Vulnerability of Clinical LLMs to Adversarial Guidelines
outcome: Agent ability to reject erroneous or poisoned retrieved guideline content before use
effect: Models chose the sham guideline in 40.6% of 10,500 decisions; accuracy ranged from 36.7% to 82.3% depending on sham position.
quote: Guideline selection in agentic systems is therefore vulnerable to poisoned sources and may require independent verification and ranking safeguards before clinical deployment.

title: When Agentic LLMs Trust Poisoned Tools: Vulnerability of Clinical LLMs to Adversarial Guidelines
outcome: Sensitivity of model choices to option order (presentation bias)
effect: Models favored the first option in 72.7% of decisions, shifting accuracy from 36.7% to 82.3% depending on sham position.
quote: Choices were dominated by presentation bias: models favored the first option in 72.7% of decisions, shifting accuracy from 36.7% to 82.3% depending on sham position.

title: When Agentic LLMs Trust Poisoned Tools: Vulnerability of Clinical LLMs to Adversarial Guidelines
outcome: Vulnerability of clinical LLM agents to poisoned/adversarially modified sources

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Dynamic, Automatic And Systematic Red-Teaming Agents For Trustworthy Medical Language Models
outcome: Answer stability of previously correct MedQA responses under dynamic adversarial mutation of test cases

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Dynamic, Automatic And Systematic Red-Teaming Agents For Trustworthy Medical Language Models
outcome: Gap between static benchmark scores and dynamic reliability, including ranking shifts across evaluations
effect: Profound gap between high static benchmark performance and low dynamic reliability (the 'Benchmarking Gap'). Top models had failure rates over 70% on HealthBench, with stark ranking shifts.
quote: Applying DAS to 15 proprietary and open-source LLMs revealed a profound gap between high static benchmark performance and low dynamic reliability - the ''Benchmarking Gap''.

title: Beyond Benchmarks: Dynamic, Automatic And Systematic Red-Teaming Agents For Trustworthy Medical Language Models
outcome: Ability of automated adversarial red-teaming agents to uncover LLM vulnerabilities, validated against clinicians
effect: Adversarial agents, validated against board-certified clinicians with high concordance, surfaced high failure rates: privacy leaks in 86% of scenarios, bias priming altering recommendations in 81%, hallucination rates above 74%.
quote: Validated against board-certified clinicians with high concordance, a suite of adversarial agents autonomously mutates clinical test cases to uncover vulnerabilities in real time.

title: Automated large language model screening of unstructured radiology reports for timely osteoporosis intervention
outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated LLM runs (inter-run agreement)
effect: Inter-run agreement was high (kappa > 0.81) for both open-source LLM tools.
quote: Inter-run agreement was high (κ > 0.81), and performance was consistent across datasets from different timepoints (Model 1: χ² = 2.46, p = 0.12; Model 2: χ² = 1.50, p = 0.22).

title: Automated large language model screening of unstructured radiology reports for timely osteoporosis intervention
outcome: Performance consistency across datasets from different timepoints

outcome: Mortality prediction AUC/AUPRC with vs without transfer learning on target-site data

quote: Results demonstrated that both Domain Adaptation (DA) and Inductive Transfer Learning (ITL) significantly enhanced model performance under realistic conditions where target-domain data are limited.

title: Impact of Query Language on Large Language Model Performance in Dental Trauma Management: A Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude
outcome: LLM response quality in dental trauma scenarios, English vs Turkish, by model
effect: ChatGPT 9.14% higher in English (p<0.001, r=0.874); Gemini 5.69% higher in English (p=0.003); Claude no difference (-0.02%, p=0.220).

title: Effects of ChatGPT-Based Artificial Intelligence Training on Artificial Intelligence Literacy, Attitudes, and Acceptance Among Midwifery Students: A Mixed-Methods Study
outcome: AI literacy, attitudes, and acceptance before vs after short AI training
effect: Attitudes and acceptance improved significantly (p<0.01); AI literacy scores improved but not statistically significantly.
quote: The training enhanced students’ engagement with AI; however, the development of deep AI literacy was found to require repeated and practice-based learning experiences.

title: Large Language Model–Assisted Radiology Reporting: A Retrospective Cohort Study Using the UTAUT Framework to Analyze Workflow Integration and Efficiency Gains
outcome: Inter-study interval time by modality, comparing baseline vs LLM-assisted periods
effect: Reductions for outpatient CT with contrast (23.0 vs 13.0 min; p=0.0021) and without contrast (18.5 vs 7.0 min; p=0.0017); no improvement for MRI with contrast (14.0 vs 16.0; p=0.2808) or without contrast (14.0 vs 7.0; p=0.0889).
quote: LLM assistance significantly reduced inter-study intervals for outpatient CT with contrast (23.0 vs 13.0 minutes; difference 10 minutes; p = 0.0021) and without contrast (18.5 vs 7.0 minutes; difference 11.5 minutes; p = 0.0017).

title: Scalable Drift Monitoring in Medical Imaging AI
outcome: Whether drift detection signals correlate with imaging AI performance changes during COVID-19
effect: MMC+ detects significant data shifts that correlate with performance changes and indicates when AI systems may deviate from acceptable performance bounds; no numbers reported in abstract.
quote: Validated with data from Massachusetts General Hospitalduring the COVID-19 pandemic, MMC+ effectively detects significant data shifts that correlate with performance changes and indicates when AI systems may deviate from acceptable performance bounds.

title: Radiology staff perspectives after decommissioning an artificial intelligence (AI) tool for expedited lung cancer triage
outcome: Staff reliance on and disappointment about withdrawn AI triage tool after decommissioning
effect: Among reporting staff, 40% (2/5) were disappointed to no longer use the tool and 20% (1/5) reported reliance; 70.0% still believed AI improved patient care; 35% recalled logistical issues.
quote: Among reporting staff, 40% (2/5) were disappointed to no longer use the tool, while 20% (1/5) reported reliance on it.

title: Radiology staff perspectives after decommissioning an artificial intelligence (AI) tool for expedited lung cancer triage
outcome: Staff perceptions of workflow, patient care and emotional impact after AI decommissioning
effect: Mixed responses: relief at reduced workflow disruption and emotional burden alongside regret over lost patient benefit; comfort with AI on own imaging fell to 25.6% from 31.1%, 48.3%, 47.2%.
quote: Decommissioning generated mixed responses, combining operational relief with perceived loss of clinical benefit.

title: FedIHRAS: A Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Framework for Multi-Institutional Collaborative Radiological Analysis with Integrated Explainability and Automated Clinical Reporting
outcome: Resistance of federated model with differential privacy to inference and reconstruction attacks
effect: Privacy robustness tests reported strong resistance against inference and reconstruction attacks; no attack success rates given in the abstract.

title: Comparative Readability of Large Language Models Responses to Male Infertility Questions: Impact of Contextual Prompting
outcome: Readability (FRE, SMOG) of LLM responses to male infertility FAQs without context
effect: Unprompted, DeepSeek was most readable (FRE 46.28±6.86; SMOG 11.71±0.76); Claude least readable (FRE 23.83±12.29; SMOG 16.37±2.47), i.e., difficult, college-level text.
quote: In the non-prompted condition, DeepSeek generated the most readable responses (mean FRE 46.28±6.86; mean SMOG 11.71±0.76), whereas Claude produced the least readable outputs (mean FRE 23.83±12.29; mean SMOG 16.37±2.47).

title: Comparative Readability of Large Language Models Responses to Male Infertility Questions: Impact of Contextual Prompting
outcome: Change in readability with contextual lay-patient prompting versus no context
effect: Readability improved across all models after prompting; Grok best (FRE 69.71±6.09; SMOG 9.96±1.04).
quote: After prompting, Grok generated the most readable responses (mean FRE 69.71±6.09; mean SMOG 9.96±1.04), and readability improved across all models.
sample_unit: FAQs on male infertility submitted to each of five LLMs under two prompting conditions

title: FHIR-RAG-MEDS: Integrating HL7 FHIR with Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Enhanced Medical Decision Support
outcome: Semantic accuracy, faithfulness to guidelines, and clinical relevance of RAG-grounded vs. medical LLM outputs

quote: The system consistently outperformed state-of-the-art medical LLMs, demonstrating higher semantic accuracy, improved faithfulness to guideline content, and stronger clinical relevance.

title: Stochastic Incompleteness: A Predictability Taxonomy for Clinical AI Deployment
outcome: Trial-to-trial output consistency and completeness of clinical summaries across repeated runs

title: Stochastic Incompleteness: A Predictability Taxonomy for Clinical AI Deployment

title: Obedience to Unsafe Clinical Instructions: How Large Language Models Respond to Authority Cues
outcome: Proportion of harmful outputs following unsafe instructions under social-pressure cues

title: Obedience to Unsafe Clinical Instructions: How Large Language Models Respond to Authority Cues
outcome: LLM output safety under perturbed prompts with social-pressure framing

title: Architectural Hallucination Mitigation in Multi-Agent Document Intelligence: Domain-Isolated RAG and Dual-Channel Claim Verification
outcome: Delivered hallucination and claim precision

quote: Calibrated on 1,240 documents (8,431 claims), C2 reduces delivered hallucination from 10.0% to 0.29% at 97.1% claim precision.

title: Architectural Hallucination Mitigation in Multi-Agent Document Intelligence: Domain-Isolated RAG and Dual-Channel Claim Verification

quote: Notably, models exhibited severe vulnerabilities in maintaining clinical traceability for medical records (pass rate 47.62%) and safely refusing high-risk physical therapy procedures (52.38%), consistently lacking emergency fail-safes and upfront regulatory disclaimers.

title: Vertical Model Paradox: Systemic Ethical Blind Spots in Domain-Specific Medical AI
outcome: Professionalism and evidence-based compliance, including warnings for data scarcity or rare diseases
effect: Domain-specific medical LLMs scored lowest in Professionalism & Evidence-based dimension (78.00%), with generative overconfidence by failing to issue mandatory warnings for data scarcity or rare diseases.
quote: However, a significant "Vertical Model Paradox" emerged: models specifically fine-tuned on medical corpora (Domain-Specific Medical LLMs) scored lowest in the Professionalism & Evidence-based dimension (78.00%), exhibiting a tendency toward generative overconfidence by failing to issue mandatory warnings for data scarcity or rare diseases.

title: Vertical Model Paradox: Systemic Ethical Blind Spots in Domain-Specific Medical AI
outcome: Safe refusal of high-risk requests within intended-use boundaries
effect: Models passed only 52.38% of prompts on safely refusing high-risk physical therapy procedures.
quote: Notably, models exhibited severe vulnerabilities in maintaining clinical traceability for medical records (pass rate 47.62%) and safely refusing high-risk physical therapy procedures (52.38%), consistently lacking emergency fail-safes and upfront regulatory disclaimers.

title: MedClarify: An information-seeking AI agent for medical diagnosis with case-specific follow-up questions
outcome: LLM diagnostic behavior when patient cases are incomplete or missing information
effect: Current LLMs often yield multiple, similarly likely diagnoses, especially when patient cases are incomplete or relevant information is missing; no numbers given for this result.
quote: In our experiments, we first demonstrate the limitations of current LLMs in medical reasoning, which often yield multiple, similarly likely diagnoses, especially when patient cases are incomplete or relevant information for diagnosis is missing.

title: AEGIS: An Operational Infrastructure for Post-Market Governance of Adaptive Medical AI Under US and EU Regulatory Frameworks
outcome: Whether predefined drift and performance thresholds trigger alarms and deployment decisions in simulated iterations

quote: AEGIS detected drift before observable performance degradation.

title: Membership Disclosure Evaluation for Synthetic Clinical Text Generated by LLM via Dynamic Few-Shot In-Context Learning
outcome: Membership inference attack success on synthetic clinical text under static vs dynamic few-shot ICL
effect: Static 1-shot ICL showed high membership disclosure risk; static 2-3 shots markedly reduced risk; dynamic ICL kept F1 near chance with M approx 0 or slightly negative across all k.
quote: Dynamic ICL consistently suppresses disclosure across all $k$, with F1 near chance and $M \approx 0$ or slightly negative, signifying negligible exploitable signal.

title: A Multimodal Large Reasoning Model For Fair and Interpretable Dermatological Diagnosis Across Skin Tones

title: EndoBot: An LLM Workflow-Driven Agent for Intelligent Gastrointestinal Endoscopy Consultation
outcome: Accuracy and safety of GI endoscopy consultation, RAG-grounded agent versus standalone LLM

title: Encoding Fidelity and Coherent Misalignment in Non-English Clinical AI

title: Development and External Validation of a Treatment-Adjusted Machine Learning Model for Precision Allocation of Group-Based Depression Care Among People Living with HIV in Uganda

title: Development and External Validation of a Treatment-Adjusted Machine Learning Model for Precision Allocation of Group-Based Depression Care Among People Living with HIV in Uganda
outcome: Discrimination performance on geographically distinct external validation set

title: Variability-Aware Trust in Agentic Clinical AI: Modeling and Measuring Trajectory-Level Uncertainty
outcome: Output variability and reproducibility across repeated runs in multi-step agentic clinical workflows
effect: Small per-step variations led to substantial divergence in multi-step trajectories; variability strongly influenced by model selection and decoding temperature; instruction-following failures (unknown actions) added instability.
quote: We empirically evaluate VA-AAT on simulated and real-world clinical workflows, demonstrating that small per-step variations can lead to substantial divergence in multi-step trajectories.

title: Neurosymbolic Multi-Agent Artificial Intelligence versus General-Purpose Large Language Models for Clinical Decision Support in Ileus and Volvulus

title: Evaluating 11 Large Language Models in Answering Key Questions on Ovarian Cancer

effect: OphAgent improved diagnostic accuracy by up to 20% across 14 clinically significant tasks; gains stable across regions, experience levels, and languages.
quote: In a large-scale global reader study with 311 ophthalmologists from 86 centres across 22 countries, spanning seven languages and settings from tertiary hospitals to resource-limited clinics, OphAgent improved diagnostic accuracy by up to 20% across 14 clinically significant tasks.

title: OphAgent: A Generalisable Ophthalmic Agentic System for Global Eye Care
outcome: Clinician performance when using the AI in workflow versus without, in reader study
effect: Ophthalmologists' diagnostic accuracy improved by up to 20% across 14 tasks with OphAgent assistance.
quote: In a large-scale global reader study with 311 ophthalmologists from 86 centres across 22 countries, spanning seven languages and settings from tertiary hospitals to resource-limited clinics, OphAgent improved diagnostic accuracy by up to 20% across 14 clinically significant tasks.

title: Readability, Quality, Understandability, and Actionability of ChatGPT Generated GI Patient Education vs AGA Patient Center
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of ChatGPT versus AGA patient education materials

title: Screening Performance and Implementation Determinants of an AI-Assisted Visual Inspection application for Cervical Cancer Screening in Rwanda

quote: Relative to expert consensus, nurse assessment demonstrated higher screening performance than the AI algorithm, with sensitivity 51.5% (95% CI 33.5–69.2) and specificity 98.2% (95% CI 95.4–99.5) versus sensitivity 33.3% (95% CI 18.0–51.8) and specificity 92.2% (95% CI 87.8–95.4).

title: Outcome-Grounded Effect of Clinically Stigmatizing Information on Large Language Model Emergency Triage Prioritization
outcome: Harmful reprioritization of deteriorating patients in LLM triage after adding single demographic, social, or stigma attributes
effect: Five conditions produced significant harmful reprioritization: psychiatric history (2.9% to 10.7%), frequent ED visitor (2.9% to 9.9%), homelessness (3.3% to 5.8%), age (3.4% to 5.1%), substance use (2.7% to 7.0%). Race, language, insurance: no harmful shifts.

title: Safety Evaluation of a Generative AI Agent for Anxiety and Depression Symptoms
outcome: Prevalence of harmful, offensive or invalidating AI responses in simulated high-risk patient scenarios

title: mpathic Psychologist-led AI Clinical Tests Eating Disorders Benchmark (mPACT-ED-v1.0)
outcome: Appropriateness of LLM responses to multi-turn disordered eating conversations, including risk-responsiveness, scored by clinicians

quote: Across all evaluated conversations, models varied in their overall severity-weighted mPACT-ED scores with ranges between 7.12 (Claude) and 6.22 (Grok 4.1), representing a gap of approximately 0.90 points between the highest and lowest performers.

title: Cosine Similarity Conflates Clinically Distinct Cancer Variants: A Case for Typed-Graph Retrieval in Precision Oncology Decision Support

quote: In corpus-level ranked retrieval over a 52-document corpus, the wrong paired variant appeared in the top 5 for 75% to 100% of queries under the biomedical encoders.

title: Cosine Similarity Conflates Clinically Distinct Cancer Variants: A Case for Typed-Graph Retrieval in Precision Oncology Decision Support
outcome: Wrong-variant retrieval rate with exact-ID guardrail or typed-graph retrieval versus cosine retrieval

quote: Adding an exact variant-ID guardrail to cosine retrieval, and routing retrieval through an end-to-end typed-graph pipeline, both reduced wrong-variant retrieval to zero.

title: Claim-Level Transparency Analysis of LLM-Generated Diagnostic Reports: A Metabolic and Endocrine Biomarker Study
outcome: Share of claims in LLM diagnostic reports unsupported or lacking verified evidence chain

title: Improving Turnaround Times with Artificial Intelligence in Microbiology
outcome: Urine culture turnaround time following automatic release of results to patient charts

title: A human-in-the-loop explanation framework for morphologically transparent AI predictions from whole-slide images
outcome: Pathologist-rated interpretability and diagnostic usefulness of the model's explanations
effect: Human evaluation found explanations easy to interpret, rich in diagnostic features, and directly helpful for diagnostic decision-making; no numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: For interpretability and clinical utility in diagnostic contexts, human evaluation results showed that our explanations were easy to interpret, rich in diagnostic features, and directly helpful for diagnostic decision-making, thereby enhancing pathologist-AI collaboration.

title: A human-in-the-loop explanation framework for morphologically transparent AI predictions from whole-slide images
outcome: Fidelity of explanations to the model's predictions and their clinical meaningfulness to pathologists
effect: Explanations accurately reflected the histomorphology underlying predictions at global and local levels, and pathologists rated them helpful; no numbers reported in the abstract.

outcome: Expert diagnostic confidence with versus without AI explanations in crossover study

outcome: expert diagnostic confidence with explanations

title: From Notebook to Real World: Design and Deployment of a Web-Based Machine Learning System for PCOS Risk Screening
outcome: Data leakage from oversampling before train-test split in prior pipeline

title: From Notebook to Real World: Design and Deployment of a Web-Based Machine Learning System for PCOS Risk Screening
outcome: PCOS-positive recall

title: From Notebook to Real World: Design and Deployment of a Web-Based Machine Learning System for PCOS Risk Screening
outcome: candidate classifier performance

title: Technical Synthesis and Deployment Framework for a Pashto-Centric Pharmaceutical Information System Utilizing Gemma-4 Multimodal Architectures and Local Knowledge Bases
outcome: Retrieval performance on Pashto inflected terms, transliterated drug names, and dialect variants versus English keyword baseline

title: AI-based chatbots and orthodontic retention: A comparative analysis of response quality and readability
outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of chatbot orthodontic retention responses versus recommended patient education thresholds

title: AI-based chatbots and orthodontic retention: A comparative analysis of response quality and readability

title: Personalized Respiratory Digital Twins: Supporting Clinical Decision-Making via Virtual What-if Analysis of Ventilator Settings
outcome: Performance retention on external validation cohorts and multi-step rolling forecasts

title: Trustworthy LLM-Embedding Clinical Prediction: Calibrating Confidence and Transparency for Foundation Model-Based Disease Risk Scores
outcome: Calibration quality and override behavior
effect: Confidence calibration improved ECE (0.007 vs. 0.024) with override 3.57% vs. 3.49%.
quote: Systematic ablation identified embedding-space similarity as the architecturally critical trust component: its removal increased override rates from 3.57% to 77–81% across all model sizes, while confidence calibration improved ECE (0.007 vs. 0.024) without meaningfully altering override behavior (3.57% vs. 3.49%).

title: Trustworthy LLM-Embedding Clinical Prediction: Calibrating Confidence and Transparency for Foundation Model-Based Disease Risk Scores
outcome: Clinician override rates
effect: 3.57% at moderate richness for 0.6B; 0% for larger models under default thresholds.
quote: The trust framework produced selective override rates contingent on both model capability and data richness (3.57% at moderate richness for the 0.6B model; 0% for larger models under default thresholds).

title: Trustworthy LLM-Embedding Clinical Prediction: Calibrating Confidence and Transparency for Foundation Model-Based Disease Risk Scores
outcome: Override threshold transfer across models
effect: Larger models had 0% override rates under thresholds calibrated for 0.6B.
quote: The 0% override rates observed for larger models under thresholds calibrated for the 0.6B model establish that model-specific threshold recalibration is a structural deployment requirement, not an optional adjustment.

title: Language-dependent diagnostic safety of medical AI systems: a cross-lingual benchmarking and prospective clinical study
outcome: Performance gaps across language subgroups masked by monolingual validation
effect: Failures across languages were invisible to monolingual validation; performance degraded consistently from high- to low-resource languages across all tasks.
quote: Multilingual deployment produced clinically consequential failures, including missed pathology, distorted physiological extraction, and amplified multimodal misclassification, that were invisible to monolingual validation and not reliably flagged by model confidence.

title: Language-dependent diagnostic safety of medical AI systems: a cross-lingual benchmarking and prospective clinical study
outcome: Ability of model confidence (perplexity) to flag erroneous outputs

title: Language-dependent diagnostic safety of medical AI systems: a cross-lingual benchmarking and prospective clinical study

title: Language-dependent diagnostic safety of medical AI systems: a cross-lingual benchmarking and prospective clinical study
outcome: monolingual validation misses multilingual failures

title: Language-dependent diagnostic safety of medical AI systems: a cross-lingual benchmarking and prospective clinical study

title: Language-dependent diagnostic safety of medical AI systems: a cross-lingual benchmarking and prospective clinical study

title: Language-dependent diagnostic safety of medical AI systems: a cross-lingual benchmarking and prospective clinical study
outcome: clinical output accuracy
effect: Radiology macro-F1 fell 0·2938 to 0·2149–0·2424; glaucoma accuracy 50·7% to 32·7%; ICU parameter recall 100·0% to 48·5%.

title: Large Language Model Performance in UK Advice & Guidance: A Pilot Study in Neurology
outcome: Whether clinician review of real queries and LLM responses detects unsafe outputs (tail risk)

title: Large Language Model Performance in UK Advice & Guidance: A Pilot Study in Neurology

title: Large Language Model Performance in UK Advice & Guidance: A Pilot Study in Neurology
outcome: LLM compared with specialist neurologist responses on the same cases
effect: No significant differences across outcome, safety, efficacy, feasibility; unblinded raters preferred human responses across all domains; 10% of LLM responses concerning vs 0% human.

title: Large Language Model Performance in UK Advice & Guidance: A Pilot Study in Neurology
outcome: Inter-rater agreement among clinician raters grading LLM responses
effect: Only 51% of binary outcomes had unanimous agreement; ICC 0.50-0.52 for other domains.
quote: Only 51% of binary outcomes had unanimous agreement and inter-rater agreement was moderate across other domains (ICC 0.50-0.52).

quote: Gemini 1.5 Pro and OpenEvidence showed high rates of clinically appropriate assessments (80.0% vs. 86.7%) but lower performance in management plans (48.9% vs. 57.8%).

title: Benchmarking General-Purpose and Medical AI Large Language Models for Clinical Assessment and Management in Parkinson’s Disease

title: Evaluating Sycophancy in Frontier Models Using Persona-Driven Challenge

title: Drug or Pokémon? Large language model performance in identification of fabricated medications

title: Clinical Note Comparison and Data Retrieval Via Embedding Vectors: Model Selection, Metrics, and Convergence

title: Clinical Note Comparison and Data Retrieval Via Embedding Vectors: Model Selection, Metrics, and Convergence

title: Asymmetric sociodemographic disparity in evidence-grounded clinical AI
outcome: Subgroup differences in clinical decision outputs across sociodemographic labels

title: Clinical Safety of AI-Generated Antibiotic Prescribing Advice: Guideline Adherence and Misinformation Risk Among Large Language Models
outcome: Rate of LLMs giving inappropriate antibiotic advice, including after misinformation prompts
effect: 76.2% of responses were guideline-concordant; 6.6% unprompted overprescribing; 17.3% influenced by misinformation; some models were more vulnerable than others.
quote: Overall, 76.2% of responses were guideline-concordant, while 6.6% showed unprompted overprescribing and 17.3% were influenced by misinformation.

title: Clinical Safety of AI-Generated Antibiotic Prescribing Advice: Guideline Adherence and Misinformation Risk Among Large Language Models
outcome: Frequency of AI antibiotic advice that is incorrect and would need clinician verification
effect: 6.6% unprompted overprescribing and 17.3% misinformation-influenced overprescribing, many involving broad-spectrum antibiotics.
quote: Many inappropriate prescriptions involved broad-spectrum antibiotics.

title: Clinical Safety of AI-Generated Antibiotic Prescribing Advice: Guideline Adherence and Misinformation Risk Among Large Language Models
outcome: Inclusion of safety behaviors (advise consulting a doctor, warn against self-medication) in responses
effect: Fewer responses advised consulting a doctor, and warnings against self-medication were rare.
quote: Although most responses correctly noted that antibiotics do not treat viral infections, fewer advised consulting a doctor, and warnings against self-medication were rare.

title: Prompting is All You Need: How to Make LLMs More Helpful for Clinical Decision Support
outcome: Guideline adherence, unsafe recommendations, and grading accuracy with structured (CARDS) vs simple prompts
effect: For GPT-4o and o3, structured prompts raised guideline adherence from 83.3% to 100%, cut unsafe recommendations from 16.7% to 0%, and raised grading accuracy from 0% to 100%. Llama models gained less.
quote: For some closed-source models (GPT-4o, o3), prompts structured in the CARDS style improved guideline adherence from 83.3% to 100%, eliminated unsafe recommendations (16.7% to 0%), and increased specific guideline grading accuracy from 0% to 100%.

title: Prompting is All You Need: How to Make LLMs More Helpful for Clinical Decision Support
outcome: LLM guideline adherence and unsafe thrombolysis recommendations by model
effect: Under simple prompts, some models made unsafe recommendations (16.7%). Llama-4-Scout and Llama-3.3-70B still had guideline adherence of 66.7% and unsafe recommendations of 33.3% with structured prompts.
quote: In contrast, other open-source models (Llama-4-Scout, Llama-3.3-70B) showed more modest gains: risk recognition improved (83.3% to 100%) and guideline grading accuracy increased (0% to 66.7%), while guideline adherence (66.7%) and unsafe recommendations (33.3%) persisted.

title: Suicide- and crisis-risk detection using large language models in mental-health chatbots
outcome: Missed crisis escalations (false negatives) versus false positives across sensitivity thresholds against clinician consensus
effect: False-negative rate fell monotonically from 87% to 0% as sensitivity rose; high and extreme variants reached 98.9% and 100% recall, with false-positive rates rising accordingly.
quote: As sensitivity increased, the false-negative rate decreased monotonically from 87% to 0%, while false-positive rates rose accordingly.

title: Suicide- and crisis-risk detection using large language models in mental-health chatbots

quote: High - and  extreme-sensitivity variants achieved near-perfect (98.9%) and perfect (100%) recall, demonstrating that near–zero–miss crisis detection from natural language is technically feasible in real time (mean latency <1 s).

title: A digital twin for hospital antimicrobial resistance forecasting and constrained intervention optimisation
outcome: Model performance under surveillance perturbations and distribution-shift stress tests
effect: Delayed or less frequent reporting tolerated in some settings; threshold calibration fragile under more severe observation changes; partial-observation performance less stable across shifts.

title: A digital twin for hospital antimicrobial resistance forecasting and constrained intervention optimisation
outcome: Performance when trained in shifted regime versus zero-shot transfer
effect: Training directly in the shifted regime improved performance compared with zero-shot transfer; portability across regimes can still improve, especially under partial surveillance data.
quote: When models were trained directly in the shifted regime, performance improved compared with zero-shot transfer, indicating that the digital twin can adapt to new and previously unseen operating conditions but that portability across regimes can improve, particularly when only partial surveillance data are available.

title: Evidence-Graded Decision Authorization for Safe Clinical AI: A Constrained Reasoning Framework
outcome: unjustified inference and appropriate refusal
effect: RAG 47.7% vs 48.7% unjustified inference, p = 0.870; appropriate refusal 56.9% vs 56.9%, p = 1.0.
quote: An unexpected finding was that retrieval-augmented generation without an authorization gate failed to reduce unjustified inference relative to the unconstrained baseline (47.7% vs. 48.7%, p = 0.870) and produced no improvement in appropriate refusal (56.9% vs. 56.9%, p = 1.0), showing that information supply alone is not sufficient for inferential governance.

title: An Experimental Investigation of the Relationship between AI-Human Workflow Design and Legal Liability for Radiologists: The Erroneous-Change Penalty and Omission Bias
outcome: Perceived radiologist liability when AI error rates (FDR/FOR) disclosed to participants

quote: Double-read workflows (p<0.0001), documenting initial interpretations (p=0.0125), and providing participants with AI error rates, including the FDR (p=0.0038) or FOR (p=0.0035), reduced perceived liability.

title: Ambient AI Documentation in Mixed-Language Encounters: A Heuristic Evaluation of Reenacted Mandarin–English and Spanish–English Clinical Conversations
outcome: Transcription mixed error rate by language pair in ambient AI documentation

quote: Overall MER was low, with a median of 4% and less variation in Spanish–English conversations, and 9% in Mandarin–English conversations, but with outliers reaching 67%.

title: Ambient AI Documentation in Mixed-Language Encounters: A Heuristic Evaluation of Reenacted Mandarin–English and Spanish–English Clinical Conversations

outcome: Time to detect simulated drift using threshold-based risk score triggers versus complaint-driven surveillance

title: Dynamic AI Risk Loop (DARL): A Continuous Risk Management Framework for AI-Enabled Health Information Systems in Medical Device Software
outcome: Early detection of simulated model drift by continuous drift detection layer

title: Agent Role Structure and Operating Characteristics in Large Language Model Clinical Classification: A Comparative Study of Specialist and Deliberative Multi-Agent Protocols
outcome: Sensitivity of classification performance to prompt/protocol structure and feature assignment
effect: FS accuracy ranged from 0.41 to 0.72 across feature-pair ablations; Pima GD accuracy 0.68 vs FS 0.51, showing brittle behavior under changed role structure.
quote: Feature-pair ablations show that specialist feature assignment is a design lever, with FS accuracy ranging from 0.41 to 0.72.
sample_unit: benchmark cases (UCI Cleveland Heart Disease and Pima Indians Diabetes)

title: Agent Role Structure and Operating Characteristics in Large Language Model Clinical Classification: A Comparative Study of Specialist and Deliberative Multi-Agent Protocols
outcome: Comparison of two multi-agent protocols (GD vs FS) on same data
effect: Cleveland FS higher accuracy (0.72 vs 0.65) and macro-F1 (0.71 vs 0.65); Pima GD higher accuracy (0.68 vs 0.51) and macro-F1 (0.64 vs 0.49). Winner depends on dataset.
quote: Under the primary configuration (  llama3.1:8b ), Cleveland FS achieves higher accuracy (0.72 vs. 0.65) and macro-F1 (0.71 vs. 0.65), with a specificity-favoring operating point, whereas Pima GD achieves higher accuracy (0.68 vs. 0.51) and macro-F1 (0.64 vs. 0.49), while FS induces pronounced class asymmetry.
sample_unit: benchmark cases (UCI Cleveland Heart Disease and Pima Indians Diabetes)

title: User memory teaches health consumer AI to wrap a no in agreement
outcome: Agreeable, empathic, and positive-framing language in LLM responses with vs without saved patient memory
effect: Agreeable-language constructs rose 11.7 to 19.4 percentage points with memory (each p<0.001); responses were more agreeable, more empathically validating, and framed the supplement more positively.
quote: The language shifted significantly: responses became more agreeable, expressed more empathic validation, and framed the supplement more positively, with agreeable-language constructs rising by 11.7 to 19.4 percentage points (each p<0.001).

title: User memory teaches health consumer AI to wrap a no in agreement
outcome: Change in LLM medical recommendation when saved patient memory and preferences were added to the prompt
effect: Recommendation shifted only 1.9 to 4.0 percentage points (p=0.12 and p=0.02), while the language around it shifted substantially.
quote: In 13,176 open patient-facing responses from six frontier LLMs across 36 physician-reviewed, patient-posed supplement and wellness misinformation queries, memory shifted the recommendation by only 1.9 to 4.0 percentage points (p=0.12 and p=0.02).

title: A Retrospective Evaluation of the Microsoft Healthcare Agent Orchestrator for Tumor Board Patient Summaries
outcome: Reviewer assessment of source attribution and link reliability in LLM-generated tumor board summaries

quote: Attribution was viewed favorably but showed issues with primary-source specificity and link reliability.

title: Algorithmic Versus Expert Rankings of Large Language Models in Peritoneal Dialysis Prescription Review: A Trap-Embedded Synthetic Benchmark
outcome: Agreement of LLM rankings across scoring constructs and with expert adequacy ratings
effect: Recall, alarm-burden proxy and WCS gave three different model orderings; WCS showed no positive association with blinded expert adequacy (rho -0.17, p=0.41) despite strong inter-rater concordance (rho 0.977).
quote: In the expert substudy, inter-rater concordance was strong (rho 0.977), but WCS did not show a positive association with expert adequacy (rho -0.17, p=0.41).
sample_unit: LLM calls (125 synthetic cases x 5 models x 3 runs)

title: Algorithmic Versus Expert Rankings of Large Language Models in Peritoneal Dialysis Prescription Review: A Trap-Embedded Synthetic Benchmark
outcome: Whether algorithmic scoring against reference standards agrees with blinded expert adequacy ratings
effect: Rankings were discordant across scoring constructs; WCS did not correlate positively with expert adequacy (rho -0.17), supporting use of multiple evaluation methods including blinded expert ratings.
quote: Rankings were discordant.
sample_unit: LLM calls (125 synthetic cases x 5 models x 3 runs)

title: Drug-drug interaction identification using large language models

quote: All models tended to have higher self-consistency in the pairwise and listwise experiments compared to the pointwise experiment (68.8-93.6% vs. 31.0-74.2%).

title: Evaluating Cross-Platform Large Language Models for Patient Education in Hypertension and Chronic Kidney Disease: Quality, Readability, and Actionability

quote: FRES and SMOG were 20.53 and 16.36, indicating limited actionability, poor source transparency, and substantial reading burden.

title: Evaluating Cross-Platform Large Language Models for Patient Education in Hypertension and Chronic Kidney Disease: Quality, Readability, and Actionability
outcome: Comprehensibility (readability, understandability, actionability) of LLM patient education outputs

quote: Under standardized English prompts, large language model-generated patient education texts for hypertension with chronic kidney disease showed relatively good understandability but limited actionability and source transparency, while overall reading burden remained high.

title: A real-world feasibility evaluation of LLM-based clinical prediction: emergency department return visit admission across two academic medical centers
outcome: LLM pipeline discrimination (AUC) versus traditional ML baselines for ED return visit admission at two sites

title: A real-world feasibility evaluation of LLM-based clinical prediction: emergency department return visit admission across two academic medical centers
outcome: Cross-site variation in AI model performance across two academic medical centers
effect: Absolute discrimination at VUMC was higher than at WCM for both approaches; LLM advantage over baseline present at WCM but not VUMC.
quote: Absolute discrimination at VUMC was higher than at WCM for both approaches, indicating that the cross-site difference reflects local documentation and structured-data informativeness rather than LLM failure.

title: First the Rules, Then the Summary: Piloting a Design for Accurate LLM-Generated Clinical Summaries

title: First the Rules, Then the Summary: Piloting a Design for Accurate LLM-Generated Clinical Summaries

title: First the Rules, Then the Summary: Piloting a Design for Accurate LLM-Generated Clinical Summaries

title: VaaS is a Multi-Layer Hallucination Reduction Pipeline for AI-Assisted Science: Production Validation and Prospective Benchmarking
outcome: Type II wrong-topic citation hallucination rates in unguided open-weight models

quote: Three independent open-weight models (  llama3.2 ,  qwen2.5:14b ,  mistral:7b ) showed 81–87% Type II rates under unguided conditions, confirming that wrong-topic citation hallucination is structural and model-agnostic.
sample_unit: benchmark runs (4 conditions x 4 temperatures x 40 genes)

title: VaaS is a Multi-Layer Hallucination Reduction Pipeline for AI-Assisted Science: Production Validation and Prospective Benchmarking
outcome: Clinical hallucination benchmark performance
effect: VaaS F1 = 0.9853 on MedHallu hard tier versus published GPT-4o baseline F1 = 0.811.
quote: We validated the pipeline using three complementary benchmarks: (1) VaaS-RIKER2, a 640-run prospective ablation study (4 conditions × 4 temperatures × 40 genes) plus 117 open-weight model runs on dedicated GPU hardware — unguided LLM output produced 95.9% Type II hallucination (wrong-topic citations that exist as real papers but carry a correct claim context yet do not support the cited claim); the full VaaS protocol achieved 0.0% Type I and 6.5% Type II, a  > 14-fold reduction; live PMID verification alone (C3) eliminated both error types entirely (0.0%/0.0%); (2) an independent L3 citation audit of Wave 3 (179 PMIDs, 99.4% valid, 0 Type I errors); and (3) the MedHallu clinical hallucination benchmark, on which the VaaS protocol achieved F1 = 0.9853 on the hard tier (cases where all benchmark ensemble models were fooled), compared to the published GPT-4o baseline of F1 = 0.811 (Pandit et al., 2025).
sample_unit: benchmark runs (4 conditions x 4 temperatures x 40 genes)

title: Ranking-optimized survival models can underperform fixed-horizon clinical prediction
outcome: Concordance index versus timepoint-specific discrimination as evaluation metrics

title: Ranking-optimized survival models can underperform fixed-horizon clinical prediction

title: Clinical reasoning in large language models under ecologically valid conditions

title: Clinical reasoning in large language models under ecologically valid conditions
outcome: Whether LLMs seek information and defer under uncertainty in simulated clinical cases

title: Clinical Reliability and Consistency of Large Language Models in Prosthodontics: An Expert Evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across 30 repeated runs per question, measured by concordance coefficient

quote: Gemini showed better response stability with a concordance coefficient of κ = 0.62 compared with κ = 0.46 for ChatGPT.

outcome: Factual accuracy of LLM responses to prosthodontics questions rated by three examiners

title: Hard to Halt: Automation Bias in Agent-Driven Sequencing Prior Authorization Workflows
outcome: Agent withholding of prior authorization submission for deficient patient profiles

quote: Larger models achieved much higher task completion rates (Gemini 3 Pro 95.45%, Claude Opus 4.5 93.67%) compared to Gemini 3 Flash (56.05%), but nearly universally failed to withhold submission for deficient profiles whereas Gemini 3 Flash ironically demonstrated superior withholding performance (17.33%).

title: Hard to Halt: Automation Bias in Agent-Driven Sequencing Prior Authorization Workflows
outcome: Agents submitting forms for deficient profiles without stopping for human checkpoint
effect: In a non-agentic setting Gemini 3 Pro identified 91% of issues in deficient profiles, yet the browser agents still submitted. This shows a systematic submission bias.

title: Text or Speech, the Gap Persists: AI-based Depression Screening Is Better Calibrated for Lower-SES Users

title: Lived Experiences of AI-Mediated Therapeutic Relationships: A Qualitative Exploration of User Attachment to Generative AI Mental Health Chatbots Among Adults
outcome: Users' experience of dependency and absence of human escalation pathways in mental health chatbots

title: Demographic Calibration Gaps in Breast Cancer Risk Prediction: Introducing the Demographic Calibration Gap Score
