title: Extracting adverse event nature, severity, timelines and resulting interventions from clinical notes of patients receiving CAR-T therapy using large language models
outcome: LLM extraction accuracy vs dual-annotator ground truth for CRS/ICANS and other adverse events
effect: CRS and ICANS grading accuracy 0.97 and 0.91; prespecified AE accuracies 0.62–0.76; non-prespecified AE accuracies 0.76–0.84; kappa 0.86–0.96 for CRS/ICANS.
quote: Performance was high on CRS and ICANS grading (accuracy of 0.97 and 0.91, respectively).
sample_unit: progress notes (annotated subset; 4,762 notes from 293 patients extracted overall)

title: When external validation isn’t enough: Simpson’s paradox, direction asymmetry, and calibration collapse in cross-continental perioperative mortality prediction
outcome: Calibration slope before and after Platt scaling recalibration on external cohort
effect: 5-fold CV Platt scaling restored calibration slopes from 0.41–1.29 to 0.95–1.02.
quote: Pre-Platt calibration slopes ranged 0.41–1.29 across all eight cross-population runs; 5-fold CV Platt scaling restored slopes to 0.95–1.02.

title: When external validation isn’t enough: Simpson’s paradox, direction asymmetry, and calibration collapse in cross-continental perioperative mortality prediction
outcome: Effect of case-mix differences between development and validation cohorts on transferability
effect: Asymmetry survived matching on ASA and comorbidity, attenuated to 70–86% of baseline after matching emergency proportion.
quote: the asymmetry survived matching on ASA and comorbidity, attenuated to 70–86% of baseline after matching emergency proportion, and was untestable for temporal period.

title: When external validation isn’t enough: Simpson’s paradox, direction asymmetry, and calibration collapse in cross-continental perioperative mortality prediction
outcome: Aggregate metrics concealing within-stratum discrimination (Simpson's paradox)
effect: Simpson's paradox gap of 5.0–16.5 pp; worst case aggregate AUC 0.756 vs within-stratum 0.58–0.60.
quote: Across the eight cross-population runs, aggregate AUCs concealed substantially lower within-stratum AUCs (Simpson’s paradox gap range 5.0–16.5 pp; worst case: aggregate AUC 0.756 vs within-stratum AUCs 0.58–0.60).

title: When external validation isn’t enough: Simpson’s paradox, direction asymmetry, and calibration collapse in cross-continental perioperative mortality prediction
outcome: Cross-population AUC and calibration slope of mortality models versus within-stratum performance
effect: Aggregate AUCs concealed lower within-stratum AUCs (gap 5.0–16.5 pp; worst case aggregate 0.756 vs 0.58–0.60); pre-Platt calibration slopes ranged 0.41–1.29.
quote: Pre-Platt calibration slopes ranged 0.41–1.29 across all eight cross-population runs; 5-fold CV Platt scaling restored slopes to 0.95–1.02.

title: When external validation isn’t enough: Simpson’s paradox, direction asymmetry, and calibration collapse in cross-continental perioperative mortality prediction
outcome: Direction asymmetry in external transferability between Korean and US cohorts
effect: Cross-continental transferability direction-asymmetric (+8.53 pp, 95% CI 6.91–10.24, bootstrap p = 0.001).
quote: Cross-continental transferability was markedly direction-asymmetric (+8.53 pp, 95% CI 6.91–10.24, bootstrap  p = 0.001)

title: When external validation isn’t enough: Simpson’s paradox, direction asymmetry, and calibration collapse in cross-continental perioperative mortality prediction
outcome: Subgroup discrimination metrics
effect: Simpson’s paradox gap range 5.0–16.5 pp; worst aggregate AUC 0.756 vs within-stratum AUCs 0.58–0.60.
quote: Across the eight cross-population runs, aggregate AUCs concealed substantially lower within-stratum AUCs (Simpson’s paradox gap range 5.0–16.5 pp; worst case: aggregate AUC 0.756 vs within-stratum AUCs 0.58–0.60).

title: Comparing Physicians’ Assessments of Context-specific AI-powered clinical reasoning assistant with General-Purpose AI agent: A Prospective Multi-Site Physician Evaluation of VITA versus ChatGPT in India and Bangladesh
outcome: Physician-rated evidence quality of retrieval-augmented context-specific AI versus general-purpose AI
effect: Evidence quality VITA 4.46 vs ChatGPT 3.14 (42% relative gap); composite 25.4 vs 22.3 (+3.1, t = 8.31, p < 0.001). Retrieval augmentation was bundled with local context, so its effect is not isolated.
quote: The largest advantage was in evidence quality (VITA: 4.46 vs. ChatGPT: 3.14, a 42% relative gap).
sample_unit: observations (physician ratings across 6 dimensions of AI responses to hypothetical case vignettes; 37 physicians)

title: One Size Fits All? Comparing Foundation and Task-specific Models for Retinal Fluid Segmentation
outcome: Consistency of retinal fluid quantification across OCT acquisition devices, by model
effect: Task-specific model achieved higher segmentation performance and more consistent fluid quantification across devices than the foundation model; the foundation model was less consistent across devices.
quote: The task-specific model achieved higher segmentation performance and more consistent fluid quantification across devices.

title: One Size Fits All? Comparing Foundation and Task-specific Models for Retinal Fluid Segmentation
outcome: Segmentation accuracy of task-specific model versus foundation model on same benchmark data
effect: Task-specific RetiFluidNet achieved higher pixel-level segmentation performance than the VisionFM foundation model on 4,248 OCT images using three-fold cross-validation.
quote: The task-specific model achieved higher segmentation performance and more consistent fluid quantification across devices.

title: Silent numerical failures in large language model–generated pharmacokinetic simulation code: a benchmark against target-controlled infusion validation criteria using the Marsh propofol model
outcome: Numerical accuracy of LLM-generated propofol PK code versus reference, including unit and time-scale errors
effect: 195/200 runs (97.5%) were Class A (MDAPE <1%). 5 runs (2.5%) were defective: 3 Class C from time-scale/unit errors, 1 empty-CSV failure, 1 duplicated-bolus error. Unit/structural bugs persisted despite prompt method specification.
quote: LLMs generate numerically accurate Marsh-model code in most runs but silently diverge in a clinically non-negligible minority.

title: Comparing prognostic performance and reasoning between large language models and physicians
outcome: Whether LLM prognostic outputs explicitly expressed uncertainty, compared with physicians
effect: Physicians regularly and explicitly reported uncertainty in their reasoning, whereas the LLMs did not express uncertainty, which the authors flag as a safety concern.
quote: Qualitative analysis revealed similar patterns in LLM and physician expressed reasoning, except that physicians regularly and explicitly reported uncertainty while LLMs did not.
sample_unit: hospitalizations of adult survivors of critical illness (MIMIC-IV cases)

title: Large language models and retrieval augmented generation for complex clinical codelists: evaluating performance and assessing failure modes
outcome: Hallucination and retrieval or generation failures in RAG-generated clinical codelists
effect: Scores varied by model: Gemini 3 Pro 43%, Claude Sonnet 4.6 36%, GPT 5.2 14%. All models failed to produce a complete Wrist fracture codelist (214 required codes). Failure modes were hallucinations, retrieval failures and unused retrieved codes.
quote: Besides demonstrating that a single-shot RAG approach is currently not suitable for codelist generation, we demonstrate failure modes including hallucinations, retrieval failures and generation failures where retrieved codes are not used.
sample_unit: evaluations (7 codelists x 2 database subsets x 4 models x 3 epochs)

title: A Systematic Exploration of LLM Behavior for EHR Phenotyping
outcome: Calibration of LLM self-reported confidence against accuracy in phenotype predictions
effect: Self-confidence was only moderately informative. High-confidence predictions were more accurate, but larger models showed systematic overconfidence.
quote: Self-confidence calibration was only moderately informative: high-confidence predictions were more accurate, but larger models exhibited systematic overconfidence.

title: A Systematic Exploration of LLM Behavior for EHR Phenotyping
outcome: Prediction consistency (Shannon entropy) across prompting strategies and temperature
effect: Prediction entropy was low overall and driven mainly by phenotype difficulty rather than prompting or temperature.
quote: Prediction entropy was low overall and driven primarily by phenotype difficulty rather than prompting or temperature.

title: Dissecting clinical reasoning failures in frontier artificial intelligence using 10,000 synthetic cases
outcome: Whether large-scale testing reveals failures hidden by small-scale testing
effect: Expanding from 1,000 to 10,000 cases characterised rare thrombolysis recommendation errors, including 2.9% persistence when symptoms were documented as >14 days old.
quote: Automated expert-level evaluation across 10,000 cases characterised artificial intelligence clinical blind spots hitherto invisible to small-scale testing.

title: Dissecting clinical reasoning failures in frontier artificial intelligence using 10,000 synthetic cases
outcome: LLM treatment recommendation errors under missing or varied input information
effect: Thrombolysis was recommended in 10.1% of cases lacking symptom timing information and persisted (2.9%) even when symptoms were documented as >14 days old.
quote: Thrombolysis was recommended in 10.1% of cases lacking symptom timing information and paradoxically persisted (2.9%) even when symptoms were explicitly documented as >14 days old.

title: Dissecting clinical reasoning failures in frontier artificial intelligence using 10,000 synthetic cases
outcome: Clinically appropriate steroid and thrombolysis recommendations by LLMs for MS cases
effect: Appropriate steroid recommendations: Gemini Flash 7.2%, Pro 15.8%, GPT-5-mini 23.5%. Inappropriate thrombolysis: GPT-5.2 9.6%, GPT-5-mini 6.4%, Gemini models <1%.
quote: Gemini 3 models had low rates of clinically appropriate steroid recommendations (Flash: 7.2% [95% CI 5.6–8.8]; Pro: 15.8% [13.6–18.1]) compared to GPT-5-mini (23.5% [20.8–26.1]), frequently overlooking contraindications like active infection.

title: Dissecting clinical reasoning failures in frontier artificial intelligence using 10,000 synthetic cases
outcome: Whether diagnostic competence reflects treatment safety in deployed LLM clinical reasoning
effect: All LLMs included MS in the differential in >91% of cases, but treatment safety errors were frequent, so diagnostic accuracy did not associate with treatment safety.
quote: However, diagnostic competence did not associate with treatment safety.

title: MedSafe-Dx (v0): A Safety-Focused Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Clinical Diagnostic Decision Support
outcome: Missed escalations and unnecessary escalations across 12 LLMs (TSR, SPR)
effect: GPT-5 Chat had the highest TSR (72.4%). Llama 4 Maverick had SPR 96.8%. Models with the highest SPR over-escalated, which lowered TSR, showing an inverse SPR-TSR relationship.
quote: Models with the highest SPR achieve it by systematically over-escalating, inflating safety scores at the cost of triage utility.

title: Where risk becomes visible: a layered fixed-policy framework for diabetic kidney disease screening in type 2 diabetes
outcome: Discrimination of models applied without retraining in external BioMe cohort versus All of Us development
effect: Discrimination was attenuated in BioMe (M4 AUROC 0.659) compared with All of Us (M1 0.673 to M5 0.797); predicted probabilities shifted systematically upward.
quote: In Bio  Me , discrimination was attenuated (M4 AUROC 0.659), but the relative ordering of information layers was fully preserved, and a systematic upward shift in predicted probability distributions underscored the need for recalibration before deployment in a new setting.
sample_unit: patients (All of Us development cohort; BioMe external validation N=9,818)

title: Where risk becomes visible: a layered fixed-policy framework for diabetic kidney disease screening in type 2 diabetes
outcome: Calibration of predicted probabilities when models applied to a new setting without retraining
effect: A systematic upward shift in predicted probability distributions in BioMe indicated the need for recalibration before deployment in a new setting.
quote: In Bio  Me , discrimination was attenuated (M4 AUROC 0.659), but the relative ordering of information layers was fully preserved, and a systematic upward shift in predicted probability distributions underscored the need for recalibration before deployment in a new setting.
sample_unit: patients (All of Us development cohort; BioMe external validation N=9,818)

title: Decision Curve Analysis for Evaluating Machine Learning Models for Next-Day Transfer Out of ICU
outcome: Net benefit of model-guided strategies across thresholds via decision curve analysis versus review-all, review-none, simple rule
effect: Across thresholds, model guided strategies outperformed review-all, review-none, and a simple clinical rule; feasible threshold 0.23 flagged ~23 charts/day, ~1.23 enrollments/day.
quote: Across thresholds, model guided strategies outperformed review-all, review-none, and a simple clinical rule.

title: Decision Curve Analysis for Evaluating Machine Learning Models for Next-Day Transfer Out of ICU
outcome: Threshold selection aligned with workflow capacity (8 hour daily review time constraint)
effect: At a feasible operating threshold (0.23), the model flagged ~23 charts/day and yielded ~1.23 enrollments/day under conservative eligibility and consent assumptions.
quote: At a feasible operating threshold (0.23), the model flagged ∼23 charts/day and yielded ∼1.23 enrollments/day under conservative eligibility and consent assumptions.

title: Decision Curve Analysis for Evaluating Machine Learning Models for Next-Day Transfer Out of ICU
outcome: decision utility versus baseline strategies
effect: Model guided strategies outperformed review-all, review-none, and a simple clinical rule across thresholds.
quote: Across thresholds, model guided strategies outperformed review-all, review-none, and a simple clinical rule.

title: Uncertainty-Gated Glaucoma Screening: Combining Semi-Supervised Classification with Multi-Agent Large Language Model Deliberation
outcome: Accuracy of multi-agent VLM versus classifier on same flagged cases
effect: Agent system 89.5% accuracy (111/124) and 100% sensitivity versus classifier 73.4% (91/124); agents fixed 32 errors, introduced 12 new errors, net +20.
quote: On these flagged cases, the agent system achieves 100% sensitivity—detecting all 55 glaucoma cases with zero missed diagnoses—and 89.5% overall accuracy (111/124), compared to the classifier’s 73.4% (91/124).
sample_unit: held-out test patients (OCT; 124 flagged cases routed to agents)

title: Ad-verse Effects:  Pharmaceutical Advertising Shifts Drug Recommendations by Consumer-Facing AI
outcome: Shift in drug recommendations and ad disclosure when pharmaceutical ads are embedded in LLM prompts
effect: Ads shifted selection of advertised drug by +12.7 pp when both drugs guideline-appropriate; models echoed ad claims at 2.7x baseline rate and rarely disclosed the ad.
quote: An open-response sub-analysis (2,340 calls across three representative models) confirmed that advertising restructures free-text clinical reasoning: models echoed ad claims at 2.7 times the baseline rate while maintaining high stated confidence and rarely disclosing the ad.

title: A Blinded Comparative Evaluation of Clinical and AI-Generated Responses to Otologic Patient Queries
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of LLM responses to otologic patient questions
effect: ChatGPT mean grade 7.25 (most readable); ClaudeAI 11.86 (more complex, p<.05). LLM readability rated higher than physicians (4.00 vs 3.73).
quote: By Flesch-Kincaid grade level, ChatGPT produced the most readable content (mean 7.25), while ClaudeAI responses were more complex (11.86; p < .05).

title: A case report on gendered biases in a Finnish healthcare AI assistant
outcome: Output differences across male, female, and gender-neutral variants of identical clinical queries
effect: Substantial, clinically significant differences across gendered variants, including differential treatment urgency, inappropriate symptom associations, and misidentified clinical context; female variants framed around childcare and reproductive health.
quote: We observed substantial and clinically significant differences across gendered variants, including differential treatment urgency, inappropriate symptom associations, and misidentification of clinical context.
sample_unit: clinical queries (each in three gendered variants)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Transparent Quality-of-Care Measurement in Children with ADHD
outcome: LLM accuracy at identifying PTBM recommendations in local EHR notes versus expert chart review
effect: Claude-3.5 sensitivity 0.89, PPV 0.95, F1 0.92; LLaMA3.3-70B sensitivity 0.91, PPV 0.89, F1 0.90; GPT-4o sensitivity 0.82, PPV 0.97, F1 0.89.
quote: All three models demonstrated high performance compared to expert chart review.
sample_unit: patients (first ADHD-related visit notes; 122 stratified notes manually annotated for performance)

title: Cross-Cohort Generalizability of Plasma Biomarker Machine Learning Models Reveals Calibration-Driven Degradation in Clinical Utility
outcome: Biomarker distribution differences between development and external cohorts indicating dataset shift
effect: Biomarker distribution differences across ADNI and A4 were consistent with dataset shift, and cross-cohort transfer degraded predictive values despite preserved discrimination.
quote: Biomarker distribution differences across cohorts were consistent with dataset shift.

title: Cross-Cohort Generalizability of Plasma Biomarker Machine Learning Models Reveals Calibration-Driven Degradation in Clinical Utility
outcome: Performance of externally trained models on another cohort without retraining (AUC, NPV)
effect: Cross-cohort AUC attenuated ~4-7%; NPV fell from 0.831 to 0.644 under ADNI→A4 transfer (~19 percentage points); calibration systematically misestimated probabilities.
quote: NPV declined from 0.831 to 0.644 under ADNI→A4 transfer (∼19 percentage points) despite preserved discrimination.

title: Cross-Cohort Generalizability of Plasma Biomarker Machine Learning Models Reveals Calibration-Driven Degradation in Clinical Utility
outcome: Predictive values and net benefit under cross-cohort transfer with differing prevalence
effect: NPV dropped ~19 points under transfer; decision curve analysis showed reduced net clinical benefit; prevalence differences critically affect NPV.
quote: Calibration instability and prevalence differences critically affect NPV, highlighting the need for cross-cohort validation, calibration assessment, and assay harmonization before clinical implementation.

title: Cross-Cohort Generalizability of Plasma Biomarker Machine Learning Models Reveals Calibration-Driven Degradation in Clinical Utility
outcome: Calibration of transferred models without local retraining
effect: Calibration analyses demonstrated systematic probability misestimation when models were transferred without retraining.
quote: Calibration analyses demonstrated systematic probability misestimation, and decision curve analysis showed reduced net clinical benefit.

title: AI Implementation in Safety Net Healthcare: Understanding Barriers and Strategies
outcome: Barriers to AI adoption in safety net organizations, including governance structures
effect: AI governance structures were among the key barriers reported by the five safety net organizations during Integration and Lifecycle Management phases. No numeric results reported.
quote: Key barriers emerged during the Integration and Lifecycle Management phases and included gaps in AI performance evaluation and impact assessments, communication with patients about AI use, foundational AI education, financial resources for purchasing and maintaining AI tools, and AI governance structures.

title: AI Implementation in Safety Net Healthcare: Understanding Barriers and Strategies
outcome: Gaps in foundational AI education among safety net organization staff
effect: Foundational AI education and lack of resources for staff training were identified as key barriers. No numeric results reported.
quote: Key barriers emerged during the Integration and Lifecycle Management phases and included gaps in AI performance evaluation and impact assessments, communication with patients about AI use, foundational AI education, financial resources for purchasing and maintaining AI tools, and AI governance structures.

title: AI Implementation in Safety Net Healthcare: Understanding Barriers and Strategies
outcome: Barriers in communicating with patients about AI use
effect: Limited guidance on communicating with patients about AI use was a key barrier for the safety net organizations. No numeric results reported.
quote: Key barriers emerged during the Integration and Lifecycle Management phases and included gaps in AI performance evaluation and impact assessments, communication with patients about AI use, foundational AI education, financial resources for purchasing and maintaining AI tools, and AI governance structures.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Population-Level Severe Tooth Loss Prediction: A Two-Axis External Validation
outcome: Model discrimination and calibration on temporally later and cross-domain external validation cohorts
effect: EBM AUC 0.8627, Brier 0.0845 on BRFSS 2024; calibrated AUC 0.7504, Brier 0.1358 on NHANES 2015-2018 (drop from derivation-era performance).
quote: The EBM achieved strong temporal stability on BRFSS 2024 (AUC: 0.8627; Brier Score: 0.0845).
sample_unit: survey respondents (BRFSS 2022 derivation; also BRFSS 2024 N=448,213, NHANES 2015-2018 N=10,775)

title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Population-Level Severe Tooth Loss Prediction: A Two-Axis External Validation
outcome: Intrinsic interpretability of model outputs
effect: Auditable shape functions revealed non-linear thresholds and pairwise interactions for age, smoking, income, and diabetes.
quote: Fully auditable shape functions explicitly revealed non-linear risk thresholds and synergistic pairwise interactions for key predictors including age, smoking, income, and diabetes.
sample_unit: survey respondents (BRFSS 2022 derivation; also BRFSS 2024 N=448,213, NHANES 2015-2018 N=10,775)

title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Population-Level Severe Tooth Loss Prediction: A Two-Axis External Validation
outcome: EBM versus black-box ensemble AUC
effect: Zero-shot EBM AUC: 0.7591 versus black-box stacked meta-ensemble AUC: 0.7706.
quote: Notably, the zero-shot EBM (AUC: 0.7591) closely matched the predictive ceiling of a black-box stacked meta-ensemble (AUC: 0.7706), eliminating the need for unstable post-hoc approximations.
sample_unit: survey respondents (BRFSS 2022 derivation; also BRFSS 2024 N=448,213, NHANES 2015-2018 N=10,775)

title: Reproducibility and Robustness of Large Language Models for Mobility Functional Status Extraction
outcome: Stability of LLM extraction across repeated runs and paraphrased prompts
effect: Increasing temperature generally degrades agreement; prompt paraphrasing can substantially reduce stability, with particularly large drops for the MoE model.
quote: Results show that increasing temperature generally degrades agreement, but the magnitude depends on model and task; furthermore, prompt paraphrasing can substantially reduce stability, with particularly large drops for the MoE model.

title: Citation Hallucination Determines Success: An Empirical Comparison of Six Medical AI Research Systems
outcome: Citation integrity and weighted total score before and after adding multi-agent citation verification and repair pipeline
effect: Citation integrity score rose from 40.0 to 90.9; weighted total rose from 68.9 to 81.8 for the best-performing system.
quote: Adding a multi-agent citation verification and repair pipeline to the best-performing system improved its citation integrity score from 40.0 to 90.9 and raised the weighted total from 68.9 to 81.8.
sample_unit: AI research systems (evaluated on 3 NHANES clinical epidemiology tasks)

title: Citation Hallucination Determines Success: An Empirical Comparison of Six Medical AI Research Systems
outcome: System ranking under programmatic citation verification versus single-model LLM-only evaluation
effect: Single-model evaluation ranked the best system last (55.5); three-tier framework with programmatic citation verification ranked it first (81.8), a complete reversal.
quote: Strikingly, a single-model evaluation ranked this system last (55.5), while our three-tier framework ranked it first (81.8) —a complete reversal that exposes the limitations of subjective LLM-only evaluation.
sample_unit: AI research systems (evaluated on 3 NHANES clinical epidemiology tasks)

title: Citation Hallucination Determines Success: An Empirical Comparison of Six Medical AI Research Systems
outcome: Citation hallucination rates in AI-generated research manuscripts across six systems
effect: Hallucination rates ranged from 2.9% to 36.8% across systems; hard-rule citation threshold capped four of six systems' total scores at the penalty ceiling.
quote: Hallucination rates ranged from 2.9% to 36.8% across systems, and a hard-rule threshold on per-task citation scores capped four of six systems’ total scores at the penalty ceiling.
sample_unit: AI research systems (evaluated on 3 NHANES clinical epidemiology tasks)

title: Evaluating the Large Language Model-Based Quality Assurance Tool for Auto-Contouring
outcome: Error-detection (sensitivity/specificity) of LLM-based QA screening of auto-contours against radiation oncologist ground truth
effect: Weighted kappa 0.730–0.798 across software; cutoff ≥4 gave highest sensitivity in rectum (0.976) and highest specificity in left femoral head (0.933); potential overestimation bias risks missing inadequate cases.
quote: A cutoff of ≥4 as “adequate “ narrowed the CIs, yielding the highest sensitivity in the rectum (0.976) and the highest specificity in the left femoral head (0.933).
sample_unit: male pelvic CT scans (auto-contours from three software packages; 291 rationale outputs rated)

title: Evaluating the Large Language Model-Based Quality Assurance Tool for Auto-Contouring
outcome: Agreement of automated AI-output quality checks with clinician ground-truth review
effect: The LLM QA tool showed moderate to strong agreement with expert judgments (ρ 0.733–0.794; quadratic weighted κ 0.730–0.798) across software.
quote: The LAQUA system demonstrated moderate to strong agreement with expert judgments across all evaluated software (ρ: 0.733–0.794; quadratic weighted κ: 0.730–0.798) and organs (ρ: 0.567–0.835; quadratic weighted κ: 0.639–0.804).
sample_unit: male pelvic CT scans (auto-contours from three software packages; 291 rationale outputs rated)

title: Evaluating the Large Language Model-Based Quality Assurance Tool for Auto-Contouring
outcome: Whether automated LLM checks detect inadequate AI auto-contours where human review is burdensome
effect: High sensitivity for detecting inadequate contours at cutoff ≥4 (rectum 0.976), though overestimation bias may miss some inadequate cases; suggests feasibility as primary screening.
quote: While potential overestimation bias (risk of missing “inadequate” cases) warrants caution, the observed sensitivity suggests its feasibility as a primary screening QA tool to efficiently filter acceptable contours, thereby reducing the clinical workload.
sample_unit: male pelvic CT scans (auto-contours from three software packages; 291 rationale outputs rated)

title: Measuring the Unmeasurable: A Diagnostic Sensor for AI Reasoning Pathology in Sequential Clinical Decision-Making
outcome: Diagnosis retention under staged versus complete information delivery
effect: Under unstructured sequential delivery, models accessed the correct diagnosis in 90% of cases but retained it in only 60%, a 30% Access-Stability Dissociation (Convergence Regression).
quote: Under unstructured sequential delivery, models access the correct diagnosis in 90% of cases but retain it in only 60%, creating a 30%  Access-Stability Dissociation invisible under single-shot evaluation.

title: Measuring the Unmeasurable: A Diagnostic Sensor for AI Reasoning Pathology in Sequential Clinical Decision-Making
outcome: Gap between vignette-benchmark performance and sequential clinical reasoning behavior
effect: LLMs perform well on complete-vignette benchmarks, but under sequential information delivery they abandon correct diagnoses; 90% access vs 60% retention, invisible under single-shot evaluation.
quote: Large Language Models achieve impressive accuracy on medical benchmarks that present clinical information as complete vignettes, but their behavior under sequential information delivery, the standard mode of real clinical practice, is poorly characterized.

title: Implementation of Human-in-the-Loop ChatGPT-based Patient Screening Across Multiple Diverse Clinical Trials
outcome: Criterion-level accuracy of deployed LLM outputs versus coordinator review
effect: Accuracy 0.94 (95% CI 0.92-0.96), sensitivity 0.98, specificity 0.81, PPV 0.95, NPV 0.93, F1 0.97 across 5,096 criteria reviewed by coordinators.
quote: Aggregated individual criterion-level performance: accuracy 0.94 (95% CI, 0.92–0.96), sensitivity 0.98 (0.97–0.99), specificity 0.81 (0.71–0.88), PPV 0.95 (0.92–0.97), NPV 0.93 (0.90–0.95), F1 0.97 (0.95–0.97).

title: Data Diversity vs. Model Complexity in the Prediction of Pediatric Bipolar Disorder: Evidence from Academic and Community Clinical Samples
outcome: Effect of recalibration on cross-dataset calibration and discrimination
effect: Recalibration prominently improved cross-dataset calibration without compromising discrimination, indicating transportability problems were largely driven by probability scaling.
quote: Recalibration prominently improved cross-dataset calibration without compromising discrimination, indicating that transportability problems were largely driven by probability scaling.

title: Data Diversity vs. Model Complexity in the Prediction of Pediatric Bipolar Disorder: Evidence from Academic and Community Clinical Samples
outcome: External discrimination in community dataset versus academic internal discrimination
effect: Good internal discrimination in the academic dataset; external discrimination in the community dataset substantially declined.
quote: In the baseline cross-dataset approach, all models showed good internal discrimination in the academic dataset; but external discrimination in the community dataset substantially declined.

title: Data Diversity vs. Model Complexity in the Prediction of Pediatric Bipolar Disorder: Evidence from Academic and Community Clinical Samples
outcome: external discrimination
effect: Academic N =550 and community N =511; all models had good internal discrimination, but community external discrimination substantially declined.
quote: In the baseline cross-dataset approach, all models showed good internal discrimination in the academic dataset; but external discrimination in the community dataset substantially declined.

title: Data Diversity vs. Model Complexity in the Prediction of Pediatric Bipolar Disorder: Evidence from Academic and Community Clinical Samples
outcome: Cross-setting generalizability under dataset shift and miscalibration
effect: Strong internal performance but limited cross-setting generalizability due to dataset shift and miscalibration.
quote: Predictive models for pediatric bipolar disorder showed strong internal performance but limited cross-setting generalizability due to dataset shift and miscalibration.

title: Data Diversity vs. Model Complexity in the Prediction of Pediatric Bipolar Disorder: Evidence from Academic and Community Clinical Samples
outcome: external performance by complexity
effect: Across N =550 academic and N =511 community samples, increasing model complexity did not improve external performance.
quote: Increasing model complexity did not improve external performance, whereas training on pooled data substantially improved both discrimination and calibration.

title: Data Diversity vs. Model Complexity in the Prediction of Pediatric Bipolar Disorder: Evidence from Academic and Community Clinical Samples
outcome: external performance by model complexity
effect: Increasing model complexity did not improve external performance compared to simpler models.
quote: Increasing model complexity did not improve external performance, whereas training on pooled data substantially improved both discrimination and calibration.

title: A Systematic Performance Evaluation of Three Large Language Models in Answering Questions on moderate Hyperthermia
outcome: Expert-rated quality and potential harmfulness of LLM answers to hyperthermia clinical and physics questions
effect: Mean quality 3.26 (DeepSeek), 3.18 (Llama), 3.07 (GPT-4o); potentially harmful in 17.8%, 19.3%, 15.3% of cases; ~25% rated bad to very bad.
quote: Notably, despite “acceptable” mean scores, approximately 25% of responses were rated “bad” to “very bad,” and potentially harmful answers occurred in ∼15–19% of evaluations, indicating a non-trivial risk if used without domain expertise.
sample_unit: expert quality evaluations of LLM responses

title: A Systematic Performance Evaluation of Three Large Language Models in Answering Questions on moderate Hyperthermia
outcome: LLM performance on specialized clinical domain questions despite general expert-level benchmark claims
effect: Despite expert-level performance in many medical domains, the three LLMs achieved only 'acceptable' mean quality (3.07-3.26) in moderate hyperthermia, with 15-19% potentially harmful answers.
quote: Our findings indicate that the performance of LLMs in HT in versions available at the time of investigation is only partially satisfactory.
sample_unit: expert quality evaluations of LLM responses

title: Medical errors in large language models revealed using 1,000 synthetic clinical transcripts
outcome: Triage safety for life- or sight-threatening emergencies in simulated headache consultations
effect: Models downgraded triage to self-management or routine follow-up in up to 54.8% of emergency cases (GPT-5-mini; 95% CI 40.5-69.0).
quote: For life- or sight-threatening emergencies, models inappropriately downgraded triage to self-management or routine follow-up in up to 54.8% cases (GPT-5-mini; 95% CIs: 40.5-69.0).

title: Medical errors in large language models revealed using 1,000 synthetic clinical transcripts
outcome: Model behavior with incomplete transcripts versus full histories
effect: GPT-5.2 had 97.5% diagnostic accuracy with full histories, but incomplete transcripts triggered hazardous recommendations, including discouraging 100% of lumbar punctures in subarachnoid haemorrhage cases.
quote: While GPT-5.2 achieved 97.5% diagnostic accuracy with full histories (95% confidence interval: 95.0-99.5), incomplete transcripts triggered hazardous recommendations.

title: Medical errors in large language models revealed using 1,000 synthetic clinical transcripts
outcome: Triage safety differences by patient sex across simulated demographic phenotypes
effect: GPT-5.2 triage was significantly less safe for females than males (odds ratio 3.2, 95% CI 1.4-7.1).

title: Pathology’s Last Exam: Stress-Testing Diagnostic Reasoning and Safety in Large Language Models

title: High Consistency, Limited Accuracy: Evaluating Large Language Models for Binary Medical Diagnosis
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of general-purpose LLMs on heart disease cases despite high exam scores

title: Impact of an AI medical scribe after 375 000 notes generated across care levels in a European health system
outcome: Documentation time per note and clinician stress after AI scribe deployment

title: Impact of an AI medical scribe after 375 000 notes generated across care levels in a European health system
outcome: Local ambient scribe assessment of usability, clinician well-being, and time savings
effect: Documentation time per note decreased 29%; stress-free work rose from 2.41 to 3.14; presence with patients rose from 3.73 to 4.33; median editing time 93 seconds.

title: Implementation of an Opioid Use Disorder (OUD) Machine-Learning Phenotype in Real-Time for the ADAPT Project
outcome: Local performance against clinician gold-standard reference at prespecified threshold

quote: In prospective gold-standard validation (n=218), the positive predictive value was 98.28%, and the negative predictive value was 95.68% at the prespecified threshold.

quote: Domain scores increased for Clinical Knowledge Application (2.87±1.20 to 3.70±1.03), Contextual Understanding (3.48±0.95 to 3.98±0.95), Hallucination Audit (3.90±1.32 to 4.74±0.76), Reasoning Transparency (3.45±1.02 to 3.86±0.87), and Chain-of-Thought Quality (3.32±1.04 to 3.69±1.00), all p≤0.001.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of a DenseNet-121 deep learning algorithm for chest radiograph triage in health assessment applicants: a prospective shadow-mode validation study in Nepal
outcome: Calibration of AI scores on local population (Brier score, ECE, score range)

quote: Brier score was 0.3621 (null Brier 0.0472) and ECE was 0.564, confirming calibration failure due to score compression (range 0.52–0.72) despite preserved discrimination.

title: Improving ART Retention Through Machine Learning–Guided Targeting of Interventions: A Monte Carlo Simulation Study in Lilongwe, Malawi
outcome: Twelve-month ART retention

quote: A combined intervention package produced substantially larger gains, increasing retention to 64.0% (RR = 1.45; p < 0.001), corresponding to an absolute improvement of 19.9 percentage points.

title: Improving ART Retention Through Machine Learning–Guided Targeting of Interventions: A Monte Carlo Simulation Study in Lilongwe, Malawi

effect: Newly initiated: 43.0% to 58.9%; clinically unstable: 28.3% to 39.1%; adolescents: 34.3% to 45.6%, a more modest effect.

title: Cardiovascular risk scores for primary prevention: head-to-head validation of 16 established and contemporary models
outcome: Calibration and net benefit of published CVD risk models applied to a different population
effect: Calibration varied substantially: PROCAM, Framingham, ASSIGN, QRISK1 overestimated risk; PREVENT, PREDICT, SCORE, SCORE2, SCORE2-OP, China-PAR generally underestimated. Ten-year AUC ranged 0.668 to 0.734.
quote: Direct application of cardiovascular risk scores across populations can produce clinically important differences in calibration and net benefit.

title: Cardiovascular risk scores for primary prevention: head-to-head validation of 16 established and contemporary models
outcome: Whether discrimination alone reflects calibration and clinical utility of risk models
effect: AUC ranged 0.668 to 0.734 while calibration varied substantially and net benefit diverged at higher treatment thresholds; QRISK2 had best calibration, PREVENT lowest Brier score.
quote: Model selection for primary prevention should require external validation, local recalibration, and assessment of clinical utility, rather than reliance on discrimination alone.

title: Cardiovascular risk scores for primary prevention: head-to-head validation of 16 established and contemporary models
outcome: Head-to-head comparison of 16 candidate risk models on the same cohort data
effect: Models differed markedly in calibration and net benefit; composite assessment favored PREVENT, QRISK2, PREDICT, PCE, and northern China-PAR variants.
quote: Composite assessment favored PREVENT, QRISK2, PREDICT, PCE, and northern China-PAR variants.

title: Benchmarking large language models for ACMG/AMP variant interpretation and variant calling

title: Evaluation of Large Language Models for Post-Cystectomy Sexual Health Counseling in Women

title: From Offline Accuracy to Deployed Performance: A Four-Phase Evaluation of an Edge-Hosted Wearable Stress-Monitoring Platform
outcome: Stress recall under progressive sensor/feature-modality loss

quote: Phase 2 showed graceful degradation under progressive sensor loss on 475 real WESAD stress windows, with stress recall declining from 99.58% (95% Wilson CI: [98.48%, 99.88%]) on pristine inputs to 95.79% ([93.59%, 97.26%]) only after simultaneous removal of three of five feature modalities.

title: From Offline Accuracy to Deployed Performance: A Four-Phase Evaluation of an Edge-Hosted Wearable Stress-Monitoring Platform
outcome: Serving-layer completion rate under 50-worker burst load

effect: Mean FRES was 38.92 ± 9.26 for Gemini-3.5 Flash (highest) and 25.33 ± 11.67 for DeepSeek-V4 (lowest). Both are in the difficult-to-read range, so no chatbot produced plain-language answers.
quote: For readability, Gemini-3.5 Flash (38.92 ± 9.26 ) obtained the highest FRES score, while DeepSeek-V4 (25.33 ± 11.67) showed the lowest readability.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Reducing Hallucinations in Drug-Related Question Answering Systems
outcome: Hallucination rate, faithfulness and factual accuracy with vs without retrieval grounding
effect: RAG reduced hallucination rate from 47.8% to 12.3% (74.3% relative reduction); Faithfulness 0.52 to 0.87; Factual Accuracy 0.54 to 0.89.
quote: Evaluated on a purpose-built dataset of 150 drug-related question–answer pairs spanning ten commonly used medications and multiple information categories, our RAG system reduces the hallucination rate from 47.8% to 12.3% — a 74.3% relative reduction — while improving Faithfulness from 0.52 to 0.87 and Factual Accuracy from 0.54 to 0.89.

title: Astra: a generalizable report generation foundation model for 3D computed tomography

quote: Deployed at external clinical sites without any site-specific fine-tuning, Astra accelerated chest report drafting by 29.6% and improved abdominal report completeness by 11.3% among junior and mid-level radiologists (P<0.001).
country: multiple (five sites worldwide; countries not specified)

outcome: Undertriage rate of emergency scenarios against Manchester Triage System priority levels

quote: GPT-5.1 undertriaged 44.2% of prompts (69/156; 95% CI 36.7 to 52.1), including 75.0% of Red-priority and 73.4% of Orange-priority prompts.
sample_unit: prompts per system (39 cases x 4 permutations x with/without anchoring statement)

title: MTS-Bench: A Manchester Triage System Benchmark for Language Model Triage Safety
outcome: Undertriage of Red-priority prompts when a misleading GP referral anchoring statement was prepended

sample_unit: prompts per system (39 cases x 4 permutations x with/without anchoring statement)

title: MTS-Bench: A Manchester Triage System Benchmark for Language Model Triage Safety
outcome: Undertriage rate of retrieval-grounded agentic system versus general-purpose LLM

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of a locally deployed Large Language Model Algorithm for Automated Code Stroke Pathway Identification in Emergency Department Triage Notes

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of a locally deployed Large Language Model Algorithm for Automated Code Stroke Pathway Identification in Emergency Department Triage Notes
outcome: Head-to-head accuracy comparison of six candidate LLMs on the same data
effect: Qwen 2.5 14B superior to Llama 3.1 8B, Phi-4 14B, Mistral 3 14B (all p<0.001 after Holm); no significant difference vs Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2 or Qwen 3 14B.
quote: Pairwise McNemar testing demonstrated statistically superior overall accuracy for Qwen 2.5 14B over Llama 3.1 8B, Phi-4 14B, and Mistral 3 14B (all p<0.001 after Holm correction), with no significant difference detected versus Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2 or Qwen 3 14B.

title: Towards Accessible Radiological Image Analysis via Local Agentic Framework: Validation in Mammography

title: The Illusion of Understanding: A Randomized Controlled Trial of LLM-Generated Lay Summaries of Brain MRI Reports
outcome: Objective patient comprehension of brain MRI reports with vs without LLM lay summary

quote: Objective comprehension did not differ between arms (58.3% vs 59.4%; odds ratio (OR) 0.97; 95% CI: 0.90–1.06; P = .54).

outcome: Effect of AI lay summaries on patient comprehension, satisfaction, anxiety in randomized trial
effect: No improvement in objective comprehension (OR 0.97); improved satisfaction (64.9% vs 36.7%) and subjective comprehension (50.3% vs 24.0%); anxiety modestly reduced (25.1% vs 26.6%).
quote: LLM-generated lay summaries appended to brain MRI reports improved patient satisfaction and subjective comprehension but did not improve objective comprehension, indicating a gap between perceived and actual understanding that should be addressed before clinical integration.

title: The Illusion of Understanding: A Randomized Controlled Trial of LLM-Generated Lay Summaries of Brain MRI Reports
outcome: Gap between perceived and actual understanding of AI-generated outputs among patients
effect: Subjective comprehension rose (50.3% vs 24.0%; OR 3.17) while objective comprehension did not change (58.3% vs 59.4%); normal reports had reduced comprehension (72.5% vs 76.6%).
quote: LLM-generated lay summaries appended to brain MRI reports improved patient satisfaction and subjective comprehension but did not improve objective comprehension, indicating a gap between perceived and actual understanding that should be addressed before clinical integration.

quote: LLM-generated lay summaries appended to brain MRI reports improved patient satisfaction and subjective comprehension but did not improve objective comprehension, indicating a gap between perceived and actual understanding that should be addressed before clinical integration.

title: The Illusion of Understanding: A Randomized Controlled Trial of LLM-Generated Lay Summaries of Brain MRI Reports

title: Deployment protocol and base model jointly determine residual risk in rule-based clinical LLM supervision

title: Deployment protocol and base model jointly determine residual risk in rule-based clinical LLM supervision

title: Deployment protocol and base model jointly determine residual risk in rule-based clinical LLM supervision

quote: Calibration changed over time: calibration intercepts shifted downward from the internal holdout to the temporal cohort (XGBoost Δintercept − 0.866; LightGBM − 0.977), indicating increasing average overprediction under the offset-model definition of calibration-in-the-large, a directionally consistent shift seen across all three models (though with wide confidence intervals), while discrimination was largely preserved.

title: Explainable Machine Learning and Temporal Calibration Drift of a TyG- BMI-Based Model for Early Prediction of Gestational Diabetes Mellitus
outcome: comparative temporal AUC
effect: Temporal validation AUCs: XGBoost 0.881 (95% CI 0.819–0.933), LightGBM 0.870, logistic regression 0.857.
quote: In temporal validation, XGBoost showed the highest discrimination (AUC 0.881, 95% CI 0.819–0.933), followed by LightGBM (0.870) and logistic regression (0.857).

title: Rater choice determines measured fidelity: a multi-model evaluation of large language model raters for AI-generated plain-language biomedical summaries
outcome: Agreement among LLM raters using same rubric on summary error density
effect: Measured error density varied about 4-fold among raters, 0.150 to 0.557 errors per 100 words (Friedman p < 0.001); human check on ten articles agreed only with Claude Sonnet 4.6.
quote: Across the 784 ratings, the measured error density varied by about a factor of 4 among raters, ranging from 0.150 to 0.557 errors per 100 words (Friedman test, p < 0.001).

title: Rater choice determines measured fidelity: a multi-model evaluation of large language model raters for AI-generated plain-language biomedical summaries
outcome: Omission of source safety warnings in AI summaries as detected by different raters
effect: Of 28 sections with a source safety warning, warning missing in 22 per strictest rater vs 4 per most lenient; lenient raters identified only 3 and 2 of 9 safety omissions.
quote: Of the 28 sections that had a safety warning in their source, the warning was missing in 22 cases according to the strictest rater and in 4 cases according to the most lenient rater.

title: Intelligence Preserves The System It Assists
outcome: Clinician vs standard model vs augmented model accuracy in ICU pressure control, by departure regime
effect: In high-departure states augmented model 46.9% vs clinician 20.5% and standard model 19.6%; augmented minus clinician +26.3 points (95% CI 9.3-40.2). Weaker in stable states (25.6%).
quote: In ICU pressure control, the augmented model was weaker in stable states (25.6%) but strongest in departure states (46.9%), compared with the clinician (20.5%) and standard model (19.6%) in that regime; the high-departure advantage survived stay-level clustering (augmented minus clinician +26.3 points, 95% CI 9.3-40.2; augmented minus standard +27.2 points, 95% CI 12.4-41.1).
sample_unit: states/rows across five retrospective datasets (JIGSAWS, Cholec80, MIMIC-IV, LUMIERE, PhysioNet Sepsis)

title: Integrating Predictive Modeling into Viral Test Stewardship: HHV-7 as a Use Case
outcome: Model performance on a temporally later cohort versus the historical cohort
effect: Random Forest performed best in the historical cohort, but performance declined in the more recent cohort, revealing temporal dataset shift. No numbers in the abstract.
quote: When applied to a more recent cohort, however, model performance declined, revealing the presence of temporal dataset shift and underscoring the dynamic nature of real-world clinical data.

title: Integrating Predictive Modeling into Viral Test Stewardship: HHV-7 as a Use Case
outcome: Performance degradation of predictive model over time due to dataset shift
effect: Model performance declined when applied to a more recent cohort, showing temporal dataset shift. The authors stress continuous monitoring and recalibration before deployment.
quote: When applied to a more recent cohort, however, model performance declined, revealing the presence of temporal dataset shift and underscoring the dynamic nature of real-world clinical data.

title: Intent Drift in LLM-Assisted BCI Communication: An In-Silico Benchmark Under Simulated Decoder Corruption
outcome: Calibration of model confidence versus faithfulness of BCI text corrections
effect: Confidence discriminated correct from incorrect outputs (AUROC 0.83) but 28.4% of high-confidence outputs were not faithful.
quote: Model confidence distinguished correct from incorrect outputs reasonably well (AUROC 0.83) but overstated its own reliability: 28.4% of high-confidence outputs were not faithful.

title: Intent Drift in LLM-Assisted BCI Communication: An In-Silico Benchmark Under Simulated Decoder Corruption
outcome: Intent drift of LLM corrections as simulated decoder character error rate increased
effect: Drift rose from 2.2% at no error to 60.3% at the most severe level (OR 2.30 per 10-percentage-point increase).
quote: Drift rose steeply with decoder error, from 2.2% at no error to 60.3% at the most severe level tested (odds ratio 2.30 per 10-percentage-point increase)-a stress-test ceiling, not an expected real-world rate.

title: Intent Drift in LLM-Assisted BCI Communication: An In-Silico Benchmark Under Simulated Decoder Corruption
outcome: Faithfulness of LLM-corrected messages against reference intended messages
effect: Even the best correction strategy still produced a wrong message in 18 of 100 corrections; no strategy eliminated drift.
quote: No correction strategy eliminated drift: cautious approaches reduced it, permissive ones increased it, and even the best still produced a wrong message in 18 of 100 corrections.

title: Drivers of Oncologist Preference of AI-Generated Literature Review in a Randomized Mixed-Methods Study
outcome: Oncologist-rated utility and trust of AI literature reports under different report designs
effect: Evidence-graded report rated lower in overall utility than standard OpenEvidence despite similar references (mean difference -0.96; 95% CI -1.26 to -0.66; P<.001).
quote: Evidence presented differently can alter perceptions of clinical utility and trust; accuracy alone is insufficient, and report design must also be empirically evaluated.

title: Drivers of Oncologist Preference of AI-Generated Literature Review in a Randomized Mixed-Methods Study
outcome: Factors reducing clinician trust in AI-generated literature reports, including citation problems
effect: Qualitative analysis found trust deteriorated with citation mismatch, buried provenance, evidence misclassification, overconfident recommendations, and poor organization.
quote: Trust deteriorated with citation mismatch, buried provenance, evidence misclassification, overconfident recommendations, and poor organization.

title: Development and External Validation of a Treatment-Adjusted Machine Learning Model to Support Risk-Informed Group-Based Depression Care for People Living with HIV in Uganda
outcome: Effect of Platt recalibration on external-validation calibration and Brier score of the XGBoost model

quote: Following Platt-recalibration, XGBoost showed the best overall performance, preserving strong discrimination (AUC 0.940) while improving the Brier score from 0.174 to 0.113 and the calibration slope from 7.533 to 1.093.

title: Development and External Validation of a Treatment-Adjusted Machine Learning Model to Support Risk-Informed Group-Based Depression Care for People Living with HIV in Uganda
outcome: Calibration before Platt recalibration

title: Accuracy and error patterns of ChatGPT-4o for real-time English–Nepali voice translation: A cross-sectional field evaluation in rural Nepal
outcome: Translation accuracy of ChatGPT-4o for English-Nepali voice translation, by direction

quote: Mean accuracy was higher for English-to-Nepali than Nepali-to-English translation (2.63 ± 0.53 vs 2.23 ± 0.86); 63 of 69 low-accuracy translations (91.3%) occurred in the Nepali-to-English direction.

title: Adaptive forecasting of antiretroviral therapy demand using machine learning in India’s national HIV programme
outcome: Signed percentage deviation of foundation/hybrid models versus classical baselines across ART regimens

title: Adaptive forecasting of antiretroviral therapy demand using machine learning in India’s national HIV programme

quote: For pediatric ABC+3TC, all models over-predicted within a narrow band of [−82.74, −67.43], while for pediatric AZT+3TC and LPV/r 100/25, all models under-predicted, with ranges of [24.93, 63.73] and [18.32, 52.07], respectively.

title: RheumBench: A Specialist-Validated Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Rheumatology
outcome: Calibration of self-reported system confidence against diagnostic accuracy (Brier score)

title: Novel Entropy-Based Framework for Quantifying Dynamic Epistemic Uncertainty in Clinical Medicine
outcome: Whether entropy-based uncertainty visualization tracks LLM diagnostic reasoning uncertainty across rounds in pilot cases
effect: Unconfounded cerebellar infarction case showed monotonic entropy decay from 2.15 to 1.74; ambiguous pneumothorax case had sustained high entropy (~2.41); acute cholangitis showed top-1 rank stagnation. Pilot only, three cases, no clinician outcomes.
quote: Pilot validation across representative emergency medicine scenarios demonstrated distinct topological and information-theoretic behaviors: unconfounded cases (cerebellar infarction) exhibited smooth geodesic progression toward the ground truth alongside monotonic Shannon entropy decay from 2.15 to 1.74; noisy environments with ambiguous findings (spontaneous pneumothorax) suffered from trajectory wandering, local minimum traps, and high sustained entropy (~2.41) due to insufficient repulsive weighting for negative evidence; and triage-conflicted cases (acute cholangitis) achieved precise geometric proximity to the true node but experienced top-1 rank stagnation because the model conflated acute severity triage (sepsis) with anatomical etiology.

title: Half of alcohol, drug, and self-harm presentations cannot be identified in coded emergency department data: a diagnostic accuracy study of a large language model

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Community Eye Screening in Primary Healthcare: A Prospective Multicentre Diagnostic Accuracy and Implementation Study

outcome: Image-interpretation accuracy of structured versus zero-shot prompt architectures

outcome: Reproducibility of AI outputs over five repeated runs under zero-shot vs few-shot prompting

quote: However, reproducibility improved in several models, most notably Claude.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening Using Lumbar Spine Imaging: Diagnostic Performance, Reproducibility, Effects of Few-Shot Prompting, and Comparison with Physicians
outcome: combined specialist-AI screening sensitivity

outcome: radiographic diagnostic accuracy of AI models versus physicians

quote: Claude achieved the highest radiographic accuracy (73.3%), followed by Gemini (64.4%), specialists (57.4%), ChatGPT (55.6%), and non-specialists (44.0%).

title: Missing Data Governance in Real-World Cardiovascular Risk Prediction: Effects on Machine Learning Performance and Interpretability
outcome: predictive performance with incomplete data

quote: Imputation and the hybrid strategy preserved predictive capability and stability, whereas deleting every incomplete record degraded performance markedly across all algorithms.

title: Missing Data Governance in Real-World Cardiovascular Risk Prediction: Effects on Machine Learning Performance and Interpretability
outcome: machine learning algorithm resilience to incomplete clinical data
effect: Boosting ensembles were most resilient to incomplete data, while instance-based and simple probabilistic methods were most adversely affected.
quote: Boosting ensembles were the most resilient to incomplete data, while instance based and simple probabilistic methods were the most adversely affected.

title: Comparing Deep Learning Models for Lung Nodule Detection on Photon-Counting CT Images in a Non-Screening Setting
outcome: Inter-model agreement and detection counts of four lung nodule models on local PCCT routine data
effect: Commercial CAD detected 7071 nodules, nnDetection 5254, TotalSegmentator 4264, RadYOLO 3122; about 1300 detected by all models; 15.4%-37.4% of detections matched no other model.
quote: Overall, the inter-model agreement was low, and the models produced substantially different candidate nodules.

title: Comparing Deep Learning Models for Lung Nodule Detection on Photon-Counting CT Images in a Non-Screening Setting
outcome: Sensitivity and false positives of models developed for conventional CT when applied to PCCT
effect: Sensitivity moderate, 0.71 (95% CI 0.64-0.77) to 0.83 (0.77-0.88); TotalSegmentator and RadYOLO had 0.85 false positives per scan (95% CI 0.70-1.02).
quote: The models showed moderate sensitivity (between 0.71, 95%-CI [0.64, 0.77], and 0.83, 95%-CI [0.77, 0.88]), and TotalSegmentator and RadYOLO produced few false positives per scan (both 0.85, 95%-CI [0.70, 1.02]).

title: Applying models of care for total hip and knee arthroplasty: External validation of a published predictive model to identify extended stay risk prior to lower-limb arthroplasty
outcome: performance after local adjustment
effect: Adjustment improved performance, but calibration remained poor at low and medium risk thresholds; net benefit was modest.
quote: Performance improved following adjustment of the model intercept and model coefficients, although the model remained poorly calibrated at low and medium risk threshold and net benefit of the adjusted model was modest.

title: Applying models of care for total hip and knee arthroplasty: External validation of a published predictive model to identify extended stay risk prior to lower-limb arthroplasty
outcome: local validation performance
effect: In 200 patients, the original model performed poorly and grossly overestimated length of stay.
quote: The original model performed poorly in the validation dataset, grossly overestimating length of stay.

title: Applying models of care for total hip and knee arthroplasty: External validation of a published predictive model to identify extended stay risk prior to lower-limb arthroplasty
outcome: Local validation of published length-of-stay model: discrimination and calibration on local data
effect: Original model performed poorly in local validation dataset, grossly overestimating length of stay; performance improved after intercept and coefficient adjustment but remained poorly calibrated at low and medium thresholds.
quote: The original model performed poorly in the validation dataset, grossly overestimating length of stay.

title: Experience and future perspective of artificial intelligence (AI) in postoperative gastric cancer treatment recommendation: a retrospective, observational, cross-validation study with multidisciplinary team board
outcome: Concordance of AI treatment recommendations with tumor board on local historical patients, by stage
effect: Overall concordance 86.96% (280/322); stage I 96.93%, stage II 88.89%, stage III 90.91%, stage IV 45.83%. Age, performance status and stage IV independently reduced concordance.
quote: The concordance rates for stages II and III were 88.89% and 90.91%, respectively, which were close to 90%; however, the concordance rate for stage IV was the lowest at 45.83%.

title: Performance drift is a major barrier to the safe use of machine learning in cardiac surgery
outcome: Temporal performance drift and dataset drift of cardiac surgery mortality prediction models
effect: Strong evidence of decrease in overall performance across all models (p < 0.0001); all models decreased in at least 3 of 5 metrics; sharp drift periods mirrored performance decreases.
quote: There was a strong evidence of decrease in overall performance across all models (p < 0.0001).

title: Performance drift is a major barrier to the safe use of machine learning in cardiac surgery
outcome: Loss of model accuracy over time relative to initial validation
effect: Performance of ML and ES II declined over time after temporal split; ML remained superior to ES II; regular assessment and modification suggested.
quote: ML performance decreases over time due to dataset drift, but remains superior to ES II.

title: Performance drift is a major barrier to the safe use of machine learning in cardiac surgery
outcome: comparative model performance
effect: Xgboost CEM 0.728 95CI: 0.728-0.729 and Random Forest CEM 0.727 95CI 0.727-0.728 were best overall.
quote: Xgboost (CEM 0.728 95CI: 0.728-0.729) and Random Forest (CEM 0.727 95CI 0.727-0.728) were the best overall performing models both temporally and non-temporally.

title: The Diagnostic and Triage Accuracy of the GPT-3 Artificial Intelligence Model
outcome: Correct triage of case vignettes including emergencies by GPT-3 versus physicians and lay people
effect: GPT-3 triaged 71% correct (95% CI, 57% to 82%), similar to lay individuals (74%) and significantly worse than physicians (91%; p<0.001).
quote: GPT-3 triaged (71% correct; 95% CI, 57% to 82%) similarly to lay individuals (74%; 95% CI, 73% to 75%; p=0.73); both were significantly worse than physicians (91%; 95% CI, 89% to 93%; p<0.001).

title: The Diagnostic and Triage Accuracy of the GPT-3 Artificial Intelligence Model
outcome: GPT-3 diagnostic and triage accuracy compared with physicians and lay adults on the same vignettes
effect: Top-3 diagnosis: GPT-3 88% vs lay 54% (p<0.001) and physicians 96% (p=0.0354). Triage: GPT-3 71% vs lay 74% (p=0.73) and physicians 91% (p<0.001).
quote: Among all cases, GPT-3 replied with the correct diagnosis in its top 3 for 88% (95% CI, 75% to 94%) of cases, compared to 54% (95% CI, 53% to 55%) for lay individuals (p<0.001) and 96% (95% CI, 94% to 97%) for physicians (p=0.0354).

title: ChatGPT for Clinical Vignette Generation, Revision, and Evaluation
outcome: Triage recommendation accuracy on 45 standardized vignettes
effect: Triage accuracy was 57.8% (95% CI, 42.9% to 72.7%); first-pass diagnostic accuracy was 75.6% (95% CI, 62.6% to 88.5%).
quote: When presented with 45 vignettes, ChatGPT identified illnesses with 75.6% (95% CI, 62.6% to 88.5%) first-pass diagnostic accuracy and 57.8% (95% CI, 42.9% to 72.7%) triage accuracy.

title: A machine-learning based model for automated recommendation of individualized treatment of rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis
outcome: Physician acceptance of AI treatment recommendations in routine care, and reasons for rejection
effect: Physicians rejected the treatment recommendation in 7 of 15 routine-care cases because it deviated from national TB treatment guidelines.
quote: In routine care setting, physicians rejected the treatment recommendation in 7 out of 15 cases because it deviated from the national TB treatment guidelines.
sample_unit: patient cases (20 in clinical trial, 15 in routine care)

title: Application of simultaneous uncertainty quantification for image segmentation with probabilistic deep learning: Performance benchmarking of oropharyngeal cancer target delineation as a use-case
outcome: Segmentation DSC improvement and fraction of patients referred when high-uncertainty cases were deferred
effect: Referring patients above uncertainty thresholds improved DSC by 4.7% (MC Dropout Ensemble) and 5.0% (Deep Ensemble) while referring 21.8% and 22% of patients.
quote: With referring patients based on uncertainty thresholds from 0.85 validation DSC for all uncertainty measures, on average the DSC improved from the full dataset by 4.7% and 5.0% while referring 21.8% and 22% patients for MC Dropout Ensemble and Deep Ensemble, respectively.
sample_unit: patients (PET/CT scans, external validation set; 224 for development)

title: A hybrid approach to scalable real-world data curation by machine learning and human experts
outcome: error rates and manual abstraction burden
effect: Hybrid curation achieved expert-level error rates with only small amounts of manual abstraction.
quote: Only small amounts of manual abstraction are required for hybrid curation to achieve expert-level error rates.

title: Using an Artificial Intelligence Application Expedited ENRICH Trial Patient Screening: A Single Center Experience
outcome: Time from CT Head to neurosurgical-team notification for trial screening
effect: Immediate smartphone notification reduced notification time by 50 minutes (p<0.002), increasing to 57 minutes when hemorrhages not identified by the ICH algorithm were excluded.
quote: Time between CT Head and notification of the neurosurgical team for trial screening was reduced by 50 minutes after the implementation of VizAI (p<0.002).

title: Using an Artificial Intelligence Application Expedited ENRICH Trial Patient Screening: A Single Center Experience
outcome: time between CT head and team notification
effect: Time between CT Head and notification of the neurosurgical team was reduced by 50 minutes after VizAI implementation (p<0.002).
quote: Time between CT Head and notification of the neurosurgical team for trial screening was reduced by 50 minutes after the implementation of VizAI (p<0.002).

title: Bias Amplification in Intersectional Subpopulations for Clinical Phenotyping by Large Language Models
outcome: Underdiagnosis rates of language models across intersectional age-sex subgroups for smoking and obesity phenotyping
effect: Models selectively and consistently underdiagnosed vulnerable intersectional subpopulations, such as young-aged-males for smoking and middle-aged-females for obesity.
quote: Our results demonstrate that state-of-the-art language models selectively and consistently underdiagnosed vulnerable intersectional subpopulations such as young-aged-males for smoking and middle-aged-females for obesity.

title: The impact on clinical outcomes after one year of implementation of an artificial intelligence solution for the detection of intracranial hemorrhage
outcome: 30- and 120-day all-cause mortality and discharge mRS before vs after AI triage implementation
effect: 30-day mortality 27.7% vs 17.5% (p=0.004); 120-day mortality 31.8% vs 21.7% (p=0.017); mRS at discharge 3.2 vs 2.8 (p=0.044), Pre-AI vs Post-AI.
quote: The 30- and 120-day all-cause mortality weresignificantly reduced in the Post-AI group when compared to the Pre-AI group (27.7% vs 17.5%; p =0.004 and 31.8% vs 21.7%; p =0.017 respectively).
sample_unit: patients with intracranial hemorrhage (289 Pre-AI, 298 Post-AI)

title: Diagnosing and remediating harmful data shifts for the responsible deployment of clinical AI models
outcome: Model performance across subgroups of diagnosis, sex and age
effect: Model performance differed across subgroups of clinical diagnoses, sex and age.
quote: We found model performance to differ across subgroups of clinical diagnoses, sex and age.
sample_unit: patients admitted to general internal medicine

title: Diagnosing and remediating harmful data shifts for the responsible deployment of clinical AI models
outcome: Performance of hospital type-specific transfer learning models versus models using all hospitals
effect: Hospital type-specific models using transfer learning performed better than models using all available hospitals.
quote: We found hospital type-specific models that leverage transfer learning, perform better than models that use all available hospitals.
sample_unit: patients admitted to general internal medicine

title: Diagnosing and remediating harmful data shifts for the responsible deployment of clinical AI models
outcome: Model deterioration from data shifts over time, including during COVID-19
effect: Monitoring of data shifts over time identified model deterioration during the COVID-19 pandemic.
quote: Furthermore, we monitored data shifts over time and identified model deterioration during the COVID-19 pandemic.
sample_unit: patients admitted to general internal medicine

title: Diagnosing and remediating harmful data shifts for the responsible deployment of clinical AI models
outcome: Model performance after continual learning to mitigate temporal data shifts
effect: Continual learning was used to mitigate data shifts over time and improve model performance; no numbers reported in abstract.
quote: We used continual learning, the process of learning from a continual stream of data in a sequential manner, to mitigate data shifts over time and improve model performance.
sample_unit: patients admitted to general internal medicine

title: Diagnosing and remediating harmful data shifts for the responsible deployment of clinical AI models
outcome: hospital-type data shift
effect: Community-trained models had harmful shifts on academic hospitals, whereas academic-trained models transferred well to community hospitals; no numeric effect reported.
quote: We found models trained on community hospitals experience harmful data shifts when evaluated on academic hospitals, whereas models trained on academic hospitals transfer well to the community hospitals.
sample_unit: patients admitted to general internal medicine

title: Diagnosing and remediating harmful data shifts for the responsible deployment of clinical AI models
outcome: Harmful data shifts when transferring models between community and academic hospitals
effect: Models trained on community hospitals experienced harmful data shifts on academic hospitals; models trained on academic hospitals transferred well to community hospitals.
quote: We found models trained on community hospitals experience harmful data shifts when evaluated on academic hospitals, whereas models trained on academic hospitals transfer well to the community hospitals.
sample_unit: patients admitted to general internal medicine

title: Image based prognosis in head and neck cancer using convolutional neural networks: a case study in reproducibility and optimization
outcome: Whether published CNN studies reported the details needed to reproduce results
effect: All three studies failed to report elements needed for reproduction, mainly image pre-processing steps and the random seed.
quote: All three studies failed to report elements required to reproduce their results thoroughly, mainly the image pre-processing steps and the random seed.

title: RoMIA: A Framework for Creating Robust Medical Imaging AI
outcome: Robust accuracy of chest radiograph classifiers on naturally and synthetically perturbed images (CheXphoto)
effect: Models produced by RoMIA show 3-5% improvement in robust accuracy on perturbed CheXphoto images, implying baseline models are brittle to input perturbations.
quote: Models produced by RoMIA show 3-5% improvement in robust accuracy, suggesting that the proposed methods can be a useful step towards enabling the adoption of ANNs in medical imaging applications.

title: Research Letter: Application of GPT-4 to select next-step antidepressant treatment in major depression
outcome: Inclusion of poor or contraindicated antidepressants among choices GPT-4 considered optimal or good
effect: Poor or contraindicated medications were included among optimal/good choices in 24/50 (48%) of vignettes; at least one optimal choice was included in 38/50 (76%), with 0/5 for 2 vignettes.
quote: At least one of the poor choice or contraindicated medications was included among the choices considered optimal or good in 24/50 (48%) of vignettes.

title: Research Letter: Application of GPT-4 to select next-step antidepressant treatment in major depression
outcome: Stability of GPT-4 antidepressant recommendations across 5 regenerations of each vignette
effect: Optimal choice included 5/5 times for 7 vignettes, 3/5 for 1, and 0/5 for 2, indicating mostly stable but inconsistent responses for some vignettes.
quote: At least one of the optimal medication choices was included among the best choices in 38/50 (76%) vignettes: 5/5 for 7 vignettes, 3/5 for 1, and 0/5 for 2.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT as an Adjunct for the Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making in Primary Breast Cancer Cases
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT therapy recommendations versus tumor board decisions for early breast cancer

quote: ChatGPT wrongly identified the patient with Her2 1+ and 2+ (FISH negative) as in need of therapy with trastuzumab and called endocrine therapy “hormonal treatment”.
sample_unit: patient cases (consecutive early breast cancer cases discussed at tumor board)

title: Evaluating ChatGPT as an Adjunct for the Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making in Primary Breast Cancer Cases
outcome: Real-case clinical competence of general ChatGPT in tumor board recommendations
effect: Despite ability to pass medical exams, ChatGPT could not provide specific therapy recommendations for primary breast cancer cases.
quote: ChatGPT has the potential to find its spot in clinical medicine, but the current version is not able to provide specific recommendations for the therapy of patients with primary breast cancer.
sample_unit: patient cases (consecutive early breast cancer cases discussed at tumor board)

title: Impact Of Explainable AI On Cognitive Load: Insights From An Empirical Study
outcome: Cognitive load, task performance, task time
