quote: We found that these explanation types strongly influence end-users' cognitive load, task performance, and task time.

title: Impact Of Explainable AI On Cognitive Load: Insights From An Empirical Study
outcome: cognitive load, task performance, and task time
effect: Explanation types strongly influenced prospective physicians' cognitive load, task performance, and task time, with local XAI explanation types ranking best on mental efficiency.
quote: We found that these explanation types strongly influence end-users' cognitive load, task performance, and task time.

title: Assessment of ChatGPT in the preclinical management of ophthalmological emergencies – an analysis of ten fictional case vignettes
outcome: Triage accuracy of ChatGPT on ophthalmological emergency vignettes
effect: Triage accuracy of 87.2%; overall potential to inflict harm to users/patients present in 32% of answers.
quote: We observed a triage accuracy of 87.2%.

title: Assessment of ChatGPT in the preclinical management of ophthalmological emergencies – an analysis of ten fictional case vignettes
outcome: Triage accuracy and harm potential in emergency vignette responses
effect: Triage accuracy 87.2%; potential to inflict harm present in 32% of answers.
quote: However, an overall potential to inflict harm to users/patients was present in 32% of answers.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Medical Evidence Summarization
outcome: Factual consistency of zero-shot LLM medical evidence summaries
effect: LLMs susceptible to generating factually inconsistent summaries; more error-prone over longer contexts; no numbers in abstract
quote: Our findings reveal that LLMs could be susceptible to generating factually inconsistent summaries and making overly convincing or uncertain statements, leading to potential harm due to misinformation.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Medical Evidence Summarization
outcome: Overly convincing or uncertain statements in LLM summaries of medical evidence
effect: LLMs made overly convincing or uncertain statements, potentially causing harm through misinformation; no numbers in abstract
quote: Our findings reveal that LLMs could be susceptible to generating factually inconsistent summaries and making overly convincing or uncertain statements, leading to potential harm due to misinformation.

title: Real-world post-deployment performance of a novel machine learning-based digital health technology for skin lesion assessment and suggestions for post-market surveillance
outcome: Real-world sensitivity and specificity versus pre-market performance and sensitivity targets
effect: Sensitivity 95.0-100.0% for melanoma and 96.0-100.0% for malignancy; benign specificity 40.7-49.4% (vA) and 70.1-73.4% (vB); 15.0-31.0% of cases eligible for discharge.
quote: We show DERM performance in-line with sensitivity targets and pre-marketing authorisation research, and it reduced the caseload for hospital specialists in two pathways.

title: Closing the accessibility gap to mental health treatment with a conversational AI-enabled self-referral tool
outcome: Change in referrals by demographic subgroup after chatbot self-referral introduction versus matched comparator services
effect: Total referrals rose 15% vs 6% in matched services; increases were larger for non-binary (235%), bisexual (30%), and ethnic minority (31%) individuals.
quote: Importantly, the tool was particularly effective for minority groups, which included non-binary (235% increase), bisexual (30% increase), and ethnic minority individuals (31% increase).

title: Almanac: Retrieval-Augmented Language Models for Clinical Medicine
outcome: Physician-rated factuality of retrieval-augmented LLM versus standard LLMs on clinical scenarios
effect: Significant increases in factuality (mean of 18% at p-value < 0.05) across all specialties, with improvements in completeness and safety.
quote: Performance on a novel dataset of clinical scenarios (n = 130) evaluated by a panel of 5 board-certified and resident physicians demonstrates significant increases in factuality (mean of 18% at p-value < 0.05) across all specialties, with improvements in completeness and safety.

title: Tissue contamination challenges the credibility of machine learning models in real world digital pathology
outcome: Model performance after digitally adding contaminant tissue patches to slides
effect: All four models degraded with contaminants. DA balanced accuracy fell from 0.74 to 0.69 with 1% prostate contaminant. GA mean absolute error rose from 1.626 to 2.371 weeks with 10% bladder. Prostate cancer models had false positives, up to a 97% false positive rate.
quote: Every model showed performance degradation in response to one or more tissue contaminants.

title: GPT-4 outperforms ChatGPT in answering non-English questions related to cirrhosis
outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to cirrhosis questions by patient language (English, Korean, Mandarin, Spanish)
effect: GPT-4 had significantly higher proportions of comprehensive and correct answers than ChatGPT in all four languages (p<0.05). ChatGPT produced erroneous non-English responses. The quality gap between English and non-English answers was smaller with GPT-4.
quote: GPT-4 showed a marked improvement in the proportion of comprehensive and correct answers compared to ChatGPT across all four languages (p<0.05).
sample_unit: questions (each translated into 3 languages, plus English)

title: Dynamic Updating of Clinical Survival Prediction Models in a Rapidly Changing Environment
outcome: model performance after dynamic updating
effect: Dynamic updating outperformed one-time discrete updating in simulations; Bayesian dynamic updating used previous updates and required less data than refitting.
quote: We found that a dynamic updating process outperformed one-time discrete updating in the simulations.

title: Scalable federated learning for emergency care using low cost microcomputing: Real-world, privacy preserving development and evaluation of a COVID-19 screening test in UK hospitals
outcome: Effect of site-personalisation (local tuning) of the global model on performance
effect: Site-personalisation gave no significant overall improvement (AUROC improvement <0.01), which the authors read as high generalisability of the global model.
quote: Site-personalisation of the global model did not give a significant improvement in overall performance (AUROC improvement <0.01), suggesting high generalisability.

title: Application of concept Drift Detection and Adaptive Framework for Non Linear Time Series Data from Cardiac Surgery
outcome: Model performance with versus without drift-adaptive framework for hospital and ICU stay prediction
effect: Models incorporating a drift adaptive framework outperformed models without one; ensemble achieved minimum MAE of 10.684 (hospital stay) and 2.827 (ICU stay).

title: ChatGPT in Occupational Medicine: A Comparative Study with Human Experts
outcome: completeness with legislative context

quote: Occupational physicians perform better than ChatGPT in generating accurate questions on a 5-point likert score, while ChatGPT with access to legislative context is comparable to professional doctors in providing complete answers.

title: ChatGPT in Occupational Medicine: A Comparative Study with Human Experts
outcome: performance versus professional doctors
effect: On a 5-point likert score, physicians performed better for accurate questions; ChatGPT with legislative context was comparable for complete answers.
quote: Occupational physicians perform better than ChatGPT in generating accurate questions on a 5-point likert score, while ChatGPT with access to legislative context is comparable to professional doctors in providing complete answers.

title: Large-language-model-based 10-year risk prediction of cardiovascular disease: insight from the UK biobank data
outcome: LLM risk prediction performance when input variables were omitted from the prompt
effect: With a few variables omitted, GPT-3.5 prediction performance was preserved, especially when physical measurement data were left out.
quote: The additional analysis of limited variables using GPT-3·5 indicated that ChatGPT’s prediction performance was preserved despite the omission of a few variables in the prompt, especially without physical measurement data

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4 in Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Board Examination using the CVSA Model
outcome: Consistency of answers across repeated regenerations of the same questions
effect: High concordance (92.06%) across three trials, with considerable consistency in regenerating answers.
quote: The model demonstrated high concordance (92.06%) and satisfactory validity.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4 in Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery Board Examination using the CVSA Model
outcome: Correctness and completeness of clinical knowledge in open-ended OHNS board questions
effect: Passing mark averaging 75% across three trials, but responses were often only partially correct, with hallucinations and self-conflicting answers observed.
quote: While demonstrating considerable consistency in regenerating answers, it often provided only partially correct responses.

title: Utilizing Large Language Models to Simplify Radiology Reports: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT3.5, ChatGPT4.0, Google Bard, and Microsoft Bing
outcome: Readability indices of radiology reports before versus after LLM simplification under three prompts
effect: All four LLMs significantly simplified 254 reports on four readability indices; performance varied by prompt and model, and ChatGPT models did best with added context such as a 7th grade target.
quote: All LLMs significantly simplified the reports, but performance varied based on the prompt used and the specific model.

title: Accuracy and generalizability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
outcome: Performance drop when transporting suicide prediction models to new datasets
effect: Transfer performance declined versus local: average AUC reduced by up to 7.7%, sensitivity by up to 16% and PPV by up to 2% at 90% specificity; sensitivity by up to 20% and PPV by up to 5% at 95% specificity.
quote: Significant and comparable decreases in the transfer performance compared to the local performance of all three ML models were observed, with the decline in performance reducing average AUC by up to 7.7%, reducing average sensitivity by up to 16%, and PPV by up to 2% at the 90% specificity level, and reducing sensitivity by up to 20% and PPV by up to 5% at the 95% specificity level.

title: Stacking multiple prediction models to optimise performance in local settings: exemplars in cardiometabolic disease
outcome: AUC of locally tuned stacked models versus de novo models across small local training sample sizes
effect: Stacked models needed roughly one-tenth of the training sample of de novo models. For CVD, stacked reached AUC 0.732 (0.728, 0.735) with 30 cases, versus 300 cases for de novo. The difference was smaller for CKD.
quote: We found that stacked models require roughly one-tenths of the training sample size compared to de novo derivation of a prediction model.
sample_unit: training cases (iterated 10 to 1000) drawn from UK Biobank

title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT in Healthcare: Non-English Clinical Environment for Retinal Vascular Disease Classification
outcome: ChatGPT diagnostic F1 on real clinical reports versus ophthalmologists and interns

quote: ChatGPT using English prompt for direct diagnosis achieved the best performance, with F1-score of 80.05%, which was inferior to ophthalmologists (89.35%) but close to ophthalmologist interns (82.69%).

title: Comparison of ChatGPT vs. Bard to Anesthesia-related Queries
outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot responses to pre-anesthesia patient queries

quote: ChatGPT responses were difficult to read (college level difficulty) while Bard responses were more conversational and about 8 th grade level from readability calculations.

title: Comparison of ChatGPT vs. Bard to Anesthesia-related Queries
outcome: Clinician-evaluated hallucination errors in chatbot responses to anesthesia queries
effect: No hallucination errors reported for ChatGPT; 30.3% error in Bard responses.

title: Geographical validation of the Smart Triage Model by age group

quote: After model revision for neonates, we achieved an AUROC of 0.83 (0.79-0.87) with 13% and 41% as the low- and high-risk thresholds, respectively.

title: Geographical validation of the Smart Triage Model by age group

effect: Aggregate under-5 AUROC 0.81 masked poor neonatal AUROC 0.62; sensitivity at low-risk threshold 0.85 vs 0.68
quote: Sensitivity at the low-risk thresholds (CI) were 0.85 (0.83-0.87) and 0.68 (0.58-0.76) for children under-5 and neonates, respectively.

title: Geographical validation of the Smart Triage Model by age group
outcome: Model performance in neonatal subgroup beyond original target population
effect: Neonates had poor discrimination (AUROC 0.62, 95% CI 0.55-0.70) and low-risk threshold sensitivity of 0.68 versus 0.85 for under-5
quote: However, a revised model is recommended for neonates due to their uniqueness in disease susceptibly, host response, and underlying physiological reserve.

title: Geographical validation of the Smart Triage Model by age group
outcome: External age-stratified discrimination
effect: External validation found under-5 AUROC 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.82) but neonate AUROC 0.62 (95% CI: 0.55-0.70).
quote: The model achieved good discrimination for children under-5 with AUROC of 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.82) but poor discrimination for neonates with AUROC of 0.62 (95% CI: 0.55-0.70).

title: Beyond the hype: large language models propagate race-based medicine
outcome: Race-based, inaccurate content in LLM responses to questions on race-based medicine misconceptions
effect: All four LLMs had examples of perpetuating race-based medicine in their responses to eight questions, each asked five times (40 responses per model).
quote: All models had examples of perpetuating race-based medicine in their responses.
sample_unit: LLM responses (8 questions x 5 repeats x 4 models)

title: Beyond the hype: large language models propagate race-based medicine
outcome: Consistency of LLM responses when the same question was asked repeatedly
effect: Models were not always consistent when the same question was asked five times; no numeric consistency rates given in the abstract.
quote: Models were not always consistent in their responses when asked the same question repeatedly.
sample_unit: LLM responses (8 questions x 5 repeats x 4 models)

title: Assessing GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 in Generating International Classification of Diseases Billing Codes
outcome: Exact-match accuracy of LLM-generated ICD billing codes against official codes
effect: ICD-9-CM exact match GPT-4 22%, GPT-3.5 10%; ICD-10-CM 13% and 10%; ICD-10-PCS 0% for both models. Incorrect codes often semantically similar but with hallucinated details.
quote: While the models appear to exhibit a general conceptual understanding of the codes and their descriptions, they have a propensity for hallucinating key details, suggesting underlying technological limitations of the base LLMs.
sample_unit: randomly selected ICD code descriptions (100 each from ICD-9-CM, ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS), each prompted to both models

title: “Assessing ChatGPT's Performance in Answering Cervical Cancer Screening Questions to ChatGPT-generated Clinical Vignettes: A Pilot Study”
outcome: Accuracy and validity of citations and source URLs provided by ChatGPT
effect: The model could not give accurate citations initially. It gave URLs on the fifth attempt, but most failed to open the relevant pages.
quote: When asked about citations to information sources, the model could not provide accurate citations initially and provided URL (Uniform Resource Locator) on the fifth attempt but most of them failed to open the relevant pages on their respective websites.
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated clinical vignettes with queries and answers

title: “Assessing ChatGPT's Performance in Answering Cervical Cancer Screening Questions to ChatGPT-generated Clinical Vignettes: A Pilot Study”
outcome: Accuracy of cervical cancer screening answers compared with current standard of care
effect: Of 5 vignettes, 1 answer was unsatisfactory, 2 were acceptable and 2 were satisfactory against the current standard of care.
quote: The answer was found to be unsatisfactory for one vignette, acceptable for two, and satisfactory for two when compared with the current standard of care.
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated clinical vignettes with queries and answers

title: Prioritizing Educational Initiatives on Emerging Technologies for Italian Pediatricians: bibliometric review and a survey
outcome: Pediatricians' knowledge, use, and projected use of AI and other technologies after education
effect: Projected increase in use through education programs: NLP +43.1%, AI +39.6%, virtual/mixed reality +38.1%; a significant gap between current and potential use.
quote: The greatest potential for increased use through education programs was projected for natural language processing (+43.1%), artificial intelligence (+39.6%), and virtual and mixed reality (+38.1%).

title: Coding Inequity: Assessing GPT-4’s Potential for Perpetuating Racial and Gender Biases in Healthcare
outcome: Change in GPT-4 diagnoses and plans when patient race/ethnicity/gender varied in standardized vignettes
effect: Differential diagnoses were more likely to include stereotyping diagnoses; plans showed significant association between demographics and recommendations for more expensive procedures and differences in patient perception.
quote: Assessment and plans created by the model showed significant association between demographic attributes and recommendations for more expensive procedures as well as differences in patient perception.
sample_unit: GPT-4 generated outputs (vignettes, differential diagnoses, treatment plans) across demographic variations

title: Coding Inequity: Assessing GPT-4’s Potential for Perpetuating Racial and Gender Biases in Healthcare
outcome: Stereotyping and demographic misrepresentation in GPT-4 generated clinical vignettes
effect: GPT-4 did not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently producing vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations, compared with true U.S. prevalence.
quote: We find that GPT-4 does not appropriately model the demographic diversity of medical conditions, consistently producing clinical vignettes that stereotype demographic presentations.
sample_unit: GPT-4 generated outputs (vignettes, differential diagnoses, treatment plans) across demographic variations

title: Evaluating Capabilities of Large Language Models: Performance of GPT4 on Surgical Knowledge Assessments
outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT answers on repeat query of surgical questions
effect: Upon repeat query, the answer selected varied for 36.4% of inaccurate questions; response accuracy changed for 6/16 questions.
quote: Upon repeat query, the answer selected by ChatGPT varied for 36.4% of inaccurate questions; the response accuracy changed for 6/16 questions.

title: Evaluating Capabilities of Large Language Models: Performance of GPT4 on Surgical Knowledge Assessments
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4 on surgical knowledge exam questions
effect: ChatGPT correctly answered 71% and 68% of multiple-choice SCORE and Data-B questions; errors included inaccurate information in complex (36.4%) and fact-based (25.0%) questions.
quote: ChatGPT correctly answered 71% and 68% of multiple-choice SCORE and Data-B questions, respectively.

title: A multidisciplinary assessment of ChatGPT’s knowledge of amyloidosis
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across repeated runs of the same amyloidosis questions
effect: GPT-3.5 scored reliably on more than 83.3% of responses; GPT-4 produced above 98.2% consistent answers.
quote: When assessing reproducibility, GPT-3.5 scored reliably on more than 83.3% of responses, while GPT-4 produced above 98.2% consistent answers.

title: Exploring the Pitfalls of Large Language Models: Inconsistency and Inaccuracy in Answering Pathology Board Examination-Style Questions
outcome: Test-retest consistency of LLM answers to same questions over two weeks
effect: ChatGPT consistency rate 85%; Google Bard 61% on test-retest over a two-week interval.
quote: ChatGPT showed a consistency rate of 85%, while Google Bard exhibited a consistency rate of 61%.

title: Evaluation of a Large Language Model to Identify Confidential Content in Adolescent Encounter Notes
outcome: Share of LLM-extracted confidential excerpts accurately derived from source note (no hallucination)
effect: Only 40 of 306 excerpts (13%) were accurately derived from the original note without hallucination; 22 (7%) represented the actual confidential content.
quote: Only 40 of the 306 manually reviewed excerpts (13%) were accurately derived from the original note (ie. contained no hallucinations), 22 (7%) of which represented the note’s actual confidential content.

title: A Machine Learning Model Integrated with the Clinical Workflow Detects Sepsis Early with High Sensitivity and Specificity
outcome: False positive rate of new sepsis model versus existing commercial model in same health system
effect: Post-deployment false positive rate 6% versus 30% for the commercial model; sensitivity 91% and specificity 94% after deployment.
quote: Notably, the post-deployment false positive rate of 6% represents a substantial reduction compared to the currently deployed commercial model in the same health system, which exhibits a false positive rate of 30%.

title: Revisiting prostate segmentation in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): On model transferability, degradation and PI-RADS adherence
outcome: Change in segmentation performance over time at the same institution after acquisition protocol change
effect: Whole gland DSC fell from 99.46±0.12% to 91.24±3.32% (P<.001); RVD changed from -0.006±0.127% to 8.10±8.16% (P<.001) after protocol change at INST1.
quote: The model presented a significant degradation for the whole gland (WG) in the presence of a change of acquisition protocol at INST1 (DSC:99.46±0.12% and 91.24±3.32%, P <.001; RVD:-0.006±0.127% and 8.10±8.16%, P <.001).
sample_unit: patient MRI sequences from five external institutions (plus 30 patients at INST1 post-deployment)

title: Revisiting prostate segmentation in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): On model transferability, degradation and PI-RADS adherence
outcome: Segmentation performance across external institutions with different scanners and PI-RADS adherence
effect: Higher performance in PI-RADS v2.1-adherent centers than non-adherent (DSC 86.24±9.67% vs 74.83±15.45%, P<.001; RVD -6.50±18.46% vs 1.64±29.12%, P=.003).
quote: The model had a significantly higher performance in centers adhering to PI-RADS v2.1 when compared to those that did not (DSC: 86.24±9.67% and 74.83±15.45%, P <.001; RVD: -6.50±18.46% and 1.64±29.12%, P =.003).
sample_unit: patient MRI sequences from five external institutions (plus 30 patients at INST1 post-deployment)

title: Performance of a large language model (ChatGPT-3.5) for Pooled Cohort Equation estimation of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT-derived PCE scores across repeated rounds of prompting
effect: ChatGPT-derived PCE scores were unstable between repeated rounds of prompting, suggesting lack of reproducibility. They were also poorly calibrated against true PCE scores, with underestimation of true risk.
quote: We found that ChatGPT-derived PCE scores, despite being moderately associated with the true PCE scores, displayed poor calibration with respect to true PCE scores, and exhibited instability between repeated rounds of prompting, suggesting lack of reproducibility.

title: Performance of a large language model (ChatGPT-3.5) for Pooled Cohort Equation estimation of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk
outcome: Sensitivity of ChatGPT PCE scores to sociodemographic contextual indicators in synthetic patient prompts
effect: ChatGPT-derived PCE scores appeared inappropriately sensitive to contextual indicators of the sociodemographic status of synthetic patients.
quote: Moreover, ChatGPT-derived PCE scores also appeared inappropriately sensitive to contextual indicators of the sociodemographic status of the synthetic patients in this study.

title: ChatGPT-CARE: a Superior Decision Support Tool Enhancing ChatGPT with Clinical Practice Guidelines
outcome: accuracy, hallucination, and clarity
effect: ChatGPT-CARE showed increased accuracy and clarity, with moderate hallucination, versus original ChatGPT.
quote: The results indicate that ChatGPT-CARE offers increased accuracy and clarity, with moderate hallucination, compared to the original ChatGPT.

title: The Impact of Physician Variation on the Training and Performance of Deep Learning Auto-Segmentation Models: the Development of Physician Inconsistency Metrics
outcome: Effect of inter-physician variation in reference segmentations on auto-segmentation model Dice performance
effect: Model trained on MD7 (highest edge roughness 0.106) had lower Dice than MD6 (58.5±15.8% vs 67.1±16.8%, p<0.001). Including MD7 data gave 7 cases with Dice ≤40% versus 4 without MD7.
quote: This study demonstrates that there is significant variation in style and quality in manual segmentations in clinical care, and that training AI auto-segmentation algorithms from real-world, clinical datasets may result in unexpectedly under-performing algorithms with the inclusion of outliers.

title: Assessing Racial and Ethnic Bias in Text Generation for Healthcare-Related Tasks by ChatGPT  1
outcome: Differences in ChatGPT output sentiment, subjectivity, and word frequency when only patient race/ethnicity or insurance was varied
effect: Mean polarity 0.14, 0.14, 0.15, 0.14 by race; subjectivity 0.46 for all; polarity and subjectivity differences not significant, but word frequency differed significantly by race and subjectivity by insurance type.
quote: The differences in polarity and subjectivity across races/ethnicities were not statistically significant.
sample_unit: deidentified EHR encounters (each run four times with race/ethnicity varied)

title: Reducing diagnostic delays in Acute Hepatic Porphyria using electronic health records data and machine learning: a multicenter development and validation study
outcome: Model performance on local historical data, plus prospective biochemical testing of flagged current patients
effect: Best referral models F-score 86-91%; diagnosis model F-score 92%. Of 372 flagged patients only 10 recruited for testing, all negative; post hoc, 71% of cases identified earlier, saving 1.2 years.
quote: However, we were only able to recruit 10 of these patients for biochemical testing, all of whom were negative.
sample_unit: patients tested for AHP in diagnosis cohort (72 cases, 347 negatives); referral cohort 100,596 patients

title: Application of MALDI-MS and Machine Learning to Detection of SARS-CoV-2 and non-SARS-CoV-2 Respiratory Infections
outcome: Accuracy of a published MALDI-MS/ML pipeline applied unchanged to local Kazakhstan samples
effect: Applied as is, SARS-CoV-2+ detection was 91.0%, but accuracy was low for NCARI (48.0%) and AC (67.0%) with the top random forest model.
quote: Applying the established MALDI-MS pipeline ”as is” resulted in a high detection rate for SARS-CoV-2+ samples (91.0%), but low accuracy for NCARI (48.0%) and AC (67.0%) by the top-performing random forest model.

title: Application of MALDI-MS and Machine Learning to Detection of SARS-CoV-2 and non-SARS-CoV-2 Respiratory Infections
outcome: Local accuracy after retraining ML models on combined South American and Kazakhstan data
effect: After retraining, SVM-RBF accuracy was 88.0%, 95.0% and 78% for Kazakhstan SARS-CoV-2+, NCARI and AC; SARS-CoV-2 vs. rest ROC AUC 0.983 [0.958, 0.987].
quote: After re-training of the ML algorithms on the SA-Kaz peak intensity matrix, the accuracy of detection by the top-performing Support Vector Machine with radial basis function kernel model was at 88.0, 95.0 and 78% for the Kazakhstan SARS-CoV-2+, NCARI, and AC subjects, respectively with a SARS-CoV-2 vs. rest ROC AUC of 0.983 [0.958, 0.987]; a high differentiation accuracy was maintained for the South American SARS-CoV-2 and NCARI.

title: Application of MALDI-MS and Machine Learning to Detection of SARS-CoV-2 and non-SARS-CoV-2 Respiratory Infections
outcome: Accuracy on external Kazakhstan samples
effect: As-is pipeline: SARS-CoV-2+ 91.0%, NCARI 48.0%, AC 67.0% by random forest.
quote: Applying the established MALDI-MS pipeline ”as is” resulted in a high detection rate for SARS-CoV-2+ samples (91.0%), but low accuracy for NCARI (48.0%) and AC (67.0%) by the top-performing random forest model.

title: Fact Check: Assessing the Response of ChatGPT to Alzheimer’s Disease Statements with Varying Degrees of Misinformation
outcome: Clinician-rated accuracy of ChatGPT explanations of Alzheimer's myths against expert judgment
effect: Mean (SD) clinician agreement score 1.0 (±0.3) across 20 myths; ChatGPT correctly identified all 20 myths as inaccurate; clinicians disagreed with explanations on 7 myths.
quote: While ChatGPT correctly identified that all the 20 myths were inaccurate, some clinicians disagreed with its explanations on 7 of the myths.
sample_unit: clinicians rating ChatGPT responses to 20 Alzheimer's disease myths

title: Accuracy and Consistency of Online Chat-based Artificial Intelligence Platforms in Answering Patients’ Questions About Heart Failure
outcome: Expert-graded adequacy of chatbot answers to heart failure questions, including contemporary recommendations
effect: ChatGPT appropriate in 27/30 (90%); Bard 23/30 (77%). Both had hallucinated facts and/or difficulty with more contemporary recommendations.
quote: Both platforms suffered from issues related to “hallucination” of facts and/or difficulty with more contemporary recommendations.

title: Accuracy and Consistency of Online Chat-based Artificial Intelligence Platforms in Answering Patients’ Questions About Heart Failure
outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT content across repeated runs of the same questions
effect: ChatGPT showed a high degree of consistency (93%); Bard provided similar content in its answers.
quote: ChatGPT provided mostly appropriate answers (27/30, 90%) and showed a high degree of consistency (93%).

title: Advancing Rheumatology Practice with AI Assistance: Evaluating ChatGPT's Performance in Real-world Cases
outcome: Correctness and completeness of ChatGPT differential diagnosis lists in rheumatology cases
effect: Correct diagnosis listed first in 65.6% of cases; differential diagnosis totally correct in 53.13% and totally complete in 62.50% of instances; no harmful or costly suggestions.
quote: ChatGPT was successful in 65.6% of the cases to suggest the correct diagnosis first in the list of differential diagnoses.

title: Disparities in seizure outcomes revealed by large language models
outcome: LLM classification accuracy and class balance across race, ethnicity, sex, income, and insurance subgroups
effect: No differences in accuracy, or positive or negative class balance of outcome classifications across demographic groups; no evidence of intrinsic bias.
quote: We found no differences in the accuracy, or positive or negative class balance of outcome classifications across demographic groups.

title: FFA-GPT: an Interactive Visual Question Answering System for Fundus Fluorescein Angiography
outcome: Ophthalmologist-rated accuracy, completeness, and harm of AI-generated answers to FFA questions
effect: 70.7% of answers error-free, 84.0% complete, 93.7% harmless; about 29% contained errors. 68.3% of reports high accuracy, 62.3% high completeness.
quote: In the manual QA evaluation, the consensus among the three ophthalmologists was that the majority of answers were characterized by high accuracy, completeness, and safety (70.7% as error-free, 84.0% as complete, and 93.7% as harmless).
sample_unit: participants (654,343 FFA images used for model development)

title: Assessing generalizability of an AI-based visual test for cervical cancer screening
outcome: Repeatability of predictions on repeat images from same patient under identical conditions
effect: Strong repeatability with MC dropout, carried over to external data even without retraining (95% limit of agreement range = 0.2-0.4).
quote: Our results indicate strong repeatability of our multiclass model utilizing Monte-Carlo (MC) dropout, which carries over well to “EXT” (95% limit of agreement range = 0.2 - 0.4) even in the absence of retraining, as well as strong classification performance of our model on “EXT” that is achieved with retraining (% extreme misclassifications = 4.0% for n = 26 “EXT” individuals added to “SEED” in a 2n normal : 2n indeterminate : n precancer+ ratio), and incremental improvement of performance following retraining with images from additional individuals.
sample_unit: women (EXT external cohort size not reported; SEED = 9,462 women, 17,013 images)
country: Multi-country (SEED dataset with geographic heterogeneity; specific countries not stated in text)

title: Assessing generalizability of an AI-based visual test for cervical cancer screening
outcome: Classification performance on external data after retraining with local samples
effect: Retraining with EXT images achieved strong performance (4.0% extreme misclassifications with n=26 EXT individuals added to SEED) with incremental improvement as more individuals were added.
quote: Our results indicate strong repeatability of our multiclass model utilizing Monte-Carlo (MC) dropout, which carries over well to “EXT” (95% limit of agreement range = 0.2 - 0.4) even in the absence of retraining, as well as strong classification performance of our model on “EXT” that is achieved with retraining (% extreme misclassifications = 4.0% for n = 26 “EXT” individuals added to “SEED” in a 2n normal : 2n indeterminate : n precancer+ ratio), and incremental improvement of performance following retraining with images from additional individuals.
sample_unit: women (EXT external cohort size not reported; SEED = 9,462 women, 17,013 images)
country: Multi-country (SEED dataset with geographic heterogeneity; specific countries not stated in text)

title: Assessing generalizability of an AI-based visual test for cervical cancer screening
outcome: Model performance variation across image capture device and geography
effect: Device-level heterogeneity affected model performance more than geography-level heterogeneity.
quote: We additionally find that device-level heterogeneity affects our model performance more than geography-level heterogeneity.
sample_unit: women (EXT external cohort size not reported; SEED = 9,462 women, 17,013 images)
country: Multi-country (SEED dataset with geographic heterogeneity; specific countries not stated in text)

title: Exploration of ChatGPT application in diabetes education: a multi-dataset, multi-reviewer study
outcome: Helpfulness and trustworthiness versus physicians
effect: ChatGPT lower than physicians: helpfulness 4.18 vs. 4.91, P <0.001; trustworthiness 4.80 vs. 5.20, P = 0.042.
quote: In the real-world dataset evaluation, ChatGPT responses received lower ratings compared to physicians’ responses (helpfulness: 4.18 vs. 4.91, P <0.001; trustworthiness: 4.80 vs. 5.20, P = 0.042).

title: Exploration of ChatGPT application in diabetes education: a multi-dataset, multi-reviewer study
outcome: Helpfulness and trustworthiness ratings of ChatGPT responses with crafted prompts versus physicians
effect: Ratings of ChatGPT responses with carefully crafted prompts were comparable to physicians, whereas uncrafted responses were rated lower (helpfulness: 4.18 vs. 4.91, P <0.001; trustworthiness: 4.80 vs. 5.20, P = 0.042).
quote: However, when carefully crafted prompts were utilized, the ratings of ChatGPT responses were comparable to those of physicians.

title: Assessment of Accuracy and Safety of LabTest Checker (LTC-AI)
outcome: Sensitivity of AI triage for emergency and urgent cases versus consultant gold standard
effect: 100% sensitivity for emergency safety and 92.3% sensitivity for urgent cases; 74.3% overall accuracy.
quote: The system achieved a 74.3% accuracy and 100% sensitivity for emergency safety and 92.3% sensitivity for urgent cases.

title: Evaluating the Human Safety Net: Observational study of Physician Responses to Unsafe AI Recommendations in high-fidelity Simulation
outcome: Whether intensivists detect and reject unsafe AI treatment recommendations in simulation
effect: Most clinicians promptly rejected unsafe AI recommendations, with many seeking senior assistance; a few accepted unsafe recommendations after nurse influence.
quote: Most clinicians promptly rejected unsafe AI recommendations, with many seeking senior assistance.

title: Evaluating the Human Safety Net: Observational study of Physician Responses to Unsafe AI Recommendations in high-fidelity Simulation
outcome: acceptance of unsafe AI recommendations
effect: A few physicians were influenced to accept unsafe AI recommendations.
quote: Additionally, we observed human-human interactions, where an experimenter played the role of a bedside nurse, influencing a few physicians to accept unsafe AI recommendations.

title: Evaluating the Human Safety Net: Observational study of Physician Responses to Unsafe AI Recommendations in high-fidelity Simulation
outcome: Rejection of unsafe AI recommendations by clinicians
effect: Most of 38 intensivists promptly rejected unsafe AI recommendations, with many seeking senior assistance.
quote: Most clinicians promptly rejected unsafe AI recommendations, with many seeking senior assistance.

title: Evaluating the use of GPT-3.5-turbo to provide clinical recommendations in the Emergency Department
outcome: Accuracy of GPT-3.5-turbo recommendations compared with a resident physician on the same ED visits
effect: GPT-3.5-turbo performed poorly compared to a resident physician, with accuracy scores 24% lower on average.
quote: We find that GPT-3.5-turbo performs poorly compared to a resident physician, with accuracy scores 24% lower on average.

title: AI facilitated sperm detection in azoospermic samples for use in ICSI
outcome: Embryologist sperm search time and sperm found with versus without AI aid on an ICSI microscope
effect: AI-aided embryologist took less time per droplet (98.90±3.19s vs 168.7±7.84s, P<0.0001) and found 1396 sperm vs 1274 without AI, no significant difference in sperm found.
quote: In cohort 2, the AI-aided embryologist took significantly less time per droplet (98.90±3.19s vs 168.7±7.84s, P<0.0001) and found 1396 sperm, while 1274 were found without AI, although no significant difference was observed.

title: AI facilitated sperm detection in azoospermic samples for use in ICSI
outcome: AI versus embryologist speed and accuracy identifying sperm in still images on same data
effect: AI was faster (0.019±0.30 x 10-5 s vs 36.10±1.18s per field, P<0.0001) and more accurate (91.95±0.81% vs 86.52±1.34%, P<0.001); AI found 611 of 688 sperm vs 560 by embryologist.
quote: In cohort 1, the AI model showed improvement in time-taken to identify all sperm per field of view (0.019±0.30 x 10 -5 s versus 36.10±1.18s, P<0.0001) and improved accuracy (91.95±0.81% vs 86.52±1.34%, P<0.001) compared to an embryologist.

title: Performance of Multimodal GPT-4V on USMLE with Image: Potential for Imaging Diagnostic Support with Explanations
outcome: GPT-4V accuracy on exam questions with images across USMLE, DRQCE, AMBOSS and subdomains
effect: Accuracy 86.2% USMLE, 73.1% DRQCE, 62.0% AMBOSS; subdomain accuracy varied from 100% (immunology, otolaryngology) to 25% (anatomy, emergency medicine).
quote: On the other hand, GPT-4V's performance varied across different medical subdomains, with the highest accuracy in immunology (100%) and otolaryngology (100%) and the lowest accuracy in anatomy (25%) and emergency medicine (25%).

title: Performance of Multimodal GPT-4V on USMLE with Image: Potential for Imaging Diagnostic Support with Explanations
outcome: Explanation errors when GPT-4V answered incorrectly (made-up text, inferencing errors, image misunderstanding)
effect: Among wrong answers, 18.2% had made-up text; 45.5% had inferencing errors; 76.3% had image misunderstandings.
quote: However, when GPT-4V answered incorrectly, the quality of generated explanation was poor: 18.2% wrong answers had made-up text; 45.5% had inferencing errors; and 76.3% had image misunderstandings.

title: Assessing Calibration and Bias of a Deployed Machine Learning Malnutrition Prediction Model within a Large Healthcare System
outcome: Calibration intercept and slope of deployed model by race and gender
effect: No significant calibration difference between White and Black patients; calibration intercept significantly differed between male and female patients, underestimating malnutrition in females.
quote: The calibration intercept was significantly different between male and female patients.

title: Assessing Calibration and Bias of a Deployed Machine Learning Malnutrition Prediction Model within a Large Healthcare System
outcome: Calibration drift of deployed model across years
effect: Both calibration intercepts and slopes statistically different between 2021 and 2022; overall intercept −1.25 (95% CI -1.28, -1.22), slope 1.55 (95% CI 1.51, 1.59).
quote: Both calibration intercepts and slopes were statistically different between 2021 and 2022.

title: Assessing Calibration and Bias of a Deployed Machine Learning Malnutrition Prediction Model within a Large Healthcare System
outcome: Calibration after recalibrating the deployed model
effect: Recalibration improved calibration across race, gender, and year.
quote: Recalibration improved calibration of the model across race, gender, and year.

title: Assessing Calibration and Bias of a Deployed Machine Learning Malnutrition Prediction Model within a Large Healthcare System
outcome: Subgroup miscalibration after recalibration mitigation
effect: Recalibration reduced miscalibration across all patient subgroups.
quote: Recalibration is effective at reducing miscalibration across all patient subgroups.

title: Assessing Calibration and Bias of a Deployed Machine Learning Malnutrition Prediction Model within a Large Healthcare System
outcome: Calibration differences across patient subgroups
effect: Calibration intercept differed significantly between male and female patients, with underestimation in females relative to males. Calibration was not significantly different between White and Black patients; numerical subgroup estimates were not reported.
quote: The calibration of MUST-Plus underestimates malnutrition in females compared to males, but demonstrates similar calibration slope, suggesting similar distributions of risk estimation.

title: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT’s Diagnostic Performance with Radiologists Using Real-World Radiology Reports of Brain Tumors
outcome: ChatGPT diagnostic accuracy when input reports came from neuroradiologists versus general radiologists
effect: Final diagnosis accuracy 82% (neuroradiologist reports) vs 52% (general radiologist reports), p=0.012; differential diagnosis accuracy stable at 96% vs 91%, p=0.33.
quote: ChatGPT’s final diagnostic accuracy using reports from neuroradiologists was higher at 82% (95% CI: 71, 89%), compared to 52% (95% CI: 33, 71%) using those from general radiologists with a p-value of 0.012.

title: Examining the Accuracy and Reproducibility of Responses to Nutrition Questions Related to Inflammatory Bowel Disease by Generative Pre-trained Transformer-4 (GPT-4)
outcome: Accuracy of GPT-4 nutrition answers graded by dietitians against current knowledge
effect: 73/88 (83.0%) correct, 61 (69.0%) comprehensive; 15/88 (17%) mixed with correct and incorrect/outdated data.
quote: 15/88 (17%) responses were graded as mixed with correct and incorrect/outdated data.

title: Examining the Accuracy and Reproducibility of Responses to Nutrition Questions Related to Inflammatory Bowel Disease by Generative Pre-trained Transformer-4 (GPT-4)
outcome: Reproducibility of GPT-4 responses when each question was entered twice
effect: Reproducible responses to 81/88 (92.0%) questions; 7 questions were not reproducible.
quote: The model provided reproducible responses to 81/88 (92.0%) questions.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT as an Agent for Providing Genetic Education
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT answers to genetic disorder questions, as rated by genetic experts
effect: ChatGPT answered 64.7% of the 68 genetic questions; limitations and inaccuracies noted, particularly in understanding human inheritance patterns.
quote: Here we show that ChatGPT answered 64.7% of the 68 genetic questions asked and was able to respond coherently to complex questions related to the three genes/conditions.

title: AI in Relationship Counselling: Evaluating ChatGPT’s Therapeutic Capabilities in Providing Relationship Advice
outcome: ChatGPT's assessment of risk during single-session relationship counselling
effect: Poor assessment of risk was identified as a limitation; no numeric results reported in the abstract.
quote: Limitations include a poor assessment of risk and reaching collaborative solutions with the participant.

title: External Validation of an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for the Analysis of Chest X-Rays in the Primary Care Setting
outcome: AI chest X-ray diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, specificity versus radiologist reference in local primary care
effect: Average accuracy 0.95 (95% CI 0.92; 0.98), sensitivity 0.48 (95% CI 0.30; 0.66), specificity 0.98 (95% CI 0.97; 0.99); lower sensitivity for mediastinum, vessels and bone conditions.
quote: Analysing the validity of the AI algorithm, the average accuracy was 0.95 (95% CI 0.92; 0.98), the sensitivity was 0.48 (95% CI 0.30; 0.66) and the specificity was 0.98 (95% CI 0.97; 0.99).

title: The use of a large language models to create plain language summaries of evidence reviews in healthcare: a feasibility study
outcome: Share of LLM-generated summaries meeting target 6th-8th grade reading level
effect: Five of 10 PLSs met the target 6th-8th grade reading level; the other five did not. Passive voice averaged 16%.
quote: Five PLSs met the target 6th-8th grade reading level.

title: ChatGPT Exhibits Gender and Racial Biases in Acute Coronary Syndrome Management
outcome: Guideline-concordant ACS management recommendations when varying patient gender and race in prompts
effect: Specifying patients as female, African American, or Hispanic decreased guideline-recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management; largest disparities in angiography/stress testing and high-intensity statins.
quote: We find that specifying patients as female, African American, or Hispanic resulted in a decrease in guideline recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management of ACS.

title: ChatGPT Exhibits Gender and Racial Biases in Acute Coronary Syndrome Management
outcome: biased clinical management recommendations
effect: Largest disparities were in coronary angiography or stress testing and high-intensity statin recommendations.
quote: Most notably, the largest disparities were seen in the recommendation of coronary angiography or stress testing for the diagnosis and further intervention of ACS and recommendation of high intensity statins.

title: ChatGPT Exhibits Gender and Racial Biases in Acute Coronary Syndrome Management
outcome: guideline-recommended ACS care
effect: Female, African American, or Hispanic patient specification decreased guideline-recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management of ACS.
quote: We find that specifying patients as female, African American, or Hispanic resulted in a decrease in guideline recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management of ACS.

title: ChatGPT Exhibits Gender and Racial Biases in Acute Coronary Syndrome Management
outcome: guideline-recommended ACS management
effect: Specifying patients as female, African American, or Hispanic decreased guideline-recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management.
quote: We find that specifying patients as female, African American, or Hispanic resulted in a decrease in guideline recommended medical management, diagnosis, and symptom management of ACS.

title: Artificial intelligence for personalized management of vestibular schwannoma: A clinical implementation study within a multidisciplinary decision making environment
outcome: Neuroradiologist preparation time and MDM discussion time with versus without AI-generated reports
effect: Preparation took 2m54s with AI reports vs 2m36s standard per case. Discussion was shorter with AI, 1m15s vs 1m21s per case.
quote: However, the computer-assisted simulated MDM (CAS-MDM) approach significantly improved MDM efficiency, with shorter discussion times per patient (1m 15s (± 0m and 28s) per case) compared to standard simulated MDM (SS-MDM) (1m 21s (± 0m and 44s) per case).

title: Spot the Difference: Can ChatGPT4-Vision Transform Radiology Artificial Intelligence?
outcome: Accuracy of GPT4V versus trained U-Net and ViT on MS progression detection
effect: Both U-Net and ViT had 94% accuracy while GPT4V had 85%; GPT4V gave overly cautious non-answers in 6 cases.
quote: Both U-Net and ViT had 94% accuracy while GPT4V had 85%.

title: Evaluating and mitigating unfairness in multimodal remote mental health assessments
outcome: Fairness (DPR, EOR, F1) of modality classifiers across race, gender, education, age subgroups
effect: Varying degrees of unfairness identified among modalities; no single modality consistently fairer across all demographic variables.
quote: Varying degrees of unfairness were identified among modalities, with no single modality consistently demonstrating better fairness across all demographic variables.

title: Evaluating and mitigating unfairness in multimodal remote mental health assessments
outcome: DPR, EOR, and F1 after mitigation
effect: Post-training mitigation improved DPR and EOR, but decreased F1 scores.
quote: Post-training mitigation effectively improved both DPR and EOR metrics at the expense of a decrease in F1 scores.

title: Large Language Models and Medical Knowledge Grounding for Diagnosis Prediction
outcome: Diagnosis prediction and rationale quality when LLMs are grounded in a medical knowledge graph via RAG
effect: Abstract reports no numeric results; it describes both challenges and opportunities in using external knowledge graph grounding for diagnosis prediction.
quote: Using real-world hospital datasets, our study serves to enrich the discourse on the role of medical KGs in grounding medical knowledge into LLMs, revealing both challenges and opportunities in harnessing external knowledge for explainable diagnostic pathway and the realization of AI-augmented diagnostic decision support systems.

title: ChatGPT Influence on Medical Decision-Making, Bias, and Equity: A Randomized Study of Clinicians Evaluating Clinical Vignettes
outcome: Whether AI-assisted decisions differed by patient race and gender in randomized vignettes
effect: Physician decision accuracy improved significantly with GPT-4 advice without introducing or exacerbating existing race or gender biases (abstract-level result; no numbers given in the text).
quote: Results showed that physicians are willing to change their initial clinical impressions given AI assistance, and that this led to a significant improvement in clinical decision-making accuracy in a chest pain evaluation scenario without introducing or exacerbating existing race or gender biases.

title: ChatGPT Influence on Medical Decision-Making, Bias, and Equity: A Randomized Study of Clinicians Evaluating Clinical Vignettes
outcome: Physician decision accuracy before versus after receiving ChatGPT+ advice on chest pain vignettes
effect: Pre-post comparison showed a significant improvement in clinical decision-making accuracy after AI assistance (no numeric estimates in the text).
quote: Results showed that physicians are willing to change their initial clinical impressions given AI assistance, and that this led to a significant improvement in clinical decision-making accuracy in a chest pain evaluation scenario without introducing or exacerbating existing race or gender biases.

title: Unveiling the Clinical Incapabilities: A Benchmarking Study of GPT-4V(ision) for Ophthalmic Multimodal Image Analysis
outcome: Repeatability of GPT-4V diagnoses across repeated runs on ocular images
effect: Overall repeatability of GPT-4V in diagnosing ocular images was 63.3% (38/60).
quote: The overall repeatability of GPT-4V in diagnosing ocular images was 63.3% (38/60).

title: Unveiling the Clinical Incapabilities: A Benchmarking Study of GPT-4V(ision) for Ophthalmic Multimodal Image Analysis
outcome: Accuracy, usability and safety of GPT-4V responses on ophthalmic clinical tasks
effect: Of 600 responses, 30.6% accurate, 21.5% highly usable, 55.6% no harm; diagnosis accuracy 16.1%, decision support 24.0%.
quote: Out of 600 responses, 30.6% were accurate, 21.5% were highly usable, and 55.6% were deemed as no harm.

title: GPT-4 and Neurologists in Screening for Mild Cognitive Impairment in the Elderly: A Comparative Analysis Study
outcome: MCI screening accuracy of GPT-4 versus three junior neurologists on same participant corpus
effect: GPT-4 accuracy 0.81 versus neurologists 0.41 to 0.49; GPT-4 discriminated MCI better, p < 0.001
quote: Results showed that the GPT-4 model had higher accuracy (0.81) compared to the neurologists (ranging from 0.41 to 0.49).

title: Applications of GPT-4 for Accurate Diagnosis of Retinal Diseases Through Optical coherence tomography Image Recognition
outcome: GPT-4 diagnostic accuracy on retinal OCT images versus retinal specialists
effect: GPT-4 diagnostic accuracy was consistently around 26% across four experiments, versus 93.75% for retinal disease specialists.
quote: In four distinct experiments, the diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4 was consistently around 26%, which showed a significant disparity compared to the diagnostic accuracy of retinal disease specialists (93.75%).

title: ChatGPT for automating lung cancer staging: feasibility study on open radiology report dataset
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT TNM staging from radiology reports against radiologist consensus
effect: Best accuracy was GPT-4 with TNM rule in the prompt: 52.2% (T), 78.9% (N), 86.7% (M); errors from numerical reasoning and anatomical or lexical knowledge gaps.
quote: The best accuracy scores were achieved by GPT-4 when it was presented with the TNM classification rule (52.2%, 78.9%, and 86.7% for the T, N, and M categories).
sample_unit: CT radiology reports (subset used for evaluation after prompt tuning)

title: Performance of ChatGPT-4 and Bard Chatbots in Responding to Common Patient Questions on Prostate Cancer 177Lu-PSMA-617 Therapy
outcome: Rate of incorrect, partially correct, or misleading chatbot answers to patient questions on 177Lu-PSMA-617 therapy
effect: Experts rated responses incorrect or partially correct at 16.6% for ChatGPT-4 and 29.1% for Bard. Bard's answers had significantly more misleading information than ChatGPT-4 (p=0.039).
quote: Experts categorized the AI-generated responses as incorrect or partially correct at a rate of 16.6% for ChatGPT-4 and 29.1% for Bard.
sample_unit: expert assessments per chatbot per domain (12 responses x 8 experts)

title: An artificial intelligence-based model to reduce the no-show rate in outpatient clinics of an academic hospital
outcome: No-show rate among highest-risk patients randomized to reminder calls versus no call
effect: Intervention group had a 26.2% reduction in no-shows, equal to a 14.3% decrease in overall no-shows.
quote: This reduction translates to a 14.3% decrease in the overall number of no-shows, demonstrating the efficacy of the reminder service.

title: Exploring Bias Assessment and Strong Calibration in AI-based Medical Risk Prediction Models
outcome: Model true positive rate differences across racial and gender subgroups
effect: Models had significantly different True Positive Rates across racial groups but not across gender groups; parity metrics and changepoint calibration testing showed disparities.
quote: Through a t-test and ANOVA test of model performance on different subgroups, we demonstrate that the models have significantly different True Positive Rates across racial groups, but not across gender groups.

title: Exploring Bias Assessment and Strong Calibration in AI-based Medical Risk Prediction Models
outcome: Effect of reweighting bias mitigation on subgroup disparity
effect: Reweighting reduced the disparity in model performance across subgroups; overall accuracy effect not reported in the abstract.
quote: When we employed the bias mitigation strategy of reweighting, however, the disparity was reduced.

title: Exploring Bias Assessment and Strong Calibration in AI-based Medical Risk Prediction Models
outcome: Calibration consistency across folds
effect: Brier scores differed across k-folds, indicating inconsistent calibration.
quote: Cross validation and the implementation of a paired t-test showed that Brier scores differed across k -folds, indicating inconsistencies in model calibration.

title: Perspectives of Medical Imaging Professionals about the Impact of AI on Swiss Radiographers
outcome: Perceived preparedness and availability of AI-specific training among imaging professionals
effect: 68.3% did not feel well trained/prepared to implement AI in practice; 87.6% noted non-availability of specific training; 93% said AI education should be in undergraduate programs.
quote: Participants (68.3%) did not feel well trained/prepared to implement AI in their practice, highlighting the non-availability of specific training (87.6%).

title: Perspectives of Medical Imaging Professionals about the Impact of AI on Swiss Radiographers
outcome: Confidence with AI terminology among participants using AI clinically
effect: AI used by 43% of participants in clinical practice, but 63.8% of them did not feel confident with AI terminology.
quote: AI is being used by 43% of participants in clinical practice, but 63.8% of them did not feel confident with AI terminology.

title: Data leakage in deep learning studies of translational EEG
outcome: Test accuracy under segment-based (leaky) versus subject-based holdout in EEG DNN classifiers
effect: In both the Alzheimer's and seizure datasets, performance on previously-unseen subjects was strongly overestimated with segment-based holdout compared with subject-based holdout; most surveyed translational DNN-EEG studies use segment-based holdout.
quote: In both datasets, we find that performance on previously-unseen subjects is strongly overestimated when models are trained using segment-based holdout.
sample_unit: datasets (two EEG datasets: Alzheimer's disease and epileptic seizures) plus literature survey

title: Brain-phenotype predictions can survive across diverse real-world data
outcome: Prediction performance when trained and tested across unharmonized external datasets versus within-dataset cross-validation
effect: Predictions generalized across three heterogeneous datasets; for HCPD and HBN the best predictions came from cross-dataset training and testing rather than within-dataset cross-validation.
quote: Notably, for the HCPD and HBN datasets, the best predictions were not from training and testing in the same dataset (i.e., cross-validation) but across datasets.
sample_unit: participants (youth neuroimaging datasets: PNC n=1291, HBN n=1110, HCPD n=428)

title: Clinical implementation and evaluation of deep learning-assisted automatic radiotherapy treatment planning for lung cancer
outcome: Overall plan quality (PQM) of DL-assisted automatic plans versus manual clinical plans on the same patients
effect: PQM 40.7 ± 13.1 manual vs 40.8 ± 13.5 automatic, equivalent quality; planning time 103.1 to 32.6 min (P<0.001); MUs 789.9 to 692.5 (P<0.001).
quote: The average PQM score was 40.7 ± 13.1 for manual plans and 40.8 ± 13.5 for automatic plans, and they had equivalent overall plan quality.

title: Clinical implementation and evaluation of deep learning-assisted automatic radiotherapy treatment planning for lung cancer
outcome: Expert clinician review of AI-generated plans for clinical acceptability
effect: Automatic plans clinically acceptable in 88% of reviews (176/200) by four expert reviewers; all accepted after fine tuning.
quote: In qualitative evaluation, automatic plans were deemed to be clinically acceptable for treatment in 88% of reviews (176/200), and all were accepted after fine tuning.

title: Evaluating and Mitigating Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Making
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy and adherence to diagnostic and treatment guidelines on real abdominal cases
effect: LLMs did not diagnose accurately across all pathologies, performed significantly worse than physicians on average, followed neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and could not interpret laboratory results.
quote: We show that current state-of-the-art LLMs do not accurately diagnose patients across all pathologies (performing significantly worse than physicians on average), follow neither diagnostic nor treatment guidelines, and cannot interpret laboratory results, thus posing a serious risk to the health of patients.

title: Evaluating and Mitigating Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Making
outcome: LLM instruction following and sensitivity to quantity and order of input information
effect: LLMs often failed to follow instructions and were sensitive to both the quantity and order of information, limiting workflow integration.
quote: Furthermore, we move beyond diagnostic accuracy and demonstrate that they cannot be easily integrated into existing workflows because they often fail to follow instructions and are sensitive to both the quantity and order of information.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT’s Accuracy in Providing Screening Mammography Recommendations among Older Women: Artificial Intelligence and Cancer Communication
outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT breast cancer screening answers for women 75+, graded by expert panel
effect: Appropriate for 11/17 questions (64%); 3 inappropriate (18%), 2 unreliable (12%), 1 no consensus (6%).
quote: The responses generated by ChatGPT were appropriate for 11/17 questions (64%).
sample_unit: questions (12 questions and 4 vignettes as reported; 17 graded)

title: Evaluating ChatGPT’s Accuracy in Providing Screening Mammography Recommendations among Older Women: Artificial Intelligence and Cancer Communication
outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT responses across three repeated runs of the same questions
effect: Two of 17 questions (12%) were graded unreliable because content was inconsistent across the three responses; 3 (18%) were inappropriate.
quote: Three questions were graded as inappropriate (18%) and 2 questions were graded as unreliable (12%).
sample_unit: questions (12 questions and 4 vignettes as reported; 17 graded)

title: Mitigating Machine Learning Bias Between High Income and Low-Middle Income Countries for Enhanced Model Fairness and Generalizability
outcome: Fairness between HIC and LMIC sites and diagnostic sensitivity after algorithmic bias mitigation
effect: Algorithmic-level bias mitigation significantly improved outcome fairness between HIC and LMIC sites while maintaining high diagnostic sensitivity (no numbers in abstract).
quote: Through a real-world COVID-19 screening case study, we demonstrate that implementing algorithmic-level bias mitigation methods significantly improves outcome fairness between HIC and LMIC sites while maintaining high diagnostic sensitivity.
sample_unit: hospital datasets (four UK hospitals, one Vietnamese hospital)

title: Mitigating Machine Learning Bias Between High Income and Low-Middle Income Countries for Enhanced Model Fairness and Generalizability
outcome: Performance divergence between HIC and LMIC settings under data imbalance
effect: Collaborative AI approaches led to divergent performance outcomes across HIC and LMIC settings, particularly with data imbalances (no numbers in abstract).
quote: In this study, we show that collaborative AI approaches can lead to divergent performance outcomes across HIC and LMIC settings, particularly in the presence of data imbalances.
sample_unit: hospital datasets (four UK hospitals, one Vietnamese hospital)

title: Conceptualizing bias in EHR data: A case study in performance disparities by demographic subgroups for a pediatric obesity incidence classifier
outcome: Model performance (AUC-ROC) across demographic subgroups including race and Medicaid enrollment
effect: Mean AUC-ROC 0.72-0.80 across classifiers; some bias found, with models performing better for African American and Medicaid-enrolled patients
quote: Some evidence of bias was identified, although this was through the models performing better for minority subgroups (African Americans and patients enrolled in Medicaid).}]}}]}}]}</br>

title: Prospective Clinical Evaluation of a Deep Learning Algorithm for Guided Point-of-Care Ultrasonography Screening of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms
outcome: Scan quality of DL-guided novice nurses versus physicians without DL guidance
effect: DL-guided novices achieved adequate scan quality in 87.5% (95% CI 82.7-92.3%) of patients, comparable to 91.3% (87.2-95.4%) for physicians (p=0.310).
quote: The DL-guided novices achieved adequate scan quality in 87.5% (95% CI: 82.7 - 92.3%) of patients, comparable to the 91.3% (95% CI: 87.2-95.4%) rate of physician scans (p=0.310).

title: Enhancing Precision in Rectal Cancer Radiotherapy: Localized Fine-Tuning of Deep-learning based Auto-segmentation (DLAS) Model for Clinical Target Volume and Organs-at-risk
outcome: CTV and OAR segmentation accuracy (DSC, 95HD, sensitivity, specificity) of locally fine-tuned vs vendor pretrained model
effect: LFT outperformed VPM for CTV in target volume, DSC, 95HD and specificity (p < 0.05); LFT significantly improved small intestine segmentation; both adequate for bladder and femoral heads.
quote: Localized fine-tuning significantly improved CTV delineation accuracy (p < 0.05) with LFT outperforming VPM in target volume, DSC, 95HD and specificity.

title: Enhancing Precision in Rectal Cancer Radiotherapy: Localized Fine-Tuning of Deep-learning based Auto-segmentation (DLAS) Model for Clinical Target Volume and Organs-at-risk
outcome: Performance degradation when models applied to data from a different CT simulator
effect: No performance degradation identified when LFT and VPM were applied to the GenEva dataset acquired on a different CT simulator.
quote: We did not identify performance degradation when LFT and VPM models were applied in the GenEva dataset.

title: Enhancing Precision in Rectal Cancer Radiotherapy: Localized Fine-Tuning of Deep-learning based Auto-segmentation (DLAS) Model for Clinical Target Volume and Organs-at-risk
outcome: LFT versus pretrained model accuracy
effect: LFT outperformed VPM for CTV target volume, DSC, 95HD and specificity; bladder and femoral heads were adequate for both.
quote: Both models exhibited adequate accuracy for bladder and femoral heads, and LFT demonstrated significant enhancement in segmenting the more complex small intestine.

title: Retrieval Augmented Generation Enabled Generative Pre-Trained Transformer 4 (GPT-4) Performance for Clinical Trial Screening
outcome: Accuracy, sensitivity, specificity of RECTIFIER versus study staff screening against expert clinician gold standard
effect: Eligibility sensitivity/specificity 92.3%/93.9% for RECTIFIER vs 90.1%/83.6% for study staff; symptomatic heart failure accuracy 97.9% vs 91.7%, MCC 0.924 vs 0.721.
quote: RECTIFIER performed better than study staff to determine the inclusion criteria of “symptomatic heart failure” with an accuracy of 97.9% vs 91.7% and an MCC of 0.924 vs 0.721, respectively.

title: Consensus, dissensus and synergy between clinicians and specialist foundation models in radiology report generation
outcome: Report quality when clinicians collaborate with AI versus AI alone, for reports containing errors
effect: Assistive clinician-AI collaboration for reports with errors produced a synergistic improvement across all clinical settings.
quote: For reports that contain errors we develop an assistive setting, the first demonstration of clinician-AI collaboration for radiology report composition, and we observe a synergistic improvement across all clinical settings.
sample_unit: certified radiologists evaluating AI-generated and human-written chest radiograph reports

title: Consensus, dissensus and synergy between clinicians and specialist foundation models in radiology report generation
outcome: Radiologist panel preference for AI reports versus clinician-written reports
effect: 55.4% of ICU AI reports were preferable or equivalent to clinician reports by half or more of the panel, 77.7% for outpatient X-rays overall, and 94% for cases with no pertinent abnormal findings.
quote: We observe a wide distribution of preferences across the panel, ranging from full consensus to dissensus, across clinical settings and regions, with 55.4% of Flamingo-CXR intensive care reports evaluated to be preferable or equivalent to clinician reports, by half or more of the panel, rising to 77.7% for outpatient x-rays overall and to 94% for the subset of cases with no pertinent abnormal findings.
sample_unit: certified radiologists evaluating AI-generated and human-written chest radiograph reports

title: Consensus, dissensus and synergy between clinicians and specialist foundation models in radiology report generation
outcome: quality variation across settings
effect: 55.4% ICU; 77.7% outpatient; 94% no abnormal findings preferable/equivalent by half or more of panel.
quote: We observe a wide distribution of preferences across the panel, ranging from full consensus to dissensus, across clinical settings and regions, with 55.4% of Flamingo-CXR intensive care reports evaluated to be preferable or equivalent to clinician reports, by half or more of the panel, rising to 77.7% for outpatient x-rays overall and to 94% for the subset of cases with no pertinent abnormal findings.
sample_unit: certified radiologists evaluating AI-generated and human-written chest radiograph reports

title: Consensus, dissensus and synergy between clinicians and specialist foundation models in radiology report generation
outcome: clinician-AI report composition
effect: Synergistic improvement across all clinical settings; no numeric effect reported in abstract.
quote: For reports that contain errors we develop an assistive setting, the first demonstration of clinician-AI collaboration for radiology report composition, and we observe a synergistic improvement across all clinical settings.
sample_unit: certified radiologists evaluating AI-generated and human-written chest radiograph reports

title: Consensus, dissensus and synergy between clinicians and specialist foundation models in radiology report generation
outcome: report quality in clinician-AI collaborative composition
effect: synergistic improvement across all clinical settings for reports that contain errors
quote: For reports that contain errors we develop an assistive setting, the first demonstration of clinician-AI collaboration for radiology report composition, and we observe a synergistic improvement across all clinical settings.
sample_unit: certified radiologists evaluating AI-generated and human-written chest radiograph reports

title: Influence of believed AI involvement on the perception of digital medical advice
outcome: Perceived reliability, empathy and willingness to follow advice by labelled source (AI, Human, Human + AI)
effect: Identical advice labelled AI or Human + AI was rated significantly less reliable and less empathetic than Human-labelled advice. Participants were also less willing to follow it (N = 2,280).
quote: “AI” and “Human + AI”-labelled advice was evaluated as significantly less reliable and less empathetic compared to “Human”-labelled advice.

title: Influence of believed AI involvement on the perception of digital medical advice
outcome: Perceived reliability and empathy of medical advice
effect: “AI” and “Human + AI”-labelled advice was evaluated as significantly less reliable and less empathetic compared to “Human”-labelled advice (N = 2,280).
quote: “AI” and “Human + AI”-labelled advice was evaluated as significantly less reliable and less empathetic compared to “Human”-labelled advice.

title: Artificial intelligence to facilitate clinical trial recruitment in age-related macular degeneration
outcome: PPV and number of eligible GA trial patients shortlisted, AI vs keyword EHR search
effect: AI shortlisted 1,139 patients (PPV 63%; 95% CI 54–71%) vs EHR search 693 (PPV 40%; 95% CI 39–42%). Combined AI-EHR: 604 patients, PPV 86%.
quote: The AI system shortlisted a larger number of eligible patients with greater precision (1,139, PPV: 63%; 95% CI: 54–71%) compared to the EHR search (693, PPV: 40%; 95% CI: 39– 42%).

title: Performance of GPT-4 on the American College of Radiology In-Service Examination
outcome: Answer reproducibility across repeated runs of the same exam questions
effect: When the exam was repeated months later, GPT-4 chose a different answer 25.5% of the time, with a small, insignificant decrease in accuracy.
quote: When the questions were repeated, GPT-4 chose a different answer 25.5% of the time and there was a small but insignificant decrease in accuracy.

title: Performance of GPT-4 on the American College of Radiology In-Service Examination
outcome: Model-stated confidence for correct versus incorrect answers
effect: Confidence was 87.1% for correct answers and 84.0% for incorrect answers (p = 0.012), so confidence was high even when wrong. Overall accuracy was 58.5%.
quote: GPT-4 showed significantly higher (p = 0.012) confidence for correct answers (87.1%) compared to incorrect (84.0%).

title: Empowering Personalized Pharmacogenomics with Generative AI Solutions
outcome: AI assistant performance on PGx question catalog, RAG-grounded GPT-4 versus ChatGPT 3.5
effect: RAG-based GPT-4 assistant performed better than ChatGPT 3.5, especially on provider-specific queries requiring specialized data and citations; no numeric results reported in the abstract.
quote: Compared with OpenAI’s ChatGPT 3.5, it demonstrated better performance, especially in provider-specific queries requiring specialized data and citations.

title: Exploring the Capabilities of ChatGPT in Women’s Health
outcome: Whether ChatGPT's self-assessed confidence and entropy distinguished correct from incorrect answers
effect: Median confidence was 70% for correct answers and for incorrect answers judged correct (p<0.001). Entropy was identical for correct and incorrect responses (median 1.46, IQR 0.44–1.77).
quote: Entropy values were identical for correct and incorrect responses (median 1.46, IQR 0.44–1.77), indicating no discernible distinction in ChatGPT’s prediction certainty.

title: Neonatal Pain Detection from Facial Expressions Using Deep Learning
outcome: Framework accuracy when low-confidence cases are deferred to manual assessment
effect: Overall framework accuracy reached 82.35% with the manual assessment branch integrated. The abstract says this integration raises recall of true pain events and reduces manual evaluation effort.
quote: Experimental results show our neural network sur- passes state-of-the-art algorithms by at least 25% in accuracy on the MNPAD dataset, with overall framework accuracy reaching 82.35% with integration of manual assessment branch.

title: Testing the reproducibility and effectiveness of deep learning models among clinics: sperm detection as a pilot study
outcome: Sperm detection model precision and recall across clinics and imaging setups in multi-center validation
effect: After training on a dataset enriched with varied imaging conditions, multi-center validation showed no significant differences in precision or recall across clinics and applications. Internal ICC was 0.97 for both precision and recall.
quote: Multi-center clinical validation showed no significant differences in model precision or recall across different clinics and applications.

title: Evaluation of a Machine Learning-guided Strategy for Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Screening in Health Systems
outcome: Difference between Lp(a)-tested population and other cohorts in ARISE features
effect: The Lp(a) tested population significantly differed from other study cohorts (UK Biobank, ARIC, CARDIA, MESA) in terms of ARISE features.
quote: The Lp(a) tested population significantly differed from other study cohorts in terms of ARISE features.
sample_unit: randomly sampled YNHHS patients (plus 7,981 YNHHS and 10,635 VUMC Lp(a)-tested patients)

title: Evaluation of a Machine Learning-guided Strategy for Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Screening in Health Systems
outcome: Association of positive ARISE score with elevated Lp(a) at two health systems
effect: Positive ARISE score associated with higher odds of elevated Lp(a) in YNHHS (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.65-2.12) and VUMC (OR 1.41, 95% CI 1.24-1.60); association weaker at VUMC.
quote: A positive ARISE score was associated with significantly higher odds of elevated Lp(a) in the YNHHS (OR 1.87, 95% CI, 1.65-2.12) and the VUMC (OR 1.41, 95% CI, 1.24-1.60).
sample_unit: randomly sampled YNHHS patients (plus 7,981 YNHHS and 10,635 VUMC Lp(a)-tested patients)

title: The Transformative Potential of Large Language Models in Mining Electronic Health Records Data
outcome: LLM accuracy compared with physicians on the same comorbidity extraction reports
effect: GPT-4 outperformed physicians (McNemar p<0.001); sensitivity 96.8% vs 88.8% for physicians; physicians slightly better in precision (97.7% vs 96.8%). GPT-3.5 not significantly different (p=0.79).
quote: GPT-4 demonstrated clear superiority in several key metrics (McNemar’s test p < 0.001).

title: Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Increases Access and Health Equity in Underserved Populations with Diabetes
outcome: Change in diabetic eye disease testing adherence by race at AI vs non-AI sites
effect: Black/African American adherence rose 11.9% at AI-switched sites vs fell 1.2% at non-AI sites; Asian vs Black gap shrank from 15.6% (61.1% vs 45.5%) to 3.5% by 2021.
quote: The adherence rate for Black/African Americans increased by 11.9% within AI-switched sites whereas it decreased by 1.2% within non-AI sites over the same time frame.

title: Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Increases Access and Health Equity in Underserved Populations with Diabetes
outcome: adherence to annual DED testing
effect: The odds ratio of adherence at AI-switched sites was 36% higher than at non-AI sites.
quote: First, after controlling for a wide range of potential confounders, our regression analysis demonstrated that the odds ratio of adherence at AI-switched sites was 36% higher than that of non-AI sites, suggesting that there was a higher increase in DED testing between 2019 and 2021 at AI-switched sites than at non-AI sites.

title: Generalizable deep neural networks for image quality classification of cervical images
