outcome: Image quality classifier performance across devices and geographies, internal vs external validation
effect: Internal AUROC 0.92 (LQ) and 0.93 (HQ), %EM 2.8%; external different-device set AUROC 0.83 and 0.82, %EM 3.9%; no meaningful difference across geographies.
quote: Our model also generalized well externally, achieving corresponding AUROCs of 0.83 and 0.82, and %EM of 3.9% when tested out-of-the-box on the external validation (“EXT”) set.

title: Generalizable deep neural networks for image quality classification of cervical images
outcome: Performance degradation (catastrophic forgetting) after retraining with new data
effect: No catastrophic forgetting upon retraining with new data; no meaningful performance difference across geographies.
quote: Additionally, our model was geography agnostic with no meaningful difference in performance across geographies, did not exhibit catastrophic forgetting upon retraining with new data, and mimicked the overall/average ground truth rater behavior well.

title: Influence of a Large Language Model on Diagnostic Reasoning: A Randomized Clinical Vignette Study
outcome: Diagnostic reasoning score: physicians with GPT-4 vs conventional resources, and GPT-4 alone
effect: Physicians with GPT-4 scored 76.3% vs 73.7% (adjusted difference 1.6 points, 95% CI -4.4 to 7.6; p=0.60). GPT-4 alone scored 15.5 points higher than the conventional resources group (p=0.03).
quote: GPT-4 alone scored 15.5 percentage points (95% CI 1.5 to 29, p=0.03) higher than the conventional resources group.

title: Influence of a Large Language Model on Diagnostic Reasoning: A Randomized Clinical Vignette Study
outcome: Human-AI team performance versus standalone LLM performance on diagnostic reasoning
effect: Access to GPT-4 did not significantly improve physician reasoning (difference 1.6 points, p=0.60), while GPT-4 alone outperformed both physician groups by 15.5 points (p=0.03).
quote: GPT-4 alone demonstrated higher performance than both physician groups, suggesting opportunities for further improvement in physician-AI collaboration in clinical practice.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT’s Usefulness and Accuracy in Diagnostic Surgical Pathology
outcome: Accuracy of bibliographic references generated by ChatGPT, manually verified
effect: Of 214 references, 70.1% correct, 12.1% inaccurate, 17.8% did not correspond to a publication.
quote: ChatGPT provided 214 bibliographic references: 70.1% were correct, 12.1% were inaccurate and 17.8% did not correspond to a publication.

title: Multicenter Development and Prospective Validation of eCARTv5: A Gradient Boosted Machine Learning Early Warning Score
outcome: Model AUROC in external validation across 21 hospitals and three health systems
effect: Retrospective external validation AUROC 0.835 (95%CI 0.834, 0.835) vs NEWS 0.766 and MEWS 0.704; AUROC remained ≥0.80 across demographics, conditions, and prospective validation.
quote: eCART’s performance remained high (AUROC ≥0.80) across a range of patient demographics, clinical conditions, and during prospective validation.

title: Multicenter Development and Prospective Validation of eCARTv5: A Gradient Boosted Machine Learning Early Warning Score
outcome: eCART discrimination compared with MEWS and NEWS on same data
effect: eCART AUROC 0.835 (95%CI 0.834, 0.835) vs NEWS 0.766 (0.766, 0.767) and MEWS 0.704 (0.703, 0.704) in retrospective validation.
quote: In retrospective validation, eCART had the highest AUROC (0.835; 95%CI 0.834, 0.835), followed by NEWS (0.766 (95%CI 0.766, 0.767)), and MEWS (0.704 (95%CI 0.703, 0.704)).

title: Randomized Controlled Comparative Effectiveness Trial of Risk Model-Guided Clinical Decision Support for Suicide Screening
outcome: Decision to screen for suicidal ideation; documented suicide risk assessments
effect: Interruptive CDS: 42% (121/289) decisions to screen vs 4% (12/307) non-interruptive (OR 17.7, p<0.001); documented assessments 63/289 vs 11/307 (p<0.001).
quote: Adjusting for provider cluster effects, Interruptive CDS led to significantly higher numbers of decisions to screen (42%=121/289 encounters) compared to Non-Interruptive CDS (4%=12/307) (odds ratio=17.7, p-value <0.001).

title: Automated speech analysis for risk detection of depression, anxiety, insomnia, and fatigue: Algorithm Development and Validation Study
outcome: Model fairness (disparity ratio) across age, sex, and education subgroups
effect: Average disparity ratio was 0.86 for sex, 0.47 for education level, and 0.33 for age groups, showing subgroup performance gaps.
quote: Fairness analysis revealed that models were consistent for sex (average Disparity Ratio (DR) = 0.86), to a lesser extent for education level (average Disparity Ratio (DR) = 0.47) and worse for age groups (average Disparity Ratio (DR) = 0.33).

title: Development and Testing of a Novel Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Medication Safety in 12 Clinical Specialties
outcome: DRP detection performance of RAG-LLM versus LLM alone
effect: RAG-LLM performed better than LLM alone; DRP detection accuracy improved in several categories but at the expense of lower precision.
quote: RAG-LLM performed better compared to LLM alone.
sample_unit: prescribing error scenarios embedded in 23 clinical vignettes

title: Development and Testing of a Novel Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Medication Safety in 12 Clinical Specialties
outcome: Medication error detection: LLM-CDSS alone versus junior pharmacist plus LLM-CDSS co-pilot
effect: In co-pilot mode, accuracy, recall, and F1 scores were optimized, with notable improvements in detecting severe DRPs.
quote: This study established that a RAG-LLM based CDSS significantly boosts the accuracy of medication error identification when used alongside junior pharmacists (co-pilot), with notable improvements in detecting severe DRPs.
sample_unit: prescribing error scenarios embedded in 23 clinical vignettes

title: Development and Testing of a Novel Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Medication Safety in 12 Clinical Specialties
outcome: standalone versus co-pilot performance
effect: Co-pilot mode optimized accuracy, recall, and F1; no numeric effect values reported in abstract.
quote: When employed in a co-pilot mode, accuracy, recall, and F1 scores were optimized, indicating effectiveness in identifying moderate to severe DRPs.
sample_unit: prescribing error scenarios embedded in 23 clinical vignettes

title: Development and Testing of a Novel Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems for Medication Safety in 12 Clinical Specialties
outcome: DRP detection performance of co-pilot mode versus autonomous LLM
effect: When employed in co-pilot mode, accuracy, recall, and F1 scores were optimized, indicating effectiveness in identifying moderate to severe DRPs.
quote: When employed in a co-pilot mode, accuracy, recall, and F1 scores were optimized, indicating effectiveness in identifying moderate to severe DRPs.
sample_unit: prescribing error scenarios embedded in 23 clinical vignettes

title: Evaluating the generalisability of region-naïve machine learning algorithms for the identification of epilepsy in low-resource settings
outcome: Model performance in own site versus other, unseen sites for active convulsive epilepsy
effect: Single-site models performed well within their own regions but worse on other regions (p<0.05); model weights and optimal thresholds varied markedly across sites.
quote: Single-site clinical models performed well within their own regions, but worse in general when evaluated on other regions (p<0.05).
country: South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya, Ghana

title: Evaluating the generalisability of region-naïve machine learning algorithms for the identification of epilepsy in low-resource settings
outcome: Variation in model performance and parameters across sites
effect: Performance dropped when models were applied to other sites; thresholds and weights varied across sites. Multi-site training lowered mean internal performance while external performance improved.
quote: Model weights and optimal thresholds varied markedly across sites.
country: South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya, Ghana

title: Assessing the Performance of Plugin-Integrated ChatGPT-4 in the German Medical Board Examination: An Experimental Study on the Advancements and Limitations of Modern AI Modelling Approaches
outcome: Ability of GPT models to express calibrated uncertainty in answers to board exam questions
effect: Models could assess uncertainty in their responses but were overconfident; a new 'confidence accuracy' metric was developed. No numeric values are given in the abstract.
quote: Moreover, the models could assess the uncertainty in their responses, albeit exhibiting overconfidence.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Drafting Emergency Department Discharge Summaries
outcome: Prevalence of hallucination and omission errors in LLM-generated ED discharge summaries
effect: GPT-4: 33% error-free; inaccuracies in 10%, hallucinations in 42%, omissions of clinically relevant information in 47%. GPT-3.5-turbo: 10% error-free.
quote: Summaries generated by GPT-4 were mostly accurate, with inaccuracies found in only 10% of cases, however, 42% of the summaries exhibited hallucinations and 47% omitted clinically relevant information.

title: Enhancing Early Detection of Cognitive Decline in the Elderly: A Comparative Study Utilizing Large Language Models in Clinical Notes
outcome: Compared LLMs (GPT-4, Llama 2) against traditional models on same test data for cognitive decline detection
effect: GPT-4 outperformed Llama 2 but did not outperform traditional models (hierarchical attention network, XGBoost); ensemble achieved precision 90.3%, recall 94.2%, F1 92.2%.
quote: GPT-4 demonstrated superior accuracy and efficiency compared to Llama 2, but did not outperform traditional models.

title: Enhancing Early Detection of Cognitive Decline in the Elderly: A Comparative Study Utilizing Large Language Models in Clinical Notes
outcome: Model performance on local EHR data against annotated reference standard
effect: Models trained on local EHR data showed diverse error profiles; ensemble improved precision from 70%-79% to above 90%; only 2 of 63 errors (3.2%) were mutual across models.
quote: LLMs and traditional machine learning models trained using local EHR data exhibited diverse error profiles.

title: Real-world evaluation of deep learning algorithms to classify functional pathogenic germline variants
outcome: VUS classification utility
effect: For variants of uncertain significance, models were generally of limited clinical utility.
quote: However, when specifically tasked with classifying variants of uncertain significance, the deep learning models were generally of limited clinical utility.

title: Red Teaming Large Language Models in Medicine: Real-World Insights on Model Behavior
outcome: Inappropriate LLM responses identified through multidisciplinary red-teaming of clinical scenarios
effect: 19.8% of 1146 responses labeled inappropriate; GPT-3.5 25.7%, GPT-4.0 16.2%, GPT-4.0 with internet 17.5%. Red teaming with 80 experts surfaced safety, privacy, hallucination, and bias failures.
quote: Results demonstrate a significant proportion of inappropriate responses across GPT-3.5, GPT-4.0, and GPT-4.0 with Internet (25.7%, 16.2%, and 17.5%, respectively) and illustrate the valuable role that non-technical clinicians can play in evaluating models.
sample_unit: LLM responses (382 unique prompts x 3 models)

title: Red Teaming Large Language Models in Medicine: Real-World Insights on Model Behavior
outcome: Responses appropriate in older model but inappropriate in updated models
effect: 11.8% of responses were appropriate with GPT-3.5 but inappropriate in updated models.
quote: Interestingly, 11.8% of responses were deemed appropriate with GPT-3.5 but inappropriate in updated models, highlighting the ongoing need to evaluate evolving LLMs.
sample_unit: LLM responses (382 unique prompts x 3 models)

title: Generalizability of Clinical Prediction Models in Mental Health - Real-World Validation of Machine Learning Models for Depressive Symptom Prediction
outcome: Generalization of depressive symptom prediction model across diverse inpatient and outpatient samples
effect: Sparse model trained on clinical information generalized strongly across diverse real-world samples despite systematic differences between samples; no numbers in abstract.
quote: Despite systematic differences between samples, a sparse machine learning model trained on clinical information exhibited strong generalization across diverse real-world samples.

title: DREAM: A framework for discovering mechanisms underlying AI prediction of protected attributes
outcome: Disease diagnosis performance when models use demographic shortcuts under domain shift
effect: Incorrect use of demographic shortcuts had a detrimental effect on downstream disease diagnosis performance under a domain shift; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: We highlight how incorrect use of these demographic shortcuts can have a detrimental effect on the performance of a clinically relevant downstream task like disease diagnosis under a domain shift.

title: Receiving information on machine learning-based clinical decision support systems in psychiatric services may increase patient trust in these systems: A randomised survey experiment
outcome: patient trust in ML CDSS
effect: Mean absolute difference in trust: 5% [95%CI: 1%;9%], p-value= 0·009 vs active; 4% [1%;8%], p-value=0·015 vs blank.
quote: The intervention increased trust in ML-based clinical decision support systems when compared to the active control (mean absolute difference in trust: 5% [95%CI: 1%;9%], p-value= 0·009) and the blank control arm (mean absolute difference in trust: 4% [1%;8%], p-value=0·015).

title: Receiving information on machine learning-based clinical decision support systems in psychiatric services may increase patient trust in these systems: A randomised survey experiment
outcome: Patient trust in ML-based clinical decision support after receiving information on the technology versus controls
effect: Intervention increased trust vs active control (5% [1%;9%], p=0.009) and vs blank control (4% [1%;8%], p=0.015); distrust decreased by 3-4%. Small effect size.
quote: The intervention increased trust in ML-based clinical decision support systems when compared to the active control (mean absolute difference in trust: 5% [95%CI: 1%;9%], p-value= 0·009) and the blank control arm (mean absolute difference in trust: 4% [1%;8%], p-value=0·015).

title: Can AI answer my questions? Using Artificial Intelligence to help provide information for patients with a stoma
outcome: Readability of LLM stoma patient-education responses (Flesch-Kincaid, Flesch Reading Ease, Coleman-Liau)
effect: All LLM responses required high school to college level education to comprehend comfortably.
quote: All responses required high school to college level education to comprehend comfortably.

title: Assessing GPT-4’s Diagnostic Accuracy with Darker Skin Tones: Underperformance and Implications
outcome: GPT-4 diagnostic accuracy by skin tone (Fitzpatrick I-II vs IV-VI)
effect: Correct diagnosis for lighter skin 44% (11/25) vs darker skin 12% (3/25), p<0.05; each Fitzpatrick unit increase lowered differential accuracy by 11.4% and diagnosis accuracy by 7.1%.
quote: GPT-4 exhibited better performance in providing the correct diagnosis for lighter skin tones (44%, n=11/25) compared to darker skin tones (12%, n=3/25), and this was statistically significant (p-value < 0.05).

title: Assessing GPT-4’s Diagnostic Accuracy with Darker Skin Tones: Underperformance and Implications
outcome: GPT-4 dermatology diagnostic accuracy compared with previously reported accuracies
effect: Overall GPT-4 correctly diagnosed 28% (14/50) of images; correct diagnosis in top differentials for 48% (24/50), much lower than prior reports up to 90%.
quote: Overall, GPT-4 correctly diagnosed the condition in 28% of the images (n=14/50), while the correct diagnosis was included in its list of top differentials for 48% of the images (n=24/50).

title: Real-World Performance of Large Language Models in Emergency Department Chest Pain Triage
outcome: ACS diagnostic accuracy of LLMs versus human experts on same retrospective chest pain data
effect: Human experts 86.37% accuracy and 89.26% specificity vs Lingyi Zhihui 76.40%/70.15%, Tongyi Qianwen 61.11%/47.95%, MediGuide-14B 84.52% accuracy; LLMs had higher sensitivity.
quote: Human experts achieved higher accuracy (86.37%) and specificity (89.26%) but lower sensitivity compared to the LLMs.

title: Leveraging a Large Language Model to Assess Quality-of-Care: Monitoring ADHD Medication Side Effects
outcome: LLM classification performance across patient age, sex, and insurance subgroups
effect: No model bias found in relation to patient age, sex, or insurance; overall sensitivity 87.2%, AUC 0.93/0.92 on holdout/deployment sets.
quote: Analyses revealed no model bias in relation to patient age, sex, or insurance.

title: Using Large Language Models to Annotate Complex Cases of Social Determinants of Health in Longitudinal Clinical Records
outcome: LLM annotation accuracy versus manual annotation ground truth for housing instability
effect: GPT-4 recall 0.924 vs human annotators 0.702; precision 0.850 vs 0.971; no evidence of hallucinations in GPT-4 outputs
quote: Compared with GPT-3.5 and the NER model, GPT-4 had the highest performance and had a much higher recall (0.924) than human annotators (0.702) in identifying patients experiencing current or past housing instability, although precision was lower (0.850) compared with human annotators (0.971).

title: Using Large Language Models to Annotate Complex Cases of Social Determinants of Health in Longitudinal Clinical Records
outcome: Comparison of GPT-4 against GPT-3.5, NER model, RegEx and human annotators on same notes
effect: GPT-4 had the highest performance among automated methods and higher recall than humans (0.924 vs 0.702) but lower precision (0.850 vs 0.971).
quote: Compared with GPT-3.5 and the NER model, GPT-4 had the highest performance and had a much higher recall (0.924) than human annotators (0.702) in identifying patients experiencing current or past housing instability, although precision was lower (0.850) compared with human annotators (0.971).

title: Large language models to help appeal denied radiotherapy services
outcome: Existence and relevance of literature citations in LLM-generated appeal letters
effect: All LLMs, including GPT-4web, were poor at supporting clinical assertions with existing, relevant, and appropriately cited primary literature.
quote: All LLMs, including GPT-4web, were poor at supporting clinical assertions with existing, relevant, and appropriately cited primary literature.
sample_unit: simulated test prompts (appeal letters per LLM)

title: Large language models to help appeal denied radiotherapy services
outcome: Benchmarking of LLM configurations on an intended-use task with blinded expert scoring
effect: GPT-4 and GPT-4web letters demonstrated superior clinical reasoning and were readier for submission than GPT-3.5 letters (p < 0.001); fine-tuned GPT-3.5ft performed worse across all domains (p < 0.001).
quote: GPT-4 and GPT-4web letters demonstrated superior clinical reasoning and were readier for submission than GPT-3.5 letters (p < 0.001).
sample_unit: simulated test prompts (appeal letters per LLM)

title: Prompt Engineering Strategies Improve the Diagnostic Accuracy of GPT-4 Turbo in Neuroradiology Cases
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and misdiagnosis rate with versus without a 90% confidence threshold
effect: Baseline top-diagnosis accuracy 55.1%, misdiagnosis 29.4%. With 90% confidence threshold, accuracy 72.9%, five-candidate applicability 85.9%, misdiagnoses 14.1%, but only half of cases analyzed.
quote: Applying a 90% confidence threshold increased the accuracy of the top diagnosis to 72.9% and the applicability of the five candidates to 85.9%, while reducing misdiagnoses to 14.1%, but limited the analysis to half of cases.

title: Prompt Engineering Strategies Improve the Diagnostic Accuracy of GPT-4 Turbo in Neuroradiology Cases
outcome: Whether confidence-based deferral reduces misdiagnosis while limiting cases analyzed
effect: 90% confidence threshold reduced misdiagnoses from 29.4% to 14.1% and raised top-diagnosis accuracy to 72.9%, but restricted analysis to half of cases.
quote: Applying a 90% confidence threshold increased the accuracy of the top diagnosis to 72.9% and the applicability of the five candidates to 85.9%, while reducing misdiagnoses to 14.1%, but limited the analysis to half of cases.

title: Machine Learning for Prediction of Childhood Mental Health Problems in Social Care
outcome: Algorithmic fairness of ML models predicting childhood mental health problems across subgroups
effect: Fairness assessments showed potential biases within the models; best SVM model AUROC 0.743 (95% CI 0.724-0.762). No subgroup numbers given in the text.
quote: Assessments of algorithmic fairness showed potential biases within these models.

title: Automated detection of large vessel occlusion: a multicenter study validating efficacy and proving clinical implications
outcome: Reliability of LVO probability categories versus mathematical calibration; association with infarct volume and mRS
effect: Four-category recategorization (unlikely, less likely, possible, suggestive) gave a reliable LVO estimate compared with mathematical calibration, and categories were significantly associated with follow-up infarct volume and 3-month mRS.
quote: Due to sparse data between 20-60% of LVO probabilities, recategorization into unlikely (0-20% LVO scores), less likely (20-60%), possible (60-90%), and suggestive (90-100%) provided a reliable estimation of LVO compared with mathematical calibration.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness and Safety of Large Language Model in Generating Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management Plans: A Comparative Study with Medical Experts Based on Real Patient Records
outcome: Error scores of GPT-4 versus blinded medical experts on the same patient records
effect: Overall error scores were comparable between experts and GPT-4 (p=0.301). Experts had fewer missing medications (p=0.008), and GPT-4 had fewer unnecessary medications (p=0.003).
quote: The overall error scores were comparable between human experts and GPT-4 (p=0.301).

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness and Safety of Large Language Model in Generating Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management Plans: A Comparative Study with Medical Experts Based on Real Patient Records
outcome: Completeness of GPT-4 management plans versus ADA guideline reference plan (missing medications)
effect: Medical experts' plans had fewer missing medications than GPT-4's (p=0.008). Safety issues appeared in 16% of GPT-4 plans.
quote: Safety issues were noted in 16% of the plans generated by GPT-4, highlighting potential risks associated with AI-generated management plans.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness and Safety of Large Language Model in Generating Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management Plans: A Comparative Study with Medical Experts Based on Real Patient Records
outcome: Drug dosage accuracy of GPT-4 plans versus expert plans
effect: No significant difference in dosage accuracy between GPT-4 and medical experts (p=0.975).
quote: No significant difference was observed in the accuracy of drug dosages (p=0.975).

title: Large Language Models for Social Determinants of Health Information Extraction from Clinical Notes – A Generalizable Approach across Institutions
outcome: Cross-institution generalization of SDoH extraction models trained on one dataset and tested on others
effect: Models performed well when trained and tested on individual datasets (LLM micro-F1 over 0.9 on level 1 corpora, over 0.84 on level 2), but cross-dataset generalization highlighted remaining obstacles.
quote: While models performed well when trained and tested on individual datasets, cross-dataset generalization highlighted remaining obstacles.

title: Performance of a Protein Language Model for Variant Annotation in Cardiac Disease
outcome: VUS reclassification rate of candidate AI versus another variant classification platform on same variants
effect: Reclassification rate was 86.1% for VarCard.io vs 34.8% for Franklin (p<0.001), showing large differences between competing tools on the same data.
quote: The reclassification rate was significantly higher for VarCard.io than for Franklin (86.1% vs 34.8%, p<0.001).

title: Multisite Pragmatic Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial of the CONCERN Early Warning System
outcome: In-hospital mortality, length of stay, sepsis and ICU transfer with vs without AI early warning system
effect: Intervention had 35.6% decreased risk of death (aHR 0.644), 11.2% decreased LOS, 7.5% decreased sepsis risk, and 24.9% increased unanticipated ICU transfer (aHR 1.249) versus usual care.
quote: A hospital-wide EWS based on nursing surveillance patterns decreased in-hospital mortality, sepsis, and LOS when integrated into the care team’s EHR workflow.

title: Assessing equitable use of large language models for clinical decision support in real-world settings: fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
outcome: Model performance before vs after fine-tuning to local EHR data (precision, recall, F1, accuracy)
effect: Fine-tuning to local EHR improved 3-label precision, recall, F1, accuracy by 21-31%, 11-21%, 16-27%, 6-10% among GatorTron, BioMegatron, BioBert and ClinicalBERT.
quote: Fine-tuning the LLMs to the local EHR data improved model performance.

title: Assessing equitable use of large language models for clinical decision support in real-world settings: fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
outcome: External validation performance of publicly trained LLMs on local Pakistani EHR data
effect: LLMs not fine-tuned to the local EHR dataset performed poorly, suggesting bias, when externally validated on it.
quote: LLMs not fine-tuned to the local EHR dataset performed poorly, suggesting bias, when externally validated on it.

title: Assessing equitable use of large language models for clinical decision support in real-world settings: fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
outcome: Performance drop when models trained on global north data applied to local South Asian EHR
effect: Publicly available LLMs, predominantly trained in global north settings, performed poorly on local EHR data and were found biased; ChatGPT was an exception, improving by 10-13% on local data.
quote: Publicly available LLMs, predominantly trained in global north settings, were found to be biased when used in a real-world clinical setting.

title: Assessing equitable use of large language models for clinical decision support in real-world settings: fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
outcome: Bias in Global South clinical setting
effect: Publicly available LLMs predominantly trained in global north settings were biased in a real-world clinical setting.
quote: Publicly available LLMs, predominantly trained in global north settings, were found to be biased when used in a real-world clinical setting.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Patient Care: A Study of Artificial Intelligence’s Responses to Blepharoplasty Concerns
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT blepharoplasty answers (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid grade level, passive voice)
effect: Flesch Reading Ease 31.48, indicating high school complexity; Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 10.92; 20.97% passive voice; no significant differences between question categories.
quote: Overall readability analysis showed a Flesch Reading Ease score of 31.48, indicating high school complexity with a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level at 10.92, and 20.97% use of passive voice.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Patient Care: A Study of Artificial Intelligence’s Responses to Blepharoplasty Concerns
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient information relative to appropriate patient reading level
effect: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 10.92 and Flesch Reading Ease of 31.48; authors conclude answers may not be suitable for patients with varying educational levels.
quote: While it can offer accurate insights, it's important to recognize that its answers might not consistently reach complete accuracy or be suitable for patients with varying educational levels.

title: Anonymizing medical documents with local, privacy preserving large language models: The LLM-Anonymizer
outcome: Residual personal identifying information missed and over-redaction after LLM-based de-identification of clinical letters
effect: With Llama-3 70B, 98.05% of PII characters removed; 1.95% of PII missed and 0.85% of characters erroneously redacted.
quote: When evaluating the performance in relation to the number of characters manually identified as containing personal information and identifiable characteristics, our system missed only 1.95% of personal identifying information and erroneously redacted only 0.85% of the characters.

title: Customizing GPT-4 for clinical information retrieval from standard operating procedures
outcome: Sufficient answers from GPT-4 versus Claude-3-opus on the same questions
effect: Claude-3-opus outperformed GPT-4 in providing sufficient answers (70.0% vs. 36.7%) and required fewer iterations for satisfactory responses.
quote: Comparing LLMs, Claude-3-opus outperformed GPT-4 in providing sufficient answers (70.0% vs. 36.7%) and required fewer iterations for satisfactory responses.

title: Customizing GPT-4 for clinical information retrieval from standard operating procedures
outcome: Answer completeness, correctness, sufficiency of customized LLM answers versus reference SOP content
effect: Interactive Q&A yielded the highest rate of completeness (80%), correctness (83%) and sufficiency (60%).
quote: Interactive Q&A yielded the highest rate of completeness (80%), correctness (83%) and sufficiency (60%).

title: Customizing GPT-4 for clinical information retrieval from standard operating procedures
outcome: answer accuracy by prompt detail
effect: Question detail influenced accuracy; intermediate-detail prompts had the highest sufficiency rates.
quote: Degree of detail of the question prompt influenced answer accuracy, with intermediate-detail prompts achieving the highest sufficiency rates.

title: Customizing GPT-4 for clinical information retrieval from standard operating procedures
outcome: answer accuracy and sufficiency across prompt detail levels
effect: intermediate-detail prompts achieved the highest sufficiency rates, with prompt detail influencing answer accuracy
quote: Degree of detail of the question prompt influenced answer accuracy, with intermediate-detail prompts achieving the highest sufficiency rates.

title: Development and Validation of a Machine Learning Model Integrated with the Clinical Workflow for Inpatient Discharge Date Prediction
outcome: Model F1-score compared with baseline discharge date estimates
effect: Model surpassed baseline estimates by up to 35.68% in F1-score.
quote: The model achieved a performance surpassing baseline estimates by up to 35.68% in the F1-score.

title: Evaluating approaches of training a generative large language model for multi-label classification of unstructured electronic health records
outcome: multi-label EHR classification performance
effect: RAG improved performance only in few-shot learning; few-shot with RAG outperformed zero-shot with RAG, but showed no significant difference compared to zero-shot with PEFT.
quote: Notably, PEFT significantly enhances model performance in both zero-shot and few-shot learning; however, RAG improves performance only in few-shot learning.

title: Multimodal Image Dataset for AI-based Skin Cancer (MIDAS) Benchmarking
outcome: Performance of published dermatology AI models on new prospectively collected dataset versus published metrics
effect: Performance reduction across all four SOTA models compared to previously published performance metrics, indicating generalizability challenges.
quote: When evaluating SOTA models using the MIDAS dataset, we observed performance reduction across all models compared to their previously published performance metrics, indicating challenges to generalizability of current SOTA algorithms.

title: Multimodal Image Dataset for AI-based Skin Cancer (MIDAS) Benchmarking
outcome: Model-to-clinician diagnostic performance comparison for malignant vs benign
effect: Dermatologists were 79% accurate with top-1 diagnosis differentiating malignant from benign; used as comparative baseline for the models.
quote: As a comparative baseline, the dermatologists performing biopsies were 79% accurate with their top-1 diagnosis at differentiating a malignant from benign lesion.

title: Buyer Beware: confounding factors and biases abound when predicting omics-based biomarkers from histological images
outcome: Deep learning biomarker prediction versus simple pathologist-assigned grade baseline
effect: Because of biomarker correlations, deep learning models may not offer significant advantages over pathologist-assigned grades for predicting certain biomarkers. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
quote: We also show that, due to the presence of such correlations, deep learning models may not offer significant advantages in predicting certain biomarkers in comparison to simply using pathologist-assigned grades for their prediction.

title: Assessing the potential of ChatGPT-4 to accurately identify drug-drug interactions and provide clinical pharmacotherapy recommendations
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of GPT-4 clinical recommendations for drug-drug interaction regimens
effect: Inappropriate recommendations potentially causing harm in 14% of responses (2/14); 63% (19/30) accurate but incomplete; intended DDI identified in 90% (27/30).
quote: Inappropriate clinical recommendations potentially causing patient harm were provided in 14% of responses provided by GPT-4 (2/14), and 63% of responses contained accurate information but incomplete recommendations (19/30).
sample_unit: GPT-4 responses (15 medication regimens x 2 prompts)

title: Bridging the Gap in Health Literacy: Harnessing the Power of Large Language Models to Generate Plain Language Summaries from Biomedical Texts
outcome: Accuracy, readability, completeness, usefulness of LLM-generated plain language summaries
effect: GPT-4 summaries were semantically equivalent to domain-expert summaries and rated high in accuracy, readability, completeness, and usefulness; the classifier identified plain language with 97.2% precision.
quote: GPT 4, a state-of-the-art LLM, successfully generated PLS that were semantically equivalent to those generated by domain experts and which were rated high in accuracy, readability, completeness, and usefulness.

title: Towards a Holistic Framework for Multimodal Large Language Models in Three-dimensional Brain CT Report Generation
outcome: Accuracy of midline shift captioning on external validation CQ500 dataset
effect: BrainGPT achieved accuracy of 0.91 in captioning midline shifts on the external validation CQ500 dataset, alongside internal testing scores.
quote: our BrainGPT model scored BLEU-1 = 44.35, BLEU-4 = 20.38, METEOR = 30.13, ROUGE-L = 47.6, and CIDEr-R = 211.77 during internal testing and demonstrated an accuracy of 0.91 in captioning midline shifts on the external validation CQ500 dataset.

title: Enhancing Doctor-Patient Communication Using Large Language Models for Pathology Report Interpretation
outcome: Patient understanding score and doctor-patient communication time with plain-language AI-interpreted pathology reports versus original reports
effect: Patient understanding rose from 5.23 to 7.98 points (P<0.001); communication time fell over 70%, from 35 to 10 minutes (P<0.001) with interpretive pathology reports.
quote: Among 698 pathology reports analyzed, the interpretation through LLMs significantly improved readability and patient understanding.

title: Boosting LLM-Assisted Diagnosis: 10-Minute LLM Tutorial Elevates Radiology Residents’ Performance in Brain MRI Interpretation
outcome: Resident diagnostic accuracy and confidence with vs without a 10-minute LLM tutorial
effect: Top-three accuracy 62.5% (55/88) after tutorial vs 44.8% (39/87) LLM without tutorial and 32.2% (28/87) conventional search; tutorial gave higher scores (binary p=0.042, numeric p=0.016) and confidence (p=0.006).
quote: The LLM tutorial led to significantly higher performance (binary scores: p = 0.042, numeric scores: p = 0.016) and confidence (p = 0.006) but resulted in no relevant differences in reading times.

title: Boosting LLM-Assisted Diagnosis: 10-Minute LLM Tutorial Elevates Radiology Residents’ Performance in Brain MRI Interpretation
outcome: Clinician performance with LLM assistance in intended workflow versus conventional search
effect: Residents with LLM assistance had higher accuracy (44.8% untrained, 62.5% after tutorial) than conventional internet search (32.2%).
quote: This was followed by the LLM-assisted workflow before the tutorial (44.8%; 39/87) and the conventional internet search workflow (32.2%; 28/87).

title: Boosting LLM-Assisted Diagnosis: 10-Minute LLM Tutorial Elevates Radiology Residents’ Performance in Brain MRI Interpretation
outcome: LLM hallucinations
effect: Hallucinations were found in 5.1% of LLM queries.
quote: Hallucinations were found in 5.1% of LLM queries.

title: Boosting LLM-Assisted Diagnosis: 10-Minute LLM Tutorial Elevates Radiology Residents’ Performance in Brain MRI Interpretation
outcome: Top-three differential diagnosis accuracy, confidence, and reading time
effect: Correct diagnosis in top three was 62.5% (55/88) post-tutorial vs 44.8% (39/87) pre-tutorial (binary p=0.042, numeric p=0.016), with higher confidence (p=0.006) and no reading time difference.
quote: The LLM tutorial led to significantly higher performance (binary scores: p = 0.042, numeric scores: p = 0.016) and confidence (p = 0.006) but resulted in no relevant differences in reading times.

title: Self-Logical Consistency Assessment of Large Language Models for Patient Feedback Classification : Algorithm Development and Validation Study
outcome: Logical hallucination rate in LLM feedback classification with vs without SLCA (self-consistency across repeated runs)
effect: SLCA reduced logical hallucinations among detected categories from 15.80% (168/1063) to 0.51% (4/786) with GPT-4 and from 7.17% (51/711) to 1.67% (10/599) with Llama-3.1.
quote: SLCA reduced logical hallucinations among detected categories from 15.80% (168/1063) to 0.51% (4/786) with GPT-4 and from 7.17% (51/711) to 1.67% (10/599) with Llama-3.1, with residual errors confined to the emergency feedback category.
sample_unit: classifications (from 100 patient feedback samples); benchmark of 49,140 classifications from 1,170 feedbacks

title: Self-Logical Consistency Assessment of Large Language Models for Patient Feedback Classification : Algorithm Development and Validation Study
outcome: Residual errors in emergency feedback category after SLCA
effect: Residual logical hallucinations after SLCA were confined to the emergency feedback category.
quote: SLCA reduced logical hallucinations among detected categories from 15.80% (168/1063) to 0.51% (4/786) with GPT-4 and from 7.17% (51/711) to 1.67% (10/599) with Llama-3.1, with residual errors confined to the emergency feedback category.
sample_unit: classifications (from 100 patient feedback samples); benchmark of 49,140 classifications from 1,170 feedbacks

title: Impact of Ambient Artificial Intelligence Notes on Provider Burnout
outcome: Clinician burnout and professional fulfillment measured with the Stanford PFI before and after ambient AI scribe use
effect: Median burnout score fell from 4.16 to 3.16 (p=0.005); burnout rate fell from 69% to 43%; work exhaustion unchanged; fulfillment 6.1 vs 6.5 (p=0.10, non-significant).
quote: Results showed a significant reduction in burnout scores, with the median burnout score improving from 4.16 to 3.16 (p=0.005), with validated Stanford PFI cutoff for overall burnout 3.33.
sample_unit: clinicians (physicians and advanced practice providers) completing pre and post surveys

title: Exploring the Potential of Large Language Models: Can ChatGPT effectively assume the role of medical professionals by providing accurate and reliable responses in childhood cancer?
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT answers across repeated runs of the same questions
effect: Reproducibility was 98% across the childhood cancer questions.
quote: Reproducibility was high at 98%.

title: Exploring the Potential of Large Language Models: Can ChatGPT effectively assume the role of medical professionals by providing accurate and reliable responses in childhood cancer?
outcome: Expert-graded empathy, communication and emotional support in ChatGPT responses
effect: B grade for empathy and A for effective communication on ten questions; emotional support scored B eight times and C twice.
quote: When evaluated on ten questions about humanistic care and emotional support for children with cancer, ChatGPT received a "B" grade in empathy and an "A" in effective communication.

title: Demographic Inaccuracies and Biases in the Depiction of Patients by Artificial Intelligence Text-to-Image Generators
outcome: Demographic accuracy of AI-generated patient images versus real-world epidemiology across 29 diseases
effect: Generated images failed to depict sex, age, and race/ethnicity accurately versus epidemiology; White and normal-weight individuals were over-represented.
quote: Comparison to the real-world epidemiology showed that the generated images failed to depict demographical characteristics such as sex, age, and race and ethnicity accurately.

title: Multimodal Large Language Model Passes Specialty Board Examination and Surpasses Human Test-Taker Scores: A Comparative Analysis Examining the Stepwise Impact of Model Prompting Strategies on Performance
outcome: Exam accuracy with stepwise prompting strategies including retrieval-augmented generation versus baseline
effect: All strategies combined (prompt engineering, RAG, five-shot, AVRM) raised GPT-4 from 60.3% to 80.7% and Gemini Pro from 48.0% to 54.3%; RAG-specific effect not given in abstract.
quote: Implementing all prompting strategies improved the overall score of GPT-4 from 60.3% to 80.7% and Gemini Pro’s from 48.0% to 54.3%.

title: Multimodal Large Language Model Passes Specialty Board Examination and Surpasses Human Test-Taker Scores: A Comparative Analysis Examining the Stepwise Impact of Model Prompting Strategies on Performance
outcome: Accuracy gain from adding an LLM-powered answer validation revision model to other prompting strategies
effect: AVRM added to prompt, RAG and 5-shot increased GPT-4 accuracy by 4.4%.
quote: The addition of the AVRM to prompt, RAG and 5-shot increased GPT-4’s accuracy by 4.4%.

title: Large language models for accurate disease detection in electronic health records
outcome: LLM versus regex method accuracy for gout detection against gold standard on same paragraphs
effect: LLM outperformed regex, achieving 92.7% PPV, 96.6% NPV, and 95.4% accuracy for gout.
quote: The LLM-based algorithm outperformed the regex method, achieving a 92.7% [88.7-95.4%] positive predictive value, a 96.6% [94.6-97.8%] negative predictive value, and an accuracy of 95.4% [93.6-96.7%] for gout.

title: Large language models for accurate disease detection in electronic health records
outcome: LLM performance robustness across model parameters and prompt structure
effect: LLM framework performed well over a wide range of parameter values.
quote: The LLM framework performed well over a wide range of parameter values.

title: An Interpretable Machine Learning Tool for In-Home Screening of Agitation Episodes in People Living with Dementia
outcome: risk stratification performance
effect: Traffic-light risk stratification increased specificity by 15% and improved all metrics.
quote: Implementing the traffic-light system for risk stratification increased specificity by 15% and improved all metrics.

title: Development and Validation of a Deep-Learning Model for Differential Treatment Benefit Prediction for Adults with Major Depressive Disorder Deployed in the Artificial Intelligence in Depression – Medication Enhancement (AID-ME) Study
outcome: Whether model predictions amplified potentially harmful biases across patient subgroups
effect: Bias examination found the model did not amplify potentially harmful biases; overall test AUC 0.65, outperforming a null model (p = 0.01).
quote: The model did not amplify potentially harmful biases.
sample_unit: patients (adults with moderate to severe major depression from antidepressant clinical trials)

title: Predicting onward care needs at admission to reduce discharge delay using machine learning
outcome: ML prediction of discharge care needs compared against clinician predictions and a hybrid model
effect: ML performance comparable to clinician predictions despite using a subset of information; each performs better for different care need types; hybrid clinician+ML model more accurate.
quote: The model performance is comparable to clinician’s predictions of discharge care needs, despite working with only a subset of the information available to the clinician.

title: Large Language Model Influence on Management Reasoning: A Randomized Controlled Trial
outcome: Physician-plus-GPT-4 score compared with GPT-4 alone on management reasoning rubrics
effect: No significant difference between GPT-4-augmented physicians and GPT-4 alone (-0.9%, 95% CI -9.0 to 7.2, p=0.8), so standalone performance matched human-AI team performance.
quote: There was no significant difference between GPT-4-augmented physicians and GPT-4 alone (-0.9%, 95% CI -9.0 to 7.2, p=0.8).

title: LLM Doc: An Assessment of ChatGPT’s Ability to Consent Patients for IR Procedures
outcome: IR physician ratings of ChatGPT-4 consent outputs for accuracy, comprehensiveness, and comfort giving them to patients
effect: Physicians rated outputs sufficient for accuracy 84% and comprehensiveness 71%; only 67% were comfortable providing the output to patients. Mean scores were 4.29 (accuracy), 3.85 (comprehensiveness), 3.82 (comfort).
quote: However, GPT-4 had a decreased capacity to produce a comprehensive output leading some physicians to be uncomfortable providing the output to patients.

title: Evaluating the accuracy and reliability of large language models in assisting with pediatric differential diagnoses: A multicenter diagnostic study
outcome: Fine-tuned GPT-3 differential diagnosis accuracy compared with human physicians on same test set
effect: Model accuracy 87% (131/150) vs physicians 91%; P = .47, comparable performance; sensitivity 85%, specificity 90%, precision 88%, F1 0.87.
quote: The model’s performance was comparable to human physicians (accuracy 91%; P = .47).

title: Enhancing Public Healthcare with IoT and AI: A Comprehensive Study on Improving Dry Eye Disease Diagnosis
outcome: Accuracy of urgent versus non-urgent classification of simulated dry eye complaints, prompted vs non-prompted
effect: Accuracy rose from 80.1% without the specialized prompt to 99.6% with it, with longer response time. Missed and unnecessary escalations were not reported separately.
quote: A comparison between prompted and non-prompted queries reveals a significant accuracy increase from 80.1–99.6%.

title: Enhancing Public Healthcare with IoT and AI: A Comprehensive Study on Improving Dry Eye Disease Diagnosis
outcome: AI response accuracy with specialized prompting
effect: Prompted versus non-prompted queries increased accuracy from 80.1–99.6%.
quote: A comparison between prompted and non-prompted queries reveals a significant accuracy increase from 80.1–99.6%.

title: Enhancing Public Healthcare with IoT and AI: A Comprehensive Study on Improving Dry Eye Disease Diagnosis
outcome: user satisfaction dimensions
effect: SE satisfaction decreased 95.5 to 84.7; MQ satisfaction increased 73.4 to 96.7.
quote: In-depth analysis shows a decrease in SE satisfaction (95.5 to 84.7) and a substantial increase in MQ satisfaction (73.4 to 96.7) with prompted queries.

title: Enhancing Clinical Documentation Workflow with Ambient Artificial Intelligence: Clinician Perspectives on Work Burden, Burnout, and Job Satisfaction
outcome: Clinician-perceived documentation burden, after-hours documentation, burnout risk, and job satisfaction after ambient AI scribe
effect: Majority agreed the tool decreased documentation burden and after-hours documentation, reduced burnout risk, and increased job satisfaction; 48% agreed an additional patient could be seen.
quote: The majority of respondents agreed that the AI tool decreased documentation burden, decreased the time spent documenting outside clinical hours, reduced burnout risk, and increased job satisfaction, with 48% agreeing that an additional patient could be seen if needed.

title: Enhancing Clinical Documentation Workflow with Ambient Artificial Intelligence: Clinician Perspectives on Work Burden, Burnout, and Job Satisfaction
outcome: Whether ambient scribe benefit differed across clinician specialty or duration of use
effect: Specialty type and number of days using the tool did not significantly affect survey responses; ease of documentation OR 6.91 (95% CI 3.90 to 12.56).
quote: Clinician specialty type and number of days using the AI tool did not significantly affect survey responses.

title: Autonomous AI for diabetic eye disease at primary care improves ophthalmic access for at-risk patients
outcome: Distribution of ophthalmic access by patient subgroup between AI and standard-of-care referral pathways
effect: AI referral pathway patients were more likely to be Black (p < 0.001) and have hypertension (p = 0.001); no difference in presenting BCVA between pathways.
quote: However, patients from the AI referral pathway were more likely to be Black (p < 0.001) and have hypertension (p = 0.001), suggesting that deployment of autonomous AI is associated with improved ophthalmic access for patients with a higher baseline risk for poor DED outcome before vision loss has occurred.

title: Real-World Performance of Large Language Models in Emergency Department Chest Pain Triage and the development of MediGuide-14B
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and specificity for ACS in chest pain triage, LLMs versus human experts
effect: MediGuide-14B accuracy 87.52% and specificity 78.63%, versus human experts 86.37% accuracy and 89.26% specificity. Accuracy was comparable, but specificity was lower than the experts'.
quote: MediGuide-14B demonstrated the highest accuracy (87.52%) and specificity (78.63%), comparable to human experts (86.37% accuracy, 89.26% specificity).

title: Expert-Level Detection of Referable Glaucoma from Fundus Photographs in a Safety Net Population: The AI and Teleophthalmology in Los Angeles Initiative
outcome: Algorithm AUC/sensitivity/specificity compared with clinician graders on same test set
effect: Algorithm matched or exceeded all independent clinician graders (AUC 0.92 vs optometrist labels, 0.93 vs expert panel labels); grader sensitivity 0.33-0.99, specificity 0.68-0.98.
quote: Algorithm performance matched or exceeded that of all independent clinician graders in detecting patient-level referable glaucoma based on LAC DHS optometrist (AUC = 0.92) or expert panel (AUC = 0.93) reference labels.

title: Expert-Level Detection of Referable Glaucoma from Fundus Photographs in a Safety Net Population: The AI and Teleophthalmology in Los Angeles Initiative
outcome: Variability of clinician grader accuracy and dependence on reference label source
effect: Clinician grader sensitivity (0.33-0.99) and specificity (0.68-0.98) ranged widely, unrelated to experience (p ≥ 0.49), showing inconsistent ground truth from single graders.
quote: Clinician grader sensitivity (range: 0.33-0.99) and specificity (range: 0.68-0.98) ranged widely and did not correlate with years of experience (p ≥ 0.49).

title: Large Language Model Augmented Clinical Trial Screening
outcome: Comparison of GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 and prompting approaches on the same data
effect: GPT-4 median criterion accuracy 0.838 vs GPT-3.5 0.761; GPT-4 generally outperformed GPT-3.5 but at higher cost ($0.15–$0.27 vs $0.02–$0.03) and time (7.9–12.4 vs 1.4–3 min).
quote: LLM performance varies by prompt, with GPT-4 generally outperforming GPT-3.5, but at higher costs and longer processing times.

title: Enhancing Real-World Data Extraction in Clinical Research: Evaluating the Impact of the Implementation of Large Language Models in Hospital Settings
outcome: Data extraction accuracy of ChatGLM and LLaMA versus manual input on free-text forms
effect: Initial manual input accuracy for free-text forms was 99.59%, ChatGLM extraction accuracy 77.13%, and LLaMA 43.86%.
quote: The initial manual input accuracy for free-text forms was 99.59%, the ChatGLM data extraction accuracy was 77.13%, and the LLaMA data extraction accuracy was 43.86%.

title: Ubie Symptom Checker: A Clinical Vignette Simulation Study
outcome: Symptom checker Top-5 hit accuracy compared with physicians and comparator symptom checkers on same vignettes
effect: Ubie Top-5 hit accuracy 63.4%, Top-10 71.6%; compared favorably to the median physician hit accuracy and comparator symptom checkers.
quote: When compared to physicians and comparator SC’s that used the same clinical vignettes set, Ubie compared favorably to the median physician hit accuracy.

title: Evaluation of Vertigo-Related Information from Artificial Intelligence Chatbot
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4o vertigo responses (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level)
effect: Readability analysis showed higher difficulty in diagnostic texts; readability judged to need improvement. No numeric readability scores reported in the abstract.
quote: Readability analysis revealed higher difficulty in diagnostic texts.

title: Development and initial evaluation of a conversational agent for Alzheimer’s disease
outcome: Reference retrieval quality and perceived helpfulness in human evaluation of guideline-based agent answers
effect: Human evaluators found comprehension and completeness good, but reference retrieval and perceived helpfulness were not optimal.
quote: However, reference retrieval and perceived helpfulness of the CA reply was not optimal.

title: A Performance Evaluation of Large Language Model in Keratoconus: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4.0, Gemini, Copilot, Chatsonic, and Perplexity
outcome: Readability of chatbot answers to keratoconus questions versus recommended patient reading levels
effect: Chatbot readability often exceeded recommended levels; Gemini easiest to read, ChatGPT-3.5 and Perplexity most difficult; ARLC score 13.17±2.13 for 'What is Keratoconus?'
quote: However, their readability often exceeded recommended levels.

title: Large language models outperform traditional natural language processing methods in extracting patient-reported outcomes in IBD
outcome: Performance across sites (UCSF vs Stanford) for tNLP versus LLM extraction
effect: On Stanford external validation (n=250), tNLP models failed to generalize (61-62% accuracy) while GPT-4 maintained accuracies >90%.
quote: On external validation at Stanford (n=250), tNLP models failed to generalize (61-62% accuracy) while GPT-4 maintained accuracies >90%.
sample_unit: clinic notes (50 UCSF test, 250 Stanford external validation)

title: Large language models outperform traditional natural language processing methods in extracting patient-reported outcomes in IBD
outcome: Model performance differences across demographic and diagnosis subgroups (fairness assessment)
effect: No biases were detected based on demographics or diagnosis.
quote: No biases were detected based on demographics or diagnosis.
sample_unit: clinic notes (50 UCSF test, 250 Stanford external validation)

title: Receiving information on machine learning-based clinical decision support systems in psychiatric services increases staff trust in these systems: A randomized survey experiment
outcome: Staff trust and distrust in ML-based clinical decision support after receiving basic information versus controls
effect: Versus active control: trust +5% (95% CI 2%; 9%), p<0.001; distrust -4% (-7%; -1%), p=0.042. Versus blank control: trust +5% (2%; 11%), p=0.003; distrust -3% (-6%; -1%), p=0.021.
quote: Providing information on ML-based clinical decision support systems in hospital psychiatry may increase healthcare staff trust in such systems.

title: A survey of Large Language Model use in a hospital, research, and teaching campus
outcome: Prevalence of LLM use in work contexts among campus staff and students, ahead of governance
effect: Over 90% of respondents had heard of LLM tools and about two-thirds had used them in their work on campus; guidelines and governance are needed to keep up with practice.
quote: Our findings show LLM tools are already widely used on our campus.

title: Comparison of Large Language Models Versus Traditional Information Extraction Methods for Real World Evidence of Patient Symptomatology in Acute and Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2
outcome: LLM symptom extraction fairness across race and gender subgroups
effect: Fairness analysis found the LLM faces significant challenges related to demographic bias, though no numbers are given in the abstract.
quote: Our findings indicate that while LLMs can match the effectiveness of rule-based IE methods, they face significant challenges related to demographic bias and generalizability due to variability in training corpora.

title: Comparison of Large Language Models Versus Traditional Information Extraction Methods for Real World Evidence of Patient Symptomatology in Acute and Post-Acute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2
outcome: LLM generalization across corpora from different institutions
effect: Evaluation revealed overfitting and insufficient generalization, especially when models were trained predominantly on limited datasets with single annotator bias.
quote: This evaluation revealed overfitting and insufficient generalization, especially when models were trained predominantly on limited datasets with single annotator bias.

title: Utilizing AI-Generated Plain Language Summaries to Enhance Interdisciplinary Understanding of Ophthalmology Notes: A Randomized Trial
outcome: Error rate in LLM-generated summaries after ophthalmologist review and editing, and on independent over-read
effect: Error rate was 26% on initial ophthalmologist review and editing and 15% on independent over-read of edited PLSs; 84.9% of errors were low risk and 0% carried risk of severe harm or death.
quote: PLS error rate on initial ophthalmologist review and editing was 26%, and 15% on independent ophthalmologist over-read of edited PLSs.

title: Low Responsiveness of Machine Learning Models to Critical or Deteriorating Health Conditions
outcome: Model responsiveness to synthesized critical or deteriorating patient conditions in mortality prediction
effect: Models failed to recognize 66% of synthesized test cases involving injuries; in some instances failed to generate adequate mortality risk scores for all test cases; similar deficiencies in 5-year breast and lung cancer models.
quote: For in-hospital mortality prediction, the models tested using our synthesized cases fail to recognize 66% of the test cases involving injuries.
sample_unit: machine learning models (ten models across four datasets, two prediction tasks)

title: Low Responsiveness of Machine Learning Models to Critical or Deteriorating Health Conditions
outcome: Recognition of severely impaired medical conditions and rapidly deteriorating health by ML models
effect: Serious deficiencies in responsiveness: inability to recognize severely impaired conditions or rapid deterioration; 66% of injury cases missed in in-hospital mortality models.
quote: We identified serious deficiencies in the models’ responsiveness, i.e., the inability to recognize severely impaired medical conditions or rapidly deteriorating health.
sample_unit: machine learning models (ten models across four datasets, two prediction tasks)

title: The Robustness of Deep Learning Models to Adversarial Attacks in Lung X-ray Classification
outcome: Model accuracy on chest X-rays under adversarial attacks (FGSM, AutoAttack)
effect: All models experienced a decrease in accuracy after adversarial attacks; MobileNet was more robust than the other CNN-based models. Exact figures are not reported in the abstract.
quote: Our findings indicate that while all models experienced a decrease in accuracy after adversarial attacks, MobileNet consistently demonstrated superior robustness compared to other CNN-based models.

title: Systematic Characterization of the Effectiveness of Alignment in Large Language Models for Categorical Decisions
outcome: Post-alignment alignment performance
effect: Models with high pre-alignment ACI sometimes degraded post-alignment; no numeric ACI values reported in abstract.
quote: Notably, models that performed well, as measured by ACI, pre-alignment sometimes degraded post-alignment, and small changes in the target preference function led to large shifts in model rankings.

title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Large Language Models: A Comparative Study of RAG-enhanced vs. Human-Generated Medical Templates
outcome: Physician-rated accuracy and usefulness of RAG-grounded LLM templates versus human-generated templates
effect: LLM templates grounded in clinical guidelines scored higher on average for accuracy and usefulness than human templates; BERTScore showed high textual similarity. No non-RAG LLM comparator, no numbers in abstract.
quote: The LLM templates scored higher on average for both accuracy and usefulness when compared to human-generated templates.

title: An Artificial Intelligence Copilot System Helps Reduce Mortality Rates of Hemodialysis Patients
outcome: Three-month mortality in hemodialysis patients, AI-assisted intervention versus control, in a pragmatic randomized trial
effect: HEWIC-assisted care reduced three-month mortality by 38.3% (5,216 intervention vs 4,749 control patients, 58 centers), with a more pronounced effect in primary hospitals.
quote: Involving 9,965 hemodialysis patients (5,216 intervention and 4,749 control) from 58 dialysis centers, the trial indicates that HEWIC’s high-risk patient identification and treatment recommendation can help reduce the three-month mortality rate of hemodialysis patients by 38.3%, with a more pronounced effect in primary hospitals.

title: Physician- and Large Language Model-Generated Hospital Discharge Summaries: A Blinded, Comparative Quality and Safety Study
outcome: Blinded reviewer quality and preference for LLM versus physician discharge summary narratives
effect: Overall quality 3.67 vs 3.77 (p=0.213); preference p=0.270; LLM more concise and coherent but less comprehensive, with more errors (2.91 vs 1.82 per summary).
quote: Across 100 encounters, LLM- and physician-generated narratives were comparable in overall quality on a 1-5 Likert scale (average 3.67 [SD 0.49] vs 3.77 [SD 0.57], p=0.213) and reviewer preference (χ2 = 5.2, p=0.270).
sample_unit: inpatient hospital medicine encounters (discharge summary narratives)

title: Physician- and Large Language Model-Generated Hospital Discharge Summaries: A Blinded, Comparative Quality and Safety Study
outcome: Errors (inaccuracies, omissions, hallucinations) and potential harm in LLM-drafted discharge summaries
effect: LLM narratives averaged 2.91 errors per summary vs 1.82 for physicians; overall potential harm 0.84 vs 0.36 (p<0.001), though low (<1 on 0-7 scale).
quote: LLM-generated narratives contained more unique errors (average 2.91 [SD 2.54] errors per summary) than physician-generated narratives (1.82 [SD 1.94]).
sample_unit: inpatient hospital medicine encounters (discharge summary narratives)

title: Biomedical Text Normalization through Generative Modeling
outcome: Normalization accuracy (mean shortest SNOMED path length) of retrieval-grounded versus ungrounded LLM strategies
effect: RAGnorm was most effective on every dataset: mean shortest path length 0.21 (oncology), 0.58 (sampled), 0.90 (top terms). Micro F1 88.01 on TAC2017 task 4, surpassing all other models.
quote: We found that RAGnorm was the most effective throughout each dataset, achieving a mean shortest path length of 0.21 for the domain-specific dataset, 0.58 for the sampled dataset, and 0.90 for the top terms dataset.

title: End-to-End Machine Learning based Discrimination of Neoplastic and Non-neoplastic Intracerebral Hemorrhage on Computed Tomography
outcome: External-cohort performance before versus after fine-tuning on a small local subset
effect: External AUC 68% and Acc 66%; after fine-tuning on a small external subset, AUC and accuracy 70% (sensitivity 70%; specificity 71%).
quote: Fine-tuning on a selected small subset of the external cohort enhanced performance, achieving an AUC and accuracy of 70% (sensitivity 70%; specificity 71%).

title: End-to-End Machine Learning based Discrimination of Neoplastic and Non-neoplastic Intracerebral Hemorrhage on Computed Tomography
outcome: Performance drop from internal test set to external validation cohort
effect: Internal test AUC 85%, Acc 86% (sens 80%, spec 93%); external cohort (n=58) AUC 68%, Acc 66% (sens 64%, spec 67%).
quote: On the external validation cohort (n=58), the classification pipeline achieved an AUC of 68% and Acc of 66% (sensitivity 64%; specificity 67%).

title: Responses of AI Chatbots to Testosterone Replacement Therapy: Patient's Beware!
outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of chatbot testosterone replacement therapy answers for patients
effect: Even the most readable chatbot, Perplexity AI, produced text at about an eleventh-grade level. ChatGPT and Perplexity differed significantly on FRES and FKGL.
quote: Despite Perplexity scoring higher in readability, the generated text still maintained an eleventh-grade complexity.

title: Reducing Surgeons’ Routine Task Burden, Enhancing Surgical Decision Making, and Ensuring Patient Safety Using SurgeryLLM
outcome: Whether RAG output incorporated evidence-based surgical guideline knowledge for patient-specific data
effect: Abstract reports SurgeryLLM demonstrably incorporated domain-specific knowledge from current evidence-based surgical guidelines; no numeric results are given in the text.
quote: SurgeryLLM, a large language model framework using Retrieval Augmented Generation demonstrably incorporated domain-specific knowledge from current evidence-based surgical guidelines when presented with patient-specific data.

title: Real-World Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chatbots for Providing Sexual Health Information: A Consensus Study Using Clinical Queries
outcome: Chatbot performance compared with nurse responses on the same sexual health questions
effect: Chatbots compared with human clinicians (nurses) by blinded expert panel; chatbots showed potential as adjuncts but all were susceptible to generating incorrect information.
quote: However, all AI chatbots showed susceptibility to generating incorrect information.

title: Comparative evaluation of large-language models and purpose-built software for medical record de-identification
outcome: Word-level PII redaction precision and recall of de-identification tools versus dual clinician annotation
effect: Best tool Azure had F1 0.933, precision 0.916, recall 0.950. Fine-tuned AnonCAT recall was 0.787 and GPT-4 ten-shot recall was 0.874, so some PII was missed. Names and dates were consistently redacted.
quote: The best performing redaction tool was the Microsoft Azure de-identification service: F1 0.933 (0.928-0.938), precision 0.916 (0.930-0.922), recall 0.950 (0.942-0.957).

title: Extracting Pulmonary Embolism Diagnoses from Radiology Impressions Using GPT-4o: A Large Language Model Evaluation Study
outcome: GPT-4o versus fine-tuned Clinical Longformer baseline on PE extraction from impressions, same validation data
effect: GPT-4o outperformed Clinical Longformer on two metrics: sensitivity 1.0 (95% CI 1.0-1.0; p<0.001) and F1 0.975 (95% CI 0.9495-0.9947; p<0.001) on validation set.
quote: GPT-4o outperformed the Clinical Longformer in two of the metrics, achieving a sensitivity of 1.0 (95% CI: [1.0, 1.0]; Wilcoxon test, p < 0.001) and an F1 score of 0.975 (95% CI: [0.9495, 0.9947]; Wilcoxon test, p < 0.001) across the validation dataset.

title: Extracting Pulmonary Embolism Diagnoses from Radiology Impressions Using GPT-4o: A Large Language Model Evaluation Study
outcome: Post-deployment performance of deployed GPT-4o on 200 operational records
effect: Sensitivity 1.0 (95% CI 1.0-1.0), specificity 0.94 (95% CI 0.8913-0.9804), F1 0.97 (95% CI 0.9479-0.9908) on 200 operational records.
quote: Post-deployment evaluations also showed strong performance of the deployed GPT-4o model with a sensitivity of 1.0 (95% CI: [1.0, 1.0]), a specificity of 0.94 (95% CI: [0.8913, 0.9804]), and an F1 score of 0.97 (95% CI: [0.9479, 0.9908]).

title: Artificial Intelligence-based chatbots in providing space maintainer related information for pediatric patients and parents: A comparative study
outcome: Readability of chatbot answers on pediatric space maintainers (FRES, FKRGL)
effect: Readability scores for both ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 required college-degree education, above typical patient/parent reading levels.
quote: The readability scores seemed to require an education of a college degree and the similarity levels were lesser than 10% for both chatbots whit a high originality.

title: The Guideline for Building Fair Multimodal Medical AI with Large Vision-Language Model
outcome: Fairness impact of including demographic and clinical metadata as inputs to multimodal medical AI
effect: Indiscriminate inclusion of all metadata may negatively impact fairness for protected subgroups. Analysis covered dermatology, radiology and ophthalmology (gender, age, skin tone) and more than 20 clinical attributes in dermatology.
quote: Our findings reveal that the indiscriminate inclusion of all metadata may negatively impact fairness for protected subgroups and show how multimodal AI utilizes demographic information in metadata to influence fairness.

title: Socio-Demographic Biases in Medical Decision-Making by Large Language Models: A Large-Scale Multi-Model Analysis
outcome: Change in LLM triage, testing, treatment, and mental health recommendations when vignette socio-demographic identifiers varied vs control
effect: Marginalized groups (Black, unhoused, LGBTQIA+) more likely to get urgent care, invasive procedures, or mental health assessments vs control (p<0.05 for all comparisons); significant biases across all nine models regardless of type or size.
quote: We find that marginalized groups—including Black, unhoused, and LGBTQIA+ individuals—are more likely to receive recommendations for urgent care, invasive procedures, or mental health assessments compared to the control group (p < 0.05 for all comparisons).
sample_unit: LLM responses (500 ED vignettes x 24 versions x 9 models x 4 questions)

title: Socio-Demographic Biases in Medical Decision-Making by Large Language Models: A Large-Scale Multi-Model Analysis
outcome: Subgroup differences in LLM clinical recommendations across 23 socio-demographic groups
effect: Significant biases across all models, proprietary and open source, regardless of size; most pronounced in mental health assessment recommendations.
quote: We observed significant biases across all models, both proprietary and open source regardless of the model’s size.
sample_unit: LLM responses (500 ED vignettes x 24 versions x 9 models x 4 questions)

title: Socio-Demographic Biases in Medical Decision-Making by Large Language Models: A Large-Scale Multi-Model Analysis

outcome: Performance drop when applying AI in a setting differing from its training setting
effect: AI performance in low-prevalence health screening was poorer than expected, suggesting experimental/regulatory performance may not translate to real-world practice.
quote: The technical prowess of AI demonstrated in experimental settings and approved by regulatory bodies may not directly translate to real-world practice, especially where the demand for AI assistance is highest.

title: Multicentre external validation of a commercial artificial intelligence software to analyse chest radiographs in health screening environments with low disease prevalence
outcome: External AI accuracy in low-prevalence CXR screening
quote: The AUROC, sensitivity, and specificity of the AI were 0.648 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.630-0.665), 35.3% (CI, 24.7-47.8), and 94.2% (CI, 93.3-95.0), respectively.

title: Multicentre external validation of a commercial artificial intelligence software to analyse chest radiographs in health screening environments with low disease prevalence
outcome: Standalone AI lesion detection

title: Multicentre external validation of a commercial artificial intelligence software to analyse chest radiographs in health screening environments with low disease prevalence
