title: Clinical Implementation of an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Magnetic Resonance-Derived Measurement of Total Kidney Volume
outcome: Difference between AI segmentation and radiologist/technologist-edited segmentation in TKV after clinician review
effect: Of 170 reviewed cases, 84 were manually edited; AI TKV output showed a small mean volume difference of -3.3% versus edited; disease class differed in five cases.
quote: Of manually edited cases (n=84), the AI-algorithm TKV output showed a small mean volume difference of -3.3%.

title: Clinical Implementation of an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Magnetic Resonance-Derived Measurement of Total Kidney Volume
outcome: Whether validated AI performance was preserved when implemented in local clinical practice
effect: Algorithm showed high agreement and was noninferior to interobserver variability; performance preserved when implementation environment matched development conditions.
quote: Performance of an AI algorithm in real-life clinical practice can be preserved if there is careful development and validation and if the implementation environment closely matches the development conditions.

title: Generalizable and robust deep learning algorithm for atrial fibrillation diagnosis across geography, ages and sexes
outcome: AF event detection performance across sex and age subgroups
effect: Performance was higher for female than male and higher for young adults (<61 years) than other age groups; attributed to higher atrial flutter prevalence in lower-performing groups. Overall generalized well.
quote: For the task of event detection ArNet2 performance was higher for female than male, higher for young adults (less than 61 years old) than other age groups and across geography.

title: Generalizable and robust deep learning algorithm for atrial fibrillation diagnosis across geography, ages and sexes
outcome: AF detection performance across four geographic test centers
effect: Model generalized well across geography overall, with better performance on USA and China test sets than Israel and Japan; variation explained by atrial flutter prevalence.
quote: Finally, ArNet2 shows better performance for the test sets from the USA and China.

title: How smart is artificial intelligence in organs delineation? Testing a CE and FDA-approved Deep-Learning tool using multiple expert contours delineated on planning CT images
outcome: Local external validation of CE/FDA-approved auto-segmentation against expert contours and similarity thresholds
effect: Unedited MV contours needed adjustment for many OARs; median DSC of adjusted versus MV contours was above 0.8 for all organs except esophagus and glottis in H&N; DSC and MDA thresholds (0.8, 3 mm) used.
quote: In this study, we evaluated the performance of a DL-based auto-segmentation algorithm on local data, representing an external validation.

title: How smart is artificial intelligence in organs delineation? Testing a CE and FDA-approved Deep-Learning tool using multiple expert contours delineated on planning CT images
outcome: Contouring time and inter-observer agreement with versus without AI assistance
effect: Median manual contouring 25.0 min versus 12.3 min for retrieving and editing DL contours (p<0.001); manually adjusted DL contours showed better inter-RO agreement than manual ones.
quote: The overall time for retrieving VOIs and their modification was 12.3 minutes (1.9-48.8), resulting in statistically significantly lower than that of the manual contouring (p<0.001).

title: How smart is artificial intelligence in organs delineation? Testing a CE and FDA-approved Deep-Learning tool using multiple expert contours delineated on planning CT images
outcome: Comparison of DL auto-contours and DL-assisted contours versus manual expert contours on same CT data
effect: DSC of adjusted MV contours statistically significantly higher than manual ones overall; median DSC 0.99/0.98 versus 0.83/0.81 by slice thickness.
quote: Overall, the DSC values obtained in the MD&MV subgroup were statistically significantly higher than MD one.

title: How smart is artificial intelligence in organs delineation? Testing a CE and FDA-approved Deep-Learning tool using multiple expert contours delineated on planning CT images
outcome: DSC performance across scanners, slice thicknesses and contrast use
effect: DSC of adjusted contours higher than manual irrespective of slice thickness, scanner, and contrast; slight but significant DSC drop from 0.99 to 0.98 with thicker slices in adjusted group.
quote: Also, in these subsets of patients, the DSC values obtained in the MD&MV subgroup were statistically significantly higher than MD one, irrespective of slice thickness and CT scanner (see Supplementary Material Figures S1, S2 ).

title: How smart is artificial intelligence in organs delineation? Testing a CE and FDA-approved Deep-Learning tool using multiple expert contours delineated on planning CT images
outcome: Radiation oncologist satisfaction with the tool on Likert scale and correlation with time saved
effect: 44% rated 4 and 43% rated 5; satisfaction correlated with time saved (p<0.001); scores higher for seniors than juniors (p=0.01).
quote: Overall, the system was generally appreciated by ROs, with 44% of vote 4 (well done) and 43% of vote 5 (very well done) correlated with the spared time for the delineation correction after MV automatic contouring (p<0.001).

title: How smart is artificial intelligence in organs delineation? Testing a CE and FDA-approved Deep-Learning tool using multiple expert contours delineated on planning CT images
outcome: Inter-observer agreement of delineated volumes of interest
effect: Manually adjusted AI volumes showed better inter-agreement than manually segmented volumes alone, with retrieving and modification time of 12.3 minutes versus 25.0 minutes for manual contouring (p<0.001).
quote: The relative volume differences and similarity indexes suggested a better inter-agreement of manually adjusted DL-based VOIs than manually segmented ones.

title: Feasibility of a deep-learning based anatomical region labeling tool for Cone-Beam Computed Tomography scans in radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Classification accuracy of CNN ARL versus simpler SVM baseline on same test data
effect: ARL achieved 99.2% overall accuracy on the test dataset versus 91.5% for the SVM baseline.
quote: ARL achieved an overall accuracy of 99.2% on the test dataset, outperforming the SVM (91.5% accuracy).

title: 40 years of actigraphy in sleep medicine and current state of the art algorithms
outcome: Sleep-wake classification and sleep outcome accuracy of complex vs simple algorithms against PSG on the same dataset
effect: Simple regression-based and heuristic algorithms showed slightly superior performance to recent complex ML/DL algorithms in sleep-wake classification and sleep outcome estimation.
quote: Despite the inclusion of recently published complex algorithms, simple regression-based and heuristic algorithms demonstrated slightly superior performance in sleep-wake classification and sleep outcome estimation.

title: 40 years of actigraphy in sleep medicine and current state of the art algorithms
outcome: Whether complex AI outperforms simpler methods on sleep scoring
effect: Complex ML/DL models did not outperform simple regression/heuristic algorithms; simpler methods were slightly superior and complex models seemed to generalize poorly.
quote: The performance of complex machine learning and deep learning models seem to suffer from poor generalization.

title: Artificial intelligence guided physician directive improves head and neck planning quality and practice Uniformity: A prospective study
outcome: Radiotherapy plan achievability, quality, and planning efficiency with versus without AI-guided physician directives
effect: Achievability increased from 52.9% to 80.4%; first-plan acceptance improved from 63.3% to 90%; maximum iterations decreased from 4 to 2; four organs-at-risk had statistically significant dose reductions (range 4.3 to 15.2 Gy).
quote: As seen in Fig. 4 a, there is a significant increase in plan achievability pre- and post-AI guidance, from 52.9% to 80.4%.

title: Artificial intelligence guided physician directive improves head and neck planning quality and practice Uniformity: A prospective study
outcome: plan achievability with vs without AI
effect: Plan achievability increased significantly from 52.9% before AI guidance to 80.4% after AI guidance.
quote: As seen in Fig. 4 a, there is a significant increase in plan achievability pre- and post-AI guidance, from 52.9% to 80.4%.

title: Integrating economic considerations into cutpoint selection may help align clinical decision support toward value-based healthcare
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Net monetary benefit of cost-benefit-based cutpoint selection versus Youden and other methods in simulations
effect: Value-optimizing cutpoint best in 86% of ICU simulations (median INB $0 vs about -$1412 to -$1478 for ROC-based methods); in falls, cost-based methods comparable (INB ~$15-16) and Youden 3% best.
quote: Overall, the threshold which maximized NMB was most commonly the value-optimizing method proposed in this study that considered downstream costs and effects in comparison to other approaches to determining model thresholds.

title: Prognostic Value of Machine-Learning-Based PRAISE Score for Ischemic and Bleeding Events in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
venue: Journal of the American Heart Association
outcome: External discrimination and calibration of PRAISE on local ACS PCI cohort versus reference outcomes
effect: C-statistics for death, MI, and major bleeding were 0.75, 0.61, and 0.62; observed to expected ratios 0.427, 0.260, and 0.106, showing poor calibration and limited discrimination locally.
quote: The PRAISE score showed limited potential for risk prediction in our validation cohort with acute coronary syndrome.

title: Prognostic Value of Machine-Learning-Based PRAISE Score for Ischemic and Bleeding Events in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention
venue: Journal of the American Heart Association
outcome: PRAISE compared with GRACE 2.0, PRECISE-DAPT, and PARIS on discrimination, calibration, reclassification, net benefit
effect: PRAISE displayed slightly greater net benefit than GRACE for 1-year death risk at 5%-10% threshold; overall performance limited.
quote: Based on the decision curve analysis, the PRAISE score displayed a slightly greater net benefit for the 1-year risk of death (5%-10%) than the GRACE score did.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Classification of Adamantinomatous Craniopharyngioma from Preoperative MRI
outcome: Accuracy and abstention rate when model defers uncertain cases
effect: Abstention mechanism raised accuracy from 80.8% to 95.5% with a 34.2% (n=12) abstention rate; 10/12 abstained cases were NOTACP.
quote: Specifically, we observed an accuracy of 95.5%, sensitivity of 0.933, specificity of 0.833, FNR of 0.067, and FPR of 0.125.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Deep Learning Classification of Adamantinomatous Craniopharyngioma from Preoperative MRI
outcome: Whether calibrated predictive uncertainty (variance) identifies uncertain predictions
effect: Mean predictive values were uninformative, but predictive variance separated classes; combining ArgMax and variance-based predictions gave 95.5% accuracy versus 68.6% for ArgMax alone.
quote: Therefore, the variance of the predictive distributions is informative in our classification task.

title: An adversarial training framework for mitigating algorithmic biases in clinical machine learning
outcome: Fairness (equalized odds) and screening performance after adversarial bias mitigation
effect: Adversarial training improved outcome fairness while retaining clinically effective screening performance (negative predictive values >0.98).
quote: Using the statistical definition of equalized odds, we show that adversarial training improves outcome fairness, while still achieving clinically-effective screening performances (negative predictive values >0.98).

title: Human visual explanations mitigate bias in AI-based assessment of surgeon skills
outcome: Underskilling and overskilling bias of surgical AI across surgeon sub-cohorts
effect: SAIS exhibited underskilling and overskilling bias at different rates across surgeon sub-cohorts; no numeric rates in the abstract.
quote: We show that SAIS exhibits an underskilling bias, erroneously downgrading surgical performance, and an overskilling bias, erroneously upgrading surgical performance, at different rates across surgeon sub-cohorts.

title: Human visual explanations mitigate bias in AI-based assessment of surgeon skills
outcome: Effect of bias mitigation strategies on subgroup bias and overall AI performance
effect: Baseline strategies mitigated bias inconsistently, whereas TWIX mitigated underskilling and overskilling bias while also improving performance across hospitals.
quote: We show that whereas baseline strategies inconsistently mitigate algorithmic bias, TWIX can effectively mitigate the underskilling and overskilling bias while simultaneously improving the performance of these AI systems across hospitals.

title: Evaluating equity in performance of an electronic health record-based 6-month mortality risk model to trigger palliative care consultation: a retrospective model validation analysis
outcome: Model accuracy, FPR, FNR across race, ethnicity, age, insurance and SES subgroups
effect: Black vs non-Hispanic white: accuracy higher (0.051), FPR lower (-0.060), FNR higher (0.049); similar pattern for Hispanic, younger, Medicaid/missing insurance, low SES patients; no consistent c-statistic, ICI or Brier differences.
quote: A similar pattern was observed among patients who were Hispanic, younger, with Medicaid/missing insurance, or living in low SES zip codes.

title: Evaluating equity in performance of an electronic health record-based 6-month mortality risk model to trigger palliative care consultation: a retrospective model validation analysis
outcome: Subgroup performance and fairness metrics on local retrospective data before deployment
effect: Subgroup analysis revealed higher FNR and lower FPR for black, Hispanic, younger, Medicaid/missing insurance, and low-SES patients, despite no consistent differences in c-statistic, ICI or Brier Score.
quote: An EHR-based mortality risk model was less likely to identify some marginalised patients as potentially benefiting from palliative care, with younger age pinpointed as a possible mechanism.

title: Evaluating the generalizability of deep learning image classification algorithms to detect middle ear disease using otoscopy
outcome: Internal versus external validation AUC for detecting middle ear disease on otoscopic images
effect: Mean internal AUC 0.95 (95%CI 0.80-1.00) versus external AUC 0.76 (95%CI 0.61-0.91); mean difference -0.19, p ≤ 0.04.
quote: Overall, external performance was significantly lower than internal performance (mean difference in AUC: -0.19, p ≤ 0.04).

title: Evaluating the generalizability of deep learning image classification algorithms to detect middle ear disease using otoscopy
outcome: Performance across three sites (Turkey, Chile, USA) when tested on external cohorts
effect: External performance across independent site cohorts dropped to mean AUC 0.76 from internal 0.95.
quote: However, performance was reduced when tested on external otoscopic images not used for training (mean AUC: 0.76, 95%CI: 0.61-0.91).

title: Self-Aware SGD: Reliable Incremental Adaptation Framework for Clinical AI Models
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
outcome: Reliability of incremental model updates under label noise and distribution shift with a sanity-check filter
effect: Self-aware SGD, which filters unreliable gradient updates, is reported to give reliable incremental updates under distribution shift with label noise. No numbers are reported in the abstract.
quote: Experimental evaluations on the Oxford University Hospital datasets highlight that self-aware SGD can provide reliable incremental updates for overcoming distribution shifts in challenging conditions induced by label noise.

title: Utility of an Artificial Intelligence Enabled Electrocardiogram for Risk Assessment in Liver Transplant Candidates
outcome: AI-ECG performance in liver transplant evaluation patients versus general population, and by QTc
effect: Performance in LT evaluation patients was similar to the general population but lower with prolonged QTc; AUROC 0.69 for post-transplant AF and 0.69 for later low LVEF.
quote: The performance of AI-ECG in patients undergoing LT evaluation is similar to that in a general population but was lower in the presence of prolonged QTc.

title: Deep learning based automatic detection algorithm for acute intracranial haemorrhage: a pivotal randomized clinical trial
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of reviewers with versus without AI assistance for intracranial haemorrhage on CT
effect: Patient-wise accuracy 0.9703 with AI vs 0.9471 without (p<0.0001); largest gain in non-radiologist physicians; neuroradiologists' gain not significant.
quote: Brain CT interpretation with AI assistance results in significantly higher diagnostic accuracy than that without AI assistance (0.9703 vs. 0.9471, p < 0.0001, patient-wise).
sample_unit: patients (brain CT cases read by 9 reviewers with and without AI)

title: Machine learning-based automatic proton therapy planning: Impact of post-processing and dose-mimicking in plan robustness
outcome: KBP-generated IMPT plan quality compared with manually generated dosimetrist plans on same patients
effect: Nominal doses from the four KBP pipelines achieved comparable target coverage and improved dose to organs at risk compared to manual plans; NPP-RSM gave best robustness/OAR sparing trade-off.
quote: Nominal doses from the four KBP pipelines showed promising results achieving comparable target coverage and improved dose to organs at risk (OARs) compared to the manual plans.

title: Machine learning-based automatic proton therapy planning: Impact of post-processing and dose-mimicking in plan robustness
outcome: Plan robustness under worst-case scenarios for KBP pipelines
effect: Too optimistic post-processing compromised robustness; even with RSM, 65% of patients did not achieve expected robustness levels.
quote: Even though RSM seemed to partially compensate for the lack of robustness in the PP plans, still 65% of the patients did not achieve the expected robustness levels.

title: Collaborative strategies for deploying artificial intelligence to complement physician diagnoses of acute respiratory distress syndrome
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI-first strategy deferring uncertain cases to physicians vs AI alone or physician alone
effect: AI deferring to physician if uncertain: accuracy 0.869 (0.835-0.903) vs AI alone 0.847 and physician alone 0.808; physician review burden only 20.7%.
quote: The physician-aided AI strategy, which defers the diagnosis to physicians only if the AI model is uncertain, resulted in improved diagnostic accuracy than both physician- and AI-alone.

title: Collaborative strategies for deploying artificial intelligence to complement physician diagnoses of acute respiratory distress syndrome
outcome: Whether AI confidence/uncertainty corresponds to accuracy and can be used to defer
effect: AI accuracy rose with confidence; accuracy was 0.596 in AI-uncertain images, where physicians reached 0.698, enabling deferral.
quote: The AI model’s accuracy increased as its confidence increased, suggesting that the AI model is capable of recognizing when it is uncertain (green line in Fig. 1c ).

title: Collaborative strategies for deploying artificial intelligence to complement physician diagnoses of acute respiratory distress syndrome
outcome: Accuracy of physician-AI collaboration strategies versus physician alone and AI alone
effect: Collaboration strategies achieved 0.824-0.871 accuracy vs physician alone 0.808; physician-aided AI beat physician alone for 8/9 physicians, significantly for 3/9. Overreliance not assessed; physicians not shown AI output.
quote: For 8/9 physicians the physician-aided AI strategy outperformed the physician’s alone accuracy.

title: Collaborative strategies for deploying artificial intelligence to complement physician diagnoses of acute respiratory distress syndrome
outcome: AI model accuracy compared with physicians on the same chest X-rays
effect: AI accuracy 0.847 (0.806–0.887) vs physicians 0.808 (0.767–0.85), p<0.05; sensitivity 0.789 vs 0.727.
quote: Overall, the deep learning-based AI system had significantly higher accuracy in detecting ARDS images compared to physicians (0.847 [95% CI 0.806–0.887] vs. 0.808 [95% CI 0.767–0.85], p value of < 0.05 using the one-sided bootstrapped two-sample hypothesis testing) (Table 2 ).

title: Collaborative strategies for deploying artificial intelligence to complement physician diagnoses of acute respiratory distress syndrome
outcome: Accuracy when physicians review only AI-uncertain cases versus all cases
effect: Physician review of only 20.8% of X-rays gave accuracy 0.869, near the weighted average requiring review of all (0.871); AI-only 0.847. Accuracy fell to 0.596 for AI in AI-uncertain cases.
quote: The weighted average of physician and AI model only marginally exceeded that of the physician-aided AI strategy, and would require physicians to review every chest X-ray.

title: Hurdles to Artificial Intelligence Deployment: Noise in Schemas and "Gold" Labels
outcome: Inter-radiologist agreement on CheXpert test set labels and reliability of majority-vote ground truth
effect: Agreement was high for pneumothorax and medical devices (>90%) but low for pneumonia and consolidation, where majority-vote ground truth was unreliable and depended on which radiologists annotated. Schema overlap across datasets and vendor was <50%.
quote: Among low agreement classes (pneumonia, consolidation), the labels assigned as "ground truth" were unreliable, suggesting that the result of majority voting is highly dependent on which group of radiologists is assigned to annotation.
sample_unit: radiologist annotations on the CheXpert test set and label schemas from two public datasets and a vendor

title: Towards greater neuroimaging classification transparency via the integration of explainability methods and confidence estimation approaches
outcome: Effect of confidence estimation methods on stability of gradient-based explanations
effect: MCD often adversely affects model gradients, while MCBN does not. Many participant-level differences were found between regular explanations and explanation distributions from combined approaches.
quote: We find that MCD often adversely affects model gradients, making it ill-suited for integration with gradient-based explainability methods.

title: Clinical Impact of a Sepsis Alert System Plus Electronic Sepsis Navigator Using the Epic Sepsis Prediction Model in the Emergency Department
outcome: Time to initial antimicrobial, SPM alert plus navigator vs SIRS-based alert sites
effect: Unadjusted 3.33 h at site A vs 3.22 h at sites B-D (p = 0.437); after matching weights, no difference versus contemporaneous SIRS sites. There was a 2.87 h improvement only versus site A historical data.
quote: After adjustment using matching weights, there was no difference in time from threshold SPM score to initial antimicrobial between contemporaneous sites.

title: Clinical Impact of a Sepsis Alert System Plus Electronic Sepsis Navigator Using the Epic Sepsis Prediction Model in the Emergency Department
outcome: Time from emergency department arrival to initial antimicrobial delivery
effect: Time to antimicrobials: 3.33 h at site A versus 3.22 h at sites B-D (p = 0.437); adjusted improvement versus site A historical was 2.87 h (p < 0.001).
quote: Implementation of an electronic sepsis alert system plus navigator using the Epic SPM showed no difference in time to initial antimicrobial delivery between the contemporaneous SPM alert plus sepsis navigator site and the SIRS-based electronic alert sites within the same health care system.

title: Explainable artificial intelligence incorporated with domain knowledge diagnosing early gastric neoplasms under white light endoscopy
outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in multi-reader multi-case study
effect: With ENDOANGEL-ED's assistance, endoscopist accuracy significantly improved (70.61% vs. 79.63%, p < 0.001).
quote: With ENDOANGEL-ED's assistance, the accuracy of endoscopists significantly improved (70.61% vs. 79.63%, p < 0.001).
sample_unit: endoscopists (man-machine comparison); dataset of 4482 images and 296 videos from 3279 patients

title: Explainable artificial intelligence incorporated with domain knowledge diagnosing early gastric neoplasms under white light endoscopy
outcome: AI accuracy compared with 77 endoscopists on same videos
effect: ENDOANGEL-ED accuracy higher than all endoscopists in internal (81.10% vs. 70.61%, p<0.001) and external videos (88.24% vs. 78.49%, p<0.001).
quote: In man-machine comparison, the accuracy of ENDOANGEL-ED was significantly higher than that of all endoscopists in internal (81.10% vs. 70.61%, p < 0.001) and external videos (88.24% vs. 78.49%, p < 0.001).
sample_unit: endoscopists (man-machine comparison); dataset of 4482 images and 296 videos from 3279 patients

title: Optical Biopsy of Dysplasia in Barrett's Oesophagus Assisted by Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Gastroenterologist sensitivity and accuracy with versus without AI assistance at follow-up; overreliance assessed
effect: AI-assisted gastroenterologists had higher sensitivity (+20.0%, p=0.025) and accuracy (+12.22%, p=0.050) than unassisted ones at follow-up; untrained users showed reduced reliance on AI after training.
quote: When tested at 23.3 (±9.1) days after training, AI-assisted gastroenterologists maintained higher sensitivity (+20.0% (3.14–36.86), p = 0.025) and accuracy (+12.22% (0.03–24.48), p = 0.050) for recognizing dysplasia than the unassisted gastroenterologists.

title: Optical Biopsy of Dysplasia in Barrett's Oesophagus Assisted by Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Clinician diagnostic performance with AI support versus without, compared with AI alone
effect: After cross-over, gastroenterologists with AI exceeded their own sensitivity (+24.45%, p=0.020) and accuracy (+13.33%, p=0.039) and outperformed the AI model alone on sensitivity (+12.89%, p=0.024).
quote: Additionally, they outperformed the sensitivity of the AI model alone (+12.89% (2.11–23.67), p = 0.024) ( Figure 4 D).

title: Optical Biopsy of Dysplasia in Barrett's Oesophagus Assisted by Artificial Intelligence
outcome: AI-assisted versus unassisted clinicians
effect: AI-assisted follow-up sensitivity 91.11% vs 71.11%; accuracy 82.78% vs 70.56%.
quote: AI-assisted gastroenterologists scored substantially better than unassisted gastroenterologists in establishing an optical biopsy of Barrett’s-associated dysplasia through EC.

title: Optical Biopsy of Dysplasia in Barrett's Oesophagus Assisted by Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Dysplasia detection sensitivity of AI-assisted gastroenterologists versus standalone AI
effect: AI-assisted gastroenterologists outperformed the sensitivity of the AI model alone (+12.89% [95% CI 2.11–23.67], p = 0.024).
quote: Additionally, they outperformed the sensitivity of the AI model alone (+12.89% (2.11–23.67), p = 0.024) ( Figure 4 D).

title: A Multilingual Chatbot Can Effectively Engage Arthroplasty Patients Who Have Limited English Proficiency
outcome: Chatbot conversational engagement in LEP versus English-primary-language patients
effect: No difference in engagement between LEP and EPL patients (12.3 vs 12.2 text responses, P = .959).
quote: There was no difference in the conversational engagement between LEP patients and those with English as their primary language (EPL) (12.3 versus 12.2 text responses, P = .959).

title: Personalised recommendations for hospitalised patients with Acute Kidney Injury using a Kidney Action Team (KAT-AKI): protocol and early data of a randomised controlled trial
outcome: Clinician disagreement with electronic AKI diagnoses leading to exclusion
effect: KAT clinicians disagreed with electronic AKI diagnoses in 20.7% of those screened; this was the most common reason for exclusion.
quote: KAT clinicians’ disagreement with the electronic AKI diagnosis (20.7% of those screened) was the most common reason for exclusion.

title: Advanced Care Planning for Hospitalized Patients Following Clinician Notification of Patient Mortality by a Machine Learning Algorithm
outcome: Documented goals-of-care discussions after high-risk notification with prescribed action
effect: Intervention patients were 5 times more likely to have documented GOCDs by discharge (OR 5.11, 95% CI 1.93-13.42; P = .001). GOCDs also occurred earlier: median 4 vs 16 days (P < .001).
quote: Patients in the intervention group from preintervention to postintervention period were associated with being 5 times more likely to have documented GOCDs (OR, 5.11 [95% CI, 1.93 to 13.42]; P = .001) by discharge compared with matched controls, and GOCD occurred significantly earlier in the hospitalization in the intervention patients as compared with matched controls (median, 4 [95% CI, 3 to 6] days vs 16 [95% CI, 15 to not applicable] days; P < .001).

title: Advanced Care Planning for Hospitalized Patients Following Clinician Notification of Patient Mortality by a Machine Learning Algorithm
outcome: GOCD intervention effect in Black vs White patient subgroups
effect: Similar findings observed for Black and White patient subgroups.
quote: Similar findings were observed for Black patient and White patient subgroups.

title: Volume of hyperintense inflammation (VHI): A quantitative imaging biomarker of inflammation load in spondyloarthritis, enabled by human-machine cooperation
outcome: Inter-observer segmentation overlap (Dice) with versus without AI-assisted human-machine workflow
effect: Median Dice improved to 0.84 with the human-machine workflow versus 0.53–0.56 inter-reader for purely manual segmentation, an increase of 28–31%.
quote: Using the human-machine workflow, the median Dice scores improved to 0.84, representing an increase of 28–31% compared to pure manual segmentation.

title: Volume of hyperintense inflammation (VHI): A quantitative imaging biomarker of inflammation load in spondyloarthritis, enabled by human-machine cooperation
outcome: Model failure on atypical marrow not represented in training data; small single-site test set
effect: Disease-region model failed in 3 of 19 further subjects with abnormal bone marrow (high fat or sclerosis) not present in training data; test set only 2 subjects.
quote: The model failed in three subjects, each of whom was found to have abnormal bone marrow (high fat content or extensive sclerosis, which were not present in the training dataset).

title: Volume of hyperintense inflammation (VHI): A quantitative imaging biomarker of inflammation load in spondyloarthritis, enabled by human-machine cooperation
outcome: expert cleaning of preliminary AI segmentations
effect: Cleaned human-machine Dice was higher than preliminary non-cleaned overlap; preliminary overlap was 0.60/0.55 for Readers 1/2.
quote: The inter-observer Dice for the two readers using the human-machine workflow was substantially higher than the overlap between each reader and the preliminary, non-cleaned segmentation (0.60 / 0.55 for Readers 1 and 2 respectively).

title: Volume of hyperintense inflammation (VHI): A quantitative imaging biomarker of inflammation load in spondyloarthritis, enabled by human-machine cooperation
outcome: inter-observer segmentation overlap with and without human cleaning
effect: Dice score was 0.84 with human-machine workflow versus 0.60 and 0.55 overlap between readers and preliminary non-cleaned segmentations
quote: The inter-observer Dice for the two readers using the human-machine workflow was substantially higher than the overlap between each reader and the preliminary, non-cleaned segmentation (0.60 / 0.55 for Readers 1 and 2 respectively).

title: Accuracy of Information and References Using ChatGPT-3 for Retrieval of Clinical Radiological Information
venue: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
outcome: Authenticity of references provided by ChatGPT-3 in radiology answers
effect: Of 343 references, 124 (36.2%) were available via internet search; 219 (63.8%) appeared generated by ChatGPT-3. Only 47 of 124 identified references (37.9%) gave enough background to answer 24 questions (37.5%).
quote: Out of 343 references provided, only 124 references (36.2%) were available through internet search, while 219 references (63.8%) appeared to be generated by ChatGPT-3.

title: Accuracy of Information and References Using ChatGPT-3 for Retrieval of Clinical Radiological Information
venue: Canadian Association of Radiologists journal = Journal l'Association canadienne des radiologistes
outcome: Correctness of ChatGPT-3 answers to radiology questions versus peer-reviewed references
effect: 59 of 88 responses (67%) were correct; 29 (33%) contained errors.
quote: A total of 59 of 88 responses (67%) to radiological questions were correct, while 29 responses (33%) had errors.

title: Deployment of Real-time Natural Language Processing and Deep Learning Clinical Decision Support in the Electronic Health Record: Pipeline Implementation for an Opioid Misuse Screener in Hospitalized Adults
outcome: Silent-mode performance of deep learning screener on live EHR notes versus physician review
effect: Silent testing on 100 adult encounters showed sensitivity 93% (95% CI 66%-99%) and specificity 92% (95% CI 84%-96%), similar to published validation studies.
quote: On-site silent testing of the deep learning algorithm demonstrated a sensitivity of 93% (95% CI 66%-99%) and specificity of 92% (95% CI 84%-96%), similar to published validation studies.
sample_unit: adult encounters reviewed in silent testing

title: Deployment of Real-time Natural Language Processing and Deep Learning Clinical Decision Support in the Electronic Health Record: Pipeline Implementation for an Opioid Misuse Screener in Hospitalized Adults
outcome: Whether end-user interviews changed BPA design and materials before rollout
effect: Five end-user interviews informed an educational flyer and modified the BPA to exclude certain patients and allow refusal of recommendations.
quote: Five interviews were conducted; they informed the development of an educational flyer and further modified the BPA to exclude certain patients and allow refusal of recommendations.
sample_unit: adult encounters reviewed in silent testing

title: Potentials and pitfalls of ChatGPT and natural-language artificial intelligence models for the understanding of laboratory medicine test results. An assessment by the European Federation of Clinical Chemistry and Laboratory Medicine (EFLM) Working Group on Artificial Intelligence (WG-AI)
outcome: Correctness and completeness of ChatGPT interpretation of simulated lab reports, including follow-up suggestions
effect: Interpretations were superficial, not always correct, only sometimes coherent; magnitude of deviation from reference interval seldom mattered; no meaningful follow-up diagnostics suggested.
quote: The interpretations were rather superficial, not always correct, and, only in some cases, judged coherently.

title: Screening for extranodal extension in HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma: evaluation of a CT-based deep learning algorithm in patient data from a multicentre, randomised de-escalation trial
outcome: Deep learning algorithm AUC for ENE versus four head and neck radiologists on same data
effect: Algorithm AUC 0·86 (95% CI 0·82-0·90), outperforming all readers (p<0·0001 for each); radiologist kappa 0·32.
quote: The deep learning algorithm AUC for ENE classification was 0·86 (95% CI 0·82-0·90), outperforming all readers (p<0·0001 for each).

title: Screening for extranodal extension in HPV-associated oropharyngeal carcinoma: evaluation of a CT-based deep learning algorithm in patient data from a multicentre, randomised de-escalation trial
outcome: Algorithm sensitivity at different false positive rate operating points compared with best reader
effect: Matching specificity to best reader (FPR 22%) gave 75% sensitivity (+13%); FPR 30% gave 90% sensitivity.
quote: Setting the algorithm false positive rate to 30% yielded 90% sensitivity.

title: Artificial intelligence for detection of intracranial haemorrhage on head computed tomography scans: diagnostic accuracy in Hong Kong
venue: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ICH detection AI on local institutional historical CT scans vs reference standard
effect: AUC 0.842 (95% CI 0.791-0.894); at ≥50% threshold 73% sensitivity, 79% specificity, 18.6% PPV, 97.8% NPV, 78.6% accuracy on 1372 local scans (6.1% ICH).
quote: The model achieved an area under the curve of 0.842 (95% confidence interval=0.791-0.894; P<0.001) for scan-based detection of ICH.

title: Artificial intelligence for detection of intracranial haemorrhage on head computed tomography scans: diagnostic accuracy in Hong Kong
venue: Hong Kong medical journal = Xianggang yi xue za zhi
outcome: False-negative scans before vs after manual review of model-nominated CT slices
effect: 22 false-negative scans reduced to six false-negative scans by manual review of the five model-nominated slices.
quote: There were 62 true-positive scans and 22 false-negative scans, which could be reduced to six false-negative scans by manual review of model-nominated CT slices.

title: Application of artificial intelligence for overall survival risk stratification in oropharyngeal carcinoma: A validation of ProgTOOL
outcome: Performance drop on external validation of ML prognostic models; ProgTOOL external validation performance
effect: ProgTOOL kept 86.5% balanced accuracy, MCC 0.78 and Brier 0.06 on 163 Helsinki patients. In the review, only 7 of 31 ML studies (22.6%) reported external validation, and most of those reported reduced performance.
quote: Most of the studies reported a reduction in performance when externally validated.

title: Technical Adequacy of Fully Automated Artificial Intelligence Body Composition Tools: Assessment in a Heterogeneous Sample of External CT Examinations
outcome: AI tool technical adequacy across external sites, scanner models and manufacturers
effect: All three tools adequate in 97.7% of 11,699 exams from 777 institutions and 83 scanner models; 79 of 81 anisometry errors from one manufacturer, 80 of 81 on one scanner model.
quote: A total of 79 of 81 (97.5%) anisometry errors occurred on scanners from a single manufacturer; 80 of 81 (98.8%) occurred on the same scanner model.

title: Technical Adequacy of Fully Automated Artificial Intelligence Body Composition Tools: Assessment in a Heterogeneous Sample of External CT Examinations
outcome: Tool failure rate on external CT data differing from local development data
effect: At least one tool failed in 268 (2.3%) of examinations; individual adequacy 97.8% bone, 99.1% muscle, 98.9% fat.
quote: At least one tool failed in 268 (2.3%) of the examinations.

title: Technical Adequacy of Fully Automated Artificial Intelligence Body Composition Tools: Assessment in a Heterogeneous Sample of External CT Examinations
outcome: Failures from input specification mismatch (incorrect DICOM header voxel dimensions)
effect: Anisometry error accounted for 81 of 92 (88.0%) exams where all three tools failed; all three tools failed whenever it occurred.
quote: A single type of image processing error (anisometry error, due to incorrect DICOM header voxel dimension information) accounted for 81 of 92 (88.0%) examinations in which all three tools failed, and all three tools failed whenever this error occurred.

title: Radiologist Worklist Reprioritization Using Artificial Intelligence: Impact on Report Turnaround Times for CTPA Examinations Positive for Acute Pulmonary Embolism
outcome: Report turnaround, wait, and read times for PE-positive CTPA exams
effect: Post-AI vs pre-AI: turnaround 47.6 vs 59.9 min (diff 12.3, 95% CI 0.6-26.0); wait 21.4 vs 33.4 min (diff 12.0); read time no difference (26.3 vs 26.5 min).
quote: For PE-positive examinations, the post-AI period, compared with the pre-AI period, had significantly shorter mean report turnaround time (47.6 vs 59.9 minutes; mean difference, 12.3 minutes [95% CI, 0.6-26.0 minutes]) and mean wait time (21.4 vs 33.4 minutes; mean difference, 12.0 minutes [95% CI, 0.9-25.3 minutes]) but no significant difference in mean read time (26.3 vs 26.5 minutes; mean difference, 0.2 minutes [95% CI, -2.8 to 3.2 minutes]).

title: BiTNet: Hybrid deep convolutional model for ultrasound image analysis of human biliary tract and its applications
outcome: Participant diagnostic accuracy and precision with versus without BiTNet assistance
effect: Mean accuracy and precision with BiTNet (0.74 and 0.61) were statistically higher than without (0.50 and 0.46), p<0.001; improved at all experience levels.
quote: The mean accuracy and precision of the participants with BiTNet as an assisting tool (0.74 and 0.61, respectively) are statistically higher than those of participants without the assisting tool (0.50 and 0.46, respectively (p<0.001)).

title: BiTNet: Hybrid deep convolutional model for ultrasound image analysis of human biliary tract and its applications
outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy and precision
effect: With BiTNet, mean accuracy/precision were 0.74/0.61 versus 0.50/0.46 without (p<0.001).
quote: The mean accuracy and precision of the participants with BiTNet as an assisting tool (0.74 and 0.61, respectively) are statistically higher than those of participants without the assisting tool (0.50 and 0.46, respectively (p<0.001)).

title: BiTNet: Hybrid deep convolutional model for ultrasound image analysis of human biliary tract and its applications
outcome: False negatives during auto-prescreening
effect: Auto-prescreening reduced radiologist workload by 35%, with false negatives as low as 1 out of every 455 images.
quote: The proposed BiTNet can reduce the workload of radiologists by 35% while keeping the false negatives to as low as 1 out of every 455 images.

title: BiTNet: Hybrid deep convolutional model for ultrasound image analysis of human biliary tract and its applications
outcome: Overconfidence in prediction probability
effect: No numeric overconfidence metric reported; modifications to EfficientNet solved overconfidence and improved both applications and healthcare professionals.
quote: Our experiments suggest that prediction probability has an impact on both applications, and our modifications to EfficientNet solve the overconfidence problem, thereby improving the performance of both applications and of healthcare professionals.

title: Artificial intelligence for tumour tissue detection and histological regression grading in oesophageal adenocarcinomas: a retrospective algorithm development and validation study
outcome: Pathologist performance with versus without AI assistance: interobserver agreement and diagnostic time
effect: Use of the AI tool by three pathologists increased interobserver agreement and substantially reduced diagnostic time per case compared with working without AI assistance. Overreliance was not reported.
quote: Use of the AI tool by three pathologists increased interobserver agreement and substantially reduced diagnostic time per case compared with working without AI assistance.
sample_unit: pathologists compared against the AI grading (test cohorts: 320 annotated slides; 3 pathologists in the assisted-reading study)

title: Artificial intelligence for tumour tissue detection and histological regression grading in oesophageal adenocarcinomas: a retrospective algorithm development and validation study
outcome: AI regression grading compared against a group of 12 pathologists on the same retrospective cases
effect: Case-level agreement was 63·6% (quadratic kappa 0·749). AI grading triggered true reclassification in seven cases, six of which had small tumour regions initially missed by pathologists.
quote: The AI-based regression grading triggered true reclassification of resected tumour slides in seven cases (including six cases who had small tumour regions that were initially missed by pathologists).
sample_unit: pathologists compared against the AI grading (test cohorts: 320 annotated slides; 3 pathologists in the assisted-reading study)

title: Artificial intelligence for tumour tissue detection and histological regression grading in oesophageal adenocarcinomas: a retrospective algorithm development and validation study
outcome: Patch-level accuracy on independent external test cohorts from multiple institutions
effect: In four independent test cohorts from three institutes and TCGA, the AI tool had high patch-level accuracy for identifying tumour and regression tissue.
quote: In the independent test cohorts the AI tool had high patch-level accuracy for identifying both tumour and regression tissue.
sample_unit: pathologists compared against the AI grading (test cohorts: 320 annotated slides; 3 pathologists in the assisted-reading study)

title: Testing domain knowledge and risk of bias of a large-scale general artificial intelligence model in mental health
outcome: Change in model diagnostic interpretation when vignette demographics (gender, race) were systematically varied
effect: Limited evidence of demographic bias overall; some gender and racial differences in model outcomes, which mirrored real-world differential prevalence estimates.
quote: We found limited evidence of model demographic bias, although we do observe some gender and racial differences in model outcomes mirroring real-world differential prevalence estimates.

title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Conversational Agent (Chatbot) for Hip Arthroscopy Patients Following Surgery
outcome: Chatbot recognition and appropriate handling of potentially urgent patient questions/complications
effect: Of 10 questions possibly representing complications, Felix failed to adequately address or recognize the concern in 3 cases; no patient harm. 101/128 questions handled appropriately (79%).
quote: Of 10 patient questions that were thought to potentially represent patient complications, in 3 cases Felix did not adequately address or recognize the health concern-none of these situations resulted in patient harm.

title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Conversational Agent (Chatbot) for Hip Arthroscopy Patients Following Surgery
outcome: Chatbot recognition of potential medical urgency in patient questions
effect: In 3 of 10 potential complication questions, Felix did not adequately address or recognize the health concern; no harm occurred.
quote: Of 10 patient questions that were thought to potentially represent patient complications, in 3 cases Felix did not adequately address or recognize the health concern-none of these situations resulted in patient harm.

title: The impact of artificial intelligence on the reading times of radiologists for chest radiographs
outcome: Radiologist reading time with versus without AI aid in the real clinical workflow
effect: Total reading times shortened with AI use vs no use (13.3 s vs. 14.8 s, p < 0.001); no abnormality detected by AI 10.8 s vs 13.1 s; abnormality detected 18.6 s vs 18.4 s (p = 0.452).
quote: Total reading times were significantly shortened with AI use, compared to no use (13.3 s vs. 14.8 s, p < 0.001).

title: Brain tumour segmentation with incomplete imaging data
outcome: Segmentation accuracy (Dice) with missing MRI sequences versus complete set
effect: Dice 0.907 (single sequence) to 0.945 (complete set) for whole tumours; 0.701 to 0.891 for component tissue types; models trained on incomplete data often equivalent to full-data models.
quote: We demonstrate that models trained on incomplete data can segment lesions very well, often equivalently to those trained on the full completement of images, exhibiting Dice coefficients of 0.907 (single sequence) to 0.945 (complete set) for whole tumours and 0.701 (single sequence) to 0.891 (complete set) for component tissue types.

title: Brain tumour segmentation with incomplete imaging data
outcome: Segmentation accuracy on heterogeneous real-world local clinical imaging sample
effect: On a 50-patient real-world tertiary-centre sample spanning 15 years, accuracy was maintained on non-isotropic acquisitions and post-operative imaging with tumour recurrence.
quote: Our analysis includes validation on a heterogeneous, real-world 50 patient sample of brain tumour imaging acquired over the last 15 years at our tertiary centre, demonstrating maintained accuracy even on non-isotropic MRI acquisitions, or even on complex post-operative imaging with tumour recurrence.

title: Quantitative assessment of myocardial fibrosis by digital image analysis: An adjunctive tool for pathologist "ground truth"
venue: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
outcome: Inter-observer agreement among pathologists before versus after seeing AI quantification of myocardial fibrosis
effect: Three pathologists reassessed fibrosis after seeing the algorithm output; overall agreement improved significantly and no longer depended on fibrosis severity. Algorithm median 13.60% vs first pathologist 8.33% (R2 0.79).
quote: The knowledge of the automatic quantification significantly improved the overall pathologist´s agreement, which became unaffected by the degree of MF severity.

title: Quantitative assessment of myocardial fibrosis by digital image analysis: An adjunctive tool for pathologist "ground truth"
venue: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
outcome: pathologist reference-standard discordance
effect: Interobserver discordance was relevant, particularly for higher percentages of MF.
quote: Interobserver discordance was relevant, particularly for higher percentages of MF.

title: Quantitative assessment of myocardial fibrosis by digital image analysis: An adjunctive tool for pathologist "ground truth"
venue: Cardiovascular pathology : the official journal of the Society for Cardiovascular Pathology
outcome: pathologist reproducibility with AI adjunct
effect: Pathologist-AI quantification was highly correlated (R2: 0.79; p < 0.001); AI knowledge significantly improved overall pathologist agreement.
quote: The knowledge of the automatic quantification significantly improved the overall pathologist´s agreement, which became unaffected by the degree of MF severity.

title: Unsupervised out-of-distribution detection for safer robotically guided retinal microsurgery
venue: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
outcome: Whether OoD detector before the distance-estimation model maintains downstream MAE under input corruption
effect: MahaAD outperformed all baselines, with MAE staying almost constant across perturbation ratios up to 0.9; it also outperformed the other baselines on real OoD samples.
quote: MahaAD outperformed all baselines, with its MAE staying almost constant for all the perturbation ratios (Fig. 5 ).
sample_unit: M-scans (258 real OoD and 258 in-distribution) in the real-OoD test; 2,000 M-scans in the simulated-corruption test

title: Unsupervised out-of-distribution detection for safer robotically guided retinal microsurgery
venue: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
outcome: Downstream model performance on corrupted or out-of-distribution input data without detection
effect: Without rejection, corrupted A-scans are processed by the retinal network, and the Raw-MahaAD, Glow, Uncertainty, and SNR detectors underperformed the No-rejection baseline.
quote: Raw-MahaAD , Glow , Uncertainty , and SNR underperformed compared to No-rejection , suggesting that they flag a large proportion of correct samples as OoD while allowing corrupted A-scans to be processed by the subsequent retinal network.
sample_unit: M-scans (258 real OoD and 258 in-distribution) in the real-OoD test; 2,000 M-scans in the simulated-corruption test

title: Generalizable calibrated machine learning models for real-time atrial fibrillation risk prediction in ICU patients
outcome: External-dataset AUC with direct validation versus recalibration
effect: Direct external validation showed partial generalizability with AUCs reaching 0.77; recalibration resulted in performances matching or exceeding internal validation (AUC 0.81).
quote: However, recalibration resulted in performances matching or exceeding that of the internal validation.

title: Generalizable calibrated machine learning models for real-time atrial fibrillation risk prediction in ICU patients
outcome: Performance variation across external ICU datasets
effect: Direct external validation showed only partial generalizability (AUCs up to 0.77) versus 0.81 internally.
quote: Direct external validation showed partial generalizability with AUCs reaching 0.77.

title: Generalizable calibrated machine learning models for real-time atrial fibrillation risk prediction in ICU patients
outcome: External dataset generalizability
effect: Direct external validation showed partial generalizability, with AUCs reaching 0.77.
quote: Direct external validation showed partial generalizability with AUCs reaching 0.77.

title: Developing and Validating a Prediction Model For Death or Critical Illness in Hospitalized Adults, an Opportunity for Human-Computer Collaboration
outcome: ML model vs clinician predictions of ICU admission or death on the same hospitalizations
effect: ML median F1 0.32, AUC 0.77 vs clinicians F1 0.33, AUC 0.64; ML more accurate than clinicians for ICU admission.
quote: ML predictions were more accurate than clinicians for ICU admission.

title: Developing and Validating a Prediction Model For Death or Critical Illness in Hospitalized Adults, an Opportunity for Human-Computer Collaboration
outcome: Combined human-plus-model prediction sensitivity versus clinicians alone or model alone
effect: Combined predictions detected 49% of deterioration events, improving sensitivity by 16% vs clinicians alone and 24% vs model alone, with PPV of 33%.
quote: Combining human and model predictions detected 49% of clinical deterioration events, improving sensitivity by 16% compared with clinicians alone and 24% compared with the model alone while maintaining a positive predictive value of 33%, thus keeping false alarms at a clinically acceptable level.

title: Development and clinical validation of real-time artificial intelligence diagnostic companion for fetal ultrasound examination
venue: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
outcome: Retrospective performance of decision support system on clinical cases against confirmed postnatal diagnoses
effect: Ascertained diagnosis in top-10 list in 93% (full phenotype) and 83% (stepwise) of syndromic cases after adjudication; specificity 94%/96%, sensitivity 99%/84%.
quote: For syndromic cases, the ascertained diagnosis was within the top-10 list in 93% and 83% of cases using the full-phenotype and stepwise input, respectively, after adjudication.

title: An Investigation of Lesion Detection Accuracy for Artificial Intelligence-Based Denoising of Low-Dose 64Cu-DOTATATE PET Imaging in Patients with Neuroendocrine Neoplasms
venue: Journal of nuclear medicine : official publication, Society of Nuclear Medicine
outcome: Lesion detection by physician readers on AI-denoised low-dose PET versus full-dose reference, despite good image-quality metrics
effect: Image quality rated good/excellent in 32/33 PET_AI; but sensitivity 66% (78/118), false discovery rate 32% (37/115); 62% (23/37) of FPs scored as definite lesions.
quote: However, lesion detection analysis performed by physicians showed high proportions of FP and FN lesions on PET<sub>AI</sub>, highlighting the need for clinical validation of AI algorithms.

title: Comprehensive clinical evaluation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation for radiotherapy in patients with cervical cancer
outcome: Contouring time and DSC for radiation oncologists with versus without AI auto-segmentation
effect: Median contouring time 82 min without vs 51 min with auto-segmentation; mean DSC 0.76 vs 0.82; HD 25.11 vs 24.40 mm; smaller SDs suggest reduced heterogeneity.
quote: The median times for contouring all OAR/CTVs without auto-segmentation and with auto-segmentation were 82 min (range, 66–101 min) and 51 min (range, 31–78 min), respectively.
sample_unit: abdominopelvic planning CT images (165 training, 15 validation)

title: Comprehensive clinical evaluation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation for radiotherapy in patients with cervical cancer
outcome: conflict between AI target volume contours and institutional routine practice
effect: 9 of 10 radiation oncologists reported auto-segmented CTVs differed from their institution's routine practice, though OARs were similar
quote: All participants, except one, answered that the CTVs were different from those of their institution, but that the OARs were similar.
sample_unit: abdominopelvic planning CT images (165 training, 15 validation)

title: Deep Neural Network Augments Performance of Junior Residents in Diagnosing COVID-19 Pneumonia on Chest Radiographs
outcome: Junior resident diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance on external CXRs
effect: Residents' performance improved inversely to training level with AI assistance; two of three junior residents showed significant improvement.
quote: Among the three junior residents, two showed significant improvement with the assistance of AI.
sample_unit: external test chest radiographs read by 3 junior residents with and without AI

title: Deep Neural Network Augments Performance of Junior Residents in Diagnosing COVID-19 Pneumonia on Chest Radiographs
outcome: Model performance drop from internal to external test set (domain shift)
effect: AUC 0.9518 on internal test set versus 0.8594 on external test set; authors suggest domain shift between datasets.
quote: This suggests a domain shift between the patient dataset and the external dataset, highlighting the need for future research on test-time training domain adaptation to address this issue.
sample_unit: external test chest radiographs read by 3 junior residents with and without AI

title: Integration of Artificial Intelligence Decision Aids to Reduce Workload and Enhance Efficiency in Thyroid Nodule Management
outcome: Targeting AI assistance to image features/reader seniority versus applying AI to all nodules
effect: Optimized selective AI use cut time for senior radiologists (reader 16: 12.5 to 10.0 s) without accuracy loss, but increased time for junior radiologists (reader 11: 15.2 to 19.4 s).
quote: This diagnostic study suggests that an optimized AI strategy in thyroid nodule management may reduce diagnostic time-based costs without sacrificing diagnostic accuracy for senior radiologists, while the traditional all-AI strategy may still be more beneficial for junior radiologists.

title: Real-World Performance of Large Vessel Occlusion Artificial Intelligence-Based Computer-Aided Triage and Notification Algorithms-What the Stroke Team Needs to Know
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Real-world sensitivity versus manufacturer-reported sensitivity for LVO detection at two stroke centers
effect: Hospital A: manufacturer sensitivity 97%; real-world 85.3% (ICA/M1), 68.5% with M2, 59.9% all proximal segments. Hospital B: manufacturer 87.8%; real-world 76.4% with M2, 59.4% all segments.
quote: Sensitivity decreased to 68.5% when M2 segments were included and to 59.9% when all proximal vessel segments were included.
sample_unit: code stroke CT angiography examinations (704 at hospital A, 642 at hospital B)

title: Real-World Performance of Large Vessel Occlusion Artificial Intelligence-Based Computer-Aided Triage and Notification Algorithms-What the Stroke Team Needs to Know
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Cases with no CADt result available
effect: 79 of 704 cases at hospital A and 20 of 642 at hospital B had no CADt result available.
quote: Real-world performance of 704 cases included 79 in which no CADt result was available.
sample_unit: code stroke CT angiography examinations (704 at hospital A, 642 at hospital B)

title: Translating radiology reports into plain language using ChatGPT and GPT-4 with prompt learning: results, limitations, and potential
venue: Visual computing for industry, biomedicine, and art
outcome: Response randomness and omitted or oversimplified information in ChatGPT translations across runs
effect: ChatGPT showed some randomness in responses with occasionally over-simplified or neglected information; a more detailed prompt mitigated this.
quote: ChatGPT also presents some randomness in its responses with occasionally over-simplified or neglected information, which can be mitigated using a more detailed prompt.

title: National Needs Assessment of Utilization of Common Newborn Clinical Decision Support Tools
outcome: Reasons neonatal decision support tools did not affect clinical care, including lack of EHR integration
effect: Lack of EHR integration was among the common reasons tools did not impact care, alongside lack of confidence in prediction accuracy and unhelpful predictions. Use was >90% for BiliTool and the EOS tool, 72% for Extremely Preterm Birth, 39% for BPD.
quote: Common reasons CDSTs did not impact clinical care included lack of electronic health record integration, lack of confidence in prediction accuracy, and unhelpful predictions.
sample_unit: completed questionnaires from neonatal care providers

title: Multi-vendor evaluation of artificial intelligence as an independent reader for double reading in breast cancer screening on 275,900 mammograms
outcome: AI performance non-inferiority across mammography vendors and screening sites
effect: DR with AI showed at least non-inferior recall rate, cancer detection rate, sensitivity, specificity and PPV for each mammography vendor and site, and superior recall rate, specificity, and PPV for some.
quote: DR with AI, compared with human DR, showed at least non-inferior recall rate, cancer detection rate, sensitivity, specificity and positive predictive value (PPV) for each mammography vendor and site, and superior recall rate, specificity, and PPV for some.

title: An artificial intelligence based app for skin cancer detection evaluated in a population based setting
outcome: Dermatological claims for (pre)malignant and benign lesions in app users versus matched controls
effect: App users had more (pre)malignant claims (6.0% vs 4.6%, OR 1.3) and more benign tumor/nevi claims (5.9% vs 1.7%, OR 3.7). Cost per additional (pre)malignancy detected was €2567.
quote: Here we report that mHealth-users had more claims for (pre)malignant skin lesions than controls (6.0% vs 4.6%, OR 1.3 (95% CI 1.2-1.4)) and also a more than threefold higher risk of claims for benign skin tumors and nevi (5.9% vs 1.7%, OR 3.7 (95% CI 3.4-4.1)).
sample_unit: adults (18,960 app users matched to 56,880 non-user controls)

title: Development, multi-institutional external validation, and algorithmic audit of an artificial intelligence-based Side-specific Extra-Prostatic Extension Risk Assessment tool (SEPERA) for patients undergoing radical prostatectomy: a retrospective cohort study
outcome: SEPERA performance and net benefit versus existing nomograms and logistic regression on same data
effect: SEPERA best across validation cohorts (pooled AUROC 0.77, AUPRC 0.61); higher net benefit than other models; correctly predicted ssEPE in 72 (68%) of 106 benign-biopsy cases vs 47 (44%) logistic regression, 0 Sayyid, 13 (12%) Soeterik non-MRI, 5 (5%) Soeterik MRI.
quote: SEPERA was well calibrated and had the best performance across all validation cohorts (pooled AUROC of 0·77 [95% CI 0·75-0·78] and pooled AUPRC of 0·61 [0·58-0·63]).

title: Development, multi-institutional external validation, and algorithmic audit of an artificial intelligence-based Side-specific Extra-Prostatic Extension Risk Assessment tool (SEPERA) for patients undergoing radical prostatectomy: a retrospective cohort study
outcome: AUROC differences across demographic and clinical subgroups in algorithmic audit
effect: No evidence of model bias; no significant difference in AUROC when stratified by race, biopsy year, age, biopsy type, biopsy location, and D'Amico risk group.
quote: In the algorithmic audit, no evidence of model bias was observed, with no significant difference in AUROC when stratified by race, biopsy year, age, biopsy type (systematic only vs systematic and MRI-targeted biopsy), biopsy location (academic vs community), and D'Amico risk group.

title: Development, multi-institutional external validation, and algorithmic audit of an artificial intelligence-based Side-specific Extra-Prostatic Extension Risk Assessment tool (SEPERA) for patients undergoing radical prostatectomy: a retrospective cohort study
outcome: Generalisation from community-hospital training data to external academic centres in three sites
effect: Trained on 1022 cases from a community hospital network and externally validated on 3914 cases at three academic centres, SEPERA was well calibrated with pooled AUROC 0.77 across validation cohorts.
quote: SEPERA was well calibrated and had the best performance across all validation cohorts (pooled AUROC of 0·77 [95% CI 0·75-0·78] and pooled AUPRC of 0·61 [0·58-0·63]).

title: Can Artificial Intelligence Pass the American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery Examination? Orthopaedic Residents Versus ChatGPT
outcome: ChatGPT accuracy on orthopaedic in-training exam questions versus resident percentiles and pass threshold
effect: ChatGPT answered 47% (97 of 207) correctly; scored 40th percentile for PGY1s, 8th for PGY2s, 1st for PGY3-5; unlikely to pass written boards. Accuracy fell with taxonomy level (54%, 51%, 34%; p = 0.034).
quote: ChatGPT selected the correct answer 47% (97 of 207) of the time, and 53% (110 of 207) of the time it answered incorrectly.

title: Clinical evaluation of a deep learning segmentation model including manual adjustments afterwards for locally advanced breast cancer
venue: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
outcome: Contouring time with auto-segmentation plus correction versus manual delineation on same patients
effect: Time reduction in 95% of cases; mean 42.4% ± 26.5% for OARs and 58.5% ± 19.1% for CTVs; absolute mean reduction 00:08:51 and 00:25:38.
quote: Only for one patient case out of 20, the time needed to correct the OARs took more time than the manual delineation (00:12:40 vs 00:10:15), leading to a decrease in time in 95% of the patients.

title: Clinical evaluation of a deep learning segmentation model including manual adjustments afterwards for locally advanced breast cancer
venue: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
outcome: Clinician qualitative scoring of AI contours as clinically acceptable, with or without corrections
effect: 92% of auto-contours were scored clinically acceptable with or without correction; CTVp unusable in seven cases, CTVn1 in six, CTVn4 in four.
quote: During qualitative measurements, the auto-contours got scored as clinical acceptable, with or without corrections, in 92% of the cases.

title: Clinical evaluation of a deep learning segmentation model including manual adjustments afterwards for locally advanced breast cancer
venue: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
outcome: AI-assisted versus manual contouring time
effect: Mean time reduction was 42.4% ± 26.5% for OARs and 58.5% ± 19.1% for CTVs.
quote: The time reduction (mean ± std) was 42.4% ± 26.5% and 58.5% ± 19.1% for OARs and CTVs, respectively, corresponding to an absolute mean reduction (hh:mm:ss) of 00:08:51 and 00:25:38.

title: Clinical evaluation of a deep learning segmentation model including manual adjustments afterwards for locally advanced breast cancer
venue: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
outcome: preclinical local validation endpoint
effect: Primary time-efficiency endpoint met: time reduction was achieved in 95% of cases including corrections.
quote: In 95% of the cases, time reduction was achieved while including corrections of the contours when needed.

title: Clinical evaluation of a deep learning segmentation model including manual adjustments afterwards for locally advanced breast cancer
venue: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
outcome: clinically unusable AI contours
effect: CTVp, CTVn1, and CTVn4 were not usable in 7, 6, and 4 cases, respectively.
quote: The CTVp was found not to be usable in a total of seven cases, CTVn1 in six cases and CTVn4 in four cases.

title: Clinical evaluation of a deep learning segmentation model including manual adjustments afterwards for locally advanced breast cancer
venue: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
outcome: impact of manual corrections on contour accuracy
effect: corrections significantly improved left CTVn1 across all metrics, but overall only a small number of cases had significantly different contours after correction (right CTVp DSC improved by 0.02 +/- 0.05)
quote: These results indicate that, although corrections were made in most of the cases, only for a small number of cases these corrections were actually significantly different.

title: Validation of predictive models for disease outcomes in paediatric ulcerative colitis: A multicentre prospective inception cohort
outcome: External prospective validation accuracy of published paediatric UC outcome prediction models versus original reports
effect: PROTECT AUC for steroid-free remission was 0.78 at 3 months but 0.57 at 12 months. Schechter criteria sensitivity/specificity/PPV/NPV were 50%/60%/35%/74%. Only PUCAI predicted acute severe colitis.
quote: The other predictive models did not achieve sufficient accuracy, which was far from that reported in the original studies.
sample_unit: children with newly diagnosed ulcerative colitis

title: Artificial intelligence in mobile health for skin cancer diagnostics at home (AIM HIGH): a pilot feasibility study
outcome: GP diagnosis and treatment plan changes when blinded versus unblinded to AI app assessment
effect: GPs never changed their working diagnosis but changed their treatment plan in 5 patients based on the app's assessments; 45 of 50 GP assessments completed successfully.
quote: GPs never changed their working diagnosis, but did change their treatment plan (n = 5) based on the app's assessments.

title: Performance and risks of ChatGPT used in drug information: an exploratory real-world analysis
venue: European journal of hospital pharmacy : science and practice
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT answers to repeated identical questions over time
effect: Answers varied over time when entered repeatedly; only 3 of 12 answers were identical, showing no to low reproducibility.
quote: The answers of ChatGPT varied over time when entered repeatedly and only three out of 12 answers were identical, showing no reproducibility to low reproducibility.

title: Performance and risks of ChatGPT used in drug information: an exploratory real-world analysis
venue: European journal of hospital pharmacy : science and practice
outcome: Content correctness and patient-harm risk of ChatGPT drug answers versus pharmacist reference
effect: Only 13 of 50 answers were correct, sufficient for management and no risk; 38% (n=19) false, 36% (n=18) partly correct; high risk of harm in 26% (n=13).
quote: Overall, only 13 of 50 answers provided correct content and had enough information to initiate management with no risk of patient harm.

title: Performance and risks of ChatGPT used in drug information: an exploratory real-world analysis
venue: European journal of hospital pharmacy : science and practice
outcome: Presence of references/citations in ChatGPT drug information answers
effect: No references were provided for the answers.
quote: The majority of answers were either false (38%, n=19) or had partly correct content (36%, n=18) and no references were provided.

title: Development, Deployment, and Implementation of a Machine Learning Surgical Case Length Prediction Model and Prospective Evaluation
outcome: Scheduler case-length prediction accuracy with versus without model assistance in live deployment
effect: Model-assisted schedulers predicted 3.4% more cases within 20% of actual length and 4.3% fewer underpredicted cases; the model alone did better still (5.9% more within 20%, 11.2% fewer underpredicted) than schedulers alone.
quote: The model assisted schedulers to predict 3.4% more cases within 20% of the actual case length and 4.3% fewer underpredicted cases.

title: Can incorrect artificial intelligence (AI) results impact radiologists, and if so, what can we do about it? A multi-reader pilot study of lung cancer detection with chest radiography
outcome: Radiologist overreliance on incorrect AI
effect: FNs rose from 2.7% to 20.7–33.0%; FPs from 51.4% to 80.5–86.0%.

title: Awareness of Racial and Ethnic Bias and Potential Solutions to Address Bias With Use of Health Care Algorithms

quote: This improved the model's discriminative capability to a C-statistic of 0.64 (95% CI 0.59-0.70) and enhanced calibration plots.

title: Drug-related readmissions in older hospitalized adults: External validation and updating of OPERAM DRA prediction tool
venue: Journal of the American Geriatrics Society
outcome: External validation discrimination and calibration of drug-related readmission model in Swedish cohort
effect: Original model C-statistic 0.62 (95% CI 0.59-0.64), calibration showed underestimation of risks; scaled Brier score 0.03.
quote: In the validation cohort, the original model showed a good overall accuracy (scaled Brier score 0.03), but discrimination was moderate (C-statistic 0.62 [95% CI 0.59-0.64]), and calibration showed underestimation of risks.

title: Use of artificial intelligence in triaging of chest radiographs to reduce radiologists' workload
outcome: Sensitivity when the AI-ranked lower 50% of radiographs were treated as negative without radiologist review versus reading all
effect: Sensitivity was 82.6% reading all without DLD and 83.5% in the 50% worklist reduction scenario; difference 0.8% (95% CI -3.8% to 5.5%), noninferior. Specificity rose from 86.7% to 90.4%.
quote: The difference in sensitivity was 0.8% (95% CI: - 3.8%, 5.5%), establishing noninferiority of 50% worklist reduction (p = 0.01).

title: Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses to Top Searched Queries About Cancer
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) and understandability of chatbot cancer information
effect: Responses written at college level; PEMAT understandability moderate (median 66.7%, range 33.3%-90.1%); actionability poor (median 20.0%).
quote: The responses were written at the college level based on the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score.

title: Assessment of Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses to Top Searched Queries About Cancer
outcome: Reading level of chatbot cancer information for consumers
effect: Responses were written at the college level based on the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score.
quote: The responses were written at the college level based on the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score.

title: BPPV Information on Google Versus AI (ChatGPT)
venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of ChatGPT responses versus Google webpages for BPPV patient questions
effect: ChatGPT FKGL 13.9 ± 2.5 vs Google 10.7 ± 2.6 (P < .001); FRE 34.9 ± 11.2 vs 46.5 ± 14.3 (P = .005), indicating lower readability.
quote: ChatGPT responses had a higher FKGL score of 13.9 ± 2.5 (P < .001) and a lower FRE score of 34.9 ± 11.2 (P = .005), both corresponding to lower readability.

venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT patient education responses
effect: ChatGPT mean FKGL 13.9 ± 2.5 (college level), higher than Google webpages at 10.7 ± 2.6; FRE 34.9 ± 11.2.
quote: ChatGPT responses had a higher FKGL score of 13.9 ± 2.5 (P < .001) and a lower FRE score of 34.9 ± 11.2 (P = .005), both corresponding to lower readability.
