title: Web-Based Application Based on Human-in-the-Loop Deep Learning for Deidentifying Free-Text Data in Electronic Medical Records: Development and Usability Study
outcome: Human annotation time and accuracy with versus without AI preannotation
effect: For 200 notes annotated by one analyst, preannotation sped up annotation by 43% (95% CI 33.9-52.1; P <.001). Recall increased from 0.9756 to 0.9886 and micro-F1 from 0.9869 to 0.9922.
quote: Through the 5-round comparison, the preannotation by the trained model sped up the annotation work by 43% (95% CI 33.9-52.1; P <.001).

title: Web-Based Application Based on Human-in-the-Loop Deep Learning for Deidentifying Free-Text Data in Electronic Medical Records: Development and Usability Study
outcome: Residual PII missed by automated deidentification on local clinical notes
effect: Overall strict entity-level F1 0.9507, recall 0.9526 on local notes (above the 0.95 benchmark), but ADDRESS recall was only 0.5 and PHONE F1 was 0.8571.
quote: Furthermore, the DEFT system can use only 600 annotated clinical notes to achieve good performance with an F 1 -score of 0.9507, which is greater than 0.95, the rule-of-thumb benchmark for evaluating the reliability of a deidentification system [ 16 , 40 ].

title: Web-Based Application Based on Human-in-the-Loop Deep Learning for Deidentifying Free-Text Data in Electronic Medical Records: Development and Usability Study
outcome: PII detection precision, recall, and F1 for clinical-note deidentification
effect: Using 600 annotated notes, model precision was 0.9487, recall 0.9526, and micro-F1 0.9507. Performance remained uneven: ADDRESS recall was 0.5.
quote: Furthermore, the DEFT system can use only 600 annotated clinical notes to achieve good performance with an F 1 -score of 0.9507, which is greater than 0.95, the rule-of-thumb benchmark for evaluating the reliability of a deidentification system [ 16 , 40 ].

title: Pan-mediastinal neoplasm diagnosis via nationwide federated learning: a multicentre cohort study
outcome: Clinician top-1 and top-3 diagnostic accuracy with versus without CAIMEN-based software assistance
effect: 46 clinicians improved average top-1 accuracy by 19.1% and top-3 accuracy by 13.0% with AI assistance; CAIMEN alone also outperformed clinicians (top-1 0.500, top-3 0.800).
quote: with assistance from the computer aided diagnosis software based on CAIMEN, the 46 clinicians improved their average top-1 accuracy by 19·1% (0·345-0·411) and top-3 accuracy by 13·0% (0·545-0·616).
sample_unit: cases (development cohort: 7825 mediastinal neoplasm cases plus 796 normal controls)

title: Adversarial Attack and Defense in Breast Cancer Deep Learning Systems
outcome: Vulnerability of breast cancer pathology deep learning classifiers to FGSM adversarial inputs
effect: FGSM attacks caused misclassification of breast cancer pathology images; the authors then built a system with better defense performance. No numeric results are reported in the abstract.
quote: We used the adversarial attack algorithm FGSM to reveal that breast cancer deep learning systems are vulnerable to attacks and thus misclassify breast cancer pathology images.

title: ChatGPT and most frequent urological diseases: analysing the quality of information and potential risks for patients
outcome: Whether ChatGPT disclosed sources for its urological patient information
effect: Chatbot does not disclose its information sources; treatment answers scored 3 of 5 on DISCERN, and all pathologies except BPH scored 4.
quote: ChatGPT information should be used with caution since the chatbot does not disclose the sources of information and may contain bias even with simple questions related to the basics of urologic diseases.

title: Experiences Regarding Use and Implementation of Artificial Intelligence-Supported Follow-Up of Atypical Moles at a Dermatological Outpatient Clinic: Qualitative Study
outcome: Barriers to consistent use of AI total body dermoscopy module, including training gaps
effect: Lack of guidance, time pressure, and insufficient training were barriers to consistent use; only 3 of 14 participants had actual experience using the TBD module.
quote: First, several organizational matters were revealed to be a barrier to consistent use of the ATBM Master's TBD module, namely lack of guidance, time pressure, and insufficient training.

title: Effects of Implementing Artificial Intelligence-Based Computer-Aided Detection for Chest Radiographs in Daily Practice on the Rate of Referral to Chest Computed Tomography in Pulmonology Outpatient Clinic
outcome: Chest CT referral rate, including referrals with negative CT results, with versus without AI-CAD
effect: AI-CAD use was associated with increased chest CT referrals (OR 1.33; P=0.008) and referrals with negative CT results (OR 1.46; P=0.005). Referrals with positive CT results were not significantly changed (OR 1.08; P=0.647).
quote: The use of AI-CAD for CR interpretation in pulmonology outpatients was independently associated with an increased frequency of overall referrals for chest CT scans and referrals with subsequent negative results.

title: Chat GPT as a Neuro-Score Calculator: Analysis of a Large Language Model's Performance on Various Neurological Exam Grading Scales
outcome: ChatGPT scoring error rate under increasingly complex phrasing and missing information variants
effect: GCS AER 10%/AME 0.150 on 10 base cases; with crucial information missing AER was 45% for 20 cases; simple prompt gave 70% error rate.
quote: The accuracy of ChatGPT decreased with increasing complexity; for example, in a variation where crucial information was missing, the AER was 45% for 20 cases.

title: Chat GPT as a Neuro-Score Calculator: Analysis of a Large Language Model's Performance on Various Neurological Exam Grading Scales
outcome: error rate with simple prompt
effect: Using a simple prompt resulted in a significantly higher error rate of 70%.
quote: Using a simple prompt resulted in a significantly higher error rate of 70%.

title: Chat GPT as a Neuro-Score Calculator: Analysis of a Large Language Model's Performance on Various Neurological Exam Grading Scales
outcome: Error rate when crucial input information was missing from neuro exam cases
effect: When crucial information was missing, average error rate was 45% for 20 cases, indicating unreliable outputs with incomplete inputs.
quote: The accuracy of ChatGPT decreased with increasing complexity; for example, in a variation where crucial information was missing, the AER was 45% for 20 cases.

title: Chat GPT as a Neuro-Score Calculator: Analysis of a Large Language Model's Performance on Various Neurological Exam Grading Scales
outcome: neuro-score calculation errors
effect: GCS base test cases had AER/AME of 10%/0.150.
quote: The GCS calculator on 10 base test cases had an AER/AME of 10%/0.150.

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Colonoscopy Detection of Advanced Neoplasias
outcome: Advanced colorectal neoplasia detection rate with vs without computer-aided detection
effect: No significant difference in advanced neoplasia detection (34.8% vs 34.6%; aRR 1.01 [95% CI 0.92 to 1.10]); adenoma detection rate also did not differ (64.2% vs 62.0%).
quote: Computer-aided detection did not improve colonoscopic identification of advanced colorectal neoplasias.
sample_unit: persons with a positive fecal immunochemical test

title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening Using Smartphone-Based Fundus Photography and Deep-Learning Artificial Intelligence in the Yucatan Peninsula: A Field Study
venue: Journal of diabetes science and technology
outcome: Head-to-head sensitivity and specificity of two AI DR algorithms on same patients
effect: In 110 patients, sensitivities of Medios and EyeArt were 99% (93%-100%) and 95% (87%-99%); specificities both 88% (73%-97%).
quote: In a head-to-head comparison of 110 patients, the sensitivities of Medios and EyeArt were 99% (93%-100%) and 95% (87%-99%).

title: Diabetic Retinopathy Screening Using Smartphone-Based Fundus Photography and Deep-Learning Artificial Intelligence in the Yucatan Peninsula: A Field Study
venue: Journal of diabetes science and technology
outcome: AI DR detection performance in real-world remote field setting
effect: Medios sensitivity 94% (88%-97%) and specificity 94% (88%-98%); EyeArt sensitivity 94% and specificity 86% in field setting.
quote: Medios and EyeArt AI algorithms demonstrated high levels of sensitivity and specificity for detecting DR when applied in this real-world field setting.

title: False Positives in Artificial Intelligence Prioritization Software for Intracranial Hemorrhage Identification in the Postoperative Period: A Report of Two Cases
outcome: False-positive ICH flags by AI prioritization software on postoperative CT
effect: Two cases in which AI prioritization software erroneously identified an acute ICH on a postoperative non-contrast CT.
quote: However, it is crucial to recognize that AI systems may produce false-positive results, especially in the postoperative period.

title: Human factors in the clinical implementation of deep learning-based automated contouring of pelvic organs at risk for MRI-guided radiotherapy
outcome: Expert-consensus vs clinically used contour agreement (DSC) and dose differences before vs after auto-contouring
effect: Contouring behavior changed after automation. Femoral head DSC vs expert consensus rose from 0.91 to 0.93 and rectum fell from 0.88 to 0.85. Max-dose differences were not statistically significant.
quote: Automation bias was observed, but it had little deleterious effect on treatment planning.

title: Human factors in the clinical implementation of deep learning-based automated contouring of pelvic organs at risk for MRI-guided radiotherapy
outcome: Presence of automation bias and its dosimetric consequence in planners using AI contours
effect: Automation bias was observed in planners. Only 4 deviating slices in 2 patients were graded low clinical significance, none moderate or high. Dose differences were not significant.
quote: Automation bias was observed, but it had little deleterious effect on treatment planning.

title: Natural Language Processing - A Surveillance Stepping Stone to Identify Child Abuse
outcome: Whether silent-mode running on live ED notes enabled algorithm refinement before clinical activation
effect: 73 of 353 notes falsely triggered the NLP, mostly from linguistic-context errors. Common false-positive scenarios were identified and the algorithm was refined to improve specificity.
quote: Analysis of an NLP algorithm in "silent mode" allowed for refinement of the algorithm and highlighted areas in which real-time CDS may help ED providers identify and pursue appropriate evaluation of injuries associated with child physical abuse.

title: Natural Language Processing - A Surveillance Stepping Stone to Identify Child Abuse
outcome: Silent-mode NLP outputs compared with actual clinician evaluation and guideline adherence on live notes
effect: Adherence to guideline-recommended evaluation was 63%. Seventy-three false triggers were found and used to refine the algorithm.
quote: Seventy-three cases falsely triggered the NLP, often due to errors in interpreting linguistic context.

title: Diagnostic Performance, Triage Safety, and Usability of a Clinical Decision Support System Within a University Hospital Emergency Department: Algorithm Performance and Usability Study
outcome: CDSS missed emergencies identified by physicians (under-triage of safety-critical cases)
effect: CDSS did not miss any physician-evaluated emergencies; all were classed as urgent or emergency. Urgent sensitivity 85%, nonurgent sensitivity 19% versus physicians.
quote: Our CDSS did not miss any cases that were evaluated to be emergencies by physicians; thus, all emergency cases evaluated by physicians were evaluated as either urgent cases or emergency cases by the CDSS.

title: Diagnostic Performance, Triage Safety, and Usability of a Clinical Decision Support System Within a University Hospital Emergency Department: Algorithm Performance and Usability Study
outcome: CDSS urgency triage sensitivity compared against physician evaluations on the same patients
effect: CDSS urgent sensitivity 85% vs physicians; physician-to-physician urgent sensitivity 85%; nonurgent 19% (CDSS) vs 35% (physicians).
quote: The mean sensitivities were 85% and 35%, respectively, when comparing the evaluations between the two physicians.

title: What can GPT-4 do for Diagnosing Rare Eye Diseases? A Pilot Study
outcome: GPT-4 diagnostic accuracy on rare eye disease cases by simulated user scenario
effect: Simulated patient scenario had no 'right' responses; family physician 50% right; junior ophthalmologist 90% right. Overall 83.3% of 30 responses judged appropriate.
quote: However, compared to the ground truth, GPT-4 could only output several possible diseases generally without "right" responses in the simulated patient scenarios.
sample_unit: GPT-4 responses (10 rare eye disease cases x 3 simulated user scenarios)

title: The recalibration and redevelopment of a model to calculate patients' probability of completing a colonoscopy following an abnormal fecal test
outcome: Discrimination (c-statistic) of original model locally versus redeveloped local model
effect: Original model c-statistic dropped from 0.66 to 0.61 in the single large FQHC; redeveloped model in the same FQHC reached c-statistic 0.65 (n=1401).
quote: The model was redeveloped in the same FQHC in a cohort of 1401 patients with a c-statistic of 0.65.

title: The recalibration and redevelopment of a model to calculate patients' probability of completing a colonoscopy following an abnormal fecal test
outcome: Performance of externally developed model on local data
effect: When applied to a single large FQHC (884 patients), the model did not recalibrate successfully; c-statistic dropped more than 0.05, from 0.66 to 0.61.
quote: When we applied the model to a single large FQHC (34 clinics, 884 eligible patients), the model did not recalibrate successfully (c-statistic dropped more than 0.05, from 0.66 to 0.61).

title: Prospective, multicenter validation of the deep learning-based cardiac arrest risk management system for predicting in-hospital cardiac arrest or unplanned intensive care unit transfer in patients admitted to general wards
outcome: AUROC of AI early warning versus MEWS/NEWS for IHCA or unplanned ICU transfer
effect: Composite outcome AUROC for DeepCARS 0.869 vs 0.756 (MEWS) and 0.767 (NEWS); fewer alarms per 1,000 beds at same sensitivity and higher rate of appropriate alarms.
quote: In terms of the composite outcome, the AUROC for the DeepCARS™ was superior to those for the MEWS and NEWS (0.869 vs. 0.756/0.767).

title: Prospective, multicenter validation of the deep learning-based cardiac arrest risk management system for predicting in-hospital cardiac arrest or unplanned intensive care unit transfer in patients admitted to general wards
outcome: Prospective performance of predictive model on live production data
effect: Prospective multicenter evaluation in real-world practice showed DeepCARS AUROC 0.869, superior to MEWS/NEWS, indicating retrospective performance was retained prospectively.
quote: This prospective study aimed to investigate the predictive accuracy of the DeepCARS™ for IHCA or unplanned intensive care unit transfer (UIT) among general ward patients, compared with that of conventional methods in real-world practice.

title: The association between use of ambient voice technology documentation during primary care patient encounters, documentation burden, and provider burnout
outcome: Documentation time per encounter and provider burnout (OLBI) after ambient scribe deployment
effect: Documentation time fell 28.8% (1.8 min; 95% CI 1.4-2.2). High DAX use had lower OLBI sub-score (MD -2.1; CI -3.8 to -0.4) but not total burnout (MD -3.0; CI -6.4 to 0.3).
quote: After DAX™ implementation average documentation time in notes per encounter was significantly reduced by 28.8% (1.8 min; 95% CI 1.4-2.2).
sample_unit: primary care providers completing burnout survey (19 with pre/post documentation time data)

title: Behavioral Health Decision Support Systems and User Interface Design in the Emergency Department
outcome: Physician sentiment on alert placement, design, workflow fit, and reasons for ignoring the alert
effect: Alert placement was largely intuitive and nonintrusive, and design was viewed positively. Some physicians ignored it because it was redundant, irrelevant, or lacked enough information. Overall effect on workflow was marginally positive.
quote: The alert placement was noted to be largely intuitive and nonintrusive.

title: Evaluation of Online Artificial Intelligence-Generated Information on Common Hand Procedures
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT answers about hand surgery vs ASSH HandCare materials
effect: AI responses: mean Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease 15, Grade Level 34 (college level); ASSH HandCare: grade level 9, reading ease 60 (eighth/ninth grade).
quote: For AI responses, the mean Flesch Kinkaid Reading Ease score was 15, and the Flesch Kinkaid Grade Level was 34, which is considered to be college level.

title: Evaluation of Online Artificial Intelligence-Generated Information on Common Hand Procedures
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient information compared with appropriate patient reading level
effect: AI answers required college-level reading (FK Grade Level 34, Reading Ease 15) versus eighth/ninth grade for ASSH materials (grade 9, ease 60).
quote: Furthermore, a high reading level was required to comprehend the information presented.

title: Evaluation of Online Artificial Intelligence-Generated Information on Common Hand Procedures
outcome: Source attribution and citation in ChatGPT answers (JAMA benchmark)
effect: JAMA benchmark score 0/4 for AI versus 3/4 for ASSH; points lost for lack of attribution, reliability and currency of sources.
quote: The areas in which the AI model lost points were primarily related to the lack of attribution, reliability and currency of the source material.

title: Artificial intelligence for breast cancer detection in screening mammography in Sweden: a prospective, population-based, paired-reader, non-inferiority study
outcome: Screen-detected breast cancer compared with standard-of-care double reading
effect: One radiologist plus AI was non-inferior to two radiologists: 261 [0·5%] vs 250 [0·4%] detected cases; relative proportion 1·04 [95% CI 1·00-1·09].
quote: 269 (0·5%) women were diagnosed with screen-detected breast cancer based on an initial positive read: double reading by one radiologist plus AI was non-inferior for cancer detection compared with double reading by two radiologists (261 [0·5%] vs 250 [0·4%] detected cases; relative proportion 1·04 [95% CI 1·00-1·09]).

title: Assessing the accuracy and consistency of ChatGPT in clinical pharmacy management: A preliminary analysis with clinical pharmacy experts worldwide
venue: Research in social & administrative pharmacy : RSAP
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT pharmacotherapy answers across repeated runs at three time points
effect: Percent agreement between weeks 1 and 3 was 79.2%, weeks 3 and 5 was 87.5%, and weeks 1 and 5 was 83.3%; hit rate 70.83% at week 1, 79.2% at week 3, 75% at week 5.
quote: The percent agreement between weeks 1 and 3 was 79.2%, whereas it was 87.5% between weeks 3 and 5, and 83.3% between weeks 1 and 5.

title: ChatGPT and Patient Information in Nuclear Medicine: GPT-3.5 Versus GPT-4
outcome: Currency of ChatGPT-generated nuclear medicine patient information rated by expert assessors
effect: GPT-3.5 lacked accuracy and currency and omitted important information; GPT-4 was enhanced across appropriateness, accuracy, and currency despite some omissions.
quote: ChatGPT powered by GPT-3.5 provided patient information that was appropriate in terms of being patient-facing but lacked accuracy and currency and omitted important information.
sample_unit: patient information sheets (7 procedures x 2 models)

title: ChatGPT and Patient Information in Nuclear Medicine: GPT-3.5 Versus GPT-4
outcome: Accuracy and omissions in ungrounded LLM-generated patient information sheets rated by expert assessors
effect: GPT-3.5 sheets were inaccurate and not fit for purpose; GPT-4 improved accuracy but still omitted some information and was largely fit for purpose.
quote: GPT-4 provided patient information enhanced across appropriateness, accuracy, and currency, despite some omission of information.
sample_unit: patient information sheets (7 procedures x 2 models)

title: Can artificial intelligence replace biochemists? A study comparing interpretation of thyroid function test results by ChatGPT and Google Bard to practising biochemists
outcome: Correct interpretation of thyroid function test cases versus clinician consensus
effect: ChatGPT and Google Bard correctly interpreted only 33.3% and 20.0% of 15 cases; both failed to identify subclinical presentations, non-thyroidal illness or secondary hypothyroidism.
quote: Of the 15 cases presented, ChatGPT and Google Bard correctly interpreted only 33.3% and 20.0% of cases, respectively.

title: Can artificial intelligence replace biochemists? A study comparing interpretation of thyroid function test results by ChatGPT and Google Bard to practising biochemists
outcome: Accuracy and safety of AI outputs against consensus reference standard
effect: Correct interpretation 33.3% (ChatGPT) and 20.0% (Bard); patient-posed queries safe in 66.7% (ChatGPT) and 60.0% (Bard) of responses.
quote: When queries were posed as a patient, 66.7% of ChatGPT responses were safe compared to 60.0% of Google Bard responses.

title: The potential of chatbots in chronic venous disease patient management
outcome: Grading of chatbot answers to complex chronic venous disease questions by two specialists
effect: ChatGPT 4.0 grade 1 on 15/20 (75%), grade 4 on 1/20 (5%); ChatGPT 3.5 grade 1 on 9/20 (45%), grade 4 on 3/20 (15%); Clinical Camel grade 1 on 0/20, grade 4 on 10/20 (50%).
quote: Clinical Camel received a grade of 1 on 0 of 20 questions (0%), grade 2 on 5 of 20 questions (25%), grade 3 on 5 of 20 questions (25%), and grade 4 on 10 of 20 questions (50%).

title: The potential of chatbots in chronic venous disease patient management
outcome: Comparison of candidate chatbots on identical questions graded by specialists
effect: ChatGPT 4.0 outperformed ChatGPT 3.5 on administrative questions (20/20 grade 1 vs 14/20, 70%) and on complex questions (75% vs 45% grade 1); Clinical Camel performed worst (0% grade 1).
quote: On administrative and non-complex medical questions, ChatGPT 4.0 performed better than ChatGPT 3.5.

title: GPT-4 Underperforms Experts in Detecting IV Fluid Contamination
venue: The journal of applied laboratory medicine
outcome: GPT-4 accuracy versus healthcare personnel for detecting IV fluid contamination of BMP results
effect: Accuracy 95% CI 0.57-0.71 for GPT-4 vs 0.73-0.80 for HCP on NS set; 0.57-0.57 vs 0.73-0.80 on D5NS set. GPT-4 less accurate than trained HCP.
quote: GPT-4 is less accurate than trained HCP for detecting IV fluid contamination of basic metabolic panel results.

title: GPT-4 Underperforms Experts in Detecting IV Fluid Contamination
venue: The journal of applied laboratory medicine
outcome: Correlation between reported confidence and correct classification
effect: No correlation between reported confidence and likelihood of a correct classification.
quote: There was no correlation between reported confidence and likelihood of a correct classification.

title: The Fidelity of Artificial Intelligence to Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Recommendations for Patients with Gastric Cancer: A Retrospective Study
outcome: Concordance of AI treatment recommendations with tumor board decisions on local historical patients
effect: Overall concordance 86.96%; by stage 96.93% (I), 88.89% (II), 90.91% (III), 45.83% (IV).
quote: The concordance rate between the AI and MTB was 86.96%.

title: The Fidelity of Artificial Intelligence to Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Recommendations for Patients with Gastric Cancer: A Retrospective Study
outcome: Factors (age, performance status, stage) affecting AI-tumor board concordance across patient subgroups
effect: Age (p=0.000), performance status 1-3 (p=0.003, 0.007, 0.000), and stage IV (p=0.017) significantly affected concordance; stage IV concordance was 45.83%.
quote: In the multivariate analysis, age (p-value = 0.000), performance status (p-value = 0.003 for performance score 1; p-value = 0.007 for performance score 2; p-value = 0.000 for performance score 3), and stage IV (p-value = 0.017) had a significant effect on concordance between the MTB and WFO.

title: Does Clinical Decision Support Increase Appropriate Medication Prescribing for Cardiovascular Risk Reduction?
venue: Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine : JABFM
outcome: Prescribing for CVD risk factors, CDS intervention vs control clinics
effect: Hypertension prescribing 34.9% with CDS use vs 34.9% control (P=.998); dyslipidemia 11.3% vs 8.7% control (P=.044); smoking cessation showed similar pattern to dyslipidemia.
quote: Prescribing for dyslipidemia was significantly higher at intervention encounters where the CDS system was used (11.3% [95% CI, 9.3 to 13.3]) compared with dismissed (7.7% [95% CI, 6.1 to 9.3]; P = .003) and to control encounters (8.7% [95% CI, 7.0 to 10.4]; P = .044); smoking cessation medication showed a similar pattern.

title: Using temporal recalibration to improve the calibration of risk prediction models in competing risk settings when there are trends in survival over time
outcome: Calibration of 10-year predicted vs observed risk after recalibrating baseline hazard with recent data
effect: Standard approach over-estimated 10-year all-cause CIF by 0.028 (95% CI 0.015, 0.041); temporal recalibration 0.013 (0.000, 0.026); period analysis 0.005 (-0.008, 0.018).
quote: Using temporal recalibration or period analysis improved the calibration of the predicted risks across the full range of follow‐up, where particular improvements can be seen in the predicted risk of death due to colon cancer and the total risk of death.

title: Using temporal recalibration to improve the calibration of risk prediction models in competing risk settings when there are trends in survival over time
outcome: Calibration drift from improving survival trends in temporally later patients
effect: Standard model over-estimated 10-year risk of colon cancer death by 0.019, other causes 0.008, all causes 0.028 in patients diagnosed 2005.
quote: Using the standard approach to develop each model led to an over‐estimation of 0.019, 0.008 and 0.028 for the 10‐year marginal CIFs for colon cancer, other causes and all causes respectively, see Table 4 .

title: Assessing AI-Powered Patient Education: A Case Study in Radiology
outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot patient-education responses
effect: Readability was rated eighth-grade level; no comparison with patient literacy targets was reported.
quote: The readability level was rated eighth-grade level.
sample_unit: reviews of chatbot responses (30 questions x 2 trials x 3 chatbot settings, rated by two reviewers)

title: Preliminary assessment of automated radiology report generation with generative pre-trained transformers: comparing results to radiologist-generated reports
outcome: Differential diagnosis accuracy (top-1, top-5) of GPT models versus radiologists
effect: Top-1: radiologists 1.00, GPT-4 0.54, GPT-3.5 0.54, GPT-2 0.21; Top-5: 1.00, 0.96, 0.89, 0.54. GPT impression and differential diagnosis scores significantly lower than radiologists (p<0.05).
quote: However, qualitative scores of the GPT series in impression and differential diagnosis scores were significantly lower than those of radiologists (p < 0.05).

title: External validity of an automated delirium prediction model (DEMO) and comparison to the manual VMS-questions: a retrospective cohort study
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of delirium model on external hospital data against chart-review reference
effect: DEMO predicted 59 of 75 delirium cases (sensitivity 0.79, 95% CI 0.68-0.87; specificity 0.75, 95% CI 0.72-0.77); acceptable performance externally.
quote: The DEMO predicted 59 out of 75 delirium cases (sensitivity 0.79, 95% CI = 0.68-0.87; specificity 0.75, 95% CI = 0.72-0.77).

title: External validity of an automated delirium prediction model (DEMO) and comparison to the manual VMS-questions: a retrospective cohort study
outcome: DEMO performance compared with manual VMS-questions on same admissions
effect: DEMO had lower specificity (0.64 vs. 0.72; p < 0.001) and comparable sensitivity (0.83 vs. 0.80; p = 0.56) in patients ≥70 years.
quote: Compared to the VMS-questions, the DEMO showed a lower specificity (0.64 vs. 0.72; p < 0.001) and a comparable sensitivity (0.83 vs. 0.80; p = 0.56).

title: Comparison of Patient Education Materials Generated by Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer Versus Experts: An Innovative Way to Increase Readability of Patient Education Materials
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT vs expert patient education materials
effect: Expert materials at 7.5 grade; ChatGPT content at 10.5 grade despite being asked for seventh grade level.
quote: The Flesch-Kincaid score is at the 7.5 grade for expert-generated materials, whereas the content generated by ChatGPT is at the 10.5 grade (despite ChatGPT being asked to generate content at the seventh grade level).

title: Comparison of Patient Education Materials Generated by Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer Versus Experts: An Innovative Way to Increase Readability of Patient Education Materials
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education materials in plain language
effect: ChatGPT content was at 10.5 grade level versus 7.5 for experts, despite a request for seventh grade level.
quote: The Flesch-Kincaid score is at the 7.5 grade for expert-generated materials, whereas the content generated by ChatGPT is at the 10.5 grade (despite ChatGPT being asked to generate content at the seventh grade level).

title: Comparison of Patient Education Materials Generated by Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer Versus Experts: An Innovative Way to Increase Readability of Patient Education Materials
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-generated patient education content rated by 2 reviewers
effect: Accuracy of ChatGPT-generated content was 50%, with most errors being information errors; it often gave breast reduction or augmentation information instead of reconstruction.
quote: The accuracy of ChatGPT-generated content is 50%, with most errors being information errors.

title: AIROGS: Artificial Intelligence for Robust Glaucoma Screening Challenge
outcome: AI glaucoma screening performance on out-of-distribution and low-quality images in real-world settings
effect: Performance decreases significantly in real-world scenarios due to out-of-distribution and low-quality images; the challenge tested robustness, with the top team reaching AUC 0.99 (95% CI 0.98-0.99) for detecting ungradable images.
quote: While AI models for glaucoma screening from CFPs have shown promising results in laboratory settings, their performance decreases significantly in real-world scenarios due to the presence of out-of-distribution and low-quality images.

title: The Potential of ChatGPT as a Self-Diagnostic Tool in Common Orthopedic Diseases: Exploratory Study
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT diagnoses across days and raters
effect: Reproducibility between days was 1.0, 0.15, 0.7, 0.6, 0.6 for CTS, CM, LSS, KOA, HOA; between raters 1.0, 0.1, 0.64, -0.12, 0.04.
quote: The reproducibility between days was 1.0, 0.15, 0.7, 0.6, and 0.6 for CTS, CM, LSS, KOA, and HOA, respectively.
sample_unit: ChatGPT answers (5 conditions x 5 raters x 5 days)

title: The Potential of ChatGPT as a Self-Diagnostic Tool in Common Orthopedic Diseases: Exploratory Study
outcome: Whether ChatGPT answers recommended seeking medical attention and strength of recommendation
effect: 7 of 125 answers had no recommendation to seek medical attention; only a few had strong recommendation (essential 4/125, recommended 12/125, best 6/125, important 94/125).
quote: Additionally, 7 out of the 125 answers did not include a recommendation to seek medical attention.
sample_unit: ChatGPT answers (5 conditions x 5 raters x 5 days)

title: The Potential of ChatGPT as a Self-Diagnostic Tool in Common Orthopedic Diseases: Exploratory Study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT for common orthopedic conditions
effect: Correct answers 25/25 CTS, 1/25 CM, 24/25 LSS, 16/25 KOA, 17/25 HOA; 23/25 incorrect for CM.
quote: The ratios of correct answers were 25/25, 1/25, 24/25, 16/25, and 17/25 for CTS, CM, LSS, KOA, and HOA, respectively.
sample_unit: ChatGPT answers (5 conditions x 5 raters x 5 days)

title: The Use of Large Language Models to Generate Education Materials about Uveitis
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of LLM-generated and rewritten uveitis patient information
effect: ChatGPT mean FKGL 6.3 ± 1.2 vs Bard 10.5 ± 0.8; online uveitis information 11.0 ± 1.4; ChatGPT rewrote to 8.0 ± 1.0, Bard did not (11.1 ± 1.6).
quote: Online health information on uveitis had a mean grade level of 11.0 ± 1.4.

title: The Use of Large Language Models to Generate Education Materials about Uveitis
outcome: Reading level of patient-targeted uveitis materials versus a 6th grade target
effect: Online content mean grade level 11.0 ± 1.4; ChatGPT 6.3 ± 1.2 with grade-level prompt; Bard 10.5 ± 0.8; ChatGPT rewrite 8.0 ± 1.0; Bard rewrite 11.1 ± 1.6.
quote: The mean FKGL of responses to ChatGPT (6.3 ± 1.2) was significantly lower (P < 0.0001) than Bard 10.5 ± 0.8.

title: Evaluation of a Deep Learning-based Algorithm for Post-Radiotherapy Prostate Cancer Local Recurrence Detection Using Biparametric MRI
outcome: AI sensitivity for recurrent prostate cancer versus radiologist on post-radiotherapy patients
effect: AI model developed on treatment-naive patients had lower sensitivity than prospective radiology: patient-level 76.1% vs 91.3% (p=0.02); lesion-level 71.4% vs 87.5% (p=0.01).
quote: The AI model performance was lower than the prospective radiology interpretation (Rad) on a patient-(AI: 76.1% vs. Rad: 91.3%, p = 0.02) and lesion-level (AI: 71.4% vs. Rad: 87.5%, p = 0.01).

title: Evaluation of a Deep Learning-based Algorithm for Post-Radiotherapy Prostate Cancer Local Recurrence Detection Using Biparametric MRI
outcome: AI detection sensitivity compared with radiologist assessment on the same patients
effect: AI was less sensitive than radiologists at patient level (76.1% vs 91.3%, p=0.02) and lesion level (71.4% vs 87.5%, p=0.01).
quote: The AI model performance was lower than the prospective radiology interpretation (Rad) on a patient-(AI: 76.1% vs. Rad: 91.3%, p = 0.02) and lesion-level (AI: 71.4% vs. Rad: 87.5%, p = 0.01).

title: Evaluation of a Deep Learning-based Algorithm for Post-Radiotherapy Prostate Cancer Local Recurrence Detection Using Biparametric MRI
outcome: AI sensitivity variation across treatment modality and prostate volume subgroups
effect: Sensitivity was higher after EBRT than brachytherapy (patient-level 81.5% vs 68.4%; lesion-level 79.4% vs 59.1%); 100% and 94.1% in glands >34 ml.
quote: The AI model performance was higher in EBRT group both on patient-level (EBRT: 81.5% [22/27] vs. brachytherapy: 68.4% [13/19]) and lesion-level (EBRT: 79.4% [27/34] vs. brachytherapy: 59.1% [13/22]).

title: Incorporation of CAD (computer-aided detection) with thin-slice lung CT in routine 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging read-out protocol for detection of lung nodules
outcome: Reader nodule detection, reading time and metastasis diagnosis with versus without CAD assistance
effect: CAD-assisted reading cut time about 33% versus diagnostic CT (60 s to 40 s). CAD found 49 extra nodules but missed 53. Nodule counts were similar (282 vs 283). Per-patient AUC did not differ significantly (0.799 vs 0.783).
quote: There was no superiority of the advanced dCT or CAD techniques regarding the diagnosis of metastasis.

title: Incorporation of CAD (computer-aided detection) with thin-slice lung CT in routine 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging read-out protocol for detection of lung nodules
outcome: AUC versus non-AI protocols
effect: Overall AUCs were FDG PET 0.720, lCT 0.810, dCT 0.783, and CADs 0.799; lCT, dCT, and CAD showed comparable AUCs 0.78–0.81.
quote: In summary, regarding the diagnosis of metastasis on a patient basis, PET AUC (0.72) was inferior to lCT, dCT, and CAD because of low sensitivity (48%) in all three readers, but lCT, dCT, and CAD showed comparable good results in all the readers (AUC between 0.78 and 0.81).

title: Incorporation of CAD (computer-aided detection) with thin-slice lung CT in routine 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging read-out protocol for detection of lung nodules
outcome: false-positive CAD markings
effect: CADp showed 1967 nodules; on average 282 were accepted and 1685 rejected as false markings.
quote: In the given 100 patients, CADp showed total of 1967 nodules, of which on average 282 were accepted by the three readers, and remaining average 1685 were rejected as false markings.

title: Incorporation of CAD (computer-aided detection) with thin-slice lung CT in routine 18F-FDG PET/CT imaging read-out protocol for detection of lung nodules
outcome: clinician filtering of CAD false-positive nodule detections
effect: Readers accepted an average of 282 CAD nodules and rejected 1685 false markings (16.8 false positives per scan)
quote: In the given 100 patients, CADp showed total of 1967 nodules, of which on average 282 were accepted by the three readers, and remaining average 1685 were rejected as false markings.

title: Automated Large Vessel Occlusion Detection Software and Thrombectomy Treatment Times: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
outcome: Treatment times and patient outcomes (90-day mRS, mortality) with vs without AI
effect: DTG time reduced by 11.2 min (95% CI -18.22 to -4.2); no difference in 90-day functional independence (OR 1.3; 95% CI 0.42-4.0); mortality 31% vs 13%.
quote: In multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, NIHSS and ASPECTS, there was no observe a difference in likelihood of 90-day disability (mRS, 0-2) in the post-AI cohort relative to pre-AI (odds ratio, 1.3; 95% CI, 0.42-4.0).

title: Automated Large Vessel Occlusion Detection Software and Thrombectomy Treatment Times: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
outcome: Functional independence, mortality, and hospital length of stay versus standard care
effect: 90-day functional independence: odds ratio, 1.3; 95% CI, 0.42-4.0. Mortality: 31% pre-AI versus 13% post-AI; P <.001. No difference in hospital length of stay.
quote: The study team did not observe any differences in IV tPA treatment times, length of stay, rates of functional independence, or safety outcomes apart from mortality, which decreased after the AI intervention.

title: Automated Large Vessel Occlusion Detection Software and Thrombectomy Treatment Times: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial
outcome: Time to thrombectomy after automated LVO detection and real-time clinical team alerts
effect: Door-to-groin time decreased by 11.2 minutes (95% CI, -18.22 to -4.2); CT initiation-to-EVT time decreased by 9.8 minutes (95% CI, -16.9 to -2.6).
quote: In mixed-effects linear regression, implementation of the AI algorithm was associated with a reduction in DTG time by 11.2 minutes (95% CI, -18.22 to -4.2).

title: Development and Integration of Machine Learning Algorithm to Identify Peripheral Arterial Disease: Multistakeholder Qualitative Study
outcome: Stakeholder-reported factors enabling real-world integration of ML-driven CDS
effect: Longitudinal, multidisciplinary stakeholder engagement and early consideration of end-user needs were identified as key to translating algorithm performance into real-world care.
quote: Longitudinal and multidisciplinary stakeholder engagement in the development and integration of ML-driven CDS underpins its effective translation into real-world care.

title: Development and Integration of Machine Learning Algorithm to Identify Peripheral Arterial Disease: Multistakeholder Qualitative Study
outcome: Stakeholder-reported barriers to ML-driven CDS integration, including feedback loops
effect: Lack of feedback loops, failure to incorporate on-the-ground context, and data silos were identified as negative factors of integration.
quote: Negative factors of integration included failure to incorporate the on-the-ground context, the lack of feedback loops, and data silos limiting the ML-driven CDS.

title: Single-lead arrhythmia detection through machine learning: cross-sectional evaluation of a novel algorithm using real-world data
outcome: External retrospective validation of previously trained ECG arrhythmia model on real-world data from new sites
effect: On external real-world data, sensitivity 98%, specificity 100%, accuracy 98%, PPV 100%, NPV 93%, F1 99% for any arrhythmia; false negative rate 1.9%.
quote: For any arrhythmia, the model had a sensitivity of 98%, a specificity of 100%, an accuracy of 98%, a positive predictive value of 100%, a negative predictive value of 93% and an F<sub>1</sub> Score of 99%.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of a large language model in rheumatology: comparison of physician and ChatGPT-4
outcome: Correct diagnosis as top-1 and top-3 diagnoses, ChatGPT-4 versus rheumatologists on same cases
effect: Top diagnosis 35% vs 39% (p = 0.30); among top 3, 60% vs 55% (p = 0.38); higher sensitivity for IRD but lower specificity than rheumatologists.
quote: ChatGPT-4 listed the correct diagnosis comparable often to rheumatologists as the top diagnosis 35% vs 39% (p = 0.30); as well as among the top 3 diagnoses, 60% vs 55%, (p = 0.38).

title: Evaluating the Sensitivity, Specificity, and Accuracy of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, Bing AI, and Bard Against Conventional Drug-Drug Interactions Clinical Tools
outcome: Chatbot drug-drug interaction detection accuracy versus subscription DDI reference tool
effect: Specificity ranged from 0.372 (ChatGPT-3.5) to 0.769 (Bing AI); accuracy 0.469 (ChatGPT-3.5) to 0.788 (Bing AI) against subscription reference.
quote: When a subscription tool was used as a reference, the specificity ranged from a low of 0.372 (ChatGPT-3.5) to a high of 0.769 (Microsoft Bing AI).

title: External validation of deep learning-based automated detection algorithm for chest radiograph: practical issues in outpatient clinic
outcome: DLAD AUC on local outpatient clinic chest radiographs versus CT-based reference standard
effect: DLAD AUC 0.920 on external local data, significantly higher than unaided pulmonologists (0.756) and radiologists (0.782); no local performance drop seen.
quote: The performance of DLAD (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] = 0.920) was significantly higher than that of pulmonologists (AUC = 0.756) and radiologists (AUC = 0.782) without assistance of DLAD.
sample_unit: chest radiographs (one per individual) with paired chest CT

title: External validation of deep learning-based automated detection algorithm for chest radiograph: practical issues in outpatient clinic
outcome: Reader AUC with versus without DLAD assistance compared with standalone DLAD AUC
effect: Standalone DLAD AUC 0.920 exceeded assisted readers (pulmonologists 0.853; radiologists 0.854); assistance improved readers but human-AI team stayed below standalone performance.
quote: With help of DLAD, the AUCs were significantly higher for both groups (pulmonologists AUC = 0.853; radiologists AUC = 0.854).
sample_unit: chest radiographs (one per individual) with paired chest CT

title: A pilot study on the capability of artificial intelligence in preparation of patients' educational materials for Indian public health issues
venue: Journal of family medicine and primary care
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of ChatGPT-generated patient education materials
effect: Median Flesch Reading Ease Score 48.2 (Q1-Q3: 39-50.65), indicating text understandable by a college student rather than a general patient audience.
quote: The median Flesch Reading Ease Score was 48.2 (Q1-Q3: 39-50.65).

title: The Vienna Prediction Model for identifying patients at low risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study
outcome: O/E ratio after post-hoc recalibration of baseline hazard on cohort data
effect: Recalibration improved the O/E ratio from 1.6 to 1.03 (95% CI 0.55–1.74) on internal bootstrap validation. External validation of the recalibrated model is still needed.
quote: Internal bootstrap validation of this recalibration step indicated an O/E ratio of 1.03 (95% CI 0.55–1.74) of the updated VPM.

title: The Vienna Prediction Model for identifying patients at low risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study
outcome: Calibration of the VPM in a new prospective cohort
effect: Calibration adequate at 1 year, but the model underestimated 2-year risk above 5%; O/E ratio 52/32 = 1.6 (95% CI 1.2–2.0); calibration slope 1.3 (95% CI 0.3–2.4).
quote: The ratio of observed and expected events (O/E ratio), equal to 52/32 = 1.6 (95% CI 1.2–2.0), indicated general underestimation of recurrence probabilities.

title: The Vienna Prediction Model for identifying patients at low risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study
outcome: Underestimation of recurrent VTE risk in the prospective local cohort
effect: At 2 years, the observed/expected event ratio was 52/32 = 1.6 (95% CI 1.2–2.0), indicating underestimation of recurrence probabilities.
quote: The ratio of observed and expected events (O/E ratio), equal to 52/32 = 1.6 (95% CI 1.2–2.0), indicated general underestimation of recurrence probabilities.

title: The Vienna Prediction Model for identifying patients at low risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study
outcome: calibration (O/E ratio)
effect: The model underestimated recurrence probabilities, with an O/E ratio of 1.6, likely due to changing case mix and diagnostics.
quote: The ratio of observed and expected events (O/E ratio), equal to 52/32 = 1.6 (95% CI 1.2–2.0), indicated general underestimation of recurrence probabilities.

title: The Vienna Prediction Model for identifying patients at low risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism: a prospective cohort study
outcome: O/E ratio after recalibration
effect: Recalibrating the baseline hazard function corrected the original model's underestimation, resulting in an ideal O/E ratio of 1.03.
quote: Internal bootstrap validation of this recalibration step indicated an O/E ratio of 1.03 (95% CI 0.55–1.74) of the updated VPM.

title: AI-clinician collaboration via disagreement prediction: A decision pipeline and retrospective analysis of real-world radiologist-AI interactions
outcome: Simulated clinician burden of disagreement-guided presentation pipeline versus baseline all-findings display
effect: With disagreement model TPR 0.8, FPR 0.03 and 5% second-read probability, burden reduced by 4.8% ± 0.2%; burden rose 12.04% at FPR 0.10. Automation-bias protection itself not measured.
quote: Combining all of these, if the disagreement model TPRs and FPRs are 0.8 and 0.03, respectively, and the conditional probability of a second read is 0.05, burden is reduced by 4.8% ± 0.2%.

title: AI-clinician collaboration via disagreement prediction: A decision pipeline and retrospective analysis of real-world radiologist-AI interactions
outcome: Sensitivity of clinician burden to disagreement-model false positive rate (operating point)
effect: An FPR of 0.01 gives 9.55% ± 0.06% burden reduction, whereas an FPR of 0.10 gives a 12.04% ± 0.09% increase.
quote: Although an FPR of 0.01 can result in an expected 9.55% ± 0.06% reduction in burden, an FPR of 0.10 actually results in a 12.04% ± 0.09% increase.

title: AI-clinician collaboration via disagreement prediction: A decision pipeline and retrospective analysis of real-world radiologist-AI interactions
outcome: Burden impact of deferring/second-read requests on predicted disagreement findings
effect: Even if all clinically significant disagreements receive a second read, burden increases only 6.67% ± 0.07%; restricting to under 5% reduces burden by 4.8% ± 0.1%.
quote: Even if all cases of disagreement on clinically significant findings receive a second read, burden is only increased by 6.67% ± 0.07%.

title: Machine learning in clinical practice: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence tool after implementation
outcome: Real-time accuracy of deployed admission prediction AI versus original performance
effect: Live sensitivity 73.1%, specificity 74.3%, PPV 50%, NPV 88.7%, accuracy 74%; real-time tool became less accurate than the original.
quote: Our study showed the diagnostic evaluation of a real-time AI clinical decision-support tool became less accurate than the original.

title: Machine learning in clinical practice: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence tool after implementation
outcome: Accuracy variation across admission destinations after deployment
effect: Accuracy lowest for psychiatric unit admission (34%), highest for gastroenterology (84%) and medical admission (80%).
quote: The accuracy of the system was at the lowest for admission to psychiatric units (34%) and at the highest for gastroenterology and medical admission (84% and 80%, respectively).

title: Effectiveness of a Vendor Predictive Model for the Risk of Pediatric Asthma Exacerbation: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis
outcome: Asthma hospitalizations, ED visits, and oral steroid courses within 90 days after model implementation versus control
effect: Adjusted difference-in-differences: hospitalization -0.9% (95% CI -1.6 to -0.3), ED visit -2.4% (-3.9 to -0.8), oral steroid -1.9% (-4.3 to 0.5, not significant).
quote: This EHR vendor model implementation was associated with a significant decrease in asthma hospitalization and ED visits within 90 days of pediatric allergy and pulmonology clinic visits, but not oral steroid courses.

title: Comparison of humans versus mobile phone-powered artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and management of pigmented skin cancer in secondary care: a multicentre, prospective, diagnostic, clinical trial
outcome: Real-world clinical accuracy of AI versus experimental (online reader study) performance
effect: The ISIC AI algorithm, superior in experimental studies, was significantly inferior to specialists in the clinic (-11·6% [-20·3 to -3·0]) for diagnosis.
quote: An AI algorithm that was superior in experimental studies was significantly inferior to specialists in a real-world scenario, suggesting that caution is needed when extrapolating results of experimental studies to clinical practice.
sample_unit: suspicious pigmented lesions (diagnostic trial; 124 patients); management trial 5696 lesions from 66 patients

title: Comparison of humans versus mobile phone-powered artificial intelligence for the diagnosis and management of pigmented skin cancer in secondary care: a multicentre, prospective, diagnostic, clinical trial
outcome: Diagnostic and management accuracy of AI versus specialist and novice clinicians on same lesions
effect: 7-class AI equivalent to specialists (1·2% [-6·9 to 9·2]) and superior to novices (21·5%); ISIC AI inferior to specialists (-11·6%); management AI inferior to specialists (-0·5% scenario A).
quote: The diagnoses of the 7-class AI algorithm were equivalent to the specialists' diagnoses (absolute accuracy difference 1·2% [95% CI -6·9 to 9·2]) and significantly superior to the novices' ones (21·5% [13·1 to 30·0]).
sample_unit: suspicious pigmented lesions (diagnostic trial; 124 patients); management trial 5696 lesions from 66 patients

title: External validation, radiological evaluation, and development of deep learning automatic lung segmentation in contrast-enhanced chest CT
outcome: Segmentation error-free rate on internal versus external validation cohorts
effect: 82% of internal and 71% of external cases had no errors; 18% and 25% respectively had clinically insignificant errors, and one external case (0.5%) had a clinically significant error.
quote: On radiological review, 82% and 71% of internal and external cases respectively had no errors.
sample_unit: patients (225 pulmonary hypertension, 28 interstitial lung disease)

title: External validation, radiological evaluation, and development of deep learning automatic lung segmentation in contrast-enhanced chest CT
outcome: Clinical significance of segmentation errors found on radiologist review of model outputs
effect: No segmentation failures; most cases error-free or with insignificant errors; one external case (0.5%) with patulous oesophagus had a clinically significant error.
quote: One external case (0.5%) with patulous oesophagus had a clinically significant error.
sample_unit: patients (225 pulmonary hypertension, 28 interstitial lung disease)

title: Prediction of pulp exposure before caries excavation using artificial intelligence: Deep learning-based image data versus standard dental radiographs
outcome: Gap between standalone AI performance and student-plus-AI performance in pulp exposure prediction
effect: Standalone AI F1 0.71 vs students 0.58-0.59 without AI and 0.61 with AI (borderline P = 0.054); students gained only slightly from AI.
quote: Although the AI model had much better performance than all groups, the participants when given AI prediction, benefited only 'slightly'.

title: Encounter Appropriateness Score for You Model: Development and Pilot Implementation of a Predictive Model to Identify Visits Appropriate for Telehealth in Rheumatology
outcome: Whether providers distinguished true model recommendations from artificial (false) recommendations in pilot
effect: Providers agreed more with true than artificial recommendations (Cohen's κ = 0.45, P < 0.001); moderate discrimination; 201 pilot encounters; model increased appropriate telehealth visits.
quote: Providers were more likely to agree with true versus artificial recommendations (Cohen's κ = 0.45, P < 0.001), and the model increased the number of appropriate telehealth visits.

title: Accuracy and Reliability of Chatbot Responses to Physician Questions
outcome: Consistency of chatbot answer accuracy when low-scoring questions were requeried 8 to 17 days later
effect: 34 of 36 low-scoring questions (1.0-2.0) were requeried; median accuracy rose from 2.0 (IQR 1.0-3.0) to 4.0 (IQR 2.0-5.3), P < .01, showing answers varied on repeat.
quote: Of 36 questions with scores of 1.0 to 2.0, 34 were requeried or regraded 8 to 17 days later with substantial improvement (median score 2.0 [IQR, 1.0-3.0] vs 4.0 [IQR, 2.0-5.3]; P < .01).

title: Early detection of autism using digital behavioral phenotyping
outcome: Sensitivity of autism screening algorithm across sex, race and ethnicity subgroups
effect: Overall AUC 0.90, sensitivity 87.8%, specificity 80.8%, NPV 97.8%, PPV 40.6%; sensitivity was similar across subgroups defined by sex, race and ethnicity.
quote: The algorithm had similar sensitivity performance across subgroups as defined by sex, race and ethnicity.
sample_unit: children (17-36 months) at pediatric well-child visits

title: Enhanced YOLOv5 network-based object detection (BALFilter Reader) promotes PERFECT filter-enabled liquid biopsy of lung cancer from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF)
outcome: Diagnostic performance of AI versus two experienced pathologists on same clinical cases, histopathology as gold standard
effect: BALFilter Reader sensitivity 66.7% ± 16.7%, specificity 100.0% ± 0.0%, accuracy 75.0% ± 12.5% in ~2 min, versus pathologists' sensitivity 61.1%, specificity 16.7%, accuracy 50.0% in 10-30 min.
quote: The overall diagnosis performance (~2 min) with sensitivity@66.7% ± 16.7%, specificity@100.0% ± 0.0% and accuracy@75.0% ± 12.5% was superior to that from two experienced pathologists (10-30 min) with sensitivity@61.1%, specificity@16.7% and accuracy@50.0%, with the histopathological result as the gold standard.

title: Detecting changes in the performance of a clinical machine learning tool over time
outcome: Monthly AUC, AUPRC, Brier score drift via SPC charts over one year
effect: Average AUC 0.78, AUPRC 0.41, Brier 0.10; no points outside statistical control despite a drop in hospital admission rate outside control
quote: The AUC, AUPRC, and Brier scores showed no statistical control violations over one year, suggesting no performance drift.

title: Detecting changes in the performance of a clinical machine learning tool over time
outcome: Silent-mode live performance versus original validation performance
effect: Live background AUC 0.78 vs original 0.75-0.81; AUPRC 0.41 vs prior 0.19-0.38
quote: The average AUC (0.78) during this follow-up is comparable to the original validations (AUCs ranging between 0.75 and 0.81), while the AUPRC (0.41) even is slightly higher (previous AUPRCs ranging between 0.19 and 0.38).

title: Detecting changes in the performance of a clinical machine learning tool over time
outcome: Performance under population shift from training cohort (higher positivity, COVID-19)
effect: Positivity 13.4% vs 11.5% in training, contamination 10.3% vs 6.3%, 328 COVID-19 cases; performance stayed within statistical control
quote: However, despite evolving practices and populations, the performance of our model consistently remained within the bounds of statistical control, negating the necessity for recalibration and indicating our model is robust to changing environments.

title: Detecting changes in the performance of a clinical machine learning tool over time
outcome: Predictive performance relative to original validation
effect: Follow-up AUC was 0.78 versus original validation AUCs between 0.75 and 0.81; AUPRC was 0.41 versus previous AUPRCs between 0.19 and 0.38.
quote: The average AUC (0.78) during this follow-up is comparable to the original validations (AUCs ranging between 0.75 and 0.81), while the AUPRC (0.41) even is slightly higher (previous AUPRCs ranging between 0.19 and 0.38).

title: Detecting changes in the performance of a clinical machine learning tool over time
outcome: model performance in shadow mode
effect: The model achieved an average AUC of 0.78 for predicting blood culture outcomes during real-time shadow evaluation.
quote: The average AUC for predicting BC outcomes was 0.78 (standard deviation (SD) = 0.02).

title: Autonomous artificial intelligence increases real-world specialist clinic productivity in a cluster-randomized trial
outcome: Clinic productivity (completed encounters per hour per specialist) with vs without autonomous AI, in cluster-randomized trial
effect: AI clinic days had 1.59 encounters/hour (95% CI 1.37-1.80) vs control 1.14 (95% CI 1.02-1.25), a 40% higher productivity; primary endpoint met.
quote: The prespecified primary endpoint is met: AI leads to 40% higher productivity (1.59 encounters/hour, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.37-1.80) than control (1.14 encounters/hour, 95% CI: 1.02-1.25), p < 0.00; the secondary endpoint (productivity in all patients) is also met.

title: ChatGPT makes medicine easy to swallow: an exploratory case study on simplified radiology reports
