title: Assessment of ChatGPT in the Prehospital Management of Ophthalmological Emergencies - An Analysis of 10 Fictional Case Vignettes
outcome: Triage accuracy and potential for harm of ChatGPT answers to ophthalmological emergency vignettes
effect: Triage accuracy 93.6%; most prehospital recommendations appropriate, but potential to inflict harm to users/patients present in 32% of answers.
quote: However, an overall potential to inflict harm to users/patients was present in 32% of answers.
sample_unit: ChatGPT answers (10 fictional vignettes entered 5 times each)

title: ChatGPT and mycosis- a new weapon in the knowledge battlefield
outcome: ChatGPT knowledge currency and accuracy in fungal infection scenario questions
effect: The authors report deficits in timely literature updates, individual advice, consistency, accuracy and data safety as the largest barriers, although most responses were judged compelling. No numbers were given.
quote: However, the largest barriers to implementation are deficits in indiviudal advice, timely literature updates, consistency, accuracy and data safety.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound with artificial intelligence-assisted assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction
outcome: Agreement of AI-assisted FoCUS LVEF with formal TTE reference on same participants
effect: Overall ICC 0.904; weighted kappa 0.83 for LVEF categories; AUC 0.98 for LVEF <50% (sensitivity 92.8%, specificity 92.3%).
quote: The overall intraclass coefficient was 0.904, and 0.921 in the novice (n = 208) and 0.845 in the experienced (n = 216) cohorts.

title: Detecting transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) using machine learning: an evaluation of the performance of an algorithm in a UK setting
outcome: AUROC of US-developed ML algorithm on UK heart failure data versus proxy case definitions
effect: AUROC 0.84 (definitive) and 0.86 (possible) with combined primary and secondary care data; 0.68 to 0.78 with primary or secondary care data alone.
quote: The algorithm demonstrated strongest predictive ability when a combination of primary care and secondary care data were used (AUROC: 0.84 in definitive cohort and 0.86 in possible cohort).

title: Doctor Versus Artificial Intelligence: Patient and Physician Evaluation of Large Language Model Responses to Rheumatology Patient Questions in a Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Rheumatologist-rated accuracy of LLM versus physician responses to patient questions
effect: Rheumatologists rated AI accuracy 6.48 ± 2.07 vs physician 9.08 ± 0.64 (P < 0.0001); patients identified AI answers at only 0.49 vs 0.97 for physicians.
quote: However, rheumatologists rated AI responses significantly poorer than physician-generated responses, suggesting that LLM chatbot responses are inferior to physician responses, a difference that patients may not be aware of.

title: Clinical Decision Support System for All Stages of Gastric Carcinogenesis in Real-Time Endoscopy: Model Establishment and Validation Study
outcome: Overall accuracy of CDSS versus experienced endoscopists on prospective real-clinic evaluation
effect: No significant difference in overall accuracy between invited endoscopists and established CDSS in prospective real-clinic evaluation (P=.23).
quote: There was no significant difference in the overall accuracy between the invited endoscopists and established CDSS in the prospective real-clinic evaluation (P=.23).

title: Clinical Decision Support System for All Stages of Gastric Carcinogenesis in Real-Time Endoscopy: Model Establishment and Validation Study
outcome: Classification accuracy on internal test versus external test from another institution
effect: Overall accuracy 90.3% (89%-91.6%) internal; 85.3% (83.4%-97.2%) on external test of 1282 images from another institution.
quote: For the performance validation, the CDSS achieved 85.3% (83.4%-97.2%) overall accuracy.

title: Large Language Models for Therapy Recommendations Across 3 Clinical Specialties: Comparative Study
outcome: Correctness, omissions and harmfulness of LLM therapy recommendations rated by physicians
effect: Significant differences in falseness across models and specialties (P<.001); errors included confusing diagnoses, vague advice, omitting critical treatments such as antibiotics for infectious diseases.
quote: Distinct error patterns emerged, such as confusing diagnoses; providing vague, ambiguous advice; or omitting critical treatments, such as antibiotics for infectious diseases.

title: Large Language Models for Therapy Recommendations Across 3 Clinical Specialties: Comparative Study
outcome: LLM failure to detail treatment risks, quality-of-life effects, and additional information sources
effect: All models lagged in detailing treatment procedure risks, explaining therapy effects on quality of life, and offering additional information sources.
quote: All models lagged in detailing the risks associated with treatment procedures, explaining the effects of therapies on quality of life, and offering additional sources of information.

title: Role of sex in lung cancer risk prediction based on single low-dose chest computed tomography
outcome: Sybil AUC for lung cancer risk by sex subgroup at 1 and 6 years
effect: 1-year AUC 0.89 females vs 0.89 males (p=0.92); 6-year AUC 0.87 females vs 0.79 males (p=0.01), better in females.
quote: At 6 years, the AUC was 0.87 (95% CI: 0.83-0.93) for females and 0.79 (95% CI: 0.72-0.86) for males, p = 0.01.
sample_unit: low-dose chest CT scans (from 6127 screening participants)

title: Role of sex in lung cancer risk prediction based on single low-dose chest computed tomography
outcome: Sybil performance on local health-system LDCT data against outcomes
effect: Sybil achieved 1-year AUCs of 0.89 in both sexes on 10,573 real-world LDCTs from one health system.
quote: In conclusion, Sybil can accurately predict future lung cancer risk in females and males in a real-world setting and performs better in females than in males for predicting 6-year lung cancer risk.
sample_unit: low-dose chest CT scans (from 6127 screening participants)

title: Comparison of ChatGPT and Traditional Patient Education Materials for Men's Health
outcome: reading-level compliance
effect: Both UCF and ChatGPT failed official readability standards; ChatGPT was worse across all 6 topics (all P < .001).
quote: Both UCF and ChatGPT failed official readability standards, although ChatGPT performed significantly worse across all 6 topics (all P < .001).
sample_unit: men's health topics (UCF resources compared with ChatGPT responses)

title: Comparison of ChatGPT and Traditional Patient Education Materials for Men's Health
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of ChatGPT patient education output (readability and understandability)
effect: ChatGPT responses were longer and more complex, failed readability standards, and had worse understandability than UCF; the sixth-grade prompt improved readability, meeting the recommended level for 2 topics.
quote: Qualitatively, UCF and ChatGPT had comparable accuracy, although ChatGPT had better comprehensiveness and worse understandability.
sample_unit: men's health topics (UCF resources compared with ChatGPT responses)

title: Comparison of ChatGPT and Traditional Patient Education Materials for Men's Health
outcome: readability after sixth-grade prompt
effect: Adjusted ChatGPT readability typically surpassed UCF and met the recommended level for 2 topics.
quote: Conversely, adjusted ChatGPT readability typically surpassed UCF, even meeting the recommended level for 2 topics.
sample_unit: men's health topics (UCF resources compared with ChatGPT responses)

title: Artificial intelligence chatbots as sources of patient education material for obstructive sleep apnoea: ChatGPT versus Google Bard
venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of chatbot patient education responses on obstructive sleep apnoea
effect: Mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was 9.0 for ChatGPT and 5.9 for Google Bard.
quote: The mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level for ChatGPT was 9.0 and Google Bard was 5.9.

title: Multi-class glioma segmentation on real-world data with missing MRI sequences: comparison of three deep learning algorithms
outcome: Segmentation performance with missing MRI sequences using sparsified training
effect: With Sparsified training, missing MRI sequences did not statistically affect performance; nn-Unet gave accurate segmentations despite incomplete MRI datasets.
quote: By applying Sparsified training, missing MRI sequences did not statistically affect the performance.
country: Multinational (12 hospitals worldwide; BraTS 2021 plus clinical data)

title: Multi-class glioma segmentation on real-world data with missing MRI sequences: comparison of three deep learning algorithms
outcome: Performance on external test set from other hospitals versus internal test set
effect: All models' median DSC on both internal and external test sets were within or above human inter-rater agreement (0.74-0.85); nn-Unet DSC internal 0.86, external 0.93.
quote: All models' median Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) for both test sets were within, or higher than, previously reported human inter-rater agreement (range of 0.74-0.85).
country: Multinational (12 hospitals worldwide; BraTS 2021 plus clinical data)

title: Assessing the Impact of Image Quality on Deep Learning Classification of Infectious Keratitis
outcome: CNN AUROC/AUPRC across five corneal photograph quality parameters (gaze, eyelid, exposure, focus, light reflection)
effect: Light reflection or eyelids obscuring the cornea were each linked to significantly higher CNN performance. No other quality parameter significantly influenced performance. Expert-level performance was reported regardless of image quality.
quote: The CNN demonstrated expert-level performance regardless of image quality.

title: Real-world validation of Artificial Intelligence-based Computed Tomography auto-contouring for prostate cancer radiotherapy planning
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Local performance of commercial auto-contouring vs manual contours on retrospective local patients (DSC, HD, clinical score)
effect: Unedited vs manual DSC ranged 0.65 (seminal vesicles) to 0.94 (bladder); median clinical score 4; 2 and 3 of 20 patients not fully satisfactory for the two observers.
quote: The average values between the two observers of DSC regarding manual vs (fully) automatic contours showed values ranging between 0.65 for seminal vesicles and 0.94 for bladder with significant differences between the two observers for prostate (after editing) and for femoral heads + femurs (this last not clinically relevant).

title: Real-world validation of Artificial Intelligence-based Computed Tomography auto-contouring for prostate cancer radiotherapy planning
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Inter-observer variability and contouring time with AI+editing vs manual contouring
effect: Inter-observer DSC improved with AI+edit (seminal vesicles 0.83 vs 0.73; prostate 0.88 vs 0.83; rectum 0.96 vs 0.81); editing time 3-7 min vs 17-24 min manual (p<0.01).
quote: After automatic contouring and manual editing, inter-observer variability improved significantly, particularly for femoral heads + femurs, rectum and seminal vesicles.

title: Real-world validation of Artificial Intelligence-based Computed Tomography auto-contouring for prostate cancer radiotherapy planning
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: clinician review of automatic contours
effect: Review found segmentation not fully satisfactory in 2/20 and 3/20 patients, requiring more extensive editing.
quote: Despite the excellent performances, in a limited fraction of patients the segmentation was not fully satisfactory (2 and 3 out of 20 patients for the two observers, respectively), requiring more extensive editing for a few patients.

title: Real-world validation of Artificial Intelligence-based Computed Tomography auto-contouring for prostate cancer radiotherapy planning
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: edited contour agreement
effect: After editing, DSC improved p ≤ 0.002; seminal vesicles 0.76 vs 0.65 and prostate 0.86 vs 0.82.
quote: After editing, DSC significantly improved (p ≤ 0.002) for both OARs and CTVs: the larger gain was found for seminal vesicles (0.76 vs 0.65) and for prostate (0.86 vs 0.82).

title: Real-world validation of Artificial Intelligence-based Computed Tomography auto-contouring for prostate cancer radiotherapy planning
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: clinician contouring time
effect: Manual vs automatic+editing time: Obs 1 24 (±3.5) to 7 min (±3); Obs 2 17 (±2.5) to 3 min (±1.5), p < 0.01.
quote: As shown in the Supplementary material ( Supplementary Fig. S5 ), the time for contouring (manual vs automatic + editing) was significantly reduced (p < 0.01) for both operators: for Obs 1 it was reduced from 24 (±3.5) to 7 min (±3) and for Obs 2 from 17 (±2.5) to 3 min (±1.5).

title: Real-world validation of Artificial Intelligence-based Computed Tomography auto-contouring for prostate cancer radiotherapy planning
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Dice Similarity Coefficient after manual editing of automatic contours
effect: After editing, DSC significantly improved (p <= 0.002) for both OARs and CTVs: the larger gain was found for seminal vesicles (0.76 vs 0.65) and for prostate (0.86 vs 0.82).
quote: After editing, DSC significantly improved (p ≤ 0.002) for both OARs and CTVs: the larger gain was found for seminal vesicles (0.76 vs 0.65) and for prostate (0.86 vs 0.82).

title: Fairness of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Foregone Preventive Dental Care for Adults
outcome: Model AUC across racial/ethnic, age, and income subgroups versus overall
effect: Overall AUC 0.84; full model AUC 0.88 for White individuals and older adults, with performance loss for other subgroups; lowest AUC 0.76 for other/multiple racial groups.
quote: While the full sample model performed similarly when applied to White individuals and older adults (AUC, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.87-0.90), there was a loss of performance for other subgroups.

title: Fairness of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Foregone Preventive Dental Care for Adults
outcome: Model performance after removing race/ethnicity, age, and income predictors
effect: Removing subgroup-sensitive predictors (race and ethnicity, age, income) did not impact model performance.
quote: Removing the subgroup-sensitive predictors (ie, race and ethnicity, age, and income) did not impact model performance.

title: Validating the Generalizability of Ophthalmic Artificial Intelligence Models on Real-World Clinical Data
outcome: Glaucoma classification and optic disc segmentation performance of public-trained vs local real-world-data-trained models on local test data
effect: Public models dropped 8.0% (OD segmentation, to 85.6%) and 18.4% (glaucoma classification, to 76.6%) on RWD; RWD-trained models outperformed public models on RWD by 2.0% and 9.5%.
quote: RWD models outperformed public models on RWD test sets by 2.0% and 9.5%, respectively, in OD segmentation and glaucoma classification tasks.

title: Validating the Generalizability of Ophthalmic Artificial Intelligence Models on Real-World Clinical Data
outcome: Performance of models trained on local real-world data versus public data when tested on local data
effect: RWD-trained models outperformed public-trained models on RWD test sets by 2.0% (OD segmentation) and 9.5% (glaucoma classification).
quote: RWD models outperformed public models on RWD test sets by 2.0% and 9.5%, respectively, in OD segmentation and glaucoma classification tasks.

title: Ability of machine-learning based clinical decision support system to reduce alert fatigue, wrong-drug errors, and alert users about look alike, sound alike medication
venue: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
outcome: Alert rate and acceptance rate of ML-based medication alerts in outpatient prescribing
effect: 28,536 alerts across 1,206,895 prescriptions (2.36% alert rate); 13,947 (48.88%) accepted; 470 intercepted errors (1.64% of alerts).
quote: Over the two-year study period, 1,206,895 prescriptions were ordered and a total of 28,536 alerts were triggered (alert rate: 2.36 %).

title: Algorithmic Fairness of Machine Learning Models for Alzheimer Disease Progression
outcome: Sensitivity and fairness metrics across ethnicity, race, and sex subgroups for AD progression models
effect: Sensitivity was lower for Hispanic participants; true positive rate difference ranged from 20.9% (5.5%) for RNN to 27.8% (9.8%) for SVM in MCI and 24.1% (5.4%) to 48.2% (17.3%) in AD. Sex fairness generally satisfied.
quote: Sensitivity for predicting progression to MCI and AD was lower for Hispanic participants compared with non-Hispanic participants; the difference (SD) in true positive rate ranged from 20.9% (5.5%) for the RNN model to 27.8% (9.8%) for the SVM model in MCI and 24.1% (5.4%) for the RNN model to 48.2% (17.3%) for the LR model in AD.

title: Algorithmic Fairness of Machine Learning Models for Alzheimer Disease Progression
outcome: Model performance for underrepresented racial and ethnic groups in a cohort that was 92.4% White
effect: Sensitivity was lower for Black and Asian participants vs non-Hispanic White participants; AD true positive rate difference for Black vs White was 14.5% (LR), 12.3% (SVM), 28.4% (RNN). Models were accurate in aggregate but failed fairness metrics.
quote: Sensitivity was similarly lower for Black and Asian participants compared with non-Hispanic White participants; for example, the difference (SD) in AD true positive rate was 14.5% (51.6%) in the LR model, 12.3% (35.1%) in the SVM model, and 28.4% (16.8%) in the RNN model for Black vs White participants, and the difference (SD) in MCI true positive rate was 25.6% (13.1%) in the LR model, 24.3% (13.1%) in the SVM model, and 6.8% (18.7%) in the RNN model for Asian vs White participants.

title: Assessing the Performance of ChatGPT in Medical Biochemistry Using Clinical Case Vignettes: Observational Study
outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT answers to the same vignettes across two repeated attempts
effect: 4 of 10 correct on the first attempt and 6 of 10 on the second; responses differed between attempts, and case 3 produced different answers across multiple attempts.
quote: But, to our surprise, for case 3, different answers were obtained with multiple attempts.

title: Framework for Radiation Oncology Department-wide Evaluation and Implementation of Commercial Artificial Intelligence Autocontouring
outcome: Commercial AI autocontour agreement with clinically approved contours on local multi-clinic CT data
effect: High agreement (DSC >0.9) in 27.8%, 32.8%, 34.1% of cases; low agreement (DSC <0.5) in 7.4%, 8.8%, 6.1%; worse in brain and H&N than pelvis and thorax.
quote: All 3 solutions had low quantitative agreement in 7.4%, 8.8%, and 6.1% of cases (DSC <0.5), performing worse in brain (median DSC = 0.65/0.78/0.75) and H&N (median DSC = 0.76/0.80/0.81).
sample_unit: patient planning CT scans (859 clinically approved contours)

title: Framework for Radiation Oncology Department-wide Evaluation and Implementation of Commercial Artificial Intelligence Autocontouring
outcome: Head-to-head comparison of three commercial autocontouring products on same patient data
effect: AI1/AI2/AI3 differed by disease site; e.g., brain median DSC 0.65/0.78/0.75; qualitative acceptability 70.7% (AI1) and 74.6% (AI2) of ROIs.
quote: Qualitatively, AI1 and AI2 contours were acceptable (rated 1-2) with at most minor edits in 70.7% and 74.6% of ROIs (2906 ratings), higher for abdomen (AI1: 79.2%) and thorax (AI2: 90.2%), and lower for H&N (29.0/35.6%).
sample_unit: patient planning CT scans (859 clinically approved contours)

title: Framework for Radiation Oncology Department-wide Evaluation and Implementation of Commercial Artificial Intelligence Autocontouring
outcome: Blinded expert clinician Likert ratings of AI-generated contours
effect: Multiple experts rated blinded AI contours; 70.7% (AI1) and 74.6% (AI2) of ROIs acceptable with at most minor edits across 2906 ratings; H&N lower (29.0/35.6%).
quote: Qualitative assessment was performed by multiple experts scoring blinded AI-contours using a Likert scale.
sample_unit: patient planning CT scans (859 clinically approved contours)

title: Framework for Radiation Oncology Department-wide Evaluation and Implementation of Commercial Artificial Intelligence Autocontouring
outcome: End-user workflow and usability survey of autocontouring solutions
effect: Survey showed strong user preference for full automation and mixed preferences for accuracy versus total number of structures generated.
quote: An end-user survey showed strong user preference for full automation and mixed preferences for accuracy versus total number of structures generated.
sample_unit: patient planning CT scans (859 clinically approved contours)

title: Quantifying the impact of AI recommendations with explanations on prescription decision making
outcome: Influence on clinician prescribing of AI with explanation versus AI alone
effect: Additional information (peer, AI, XAI) strongly influenced prescriptions, significantly for AI. Simple XAI did not have higher influence than AI alone; marginal impact of simple XAI was low.
quote: We found that additional information (peer, AI or XAI) had a strong influence on prescriptions (significantly for AI, not so for peers) but simple XAI did not have higher influence than AI alone.

title: Quantifying the impact of AI recommendations with explanations on prescription decision making
outcome: Correlation between self-reported XAI usefulness and actual influence on prescriptions
effect: No correlation between clinicians' self-reported XAI usefulness and whether XAI influenced their prescriptions, casting doubt on self-reports as a valid metric for assessing XAI.
quote: There was no correlation between attitudes to AI or clinical experience on the AI-supported decisions and nor was there correlation between what doctors self-reported about how useful they found the XAI and whether the XAI actually influenced their prescriptions.

title: Population-wide evaluation of artificial intelligence and radiologist assessment of screening mammograms
outcome: Standalone AI vs first-reader radiologists on cancer detection accuracy, same data
effect: AI matched at first-reader specificity was comparable on all measures (sensitivity 62.6% vs 63.5%, p=0.43); AI matched at sensitivity had lower specificity (97.5% vs 97.7%) and higher recall rate; different cancers detected.
quote: Standalone AI spec did not differ statistically significantly from the first reader across any accuracy measures (Table 2 ).

title: Population-wide evaluation of artificial intelligence and radiologist assessment of screening mammograms
outcome: Effect of AI decision threshold choice on accuracy relative to readers
effect: Threshold matched at reader specificity gave equivalent accuracy; threshold matched at sensitivity gave lower specificity (97.5% vs 97.7%), PPV 17.5% vs 18.7%, and higher recall rate (3.0% vs 2.8%).
quote: The accuracy of the AI system was comparable to that of first readers in a double-read mammography screening population, mainly when the AI score cut-off was matched at first reader specificity, highlighting the importance of choosing an appropriate threshold.

title: Population-wide evaluation of artificial intelligence and radiologist assessment of screening mammograms
outcome: Screen-detected and interval cancer detection
effect: AI_sens/AI_spec detected fewer screen-detected cancers (1166/1156 vs 1252) but more interval cancers (126/117 vs 39), p<0.0001.
quote: Both AI<sub>sens</sub> and AI<sub>spec</sub> detected significantly fewer screen-detected cancers (1166 (AI<sub>sens</sub>), 1156 (AI<sub>spec</sub>) vs 1252; p < 0.0001) but found more interval cancers compared to first readers (126 (AI<sub>sens</sub>), 117 (AI<sub>spec</sub>) vs 39; p < 0.0001) with varying types of cancers detected across multiple subgroups.

title: Evaluating the performance of artificial intelligence software for lung nodule detection on chest radiographs in a retrospective real-world UK population
outcome: Local retrospective performance against radiologist report and cancer diagnosis reference standards
effect: Versus radiologist reports: sensitivity 54.5%, specificity 83.2%, PPV 5.5%, NPV 99.0%. Versus cancer diagnosis: sensitivity 60.9%, PPV 5.6%. Considerable underperformance in real-world cohort.
quote: The software demonstrated considerable underperformance in this real-world patient cohort.

title: Evaluating the performance of artificial intelligence software for lung nodule detection on chest radiographs in a retrospective real-world UK population
outcome: Generalisability of training/testing data to local population; false positive failure analysis
effect: Normal or variant anatomy misidentified as abnormality in 69.9% of 943 false positives; lack of generalisability in training and testing datasets suggested as factor.
quote: Failure analysis suggested a lack of generalisability in the training and testing datasets as a potential factor.

title: Evaluating the performance of artificial intelligence software for lung nodule detection on chest radiographs in a retrospective real-world UK population
outcome: Low PPV in low-prevalence population causing false positives and over-investigation
effect: PPV 5.5% with 1.6% cancer prevalence; 943 false positives; low PPV risks over-investigation and limits clinical translation.
quote: The low PPV carries the risk of over-investigation and limits the translation of the software to clinical practice.

title: An AI Dietitian for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Management Based on Large Language and Image Recognition Models: Preclinical Concept Validation Study
outcome: LLM performance on dietitian exam and expert-reviewed responses to common medical nutrition therapy questions
effect: ChatGPT and GPT 4.0 passed the Chinese Registered Dietitian exam; dietitians rated 162 of 168 ChatGPT responses favorably; recommendations mostly aligned except root vegetables and dry beans.
quote: Professional dietitians' reviews of ChatGPT's responses to common questions were largely positive, with 162 out of 168 providing favorable reviews.
sample_unit: patients surveyed (plus 168 dietitian reviews of ChatGPT responses and exam questions)

title: Heart-to-heart with ChatGPT: the impact of patients consulting AI for cardiovascular health advice
outcome: ChatGPT response quality (correct, concise, comprehensive, comprehensible) by prompt health literacy level
effect: Prompts written at higher health literacy levels generally yielded higher-quality answers, implying lower-quality responses for lower-literacy prompts. Some responses were hazardously incorrect and incomplete.
quote: Prompts formulated at higher levels of health literacy generally yielded higher-quality answers.

title: External validation of a lung cancer-based prediction model for two-year mortality in esophageal cancer patient cohorts
venue: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
outcome: Calibration and discrimination of lung cancer model when applied to esophageal cancer patients
effect: dCRT needed intercept adjustment (c-statistic 0.67, 95%CI 0.58 to 0.75); nCRT initial miscalibration (CS 1.72) required intercept and slope recalibration (c-statistic 0.62, 95%CI 0.57 to 0.67).
quote: For nCRT patients the model needed adjustment of both the slope and the intercept because of initial miscalibration in the validation population (CITL 0.00; CS 1.72).

title: External validation of a lung cancer-based prediction model for two-year mortality in esophageal cancer patient cohorts
venue: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
outcome: Calibration after model recalibration
effect: After recalibration, calibration was CITL 0 and CS 1 in nCRT patients.
quote: After recalibration, the model showed perfect calibration (i.e., CITL 0, CS 1), as is common after recalibration.

title: Clinical decision-making in benzodiazepine deprescribing by healthcare providers vs. AI-assisted approach
outcome: Accuracy and ambiguity of ChatGPT-4 deprescribing outputs versus HCP judgement
effect: 22.1% ambiguous outputs, generic answers and inaccuracies; overall agreement 95% but κ = .200; criteria agreement 74.7% to 91.3%, with low kappas.
quote: Important limitations of GPT-4 responses were identified, including 22.1% ambiguous outputs, generic answers and inaccuracies, posing inappropriate decision-making risks.

title: Simplifying radiologic reports with natural language processing: a novel approach using ChatGPT in enhancing patient understanding of MRI results
venue: Archives of orthopaedic and trauma surgery
outcome: Patient-rated comprehensibility of ChatGPT-simplified MRI reports by report complexity
effect: Simplicity of word choice and sentence structure rated "Agree" on average; patients better at knowing what the text was about (p = 0.001) and drawing correct conclusions (p = 0.013829) the more simplified the report.
quote: Participants reported being significantly better at knowing what the text was about (p = 0.001) and drawing the correct conclusions the more simplified the report of findings was (p = 0.013829).

title: Effect of an artificial intelligence-assisted system on endoscopic diagnosis of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions: a multicentre, tandem, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
outcome: Miss rate of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions, AI-first vs routine-first
effect: Per-lesion miss rates 1.7% (2/118) AI-first vs 6.7% (6/90) routine-first (RR 0.25, 95% CI 0.06-1.08; p=0.079); per-patient 1.9% vs 5.1% (RR 0.37, 0.08-1.71; p=0.40).
quote: Per-lesion miss rates were 1·7% (2/118; 95% CI 0·0-4·0) in the AI-first group versus 6·7% (6/90; 1·5-11·8) in the routine-first group (risk ratio 0·25, 95% CI 0·06-1·08; p=0·079).

title: Effect of an artificial intelligence-assisted system on endoscopic diagnosis of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions: a multicentre, tandem, double-blind, randomised controlled trial
outcome: Clinician performance (lesion miss rate) with versus without AI assistance in intended deployment mode
effect: Endoscopists with AI had lower point-estimate miss rates (per-lesion 1.7% vs 6.7%), but confidence intervals were wide and not statistically significant (p=0.079).
quote: The observed effect of AI-assisted endoscopy on the per-lesion and per-patient miss rates of superficial oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma and precancerous lesions under WLE and non-magnified NBI was consistent with substantial benefit through to a neutral or small negative effect.

title: Health Disinformation Use Case Highlighting the Urgent Need for Artificial Intelligence Vigilance: Weapons of Mass Disinformation
outcome: Ability of LLM guardrails to block generation of harmful health disinformation
effect: 102 distinct disinformation blog articles (>17,000 words) on vaccines and vaping generated in 65 minutes, plus 20 realistic images in under 2 minutes, without specialized knowledge in bypassing guardrails.
quote: These observations demonstrate that when the guardrails of AI tools are insufficient, the ability to rapidly generate diverse and large amounts of convincing disinformation is profound.

title: Health Disinformation Use Case Highlighting the Urgent Need for Artificial Intelligence Vigilance: Weapons of Mass Disinformation
outcome: Presence of coercive, manipulative language in LLM-generated health content targeted at groups
effect: Every one of the 102 generated posts was coercive and targeted at diverse groups such as young adults, young parents, older persons, pregnant people, and those with chronic conditions.
quote: Each post was coercive and targeted at diverse societal groups, including young adults, young parents, older persons, pregnant people, and those with chronic health conditions.

title: A Mobile App That Addresses Interpretability Challenges in Machine Learning-Based Diabetes Predictions: Survey-Based User Study
outcome: Clinician comprehension of diabetes prediction process, data, features and feature importance after using explanations
effect: Reported substantial improvement in medical professionals' comprehension of the prediction process, training data sets, features used and feature importance; most reported heightened understanding and trust. No numbers in abstract.
quote: The evaluation study findings underscore the substantial improvement in medical professionals' comprehension of key aspects, including the (1) diabetes prediction process, (2) data sets used for model training, (3) data features used, and (4) relative significance of different features in prediction outcomes.

title: Feasibility of Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty maps to evaluate deep learning-based synthetic CTs for adaptive proton therapy
outcome: Correlation of MCD uncertainty maps with sCT error maps
quote: Evaluation of the correlation showed an average of r = 0.92 ± 0.03 and r = 0.92 ± 0.03 for errors between uncertainty-HU, r = 0.66 ± 0.09 and r = 0.62 ± 0.06 between uncertainty-range, r = 0.64 ± 0.06 and r = 0.58 ± 0.07 between uncertainty-WET, and r = 0.65 ± 0.09 and r = 0.67 ± 0.07 between uncertainty and dose difference for DCNN and cycleGAN model, respectively.

title: Demographic Representation in 3 Leading Artificial Intelligence Text-to-Image Generators
outcome: Female and non-White surgeon representation in AI-generated images versus real-world demographics
effect: Midjourney and Stable Diffusion depicted female surgeons at 0% and 1.8% and non-White surgeons at 0.5% and 0.6% (P < .001); DALL-E 2 matched attendings (15.9% vs 14.7% female) but underestimated trainees.
quote: In contrast, Midjourney and Stable Diffusion had significantly lower representation of images of female (0% and 1.8%, respectively; P < .001) and non-White (0.5% and 0.6%, respectively; P < .001) surgeons than DALL-E 2 or true demographic data.

title: Demographic Representation in 3 Leading Artificial Intelligence Text-to-Image Generators
outcome: Model output demographic representation compared with real-world attending surgeon and trainee demographics
effect: Two of three models depicted over 98% of surgeons as White and male; all 3 models underestimated trainee representation (DALL-E 2 female 15.9% vs 35.8%, P < .001).
quote: In this study, 2 leading publicly available text-to-image generators amplified societal biases, depicting over 98% surgeons as White and male.

title: Developer Perspectives on Potential Harms of Machine Learning Predictive Analytics in Health Care: Qualitative Analysis

quote: Even though MLPA developers recognized that their products can harm patients, public, and even health systems, robust procedures to assess the potential for harms and the need for mitigation do not exist.

title: Optimizing Ophthalmology Patient Education via ChatBot-Generated Materials: Readability Analysis of AI-Generated Patient Education Materials and The American Society of Ophthalmic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Patient Brochures
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient materials with vs without 6th-grade reading level prompt
effect: Prompting for a 6th-grade level significantly improved readability for both chatbots; prompted ChatGPT 4.0 reached Flesch Reading Ease 67.9 and SMOG 10.2, versus 36.5 and 14.7 unprompted.
quote: When prompted to produce PEM at a 6th-grade reading level, both ChatGPT 4.0 and Bard were able to significantly improve in their readability scores, with prompted ChatGPT 4.0 being able to consistently generate content that was easier to read (Flesch Reading Ease Score: 67.9, Simple Measure of Gobbledygook: 10.2).
sample_unit: patient education topics (each generated by 2 chatbots with and without a 6th-grade prompt)

title: Optimizing Ophthalmology Patient Education via ChatBot-Generated Materials: Readability Analysis of AI-Generated Patient Education Materials and The American Society of Ophthalmic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Patient Brochures
outcome: Reading difficulty of unprompted AI-generated patient education materials
effect: Unprompted ChatGPT 4.0 material was hardest to read (FRE 36.5; SMOG 14.7); unprompted Bard was easier (FRE 52.3; SMOG 12.7), though still above a 6th-grade level.
quote: Across all readability indices, PEM generated by ChatGPT 4.0 consistently had the highest readability scores, indicating that the material generated by this AI chatbot may be most difficult to read in its unprompted form (Flesch Reading Ease Score: 36.5; Simple Measure of Gobbledygook: 14.7).
sample_unit: patient education topics (each generated by 2 chatbots with and without a 6th-grade prompt)

title: Prospective implementation of AI-assisted screen reading to improve early detection of breast cancer
outcome: Proportion of cases flagged for review and additional cancers detected after threshold adjustment
effect: Threshold moved to a more specific point for workload capacity: flagged cases fell from 10.6–11.2% (pilots) to 7.4% live, CDR still +0.7/1,000. Simulated higher-specificity point flagged 2.9% while detecting 10 of 11 additional cancers.
quote: Before launching the AI system into live use, its decision threshold was adjusted to a more specific predetermined operating point to accommodate the site’s workload capacity, resulting in a smaller proportion of cases (7.4%, 1,186/15,953) flagged for additional review in live use.

title: Prospective implementation of AI-assisted screen reading to improve early detection of breast cancer
outcome: Cancer detection, recalls, predictive value, and reading workload in the human–AI workflow
effect: Compared with double reading, AI-assisted reading added 0.7-1.6 cancers per 1,000 cases, 0.16-0.30% recalls and 4-6% overall reading workload; PPV increased 0.1-1.9%.
quote: The results showed that, compared to double reading, implementing the AI-assisted additional-reader process could achieve 0.7-1.6 additional cancer detection per 1,000 cases, with 0.16-0.30% additional recalls, 0-0.23% unnecessary recalls and a 0.1-1.9% increase in positive predictive value (PPV) after 7-11% additional human reads of AI-flagged cases (equating to 4-6% additional overall reading workload).

title: Prospective implementation of AI-assisted screen reading to improve early detection of breast cancer
outcome: cancer detection and recalls
effect: Comparing human readers with and without the AI assistant demonstrated a 7% relative increase in cancer detection rate (24 more cases) and a 3% relative increase in PPV.
quote: Across the three phases, the implementation of the AI-assisted additional-reader workflow resulted in 24 more cancer cases detected (7% relative increase in cancer detection rate (CDR)) and 70 more women recalled (0.28% increase in absolute recall rate), at a positive predictive value (PPV) for screening of 20.0% (3% relative increase) (Table 3 ).

title: Impact of real-life use of artificial intelligence as support for human reading in a population-based breast cancer screening program with mammography and tomosynthesis
outcome: Cancer detection rate, recall rate, and positive predictive value of recalls
effect: With versus without AI: CDR 9.0‰ vs 5.8‰; PPV 14.6% vs 10.6%; recall rate 6.1% vs 5.4% (all p < 0.001).
quote: The implementation of an AI system for concurrent decision support for reading DM and DBT screening exams increased the breast cancer detection rate (CDR) by 3.2‰ (9.0‰ vs 5.8‰; p < 0.001) and the positive predictive value (PPV) of the recalled women by 4% (14.6% vs 10.6%; p < 0.001) with an acceptable increase in recall rate (RR) by 0.7% (6.1% vs 5.4%; p < 0.001).
sample_unit: women (screening examinations; 11,998 AI-supported and 11,998 matched historical controls)

title: Measuring the Impact of AI in the Diagnosis of Hospitalized Patients

title: Measuring the Impact of AI in the Diagnosis of Hospitalized Patients
outcome: Whether image-based AI explanations mitigate clinician errors from biased AI

quote: Although standard AI models improve diagnostic accuracy, systematically biased AI models reduced diagnostic accuracy, and commonly used image-based AI model explanations did not mitigate this harmful effect.

title: Measuring the Impact of AI in the Diagnosis of Hospitalized Patients
outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with vs without AI input, including biased AI and overreliance
effect: Standard AI raised accuracy 2.9 points over baseline; systematically biased AI decreased accuracy by 11.3 points vs baseline (95% CI, 7.2 to 15.5).

title: Measuring the Impact of AI in the Diagnosis of Hospitalized Patients

title: Assessing the potential of GPT-4 to perpetuate racial and gender biases in health care: a model evaluation study

effect: Overtriaged 9,897 (46.1%) and undertriaged 1,176 (5.5%) cases; undertriaged complaints included abnormal lab/imaging results, visual disturbance, and fever.

title: Implementation of Artificial Intelligence-Based Computer Vision Model for Sleeve Gastrectomy: Experience in One Tertiary Center
outcome: Agreement between AI and surgeon annotations of safety milestones on local videos
effect: AI-surgeon agreement was 98-100% for four milestones. For distance from esophagus ≥1 cm, true agreement was 100% but false agreement was 13.6% (kappa 0.2, p=0.006).
quote: Outcomes suggest its accuracy in four of five safety milestone annotations.

title: Assessing the clinical reasoning of ChatGPT for mechanical thrombectomy in patients with stroke
outcome: ChatGPT thrombectomy decisions compared with board-certified stroke neurologists and neurointerventionalists on same patients
effect: ChatGPT agreed with the physician's decision whether or not to pursue thrombectomy in 54.3% of cases; mistakes in 8.8% of cases.
quote: ChatGPT agreed with the physician's decision whether or not to pursue thrombectomy in 54.3% of the cases.
sample_unit: patients with large vessel occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy

title: Assessing the clinical reasoning of ChatGPT for mechanical thrombectomy in patients with stroke
outcome: Frequency of math, logic and misinterpretation errors in ChatGPT clinical reasoning outputs
effect: ChatGPT had mistakes in 8.8% of cases, consisting of mathematics, logic, and misinterpretation errors.
quote: ChatGPT had mistakes in 8.8% of the cases, consisting of mathematics, logic, and misinterpretation errors.
sample_unit: patients with large vessel occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy

title: Evaluation of information provided to patients by ChatGPT about chronic diseases in Spanish language
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT Spanish patient information (Flesch/Szigriszt scores)
effect: Responses were 'moderately difficult' (median 54.73, IQR 51.59-58.58); heart failure lowest (median 50.6, IQR 46.3-53.8).
quote: In readability, responses were "moderately difficult" (54.73, interquartile range (IQR) 51.59-58.58), with better results for CKD (median 56.1, IQR 53.5-59.1) and RA (56.4, IQR 53.7-60.7), than for heart failure responses (median 50.6, IQR 46.3-53.8).

title: Evaluation of information provided to patients by ChatGPT about chronic diseases in Spanish language
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of ChatGPT Spanish responses to patient questions
effect: Responses were 'moderately difficult' to read (median 54.73); authors conclude readability needs to improve before recommending as a patient tool.
quote: Our study suggests that the ChatGPT tool can be a reliable source of information in spanish for patients with chronic diseases with different reliability for some of them, however, it needs to improve the readability of its answers to be recommended as a useful tool for patients.

title: Can Large Language Models Generate Outpatient Clinic Letters at First Consultation That Incorporate Complication Profiles From UK and USA Aesthetic Plastic Surgery Associations?
outcome: Readability grade level of LLM-generated clinic letters versus recommended sixth-grade target
effect: ChatGPT4 letters with complication profiles had average readability grades between eighth and ninth, above the targeted sixth-grade level.
quote: ChatGPT4 achieved the highest compliance in integrating complication profiles from BAAPS and ASPS websites, with average readability grades between eighth and ninth.

title: Can Artificial Intelligence Improve the Readability of Patient Education Materials on Aortic Stenosis? A Pilot Study
outcome: Reading grade level of original online aortic stenosis patient education materials versus recommended 6th grade
effect: All 21 original PEMs were above 6th-grade level; mean FRE 51.9, FKGL 9.4, GFI 11.3, SMOGI 10.1, i.e., 10th-12th grade reading level.
quote: Mean (SD) FRE, FKGL, GFI, and SMOGI scores of original PEMs were 51.9 (11.6), 9.4 (2.0), 11.3 (2.1), 10.1 (1.2), respectively, indicating difficult readability at the 10th–12th grade reading level (Table 1 ).

title: Can Artificial Intelligence Improve the Readability of Patient Education Materials on Aortic Stenosis? A Pilot Study
outcome: Readability of LLM-rewritten patient education materials versus originals
effect: ChatGPT-3.5 improved all four measures (FRE 76.9 vs 51.9, p<0.001), reaching ~6th-7th grade; Bard improved three of four (FRE 66.5), ~8th-9th grade; neither reached below 6th grade.
quote: Conversion of PEMs by ChatGPT-3.5 demonstrated significantly improved mean readability scores across all four validated measures: FRE (76.9 ± 1.2 vs 51.9 ± 11.6, p < 0.001), FKGL (5.9 ± 0.8 vs 9.4 ± 2.0, p < 0.001), GFI (7.7 ± 0.9 vs 11.3 ± 2.1, p < 0.001), and SMOGI (8.8 ± 0.6 vs 10.1 ± 1.2, p < 0.001) scores, indicating fairly easy readability at the approximately 6th–7th grade reading level.

title: Can Artificial Intelligence Improve the Readability of Patient Education Materials on Aortic Stenosis? A Pilot Study
outcome: Head-to-head LLM readability and conversion time
effect: ChatGPT had easier FRE/FKGL/GFI/SMOGI than Bard and was faster: 5.38 s ± 0.67 s vs 8.57 s ± 1.29 s.
quote: Compared to Bard, ChatGPT-3.5 demonstrated significantly easier readability after conversion as per FRE (76.9 ± 1.2 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 66.5 ± 5.2 [Bard], p < 0.001), FKGL (5.9 ± 0.8 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 6.9 ± 0.8 [Bard], p = 0.001), GFI (7.7 ± 0.9 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 9.3 ± 1.0 [Bard], p < 0.001), and SMOGI (8.8 ± 0.6 [ChatGPT-3.5] vs 10.0 ± 0.8 [Bard], p < 0.001) scores (Fig. 1 ).

title: Talking technology: exploring chatbots as a tool for cataract patient education
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading ease of chatbot versus AAO website answers to cataract FAQs
effect: Reading ease: Bard 55.5 ± 8.48, AAO 51.96 ± 12.46, Bing AI 41.77 ± 9.53, ChatGPT 34.38 ± 9.75 (p<0.001); ChatGPT and Bing AI were harder to read than the AAO website. Chatbots also scored lower on PEMAT understandability than the AAO website.
quote: Flesch-Kincaid readability ease analysis showed that Bard (55,5 ± 8,48) had the highest mean score, followed by AAO website (51,96 ± 12,46), Bing AI (41,77 ± 9,53), and ChatGPT (34,38 ± 9,75, (p < 0.001)).

title: Large language models to identify social determinants of health in electronic health records
outcome: Change in model predictions when race/ethnicity and gender descriptors were added to text
effect: Fine-tuned models were less likely than ChatGPT to change predictions when race/ethnicity and gender descriptors were added, suggesting less algorithmic bias (p < 0.05).
quote: Fine-tuned models were less likely than ChatGPT to change their prediction when race/ethnicity and gender descriptors were added to the text, suggesting less algorithmic bias (p < 0.05).

title: Validation of a Deep Learning Chest X-ray Interpretation Model: Integrating Large-Scale AI and Large Language Models for Comparative Analysis with ChatGPT
outcome: Hallucination rate in AI chest X-ray readings rated by two radiologists
effect: KARA-CXR non-hallucination rate 75% vs ChatGPT 38%; hallucinations frequent, especially in ChatGPT. Interobserver agreement 0.91 (KARA) and 0.85 (GPT4).
quote: KARA-CXR demonstrated a non-hallucination rate of 75%, which is significantly higher than ChatGPT's 38%.

title: Validation of a Deep Learning Chest X-ray Interpretation Model: Integrating Large-Scale AI and Large Language Models for Comparative Analysis with ChatGPT
outcome: Comparison of candidate AI systems on same chest X-ray data for accuracy
effect: KARA-CXR rated 'Acceptable' 70.50% and 68.00% by two observers vs ChatGPT 40.50% and 47.00%; KARA-CXR significantly more accurate.
quote: In the 'Acceptable' accuracy category, KARA-CXR was rated at 70.50% and 68.00% by two observers, while ChatGPT achieved 40.50% and 47.00%.

title: Comprehensiveness, Accuracy, and Readability of Exercise Recommendations Provided by an AI-Based Chatbot: Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Readability level of AI-generated exercise recommendations (Flesch-Kincaid grade, reading ease)
effect: Average readability was college level (mean 13.7, SD 1.7), with average Flesch reading ease score of 31.1 (SD 7.7).
quote: Average readability level of AI-generated exercise recommendations was at the college level (mean 13.7, SD 1.7), with an average Flesch reading ease score of 31.1 (SD 7.7).

title: Comprehensiveness, Accuracy, and Readability of Exercise Recommendations Provided by an AI-Based Chatbot: Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient-directed exercise materials
effect: College-level readability (mean grade 13.7, SD 1.7); Flesch reading ease 31.1 (SD 7.7).
quote: Average readability level of AI-generated exercise recommendations was at the college level (mean 13.7, SD 1.7), with an average Flesch reading ease score of 31.1 (SD 7.7).

title: Comprehensiveness, Accuracy, and Readability of Exercise Recommendations Provided by an AI-Based Chatbot: Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Comprehensiveness and factual accuracy of AI exercise recommendations versus gold-standard guidelines
effect: Recommendations were 41.2% (107/260) comprehensive and 90.7% (146/161) accurate; most inaccuracy (8/15, 53%) related to preparticipation medical clearance.
quote: AI-generated exercise recommendations were 41.2% (107/260) comprehensive and 90.7% (146/161) accurate, with the majority (8/15, 53%) of inaccuracy related to the need for exercise preparticipation medical clearance.

title: Comprehensiveness, Accuracy, and Readability of Exercise Recommendations Provided by an AI-Based Chatbot: Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Bias or discrimination in AI-generated content for specific populations
effect: Qualitative themes included potential bias and direct discrimination against certain age-based populations and individuals with disabilities.
quote: Several recurring themes and observations of AI-generated output included concern for liability and safety, preference for aerobic exercise, and potential bias and direct discrimination against certain age-based populations and individuals with disabilities.

title: Evaluating the Accuracy of ChatGPT and Google BARD in Fielding Oculoplastic Patient Queries: A Comparative Study on Artificial versus Human Intelligence
outcome: Accuracy of chatbot answers to oculoplastic patient questions graded by specialists against expert judgment
effect: Comprehensive/correct but inadequate/mixed/completely incorrect: ChatGPT 71.4%, 12.9%, 10.5%, 5.1%; BARD 53.1%, 18.3%, 18.1%, 10.5%.
quote: The rates of comprehensive, correct but inadequate, mixed, and completely incorrect answers for ChatGPT were 71.4%, 12.9%, 10.5%, and 5.1%, respectively, compared with 53.1%, 18.3%, 18.1%, and 10.5%, respectively, for BARD.

title: Artificial intelligence and ChatGPT: An otolaryngology patient's ally or foe?
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT clinical content on ENT procedures (risks, steps, recovery)
effect: Appropriate treatment alternatives in all procedures; lacked precision in procedural steps, missed key surgical details, did not provide all major risks; total laryngectomy recovery wrongly said patient could speak immediately.
quote: When queried for methodology, risks, and procedural steps, ChatGPT lacked precision in the description of procedural steps, missed key surgical details, and did not accurately provide all major risks of each procedure.
sample_unit: ChatGPT responses (5 questions x 5 otolaryngologic procedures)

title: Chatbot Performance in Defining and Differentiating Palliative Care, Supportive Care, Hospice Care
venue: Journal of pain and symptom management
outcome: Readability of chatbot palliative care definitions (Flesch Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease) versus recommended patient material levels
effect: Readability scores of outputs from all three platforms did not meet recommended levels for patient educational materials.
quote: Readability scores did not meet recommended levels for patient educational materials.
sample_unit: AI chatbot platforms (each defining 3 terms, outputs rated by 6 blinded palliative care physicians)

title: Chatbot Performance in Defining and Differentiating Palliative Care, Supportive Care, Hospice Care
venue: Journal of pain and symptom management
outcome: Reliability of references provided by chatbots, rated by physicians on 0-10 scale
effect: Mean reliability scores were 6.3 (2.5) for ChatGPT, 3.2 (3.1) for Bard, and 7.1 (2.4) for Bing Chat; references were often unreliable.
quote: References were often unreliable.
sample_unit: AI chatbot platforms (each defining 3 terms, outputs rated by 6 blinded palliative care physicians)

title: Auditing Learned Associations in Deep Learning Approaches to Extract Race and Ethnicity from Clinical Text
venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
outcome: Concordance between model salient features and manually identified race/ethnicity text spans
effect: Models performed well on the surface, but the audit found concerning learned associations and potential for future harms. No numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: We show that while models perform well on the surface, there exist concerning learned associations and potential for future harms from RE-identification models if left unaddressed.

title: Towards Fair Patient-Trial Matching via Patient-Criterion Level Fairness Constraint
venue: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
outcome: Reduction of biased predictions in patient-trial matching with fairness constraint
effect: Reported qualitatively: the proposed fairness framework alleviated predictions tending to be biased on real-world patient-trial and patient-criterion matching tasks; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: The experimental results on real-world patient-trial and patient-criterion matching tasks demonstrate that the proposed framework can successfully alleviate the predictions that tend to be biased.

title: A Novel Evaluation Model for Assessing ChatGPT on Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery Certification Examinations: Performance Study
outcome: Reproducibility of answers across regenerated trials and effect of prompting on accuracy
effect: Passing mark averaged 75% across 3 trials with higher accuracy with prompts; considerable consistency in regenerating answers but often only partially correct responses.
quote: While demonstrating considerable consistency in regenerating answers, it often provided only partially correct responses.

title: A Novel Evaluation Model for Assessing ChatGPT on Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery Certification Examinations: Performance Study
outcome: Exam-based competency of ChatGPT on open-ended OHNS board questions
effect: ChatGPT achieved a passing mark (average 75% across 3 trials); concordance 92.06%; hallucinations and self-conflicting answers observed.
quote: In an open-ended question assessment, ChatGPT achieved a passing mark (an average of 75% across 3 trials) in the attempts and demonstrated higher accuracy with prompts.

title: A Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT)-Powered Chatbot as a Simulated Patient to Practice History Taking: Prospective, Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Share of GPT answers based on script information versus fictitious information
effect: Script-covered questions (n=502): 94.4% (n=471) answers based on explicit script information. Questions not covered (n=195): 56.4% (n=110) of answers used fictitious information.
quote: When questions were explicitly covered by the script (n=502, 60.3%), the GPT-provided answers were mostly based on explicit script information (n=471, 94.4%).

title: Potential impact of a new sepsis prediction model for the primary care setting: early health economic evaluation using an observational cohort
outcome: Referral rates and costs at different model cut-offs compared with usual care
effect: Observed referral cost €5890 per patient vs €5954-€6742 at model cut-offs; low cut-offs raised sepsis referral (99%, 91% vs 88%) but unnecessary referral rose to 85% and 56%; no cut-off saved costs.
quote: However, referral was also substantially higher for patients who did not need hospital assessment.

title: Potential impact of a new sepsis prediction model for the primary care setting: early health economic evaluation using an observational cohort
outcome: Adequacy of model score as replacement for clinical judgement
effect: Authors conclude discrimination is insufficient to replace GP judgement; advise using score to estimate risk within overall judgement rather than strict cut-offs.
quote: Given the results of the current study, it can be concluded that the discrimination of our new sepsis score is not sufficient to replace the clinical judgement of the GP based on the results of this early economic evaluation.

title: Potential impact of a new sepsis prediction model for the primary care setting: early health economic evaluation using an observational cohort
outcome: Costs versus current care
effect: Observed referral had the lowest average cost, €5890/patient; prediction-model scenarios ranged €5954–€6742/patient.
quote: The decision tree analysis shows that the observed probabilities of referral led to the lowest costs with average patient costs of €5890.

title: Potential impact of a new sepsis prediction model for the primary care setting: early health economic evaluation using an observational cohort
outcome: Cost per patient of model-guided referral versus usual GP care
effect: Model-based referral cost €5954-€6742 per patient vs €5890 observed; probabilistic analysis showed higher model costs than usual care in 83% of runs.
quote: In the probabilistic sensitivity analyses, costs for the prediction model were higher than usual care in 83% of the runs ( figure 3 ).

title: Potential impact of a new sepsis prediction model for the primary care setting: early health economic evaluation using an observational cohort
outcome: Referral and mortality effects of different risk cut-offs
effect: Low cut-offs (2, 3) increased unnecessary referrals (85%, 56% vs 15% observed); cut-off 4 lowered sepsis referral to 60% and raised estimated sepsis mortality (18 vs 9 cases).
quote: At higher prediction model cut-offs (scores 3 and 4), sepsis mortality will increase according to the expert opinion analysis.

title: Pilot Study of a Mobile Phone Chatbot for Medication Adherence and Toxicity Management Among Patients With GI Cancers on Capecitabine
outcome: Proportion of chatbot text exchanges with incorrect medication or symptom recommendations
effect: 284 of 3,895 (7.3%) medication-related and 13 of 527 (2.5%) symptom-related exchanges had incorrect recommendations; accurate in >90% of exchanges.
quote: We identified 284 of 3,895 (7.3%) medication-related and 13 of 527 (2.5%) symptom-related text messaging exchanges with incorrect recommendations.

title: ChatGPT is not ready yet for use in providing mental health assessment and interventions
outcome: Appropriateness and safety of ChatGPT recommendations across simulated mental health cases of rising complexity
effect: Case A recommendations were relatively appropriate but non-specific. In more complex cases B and C, recommendations became inappropriate, even dangerous.
quote: However, as complexity of clinical cases increased (cases B and C), the information and recommendations generated by ChatGPT became inappropriate, even dangerous; and the limitations of the program became more glaring.

title: Deep Learning Auto-Segmentation Network for Pediatric Computed Tomography Data Sets: Can We Extrapolate From Adults?
venue: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
outcome: Segmentation Dice score in pediatric age groups with vs without pediatric training data
effect: Adult-only models underperformed on pediatric data (mean DSC below 0.5 for bladder and spleen in the 0-2 group). Adding pediatric data gave mean DSC above 0.85 for all organs in every age group.
quote: The addition of pediatric training data demonstrated significant improvement for all age groups, achieving a mean DSC of above 0.85 for all organs in every age group.

title: Deep Learning Auto-Segmentation Network for Pediatric Computed Tomography Data Sets: Can We Extrapolate From Adults?
venue: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
outcome: Performance of adult-trained segmentation models when applied to pediatric CT data
effect: Models trained only on adult data underperformed on pediatric data, especially ages 0 to 2, with mean DSC below 0.5 for bladder and spleen.
quote: AI models trained exclusively on adult data underperformed on pediatric data, especially for the 0 to 2 age group: mean DSC was below 0.5 for the bladder and spleen.

title: Deep Learning Auto-Segmentation Network for Pediatric Computed Tomography Data Sets: Can We Extrapolate From Adults?
venue: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
outcome: Segmentation performance differences across CT scanners
effect: No significant difference in cross-scanner performance was found, suggesting robust cross-scanner generalization.
quote: No significant difference emerged in the cross-scanner performance evaluation, suggesting robust cross-scanner generalization.

title: Evaluating capabilities of large language models: Performance of GPT-4 on surgical knowledge assessments
outcome: Stability of ChatGPT answers and accuracy on repeated queries of previously incorrect surgical questions
effect: Selected answer varied for 36.4% of questions answered incorrectly on first query; response accuracy changed for 6/16 (37.5%) questions.
quote: Upon repeat query, the answer selected by ChatGPT varied for 36.4% of questions answered incorrectly on the first query; the response accuracy changed for 6/16 (37.5%) questions.

title: Assessment of Quality and Readability of Information Provided by ChatGPT in Relation to Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT answers versus recommended 8th-grade level
effect: ChatGPT 3.5 mean RGL 18.08 and ChatGPT 4 mean RGL 17.9, exceeding the average American reading grade level by 10.08 and 9.09 grade levels respectively.
quote: However, readability levels for both versions significantly exceeded the average 8th-grade reading level for American patients.

title: Assessment of Quality and Readability of Information Provided by ChatGPT in Relation to Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury
outcome: Comprehensibility (readability) of AI-generated patient education content
effect: Mean RGL of 18.08 (ChatGPT 3.5) and 17.9 (ChatGPT 4), far above the 8th-grade level of average American adults.
quote: While ChatGPT can provide both reliable and good quality information on ACL injuries and treatment options, the readability of the content may limit its utility.

title: Assessing ChatGPT's Proficiency in Simplifying Radiological Reports for Healthcare Professionals and Patients
outcome: Radiologist-rated quality of plain-language simplification of radiology reports, including Hindi translation
effect: Highest score for detailing the report (94.17%), lowest for drawing conclusions for the patient (85%); case-wise scores similar (p=0.97). Hindi translation was not suitable for patient communication.
quote: The current free version of ChatGPT-3.5 was able to simplify radiological reports effectively, removing technical jargon while preserving essential diagnostic information.

title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT vs gold clinical diagnosis and ophthalmologists
effect: Best F1 80.05% (Direct-English) vs ophthalmologists 89.35% and interns 82.69%; Chinese direct prompts 70.47%; VKH F1 0% in all prompts.
quote: From the perspective of clinical practice, ChatGPT’s diagnostic performance still did not reach the level of ophthalmologists or even ophthalmology interns.

title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Robustness of diagnostic performance to prompt language and prompt variation
effect: Chinese vs English prompts differed in recall (P=.03) and F1 (P=.04); mean F1 70.02% (Chinese) vs 76.47% (English).
quote: As shown in Table 4 , the results indicated significant differences in the recall ( P =.03) and F 1 -score ( P =.04) between Chinese and English prompts, while no significant difference was observed in the precision ( P =.18).

title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Diagnostic performance versus clinicians
effect: Overall F1: ophthalmologists 89.35%, interns 82.69%, ChatGPT English prompts 76.76%, Chinese prompts 73.04%.
quote: Although ChatGPT performed better than experts for some disease types (eg, Direct-English and Step-English prompts for the normal and CRVO categories and all prompts for the BRVO category), the overall performance of ophthalmologists was the best (89.35%), followed by ophthalmology interns (82.69%), ChatGPT with Direct-English and Step-English prompts (76.76%), and ChatGPT with Direct-Chinese and Step-Chinese prompts (73.04%).

title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Hallucinations and misinformation
effect: Step-English still had 44.31% incompleteness, 0.59% hallucinations, and 1.96% misinformation; Step-Chinese was higher, all P<.001.
quote: Although the average number of inference errors was similar (0.4 per report) between Step-Chinese and Step-English prompts ( P =.88, Wilcoxon rank-sum test), Step-English prompts brought less incompleteness (44.31%), hallucinations (0.59%), and misinformation (1.96%) (all P <.001, Chi-square test).

title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Rate of hallucinations and misinformation in ChatGPT reasoning on FFA reports
effect: Step-Chinese: hallucinations 5.88%, misinformation 7.84%; Step-English: 0.59% and 1.96%; 0.4 reasoning errors per report.
quote: Notably, although ChatGPT can derive a reasoning process to improve clinical interpretability, ophthalmologists identified some harmful mistakes, such as generating medical findings not mentioned in the original reports and quoting incorrect prior knowledge.

title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Performance gap across languages and disease categories due to English-centric training
effect: F1 fell 6.45% with Chinese prompts; VKH and CSC F1 under 4% vs DR/normal above 80%.
quote: The performance gap between different diseases and prompting strategies demonstrates the potential unfairness brought by the overrepresentation of the major diseases, languages, and countries.

title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Performance by disease category
effect: Normal and DR F1 exceeded 80%, while VKH and CSC F1 were less than 4%.
quote: ChatGPT performed better in the normal and DR categories, with the F 1 -scores exceeding 80%, but performed worse in the VKH and CSC categories, achieving F 1 -scores of less than 4%.

title: Uncovering Language Disparity of ChatGPT on Retinal Vascular Disease Classification: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: diagnostic performance drop with Chinese versus English prompts
effect: ChatGPT exhibited a significant decline in diagnostic performance with Chinese prompts, with a 6.45% decrease in F1-score.
quote: Given that the development and validation of ChatGPT predominantly relied on English-centric data sets [ 31 ] and that non-English medical corpora are even more scarce, compared to with English prompts, ChatGPT exhibited a significant decline in diagnostic performance with Chinese prompts, with a 6.45% decrease in F 1 -score.

title: Danger, Danger, Gaston Labat! Does zero-shot artificial intelligence correlate with anticoagulation guidelines recommendations for neuraxial anesthesia?
outcome: GPT-3.5 accuracy on guideline-based neuraxial bleeding risk assessment versus truth table
effect: Baseline performance slightly above chance; with detailed prompts and explicit guidelines, AUC 0.70 (95% CI 0.64 to 0.77); performance varied among medication classes.
quote: Baseline performance of GPT-3.5 was slightly above chance.

title: Clinical Validation of Computer-Aided Diagnosis Software for Preventing Retained Surgical Sponges
venue: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
outcome: Specificity of CAD in clinical setting versus development-phase performance
effect: CAD flagged possible retained items in 150 of 1,053 images; specificity 85.8%, similar to development-phase data, so real-world performance matched development performance.
quote: Specificity was 85.8%, which is similar to the data obtained during the development of the software.

title: ChatGPT: Is This Patient Education Tool for Urological Malignancies Readable for the General Population?
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading ease of ChatGPT patient information versus institutional patient information sheets
effect: ChatGPT readability was non-inferior to Cancer Council Australia and UpToDate sheets, and improved further when the prompt targeted a 16-year-old audience. No numeric scores are reported in the abstract.
quote: Ease of use of the information generated from ChatGPT was increased further when the question was modified to target an audience of 16 years of age, the average level of education attained by an Australian.
sample_unit: ChatGPT responses and patient information sheets (three urological malignancies)

title: Evaluating the ChatGPT family of models for biomedical reasoning and classification
outcome: LLM prompting performance versus simple BoW and fine-tuned BioBERT baselines on same classification and reasoning data
effect: Fine-tuned BioBERT best (classification F1 0.800-0.902; reasoning 0.851). Best LLM few-shot CoT F1 0.671-0.770 and 0.682, comparable to BoW (0.602-0.753; 0.675). LLM took 78 h vs 0.078 h BioBERT and 0.008 h BoW.
quote: The simple BoW model performed similarly to the most complex LLM prompting.

title: The effect of computerised decision support alerts tailored to intensive care on the administration of high-risk drug combinations, and their monitoring: a cluster randomised stepped-wedge trial
outcome: Administered high-risk drug combinations per 1000 drug administrations per patient
effect: Mean 26·2 (SD 53·4) intervention vs 35·6 (65·0) control; 12% decrease (95% CI 5-18%; p=0·0008) after adjustment for clustering and prognostic factors.
quote: Tailoring potential DDI alerts to the ICU led to a 12% decrease (95% CI 5-18%; p=0·0008) in the number of administered high-risk drug combinations per 1000 drug administrations per patient, after adjusting for clustering and prognostic factors.

title: Detection of fibrosing interstitial lung disease-suspected chest radiographs using a deep learning-based computer-aided detection system: a retrospective, observational study
outcome: Reader sensitivity, specificity, accuracy and ROC-AUC without versus with AI assistance, non-experts and experts
effect: Non-expert ROC-AUC 0.795 to 0.825 (p=0.005); sensitivity 0.744 to 0.802 (p=0.003); no sensitivity change in experts (p=0.285); specificity and accuracy unchanged.
quote: After using BMAX, sensitivity was improved from 0.744 (95% CI; 0.697 to 0.791) to 0.802 (95% CI; 0.754 to 0.850) among non-experts (p=0.003), but not among experts (p=0.285).
sample_unit: chest radiograph images read by 25 physicians (20 non-experts, 5 experts)

title: Impact of a deep learning sepsis prediction model on quality of care and survival
outcome: In-hospital sepsis mortality and bundle compliance before versus after AI deployment, quasi-experimental
effect: 1.9% absolute reduction (17% relative) in in-hospital sepsis mortality (95% CI 0.3%-3.5%); 5.0% absolute increase in sepsis bundle compliance (95% CI 2.4%-8.0%); 4% reduction in 72-h SOFA change.
quote: The deployment of COMPOSER was significantly associated with a 1.9% absolute reduction (17% relative decrease) in in-hospital sepsis mortality (95% CI, 0.3%-3.5%), a 5.0% absolute increase (10% relative increase) in sepsis bundle compliance (95% CI, 2.4%-8.0%), and a 4% (95% CI, 1.1%-7.1%) reduction in 72-h SOFA change after sepsis onset in causal inference analysis.

title: Automatic triage of twelve-lead electrocardiograms using deep convolutional neural networks: a first implementation study
outcome: Prospective performance of ECG triage AI on live clinical data versus final clinical diagnosis triage classes

quote: Our work has demonstrated that data-based approaches to drift detection can detect data drift (both natural and synthetic) in instances when monitoring model performance in aggregate cannot.

title: Empirical data drift detection experiments on real-world medical imaging data
outcome: Timeliness of drift detection given sample size requirements for alerting
effect: Detection needs about 4000 new CXRs, which may take days at large providers or months at smaller ones, so alerts may not be timely enough for clinicians to intervene.
quote: This finding has direct implications for the practical use of drift detection techniques: if it takes days (large radiology providers) or months (smaller providers) to perform 4000 new CXRs, then existing techniques for drift detection may not be timely enough to allow clinicians using the tool to intervene promptly.
