title: The Use of Generative AI for Scientific Literature Searches for Systematic Reviews: ChatGPT and Microsoft Bing AI Performance Evaluation
outcome: Existence and relevance of citations generated by ChatGPT and Bing AI versus human systematic review benchmark
effect: ChatGPT: 7 (0.5%) of 1287 studies relevant; 7 grade A, 18 B, 167 C, 211 F (fake titles). Bing AI: 19 (40%) of 48 relevant, versus 24 in the human benchmark.
quote: In the qualitative evaluation, ChatGPT had 7 grade A, 18 grade B, 167 grade C, and 211 grade F studies, and Bing AI had 19 grade A and 28 grade C studies.

title: Prospective validation of clinical deterioration predictive models prior to intensive care unit transfer among patients admitted to acute care cardiology wards
outcome: Temporal model discrimination and calibration during the COVID-19 pandemic
effect: Models developed five years before study initiation were well-calibrated, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve ranging from 0.725 to 0.737 during the COVID-19 pandemic.
quote: We conclude that predictive statistical models developed five years before study initiation had good model performance despite the passage of time and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Prospective validation of clinical deterioration predictive models prior to intensive care unit transfer among patients admitted to acute care cardiology wards
outcome: Prospective live-data performance of pre-COVID model with scores hidden (display-off)
effect: Among 5184 display-off visits (311 ICU transfers), AUCs ranged 0.725 to 0.737; models well-calibrated despite five years' passage and COVID-19.
quote: We conclude that predictive statistical models developed five years before study initiation had good model performance despite the passage of time and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT as a Tool for Answering Clinical Questions in Pharmacy Practice
outcome: Accuracy of citations and answers in ChatGPT drug information responses
effect: ChatGPT scored 21 of 44 points (47.73%) overall; drug information enhanced prompt 33% and patient case 20%; generated misleading or fictional answers and citations.
quote: ChatGPT scored higher in calculation and multiple-choice questions but scored lower in drug information and patient case questions, generating misleading or fictional answers and citations.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT as a Tool for Answering Clinical Questions in Pharmacy Practice
outcome: ChatGPT clinical knowledge accuracy on pharmacy patient case and drug information questions
effect: Overall score 21/44 (47.73%); patient case category scored 20%, enhanced prompt drug information 33%, while calculations 100%.
quote: ChatGPT scored higher in pharmacy calculation (100%), drug information (83%), and top 200 drugs (80%) categories and lower in drug information enhanced prompt (33%) and patient case (20%) categories.

title: Use of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots in Interpretation of Pathology Reports
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of original vs chatbot-simplified pathology reports
effect: Grade level fell from 13.19 to 8.17 (chatbot 1) and 7.45 (chatbot 2); Flesch Reading Ease rose from 10.32 to 61.32 and 70.80 (all P<.001).
quote: For the 1134 reports included, the Flesch-Kincaid grade level decreased from a mean of 13.19 (95% CI, 12.98-13.41) to 8.17 (95% CI, 8.08-8.25; t = 45.29; P < .001) by chatbot 1 and 7.45 (95% CI, 7.35-7.54; t = 49.69; P < .001) by chatbot 2.

title: Use of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots in Interpretation of Pathology Reports
outcome: Medical correctness and hallucinations in chatbot-simplified pathology reports
effect: Chatbot 1: 87.57% correct, 8.99% partially correct, 3.44% incorrect, 32 hallucinations (2.82%). Chatbot 2: 97.44% correct, 0.44% incorrect, 3 hallucinations (0.26%).
quote: Chatbot 1 had 32 instances of hallucinations (2.82%), while chatbot 2 had 3 (0.26%).

title: Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT) - 3.5 Responses Require Advanced Readability for the General Population and May Not Effectively Supplement Patient-Related Information Provided by the Treating Surgeon Regarding Common Questions About Rotator Cuff Repair
venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of ChatGPT-3.5 responses to patient rotator cuff repair questions
effect: Mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was 13.4 (range, 11.2-15.0), i.e., advanced readability above general population level.
quote: The mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was 13.4 (range, 11.2-15.0).

title: Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT) - 3.5 Responses Require Advanced Readability for the General Population and May Not Effectively Supplement Patient-Related Information Provided by the Treating Surgeon Regarding Common Questions About Rotator Cuff Repair
venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-3.5 patient education responses
effect: Mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 13.4 (range 11.2-15.0); responses described as having a complex language style.
quote: Additionally, the responses lacked reliable source material citations, and the readability of the responses was relatively advanced with a complex language style.

title: Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (ChatGPT) - 3.5 Responses Require Advanced Readability for the General Population and May Not Effectively Supplement Patient-Related Information Provided by the Treating Surgeon Regarding Common Questions About Rotator Cuff Repair
venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
outcome: Presence of reliable source citations in ChatGPT-3.5 responses (JAMA Benchmark)
effect: JAMA Benchmark score was 0, indicating absence of reliable source material citations; DISCERN mean 43.4 (fair quality).
quote: The Journal of the American Medical Association Benchmark criteria score was 0, indicating the absence of reliable source material citations.

title: Testing the generalizability and effectiveness of deep learning models among clinics: sperm detection as a pilot study
outcome: Model precision and recall across clinics and imaging conditions after training on diverse multi-condition data
effect: Rich training dataset yielded ICC 0.97 (95% CI 0.94-0.99) for precision and 0.97 (0.93-0.99) for recall; multi-center validation showed no significant differences in precision or recall across clinics.
quote: Multi-center clinical validation showed no significant differences in model precision or recall across different clinics and applications.

title: Testing the generalizability and effectiveness of deep learning models among clinics: sperm detection as a pilot study
outcome: Generalizability of detection model to new samples and external clinics after enriching training data
effect: Internal blind tests and external multi-center validation showed ICC of 0.97 for precision and recall, with no significant differences across clinics.
quote: The results validated the hypothesis that the richness of data in the training dataset is a key factor impacting model generalizability.

title: Evaluation of GPT-4 ability to identify and generate patient instructions for actionable incidental radiology findings
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: GPT-4 hallucinations and inferred recommendations in generated text
effect: No findings hallucinated outright; 2.8% of cases included generated text about recommendations inferred without specific reference.
quote: No findings were "hallucinated" outright. However, 2.8% of cases included generated text about recommendations that were inferred without specific reference.

title: Barriers to Implementing Registered Nurse-Driven Clinical Decision Support for Antibiotic Stewardship: Retrospective Case Study
outcome: Barriers to workflow fit and adoption of RN-driven CDS across sites (CFIR-coded)
effect: Barriers found in all CFIR domains; triage, rooming and documentation workflows varied by institution, and competing duties and RN shortages lowered intervention priority and uptake across 43 practices.
quote: Even in a relatively straightforward clinical workflow, workflow and cultural differences appreciably impacted intervention adoption.

title: A quality and readability comparison of artificial intelligence and popular health website education materials for common hand surgery procedures
outcome: Reading grade level of patient education materials versus recommended 4th-6th grade
effect: ChatGPT 4th-grade, ChatGPT scientific, WebMD, and Mayo Clinic materials exceeded recommended levels by at least four grade levels (10th, 14th, 13th, 11th grade).
quote: ChatGPT - 4th Grade Reading Level, ChatGPT - Scientific Reading Level, WebMD, and Mayo Clinic written materials on average exceeded recommended reading grade levels (4th-6th grade) by at least four grade levels (10th, 14th, 13th, and 11th grade, respectively).
sample_unit: hand surgery procedures (each with 4 education sources, rated by 5 surgeons)

title: A quality and readability comparison of artificial intelligence and popular health website education materials for common hand surgery procedures
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education materials
effect: ChatGPT prompted for fourth-grade level still produced 10th-grade text and did not adequately simplify information; quality was inferior to patient-friendly websites.
quote: When prompted to provide more easily read materials, ChatGPT generates less robust information compared to patient-friendly websites and does not adequately simplify the educational information.
sample_unit: hand surgery procedures (each with 4 education sources, rated by 5 surgeons)

title: External Validation of a Machine Learning Model for Schizophrenia Classification
outcome: Sensitivity for schizophrenia and misclassification of bipolar and depression patients on independent outpatient data
effect: Sensitivity 0.75 for schizophrenia; misclassification rates 59% for bipolar disorder and 55% for major depression, indicating poor specificity in the external sample.
quote: The misclassification rates were 59% and 55% for bipolar disorder and major depression patients, respectively.

title: Assessment of the Quality and Readability of Information Provided by ChatGPT in Relation to the Use of Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy for Osteoarthritis
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT responses about PRP therapy versus recommended 8th grade level
effect: Mean reading grade levels of 17.18 (ChatGPT 3.5) and 16.36 (ChatGPT 4), significantly above the recommended 8th grade level for patient education materials.
quote: However, both versions produced content significantly above the recommended 8th grade reading level for patient education materials (PEMs), with mean reading grade levels (RGLs) of 17.18 for ChatGPT version 3.5 and 16.36 for ChatGPT version 4, indicating a potential barrier to their utility in patient education.

title: Assessment of the Quality and Readability of Information Provided by ChatGPT in Relation to the Use of Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy for Osteoarthritis
outcome: Reading level of generated patient education content versus recommended level
effect: Mean reading grade levels of 17.18 (v3.5) and 16.36 (v4) versus recommended 8th grade level.
quote: However, both versions produced content significantly above the recommended 8th grade reading level for patient education materials (PEMs), with mean reading grade levels (RGLs) of 17.18 for ChatGPT version 3.5 and 16.36 for ChatGPT version 4, indicating a potential barrier to their utility in patient education.

title: Identifying potentially depressed older Chinese adults in the community: Hong Kong's Elderly Health Service cohort
outcome: Calibration of DRAT-up before and after local recalibration in older Chinese adults
effect: Original DRAT-up underestimated risk in older Chinese adults; recalibrating it improved calibration.
quote: The original DRAT-up model underestimated the risk of developing depressive symptoms in older Chinese adults; recalibrating it improved calibration.

title: Identifying potentially depressed older Chinese adults in the community: Hong Kong's Elderly Health Service cohort
outcome: Performance of European-developed model when applied to a new population (older Chinese adults)
effect: The original DRAT-up model underestimated risk of developing depressive symptoms in older Chinese adults; the new setting-specific model had better discrimination (C 0.68).
quote: The original DRAT-up model underestimated the risk of developing depressive symptoms in older Chinese adults; recalibrating it improved calibration.

title: Identifying potentially depressed older Chinese adults in the community: Hong Kong's Elderly Health Service cohort
outcome: Local calibration of existing depression risk model
effect: The original DRAT-up underestimated 2-year depressive-symptom risk in 174,806 older Chinese adults.
quote: The original DRAT-up model underestimated the risk of developing depressive symptoms in older Chinese adults; recalibrating it improved calibration.

title: Prognostic clinical decision support for pneumonia in the emergency department: A randomized trial
outcome: Inappropriate ED disposition in randomized trial of prognostic CDS versus usual care
effect: Inappropriate disposition 3% usual care vs 2% CDS (adjusted OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.32-2.95); length of stay similar; adverse safety outcomes uncommon in both arms.
quote: EHR-based prognostic CDS did not improve ED disposition decisions for children with pneumonia.

title: Prognostic clinical decision support for pneumonia in the emergency department: A randomized trial
outcome: Workflow integration problems and implementation barriers during the pilot trial
effect: Low subject accrual and workflow integration problems likely limited effectiveness; implementation barriers included reaching the right person at the right time and the pandemic.
quote: Although the intervention's content was favorably received, low subject accrual and workflow integration problems likely limited effectiveness.

title: Multi-Instance Learning for Vocal Fold Leukoplakia Diagnosis Using White Light and Narrow-Band Imaging: A Multicenter Study
outcome: Laryngologist AUC and accuracy with versus without AI assistance in human-machine comparison
effect: AI significantly improved AUC and accuracy for all 12 laryngologists (p < 0.05); diagnostic abilities and consistency improved, particularly for junior laryngologists.
quote: In the human-machine comparison, AI significantly improved AUC and accuracy for all laryngologists (p < 0.05).

title: Multi-Instance Learning for Vocal Fold Leukoplakia Diagnosis Using White Light and Narrow-Band Imaging: A Multicenter Study
outcome: Model AUC on internal versus external multi-hospital validation sets
effect: AUC 0.868 internal and 0.884 external (two other hospitals, 1617 images); video validation AUC 0.825 (95% CI 0.704-0.946).
quote: The model achieved the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.868 and 0.884 in the internal and external validation sets, respectively.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4.0 Responses on Hyperlipidemia for Patient Education
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT patient-education responses versus the NIH eighth-grade recommendation
effect: Version 3.5 had a significantly higher grade reading level than version 4.0 (p = 0.0002). Version 4.0 was more readable but still exceeded the NIH-recommended eighth-grade level.
quote: Version 4.0 offered more concise and readable information, aligning with the readability of most online medical resources despite exceeding the National Institutes of Health's (NIH's) recommended eighth-grade reading level.
sample_unit: chatbot responses (25 questions x 3 prompt forms x 2 model versions)

title: Pilot Study to Optimize Goal-directed Hemodynamic Management During Pancreatectomy
outcome: Intraoperative hypotension, cardiac index, stroke volume variation with algorithm-guided response
effect: IOH reduced 33.3% (5.2% vs 7.8%, P<0.01); cardiac index >2 up 31.6% (83.7% vs 63.6%); SVV <12 up 37.6% (73.2% vs 53.2%); groups differed in case mix; 10 PRE vs 24 POST patients
quote: There was a 33.3% reduction in IOH (5.2% ± 0.1% versus 7.8% ± 0.3%, P < 0.01, a 31.6% increase in cardiac index >2.0 (83.7% + 0.2% versus 63.6% + 0.5%, P < 0.01), and a 37.6% increase in stroke volume variation <12 (73.2% + 0.3% versus 53.2% + 0.5%, P < 0.01).

title: Use of artificial intelligence chatbots in clinical management of immune-related adverse events
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and completeness of chatbot answers to irAE guideline questions
effect: Accuracy 3.87 (ChatGPT) vs 3.5 (Bard), p<0.01; completeness 3.83 vs 3.46; scores of 1-2 rare for ChatGPT (6/800, 0.75%); patient scenarios accuracy 3.725, completeness 3.61.
quote: Overall, both engines scored highly for accuracy (mean scores for ChatGPT and Bard were 3.87 vs 3.5, p<0.01) and completeness (3.83 vs 3.46, p<0.01).
sample_unit: questions (plus 20 patient scenarios), rated by 8 physician experts

title: ChatGPT-4 Can Help Hand Surgeons Communicate Better With Patients
venue: Journal of hand surgery global online
outcome: Readability grade level of patient materials before vs after ChatGPT-4 rewrite to sixth-grade level
effect: Mean decrease of two grade levels; FKGL 8.3 to 6.0, SMOG 8.1 to 6.1 (both P<.001); other formulas remained above sixth grade (ARI 7.1, GFI 8.6, CLI 8.0, LWF 7.1).
quote: The mean decrease after ChatGPT-4 alteration was two grade levels.

title: ChatGPT-4 Can Help Hand Surgeons Communicate Better With Patients
venue: Journal of hand surgery global online
outcome: Whether ChatGPT-4 rewriting produces plain-language patient education material
effect: Mean FRE rose from 61.6 to 76.9 (P<.001); grade-level scores fell across all six formulas; word count fell from 728.3 to 303.6.
quote: The mean (± SD) FRE in the pre- and post-ChatGPT-4–edited text samples was 61.6 (±7.5) and 76.9 (± 8.2), respectively ( P < .001).

title: ChatGPT-4 Can Help Hand Surgeons Communicate Better With Patients
venue: Journal of hand surgery global online
outcome: Readability of AI-rewritten patient education materials across six grade-level formulas
effect: ChatGPT-4 reached sixth-grade level on FKGL (6.0) and SMOG (6.1), but remained above sixth grade on ARI (7.1), CLI (8.0), LWF (7.1), and GFI (8.6) (all P < .001).
quote: Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer version 4 was successful in terms of FKGL and SMOG in simplifying the included texts to a mean sixth-grade readability level but unsuccessful for the four other included readability tests that report grade level.

title: Clinical implementation of a commercial synthetic computed tomography solution for radiotherapy treatment of glioblastoma
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Dosimetric difference between sCT and CT plans in retrospective commissioning cohort
effect: Mean dose difference to targets within ±0.7%; OAR differences within ±1.3% on regridded images, up to -4.2% for chiasma D2% at original voxel size; gamma 1%/1mm 93.6%.
quote: Dosimetric outcomes in both commissioning and validation stages confirmed sCT's equivalence to CT.

title: Clinical implementation of a commercial synthetic computed tomography solution for radiotherapy treatment of glioblastoma
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Prospective validation of sCT dosimetric performance in clinical use
effect: Validation cohort (30 patients) gamma passing rates 96.6%/99.9%/100% at 1%/1mm, 2%/2mm, 3%/3mm; target mean dose differences within ±0.7%.
quote: Mean dose difference to target structures was found to be within ± 0.7 % regardless of image resolution and cohort.

title: Equity and AI governance at academic medical centers
venue: The American journal of managed care
outcome: Whether equity is considered in AI governance processes at academic medical centers
effect: A minority of participants reported considering inequity, racism, or bias in governance; a lack of consistent equity consideration was found among academic medical centers developing governance for predictive technologies.
quote: We found a lack of consistent equity consideration among academic medical centers as they develop their governance processes for predictive technologies despite considerable national attention to the ways these technologies can cause or reproduce inequities.
sample_unit: interview participants (chief medical informatics officers and similar) from 13 academic medical centers

title: Visual explanations for polyp detection: How medical doctors assess intrinsic versus extrinsic explanations
outcome: Physician preference and perceived understanding/trust for intrinsic (GradCAM) versus extrinsic (SHAP) visual explanations
effect: Intrinsic explanations preferred (30 of 47 multiple-choice respondents chose intrinsic as useful; 14 wanted both; 3 extrinsic). Extrinsic described as confusing. Fleiss kappa 0.049 (poor agreement on preferred method).
quote: Our results show that intrinsic explanations are preferred.

title: Visual explanations for polyp detection: How medical doctors assess intrinsic versus extrinsic explanations
outcome: Whether physicians' judgments of saliency explanations reflect understanding versus expectation of lesion alignment
effect: Preference for the intrinsic method may be superficial rather than reflect understanding of what the explanations convey; explanations aligned with the lesion may be favored, risking unwarranted judgments and misplaced trust.
quote: However, the free-form responses in our survey strongly suggest that the underlying reason for the doctors’ preference for this method may be more superficial than actually understanding what information the different explanations convey.

title: Visual explanations for polyp detection: How medical doctors assess intrinsic versus extrinsic explanations
outcome: clinician misunderstanding of explanations
effect: Extrinsic explanations were described by several participants as complicated, confusing, hard to interpret, hard to understand, unnatural, and harder to grasp.
quote: Based on similar free-form answers from several participants, describing Method B as “complicated”, “confusing”, “hard to interpret”, “hard to understand”, “doesn’t feel natural”, and “harder to grasp visually”, we conclude that the extrinsic explanations functionality of highlighting in which direction each collection of image pixels drives the prediction is counterintuitive to domain experts not familiar with such a way to represent information.

title: Visual explanations for polyp detection: How medical doctors assess intrinsic versus extrinsic explanations
outcome: inter-rater agreement on AI explanation methods
effect: Fleiss' kappa was 0.049 (95% CI, 0.033 to 0.066, p < 0.001), indicating poor agreement among participants on preferred explanation methods.
quote: The results, as detailed in Table 3 , show a Fleiss’ kappa value of 0.049.

title: Reliability and readability analysis of ChatGPT-4 and Google Bard as a patient information source for the most commonly applied radionuclide treatments in cancer patients
venue: Revista espanola de medicina nuclear e imagen molecular
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of chatbot responses versus general public reading level
effect: Mean FKRGL for GPT-4 was 14.25-14.65 and for Bard 11.35-13.01 across RAI, PSMA-TRT, PRRT and TARE; all above the general public reading grade level.
quote: In terms of readability the FRKGL scores of the responses of GPT-4 and Google Bard about RAI, PSMA-TRT, PRRT and TARE treatments were above the general public reading grade level.
sample_unit: questions (30 each for RAI, PRRT, TARE; 29 for PSMA-TRT), each asked to two chatbots

title: Reliability and readability analysis of ChatGPT-4 and Google Bard as a patient information source for the most commonly applied radionuclide treatments in cancer patients
venue: Revista espanola de medicina nuclear e imagen molecular
outcome: Readability of chatbot patient information responses relative to general public
effect: GPT-4 mean FKRGL 14.25-14.65 and Bard 11.35-13.01, above general public reading grade level, potentially preventing understanding.
quote: Although the information provided by AI chatbots may be acceptable in medical terms, it can not be easy to read for the general public, which may prevent it from being understandable.
sample_unit: questions (30 each for RAI, PRRT, TARE; 29 for PSMA-TRT), each asked to two chatbots

title: Enhancing readability of USFDA patient communications through large language models: a proof-of-concept study
outcome: Reading grade level of original FDA DSCs and medication guides
effect: Original materials were difficult to read (DSCs grade level 13, MGs 22).
quote: Original materials were difficult to read (DSCs grade level 13, MGs 22).
sample_unit: FDA drug safety communications and medication guides

title: Enhancing readability of USFDA patient communications through large language models: a proof-of-concept study
outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified materials versus originals, with technical accuracy retained
effect: LLMs reduced grade levels (single prompt DSCs: ChatGPT 10.1, Gemini 8; MGs: ChatGPT 7.1, Gemini 6.5); outputs retained technical accuracy and key messages.
quote: LLMs significantly improved readability, reducing the grade levels to more accessible readings (Single prompt - DSCs: ChatGPT 4.0© 10.1, Gemini© 8; MGs: ChatGPT 4.0© 7.1, Gemini© 6.5.
sample_unit: FDA drug safety communications and medication guides

title: Pathophysiological Features in Electronic Medical Records Sustain Model Performance under Temporal Dataset Shift
venue: AMIA Joint Summits on Translational Science proceedings. AMIA Joint Summits on Translational Science
outcome: Discrimination deterioration of EMR prediction models over time under temporal dataset shift
effect: Across three clinical prediction tasks, model discrimination deteriorated over time; pathophysiological features helped mitigate this deterioration. No numeric results are reported in the abstract.
quote: We investigate three standard clinical prediction tasks and find that while feature contributions to initial performance differ across tasks, pathophysiological features help mitigate temporal discrimination deterioration.

title: Evaluating the accuracy and readability of ChatGPT in providing parental guidance for adenoidectomy, tonsillectomy, and ventilation tube insertion surgery
outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT responses versus AMA-recommended sixth-grade level
effect: Mean FRE 57.15 (±10.73), FKGL 9.95 (±1.91); only 3 (9.1%) responses at or below sixth-grade level; over three-quarters at or above 10th-grade level.
quote: Upon analyzing the responses from ChatGPT, 3 (9.1 %) were at or below the sixth-grade reading level recommended by the American Medical Association (AMA).
sample_unit: questions (ChatGPT responses), each rated by 7 otolaryngologists (231 evaluations)

title: Automatized self-supervised learning for skin lesion screening
outcome: Dermatologist confidence and agreement with top-10 AI-identified ugly ducklings when assisted by the tool
effect: Tool increased dermatologists' confidence in diagnosis; average majority agreement with top-10 AI-identified ugly ducklings reached 100% when assisted.
quote: The study also found that the tool increased dermatologists' confidence when formulating a diagnosis, and the average majority agreement with the top-10 AI-identified UDs reached 100% when assisted by our tool.

title: Evaluation of information accuracy and clarity: ChatGPT responses to the most frequently asked questions about premature ejaculation
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses on premature ejaculation (FKGL, FRES)
effect: Mean FKGL 15.68 ± 1.67 and FRES 15.8 ± 8.73; requires about 14 to 15 years of formal schooling; treatment texts hardest to understand.
quote: In addition, the FKGL scores indicate a significant degree of linguistic intricacy, requiring a level of knowledge comparable to about 14 to 15 years of formal schooling in order to understand.

title: Evaluation of information accuracy and clarity: ChatGPT responses to the most frequently asked questions about premature ejaculation
outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT patient information versus recommended threshold
effect: FKGL 15.68 ± 1.67, FRES 15.8 ± 8.73; complexity exceeds the recommended reading threshold for effective health communication.
quote: The results of this research suggest that compared to texts on other topics the PE texts produced by ChatGPT exhibit a higher degree of complexity, which exceeds the recommended reading threshold for effective health communication.

title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models' Performance in Domain-Specific Medicine: Development and Usability Study With DocOA
outcome: Accuracy of RAG-grounded DocOA versus ungrounded GPT-3.5/GPT-4 on osteoarthritis benchmark
effect: Overall benchmark accuracy 0.88 for DocOA vs 0.24 for GPT-4 and 0.16 for GPT-3.5 (P<.001); human-rated inaccuracy 19.3% vs 50% and 57%.
quote: The rate of inaccuracy was the highest for GPT-3.5 (57%, n=1200), followed by GPT-4 and DocOA at 50% (n=1200) and 19.3% (n=1200), respectively.
sample_unit: benchmark questions (337 guideline-item, 145 management-option, 216 treatment-strategy, 80 real-case QA)

title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models' Performance in Domain-Specific Medicine: Development and Usability Study With DocOA
outcome: General LLM accuracy against current clinical guidelines for osteoarthritis management
effect: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 accuracy was 0.01 and 0.07 on treatment strategy QA and 0.03 and 0.01 on real-case QA; GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 were unsatisfactory on guideline-based questions.
quote: The accuracy of GPT-3.5 in GIQA, MOQA, TSQA, and RCQA was 0.26, 0.22, 0.01, and 0.03, respectively.
sample_unit: benchmark questions (337 guideline-item, 145 management-option, 216 treatment-strategy, 80 real-case QA)

title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models' Performance in Domain-Specific Medicine: Development and Usability Study With DocOA
outcome: General LLM performance on domain-specific clinical competencies versus general medical benchmark expectations
effect: General LLMs had unsatisfactory performance on OA management, with marked decline as tasks shifted from knowledge to personalized treatment recommendations.
quote: By contrast, general-purpose models such as GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 exhibit unsatisfactory performance when benchmarked against OA management.
sample_unit: benchmark questions (337 guideline-item, 145 management-option, 216 treatment-strategy, 80 real-case QA)

title: Evaluating and Enhancing Large Language Models' Performance in Domain-Specific Medicine: Development and Usability Study With DocOA
outcome: Potentially biased generated content
quote: The likelihoods of potentially biased content were 13.3% (n=1200), 9.5% (n=1200), and 2.8% (n=1200) for GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and DocOA, respectively.
sample_unit: benchmark questions (337 guideline-item, 145 management-option, 216 treatment-strategy, 80 real-case QA)

title: Predicting Self-Reported Social Risk in Medically Complex Adults Using Electronic Health Data
outcome: Model performance (AUC) across race/ethnicity strata to assess algorithmic bias
effect: Final 30-predictor model had overall AUC of 0.68 and remained robust within different race/ethnic strata; no subgroup performance gap reported in the abstract.
quote: The model remained robust within different race/ethnic strata.
sample_unit: patients (primary modeling cohort; external validation n=2820 survey respondents)

title: Chinese Oncologists' Perspectives on Integrating AI into Clinical Practice: Cross-Sectional Survey Study
outcome: Oncologists' concern about overreliance on AI
effect: 162/228 (71%) of oncologists were concerned about overreliance on AI; 163/228 (71.5%) worried AI could mislead diagnosis and treatment.
quote: The study revealed that the most prominent concerns were the potential for AI to mislead diagnosis and treatment (163/228, 71.5%); an overreliance on AI (162/228, 71%); data and algorithm bias (123/228, 54%); issues with data security and patient privacy (123/228, 54%); and a lag in the adaptation of laws, regulations, and policies in keeping up with AI's development (115/228, 50.4%).

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-Generated Educational Patient Pamphlets for Common Interventional Radiology Procedures
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT-generated IR procedure pamphlets reviewed by two radiologists
effect: Shortcomings in 30% (30/100) of pamphlets, with 34 specific inaccuracies, including missing sedation information (10/34) and inaccurate procedural complication details (8/34).
quote: In a thorough analysis of the education pamphlets, we identified shortcomings in 30% (30/100) of pamphlets, with a total of 34 specific inaccuracies, including missing information about sedation for the procedure (10/34), inaccuracies related to specific procedural-related complications (8/34).

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-Generated Educational Patient Pamphlets for Common Interventional Radiology Procedures
outcome: Consistency of pamphlets across repeated identical requests by different users
effect: Line-by-line comparison across users and procedures showed statistically significant inconsistencies (P < 0.001), despite consistent themes within groups.
quote: A key-word co-occurrence network showed consistent themes within each group of pamphlets, while a line-by-line comparison at the level of users and across different procedures showed statistically significant inconsistencies (P < 0.001).

title: Evaluating ChatGPT Responses on Atrial Fibrillation for Patient Education
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of ChatGPT patient education responses by prompt form
effect: Form 2 (patient-friendly) mean grade level 12.80 ± 3.38; Form 1 14.23 ± 2.34; Form 3 16.73 ± 2.65; Form 4 14.85 ± 2.76; all above typical patient reading level.
quote: Form 2 answers had a lower mean grade level (12.80 ± 3.38) than Forms 1 (14.23 ± 2.34), 3 (16.73 ± 2.65), and 4 (14.85 ± 2.76) (p < 0.05).
sample_unit: ChatGPT responses (16 questions x 4 prompt forms)

title: Evaluating ChatGPT Responses on Atrial Fibrillation for Patient Education
outcome: Whether ChatGPT provided references in atrial fibrillation answers, including when prompted for sources
effect: References provided in only 3 (4.7%) of answers; when prompted for sources, only 3 of 16 (18.8%) responses included them.
quote: Across all forms, references were provided in only three (4.7%) answers.
sample_unit: ChatGPT responses (16 questions x 4 prompt forms)

title: GastroBot: a Chinese gastrointestinal disease chatbot based on the retrieval-augmented generation
outcome: Faithfulness, context recall, answer relevance of RAG-grounded chatbot; manual comparison with other models
effect: Context recall 95%, faithfulness to source 93.73%, answer relevance 92.28%; manual assessment showed GastroBot delivered more valuable knowledge with completeness and consistency than other models.
quote: During manual assessment of GastroBot, in comparison with other models, our GastroBot model delivers a substantial amount of valuable knowledge while ensuring the completeness and consistency of the results.

title: Accuracy of artificial intelligence-based segmentation of the mandibular canal in CBCT
outcome: Accuracy (RMS error) and time of AI vs manual tracing by clinicians of differing experience
effect: RMS error vs experienced clinicians ranged 0.21 to 7.65 mm, mean 3.5 mm; experienced manual tracing required more time than AI-driven segmentation.
quote: Regarding time efficiency, tracing by experienced users required more time compared to AI-driven segmentation.

title: The assessment of the validity, safety, and utility of ChatGPT for patients with herniated lumbar disc: A preliminary study
outcome: Validity of ChatGPT answers to common herniated lumbar disc patient questions, rated by two physicians
effect: Validity scored 4 points for 9/12 questions (75.0%) and 3 points for 3/12 (25.0%). Safety scored 4 for 11/12 (91.7%) and 3 for 1/12 (8.3%).
quote: However, users should exercise caution as ChatGPT may occasionally provide incomplete answers to some questions on HLD.

title: Deep learning for colorectal cancer detection in contrast-enhanced CT without bowel preparation: a retrospective, multicentre study
outcome: Radiologist detection accuracy with versus without DL assistance in intended use mode
effect: DL assistance improved radiologist accuracy: 93.4% vs 86.0% (internal test set) and 93.6% vs 85.3% (external test set 1), both p < 0.0001.
quote: In both the internal test set and external test set 1, the DL model yielded higher accuracy than that of radiologists (97.2% vs 86.0%, p < 0.0001; 94.9% vs 85.3%, p < 0.0001), and significantly improved the accuracy of radiologists (93.4% vs 86.0%, p < 0.0001; 93.6% vs 85.3%, p < 0.0001).
sample_unit: CT scans (cancer vs normal across internal, two external, and real-world test sets)

title: Deep learning for colorectal cancer detection in contrast-enhanced CT without bowel preparation: a retrospective, multicentre study
outcome: DL model performance compared with radiologists on the same test data
effect: DL accuracy exceeded radiologists in internal (97.2% vs 86.0%) and external set 1 (94.9% vs 85.3%), p<0.0001; in real-world set sensitivity was comparable (94.3% vs 96.2%).
quote: In the real-world test set, the DL model delivered sensitivity comparable to that of radiologists who had been informed about clinical indications for most cancer cases (94.3% vs 96.2%, p > 0.99), and it detected 2 cases that had been missed by radiologists.
sample_unit: CT scans (cancer vs normal across internal, two external, and real-world test sets)

title: Deep learning for colorectal cancer detection in contrast-enhanced CT without bowel preparation: a retrospective, multicentre study
outcome: DL model AUC on internal, external multisite, and real-world test sets
effect: AUCs ranged between 0.957 and 0.994 across the four test sets, including two external sets and a real-world set.
quote: In the four test sets, the DL model had the area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUCs) ranging between 0.957 and 0.994.
sample_unit: CT scans (cancer vs normal across internal, two external, and real-world test sets)

title: Machine learning models' assessment: trust and performance
outcome: Performance (geometric mean) of candidate models versus the GRACE score on the same dataset
effect: The rule-based approach outperformed the GRACE model's performance while providing a high level of trust. No numeric results are given in the abstract.
quote: It provides a high level of trust in the respective operation while outperformed the GRACE model's performance, enhancing the required physicians' acceptance.

title: Patient-centered radiology reports with generative artificial intelligence: adding value to radiology reporting
outcome: Non-physician rater comprehension of original vs AI patient-friendly radiology reports (5-point Likert)
effect: Mean comprehension rose from 2.71 ± 0.73 for original reports to 4.69 ± 0.48 for patient-friendly reports (p < 0.001).
quote: The average comprehension score for the original report was 2.71 ± 0.73, while the score for the patient-friendly reports significantly increased to 4.69 ± 0.48 (p < 0.001).

title: Patient-centered radiology reports with generative artificial intelligence: adding value to radiology reporting
outcome: Rate of artificial hallucinations and potentially harmful translations in AI-generated reports
effect: 1.12% artificial hallucinations and 7.40% potentially harmful translations.
quote: There were 1.12% artificial hallucinations and 7.40% potentially harmful translations.

title: Application of simultaneous uncertainty quantification and segmentation for oropharyngeal cancer use-case with Bayesian deep learning
outcome: Whether uncertainty measures predict quality of deep learning tumor segmentation
effect: Uncertainty-based approach predicted segmentation quality in 86.6% of cases, identified low-performance cases for semi-automated correction, and visualized likely failure regions.
quote: We show that our uncertainty-based approach accurately predicts the quality of the deep learning segmentation in 86.6% of cases, identifies low performance cases for semi-automated correction, and visualizes regions of the scans where the segmentations likely fail.

title: Assessing the role of advanced artificial intelligence as a tool in multidisciplinary tumor board decision-making for primary head and neck cancer cases
outcome: Concordance of LLM treatment recommendations with current guidelines and tumor board decisions
effect: ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 suggested significantly more therapy options than the MDT; some recommended modalities, such as primary immunotherapy, are not part of current treatment guidelines.
quote: For clinical recommendation, explanation and summarization ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 scored well, but demonstrated to be mostly an assisting tool, suggesting significantly more therapy options than our MDT, while some of the recommended treatment modalities like primary immunotherapy are not part of the current treatment guidelines.
sample_unit: consecutive head and neck cancer patients discussed at tumor board

title: Performance of ChatGPT and Google Translate for Pediatric Discharge Instruction Translation
outcome: Potentially clinically significant translation errors (severity score ≤3) for Haitian Creole versus professional translation
effect: Haitian Creole errors: ChatGPT 33.3% (P < .001), Google Translate 23.3% (P = .024), professional translations 8.3%.
quote: ChatGPT (33.3%, P < .001) and Google Translate (23.3%, P = .024) contained more potentially clinically significant errors (severity score ≤3) for Haitian Creole than professional translations (8.3%).
sample_unit: standardized pediatric discharge instructions (each translated into 3 languages by 3 sources)

title: Performance of ChatGPT and Google Translate for Pediatric Discharge Instruction Translation
outcome: Translation quality (adequacy, fluency, meaning, severity) compared with professional translations, by language
effect: Machine translation was comparable to professional translation for Spanish and Portuguese but significantly worse for Haitian Creole on adequacy, fluency, meaning, and severity.
quote: Machine translation platforms have comparable performance to professional translations for Spanish and Portuguese but shortcomings in quality, accuracy, and preference persist for Haitian Creole.
sample_unit: standardized pediatric discharge instructions (each translated into 3 languages by 3 sources)

title: Evaluating the Success of ChatGPT in Addressing Patient Questions Concerning Thyroid Surgery
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT thyroid surgery responses versus recommended grade 6 level
effect: Readability scores were consistently higher than the recommended grade 6 level, indicating information may not be easily comprehensible to the general public.
quote: However, the readability scores were consistently higher than the recommended grade 6 level, indicating the information may not be easily comprehensible to the general public.

title: Evaluating the Success of ChatGPT in Addressing Patient Questions Concerning Thyroid Surgery
outcome: Comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education responses in plain language
effect: Readability scores consistently exceeded the grade 6 level; ChatGPT's current formulation is not optimally tailored for patient comprehension.
quote: However, the readability scores were consistently higher than the recommended grade 6 level, indicating the information may not be easily comprehensible to the general public.

title: Clinical domain knowledge-derived template improves post hoc AI explanations in pneumothorax classification
outcome: Overlap (IoU, DSC) between XAI explanations and radiologist-delineated pneumothorax lesions, baseline versus template-guided
effect: Template guidance improved baseline XAI in all 12 scenarios; average incremental improvement was 97.8% in IoU and 94.1% in DSC, indicating baseline explanations often diverged from true lesion areas.
quote: The proposed approach consistently improved baseline XAI methods across twelve benchmark scenarios built on three XAI methods, two DL models, and two datasets.
sample_unit: benchmark scenarios (3 XAI methods x 2 models x 2 datasets)

title: Use of large language models to optimize poison center charting
outcome: Expert-rated appropriateness of LLM summaries and accuracy of tabulated data points
effect: 80% of summaries had median score high enough to be appropriate for entry into the medical record; 91% of data points correctly abstracted into table format.
quote: Eighty percent of summaries had a median score high enough to be deemed appropriate for entry into the medical record.

title: Dimensional Measures of Psychopathology in Children and Adolescents Using Large Language Models
outcome: Differences in LLM-extracted RDoC positive valence scores by patient race
effect: Modest but statistically significant differences in positive valence scores by race (p < .05 for Asian, Black, and Hispanic individuals).
quote: Tests for bias suggested modest but statistically significant differences in positive valence scores by race (p < .05 for Asian, Black, and Hispanic individuals).

title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence-Generated Vascular Severity Score Improved Plus Disease Diagnosis in Retinopathy of Prematurity
outcome: Expert plus disease diagnosis agreement with reference standard, without vs with AI severity score assistance
effect: Weighted κ improved from 0.69 to 0.81; AUC from 0.94 to 0.98 (difference 0.04); AUPR from 0.86 to 0.95 (difference 0.09).
quote: Expert agreement improved significantly, from substantial (κ value, 0.69 [0.59, 0.75]) to near perfect (κ value, 0.81 [0.71, 0.86]), when AI-based VSS was integrated.

title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence-Generated Vascular Severity Score Improved Plus Disease Diagnosis in Retinopathy of Prematurity
outcome: Clinician plus disease discrimination
quote: Additionally, a significant improvement in plus disease discrimination was achieved as measured by mean AUC (from 0.94 [95% confidence interval (CI), 0.92-0.96] to 0.98 [95% CI, 0.96-0.99]; difference, 0.04 [95% CI, 0.01-0.06]) and AUPR (from 0.86 [95% CI, 0.81-0.90] to 0.95 [95% CI, 0.91-0.97]; difference, 0.09 [95% CI, 0.03-0.14]).

title: Validation and three years of clinical experience in using an artificial intelligence algorithm as a second read system for prostate cancer diagnosis-real-world experience
outcome: Pathologist review of AI alerts to resolve false-positive AI cancer calls
effect: In validation, all 17 false-positive slide alerts were resolved by pathologist review as benign mimics; in deployment, 1733 benign cases alerted but only 128 (2.9%) changed after review.
quote: Following pathologist review, all 17 slide alerts were resolved and shown to be triggered by glands (normal, atrophic, and seminal vesicle) as well as inflammation ( Table 2 ), features that may mimic malignant glands.
sample_unit: cases (122,441 slides) in 3-year deployment; validation 101 cases/1279 slides

title: Validation and three years of clinical experience in using an artificial intelligence algorithm as a second read system for prostate cancer diagnosis-real-world experience
outcome: Diagnostic revisions following AI-assisted second review in routine pathology workflow
effect: Over 3 years, diagnoses revised before sign-out yielded an overall AI Impact™ of 1.8%, ranging from 0.75% up to 3.5% per individual pathologist.
quote: In our real-world data, AI Impact™ ranged from 0.75% up to 3.5% per individual pathologist, with a normalized group effect of 1.8%.
sample_unit: cases (122,441 slides) in 3-year deployment; validation 101 cases/1279 slides

title: Validation and three years of clinical experience in using an artificial intelligence algorithm as a second read system for prostate cancer diagnosis-real-world experience
outcome: Local validation accuracy on Puerto Rican cohort vs original developer populations
effect: Cancer detection AUC 0.994 (95% CI 0.988-0.997), sensitivity 96.6%, specificity 96.7%, NPV 99.2%; Gleason GG1 vs GG2+ AUC 0.901, similar to original populations.
quote: Results show a similar high diagnostic accuracy for cancer in this Puerto Rican population as in the original populations vs benign with an AUC of 0.994 (95% CI: 0.988–0.997).
sample_unit: cases (122,441 slides) in 3-year deployment; validation 101 cases/1279 slides

title: Validation and three years of clinical experience in using an artificial intelligence algorithm as a second read system for prostate cancer diagnosis-real-world experience
outcome: Pathologist-plus-AI second read vs pathologist alone diagnosis changes (AI Impact)
effect: 2.9% (128/4385) benign cases and 1.21% (24/1984) GG1 cases revised after AI alerts; overall AI Impact 1.8%, ranging 0.75% to 3.5% per pathologist.
quote: After review by the pathologist, 0.3% (155/57119) of the benign slides and 2.9% (128/4385) of benign cases required a change of diagnosis.
sample_unit: cases (122,441 slides) in 3-year deployment; validation 101 cases/1279 slides

title: Validation and three years of clinical experience in using an artificial intelligence algorithm as a second read system for prostate cancer diagnosis-real-world experience
outcome: False-negative cancer findings in slides labeled benign by AI
effect: AI called nine cancer slides benign; seven were GG1, and the other two were GG2 and GG4. No cancers were missed at the case level out of 1279 WSI.
quote: At the slide level, Galen™ called nine slides benign that were cancer.
sample_unit: cases (122,441 slides) in 3-year deployment; validation 101 cases/1279 slides

title: Validation and three years of clinical experience in using an artificial intelligence algorithm as a second read system for prostate cancer diagnosis-real-world experience
outcome: cancer detection accuracy in local validation
effect: In the local validation set, the AI achieved an AUC of 0.994, with 96.6% sensitivity and 96.7% specificity.
quote: The AUC for cancer detection in the validation set was 0.994 (95% CI 0.988–0.997), with a 96.7% (95% CI 95.6–97.8) specificity and a 96.6% (95% CI 93.3–98.8) sensitivity.
sample_unit: cases (122,441 slides) in 3-year deployment; validation 101 cases/1279 slides

title: Assessing the Utility, Impact, and Adoption Challenges of an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Prescription Advisory Tool for Type 2 Diabetes Management: Qualitative Study
outcome: Clinician concerns about accountability and liability for AI tool use in prescribing
effect: Issues surrounding accountability and liability were among the themes that hindered adoption of the APA tool in clinical practice.
quote: However, the interpretability of the risk scores, concerns about overreliance and automation bias, and issues surrounding accountability and liability hindered the adoption of the APA tool in clinical practice.

title: Assessing the Utility, Impact, and Adoption Challenges of an Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Prescription Advisory Tool for Type 2 Diabetes Management: Qualitative Study
outcome: Clinician-reported concerns about overreliance and automation bias with AI prescription advisory
effect: Concerns about overreliance and automation bias were raised by clinicians and hindered adoption; not measured directly.
quote: However, the interpretability of the risk scores, concerns about overreliance and automation bias, and issues surrounding accountability and liability hindered the adoption of the APA tool in clinical practice.

title: A comparative evaluation of ChatGPT 3.5 and ChatGPT 4 in responses to selected genetics questions
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of GPT-4 genetics answers, including outdated information
effect: GPT-4 was more accurate than GPT-3.5 (P < .0001), but notable accuracy errors remained and outdated information was a challenge.
quote: The study underscores GPT-4's potential role in genetic education, showing notable progress yet facing challenges like outdated information and the necessity of ongoing refinement.

title: Improving Clinician Performance in Classifying EEG Patterns on the Ictal-Interictal Injury Continuum Using Interpretable Machine Learning
outcome: Clinician EEG pattern classification accuracy with versus without AI assistance
effect: Mean user diagnostic accuracy improved from 47 to 71% (P<0.04) with AI assistance among eight medical professionals.
quote: Mean user diagnostic accuracy improved from 47 to 71% (P<0.04).
sample_unit: clinicians (medical professionals classifying 100 EEG samples with and without AI)

title: Assessment of ChatGPT-3.5's Knowledge in Oncology: Comparative Study with ASCO-SEP Benchmarks
outcome: ChatGPT-3.5 accuracy on oncology multiple-choice questions from ASCO-SEP
effect: 56.1% (583/1040) correct overall; lowest in gastrointestinal cancer (102/209; 48.8%); highest in developmental therapeutics (8/10; 80%); no significant difference across diagnosis, treatment, other (P=.16)
quote: Overall, ChatGPT-3.5 achieved a score of 56.1% (583/1040) for the correct answers provided.

title: Identify and mitigate bias in electronic phenotyping: A comprehensive study from computational perspective
outcome: Effect of bias mitigation strategies on fairness of pneumonia and sepsis phenotyping models
effect: Five mitigation strategies (pre-, in-, post-processing) were evaluated on 9 phenotyping methods; the abstract reports no quantitative results or direction of effect.
quote: In this work, we are motivated to bridge this gap through a comprehensive experimental study to identify the bias existing in electronic phenotyping models and evaluate the widely-used debiasing methods' performance on these models.

title: Large Language Models Versus Expert Clinicians in Crisis Prediction Among Telemental Health Patients: Comparative Study
outcome: GPT-4 versus 6 clinicians on predicting suicidal ideation with plan from intake data
effect: Chief complaint only: clinician precision 0.7 vs GPT-4 0.6; sensitivity 0.53 vs 0.62. Adding attempt history: clinician sensitivity 0.59, precision 0.77; GPT-4 sensitivity 0.59, precision 0.54.
quote: Overall, the clinicians' average precision (0.7) was higher than that of GPT-4 (0.6) in identifying the SI with plan at intake (n=140) versus no SI (n=200) when using the chief complaint alone, while sensitivity was higher for the GPT-4 (0.62) than the clinicians' average (0.53).

title: Applying generative AI with retrieval augmented generation to summarize and extract key clinical information from electronic health records
outcome: Summarization accuracy with versus without RAG grounding; hallucination mitigation
effect: Zero-shot summaries had 93.25% accuracy; adding RAG gave a 6% increase to 99.25% accuracy. RAG did not further improve accuracy in the risk factor extraction task (about 90%).
quote: The addition of RAG improved the summarization process, leading to a 6% increase and achieving an accuracy of 99.25%.
sample_unit: notes (25 for summarization task; 1,399 for extraction task)

title: Applying generative AI with retrieval augmented generation to summarize and extract key clinical information from electronic health records
outcome: Output accuracy against manually built gold standard dataset
effect: Summaries 93.25% accurate overall; risk factor extraction 90% accurate; hallucination when details were not explicitly provided in notes.
quote: The model also proved its capability in extracting risk factors with an accuracy of 90%.
sample_unit: notes (25 for summarization task; 1,399 for extraction task)

title: Transcending Language Barriers: Can ChatGPT Be the Key to Enhancing Multilingual Accessibility in Health Care?
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: ChatGPT report simplification quality (correctness, harm, completeness, term explanation) by output language
effect: Spanish outperformed Hindi and Russian in categories 1 and 3 (P<.05); Hindi worse than English in all four categories (P<.05); all translations worse than English in term explanation (P<.001).
quote: The Spanish translation outperformed the Hindi and Russian version significantly in categories 1 and 3 (P < .05).

title: Awareness and intention-to-use of digital health applications, artificial intelligence and blockchain technology in breast cancer care
outcome: Intention-to-use AI before vs after 30-min educational presentation
effect: Among 30 respondents, intention-to-use AI rose from 5.37 (±1.81) to 5.83 (±1.64), not statistically significant; blockchain intention rose significantly from 4.30 to 5.90 (p < 0.01).
quote: In this sub-group, the mean intention-to-use AI was 5.37 (±1.81) before the session and 5.83 (±1.64) afterwards, which did not show a statistically significant change.

title: Removing Adversarial Noise in X-ray Images via Total Variation Minimization and Patch-Based Regularization for Robust Deep Learning-based Diagnosis
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Classifier accuracy under FGSM adversarial attack, before and after total variation denoising
effect: Average accuracy fell from 95.56% to 19.83% under adversarial attack; after denoising it rose from 19.83% to 88.23% on adversarial images.
quote: Post-denoising, the model exhibits a remarkable accuracy improvement, surging from 19.83 to 88.23% on adversarial images.

title: Performance of Large Language Models on Medical Oncology Examination Questions
outcome: Errors in LLM oncology answers, including outdated knowledge from recent publications, and potential clinical harm
effect: Incorrect responses most commonly involved information retrieval errors, particularly with recent publications; 18 of 22 incorrect answers (81.8%) would have medium or high likelihood of moderate to severe harm.
quote: Incorrect responses were most commonly associated with errors in information retrieval, particularly with recent publications, followed by erroneous reasoning and reading comprehension.

title: Performance of Large Language Models on Medical Oncology Examination Questions
outcome: Exam-question accuracy versus clinical safety of LLM answers
effect: Best LLM scored 85.0% on exam questions, yet 18 of 22 incorrect answers (81.8%) had medium or high likelihood of moderate to severe harm if acted upon.
quote: If acted upon in clinical practice, 18 of 22 incorrect answers (81.8%; 95% CI, 59.7%-94.8%) would have a medium or high likelihood of moderate to severe harm.

title: Performance Drift in Machine Learning Models for Cardiac Surgery Risk Prediction: Retrospective Analysis
outcome: Temporal performance drift of cardiac surgery mortality risk models on holdout 2017-2019 data
effect: Strong evidence of decrease in overall performance (CEM) across all models (P<.0001); all models decreased in at least 3 of 5 metrics; XGBoost CEM median fell by 0.0288 from 2017 to 2019.
quote: There was strong evidence of a decrease in overall performance across all models ( P <.0001).

title: Performance Drift in Machine Learning Models for Cardiac Surgery Risk Prediction: Retrospective Analysis
outcome: Loss of accuracy relative to initial validation over time in temporally split holdout
effect: All models showed decreased CEM, AUC, and F1 over the 2017-2019 holdout; XGBoost AUC slope -0.000678; NN net benefit fell from 0.9035 to 0.8808 in projection.
quote: We found strong evidence that all models showed a decrease in at least 3 of the 5 individual metrics within the CEM.

title: Performance Drift in Machine Learning Models for Cardiac Surgery Risk Prediction: Retrospective Analysis
outcome: Comparison of ML models against EuroSCORE II on same data
effect: XGBoost CEM 0.728 and RF 0.727 vs EuroSCORE II 0.541; EuroSCORE II performed worst across all comparisons (CEM difference to XGBoost 0.1876).
quote: Furthermore, EuroSCORE II substantially underperformed against all ML models across all comparisons; this presents an urgent need to understand the drift effects of this score and is not limited to calibration drift.

title: Performance Drift in Machine Learning Models for Cardiac Surgery Risk Prediction: Retrospective Analysis
outcome: Performance on temporally later external holdout versus development data
effect: Temporal external validation on 2017-2019 holdout showed performance decline across all models, demonstrating that earlier data overestimate later performance.
quote: There was strong evidence of a decrease in AUC performance across all models ( P <.0001).

title: Performance Drift in Machine Learning Models for Cardiac Surgery Risk Prediction: Retrospective Analysis
outcome: Calibration drift
effect: Adjusted ECE decreased across all models (P<.0001) except LR (P>.05).
quote: There was strong evidence of a decrease in adjusted ECE performance across all models ( P <.0001), except LR ( P >.05).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Postoperative Care: Assessing Large Language Models for Patient Recommendations in Plastic Surgery
outcome: Readability, understandability and actionability of LLM postoperative care responses across three models
effect: Gemini significantly more readable (p=0.001) and understandable (p=0.014; p=0.001) than GPT-3.5 and GPT-4; no difference in actionability (p=0.830); accuracy equal (p=0.849).
quote: The three LLMs provided equally accurate information, with GPT-3.5 averaging the highest on the Likert scale (LS) (4.18 ± 0.93) (p = 0.849), while Gemini provided significantly more readable (p = 0.001) and understandable responses (p = 0.014; p = 0.001).

title: ChatENT: Augmented Large Language Model for Expert Knowledge Retrieval in Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Error rate and hallucinations of retrieval-grounded ChatENT versus base ChatGPT4.0 on OHNS exam questions
effect: ChatENT outperformed ChatGPT4.0 with 58.4% (Canadian Royal College sample questions) and 26.0% (US board practice questions) error reduction; fewer hallucinations and greater consistency.
quote: ChatENT showed enhanced performance in the analysis and interpretation of OHNS information, outperforming ChatGPT4.0 in both the Canadian Royal College OHNS sample examination questions challenge and the US board practice questions challenge, with a 58.4% and 26.0% error reduction, respectively.

title: Can AI Answer My Questions? Utilizing Artificial Intelligence in the Perioperative Assessment for Abdominoplasty Patients
outcome: Readability grade level of LLM answers to abdominoplasty perioperative questions
effect: ChatGPT-3.5 required the highest reading level for comprehension, followed by Gemini, Claude, then CoPilot; ChatGPT-3.5 and Gemini used more professional language. No numeric values reported in abstract.
quote: ChatGPT-3.5 required the highest level for comprehension, followed by Gemini, Claude, then CoPilot.

title: Comparison of the use of a clinically implemented deep learning segmentation model with the simulated study setting for breast cancer patients receiving radiotherapy
outcome: Whether pilot/simulated-setting performance and acceptability carried over to clinical use
effect: 93% of contours clinically acceptable or usable as starting point in clinic vs 92% in pilot; OAR time reduction unchanged; target volumes (nodal levels 1-4) needed significantly more time, though time reduction was still 33% vs manual.
quote: Ninety-three percent of all contours in clinic were scored as clinically acceptable or usable as a starting point, comparable to 92% achieved in the pilot study.

title: AUA Guideline Committee Members Determine Quality of Artificial Intelligence‒Generated Responses for Female Stress Urinary Incontinence
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses on stress urinary incontinence using Flesch Reading Ease
effect: Every response rated "hard to read", equivalent to a college graduate reading level, despite understandability rated at 89%.
quote: Every response was "hard to read" translating to a college graduate reading level.

title: AUA Guideline Committee Members Determine Quality of Artificial Intelligence‒Generated Responses for Female Stress Urinary Incontinence
outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT patient-facing SUI responses
effect: All responses were "hard to read", translating to a college graduate reading level.
quote: Every response was "hard to read" translating to a college graduate reading level.
sample_unit: ChatGPT responses to patient SUI questions rated by 3 expert raters

title: Prospective Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Triage of Incidental Pulmonary Emboli on Contrast-Enhanced CT Examinations of the Chest or Abdomen
outcome: Report turnaround time and sensitivity with vs without AI triage notification
effect: Sensitivity rose from 80.0% without AI to 96.2% with AI (p = .03), specificity unchanged at 99.9%. Mean turnaround for IPE-positive exams did not differ significantly: 78.3 vs 74.6 minutes (p = .26).
quote: The mean report turnaround time for IPE-positive examinations was not significantly different between radiologists without AI and radiologists with AI (78.3 vs 74.6 minutes, p = .26).

title: Prospective Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Triage of Incidental Pulmonary Emboli on Contrast-Enhanced CT Examinations of the Chest or Abdomen
outcome: sensitivity and specificity
effect: Sensitivity was 80.0% without AI vs 96.2% with AI (p=.03), with no significant difference in specificity.
quote: Radiologists without AI, in comparison to radiologists with AI, showed significantly lower sensitivity (80.0% vs 96.2%, respectively; p = .03), without a significant difference in specificity (99.9% vs 99.9%, p = .58), for the detection of IPE.

title: Prospective Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Triage of Incidental Pulmonary Emboli on Contrast-Enhanced CT Examinations of the Chest or Abdomen
outcome: diagnostic performance
effect: Sensitivity was 80.0% without AI vs 96.2% with AI (p=.03), with no significant difference in specificity.
quote: Radiologists without AI, in comparison to radiologists with AI, showed significantly lower sensitivity (80.0% vs 96.2%, respectively; p = .03), without a significant difference in specificity (99.9% vs 99.9%, p = .58), for the detection of IPE.

title: A comparative study of large language model-based zero-shot inference and task-specific supervised classification of breast cancer pathology reports
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Macro F1 of zero-shot LLMs versus supervised models on the same pathology report classification tasks
effect: GPT-4 performed either significantly better than or as well as the best supervised model, LSTM-Att (average macro F1 0.86 vs 0.75); other LLMs performed poorly.
quote: Across all 12 tasks, the GPT-4 model performed either significantly better than or as well as the best supervised model, LSTM-Att (average macro F1-score of 0.86 vs 0.75), with advantage on tasks with high label imbalance.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4's performance as a digital health advisor for otosclerosis surgery
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4 responses on otosclerosis surgery versus 6th-grade level
effect: Readability indices showed texts were above the 6th-grade level, suggesting they may not be easily comprehensible to the average reader.
quote: The readability analysis indicated that the texts were above the 6th-grade level, suggesting they may not be easily comprehensible to the average reader.

title: External validation of the myocardial-ischaemic-injury-index machine learning algorithm for the early diagnosis of myocardial infarction: a multicentre cohort study

quote: The reweighing strategy almost perfectly mitigated any measured performance disparity between the bias groups, to respective values of relative ΔTPR and relative ΔFPR of 0.44 ± 1.80% and −0.69 ± 1.45% for the Near Bias scenario, and −0.80 ± 0.64% and −0.32 ± 2.13% for the Far Bias scenario.

title: Towards objective and systematic evaluation of bias in artificial intelligence for medical imaging
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Hidden subgroup performance gaps despite high aggregate accuracy

quote: The presence of the bias effect resulted in significant performance disparities compared to the No Bias scenario, with a relative ΔTPR of 22.12 ± 2.72% ( P <.0001) and ΔFPR of 20.32 ± 2.81% ( P <.0001) in the Near Bias scenario, and a relative ΔTPR of 17.35 ± 2.78% ( P =.0002) and relative ΔFPR of 11.88 ± 6.22% ( P =.0008) in the Far Bias scenario.

title: Towards objective and systematic evaluation of bias in artificial intelligence for medical imaging
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

title: The limits of fair medical imaging AI in real-world generalization

sample_unit: datasets (six chest X-ray datasets plus dermatology and ophthalmology datasets)

title: The limits of fair medical imaging AI in real-world generalization

title: Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of large language models in clinical decision-making

title: Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of large language models in clinical decision-making

title: Adaptation of risk prediction equations for cardiovascular outcomes among patients with type 2 diabetes in real-world settings: a cross-institutional study using common data model approach

title: Adaptation of risk prediction equations for cardiovascular outcomes among patients with type 2 diabetes in real-world settings: a cross-institutional study using common data model approach

title: Adaptation of risk prediction equations for cardiovascular outcomes among patients with type 2 diabetes in real-world settings: a cross-institutional study using common data model approach

title: The clinical value of artificial intelligence in assisting junior radiologists in thyroid ultrasound: a multicenter prospective study from real clinical practice
outcome: Junior and senior radiologist diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance
effect: Junior+AI improved specificity 0.837 to 0.921, accuracy 0.833 to 0.895, AUC 0.829 to 0.871 (all p<0.001), with no sensitivity gain; the AI alone had AUC 0.901, and the senior+AI gain was not significant.
quote: Compared to independent readings by junior radiologists, AI-assisted readings significantly improved their specificity, accuracy, and AUC (0.837 vs. 0.921, 0.833 vs. 0.895, 0.829 vs. 0.871, respectively; all p < 0.001), where specificity and accuracy were comparable to those of senior radiologists ( p > 0.05) (Table 4 ).

title: The clinical value of artificial intelligence in assisting junior radiologists in thyroid ultrasound: a multicenter prospective study from real clinical practice
outcome: Junior radiologists misled by incorrect AI outputs

quote: In total, there were substantially more cases where the junior radiologists benefited from consulting diagnostic results by the AI system than being misled (193 vs 31 summing up benign and malignant classified nodules).

title: The clinical value of artificial intelligence in assisting junior radiologists in thyroid ultrasound: a multicenter prospective study from real clinical practice

quote: Additionally, this study performed analysis of diagnosis of thyroid nodules by radiologists of different levels and the AI system across the three medical centers using different diagnostic criteria namely pathology and consensus of senior specialists separately, yielding consistent results.

title: The clinical value of artificial intelligence in assisting junior radiologists in thyroid ultrasound: a multicenter prospective study from real clinical practice
outcome: diagnostic performance of AI versus clinicians
effect: AI demonstrated superior AUC compared to junior radiologists (0.901 vs. 0.829) and comparable AUC to senior radiologists (0.901 vs. 0.892).
quote: Summing over all cases which were analyzed separately using either pathology or the arbitration committee as the diagnostic criteria, or in our proposed term, the 2e diagnostic criteria, the AI system demonstrated superior sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and AUC compared to junior radiologists (0.868 vs. 0.820, 0.934 vs. 0.837, 0.917 vs. 0.833, 0.901 vs. 0.829, respectively; all p < 0.001), and showed comparable results to senior radiologists’ readings (0.868 vs. 0.849, 0.934 vs. 0.934, 0.917 vs. 0.912, 0.901 vs. 0.892, respectively; all p > 0.05).
