title: Development and evaluation of a large language model of ophthalmology in Chinese
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of the LLM versus ophthalmologists on clinical vignettes
effect: Ophthalmologists' correct diagnosis rate was 96.1% vs 81.1% for MOPH, described as not statistically significant (p>0.05).
quote: In diagnostic accuracy, although the rate of correct diagnosis by ophthalmologists was superior to that by MOPH (96.1% vs 81.1%, p>0.05), the difference was not statistically significant.
sample_unit: exam questions, evidence-based questions, and clinical vignettes

title: Cutting Edge to Cutting Time: Can ChatGPT Improve the Radiologist's Reporting?
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Reporting time and report quality with versus without GPT-4 assistance
effect: Total and case reporting times decreased with AI assistance but not significantly (p>0.05); quality of finalized reports comparable with no significant differences. Time excluding editing was significantly lower (p<0.05).
quote: Quality scores of the finalized reports with and without AI-assistance were comparable with no significant differences.

title: Development and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Framework for Ophthalmology
outcome: Alignment with scientific consensus of retrieval-augmented LLM versus baseline LLM
effect: Consensus improved from 46.5% to 84.0% (difference 37.5%; 95% CI 29.0%-46.0%; P<.001); not different from GPT-4 (79.2%).
quote: Our LLM surpassed the baseline model in aligning with scientific consensus, improving consensus from 46.5% to 84.0% (difference = 37.5%; 95% CI, 29.0%-46.0%; P < .001) and not different from GPT-4 with a value of 79.2% (difference = 4.8%; 95% CI, −0.3% to 10.0%; P = .06).

title: Development and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model Framework for Ophthalmology
outcome: Human ranking score of candidate LLMs compared on the same 300 questions
effect: Ten LLMs benchmarked; ChatZOC scored 0.60 vs baseline 0.48 (difference 0.12; P=.02) and GPT-4 0.61 (P=.89).
quote: Evaluation using 300 questions sampled from the COD showed that the human ranking score of our ophthalmic LLM had achieved a score of 0.60, different from the baseline model of 0.48 (difference = 0.12; 95% CI, 0.02-0.22; P = .02) and not different from GPT-4 with a score of 0.61 (difference = 0.01; 95% CI, −0.11 to 0.13; P = .89), as shown in Table 2 .

title: Diagnosing Solid Lesions in the Pancreas With Multimodal Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in randomized crossover trial
effect: Novice endoscopist accuracy rose from 0.69 (95% CI, 0.61-0.76) without AI to 0.90 (95% CI, 0.83-0.94) with AI assistance (P < .001).
quote: The diagnostic accuracy of novice endoscopists was significantly enhanced with AI assistance (0.69 [95% CI, 0.61-0.76] vs 0.90 [95% CI, 0.83-0.94]; P < .001), and the supplementary interpretability information alleviated the skepticism of the experienced endoscopists.
sample_unit: patients in prospective crossover trial (12 endoscopists)

title: Diagnosing Solid Lesions in the Pancreas With Multimodal Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Model AUC on internal versus external multicenter test datasets
effect: AUC was 0.996 (95% CI, 0.993-0.998) internally and 0.955, 0.924, and 0.976 in the 3 external test datasets, showing a modest drop externally.
quote: The area under the curve of the joint-AI model ranged from 0.996 (95% CI, 0.993-0.998) in the internal test dataset to 0.955 (95% CI, 0.940-0.968), 0.924 (95% CI, 0.888-0.955), and 0.976 (95% CI, 0.942-0.995) in the 3 external test datasets, respectively.
sample_unit: patients in prospective crossover trial (12 endoscopists)

title: Prompt engineering on leveraging large language models in generating response to InBasket messages
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Physician acceptance of AI-drafted replies after iterative, versioned prompt engineering
effect: Acceptance of draft suitability rose from 62% to 84% (P<.001) in the validation set (N=200); 74% of production drafts were rated helpful.
quote: After 3 iterations of prompt engineering, physician acceptance of draft suitability increased from 62% to 84% (P <.001) in the validation dataset (N = 200), and 74% of drafts in the test dataset were rated as "helpful."

title: Prompt engineering on leveraging large language models in generating response to InBasket messages
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Hallucinated clinical information in AI-drafted patient message replies
effect: 7 (6%) of 116 training-set drafts contained hallucinated information; none in the validation set; 16% of validation drafts rejected by physicians.
quote: Interesting, 7 (6%) of the 116 original messages from the test set were found to contain hallucinated information in the LLM responses.

title: Prompt engineering on leveraging large language models in generating response to InBasket messages
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Patient preference for human versus initial-prompt AI response tone and quality
effect: Patients preferred human-generated responses for tone (N = 159, 68%) and overall quality (N = 160, 69%) over initial-prompt AI responses.
quote: There was notable preference for human-generated responses in the first phase of evaluation for both tone ( N = 159, 68%) and quality ( N = 160, 69%) ( Figure 4A ).

title: Prompt engineering on leveraging large language models in generating response to InBasket messages
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Patient preference for tone and quality after feedback-driven prompt revision
effect: Patient preference for optimized prompt (V3) drafts was 62% for tone and quality, versus <15% for the initial prompt (P<.001).
quote: When comparing responses created from the final prompt to the initial prompt, patient preference shifted to the optimized prompt (V3) based LLM-generated responses for tone ( Figure 4B , N = 154, 62%) and quality ( Figure 4B , N = 154, 62%), significantly higher than preference to the first iteration of prompt based LLM-generated response (<15% for both tone or overall quality) with P -value less than .001.

title: Prompt engineering on leveraging large language models in generating response to InBasket messages
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Patient advisors’ ability to identify AI-generated responses when blinded to authorship
effect: Patient advisors correctly identified AI-generated responses only 24% of the time; 50% were attributed to humans, and authorship was undetermined for 26%.
quote: As shown in Figure 5 , in the final round of patient evaluation, patients determined that 77% ( N = 192) of responses completely addressed patient questions, and patients correctly identified messages were AI-generated only 24% of the time.

title: Prompt engineering on leveraging large language models in generating response to InBasket messages
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: patient preference for AI response
effect: Patient preference for tone and quality increased from <15% to 62% with local prompt tuning.
quote: When comparing responses created from the final prompt to the initial prompt, patient preference shifted to the optimized prompt (V3) based LLM-generated responses for tone ( Figure 4B , N = 154, 62%) and quality ( Figure 4B , N = 154, 62%), significantly higher than preference to the first iteration of prompt based LLM-generated response (<15% for both tone or overall quality) with P -value less than .001.

venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA

title: Integrated image-based deep learning and language models for primary diabetes care
outcome: Referable DR identification accuracy of PCPs with vs without AI assistance
effect: Average PCP accuracy for identifying referable DR was 81.0% unassisted and 92.3% assisted by DeepDR-Transformer.
quote: For identifying referable DR, the average PCP's accuracy was 81.0% unassisted and 92.3% assisted by DeepDR-Transformer.
sample_unit: patients (397 unassisted PCP arm; 372 PCP+DeepDR-LLM arm)

title: Integrated image-based deep learning and language models for primary diabetes care
outcome: Patient adherence to self-management and DR referral, PCP with vs without DeepDR-LLM
effect: Newly diagnosed patients in PCP+DeepDR-LLM arm showed better self-management (P<0.05); patients with referral DR more likely to adhere to referrals (P<0.01).
quote: For patients with referral DR, those in the PCP+DeepDR-LLM arm were more likely to adhere to DR referrals (P < 0.01).
sample_unit: patients (397 unassisted PCP arm; 372 PCP+DeepDR-LLM arm)

title: Computer-aided detection of tuberculosis from chest radiographs in a tuberculosis prevalence survey in South Africa: external validation and modelled impacts of commercially available artificial intelligence software
outcome: AI accuracy across subgroups (age, HIV status, TB history)
effect: All products generally performed worst in older individuals, people with previous tuberculosis, and people with HIV; thresholds, sensitivity, and specificity varied across groups.
quote: All products generally performed worst in older individuals, people with previous tuberculosis, and people with HIV.

outcome: Comparative accuracy (AUC) of 12 commercial CAD products on same data
effect: Lunit and Nexus had AUCs near 0.9; qXR, JF CXR-2, InferRead, Xvision, ChestEye 0.8-0.9; XrayAME, RADIFY, TiSepX-TB under 0.8.
quote: Diverse accuracy was noted: Lunit and Nexus had AUCs near 0·9, followed by qXR, JF CXR-2, InferRead, Xvision, and ChestEye (AUCs 0·8-0·9).

title: Computer-aided detection of tuberculosis from chest radiographs in a tuberculosis prevalence survey in South Africa: external validation and modelled impacts of commercially available artificial intelligence software
outcome: Accuracy differences among CAD products
effect: Lunit and Nexus had AUCs near 0·9; qXR, JF CXR-2, InferRead, Xvision, and ChestEye had AUCs 0·8-0·9.
quote: Diverse accuracy was noted: Lunit and Nexus had AUCs near 0·9, followed by qXR, JF CXR-2, InferRead, Xvision, and ChestEye (AUCs 0·8-0·9).

title: Spending Analysis of Machine Learning-Based Communication Nudges in Oncology
outcome: Mean daily end-of-life spending with risk-informed prompts for serious illness conversations versus standard care
effect: Mean daily spending was $377.96 vs. $449.92; adjusted mean difference, -$75.33; 95% confidence interval, -$136.42 to -$14.23; P=0.02. Adjusted savings were $13,747 per decedent.
quote: The intervention was associated with lower unadjusted mean daily spending in the last 6 months of life for the intervention group versus controls ($377.96 vs. $449.92; adjusted mean difference, -$75.33; 95% confidence interval, -$136.42 to -$14.23; P=0.02), translating to $13,747 total adjusted savings per decedent and $13 million in cumulative savings across all decedents in the intervention group.

title: ChatGPT yields low accuracy in determining LI-RADS scores based on free-text and structured radiology reports in German language
outcome: Test-retest reproducibility of LI-RADS scores across five repeated runs (ICC), structured vs free-text
effect: Test-retest reliability ICC was 0.81 for free-text vs 0.50 for structured reports on 50 lesions passed five times.
quote: the test-retest reliability was higher (ICC = 0.81 vs. 0.50), in free-text compared to structured reports, respectively

title: ChatGPT yields low accuracy in determining LI-RADS scores based on free-text and structured radiology reports in German language
outcome: Accuracy of LI-RADS classification by GPT-3.5 against radiologist consensus ground truth
effect: Accuracy was 53% on unstructured and 44% on structured reports; kappa 0.51 and 0.44.
quote: The accuracy of ChatGPT at determining LI-RADS categories was poor (53% and 44% on unstructured and structured reports).

title: Autonomous artificial intelligence for diabetic eye disease increases access and health equity in underserved populations
outcome: Change in DED testing adherence by race across AI-switched vs non-AI sites
effect: Adherence for Black/African Americans rose 12.2 percentage points at AI-switched sites vs a 0.6% point decrease at non-AI sites (p<0.001); Asian–Black adherence gap shrank from 15.6% to 3.5%.
quote: Second, the adherence rate for Black/African Americans increased by 12.2 percentage points within AI-switched sites but decreased by 0.6% points within non-AI sites (p < 0.001), suggesting that autonomous AI deployment improved access to retinal evaluation for historically disadvantaged populations.

title: Assessing breast disease with deep learning model using bimodal bi-view ultrasound images and clinical information
outcome: Radiologist diagnostic AUC with versus without AI aid
effect: BreNet-aided scheme increased the pooled AUC of the radiologists from 0.841 to 0.934 for reviewing images, and from 0.892 to 0.934 in the real-world test.
quote: BreNet-aided scheme increased the pooled AUC of the radiologists from 0.841 to 0.934 for reviewing images, and from 0.892 to 0.934 in the real-world test.

title: Assessing breast disease with deep learning model using bimodal bi-view ultrasound images and clinical information
outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with six radiologists on same data
effect: BreNet AUC 0.996 vs. radiologists 0.841.
quote: The diagnostic performance of BreNet was superior to that of the radiologists (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.996 vs. 0.841).

title: Artificial Intelligence-based automated CT brain interpretation to accelerate treatment for acute stroke in rural India: An interrupted time series study
outcome: Time to intervention from NCCT imaging before vs after AI deployment in stroke patients
effect: Median TTI fell from 80 min (IQR 56.8-139.5) at baseline to 58.5 min (IQR 30.3-118.2) after AI deployment (location shift -21.0, 95% CI -38.0 to -7.0).
quote: Impact analysis in a total of 174 stroke patients (72 in baseline and 102 after deployment) demonstrated a significant reduction of median TTI from 80 minutes (IQR: 56·8-139·5) during baseline to 58·50 (IQR: 30·3-118.2) minutes after AI deployment (Wilcoxon rank sum test-location shift: -21·0, 95% CI: -38·0, -7·0).
sample_unit: stroke patients (72 baseline, 102 after AI deployment); diagnostic accuracy on 864 NCCT scans

title: Comparison of the Quality of Discharge Letters Written by Large Language Models and Junior Clinicians: Single-Blinded Study
outcome: GPT-4 vs junior clinician discharge letter quality rated by blinded primary care physicians
effect: GPT-4 higher on information provision (4.32 vs 3.70, P=.03); no significant differences in clarity, collegiality, conciseness, follow-up, or overall satisfaction (3.96 vs 3.62, P=.36).
quote: GPT-4 outperformed human counterparts in information provision (mean 4.32, SD 0.95 vs 3.70, SD 1.27; P=.03) and had no instances of hallucination.
sample_unit: letter ratings (5 cases rated by primary care physicians, GPT-4 vs junior clinician letters)

title: Comparison of the Quality of Discharge Letters Written by Large Language Models and Junior Clinicians: Single-Blinded Study
outcome: GPT-4 letter quality compared against junior clinicians on same case records
effect: GPT-4 outperformed on information provision (P=.03); equivalent on clarity (P=.12), collegiality (P=.05), conciseness (P=.71), follow-up (P=.08), overall satisfaction (P=.36).
quote: Discharge letters written by GPT-4 had equivalent quality to those written by junior clinicians, without any hallucinations.
sample_unit: letter ratings (5 cases rated by primary care physicians, GPT-4 vs junior clinician letters)

title: Continuous prediction and clinical alarm management of late-onset sepsis in preterm infants using vital signs from a patient monitor
venue: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
outcome: simulated real-time alarm performance
effect: 24 h multi-threshold policy: sensitivity 71.6 %, PPV 9.9 %, average 1.15 alarms per day per patient.
quote: When setting the expected alarm window to 24 h and using a multi-threshold alarm policy, the sensitivity metric was 71.6 %, while the positive predictive value was 9.9 %, resulting in an average of 1.15 alarms per day per patient.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Consent Aid for Carpal Tunnel Release
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid readability grade of ChatGPT vs EIDO patient information for carpal tunnel release
effect: Flesch-Kincaid score 12.3 for ChatGPT vs 7.5 for EIDO, indicating more complex reading age for ChatGPT information.
quote: Flesch-Kincaid readability scoring was 12.3 for ChatGPT and 7.5 for EIDO, suggesting a more complex reading age for the ChatGPT information.
sample_unit: patient information documents (carpal tunnel release consent information)

title: Evaluating Chatbot responses to patient questions in the field of glaucoma
outcome: Expert-graded accuracy and comprehensiveness of ChatGPT glaucoma answers (1-4 scale)
effect: Mean panel score 3.29 (SD 0.484); 7 of 24 (29.2%) question-response pairs had mean inter-grader score of 3 or less, so most were adequate but a substantial minority incomplete or inaccurate.
quote: Out of the 24 question-response pairs, seven (29.2%) of them had a mean inter-grader score of 3 or less.

title: Accuracy and safety of an autonomous artificial intelligence clinical assistant conducting telemedicine follow-up assessment for cataract surgery
outcome: Accuracy of AI identification of post-cataract patients needing further review versus supervising ophthalmologist
effect: Overall outcome sensitivity 94%, specificity 86%; kappa 0.758-0.970 with clinicians. 4 patients discharged by Dora but not the clinician needed no review on callback.
quote: Dora R1 demonstrated an overall outcome sensitivity of 94% and specificity of 86% and showed moderate to strong agreement (kappa: 0.758-0.970) with clinicians in all parameters.

title: Increasing Generative Artificial Intelligence Competency among Students Enrolled in Doctoral Nursing Research Coursework
outcome: Self-rated generative AI competency after brief didactic and lab training on ChatGPT use and limitations
effect: All 10 students reported increasing self-rated generative AI competency by one to two points on a five-point scale; they identified strengths and limitations of ChatGPT across three tasks.
quote: All of them reported increasing their self-rated competency in generative AI by one to two points on a five-point rating scale.

title: Clinical validation of commercial deep-learning based auto-segmentation models for organs at risk in the head and neck region: a single institution study
outcome: Agreement of AI auto-contours with expert contours on local historical clinical cases (DSC, mean distance)
effect: Local validation on 40 cases: mandible DSC 0.90 and 0.91; chiasm DSC 0.28 and 0.30; manual editing likely needed before treatment planning use.
quote: EC and AC agreement was highest for the mandible (DSC 0.90 ± 0.16) and (DSC 0.91 ± 0.03), and lowest for the chiasm (DSC 0.28 ± 0.14) and (DSC 0.30 ± 0.14) for AccuContour and ProtégéAI respectively.

title: Readability and Information Quality in Cancer Information From a Free vs Paid Chatbot
outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of chatbot cancer responses with vs without sixth-grade-level prompt
effect: Prompting raised median reading ease in free (52.60 to 71.55) and paywalled (62.48 to 75.64) chatbot versions, both P < .001, without significant change in DISCERN quality.
quote: Prompting was associated with increases in reading ease in both free (median [IQR], 71.55 [68.20-78.99]; P < .001)and paywalled versions (median [IQR], 75.64 [70.53-81.12]; P < .001).

title: Readability and Information Quality in Cancer Information From a Free vs Paid Chatbot
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses with explicit sixth-grade reading level instruction
effect: Asking for a sixth grade reading level increased median Flesch scores to 71.55 (free) and 75.64 (paywalled), both P < .001; DISCERN quality did not differ.
quote: However, prompting the free chatbot to reword responses at a sixth grade reading level was associated with increased reading ease scores than the paywalled chatbot nonprompted responses (median [IQR], 71.55 [68.20-78.99]) (P < .001).

title: Evaluating generative AI responses to real-world drug-related questions
outcome: Recognition of suicidal ideation and emergency escalation in AI responses to real forum questions
effect: Clinicians rated responses as high quality, but instances of dangerous disinformation were found, including disregard for suicidal ideation, incorrect emergency helplines, and endorsement of home detox.
quote: While clinicians rated the AI-generated responses as high quality, we discovered instances of dangerous disinformation, including disregard for suicidal ideation, incorrect emergency helplines, and endorsement of home detox.

title: Evaluating generative AI responses to real-world drug-related questions
outcome: Consistency of AI advice across equivalent question phrasings
effect: The AI systems produced inconsistent advice depending on question phrasing.

outcome: Readability of chatbot answers to cardiology, oncology and psoriasis questions on four readability scales
effect: Flesch Reading Ease 16.3 (Chatbot D) to 39.8 (Chatbot A); Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 12.5 to 15.9; Gunning Fog 15.77 to 19.73; Dale-Chall 10.3 to 11.9, all difficult college-level text.
quote: The Flesch Reading Ease Scale ranged from 16.3 (12.2 - 21.9) (Chatbot D) to 39.8 (29.0 - 50.4) (Chatbot A).

title: The diagnostic and triage accuracy of the GPT-3 artificial intelligence model: an observational study
outcome: Recognition and appropriate triage of emergent cases by GPT-3
effect: GPT-3 triaged 70% correct (34/48) versus 91% for physicians; GPT-3 deprioritised truly emergent cases in seven instances.
quote: For triage error analysis, GPT-3 deprioritised truly emergent cases in seven instances.

title: The diagnostic and triage accuracy of the GPT-3 artificial intelligence model: an observational study
outcome: GPT-3 diagnostic and triage accuracy compared with physicians and laypeople on same vignettes
effect: Diagnosis top-3: GPT-3 88% vs lay 54% (p<0.0001) vs physicians 96% (p=0.012). Triage: GPT-3 70% vs lay 74% (p=0.60) vs physicians 91% (p<0.0001).
quote: GPT-3 triaged 70% correct (34/48, 57-82) versus 74% (3706/5000, 73-75; p=0.60) for lay individuals and 91% (608/666, 89-93%; p<0.0001) for physicians.

title: The diagnostic and triage accuracy of the GPT-3 artificial intelligence model: an observational study
outcome: Calibration of GPT-3 confidence in diagnosis and triage (Brier score)
effect: Confidence reasonably well calibrated: Brier score 0.18 for diagnosis and 0.22 for triage.
quote: As measured by the Brier score, GPT-3 confidence in its top prediction was reasonably well calibrated for diagnosis (Brier score=0·18) and triage (Brier score=0·22).

title: Readability analysis of ChatGPT's responses on lung cancer
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT lung cancer answers on nine readability formulas
effect: Mean Flesch Reading Ease 40.52; Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 12.56; Gunning FOG 13.63; SMOG 14.61; ARI 15.04; Coleman-Liau 14.24; answers at college level and above and difficult to read.
quote: The readability levels of the answers generated by ChatGPT are "collage" and above and are difficult to read.

title: Deep learning-based automatic ASPECTS calculation can improve diagnosis efficiency in patients with acute ischemic stroke: a multicenter study
outcome: Physician ASPECTS diagnostic AUC and reading time with versus without the AI system
effect: Combining the system with physicians improved AUC from 67.43% to 89.76% and reduced diagnosis time from 130.6 ± 66.3 s to 33.3 ± 8.3 s (p < 0.001).
quote: Combining the system with physicians improved AUC from 67.43 to 89.76%, reducing diagnosis time from 130.6 ± 66.3 s to 33.3 ± 8.3 s (p < 0.001).

title: A Qualitative Evaluation of ChatGPT4 and PaLM2's Response to Patient's Questions Regarding Age-Related Macular Degeneration
outcome: Consensus alignment and completeness of LLM answers to AMD patient questions, rated by ophthalmologists

quote: Out of 133 questions, ChatGPT4 received a score of five from both reviewers to 118 questions (88.72%) for C1, to 130 (97.74%) for C2, to 131 (98.50%) for C3, to 133 (100%) for C4, to 132 (99.25%) for C5, and to 122 (91.73%) for C6, while PaLM2 to 81 questions (60.90%) for C1, to 114 (85.71%) for C2, to 115 (86.47%) for C3, to 124 (93.23%) for C4, to 113 (84.97%) for C5, and to 93 (69.92%) for C6.

title: Optimizing GPT-4 Turbo Diagnostic Accuracy in Neuroradiology through Prompt Engineering and Confidence Thresholds
outcome: Diagnostic precision with and without a confidence threshold on LLM outputs
effect: Baseline accuracy 55.1%; with five-candidate list and 90% confidence threshold, precision rose to 72.9%, candidate list correct 85.9%, misdiagnosis rate 14.1%.
quote: By reformatting responses to list five diagnostic candidates and applying a 90% confidence threshold, the highest precision of the diagnosis increased to 72.9%, with the candidate list providing the correct diagnosis at 85.9%, reducing the misdiagnosis rate to 14.1%.

title: Optimizing GPT-4 Turbo Diagnostic Accuracy in Neuroradiology through Prompt Engineering and Confidence Thresholds

quote: However, this threshold reduced the number of cases that responded.

title: Single-center outcomes of artificial intelligence in management of pulmonary embolism and pulmonary embolism response team activation
venue: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research

title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
outcome: Change in AUROC when models were applied to new datasets/settings
effect: Transported LR from APCD dropped from 0.879 to 0.797 (HIDD) and 0.749 (KHIN); KHIN model rose from 0.787 to 0.845 (APCD) and 0.829 (HIDD). LSTM HIDD to KHIN AUROC 0.595.
quote: When transporting models developed on source data to target data, their transported performance does not necessarily drop, showing data-dependent transportability.

title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
outcome: Feature prevalence differences (SMD) between development and target datasets and their effect on transportability
effect: Datasets differed in captured encounters (e.g., SMD -0.7 for acute appendicitis; 1.4-1.8 for outpatient codes), and predictor importance differed across datasets, with varying transported performance.
quote: Overall, the same ML-based suicide prediction model might identify a different set of important predictors when trained from different datasets, together with data differences, suggesting varying transported performance.

title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
outcome: Comparison of complex models (LSTM, GBM) with simpler logistic regression on same data
effect: Complex models did not outperform LR locally or transported; on KHIN LSTM AUROC 0.759 vs LR 0.787; LSTM HIDD to KHIN 0.595.
quote: More complex models, particularly deep long short-term memory neural network models, did not outperform simpler regularized logistic regression models in terms of both local and transported performance.

title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
outcome: local versus transported AUROC
effect: On APCD target, local LR AUROC 0.879 versus transported HIDD 0.802 and KHIN 0.845.
quote: For example, as shown in Table 2 and Fig. 2c , the LR model trained from APCD could achieve an average AUROC of 0.879 ([0.876, 0.882]) on the APCD testing data, and the transported model trained from HIDD and KHIN achieved an average AUROC of 0.802 ([0.795, 0.808]) and 0.845 ([0.841, 0.849]), respectively, when tested on the same APCD data.

title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
outcome: Locally trained versus transported model performance on target data
effect: Local models on target data generally matched or exceeded transported models; APCD local LR AUROC 0.879 vs 0.797 to HIDD and 0.749 to KHIN when transported.
quote: the LR model trained from APCD could achieve an average AUROC of 0.879 ([0.876, 0.882]) on the APCD testing data, and the transported model trained from HIDD and KHIN achieved an average AUROC of 0.802 ([0.795, 0.808]) and 0.845 ([0.841, 0.849]), respectively, when tested on the same APCD data.

title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
outcome: Performance variation across sites/data sources
effect: LR AUROC varied by source and target: local 0.879 (APCD), 0.831 (HIDD), 0.787 (KHIN); transported values ranged 0.735 to 0.845.
quote: Transported models exhibited varying performance, showing drops or even improvements compared to their source performance.

title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
outcome: transported AUROC across external datasets
effect: APCD LR AUROC 0.879 on source dropped to 0.797 on HIDD and 0.749 on KHIN.
quote: As shown in Table 2 , the locally learned LR model on APCD could achieve an average AUROC of 0.879 ([0.876, 0.882]), and transported performance of 0.797 ([0.785, 0.809]) and 0.749 ([0.739, 0.757]) to HIDD and KHIN, respectively.

title: Accuracy and transportability of machine learning models for adolescent suicide prediction with longitudinal clinical records
outcome: Predictive performance of complex deep learning versus simpler regularized logistic regression models
effect: Logistic regression achieved comparable AUROC to LSTM on APCD (0.879 vs 0.901) and HIDD (0.831 vs 0.811), and outperformed LSTM on KHIN (0.787 vs 0.759); transported LSTM performance dropped substantially.
quote: More complex models, particularly deep long short-term memory neural network models, did not outperform simpler regularized logistic regression models in terms of both local and transported performance.
