outcome: Whether single external validation cohort choice misrepresents model performance
effect: Validation in IMASH (0.52), Leeds (0.66), or ISAT (0.68) would suggest poor to moderate discrimination, while SHOP (0.84) was likely optimistic versus mean 0.74.
quote: For example, validating the model in the IMASH (0.52), Leeds (0.66), or the ISAT cluster (0.68) would indicate poor to moderate discrimination.

title: Pitfalls of single-study external validation illustrated with a model predicting functional outcome after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
outcome: External-cluster performance drop
effect: Six clusters had substantial discrimination decreases versus optimism-corrected c-statistic 0.77 and pooled mean 0.75.
quote: We observed a substantial decrease in discriminative performance in 6 clusters compared to the optimism-corrected c -statistic (benchmark) and the pooled mean c-statistic (reference for overall external performance).

title: Pitfalls of single-study external validation illustrated with a model predicting functional outcome after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage
outcome: Generalizability to new cohorts
effect: Leeds membership model c-statistic 0.69, but discrimination was unsatisfactory, indicating poor generalizability.
quote: In the Leeds cluster the derivation and validation samples were similar (membership model c -statistic 0.69), but the discriminative performance was unsatisfactory indicating poor generalizability of the model (Supplementary Material 7).

title: Evaluating the Appropriateness, Consistency, and Readability of ChatGPT in Critical Care Recommendations
outcome: Consistency of responses when the same question was asked repeatedly
effect: No significant difference in consistency between ChatGPT 3.5 and 4.0 (40% vs 28%, P = 0.291); both gave different results when the same question was repeated.
quote: Despite potential for clinical application, both models lacked consistency producing different results when asked the same question multiple times.

title: Evaluating the Appropriateness, Consistency, and Readability of ChatGPT in Critical Care Recommendations
outcome: Hallucinations delivered with high confidence in critical care recommendations
effect: Both ChatGPT versions produced hallucinations, described as misinformation delivered with high confidence; no numeric hallucination rate was reported.
quote: Both models produced "hallucinations"-misinformation delivered with high confidence-which highlights the risk of relying on these tools without domain expertise.

title: Reducing Failed Extubations in Preterm Infants Via Standardization and Real-Time Decision Support
outcome: Failed extubation rate (reintubation <5 days) before vs after standardization and EMR calculator
effect: Failed extubations fell from 10.3% to 2.3%, with special cause variation after both PDSA cycles; ventilator days fell 10.8 to 7.0. Uncontrolled pre-post design.
quote: We observed a reduction in failed extubations from 10.3% to 2.3%, with special cause variation noted after both plan-do-study-act cycle #1 and #2.
sample_unit: infants <32 weeks GA or <1500 g birth weight

title: Reducing Failed Extubations in Preterm Infants Via Standardization and Real-Time Decision Support
outcome: Balancing measures: days on mechanical ventilation and infants intubated <3 days
effect: Average infants intubated <3 days increased (60.2%-73.6%) while average ventilator days decreased (10.8-7.0).
quote: Additionally, the average number of infants intubated <3 days increased (60.2%-73.6%), whereas average ventilator days decreased (10.8-7.0).
sample_unit: infants <32 weeks GA or <1500 g birth weight

title: Patient and Provider Experience with Artificial Intelligence Screening Technology for Diabetic Retinopathy in a Rural Primary Care Setting
outcome: Provider and patient acceptance and workflow fit of AI diabetic retinopathy screening during initial implementation
effect: All providers agreed the tool would improve access and screening rates; 31% of providers cited initial challenges incorporating it into visits. 75% of patients were open to more regular screening; 81% wanted screening to continue.
quote: Some providers also identified initial challenges in incorporating the tool into the primary care visit (31%).
sample_unit: survey respondents (102 patients and 13 primary care providers)

title: Is ChatGPT a Reliable Source of Patient Information on Asthma?
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT asthma responses (FRES, FKGL, SMOG) versus recommended patient reading levels
effect: Average readability 33.50±14.37 FRES, 12.79±2.89 FKGL, 13.47±2.38 SMOG; all responses difficult and none followed recommended readability levels.
quote: However, all responses were of difficult readability, and none followed the recommended readability levels.

title: Is ChatGPT a Reliable Source of Patient Information on Asthma?
outcome: Comprehensibility of AI-generated patient information measured by readability scores
effect: Mean FRES 33.50±14.37, FKGL 12.79±2.89, SMOG 13.47±2.38; all responses of difficult readability.
quote: However, all responses were of difficult readability, and none followed the recommended readability levels.

title: Is ChatGPT a Reliable Source of Patient Information on Asthma?
outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT answers to the same question asked twice by different users
effect: Only two (6.67%) of the 30 questions had inconsistent answers.
quote: Only two (6.67%) of the 30 questions had inconsistent answers.

title: Evaluating accuracy and reproducibility of ChatGPT responses to patient-based questions in Ophthalmology: An observational study
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT responses across repeated runs of the same question
effect: ChatGPT provided reproducible responses to 91.5% of questions (no difference in grading categories between two responses).
quote: ChatGPT provided reproducible responses to 91.5% of questions.

title: Evaluating accuracy and reproducibility of ChatGPT responses to patient-based questions in Ophthalmology: An observational study
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT answers to patient ophthalmology questions graded by ophthalmologists
effect: ChatGPT provided "comprehensive" responses to 70/117 (59.8%) of questions; described as moderate accuracy.
quote: Totally, 117 questions were inputted into ChatGPT, which provided "comprehensive" responses to 70/117 (59.8%) of questions.

title: Applying AI to Safely and Effectively Scale Care to Address Chronic MSK Conditions
outcome: Pain response, mental health, engagement, satisfaction and adverse events with AI-supported care versus DCP alone
effect: Pain response 64% vs 63% (p=0.399); anxiety p=0.928; depression p=0.187; adverse events 0.58% vs 0.69% (p=0.231). Outcomes were similar, so AI-supported scaling did not compromise outcomes.
quote: Similar improvements in pain response were observed, regardless of the group (response rate: 64% vs. 63%; p = 0.399).

title: Vignette-based comparative analysis of ChatGPT and specialist treatment decisions for rheumatic patients: results of the Rheum2Guide study
outcome: Blinded rater preference and quality ratings of LLM plans versus clinical rheumatology board plans
effect: Raters preferred the board's plans in 68.8% (110/160) versus GPT-4 16.3% (26/160) and GPT-3.5 15.0% (24/160); board plans rated significantly higher on guideline adherence, appropriateness, completeness and quality.
quote: In 68.8% (110/160) of cases, raters preferred the RB's treatment plans over those generated by GPT-4 (16.3%; 26/160) and GPT-3.5 (15.0%; 24/160).
sample_unit: ratings (20 fictional vignettes rated by 4 rheumatologists)

title: Comparative Evaluation of LLMs in Clinical Oncology
outcome: LLM accuracy on oncology questions versus human exam benchmark
effect: Only GPT-4 performed above the 50th percentile of the human benchmark; performance was worse in clinical oncology subcategories than in foundational topics; all LLMs had clinically significant error rates.
quote: Relative to a human benchmark (2013 and 2014 examination results), GPT-4 was the only model to perform above the 50th percentile.

title: Comparative Evaluation of LLMs in Clinical Oncology
outcome: Accuracy of question subsets selected by prompt repetition consistency and self-appraised confidence
effect: Combining model selection, prompt repetition, and confidence self-appraisal identified high-performing question subgroups with accuracies of 81.7% (Claude-v1) and 81.1% (GPT-4).
quote: A combination of model selection, prompt repetition, and confidence self-appraisal allowed for the identification of high-performing subgroups of questions with observed accuracies of 81.7 and 81.1% in the Claude-v1 and GPT-4 models, respectively.

title: Comparative Evaluation of LLMs in Clinical Oncology
outcome: Overconfidence in LLM self-appraised confidence scores
effect: Study reports examples of overconfidence and consistent inaccuracies across all LLMs, despite confidence self-appraisal being useful for identifying higher-accuracy subgroups.
quote: Although this performance is impressive, all LLMs continue to have clinically significant error rates, including examples of overconfidence and consistent inaccuracies.

title: Comparative Evaluation of LLMs in Clinical Oncology
outcome: Model accuracy differences across malignancy types by patient sex predominance
effect: Worse performance observed within clinical oncology for female-predominant malignancies.
quote: Within the clinical oncology subdomain, worse performance was observed in female-predominant malignancies.

title: Potential Use of ChatGPT for the Treatment of Infectious Diseases in Vulnerable Populations
outcome: Accuracy of LLM antibiotic choice, dose and duration answers in special populations
effect: Comprehensive and correct: 38.1% pregnancy, 36.1% allergy, 27.5% older adults; error rates 11.9% pregnancy, 18.1% allergy, 25% older adults, 79.2% kidney disease, 43.8% children.
quote: ChatGPT produced high rates of inaccurate information for treating infectious diseases in special population.

title: Potential Use of ChatGPT for the Treatment of Infectious Diseases in Vulnerable Populations
outcome: Dosing errors in LLM antibiotic recommendations for kidney disease and children
effect: Error rate in patients with kidney disease was 79.2%; for children, 43.8% of answers contained errors.
quote: The error rate in patients with kidney disease was 79.2%.

title: Potential Use of ChatGPT for the Treatment of Infectious Diseases in Vulnerable Populations
outcome: Rate of incorrect LLM treatment recommendations needing clinician verification
effect: High rates of inaccurate information; error rates 11.9% to 79.2% across special populations; recommendations should be checked by healthcare professionals.
quote: Thus, recommendations generated by ChatGPT should be used with caution and checked by healthcare professionals to ensure accuracy and comprehensiveness prior to use.

title: Real-world evaluation of RetCAD deep-learning system for the detection of referable diabetic retinopathy and age-related macular degeneration
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity at the pre-defined cut-point versus the locally optimal cut-point (Youden) for DR and AMD
effect: For AMD at the pre-defined cut-point, sensitivity was 88.9% and specificity 66.7%. The optimal cut-point of 52.6 gave sensitivity 87.0% and specificity 75.0%. For DR, the optimal cut-point of 41.2 gave sensitivity 93.7% versus 86.1% at the pre-defined cut-point.
quote: At the pre-defined cut-point sensitivity was 88.9% (77.8%-94.8%) and specificity was 66.7% (56.8%-75.3%).

title: A Machine Learning Method for Differentiation Crohn's Disease and Intestinal Tuberculosis
outcome: Comparison of six candidate ML models, and ML versus multidisciplinary team, on the same data
effect: XGBoost performed best of six models (AUROC 0.946, accuracy 0.884); in clinical practice ML-MDT agreement was 90.7%, kappa 0.780
quote: XGBoost displays the best performance among the six ML models.

title: Use of Generative AI to Identify Helmet Status Among Patients With Micromobility-Related Injuries From Unstructured Clinical Notes
outcome: Test-retest reproducibility of LLM helmet-status classification across 5 new chat sessions and days
effect: LLM did not perfectly replicate analyses across sessions and days (Fleiss κ = 0.91 across 5 trials; P < .001); it consistently replicated its hallucinations.
quote: The LLM did not perfectly replicate its analyses across new sessions and days (Fleiss κ = 0.91 across 5 trials; P < .001).

title: Use of Generative AI to Identify Helmet Status Among Patients With Micromobility-Related Injuries From Unstructured Clinical Notes
outcome: LLM validity versus researcher-reviewed criterion standard
effect: High validity compared with the criterion standard (n = 400; κ = 0.98 [95% CI, 0.96-1.00]).
quote: It also showed high validity compared with the criterion standard (n = 400; κ = 0.98 [95% CI, 0.96-1.00]).

title: Metabolic syndrome risk prediction in an Australian sample with first-episode psychosis using the psychosis metabolic risk calculator: A validation study
venue: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
outcome: Calibration and discrimination before versus after local recalibration of the model
effect: Calibration intercept full model 0.362 to 0.009; slope 1.187 to 1.003; Brier 0.062 to 0.042; C-statistic 0.72 to 0.74; net benefit range widened after recalibration.
quote: Recalibration and updating led to slightly improved C-statistics, greatly improved agreement between observed and predicted risk, and a narrow window of likely clinical usefulness improved significantly.

title: Metabolic syndrome risk prediction in an Australian sample with first-episode psychosis using the psychosis metabolic risk calculator: A validation study
venue: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
outcome: Differences between development (UK) and local Australian populations and resulting performance
effect: Australian sample differed from UK sample on most sociodemographic, clinical and biochemical characteristics; calibration was poor and ethnicity predictor could not be used.
quote: The Australian sample differed from the original UK PsyMetRiC development sample on most sociodemographic, clinical and biochemical characteristics.

title: Metabolic syndrome risk prediction in an Australian sample with first-episode psychosis using the psychosis metabolic risk calculator: A validation study
venue: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
outcome: Local discrimination and calibration
effect: Full C=0.72 (95% C.I., 0.65, 0.77); partial C=0.71 (95% C.I., 0.64-0.75); calibration showed consistent under-prediction.
quote: Calibration plots were similar across imputed datasets, showing consistent under-prediction of risk, more extreme for the full model, with predictions becoming more inaccurate at higher predicted risk scores.

title: Metabolic syndrome risk prediction in an Australian sample with first-episode psychosis using the psychosis metabolic risk calculator: A validation study
venue: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
outcome: Model discrimination and calibration on local historical data against reference standard
effect: C-statistics 0.72 (full) and 0.71 (partial) acceptable, but calibration showed consistent under-prediction of risk; only a very narrow window of clinical usefulness with original model.
quote: Calibration plots were similar across imputed datasets, showing consistent under-prediction of risk, more extreme for the full model, with predictions becoming more inaccurate at higher predicted risk scores.

title: Metabolic syndrome risk prediction in an Australian sample with first-episode psychosis using the psychosis metabolic risk calculator: A validation study
venue: Australasian psychiatry : bulletin of Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Psychiatrists
outcome: Model performance when applied to a new population (Australia)
effect: Original UK model under-predicted risk in Australian sample (calibration intercept 0.362 full model); C-statistics 0.72 and 0.71 vs UK 0.75 and 0.74.
quote: However, calibration plots demonstrated consistent under-prediction of risk.

title: Evaluation of Generative Language Models in Personalizing Medical Information: Instrument Validation Study
outcome: Whether generated patient text reading level matched requested user reading level
effect: GPT-3.5 6th-grade FKGL 9.08 and 8th-grade 10.27, above target; GPT-4 6th-grade FKRE 74.54, above target 6th-grade band (80-90 easy).
quote: GPT-3.5 only aligned with the prespecified education levels at the bachelor's degree.

title: Evaluation of Generative Language Models in Personalizing Medical Information: Instrument Validation Study
outcome: Reproducibility of output readability across repeated runs
effect: Each scenario run 5 times; average FKRE SD 4.91 (GPT-3.5) and 4.86 (GPT-4); average FKGL SD 0.99 and 1.05, showing stable readability across repeats.
quote: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 demonstrated relatively consistent results in variability across all educational levels, suggesting that both versions of ChatGPT maintain uniform performance irrespective of the complexity of language in the clinical vignettes used.

title: Decoding Radiology Reports: Artificial Intelligence-Large Language Models Can Improve the Readability of Hand and Wrist Orthopedic Radiology Reports
outcome: Readability (FRES, FKRL) of LLM-generated plain-language reports versus original radiology reports
effect: Statistically significant improvement in mean FRES and FKRL for radiograph, CT, and MRI reports; mean reading level of all AI-LLM-generated reports improved to below an eighth-grade level.
quote: For all AI-LLM-generated reports, the mean reading level improved to below an eighth-grade reading level.

title: Decoding Radiology Reports: Artificial Intelligence-Large Language Models Can Improve the Readability of Hand and Wrist Orthopedic Radiology Reports
outcome: Hallucination rate and accuracy of LLM-generated patient-facing report explanations
effect: Hallucination rate 3% (radiograph), 6% (CT), 6% (MRI); mean Likert accuracy 4.1 ± 0.6, 3.9 ± 0.6, 3.9 ± 0.7.
quote: The hallucination rate in the AI-LLM-generated radiograph report, CT report, and MRI report was 3%, 6%, and 6%, respectively.

title: Interpretation of Clinical Retinal Images Using an Artificial Intelligence Chatbot
outcome: Proportion of retina cases correctly diagnosed by custom GPT-4 chatbot using multimodal images
effect: Correct diagnosis in 35 of 69 cases (50.7%); needed full patient description for 23 of 35 correct cases (65.7%); OR 10.1 (95% CI 3.3-30.3) for full description vs age and sex only.
quote: The diagnostic ability of the chatbot in interpretation of multimodal imaging without text-based information is currently limited.

title: [Efficacy and safety of artificial intelligence-based large language models for decision making support in herniology: evaluation by experts and general surgeons]
outcome: Validity of references and evidence cited by ChatGPT
effect: Chatbot failed to provide valid references and actual evidence, and falsified half of references.
quote: The chat-bot failed to provide valid references and actual evidence, as well as falsified half of references.
sample_unit: questions (5 ChatGPT responses rated by experts and surgeons)

title: [Efficacy and safety of artificial intelligence-based large language models for decision making support in herniology: evaluation by experts and general surgeons]
outcome: Expert versus non-expert ratings of ChatGPT recommendation quality
effect: Experts scored ChatGPT responses lower than non-experts: 2 (1-2) vs. 2 (2-3), p<0.001.
quote: Experts scored the quality of ChatGPT responses lower than non-experts (2 (1-2) vs. 2 (2-3), p<0.001).
sample_unit: questions (5 ChatGPT responses rated by experts and surgeons)

title: Should they stay or should they go? Stroke transfers across a hospital network pre- and post-implementation of an automated image interpretation and communication platform
venue: Interventional neuroradiology : journal of peritherapeutic neuroradiology, surgical procedures and related neurosciences
outcome: Rate of transferred stroke patients treated with EVT before vs after AI implementation
effect: EVT rate among transfers rose from 32.1% pre-AI to 45.7% post-AI (p=0.02); adjusted OR 1.85 (95% CI 1.12-3.06). Non-randomized pre-post design; outcome is a process measure rather than patient outcomes.
quote: The rate of transfers treated with EVT significantly increased (32.1% pre-AI vs. 45.7% post-AI, p = 0.02).
sample_unit: patients with acute ischemic stroke presenting to spoke hospitals

title: Generalizability of electroencephalographic interpretation using artificial intelligence: An external validation study
outcome: AI accuracy in geographically distinct population and different EEG equipment versus expert gold standard
effect: Overall accuracy 92% (95% CI 90%-94%) for SCORE-AI versus 94% (92%-96%) for experts; no significant difference for any metric or category.
quote: SCORE-AI achieved diagnostic performance equal to human experts in an EEG dataset independent of the development dataset, in a geographically distinct patient population, recorded with different equipment and technical settings than the development dataset.

title: Generalizability of electroencephalographic interpretation using artificial intelligence: An external validation study
outcome: AI diagnostic accuracy compared with three blinded experts on same EEG data
effect: Overall accuracy 92% (95% CI 90%-94%) for SCORE-AI versus 94% (95% CI 92%-96%) for experts; no significant difference for any metric or category.
quote: SCORE-AI performed equally well compared to the experts, with an overall accuracy of 92% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 90%-94%) versus 94% (95% CI = 92%-96%).

title: Evaluating the Efficacy of ChatGPT as a Patient Education Tool in Prostate Cancer: Multimetric Assessment
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4 prostate cancer patient education responses versus appropriate reading level
effect: Consensus 'difficult to read'; Flesch Reading Ease mean 45.97, Gunning Fog 14.55, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 12.12, averaging an 11th-grade reading level.
quote: The readability algorithm consensus was "difficult to read" (Flesch Reading Ease score mean 45.97, SD 8.69; Gunning Fog Index mean 14.55, SD 4.79), averaging an 11th-grade reading level, equivalent to 15- to 17-year-olds (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level mean 12.12, SD 4.34; The Coleman-Liau Index mean 12.75, SD 1.98; SMOG Index mean 11.06, SD 3.20).

title: Evaluating the Efficacy of ChatGPT as a Patient Education Tool in Prostate Cancer: Multimetric Assessment
outcome: Reference hallucination and quality of citations in ChatGPT-4 outputs
effect: REF-AI identified 2 reference hallucinations; 28/30 (93%) references appropriately supplemented text; 26/30 (86%) from reputable government organizations.
quote: REF-AI identified 2 reference hallucinations, while the majority (28/30, 93%) of references appropriately supplemented the text.

title: Generative artificial intelligence versus clinicians: Who diagnoses multiple sclerosis faster and with greater accuracy?
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT when age, sex, and race/ethnicity were varied in scripted MS conversations
effect: After MRI data were included, odds of accurate diagnosis were 4.0-fold greater for Gen Z (p=0.01). Accuracy was 68% lower in males (p=0.009) and 75% lower for White subjects than for non-White subjects (p=0.0004).
quote: Post-MRI data inclusion within GPT-3.5, the odds of an accurate diagnosis was 4.0-fold greater for Gen Z participants, relative to non-Gen Z participants (p=0.01) with the diagnostic accuracy being 68% less in males relative to females (p=0.009), and 75% less for White subjects, relative to non-White subjects (p=0.0004).
sample_unit: scripted conversations (100 real people with MS plus 529 simulated derivatives)

title: A pilot feasibility study comparing large language models in extracting key information from ICU patient text records from an Irish population
outcome: LLM ICU summary capture of key clinical events and hallucinations, adjudicated by intensivists
effect: Key event identification was 41.5 ± 15.2% for GPT-4 API, 19.2 ± 20.9% for ChatGPT and 16.5 ± 14.1% for Llama2 (p = 0.002). GPT-4 API produced minor hallucinations.
quote: Overall ability to identify a pre-defined list of important clinical events in the summary was 41.5 ± 15.2% for GPT-4 API, 19.2 ± 20.9% for ChatGPT and 16.5 ± 14.1% for Llama2 (p = 0.002).
sample_unit: ICU episodes (one summary per LLM per episode)

title: A pilot feasibility study comparing large language models in extracting key information from ICU patient text records from an Irish population
outcome: Performance of LLM summaries on intended-use ICU discharge summary task with local data
effect: All models had narrative coherence problems and omitted key clinical data; only moderately captured clinically meaningful data in correct order.
quote: All encountered issues with narrative coherence and omitted key clinical data and only moderately captured all clinically meaningful data in the correct order.
sample_unit: ICU episodes (one summary per LLM per episode)

title: Evaluation of AI-Driven LabTest Checker for Diagnostic Accuracy and Safety: Prospective Cohort Study
outcome: Sensitivity of AI triage for emergency and urgent cases versus consultant gold standard
effect: 100% sensitivity for emergency safety and 92.3% sensitivity for urgent cases; overall triage accuracy 74.3%.
quote: The system achieved a 74.3% accuracy and 100% sensitivity for emergency safety and 92.3% sensitivity for urgent cases.

title: Assessment of readability, reliability, and quality of ChatGPT®, BARD®, Gemini®, Copilot®, Perplexity® responses on palliative care
outcome: Readability of chatbot palliative care answers versus recommended 6th grade level
effect: Answers of all 5 chatbots were at an educational level well above the 6th grade level; differences significant in all formulas (P < .001). Readability easiest to hardest: Bard, Copilot, Perplexity, ChatGPT, Gemini.
quote: The answers of all 5 artificial intelligence robots were determined to be at an educational level well above the 6th grade level.

title: Assessment of readability, reliability, and quality of ChatGPT®, BARD®, Gemini®, Copilot®, Perplexity® responses on palliative care
outcome: Reading level of chatbot patient education content versus recommended 6th grade level
effect: All 5 chatbots' median readability indexes were significantly above the 6th grade level in all formulas (P < .001).
quote: According to the results of our study answers of all 5 AI chatbots were compared with the 6th grade reading level, statistically significant differences were observed in the all formulas (P < .001).

title: Bridging the Gap: Can Large Language Models Match Human Expertise in Writing Neurosurgical Operative Notes?
outcome: Rated accuracy, content and organization of AI vs surgeon-written operative notes on the same cases
effect: AI accuracy 4.44 vs surgeon 4.33 (P = 0.512); AI content lower, 3.73 vs 4.42 (P < 0.001).
quote: The mean AI accuracy was not different from the mean surgeon accuracy (4.44 vs. 4.33; P = 0.512), the mean AI content was lower than the mean surgeon content (3.73 vs. 4.42; P < 0.001).
sample_unit: surveys of surgeon- or AI-written operative notes

title: Development and evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based workflow for the prioritization of patient portal messages
outcome: Time high-scoring patient messages sit unread, pre-post difference-in-difference
effect: Improvement beyond trend of 21 minutes in time high-scoring messages sit unread (63 vs 42 minutes for messages sent outside business hours).
quote: In a pre-post analysis (n = 396 466), an improvement exceeding the trend was observed in the time high-scoring messages sit unread (21 minutes, 63 vs 42 for messages sent outside business hours).

title: Evaluating cognitive performance: Traditional methods vs. ChatGPT
outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT cognitive test scoring with physician scoring
effect: GPT-3.5 differed from physicians on memory (P<0.001; 8 of 21 items) and language (P=0.009 healthy; P=0.002 stroke); GPT-4 showed no significant difference from physicians on memory (P=0.8).
quote: Among healthy subjects, there were significant differences in memory scores between the physician group, GPT-3.5 group, and GPT-4 group ( P < 0.001), with a significant difference in GPT-3.5 and physician group scores ( P < 0.001).

title: Evaluating cognitive performance: Traditional methods vs. ChatGPT
outcome: GPT-3.5 scoring discrepancies after refined prompts and scoring rules
effect: Refined interaction protocols and scoring rules reduced most GPT-3.5 vs physician differences; only memory sections 8 and 14 remained different (P<0.05).
quote: After testing, optimizing the interaction process and scoring rules can reduce most of the differences, with only differences observed in 8th and 14th sections of memory ( P < 0.05), and no significant differences observed in the rest ( P > 0.05) ( Figure 6 ).

title: Evaluating cognitive performance: Traditional methods vs. ChatGPT
outcome: memory evaluation scores
effect: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 scores differed significantly (p<0.001), and GPT-4 showed no significant difference from physician scores (p=0.8).
quote: There was a significant difference in GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 group scores ( P < 0.001), while there was no significant difference in GPT-4 and physician group scores ( P = 0.8) ( Figure 1 ).

title: Evaluating cognitive performance: Traditional methods vs. ChatGPT
outcome: memory evaluation accuracy
effect: GPT-3.5 had significant discrepancies in 8 out of 21 specific memory measures compared to physician assessments (p<0.05).
quote: Furthermore, within the domain of memory evaluation, GPT-3.5 exhibited discrepancies in 8 out of 21 specific measures when compared to assessments conducted by physicians (P < 0.05).

title: AICyte-alone capabilities as an independent screener for triaging cervical cytology using a 50% negative cutoff value
outcome: Missed lesions among cases AI labeled negative and not needing review
effect: 49 LSIL+ cases were designated by AICyte as not needing further review; NPV 98.80% for ASC-H+ and 99.94% for LSIL+. Follow-up found 8 CIN1 and 18 negative cases; the rest had no histology.
quote: Of the 49 low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or higher that were designed by AICyte as not needing further review, the cytohistologic correlation revealed eight cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 1 and 18 negative cases; and the remaining cases were without histologic follow-up.

title: AICyte-alone capabilities as an independent screener for triaging cervical cytology using a 50% negative cutoff value
outcome: AI-alone false-negative cytology
effect: 49 LSIL-or-higher cases were designated no further review; cytohistologic correlation found eight CIN1 and 18 negative, with remaining cases without histologic follow-up.
quote: Of the 49 low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion or higher that were designed by AICyte as not needing further review, the cytohistologic correlation revealed eight cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia 1 and 18 negative cases; and the remaining cases were without histologic follow-up.

title: Chatbots talk Strabismus: Can AI become the new patient Educator?
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Ease) of chatbot answers to patient strabismus questions versus AAPOS website
effect: AAPOS was easiest to read (mean 55.8 ± 14.11), closely followed by Copilot; ChatGPT and Bard had lower readability scores.
quote: Flesch-Kincaid Ease Scores revealed the AAPOS as the easiest to read (mean score: 55.8 ± 14.11), closely followed by Copilot.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT platform in delivering heart failure educational material: A comparison with the leading national cardiology institutes
outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT heart failure patient education responses
effect: ChatGPT responses were longer and more challenging to read than other materials, written at undergraduate and 9-10th grade level, similar to the Heart Failure Society of America materials.
quote: Our study revealed that responses generated by ChatGPT were longer and more challenging to read compared to other materials.
sample_unit: educational materials (ChatGPT responses to common heart failure patient questions vs institutional materials)

title: Evaluating ChatGPT platform in delivering heart failure educational material: A comparison with the leading national cardiology institutes
outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT patient education materials
effect: Responses written at a higher educational level (undergraduate and 9-10th grade), similar to those from the Heart Failure Society of America.
quote: Additionally, these responses were written at a higher educational level (undergraduate and 9-10th grade), similar to those from the Heart Failure Society of America.
sample_unit: educational materials (ChatGPT responses to common heart failure patient questions vs institutional materials)

title: Assessing Artificial Intelligence-Generated Responses to Urology Patient In-Basket Messages
outcome: Acceptability of ChatGPT drafted replies to easy versus difficult patient messages
effect: 56% of responses to easy questions acceptable to send vs 34% for difficult questions (P = .03); easy-question responses were more accurate, complete, helpful, and intelligible.
quote: ChatGPT performed better on easy questions with 56% of responses to easy questions being acceptable to send as compared to 34% of difficult questions (P = .03).

title: Mitigating Sociodemographic Bias in Opioid Use Disorder Prediction: Fairness-Aware Machine Learning Framework
outcome: Reduction in subgroup performance bias after equality-of-odds mitigation, with overall accuracy and recall
effect: Bias fell by 21.66% (sex), 1.48% (race), 21.04% (income) with NN-SGD, and up to 41.62% (race) with NN-Adam. WMV classifier recall was 85.37% and 92.68%, accuracy 58.85% and 90.21%.
quote: Our bias mitigation algorithm substantially reduced bias with NN-SGD, by 21.66% for sex, 1.48% for race, and 21.04% for income, and with NN-Adam by 16.96% for sex, 8.87% for marital status, 8.45% for working condition, and 41.62% for race.
sample_unit: survey respondents (2020 National Survey on Drug Use and Health)

title: Prompt engineering with a large language model to assist providers in responding to patient inquiries: a real-time implementation in the electronic health record
outcome: Provider use of and negative sentiment toward GPT-4 drafts, engineered vs original prompt
effect: Negative sentiment fell from 12.0% to 8.2% (OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.36-0.52), but message usage decreased in the mixed model (beta -0.10, 95% CI -0.11 to -0.09, P<.01).
quote: In mixed linear regression accounting for the provider and number of messages per provider, the engineered prompt in the post-period was associated with a decrease in message usage (beta coefficient, −0.10; 95% CI, −0.11 to −0.09, P < .01).

title: Prompt engineering with a large language model to assist providers in responding to patient inquiries: a real-time implementation in the electronic health record
outcome: Provider uptake and negative sentiment toward AI-generated patient-message drafts
effect: Only 1327 (17.5%) of 7605 drafts were used; negative sentiment was 12.0% (n = 468) before and 8.2% (n = 307) after prompt engineering.
quote: A total of 7605 draft messages were generated by GPT-4 and 1327 (17.5%) were used as a reply to a patient’s inquiry.

title: Prompt engineering with a large language model to assist providers in responding to patient inquiries: a real-time implementation in the electronic health record
outcome: rate of unedited messages sent
effect: 2.6% of generated messages were sent identical or nearly identical to the AI draft.
quote: Across all messages, those that were left identical or nearly identical in editing by providers was 2.6% ( n = 202).

title: Improving accuracy of GPT-3/4 results on biomedical data using a retrieval-augmented language model
outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rate of retrieval-grounded RAG vs general LLMs on DLBCL questions
effect: RAG had highest mean accuracy (2.46 vs GPT-4 2.26, GPT-3.5 1.82, Prometheus 1.74) and fewest answers with hallucinations (3/19 vs GPT-3.5 13/19, GPT-4 8/19).
quote: Overall, the RAG model enhanced with domain specific data outperformed other LLMs with respect to accuracy and relevance of answers, and produced answers with the fewest observed hallucinations.

title: Improving accuracy of GPT-3/4 results on biomedical data using a retrieval-augmented language model
outcome: Fabricated or incorrect references in generative AI outputs
effect: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 gave numerical response rates inconsistent with cited references, with fabricated or incorrect references; GPT models had hallucinations in 13/19 and 8/19 answers.
quote: Numerical overall and complete response rates (ORR and CRR, respectively) reported by GPT-3.5 (ORR = 65.1%, CRR = 35.1%) and GPT-4 (ORR = 62.7%, CRR = 39.2%) were not consistent with their references cited and had either fabricated or provided incorrect references.

title: Improving accuracy of GPT-3/4 results on biomedical data using a retrieval-augmented language model
outcome: Outdated knowledge from training cutoff and incomplete retrieval corpus affecting answers
effect: RAG answer to glofitamab response rate question was inaccurate because the key trial paper was not in the corpus; GPT models trained only up to September 2021.
quote: The RAG model result was not accurate in answering this question because the official glofitamab trial efficacy paper [ 36 ] was not available on PubMed Central ( https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/ ) and therefore not included in the corpus.

title: Improving accuracy of GPT-3/4 results on biomedical data using a retrieval-augmented language model
outcome: accuracy differences between candidate LLMs
effect: On the same 19 questions, RAG had highest accuracy 2.46/relevance 2.61, GPT-4 highest readability 2.88; hallucinations ranged from RAG 3/19 to GPT-3.5 13/19.
quote: Results here demonstrated that the RAG model performed better on biomedical-specific tasks than the other LLMs evaluated, specifically with respect to accuracy and relevance of results.

title: Improving accuracy of GPT-3/4 results on biomedical data using a retrieval-augmented language model
outcome: wrong-disease retrieval in RAG
effect: For question #13, retrieval returned multiple myeloma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia articles rather than DLBCL material, and the summarizer produced an incorrect answer.
quote: For example, question #13 asked about minimal residual disease (MRD) in DLBCL, but the document retriever returned articles about MRD in multiple myeloma and chronic lymphocytic leukemia—two distinct hematological malignancies from DLBCL.

title: The evaluation of the performance of ChatGPT in the management of labor analgesia
outcome: Expert-rated safety, accuracy, completeness of ChatGPT4 responses to labor analgesia scenarios
effect: Deemed safe in 73% of responses (27% unsafe); none unanimously safe across seven experts; accuracy 4/5 (partly accurate); completeness 3.5/5 (somewhat incomplete).
quote: ChatGPT4 was deemed safe in 73% of responses to the presented obstetric anesthesia clinical scenarios (27% of responses were deemed unsafe).
sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (each rated by 7 expert obstetric anesthesiologists)

title: The evaluation of the performance of ChatGPT in the management of labor analgesia
outcome: Clinical decision-making performance of ChatGPT4 versus expert standards despite prior success on knowledge exam questions
effect: Roughly a quarter of responses to clinical scenarios were unsafe, although the model has answered knowledge-based anesthesia questions with reasonable accuracy.
quote: In summary, approximately one quarter of all responses by ChatGPT4 were deemed unsafe by expert obstetric anesthesiologists.
sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (each rated by 7 expert obstetric anesthesiologists)

title: Assessing the Readability, Reliability, and Quality of AI-Modified and Generated Patient Education Materials for Endoscopic Skull Base Surgery
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of patient materials before and after ChatGPT modification
effect: ChatGPT improved FRE of the 10 least readable articles (19.7 ± 4.4 vs. 56.9 ± 5.9, p < 0.001), from university to 10th grade level, still above the recommended sixth-grade level.
quote: ChatGPT improved FRE readability of the 10 least readable online articles (19.7 ± 4.4 vs. 56.9 ± 5.9, p < 0.001), from university to 10th grade level.

title: Assessing the Readability, Reliability, and Quality of AI-Modified and Generated Patient Education Materials for Endoscopic Skull Base Surgery
outcome: Reading level of online and AI-generated patient education materials versus recommended literacy
effect: Existing ESBS articles were unreadable (mean FRE 39.4 ± 12.4); ChatGPT-modified articles reached about 10th grade level, and the generated article had FRE 38.9, above the recommended sixth-grade level.
quote: ChatGPT improves the readability of articles, though most still remain above the recommended literacy level for patient education materials.

title: Do ChatGPT and Gemini Provide Appropriate Recommendations for Pediatric Orthopaedic Conditions?
outcome: Legitimacy of research citations in Gemini responses, checked via PubMed and Google Scholar
effect: Gemini cited 16 papers in 6 of 24 responses; 12 of 16 had errors (7 unidentifiable, 5 with discrepancies in year, journal, or authorship). ChatGPT cited none.
quote: 12 of the 16 studies referenced contained errors and either were unable to be identified (7) or contained discrepancies (5) regarding publication year, journal, or proper accreditation of authorship.

title: Do ChatGPT and Gemini Provide Appropriate Recommendations for Pediatric Orthopaedic Conditions?
outcome: Agreement of LLM responses with AAOS pediatric orthopaedic clinical practice guidelines
effect: ChatGPT and Gemini agreed with AAOS CPGs at 67% and 69%; no significant difference between models; neutral statements or disagreement rate was substantial.
quote: ChatGPT and Gemini performed similarly, agreeing with the AAOS CPGs at a rate of 67% and 69%.

title: Comparing ChatGPT and a Single Anesthesiologist's Responses to Common Patient Questions: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Survey of a Panel of Anesthesiologists
outcome: Rate of possible harm in ChatGPT-drafted answers versus anesthesiologist answers, rated by blinded anesthesiologists
effect: Possibility of harm 4.7% for ChatGPT vs 1.7% for the anesthesiologist (p = .04); agreement with scientific consensus 96.6% vs 99.3% (p = .02).
quote: ChatGPT underperformed the anesthesiologist regarding rate of responses in agreement with scientific consensus (96.6% vs. 99.3%, p = .02) and possibility of harm (4.7% vs. 1.7%, p = .04), but performed similarly in other measures (percentage of responses with inappropriate/incorrect information (5.7% vs. 2.7%, p = .07) and missing information (10.0% vs. 7.0%, p = .19)).

title: Currently Available Large Language Models Do Not Provide Musculoskeletal Treatment Recommendations That Are Concordant With Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines
venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
outcome: Concordance of LLM treatment recommendations with AAOS clinical practice guidelines
effect: 135 responses (70.3%) concordant, 43 (22.4%) indeterminate, 14 (7.3%) discordant; ChatGPT-4 79.2% concordant, Mistral-7B 58.3%; no significant difference across LLMs (P = .12).
quote: Overall, 135 responses (70.3%) were concordant, 43 (22.4%) were indeterminate, and 14 (7.3%) were discordant.
sample_unit: LLM responses (48 AAOS guideline recommendations x 4 LLMs)

title: Currently Available Large Language Models Do Not Provide Musculoskeletal Treatment Recommendations That Are Concordant With Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines
venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
outcome: Proportion of LLM recommendations with verifiable references or citations
effect: Only 20 (10.4%) of recommendations were transparent and provided references with full bibliographic details or links to specific peer-reviewed content.
quote: Of all recommendations, only 20 (10.4%) were transparent and provided references with full bibliographic details or links to specific peer-reviewed content to support recommendations.
sample_unit: LLM responses (48 AAOS guideline recommendations x 4 LLMs)

title: Currently Available Large Language Models Do Not Provide Musculoskeletal Treatment Recommendations That Are Concordant With Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines
venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
outcome: Whether LLM answers provided traceable supporting sources
effect: Only 10.4% of responses gave full references or links; users cannot fully interpret sources of recommendations.
quote: Only 10% of responses by LLMs were transparent, precluding users from fully interpreting the sources from which recommendations were provided.
sample_unit: LLM responses (48 AAOS guideline recommendations x 4 LLMs)

title: Currently Available Large Language Models Do Not Provide Musculoskeletal Treatment Recommendations That Are Concordant With Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines
venue: Arthroscopy : the journal of arthroscopic & related surgery : official publication of the Arthroscopy Association of North America and the International Arthroscopy Association
outcome: Off-the-shelf LLM clinical competence on guideline-based treatment recommendations
effect: More than 1-in-4 recommendations (29.7% indeterminate or discordant) did not reflect CPGs; concordance ranged 58.3% to 79.2% across four LLMs.
quote: Among leading commercially available LLMs, more than 1-in-4 recommendations concerning the evaluation and management of rotator cuff and anterior cruciate ligament injuries do not reflect current evidence-based CPGs.
sample_unit: LLM responses (48 AAOS guideline recommendations x 4 LLMs)

title: Large language models: a new frontier in paediatric cataract patient education
outcome: Readability (SMOG, FKGL) of LLM patient education materials with explicit sixth-grade prompt versus generic prompt
effect: ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 prompt B responses were more readable than prompt A (p<0.001); ChatGPT-4 SMOG 5.59±0.5, FKGL 4.31±0.7; rewrote existing PEMs to SMOG 5.14±0.3.
quote: ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 prompt B responses were more readable than prompt A responses (p<0.001).

title: Large language models: a new frontier in paediatric cataract patient education
outcome: Whether LLMs can write or rewrite patient materials to a target sixth-grade reading level
effect: ChatGPT-4 consistently rewrote existing materials to or below sixth-grade level (SMOG 5.14±0.3) and generated more readable responses than the other two LLMs (p<0.001).
quote: ChatGPT-4 generated more readable responses (lower SMOG and FKGL scores; 5.59±0.5 and 4.31±0.7, respectively) than the other two LLMs (p<0.001) and consistently rewrote them to or below the specified sixth-grade reading level (SMOG: 5.14±0.3).

title: Primary care clinician engagement in implementing a machine-learning algorithm for targeted screening of familial hypercholesterolemia
outcome: Clinician FH knowledge following bundled education and clinical decision-support implementation
effect: Following the bundled intervention, respondents correctly answering at least 2/3rds of FH knowledge questions increased from 40 to 65 %. Surveys included n = 55 at baseline and n = 23 at follow-up; comparisons were unpaired.
quote: Objective PCC knowledge scores improved from 40 to 65 % of responders correctly responding to at least 2/3rds of survey questions.

title: CLARA-MeD Tool - A System to Help Patients Understand Clinical Trial Announcements and Consent Forms in Spanish
venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
outcome: Share of ChatGPT-generated term definitions that experts needed to correct
effect: Experts validated ChatGPT-prepared definitions; 28.99% needed to be fixed.
quote: To prepare definitions for new terms, we used ChatGPT and experts validated them (28.99% needed to be fixed).
sample_unit: documents (15 clinical trial announcements, 15 consent forms, 15 patient information documents)

title: Generating colloquial radiology reports with large language models
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Accuracy of LLM colloquial radiology translations with vs without extracted medical term definitions in prompt
effect: Across all grade levels, the approach was 20% more accurate than baseline; 88% (Findings) and 93% (Impression) accuracy at 8th-grade level.
quote: Across all grade levels, our approach was 20% more accurate than the baseline method.

title: Generating colloquial radiology reports with large language models
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Readability of LLM-generated colloquial radiology reports versus original reports
effect: Translations were more readable than original reports by standard readability indices; 8th-grade level balanced accuracy and readability.
quote: Overall, translations were more readable than the original reports, as evaluated using standard readability indices.

title: Generating colloquial radiology reports with large language models
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: accuracy-readability balance by reading level
effect: Eighth-grade translations struck the optimal accuracy-readability balance and corresponded to patient-facing communication recommendations.
quote: We find that our translations at the eighth-grade level strike an optimal balance between accuracy and readability.

title: Performance of large language models (LLMs) in providing prostate cancer information
outcome: Readability of LLM prostate cancer answers (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid grade level)
effect: Bard had the simplest output, with the highest FRE of 54.7 and the lowest FK grade level of 10.2 (both p < 0.001). Even the most readable output sits at roughly a 10th-grade level.
quote: For readability, Bard generated simpler sentences with the highest FRE score (54.7, p < 0.001) and lowest FK reading level (10.2, p < 0.001).

title: A Blinded Comparison of Three Generative Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Orthopaedic Surgery Therapeutic Questions
outcome: Blinded expert preference and rubric scores for a retrieval-based chatbot versus general chatbots
effect: AskOE was preferred over ChatGPT (P<0.001) and Bing (P<0.001) and had significantly higher total evaluation scores than both (P<0.001).
quote: Across all questions and answers, AskOE was preferred by reviewers to a significantly greater extent than both ChatGPT (P<0.001) and Bing (P<0.001).

title: Generative Pre-trained Transformer for Pediatric Stroke Research: A Pilot Study
outcome: Agreement of GPT data entry with human rater reference standard across iterations
effect: Fourth iteration agreement 93.6%; 2247 of 2400 items correct, 153 (6.4%) incorrect; range 62% to 100% across patients; early iterations scored as low as 0.26.
quote: Of 2400 individual items assessed, our model entered 2247 (93.6%) correctly and 153 (6.4%) incorrectly.

title: What Do People Want to Know About Cochlear Implants: A Google Analytic Study
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT 3.5 responses and website content versus recommended patient education level
effect: Website readability on average did not meet the recommended standard; only two websites were at or below 8th-grade level. ChatGPT readability was significantly poorer than websites (p < 0.001).
quote: Responses by ChatGPT had significantly poorer readability compared to the websites (p < 0.001).
sample_unit: Google People Also Ask questions (top 50 for each of two queries)

title: What Do People Want to Know About Cochlear Implants: A Google Analytic Study
outcome: Reading level of online cochlear implant patient materials versus recommended 8th-grade level
effect: Average readability did not meet the recommended standard for patient education materials; only two websites were at or below the 8th-grade level.
quote: Among all types of websites, readability, on average, did not meet the recommended standard for health-related patient education materials.
sample_unit: Google People Also Ask questions (top 50 for each of two queries)

title: Leveraging Generative Artificial Intelligence Models in Patient Education on Inferior Vena Cava Filters
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, Flesch Reading Ease) of AI-generated IVC filter patient education materials
effect: ChatGPT mean Gunning Fog 17.76 ± 1.62; Copilot lowest at 11.58 ± 1.55; mean Flesch-Kincaid for both cohorts did not meet recommended U.S. grade reading levels.
quote: Nevertheless, the mean Flesch-Kincaid readability for both cohorts does not meet the recommended U.S. grade reading levels.
sample_unit: AI-generated responses to IVC filter patient education questions

title: Leveraging Generative Artificial Intelligence Models in Patient Education on Inferior Vena Cava Filters
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education text relative to recommended reading levels
effect: Both ChatGPT and Copilot outputs exceeded recommended grade levels; Copilot more readable than ChatGPT (Flesch Reading Ease p = 8.70408 × 10^-8; power 0.392).
quote: Nevertheless, the mean Flesch-Kincaid readability for both cohorts does not meet the recommended U.S. grade reading levels.
sample_unit: AI-generated responses to IVC filter patient education questions

title: Viability of Open Large Language Models for Clinical Documentation in German Health Care: Real-World Model Evaluation Study
outcome: Independent human rater usability of generated reports on real-world data
effect: 95 (93.1%) of 102 reports generated by the selected model were rated usable as is or with only minor changes by both human raters.
quote: In the manual evaluation by human experts, 95 (93.1%) of the 102 reports generated by that model were evaluated as usable as is or with only minor changes by both human raters.

title: Improving readability and comprehension levels of otolaryngology patient education materials using ChatGPT
outcome: Readability (FRE, FK grade) of patient education materials before vs after ChatGPT simplification
effect: Overall FRE scores and FK grades improved significantly after ChatGPT translation (p < 0.001) by ChatGPT scoring; Word also showed significant improvement for AAO-HNS materials overall (p < 0.001), but not for individual topics or subspecialty categories. ChatGPT exaggerated the change versus Word.
quote: Overall FRE scores and FK grades demonstrated significant improvements following translation of materials, as scored by ChatGPT (p < 0.001).
sample_unit: patient education topics (37 ALA and 72 AAO-HNS)

title: Improving readability and comprehension levels of otolaryngology patient education materials using ChatGPT
outcome: Whether LLM simplification makes patient education materials more plain-language and readable
effect: Materials were written above recommended reading levels; ChatGPT translation significantly improved FRE and FK scores (p < 0.001), though ChatGPT self-scoring exaggerated the improvement relative to Word.
quote: Otolaryngology patient education materials were found to be written at higher reading levels than recommended.
sample_unit: patient education topics (37 ALA and 72 AAO-HNS)

title: Patient education resources for oral mucositis: a google search and ChatGPT analysis
venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Universal readability of ChatGPT education responses
effect: 100% of ChatGPT responses answered the prompt; 20% met universal readability when asked to write for the appropriate audience.
quote: 100% of the ChatGPT-generated responses answered the prompt, and 20% met the criteria for universal readability when asked to write for the appropriate audience.

title: Comparative analysis of GPT-4-based ChatGPT's diagnostic performance with radiologists using real-world radiology reports of brain tumors
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4 versus neuroradiologists and general radiologists on same report text
effect: GPT-4 final diagnostic accuracy 73% vs radiologists 65-79%; differential diagnosis accuracy 94% vs radiologists 73-89%.
quote: In a study analyzing 150 radiological reports, GPT-4 achieved a final diagnostic accuracy of 73%, while radiologists' accuracy ranged from 65 to 79%.
sample_unit: radiology reports (brain MRI, preoperative brain tumor patients)

title: Performance of ChatGPT 3.5 and 4 as a tool for patient support before and after DBS surgery for Parkinson's disease
venue: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
outcome: Accuracy and harmfulness of LLM answers to DBS questions for Parkinson's disease, graded by specialists
effect: Correct responses 57.5% (GPT 3.5) and 83.8% (GPT 4); GPT 3.5 gave potentially harmful answers in 6.3% (5/80); no GPT 4 responses were harmful.
quote: The proportion of responses graded as correct was 57.5% and 83.8% for GPT 3.5 and GPT 4, respectively.
sample_unit: questions (40 questions in English and Portuguese, each answered by GPT 3.5 and GPT 4)

title: Performance of ChatGPT 3.5 and 4 as a tool for patient support before and after DBS surgery for Parkinson's disease
venue: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
outcome: Expert grading of responses by two specialists with third-reviewer adjudication
effect: Two specialists graded independently; third reviewer resolved disagreements; used to estimate accuracy and harm rates. Methods only, no test of the practice's aim.
quote: ChatGPT models 3.5 and 4 responses to 40 questions in English and Portuguese were independently graded by two experienced specialists in functional neurosurgery and neurological movement disorders and resolved by a third reviewer.
sample_unit: questions (40 questions in English and Portuguese, each answered by GPT 3.5 and GPT 4)

title: ChatGPT as an Information Source for Patients with Migraines: A Qualitative Case Study
outcome: Consistency and comprehensibility of source citations in ChatGPT migraine responses
effect: Source citations were inconsistent and sometimes not comprehensible, which reduced overall comprehensibility of the information. No numeric results reported.
quote: However, source citations were found to be inconsistent and, in some cases, not comprehensible, which affected the overall comprehensibility of the information.

title: Assessing the Accuracy, Completeness, and Reliability of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Responses in Dentistry: A Pilot Study Evaluating the ChatGPT Model
outcome: Correctness of references cited in ChatGPT dental responses
effect: References were more incorrect than correct, with no difference between descriptive and binary questions.
quote: References were more incorrect than correct, with no differences between descriptive and binary questions.

title: Application of artificial intelligence in lung cancer screening: A real-world study in a Chinese physical examination population
outcome: Malignant nodule and lung cancer detection rate, AI-assisted reading versus manual interpretation
effect: AI detection of malignant pulmonary nodules 97.2% vs 86.4% manual (p<0.001); lung cancer detection rate 98.9% vs 90.3% (p<0.001); AI had higher screening positive rate.
quote: Moreover, AI scanning demonstrated a markedly superior detection rate of malignant pulmonary nodules compared with manual scanning (97.2% vs. 86.4%, p < 0.001).

title: Psychosis metabolic risk calculator (PsyMetRiC) in early psychosis: External validation study in Finland
outcome: Calibration of PsyMetRiC before vs after local logistic recalibration
effect: Calibration intercept improved from 0.16 to 0.01 (full) and -0.14 to 0.01 (partial); discrimination unchanged (C 0.72/0.70); net benefit improved further after recalibration.
quote: Following recalibration of PsyMetRiC-Fi to account for population differences, calibration of both models improved substantially with no detriment to discriminative accuracy.

title: Psychosis metabolic risk calculator (PsyMetRiC) in early psychosis: External validation study in Finland
outcome: Discrimination and net benefit of PsyMetRiC compared with FINDRISC on same data
effect: C-statistic 0.72 (full) and 0.70 (partial) vs 0.63 for FINDRISC; at 15% threshold net benefit 0.13 for PsyMetRiC-Fi vs 0.01 for FINDRISC.
quote: Both PsyMetRiC versions showed superior discriminative accuracy in this early psychosis population compared with using FINDRISC.

title: Psychosis metabolic risk calculator (PsyMetRiC) in early psychosis: External validation study in Finland
outcome: Local historical data validation of predictive model against reference standard
effect: External validation in 278 Finnish patients found acceptable discrimination but miscalibration that required recalibration, showing local validation identified performance problems.
quote: Calibration plots (Figure 2 , Figure S3 ) show varying degrees of miscalibration for PsyMetRiC across imputed datasets, with predominantly risk underprediction in the full-model, and overprediction in the partial-model.

title: Psychosis metabolic risk calculator (PsyMetRiC) in early psychosis: External validation study in Finland
outcome: development-validation population comparison
effect: Finnish and UK samples differed; White European/NR 100% vs 55.3%, male 58.60% vs 67.59%.
quote: The Finnish sample differed from the UK PsyMetRiC development sample on most sociodemographic, lifestyle and biochemical characteristics (Table 1 ).

title: Generative artificial intelligence as a source of breast cancer information for patients: Proceed with caution
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses to breast cancer questions (Flesch Kincaid scale)
effect: Average readability was poor at 37.9 (range 18.0-60.5), with high concordance across repetitions (ICC 0.73).
quote: The average readability was poor at 37.9 (range, 18.0-60.5) with high concordance (ICC, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.57-0.90; p < .001).

title: Generative artificial intelligence as a source of breast cancer information for patients: Proceed with caution
outcome: Validity of references cited by ChatGPT in responses
effect: Average 1.97 references per response (total 119); peer-reviewed articles cited only once; nonexistent websites in 41%.
quote: ChatGPT cited peer-reviewed articles only once and often referenced nonexistent websites (41%).

title: Generative artificial intelligence as a source of breast cancer information for patients: Proceed with caution
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT responses to patient breast cancer questions
effect: Average accuracy score 1.88 (4=worst); responses incorrect 24% of the time; clinical concordance 2.79.
quote: Because ChatGPT 3.5 responses were incorrect 24% of the time and did not provide real references 41% of the time, patients should be cautioned about using ChatGPT for medical information.

title: Digesting Digital Health: A Study of Appropriateness and Readability of ChatGPT-Generated Gastroenterological Information
outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT responses to gastrointestinal emergency questions
effect: None of ChatGPT's responses to questions related to gastrointestinal emergencies were designated appropriate.
quote: Notably, none of ChatGPT's responses to questions related to gastrointestinal emergencies were designated appropriate.

title: Digesting Digital Health: A Study of Appropriateness and Readability of ChatGPT-Generated Gastroenterological Information
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT gastroenterology responses (Flesch Reading Ease, FK grade, SMOG)
effect: Mean readability scores showed outputs were written at a college-level reading proficiency.
quote: The mean readability scores showed that outputs were written at a college-level reading proficiency.

title: Digesting Digital Health: A Study of Appropriateness and Readability of ChatGPT-Generated Gastroenterological Information
outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT patient information versus appropriate level
effect: Outputs were written at a college-level reading proficiency, above typical patient literacy.
quote: The mean readability scores showed that outputs were written at a college-level reading proficiency.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of a machine learning algorithm using point-of-care high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I for rapid rule-out of myocardial infarction: a retrospective study
outcome: Rule-out efficacy and safety across clinical subgroups and across two geographic cohorts
effect: Superior rule-out efficacy persisted across all clinically relevant subgroups (age, sex, symptom onset, eGFR, comorbidities); additional analyses were run for each cohort separately. Overall NPV 99.96%, sensitivity 99.68%.
quote: Superior efficacy persisted across all clinically relevant subgroups.

title: Assessing GPT-4 multimodal performance in radiological image analysis
outcome: GPT-4V accuracy identifying modality, anatomical region, and pathology on ER images versus senior radiologists
effect: Modality 100% (221/221), anatomical region 87.1% (189/217), pathology 35.2% (76/216); pathology accuracy 9.1% in US, 36.4% in CT, 66.7% in X-ray.
quote: GPT-4V identified the imaging modality correctly in 100% of cases (221/221), the anatomical region in 87.1% (189/217), and the pathology in 35.2% (76/216).

title: Assessing GPT-4 multimodal performance in radiological image analysis
outcome: Reliability of GPT-4V as standalone diagnostic tool; diagnostic hallucination rate
effect: Pathology identification only 35.2% correct; authors report diagnostic hallucination rate >40% and state it cannot be trusted as a standalone clinical tool.
quote: Although GPT-4V shows promise in radiological image interpretation, its high diagnostic hallucination rate (> 40%) indicates it cannot be trusted for clinical use as a standalone tool.

title: Comparison of AI-integrated pathways with human-AI interaction in population mammographic screening for breast cancer
outcome: Effect of simulated automation bias (readers agreeing with incorrect AI) on system sensitivity/specificity
effect: Negative interaction in AI triage dropped sensitivity by 5.6 points to about 73.1% and specificity to 93.5%; single-reader negative interaction lowered sensitivity/specificity to ~62.6% and 93.9%.
quote: The sensitivity can quickly drop by 5.6 percentage points to about 73.1% (6.7 percentage points lower than the baseline standard of care) and the specificity can drop to 93.5% when human readers follow the mistakes made by the AI reader.

title: Comparison of AI-integrated pathways with human-AI interaction in population mammographic screening for breast cancer
outcome: Performance of AI band-pass pathway where AI makes final decisions without human read
effect: AI band-pass without human reads for high/low scores gave 81.7% sensitivity, 96.6% specificity vs 79.8%/96.0% standard, with 80.7% fewer human reads; authors note lack of human decision-maker faces adoption challenges.
quote: However, having an AI reader make the final reading decision, without human involvement, faces challenges before clinical adoption.

title: Comparison of AI-integrated pathways with human-AI interaction in population mammographic screening for breast cancer
outcome: AI reader and AI-integrated pathways compared with radiologists and standard of care on same data
effect: AI standalone sensitivity 75.0 vs 66.3% for mean individual radiologist; reader-replacement achieved 82.3% sensitivity and 96.3% specificity vs standard of care 79.8%/96.0%.
quote: The AI reader-replacement scenario produced higher system sensitivity (82.3%; 95% CI 81.5–83.1, P < 0.0025) and higher specificity (96.3%; 95% CI 96.2–96.3, P < 4.3 × 10 −6 ) than the current standard of care system (Fig. 3 A and Supplementary Table 2 ).

title: Comparison of AI-integrated pathways with human-AI interaction in population mammographic screening for breast cancer
outcome: screening performance and workload
effect: AI band-pass: sensitivity 81.7% vs 79.8%, specificity 96.6% vs 96.0%; 779 fewer false positives, 25 more cancers, −80.7% human reads.
quote: The AI band-pass screening scenario also achieved both higher system sensitivity (81.7%, P < 0.0058) and specificity (96.6%, P < 2.2 × 10 −25 ) than the current standard of care system (Fig. 3 A and Supplementary Table 2 ).

title: Comparison of AI-integrated pathways with human-AI interaction in population mammographic screening for breast cancer
outcome: standalone AI versus standard care
effect: AI standalone sensitivity was lower than standard care, 75.0% vs 79.8%; specificity was non-inferior, 96.0% vs 96.0%.
quote: However, operating as a sole reader, the AI reader had lower sensitivity (75.0 vs. 79.8%; P < 1.98 × 10 −5 ) at non-inferior specificity (96.0 vs. 96.0%: P = 0.56) than the current standard of care (two readers with arbitration; Supplementary Tables 1 , 2 ).

title: Comparison of AI-integrated pathways with human-AI interaction in population mammographic screening for breast cancer
outcome: automation bias across workflows
effect: Automation bias degraded multi-reader settings but improved single-reader; AI reader-replacement sensitivity fell below standard care only after roughly 30%+ discordant reversals.
quote: Automation bias degrades performance in multi-reader settings but improves it for single-readers.

title: Comparison of AI-integrated pathways with human-AI interaction in population mammographic screening for breast cancer
outcome: cancer detection sensitivity of standalone AI versus standard of care
effect: Operating as a sole reader, AI had significantly lower sensitivity (75.0% vs 79.8%, P < 1.98 x 10^-5) at non-inferior specificity (96.0% vs 96.0%, P = 0.56) than standard of care.
quote: However, operating as a sole reader, the AI reader had lower sensitivity (75.0 vs. 79.8%; P < 1.98 × 10 −5 ) at non-inferior specificity (96.0 vs. 96.0%: P = 0.56) than the current standard of care (two readers with arbitration; Supplementary Tables 1 , 2 ).

title: Enhanced PROcedural Information READability for Patient-Centered Care in Interventional Radiology With Large Language Models (PRO-READ IR)

quote: The readability assessment across all procedural instructions showed a better Flesch-Kincaid mean grade of GPT-4 instructions compared with radiologyinfo.org (7.8 ± 0.87 versus 9.6 ± 0.83; P = .007) indicating excellent readability at 7th- to 8th-grade level compared with 9th to 10th grade.

title: Enhanced PROcedural Information READability for Patient-Centered Care in Interventional Radiology With Large Language Models (PRO-READ IR)

quote: Both large language models significantly underestimated disability in a population of people, and linguistic analysis showed that descriptions of people, patients, and athletes with a disability were generated as having significantly fewer favorable qualities and significantly more limitations than people without a disability in both ChatGPT and Gemini.

outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT-4 answers across repeated runs one week apart

title: Prospective Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Triage of Intracranial Hemorrhage on Noncontrast Head CT Examinations

title: Enhancing Patient Selection in Sepsis Clinical Trials Design Through an AI Enrichment Strategy: Algorithm Development and Validation

quote: When the model was evaluated using a mixed confidence approach, with a confidence level of 85% for recovery and a confidence level of 75% for rapid death and persistent ill, the model with CP reduced overall prediction errors by 27.6% (n=62) and 30.7% (n=412) in the internal and external validation cohorts, respectively, compared with the model without CP ( Table 2 ).

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Assessment of Pediatric Dental Panoramic Radiographs (DPRs): A Clinical Study

title: Gender Representation of Health Care Professionals in Large Language Model-Generated Stories
outcome: Gender pronoun proportions for doctors, surgeons, and nurses in LLM-generated stories

title: Large language model triaging of simulated nephrology patient inbox messages

title: Large language model triaging of simulated nephrology patient inbox messages
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM triage across repeated runs two weeks apart

title: A New Era in Medical Information: ChatGPT Outperforms Medical Information Provided by Online Information Sheets About Congenital Malformations
outcome: Readability and reading time of ChatGPT answers versus online information sheets

title: ChatGPT is capable of providing satisfactory responses to frequently asked questions regarding total shoulder arthroplasty

title: Comparing the Ability of Google and ChatGPT to Accurately Respond to Oculoplastics-Related Patient Questions and Generate Customized Oculoplastics Patient Education Materials
