title: Using ChatGPT to Provide Patient-Specific Answers to Parental Questions in the PICU
outcome: Understandability (PEMAT) and Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT answers to parental questions
effect: PEMAT understandability median 100% (IQR 87.5-100), but Flesch-Kincaid grade level was 8.7. No differences in understandability among scenarios or question types.
quote: Responses had high accuracy (median 5.0, [interquartile range (IQR), 4.0-6.0]), empathy (median 5.0, [IQR, 5.0-6.0]), completeness (97% of all questions), and understandability (PEMAT % median 100, [IQR, 87.5-100]; Flesch-Kincaid level 8.7).
sample_unit: physician reviewer scores of ChatGPT responses (3 scenarios x 8 questions x 6 reviewers)

title: Artificial intelligence based real-time prediction of imminent heart failure hospitalisation in patients undergoing non-invasive telemedicine
outcome: ROC AUC of ML risk score versus conventional heuristic algorithm on the same data
effect: ML model outperformed the conventional algorithm: ROCAUC 0.855 vs. 0.727, p < 0.001.
quote: The machine learning model significantly outperformed the conventional algorithm (ROCAUC 0.855 vs. 0.727, p < 0.001).

title: Implementation of an AI Algorithm in Clinical Practice to Reduce Missed Incidental Pulmonary Embolisms on Chest CT and Its Impact on Short-Term Survival
outcome: 90-day mortality before versus after AI implementation
effect: No significant decrease in 90-day mortality despite improved detection; HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.45-1.96; P = 0.88).
quote: The survival analysis showed no significantly decreased 90-day mortality rate, with a hazards ratio of 0.95 (95% confidence interval, 0.45-1.96; P = 0.88).

title: Implementation of an AI Algorithm in Clinical Practice to Reduce Missed Incidental Pulmonary Embolisms on Chest CT and Its Impact on Short-Term Survival
outcome: Radiologist missed iPE rate with AI in clinical workflow versus before AI
effect: Missed iPEs by radiologists fell from 50% (cohort 1) to 7.1% after AI implementation, P < 0.001; standalone AI sensitivity 90-95%, PPV 69-95%.
quote: The rate of missed iPEs by radiologists dropped to 7.1% after AI implementation, showing a significant improvement ( P < 0.001).

title: Predicting nosocomial pneumonia risk in level-1 trauma patients: An external validation study using the trauma quality improvement program
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of the Croce model before versus after recalibration on TQIP data
effect: After recalibration, discriminatory capacity and calibration for the lower predicted probabilities improved.
quote: After recalibration, discriminatory capacity and calibration for the lower predicted probabilities improved.

title: Predicting nosocomial pneumonia risk in level-1 trauma patients: An external validation study using the trauma quality improvement program
outcome: discrimination of nosocomial pneumonia prediction model
quote: The original model demonstrated good to excellent discrimination for both periods (c-statistic<sub>2013-2015</sub> 0.84, 95%CI 0.83-0.84; c-statistic<sub>2017-2019</sub> 0.92, 95%CI 0.91-0.92).

title: Evaluating the use of large language models to provide clinical recommendations in the Emergency Department
outcome: LLM accuracy versus resident physician on admission, radiology, and antibiotic recommendations
effect: GPT-4-turbo and GPT-3.5-turbo accuracy 8% and 24% lower than the resident physician on average; LLMs overly cautious, high sensitivity at cost of specificity.
quote: We found that both GPT-4-turbo and GPT-3.5-turbo performed poorly compared to a resident physician, with accuracy scores 8% and 24%, respectively, lower than physician on average.

title: Bridging Gaps in Health Literacy for Cleft Lip and Palate: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Educational Materials
venue: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
outcome: Readability and clarity of patient education materials before and after ChatGPT-4 simplification
effect: ChatGPT-4 modification significantly improved readability from median 9th-grade to median 6th-grade level with enhanced clarity.
quote: Modifications using ChatGPT-4 significantly improved readability, achieving a median 6th-grade level and enhanced clarity.

title: Bridging Gaps in Health Literacy for Cleft Lip and Palate: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Educational Materials
venue: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
outcome: Reading grade level of existing cleft lip and palate patient educational materials
effect: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level showed texts written at a median 9th-grade reading level, above the recommended 6th-grade level.
quote: Initial evaluations using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level formula showed that the texts were written at a median 9th-grade reading level.

title: Bridging Gaps in Health Literacy for Cleft Lip and Palate: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Interactive Educational Materials
venue: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
outcome: PEM readability and clarity
effect: Median reading level improved from 9th-grade to 6th-grade after ChatGPT-4; clarity enhanced.
quote: Modifications using ChatGPT-4 significantly improved readability, achieving a median 6th-grade level and enhanced clarity.

title: ChatGPT for improving postoperative instructions in multiple fields of plastic surgery
venue: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
outcome: Readability grade level of postoperative instructions after ChatGPT rewriting to target reading level
effect: Original instructions were 7th-8th grade; all fourth-grade-prompted rewrites reduced to sixth grade or below, but none reached fourth grade; only one sixth-grade-prompted rewrite reached sixth grade.
quote: Overall, the average readability of the original postoperative instructions ranged between the seventh and eighth grade levels.

title: ChatGPT for improving postoperative instructions in multiple fields of plastic surgery
venue: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
outcome: understandability and actionability
effect: Understandability scores increased as reading levels decreased, whereas actionability decreased for fourth-grade rewrites.
quote: Understandability scores increased as reading levels decreased, whereas actionability scores decreased for fourth-grade rewrites.

title: ChatGPT for improving postoperative instructions in multiple fields of plastic surgery
venue: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
outcome: Achievement of target reading level
effect: Only one of four sixth-grade ChatGPT rewrites reached the sixth-grade level, and none achieved the fourth-grade level.
quote: Only one of the sixth-grade ChatGPT instructions was lowered to the sixth-grade level.

title: The Impact of Race, Ethnicity, and Sex on Fairness in Artificial Intelligence for Glaucoma Prediction Models
outcome: Subgroup fairness (equalized odds) by sex, race, ethnicity across sites
effect: Bias found for sex, race, and ethnicity; models fairest on internal test were not necessarily fairest at external sites; M2/M3 showed much more bias for sex and race at external sites.
quote: We found that models trained with sensitive attributes as input features (M2) or trained separately for different groups (M3) demonstrated much more bias for sex and race when evaluated on external test sites.

title: The Impact of Race, Ethnicity, and Sex on Fairness in Artificial Intelligence for Glaucoma Prediction Models
outcome: Internal versus external test set performance and fairness
effect: Models appearing fairest on internal test set were not fairest at independent external sites; AUROC dropped at external sites (external #2 0.67-0.70 vs internal 0.77-0.82).
quote: These results lead to a second key insight, which is that models that appear fairest when evaluated on a standard internal test set are not necessarily the fairest models for completely independent external sites.

title: The Impact of Race, Ethnicity, and Sex on Fairness in Artificial Intelligence for Glaucoma Prediction Models
outcome: Fairness and performance under demographic dataset shift between training and external sites
effect: White 65.6% vs 16.1% vs 46.0%, Black 20.7% vs 76.3% vs 8.7% across training, external #1, external #2; fairness did not generalize consistently across sites.
quote: The failure of modeling approaches to remain consistently fair when deployed to external validation sets could be considered as a specific case of the failure of model performance metrics to generalize in the face of dataset shifts, 11 , 40 , 41 , 42 which occur when data distributions differ between the training and testing/deployment environments.

title: The Impact of Race, Ethnicity, and Sex on Fairness in Artificial Intelligence for Glaucoma Prediction Models
outcome: Effect of including versus excluding sensitive attributes on performance and fairness
effect: Excluding attributes gave better AUROC (0.77-0.82) but worse fairness internally; at external #1 including gave better AUROC but worse fairness; at external #2 including gave both better. Removal did not eliminate bias.
quote: Since removing sex, race, and ethnicity is not a comprehensive solution to eliminate bias in glaucoma algorithm predictions, it may be reasonable to include them if external validation and thorough subpopulation analyses are performed.

title: The Impact of Race, Ethnicity, and Sex on Fairness in Artificial Intelligence for Glaucoma Prediction Models
outcome: Demographic shift across sites
effect: Training/external demographics differed: White 65.6% vs. 16.1% vs. 46.0%; Black 20.7% vs. 76.3% vs. 8.7%; Hispanic 4.26% vs. 2.3% vs. 12.0%.
quote: For example, there is a substantial demographic shift in regards to White (65.6% vs. 16.1% vs. 46.0%), Black (20.7% vs. 76.3% vs. 8.7%), and Hispanic (4.26% vs. 2.3% vs. 12.0%) patients between the training set, external site #1, and external site #2, respectively.

title: The Impact of Race, Ethnicity, and Sex on Fairness in Artificial Intelligence for Glaucoma Prediction Models
outcome: Bias after removing sensitive attributes
effect: Excluding sensitive attributes improved internal AUROC (0.77-0.82) but worsened fairness; removing sex, race, and ethnicity did not eliminate bias.
quote: We found evidence of bias for sex, race, and ethnicity that was not wholly ameliorated by removing these sensitive attributes as inputs to the models.

title: Assessing the performance of large language models (LLMs) in answering medical questions regarding breast cancer in the Chinese context
outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to breast cancer treatment questions against oncologist scoring
effect: Accuracy of the three models on breast cancer treatment questions was lowest, averaging 44.4%; overall about 57-67% comprehensive answers per model.
quote: The accuracy of the three models in answering questions regarding breast cancer treatment was the lowest, with an average of 44.4%.

title: A Novel Cognitive Behavioral Therapy-Based Generative AI Tool (Socrates 2.0) to Facilitate Socratic Dialogue: Protocol for a Mixed Methods Feasibility Study
outcome: Harmful responses in simulated scenarios and whether the AI supervisor corrected them
effect: In about 500 scenarios, Socrates 2.0 gave harmful responses in under 1% of cases, and the AI supervisor promptly corrected the dialogue each time.
quote: Moreover, tests in approximately 500 scenarios showed that Socrates 2.0 engaged in harmful responses in under 1% of cases, with the AI supervisor promptly correcting the dialogue each time.
sample_unit: participants (planned 100 users and 50 clinicians; 55 recruited so far)

title: Automatic structuring of radiology reports with on-premise open-source large language models
outcome: LLM report structuring accuracy (MCC) in English versus German reports
effect: Average MCC 0.75 (94% HDI 0.70-0.80) for English versus 0.66 (0.62-0.70) for German; LLM-human MCC differences within ROPE for both languages.
quote: However, the understanding of semantics varied across languages and imaging findings.
sample_unit: chest radiograph reports (202 English MIMIC-CXR, 197 German)

title: Large-scale identification of social and behavioral determinants of health from clinical notes: comparison of Latent Semantic Indexing and Generative Pretrained Transformer (GPT) models
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Macro-F1 for SBDH detection of LSI versus GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and ICD-9 on gold standard sets
effect: Macro-F1 for LSI 0.74 was better than ICD-9 (0.71) and GPT-3.5 (0.54) but lower than GPT-4 (0.80); on common subsets, ICD-9 combined with LSI, GPT-3.5 or GPT-4 did not differ significantly.
quote: Using manually curated gold standard (GS) sets for nine SBDH categories, the macro-F1 score of LSI (0.74) was better than ICD-9 (0.71) and GPT-3.5 (0.54), but lower than GPT-4 (0.80).

title: Empowering patients: how accurate and readable are large language models in renal cancer education
outcome: Reading level of LLM and official patient materials relative to recommended sixth-grade level
effect: All examined texts, official PEMs and LLM outputs, remained above the recommended literacy threshold; AUA most readable at 9.84 ± 1.2.
quote: Nevertheless, it is crucial to acknowledge that the readability levels of all examined texts remain elevated above the recommended literacy threshold for the general population.
sample_unit: patient questions on kidney cancer, each answered by 3 chatbots and rated by 4 urologists

title: Empowering patients: how accurate and readable are large language models in renal cancer education
outcome: Readability grade level of LLM-generated kidney cancer patient education responses versus recommended sixth-grade level
effect: Default LLM outputs exceeded sixth-grade level: ChatGPT-4.0 11.03 ± 1.76, Perplexity 12.66 ± 1.83, Gemini 10.83 ± 2.31; AUA PEM 9.84, EAU 11.88.
quote: Our analysis revealed overall higher than recommended readability scores for the responses generated by LLMs (ChatGPT 11.03 ± 1.76, Perplexity 12.66 ± 1.83, and Gemini AI 10.83 ± 2.31).
sample_unit: patient questions on kidney cancer, each answered by 3 chatbots and rated by 4 urologists

title: Empowering patients: how accurate and readable are large language models in renal cancer education
outcome: Accuracy and guideline adherence of LLM kidney cancer answers rated by urologists on 5-point scale
effect: Overall high accuracy (ChatGPT 1.5, Gemini 1.9, Perplexity 2.2) with minor omissions; treatment least accurate (Perplexity 3.1); Gemini gave an answer not adhering to guidelines.
quote: Gemini AI, for example, provided answers that did not fully adhere to official guidelines, such as stating “A biopsy is the only definitive way to diagnose kidney cancer.”
sample_unit: patient questions on kidney cancer, each answered by 3 chatbots and rated by 4 urologists

title: Suitability of ChatGPT as a Source of Patient Information for Screening Mammography
outcome: Understandability and actionability of ChatGPT breast screening information sheets (PEMAT-P, CDC Index)
effect: GPT3.5 PEMAT-P understandability 68.0%, actionability 36.7%, CDC Index 58.8%; GPT4 understandability 75.0%, actionability 53.3%, CDC Index 66.0%. Both poor and unclear.
quote: Both ChatGPT versions exhibited poor understandability and actionability and were unclear in their messaging.

title: Suitability of ChatGPT as a Source of Patient Information for Screening Mammography
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT breast screening content versus BreastScreen NSW gold standard
effect: GPT3.5 lacked accuracy, omitting key insights; GPT4 was superior but still included several key omissions.
quote: GPT4 was deemed superior to GPT3.5 but included several key omissions: PEMAT-P understandability 75.0% (SD = 17) and actionability 53.3% (SD = 11.54); CDC Index 66.0% (SD = 4.1).

title: Investigating the capabilities of advanced large language models in generating patient instructions and patient educational material
venue: European journal of hospital pharmacy : science and practice
outcome: reading level
effect: Simple prompts: ChatGPT 4.0 at 10th-grade; Gemini 1.0 Pro at 7th-grade.
quote: Simple prompts resulted in ChatGPT 4.0 outputs at a 10th-grade reading level, while Gemini 1.0 Pro outputs were at a 7th-grade level.

title: Investigating the capabilities of advanced large language models in generating patient instructions and patient educational material
venue: European journal of hospital pharmacy : science and practice
outcome: Understandability and actionability of LLM patient education material (PEMAT-P)
effect: ChatGPT 4.0 mean understandability 80% and actionability 60%; Gemini 1.0 Pro 67% and 60%. Detailed prompts yielded outputs comprehensible to the average adult.
quote: ChatGPT 4.0 had mean understandability and actionability scores of 80% and 60%, respectively, compared with 67% and 60% for Gemini 1.0 Pro.

title: The future of AI clinicians: assessing the modern standard of chatbots and their approach to diagnostic uncertainty
outcome: Chatbot accuracy on diagnostic uncertainty questions versus Family Medicine residents
effect: Both chatbots scored lower than residents (p < 0.01). Claude-3 57.7% (52/90) and GPT-4o 53.3% (48/90) versus PGY-1 61.1% and PGY-2 63.3%.
quote: Compared to the residents, both chatbots scored lower on diagnostic uncertainty questions (p < 0.01).

title: Large language model uncertainty proxies: discrimination and calibration for medical diagnosis and treatment
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of LLM uncertainty proxies (verbalized confidence, token probability, sample consistency) for diagnosis and treatment
effect: Sample consistency by sentence embedding had the best discrimination (ROC AUC 0.68-0.79) but poor calibration. SC by GPT annotation had ROC AUC 0.66-0.74 with accurate calibration. Verbalized confidence consistently overestimated confidence.
quote: SC by sentence embedding achieved the highest discriminative performance (ROC AUC 0.68-0.79), yet with poor calibration.

title: The Impact of Computer-aided Detection Technology in Adenoma Detection Rate Among Experienced Endoscopists in the Community Setting
venue: Journal of community hospital internal medicine perspectives
outcome: Adenoma detection rate before vs after CAD implementation in community setting
effect: Group ADR increased significantly (p < 0.05) after CAD (1838 colonoscopies in 2021 vs 2629 in 2022), driven by more small (<6 mm) polyps.
quote: Our study demonstrates that the incorporation of CAD technology in a group of experienced endoscopists in a community setting significantly improved ADR.

title: Advancing Patient Education in Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension: The Promise of Large Language Models
outcome: Readability (SMOG, FKGL) of LLM-generated PEMs versus 6th-grade target
effect: Only ChatGPT-4 generated PEMs at the specified 6th-grade reading level (SMOG 5.5 ± 0.6, FKGL 5.6 ± 0.7); ChatGPT-3.5 and Bard did not.
quote: Only ChatGPT-4 was able to generate PEMs at the specified 6th-grade reading level (SMOG: 5.5 ± 0.6, FKGL: 5.6 ± 0.7).
sample_unit: LLM-generated and rewritten patient education materials

title: Advancing Patient Education in Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension: The Promise of Large Language Models
outcome: Readability, quality and accuracy of PEMs rewritten to plain language by LLMs
effect: ChatGPT-4 rewrote published PEMs to below 6th-grade level (SMOG 5.6 ± 0.6, FKGL 5.7 ± 0.8, p<0.001) without decrease in quality (DISCERN ≥4) or accuracy (Likert misinformation = 1).
quote: Original published PEMs were rewritten to below a 6th-grade reading level with Prompt C, without a decrease in quality, understandability, or accuracy only by ChatGPT-4 (SMOG: 5.6 ± 0.6, FKGL: 5.7 ± 0.8, p < 0.001, DISCERN ≥4, Likert misinformation = 1).
sample_unit: LLM-generated and rewritten patient education materials

title: Performance of Machine Learning Suicide Risk Models in an American Indian Population
outcome: Calibration before and after local recalibration with isotonic regression
effect: Spiegelhalter z was -89.9 (VU) and 15.5 (MHRN) before; after isotonic recalibration cross-validated z was 0.18 (P=.86) for VU and 0.19 (P=.85) for MHRN.
quote: After recalibration using isotonic regression, the cross-validated Spiegelhalter z score was 0.18 ( P = .86) for the VU and 0.19 ( P = .85) for the MHRN primary care model.

title: Performance of Machine Learning Suicide Risk Models in an American Indian Population
outcome: Model performance when extended to new population (majority American Indian)
effect: MHRN AUROC 0.81 for 90-day attempts and 0.86 for death, but VU only 0.68 and 0.63; all models poorly calibrated initially.
quote: The MHRN model was significantly more accurate than the VU model.

title: Performance of Machine Learning Suicide Risk Models in an American Indian Population
outcome: ML models compared with existing screening on the same local data (AUROC)
effect: 90-day attempt AUROC: MHRN 0.81, VU 0.68, existing screening 0.66; screening identified no suicide deaths (sensitivity 0.0%) while MHRN AUROC for death was 0.86.
quote: Our results show that the machine learning models used in this study had substantially higher AUROC values than existing approaches, even when compared with a substantial uptick in ASQ administration (eTable 5 in Supplement 1 ).

title: Performance of Machine Learning Suicide Risk Models in an American Indian Population
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of existing suicide risk models on local IHS historical data versus reference outcomes
effect: MHRN AUROC 0.81 (95% CI 0.77-0.85) vs VU 0.68 (0.64-0.72) for 90-day attempts; Spiegelhalter z -89.9 (VU) and 15.5 (MHRN), both P<.001, before recalibration.
quote: Although the generalization of the MHRN models is notable, all models were poorly calibrated initially, demonstrating the importance of recalibration when applying models to new populations.

title: Performance of Machine Learning Suicide Risk Models in an American Indian Population
outcome: Calibration of models applied to new population
effect: Spiegelhalter z scores -89.9 (VU) and 15.5 (MHRN), P<.001, indicating poor calibration despite reasonable AUROC.
quote: For the outcome of 90-day suicide attempts, the Spiegelhalter z score was −89.9 ( P < .001) for the VU model and 15.5 ( P < .001) for the MHRN primary care model.

title: Performance of Machine Learning Suicide Risk Models in an American Indian Population
outcome: AIAN representation in validation cohorts
effect: Analytic sample was 94.0% AIAN; VU validation reported no AIAN; MHRN validation had 37 717 of 3 387 741 visits (1.1%) AIAN.
quote: In comparison, the validation sample for the VU model did not report any American Indian or Alaska Native patients (2080 of 77 973 patients [2.7%] are reported as other race) and reported 85 of 77 973 patients (0.1%) with an attempt included in the analysis.

title: External Validation of a Commercial Artificial Intelligence Algorithm on a Diverse Population for Detection of False Negative Breast Cancers
outcome: AI detection of false negative cancers on local retrospective screening mammograms against 1-year follow-up ground truth
effect: AI detected 7/13 (54%) false negative cancers in the FFDM cohort and 4/10 (40%) in the DBT cohort missed by the radiologist; median detection 272 and 248 days sooner.
quote: Artificial intelligence was able to detect 7/13 false negative cancers (54%) in the FFDM cohort and 4/10 (40%) in the DBT cohort on the preceding screening mammogram that was interpreted as negative by the radiologist.
sample_unit: screening mammography examinations (26,694 FFDM and 3,183 DBT)

title: Early Warning Scores With and Without Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Discrimination of AI early warning scores versus simpler non-AI scores for clinical deterioration on the same data
effect: eCART AUROC 0.895 (95% CI 0.891-0.900) vs NEWS2 0.831, NEWS 0.829, RI 0.828, EDI 0.808, MEWS 0.757; NEWS, a non-AI score, significantly outperformed EDI.
quote: In this cohort study of inpatient encounters, eCART outperformed the other AI and non-AI scores, identifying more deteriorating patients with fewer false alarms and sufficient time to intervene.

title: Early Warning Scores With and Without Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Positive predictive values at thresholds matched to NEWS sensitivity or specificity levels, indicating false alarm burden
effect: At the moderate-risk level PPV ranged from 6.3% (EDI 41) to 17.3% (eCART 94); at the high-risk level from 14.5% (EDI 54) to 23.3% (eCART 97).
quote: After matching scores at the moderate-risk sensitivity level for a NEWS score of 5, overall positive predictive values (PPVs) ranged from a low of 6.3% (95% CI, 6.1%-6.4%) for an EDI score of 41 to a high of 17.3% (95% CI, 16.9%-17.8%) for an eCART score of 94.

title: Real-World evaluation of an AI triaging system for chest X-rays: A prospective clinical study
outcome: AI triage performance across age, gender, and ethnic subgroups
effect: Consistently high accuracy across age groups (Young, Adult, Senior), genders, and ethnicities (Chinese, Malay, Indian, Others), with sensitivity, specificity, and AUC consistently above 84%.
quote: Subgroup analysis revealed consistently high accuracy across various age groups (Young, Adult, Senior), genders, and ethnicities (Chinese, Malay, Indian, Others), with sensitivity, specificity, and AUC consistently above 84%.

title: Discrepancies in ChatGPT's Hip Fracture Recommendations in Older Adults for 2021 AAOS Evidence-Based Guidelines
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT recommendation strength across repeated runs
effect: Fleiss kappa was 0.409, indicating a moderate level of agreement across repeated runs A, B, and C.
quote: For the reliability of the strengths of the recommendation, the Fleiss kappa was 0.409, indicating a moderate level of agreement.

title: Discrepancies in ChatGPT's Hip Fracture Recommendations in Older Adults for 2021 AAOS Evidence-Based Guidelines
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT recommendation strengths versus 2021 AAOS guidelines
effect: Accuracy 0.684, 0.579, 0.632 for outputs A, B, C; precision 0.740, 0.737, 0.718.
quote: Regarding the strengths of the recommendation compared with the 2021 AAOS guidelines, we observed accuracy of 0.684, 0.579, and 0.632 for outputs A, B, and C, respectively.

title: Randomized Controlled Trial to Assess the Feasibility of a Novel Clinical Decision Support System Based on the Automatic Generation of Alerts through Remote Patient Monitoring
outcome: Alert burden on healthcare professionals from high-volume remote monitoring alerts
effect: Case group generated far more alerts (61,827 vs. 1825; p < 0.05) but without overloading healthcare professionals thanks to automatic AI alert management.
quote: The case group received a more exhaustive follow-up, with a higher number of alerts (61,827 vs. 1825; p < 0.05) but without overloading healthcare professionals thanks to automatic alert management through artificial intelligence.

title: Evaluation of the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Clinical Practice of Radiology in Saudi Arabia
outcome: Radiology professionals' self-reported AI knowledge, training adequacy, and barriers to AI implementation
effect: 58.6% reported limited AI knowledge and inadequate training; 43.6% identified skill development and the complexity of AI educational programs as major barriers to implementation.
quote: However, 58.6% reported limited AI knowledge and inadequate training, with 43.6% identifying skill development and the complexity of AI educational programs as major barriers to implementation.

title: Designing and testing clinical simulations of an early warning system for implementation in acute care settings
outcome: Whether pre-go-live simulation with nurses identified CDS improvements and training needs
effect: 6 simulation sessions with 17 nurses yielded four debriefing themes that informed CDS improvements, real-world enhancements, and training requirements before go-live.
quote: Standardized simulation testing procedures identified and informed the necessary CDS improvements, the enhancements needed for real-world use, and the training requirements to effectively prepare end-users for system go-live.

title: Designing and testing clinical simulations of an early warning system for implementation in acute care settings
outcome: Whether end-user simulation testing revealed usability and workflow-fit issues to act on before implementation
effect: Simulation debriefs with 17 nurses produced four themes used to inform implementation strategies and how the CDS should be improved for practical real-world use.
quote: Four themes were extracted from the simulation debriefing sessions and used to inform implementation strategies.

title: Fairness in AI-Driven Oncology: Investigating Racial and Gender Biases in Large Language Models
outcome: Occupation predictions (oncologist vs nurse) when varying race and gender in prompts
effect: Chatbots about two times more likely to predict Blacks and Native Americans as oncology nurses than oncologists compared to Asians (p<0.01, p<0.001); females more likely than males to be predicted as nurses (p<0.001).
quote: LLM chatbots are about two times more likely to predict Blacks and Native Americans as oncology nurses than oncologists, compared to Asians (p < 0.01 and < 0.001, respectively).

title: Fairness in AI-Driven Oncology: Investigating Racial and Gender Biases in Large Language Models
outcome: Stereotyping and demographic representativeness in AI-generated oncology cases and job descriptions
effect: Generated cancer cases unrepresentative of real-world demographics and encoded substance-use stereotypes, e.g., Hispanics had ~20% greater proportion of smokers than Whites in ChatGPT breast cancer cases.
quote: AI-generated cancer cases are not fully representative of real-world demographic distributions and encode stereotypes on substance abuse, such as Hispanics having a greater proportion of smokers than Whites by about 20% in Chat GPT breast cancer cases.

title: GPT-4-based AI agents-the new expert system for detection of antimicrobial resistance mechanisms?
outcome: Concordance and specificity of GPT-agent versus microbiologists against routine diagnostics

title: GPT-4-based AI agents-the new expert system for detection of antimicrobial resistance mechanisms?
outcome: Non-customized GPT-4 ability to interpret resistance categories and agreement with routine diagnostics
effect: Non-customized GPT-4 could interpret 169/862 (19.6%) categories; 137/169 (81.1%) agreed with routine diagnostics.
quote: Non-customized GPT-4 could interpret 169/862 (19.6%) categories, and 137/169 (81.1%) agreed with routine diagnostics.

title: Can ChatGPT reliably answer the most common patient questions regarding total shoulder arthroplasty?
venue: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery

effect: Overall grade B-; the chatbot neglected recent research, resulting in recommendations that warrant professional clarification; errors when supplementing its own responses.
quote: However, the chatbot neglected recent research in its responses, resulting in recommendations that warrant professional clarification.

title: Can ChatGPT reliably answer the most common patient questions regarding total shoulder arthroplasty?
venue: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery

effect: Deferred to orthopedic surgeons in 8 of 15 questions; also often went beyond the scope of the question after the first 2 sentences.
quote: The interface deferred specific questions to orthopedic surgeons in 8 of 15 questions, suggesting its awareness of its own limitations.

title: Artificial intelligence chatbots as sources of patient education material for cataract surgery: ChatGPT-4 versus Google Bard
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid level) and PEMAT-P understandability of chatbot cataract surgery patient education responses
effect: Mean Flesch-Kincaid level was 8.02 for Google Bard versus 5.75 for ChatGPT-4 (p<0.001). PEMAT-P understandability was 85.8% for ChatGPT-4 versus 80.9% for Bard (p<0.001). Actionability was about 42.5% vs 44.2% (p=0.344).

title: Performance of ChatGPT in providing patient information about upper tract urothelial carcinoma

outcome: Relationship between tool's self-reported confidence and diagnostic accuracy

title: Grading of diabetic retinopathy using a pre-segmenting deep learning classification model: Validation of an automated algorithm

quote: Two of three stand-alone DL algorithms achieved noninferior sensitivity (DL-1: 64.8%, P < .001; DL-2: 56.7%, P = .03; DL-3: 58.9%, P < .001) compared with the single first reader (62.8%), and specificity was noninferior for DL-1 (92.8%; P < .001) and DL-2 (96.8%; P < .001) and superior for DL-3 (97.9%; P < .001) compared with the single first reader (96.5%).

title: Deep Learning Algorithms for Breast Cancer Detection in a UK Screening Cohort: As Stand-alone Readers and Combined with Human Readers
outcome: DL algorithms combined with human readers compared with double reading
effect: Combining DL with human readers achieved noninferior sensitivity (67.0%, 65.6%, 65.4% vs 67.4%; P<.001 for all) and superior specificity (97.4%, 97.6%, 97.6% vs 97.1%; P<.001 for all) compared with double reading.
quote: Combining the DL algorithms with human readers achieved noninferior sensitivity (67.0%, 65.6%, and 65.4% for DL-1, DL-2, and DL-3, respectively; P < .001 for all) compared with double reading (67.4%), and superior specificity (97.4%, 97.6%, and 97.6%; P < .001 for all) compared with double reading (97.1%).

title: Using Large Language Models to Abstract Complex Social Determinants of Health From Original and Deidentified Medical Notes: Development and Validation Study
outcome: Whether requiring verbatim evidence and justification reduces hallucination and omitted context
effect: GPT-4 evidence similar or identical to manual abstractors in most cases; no hallucinations observed in GPT-4 output.
quote: Our work also suggests that requiring the LLM to provide verbatim evidence and justification from the original text can help reduce the risk that relevant context about housing information is omitted from LLM results.
sample_unit: manually abstracted clinical notes (from 355 pregnant patients)

title: Using Large Language Models to Abstract Complex Social Determinants of Health From Original and Deidentified Medical Notes: Development and Validation Study
outcome: LLM recall and precision versus adjudicated manual labels for housing instability
effect: GPT-4 recall 0.924 vs manual 0.702, precision 0.850 vs manual 0.971; GPT-3.5 recall 0.717, precision 0.759.
quote: For current and past housing instability, the recall of GPT-4 was higher (0.924) than that of GPT-3.5 (0.717), RegEx (0.649), and manual abstraction (0.702).
sample_unit: manually abstracted clinical notes (from 355 pregnant patients)

title: Using Large Language Models to Abstract Complex Social Determinants of Health From Original and Deidentified Medical Notes: Development and Validation Study
outcome: Comparison of GPT-4, GPT-3.5, NER model, RegEx and manual abstraction on same notes
effect: GPT-4 had highest performance among automated methods with higher recall than humans (0.924 vs 0.702) but lower precision (0.850 vs 0.971).
quote: GPT-4 outperformed GPT-3.5, JSL, and RegEx in identifying patients experiencing current or past housing instability.
sample_unit: manually abstracted clinical notes (from 355 pregnant patients)

title: Using Large Language Models to Abstract Complex Social Determinants of Health From Original and Deidentified Medical Notes: Development and Validation Study
outcome: Reproducibility of GPT output across runs
effect: GPT-4 results differ slightly each run, explaining small performance differences; nondeterminism was not tested formally.
quote: These minor increases in precision are likely because results from GPT-4 are slightly different each time the model is run, resulting in slight differences in performance.
sample_unit: manually abstracted clinical notes (from 355 pregnant patients)

title: Using Large Language Models to Abstract Complex Social Determinants of Health From Original and Deidentified Medical Notes: Development and Validation Study
outcome: Subgroup FPR/FNR differences
effect: Differences observed, but 95% CIs overlapped for all groups except n<5 cases.
quote: However, when we examined the overlap of the 95% CIs between groups, we found that in all cases, except in cases where the sample sizes were extremely small (n<5), there was overlap between CIs for all the groups, suggesting that the differences between groups are not significant.
sample_unit: manually abstracted clinical notes (from 355 pregnant patients)

title: Using Large Language Models to Abstract Complex Social Determinants of Health From Original and Deidentified Medical Notes: Development and Validation Study
outcome: FPR and FNR differences across age, race, ethnicity subgroups for GPT-4 and GPT-3.5
effect: Differences in FPR/FNR observed between all groups, but 95% CIs overlapped except where n<5, suggesting differences not significant; larger sample needed.
quote: We did observe differences in FPR and FNR between all of the groups within the 3 demographic categories.
sample_unit: manually abstracted clinical notes (from 355 pregnant patients)

title: Using Large Language Models to Abstract Complex Social Determinants of Health From Original and Deidentified Medical Notes: Development and Validation Study
outcome: Reference-label ambiguity
effect: 25% (103/415) dual abstraction; Cohen k coefficient 0.589, moderate agreement.
quote: Before adjudication, dually abstracted notes had a Cohen k coefficient of 0.589, which reflects moderate agreement [ 40 ] and highlights the ambiguity and subjectivity of abstracting complex concepts such as housing instability compared with other SDOH mentions such as employment or parental status, despite the abstractors having been trained on the same guidelines (see Supplementary Methods in Multimedia Appendix 1 ).
sample_unit: manually abstracted clinical notes (from 355 pregnant patients)

title: Using Large Language Models to Abstract Complex Social Determinants of Health From Original and Deidentified Medical Notes: Development and Validation Study
outcome: Prompt-text evidence misuse
effect: GPT-3.5 used prompt sentences as evidence and flagged current or past instability in several cases.
quote: In several cases, GPT-3.5 used sentences from the prompt text as evidence and justification and flagged the note as current or past instability.
sample_unit: manually abstracted clinical notes (from 355 pregnant patients)

title: Enhancing the interoperability and transparency of real-world data extraction in clinical research: evaluating the feasibility and impact of a ChatGLM implementation in Chinese hospital settings
outcome: Free-text extraction accuracy of LLMs versus manual reference
effect: Manual input accuracy for free-text forms was 99.59%, ChatGLM extraction accuracy 77.13%, and LLaMA extraction accuracy 43.86%.
quote: The initial manual input accuracy for free-text forms was 99.59%, the ChatGLM data extraction accuracy was 77.13%, and the LLaMA data extraction accuracy was 43.86%.

title: Cardiac anatomic digital twins: findings from a single national centre
outcome: Need for manual correction of AI-generated anatomic twin segmentations
effect: Manual corrections of the AI-generated digital anatomic twins were always necessary; the AI only facilitated rapid creation.
quote: While artificial intelligence facilitated the rapid creation of digital anatomic twins, manual corrections were always necessary.

title: A Pilot Study of Medical Student Opinions on Large Language Models
outcome: Association of prior AI understanding/exposure with cross-checking LLM output and LLM use
effect: Those with some baseline AI understanding or exposure were 5.06 (p=0.021) and 3.38 (p=0.039) times more likely to cross-check LLM information than those with little to none (observational association).
quote: Previous AI knowledge and exposure correlated with more conscientious use of these tools such as cross-checking information.

title: Assessing the accuracy and consistency of answers by ChatGPT to questions regarding carbon monoxide poisoning
outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT answers across ten repeated entries of the same question
effect: About 50% of cases showed high consistency; about one-third of cases showed unacceptable blurring of the answers.
quote: In approximately 50% of the cases, the responses generated by ChatGPT exhibited a high degree of consistency, whereas in approximately one-third of the cases, the responses exhibited unacceptable blurring of the answers.

title: Assessing the accuracy and consistency of answers by ChatGPT to questions regarding carbon monoxide poisoning
outcome: ChatGPT accuracy on single-choice carbon monoxide poisoning exam questions in Chinese and English
effect: Accuracy was 61.1% in Chinese and 57% in English against the question bank reference answers.
quote: Meanwhile, the accuracy of these responses was less favorable, with an accuracy rate of 61.1% in Chinese and 57% in English.
sample_unit: single-choice questions (each entered 10 times in Chinese and English)

title: Evaluation Framework of Large Language Models in Medical Documentation: Development and Usability Study
outcome: Error types and counts in LLM-generated ED records, and correlation with clinical scores
effect: Invalid generation errors most common (35.38% of errors); structural malformation had largest negative impact on clinical score (r=-0.654); error count correlated with lower scores (r=-0.633).
quote: Quantitative analysis revealed that invalid generation errors were the most common, constituting 35.38% of total errors, while structural malformation errors had the most significant negative impact on the clinical evaluation score (Pearson r=-0.654; P<.001).

title: Impact of Deep Learning-Based Computer-Aided Detection and Electronic Notification System for Pneumothorax on Time to Treatment: Clinical Implementation
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Time to supplemental oxygen, aspiration or tube thoracostomy, and surgical consultation
effect: CAD plus ENS versus CAD-only: oxygen -143.8 min (95% CI, -277.8 to -9.9; P = .035); aspiration/tube thoracostomy 14.4 min (95% CI, -35.0 to 63.9); surgical consultation 86.3 min (95% CI, -175.1 to 347.6).
quote: There was a significant reduction in TTT for supplemental oxygen therapy for the CAD and ENS group compared with the CAD-only group in the postimplementation period (-143.8 min; 95% confidence interval [CI], -277.8 to -9.9; P = .035).

title: Impact of Deep Learning-Based Computer-Aided Detection and Electronic Notification System for Pneumothorax on Time to Treatment: Clinical Implementation
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Time to treatment for pneumothorax, CAD plus electronic notification vs CAD-only
effect: TTT for oxygen reduced -143.8 min (95% CI -277.8 to -9.9; P=.035); no significant difference for aspiration/tube thoracostomy (14.4 min) or thoracic surgery consultation (86.3 min).
quote: There was a significant reduction in TTT for supplemental oxygen therapy for the CAD and ENS group compared with the CAD-only group in the postimplementation period (-143.8 min; 95% confidence interval [CI], -277.8 to -9.9; P = .035).

title: The quality and safety of using generative AI to produce patient-centred discharge instructions
outcome: Potentially harmful safety issues, hallucinations and new medications in AI-generated discharge instructions
effect: Potentially harmful safety issues attributable to the AI tool in 18% of 100 summaries, including 6% with hallucinations and 3% with new medications.
quote: When tested on 100 discharge summaries from MIMIC-IV, potentially harmful safety issues attributable to the AI tool were found in 18%, including 6% with hallucinations and 3% with new medications.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Prompted Explanations of Common Primary Care Diagnoses
outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) and PEMAT understandability of chatbot patient education text
effect: Claude 2 FRE 67.0, FKGL 7.4, understandability 69%; ChatGPT FRE 58.5, FKGL 9.3, 69%; Bard FRE 50.1, FKGL 9.9, 52%; HuggingChat FRE 48.7, FKGL 11.6, 57%.
quote: Claude 2 and ChatGPT demonstrated superior readability and understandability, but practical application and patient outcomes need further exploration.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Prompted Explanations of Common Primary Care Diagnoses
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of AI-generated patient education text
effect: FKGL 7.4 (Claude 2), 9.3 (ChatGPT), 9.9 (Bard), 11.6 (HuggingChat); most above a typical 6th-8th grade target.
quote: HuggingChat scores were FRE (48.7) and FKGL (11.6), PEMAT (57% and 29%).
sample_unit: AI-generated patient education paragraphs (7 diagnoses x 4 chatbots)

title: FAIM: Fairness-aware interpretable modeling for trustworthy machine learning in healthcare
outcome: Fairness metrics and discriminatory performance of FAIM versus common bias mitigation methods for hospital admission prediction
effect: FAIM models showed satisfactory discriminatory performance and significantly mitigated bias on fairness metrics, outperforming commonly used bias mitigation methods in both datasets. No numeric values in the abstract.
quote: For both datasets, FAIM models not only exhibit satisfactory discriminatory performance but also significantly mitigate biases as measured by well-established fairness metrics, outperforming commonly used bias mitigation methods.

title: Efficacy of Early Warning Scores as the Prediction Tool for Detecting Patients With Acute Deterioration in a High Dependent Unit
outcome: Suitability of vendor-default VSI threshold for local HDU population
effect: The optimal VSI threshold by ROC analysis was 1.5, versus the default high-risk threshold of 3.0, which flagged only 20.7% of vital sign sets among those with outcomes.
quote: Using a high-risk threshold of VSI≧3.0, the proportion of patients identified as high risk was 20.7%, even among those with outcomes.

title: Efficacy of Early Warning Scores as the Prediction Tool for Detecting Patients With Acute Deterioration in a High Dependent Unit
outcome: Whether default risk cutoffs identify high-risk patients
effect: Lowering VSI threshold to ≥1.5 raised identification of patients with outcomes from 36% to 84% about two hours before the first outcome; NEWS optimal threshold 6.0-8.0.
quote: From time trend analysis, lowering the threshold to VSI≧1.5 for high-risk led to a significant increase in the identification of patients with outcomes from 36% to 84% at about two hours before the first outcome (Figure 4 ).

title: Efficacy of Early Warning Scores as the Prediction Tool for Detecting Patients With Acute Deterioration in a High Dependent Unit
outcome: Composite outcome prediction
quote: The AUC for NEWS was significantly superior to that of VSI for the composite outcome (p=0.014).

title: Efficacy of Early Warning Scores as the Prediction Tool for Detecting Patients With Acute Deterioration in a High Dependent Unit
outcome: predictive accuracy of AI versus simpler score for composite outcome
effect: NEWS was superior to VSI for composite outcome (AUC 0.701 vs 0.647, p=0.014) and unexpected ICU transfer (AUC 0.834 vs 0.767)
quote: The AUC for NEWS was significantly superior to that of VSI for the composite outcome (p=0.014).

title: Exploring the opportunities of large language models for summarizing palliative care consultations: A pilot comparative study
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of LLM-generated palliative care consultation summaries
effect: Grade levels ranged from 10.7 (LLaMA 70B) to 15.2 (GPT-3.5) versus a reference of 10.6; LLaMA 7B 11.9, LLaMA 13B 12.6, GPT-4 13.1.
quote: GPT-3.5's summaries were the most complex at a grade level of 15.2, while GPT-4's summaries had a grade level of 13.1, making them moderately accessible.

title: Can ChatGPT help patients understand radiopharmaceutical extravasations?
outcome: Validity of references cited by ChatGPT in answers about radiopharmaceutical extravasation
effect: One physician's reference check found no hallucinations. Fully validated references were used for 11 of 15 questions and general medical and ethical guidelines for 4 questions.
quote: The reference check revealed no AI hallucinations.

title: Can ChatGPT help patients understand radiopharmaceutical extravasations?
outcome: Inconsistency of ChatGPT responses across three repeated queries per question
effect: Irrelevant or minor inconsistencies in 87% of questions; some differences relevant to main content in the other 13%.
quote: The evaluators also rated the inconsistency across the three ChatGPT responses for each question and found irrelevant or minor inconsistencies in 87% of questions and some differences relevant to main content in the other 13% of the questions.

title: A data-driven framework for identifying patient subgroups on which an AI/machine learning model may underperform
outcome: Hidden subgroup performance disparities masked by average model performance
effect: Average performance may be high while some subgroups have significantly lower performance; AFISP applied to a deterioration model to detect significant subgroup disparities (no numeric results in abstract).
quote: While a model's average performance on a dataset may be high, the model can have significantly lower performance for certain subgroups, which may be hard to detect.

title: Comparing the Accuracy and Readability of Glaucoma-related Question Responses and Educational Materials by Google and ChatGPT
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT responses to glaucoma FAQs versus Google
effect: ChatGPT responses averaged grade 14.3 vs Google 9.4 (p<0.001); FRE 35.2 vs 53.0; procedure explanations grade 16.6 when unspecified.
quote: ChatGPT responses to patient FAQs were written at a significantly higher average grade level than Google responses (14.3 vs 9.4, respectively, p < 0.001) ( Table 2 ).

title: Comparing the Accuracy and Readability of Glaucoma-related Question Responses and Educational Materials by Google and ChatGPT
outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT procedure explanations when a seventh-grade level was requested
effect: Average grade level fell from 16.6 to 9.4 and FRE rose from 33.1 to 67.4 (p<0.001); expert-rated inaccuracy 19.0% vs 28.6% (p=0.47).
quote: When instructed to generate education materials at a seventh grade reading level, readability significantly improved to an average grade level of 9.4 and an FRE of 67.4 (“standard”) ( p < 0.001).

title: Comparing the Accuracy and Readability of Glaucoma-related Question Responses and Educational Materials by Google and ChatGPT
outcome: distinguishing AI-generated content
effect: Experts correctly identified AI-generated FAQ responses 39.5% (34/86).
quote: Among the responses that experts attempted to identify, 39.5% (34/86) were correctly identified as the AI-generated response ( Table 5 ).

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted delineation for postoperative radiotherapy in patients with lung cancer: a prospective, multi-center, cohort study
outcome: Contouring accuracy and time for residents with AI assistance versus fully manual delineation
effect: AI-assisted CTV median DSC 0.745 vs 0.703, HD 20.03 vs 21.55 mm, MDA 2.57 vs 3.06 mm (all P<0.05); CTV time cut ~43.2%, OAR time ~56.2%.
quote: AI-assisted CTV and OARs delineation for PORT significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency in the real-world setting, compared with pure AI auto-segmentation or fully manual delineation by junior oncologists.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted delineation for postoperative radiotherapy in patients with lung cancer: a prospective, multi-center, cohort study
outcome: Performance of clinicians using AI in workflow versus standalone AI and manual delineation
effect: AI-assisted CTV had lower HD and MDA and higher DSC than comparators (DSC 0.745 vs 0.703, P<0.05); time shortened 43.2% for CTV and 56.2% for OARs.
quote: Our findings demonstrated that the implementation of AI-assisted technology could lead to significantly improved contouring accuracy, greater interobserver consistency, as well as considerable time savings.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted delineation for postoperative radiotherapy in patients with lung cancer: a prospective, multi-center, cohort study
outcome: Clinician-edited AI contour accuracy
quote: AI-assisted delineation achieved significantly higher accuracy compared to unmodified AI auto-contouring and fully manual delineation by radiation oncologists, with median HD, MDA, and DCS values of 20.03 vs. 21.55 mm, 2.57 vs. 3.06 mm, 0.745 vs. 0.703 (all P<0.05) for CTV, respectively.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted delineation for postoperative radiotherapy in patients with lung cancer: a prospective, multi-center, cohort study
outcome: OAR contouring accuracy versus clinicians
effect: AI-assisted OAR DSC was >0.8; left/right lungs, heart, and liver DSC >0.9; all P<0.05 versus manual contours.
quote: Additionally, the accuracy of the AI-assisted delineation significantly outperformed fully manual contours by junior radiation oncologists, with DSC greater than 0.8, among which the left and right lungs, heart and liver performed better, with DSC greater than 0.9 (all P< 0.05).

title: Evaluating a predictive model of avoidable hospital events for race- and sex-based bias
outcome: Calibration-type bias: true avoidable hospital event risk by race/sex at equal risk scores
effect: No race difference (ME = 0.0003, 95%CI -0.0003 to 0.0009); males slightly lower (ME = -0.0008, 95% CI -0.0013 to -0.0003); no sex difference in intervention target group (ME = 0.0002, 95% CI -0.0031 to 0.0036).
quote: We implemented a simple bias assessment methodology and found no evidence of meaningful race- or sex-based bias in this model.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Radiologist Burnout
outcome: Association between radiologist AI use and burnout (emotional exhaustion or depersonalization)
effect: AI use associated with increased odds of burnout (OR 1.20; 95% CI 1.10-1.30), driven by emotional exhaustion (OR 1.21). Weighted burnout prevalence 40.9% vs 38.6%. Stronger with high workload and lower AI acceptance.
quote: After adjusting for covariates, AI use was significantly associated with increased odds of burnout (odds ratio [OR], 1.20; 95% CI, 1.10-1.30), primarily driven by its association with EE (OR, 1.21; 95% CI, 1.10-1.34).

title: The Future of Surgical Diagnostics: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Detection of Ganglion Cells for Hirschsprung Disease
venue: Laboratory investigation; a journal of technical methods and pathology
outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy and time with versus without AI heatmap support
effect: Accuracy rose from 77% to 85.8% with model heatmap support; diagnosis time fell from 139.7 to 70.5 seconds. Overreliance was not assessed.
quote: In the reader study, on average, the pathologists' diagnostic accuracy increased from 77% to 85.8% with the model's heatmap support, whereas the diagnosis time decreased from an average of 139.7 to 70.5 seconds.
sample_unit: patients (668 slides; 10 pathologists read 50 frozen WSIs in reader study)

title: Assessing the Performance of ChatGPT in Answering Patients' Questions Regarding Congenital Bicuspid Aortic Valve
outcome: Verifiability of sources and citations in ChatGPT answers about bicuspid aortic valve

outcome: Calibration change after intercept and logistic recalibration on local data

quote: Logistic recalibration improved the calibration of all models ( Figures 2C – 5C ).

title: Clinical prediction models for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: an external validation based on a systematic review and the Dutch Arthroplasty Register
outcome: Availability of model predictors and outcomes in local registry
effect: 90% (40/44) of models used outcomes or predictors missing in the LROI; only 4 of 44 models (9%) could be externally validated.
quote: Thus, 4 out of 44 models (9%) on a TJA population could be externally validated using LROI data.

title: Clinical prediction models for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: an external validation based on a systematic review and the Dutch Arthroplasty Register
outcome: Calibration reporting in development papers of published models
effect: Development papers did not present calibration plots, so calibration could not be compared; discrimination was similar between cohorts but calibration poor in validation.
quote: Calibration plots were not presented in the development papers, and therefore could not be compared.

title: Clinical prediction models for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: an external validation based on a systematic review and the Dutch Arthroplasty Register
outcome: Reporting gaps in original model development papers
effect: Outcome definition for models 1-3 not described; baseline characteristics and AUC of model 4 development cohort not reported; unclear which previous surgeries were included.
quote: In the paper of models 1 to 3, the exact definition of the outcome was not described, and therefore the authors may have used another definition.

title: Clinical prediction models for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: an external validation based on a systematic review and the Dutch Arthroplasty Register
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of published models on local registry data
effect: AUCs 0.64, 0.67, 0.79, 0.53; all models had far from optimal calibration; model 3 largely underestimated mortality risk while the others overestimated revision risk.
quote: All models had far from optimal calibrated risk predictions ( Figures 2A – 5A ).

title: Clinical prediction models for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: an external validation based on a systematic review and the Dutch Arthroplasty Register
outcome: Differences between development and validation populations and variable definitions
effect: ASA and head diameter distributed differently between development and LROI cohorts; approach and previous surgery definitions differed; ASA differences may have prevented perfect calibration even after recalibration.
quote: The difference in ASA distribution may have prevented perfect calibration of LROI data, even after applying recalibration.

title: Clinical prediction models for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: an external validation based on a systematic review and the Dutch Arthroplasty Register
outcome: Model performance on external, later, population-based registry data versus development performance
effect: External validation showed suboptimal predictive performance in the Dutch population; discrimination was similar to development but calibration was insufficient.

title: Clinical prediction models for patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty: an external validation based on a systematic review and the Dutch Arthroplasty Register
outcome: external validation performance
effect: 4 models externally validated; AUCs 0.64, 0.67, 0.79, and 0.53; calibration was insufficient.

title: ChatGPT as a Source for Patient Information on Patellofemoral Surgery-A Comparative Study Amongst Laymen, Doctors, and Experts
outcome: Rating of ChatGPT patient-information answers by experts versus non-experts

title: Application of NotebookLM, a large language model with retrieval-augmented generation, for lung cancer staging
outcome: Lung cancer staging accuracy with RAG grounding versus GPT-4o with and without reference knowledge

title: External validation and performance analysis of a deep learning-based model for the detection of intracranial hemorrhage

title: Facilitating Trust Calibration in Artificial Intelligence-Driven Diagnostic Decision Support Systems for Determining Physicians' Diagnostic Accuracy: Quasi-Experimental Study
outcome: Physician diagnostic accuracy with vs without prompt to judge whether AI list contains correct diagnosis

title: Facilitating Trust Calibration in Artificial Intelligence-Driven Diagnostic Decision Support Systems for Determining Physicians' Diagnostic Accuracy: Quasi-Experimental Study
outcome: Whether physicians detect incorrect AI outputs (trust calibration correctness) and overconfidence in AI

title: Randomized Pilot of a Clinical Decision Support Tool to Increase Suicide Screening for at-Risk Primary Care Patients With Opioid Use Disorder
outcome: CSSRS suicide risk assessment completion within 14 days after visit
