title: Randomized Pilot of a Clinical Decision Support Tool to Increase Suicide Screening for at-Risk Primary Care Patients With Opioid Use Disorder
outcome: Completion of structured suicide risk assessment within 14 days of an eligible visit
effect: Adding suicide-risk alerts recommending CSSRS completion yielded completion rates of 20.3% versus 17.4% without suicide-risk alerts; OR=1.22, 95% CI=0.41, 3.65.
quote: Regarding the primary outcome, only 17.4% of control and 20.3% of intervention patients had a CSSRS completed at a visit in the 14 days after an eligible outpatient visit, with no significant difference between groups ( Table 2 ; OR=1.22, 95% CI=0.41, 3.65).

title: Extracting International Classification of Diseases Codes from Clinical Documentation Using Large Language Models
outcome: LLM ICD-10-CM code extraction agreement against human coder reference standard
effect: GPT-4 highest percent agreement 15.2%, Claude 3 12.7%, GPT-3.5 12.4%; Cohen's kappa -0.02 to 0.01 (minimal to no agreement).
quote: Current LLMs have poor performance in extraction of ICD-10-CM codes from inpatient notes when compared against the human coder.

title: Assessment of Large Language Models (LLMs) in decision-making support for gynecologic oncology
outcome: Consistency of LLM answers over days of testing
effect: Gemini Advanced gave correct answers more frequently (>60% every day during the testing period); accuracy differed by model: GemAdv 81.87%, Copilot 70.67%, CG-4 61.60%.
quote: GemAdv consistently provided correct answers more frequently (>60 % every day during the testing period).

title: Evaluation of the reliability and readability of answers given by chatbots to frequently asked questions about endophthalmitis: A cross-sectional study on chatbots
outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of chatbot answers to patient questions about endophthalmitis
effect: A-Eye Consult and ChatGPT-4.0 responses were more complex than those of the other LLMs, while being more reliable and accurate. No FRE or FKGL values are reported in the abstract.
quote: A-Eye Consult and ChatGPT-4.0 responses, while more complex than those of other LLMs, provided more reliable and accurate information.

title: Artificial intelligence versus clinical judgement: how accurately do generative models reflect CNS guidelines for chiari malformation?
outcome: Readability of AI responses (Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG, Flesch Reading Ease)
effect: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level ranged 14.48 (Gemini) to 16.48 (Copilot); Gunning Fog 16.18 to 18.8; SMOG 16 to 17.54; Flesch Reading Ease low across all models (highest 21.3, Gemini).
quote: All responses showcased high complexity and difficult readability.

title: Artificial intelligence versus clinical judgement: how accurately do generative models reflect CNS guidelines for chiari malformation?
outcome: Concordance of AI answers with CNS Chiari guideline recommendations
effect: Concordance ranged from 23.1% (ChatGPT 4o) to 69.2% (Perplexity); Copilot 61.5%, Gemini 30.8%; non-concordant answers were mostly over-conclusive.
quote: Perplexity displayed the highest concordance rate of 69.2 %, with non-concordant responses classified as 0 % insufficient and 30.8 % over-conclusive.

title: Risk stratification of potential drug interactions involving common over-the-counter medications and herbal supplements by a large language model
venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
outcome: Accuracy and agreement of LLM drug interaction risk ratings versus Lexicomp reference
effect: All models underperformed, with accuracies below 50% and poor Cohen's kappa agreement with Lexicomp; GPT-4 and GPT-4o modestly better than GPT-3.5 at identifying higher-risk interactions.
quote: Our findings reveal that all models generally underperform, with accuracies below 50% and poor agreement with Lexicomp standards as measured by Cohen's kappa.
sample_unit: drug interaction pairs (43 Rx-OTC, 30 Rx-herbal supplement)

title: Large-scale observational study of AI-based patient and surgical material verification system in ophthalmology: real-world evaluation in 37 529 cases
outcome: Medical errors when AI authentication was not implemented or properly used
effect: Five postimplementation errors (0.027%) occurred, four in non-authenticated cases. Initial surgical laterality authentication was 84.5% vs 99.4% post implementation; two laterality errors occurred during initial implementation.
quote: Post implementation, five medical errors (0.027%) occurred, with four in non-authenticated cases (where the AI system was not fully implemented or properly used), compared with one (0.0053%) pre-implementation (p=0.125).

title: Large-scale observational study of AI-based patient and surgical material verification system in ophthalmology: real-world evaluation in 37 529 cases
outcome: Errors from IOL models not in AI training due to delayed updates
effect: 7.3% of 9713 post-implementation IOL surgeries involved unlearned lenses, leading to two incorrect IOL implantations; model updated only three times due to budget and stability constraints.
quote: Of the 9713 IOL surgeries performed post implementation, 7.3% involved unlearned lenses, leading to two cases of incorrect IOL implantation.

title: Large-scale observational study of AI-based patient and surgical material verification system in ophthalmology: real-world evaluation in 37 529 cases
outcome: Surgical safety failures despite accurate AI detection in the clinical workflow
effect: Pre-implementation testing demonstrated 100% accuracy in 300 cases; deployment included a wrong-eye anaesthetic injection despite AI warnings, which the nurse could not relay even after eight attempts.
quote: The AI-based surgery safety system continued to point out the mistake, but the attending nurse could not relay this to the surgeon even after eight attempts, leading to a local anaesthetic injection in the wrong eye.

title: Large-scale observational study of AI-based patient and surgical material verification system in ophthalmology: real-world evaluation in 37 529 cases
outcome: errors involving unlearned inputs
effect: Two errors involved unlearned intraocular lenses due to delayed AI updates, causing non-authentication.
quote: Of the four non-authenticated errors, two were laterality errors during the initial implementation period and two were IOL implantation errors involving unlearned IOLs (7.3% of cases) due to delayed AI updates.

title: Large-scale observational study of AI-based patient and surgical material verification system in ophthalmology: real-world evaluation in 37 529 cases
outcome: system accuracy in pre-implementation testing
effect: The system demonstrated 100% accuracy in a pre-implementation test of 300 cases.
quote: Pre-implementation testing with 300 cases (50% intentionally erroneous) demonstrated 100% system accuracy ( online supplemental figure 6 ).

title: Evaluating the dosimetric impact of deep-learning-based auto-segmentation in prostate cancer radiotherapy: Insights into real-world clinical implementation and inter-observer variability
venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
outcome: Geometric and dosimetric agreement of AI contours versus original and expert manual contours
effect: AC-vs-manual geometric differences were smaller than manual-vs-manual for bladder and femoral heads; IMRT PTV D95 77.62±0.38 Gy (AC) vs 77.58±0.69 (OC) and 77.71±0.53 (EC); contouring time 0.53 vs 24.9 min.
quote: Our automated contouring system can reduce inter-expert variability and achieve dosimetric accuracy comparable to gold standard reference contours, highlighting its potential for streamlining clinical workflows.

title: Assessing the quality of AI information from ChatGPT regarding oral surgery, preventive dentistry, and oral cancer: An exploration study
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT dental answers, including diagnostic methods and post-operative instructions
effect: Preventive dentistry scored 4.3/5; oral surgery 3.9/5 and oral cancer 3.6/5, with gaps in post-operative instructions, personalized risk assessments, and specialized diagnostic methods.
quote: While achieving the highest score for preventive dentistry at 4.3/5 and being able to communicate the complex information coherently, the tool showed lower accuracy for oral surgery and oral cancer, scoring 3.9/5 and 3.6/5, respectively, with several gaps for post-operative instructions, personalized risk assessments, and specialized diagnostic methods.

title: Assessing the efficacy of artificial intelligence to provide peri-operative information for patients with a stoma
outcome: Readability of LLM stoma information (Flesch-Kincaid, Flesch Reading Ease, Coleman-Liau)
effect: All responses from all four LLMs required high school to college level education to comprehend comfortably; CoPilot and ChatGPT-4 performed better on readability.
quote: All responses required high school to college level education to comprehend comfortably.

title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-3.5 and Google Gemini on PCOS assessment and management based on recommendations from the 2023 guideline
outcome: Readability scores of chatbot responses to PCOS questions
effect: Gemini obtained a higher readability score compared to the other chatbots (p < 0.001).
quote: However, Gemini obtained a higher readability score compared to the other chatbots (p < 0.001).

title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-3.5 and Google Gemini on PCOS assessment and management based on recommendations from the 2023 guideline
outcome: Accuracy and quality of chatbot answers versus 2023 PCOS guideline recommendations
effect: ChatGPT-4 and ChatGPT-3.5 scored higher than Gemini in accuracy and quality (p = 0.001, p < 0.001 and p = 0.007, p < 0.001 respectively).
quote: ChatGPT-4 and ChatGPT-3.5 attained higher scores in accuracy and quality compared to Gemini (p = 0.001, p < 0.001 and p = 0.007, p < 0.001 respectively).

title: Enhancing Access to Orthopedic Education: Exploring the Potential of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Improving Health Literacy on Rotator Cuff Injuries
outcome: Reading grade level of patient education materials before vs after LLM rewriting to eighth-grade target
effect: Mean reading grade fell from 10.02 ± 1.86 to 5.67 ± 1.77; mean reduction 4.33 ± 1.50 (p < 0.001); all 25 rewritten PEMs below eighth-grade level.
quote: The average reduction in reading grade level was 4.33 ± 1.50 (p < 0.001), indicating a substantial improvement in the readability of the materials.

title: Enhancing Access to Orthopedic Education: Exploring the Potential of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Improving Health Literacy on Rotator Cuff Injuries
outcome: Readability and length of patient education materials after plain-language rewriting by generative AI
effect: Rewritten PEMs averaged 5.67 grade level versus 10.02 originally; word count fell from 755.0 to 312.2 (mean reduction 442.68, p < 0.001).
quote: Following the application of ChatGPT's rewriting tool, all 25 PEMs were revised to meet readability standards below the eighth-grade level.

title: Use of Online Large Language Model Chatbots in Cornea Clinics
outcome: Readability of LLM responses measured with 12 readability metrics across four chatbots
effect: Google Bard led in 75% of readability metrics assessed; ChatGPT scored highest on rubric criteria including comprehension. Specific reading grade levels are not reported in the abstract.
quote: However, Google Bard excelled in readability, leading in 75% of the metrics assessed.

title: Use of Online Large Language Model Chatbots in Cornea Clinics
outcome: Specialist-rated patient risk from LLM responses to cornea scenarios
effect: Three blinded cornea specialists found no responses that posed risks to patients; ChatGPT scored overall 3.35 ± 0.42 (83.8%).
quote: Importantly, no responses were found to pose risks to patients, ensuring the safety and reliability of the information provided.

title: Developing and Evaluating Large Language Model-Generated Emergency Medicine Handoff Notes
outcome: Physician-rated safety and usefulness of LLM handoff notes versus physician-written notes, critical risks
effect: Mean safety 4.06 (0.86) vs 4.50 (0.56) for physician-written; usefulness 4.04 vs 4.36 out of 5; no LLM summary rated a critical patient safety risk.
quote: None of the LLM-generated summaries were classified as a critical patient safety risk.
sample_unit: emergency medicine patient records (50-summary subsample reviewed by 3 physicians)

title: Artificial intelligence related safety issues associated with FDA medical device reports
outcome: Share of FDA device reports with enough information to identify an AI/ML contribution
effect: Of 429 reports, 108 (25.2%) were potentially AI/ML related and 148 (34.5%) had insufficient information to determine AI/ML contribution.
quote: Of the 429 reports reviewed, 108 (25.2%) were potentially AI/ML related, with 148 (34.5%) containing insufficient information to determine an AI/ML contribution.

title: The utility of Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer as a patient resource in paediatric otolaryngology
venue: The Journal of laryngology and otology
outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT recommendations across question variations
effect: Consistent responses were obtained with question variation; no numbers reported in abstract.
quote: Consistent responses were obtained with question variation.

title: Quality of Information Provided by Artificial Intelligence Chatbots Surrounding the Reconstructive Surgery for Head and Neck Cancer: A Comparative Analysis Between ChatGPT4 and Claude2
venue: Clinical otolaryngology : official journal of ENT-UK ; official journal of Netherlands Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology & Cervico-Facial Surgery
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of chatbot responses on head and neck reconstructive surgery
effect: ChatGPT4 FKGL mean 4.57 vs Claude2 6.05 (p < 0.001); ChatGPT4 requiring easy-fairly easy English in 93% of cases.
quote: Regarding readability, ChatGPT4 presented lower complexity than Claude2 (FKGL mean score 4.57 vs. 6.05, p < 0.001) requiring an easy-fairly easy English in 93% of cases.

title: Evaluation of Responses to Questions About Keratoconus Using ChatGPT-4.0, Google Gemini and Microsoft Copilot: A Comparative Study of Large Language Models on Keratoconus
outcome: Readability and complexity of LLM answers for patients (Flesch reading ease, Flesch-Kincaid grade level)
effect: ChatGPT-4.0 answers were more complex for patients than those of Gemini and Copilot, though rated reliable and accurate; 92% of its answers were rated agree/strongly agree.
quote: Although the answers of ChatGPT-4.0 to questions about keratoconus were more complex for patients than those of other language programs, the information provided was reliable and accurate.

title: From theoretical models to practical deployment: A perspective and case study of opportunities and challenges in AI-driven cardiac auscultation research for low-income settings
outcome: Generalisation of heart murmur detection models to out-of-distribution data
effect: The abstract reports that the case-study model and other state-of-the-art models generalise with difficulty to out-of-distribution data. No numeric results are given.
quote: The difficulty with which this model, and other state-of-the-art models, generalise to out-of-distribution data is also discussed.

title: Reliability and quality of information provided by artificial intelligence chatbots on post-contrast acute kidney injury: an evaluation of diagnostic, preventive, and treatment guidance
outcome: Readability (Coleman-Liau index) and understandability of chatbot responses on contrast-associated AKI
effect: Coleman-Liau index greater than 11 for all chatbots, requiring university-level education; PEMAT-P understandability and applicability and WRRS scores low for all chatbots.
quote: Based on the Coleman-Liau index, the readability of the responses was greater than 11 for all artificial intelligence chatbots, suggesting a high level of complexity requiring a university-level education.

title: A randomized controlled trial on evaluating clinician-supervised generative AI for decision support
outcome: Decision accuracy in simulated CPR with clinician-supervised vs autonomous ChatGPT vs paper guide
effect: Supervised-ChatGPT group showed significantly higher decision accuracy than paper guide and ChatGPT groups, though scenario completion time was longer. In one instance ChatGPT suggested a risky option.
quote: Results indicate that the Supervised-ChatGPT group showed significantly higher decision accuracy compared to the paper guide and ChatGPT groups, although the scenario completion time was longer.

title: A randomized controlled trial on evaluating clinician-supervised generative AI for decision support
outcome: Performance of users with different AI configurations (autonomous vs clinician-supervised) compared to non-AI paper guide
effect: Supervised-ChatGPT had significantly higher decision accuracy than paper guide and autonomous ChatGPT; lower LF/HF ratio; highest trust; longer completion time.
quote: Results indicate that the Supervised-ChatGPT group showed significantly higher decision accuracy compared to the paper guide and ChatGPT groups, although the scenario completion time was longer.

title: A multimetric health literacy analysis of phalloplasty techniques: Comparing artificial intelligence and online resources
venue: Journal of plastic, reconstructive & aesthetic surgery : JPRAS
outcome: Reading grade level (SMOG) of AI and website phalloplasty patient information
effect: Website readability was higher than AI platforms, though not statistically significant (p=0.10). All means exceeded the eighth-grade reading level.
quote: All means exceeded the eighth-grade reading level, with AI outperforming websites in understandability and actionability (p<0.0001 and p=0.006).

title: AI depictions of psychiatric diagnoses: a preliminary study of generative image outputs in Midjourney V.6 and DALL-E 3
outcome: Stereotyping or stigmatising content in AI-generated images of psychiatric diagnoses
effect: Images frequently reflected cultural stereotypes, historical visual tropes, gender biases and stigmatising portrayals of certain mental health conditions; no quantified rates reported.
quote: These images frequently reflected cultural stereotypes and historical visual tropes including gender biases and stigmatising portrayals of certain mental health conditions.

title: The analytical and clinical validity of AI algorithms to score TILs in TNBC: can we use different machine learning models interchangeably?
outcome: Comparison of ten AI TIL models on analytical and prognostic validity against invasive disease-free survival
effect: Analytical validity differed across models (Spearman's r = 0.63-0.73, p < 0.001); eight of ten models were prognostic with overlapping HR = 0.40-0.47 (p < 0.004) in external cohort.
quote: A significant difference in analytical validity (Spearman's r = 0.63-0.73, p < 0.001) is highlighted across AI methodologies and training strategies.
sample_unit: patients (79 Yale analytical/development cohort; 215 Swedish prognostic validation cohort)

title: The analytical and clinical validity of AI algorithms to score TILs in TNBC: can we use different machine learning models interchangeably?
outcome: Prognostic performance of AI TIL models in independent external cohort
effect: Eight of ten AI models showed prognostic validity in the external Swedish cohort (HR = 0.40-0.47; p < 0.004), while analytical validity differed across models.
quote: Interestingly, the prognostic performance of digital TILs is demonstrated for eight out of ten AI models, even less extensively trained ones, with similar and overlapping hazard ratios (HR) in the external validation cohort (Cox regression analysis based on IDFS-endpoint, HR = 0.40-0.47; p < 0.004).
sample_unit: patients (79 Yale analytical/development cohort; 215 Swedish prognostic validation cohort)

title: Evaluating the Performance of ChatGPT in the Prescribing Safety Assessment: Implications for Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Prescribing
outcome: ChatGPT accuracy on PSA data interpretation section versus other prescribing sections
effect: Data Interpretation scored 32/72 (44.44%) with variability across trials, versus 87.50% for Adverse Drug Reactions and 88.89% for Communicating Information; overall papers 66.33%-85.67%.
quote: However, it struggled in "Data Interpretation", scoring 32/72 (44.44%), showing variability across trials and indicating limitations in handling more complex clinical reasoning tasks.
sample_unit: questions (4 PSA practice papers x 30 questions, each run in 3 trials)

title: Development and validation of a deep learning pipeline to diagnose ovarian masses using ultrasound screening: a retrospective multicenter study
outcome: Reader accuracy, sensitivity and specificity with versus without AI assistance for ovarian mass diagnosis
effect: Junior/intermediate radiologists improved with AI (ACC 80.8 vs 75.3, p=0.00015; SEN 79.5 vs 74.6, p=0.029; SPE 81.7 vs 75.8, p=0.0032); GPs with AI reached radiologist-level performance.
quote: There was a significant improvement in junior and intermediate radiologists who were assisted by AI compared to those who were not assisted by AI (ACC: 80.8 vs. 75.3, p = 0.00015; SEN: 79.5 vs. 74.6, p = 0.029; SPE: 81.7 vs. 75.8, p = 0.0032).

title: Development and validation of a deep learning pipeline to diagnose ovarian masses using ultrasound screening: a retrospective multicenter study
outcome: AI diagnostic performance compared with senior radiologists on the same external video data
effect: OvaMTA AUC 0.911 on 159 videos, comparable to senior radiologists (ACC 86.2 vs 88.1, p=0.50; SEN 81.8 vs 88.6, p=0.16; SPE 89.2 vs 87.6, p=0.68).
quote: In video-based external testing, OvaMTA recognised 159 videos with ovarian masses with AUC of 0.911, and is comparable to the performance of senior radiologists (ACC: 86.2 vs. 88.1, p = 0.50; SEN: 81.8 vs. 88.6, p = 0.16; SPE: 89.2 vs. 87.6, p = 0.68).

title: Development and validation of a deep learning pipeline to diagnose ovarian masses using ultrasound screening: a retrospective multicenter study
outcome: Model performance on internal versus external test cohorts from other hospitals
effect: Detection AUC 0.970 internal vs 0.877 external; Dice 0.887 internal vs 0.819 external; diagnosis AUC 0.941 on both internal and external sets.
quote: OvaMTA-Seg also performed well in ovarian mass detection from test images, including healthy ovaries and masses (internal test area under the curve [AUC]: 0.970; external test AUC: 0.877).

title: Impact of Demographic Modifiers on Readability of Myopia Education Materials Generated by Large Language Models
outcome: Readability (SMOG, Flesch-Kincaid, Flesch Reading Ease) of myopia education text across race, ethnicity and gender prompt modifiers
effect: No readability differences by gender, race, or ethnicity for ChatGPT or Copilot; Gemini readability differed significantly by race in the prompt (p<0.05). 150 responses analyzed.
quote: Gemini-generated responses differed significantly in their SMOG Index, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, and Flesch Reading Ease based on the race mentioned in the prompt (p<0.05).

title: Evaluating a Foundation Artificial Intelligence Model for Glaucoma Detection Using Color Fundus Photographs
outcome: Glaucoma detection AUC across race and age subgroups
effect: Performance consistent across race and age: Black (AUC = 0.87) vs. other (AUC = 0.86), and >60 years (AUC = 0.84) vs. <60 years (AUC = 0.87).
quote: Performance was consistent across race and age for all training size and cycle number combinations: Black (AUC = 0.87) vs. other (AUC = 0.86), and >60 years (AUC = 0.84) vs. <60 years (AUC = 0.87).

title: Evaluating a Foundation Artificial Intelligence Model for Glaucoma Detection Using Color Fundus Photographs
outcome: AUC by fine-tuning sample size and training epochs
effect: AUC rose from 0.52 (50 images, 5 epochs) to 0.86 (2000 images, 50 epochs); 0.82 at ~500 and 0.83 at ~1000 images, with diminishing gains.
quote: Performance increased with larger training datasets and more training cycles, improving from 50 training images and 5 epochs (AUC: 0.52) to 2000 training images and 50 epochs (AUC: 0.86), with reduced gain in performance from approximately 500 and 1000 training images (AUC of 0.82 and 0.83, respectively).

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Generated Patient Education Guides on Epilepsy: A Cross-Sectional Study of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
outcome: Readability (Flesch ease scores, grade level) of AI-generated epilepsy patient education guides
effect: Flesch ease scores for ChatGPT vs Gemini were 38.6 vs 43.6 (GTCS), 18.7 vs 45.5 (myoclonic), 22.4 vs 55.8 (status epilepticus); Gemini significantly better (p=0.0493). Grade level did not differ (p=0.67).
quote: Ease scores generated by ChatGPT and Google Gemini were 38.6 and 43.6 for generalized tonic-clonic seizures (GTCS), 18.7 and 45.5 for myoclonic seizures, and 22.4 and 55.8 for status epilepticus, respectively, showing Google Gemini generated responses notably better (p=0.0493).
sample_unit: AI-generated patient education guides (three epilepsy topics per tool)

title: Ambient artificial intelligence scribes: physician burnout and perspectives on usability and documentation burden
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Physician task load, burnout, and usability before vs after ambient AI scribe pilot
effect: Task load fell by 24.42 points (p <.001), burnout fell by 1.94 points (p <.001), and usability rose by 10.9 points (p <.001) in paired analysis (n = 38).
quote: Paired survey analysis (n = 38) revealed large statistically significant reductions in task load (-24.42, p <.001) and burnout (-1.94, p <.001), and moderate statistically significant improvements in usability scores (+10.9, p <.001).

title: Artificial intelligence chatbots versus traditional medical resources for patient education on "Labor Epidurals": an evaluation of accuracy, emotional tone, and readability
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of chatbot responses versus ASA patient materials on labor epidurals
effect: ASA materials scored highest for readability, followed by Gemini and ChatGPT. Gemini content was more complex. The authors conclude chatbots need improved readability.
quote: ASA materials were the most accessible, while Gemini content was more complex.

title: Comparative benchmarking of failure detection methods in medical image segmentation: Unveiling the role of confidence aggregation
outcome: Ability of automated failure detection methods to flag segmentation failures under test-time distribution shift
effect: Pairwise Dice score between ensemble predictions performed best as a simple, robust failure detection baseline; pixel confidence aggregation was important. No numeric results reported in the abstract.
quote: Our findings highlight the importance of pixel confidence aggregation and we observe superior performance of the pairwise Dice score (Roy et al., 2019) between ensemble predictions, positioning it as a simple and robust baseline for failure detection in medical image segmentation.
sample_unit: five public 3D medical image collections (number of images not reported)

title: EyeGPT for Patient Inquiries and Medical Education: Development and Validation of an Ophthalmology Large Language Model
outcome: Hallucination proportion and response score with vs without retrieval grounding in ophthalmology textbooks
effect: Adding book retrieval improved score (mean 13.08 vs 15.14; P=.001) and reduced hallucinations (71/120, 59.2% vs 57/120, 47.4%, P=.02) versus fine-tuned model alone.
quote: Incorporating information retrieval from reliable sources, particularly ophthalmology textbooks, further improved the model's response compared with solely the best fine-tuned model (mean 13.08, SD 5.43 vs mean 15.14, SD 4.64; P=.001) and reduced hallucinations (71/120, 59.2% vs 57/120, 47.4%, P=.02).

title: EyeGPT for Patient Inquiries and Medical Education: Development and Validation of an Ophthalmology Large Language Model
outcome: Ophthalmologist answers ranked best with vs without EyeGPT assistance
effect: EyeGPT-assisted ophthalmologists ranked best in accuracy for 94 (78.3%) and trustworthiness for 93 (77.5%) of 120 questions; unassisted ophthalmologists ranked best for 14 (11.7%) and 15 (12.5%).
quote: With the assistance of EyeGPT, the answers provided by the ophthalmologists excelled, ranking highest in accuracy and trustworthiness in 94 (78.3%) and 93 (77.5%) of the 120 questions, respectively.

title: EyeGPT for Patient Inquiries and Medical Education: Development and Validation of an Ophthalmology Large Language Model
outcome: EyeGPT answers compared with unassisted ophthalmologists across four dimensions
effect: EyeGPT ranked best more often for understandability (19.2% vs 10%) and empathy (34.2% vs 6.7%) but slightly lower for accuracy (10% vs 11.7%) and trustworthiness (10% vs 12.5%).
quote: however, the accuracy and trustworthiness of EyeGPT answers were slightly lower than those by the ophthalmologists (accuracy: 12/120, 10% vs 14/120, 11.7%; trustworthiness: 12/120, 10% vs 15/120, 12.5%), highlighting areas for improvement.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in extracting cognitive exam dates and scores
outcome: LLM extraction errors including hallucinations and wrong-test or wrong-date reports in clinical notes
effect: MMSE: LlaMA-2 had 27 total hallucinations, 19 wrong-test, 25 missed scores, 23 wrong dates; ChatGPT had 3 hallucinations, 17 wrong-test, 19 wrong dates.
quote: LlaMA-2 errors included 27 cases of total hallucination, 19 cases of reporting other scores instead of MMSE, 25 missed scores, and 23 cases of reporting only the wrong date.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in extracting cognitive exam dates and scores
outcome: LLM extraction accuracy against expert-reviewer reference standard
effect: MMSE accuracy 83% (ChatGPT) vs 66.4% (LlaMA-2); CDR accuracy 87.1% vs 74.5%; CDR precision 48.3% vs 16.1%.
quote: For MMSE information extraction, ChatGPT (vs. LlaMA-2) achieved accuracy of 83% (vs. 66.4%), sensitivity of 89.7% (vs. 69.9%), true-negative rates of 96% (vs 60.0%), and precision of 82.7% (vs 62.2%).

title: Comparative Analysis of Generative Pre-Trained Transformer Models in Oncogene-Driven Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Introducing the Generative Artificial Intelligence Performance Score
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT NSCLC treatment recommendations versus NCCN guidelines, including hallucination rate
effect: GPT-4 base score 90% vs 60% for GPT-3.5; hallucinations 34% vs 53%; G-PS 0.34 vs -0.15 (P<.01).
quote: Analyzing 160 responses, generative pre-trained transformer (GPT)-4 outperformed GPT-3.5, showing higher base score (90% v 60%; P < .01) and fewer hallucinations (34% v 53%; P < .01).

title: Comparative Analysis of Generative Pre-Trained Transformer Models in Oncogene-Driven Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Introducing the Generative Artificial Intelligence Performance Score
outcome: Generative model performance on intended-use oncology treatment recommendations against NCCN guidelines
effect: GPT-4 hallucinated in 34% of responses and GPT-3.5 in 53%; GPT-4 G-PS 0.34, GPT-3.5 -0.15.
quote: Although the rate of hallucinations improved in the GPT-4 model, future generative AI use in clinical care requires high levels of accuracy with minimal to no room for hallucinations.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Improved Understanding of Communications With Patients With Cancer in a Call Center Setting: Proof-of-Concept Study
outcome: Intent classification accuracy of GPT-4 versus LSTM and BERT on same test sentences
effect: GPT-4 few-shot accuracy 85.2% versus LSTM 73.7% and BERT 71.3%; GPT-4 over 15% better on ambiguous categories.
quote: GPT-4, which uses only a few examples (a few shots), attained a remarkable accuracy of 85.2%, considerably outperforming the LSTM and BERT models, which achieved accuracies of 73.7% and 71.3%, respectively.

title: Enhancing Multilingual Patient Education: ChatGPT's Accuracy and Readability for SSNHL Queries in English and Spanish
outcome: Understandability and readability of ChatGPT patient education responses in English and Spanish
effect: Google's Spanish responses had better readability (effect size 0.35, P < .001) and Google's English responses were more understandable (effect size 0.67, P = .018); authors conclude ChatGPT readability and understandability need improvement.
quote: However, improvements in its readability and understandability are warranted for more accessible patient education.
sample_unit: responses to guideline-derived SSNHL patient questions

title: Development, deployment, and continuous monitoring of a machine learning model to predict respiratory failure in critically ill patients
outcome: Model discrimination when applied to an external site dataset (MIMIC-IV)
effect: The UCSD-trained model's AUC dropped to 0.73 on MIMIC-IV, compared with 0.897 cross-validated and 0.908 prospective at UCSD.
quote: The final Vent.io model trained using UCSD data obtained an AUC of 0.73, lower than the minimum of 0.85 set by the PCCP, prompting a fine-tuning process.
sample_unit: ICU encounters (26,045 development, 276 prospective silent-mode, 35,534 MIMIC-IV)

title: Development, deployment, and continuous monitoring of a machine learning model to predict respiratory failure in critically ill patients
outcome: External-site AUC before and after fine-tuning on local data
effect: Fine-tuning on MIMIC-IV data raised AUC from 0.73 to 0.873. Acceptable performance was reached using 25% or more of the local training data.
quote: The fine-tuned Vent.io model achieved an AUC of 0.873.

title: Are AI chatbots concordant with evidence-based cancer screening recommendations?
outcome: Hallucinations and non-concordance of ChatGPT cancer screening information against USPSTF recommendations
effect: 43 of 60 (71.7%) criteria completely concordant; 14 (23.3%) not concordant or not present; hallucinations in 9 of 60 criteria (15%).
quote: ChatGPT hallucinations (i.e., completely made up, non-sensical or irrelevant information) were found in 9 of 60 criteria (15 %).

title: Are AI chatbots concordant with evidence-based cancer screening recommendations?
outcome: Concordance of AI clinical knowledge with current USPSTF screening guidelines
effect: 43 of 60 (71.7%) criteria completely concordant, 3 (5%) moderately concordant, 14 (23.3%) not concordant or not present; 9 of 14 non-concordant from oldest age group prompts.
quote: 43 of 60 (71.7 %) criteria were completely concordant, 3 (5 %) were moderately concordant and 14 (23.3 %) were not concordant or not present, with most of the non-concordant criteria (9 of 14, 64.3 %) being from prompts for the oldest age groups.

title: Assessing the readability, quality and reliability of responses produced by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity regarding most frequently asked keywords about low back pain
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on low back pain versus recommended 6th grade level
effect: Readability of responses from all three chatbots was above the recommended 6th grade level (p < 0.001); Perplexity had higher quality, reliability scores (EQIP, JAMA, modified DISCERN, GQS; p < 0.001).
quote: It was determined that the readability of the responses given by all AI chatbots was higher than the recommended 6th grade readability level (p < 0.001).

title: Enhancing Diagnostic Accuracy of Lung Nodules in Chest Computed Tomography Using Artificial Intelligence: Retrospective Analysis
outcome: False positive and false negative rates of lung nodule detection before vs after AI implementation
effect: At Hospital A, false negative rate fell from 8.4% to 5.16% while false positive rate rose from 2.36% to 9.77% (P<.001); accuracy fell from 93.33% to 92.23% (A) and 95.27% to 92.77% (C).
quote: At Hospital A, the false negative rate decreased from 8.4% to 5.16% (χ<sup>2</sup><sub>1</sub>=9.85; P=.002), while the false positive rate increased from 2.36% to 9.77% (χ<sup>2</sup><sub>1</sub>=53.48; P<.001).

title: A prospective pragmatic evaluation of automatic trial matching tools in a molecular tumor board
outcome: Trial matching tool accuracy against expert molecular tumor board reference standard
effect: Mean precision = 0.33, recall = 0.32, AP@3 = 0.45, NDCG@3 = 0.34; 38% of patients had no trials suggested.
quote: The mean performances were precision = 0.33, recall = 0.32, AP@3 = 0.45, and NDCG@3 = 0.34.

title: Extensive benchmarking of a method that estimates external model performance from limited statistical characteristics
outcome: Internal versus external AUROC
effect: MDCR median internal-external AUROC absolute difference was 0.027 (IQR 0.013–0.055), larger than estimation error 0.011 (IQR 0.005–0.017).
quote: The upper quartile of AUROC estimation errors is usually below 0.02, whereas the values of internal-external AUROC difference are higher; for example, the median error in the internal resource MDCR benchmark is 0.011 (IQR 0.005–0.017), and the internal-external absolute difference is 0.027 (IQR 0.013–0.055).
sample_unit: patients with pharmaceutically-treated depression across five data sources

title: Extensive benchmarking of a method that estimates external model performance from limited statistical characteristics
outcome: Difference between internal and external performance across data sources with differing populations
effect: Median internal-external AUROC difference 0.027 (IQR 0.013–0.055) in MDCR; calibration difference 0.329 (0.167–0.836); age distributions differed markedly (65+ was 0.7% in CCAE vs 97% in MDCR).
quote: The upper quartile of AUROC estimation errors is usually below 0.02, whereas the values of internal-external AUROC difference are higher; for example, the median error in the internal resource MDCR benchmark is 0.011 (IQR 0.005–0.017), and the internal-external absolute difference is 0.027 (IQR 0.013–0.055).
sample_unit: patients with pharmaceutically-treated depression across five data sources

title: Extensive benchmarking of a method that estimates external model performance from limited statistical characteristics
outcome: Model performance variation across external data sources (sites)
effect: Internal AUROC 0.61 vs actual external AUROC 0.587 in MDCR for one diarrhea model; internal-external differences exceeded estimation errors across AUROC, calibration, Brier and scaled Brier metrics.
quote: Importantly, the estimated and actual external performance is similar, e.g., when training a linear diarrhea model with a medium-sized feature set on CCAE, the internal AUROC is 0.61, the actual external AUROC in MDCR is 0.587, and the estimated AUROC is 0.585.
sample_unit: patients with pharmaceutically-treated depression across five data sources

title: Extensive benchmarking of a method that estimates external model performance from limited statistical characteristics
outcome: Internal-external calibration and accuracy differences
effect: Internal-external differences in MDCR were calibration 0.329, Brier 0.012, and scaled Brier 0.308.
quote: The other metrics accuracy differences are even more pronounced; for example in MDCR, calibration differences are 0.013 (0.003–0.050) versus 0.329 (0.167–0.836), Brier score differences are 3.2 ⋅ 10 −5 (1.3 ⋅ 10 −5 –8.3 ⋅ 10 −5 ) versus 0.012 (0.0042–0.018), and scaled Brier score differences are 0.008 (0.001–0.022) versus 0.308 (0.167–0.440).
sample_unit: patients with pharmaceutically-treated depression across five data sources

title: Assessing online chat-based artificial intelligence models for weight loss recommendation appropriateness and bias in the presence of guideline incongruence
outcome: Rate at which chatbot refused/deferred to physician on obesity management questions
effect: Google Gemini refused 2 of 10 questions and insisted on consulting a physician; Microsoft Copilot answered all 10.
quote: Google Gemini refused to respond to two questions and insisted on consulting a physician.

title: Assessing online chat-based artificial intelligence models for weight loss recommendation appropriateness and bias in the presence of guideline incongruence
outcome: Appropriateness and completeness of chatbot obesity treatment answers versus ADA/AACE guidelines
effect: All Copilot and 8/10 Gemini responses appropriate; none inappropriate. Copilot complete 10/10 versus Gemini 5/10.
quote: Microsoft Copilot (10/10; 100%) provided a higher proportion of complete responses than Google Gemini (5/10; 50%).

title: A deep learning model for carotid plaques detection based on CTA images: a two stepwise early-stage clinical validation study
outcome: Radiologist plaque-detection sensitivity with versus without AI assistance in simulated clinical scenarios
effect: The model improved radiologists' sensitivity in diagnosing plaques in the Model-human study. Overreliance was not reported as assessed, and no numbers are given in the abstract.
quote: Furthermore, in Model-human Real Clinical Scenarios study, we found that the model improved the radiologists' sensitivity in diagnosing plaques.

title: A deep learning model for carotid plaques detection based on CTA images: a two stepwise early-stage clinical validation study
outcome: Model diagnostic performance compared against 6 radiologists on the same plaque cases
effect: Model diagnostic results were higher than those of 4 out of 6 radiologists (p < 0.001). Model diagnostic time was 6 s, significantly shorter than that of all radiologists (p < 0.001).
quote: Especially, in the clinical application scenario analysis, the model's diagnostic results for plaques were found to be higher than those of 4 out of 6 radiologists (p < 0.001).

title: Large-Scale Validation of the Feasibility of GPT-4 as a Proofreading Tool for Head CT Reports
outcome: Error detection sensitivity and review time of GPT-4 versus human radiologist readers on same reports
effect: Human readers had worse factual error detection sensitivity (0.33-0.69 vs 0.89) and took longer (82-121 s vs 16 s, P<.001) than GPT-4.
quote: Compared with GPT-4, human readers had worse factual error detection sensitivity (0.33-0.69 vs 0.89; P = .008 for radiologist 4, P < .001 for others) and took longer to review (82-121 seconds vs 16 seconds, P < .001).

title: Assessing the performance of AI chatbots in answering patients' common questions about low back pain
outcome: Readability of chatbot answers to low back pain questions (Flesch Reading Ease Score)
effect: Answers were 'reasonably difficult' to read, mean (SD) FRES 50.94 (3.06).
quote: Overall, LLM-chatbots provided answers that were 'reasonably difficult' to read, with a mean (SD) FRES score of 50.94 (3.06).

title: Assessing the performance of AI chatbots in answering patients' common questions about low back pain
outcome: Accuracy of chatbot low back pain recommendations against clinical guidelines
effect: Of 120 responses yielding 1069 recommendations, 55.8% were accurate, 42.1% inaccurate and 1.9% unclear.
quote: Out of 120 responses yielding 1069 recommendations, 55.8% were accurate, 42.1% inaccurate and 1.9% unclear.

title: Large language models improve the identification of emergency department visits for symptomatic kidney stones
outcome: Change in LLM predictions when race and gender were varied in prompts
effect: GPT-4 exhibited no racial or gender disparities, whereas GPT-3.5 failed to effectively model racial diversity.
quote: Bias assessment found that GPT-4 exhibited no racial or gender disparities, in contrast to GPT-3.5, which failed to effectively model racial diversity.

title: Large language models improve the identification of emergency department visits for symptomatic kidney stones
outcome: Fairness of LLM performance across race and gender subgroups
effect: GPT-4 showed no racial or gender disparities; GPT-3.5 failed to effectively model racial diversity.
quote: Bias assessment found that GPT-4 exhibited no racial or gender disparities, in contrast to GPT-3.5, which failed to effectively model racial diversity.

title: A phenotype-based AI pipeline outperforms human experts in differentially diagnosing rare diseases using EHRs
outcome: Top-3 recall of physicians with versus without PhenoBrain assistance on 75 cases
effect: Combining PhenoBrain's predictions with specialists increased top-3 recall to 0.768, versus PhenoBrain alone 0.613 and specialists lower.
quote: Combining PhenoBrain's predictions with specialists increased the top-3 recall to 0.768, demonstrating its potential to enhance diagnostic accuracy in clinical workflows.

title: A phenotype-based AI pipeline outperforms human experts in differentially diagnosing rare diseases using EHRs
outcome: Top-3 and top-10 recall of AI versus specialist physicians, LLMs, and 13 prediction methods
effect: Top-3 recall 0.613 and top-10 recall 0.813 in 75 cases, surpassing 50 specialists, ChatGPT and GPT-4; 0.513/0.654 in 1936 test cases surpassing 13 methods.
quote: In a human-computer study with 75 cases, PhenoBrain exhibited exceptional performance with a top-3 recall of 0.613 and a top-10 recall of 0.813, surpassing the performance of 50 specialist physicians and large language models like ChatGPT and GPT-4.

title: Large Language Models Outperform Traditional Natural Language Processing Methods in Extracting Patient-Reported Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
outcome: Traditional NLP accuracy at external site versus development site
effect: On external validation at Stanford (n = 250), tNLP models failed to generalize (61%-62% accuracy) while GPT-4 maintained accuracies >90%.
quote: On external validation at Stanford (n = 250), tNLP models failed to generalize (61%-62% accuracy) while GPT-4 maintained accuracies >90%.
sample_unit: clinic notes (50 UCSF test set, 250 Stanford external validation)

title: Large Language Models Outperform Traditional Natural Language Processing Methods in Extracting Patient-Reported Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
outcome: Model performance differences by demographics or diagnosis
effect: No biases were detected based on demographics or diagnosis.
quote: No biases were detected based on demographics or diagnosis.
sample_unit: clinic notes (50 UCSF test set, 250 Stanford external validation)

title: Real world clinical experience of using Brainomix e-CTA software in a medium size acute National Health Service Trust
outcome: e-CTA LVO detection accuracy on local consecutive cases versus consultant neuroradiologist ground truth
effect: Sensitivity 0.78 (95% CI 0.64-0.88), specificity 0.93, PPV 0.5 (0.42-0.58), NPV 0.98; error rate 9% (52/584) at 9% LVO prevalence.
quote: We demonstrated that PPV of e-CTA is poor in consecutive cases in a real-world NHS setting.

title: Real world clinical experience of using Brainomix e-CTA software in a medium size acute National Health Service Trust
outcome: Predictive values at local low prevalence of LVO
effect: With LVO prevalence 9% (n=50), PPV was only 0.5 (0.42-0.58) despite specificity 0.93, showing clinical utility may be overstated.
quote: We hypothesized that in real world use where prevalence is low, its clinical utility may be overstated.

title: Provision of Radiology Reports Simplified With Large Language Models to Patients With Cancer: Impact on Patient Satisfaction
outcome: Patient knowledge, confidence, and understanding with simplified vs original CT report impressions
effect: Simplified report group had significantly better knowledge of primary site and disease extent and higher confidence and understanding (P < .05 for all).
quote: In phase II, simplified report group patients demonstrated significantly better knowledge of primary site and extent of their disease as well as showed significantly higher confidence and understanding of the report (P < .05 for all).

title: Provision of Radiology Reports Simplified With Large Language Models to Patients With Cancer: Impact on Patient Satisfaction
outcome: Radiologist review catching errors in LLM-simplified reports before release
effect: Radiologist supervision identified 3 of 50 simplified reports requiring corrections before provision to patients.
quote: Only three (of 50) simplified reports required corrections by the radiologist.

title: Leveraging Guideline-Based Clinical Decision Support Systems with Large Language Models: A Case Study with Breast Cancer
outcome: Match of OncoDoc2 recommendations from LLM inputs versus clinician gold standard
effect: Best LLM combination reached 75.57% accuracy on question answering, but only 16.67% of OncoDoc2 recommendations based on LLM inputs matched the gold standard.
quote: However, this approach yielded poor results as a CDSS, with only 16.67% of the recommendations generated by OncoDoc2 based on LLM inputs matching the gold standard.

title: Triaging mammography with artificial intelligence: an implementation study
outcome: Time to additional imaging and biopsy diagnosis with AI prioritization vs standard
effect: Mean time to additional imaging fell 25% (25.6 to 19.1 days, p<0.001); time to biopsy fell 30% (55.9 to 39.2 days, p=0.003); all 6 cancers AI-prioritized.
quote: In comparison, mean T A in the experimental group was reduced by 25% to 19.1 days (ΔT A =−6.4 days, upper limit of one-sided 95% CI = −0.3, p <0.001), while the mean T B was reduced by 30% to 39.2 days (ΔT B =−16.8 days, upper limit of one-sided 95% CI = −5.1, p =0.003).

title: Triaging mammography with artificial intelligence: an implementation study
outcome: Real-world prioritization rate vs retrospective expectation
effect: AI prioritized 29% of cases in deployment vs 14% anticipated from retrospective testing, requiring more immediate reads than planned.
quote: First, the proportion of cases prioritized by AI for immediate radiologist review was 29%, much higher than the proportion anticipated based on retrospective testing (14%).

title: Triaging mammography with artificial intelligence: an implementation study
outcome: Staff capacity to provide immediate interpretation and same-visit diagnostic imaging
effect: Radiologists were unavailable within 30 minutes for 6% (8/131) of prioritized cases; 15% (5/33) needing additional imaging were not offered same-visit imaging for operational reasons.
quote: For 6% (8/131) of AI-prioritized cases, a radiologist was not available to perform an interpretation within 30 minutes; these participants obtained their final screening results by letter as usual (all had negative or benign findings).

title: Triaging mammography with artificial intelligence: an implementation study
outcome: Failures of AI integration with site software
effect: AI integration with site software failed in 3 cases due to a software error.
quote: In 3 cases AI integration with site software failed due to a software error.

title: Abdominal and Pelvic MRI Protocol Prediction Using Natural Language Processing
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Expert review of model protocol errors to judge whether they were correct or reasonable alternatives
effect: Expert review found 81.9% of errors were correct or reasonable alternative protocols, raising real-world accuracy from 88.5% to 97.9%.
quote: Subsequent expert review of the errors performed to satisfy departmental leadership showed 81.9% were in fact correct or reasonable alternative protocols, yielding real-world performance accuracy of 97.9%.

title: Assessing chatbots ability to produce leaflets on cataract surgery: Bing AI, chatGPT 3.5, chatGPT 4o, ChatSonic, Google Bard, Perplexity, and Pi
venue: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery
outcome: Presence of misinformation in chatbot-generated cataract surgery leaflets
effect: Only ChatGPT 3.5 included some misinformation among 7 chatbots; Bing AI, ChatSonic, and Perplexity included reliable references, the other chatbots provided none.
quote: Only ChatGPT 3.5 included some misinformation in its response.

title: Incidence of cardiac arrest following implementation of a predictive analytics display in a pediatric intensive care unit
outcome: Cardiac arrest incidence and return of spontaneous circulation
effect: After display implementation, cardiac arrests decreased from 3.0 to 2.4 per 1000 patient days (non-significant); ROSC increased 50% (p = 0.025); arrests without ROSC decreased from 1.4 to 0.4 per 1000 patient days (p = 0.01).
quote: We observed a non-significant decrease in the rates of cardiac arrest events and an increase in the rate of cardiac arrests events where ROSC was achieved following the implementation of a predictive analytics display of risk scores.

title: Human-centred AI for emergency cardiac care: Evaluating RAPIDx AI with PROLIFERATE_AI
outcome: Usability and workflow integration barriers reported by ED clinicians using RAPIDx AI
effect: Novice users faced usability and workflow integration barriers; residents/interns had the lowest comprehension (median 0.198) and emotional engagement (median 0.112). Experienced clinicians suggested automation and streamlined workflows.
quote: Novice users faced usability and workflow integration barriers, while experienced clinicians suggested automation and streamlined workflows.

title: Human-centred AI for emergency cardiac care: Evaluating RAPIDx AI with PROLIFERATE_AI
outcome: Comprehension and usability differences by user experience level
effect: Registrars had the highest comprehension (median 0.466); residents/interns the lowest (median 0.198). Novices had usability challenges and needed targeted training.
quote: RAPIDx AI enhances diagnostic accuracy and efficiency for experienced users, but usability challenges for novices highlight the need for targeted training and interface refinements.

title: External validation of 12 existing survival prediction models for patients with spinal metastases
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Discrimination (AUC) and calibration of 12 survival models on a local single-center cohort
effect: Revised Katagiri AUC 0.79-0.81, Bollen 0.76-0.77, OSRI 0.75-0.77; other 9 models 0.59-0.76. None of the 12 models had appropriate calibration.
quote: Twelve survival prediction models for patients with spinal metastases yielded poor to fair discrimination and poor calibration.

title: Radiation therapists' perspectives on artificial intelligence: Insights from a single institution on Improving effectiveness and educational supports
venue: Technical innovations & patient support in radiation oncology
outcome: Self-rated AI knowledge and interest in learning among radiation therapists
effect: 37.8% rated their AI knowledge as none or limited; 93.2% expressed interest in learning more about AI; online modules (36.5%) and in-person workshops (35.1%) were the preferred educational supports.
quote: Additionally, 37.8 % rated their knowledge of AI as none or limited, but 93.2 % expressed interest in learning more about AI.

title: Exploring potential drug-drug interactions in discharge prescriptions: ChatGPT's effectiveness in assessing those interactions
venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
outcome: ChatGPT-4.0 pDDI prediction compared with Micromedex checker on the same discharge prescriptions
effect: ChatGPT matched Micromedex for interaction occurrence (100%) but had limited accuracy for severity (37.3%) and moderate accuracy for onset (65.2%).
quote: ChatGPT-4.0 accurately identified pDDIs (100 % for occurrence) but had limited accuracy for severity (37.3 %) and moderate accuracy for onset (65.2 %).

title: Exploring potential drug-drug interactions in discharge prescriptions: ChatGPT's effectiveness in assessing those interactions
venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT drug-interaction knowledge (occurrence, severity, onset) versus Micromedex reference
effect: Occurrence identified 100%; severity accuracy 37.3%; onset accuracy 65.2%, with limits in documentation prediction.
quote: ChatGPT-4.0 accurately identified pDDIs (100 % for occurrence) but had limited accuracy for severity (37.3 %) and moderate accuracy for onset (65.2 %).

title: An interpretable machine learning tool for in-home monitoring of agitation episodes in people living with dementia: a proof-of-concept study
outcome: Performance of actionable traffic-light risk categories versus raw binary classification
effect: Traffic-light categories improved accuracy 71.36 to 78.87, precision 71.81 to 80.06, specificity 75.28 to 90.33, ROC AUC 77.63 to 80.73.
quote: Incorporating a stratification technique via a traffic-light system, which included an additional Amber category (medium probability estimate), increased sensitivity by 5% and specificity by 15% and improved all metrics.
sample_unit: people living with dementia (512 labelled weeks; 32,896 person-days)

title: An interpretable machine learning tool for in-home monitoring of agitation episodes in people living with dementia: a proof-of-concept study
outcome: Robustness to imputation strategies
effect: Final model was robust to different imputation strategies; no numeric values reported in text.
quote: In Table S7 we evaluate the final model's sensitivity to different imputation strategies and find that the model is robust to these approaches.
sample_unit: people living with dementia (512 labelled weeks; 32,896 person-days)

title: An interpretable machine learning tool for in-home monitoring of agitation episodes in people living with dementia: a proof-of-concept study
outcome: Sensitivity versus alternative models
effect: LightGBM sensitivity was significantly higher than logistic regression (p-value < ×10−3) and other tree-based models (p-value < 5 × 10−3).
quote: The LightGBM yielded significantly higher sensitivity than logistic regression ( p − value < ×10 −3 ) and the other examined tree-based models ( p − value < 5 × 10 −3 ) (see Table S5 ).
sample_unit: people living with dementia (512 labelled weeks; 32,896 person-days)

title: ChatGPT 3.5 Better Improves Comprehensibility of English, than Spanish, Generated Responses to Osteosarcoma Questions
outcome: Change in readability after asking ChatGPT to 'Make text easier to understand'
effect: English FRES 51.8 to 63.3 and FKGL 10.51 to 8.27; Spanish FRES 51.6 to 66.1 and FKGL 10.29 to 7.2 (all p<0.001), though simplified text remained above 5th-6th grade level.
quote: While the modifications significantly improved the readability within each respective language, when comparing between English and Spanish it was better at modifying English responses.

title: ChatGPT 3.5 Better Improves Comprehensibility of English, than Spanish, Generated Responses to Osteosarcoma Questions
outcome: Language-stratified comprehensibility
effect: No baseline difference: FRES p = 0.307, FKGL p = 0.294; after modification, language differences were significant: p = 0.003 and p = 0.011.
quote: There was a statistically significant difference in comprehensibility of English responses compared to Spanish responses with FRES and the FKGL after modification between both languages ( p = 0.003 and p = 0.011).

title: ChatGPT 3.5 Better Improves Comprehensibility of English, than Spanish, Generated Responses to Osteosarcoma Questions
outcome: Factual accuracy of osteosarcoma answers
effect: No factually inaccurate English or Spanish responses; average accuracy Likert scores were 4.5 and 4.6.
quote: In both English and Spanish, none of the ChatGPT generated responses were found to be factually inaccurate.

title: ChatGPT 3.5 Better Improves Comprehensibility of English, than Spanish, Generated Responses to Osteosarcoma Questions
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT responses to osteosarcoma questions versus recommended patient reading level
effect: Baseline FKGL 10.51 (English) and 10.29 (Spanish), FRES about 51.7; above the 5th-6th grade recommended level, and still 8.27 and 7.2 after simplification.
quote: Thus, ChatGPT responses for osteosarcoma related queries may not be at an appropriate level for the general population emphasizing the need for physician oversight and simplification command.

title: ChatGPT 3.5 Better Improves Comprehensibility of English, than Spanish, Generated Responses to Osteosarcoma Questions
outcome: reading grade level of AI-generated responses
effect: Baseline English responses had an average FRES of 51.8 and FKGL of 10.51 (10th grade), while Spanish responses had FRES 51.6 and FKGL 10.29, exceeding average patient literacy levels.
quote: The average original FRES was 51.8 making it moderately difficult to understand and the FKGL was 10.51 corresponding to a 10th grade reading level.

title: ChatGPT is a comprehensive education tool for patients with patellar tendinopathy, but it currently lacks accuracy and readability
outcome: Reading level (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of ChatGPT-4 patient education responses
effect: Most responses were written at a college reading level (median FKGL 15.4, IQR 14.4-16.6).
quote: Most responses were written at a college reading level (median and interquartile range [IQR] of FKGL score: 15.4 [14.4-16.6]).

title: ChatGPT is a comprehensive education tool for patients with patellar tendinopathy, but it currently lacks accuracy and readability
outcome: Plain-language readability and understandability/actionability of ChatGPT-4 responses
effect: FKGL median 15.4 (college level); PEMAT understandability median 83% (IQR 70-92%); actionability median 60% (IQR 40-60%).
quote: The median of PEMAT for understandability was 83% (IQR: 70%-92%), and for actionability, it was 60% (IQR: 40%-60%).

title: ChatGPT is a comprehensive education tool for patients with patellar tendinopathy, but it currently lacks accuracy and readability
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of ChatGPT-4 responses to patellar tendinopathy queries
effect: 16 (33%) of 48 responses rated accurate; only 17% of treatment-related questions received accurate responses; 75% comprehensive.
quote: Sixteen (33%) of the 48 responses were rated accurate, while 36 (75%) were rated comprehensive.

title: ChatGPT is a comprehensive education tool for patients with patellar tendinopathy, but it currently lacks accuracy and readability
outcome: Semantic consistency of responses across different terminologies and over two months
effect: Median STS scores over two months and across terminologies were all ≥ 0.9.
quote: The medians of STS scores in the meaning of texts over two months and across terminologies were all ≥ 0.9.

title: Accounting for racial bias and social determinants of health in a model of hypertension control
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: False positive and false negative rates by race at standard 0.5 threshold
effect: FPR 27.71% for Black vs 5.92% for White patients (factor 4.68); FNR 43.11% vs 73.82% (factor 0.58); FPR/FNR 8 times higher for Black patients.
quote: These statistics demonstrate that the models are biased and are more likely to classify Black patients as belonging to the very high SBP group.

title: Accounting for racial bias and social determinants of health in a model of hypertension control
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Effect of race-specific decision thresholds on error-rate parity between Black and White patients
effect: Thresholds of 0.296 (Black) and 0.245 (White) equalized FNR at 25%; FPR became 41.11% vs 47.20%; FPR/FNR ratio factor 0.87 versus ~8 before. Weighted F1 fell to 65.77% and 60.91%.
quote: The resulting FPR of the model for Black patients becomes 41.11% and the FPR for White patient model becomes 47.20%.

title: Accounting for racial bias and social determinants of health in a model of hypertension control
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Influence of race as a model input on predictions and bias
effect: Race_Black was the third most important feature (OR 1.94, CI 1.90-1.98); the non-stratified model showed implicit racial disparity.
quote: We found implicit racial disparity in the non-stratified predictive model.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Generate Clinical Histories for Oncologic Imaging Requisitions
outcome: LLM-generated vs original physician requisition histories: completeness, quality, radiologist preference, perceived harm
effect: LLM histories more often included primary diagnosis (99.5% vs 89%), acute symptoms (15% vs 4%), surgery (61% vs 12%); radiologists preferred LLM histories 89% vs 5%; lower likelihood of harm 3% vs 55%.
quote: Compared with original requisition histories, LLM-generated histories were more complete and were preferred by radiologists for imaging interpretation and perceived safety.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Generate Clinical Histories for Oncologic Imaging Requisitions
outcome: Radiologist review of LLM-generated histories against reference standard and original histories for quality and harm
effect: GPT-4 extracted oncologic parameters from clinical notes with F1 = 0.983; 10 radiologists preferred LLM histories 89% vs 5% and rated lower likelihood of harm (3% vs 55%).
quote: Radiologists preferred LLM-generated histories for imaging interpretation (89% vs 5%, 7% equal; P < .001), indicating they would enable more complete interpretation (86% vs 0%, 15% equal; P < .001) and have a lower likelihood of harm (3% vs 55%, 42% neither; P < .001).

title: Development, validation, and clinical evaluation of a machine-learning based model for diagnosing early infection after cardiovascular surgery (DEICS): a multi-center cohort study
outcome: Discrimination of candidate ML models versus traditional logistic regression for early postoperative infection
effect: XGBoost had the highest AUROC, 0.96 (95% CI 0.93-0.98), and was chosen over the other ML models and the logistic regression comparator; Brier score 0.02.
quote: The XGBoost model achieved the highest performance with an AUROC of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.93-0.98).

title: Development, validation, and clinical evaluation of a machine-learning based model for diagnosing early infection after cardiovascular surgery (DEICS): a multi-center cohort study
outcome: ICU stay, hospital costs and antibiotic use density with model-guided versus empirical antibiotic upgrade
effect: The model-guided group had lower AUD (P<0.01), shorter ICU stay (median 5 vs 6 days, P=0.01) and lower costs (median ¥150,000 vs ¥200,000, P=0.01). The matched comparison was retrospective, not randomized.
quote: According to the XGBoost model, the DEICS group significantly demonstrated reduced AUD ( P < 0.01) in the matched cohort, along with decreased ICU stay time (median: 5 vs. 6 days, P = 0.01) and hospital costs (median: ¥150 000 vs. median: ¥200 000, P = 0.01) in the EPI cohort.

title: Consecutive prediction of adverse maternal outcomes of preeclampsia, using the PIERS-ML and fullPIERS models: A multicountry prospective observational study
outcome: Model discrimination and net benefit when extended to consecutive daily prediction beyond 48 h
effect: fullPIERS AUC-PRC stayed low (0.2-0.4); PIERS-ML AUC-PRC peaked at 0.65 on day 0 then decreased notably; decision curve advantage diminished over time.
quote: We observed deteriorating performance of both models over time.
country: Multicountry (Americas, sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Europe, Oceania)

title: Consecutive prediction of adverse maternal outcomes of preeclampsia, using the PIERS-ML and fullPIERS models: A multicountry prospective observational study
outcome: Performance of models used outside intended initial-assessment use (repeated use past 48 h)
effect: PIERS-ML performance declined notably for most risk groups beyond 48 h; fullPIERS AUC-PRC (0.2-0.4) close to daily fraction of adverse outcomes, indicating low discriminative capacity.
quote: We recommend using the models for consecutive prediction with greater caution and interpreting predictions with increasing uncertainty as the pregnancy progresses.
country: Multicountry (Americas, sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Europe, Oceania)

title: Screening performance and characteristics of breast cancer detected in the Mammography Screening with Artificial Intelligence trial (MASAI): a randomised, controlled, parallel-group, non-inferiority, single-blinded, screening accuracy study
outcome: Cancer detection with AI-supported screening versus standard double reading
effect: Cancer-detection rates were 6·4 per 1000 (95% CI 5·7-7·1) versus 5·0 per 1000 (4·4-5·6); ratio 1·29 (95% CI 1·09-1·51; p=0·0021).
quote: Cancer-detection rates were 6·4 per 1000 (95% CI 5·7-7·1) screened participants in the intervention group and 5·0 per 1000 (4·4-5·6) in the control group, a ratio of 1·29 (95% CI 1·09-1·51; p=0·0021).

title: Overcoming barriers and enabling artificial intelligence adoption in allied health clinical practice: A qualitative study
outcome: Barriers to AI adoption perceived by allied health professionals, including AI knowledge
effect: Twenty-four barriers and 24 enablers were identified by 25 participants across four focus groups; lack of AI knowledge was among the barriers, and AI training and education was among the enablers.
quote: Barriers included: lack of AI knowledge, explainability challenges, risk to professional practice, negative impact on professional practice, and role replacement.

title: Performance of Lung Cancer Prediction Models for Screening-detected, Incidental, and Biopsied Pulmonary Nodules
outcome: Generalization of lung cancer prediction models across clinical settings and sites outside training distribution
effect: Eight models failed to generalize across clinical settings and sites; single-time-point CT AI performed well on screening nodules but not other settings; all models performed poorly on biopsied nodules.
quote: Eight lung cancer prediction models failed to generalize well across clinical settings and sites outside of their training distributions.

title: GPT-4 assistance for improvement of physician performance on patient care tasks: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: Physician management reasoning score with GPT-4 plus conventional resources versus conventional resources alone
effect: LLM-assisted physicians scored 6.5% higher (95% CI 2.7 to 10.2, P<0.001); no significant difference between LLM-augmented physicians and LLM alone (-0.9%, P=0.8); LLM users spent 119.3 s more per case.
quote: Physicians using the LLM scored significantly higher compared to those using conventional resources (mean difference = 6.5%, 95% confidence interval (CI) = 2.7 to 10.2, P < 0.001).

title: Towards human-AI collaboration in radiology: a multidimensional evaluation of the acceptability of AI for chest radiograph analysis in supporting pulmonary tuberculosis diagnosis
outcome: Local diagnostic accuracy of qXR for TB versus radiologist and microbiological reference standard
effect: qXR showed near-human performance and met the WHO suggested accuracy profile; no numeric values reported in the abstract.
quote: qXR displays near-human performance satisfying the World Health Organization's suggested accuracy profile.

title: Towards human-AI collaboration in radiology: a multidimensional evaluation of the acceptability of AI for chest radiograph analysis in supporting pulmonary tuberculosis diagnosis
outcome: Radiologist-reported workflow disruption and workload burden with AI
effect: Radiologists reported high satisfaction, minimal workflow disruption, and limited increases in workload burden.
quote: Radiologists reported high satisfaction with using qXR based on minimal workflow disruptions, respect for their professional autonomy, and limited increases in workload burden despite poor algorithm explainability.

title: Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Virtual Assistant for Emergency Triage in Neurology
outcome: Virtual assistant diagnostic and safety performance versus ChatGPT 3.5 and 4, rated by neurologists
effect: VA superior to both ChatGPT versions in all evaluated diagnostic and safety aspects (P<0.0001).
quote: VA showed superiority over both versions of ChatGPT in all evaluated diagnostic and safety aspects ( P <0.0001).

title: Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Virtual Assistant for Emergency Triage in Neurology
outcome: Neurologist agreement with AI outputs on real patient inputs and assistant recommendations
effect: Neurologists agreed with VA in 98.5% of cases for syndromic diagnosis; definitive diagnosis always in top 5 differentials; agreed with all diagnostic parameters and recommendations in stage 2.
quote: In stage 1, neurologists agreed with the VA in 98.5% of the cases for syndromic diagnosis, and in all cases, the definitive diagnosis was among the top 5 differentials.

title: Advancing Privacy-Preserving Health Care Analytics and Implementation of the Personal Health Train: Federated Deep Learning Study
outcome: Whether patient-level data stayed inside hospital environments during federated model training
effect: No data were shared outside the hospital during execution and training across 12 hospitals in 8 nations; a secure aggregation server was used for model averaging.
quote: During the execution and training of the deep learning algorithm, no data were shared outside the hospital.

title: Impact of pectoral muscle removal on deep-learning-based breast cancer risk prediction
outcome: 1-5 year breast cancer risk discrimination (AUC) after fine-tuning MIRAI on local Slovenian mammograms
effect: Fine-tuned MIRAI on mammograms with pectoral muscle removed reached AUC 0.82-0.93 with screening positive exams and 0.71-0.79 without, versus 0.77-0.91 and 0.64-0.67 for Original MIRAI.
quote: Fine-tuned MIRAI on mammograms with PM removed achieved significantly higher 1-5 Year BCR discrimination performance (with screening positive exams: 0.82-0.93, without screening positive exams: 0.71-0.79).

title: Quality of Information on Wilms Tumor From Artificial Intelligence Chatbots: What Are Your Patients and Their Families Reading?
outcome: Reading level (Flesch-Kincaid) of chatbot outputs on Wilms tumor
effect: Median Flesch-Kincaid Readability 46.7 (IQR 41.1-52.2), advanced reading ease comparable to a high school or college student.
quote: The median word count per output from the AIs was 275 (IQR 156-322), with an advanced ease of reading level comparable to a high school or college student, median Flesch-Kincaid Readability level of 46.7 (IQR 41.1-52.2).

title: Unveiling GPT-4V's hidden challenges behind high accuracy on USMLE questions: Observational Study
outcome: Gap between exam-question accuracy and explanation quality/image interpretation of GPT-4V
effect: High accuracy (73.1-88.9%) but among incorrect answers 18.2% (10/55) inaccurate text, 45.5% (25/55) inference errors, 76.3% (42/55) image misunderstandings.
quote: However, incorrect answers often had poor explanation quality: 18.2% (10/55) contained inaccurate text, 45.5% (25/55) had inference errors, and 76.3% (42/55) demonstrated image misunderstandings.

title: Unveiling GPT-4V's hidden challenges behind high accuracy on USMLE questions: Observational Study
outcome: Effect of human expert assistance on GPT-4V errors
effect: With human expert assistance, GPT-4V reduced errors by an average of 40% (22/55); image interpretation flaws not efficiently resolved through expert interaction.
quote: With human expert assistance, GPT-4V reduced errors by an average of 40% (22/55).

title: Instability of the AUROC of Clinical Prediction Models
outcome: Between-study variation in AUC across external validations of the same model
effect: Mean tau of 0.055 (SD 0.015); with tau=0.05 the 95% prediction interval for AUC in a new setting is at least +/-0.1 regardless of validation count.
quote: If τ$$ \tau $$ = 0.05, then the 95% prediction interval for the AUC in a new setting has a width of at least +/-$$ +/- $$ 0.1, no matter how many validations have been done.

title: Instability of the AUROC of Clinical Prediction Models
outcome: Heterogeneity of AUC across settings due to population, standard of care, and predictor definitions
effect: Large heterogeneity among validated AUCs gives great irreducible uncertainty in predicting AUC in a new setting; frequentist methods underestimate this uncertainty with fewer than 5 validations.
quote: Due to large heterogeneity among the validated AUC values of a CPM, there is great irreducible uncertainty in predicting the AUC in a new setting.

title: Artificial intelligence for direct-to-physician reporting of ambulatory electrocardiography
outcome: Ground truth via cardiologist consensus panels annotating sampled events
effect: Random sample of 5,235 rhythm events, including 2,236 critical arrhythmias, was annotated by one of 17 cardiologist consensus panels to compare AI and technicians.
quote: To compare the performance of the AI model and the technicians, a random sample of 5,235 rhythm events identified by the AI model or by technicians, of which 2,236 events were identified as critical arrhythmias, was selected for annotation by one of 17 cardiologist consensus panels.

title: Comparative evaluation and performance of large language models on expert level critical care questions: a benchmark study
outcome: Consistency of LLM answers across repeated runs on critical care MCQs
effect: Overall consistency was high, but all models gave consistently incorrect answers to some questions.
quote: Despite high overall consistency, all models gave consistently incorrect answers.

title: [EMERGING THERAPIES FOR LI-FRAUMENI SYNDROME AND RHABDOMYOSARCOMA: CAN CHAT GPT ASSESS THE THERAPIES IT SUGGESTS USING THE BRADFORD-HILL CRITERIA?]
outcome: Accuracy and clinical usefulness by prompt structure
effect: Targeted prompts generated more accurate and clinically useful responses; no numerical results reported.
quote: Targeted prompts (instructions for structuring the response, formulated as questions) lead to the generation of more accurate and clinically useful model responses but these, too, should be approached with caution.

title: [EMERGING THERAPIES FOR LI-FRAUMENI SYNDROME AND RHABDOMYOSARCOMA: CAN CHAT GPT ASSESS THE THERAPIES IT SUGGESTS USING THE BRADFORD-HILL CRITERIA?]
outcome: informativeness of AI treatment suggestions
effect: Treatment suggestions based solely on the case presentation and a general question were found to be insufficiently informative.
quote: In-depth exploration suggested that ChatGPT treatment suggestions based solely on the presentation of the case and a general question are insufficiently informative.

title: Advancing health equity: evaluating AI translations of kidney donor information for Spanish speakers
outcome: Linguistic accuracy of AI Spanish translations rated by native-speaking nephrologists (1-5)
effect: Mean linguistic accuracy 4.89 ± 0.32 for GPT-3.5 and 5.00 ± 0.00 for GPT-4.0 (p = 0.08); excellent translations 89% vs 100% (p = 0.24).
quote: The mean linguistic accuracy scores were 4.89 ± 0.32 for GPT-3.5 and 5.00 ± 0.00 for GPT-4.0 (p = 0.08).

title: Smart Pharmaceutical Monitoring System With Personalized Medication Schedules and Self-Management Programs for Patients With Diabetes: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: Expert-rated medication schedule accuracy and safety: evidence-database-constrained system vs ungrounded GPT-4
effect: DUMS vs GPT-4 accuracy 4.43 vs 3.84 and safety 4.44 vs 3.91 (both P<.001); total score 37.96 vs 36.35 (P<.001).
