quote: The evaluation results revealed that the DUMS group achieved significantly higher accuracy and safety scores than the GPT-4 group ( P <.001), with full consideration of multiple aspects of DDI, pharmacokinetics, and dietary restrictions.
sample_unit: prescriptions of older patients with diabetes (60 medication plans rated by 12 specialists)

title: Smart Pharmaceutical Monitoring System With Personalized Medication Schedules and Self-Management Programs for Patients With Diabetes: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: Head-to-head expert ratings of DUMS, pharmacist-refined output, and GPT-4 on same prescriptions
effect: Total scores: DUMS 37.96, intervention 39.52, GPT-4 36.35 (all pairwise P<.001); DUMS outperformed GPT-4 on accuracy, safety, comprehensiveness, richness.
quote: The total evaluation scores showed that the mean values of the DUMS group, intervention group, and GPT-4 group were 37.96 (SD 0.56), 39.52 (SD 0.80), and 36.35 (SD 0.89), respectively.
sample_unit: prescriptions of older patients with diabetes (60 medication plans rated by 12 specialists)

title: Smart Pharmaceutical Monitoring System With Personalized Medication Schedules and Self-Management Programs for Patients With Diabetes: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: medication schedule and self-management program performance compared to software and clinicians
effect: DUMS and pharmacist refinement scored significantly higher than GPT-4 in schedule accuracy (4.43 and 4.49 vs 3.84), safety (4.44 vs 3.91), and total scores (37.96 and 39.52 vs 36.35; all P<.001).
quote: Reliability analysis demonstrated that the DUMS group outperformed the GPT-4 group in medication schedule accuracy and safety, as well as comprehensiveness and richness of the self-management program (P<.001).
sample_unit: prescriptions of older patients with diabetes (60 medication plans rated by 12 specialists)

title: Deep learning-based video-level view classification of two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography
outcome: Accuracy drop from held-out test set to field deployment for view classification
effect: Overall accuracy 0.9881 on test set versus 0.9607 after field deployment; recall 0.9867 vs 0.9499; F1 0.9867 vs 0.9530.
quote: After field deployment, the model's overall accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score for view classification were 0.9607, 0.9586, 0.9499, and 0.9530, respectively.

title: Chat GPT vs. Clinical Decision Support Systems in the Analysis of Drug-Drug Interactions
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT pDDI results across repeated queries
effect: Repeating each query yielded inconsistent results in 90% of cases.
quote: To assess the consistency of the results provided by Chat GPT, we repeated each query and found inconsistent results in 90% of the cases.

title: Chat GPT vs. Clinical Decision Support Systems in the Analysis of Drug-Drug Interactions
outcome: ChatGPT detection of clinically relevant drug-drug interactions versus CDSSs
effect: ChatGPT identified 80 pDDIs versus 280 with CDSSs; QTc-prolongation pDDIs almost entirely missed (85 vs. 8); obvious errors and inconsistent results.
quote: Chat GPT almost entirely neglected pDDIs with the risk to QTc prolongation (85 vs. 8), which could also not be sufficiently improved by using a specific prompt.

title: ChatGPT versus physician-derived answers to drug-related questions
outcome: Whether ChatGPT answers included supporting references or sources
effect: References did not accompany ChatGPT answers; it did not elaborate on the most clinically relevant option when giving multiple answers. Authors conclude this makes it less useful as a primary information source.
quote: References did not accompany answers from ChatGPT, and ChatGPT did not elaborate on what would be considered most clinically relevant when providing multiple answers.

title: Artificial Intelligence Shows Limited Success in Improving Readability Levels of Spanish-language Orthopaedic Patient Education Materials
outcome: Reading grade level of AAOS Spanish patient education materials versus recommended sixth grade
effect: None of 77 materials met the recommended sixth-grade level or below by both formulas; 32% (25 of 77) were written at a seventh- to eighth-grade level.
quote: Before AI adaptations, none of the 77 education materials met the recommended reading level of sixth grade or below according to both readability formulas.

title: Artificial Intelligence Shows Limited Success in Improving Readability Levels of Spanish-language Orthopaedic Patient Education Materials
outcome: Readability of AI-adapted Spanish patient education materials versus recommended sixth-grade level
effect: After a single simplification attempt, only 23% (18) and 16% (12) of AI adaptations were at or below sixth grade per Fernández-Huerta and SOL; 52% rated accurate, 56% useful.
quote: Only 23% (18) and 16% (12) of the AI adaptations were written at or below the recommended sixth-grade level per the Fernández-Huerta and SOL grade levels, respectively.

title: Artificial Intelligence Shows Limited Success in Improving Readability Levels of Spanish-language Orthopaedic Patient Education Materials
outcome: AI-adapted accuracy and usefulness
effect: 52% (40) were rated accurate and 56% (43) useful by evaluating orthopaedic surgeons.
quote: Of the AI adaptations, 52% (40) were rated as accurate and 56% (43) were rated as useful for patient education by the evaluating orthopaedic surgeons.

title: Assessing ChatGPT Responses to Frequently Asked Patient Questions in Reconstructive Urology
outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT-4o responses to reconstructive urology questions
effect: Responses were at a college graduate reading level.
quote: Responses were at a college graduate reading level.

title: Assessing ChatGPT Responses to Frequently Asked Patient Questions in Reconstructive Urology
outcome: understandability and actionability
effect: Prompt engineering improved understandability 89.6% to 96.2% and actionability 38.3% to 93.5% (both P < .001).
quote: Using prompt engineering in the incontinence domain, scores for DISCERN (3.57-4.75, P = .007), PEMAT-P understandability (89.6% to 96.2%, P < .001), actionability (38.3% to 93.5%, P < .001), and reading level (grade 12.4-5.4, P < .01) all improved significantly while misinformation and word count did not change significantly.

title: What makes a 'good' decision with artificial intelligence? A grounded theory study in paediatric care
outcome: Automation bias when model explanation conflicted with clinician prior knowledge
effect: Many participants assumed their own judgement was incorrect when the model's explanation conflicted with it; others rejected the incorrect explanation using their medical knowledge.
quote: We found evidence of automation bias, with many participants assuming that if the model's explanation conflicted with their prior knowledge that their judgement was incorrect; others concluded the exact opposite, drawing from their medical knowledge base to reject the incorrect information provided in the explanation.

title: Evaluating the utility of ChatGPT in enhancing parental education and clinical support in hypospadias care
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of ChatGPT responses on hypospadias diagnosis, treatment, and postoperative care
effect: 41% of responses completely accurate, 35% accurate but inadequate, 24% inaccurate; Fleiss' Kappa 0.607 among six pediatric urologists.
quote: In the qualitative assessment, 41 % of responses were deemed completely accurate, with 35 % considered accurate but inadequate, and 24 % rated as inaccurate.

title: Evaluation of large language models for providing educational information in orthokeratology care
venue: Contact lens & anterior eye : the journal of the British Contact Lens Association
outcome: Readability of LLM responses on orthokeratology rated by ophthalmologists and parents
effect: GPT-4 readability 3.79 ± 1.03, lower than Yi-34B (4.65 ± 0.51) and Qwen-72B (4.65 ± 0.61) (P < 0.001).
quote: GPT-4 (3.79 ± 1.03) scored lower in readability than Yi-34B (4.65 ± 0.51) and Qwen-72B (4.65 ± 0.61) (P < 0.001).

title: Exploring the Utility of ChatGPT in Cleft Lip Repair Education
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT cleft lip patient education responses (FRES, FKGL)
effect: Mean FRES 44.35 and FKGL 10.87, approximately a 10th-grade literacy level, above the commonly recommended patient-material reading level.
quote: Readability metrics revealed a mean FRES of 44.35 and a FKGL of 10.87, corresponding to approximately a 10th-grade literacy standard.

title: Exploring the Utility of ChatGPT in Cleft Lip Repair Education
outcome: Presence of citations/sources in ChatGPT responses to cleft lip questions
effect: None of the responses contained grossly inaccurate or harmful information, but the responses lacked citations.
quote: None of the responses contained grossly inaccurate or potentially harmful medical information but lacked citations.

title: Validation of 30-Day Pediatric Hospital Readmission Risk Prediction Models
outcome: Performance of derivation-hospital models on temporal and external hospitals (dataset shift)
effect: Temporal validation median AUROC fell to 0.65 NAM, 0.73 RAM, 0.67 YIM vs original 0.76, 0.84, 0.79. External validation showed similar findings with hospital-level variation.
quote: Temporal validation demonstrated reduced discrimination across all 3 models (median AUROC, 0.65 [95% CI 0.62-0.67] for the NAM; 0.73 [95% CI 0.72-0.75) for RAM; 0.67 [95% CI 0.63-0.70) for the YIM compared with the original estimates (median AUROC 0.76 [95% CI 0.85-0.78] for the NAM; 0.84 [95% CI 0.83-0.84] for the RAM; 0.79 [95% CI 0.77-0.80] for the YIM).

title: Validation of 30-Day Pediatric Hospital Readmission Risk Prediction Models
outcome: Calibration and discrimination of models at other hospitals versus developer estimates
effect: Only 3 hospitals for RAM (6.4%) and 9 for NAM and YIM (19.1%) were adequately calibrated; most hospitals had over- or underestimation of risk.
quote: Of 47 other PHIS hospitals, only 3 for the RAM (6.4%) and 9 for both the NAM and YIM (19.1%) were adequately calibrated.

title: Validation of 30-Day Pediatric Hospital Readmission Risk Prediction Models
outcome: Variation in model AUROC across hospitals
effect: External validation median (range) AUROC 0.64 (0.60-0.68) NAM, 0.73 (0.64-0.80) RAM, 0.65 (0.53-0.74) YIM, showing demonstrable variation across hospitals.
quote: External validation yielded similiar findings as the temporal validation, although with demonstrable variation in performance across hospitals (median [range] AUROC, 0.64 [0.60-0.68] for the NAM; 0.73 [0.64-0.80] for the RAM; 0.65 [0.53-0.74] for the YIM).

title: Validation of 30-Day Pediatric Hospital Readmission Risk Prediction Models
outcome: Temporal degradation of model discrimination from derivation period to 2019
effect: Median AUROC declined across all three models in temporal validation, e.g., NAM 0.76 to 0.65, RAM 0.84 to 0.73, YIM 0.79 to 0.67.
quote: This prognostic study found that the readmission risk prediction models had reduced predictive accuracy across time and variability in hospital-level performance.

title: Evaluation and failure analysis of four commercial deep learning-based autosegmentation software for abdominal organs at risk
venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
outcome: Causes of autosegmentation outliers under real-world imaging variations such as contrast and devices
effect: Barium contrast caused incomplete stomach delineation in 10/12 Limbus outliers and 21/25 Radformation outliers; IV contrast linked to fragmented kidney contours in MIM (25/26 outliers).
quote: Only Limbus and Radformation provided stomach segmentation, and imaging with barium contrast directly caused incomplete stomach delineation in 10/12 Limbus outliers and 21/25 Radformation outliers.

title: Optimising test intervals for individuals with type 2 diabetes: A machine learning approach
outcome: Model fairness across income and education subgroups
effect: Fairness metric suggests models perform well in terms of equality across income and education levels; AUC ranged 0.53 to 0.89 across test intervals.
quote: The fairness metric suggests models perform well in terms of equality.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Ability to Address Frequently Asked Questions in Gender-Affirmation Surgery
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses to gender-affirmation surgery questions versus physician responses
effect: ChatGPT responses were significantly more complex across five readability metrics than physician responses, though they scored higher on DISCERN and PEMAT. The authors note the high reading level raises implementation concerns.
quote: We found that ChatGPT's responses were significantly more complex across five readability metrics but had significantly higher DISCERN and PEMAT scores compared to physician responses, indicating superior reliability, quality, and understandability.

title: Transforming Informed Consent Generation Using Large Language Models: Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Readability and understandability of LLM-generated consent form key information versus human-written
effect: LLM RUAKI readability 76.39% vs 66.67%; Flesch-Kincaid grade level 7.95 vs 8.38; understandability 90.63% vs 67.19% (P=.02); actionability 100% vs 0% (P<.001).
quote: The LLM outperformed human-generated ICFs in readability (Readability, Understandability, and Actionability of Key Information score of 76.39% vs 66.67%; Flesch-Kincaid grade level of 7.95 vs 8.38) and understandability (90.63% vs 67.19%; P=.02).
sample_unit: clinical trial protocols (key information sections of informed consent forms)

title: An Explainable AI Application (AF'fective) to Support Monitoring of Patients With Atrial Fibrillation After Catheter Ablation: Qualitative Focus Group, Design Session, and Interview Study
outcome: Cardiologists' rating of explainability strategies and physician motivation to adopt an explainable AI app
effect: 4 of 7 explainability strategies were deemed highly effective and feasible for pilot. The prototype had above-average user experience ratings and motivated adoption through ease of use, reliable information, and explainable functionality.
quote: A total of 4 strategies were deemed highly effective and feasible for pilot deployment.

title: Automated hallucination detection for synthetic CT images used in MR-only radiotherapy workflows
outcome: Automated detection of false bone/air hallucinations in AI-generated sCT images
effect: Screener specificity 0.78, 0.93, 0.98 at distance parameters 0.8, 1.0, 1.2 cm; flagged false high-density hallucinations in abdomen of sCT for all test patients.
quote: The average specificity of the DLAS model was 0.78, 0.93 and 0.98 for distance parameters of 0.8, 1.0 and 1.2 cm, respectively.

title: Automated hallucination detection for synthetic CT images used in MR-only radiotherapy workflows
outcome: Presence of AI-generated hallucinations (false bone) in commercial sCT images
effect: Screener identified false high-density hallucination regions in the abdomen of AI-generated sCT images for all testing patients (n=10).
quote: The screener identified false high-density hallucination regions in the abdomen of AI-generated sCT images for all testing patients, highlighting potential issues with the training data used for the AI sCT model.

title: Evaluation of the Performance of Three Large Language Models in Clinical Decision Support: A Comparative Study Based on Actual Cases
outcome: LLM diagnosis, differential diagnosis, examination and treatment quality scored by experts on real cases
effect: Med-Go median 37.5 (IQR 31.9-41.5), Gemini 33.0 (IQR 25.5-36.6), p<0.001; differential diagnosis weakest, treatment strongest; inaccuracies could lead to adverse decisions.
quote: Analysis revealed that responses related to differential diagnosis were the weakest, while those pertaining to treatment recommendations were the strongest.

title: Progression-Free Survival Prediction Performance of ChatGPT: Analysis With Real Life Data in Early and Locally Advanced Prostate Cancer
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-predicted progression-free survival versus actual PFS from real patient data
effect: ChatGPT overestimated PFS; significant discrepancy between predicted and actual (p < 0.05); mean discrepancy 9.19 months; bias 48.57; Cohen's d = 0.189.
quote: The AI chatbot tended to overestimate the overall PFS times.

title: A Review of ChatGPT as a Reliable Source of Scientific Information Regarding Endodontic Local Anesthesia
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-provided references (wrong, unretrievable, or fabricated citations)
effect: Of 51 references, 59% (30) wrong, 12% (6) could not be retrieved, 18% (9) hallucinated (made up).
quote: Of the 51 total references for Chatbot, 59% (30 of 51) had the wrong reference, 12% (6 of 51) of the references couldn't be retrieved and 18% (9 of 51) of the references were hallucinations (made up references).

title: A Review of ChatGPT as a Reliable Source of Scientific Information Regarding Endodontic Local Anesthesia
outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT answers with peer-reviewed evidence-based literature on endodontic anesthesia
effect: ChatGPT matched literature-based responses in 16 of 32 questions (50% reliable).
quote: ChatGPT was reliable 50% of the time when compared to the peer-reviewed, evidence-based literature.

title: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons OrthoInfo provides more readable information regarding rotator cuff injury than ChatGPT
venue: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
outcome: Readability grade level and Flesch Reading Ease of ChatGPT vs OrthoInfo responses on rotator cuff injury
effect: ChatGPT average grade level 14.7 vs OrthoInfo 11.9 (p<0.01); Flesch Reading Ease 25.9 vs 52.5 (p<0.01).
quote: ChatGPT responses required a higher education level to comprehend, with an average grade level of 14.7, compared to OrthoInfo's 11.9 (p ​< ​0.01).

title: Artificial intelligence for individualized treatment of persistent atrial fibrillation: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: Freedom from documented AF at 12 months, AI-guided tailored ablation vs PVI-only, plus safety
effect: Primary endpoint met: 88% tailored vs 70% anatomical (log-rank P<0.0001). No significant difference in freedom from any atrial arrhythmia after one ablation. Safety endpoint did not differ; procedure and ablation times twice as long.
quote: However, no significant difference between arms was observed for the freedom from any atrial arrhythmia endpoint after one ablation.

title: Perioperative goal-directed therapy with artificial intelligence to reduce the incidence of intraoperative hypotension and renal failure in patients undergoing lung surgery: A pilot study
outcome: Intraoperative hypotension, postoperative AKI, MINS versus standard care in RCT
effect: Hypotension duration was shorter with HPI (0 vs 2.33 min; p=0.01), but AKI did not differ (6.7% vs 4.2%; p=0.72). MINS trend was lower (17.1% vs 31.8%; p=0.07).
quote: The incidence of postoperative AKI showed no differences between the groups (6.7 % vs.4.2 %; p = 0.72).

title: Perioperative goal-directed therapy with artificial intelligence to reduce the incidence of intraoperative hypotension and renal failure in patients undergoing lung surgery: A pilot study
outcome: Frequency and duration of hypotension with HPI-guided treatment versus no specific hemodynamic protocol
effect: HPI-guided treatment reduced hypotensive episodes: 0 [0-1] vs. 1 [0-2]; p = 0.01; and duration: 0 min [0-3.17] vs. 2.33 min [0-7.42]; p = 0.01.
quote: The number of hypotensive episodes was lower in the intervention group compared to the control group (0 [0-1] vs. 1 [0-2]; p = 0.01), the duration of hypotension was shorter in the intervention group (0 min [0-3.17] vs. 2.33 min [0-7.42]; p = 0.01).

title: Evaluating large language model performance to support the diagnosis and management of patients with primary immune disorders
venue: The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and clinical reasoning quality (R-IDEA) of LLMs on rare primary immune disorder vignettes
effect: Three models had accuracy >88% and R-IDEA ≥8 (GPT-4o 96.2%); the other three had accuracy near 60% or lower and R-IDEA ≤0.55 (Mistral-7B 42.3%).
quote: Conversely, the remaining 3 models fell below acceptable accuracy rates near 60% or lower and had poor R-IDEA scores (≤0.55), with Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 attaining the worst diagnostic accuracy (42.3%).

title: A Cross-Sectional Study Comparing Patient Education Guides Created by ChatGPT and Google Gemini for Common Cardiovascular-Related Conditions
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid readability (ease and grade level) of AI-generated patient education guides
effect: Flesch reading ease was 41.75 for Gemini vs 34.10 for ChatGPT (p = 0.080, not significant); grade level did not differ significantly between tools. Authors judged readability adequate.
quote: Although Google Gemini had a higher ease score (41.75) compared to ChatGPT (34.10), this difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.080).

title: Evaluating large language models as patient education tools for inflammatory bowel disease: A comparative study
outcome: Readability and comprehensibility of LLM answers to IBD patient questions
effect: Models were rated satisfactory for comprehensibility overall, but readability differed: Claude-3-Opus answers had better readability than the other two models. No numbers given in the abstract.
quote: Notably, Claude-3-Opus generated answers with better readability than the other two models.

title: Enhancing Patient Education on Cardiovascular Rehabilitation with Large Language Models
outcome: Readability of LLM cardiac rehabilitation education responses (Gunning Fog, Flesch-Kincaid, Flesch Reading Ease)
effect: Mean readability scores did not meet US grade reading level recommendations for ChatGPT 3.5, Copilot, and Gemini; Gemini and Copilot were easier to read than ChatGPT 3.5.
quote: The findings of this study demonstrate that the mean Gunning Fog, Flesch Kincaid, and Flesch Reading Ease scores do not meet US grade reading level recommendations across three models: ChatGPT 3.5, Copilot, and Gemini.

title: Readability of Hospital Online Patient Education Materials Across Otolaryngology Specialties
outcome: Reading grade level of hospital and national organization patient education materials versus NIH sixth-grade standard
effect: Nearly all OPEMs exceeded NIH readability standards, averaging 8th-12th grade level across subspecialties; AAO, CSOHNS and ALA materials were harder to read than hospital materials (e.g., AAO 13.3 in head and neck).
quote: This study reveals that nearly all otolaryngology OPEMs exceed NIH readability guidelines, creating significant barriers to patient comprehension.
sample_unit: hospitals (online patient education materials for seven otolaryngology procedures)

title: Readability of Hospital Online Patient Education Materials Across Otolaryngology Specialties
outcome: Readability, accuracy, content and tone of ChatGPT-4o generated patient education materials versus hospital and organization materials
effect: ChatGPT OPEMs averaged 6.8 grade level, more readable than hospital and organization OPEMs (p ≤ 0.016) with accuracy 4.8-4.9/5; re-prompting for below sixth grade lowered content scores.
quote: ChatGPT‐4o generated OPEMs were consistently more readable than both hospital and institutional OPEMs across all specialties ( p ≤ 0.016), except for ENTUK in facial plastics (6.6 vs. 7.2, p = 0.219).
sample_unit: hospitals (online patient education materials for seven otolaryngology procedures)

title: Readability of Hospital Online Patient Education Materials Across Otolaryngology Specialties
outcome: ChatGPT OPEM patient-centered tone
effect: Patient-centered tone was 4.9/5 for sleep medicine and 5/5 for others.
quote: ChatGPT‐generated OPEMs also scored highly for accuracy (4.8/5 to 4.9/5) and patient‐centered tone (4.9/5 for sleep medicine, 5/5 for others).
sample_unit: hospitals (online patient education materials for seven otolaryngology procedures)

title: Comparison of 1-year mortality predictions from vendor-supplied versus academic model for cancer patients
outcome: Local AUC of vendor EOLCI for 1-year mortality versus vendor-stated AUC
effect: EOLCI AUC 0.73 (95% CI 0.70-0.76) vs vendor-stated 0.86; academic model AUC 0.82 (0.80-0.85). PPV 0.38 vs 0.65.
quote: The EOLCI's discrimination performance was lower than the vendor-stated value (AUC of 0.86) and the academic model's performance.

title: Comparison of 1-year mortality predictions from vendor-supplied versus academic model for cancer patients
outcome: Vendor model compared against academic model on same patients for 1-year mortality AUC and PPV
effect: AUC 0.73 (EOLCI) vs 0.82 (academic); PPV 0.38 vs 0.65, showing the vendor model performed worse than the comparator.
quote: AUC for 1-year mortality for EOLCI and academic model was 0.73 (95% CI [0.70-0.76]) and 0.82 (95% CI [0.80-0.85]), respectively.

title: R-AI-diographers: a European survey on perceived impact of AI on professional identity, careers, and radiographers' roles
outcome: Radiographers' optimism about AI by prior AI education, hands-on experience, and digital literacy
effect: Optimism higher with prior AI education (mean 2.15 vs 1.89; p<0.001) and hands-on AI experience (correlation 0.047; p=0.038).
quote: This was particularly strong for those with prior AI education (mean: 2.15 vs. 1.89; p-value: < 0.001), hands-on experience with AI (correlation: 0.047; p-value: 0.038), from countries with higher digital literacy (mean: 2.00 vs.1.93; p-value: 0.027) and a higher academic level of radiography education (mean: 3.28 vs. 3.15; p-value: 0.002).

title: Can ChatGPT and Gemini justify brain CT referrals? A comparative study with human experts and a custom prediction model
outcome: Agreement (kappa) with human expert iGuide justification of brain CT referrals, chatbots vs custom prediction model
effect: Chatbots' performance was limited (κ = 0.3), improving for more complete referrals; the custom prediction model reached κ = 0.853 on the same referrals.
quote: The prediction model outperformed the chatbots in justification analysis (κ = 0.853).

title: Accuracy and Readability of ChatGPT Responses to Patient-Centric Strabismus Questions
venue: Journal of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of ChatGPT responses to patient strabismus questions
effect: Average Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 15, higher than high school reading level; low readability.
quote: On average, responses scored a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level score of 15, equating to a higher than high school grade reading level.

title: Accuracy and Readability of ChatGPT Responses to Patient-Centric Strabismus Questions
venue: Journal of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus
outcome: Reading level of chatbot answers relative to patient reading level
effect: Mean FK grade level 15, exceeding high school level, demonstrating low readability.
quote: The average reading level exceeded a high school level and demonstrated low readability.

title: Accuracy and Readability of ChatGPT Responses to Patient-Centric Strabismus Questions
venue: Journal of pediatric ophthalmology and strabismus
outcome: Consistency of response accuracy across repeated runs, time points, and locations
effect: Acceptable responses 77% California vs 51% Florida (P<.001); inaccurate/harmful 6.9% vs 1.5%; acceptable 60% day 0, 64% 1 week, 67% 1 month.
quote: Although most of ChatGPT's responses to strabismus questions were clinically acceptable, there were variations in responses across time and geographic regions.

title: Assessment and comparison of artificial intelligence-generated information regarding shoulder arthroplasty from multiple interfaces
venue: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of AI answers to shoulder arthroplasty patient questions
effect: ChatGPT majority of FRES scores <20 (academic-level text); CoPilot FRES >30 but still required minimum 12th-grade education; CoPilot easier to read (P = .0031).
quote: Although answers provided by CoPilot were "easier" to read, they still required a 12th-grade education, which may be too complex for most patients, posing a challenge for patient comprehension.

title: Assessment and comparison of artificial intelligence-generated information regarding shoulder arthroplasty from multiple interfaces
venue: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient information versus appropriate patient reading level
effect: ChatGPT FRES mostly <20 with academic-level FKGL; CoPilot required at least 12th-grade education, likely too complex for most patients.
quote: In comparison, the ChatGPT generated more complex texts, with the majority of the FRES scores <20, and FKGL score signifying complexity of academic level text.

title: Assessment and comparison of artificial intelligence-generated information regarding shoulder arthroplasty from multiple interfaces
venue: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
outcome: Quality and source types of citations provided by CoPilot
effect: CoPilot provided citations; academic sources 31.1% (rTSA) and 26.7% (aTSA); substantial nonmedical media and commercial sources cited. ChatGPT gave no citations (JAMA score 0 vs 3).
quote: There were a substantial amount of nonmedical media sites, and commercial sources that were cited for both aTSA and rTSA questions by CoPilot.

title: Large language models for error detection in radiology reports: a comparative analysis between closed-source and privacy-compliant open-source models
outcome: Error detection rate of LLMs against known inserted errors in radiology reports
quote: Closed-source LLMs achieved higher error detection rates than open-source LLMs (GPT-4o: 88% [348/397; 95% CI: 86, 92], GPT-4: 83% [328/397; 95% CI: 80, 87], Llama 3-70b: 79% [311/397; 95% CI: 76, 83], Mixtral 8x22b: 73% [288/397; 95% CI: 68, 77]; p < 0.001).

title: Boosting GPT models for genomics analysis: generating trusted genetic variant annotations and interpretations through RAG and Fine-tuning
outcome: Accuracy of genetic variant annotations from RAG grounding versus fine-tuning
effect: RAG with 190 million curated variant annotations gave accurate annotations and outperformed fine-tuning on data volume, accuracy and cost. Fine-tuning improved only some fields, and accuracy across more fields remained suboptimal.
quote: Our project also revealed that RAG outperforms fine-tuning in factual knowledge injection in terms of data volume, accuracy, and cost-effectiveness.

title: Artificial intelligence in neurovascular decision-making: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4 and multidisciplinary expert recommendations for unruptured intracranial aneurysms
outcome: GPT-4 treatment recommendation quality and congruence with neurovascular board decisions
effect: No factual hallucinations; no specific recommendation derivable in 25% of cases; median expert quality rating 3.4/5; congruent with board in 65% of cases; moderate to low interrater agreement.
quote: None of the recommendations generated reflected evidence of factual hallucination, although in 25% of the case studies no specific recommendation could be derived from the GPT-4 responses.
sample_unit: patients with unruptured intracranial aneurysms (case scenarios)

title: Validation of a Digital Pathology-Based Multimodal Artificial Intelligence Biomarker in a Prospective, Real-World Prostate Cancer Cohort Treated with Prostatectomy
venue: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
outcome: External validation of MMAI prognostic association with BCR and adverse pathology in a Swedish RP cohort
effect: MMAI associated with BCR (sHR 2.45; 95% CI 1.77-3.38; P<0.001) and adverse pathology (OR 4.85; 95% CI 2.54-10.78; P<0.001); 5-year BCR 25% intermediate-high vs 4% low.
quote: MMAI was significantly associated with BCR [subdistribution HR, 2.45; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.77-3.38; P < 0.001] and AP at RP (OR, 4.85; 95% CI, 2.54-10.78; P < 0.001).

title: Integrating blockchain technology with artificial intelligence for the diagnosis of tibial plateau fractures
venue: European journal of trauma and emergency surgery : official publication of the European Trauma Society
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI models versus orthopedic and radiology attending physicians on external validation set
effect: Distributed AI accuracy 0.9636 vs centralized 0.9632 (p>0.05), orthopedic physician 0.9291, radiology attending 0.9175 (p<0.05). AI diagnosis time 4.99 min vs about 25-26 min for physicians.
quote: In the external validation set, the accuracy reached 0.9636 [95% CI (0.9388, 0.9762)], was slightly higher than that of the centralized YOLOv8n model at 0.9632 [95% CI (0.9387, 0.9755)] (p > 0.05), and exceeded the orthopedic physician at 0.9291 [95% CI (0.9002, 0.9482)] and radiology attending physician at 0.9175 [95% CI (0.8891, 0.9393)], with a statistically significant difference (p < 0.05).

title: Evaluating the Efficacy of Large Language Models in Guiding Treatment Decisions for Pediatric Refractive Error
outcome: LLM recommendation quality with incomplete or abnormal input data
effect: ChatGPT-4o performed better with incomplete or abnormal data, maintaining higher quality scores than the other models; the abstract does not give the numbers for the other models.
quote: Additionally, it performed better with incomplete or abnormal data, maintaining higher quality scores.

title: Assessing the accuracy of ChatGPT in interpreting blood gas analysis results ChatGPT-4 in blood gas analysis
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4 interpretation of blood gas values and treatment recommendations
effect: 100% accuracy for pH, oxygenation, sodium, chloride; hemoglobin 92.5%; bilirubin 72.5%; some unnecessary bicarbonate treatment recommendations.
quote: In several cases, the model recommended unnecessary bicarbonate treatment, suggesting an area for improvement in clinical judgment for acid-base balance management.

title: Comparing physician and large language model responses to influenza patient questions in the online health community
outcome: Incorrect information, omission, and harm in LLM vs physician influenza advice rated by physician panel
effect: No significant difference in incorrect information, omission, harm extent or empathy; LLM advice was more likely to cause harm and to be in line with medical consensus.
quote: Nevertheless, compared to physician advice, LLM advice was more likely to cause harm and to be in line with medical consensus.

title: Potential role of ChatGPT in simplifying and improving informed consent forms for vaccination: a pilot study conducted in Italy
outcome: Readability (Gulpease) and professional ratings of consent forms: human standard vs ChatGPT-rewritten vs fully ChatGPT-generated
effect: Gulpease: A 36, B 66, C 82 (C most readable). Professionals rated A and C highest; B lowest (overall median 3.0 A and C vs 2.0 B); A vs C not significantly different.
quote: Using the Gulpease Index, the scores obtained for each consent form were: 36 for consent form A, namely incomprehensible for elementary level, very difficult for middle and high school levels.

title: Potential role of ChatGPT in simplifying and improving informed consent forms for vaccination: a pilot study conducted in Italy
outcome: Reading ease of vaccination consent form after ChatGPT rewrite
effect: Standard form Gulpease 36 (high complexity); ChatGPT-modified form C scored 82 (very easy for higher education, easy for general population) with comprehensibility rated similar to the standard form.
quote: Consent form A and consent form C obtained the highest scores in terms of adequacy, comprehensibility, completeness and overall judgement ( table 2 , figure 1 ).

title: Potential role of ChatGPT in simplifying and improving informed consent forms for vaccination: a pilot study conducted in Italy
outcome: Clinician ratings of consent forms
effect: C (ChatGPT rephrasing A) vs B (AI-only): adequacy median 4.0 vs 3.0; overall judgement 3.0 vs 2.0; B-C differences p<0.01 and p=0.002.
quote: Consent form B, generated entirely by ChatGPT, scored lower, suggesting that collaboration between AI and humans yields better results: ChatGPT alone might not be sufficient to produce the best and most accepted product, and that the best results are achieved through the collaborative use of LLMs and human expertise.

title: Potential role of ChatGPT in simplifying and improving informed consent forms for vaccination: a pilot study conducted in Italy
outcome: Tone appropriateness of ChatGPT form
effect: D had Gulpease 63 but was excluded as excessively colloquial.
quote: Although consent form D received a score of 63, which is equivalent to easy reading for the population with a middle school degree and above, it was discarded because it contained an excessively colloquial tone.

title: Epilepsy surgery candidate identification with artificial intelligence: An implementation study
venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
outcome: LLM accuracy extracting epilepsy surgery referral information from clinic notes, and error types
effect: LLM accuracy ranged 80% to 100% across 7 prompts; errors were most frequent when summarising the management plan and included hallucinations, omissions and copying erroneous information.
quote: Errors included hallucinations, omissions, and copying erroneous information.

title: American academy of Orthopedic Surgeons' OrthoInfo provides more readable information regarding meniscus injury than ChatGPT-4 while information accuracy is comparable
venue: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT-4 responses versus OrthoInfo for meniscus injury questions
effect: ChatGPT average reading grade level 13.8 vs 9.8 for OrthoInfo (p<0.01); Flesch Reading Ease 32.0 vs 59.9 (p<0.01).
quote: ChatGPT responses required a significantly higher education level to comprehend, with an average reading grade level of 13.8 compared to 9.8 for OrthoInfo (p ​< ​0.01).

title: American academy of Orthopedic Surgeons' OrthoInfo provides more readable information regarding meniscus injury than ChatGPT-4 while information accuracy is comparable
venue: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient information relative to appropriate user reading level
effect: ChatGPT responses averaged grade 13.8 versus 9.8 for OrthoInfo; Flesch Reading Ease 32.0 vs 59.9, indicating lower readability.
quote: While AI-generated responses were accurate, their readability made them less accessible than OrthoInfo, which is designed for a broad audience.

title: Multimodal machine learning to predict surgical site infection with healthcare workload impact assessment
outcome: Model performance for SSI within 48 h versus clinician triage
effect: Multimodal model comparable to clinician triage (0.762 [0.690-0.835] vs 0.777 [0.721-0.832]), with excellent performance on external validation.
quote: The multimodal neural network model to predict confirmed SSI within 48 h remained comparable to clinician triage (0.762 [0.690-0.835] vs 0.777 [0.721-0.832]), with an excellent performance on external validation.

title: Multimodal machine learning to predict surgical site infection with healthcare workload impact assessment
outcome: Model performance on external validation
effect: Model showed excellent performance on external validation.
quote: The multimodal neural network model to predict confirmed SSI within 48 h remained comparable to clinician triage (0.762 [0.690-0.835] vs 0.777 [0.721-0.832]), with an excellent performance on external validation.

title: Characterization of artificial intelligence performance for lesion detection using synthetic lesions in PET imaging
outcome: Comparison of two lesion detection AIs on same synthetic lesion library by sensitivity and precision
effect: One AI consistently outperformed the other in number of reported lesions, sensitivity, and precision. 10 mm lesions detected at 90% sensitivity at 8:1 vs 16:1 lesion-to-background ratio for the two algorithms.
quote: One AI consistently outperformed the other in terms of number of reported lesions, sensitivity, and precision.

title: Leveraging ChatGPT to Produce Patient Education Materials for Common Hand Conditions
venue: Journal of hand surgery global online
outcome: Share of AI-generated patient education materials at or below sixth-grade reading level
effect: Question 1: neither model produced any PEMs at or below sixth-grade level. Question 2: ChatGPT 3.5 produced none; ChatGPT 4.0 produced 28% at or below sixth-grade level (P < .001).
quote: Our study shows neither ChatGPT 3.5 nor 4.0 could produce responses at the recommended sixth-grade reading level.
sample_unit: hand conditions (each generating patient education materials per model and prompt)

title: Leveraging ChatGPT to Produce Patient Education Materials for Common Hand Conditions
venue: Journal of hand surgery global online
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education materials relative to plain-language targets
effect: ChatGPT 3.5 Flesch Kincaid Grade 12.20 and ChatGPT 4.0 5.49 on question 2; neither version generated more than 50% of responses at an acceptable reading level.
quote: However, neither version generated more than 50% of responses at an acceptable reading level, regardless of a priming phase beforehand.
sample_unit: hand conditions (each generating patient education materials per model and prompt)

title: Artificial intelligence applied to electrocardiogram to rule out acute myocardial infarction: the ROMIAE multicentre study
outcome: AMI diagnostic AUC of AI-ECG versus HEART, GRACE 2.0, troponin, and physician score
effect: AI-ECG AUC 0.878 (95% CI 0.868-0.888), comparable with HEART 0.877 and superior to GRACE 2.0, hs-troponin, and Physician AMI score.
quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for AI-ECG was 0.878 (95% CI, 0.868-0.888), comparable with the HEART score (0.877; 95% CI, 0.869-0.886) and superior to the GRACE 2.0 score, high-sensitivity troponin level, and Physician AMI score.

title: A preliminary investigation into the potential, pitfalls, and limitations of large language models for mammography interpretation
outcome: GPT-4 mammography interpretation accuracy on intended-use clinical task
effect: Projection identified correctly in 53.3% of cases; sensitivity 50.0%, specificity 37.5%; significant false positives, false negatives, and hallucinations.
quote: The study highlighted GPT-4's embryonic interpretative abilities with a sensitivity of 50.0% and specificity of 37.5%.

title: Safety of human-AI cooperative decision-making within intensive care: A physical simulation study
outcome: Whether physicians verified unsafe AI outputs against clinical data before acting
effect: No increased fixations on the chart or monitor after an unsafe AI reveal; clinicians did not look back to debug the AI, though most unsafe recommendations were rejected.
quote: Nor did physicians devote significantly more attention to looking back at the ‘traditional’ (non-AI based) clinical data after seeing an unsafe AI recommendation to understand why the recommendation might be unsafe (i.e., there was no outward evidence of a desire to ‘debug’ the unsafe AI recommendation).

title: Safety of human-AI cooperative decision-making within intensive care: A physical simulation study
outcome: Human-AI team behavior in a high-fidelity simulation, including AI influence on physician decisions
effect: Physicians changed prescriptions in 46% (105/228) of trials after seeing AI advice; unsafe recommendations mostly rejected, showing human-AI behavior needs assessment beyond standalone AI.
quote: Physicians changed their prescription (dose of fluids and/or vasopressors) in 46 ± 3% (105/228), 95% CI: 0.40–0.52, of trials after seeing what the AI suggested.

title: Safety of human-AI cooperative decision-making within intensive care: A physical simulation study
outcome: Clinician performance with AI in simulated intended workflow, including effect on decisions
effect: AI advice altered treatment decisions; 92% of unsafe recommendations stopped or escalated versus 29% of safe ones stopped, which standalone metrics would not reveal.
quote: The proportion stopping unsafe AI recommendations rose to 92 ± 3%, 95% CI: 0.86–0.98 (p = 0.0823) when including physicians who asked for a senior opinion, which would most likely lead to the unsafe AI recommendation being rejected (see Fig 3a ).

title: Safety of human-AI cooperative decision-making within intensive care: A physical simulation study
outcome: Whether AI explanations drew more visual attention when recommendations were unsafe
effect: Fixations on AI explanation ROI not significantly different between safe and unsafe scenarios, questioning explanations as a mitigation.
quote: Finally, the number of gaze fixations on the AI explanation ROI was not significantly different between safe and unsafe scenarios.

title: Safety of human-AI cooperative decision-making within intensive care: A physical simulation study
outcome: unsafe AI influence on doses
effect: Unsafe AI shifted fluids by 40 ml/h and vasopressors by 0.08 mcg/kg/min; safe AI shifted 80 ml/h and 0.01 mcg/kg/min.
quote: Both safe and unsafe AI recommendations influenced human decisions to different extents: fluid doses shifted on average by 80 ml/h (and vasopressor doses by 0.01 mcg/kg/min) after a safe AI recommendation compared to 40 ml/h (and 0.08 mcg/kg/min) after an unsafe AI recommendation.

title: Safety of human-AI cooperative decision-making within intensive care: A physical simulation study
outcome: detection of unsafe AI outputs
effect: Unsafe recommendations stopped 83 ± 4% versus safe 29 ± 4%; stopped/escalated unsafe recommendations rose to 92 ± 3%.
quote: In total, unsafe AI recommendations were stopped more often than safe AI recommendations (83 ± 4%, 95% CI: 0.75–0.91 vs. 29 ± 4%, 95% CI: 0.21–0.37, p < 0.0001).

title: Safety of human-AI cooperative decision-making within intensive care: A physical simulation study
outcome: Physician rejection of unsafe versus safe AI treatment recommendations
effect: Unsafe AI recommendations were stopped more often than safe ones (83 ± 4%, 95% CI: 0.75–0.91 vs 29 ± 4%, 95% CI: 0.21–0.37, p < 0.0001), rising to 92 ± 3% with senior consultation.
quote: In total, unsafe AI recommendations were stopped more often than safe AI recommendations (83 ± 4%, 95% CI: 0.75–0.91 vs. 29 ± 4%, 95% CI: 0.21–0.37, p < 0.0001).

title: Leveraging Medical Knowledge Graphs Into Large Language Models for Diagnosis Prediction: Design and Application Study
outcome: Diagnostic prediction accuracy of LLM with versus without knowledge graph retrieved paths
effect: DR.KNOWS with KG paths showed higher accuracy in extracting diagnostic concepts and improved diagnostic prediction metrics over QuickUMLS, T5 and ChatGPT baselines; prompt-tuned T5 with KG paths achieved highest ROUGE-L and CUI F1.
quote: Prompt-based fine-tuning of Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer with DR.KNOWS knowledge paths achieved the highest ROUGE-L (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation-Longest Common Subsequence) and concept unique identifier F<sub>1</sub>-scores, highlighting the benefits of KG integration.

title: A comprehensive validation study on the influencing factors of cough-based COVID-19 detection through multi-center data with abundant metadata
outcome: Model AUC across clinical, crowdsourced, and open-source datasets
effect: AUC 0.79 for clinical data and 0.69 for crowdsourced data; poor detection performance on open-source datasets shows limitation of existing models.
quote: The area under receiver operating characteristic curve is 0.79 for clinical data and 0.69 for crowdsourced data, indicating differences between clinical validation and real-world application.

title: External Validation of a Winning Artificial Intelligence Algorithm from the RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine Fracture Detection Challenge
outcome: Local sensitivity, specificity, F1, AUC of AI on external trauma center CT scans versus competition data
effect: Sensitivity 86% and specificity 70% in external validation versus 85% and 94% in competition group; sensitivity held but specificity dropped.
quote: Sensitivity and specificity were 86% and 70% in the external validation group and 85% and 94% in the competition group, respectively.

title: External Validation of a Winning Artificial Intelligence Algorithm from the RSNA 2022 Cervical Spine Fracture Detection Challenge
outcome: Difference between development and external validation population characteristics and effect on performance
effect: External validation set comprised older patients than the competition set (53.5 ± 21.8 vs 58 ± 22.0 years; P < .05); specificity fell from 94% to 70%.
quote: The external validation data set comprised older patients in comparison to the competition set (53.5 ± 21.8 years versus 58 ± 22.0, respectively; P < .05).

title: Real-world feasibility, accuracy and acceptability of automated retinal photography and AI-based cardiovascular disease risk assessment in Australian primary care settings: a pragmatic trial
outcome: Predictive accuracy of AI rpCVD score versus WHO CVD risk score for 10-year incident CVD
effect: rpCVD AUC = 0.672 (95% CI: 0.658-0.686) versus WHO CVD risk score AUC = 0.693 (95% CI: 0.680-0.707); comparable accuracy using retinal images alone.
quote: Despite this, the rpCVD system, which relies solely on retinal images, demonstrated a similar level of accuracy in predicting 10-year incident CVD (AUC = 0.672, 95% CI: 0.658-0.686) compared to the WHO CVD risk score (AUC = 0.693, 95% CI: 0.680-0.707).

title: Feasibility and Optimization of Donation Advisor: a Decision Support Tool for Deceased Organ Donation and Transplantation
outcome: Report usability and usefulness after iterative clinician interview feedback across five report versions
effect: 19 of 34 clinicians interviewed; feedback produced 5 report versions with fewer revisions each time; predictive scores useful to most practitioners (83%).
quote: The usefulness and usability of the DA report has improved through user feedback; both barriers and drivers to implementation exist.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models for High-Quality Lay Summaries: Efficacy of ChatGPT-4 with Custom Prompts in a Consecutive Series of Prostate Cancer Manuscripts
outcome: Readability (FKRE) of AI lay summaries with reading-level-targeted extended prompt vs simple prompt
effect: Extended prompt raised median FKRE from 29.1 to 40.9 (p<0.001); FKRE<30 in 11.3% vs 52.5%; grade level 12.8 vs 14.8; insufficient summaries 13.8% vs 52.5%.
quote: Compared to the ChatGPT-4 simple prompt, the FKRE scores were significantly higher for the lay summaries generated with the extended ChatGPT-4 prompt (40.9 vs. 29.1; p < 0.001).
sample_unit: articles (prostate cancer abstracts summarized per prompt)

title: Leveraging Large Language Models for High-Quality Lay Summaries: Efficacy of ChatGPT-4 with Custom Prompts in a Consecutive Series of Prostate Cancer Manuscripts
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated plain-language summaries relative to lay comprehension
effect: Even with the extended prompt, median FKGL was 12.8 and reading age 19.5 years, above the ~12-year reading age recommended; the simple prompt gave FKGL 14.8 and reading age 21.5.
quote: Reading age in years; median (IQR) 21.5 (20.5–22.9) 19.5 (18.5–20.5) <0.001
sample_unit: articles (prostate cancer abstracts summarized per prompt)

title: Diagnostic Performance of an Artificial Intelligence Software for the Evaluation of Bone X-Ray Examinations Referred from the Emergency Department
outcome: Local retrospective ED bone X-ray performance of AI vs senior radiologist reference standard
effect: Fracture detection: AI Sens 95.8%, Spec 97.6% (residents 90.6%, 98%). Dislocation detection: residents higher (Sens 77.8%, Spec 100%) than AI, so local performance was strong for fractures but weaker for dislocations.
quote: The RR achieved higher Sens (77.8%) and Spec (100%) for dislocation detection compared to AI.

title: Non-Contrast Computed Tomography-Based Triage and Notification for Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke: A Before and After Study Utilizing Artificial Intelligence on Treatment Times and Outcomes
outcome: Treatment times and clinical outcomes before vs after AI LVO triage implementation
effect: Post-AI reduced door-to-EVT time by 30.2 min (95% CI -56 to -4.3), CT-to-EVT by 29.4 min; door-to-tPA not significant; mRS 0-1 26% vs 40%, not significant.
quote: The implementation of Heuron ELVO significantly reduced the door-to-EVT time (30.2 min, 95% CI, -56. to -4.3), CT-to-neurologist examination time (16.4 min, 95% CI, -27.6 to -5.3), and CT-to-EVT time (29.4 min, 95% CI, -53.6 to -5.0).
sample_unit: patients with LVO stroke (84 pre-AI, 48 post-AI)

title: Development and Implementation of a Clinical Decision Support System to Enhance Efficiency and Accuracy in Medication Prescription Review in a Tertiary Care Hospital: A Retrospective Hospital CDSS Register Study
outcome: Medication alert rate and proportion of patients receiving alerts before vs after CDSS implementation
effect: Alert rate fell from 2.52% to 2.30% of orders; patients receiving alerts fell from 30.34% to 28.08%. Across 115 wards, 45.22% had fewer patients alerted and 20.87% had more.
quote: Among these, 130,286 (2.52%) and 133,562 (2.30%) prescriptions triggered alerts, indicating a significant reduction in the alert rate of 0.22%

title: Complete Blood Count and Monocyte Distribution Width-Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Sepsis Detection: Multicentric Development and External Validation Study
outcome: External validation performance across cohorts with distribution shifts versus internal validation
effect: Internal AUC 0.91-0.98; external AUC 0.75-0.95 across 5 external cohorts; performance worsened vs internal but differences not significant.
quote: While the performance of all models worsened compared with the internal test sets, the differences were not significant, as shown in Figure S11 in Multimedia Appendix 1 .

title: Complete Blood Count and Monocyte Distribution Width-Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Sepsis Detection: Multicentric Development and External Validation Study
outcome: ML models compared against baseline biomarkers and prior ML models on same internal test data
effect: XGB, RF, and LR significantly outperformed MDW, CRP, Sepsis Index, COMPOSER, and Mindray SVM baselines across all decision thresholds.
quote: XGB, RF, and LR significantly outperformed all the baseline comparison methods (ie, MDW [ 37 ], CRP [ 44 ], Sepsis Index [ 45 ], COMPOSER [ 25 ], as well as the SVM model developed in the study by Aguirre and Urrechaga [ 31 ]; Figures 1 and 2 ; Figure S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1 ) and did so across all possible decision thresholds.

title: Complete Blood Count and Monocyte Distribution Width-Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Sepsis Detection: Multicentric Development and External Validation Study
outcome: Model performance reported separately across five external sites/settings and analyzers
effect: Performance varied by site: acceptable-to-excellent on external cohorts, but low PPV and sNB in OGSA-ICU with a different analyzer and no MDW.
quote: The XGB-based system achieved low PPV and sNB on the OGSA-ICU dataset, as also shown in Figure S13 in Multimedia Appendix 1 , which was also the second most dissimilar to the internal training set (PA-ED).

title: Complete Blood Count and Monocyte Distribution Width-Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Sepsis Detection: Multicentric Development and External Validation Study
outcome: Performance under dataset shift (covariate, label, missingness) between training and external cohorts
effect: Good generalization overall, but XGB had low sNB on UD-ED (most dissimilar to training set) and low PPV and sNB on OGSA-ICU (missing MDW, second most dissimilar).
quote: The XGB model achieved acceptable-to-excellent performance on all external datasets and with respect to all metrics, except for the sNB on the UD-ED: this dataset was, among the external validation datasets, the most dissimilar to the internal training set (PA-ED).

title: Complete Blood Count and Monocyte Distribution Width-Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Sepsis Detection: Multicentric Development and External Validation Study
outcome: Performance when a key input (MDW) was entirely missing, using imputation
effect: Lack of MDW (100% missing) led to a large decrease in PPV despite imputation, though overall performance was acceptable.
quote: While, indeed, the obtained results show that acceptable results could be obtained even in the presence of significant missingness shift, the lack of MDW led to a relevant drop in performance, thus highlighting the need for collecting complete data in practical scenarios.

title: Complete Blood Count and Monocyte Distribution Width-Based Machine Learning Algorithms for Sepsis Detection: Multicentric Development and External Validation Study
outcome: robustness to missingness and distribution shifts
effect: External validation was generally acceptable, but missing MDW caused a relevant performance drop, especially PPV.
quote: While, indeed, the obtained results show that acceptable results could be obtained even in the presence of significant missingness shift, the lack of MDW led to a relevant drop in performance, thus highlighting the need for collecting complete data in practical scenarios.

title: Stroke Diagnosis and Prediction Tool Using ChatGLM: Development and Validation Study
outcome: Stroke diagnosis accuracy in internal validation versus two external test cohorts from different periods and hospital
effect: Accuracy 99% internal validation, 95.5% at the training hospital in a later period, and 79.1% at a second hospital; IVT eligibility accuracy 89.4% internal versus 60% and 80% externally.
quote: The LLM, which is based on clinical notes and NCCT, demonstrates exceptionally high accuracy in stroke diagnosis, achieving 99% in the internal validation dataset and 95.5% and 79.1% in two external test cohorts.

title: From RAGs to riches: Utilizing large language models to write documents for clinical trials
outcome: Clinical thinking/logic score of generated protocol sections, RAG vs off-the-shelf GPT-4
effect: RAG-augmented LLM scored about twice as high on clinical thinking and logic; eligibility criteria ~33% to ~86%, endpoints ~50% to ~73%; only this dimension survived Bonferroni correction.
quote: However, the RAG-augmented LLM substantially outperforms the off-the-shelf LLM in terms of clinical thinking and logic , where the output of the RAG-augmented LLM scores approximately twice as high as the off-the-shelf LLM.

title: From RAGs to riches: Utilizing large language models to write documents for clinical trials
outcome: Presence and correctness of cited references in generated protocol text
effect: Off-the-shelf GPT-4 does not natively source references so transparency could not be scored; RAG-augmented LLM references were correct and appropriate nearly 80% of the time.
quote: Regarding transparency and references , the RAG-augmented LLM (by design) includes references, which we show to be correct and appropriate nearly 80% of the time.

title: From RAGs to riches: Utilizing large language models to write documents for clinical trials
outcome: Adherence of off-the-shelf LLM recommendations to current regulatory guidance
effect: Off-the-shelf LLM scored just over 40% on clinical thinking and logic; example excluded HIV, diabetes, liver and kidney disease patients from a TB trial contrary to FDA guidance.
quote: However, for clinical thinking and logic , the off-the-shelf LLM scores poorly (assessment score just over 40%), meaning that recommendations from the off-the-shelf LLM often do not follow the latest regulatory guidance or contain other errors.

title: AI-powered prostate cancer detection: a multi-centre, multi-scanner validation study
outcome: AI performance reported by site and scanner across multiple sites and vendors
effect: AI performed well per-site (AUC ≥ 0.83) at the patient-level independent of scanner age and field strength; six machines from two manufacturers across six sites.
quote: AI performed well per-site (AUC ≥ 0.83) at the patient-level independent of scanner age and field strength.

title: AI-powered prostate cancer detection: a multi-centre, multi-scanner validation study
outcome: AI compared with MDT-supported radiologists on same data for GG≥2 prostate cancer detection
effect: Per patient, Pi was non-inferior to radiologists (10% margin), AUC 0.91 vs 0.95; sensitivity 95% vs 99%, specificity 67% vs 73%.
quote: Evaluated per patient, Pi was non-inferior to radiologists (considering a 10% performance difference as acceptable), with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.91 vs. 0.95.

title: AI-powered prostate cancer detection: a multi-centre, multi-scanner validation study
outcome: Performance on separate validation dataset from different hospitals than training
effect: Validation on separate dataset (252 patients, six sites) from different UK hospitals gave AUC 0.91 for the AI, non-inferior to radiologists.
quote: We compared a new AI solution, validated on a separate dataset from different UK hospitals, to the original multidisciplinary team (MDT)-supported radiologist's interpretations.

title: Evaluating Adherence to Canadian Radiology Guidelines for Incidental Hepatobiliary Findings Using RAG-Enabled LLMs

title: Improving the Real-Time Classification of Disease Severity in Ulcerative Colitis: Artificial Intelligence as the Trigger for a Second Opinion

title: COVID-BLUeS - a Prospective Study on the Value of AI in Lung Ultrasound Analysis

title: GPT-4 as a Clinical Decision Support Tool in Ischemic Stroke Management: Evaluation Study

quote: For mortality prediction, GPT-4 accurately identified 10 (77%) out of 13 deaths within its top 25 high-risk predictions (AUC 0.89, 95% CI 0.8077-0.9739; hazard ratio 6.98, 95% CI 2.88-16.9; P<.001), outperforming supervised machine learning models such as PRACTICE (AUC 0.70; log-rank P=.02) and PREMISE (AUC 0.77; P=.07).

outcome: Readability grade level of GPT-4 and ophthalmologist responses to patient surgery questions across six metrics

quote: Across all metrics (FK-RE; FK-GL; GFS; SI; CLI; and ARI), GPT-4 responses were at a higher grade level (34.39 [8.51]; 13.19 [2.63]; 16.37 [2.04]; 12.18 [1.43]; 15.72 [1.40]; 12.99 [1.86]) than ophthalmologists' responses (50.61 [15.53]; 10.71 [2.99]; 14.13 [3.55]; 10.07 [2.46]; 12.64 [2.93]; 10.40 [3.61]), with both sources necessitating a 12th-grade education for comprehension.

title: Eyes on the Text: Assessing Readability of Artificial Intelligence and Ophthalmologist Responses to Patient Surgery Queries
venue: Ophthalmologica. Journal international d'ophtalmologie. International journal of ophthalmology. Zeitschrift fur Augenheilkunde
outcome: Reading level of AI and clinician patient materials versus NIH 6th-7th grade recommendation
effect: Both GPT-4 and ophthalmologist answers exceeded the NIH 6th- to 7th-grade recommendation, with GPT-4 showing a greater gap; GPT-4 used 24.42% complex words vs 17.76%.
quote: Both GPT-4- and ophthalmologist-written answers exceeded this recommendation, with GPT-4 showing a greater gap.

title: Comparative Analysis of Artificial Intelligence Platforms in Generating Post-Operative Instructions for Rhinologic Surgery
venue: Indian journal of otolaryngology and head and neck surgery : official publication of the Association of Otolaryngologists of India
outcome: Readability, understandability and actionability of AI-generated post-operative instructions (PEMAT)
effect: Instructions from ChatGPT and Gemini were understandable but poor for actionability and readability; numeric scores not reported in the abstract.
quote: ChatGPT and Gemini were capable of generating understandable post-operative instructions but were poor for actionability and readability.
sample_unit: AI-generated post-operative instruction sets (4 procedures x 2 platforms)

title: Ethics in Patient Preferences for Artificial Intelligence-Drafted Responses to Electronic Messages
outcome: Patient satisfaction, usefulness, feeling cared for by AI vs human vs no disclosure of message authorship
effect: AI disclosure lowered satisfaction slightly vs human disclosure (0.13; 95% CI 0.05-0.22) and vs no disclosure (0.09; 95% CI 0.01-0.17); >75% satisfied regardless of disclosure.
quote: The mean change in score between AI and human disclosure was 0.13 (95% CI, 0.05-0.22) points for satisfaction, favoring human disclosure, and 0.09 (95% CI, 0.01-0.17) points for satisfaction between AI and no disclosure, favoring no disclosure.

title: Ethics in Patient Preferences for Artificial Intelligence-Drafted Responses to Electronic Messages
outcome: Patient reactions to and preferences among AI disclosure wording variants
effect: Evaluated reactions to disclosure; 893 (61.4%) ranked five disclosure versions; brief statement preferred; disclosure did not greatly reduce satisfaction.
quote: Participants preferred the shortest disclosure statement, which stated, “This message was written by Dr T. with the support of automated tools,” a takeaway that we are implementing at our health system.

title: External Testing of a Commercial AI Algorithm for Breast Cancer Detection at Screening Mammography
outcome: AI breast cancer detection performance by breast density and lesion features (architectural distortion, calcification)
effect: Performance was good overall but differed significantly by breast density classification and by presence or absence of architectural distortion or calcification. No numbers in the abstract.
quote: The commercial artificial intelligence algorithm for breast cancer detection on screening mammograms performed well overall, but performance differed significantly based on breast density classification and presence or absence of architectural distortion or calcification.

title: Using Large Language Models in the Diagnosis of Acute Cholecystitis: Assessing Accuracy and Guidelines Compliance
outcome: LLM accuracy against Tokyo Guidelines 2018 on acute cholecystitis questions
effect: ChatGPT4.0 gave accurate and comprehensive answers for 4/10 (40%), accurate but not comprehensive for 5/10 (50%), and one (10%) partially accurate, partially inaccurate; no entirely inaccurate answers.
quote: One response (10%) was rated as "partially accurate, partially inaccurate."

title: Still a Long Way to Go, the Potential of ChatGPT in Personalized Dietary Prescription, From a Perspective of a Clinical Dietitian
venue: Journal of renal nutrition : the official journal of the Council on Renal Nutrition of the National Kidney Foundation
outcome: Deviation of ChatGPT meal plan energy and protein content from CKD targets

quote: For the quantitative analysis, the prescribed energy levels were generally lower than the targets, ranging from -28.9% to -17.0%, and protein contents were tremendously higher than the targets, ranging from 59.3% to 157%.

title: AI-assisted decision-making in mild traumatic brain injury
outcome: Critical errors in GPT-4 responses to mild TBI cases, as identified by emergency physicians
effect: Responses containing critical errors had significantly lower satisfaction and scientific adequacy (p < 0.001). Ease of understanding did not differ between responses with and without critical errors (p = 0.133).
quote: However, responses with critical errors significantly reduced satisfaction and scientific adequacy (p < 0.001).

title: AI-assisted decision-making in mild traumatic brain injury
outcome: Readability of GPT-4 responses (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) versus case descriptions
effect: GPT-4 responses were significantly more difficult to read than the case descriptions (p < 0.001).
quote: GPT-4 responses were significantly more difficult to read than the case descriptions (p < 0.001).

title: Multi-Center Benchmarking of a Commercially Available Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) Score Assignment and Lesion Detection in Prostate MRI
outcome: AI versus radiologist sensitivity and specificity for csPCa on same MRI exams

quote: Sensitivity and specificity for clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa, defined as ISUP ≥ 2) were 92%/64% for radiologists vs. 91%/57% for AI detection on patient level and 90%/70% vs. 81%/78% on lesion level, respectively (cut-off PI-RADS ≥ 4).

title: Multi-Center Benchmarking of a Commercially Available Artificial Intelligence Algorithm for Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) Score Assignment and Lesion Detection in Prostate MRI
outcome: csPCa cases missed by AI at patient level and negative predictive value
effect: Two csPCa cases missed by AI on patient level; NPV 0.88 at PI-RADS ≥3 cutoff.
quote: Two cases of csPCa were missed by the AI on patient-level, resulting in a negative predictive value (NPV) of 0.88 at a cut-off of PI-RADS ≥ 3.

title: The Potential of ChatGPT as a Source of Information for Kidney Transplant Recipients and Their Caregivers
outcome: Proportion of ChatGPT outputs rated potentially risky by pediatric nephrologists

quote: Twelve outputs were considered potentially risky, but only three had a risk grade of moderate or higher.

title: Artificial intelligence (ChatGPT) ready to evaluate ECG in real life? Not yet!

quote: Cardiologists demonstrated superior accuracy (92.52%) compared to ChatGPT-based models (GPT-ECGReader: 57.94%, GPT-ECGInterpreter: 62.62%, GPT-ECGAnalyzer: 62.62%).

title: Emerging algorithmic bias: fairness drift as the next dimension of model maintenance and sustainability
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Emergence of subgroup performance disparities over time after deployment (fairness drift)
effect: Fairness drift observed by race and sex; pneumonia model race accuracy and specificity gaps grew (P<.01 for trend); sex accuracy and specificity gaps increased in original models for all 3 outcomes (P<.01).
quote: We observed fairness drift in both the original and temporally updated models.

title: Emerging algorithmic bias: fairness drift as the next dimension of model maintenance and sustainability
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Performance and calibration drift of deployed prediction models over 10 years
effect: Accuracy and calibration deteriorated over time in all models, largest for readmission; surveillance-based updating stabilized calibration for mortality and pneumonia but did not restore accuracy.
quote: Accuracy and calibration deteriorated over time in all models, with the largest population-level performance changes observed for the readmission model.

title: Emerging algorithmic bias: fairness drift as the next dimension of model maintenance and sustainability
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Effect of recalibration triggered by drift detection on overall performance and fairness
effect: Updating restored readmission accuracy and calibration but not mortality/pneumonia accuracy; reduced readmission sensitivity below initial; effects on fairness gaps varied.
quote: For the readmission model, the surveillance-based model updating process restored both accuracy and calibration to levels comparable or better than initial performance.

title: Emerging algorithmic bias: fairness drift as the next dimension of model maintenance and sustainability
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Fairness gaps by race and sex over time with and without population-level model updating
effect: Updating restored fairness gaps in some cases (readmission sex gaps) and exacerbated or did not close them in others (pneumonia race gap not closed; ICI gap larger for males); overall performance affected more than fairness.
quote: During periods of fairness drift, updating models restored fairness in some cases and exacerbated fairness gaps in others.

title: Emerging algorithmic bias: fairness drift as the next dimension of model maintenance and sustainability
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Subgroup performance gaps at initial validation by race and sex
effect: Specificity and accuracy higher for female vs male in all models; sensitivity lower for female in readmission and pneumonia models; no AUC, O:E, or ICI differences by race or sex.
quote: Sensitivity was lower for female vs male patients in models for readmission and pneumonia.

title: Emerging algorithmic bias: fairness drift as the next dimension of model maintenance and sustainability
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: fairness impact of model updates
effect: Updating restored fairness in some cases and exacerbated fairness gaps in others; no numeric estimate reported.
quote: During periods of fairness drift, updating models restored fairness in some cases and exacerbated fairness gaps in others.

title: Evaluating if ChatGPT Can Answer Common Patient Questions Compared With OrthoInfo Regarding Rotator Cuff Tears
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT responses versus OrthoInfo and sixth-grade target
effect: Standard ChatGPT FK mean 14.3 vs OrthoInfo 10.33 (P=0.002); sixth-grade prompt FK mean 7.71, still above sixth grade.

title: Evaluating if ChatGPT Can Answer Common Patient Questions Compared With OrthoInfo Regarding Rotator Cuff Tears

title: Evaluating if ChatGPT Can Answer Common Patient Questions Compared With OrthoInfo Regarding Rotator Cuff Tears
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
outcome: ChatGPT accuracy and appropriateness rated by surgeons against OrthoInfo reference
effect: Standard responses accuracy 4.7±0.47 and appropriateness 4.5±0.57, above 4/5 cutoff but below OrthoInfo 5.0 (P=0.004; P=0.016); sixth-grade below cutoff.
quote: However, standard ChatGPT responses were less accurate (4.7 ± 0.47 vs. 5.0 ± 0.0; P = 0.004) and appropriate (4.5 ± 0.57 vs. 5.0 ± 0.0; P = 0.016) when compared with OrthoInfo responses.

title: Evaluating if ChatGPT Can Answer Common Patient Questions Compared With OrthoInfo Regarding Rotator Cuff Tears
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses
effect: Standard ChatGPT responses at FK grade 14.3, above average American reading level and above OrthoInfo (10.33); sixth-grade prompt gave 7.71 but reduced accuracy.
quote: Not only does this far surpass the average American reading level, but this reading level is also greater than what is presented online, showcased by its notable difference when compared with the reading level for OrthoInfo.

title: Evaluating if ChatGPT Can Answer Common Patient Questions Compared With OrthoInfo Regarding Rotator Cuff Tears
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews

title: Improving the Robustness and Clinical Applicability of Automatic Respiratory Sound Classification Using Deep Learning-Based Audio Enhancement: Algorithm Development and Validation
outcome: Physician diagnostic sensitivity, confidence and trust with versus without model-assisted enhanced-audio workflow
effect: Workflows integrating enhanced audio gave an 11.61% increase in diagnostic sensitivity, with improved efficiency, diagnostic confidence, and trust.
quote: Quantitative analysis from the physician validation study revealed improvements in efficiency, diagnostic confidence, and trust during model-assisted diagnosis, with workflows that integrated enhanced audio leading to an 11.61% increase in diagnostic sensitivity and facilitating high-confidence diagnoses.

title: Improving the Robustness and Clinical Applicability of Automatic Respiratory Sound Classification Using Deep Learning-Based Audio Enhancement: Algorithm Development and Validation
outcome: Respiratory sound classification performance under noisy input, with and without audio enhancement
effect: Audio enhancement gave a 21.88% increase in ICBHI score (P<.001) on ICBHI and a 4.1% improvement (P<.001) on Formosa in multi-class noisy scenarios.
quote: The integration of the audio enhancement module resulted in a 21.88% increase with P<.001 in the ICBHI classification score on the ICBHI dataset and a 4.1% improvement with P<.001 on the Formosa Archive of Breath Sound dataset in multi-class noisy scenarios.

title: Assessing Racial and Ethnic Bias in Text Generation by Large Language Models for Health Care-Related Tasks: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Differences in sentiment, subjectivity, reading ease, word frequency and entity count of LLM discharge instructions across race/ethnicity

quote: The only observed statistically significant difference between race/ethnicity groups was found in entity count (GPT-4, df=42, P=.047).

title: Artificial intelligence (ChatGPT 4.0) vs. Human expertise for epileptic seizure and epilepsy diagnosis and classification in Adults: An exploratory study

effect: Human experts consistently outperformed ChatGPT with near-perfect accuracy and higher kappa; ChatGPT specificity was low (26.7% for epilepsy diagnosis, 33.3% for acute symptomatic vs unprovoked seizures).
quote: Human experts consistently outperformed ChatGPT with near-perfect accuracy and higher κ values.

title: Comparing AAOS appropriate use criteria with ChatGPT-4o recommendations on treating distal radius fractures
outcome: Agreement between ChatGPT-4o and AAOS appropriate use criteria for distal radius fracture treatments
effect: Agreement ranged from 99.17% (immobilization without reduction) and 90.42% (volar locking plates) to 15% (dorsal plating); mean error ranged 0.6 to -2.9; ChatGPT-4o favored conservative approaches.
quote: ChatGPT-4o does not consistently align with the appropriate use criteria in determining appropriate management of distal radius fractures.

title: Enhancing diagnostic capability with multi-agents conversational large language models

effect: MAC demonstrated high consistency across repeated runs (no numeric values in the abstract).
quote: MAC demonstrated high consistency across repeated runs.

title: Artificial intelligence assisted identification of newborn auricular deformities via smartphone application

quote: Multi-center real-world data validation demonstrated satisfactory accuracy, with a range of 0.74-0.82 for six-class classification and 0.79-0.86 for normal/abnormal classification, indicating strong generalizability.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Patient Support: Assessing Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Answering Postoperative Rhinoplasty Questions
outcome: Reading level of AI responses relative to patient education standards

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Insertable Cardiac Monitors on Device Clinic Workflow and Resource Utilization

title: Generalizability of clinical prediction models in mental health
