outcome: Reading grade level of LLM patient-facing responses versus appropriate user reading level
effect: FKGL 14.95 and SMOG 15.49 (college level or higher); FRE 27.41 (very difficult). Treatment-related questions were easiest to read.
quote: Readability scores revealed a SMOG score of 15.49 ± 1.74, an FKGL score of 14.95 ± 1.95, and an FRE score of 27.41 ± 9.71, indicating that a high level of education is required to comprehend the responses.

title: ChatGPT Performance on 120 Interdisciplinary Allergology Questions-Systematic Evaluation With Clinical Error Impact Assessment for Critical Erroneous AI-Guided Chatbot Advice
venue: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of ChatGPT responses to allergology questions
effect: Readability was at an academic level for most responses.
quote: Readability was at an academic level for most responses.

title: ChatGPT Performance on 120 Interdisciplinary Allergology Questions-Systematic Evaluation With Clinical Error Impact Assessment for Critical Erroneous AI-Guided Chatbot Advice
venue: The journal of allergy and clinical immunology. In practice
outcome: Clinical accuracy errors, including critical errors, in ChatGPT allergology answers
effect: Mean accuracy 4.1/5 (SD 0.78); six critical errors (1 dermatology, 2 pediatrics, 3 pulmonology); a pediatric food allergen error was potentially life-threatening.
quote: Six critical errors were identified: 1 in dermatology, 2 in pediatrics, and 3 in pulmonology.

title: External validation of a machine learning prediction model for massive blood loss during surgery for spinal metastases: a multi-institutional study using 880 patients
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Distributional shift between development and validation cohorts in predictive variables
effect: Poor performance attributed partly to distributional shift, as the validation cohort had key differences in predictive variables used by the model.
quote: This poor performance might be attributed to overfitting and sampling bias as the development cohort had an insufficient sample size, and distributional shift as our cohort had key differences in predictive variables used by the model.

title: External validation of a machine learning prediction model for massive blood loss during surgery for spinal metastases: a multi-institutional study using 880 patients
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility on external cohorts versus developer results
effect: Model overestimated risk; Brier 0.278, AUC 0.631 (95%CI 0.583-0.680), calibration slope 0.283, net harm on decision curve analysis from 20% threshold.
quote: Using the most favorable quantification method, the predictive model overestimated risk in our total validation cohort and scored poorly on overall fit (Brier score: 0.278), discrimination (AUC: 0.631 [95%CI: 0.583, 0.680]), calibration, (intercept: -2.082, [95%CI: -2.285, -1.879]), slope: 0.283 [95%CI: 0.173, 0.393]), and clinical utility, with net harm observed in decision curve analysis from 20%.

title: External validation of a machine learning prediction model for massive blood loss during surgery for spinal metastases: a multi-institutional study using 880 patients
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Performance across sites/regions (North American and European cohorts separately)
effect: Similar poor performance observed in North American (n=539) and European (n=341) cohorts analyzed separately and in the subanalysis (n=676).
quote: Similar poor performance results were observed in the subanalysis excluding the additional included patients (n=676) and when analyzing the North American (n=539) and European (n=341) cohorts separately.

title: External validation of a machine learning prediction model for massive blood loss during surgery for spinal metastases: a multi-institutional study using 880 patients
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Overestimated performance from insufficient sample size, overfitting, and lack of external validation
effect: Poor external performance attributed to overfitting and sampling bias from an insufficient development sample size.
quote: These findings emphasize the importance of extensive validation in different geographical areas and addressing biases and pitfalls of ML model development before clinical implementation, as untested models may do more harm than good.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation enhances large language model performance on the Japanese orthopedic board examination
venue: Journal of orthopaedic science : official journal of the Japanese Orthopaedic Association
outcome: Exam accuracy with versus without retrieval-augmented generation from an orthopedic textbook database
effect: GPT-4o rose from 62% to 72% and o1-preview from 67% to 84% with RAG. GPT-3.5 Turbo showed no improvement (29% to 28%).
quote: GPT-4o rose from 62 % to 72 %, while o1-preview increased from 67 % to 84 %.

title: International external validation of the SORG machine learning algorithm for predicting sustained postoperative opioid prescription after anterior cervical discectomy and fusion using a Taiwanese cohort of 1,037 patients
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Differences between development and Taiwanese validation cohort demographics, predictors, and outcome incidence
effect: Validation cohort differed in demographics, medicolegal and cultural context and key predictors; sustained opioid use incidence was 9.9% (270/2737) in development vs 3.3% (34/1037) in Taiwan (p < .01).
quote: Comparing the validation cohort to the developmental revealed significant differences in demographic profiles, medicolegal frameworks, ethnic cultural contexts and key predictors of postoperative opioid use identified by the SORG-MLA.

title: International external validation of the SORG machine learning algorithm for predicting sustained postoperative opioid prescription after anterior cervical discectomy and fusion using a Taiwanese cohort of 1,037 patients
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Calibration of SORG-MLA in the Taiwanese cohort
effect: Calibration curves showed the model overestimated risk of prolonged opioid use; recalibration with contemporary data recommended, though AUROC was 0.78 and AUPRC 0.35.
quote: Calibration curves indicated that the model overestimated the risk of prolonged opioid use.

title: International external validation of the SORG machine learning algorithm for predicting sustained postoperative opioid prescription after anterior cervical discectomy and fusion using a Taiwanese cohort of 1,037 patients
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Performance of SORG-MLA when applied to a new country population
effect: Discrimination was good (AUROC 0.78, AUPRC 0.35) and Brier 0.033 vs null 0.040, but risk was overestimated, indicating incomplete generalization.
quote: The model demonstrated good discriminative ability, with an AUROC of 0.78 and an AUPRC of 0.35.

title: Dynamic Updating of Psychosis Prediction Models in Individuals at Ultra-High Risk of Psychosis
venue: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
outcome: Calibration, discrimination, and net benefit of updated versus original psychosis prediction models over time
effect: All 3 updating methods improved performance vs original (recalibration p=.009; refitting p=.020; dynamic updating p=.001). Dynamic updating best: C-index 0.71, calibration slope 1.12.
quote: All 3 updating methods improved the predictive performance compared with the original model (recalibration: p = .009; refitting: p = .020; dynamic updating: p = .001).
sample_unit: individuals at ultra-high risk of psychosis

title: Dynamic Updating of Psychosis Prediction Models in Individuals at Ultra-High Risk of Psychosis
venue: Biological psychiatry. Cognitive neuroscience and neuroimaging
outcome: Temporal deterioration of static model calibration over the validation period
effect: The original static model was poorly calibrated over the entire validation period.
quote: The original model was poorly calibrated over the entire validation period.
sample_unit: individuals at ultra-high risk of psychosis

title: Pharmacist-led surgical medicines prescription optimization and prediction service improves patient outcomes - a machine learning based study
outcome: AUC drop from internal to temporally later external validation
effect: Internal validation AUC 0.886 vs external (2021-2022 data) AUC 0.786, ΔAUC 0.100
quote: Internal validation showed an AUC of 0.886, while external validation showed an AUC of 0.786, with a ΔAUC of 0.100, indicating the model’s consistency and generalizability across different datasets ( Supplementary Figure S4 ).

title: Pharmacist-led surgical medicines prescription optimization and prediction service improves patient outcomes - a machine learning based study
outcome: Comparative discrimination of candidate models predicting prescriber acceptance
effect: Among 11 models, Random Forest achieved AUC = 0.893, compared with LightGBM = 0.797, DT = 0.780, XGBoost = 0.777, and GBM = 0.773.
quote: Among the 11 ML models, the RF model had the best predictive performance in terms of AUC (AUC = 0.893), followed by the LightGBM model (AUC = 0.797), DT model (AUC = 0.780), XGBoost model (AUC = 0.777), and GBM model (AUC = 0.773) ( Figure 3A ).

title: Pharmacist-led surgical medicines prescription optimization and prediction service improves patient outcomes - a machine learning based study
outcome: Predictive model performance on a temporally later dataset
effect: The selected random forest model achieved an AUC of 0.786 on a temporally later validation dataset, a decrease from 0.886 during internal validation.
quote: Internal validation showed an AUC of 0.886, while external validation showed an AUC of 0.786, with a ΔAUC of 0.100, indicating the model’s consistency and generalizability across different datasets ( Supplementary Figure S4 ).

title: Pharmacist-led surgical medicines prescription optimization and prediction service improves patient outcomes - a machine learning based study
outcome: Clinical outcomes and costs after AI deployment
effect: After implementing the AI-assisted service, recommendation acceptance rose to 71.30%, median length of stay dropped to 7 days, and both total and medication costs decreased significantly.
quote: Compared to the ML development period and external validation period, the acceptance rate of pharmacists’ recommendations in the post-implementation evaluation period increased from 40.63% to 71.30%, the length of stay was reduced from 13 days (IQR: 8, 22) ( P < 0.001) to 7 days (IQR: 9, 15) ( p < 0.001), total hospitalization costs decreased from 32,263.42 RMB (IQR: 16,880.46,68,921.29) ( p < 0.001) to 20,842.89 RMB (IQR: 13,516.59, 32,055.51) ( p < 0.001), cost of medication decreased from 7847.67 RMB (IQR: 3815.45,19,980.16) ( p < 0.001) to 4,712.92 RMB (IQR: 2866.63, 7716.55) ( p < 0.001), and the ADR rate was reduced from 0.4% to 0.18% ( p = 0.095).

title: Performance of popular large language models in glaucoma patient education: A randomized controlled study
venue: Advances in ophthalmology practice and research
outcome: Recommended reading age and reading difficulty of LLM glaucoma education answers
effect: ChatGPT-4.0 had higher recommended reading age and reading difficulty scores than the other models; the abstract gives no numbers. Baichuan 2 and ChatGPT-4.0 were rated best overall.
quote: In the first stage, Baichuan 2 and ChatGPT-4.0 outperformed the other two models, though ChatGPT-4.0 had higher recommended reading age and reading difficulty scores.

title: Ability of ChatGPT to Replace Doctors in Patient Education: Cross-Sectional Comparative Analysis of Inflammatory Bowel Disease
outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT vs specialist doctor answers to IBD patient questions
effect: Median 7th grade for both ChatGPT (Q1 7th, Q3 8th) and doctors (Q1 4th, Q3 8th); no significant difference (P=.09).
quote: Regarding readability, no statistical difference was found between the responses of specialist doctors (median: 7th grade; Q1: 4th grade; Q3: 8th grade) and those of ChatGPT (median: 7th grade; Q1: 7th grade; Q3: 8th grade) according to the Mann-Whitney U test (P=.09).

title: Toward a human-centric co-design methodology for AI detection of differences between planned and delivered dose in radiotherapy
venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
outcome: Stakeholder and expert-user acceptance of an interface co-designed with end users
effect: Co-design sprint produced a simulated prototype supported by all stakeholders; expert users responded well and were confident it could lead to viable clinical implementation (no comparator).
quote: The prototype was well-received by expert users.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT for converting clinic letters into patient-friendly language: a quantitative study
outcome: Patient representatives' understanding, satisfaction, need for help, and clinical information loss for AI plain-language letters versus originals
effect: No loss of clinical information; significant increase in understanding and satisfaction, and decreased need to obtain medical help to translate letter contents, versus clinician-written originals.
quote: Translation of letters by ChatGPT-4 Classic resulted in no loss of clinical information, but did result in significant increase in understanding, satisfaction, and decrease in the need to obtain medical help to translate the letter contents by patient representatives compared with clinician-written originals.

title: Accuracy of Large Language Model-based Automatic Calculation of Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System MRI Scores from Pelvic MRI Reports
outcome: O-RADS MRI score accuracy of AI strategies versus original reporting radiologists on the same lesions
effect: Hybrid model accuracy exceeded reporting radiologists (97% [153/158] vs 88% [139/158]; P = .004); hybrid also outperformed LLM-only (97% vs 90%; P = .006).
quote: For lesions with an originally reported O-RADS score, hybrid model accuracy exceeded that of reporting radiologists (97% [153 of 158] vs 88% [139 of 158]; P = .004).

title: Large-Scale Evaluation and Liver Disease Risk Prediction in Finland's National Electronic Health Record System: Feasibility Study Using Real-World Data
outcome: Availability of model input variables in structured national EHR data for risk score calculation
effect: Using structured data only 33/51,275 identified as low risk and 308/51,275 (<1%) as moderate risk; with approximation and free text 18,895 (37%) low and 2125 (4%) moderate; no high-risk identified because waist-hip ratio was missing.
quote: We found that Kanta currently lacks many CLivD risk model input parameters in the structured format required to calculate precise risk scores.

title: Conversational Guide for Cataract Surgery Complications: A Comparative Study of Surgeons versus Large Language Model-Based Chatbot Generated Instructions for Patient Interaction
outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot versus surgeon patient-counselling responses
effect: Surgeons' readability score 10.64 was significantly less complex than chatbot's 12.54 (p < 0.001); chatbot answers were longer and more detailed.
quote: The readability scores for the surgeons (10.64) were significantly less complex than the chatbot (12.54) (p < 0.001).

title: Online patient information on labour epidural analgesia provided by UK National Health Services hospitals: assessment of readability and improvement of readability standards using ChatGPT
outcome: Proportion of hospital online labour epidural materials meeting sixth-grade readability target

title: Online patient information on labour epidural analgesia provided by UK National Health Services hospitals: assessment of readability and improvement of readability standards using ChatGPT

title: Online patient information on labour epidural analgesia provided by UK National Health Services hospitals: assessment of readability and improvement of readability standards using ChatGPT

title: Real-time surveillance system for patient deterioration: a pragmatic cluster-randomized controlled trial
outcome: In-hospital mortality, length of stay, sepsis, and ICU transfers with versus without the early warning system
effect: Intervention had 35.6% lower instantaneous risk of death (aHR 0.64), 11.2% shorter length of stay, and 7.5% lower sepsis risk; unanticipated ICU transfer risk rose 24.9% (aHR 1.25).
quote: A machine learning-based EWS, modeled on nursing surveillance patterns, decreased inpatient deterioration risk with statistical significance.

title: AI Chatbots as Sources of STD Information: A Study on Reliability and Readability
outcome: Readability of chatbot STD responses versus 6th-grade patient education standard

title: AI Chatbots as Sources of STD Information: A Study on Reliability and Readability

title: Evaluation of AI Summaries on Interdisciplinary Understanding of Ophthalmology Notes
outcome: Errors in LLM plain language summaries identified on ophthalmologist review and their risk of harm

quote: PLS error rate on ophthalmologist review was 26% (126 of 489).
sample_unit: ophthalmologist review responses on LLM-generated plain language summaries (plus 362 nonophthalmology respondents preferring PLS)

title: Evaluation of AI Summaries on Interdisciplinary Understanding of Ophthalmology Notes
outcome: Clinician understanding, satisfaction, clarity and readability of notes with vs without LLM plain language summary
effect: Diagnostic understanding +9.0 percentage points (95% CI 0.3-18.2); note detail satisfaction +21.5 points; explanation clarity +23.0 points; Flesch Reading Ease 51.8 vs 43.6.
quote: Nonophthalmology clinicians and professionals reported enhanced diagnostic understanding (percentage point increase, 9.0; 95% CI, 0.3-18.2; P = .01), increased note detail satisfaction (percentage point increase, 21.5; 95% CI, 11.4-31.5; P < .001), and improved explanation clarity (percentage point increase, 23.0; 95% CI, 12.0-33.1; P < .001) for notes containing a PLS.
sample_unit: ophthalmologist review responses on LLM-generated plain language summaries (plus 362 nonophthalmology respondents preferring PLS)

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of a Commercial AI-based Platform in Evaluating Endodontic Treatment Outcomes on Periapical Radiographs Using CBCT as the Reference Standard
outcome: AI platform vs experienced endodontists on sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, AUC against CBCT reference standard
effect: AI sensitivity higher (67.3% vs 49.3% tooth) but specificity lower (82.3% vs 92.5%); accuracy comparable at tooth level (76.3% vs 75.3%), lower at root level (78.5% vs 81.6%); AUC 0.75 vs 0.71.
quote: The AI-driven platform demonstrated higher sensitivity but lower specificity than clinicians at both tooth (sensitivity: 67.3% vs 49.3%, P < .001; specificity: 82.3% vs 92.5%, P < .001) and root levels (sensitivity: 54.3% vs 43.8%, P = .003; specificity: 86.7% vs 94.5%, P < .001).

title: Clinical implementation of AI-based screening for risk for opioid use disorder in hospitalized adults
outcome: Addiction medicine consultation rate (primary) and 30-day readmissions (secondary), pre vs post AI screener
effect: Consultations unchanged (1.35% vs 1.51%, P<0.001 for non-inferiority); 30-day readmissions reduced (OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.30-0.91, P=0.02); US$6,801 per readmission avoided.
quote: In secondary outcome analysis, the AI screener was associated with a reduction in 30-day readmissions (odds ratio: 0.53, 95% confidence interval: 0.30-0.91, P = 0.02) with an incremental cost of US$6,801 per readmission avoided, demonstrating its potential as a scalable, cost-effective solution for OUD care.

title: Can popular AI large language models provide reliable answers to frequently asked questions about rotator cuff tears?
outcome: Readability and understandability of LLM answers to rotator cuff tear questions

quote: The median PEMAT Understandability score was 83.33, with 77.3% sufficiency, while the Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease score had a median of 42.05 with 88.9% sufficiency.

title: Comparison of Initial Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Final Physician Recommendations in AI-Assisted Virtual Urgent Care Visits
outcome: Quality rating of AI recommendations versus treating physician decisions on same visits

title: FairDiffusion: Enhancing equity in latent diffusion models via fair Bayesian perturbation
outcome: Image generation quality across gender, race, and ethnicity subgroups

title: FairDiffusion: Enhancing equity in latent diffusion models via fair Bayesian perturbation

effect: FairDiffusion improved both image quality and semantic alignment of clinical features; no numeric values are given in the abstract.

title: Psychological Factors Influencing Appropriate Reliance on AI-enabled Clinical Decision Support Systems: Experimental Web-Based Study Among Dermatologists

quote: Reliance on AI was stronger for correct advice than for incorrect advice (t<sub>222</sub>=4.2; P<.001; Cohen d=0.1).

title: Psychological Factors Influencing Appropriate Reliance on AI-enabled Clinical Decision Support Systems: Experimental Web-Based Study Among Dermatologists
outcome: Dermatologist accuracy with versus without AI support in lesion classification

title: Automated computation of the HEART score with the GPT-4 large language model
venue: The American journal of emergency medicine

effect: Weighted kappa with adjudicators was 0.67 for the LLM and 0.66 for the APP. The LLM's mean HEART score was higher (5.06 vs 4.69 adjudicators, 4.23 APP). No significant difference in 60-day MACE prediction (all p > .05).
quote: Among the remaining 551 participants, agreement by Cohen's weighted kappa between the LLM and adjudicators was 0.67 which was similar to the agreement of 0.66 between the APP and adjudicators.

title: Retrieval augmented generation for 10 large language models and its generalizability in assessing medical fitness
outcome: Accuracy of fitness-for-surgery assessment with RAG grounding in guidelines vs non-RAG GPT-4
effect: GPT4_international RAG achieved 96.4% accuracy vs 92.9% for non-RAG GPT-4 and 92.9% for RAG with local guidelines; humans 86.6%.
quote: The Generative Pre-training Transformer (GPT)4_international model emerged as the most accurate model with the highest accuracy in predicting medical fitness for surgery (96.4%) compared to answers given by human evaluators (86.6%), as well as its non-RAG counterpart (92.9%) and RAG counterpart with local guidelines (92.9%) (Fig. 1 and Supplementary Table 2 ).

title: Retrieval augmented generation for 10 large language models and its generalizability in assessing medical fitness
outcome: Compare LLM-RAG accuracy against clinicians on same scenarios for surgical fitness
effect: GPT4_international outperformed human evaluators (96.4% vs 86.6%, OR 4.84, p=0.016); false negative rate 25% vs 62.5% for humans.
quote: The GPT4_international model performed better than humans in evaluations of patient’s fitness for surgery (Odds Ratio (OR) = 4.84, p = 0.016).

title: Retrieval augmented generation for 10 large language models and its generalizability in assessing medical fitness

sample_unit: clinical scenarios (3234 LLM responses vs 448 human responses)

title: Retrieval augmented generation for 10 large language models and its generalizability in assessing medical fitness
outcome: Accuracy in sicker ASA 3 patients across models in simulated scenarios
effect: GPT4 models had highest accuracy in ASA 3 patients, while Gemini and Llama2-13b had less than 50% accuracy.
quote: The comparison, the Gemini and Large Language Model Meta AI (LLAMA)2-13b models had less than 50% accuracy when assessing ASA 3 patients (Supplementary Fig 1 ).

title: Retrieval augmented generation for 10 large language models and its generalizability in assessing medical fitness
outcome: Repeated-run reproducibility
effect: GPT4 RAG S.C.O.R.E reproducibility 4.86/5; safety 4.93/5.
quote: The S.C.O.R.E (Safety, Consensus, Objectivity, Reproducibility, Explainability) evaluation showed that the GPT4 RAG model was able to have high reproducibility of results (4.86 out of 5) and provided safe instructions (4.93 out of 5) (Supplementary Table 7 ).

title: Implementation of a national AI technology program on cardiovascular outcomes and the health system

title: Patient education strategies in pediatric orthopaedics: using ChatGPT to answer frequently asked questions on scoliosis

title: Primary Care Provider Preferences Regarding Artificial Intelligence in Point-of-Care Cancer Screening

title: Using Large Language Models to Automate Data Extraction From Surgical Pathology Reports: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: LLM extraction concordance with human reviewers on 12 questions across 84 reports

title: Sensitivity of a deep-learning-based breast cancer risk prediction model

title: Can off-the-shelf visual large language models detect and diagnose ocular diseases from retinal photographs?
outcome: Ophthalmologist-rated quality of VLLM diagnostic descriptions of retinal images
effect: Only 21.2% of GPT-4V default, 4.8% of GPT-4V data analyst and 28.6% of Gemini responses rated good; all VLLMs inadequate for accurate diagnosis despite 97.1% detection by GPT-4V default.
quote: Despite the relatively high detection rates, the quality of diagnostic descriptions was generally suboptimal-with only 21.2% of GPT-4V's (default) responses, 4.8% of GPT-4V's (data analyst) responses and 28.6% for Google Gemini's responses rated as good.

title: Sociodemographic biases in medical decision making by large language models
outcome: Change in LLM clinical recommendations when patient sociodemographic labels varied with clinical details held constant
effect: Black, unhoused, or LGBTQIA+ labeled cases were more often directed to urgent care, invasive interventions or mental health evaluations; LGBTQIA+ subgroups got mental health assessments ~6-7 times more than clinically indicated; differences persisted after multiple-hypothesis correction.
quote: Compared to both a physician-derived baseline and each model's own control case without sociodemographic identifiers, cases labeled as Black or unhoused or identifying as LGBTQIA+ were more frequently directed toward urgent care, invasive interventions or mental health evaluations.
sample_unit: emergency department cases (each in 32 sociodemographic variations; >1.7 million model outputs)

title: Sociodemographic biases in medical decision making by large language models
outcome: Differences in recommended imaging and testing by income label across LLMs
effect: High-income-labeled cases received significantly more advanced imaging (CT/MRI) recommendations (P < 0.001), while low- and middle-income-labeled cases were often limited to basic or no further testing.
quote: Similarly, cases labeled as having high-income status received significantly more recommendations (P < 0.001) for advanced imaging tests such as computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging, while low- and middle-income-labeled cases were often limited to basic or no further testing.
sample_unit: emergency department cases (each in 32 sociodemographic variations; >1.7 million model outputs)

title: Cross-institutional validation of a polar map-free 3D deep learning model for obstructive coronary artery disease prediction using myocardial perfusion imaging: insights into generalizability and bias
venue: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
outcome: Performance drop of AI model between development-site and external-site cohorts
effect: External cohort AUC lower than internal: patient-based 0.713 vs. 0.813; vessel-based 0.733 vs. 0.782.
quote: The model showed significantly lower performance in the external cohort compared to the internal cohort in both patient-based (AUC: 0.713 vs. 0.813) and vessel-based (AUC: 0.733 vs. 0.782) analyses, but still outperformed stress TPD (all p < 0.001).

title: Cross-institutional validation of a polar map-free 3D deep learning model for obstructive coronary artery disease prediction using myocardial perfusion imaging: insights into generalizability and bias
venue: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
outcome: Performance variation across sites
effect: Model performance was significantly lower at the external site than the internal site (patient AUC 0.713 vs 0.813).
quote: The model showed significantly lower performance in the external cohort compared to the internal cohort in both patient-based (AUC: 0.713 vs. 0.813) and vessel-based (AUC: 0.733 vs. 0.782) analyses, but still outperformed stress TPD (all p < 0.001).

title: Cross-institutional validation of a polar map-free 3D deep learning model for obstructive coronary artery disease prediction using myocardial perfusion imaging: insights into generalizability and bias
venue: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
outcome: AI performance differences across patient subgroups (stress type, age)
effect: Performance lower in treadmill stress MPI patients in the internal cohort and in patients over 70 years old in the external cohort.
quote: The performance was lower in patients who underwent treadmill stress MPI in the internal cohort and in patients over 70 years old in the external cohort.

title: Cross-institutional validation of a polar map-free 3D deep learning model for obstructive coronary artery disease prediction using myocardial perfusion imaging: insights into generalizability and bias
venue: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
outcome: AI model compared with conventional stress TPD on same data
effect: The DL model outperformed stress TPD in both internal and external cohorts (all p < 0.001), despite lower external performance.
quote: The model showed significantly lower performance in the external cohort compared to the internal cohort in both patient-based (AUC: 0.713 vs. 0.813) and vessel-based (AUC: 0.733 vs. 0.782) analyses, but still outperformed stress TPD (all p < 0.001).

title: Labor-Efficient Pathological Auxiliary Diagnostic Model for Primary and Metastatic Tumor Tissue Detection in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
venue: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
outcome: Pathologist diagnostic accuracy and time with vs without AI assistance for lymph node metastasis detection
effect: PANseg augmented the diagnostic accuracy of 6 pathologists from 0.888 to 0.961, while reducing the average diagnostic time by 32.6% (72.0 vs 48.5 minutes).
quote: In lymph node metastasis detection, PANseg augmented the diagnostic accuracy of 6 pathologists from 0.888 to 0.961, while reducing the average diagnostic time by 32.6% (72.0 vs 48.5 minutes).

title: Labor-Efficient Pathological Auxiliary Diagnostic Model for Primary and Metastatic Tumor Tissue Detection in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
venue: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
outcome: Performance on external test set and unseen sample types versus internal tests
effect: External AUROC 0.950 vs FSB 0.958; unseen fresh-frozen specimens AUROC 0.878 and biopsy sections 0.821, lower than internal (0.969-0.991).
quote: Moreover, the model demonstrated considerable generalizability with previously unseen sample types, attaining AUROCs of 0.878 on fresh-frozen specimens (20 patients/20 WSIs) and 0.821 on biopsy sections (20 patients/20 WSIs).

title: An AI-Powered Strategy for Managing Patient Messaging Load and Reducing Burnout
outcome: Draft utilization and time savings by role and specialty
effect: Overall draft utilization 38%; clinicians 43% vs scheduling staff 33%. Time saved 23 seconds for support staff vs 3 seconds for clinicians; variability across specialties.
quote: However, the effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI)-generated draft responses varies by clinical role and specialty, indicating the need for tailored implementations.

title: How Do Radiologists Currently Monitor AI in Radiology and What Challenges Do They Face? An Interview Study and Qualitative Analysis
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Extent of ongoing monitoring of deployed radiology AI
effect: Monitoring was nascent; most AI projects had not reached full live deployment. Manual retrospective comparison with the radiology report was most common; automated and statistical methods were much less common.
quote: The findings suggest that AI monitoring in radiology is still relatively nascent as most of the AI projects had not yet progressed into a fully live clinical deployment.

title: How Do Radiologists Currently Monitor AI in Radiology and What Challenges Do They Face? An Interview Study and Qualitative Analysis
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Challenges radiologists face in monitoring AI, including resource capacity
effect: Lack of resources to support AI monitoring and uncertainty about building a robust, scalable monitoring process were the biggest challenges.
quote: The biggest challenges are a lack of resources to support AI monitoring and uncertainty about how to create a robust and scalable process of monitoring the breadth and variety of radiology AI applications available.

title: Extracting Pulmonary Embolism Diagnoses From Radiology Impressions Using GPT-4o: Large Language Model Evaluation Study
outcome: GPT-4o versus baseline Clinical Longformer on PE extraction performance, same validation set
effect: GPT-4o outperformed Clinical Longformer in 2 metrics: sensitivity 1.0 (P<.001) and F1-score 0.975 (95% CI 0.9495-0.9947; P<.001) on validation dataset.
quote: GPT-4o outperformed the Clinical Longformer in 2 of the metrics, achieving a sensitivity of 1.0 (95% CI 1.0-1.0; Wilcoxon test, P<.001) and an F1-score of 0.975 (95% CI 0.9495-0.9947; Wilcoxon test, P<.001) across the validation dataset.
sample_unit: operational radiology report impressions (postdeployment); 200 validation impressions

title: Extracting Pulmonary Embolism Diagnoses From Radiology Impressions Using GPT-4o: Large Language Model Evaluation Study
outcome: Postdeployment performance of GPT-4o on operational records against reference labels
effect: On 200 operational records, sensitivity 1.0 (95% CI 1.0-1.0), specificity 0.94 (95% CI 0.8913-0.9804), F1 0.97 (95% CI 0.9479-0.9908).
quote: Postdeployment evaluations also showed strong performance of the deployed GPT-4o model with a sensitivity of 1.0 (95% CI 1.0-1.0), a specificity of 0.94 (95% CI 0.8913-0.9804), and an F1-score of 0.97 (95% CI 0.9479-0.9908).
sample_unit: operational radiology report impressions (postdeployment); 200 validation impressions

title: One-class support vector machines for detecting population drift in deployed machine learning medical diagnostics
outcome: Share of simulated drifted records flagged as outliers versus inliers by OCSVM at three noise levels
effect: Records misclassified as inliers: 27/10,000 (0.27%) at 5% noise, 486 (4.86%) at 10%, 851 (8.51%) at 30%. Most drifted records were flagged, but detection fell as overlap with training data grew.
quote: At the lowest noise level (5%), the model classified 27 records as inliers (27 out of 10,000).

title: One-class support vector machines for detecting population drift in deployed machine learning medical diagnostics
outcome: Ability of unsupervised OCSVM monitor to detect simulated input population drift without ground-truth labels
effect: Sensitivity to drift decreased as overlap increased: inliers 27 (5% noise), 486 (10%), 851 (30%) of 10,000 each. Proof of concept on simulated data only.
quote: We hypothesised that increased noise would correlate with more OCSVM-detected inliers, indicating a sensitivity to population drift.

title: The Role of ChatGPT in osteoporosis management: a comparative analysis with clinical expertise
outcome: ChatGPT diagnostic and treatment recommendation accuracy and response time versus five physiatrists on same scenarios
effect: 91% of ChatGPT responses entirely accurate; 8% incomplete; mean answer time 2.3 ± 0.76 min for ChatGPT versus 5.4 ± 2.45 min for clinicians (p < 0.001).
quote: ChatGPT exhibited a high degree of diagnostic accuracy, with 91% of responses being entirely accurate.

title: Artificial intelligence-large language models (AI-LLMs) for reliable and accurate cardiotocography (CTG) interpretation in obstetric practice
outcome: AI-LLM CTG interpretation quality scores compared with junior and senior doctors on same images
effect: ChatGPT-4o 77.86 vs SHDs 80.43 (p>0.05) and JHDs 61.57; Gemini Advanced 57.14 and Copilot 47.29 scored below JHDs.
quote: ChatGPT-4o scored 77.86, outperforming the Gemini Advanced (57.14), Copilot (47.29), and JHDs (61.57).
sample_unit: CTG images interpreted by each of 3 AI-LLMs, 5 senior doctors and 5 junior doctors, scored by 5 blinded experts

title: Real-World Assessment of the Efficacy of Computer-Assisted Diagnosis in Colonoscopy: A Single Institution Cohort Study in Singapore
outcome: Negative predictive value of adenoma characterization by anatomic region, reflecting local polyp prevalence
effect: NPV was 80.3% for rectosigmoid lesions vs 54.2% for colonic lesions, attributed to hyperplastic polyp prevalence of 11.4% vs 5.4%. Overall sensitivity 89.4%, specificity 61.7%, NPV 69.8%.
quote: The negative predictive value for rectosigmoid lesions (80.3%) was notably higher than for colonic lesions (54.2%), attributed to the increased prevalence of hyperplastic rectosigmoid polyps (11.4%) vs other colonic regions (5.4%).

title: Learning to Fake It: Limited Responses and Fabricated References Provided by ChatGPT for Medical Questions
outcome: Proportion of ChatGPT-provided references that were fabricated
effect: Of 59 references evaluated, 41 (69%) were fabricated, although they appeared real; fabricated citations used real authors, pertinent titles, and credible journal formats.
quote: Of the 59 references evaluated, 41 (69%) were fabricated, although they appeared real.
sample_unit: ChatGPT responses rated by expert authors (20 questions; 59 references evaluated)

title: Learning to Fake It: Limited Responses and Fabricated References Provided by ChatGPT for Medical Questions
outcome: Fabricated references and factual errors in AI-generated text for medical manuscripts
effect: 69% of references fabricated; median quality score 60% (Q1 50%, Q3 85%); 5 major and 7 minor factual errors among 17 evaluated responses.
quote: Users of ChatGPT should pay particular attention to the references provided before integration into medical manuscripts.
sample_unit: ChatGPT responses rated by expert authors (20 questions; 59 references evaluated)

title: Artificial Intelligence for Kidney Stone Spectra Analysis: Using Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Quality Assurance in the Clinical Laboratory
outcome: Concordance among predictions selected for automatic classification versus secondary human review
effect: Concordance was 98.7% (95% CI, 98.56%-98.9%) for autoPass candidates versus 84.3% (95% CI, 84.0%-84.6%) for cases flagged for manual secondary review.
quote: When the stone spectra were grouped into those stones selected for autoPass (candidate for automatic classification) and those not selected (flagged for manual secondary review), the concordance rates were 98.7% (95% CI, 98.56%-98.9%) and 84.3% (95% CI, 84.0%-84.6%), respectively.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Kidney Stone Spectra Analysis: Using Artificial Intelligence Algorithms for Quality Assurance in the Clinical Laboratory
outcome: report revision rate
effect: The report revision rate was nearly 8 times higher during the AI implementation period compared to the control period (RR 7.9, 95% CI 4.1-15.2).
quote: The report revision rate during the AI implementation period was nearly 8 times higher than that during the control period (relative risk, 7.9; 95% CI, 4.1-15.2).

title: Inherent Bias in Large Language Models: A Random Sampling Analysis
outcome: Change in GPT-4 simulated physician choices when patient and physician demographics varied
effect: Simulated physicians favored patients with demographics similar to their own, with most pairwise comparisons significant (P<.05). Nondescript physicians favored White, male, and young patients.
quote: Overall, simulated physicians consistently demonstrated racial, gender, age, political affiliation, and sexual orientation bias in clinical decision-making.
sample_unit: simulated physician decisions (13 questions x 1000 repetitions)

title: The Real-World Impact of Vestibular Schwannoma Fully Automated Volume Measures on the Evaluation of Size Change and Clinical Management Outcomes in a Multidisciplinary Meeting Setting
venue: The journal of international advanced otology
outcome: Effect of AI volume measures on radiological classification and management decisions in simulated MDMs
effect: AI volumes changed radiological classification of size change (z=2.49, P=.01) but not management decisions (z=0.30, P=.76) versus linear measures.
quote: Provision of fully automated VS volume measurements to "real-world" MDM preparation significantly impacted the radiological classification of VS size change but did not influence management decisions.

title: Evaluating a customised large language model (DELSTAR) and its ability to address medication-related questions associated with delirium: a quantitative exploratory study
outcome: Statement accuracy and data credibility/source quality of custom delirium LLM outputs versus SLRs
effect: DELSTAR gave more accurate, comprehensive information than SLRs (p < 0.05), but mainly relied on less reliable internet sources; improvements needed in high-quality data use and citation.
quote: DELSTAR demonstrated more accurate and comprehensive information compared to information retrieved by traditional systematic literature reviews (SLRs) (p < 0.05) and accessed Application Programmer Interfaces (API), private databases, and high-quality sources despite mainly relying on less reliable internet sources.
sample_unit: not reported (statements and benchmark dataset items)

title: Feasibility Study for Using Large Language Models to Identify Goals-of-Care Documentation at Scale in Patients With Advanced Cancer
outcome: Hallucination index: share of LLM-quoted source text not matching EHR text
effect: Hallucination index for explanations was low; the LLM did not produce text that was not found in EHRs (326 patients, ~1,400 notes).
quote: The hallucination index for explanations was low, suggesting that the LLM did not produce text that was not found in EHRs.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Large Language Models in Providing Patient Education for Chinese Patients With Ocular Myasthenia Gravis: Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Readability of LLM responses to OMG patient questions, rated by ophthalmologists and patients
effect: GEMINI easiest to understand; GPT-4o most complex, suitable for higher-education readers. Patients rated Ernie 3.5 slightly more readable than ChatGPT o1-preview (4.31 vs 4.03, P=.01).
quote: GEMINI (Google DeepMind) provided the easiest-to-understand responses in readability assessments, while GPT-4o had the most complex responses, suitable for readers with higher education levels.
sample_unit: patients with ocular myasthenia gravis (phase 2); 23 patient questions and 130 exam questions in phase 1

title: Can ChatGPT be trusted as a resource for a scholarly article on treatment planning implant-supported prostheses?
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT literature-based answers on implant treatment planning versus best available evidence
effect: ChatGPT's original answers to all six questions were revised after higher-quality, timely studies were supplied, and the revisions often reversed the original conclusions (e.g., splinting, cantilevers, overdenture preference).
quote: ChatGPT has not demonstrated the ability to accurately cull the literature, stratify the rigor of the evidence, and extract accurate implications from the studies selected to deliver the best evidence-based answers to questions on treatment planning implant-supported prostheses.

title: Can ChatGPT be trusted as a resource for a scholarly article on treatment planning implant-supported prostheses?
outcome: Reliability of ChatGPT as a source for synthesizing literature for scholarly articles
effect: Rated on 4 indices (retrievable source, representative literature, accurate interpretation, conclusion reflects best evidence); concluded ChatGPT could not reliably synthesize the literature for the 6 questions.
quote: ChatGPT has not demonstrated the ability to accurately cull the literature, stratify the rigor of the evidence, and extract accurate implications from the studies selected to deliver the best evidence-based answers to questions on treatment planning implant-supported prostheses.

title: Assessing the quality of ChatGPT's responses to commonly asked questions about trigger finger treatment
venue: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of ChatGPT responses about trigger finger
effect: Average readability corresponded to university level, making information difficult for patients with low health literacy.
quote: The average readability level corresponded to the university level, making the information difficult to understand for patients with low health literacy.

title: Assessing the quality of ChatGPT's responses to commonly asked questions about trigger finger treatment
venue: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
outcome: Presence of scientific references in ChatGPT responses (JAMA Benchmark)
effect: Absence of scientific references was a significant drawback per JAMA Benchmark criteria.
quote: According to the JAMA Benchmark criteria, the absence of scientific references was a significant drawback.

title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: Calibration of LLM confidence estimates for deprescribing recommendations
effect: Confidence poorly calibrated; severely left-skewed with minimum confidence 58.5% (eligibility) and 54.5% (deprescribing); selective prediction only marginally improved performance.
quote: However, despite some minor improvements, we find that the LLM is poorly calibrated, as shown in Figure 6 B.

title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: LLM making deprescribing recommendations, including potentially harmful ones, on clinical cases
effect: Deprescribing step PPV 0.47; LLM recommended deprescribing far more often (11.6%) than students (1.91%); harmful cases observed, e.g., suggesting deprescribing anticoagulation after recent thromboembolism.
quote: Cases with the potential for human harm were observed, such as suggesting deprescribing anticoagulation in a patient with recent thromboembolism.

title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: Selective prediction (abstention/deferral to humans) effect on LLM F1 performance
effect: Consistency-based deferral raised F1 to 0.85-0.88 (step 1) and 0.62-0.73 (step 2); verbalized confidence gave narrower ranges (0.58-0.69 step 2); gains marginal due to poor calibration.
quote: Selective prediction marginally improved the LLM’s filtering accuracy by enabling it to defer uncertain cases to human reviewers.

title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: LLM application of deprescribing criteria to patient cases, error types
effect: Errors due to complex inclusion/exclusion criteria (54.5%) and ambiguous clinical contexts such as missing information (39.3%); step 2 PPV 0.47, F1 0.58.
quote: Adjudication revealed that while the model excelled at identifying when there was a deprescribing criterion related to one of the patient's medications, it often struggled with determining whether that criterion applied to the specific case due to complex inclusion and exclusion criteria (54.5% of errors) and ambiguous clinical contexts (eg, missing information; 39.3% of errors).

title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: LLM versus medical students on criteria filtering and deprescribing recommendation, adjudicated
effect: LLM better at criteria filtering (80.1% vs 59.5% correct, P=.02) but worse, not significantly, at applying criteria (P=.178).
quote: However, in applying relevant criteria, GPT-4o performed worse than the medical students, though the difference was not statistically significant (McNemar test: χ 2 1 =1.818; P =.178).

title: Identifying Deprescribing Opportunities With Large Language Models in Older Adults: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: errors from missing or ambiguous data
effect: Complex inclusion/exclusion caused 54.5% of errors; ambiguous contexts including missing information caused 39.3%.
quote: Adjudication revealed that while the model excelled at identifying when there was a deprescribing criterion related to one of the patient's medications, it often struggled with determining whether that criterion applied to the specific case due to complex inclusion and exclusion criteria (54.5% of errors) and ambiguous clinical contexts (eg, missing information; 39.3% of errors).

title: Effect of a ChatGPT-based digital counseling intervention on anxiety and depression in patients with cancer: A prospective, randomized trial
outcome: Change in HADS anxiety and depression scores, ChatGPT counseling vs clinician-led education
effect: ChatGPT group had lower median HADS-Anxiety (6 vs 8; P=0.002) and HADS-Depression (6 vs 9; P<0.001) than controls; ChatGPT use predicted anxiety reduction (OR 18.684).
quote: At follow-up, the ChatGPT group exhibited significantly lower median HADS-Anxiety (6 [0-17] vs. 8 [1-17]; P = 0.002) and HADS-Depression (6 [0-20] vs. 9 [0-19]; P < 0.001) scores compared to controls.

title: Prospective external validation of the automated PIPRA multivariable prediction model for postoperative delirium on real-world data from a consecutive cohort of non-cardiac surgery inpatients
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of PIPRA on prospective local hospital data
effect: AUROC=0.77 (95% CI 0.72 to 0.82); generally accurate calibration, slightly overpredicting risk in high-risk patients; POD occurred in 11.5% (n=100).
quote: The PIPRA model showed good discrimination (AUROC=0.77, 95% CI: 0.72 to 0.82) and generally accurate calibration, though slightly overpredicting risk in high-risk patients.

title: Deep learning-based classification of lymphedema and other lower limb edema diseases using clinical images
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI models versus human evaluators on lower limb edema images
effect: EfficientNetV2 achieved the highest accuracy of 78.6%; human evaluators' diagnostic accuracy plateaued at 62.7%.
quote: The AI system consistently outperformed human evaluators, whose diagnostic accuracy plateaued at 62.7%.

title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
outcome: Discrimination of AI early warning score versus NEWS and MEWS on same data
effect: VC-MAES AUROC 0.896 vs NEWS 0.797 and MEWS 0.722; AUPRC 0.336 vs 0.125 (NEWS) and 0.079 (MEWS).
quote: These results indicate that VC-MAES outperformed both NEWS and MEWS in terms of both AUROC and AUPRC ( Figure 1 ).

title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
outcome: Prospective silent-mode performance of the early warning model on live data
effect: Model generated real-time predictions undisclosed to clinicians; prospective AUROC 0.918 (full data) on 6039 encounters at an external site.
quote: The model generated predictions in real-time; however, these predictions were neither disclosed to healthcare providers nor incorporated into clinical decision-making processes.

title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
outcome: AUROC of early warning score under missing inputs and forced imputation
effect: AUROC 0.918 with actual data fell to 0.883 with mean-based imputation and 0.827 with MICE; specificity at 80% sensitivity fell from 85.5% to 78.3%.
quote: When missing values were imputed using values randomly drawn from within one SD of the mean observed values for the corresponding non-event and event groups, the AUROC decreased to 0.883 (95% CI: 0.875–0.891) compared with 0.918 (95% CI: 0.912–0.924) under the model’s default normal-value imputation method (DeLong test, p < 0.001).

title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
outcome: Model AUROC with minimal inputs versus full inputs, with normal-value imputation
effect: With only vital signs and age, AUROC 0.896 (vs NEWS 0.797, MEWS 0.722); adding available clinical data raised it to 0.918 (p<0.001).
quote: Upon reintroducing the full set of originally collected clinical data, previously treated as missing, the VC-MAES performance improved significantly compared with the vital-signs-only scenario.

title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
outcome: Missing-input and imputation stress testing
effect: Mean imputation decreased AUROC from 0.918 to 0.883; MICE declined further to 0.827.
quote: When missing values were imputed using values randomly drawn from within one SD of the mean observed values for the corresponding non-event and event groups, the AUROC decreased to 0.883 (95% CI: 0.875–0.891) compared with 0.918 (95% CI: 0.912–0.924) under the model’s default normal-value imputation method (DeLong test, p < 0.001).

title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
outcome: Missing patient data and predictive accuracy
effect: Withheld clinical data lowered AUROC/AUPRC; reintroducing data increased AUROC 0.896 to 0.918 and AUPRC 0.336 to 0.352.
quote: The AUROC increased from 0.896 to 0.918 (95% CI: 0.912–0.924; DeLong test p < 0.001), and the AUPRC increased from 0.336 (95% CI: 0.312–0.361) to 0.352 (95% CI: 0.329–0.373), further enhancing the model’s predictive capabilities.

title: Preserving Informative Presence: How Missing Data and Imputation Strategies Affect the Performance of an AI-Based Early Warning Score
outcome: discrimination of AI versus traditional early warning scores
effect: AUROC 0.896 vs 0.797 (NEWS) and 0.722 (MEWS); AUPRC 0.336 vs 0.125 (NEWS) and 0.079 (MEWS)
quote: VC-MAES achieved the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.896 using only vital signs and age, outperforming traditional EWSs, including the National Early Warning Score (0.797) and the Modified Early Warning Score (0.722).

title: Thyro-GenAI: A Chatbot Using Retrieval-Augmented Generative Models for Personalized Thyroid Disease Management
outcome: Specialist-ranked response quality of RAG chatbot versus non-RAG service LLMs
effect: Thyro-GenAI had highest overall response quality inverse-weighted mean rank: 3.0 vs ChatGPT 2.3, Perplexity 2.8, Claude 1.9; reference quality 3.1 vs 2.3, 3.2, 1.8.
quote: The overall inverse-weighted mean rankings for Thyro-GenAI, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude were 3.0, 2.3, 2.8, and 1.9, respectively.
sample_unit: personalized clinical questions about thyroid disease

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Models in Clinical Infectious Disease Consultations: A Cross-Sectional Analysis Among Specialists and Resident Trainees
outcome: Whether clinician reviewers detect harmful or inaccurate AI outputs
effect: Specialists were five times more likely than residents to rate responses harmless; post hoc analysis showed specialists may disregard conflicting or inaccurate information. Fewer than two-fifths of responses were deemed harmless.
quote: Post hoc analysis revealed that specialists may inadvertently disregard conflicting or inaccurate information in their assessments.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Models in Clinical Infectious Disease Consultations: A Cross-Sectional Analysis Among Specialists and Resident Trainees
outcome: Human vulnerability to failing to detect incorrect or harmful AI outputs
effect: Specialists rated responses higher than resident trainees in all domains (p < 0.001) and were five times more likely to consider responses harmless, indicating vulnerabilities in safeguarding against harmful outputs.
quote: In our analysis, we have demonstrated disconcerting human vulnerabilities in safeguarding against potentially harmful outputs, which seemed to be most apparent among experienced specialists.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Models in Clinical Infectious Disease Consultations: A Cross-Sectional Analysis Among Specialists and Resident Trainees
outcome: Comparative performance of candidate LLM chatbots on the same clinical scenarios
effect: GPT-4.0 had higher composite scores than Gemini Pro (p = 0.001) and Claude 2 (p = 0.006), and was better on factual consistency, comprehensiveness, and absence of harm.
quote: Analysis showed that GPT-4.0 achieved significantly higher composite scores compared to Gemini Pro (p = 0.001) and Claude 2 (p = 0.006).

title: Deep Learning-Based Glaucoma Detection Using Clinical Notes: A Comparative Study of Long Short-Term Memory and Convolutional Neural Network Models
outcome: Model performance across racial subgroups (Asian, Black, White) for glaucoma detection
effect: CNN Overall AUC 0.80, LSTM 0.01 lower. Both models showed disparities and biases across racial groups; CNN showed reduced group disparities compared to LSTM.
quote: Both models showed disparities and biases in performance across different racial groups.

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Calibration testing against predefined AUC and accuracy-deviation thresholds before clinical integration
effect: Initial model fell below the AUC threshold (0.81). After developer updates, version 0.15.0 reached AUC 0.81 and no metric deviated >10%, enabling PACS integration.
quote: Initial calibration testing of the AI model yielded promising results; however, the AUC and relative accuracy deviation fell below the established thresholds ( Figure 5 a, Table 6 ).

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Monthly technical monitoring of missing or incomplete AI outputs
effect: Defects (no output or incomplete image analysis) exceeded the 10% threshold several times. The average defect proportion declined from 9.0% to 1.0% after feedback-driven fixes.
quote: The average proportion of technical defects declined from 9.0% to 1.0%, while the clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0.

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Monthly expert radiologist review of sampled AI outputs (clinical assessment score)
effect: Across 1160 sampled studies, the clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0. A dip in months 15–16 followed a change of reviewer.
quote: The clinical evaluation plot shows a steady upward trend ( Figure 7 ).

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Local diagnostic performance against acceptance thresholds and claimed accuracy
effect: Initial AUC was 0.73, below the 0.81 acceptance threshold; relative accuracy deviation also failed acceptance criteria.
quote: Initial calibration testing of the AI model yielded promising results; however, the AUC and relative accuracy deviation fell below the established thresholds ( Figure 5 a, Table 6 ).

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Technical failures associated with local configuration and examination parameters
effect: Technical defects exceeded the 10% threshold, predominantly involving incomplete image analysis; identified contributors included mammography unit configuration problems and incorrect examination parameters.
quote: Key contributing factors included mammography unit configuration problems, incorrect examination parameters set by technicians, PACS technical issues, and AI developer errors.

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Technical defects and clinical assessment following monitoring-driven corrective updates
effect: Following iterative testing, monitoring, feedback, and updates, average technical defects declined from 9.0% to 1.0%; clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0 in an uncontrolled before–after comparison.
quote: The average proportion of technical defects declined from 9.0% to 1.0%, while the clinical assessment score improved from 63.4 to 72.0.

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Functional testing findings
effect: Initial expert radiologist review of AI outputs identified missing labels and inappropriate use of color graphic masks.
quote: Initial functional testing of the AI model (version 0.14.0) revealed two inconsistencies with the Baseline Functional Requirements: (1) absence of a “For research purposes only” label in both DICOM SR and additional image series, and (2) using color graphic masks to highlight pathological findings ( Figure 4 ).

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Initial calibration testing performance
effect: Validation on local historical data found that the model's initial AUC and relative accuracy deviation failed to meet established thresholds.
quote: Initial calibration testing of the AI model yielded promising results; however, the AUC and relative accuracy deviation fell below the established thresholds ( Figure 5 a, Table 6 ).

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Performance after model adjustments
effect: Following model adjustments based on local testing, the AUC improved by 24.7% (from 0.73 to 0.91) and accuracy by 15.6%.
quote: Specifically, the AUC rose by 24.7% (from 0.73 to 0.91), the accuracy improved by 15.6% (from 0.77 to 0.89), sensitivity grew by 37.1% (from 0.62 to 0.85), and specificity increased by 10.7% (from 0.84 to 0.93).

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Performance of updated model version
effect: Repeat local calibration testing of the updated model version verified that the AUC increased to 0.81, meeting acceptance criteria.
quote: The second calibration testing of model version 0.15.0 demonstrated an improvement in diagnostic accuracy. The AUC increased to 0.81, meeting the threshold criteria, and no metric deviated downward by more than 10% compared to the claimed values ( Figure 5 b, Table 6 ).

title: Evolution of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Application for Mammography
outcome: Technical defects over time
effect: Technical monitoring detected instances where technical defects, such as incomplete image analysis or missing outputs, exceeded the 10% threshold.
quote: The technical defect monitoring plot highlights several instances where the technical defects exceeded the established threshold ( Figure 6 a).

title: Assessing the Usability of ChatGPT Responses Compared to Other Online Information in Hand Surgery
outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT versus Google responses to hand surgery patient questions
effect: Google averaged an eighth-grade reading level for moderate-high consensus topics versus college sophomore level for ChatGPT (P<.0001); low consensus topics had poor readability throughout; ChatGPT-4 was less readable than ChatGPT-3.5 for low consensus topics (P<.01).
quote: Compared to Google, ChatGPT does not provide readable responses when providing reliable medical information.
sample_unit: responses (3 queries x 20 repetitions x 3 sources)

title: AI in clinical decision-making: ChatGPT-4 vs. Llama2 for otolaryngology cases
venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and appropriateness of recommended examinations and treatment versus expert decisions
effect: ChatGPT-4 diagnosed 82% correctly vs Llama2 76%; appropriate tests 88% vs 83%; appropriate treatment 80% vs 72%; both sometimes suggested inappropriate tests.
quote: Sometimes, both systems suggested inappropriate tests.

title: Detecting emergencies in patient portal messages using large language models and knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Emergency detection performance of LLM with vs without retrieval grounding in triage book
effect: Prompt-only sensitivity 0.73, precision 0.27; naive RAG 0.83/0.45; KG local 0.95/0.63; KG global sensitivity 0.98, precision 0.80, F1 0.88; all differences significant (P = .001).
quote: The Friedman tests revealed significant differences among all models for each metric ( P = .001).

title: Detecting emergencies in patient portal messages using large language models and knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: missed and unnecessary emergency escalations
effect: Global-search KG RAG misclassified 10 non-emergency messages (0.98%) as emergencies and 1 emergency message (0.1%) as non-emergency.
quote: The RAG from Knowledge Graph (global search) model misclassified 10 non-emergency messages (0.98%) as emergencies and 1 emergency message (0.1%) as a non-emergency.

title: Detecting emergencies in patient portal messages using large language models and knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Recognition of emergencies in patient messages by LLM without retrieval
effect: Prompt-only model sensitivity 0.73 [0.57, 0.86], missing about a quarter of emergency messages; an emergency drug-interaction message was missed by three of four models.
quote: The prompt-only model, while achieving an accuracy of 0.91 [0.89, 0.93], showed limitations in sensitivity (0.73 [0.5, 0.86]) and precision (0.27 [0.19, 0.35]), indicating a lower capability to correctly identify emergency messages and a higher rate of false positives.

title: Detecting emergencies in patient portal messages using large language models and knowledge graph-based retrieval-augmented generation
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Knowledge gaps causing missed serious condition
effect: Global-search RAG missed an emergency drug-interaction message, likely because the knowledge graph lacked COVID-19 drug-drug interaction resources.
quote: This misclassification likely occurred due to the absence of specific COVID-19 drug-drug interaction resources in the knowledge graph.

title: Clinician-artificial intelligence collaboration: A win-win solution for efficiency and reliability in atrial fibrillation diagnosis
outcome: PAF detection accuracy and clinician workload with clinician-AI collaboration versus clinician alone or AI alone
effect: Clinicians alone missed 13.7% of PAF patients; AI alone misidentified 23.3% of non-AF patients as PAF. Collaboration correctly identified all patients and reduced clinician workload by 76.7%.
quote: After implementing the proposed clinician-AI collaboration strategy, all patients were correctly identified, and clinicians' workload was reduced by 76.7%.

title: Clinician-artificial intelligence collaboration: A win-win solution for efficiency and reliability in atrial fibrillation diagnosis
outcome: PAF diagnostic correctness
effect: All patients were correctly identified, and clinicians' workload was reduced by 76.7%.
quote: After implementing the proposed clinician-AI collaboration strategy, all patients were correctly identified, and clinicians' workload was reduced by 76.7%.

title: Clinician-artificial intelligence collaboration: A win-win solution for efficiency and reliability in atrial fibrillation diagnosis
outcome: AI model diagnostic performance compared with clinicians on the same Holter data
effect: Clinicians alone overlooked 13.7% of PAF patients but identified all non-AF patients; AI rarely missed PAF but misidentified 23.3% of non-AF patients as PAF.
quote: Conversely, AI alone rarely missed PAF patients but misidentified 23.3% of non-AF patients as having PAF.

title: Clinician-artificial intelligence collaboration: A win-win solution for efficiency and reliability in atrial fibrillation diagnosis
outcome: Human-AI diagnostic performance
effect: All patients were correctly identified, and clinicians' workload was reduced by 76.7%.
quote: After implementing the proposed clinician-AI collaboration strategy, all patients were correctly identified, and clinicians' workload was reduced by 76.7%.

title: Review and reflections on live AI mammographic screen reading in a large UK NHS breast screening unit
outcome: AI silent-mode outputs compared with actual double-reader decisions before clinical use
effect: 9,547 cases; 1,135 positive discordant reviewed, 1 additional recall (no cancer); 8 cancers (8.79%) recalled by humans missed by AI; no additional cancers detected by AI.
quote: Having missed a significant number of cancers makes it unreliable and not safe to be used in clinical practice.

title: Review and reflections on live AI mammographic screen reading in a large UK NHS breast screening unit
outcome: AI performance on local screening population versus human readers
effect: Eight cancers (8.79% of total cancers detected) recalled by human readers were not detected by AI; no additional cancers detected by AI.
quote: Performance of AI was inferior to human readers in our unit.

title: Prospective multicenter external validation of the rib fracture frailty index
venue: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of RFF Index versus age for composite outcome in rib fracture patients
effect: RFF had higher discrimination (OR 0.09, 95% CI 0.08-0.11 vs OR 0.06, 95% CI 0.04-0.08; p=0.04) and better calibration than age, though only in lower injury burden patients.
quote: The RFF score had higher discrimination (OR, 0.09; 95% CI, 0.08-0.11 vs. OR, 0.06; 95% CI, 0.04-0.08; p = 0.04) and calibration performance compared with age, but on secondary analysis, higher predictive performance was limited to patients with lower injury burden.

title: Prospective multicenter external validation of the rib fracture frailty index
venue: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
outcome: RFF Index performance across lower versus higher Injury Severity Score subgroups
effect: Higher predictive performance over age was limited to patients with lower injury burden (ISS <15); both models had poor calibration for discharge home after hospitalization >=5 days.
quote: The RFF score had higher discrimination (OR, 0.09; 95% CI, 0.08-0.11 vs. OR, 0.06; 95% CI, 0.04-0.08; p = 0.04) and calibration performance compared with age, but on secondary analysis, higher predictive performance was limited to patients with lower injury burden.

title: Increasing Advance Care Planning Discussions and Documentation
venue: Journal of the advanced practitioner in oncology
outcome: Provider-perceived workflow disruption from AI-triggered ACP notifications
effect: 83.3% of 12 survey respondents (55% response rate) reported the notification and ACP implementation was not disruptive to workflow.
quote: When asked whether the ACP implementation was disruptive to workflow, 83.3% of respondents reported it was not.

title: Increasing Advance Care Planning Discussions and Documentation
venue: Journal of the advanced practitioner in oncology
outcome: ACP discussion documentation after provider education on the mortality-alert response workflow
effect: Documentation increased from three of eight patients (37.5%) before education to three of seven (42.9%) afterward; p =.999. All documented ACP discussions used bookends.
quote: As seen in Figure 1 , out of the eight patients in the pre-education group, three (37.5%) had an ACP conversation documented, compared to three out of seven (42.9%) in the post-education group, which was not significantly different ( p =.999).

title: Increasing Advance Care Planning Discussions and Documentation
venue: Journal of the advanced practitioner in oncology
outcome: Patients missed by model routing because of inaccurate admitting-service classification
effect: Some patients inaccurately admitted under “hematology” were not captured. In November 2022, model eligibility expanded to both services; the missed-patient count was not reported.
quote: In November 2022, the model was again adjusted to include patients with hematologic malignancies admitted under both the “hematology” and “hematology oncology” service, since data analysis indicated some patients were inaccurately admitted under the “hematology” service and had thus not been captured by the model.

title: Increasing Advance Care Planning Discussions and Documentation
venue: Journal of the advanced practitioner in oncology
outcome: insufficient patient flagging
effect: The model initially flagged fewer patients than expected for increased mortality risk, prompting a threshold adjustment to include medium-risk patients.
quote: Fewer patients than expected were flagged as being at increased risk of mortality. Therefore, in July 2022, the prediction model was adjusted to include patients at medium risk of mortality, in addition to high and critical risk.

title: Readability of Orthopaedic Patient Educational Material: An artificial intelligence application
venue: Journal of clinical orthopaedics and trauma
outcome: Reading grade level of patient education materials after GPT rewriting to 6th grade level
effect: All GPT models lowered the mean combined grade level; GPT-4o-Mini and GPT-4o were most effective and consistent; GPT-3.5-Turbo least effective.
quote: All GPT AI models lowered the mean combined grade level (Table 2).

title: Readability of Orthopaedic Patient Educational Material: An artificial intelligence application
venue: Journal of clinical orthopaedics and trauma
outcome: Plain-language readability of AI-rewritten patient education materials versus originals
effect: All GPT models lowered mean combined grade level; rewritten articles screened with no falsified information or medical inaccuracies.
quote: AI is a viable option for reducing the reading difficulty of patient educational materials while maintaining accuracy.

title: Impact of an Alert-Based Inpatient Clinical Decision Support Tool to Prevent Drug-Induced Long QT Syndrome: Large-Scale, System-Wide Observational Study
outcome: Drug-induced QT prolongation and mortality before vs after alert deployment
effect: Alert identified high-risk patients (OR 2.28, 95% CI 2.10-2.47) but diLQTS risk unchanged after deployment (OR 1.13, 95% CI 0.94-1.36); inpatient mortality higher post-deployment (OR 1.43, 95% CI 1.09-1.88).
quote: We found that despite successful identification of high-risk patients for diLQTS, deployment of an alert-based CDS did not impact the risk of diLQTS.

title: Impact of an Alert-Based Inpatient Clinical Decision Support Tool to Prevent Drug-Induced Long QT Syndrome: Large-Scale, System-Wide Observational Study
outcome: diLQTS and mortality after deployment
effect: the risk of diLQTS was not significantly different, and mortality was significantly higher after deployment
quote: When compared with rates prior to implementation, the risk of diLQTS was not significantly different after the CDS tools were deployed across the system, although mortality was significantly higher after the tools were implemented.

title: Impact of an Alert-Based Inpatient Clinical Decision Support Tool to Prevent Drug-Induced Long QT Syndrome: Large-Scale, System-Wide Observational Study
outcome: risk of diLQTS
effect: successful identification of high-risk patients did not translate to reduced clinical risk in practice
quote: We found that despite successful identification of high-risk patients for diLQTS, deployment of an alert-based CDS did not impact the risk of diLQTS.

title: Assessing the quality and readability of patient education materials on chemotherapy cardiotoxicity from artificial intelligence chatbots: An observational cross-sectional study
outcome: Reading grade level of chatbot patient education materials on chemotherapy cardiotoxicity
effect: Mean reading grade level across all chatbots was 13.7; ChatGPT 14.2, Copilot 14.0, Gemini 12.5, Meta 14.2, despite high understandability (median PEMAT 91.7%).
quote: Mean reading grade level (RGL) across all chatbots was 13.7.

title: Assessing the quality and readability of patient education materials on chemotherapy cardiotoxicity from artificial intelligence chatbots: An observational cross-sectional study
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient education materials versus appropriate patient reading level
effect: Mean RGL 13.7 across chatbots (12.5 to 14.2), described as poor readability for patient materials.
quote: AI chatbots produce high quality PEM with poor readability.

title: Temporal validation of machine learning models for pre-eclampsia prediction using routinely collected maternal characteristics: A validation study
outcome: Discrimination (AUC) of ML models versus logistic regression for pre-eclampsia prediction
effect: XGBoost AUC 0.75 (0.73-0.78) and logistic regression 0.76 (0.74-0.78); random forest 0.71 (0.69-0.74); neither ML model outperformed logistic regression.
quote: During temporal validation of PE prediction models, logistic regression and XGBoost models exhibited stable prediction performance; however, both ML models did not outperform the logistic regression model.

title: Temporal validation of machine learning models for pre-eclampsia prediction using routinely collected maternal characteristics: A validation study
outcome: Temporal validation of existing models on newer local data: discrimination and calibration
effect: Models 1 and 3 showed stable discrimination versus development; model 2 had significantly lower discrimination. Calibration slopes: model 3 1.02, model 1 1.15, model 2 0.62.
quote: Compared to the original development models, the temporally validated models 1 and 3 showed stable discrimination performance, whereas model 2 showed significantly lower discrimination performance.
