effect: WER 2.3% for High German vs 17.66% for Swiss German; classification accuracy still reached 90-100% for ESI levels and CEDIS codes despite the higher WER.
quote: STT models achieved word error rates (WER) of 2.3% for High German and 17.66% for Swiss German.

title: AI-driven personalized nutrition: RAG-based digital health solution for obesity and type 2 diabetes
outcome: Adherence of RAG-generated recipes to health guidelines and sustainability criteria
effect: 80.1% adherence to health guidelines (calories, fiber, fats) and 92% compliance with sustainability criteria across 1,000 recipes; no non-RAG comparator reported.
quote: In evaluating 1,000 recipes, the system achieved 80.1% adherence to health guidelines meeting targets for calories, fiber, and fats and 92% compliance with sustainability criteria, emphasizing seasonal and locally sourced ingredients.

title: Evaluating Accuracy and Readability of Responses to Midlife Health Questions: A Comparative Analysis of Six Large Language Model Chatbots
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of chatbot responses to midlife health questions
effect: Even the most readable chatbot (Perplexity) had a grade level of 11.11 ± 1.93, so all chatbot responses were at or above roughly an 11th-grade reading level.
quote: Perplexity showed the highest score of 41.24 ± 10.57 in readability and lowest in grade level (11.11 ± 1.93), meaning its text is the easiest to read and requires a lower level of education.

title: Domain-Specific Customization for Language Models in Otolaryngology: The ENT GPT Assistant
outcome: MCQ accuracy of customized otolaryngology LLM versus general LLMs and otolaryngologists
effect: E-GPT-A overall accuracy 74.6% vs GPT-3.5 60.4%, Claude 2.0 61.7%, Claude 2.1 60.8%, GPT-4 68.3%; otolaryngologists and trainees averaged 71.1%. Lower in pediatrics (62.5%) and facial plastics (67.5%).
quote: E-GPT-A achieved an overall accuracy of 74.6%, outperforming GPT-3.5 (60.4%), Claude 2.0 (61.7%), Claude 2.1 (60.8%), and GPT-4 (68.3%).

title: Comparison of artificial intelligence-generated and physician-generated patient education materials on early diabetic kidney disease
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy, completeness, safety of LLM PEMs generated with vs without uploaded ADA guidelines
effect: No difference for ERNIE Bot 4.0; GPT-4o completeness differed (p=0.0156); ChatGLM4 did better without guidelines in completeness (p=0.0213) and safety (p=0.0300).
quote: Interestingly, in our study, LLMs performed worse with guidelines than without guidelines.

title: Comparison of artificial intelligence-generated and physician-generated patient education materials on early diabetic kidney disease
outcome: Compared LLM-generated patient education materials against a physician-written PEM on expert and patient ratings
effect: ERNIE Bot 4.0 non-guideline PEM performed on par with physician PEM for patient comprehensibility, completeness, safety; 60% (30/50) of patients rated it as good or better than the physician's.
quote: We found that ERNIE Bot 4.0 performed on par with physicians in terms of patient comprehensibility, completeness, and safety.

title: Comparison of artificial intelligence-generated and physician-generated patient education materials on early diabetic kidney disease
outcome: Expert-rated total PEM quality versus physician PEM
effect: ERNIE Bot 4.0 was comparable to physician-sourced PEM; other LLMs generally had lower total scores.
quote: In terms of the total scores, the PEMs generated by ERNIE Bot 4.0 are comparable to the physician-sourced PEM, the PEMs generated by other LLMs generally had lower scores than the physician-sourced PEM( Figure 2A ).

title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and a Paediatric Intensive Care Specialist in Responding to Medical Education Questions: A Multicenter Evaluation
venue: Journal of paediatrics and child health
outcome: Expert-rated completeness and accuracy of ChatGPT-4 vs PICU specialist answers on factual and reasoning questions
effect: ChatGPT-4 preferred in 60% of factual comparisons (p<0.001) and more complete (p=0.02); specialist preferred in 67% of clinical reasoning comparisons, ChatGPT-4 less accurate (p<0.0001).
quote: ChatGPT-4 demonstrated superior completeness in factual knowledge (p = 0.02) but lower accuracy in clinical reasoning (p < 0.0001).

title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and a Paediatric Intensive Care Specialist in Responding to Medical Education Questions: A Multicenter Evaluation
venue: Journal of paediatrics and child health
outcome: Blinded expert preference between ChatGPT-4 and PICU specialist answers to same questions
effect: ChatGPT-4 preferred in 60% of factual knowledge comparisons (p<0.001); specialist preferred in 67% of clinical reasoning comparisons (p<0.0001); integration of both favoured in 37%.
quote: ChatGPT-4 was preferred in 60% of factual knowledge comparisons (p < 0.001), while the PICU specialist's responses were preferred in 67% of clinical reasoning comparisons (p < 0.0001).

title: Performance of AI-Chatbots to Common Temporomandibular Joint Disorders (TMDs) Patient Queries: Accuracy, Completeness, Reliability and Readability
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses to TMD patient questions across six readability indices

title: Performance of AI-Chatbots to Common Temporomandibular Joint Disorders (TMDs) Patient Queries: Accuracy, Completeness, Reliability and Readability

quote: The observed lexical complexity suggests the need to refine outputs for populations with limited health literacy.

title: Academic Detailing to Enhance Adoption of Clinical Decision Support for Patients at Risk of Opioid Overdose

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Addressing Patient Questions on Endodontic Pain: A Comparative Analysis of Accessible Chatbots
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses to endodontic pain questions (SMOG, Flesch-Kincaid)

title: Performance of a virtual assistant based on ChatGPT-4 in the diagnosis of syndromes with orofacial manifestations
venue: Oral surgery, oral medicine, oral pathology and oral radiology
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy, completeness, and up-to-dateness of differential diagnoses and recommended exams
effect: Correct diagnosis identified in 96.2% of cases (80.8% first hypothesis); completeness and up-to-dateness scored lowest; failed to mention all diagnostic steps in 7.69% of cases.
quote: Despite the high accuracy rate, the assistant failed to mention all diagnostic steps in 7.69% of the cases.

title: Validation of artificial intelligence algorithm LuxIA for screening of diabetic retinopathy from a single 45° retinal colour fundus images: the CARDS study
outcome: AI performance reported separately by acquisition device (Topcon vs ZEISS cameras)
effect: On ZEISS images: accuracy 90.6%, specificity 92.3%, sensitivity 83.3%, lower sensitivity than Topcon images; overall sensitivity 97.1%, specificity 94.8%.
quote: LuxIA validation on ZEISS-obtained images demonstrated high accuracy (90.6%), specificity (92.3%) and lower sensitivity (83.3%) as compared with Topcon-obtained images.

title: Predicting onward care needs at admission to reduce discharge delay using explainable machine learning
outcome: ML model discrimination compared with clinician predictions of discharge care needs
effect: ML one-vs-rest AUROC 0.915 [0.907 0.924], comparable to clinicians' predictions; each better for different care need types.
quote: The model performance (one-vs-rest AUROC = 0.915 [0.907 0.924] (95% confidence interval), is comparable to clinician's predictions of discharge care needs, despite working with only a subset of the information available to the clinician.

title: Predicting onward care needs at admission to reduce discharge delay using explainable machine learning
outcome: Accuracy of combined clinician-plus-machine predictions versus either alone
effect: Hybrid clinician-ML model achieved OVR AUROC 0.936 [0.928 0.943], more accurate than ML alone (0.915).
quote: Finally, we demonstrate that combining clinician and machine predictions, in a hybrid model, provides even more accurate early predictions of onward social care requirements (OVR AUROC = 0.936 [0.928 0.943]) and demonstrates the potential for human-in-the-loop decision support systems in clinical practice.

title: Simulating mismatch between calibration and target population in AI for mammography the retrospective VAIB study
outcome: Distortion in cancer detection rate when calibration population mismatches target population
effect: Mismatched acquisition year: CDR distortion -3% to +19%; age: -0.2% to +27%; breast density: +1% to 16%; mammography vendor: -32% to +33%.
quote: Mismatches between calibration population and target clinical population lead to clinically important deviations.

title: Simulating mismatch between calibration and target population in AI for mammography the retrospective VAIB study
outcome: Effect of calibration on non-representative data on cancer detection rate
effect: Calibrating on non-representative datasets distorted CDR, e.g., vendor mismatch -32% to +33%, indicating thresholds unsuited to target population.
quote: Mismatching mammography vendors lead to a distortion in CDR between -32% to + 33%.

title: Simulating mismatch between calibration and target population in AI for mammography the retrospective VAIB study
outcome: CDR distortion when calibration vendor differs from target acquisition device

title: Simulating mismatch between calibration and target population in AI for mammography the retrospective VAIB study
outcome: CDR deviation from nonrepresentative calibration data

quote: Mismatches between calibration population and target clinical population lead to clinically important deviations.

title: Simulating mismatch between calibration and target population in AI for mammography the retrospective VAIB study
outcome: CDR distortion from temporal calibration mismatch
effect: Acquisition-year mismatch distorted CDR between -3% to +19%.

title: Parental education in pediatric dysphagia: A comparative analysis of three large language models
venue: Journal of pediatric gastroenterology and nutrition
outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of LLM answers to parents' pediatric dysphagia questions
effect: Even the most readable model (Gemini) had FRE 48.7 ± 9.9 and FKGL 10.1 ± 1.6, so answers were written at roughly a 10th-grade level.
quote: In terms of readability, Gemini achieved the highest scores (FRE = 48.7 ± 9.9 and FKGL = 10.1 ± 1.6).

title: The impact of AI feedback on the accuracy of diagnosis, decision switching and trust in radiography
outcome: Radiographer diagnostic accuracy with vs without AI feedback (heatmap, binary), including overreliance when AI incorrect
effect: AI feedback improved accuracy overall (AI correct +13.4 points) but reduced it when AI incorrect (-4.8 overall; -9.6 students); heatmap lowered accuracy in pathological cases (65.85% to 57.62%) before binary feedback raised it (72.35%).
quote: The AI feedback (i.e., heatmap and binary AI decision) proved beneficial to participants except for situations where the AI was incorrect and pathological examinations in the student group (decrease in accuracy of 3.4%).

title: The impact of AI feedback on the accuracy of diagnosis, decision switching and trust in radiography
outcome: AI performance drop from lab test set to clinical dataset
effect: AI performed well on the MURA test set but made correct predictions on only 12 of 21 clinical examinations (57.1% accuracy).
quote: This study uses an AI which performed well in the laboratory (test set) but poorly with more clinically relevant images (clinical dataset).

title: The impact of AI feedback on the accuracy of diagnosis, decision switching and trust in radiography
outcome: automation bias after incorrect AI feedback
effect: Incorrect AI feedback reduced accuracy by 4.8% overall, 9.6% in students and 4.3% in radiographers.
quote: A greater impact was seen in the student group where accuracy fell by 9.6% compared with 4.3% amongst radiographers, suggesting in this sample that the student group is more susceptible to automation bias ( Table 5b ).

title: The impact of AI feedback on the accuracy of diagnosis, decision switching and trust in radiography
outcome: heatmap explanation effect on pathological accuracy
effect: Pathological cases: no AI 65.85%, heatmap 57.62%, binary feedback 72.35%; heatmap significantly decreased performance.
quote: Further inspection of the descriptive statistics would indicate that there was a statistically significant decrease in performance following presentation of the heatmap, followed by an increase, exceeding the performance with the un-aided interpretation (No AI feedback 65.85%, post-heatmap 57.62%, post-binary feedback 72.35%), indicating that the heatmap was detrimental to performance in pathological cases.

title: The impact of AI feedback on the accuracy of diagnosis, decision switching and trust in radiography
outcome: AI performance as used by clinicians, effect on user accuracy versus standalone model
effect: The AI was correct on 57.1% of exams, yet net user accuracy improved with AI feedback in most conditions; harmful when AI was incorrect.
quote: In most conditions there was a positive impact from the AI feedback despite the poor performance of the model.

title: The impact of AI feedback on the accuracy of diagnosis, decision switching and trust in radiography
outcome: Whether saliency heatmap explanations improved clinician diagnostic accuracy
effect: Heatmap explanation decreased accuracy in pathological cases (students 63.3% to 50.7%) and caused confusion, even when AI binary diagnosis was correct.
quote: Further inspection of the descriptive statistics would indicate that there was a statistically significant decrease in performance following presentation of the heatmap, followed by an increase, exceeding the performance with the un-aided interpretation (No AI feedback 65.85%, post-heatmap 57.62%, post-binary feedback 72.35%), indicating that the heatmap was detrimental to performance in pathological cases.

title: The impact of AI feedback on the accuracy of diagnosis, decision switching and trust in radiography
outcome: Automation bias and users' susceptibility, especially less experienced users
effect: Students more likely to change their mind (32.7% vs 19.3% following binary feedback) and showed greater accuracy drop when AI incorrect; authors recommend education on AI weaknesses.
quote: Participants in this study tended to follow the diagnosis from the system, resulting in decreased accuracy in the diagnostic task in some cases.

title: Comparison of Large Language Models' Performance on 600 Nuclear Medicine Technology Board Examination-Style Questions
outcome: Accuracy of LLMs on nuclear medicine board-style questions with versus without retrieval-augmented generation
effect: With RAG, top OpenAI models reached 0.787 and 0.783 overall accuracy; Anthropic Opus 0.773 and Gemini 1.5 Pro 0.750 with RAG; RAG increased accuracy of an off-the-shelf model.
quote: This study also demonstrates that adding a RAG workflow can increase the accuracy of an off-the-shelf model.
sample_unit: nuclear medicine technology board examination-style questions

title: Large Language Models for Diagnosing Focal Liver Lesions From CT/MRI Reports: A Comparative Study With Radiologists
venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without LLM assistance
effect: No incremental diagnostic value of ChatGPT-4o for any radiologist (p-values 0.63 to >0.99), although standalone LLM accuracy matched junior radiologists.
quote: No incremental diagnostic value of ChatGPT-4o was observed for any radiologist (p-values, 0.63 to > 0.99).

title: Large Language Models for Diagnosing Focal Liver Lesions From CT/MRI Reports: A Comparative Study With Radiologists
venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy compared with radiologists and real-world radiology reports on the same cases
effect: Two-step ChatGPT-4o 78.9% matched reports (80.0%) and junior radiologists (78.9%-82.0%) but was below middle-level radiologists (84.6%-85.5%).
quote: Regarding the final diagnosis, the accuracy of two-step ChatGPT-4o (78.9%) was higher than single-step ChatGPT-4o (68.0%, p < 0.001) and single-step Gemini (73.2%, p = 0.004), similar to real-world radiology reports (80.0%, p = 0.34) and junior radiologists (78.9%-82.0%; p-values, 0.21 to > 0.99), but lower than middle-level radiologists (84.6%-85.5%; p-values, 0.001 to 0.02).

title: Qualitative Results from a Pilot Study of an Automated Directly Observed Therapy Intervention Using Artificial Intelligence with Conditional Economic Incentives among Young Adults with HIV
outcome: Participant desire for information about app privacy features

title: Predicting survival outcomes in renal cell carcinoma spinal metastases: a multicenter evaluation of existing prognostic systems
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of existing survival prediction models on external multicenter Chinese data

title: Predicting survival outcomes in renal cell carcinoma spinal metastases: a multicenter evaluation of existing prognostic systems
venue: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
outcome: Need for recalibration of models when applied to a new population

quote: However, recalibration is needed to address underestimation, particularly in East Asian populations.

effect: Explanations increased trust when AI matched expert ground truth; with incorrect AI outputs, response was mixed: correctly reduced trust in experienced clinicians but mixed among less experienced clinicians.
quote: When clinical scenarios were complex with incorrect AI outcomes, a mixed response to explainability led to correctly reduced trust in experienced clinicians but mixed feedback amongst less experienced clinicians.

title: Translating the machine; An assessment of clinician understanding of ophthalmological artificial intelligence outputs
outcome: Clinicians' self-reported knowledge of interacting with AI and desire for training
effect: All clinicians had a general consensus on lack of current knowledge in interacting with AI and desired more training.
quote: All clinicians had a general consensus on lack of current knowledge in interacting with AI and desire more training.

title: Translating the machine; An assessment of clinician understanding of ophthalmological artificial intelligence outputs

title: Translating the machine; An assessment of clinician understanding of ophthalmological artificial intelligence outputs
outcome: variation by staff expertise
effect: Explainability methods had important differences in impact on trust depending on scenario nature and staff expertise.
quote: We noted important differences in the impact of various explainability methods on trust, depending on the clinical or AI scenario nature and the staff expertise.

title: Evaluating algorithmic bias on biomarker classification of breast cancer pathology reports
outcome: Model fairness metrics (BER, DP, EOD, EOP) across race, ethnicity, age, SES, and registry subgroups
effect: BER showed significant differences by registry (ratios >1.25 for all registries vs Seattle) but no significant bias by race, Hispanic ethnicity, age, or SES (BER ratio <1.25); DP, EOD, EOP insignificant.
quote: We observed significant differences in BER by registry, but no significant bias using the DP, EOD, and EOP metrics for socio-demographic or racial categories.

title: Evaluating algorithmic bias on biomarker classification of breast cancer pathology reports
outcome: Performance variation across registries (sites)
effect: Predictive accuracy differed between registries, with highest accuracy in the registry contributing the most data (Seattle); BER ratios for all registries >1.25.
quote: We found differences in predictive accuracy between registries, with the highest accuracy in the registry that contributed the most data (Seattle Registry, BER ratios for all registries >1.25).

title: Evaluating the Efficacy of ChatGPT vs. Google Gemini in Generating Patient Education Materials for GLP-1 Receptor Agonists (Semaglutide, Liraglutide, Tirzepatide): A Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid readability of AI-generated GLP-1 patient education brochures, ChatGPT vs Gemini
effect: Gemini had better readability scores than ChatGPT, which produced longer brochures with higher word counts. The abstract reports no numeric reading grade levels.
quote: ChatGPT generated longer brochures with higher word counts compared to Google Gemini, which had better readability scores.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Primary Care Decision-Making: Survey of Healthcare Professionals in Saudi Arabia
outcome: Familiarity with AI among primary care healthcare professionals
effect: 14.8% very familiar with AI and 47.2% unfamiliar; lack of training was a barrier for 34%.
quote: Awareness of AI tools was mixed, with 14.8% of respondents very familiar with AI and 47.2% unfamiliar.

title: Advancing emergency upper extremity care: A pilot study of ChatGPT's potential role in diagnosing and managing hand and wrist trauma
outcome: Blinded attending scores of ChatGPT versus plastic surgery residents on hand trauma vignettes
effect: ChatGPT had higher total average scores (mean = 26.6 vs. 22.7, p < 0.05) and ER management scores (9.9 vs. 6.7, p < 0.05); no notable differences in diagnosis or definitive treatment scores.
quote: ChatGPT had significantly higher total average scores (mean = 26.6 vs. 22.7, p < 0.05) and ER management scores (mean = 9.9 vs. 6.7, p < 0.05) when compared to residents.
sample_unit: clinical vignettes (16 ChatGPT and 16 resident responses per scenario)

title: Evaluation and Bias Analysis of Large Language Models in Generating Synthetic Electronic Health Records: Comparative Study
outcome: Gender and racial representation bias (statistical parity difference) in LLM-generated synthetic EHRs across 20 diseases
effect: Biases observed across all 7 models; larger models more biased. Hispanic underrepresented (average SPD -11.93%, SD 8.36%); Yi-34B overrepresented Black (mean SPD +14.90%); Llama 2-13B hypertension 95.7% male vs 52.17% real (SPD +43.50%).
quote: However, this increased performance was accompanied by a notable escalation in both gender and racial biases, highlighting a performance-bias trade-off.

title: Evaluation and Bias Analysis of Large Language Models in Generating Synthetic Electronic Health Records: Comparative Study
outcome: Whether LLM outputs shift inappropriately by demographic attributes in synthetic EHR generation compared with real prevalence
effect: Sex polarization: Qwen-14B produced 97.3% female for multiple sclerosis vs 75.78% real (SPD +21.50%); racial skews varied by disease and model.
quote: Sex polarization emerged: female-dominated diseases (eg, multiple sclerosis) saw amplified female representation in outputs (Qwen-14B: 973/1000, 97.3% female vs 564,424/744,778, 75.78% real; SPD=+21.50%), while balanced diseases and male-dominated diseases skewed the male group (eg, hypertension Llama 2-13 B: 957/1000, 95.7% male vs 79,540,040/152,466,669, 52.17% real; SPD=+43.50%).

title: Performance Degradation between Development and Deployment of a Predictive Model for Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in Hospitalized Children
outcome: AUROC of pediatric CLABSI model on retrospective versus prospective deployment data
effect: AUROC fell from 0.97 on retrospective data to <0.60 in offline deployment validation; feature leakage and overfitting were among primary root causes.
quote: The area under the receiver-operating characteristic (AUROC) fell from 0.97 from retrospective data to <0.60 despite multiple iterations of troubleshooting.

title: Performance Degradation between Development and Deployment of a Predictive Model for Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in Hospitalized Children
outcome: Compatibility of model input features between development data and real-time production data
effect: Train/serve skew and challenging feature translation between real-time and historical data models caused performance to fall from AUROC 0.97 to <0.60.
quote: Primary root causes included train/serve skew, feature leakage, and overfitting.

title: Augmented reality microscopy to bridge trust between AI and pathologists
outcome: Pathologist interobserver agreement at PD-L1 CPS ≥5 with vs without AI assistance
effect: Fleiss' kappa rose from 0.52 (manual) to 0.76 (AI-assisted), p<0.01; agreement among all 11 pathologists 43% vs 69%; any two 77% vs 91%.
quote: Agreement among pathologists by Fleiss’ Kappa showed overall improved agreement from 0.52 (0.40–0.65) with manual scoring on day 1 to 0.76 (0.62-0.87) with AI-assisted scoring on day 2 with statistical significance ( p < 0.01, Bootstrapping of differences) (Fig. 3 c).
sample_unit: pathologists scoring 35 biopsy regions of interest

title: Augmented reality microscopy to bridge trust between AI and pathologists
outcome: AI performance as used by pathologists in workflow (manual vs AI-assisted scoring agreement and positive calls)
effect: AI assistance increased ICC (e.g., total tumor cells 0.38 to 0.90) and positive CPS≥5 cases from 15 to 26 (31% increase).
quote: Pathologists identified 15 cases as PD-L1 CPS ≥ 5 positive with manual scoring on day 1 compared to 26 cases as PD-L1 CPS ≥ 5 positive by AI-assisted scoring on day 2, corresponding to a 31% increase of positive cases found when using AI-assistance.
sample_unit: pathologists scoring 35 biopsy regions of interest

title: Augmented reality microscopy to bridge trust between AI and pathologists
outcome: Pathologist-in-loop finetuning concordance
quote: Compared to the original IHC foundation model, the finetuned Gastric PD-L1 CPS AI Model showed improved concordance against the reference consensus increasing agreement from 81.8% (95% CI, 68.6%, 94.3%) to 96.4% (95% CI, 88.6%, 100%) ( p < 0.05, McNemar’s test) and Cohen’s Kappa κ from 0.62 (95% CI, 0.36, 0.86) to 0.91 (95% CI, 0.71, 1.0) ( p < 0.05, Bootstrapping) (Fig. 1c ).
sample_unit: pathologists scoring 35 biopsy regions of interest

title: Augmented reality microscopy to bridge trust between AI and pathologists
outcome: AI versus pathologist concordance
effect: At CPS ≥5, AI-pathologist κ=0.46 (95% CI, 0.37, 0.54) vs pathologist-pathologist κ=0.39 (95% CI, 0.29, 0.48); p < 0.05.
quote: At a PD-L1 CPS ≥ 5 cut-off, the concordance between PD-L1 AI scores and pathologists’ manual scores was higher (Cohen’s κ = 0.46; 95% CI, 0.37, 0.54) than the average concordance among pathologists’ manual scores (Cohen’s κ = 0.39; 95% CI, 0.29, 0.48) with statistical significance ( p < 0.05, Bootstrapping) as well as higher than for the original IHC foundation model ( p < 0.001, Bootstrapping).
sample_unit: pathologists scoring 35 biopsy regions of interest

title: A controlled trial examining large Language model conformity in psychiatric assessment using the Asch paradigm
outcome: GPT-4o accuracy under simulated peer pressure (incorrect peer responses) versus no pressure across three diagnostic domains
effect: No pressure: 100% accuracy in all domains. Full pressure: 50% circle, 40% tumor, 0% psychiatric assessment. Partial pressure: 80% circle, 100% tumor, 0% psychiatric. Pressure vs none differences significant (P<.05).
quote: Under full pressure, accuracy declined systematically with increasing diagnostic uncertainty: 50% in circle recognition, 40% in tumor identification, and 0% in psychiatric assessment.

title: Artificial intelligence-based echocardiography assessment to detect pulmonary hypertension
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy for PH of AI-derived versus manual TRJV measurements on same echocardiograms
effect: AUC 0.88 (95% CI 0.84-0.90) for automated versus 0.88 (95% CI 0.86-0.91) for manual; noninferior. ICC 0.94 (95% CI 0.94-0.95); TRJV measured in 87% of echocardiograms.
quote: Automated TRJV measurements showed equally high diagnostic accuracy for PH as manual measurements (area under the curve 0.88, 95% CI 0.84-0.90 versus 0.88, 95% CI 0.86-0.91).

title: How Successful Is AI in Developing Postsurgical Wound Care Education Material?

quote: The Turkish readability index of the education material was found to be 68.9 and easily understandable.

title: Evaluating large language and large reasoning models as decision support tools in emergency internal medicine
outcome: LLM final clinical rating compared with human physician reports on same cases
effect: o1 mean final rating 3.63 vs human physicians 3.67 (p = 0.62); Claude-3.5-Sonnet 3.38 and Llama-3.2-70B 3.23 scored significantly lower (p < 0.01 vs. o1).
quote: The o1 model achieved a mean final rating (3.63) statistically indistinguishable from human physicians (3.67; p = 0.62).

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT responses to common patient questions on ankle fusion
venue: Foot and ankle surgery : official journal of the European Society of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT responses to patient questions on ankle fusion
effect: Mean readability was grade level 11.6, a high reading level needed to understand the responses.
quote: However, the readability level was high, with a mean of 11.6 grade level.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT responses to common patient questions on ankle fusion
venue: Foot and ankle surgery : official journal of the European Society of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses to patient questions

title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
outcome: omissions in AI clinical notes
effect: 1712/49,590 transcript sentences were omitted (3.45%); 286 (16.7%) major and 1426 (83.3%) minor.
quote: Of the 49,590 sentences from our consultation transcripts, 1712 sentences were omitted (3.45%), of which 286 (16.7%) of which were classified as major and 1426 (83.3%) as minor.

title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
outcome: Hallucination and omission rates in LLM-generated notes across 18 experiments, clinician-annotated by severity
effect: Of 12,999 sentences, 191 had hallucinations (1.47%), 84 (44%) major; 1712 of 49,590 transcript sentences omitted (3.45%), 286 (16.7%) major. Iterative refinement cut major omissions from 61 to 0.
quote: Of 12,999 sentences in 450 clinical notes, 191 sentences had hallucinations (1.47%), of which 84 sentences (44%) were major (could impact patient diagnosis and management if left uncorrected).

title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
outcome: LLM-generated vs clinician-written notes: hallucinations and omissions on same transcripts
effect: Clinician-written notes had slightly more hallucinations but fewer omissions than LLM notes (Experiment 17); LLM best configurations had fewer errors per note than reported human rates.
quote: Interestingly, findings suggested slightly more hallucinations in clinician-written notes but fewer omissions, highlighting key differences in human vs. LLM-generated note content.

title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
outcome: Hallucination and omission rates of generative LLM clinical notes
effect: 1.47% hallucination rate and 3.45% omission rate; hallucinations more often major (44%) than omissions (16.7%).
quote: Our experiment results show that omissions are more common than hallucinations (3.45% to 1.47%, respectively).

title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
outcome: Re-testing errors after prompt and workflow changes to note-generation pipeline
effect: Prompt change from Exp 3 to 8 reduced major hallucinations 75% (4 to 1), major omissions 58% (24 to 10); atomisation (Exp 5) increased major hallucinations from 4 to 25, showing changes can degrade safety.
quote: The change in the prompt from Experiments 3 to 8 reduced the incidence of major hallucinations by 75% (from 4 to 1), major omissions by 58% (24 to 10), and minor omissions by 35% (114 to 74) (Fig. 8 ).

title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
outcome: major hallucinations in AI clinical notes
effect: 191/12,999 note sentences hallucinated (1.47%); 84 (44%) were major and could affect diagnosis or management if uncorrected.
quote: Of 12,999 sentences in 450 clinical notes, 191 sentences had hallucinations (1.47%), of which 84 sentences (44%) were major (could impact patient diagnosis and management if left uncorrected).

title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
outcome: structured prompt changes reduced note errors
effect: Major hallucinations reduced 75% (4 to 1), major omissions 58% (24 to 10), and minor omissions 35% (114 to 74).
quote: The change in the prompt from Experiments 3 to 8 reduced the incidence of major hallucinations by 75% (from 4 to 1), major omissions by 58% (24 to 10), and minor omissions by 35% (114 to 74) (Fig. 8 ).

title: A framework to assess clinical safety and hallucination rates of LLMs for medical text summarisation
outcome: workflow modification worsened note errors
effect: Atomisation increased major hallucinations 4 to 25, minor hallucinations 5 to 29, major omissions 24 to 47, and minor omissions 114 to 188.
quote: We found that major hallucinations increased from 4 to 25, minor hallucinations from 5 to 29, major omissions from 24 to 47, and minor omissions from 114 to 188 (Fig. 10 ).

title: A Comparison of Skin Lesions' Diagnoses Between AI-Based Image Classification, an Expert Dermatologist, and a Non-Expert
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI versus expert dermatologist and non-expert on same images
effect: AI sensitivity 93.59% and specificity 70.42% for malignant lesions; similar sensitivity and notably higher specificity than expert dermatologist and non-expert.
quote: The AI model demonstrated similar sensitivity and notably higher specificity compared to the expert dermatologist and non-expert.

title: Summarizing clinical evidence utilizing large language models for cancer treatments: a blinded comparative analysis
outcome: Accuracy, completeness and hallucination Likert scores of LLM clinical evidence synopses rated by hematologists
effect: No LLM achieved perfect accuracy, completeness or relevance; hallucination scores ranged from 4.00 (Claude) to 1.92 (Llama); all outputs needed expert editing.
quote: Claude performed at a consistently higher level than other LLMs, all tested LLMs required careful editing from a domain expert to become usable.

title: Summarizing clinical evidence utilizing large language models for cancer treatments: a blinded comparative analysis
outcome: Head-to-head comparison of four LLMs on the same synopsis task across quality domains
effect: Claude outperformed others (accuracy 3.92 vs ChatGPT 3.25, Gemini 3.17, Llama 1.92); Llama performed considerably poorer across all domains.
quote: Llama performed considerably poorer across all the studied domains.

title: AI-driven simplification of surgical reports in gynecologic oncology: A potential tool for patient education
outcome: Patient understanding of GPT-4 simplified versus original surgical reports
effect: Simplified reports significantly improved patients' understanding, particularly of the procedure, its outcome, and potential risks.
quote: The simplified surgical reports generated by GPT-4 significantly improved our patients' understanding, particularly with regard to the surgical procedure, its outcome, and potential risks.

title: AI-driven simplification of surgical reports in gynecologic oncology: A potential tool for patient education
outcome: Clinical expert rating of accuracy and medical precision of AI-simplified reports
effect: Clinical experts raised concerns about lack of medical precision in the simplified reports despite better accessibility.
quote: However, despite the reports being more accessible and relevant, clinical experts highlighted concerns about their lack of medical precision.

title: Comparative performance of large language models in structuring head CT radiology reports: multi-institutional validation study in Japan
outcome: Accuracy comparison of three LLMs across three prompt strategies on same reports
effect: Claude significantly higher accuracy than GPT and Gemini for intracranial hemorrhage (p<0.0001); Gemini significantly lower than Claude and GPT for skull fracture (p<0.0001); Claude accuracy 0.98-0.99.
quote: In many comparisons, Claude demonstrated significantly higher accuracy than both GPT and Gemini ( p < 0.0001), while no statistically significant difference was observed between GPT and Gemini.
sample_unit: head CT radiology reports (one per patient)

title: Comparative performance of large language models in structuring head CT radiology reports: multi-institutional validation study in Japan
outcome: Effect of prompting strategy and repeated-run reproducibility on classification accuracy
effect: Claude and GPT stable across prompts; Gemini significantly higher with Chain of Thought than Standard or Self Consistency. Each combination run three times; reproducibility compared across runs.
quote: For both intracranial hemorrhage and skull fracture classification, Claude and GPT maintained relatively consistent accuracy across different prompting methods, whereas Gemini achieved significantly higher accuracy with Chain of Thought prompting than with either Standard or Self Consistency prompting.
sample_unit: head CT radiology reports (one per patient)

title: Comparative performance of large language models in structuring head CT radiology reports: multi-institutional validation study in Japan
outcome: accuracy variation by prompt strategy
effect: Gemini Chain of Thought significantly outperformed Standard and Self Consistency for both labels (p < 0.0001); skull fracture accuracy 0.99 versus 0.98 and 0.98.
quote: For both intracranial hemorrhage and skull fracture classification, Claude and GPT maintained relatively consistent accuracy across different prompting methods, whereas Gemini achieved significantly higher accuracy with Chain of Thought prompting than with either Standard or Self Consistency prompting.
sample_unit: head CT radiology reports (one per patient)

title: AI-driven rehabilitation: evaluation of ChatGPT-4o for generating personalized physical rehabilitation plans in comorbid patients
outcome: Expert review of LLM-generated rehabilitation plans for suitability for use
effect: 72.00% of plans were 'Suitable for use with corrections'; none were 'Completely unsuitable'; conclusion: not yet implementable without expert review and modification.
quote: 72.00% of the generated plans were classified as "Suitable for use with corrections".

title: Predictive performance of cardiovascular disease risk prediction models in older adults: a validation and updating study
outcome: Discrimination, calibration and net benefit of CVD models after recalibration or coefficient updating in older adults
effect: After updating, C statistics ranged 0.62-0.64 for men and 0.68-0.69 for women; updated models showed good calibration and added net benefit at 4%-10% (women) and 5%-12% (men) thresholds.
quote: Following updating, the discrimination power of models increased for both sexes (C statistics ranged 0.62-0.64 for men and 0.68-0.69 for women).

title: Predictive performance of cardiovascular disease risk prediction models in older adults: a validation and updating study
outcome: Generalization of models developed in middle-aged adults to older adults
effect: Models developed for middle-aged populations needed updating to improve prediction in older adults; further external validation in diverse older populations recommended before clinical implementation.
quote: Updating models, by adjusting model coefficients to better reflect the characteristics and risk factors of older adults, improves CVD risk prediction in a large cohort of relatively healthy Caucasian population aged 70+.

title: Predictive performance of cardiovascular disease risk prediction models in older adults: a validation and updating study
outcome: CVD risk model discrimination after updating
effect: C statistics ranged 0.62-0.64 for men and 0.68-0.69 for women following updating
quote: Following updating, the discrimination power of models increased for both sexes (C statistics ranged 0.62-0.64 for men and 0.68-0.69 for women).

title: Benchmarking large language models GPT-4o, llama 3.1, and qwen 2.5 for cancer genetic variant classification
outcome: Effect of retrieval-augmented generation on variant classification accuracy
effect: Prompt engineering significantly improved accuracy, while RAG further enhanced performance. Accuracy of GPT-4o in distinguishing clinically relevant variants from VUS was 0.7318 (baseline).
quote: Prompt engineering significantly improved accuracy, while retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) further enhanced performance.

title: Benchmarking large language models GPT-4o, llama 3.1, and qwen 2.5 for cancer genetic variant classification
outcome: Output consistency across 100 repeated runs of variant classification
effect: Stability analysis across 100 iterations revealed greater consistency with the CIViC system than with OncoKB, with greater inconsistencies for variants with weaker evidence.
quote: Stability analysis across 100 iterations revealed greater consistency with the CIViC system than with OncoKB.

title: Benchmarking large language models GPT-4o, llama 3.1, and qwen 2.5 for cancer genetic variant classification
outcome: Accuracy of LLM clinical knowledge on variant actionability versus expert annotations
effect: GPT-4o accuracy 0.7318, Qwen 2.5 0.5731, Llama 3.1 0.4976 in distinguishing clinically relevant variants from VUS; all models tended to overclassify to higher evidence levels.
quote: All three models showed a tendency to assign variants to higher evidence levels, suggesting a propensity for overclassification.

title: Artificial intelligence algorithm improves radiologists' bone age assessment accuracy
venue: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
outcome: Radiologist bone age accuracy (MAD) with vs without AI assistance, and automation bias assessed
effect: MAD improved from 0.74 to 0.46 years with AI (p<0.001); >1 year error proportion 24.0% vs 8.4%; improved predictions 16.8% vs worsened 2.3%; less experienced radiologists prone to automation bias.
quote: The overall accuracy of senior, mid-level, and junior radiologists improved significantly with AI assistance than without AI assistance (MAD: 0.74 vs 0.46 years, p < 0.001; proportion of assessments for which MAD exceeded 1 year: 24.0% vs 8.4%, p < 0.001).

title: Artificial intelligence algorithm improves radiologists' bone age assessment accuracy
venue: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
outcome: Automation bias and AI disagreements by experience
effect: Worsened ≥1 y: 28 (2.3%) vs improved ≥1 y: 201 (16.8%); disagreements: S1/S2 65/65, M1/M2 23/55, J1/J2 18/27.
quote: Radiologists reading BAs were prone to automation bias when being supported by an AI algorithm, especially in less experienced radiologists.

title: Artificial intelligence algorithm improves radiologists' bone age assessment accuracy
venue: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
outcome: Effect of AI on radiologist performance in reader-study workflow versus standalone
effect: Radiologist MAD improved from 0.74 to 0.46 years with AI assistance (p<0.001); proportion >1 year error fell 24.0% to 8.4%.
quote: As illustrated in Fig. 5 , the radiologists’ assessment accuracy improved significantly ( p < 0.001) with AI assistance (MAD, 0.46 years) when compared with that without AI assistance (MAD, 0.74 years).

title: A comparative analysis of large language models versus traditional information extraction methods for real-world evidence of patient symptomatology in acute and post-acute sequelae of SARS-CoV-2
outcome: Symptom extraction performance across patient demographic subgroups (fairness analysis)
effect: BioMedICUS generally showed stronger performance across patient demographics; both fine-tuned LLaMA models faced challenges in demographic fairness and generalizability.
quote: However, both LLaMA models faced challenges in demographic fairness and generalizability.

title: LLMonFHIR: A Physician-Validated, Large Language Model-Based Mobile Application for Querying Patient Electronic Health Data
outcome: Physician ratings of accuracy, understandability, relevance of LLM responses to patient record queries
effect: 210 responses rated by physicians; median scores of 5/5 for accuracy, understandability, and relevance; challenges noted summarizing conditions and retrieving lab results, with occasional omissions.
quote: A total of 210 LLMonFHIR responses were evaluated by physicians, receiving high median scores for accuracy (5/5), understandability (5/5), and relevance (5/5).

title: Patient Triage and Guidance in Emergency Departments Using Large Language Models: Multimetric Study
outcome: MEWS scoring accuracy of GPT-4 models compared with nurses' manual calculation
effect: GPT-4o accuracy after prompt engineering was 96.20% vs 81.8% for nurses' manual calculation from a previous study; GPT-4-Turbo reached 100%.
quote: This is particularly notable when compared to the finding of a previous study, which indicated that the overall accuracy rate of nurses’ manual calculations was 81.8% [ 20 ].
sample_unit: simulated patient scenarios (MEWS triage); 264 scenarios for department guidance

title: Patient Triage and Guidance in Emergency Departments Using Large Language Models: Multimetric Study
outcome: MEWS triage accuracy before vs after prompt engineering with structured prompt
effect: GPT-4-Turbo accuracy rose from 63.93% to 100%; GPT-4o from 63.41% to 96.20%; average difference from standard score fell to 0 and 0.08.
quote: GPT-4-Turbo achieved an impressive accuracy of 100% across all the 10 runs.
sample_unit: simulated patient scenarios (MEWS triage); 264 scenarios for department guidance

title: Patient Triage and Guidance in Emergency Departments Using Large Language Models: Multimetric Study
outcome: Repeated-run consistency
effect: GPT-4o Kendall mean 0.8327 to 0.8646; GPT-4-Turbo 0.6176 to 1.00 after prompt engineering.
quote: For GPT-4-Turbo, the mean value dramatically improved from 0.6176 (SD 0.2135) in trial 1 to 1.00 (SD 0) in trial 2.
sample_unit: simulated patient scenarios (MEWS triage); 264 scenarios for department guidance

title: Patient Triage and Guidance in Emergency Departments Using Large Language Models: Multimetric Study
outcome: Run-to-run consistency (Kendall correlation) of MEWS scoring across 10 repeated runs, before vs after prompt engineering
effect: GPT-4-Turbo mean Kendall coefficient improved from 0.6176 (SD 0.2135) to 1.00 (SD 0); GPT-4o improved from 0.8327 to 0.8646 (not significant, P=.32).
quote: For GPT-4-Turbo, the mean value dramatically improved from 0.6176 (SD 0.2135) in trial 1 to 1.00 (SD 0) in trial 2.
sample_unit: simulated patient scenarios (MEWS triage); 264 scenarios for department guidance

title: Patient Triage and Guidance in Emergency Departments Using Large Language Models: Multimetric Study
outcome: Overreliance on patient medical history in department guidance errors
effect: Physicians attributed 43.42% of overall guidance errors to overreliance on patient medical history rather than current symptoms.
quote: Another key finding in this part of the experiment was that the guidance provided by ChatGPT (GPT-4o model) was sometimes influenced by the medical history of patients, where physicians attributed 43.42% of the overall guidance error to an overreliance on the medical history of patients.
sample_unit: simulated patient scenarios (MEWS triage); 264 scenarios for department guidance

title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for providing sexual health information: a consensus study using real-world clinical queries
outcome: Overall correctness of chatbots grounded in curated knowledge base versus ungrounded base ChatGPT
effect: Prompt-tuned with knowledge base: Alice 85.2%, Azure 69.3% correct versus base ChatGPT 64.8% (p<0.0001); prompt-tuned chatbots outperformed ChatGPT across all measures.
quote: Alice demonstrated the highest overall correctness at 85.2% (95% CI, 82.1-88.0%), followed by Azure at 69.3% (95% CI, 65.3-73.0%), and ChatGPT at 64.8% (95% CI, 60.7-68.7%).

title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for providing sexual health information: a consensus study using real-world clinical queries
outcome: Accuracy of chatbot outputs against expert reference standard
effect: Overall correctness ranged 64.8% (ChatGPT) to 85.2% (Alice); nurses correct on 98.5%; all chatbots susceptible to incorrect information.
quote: However, we found that all AI chatbots, including the prompt-tuned chatbots, are susceptible to hallucinations - the generation of false or irrelevant information that is not grounded in the provided data or knowledge base - at some point.

title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots for providing sexual health information: a consensus study using real-world clinical queries
outcome: side-by-side candidate correctness
effect: Overall correctness differed: Alice 85.2%, Azure 69.3%, ChatGPT 64.8%; p < 0.0001.
quote: Alice demonstrated the highest overall correctness at 85.2% (95% CI, 82.1-88.0%), followed by Azure at 69.3% (95% CI, 65.3-73.0%), and ChatGPT at 64.8% (95% CI, 60.7-68.7%).

title: Feasibility study of automatic radiotherapy treatment planning for cervical cancer using a large language model
outcome: LLM-generated VMAT plan quality and planning time versus manual physicist plans
effect: Qwen-2.5-max and Llama-3.2 plans took 16.3±5.0 and 9.8±2.1 min vs ~20 min manual; CI 0.929, 0.928 vs 0.926 manual; HI 0.058, 0.059 vs 0.065; OAR sparing not significantly different.
quote: The average conformity index (CI) for Qwen-2.5-max plans, Llama-3.2 plans, and manual plans on the test set were 0.929 ± 0.007, 0.928 ± 0.007, and 0.926 ± 0.007, respectively.
sample_unit: cervical cancer patients (5 for prompt tailoring, 30 for testing)

title: Implementing an Automated Prediction Model to Improve Prescribing of HIV Preexposure Prophylaxis
venue: NEJM catalyst innovations in care delivery
outcome: New PrEP prescriptions and HIV testing at pilot versus matched control clinics
effect: New PrEP prescriptions were 4.5 times higher at pilot clinics (0.09% vs. 0.02%), but the 5.5% increase in HIV tests per 100 patients was not statistically significant.
quote: Although numbers of PrEP prescriptions remained low, the proportion of all patients with new PrEP prescriptions was 4.5 times higher at pilot clinics compared with matched control clinics (0.09% vs. 0.02%).

title: Benchmarking the Confidence of Large Language Models in Answering Clinical Questions: Cross-Sectional Evaluation Study
outcome: Calibration of LLM self-reported confidence: correlation with accuracy and confidence gap between correct and incorrect answers
effect: Correlation between mean confidence for correct answers and accuracy was inverse (r=-0.40; P=.001). Confidence difference between correct and incorrect responses ranged 0.6% to 5.4%; GPT-4o highest (5.4%, P=.003).
quote: The correlation between the mean confidence scores for correct answers and model accuracy was inverse and statistically significant (r=-0.40; P=.001), indicating that worse-performing models exhibited paradoxically higher confidence.

title: Uncertainty quantification for deep learning-based metastatic lesion segmentation on whole body PET/CT
outcome: uncertainty quantification for segmentation reliability
effect: TTA was superior overall; FP detection AUCs ranged 0.77-0.81; correlations were mixed, with best ρ values 0.57, 0.72, 0.35, and 0.96.
quote: Performance for the correlation analysis was mixed, where the strongest performance was achieved by test time augmentation for SUV<sub>total</sub>capture (ρ= 0.57) and segmentation Dice coefficient (ρ= 0.72), by Monte Carlo dropout for SUV<sub>mean</sub>capture (ρ= 0.35), and by probability entropy for segmentation cross entropy (ρ= 0.96).

title: Impact of test set composition on AI performance in pediatric wrist fracture detection in X-rays
outcome: Model performance on random versus difficulty-balanced representative test sets
effect: YOLOv11 precision fell from 0.95 in the random test set to 0.83 in the balanced set with more challenging cases; recall, accuracy, and F1 showed similar declines across all model variants.
quote: For example, the precision for YOLOv11 models decreased from 0.95 in the random set to 0.83 in the balanced set.

title: Performance of the Large Language Models in African rheumatology: a diagnostic test accuracy study of ChatGPT-4, Gemini, Copilot, and Claude artificial intelligence
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy differences across age subgroups and disease categories
effect: Patients under 50 had significantly higher odds of correct diagnosis with Copilot (OR = 3.36; 95% CI 1.16-9.71; p = 0.025); ChatGPT-4 and Claude sensitivity <67% for neoplastic diseases.
quote: Patients under 50 years old had a significantly higher probability of receiving a correct diagnosis with Copilot (OR = 3.36; 95% CI [1.16-9.71]; p = 0.025).

title: Performance of the Large Language Models in African rheumatology: a diagnostic test accuracy study of ChatGPT-4, Gemini, Copilot, and Claude artificial intelligence
outcome: Comparison of four candidate LLMs' diagnostic accuracy on same patient data against expert diagnoses
effect: ChatGPT-4 86.41%, Claude AI 85.44%, Copilot 75.73%, Gemini 71.84%; inter-model kappa 0.43 to 0.59. Compared against each other, not against clinicians.
quote: ChatGPT-4 achieved the highest diagnostic accuracy (86.41%), followed by Claude AI (85.44%), Copilot (75.73%), and Gemini (71.84%).

title: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT-4 for Automated Mapping of Local Medical Terminologies to SNOMED CT
venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
outcome: Valid SNOMED CT term match and exact match rates for RAG-grounded versus other GPT-4 mapping approaches
effect: RAG had 96.2% valid term match and 57.6% exact match, versus fine-tuned 69.2% valid and 47.2% exact; RAG structural errors were 14%, lower than other models.
quote: The RAG model achieved the highest performance with a 96.2% valid SNOMED CT term match rate and a 57.6% overall exact match rate, surpassing the fine-tuned model (69.2% valid term match, 47.2% exact match).

title: Impact of an Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Enhanced Electronic Health Record System on Quality Measures in Nursing Homes: A Difference-in-Differences Analysis
venue: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association
outcome: Change in CMS nursing home quality measures after EHR+AI implementation versus EHR-only sites
effect: Greater improvements in 16 of 18 quality measures in EHR+AI sites; major falls -9% (95% CI -17, -1); residents needing help with daily activities -22% (95% CI -29, -15).
quote: Statistically greater improvements were observed in 16 of 18 quality measures (89%) in EHR+AI sites, with 11 measures (61%) also meeting the parallel trends assumption.

title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and Human Translation of an Outcome Questionnaire: A Randomized, Double-Blinded Non-inferiority Study
outcome: Patient-rated readability, comprehension, and language of AI vs human translation
effect: Before face validation, ChatGPT-4 translation scored median 4 vs 5 for human on readability (p=0.008), understandability (p=0.004), appropriate language (p=0.001), overall (p=0.002); 90% preferred human version.
quote: Before face validation, the human-translated version of the questionnaire was rated at least one point higher on the parameters of readability, comprehension, appropriate use of language, and overall opinion of the questionnaire (Table 2 ).

title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and Human Translation of an Outcome Questionnaire: A Randomized, Double-Blinded Non-inferiority Study
outcome: Translation quality ratings after face validation with patient end users and revision
effect: After face validation, no significant differences: readability p=0.341, understandability p=0.082, appropriate language p=0.359, overall p=0.100; preference for human fell from 90% to 50%.
quote: After face validation, there were no significant differences regarding readability, comprehension, appropriate use of language, and overall opinion of the questionnaire (Table 2 ).

title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and Human Translation of an Outcome Questionnaire: A Randomized, Double-Blinded Non-inferiority Study
outcome: Patient-rated comprehension before and after patient face validation and questionnaire revision
effect: ChatGPT-4 understandability increased from 4 (2–5) to 5 (3–5); human medians remained 5. Between-translation p-values were 0.004 before and 0.082 after face validation. Results were not stratified by literacy.
quote: While the human-translated questionnaire initially performed better in terms of readability, comprehension, and appropriate use of language, the differences between the two versions disappeared following face validation.

title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and Human Translation of an Outcome Questionnaire: A Randomized, Double-Blinded Non-inferiority Study
outcome: questionnaire assessment scores
effect: Comparing AI to human translation revealed ChatGPT-4 scored significantly lower on readability, understandability, and appropriate language before face validation.
quote: Before face validation, the human-translated version of the questionnaire was rated at least one point higher on the parameters of readability, comprehension, appropriate use of language, and overall opinion of the questionnaire

title: Comparing ChatGPT-4 and Human Translation of an Outcome Questionnaire: A Randomized, Double-Blinded Non-inferiority Study
outcome: differences after face validation
effect: Conducting face validation with representative patients allowed correction of the AI's shortcomings, eliminating significant differences in understandability compared to human translation.
quote: However, the lack of significant differences after face validation implies that ChatGPT-4’s shortcomings were corrected through the face validation process.

title: Generative AI mitigates representation bias and improves model fairness through synthetic health data
outcome: Downstream model fairness by subpopulation after synthetic-data bias mitigation
effect: Synthetic data from CA-GAN improved model fairness in Black patients and female patients, evaluated separately per subpopulation; predictive performance in the downstream task also improved.
quote: We show that synthetic data generated by our CA-GAN improves model fairness in Black patients as well as female patients when evaluated separately for each subpopulation.

title: Generative AI mitigates representation bias and improves model fairness through synthetic health data
outcome: Effect of augmenting underrepresented subgroup data on downstream predictive performance
effect: CA-GAN generated authentic minority-class data while maintaining the original data distribution, resulting in improved downstream predictive performance.
quote: Furthermore, CA-GAN generates authentic data of the minority class while faithfully maintaining the original distribution of data, resulting in improved performance in a downstream predictive task.

title: Assessing information provided via artificial intelligence regarding distal biceps tendon repair surgery
outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of ChatGPT answers to patient questions on distal biceps repair
effect: FRES 24.49 (Fact), 22.82 (Policy), 21.77 (Value); FKGL 14.96, 14.78, 15.00, roughly college-graduate reading level.
quote: The accuracy and reliability of these answers were shown to be low, with nearly a college-graduate level of readability.

title: Comparison of ChatGPT and Internet Research for Clinical Research and Decision-Making in Occupational Medicine: Randomized Controlled Trial
outcome: Case performance of clinicians using ChatGPT versus own research on occupational medicine cases
effect: ChatGPT group did better on specific research questions (2.5 vs 1.8 hazardous substances, P=.01), but made fewer correct clinical decisions (report filed: 7 vs 14, P=.007; OR 6.00, 95% CI 1.54-23.36).
quote: However, clinical decisions, for example, whether an occupational disease report should be filed, were more often made correctly as a result of the participant's own research (n=29; eg, case 1: Should an occupational disease report be filed? Yes for 7 participants in the ChatGPT group vs 14 in their own research group; P=.007; odds ratio 6.00, 95% CI 1.54-23.36).

title: Evaluating large language models in echocardiography reporting: opportunities and challenges
outcome: Correlation of automatic metrics with cardiologist ratings and sensitivity to changed measurement numbers
effect: Automatic-human metric correlations were fair to modest (best RadGraph F1 vs clinical utility r = 0.42); automatic metrics showed only 0-5% drop when measurement numbers were changed.
quote: automatic metrics showed insensitivity (0-5% drop) to changes in measurement numbers

title: Coronary Computed Tomographic Angiography to Optimize the Diagnostic Yield of Invasive Angiography for Low-Risk Patients Screened With Artificial Intelligence: Protocol for the CarDIA-AI Randomized Controlled Trial
outcome: Proportion of normal or nonobstructive CAD diagnosed via ICA, AI triage versus usual care
effect: Protocol only; no results yet. 252 patients to be randomized 1:1; 81 enrolled as of April 14, 2025; results expected 2026.
quote: CarDIA-AI is a pragmatic, open-label, superior randomized controlled trial involving 2 Canadian cardiac centers.

title: Application of AI Chatbot in Responding to Asynchronous Text-Based Messages From Patients With Cancer: Comparative Study
outcome: Potentially adverse-outcome rate of chatbot vs physician responses in medical decision-making
effect: 3.12% (59/1893) of chatbot responses potentially leading to adverse outcomes vs 2.01% (38/1893) for physicians; lower accuracy (96.88% vs 97.99%, P<.001) in decision-making scenario.
quote: Errors in chatbot responses were primarily due to misinterpretations of medical terminology or the lack of updated guidelines, with 3.12% (59/1893) of its responses potentially leading to adverse outcomes, compared with 2.01% (38/1893) for physicians.
