effect: Fleiss kappa 0.449 to 0.763 across LLM-prompt combinations (moderate to substantial); best consistency 60.3% (Claude 3.5 with P-COT); no significant English vs Chinese differences in most combinations.
quote: The reliability of the different LLM-prompt combinations showed moderate to substantial agreement (Fleiss kappa ranged from 0.449 to 0.763).
sample_unit: questions derived from ESC 2024 AF guideline recommendations

title: Prompting Pro Tips! Best Practices for Generating Clinical Narrative Summaries
outcome: clinical adequacy, hallucinations, and bias
effect: Structured adequacy 39% compared to 9%, but structured prompts were more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias.
quote: The structured approach was more likely to produce a clinically adequate summary (39% compared to 9%) but also more likely to introduce hallucinations and bias.
sample_unit: LLMs evaluated on 8 clinical scenarios each with structured and vague prompts

title: Dental Trauma Evo - Development of an Artificial Intelligence-powered Chatbot to Support Professional Management of Dental Trauma
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of chatbot dental trauma management recommendations against IADT guidelines
effect: 100% accuracy in recommending appropriate management; initial completeness as low as 53% for primary tooth fractures, improved to 100% in most cases after code adjustments; avulsed open-apex reimplantation reached 93%.
quote: The chatbot achieved 100% accuracy in recommending appropriate clinical management.

title: Psychological, economic, and ethical factors in human feedback for a chatbot-based smoking cessation intervention
outcome: Which smoker subgroups an RL policy prioritizes for scarce human feedback
effect: The benefit-maximizing RL model prioritizes people who would benefit most and also those already doing well who want feedback. Alternative ethical principles shift priority to other subgroups, with interdependencies.
quote: It not only prioritizes people who would benefit most, but also those who are already doing well and want feedback.

title: A general framework for governing marketed AI/ML medical devices
outcome: Adequacy of FDA MAUDE adverse event reporting for assessing safety of AI/ML devices
effect: Analysis of adverse event data for approximately 950 AI/ML devices found the existing FDA adverse event reporting system insufficient for properly assessing safety and effectiveness of AI/ML devices.
quote: In particular, we evaluate the data pertaining to adverse events associated with approximately 950 medical devices incorporating AI/ML functions for devices approved between 2010 through 2023, and we find that the existing system is insufficient for properly assessing the safety and effectiveness of AI/ML devices.
sample_unit: FDA-marketed AI/ML medical devices (approximate count; adverse event reports in MAUDE)

title: Comparative evaluation of responses from DeepSeek-R1, ChatGPT-o1, ChatGPT-4, and dental GPT chatbots to patient inquiries about dental and maxillofacial prostheses
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease) of chatbot answers to patient questions
effect: Readability differed significantly between chatbots (p<.05); DeepSeek-R1 was best and Dental GPT worst. Understandability and actionability did not differ significantly. No readability values are given in the abstract.
quote: DeepSeek-R1 performed best, while Dental GPT had the lowest performance in readability.

title: Evaluating DeepResearch and DeepThink in anterior cruciate ligament surgery patient education: ChatGPT-4o excels in comprehensiveness, DeepSeek R1 leads in clarity and readability of orthopaedic information
venue: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
outcome: Reading level (FKGL, FRES) of LLM patient education responses about ACL surgery
effect: DeepSeek FKGL 8.9 vs ChatGPT 14.2 (p<0.001); FRES 61.3 vs 32.7 (p<0.001). ChatGPT text was at a college-level reading grade, DeepSeek nearer general audience.
quote: DeepSeek had lower FKGL (8.9 vs. 14.2, p < 0.001) and higher FRES (61.3 vs. 32.7, p < 0.001), indicating greater ease of reading for a general audience.

title: Evaluating DeepResearch and DeepThink in anterior cruciate ligament surgery patient education: ChatGPT-4o excels in comprehensiveness, DeepSeek R1 leads in clarity and readability of orthopaedic information
venue: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
outcome: Clarity and readability of AI patient education outputs for laypersons
effect: DeepSeek clarity 3.9 vs ChatGPT 3.0 (p<0.001); DeepSeek FKGL 8.9 vs 14.2, so ChatGPT output less comprehensible to lay readers.
quote: DeepSeek's answers were clearer and more accessible to laypersons (mean clarity 3.9 vs. 3.0, p < 0.001)

title: Validation of a novel artificial intelligence model (SpinePose) to automatically and accurately predict spinopelvic parameters using scoliosis radiographs in an external cohort
outcome: Model accuracy on external-institution radiographs versus manual ground truth
effect: No significant differences between predicted and ground truth: SVA 50.7 vs 52.3 mm (p=0.85); PT 27.6 vs 30.5° (p=0.24); PI 58.0 vs 61.8° (p=0.17); LL 40.4 vs 42.4° (p=0.77); T1PA 24.8 vs 28.0° (p=0.21).
quote: SpinePose accurately predicted all 5 spinopelvic parameters without any statistically significant differences: SVA, 50.7 mm vs 52.3 mm (p = 0.85); PT, 27.6° vs 30.5° (p = 0.24); PI, 58.0° vs 61.8° (p = 0.17); LL, 40.4° vs 42.4° (p = 0.77); and T1PA, 24.8° vs 28.0° (p = 0.21) when comparing ground truth annotations with predicted values.

title: Comparison of quality, empathy and readability of physician responses versus chatbot responses to common cerebrovascular neurosurgical questions on a social media platform
outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT responses versus physician responses to patient questions
effect: Physician responses had significantly higher ease of readability and lower grade-level readability than ChatGPT (p < 0.001); ChatGPT responses exceeded average American literacy.
quote: However, these responses are at readability levels higher than the literacy of the average American population.

title: Comparison of quality, empathy and readability of physician responses versus chatbot responses to common cerebrovascular neurosurgical questions on a social media platform
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of chatbot answers to patient questions, measured with six readability indexes
effect: Physician responses had significantly higher ease of readability and lower grade-level readability compared to ChatGPT (p < 0.001).
quote: Physician responses had significantly higher ease of readability and lower grade-level readability compared to ChatGPT (p < 0.001).

title: Harnessing GPT-4 for automated error detection in pathology reports: Implications for oncology diagnostics
outcome: Error detection rate, false positives, and processing time of GPT-4 versus six pathologists on the same reports
effect: GPT-4 detected 88% of errors (350/400) vs 95% (382/400) for the top senior pathologist; 4.03 s vs 65.64 s per report; false positives 2.3% vs 0.3%.
quote: GPT-4 detected 88% of errors (350/400; 95% CI: [84, 91]), compared to a 95% detection rate by the top senior pathologist (382/400; 95% CI: [93, 97]).

title: Dimensionality Reduction and Nearest Neighbors for Improving Out-of-Distribution Detection in Medical Image Segmentation
venue: The journal of machine learning for biomedical imaging
outcome: Out-of-distribution failure detection
effect: KNN drastically improved scalability and performance over MD; no numbers reported.
quote: KNN drastically improved scalability and performance over MD when both were applied to raw and average-pooled bottleneck features.

title: Dimensionality Reduction and Nearest Neighbors for Improving Out-of-Distribution Detection in Medical Image Segmentation
venue: The journal of machine learning for biomedical imaging
outcome: Out-of-distribution failure detection
effect: Images the models failed on were detected with high performance and minimal computational load; no numbers reported.
quote: By reducing the dimensions of the bottleneck features with either principal component analysis or uniform manifold approximation and projection, images the models failed on were detected with high performance and minimal computational load.

title: Enhancing the Accuracy of Human Phenotype Ontology Identification: Comparative Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models
outcome: HPO description accuracy of physicians with vs without MLLM assistance, plus standalone MLLM accuracy
quote: Of the 270 descriptions collected from each group, the MLLM-assisted group achieved a correctness rate of 67.4% (182/270), while the manual group achieved 20.4% (55/270).
sample_unit: junior physicians (27 patient images each, 540 descriptions)

title: Enhancing the Accuracy of Human Phenotype Ontology Identification: Comparative Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models
outcome: Whether physicians detected or were misled by incorrect AI outputs (anchoring)
effect: For Bardet-Biedl syndrome, MLLM missed 'polydactyly'; error rate was higher in MLLM-assisted group (6/10) than manual (4/10), though overall accuracy improved.
quote: This led to a higher error rate in the MLLM-assisted group (6/10 physicians) compared to the manual group (4/10).
sample_unit: junior physicians (27 patient images each, 540 descriptions)

title: Enhancing the Accuracy of Human Phenotype Ontology Identification: Comparative Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models
outcome: Hallucinated HPO identifiers and terms
quote: Specifically, ChatGPT-4o, Llama3.2:11b, and Llama3.2:90b generated incorrect IDs in 57.3% (67/117), 98% (62/63), and 82% (46/56) of cases, respectively, and fabricated terms in 34.2% (40/117), 41% (26/63), and 32% (18/56) of cases, respectively.
sample_unit: junior physicians (27 patient images each, 540 descriptions)

title: Enhancing the Accuracy of Human Phenotype Ontology Identification: Comparative Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models
outcome: Clinician performance with AI in workflow versus without AI and versus standalone model
effect: Physician+ChatGPT-4o accuracy 67.4% exceeded standalone ChatGPT-4o (48%) and manual searching (20.4%).
quote: Our study reveals that collaboration between junior physicians and ChatGPT-4o significantly enhances HPO description accuracy for rare diseases, outperforming both traditional methods and standalone MLLM use.
sample_unit: junior physicians (27 patient images each, 540 descriptions)

title: Enhancing the Accuracy of Human Phenotype Ontology Identification: Comparative Evaluation of Multimodal Large Language Models
outcome: Standalone MLLM HPO identification accuracy
quote: Among the 27 patient images, ChatGPT-4o achieved an accuracy rate of 48% (13/27), while Llama3.2:11b and Llama3.2:90b achieved rates of 15% (4/27) and 18% (5/27), respectively ( Table 3 ).
sample_unit: junior physicians (27 patient images each, 540 descriptions)

title: Diagnostic accuracy of an artificial intelligence-based platform in detecting periapical radiolucencies on cone-beam computed tomography scans of molars
outcome: Diagnostic performance versus endodontist reference standard on retrospective CBCT scans, pre- vs postoperative
effect: Preoperative non-root-filled molars: sensitivity 93.9% (teeth), specificity 65.2%, PPV 71.8%; postoperative scans showed lower PPV (teeth 54.2%; roots 46.9%) and F1 (teeth 67.2%; roots 59.2%).
quote: Postoperative scans showed significantly lower PPV (teeth: 54.2 %; roots: 46.9 %) and F1 scores (teeth: 67.2 %; roots: 59.2 %).

title: Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Gatekeeping in Referrals to Specialized Care
outcome: AI model accuracy, sensitivity, specificity versus human gatekeepers against physician consensus standard
effect: AI had higher accuracy and specificity and lower sensitivity than current human gatekeeper approach; AI accuracy 0.716, sensitivity 0.542, specificity 0.801.
quote: When compared against the consensus standard, the AI model had higher accuracy and specificity and lower sensitivity than the current approach.

title: Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence for Gatekeeping in Referrals to Specialized Care
outcome: AI accuracy across five specialties
effect: Accuracy ranged from 0.811 (rheumatology) to 0.649 (proctology); overall 0.716.
quote: Regarding individual specialties, rheumatology exhibited the highest accuracy (0.811; 95% IC, 0.767-0.849), while proctology had the lowest (0.649; 95% IC, 0.597-0.697).

title: Clinical Trial Design Approach to Auditing Language Models in Health Care Setting
outcome: Ability of blinded expert audit of deployed model outputs to detect issues
effect: The continuous single-blind expert audit identified the core issues in the operational models, enabling early interventions that maintained data integrity; no numeric results were reported.
quote: Deployed at the British Columbia Cancer Registry, our audit process effectively identified the core issues in the operational models.

title: Predicting 30-Day Postoperative Mortality and American Society of Anesthesiologists Physical Status Using Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models: Development and Validation Study
outcome: F1 for 30-day mortality and ASA class prediction with versus without RAG grounding
effect: Mortality F1 0.4663 with RAG and few-shot vs 0.0879 without RAG; ASA micro F1 0.8409 vs 0.6340 without RAG.
quote: The LLaMA-RAG model significantly improved the prediction of postoperative mortality and ASA classification, especially for rare high-risk cases.

title: Promoting patient health literacy in burn care through artificial intelligence language learning models: A study of text analysis and simplification
venue: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
outcome: Readability grade level of burn care patient materials after AI simplification, versus 6th-8th grade target
effect: Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, and Meta AI reduced readability scores to within the 6th to 8th-grade level. ChatGPT 4o is not reported as reaching the target. Clinician oversight is still needed for accuracy.
quote: Additionally, when tasked with simplifying the texts, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini, and Meta AI reduced the readability scores to within the desired 6th to 8th-grade level.

title: Performance evaluation of large language models in pediatric nephrology clinical decision support: a comprehensive assessment
outcome: Performance of RAG-grounded specialized model versus generalist LLMs on pediatric nephrology cases
effect: Domain-specific fine-tuning with retrieval-augmented generation on validated materials improved performance across all clinical criteria without enhancing reasoning capabilities.
quote: Domain-specific fine-tuning improved performance across all clinical criteria without enhancing reasoning capabilities.

title: Performance evaluation of large language models in pediatric nephrology clinical decision support: a comprehensive assessment
outcome: Hallucination occurrences in LLM answers to pediatric nephrology cases
effect: All models exhibited hallucinations (2-8 occurrences).
quote: All models exhibited hallucinations (2-8 occurrences) and potentially life-threatening decisions (0-2 occurrences).

title: Performance evaluation of large language models in pediatric nephrology clinical decision support: a comprehensive assessment
outcome: Hallucinations and potentially dangerous recommendations in LLM outputs
effect: All models had hallucinations (2-8) and potentially life-threatening decisions (0-2); authors conclude strict supervision is needed.
quote: All models exhibited hallucinations (2-8 occurrences) and potentially life-threatening decisions (0-2 occurrences).

title: Evaluating AI chatbots in penis enhancement information: a comparative analysis of readability, reliability and quality
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on penis enhancement (FKGL, FRES)
effect: All three chatbots produced hard-to-read responses, with no significant differences between them (FKGL p = 0.167; FRES p = 0.366).
quote: All chatbot responses exhibited difficulty in readability and understanding according to FKGL and FRES, with no statistically significant differences among them (FKGL: p = 0.167; FRES: p = 0.366).

title: Detecting and Remediating Harmful Data Shifts for the Responsible Deployment of Clinical AI Models
outcome: Model performance with drift-triggered updating versus locked model during COVID-19
effect: Data shift-triggered continual updating improved performance over a locked model during COVID-19 (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.44 [0.02]; P = .007, Mann-Whitney U test).
quote: Overall, data shift–triggered continual updating improved model performance over time and was more effective than maintaining a locked model during the COVID-19 pandemic (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.44 [0.02]; P = .007, Mann-Whitney U test) ( Figure 4 B).

title: Detecting and Remediating Harmful Data Shifts for the Responsible Deployment of Clinical AI Models
outcome: Performance gain from fine-tuning/transfer learning on target hospital data
effect: Community hospitals benefited from community-specific pretraining (Delta AUROC 0.05 [0.03]; Delta AUPRC 0.06 [0.04]); hospital type-specific fine-tuning improved all sites except hospital 2.
quote: Hospital type–specific fine-tuning improved performance for all sites except hospital 2, where ablating hospital 3 yielded the best performance.

title: Detecting and Remediating Harmful Data Shifts for the Responsible Deployment of Clinical AI Models
outcome: Model performance across diagnostic, age, and sex subgroups
effect: Performance was lower for neoplasms (AUROC 0.77) and health status factors (AUROC 0.75) than circulatory (0.86) or infectious diseases (0.87); varied by age, consistent across sex.
quote: Performance varied by age but remained consistent across sex ( Figure 1 D).

title: Detecting and Remediating Harmful Data Shifts for the Responsible Deployment of Clinical AI Models
outcome: Drift-triggered versus fixed-interval model updating performance
effect: Data shift-triggered model updating improved performance compared with updating at fixed intervals; best P value threshold .01.
quote: To mitigate model deterioration, we leveraged continual learning ( Figure 4 A) and found that data shift–triggered model updating improved performance compared with updating at fixed intervals (eFigure 9 in Supplement 1 ).

title: Detecting and Remediating Harmful Data Shifts for the Responsible Deployment of Clinical AI Models
outcome: Cross-setting dataset shift
effect: Community-to-academic transfer decreased age ≥65 AUROC −0.05 [0.003] and AUPRC −0.02 [0.01]; younger AUPRC −0.26 [0.02].
quote: Transferring from community to academic hospitals led to decreased model performance for patients aged 65 or older (Delta AUROC [SD], −0.05 [0.003]; Delta AUPRC [SD], −0.02 [0.01]) and to mixed results for younger patients (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.07 [0.02]; Delta AUPRC [SD], −0.26 [0.02]).

title: Detecting and Remediating Harmful Data Shifts for the Responsible Deployment of Clinical AI Models
outcome: Detection of data drift and performance degradation in deployed mortality model
effect: Label-agnostic pipeline detected shifts (age groups, admission source, hospital type, BNP, D-dimer); shifts led to reduced AUROC/AUPRC overall and across subgroups.
quote: We observed that the identified data shifts led to reduced AUROC, AUPRC, or both for the overall population (eFigure 6 in Supplement 1 ) and across subgroups (eFigure 7 in Supplement 1 ).

title: Detecting and Remediating Harmful Data Shifts for the Responsible Deployment of Clinical AI Models
outcome: Performance change when model transferred between hospital types
effect: Community-to-academic transfer decreased performance for patients aged 65 or older (Delta AUROC -0.05; Delta AUPRC -0.02) and gave mixed results for younger patients.
quote: Transferring from community to academic hospitals led to decreased model performance for patients aged 65 or older (Delta AUROC [SD], −0.05 [0.003]; Delta AUPRC [SD], −0.02 [0.01]) and to mixed results for younger patients (Delta AUROC [SD], 0.07 [0.02]; Delta AUPRC [SD], −0.26 [0.02]).

title: Detecting and Remediating Harmful Data Shifts for the Responsible Deployment of Clinical AI Models
outcome: Label-agnostic drift detection
effect: Detected shifts from younger age/admission source, community-to-academic transfer, and BNP/D-dimer changes.
quote: Significant data shifts were detected as a result of changes in younger age groups and admissions from nursing homes and acute care centers, transferring from community to academic hospitals, and changes in brain natriuretic peptide and D-dimer.

title: Nomograms versus artificial intelligence platforms: which one can better predict sentinel node positivity in melanoma patients?
outcome: Comparison of nomograms versus public AI platforms for predicting sentinel node positivity on same patients
effect: Only MSKCC nomogram (P=0.04) and ChatGPT (P=0.02) differed between positive and negative SNB; ChatGPT AUC 0.702, adding MSKCC gave 0.715. No concordance among nomograms or among AI platforms (P<0.001).
quote: Only ChatGPT score was statistically significant for SNB positivity after univariate logistic regression (odds ratio: 1.05; 95% confidence interval: 1.004-1.108; P = 0.03).
sample_unit: melanoma patients who underwent sentinel node biopsy

title: Enhancing the Readability of Online Patient Education Materials Using Large Language Models: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Reading grade level of original online patient education materials versus sixth-grade recommendation
effect: Original mean grade levels were 10.7 (AHA), 10.0 (ACS), and 9.6 (ASA), all above the recommended sixth-grade level.
quote: The original readability scores for the American Heart Association (AHA), American Cancer Society (ACS), and American Stroke Association (ASA) websites were above the recommended sixth-grade level, with mean grade level scores of 10.7,10.0, and 9.6, respectively.

title: Enhancing the Readability of Online Patient Education Materials Using Large Language Models: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified patient education materials versus originals (average grade level)
effect: Average grade level improved from 10.1 to 7.6 (ChatGPT), 6.6 (Gemini), and 5.6 (Claude), all P<.001; understandability (PEMAT-U) largely preserved.
quote: Compared with the original website, ChatGPT improved the readability to 7.6 from 10.1 ( P <.001); Gemini, to 6.6 ( P <.001); and Claude, to 5.6 ( P <.001).

title: Enhancing the Readability of Online Patient Education Materials Using Large Language Models: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Inaccuracies in LLM-simplified patient education materials versus original content
effect: ChatGPT 0/60 inaccurate; Gemini 2/60 (3.3%) and Claude 2/60 (3.3%) inaccurate, e.g., 'Tiny heart trouble' for coronary microvascular disease.
quote: ChatGPT had no inaccuracies on all 3 sites, while Gemini experienced 2 inaccuracies on the AHA website and Claude experienced one inaccuracy on the ACA and one on the ASA website.

title: Enhancing the Readability of Online Patient Education Materials Using Large Language Models: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: achievement of target reading level
effect: Only Claude consistently achieved fifth-grade level on all 3 websites (5.5-5.9); Gemini on one website; ChatGPT on none.
quote: Of LLM-simplified versions of the PEM, only Claude consistently achieved a mean fifth-grade reading level on all 3 websites (5.5-5.9), while Gemini did on one of the websites, and ChatGPT on none.

title: GPT-4 generates accurate and readable patient education materials aligned with current oncological guidelines: A randomized assessment
outcome: Reading level of original patient materials versus appropriate level
effect: Original EAU PEMs required higher reading grade level (FKGL 11.6, GFS 14.3) than GPT-4 PEMs (FKGL 6.1, GFS 7.4); the original PEMs did not meet EU readability standards.
quote: Moreover, it has been noted that certain sections of PEMs exhibit poor readability, not meeting the readability standards set by the European Union (EU) for patient facing material [ 8 ].
sample_unit: ratings of patient education materials (PEMs) per arm in the randomized assessment
country: Multi-country (European Union / Young Academic Urologists groups)

title: GPT-4 generates accurate and readable patient education materials aligned with current oncological guidelines: A randomized assessment
outcome: Accuracy of GPT-4 PEMs grounded in EAU guidelines versus original PEMs
effect: Guideline-grounded GPT-4 PEMs were not significantly different from original PEMs in accuracy (e.g., prostate localized 4.3 vs 3.7, p=.122); no comparison against ungrounded GPT-4.
quote: For localized disease, the original PEM was not significantly different from the GPT-4 generated PEM for mean (SD) accuracy [prostate cancer: 4.3 (0.7) vs 3.7 (1.1), p = .122;
sample_unit: ratings of patient education materials (PEMs) per arm in the randomized assessment
country: Multi-country (European Union / Young Academic Urologists groups)

title: GPT-4 generates accurate and readable patient education materials aligned with current oncological guidelines: A randomized assessment
outcome: Accuracy, completeness, clarity of GPT-4 PEMs versus original PEMs rated by expert urologists
effect: No significant differences for localized or metastatic disease; correctness trifecta reached in 92/160 original vs 81/160 GPT-4 PEMs (p=.217).
quote: The correctness trifecta was reached in 92/160 rated original PEM and 81/160 rated GPT-4 generated PEM (p = .217).
sample_unit: ratings of patient education materials (PEMs) per arm in the randomized assessment
country: Multi-country (European Union / Young Academic Urologists groups)

title: GPT-4 generates accurate and readable patient education materials aligned with current oncological guidelines: A randomized assessment
outcome: Expert-rated quality of unedited GPT-4 PEMs that would need review before release
effect: Unedited GPT-4 PEMs were rated similar to original PEMs, but agreement on all three correctness metrics was reached in only 81/160 ratings; authors say human oversight is still required.
quote: Neither original PEMs nor GPT-4 generated PEMs are flawless, despite an overall agreement on correctness of the information by the expert raters in our study.
sample_unit: ratings of patient education materials (PEMs) per arm in the randomized assessment
country: Multi-country (European Union / Young Academic Urologists groups)

title: GPT-4 generates accurate and readable patient education materials aligned with current oncological guidelines: A randomized assessment
outcome: Patient material reading level
effect: GPT-4 PEMs had lower reading grade levels than originals: FKGL 6.1 vs 11.6; GFS 7.4 vs 14.3; SI 6.3 vs 10.6; all p < .001.
quote: In line, the required reading education levels were higher (less readable) for original PEMs [FKGL: 11.6 (2.4); GFS: 14.3 (2.5); SI: 10.6 (1.8); CLI: 14.2 (1.5); ARI: 11.6 (3.0)] compared to GPT4-generated PEMs [FKGL: 6.1 (0.9), p < .001; GFS: 7.4 (0.8), p < .001; SI: 6.3 (0.6), p < .001; CLI: 11.7 (1.3), p = .004; ARI: 6.1 (1.3), p < .001, see Fig 2 ].
sample_unit: ratings of patient education materials (PEMs) per arm in the randomized assessment
country: Multi-country (European Union / Young Academic Urologists groups)

title: GPT-4 generates accurate and readable patient education materials aligned with current oncological guidelines: A randomized assessment
outcome: GPT-4 PEMs versus original PEMs
effect: GPT-4 PEMs had FKRE 70.8 vs 43.5 for originals (p < .001) and correctness trifecta 81/160 vs 92/160 (p = .217).
quote: The readability scores for original PEMs [Mean (SD) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease: 43.5 (10.8)] were lower than for GPT-4 generated PEMs [Mean (SD) Flesch Kincaid Reading Ease: 70.8 (4.9), p < .001].
sample_unit: ratings of patient education materials (PEMs) per arm in the randomized assessment
country: Multi-country (European Union / Young Academic Urologists groups)

title: Mortality Prediction Performance Under Geographical, Temporal, and COVID-19 Pandemic Dataset Shift: External Validation of the Global Open-Source Severity of Illness Score Model
outcome: External validation of mortality model discrimination and calibration in a new country's ICU data
effect: GOSSIS-1 AUC 0.908, comparable to APACHE-III (0.908) and JROD (0.910); SMR 0.89 (95% CI 0.88-0.90) vs APACHE-II 0.39 and APACHE-III 0.46. Suboptimal calibration for neurologic and trauma categories.
quote: GOSSIS-1 demonstrates robust discrimination despite substantial geographic dataset shift but shows important calibration variations across disease categories.

title: Mortality Prediction Performance Under Geographical, Temporal, and COVID-19 Pandemic Dataset Shift: External Validation of the Global Open-Source Severity of Illness Score Model
outcome: Model calibration and performance drift over time including COVID-19 pandemic period
effect: Temporal stability 2015-2019, but performance deteriorated during COVID-19 in 2020 across disease categories, more pronounced for GOSSIS than APACHE-III.
quote: While the model showed temporal stability from 2015 to 2019, performance deteriorated during the COVID-19 pandemic, broadly reducing performance across disease categories in 2020.

title: Mortality Prediction Performance Under Geographical, Temporal, and COVID-19 Pandemic Dataset Shift: External Validation of the Global Open-Source Severity of Illness Score Model
outcome: Model performance under geographic dataset shift between development and local populations
effect: Despite demographic and clinical differences, GOSSIS-1 kept strong discrimination (AUC 0.908) but calibration varied by disease category.
quote: Despite the demographic and clinical differences of the validation cohort, GOSSIS-1 maintained strong discrimination, achieving an area under the curve of 0.908, comparable to APACHE-III (0.908) and JROD (0.910).

title: Mortality Prediction Performance Under Geographical, Temporal, and COVID-19 Pandemic Dataset Shift: External Validation of the Global Open-Source Severity of Illness Score Model
outcome: Comparison of GOSSIS-1 with APACHE-II, APACHE-III, and JROD on same data
effect: GOSSIS-1 calibration SMR 0.89 significantly better than APACHE-II (0.39) and APACHE-III (0.46), close to JROD (0.97); AUC comparable to APACHE-III and JROD.
quote: It also exhibited superior calibration, achieving a standardized mortality ratio (SMR) of 0.89 (95% CI, 0.88-0.90), significantly outperforming APACHE-II (SMR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.39-0.40) and APACHE-III (SMR, 0.46; 95% CI, 0.46-0.47), and demonstrating a performance close to that of JROD (SMR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.99).

title: External validation of a digital pathology-based multimodal artificial intelligence-derived prognostic model in patients with advanced prostate cancer starting long-term androgen deprivation therapy: a post-hoc ancillary biomarker study of four phase 3 randomised controlled trials of the STAMPEDE platform protocol
outcome: Prognostic performance of locked MMAI algorithm on external multi-trial cohort (PCSM association)
effect: MMAI per SD increase strongly associated with PCSM (HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.30-1.51, p<0.0001) in 3167 patients from four STAMPEDE trials
quote: The MMAI algorithm (per SD increase) was strongly associated with PCSM (hazard ratio [HR] 1·40, 95% CI 1·30-1·51, p<0·0001).

title: Racial bias in AI-mediated psychiatric diagnosis and treatment: a qualitative comparison of four large language models
outcome: Bias in LLM diagnostic and treatment outputs when patient race was neutral, implied, or explicit
effect: LLMs often proposed inferior treatments when race was explicitly or implicitly indicated; diagnostic decisions showed minimal bias. NewMes-15 showed most bias, Gemini least.
quote: Results indicated that LLMs often proposed inferior treatments when patient race was explicitly or implicitly indicated, though diagnostic decisions demonstrated minimal bias.
sample_unit: LLM outputs (10 cases x 3 conditions x 4 models)

title: The utility of generative artificial intelligence Chatbot (ChatGPT) in generating teaching and learning material for anesthesiology residents
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT responses when asked for specific literature references
effect: The chatbot frequently generated inaccurate responses when asked for specific literature references. Overall, 52 of 95 (55%) responses were completely accurate by both raters.
quote: Notably, the chatbot frequently generated inaccurate responses when asked for specific literature references and when the input prompt contained deliberate errors (biased prompts).

title: The utility of generative artificial intelligence Chatbot (ChatGPT) in generating teaching and learning material for anesthesiology residents
outcome: ChatGPT accuracy when prompts contained deliberate medical errors (biased prompts)
effect: The chatbot frequently generated inaccurate responses when input prompts contained deliberate errors (biased prompts).
quote: Notably, the chatbot frequently generated inaccurate responses when asked for specific literature references and when the input prompt contained deliberate errors (biased prompts).

title: Longitudinal Comparison of Geographic Atrophy Enlargement Using Manual, Semiautomated, and Deep Learning Approaches
outcome: Share of AI-generated GA masks acceptable without human edits and free of longitudinal regression errors
effect: AI masks acceptable in 84.8% of visits; 81.4% of cases showed no regression over time, so about 15% needed human intervention.
quote: Artificial intelligence masks were deemed acceptable in 84.8% of visits, and 81.4% of cases showed no regression over time.

title: Enhancing patient-centered care with AI: a study of responses to neuroendocrine neoplasms queries
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy, clarity and completeness of LLM answers to neuroendocrine neoplasm management questions
effect: Mean scores: ChatGPT Plus 3.72, Copilot 3.54, Perplexity 3.22, with clarity rated highest; the chemotherapy indications question scored lowest.
quote: The chemotherapy indications question received the lowest scores, underscoring LLM challenges in handling complex clinical decisions.
sample_unit: raters (22 expert physicians and 24 NEN patients) scoring responses to 9 questions

title: Efficiency and Quality of Generative AI–Assisted Radiograph Reporting
outcome: Radiologist documentation time with versus without generative AI draft reports, plus peer-reviewed quality
effect: Model-assisted interpretations were faster (159.8 s vs 189.2 s; P = .02; 15.5% efficiency increase), with no difference in clinical accuracy (P = .41) or textual quality (P = .06) on peer review of 800 studies.
quote: Interpretations with model assistance (mean [SE], 159.8 [27.0] seconds) were faster than the baseline set of those without (mean [SE], 189.2 [36.2] seconds) (P = .02), representing a 15.5% documentation efficiency increase.
sample_unit: radiographs (11,980 with and 11,980 without model use) for documentation efficiency analysis

title: Efficiency and Quality of Generative AI–Assisted Radiograph Reporting
outcome: Prospective flagging of unexpected clinically significant pneumothorax on live radiographs
effect: The model flagged studies with clinically significant, unexpected pneumothorax with sensitivity of 72.7% and specificity of 99.9% among 97,651 studies screened.
quote: Moreover, the model flagged studies containing a clinically significant, unexpected pneumothorax with a sensitivity of 72.7% and specificity of 99.9% among 97 651 studies screened.
sample_unit: radiographs (11,980 with and 11,980 without model use) for documentation efficiency analysis

title: Artificial intelligence vs human expertise: A comparison of plantar fascia thickness measurements through MRI imaging
outcome: Plantar fascia thickness measurement reliability of ChatGPT-4 versus experienced clinician on same MRI data
effect: Clinician ICC 0.983-0.989 vs ChatGPT-4 ICC 0.391-0.432; ChatGPT-4 mean 6.47 mm vs clinician 4.20 mm; thin fascia MAE 2.70 mm, MRE 77.17% (blinded).
quote: ChatGPT-4 demonstrated lower reliability in plantar fascia thickness measurements compared to an experienced clinician, with increased error rates in thin structures.

title: CMedRAGBot: A Chinese Medical Chatbot Based on Graph RAG and Large Language Models
outcome: Exam question accuracy of LLMs with versus without knowledge-graph RAG grounding
effect: Integrating CMedRAGBot (graph RAG) significantly improved test accuracy of all five LLMs, with increases of up to approximately 10%.
quote: The results indicate that the integration of CMedRAGBot significantly improves the test accuracy of all models, with increases of up to approximately 10%.

title: The use of a large language model to create plain language summaries of evidence reviews in healthcare: A feasibility study
outcome: Reading level of LLM-generated plain language summaries against 6th-8th grade target
effect: Five of 10 PLSs met the target 6th to 8th grade reading level; passive voice averaged 16%.
quote: Five PLSs met the target 6th to 8th grade reading level.

title: The use of a large language model to create plain language summaries of evidence reviews in healthcare: A feasibility study
outcome: Accuracy of LLM-generated summaries of evidence reviews, including reported results
effect: Three PLSs accurately reported results, four had minor result errors, and three had major errors for incorrectly reporting total participants.
quote: We judged three PLSs as having major result errors for incorrectly reporting total participants.

title: A multimodal vision foundation model for clinical dermatology
outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in reader studies
effect: AI assistance improved clinicians' skin cancer diagnostic accuracy by 11% on dermoscopy images and nondermatologist providers' differential diagnosis by 16.5% across 128 conditions.
quote: PanDerm outperformed clinicians by 10.2% in early-stage melanoma detection through longitudinal analysis, improved clinicians' skin cancer diagnostic accuracy by 11% on dermoscopy images and enhanced nondermatologist healthcare providers' differential diagnosis by 16.5% across 128 skin conditions on clinical photographs.
country: multiple (11 clinical institutions, not specified in text)

title: A multimodal vision foundation model for clinical dermatology
outcome: AI performance compared with clinicians on early-stage melanoma detection
effect: PanDerm outperformed clinicians by 10.2% in early-stage melanoma detection through longitudinal analysis.
quote: PanDerm outperformed clinicians by 10.2% in early-stage melanoma detection through longitudinal analysis, improved clinicians' skin cancer diagnostic accuracy by 11% on dermoscopy images and enhanced nondermatologist healthcare providers' differential diagnosis by 16.5% across 128 skin conditions on clinical photographs.
country: multiple (11 clinical institutions, not specified in text)

title: Monitoring strategies for continuous evaluation of deployed clinical prediction models
outcome: Fidelity of post-deployment performance estimates to ground truth under feedback loops and drift
effect: Adherence Weighted and Sampling Weighted strategies had highest fidelity to ground truth classifier performance; standard approaches yielded the most inaccurate estimations.
quote: Measured across accuracy, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, average precision, brier score, expected calibration error, F1, precision, sensitivity, and specificity, in the presence of feedback loops, Adherence Weighted and Sampling Weighted strategies have the highest fidelity to the ground truth classifier performance while standard approaches yield the most inaccurate estimations.

title: Monitoring strategies for continuous evaluation of deployed clinical prediction models
outcome: AUROC after retraining following data drift with feedback loops, by monitoring strategy
effect: Standard unweighted retraining gave AUROC 0.52 (drop from 0.72); Adherence Weighted and Sampling Weighted retraining recovered to 0.67, comparable to a new model trained from scratch.
quote: Furthermore, in simulations with true data drift, retraining using standard unweighted approaches results in a AUROC score of 0.52 (drop from 0.72).

title: Implementation of a machine learning model and direct-to-patient outreach program for targeted screening for familial hypercholesterolemia
outcome: Share of model-flagged patients removed after expert chart review against the clinical record
effect: 208 of 388 flagged patients (54%) were removed from outreach after expert review; 115 of the 208 (55%) had a low likelihood of FH.
quote: After expert review, 208 (54%) patients were removed from outreach for meeting exclusion criteria.
sample_unit: patients flagged by the machine learning model

title: Implementation of a machine learning model and direct-to-patient outreach program for targeted screening for familial hypercholesterolemia
outcome: Clinical visits and new diagnoses yielded by direct-to-patient outreach to model-flagged high-risk patients
effect: Outreach yielded 72 clinical visits (19%) and 58 new diagnoses of possible/probable/definite FH (15%), versus about 0.4% expected in general-population screening. The process was labor intensive.
quote: A high-touch, direct-to-patient outreach process yielded 72 clinical visits (19%) and 58 new diagnoses of possible/probable/definite FH (15%).
sample_unit: patients flagged by the machine learning model

title: Proactive vs. passive algorithmic ethics practices in healthcare: the moderating role of healthcare engagement type in patients' responses
outcome: patient attitudes toward provider
effect: Proactive vs passive ethics practices improved attitudes: M=5.67, SD=1.00 vs M=4.28, SD=1.52; F(1, 504)=154.677, p<.001.
quote: Participants exposed to proactive algorithmic ethics practices reported more favorable attitudes toward the healthcare provider (M = 5.67, SD = 1.00) than those exposed to passive practices (M = 4.28, SD = 1.52).

title: Current utilization and impact of AI LVO detection tools in acute stroke triage: a multicenter survey analysis
outcome: Formal protocol integration and designated personnel for AI alert response
effect: Just 37.5% reported formal protocol integration, and 43.6% had designated personnel for AI alert response.
quote: Just 37.5% reported formal protocol integration, and 43.6% had designated personnel for AI alert response.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted diagnosis and prognostication in low ejection fraction using electrocardiograms in inpatient department: a pragmatic randomized controlled trial
outcome: Newly diagnosed low EF within 30 days after ECG, AI-ECG alerts versus standard care
effect: Detection rose 1.5% vs 1.1% (HR 1.50, 95% CI 1.11-2.03, P=0.023); high-risk patients 13.0% vs 8.9% (HR 1.55); echocardiogram use unchanged (17.1% vs 17.3%).
quote: The intervention significantly increased the detection of newly diagnosed low EF in the overall cohort (1.5% vs. 1.1%, HR 1.50, 95% CI: 1.11-2.03, P = 0.023), with a more pronounced effect among AI-identified high-risk patients (13.0% vs. 8.9%, HR 1.55, 95% CI: 1.08-2.21).

title: Leveraging ChatGPT for improved decision-making in interfacility transfers for plastic surgery emergencies based on United States guidelines
outcome: Under-triage and over-triage of interfacility transfer decisions versus guideline gold standard
effect: Overall 77% alignment (23% misalignment); primer 1 mostly under-referred, primers 2 and 3 mostly over-referred.
quote: This finding is clinically meaningful, as under-triage in emergent settings could delay care, whereas over-triage may unnecessarily burden specialist services.

title: Leveraging ChatGPT for improved decision-making in interfacility transfers for plastic surgery emergencies based on United States guidelines
outcome: robustness to prompt phrasing
effect: Burn scenarios: primer 1 alignment 55% versus primers 2 and 3 85% each; p = 0.041.
quote: For burn scenarios, primer 1 produced the lowest alignment (55%) compared to primers 2 and 3 (85% each, p = 0.041), suggesting context-specific phrasing may better guide AI outputs.

title: Leveraging ChatGPT for improved decision-making in interfacility transfers for plastic surgery emergencies based on United States guidelines
outcome: Effect of prompt phrasing on guideline alignment and error direction of transfer recommendations
effect: Primer 1 and 3 had 77% alignment, primer 2 73% (p=0.24); primer 1 under-referred (93% of misalignments), primers 2 and 3 over-referred (88%, 100%; p<0.001). Burns: primer 1 55% vs 85% (p=0.041).
quote: The nature of the errors varied significantly by primer with primer 1 significantly more likely to under-refer (93% of its misalignments), while primers 2 and 3 tended toward over-referral (88% and 100% of misalignments, respectively; p < 0.001).

title: Gender Disparities in Artificial Intelligence-Generated Images of Hospital Leadership in the United States
outcome: Gender and race/ethnicity representation in AI-generated images of hospital leaders versus real-world US hospital data
effect: DALL-E overrepresented men (86.5%) and White individuals (94.5%); Midjourney 69.5% men, 75.0% White; Imagen 50.3% men, 51.5% White. Significant differences across models and versus real-world data.
quote: Artificial intelligence text-to-image models reflect and amplify systemic biases, overrepresenting men and White leaders, while underrepresenting diversity.

title: Effectiveness of ChatGPT for Clinical Scenario Generation: A Qualitative Study
outcome: Expert-panel review of GPT-4 cardiovascular scenarios for clinical accuracy and guideline adherence
effect: All five experts found the scenarios realistic and guideline-consistent, but they also documented specific errors, incorrect recommendations, missing information, and inconsistencies with standard nursing practice.
quote: All the experts agreed that the scenarios were realistic and followed clinical guidelines.

title: Performance of large language models on family medicine licensing exams
outcome: LLM performance on licensing exam questions, as proxy for clinical competence
effect: Five models exceeded the 65% passing threshold with simple prompts; seven did so with few-shot prompts; o1-preview reached 85.5%. Authors note multiple-choice formats cannot address broader clinical competencies.
quote: Five models exceeded the 65% passing threshold under simple prompts; seven did so with few-shot prompts.

title: Evaluating AI Chatbots for Preoperative and Postoperative Counseling for Mandibular Distraction Osteogenesis
outcome: SMOG readability of chatbot responses on mandibular distraction osteogenesis counseling
effect: Mean SMOG 17.31 (SD 3.59), graduate school reading level; Open Evidence 22.24 vs ChatGPT 15.89, Gemini 15.66, Copilot 15.44 (P<0.001).
quote: Significant differences in readability across all AI models were found (mean=17.31 SD=3.59, P <0.001), indicating the average response was at a graduate school reading level.

title: Evaluating AI Chatbots for Preoperative and Postoperative Counseling for Mandibular Distraction Osteogenesis
outcome: Modified DISCERN scores for citation of sources and additional sources provided
effect: Additional sources provided mean=2.19 (SD 1.52); citation of sources mean=2.93 (SD 1.96), the lowest-scoring items.
quote: Additional sources provided and citation of sources had the lowest means (mean=2.19 SD=1.52; mean=2.93 SD=1.96).

title: External validation of an AI-based preoperative frailty index using real-world data
venue: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
outcome: Association of AI frailty index with postoperative outcomes in an external cohort
effect: Highest frailty quintile had higher odds of 30-day mortality (OR 4.33, 95% CI 3.91-4.80) and 2.53 times longer hospital stays vs lowest level.
quote: The developed preoperative frailty index effectively predicts postoperative outcomes in a large and diverse external cohort.

title: External validation of an AI-based preoperative frailty index using real-world data
venue: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
outcome: Predictive performance of general vs service-specific frailty indices
effect: General frailty index performed comparably to or slightly better than service-specific indices across surgical specialties.
quote: The general frailty index performed comparably to or slightly better than service-specific indices across surgical specialties.

title: Improving Patient Communication by Simplifying AI-Generated Dental Radiology Reports With ChatGPT: Comparative Study
outcome: Readability and patient-rated comprehension of original vs ChatGPT-simplified radiology reports
effect: FRE 51.1 (original) vs 55.0 and 56.4 (simplified), P<.001; ability to understand findings without help: mean 1.5 (SD 0.7) text 3 vs 3.1 (SD 1.4) text 1.
quote: Both simplified report versions (texts 2 and 3) received significantly better ratings across all evaluated aspects, highlighting a preference for more accessible medical documents in the future.

title: Improving Patient Communication by Simplifying AI-Generated Dental Radiology Reports With ChatGPT: Comparative Study
outcome: Readability of patient-facing reports
effect: FRE: text 1=51.1, text 2=55.0, text 3=56.4; P<.001; LIX lower in simplified texts.
quote: Both simplified texts showed significantly higher readability scores (text 1: FRE score=51.1; text 2: FRE score=55.0; and text 3: FRE score=56.4; P<.001) and lower LIX scores, indicating enhanced clarity.

title: Improving Patient Communication by Simplifying AI-Generated Dental Radiology Reports With ChatGPT: Comparative Study
outcome: Patient-rated tone and empathy
effect: Tone F2,297=17.72; P<.001; empathy F2,295=49.57; P<.001; texts 2/3 rated higher than text1.
quote: Patients rated the tone of the radiology reports as significantly more respectful and considerate of their situation in the simplified text versions (texts 2 and 3) compared with the original AI-generated radiology reports.

title: Clinical Decision Support for Septic Shock in the Emergency Department: A Cluster Randomized Trial
outcome: Antibiotic and bolus within 1 hour; hypotensive shock; time-to-antibiotic in stepped-wedge cluster RCT of predictive CDS
effect: Antibiotic and bolus within 1 hour: 39.0% intervention vs 38.9% control (aOR 1.07 [0.61-1.88]); shock aOR 1.12 (0.53-2.46); antibiotic timeliness aHR 0.85 (0.63-1.16). No difference.
quote: Antibiotic and bolus within 1 hour occurred in 39.0% of patients in the intervention arm versus 38.9% of patients in the control arm (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]: 1.07 [0.61-1.88]).
sample_unit: ED encounters meeting inclusion criteria (children with suspected sepsis)

title: Evaluating evidence-based health information from generative AI using a cross-sectional study with laypeople seeking screening information
outcome: Information quality by user education and LLM experience in laypeople's prompting
effect: Higher education (β=0.16, p=0.032) and more LLM experience (β=0.26, p=0.007) gave higher quality; frequent health-information LLM use was negatively associated (β=-0.25, p=0.009).
quote: However, more frequent LLM usage for seeking health information was negatively associated with information quality ( β = −0.25, p = 0.009).

title: Evaluating evidence-based health information from generative AI using a cross-sectional study with laypeople seeking screening information
outcome: Evidence-based response quality after prompting boost
effect: Improved quality: MAPPinfo F(1,294)=15.26, p<0.001, ηp²=0.05; ebmNucleus F(1,294)=12.12, p=0.001, ηp²=0.04.
quote: The boosting intervention for more informed prompting moderately improved the quality of elicited health information across all LLMs (Fig. 2a–c ), as indicated by ANOVA main effects for MAPPinfo ( F (1,294) = 15.26, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 05 ) and ebmNucleus ( F (1,294) = 12.12, p = 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 04 ).

title: Evaluating evidence-based health information from generative AI using a cross-sectional study with laypeople seeking screening information
outcome: Evidence-based score sensitivity to prompt informedness
effect: Scores depended on prompt informedness: MAPPinfo F(2,351)=40.25, p<0.001, ηp²=0.19; ebmNucleus F(2,351)=528.41, p<0.001, ηp²=0.75.
quote: Our systematic variation of prompt informedness revealed the expected pattern across the tested LLMs (Fig. 1a–c ), demonstrating that more informed prompting led to higher scores according to both assessment schemes MAPPinfo ( F (2,351) = 40.25, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 19 ) and ebmNucleus ( F (2,351) = 528.41, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 75 ).

title: Evaluating evidence-based health information from generative AI using a cross-sectional study with laypeople seeking screening information
outcome: evidence-based health communication quality by prompt informedness
effect: More informed prompts yielded higher quality scores across models on MAPPinfo (F=40.25, p<0.001) and ebmNucleus (F=528.41, p<0.001), while low-informed prompts produced poor-quality outputs.
quote: Our systematic variation of prompt informedness revealed the expected pattern across the tested LLMs (Fig. 1a–c ), demonstrating that more informed prompting led to higher scores according to both assessment schemes MAPPinfo ( F (2,351) = 40.25, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 19 ) and ebmNucleus ( F (2,351) = 528.41, p < 0.001, η p 2 = 0 . 75 ).

title: Incorporating end-user perspectives into the development of a machine learning algorithm for first time perinatal depression prediction
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Whether end-user input from patients and providers shaped algorithm development and implementation planning
effect: Focus group and engagement studio findings were incorporated into iterative algorithm development and informed an implementation pilot plan. Participants reported positively about their engagement.
quote: Qualitative findings were incorporated into iterative algorithm development and informed an implementation pilot plan.
sample_unit: participants (12 providers in a focus group; 21 patients in community engagement studios)

title: Incorporating end-user perspectives into the development of a machine learning algorithm for first time perinatal depression prediction
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Stakeholder views on variable completeness, interpretability, and acceptability to inform the use case
effect: Providers and patients agreed on the interpretability of the variables and suggested additional predictors. Patients wanted to discuss results with providers, while providers cited limited bandwidth.
quote: Providers and patients showed consensus on the interpretability of the prediction algorithm's variables and discussed additional variables believed to be predictive of depression to ensure its completeness.
sample_unit: participants (12 providers in a focus group; 21 patients in community engagement studios)

title: How reliable are ChatGPT and Google's answers to frequently asked questions about unicondylar knee arthroplasty from a scientific perspective?
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT versus Google answers (FKGL, SMOG, FRES) for patient comprehension
effect: Google had a higher FRES score, so its content was simpler. ChatGPT's academic language may be hard for some patient groups. Numeric FKGL, SMOG and FRES values are not given in the abstract.
quote: However, the academic language used by ChatGPT may be challenging for some patient groups, whereas Google's superficial information is a significant limitation.

title: Use of natural language processing to identify patients with inflammatory breast cancer across a health-care system
outcome: Positive predictive value of NLP flags with vs without human review
effect: PPV improved from 55.4% (NLP alone) to 78.4% with human-in-the-loop review; T4d-only 57.1% to 90.9%, suspected-only 40.2% to 63.2%.
quote: Adding a human-in-the-loop review improved the overall PPV to 78.4%, with notable gains in patient charts containing T4d (90.9%) and suspected inflammatory breast cancer tags (63.2%).

title: Use of natural language processing to identify patients with inflammatory breast cancer across a health-care system
outcome: Confirmed inflammatory breast cancer cases missed by the NLP-plus-human screening system
effect: Among 255 confirmed cases, the system identified 235 and missed 20, yielding sensitivity of 92.2%; negative predictive value was 33.3%.
quote: Of 255 confirmed paients with inflammatory breast cancer in this cohort, our NLP plus human-in-the-loop system correctly identified 235 cases (true positives), missing 20 cases (false negatives), yielding a sensitivity of 92.2%.

title: Use of natural language processing to identify patients with inflammatory breast cancer across a health-care system
outcome: Case identification vs standard care
effect: Of 255 confirmed inflammatory breast cancer cases, 57 (22.4%) were identified solely by the AI pipeline and would have been missed by traditional surveillance.
quote: Of these confirmed cases, 57 (22.4%) were identified solely through the NLP pipeline and would have been missed through traditional surveillance methods.

title: Use of natural language processing to identify patients with inflammatory breast cancer across a health-care system
outcome: Positive predictive value with human-in-the-loop
effect: Initial NLP screening had a 55.4% positive predictive value, which improved to 78.4% when a human-in-the-loop review was added.
quote: Initial NLP screening achieved 55.4% positive predictive value, improving to 78.4% with human-in-the-loop review.

title: Evaluating Equity in Usage and Effectiveness of the CONCERN Early Warning System
outcome: In-hospital mortality effect of AI early warning by sociodemographic subgroup (sex, race, ethnicity, language)
effect: Overall adjusted HR 0.644 (95% CI 0.532-0.778); consistent across most groups; non-English primary language had greater mortality reduction (adjusted HR 0.419, 95% CI 0.287-0.610, p=0.0082).
quote: The CONCERN EWS was significantly associated with reduced risk of in-hospital mortality overall (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.532-0.778, p < 0.0001), with consistent effectiveness across most groups.

title: Evaluating Equity in Usage and Effectiveness of the CONCERN Early Warning System
outcome: Clinician launches of the CONCERN Detailed Prediction Screen by patient demographics
effect: Clinicians' Detailed Prediction Screen launches did not significantly differ by sex, race, ethnicity, or primary language, suggesting equitable usage.
quote: Clinicians' CONCERN Detailed Prediction Screen launches did not significantly differ by patients' demographic characteristics, suggesting equitable usage.

title: Economic analysis of an AI-enabled ECG alert system: impact on mortality outcomes from a pragmatic randomized trial
outcome: 90-day all-cause mortality and cost-effectiveness of AI-ECG alerts versus usual care in randomized trial
effect: 90-day mortality 3.6% intervention vs 4.3% control; overall cost similar ($6204 vs $5803); ICER $59,500 per death averted (95% CI: $-4657 to $385,950).
quote: Among 15,965 patients, 90-day all-cause mortality was 3.6% in the intervention group versus 4.3% in controls.

title: Evaluating artificial intelligence bias in nephrology: the role of diversity, equity, and inclusion in AI-driven decision-making and ethical regulation
outcome: LLM willingness to make decisions based on potentially discriminatory sociodemographic criteria in simulated nephrology cases
effect: ChatGPT 3.5 answered all scenario questions and never refused; ChatGPT 4.0 declined in 13 (16.3%) scenarios in round one and 5 (6.3%) in round two.
quote: ChatGPT 3.5 provided a response to all scenario questions and did not refuse to make decisions under any circumstances.

title: Continual learning across population cohorts with distribution shift: insights from multi-cohort metabolic syndrome identification
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Model performance with continual learning versus plain sequential training across hospital and non-hospital cohorts
effect: CL outperformed sequential training control; cumulative AUROC 0.85 and AUPRC 0.65 on combined test set
quote: The CL method outperformed the control (sequential training without any strategies) method.

title: Continual learning across population cohorts with distribution shift: insights from multi-cohort metabolic syndrome identification
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Performance degradation from distribution shift between hospital and non-hospital settings
effect: Distribution shift causes catastrophic forgetting; training order hospital to non-hospital gave AUROC 0.85 versus 0.79 for reverse order (7.6% improvement)
quote: Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is susceptible to misdiagnosis by DL models due to distribution shifts.

title: Implementation costs and cost-effectiveness of ultraportable chest X-ray with artificial intelligence in active case finding for tuberculosis in Nigeria
outcome: TB cases detected and implementation costs compared with symptom screening
effect: Abnormality ≥ 0.50 detected 76 cases at US$56589, versus 77 cases at US$48939 for any symptom screening; the AI-only algorithm was strictly dominated.
quote: Abnormality ≥ 0.50 algorithm was strictly dominated as it led to 1 fewer diagnosis but costed more than the any symptom algorithm.

title: Implementation costs and cost-effectiveness of ultraportable chest X-ray with artificial intelligence in active case finding for tuberculosis in Nigeria
outcome: cost per case at varied prevalence
effect: AI screening had a lower cost per case detected than any-symptom screening only when the proportion of asymptomatic TB exceeded 30%.
quote: Our analysis showed that using CXR and AI had lower cost per case detected than any symptom screening criteria when asymptomatic TB was higher than 30% of all bacteriologically-confirmed TB detected.

title: Implementation costs and cost-effectiveness of ultraportable chest X-ray with artificial intelligence in active case finding for tuberculosis in Nigeria
outcome: cost per case detected
effect: AI combined with symptom screening detected more cases at US$773 per case, whereas cough-only screening missed 60% of cases at US$1198 per case.
quote: The combined screening algorithm using both symptoms and CXR-AI detected more bacteriologically-confirmed cases at US$773 per case detected, whereas symptom-only screening criteria missed 60% cases at a much higher US$1198 per case detected cost for cough ≥ 2 weeks criteria and 10% missed cases at cost lower than CXR algorithm of US$636 per case detected.

title: Real-World Diagnostic Performance and Clinical Utility of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Interpretation for Detection of Lung Metastasis on CT in Patients With Colorectal Cancer
outcome: Radiologist acceptance of AI false-positive detections (automation bias)
effect: Stand-alone AI had 381 false-positive detections in 634 patients without metastasis; only one AI false positive was reported as positive by radiologists.
quote: Stand-alone AI correctly detected metastasis in 24 of 29 patients but had 381 false-positive detections in 634 patients without metastasis; only one AI false-positive was reported as positive by interpretating radiologists.

title: Real-World Diagnostic Performance and Clinical Utility of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Interpretation for Detection of Lung Metastasis on CT in Patients With Colorectal Cancer
outcome: Radiologist-with-AI vs conventional reading performance, and stand-alone AI performance
effect: AI-assisted sensitivity 72.4% vs 32.1% conventional (p=.008); accuracy 98.5% vs 96.0%. Stand-alone AI had 381 false positives in 634 patients, but radiologists reported only one, so team performance exceeded stand-alone AI.
quote: The AI-assisted interpretation group compared with the conventional interpretation group showed higher sensitivity (72.4% vs 32.1%, respectively; p = .008), accuracy (98.5% vs 96.0%, p = .005), and frequency of management changes (55.2% vs 25.0%, p = .02), without significant difference in specificity (99.7% vs 98.9%, p = .11), diagnostic yield (3.2% vs 1.4%, p = .30), or false-referral rate (0.3% vs 1.1%, p = .10).

title: Real-World Diagnostic Performance and Clinical Utility of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Interpretation for Detection of Lung Metastasis on CT in Patients With Colorectal Cancer
outcome: Radiologist rejection of false-positive AI detections
effect: Stand-alone AI had 381 false-positive detections in 634 patients without metastasis; only one AI false-positive was reported as positive by radiologists.
quote: Stand-alone AI correctly detected metastasis in 24 of 29 patients but had 381 false-positive detections in 634 patients without metastasis; only one AI false-positive was reported as positive by interpretating radiologists.

title: Evaluating sepsis watch generalizability through multisite external validation of a sepsis machine learning model
outcome: Sepsis Watch discrimination on local historical data at a new community health system
effect: AUROC ranged from 0.906 to 0.960 and AUPRC from 0.177 to 0.252 across four sites; performance described as strong and robust with little variation.
quote: Ultimately, the reproducibility of the Sepsis Watch model in a community health system setting confirmed its strong and robust performance and portability across different geographical and demographic contexts with little variation.

title: Evaluating sepsis watch generalizability through multisite external validation of a sepsis machine learning model
outcome: Site-level variation in model performance across four emergency departments
effect: AUROC 0.906 to 0.960 and AUPRC 0.177 to 0.252 across the four sites, indicating little variation.
quote: The AUROC ranged from 0.906 to 0.960, and the AUPRC ranged from 0.177 to 0.252 across the four sites.

title: Generative AI Is Not Ready for Clinical Use in Patient Education for Lower Back Pain Patients, Even With Retrieval-Augmented Generation
venue: AMIA Joint Summits on Translational Science proceedings. AMIA Joint Summits on Translational Science
outcome: Accuracy, completeness, redundancy, readability of RAG-based versus non-RAG LLM patient education for low back pain
effect: RAG-based LLMs outperformed traditional LLMs, giving more accurate, complete, and readable materials with less redundancy, though still not ready for clinical practice.
