title: Evaluating the readability, quality, and reliability of responses generated by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity on the most commonly asked questions about Ankylosing spondylitis
outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot responses to ankylosing spondylitis queries (GFOG, FRES, SMOG)
effect: Readability levels of chatbot answers were above the 6th grade level, with statistically significant differences between chatbots (p < 0.001).
quote: It was found that the readability levels of the answers produced by AI-based chatbots were above the 6th grade level and showed a statistically significant difference (p < 0.001).

title: Evaluating the readability, quality, and reliability of responses generated by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity on the most commonly asked questions about Ankylosing spondylitis
outcome: Reading level of chatbot patient-facing answers relative to recommended level
effect: Answers exceeded the recommended readability level (above 6th grade) across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity.
quote: It has been found that the answers given by AI chatbots to AS-related questions exceed the recommended readability level and the reliability and quality assessment raises concerns due to some low scores.

title: Impact of AI-Assisted Diagnosis on American Patients' Trust in and Intention to Seek Help From Health Care Professionals: Randomized, Web-Based Survey Experiment
outcome: Patient reactions to AI-use disclosure in doctor profile
effect: Plain disclosure of AI use lowered trust and help-seeking across demographics; trust gap smaller with AI use frequency (β=.09) and larger with self-reported knowledge (β=-.04, P=.08).
quote: Therefore, merely incorporating AI into medical diagnoses without solid trust-building ethics may inadvertently reduce patient’s trust.

title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o and Four Open-Source Large Language Models in Generating Diagnoses Based on China's Rare Disease Catalog: Comparative Study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of qwen2.5:7b with versus without retrieval-augmented generation
effect: RAG raised qwen2.5:7b accuracy to 79.3% (χ²1=31.11, P<.001) with 85.9% retrieval precision.
quote: RAG implementation enhanced qwen2.5:7b's accuracy to 79.3% (χ²1=31.11, P<.001) with 85.9% retrieval precision.

title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o and Four Open-Source Large Language Models in Generating Diagnoses Based on China's Rare Disease Catalog: Comparative Study
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy difference between Chinese and English inputs
effect: Llama3.1:8b 67.8% English vs 31.4% Chinese (P<.001); Llama3.1:70b 90.1% vs 80.2% (P=.02); qwen2.5 models comparable across languages.
quote: Language effects varied across models: qwen2.5:7b showed comparable performance in Chinese (51.2%) and English (47.9%; χ²1=0.32, P=.57), whereas Llama3.1:8b exhibited significantly higher English accuracy (67.8% vs 31.4%; χ²1=40.20, P<.001).

title: Automatic contour quality assurance using deep-learning based contours
outcome: Ability of automated two-contour QA (geometric vs geometric plus dose metrics) to flag dosimetric errors in auto-contours
effect: Adding dose metrics raised ROC-AUC and PR-AUC for Dmean error in H&N small structures. For Dmax error, it improved H&N small, H&N medium and GYN structures.
quote: In many instances, utilizing dose with geometric comparisons can improve the ability of a verification model to flag potential errors from a primary auto-contouring model.

title: Automatic contour quality assurance using deep-learning based contours
outcome: ability of post-processing comparison metrics to flag dosimetric errors
effect: including dose metrics increased ROC-AUC and PR-AUC for H&N small structures for D_error,mean, and for small, medium, and GYN structures for D_error,max
quote: In many instances, utilizing dose with geometric comparisons can improve the ability of a verification model to flag potential errors from a primary auto-contouring model.

title: Empirically derived evaluation requirements for responsible deployments of AI in safety-critical settings
outcome: Nurse performance with vs without AI recommendations, by AI correctness, assessing overreliance in joint human-AI system
effect: With AI recommendations nurses improved when AI was most correct (+52.8% emergency, +67.4% non-emergency) but worsened when AI was most misleading (−120.5% emergency, −96.3% non-emergency) versus no AI.
quote: Compared to nurses working without AI augmentation, nurses working with AI recommendations performed better on both emergency ( + 52.8%, odds ratio = 1.86, 95% CI [1.49, 2.23], z = 6.06, p < 0.001) and non-emergency ( + 67.4%, odds ratio = 1.62, 95% CI [1.35, 1.89], z = 5.59, p < 0.001) cases when the AI algorithm was most correct, but worse on both emergency (−120.5%, odds ratio = 0.414, 95% CI [0.327, 0.501], z = −8.25, p < 0.001) and non-emergency (−96.3%, odds ratio = 0.418, 95% CI [0.333, 0.503], z = −8.41, p < 0.001) cases when the AI algorithm was most erroneous or misleading.
sample_unit: participants (450 nursing students and 12 licensed nurses; 4125 case records analyzed)

title: Empirically derived evaluation requirements for responsible deployments of AI in safety-critical settings
outcome: Joint nurse-AI performance versus AI standalone metrics in the intended interface
effect: Favorable standalone AI benchmarks did not ensure safe joint performance; AI augmentation both improved and degraded nurse performance depending on AI correctness.
quote: Due to these interactions, optimizing the performance of AI algorithms alone does not necessarily optimize the performance of the joint human-AI system 44 , 45 .
sample_unit: participants (450 nursing students and 12 licensed nurses; 4125 case records analyzed)

title: Empirically derived evaluation requirements for responsible deployments of AI in safety-critical settings
outcome: Whether nurses detected incorrect AI recommendations (automation bias/overreliance)
effect: When AI recommendations were most misleading, nurses' concern for emergency patients was indistinguishable from non-emergency patients and vice versa; degradation nearly twice the maximum improvement.
quote: When AI recommendations were most misleading, nurses’ concern was not significantly different from their concern for the opposite category of patients without AI augmentation.
sample_unit: participants (450 nursing students and 12 licensed nurses; 4125 case records analyzed)

title: Empirically derived evaluation requirements for responsible deployments of AI in safety-critical settings
outcome: effect of visual AI explanations
effect: Explanations alone: +23.9% for correct emergency cases; −33.6% for misleading non-emergency cases; not significant in other comparisons.
quote: When only AI explanations were shown, nurses performed better on emergency cases when the AI algorithm was most correct ( + 23.9%, odds ratio = 1.29, 95% CI [1.05, 1.53], z = 2.64, p = 0.008), worse on non-emergency cases when the AI algorithm was most misleading (−33.6%, odds ratio = 0.746, 95% CI [0.599, 0.893], z = −2.91, p = 0.004), and not significantly different on either emergency cases when the AI algorithm was most misleading or non-emergency cases when the AI algorithm was most correct.
sample_unit: participants (450 nursing students and 12 licensed nurses; 4125 case records analyzed)

title: Empirically derived evaluation requirements for responsible deployments of AI in safety-critical settings
outcome: Whether explanation-based interface cues surfaced AI errors and reduced misleading influence
effect: Explanations designed to highlight algorithm errors did not attenuate degraded performance under misleading AI and could themselves degrade performance.
quote: The addition of AI explanations did not attenuate these effects and could themselves degrade performance.
sample_unit: participants (450 nursing students and 12 licensed nurses; 4125 case records analyzed)

title: Empirically derived evaluation requirements for responsible deployments of AI in safety-critical settings
outcome: Whether pre-deployment human-in-the-loop evaluation reveals safety risks of AI tool before clinical use
effect: Simulated evaluation with nurses revealed severe potential risks (degradation from misleading AI) prior to deployment despite favorable benchmark performance.
quote: The study we conducted is an example of one such evaluation which was able to empirically reveal severe potential risks prior to deployment.
sample_unit: participants (450 nursing students and 12 licensed nurses; 4125 case records analyzed)

title: Assessing the power of AI: a comparative evaluation of large language models in generating patient education materials in dentistry
outcome: PEMAT understandability and actionability of LLM-generated dental patient education materials against 70% threshold
effect: ChatGPT-4.0 exceeded the 70% PEMAT understandability threshold in 3 of 4 scenarios; Claude 3.5 Sonnet did so in 2 scenarios and did not consistently meet 70% for actionability.
quote: ChatGPT-4.0 excelled in understandability, surpassing the PEMAT threshold of 70% in three of the four scenarios.
sample_unit: LLM-generated patient education materials (4 models x 4 dental scenarios)

title: Bridging Health Literacy Gaps in Spine Care: Using ChatGPT-4o to Improve Patient-Education Materials
venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
outcome: Readability (FKGL) of spine patient-education materials before vs after ChatGPT-4o revision to sixth-grade level
effect: Original PEMs mean FKGL 10.2 ± 2.6; ChatGPT-4o revisions mean FKGL 6.6 ± 1.3 (p < 0.05); SMOG, language complexity, and passive voice also improved.
quote: ChatGPT-4o generated articles with a significantly reduced mean FKGL of 6.6 ± 1.3 (p < 0.05).

title: Bridging Health Literacy Gaps in Spine Care: Using ChatGPT-4o to Improve Patient-Education Materials
venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
outcome: Readability of patient education materials after AI plain-language rewriting versus originals
effect: Mean FKGL fell from 10.2 ± 2.6 to 6.6 ± 1.3 (p < 0.05) while reportedly maintaining accuracy and adequate detail; test-retest ICC 0.91 to 0.98.
quote: ChatGPT-4o demonstrated the potential to enhance PEM readability while maintaining content quality.

title: Bridging Health Literacy Gaps in Spine Care: Using ChatGPT-4o to Improve Patient-Education Materials
venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
outcome: readability metric test-retest reliability across repeated runs
effect: ICC ranged from 0.91 to 0.98 across all metrics
quote: Excellent test-retest reliability was observed across all of the metrics (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC] range, 0.91 to 0.98).

title: Large Language Model-Assisted Surgical Consent Forms in Non-English Language: Content Analysis and Readability Evaluation
outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified Korean consent forms (KReaD and Natmal scores)
effect: KReaD fell from 1777 (SD 28.47) to 1335.6 (SD 59.95), P<.001; Natmal from 1452.3 (SD 88.67) to 1245.3 (SD 96.96), P=.007. Sentence length and difficult word ratio decreased.
quote: Artificial intelligence-assisted editing significantly improved readability, reducing the KReaD score from 1777 (SD 28.47) to 1335.6 (SD 59.95) (P<.001) and the Natmal score from 1452.3 (SD 88.67) to 1245.3 (SD 96.96) (P=.007).
sample_unit: surgical consent forms (liver resection) from 7 institutions, rated by 7 specialists

title: Large Language Model-Assisted Surgical Consent Forms in Non-English Language: Content Analysis and Readability Evaluation
outcome: Specialist clinician review of LLM-edited consent forms for risk, benefit, alternative content quality
effect: Specialist review detected declines in risk description (β=-0.371; P=.01) and overall impression (β=-0.500; P=.03) after LLM editing; evaluators found no explicit omissions but perceived text as overly simplified.
quote: The linear mixed-effects model confirmed significant reductions in risk descriptions (β₁=-0.371; P=.01) and overall impression (β₁=-0.500; P=.03), suggesting potential omissions in critical safety information.
sample_unit: surgical consent forms (liver resection) from 7 institutions, rated by 7 specialists

title: Consulting the Digital Doctor: Efficacy of ChatGPT-3.5 in Answering Questions Related to Diabetic Foot Ulcer Care
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT-3.5 responses to diabetic foot ulcer questions
effect: ChatGPT-3.5 answered at a mean grade level of 11.9±1.8, nearly 4 grade levels higher than the American average.
quote: ChatGPT-3.5 answered at the mean grade level of 11.9±1.8.

title: Consulting the Digital Doctor: Efficacy of ChatGPT-3.5 in Answering Questions Related to Diabetic Foot Ulcer Care
outcome: Readability of AI patient-facing responses relative to patient comprehension
effect: Mean grade level 11.9±1.8, nearly 4 grade levels above the American average; reviewers nonetheless praised simplicity (n=11/11).
quote: ChatGPT-3.5 answered at the mean grade level of 11.9±1.8.

title: Consulting the Digital Doctor: Efficacy of ChatGPT-3.5 in Answering Questions Related to Diabetic Foot Ulcer Care
outcome: Incorrect or incomplete information in ChatGPT-3.5 responses, as rated by plastic surgeons
effect: Three responses presented incorrect information; 10/11 omitted key information such as DVT symptoms and comorbid conditions affecting limb salvage. Mean accuracy 8.7±0.3, danger 2.2±0.6.
quote: Three responses presented incorrect information, and the majority of responses (n=10/11) left out key information, such as deep vein thrombosis symptoms and comorbid conditions impacting limb salvage.

title: Appropriateness of acute breast symptom recommendations provided by ChatGPT
outcome: Response appropriateness for lay-language versus medical-terminology phrasing of equivalent breast symptom questions
effect: ChatGPT-3.5 responses were appropriate for 7/7 (100%) common acute breast symptom questions when phrased both colloquially and using standard medical terminology.
quote: ChatGPT-3.5 generated responses were appropriate for 7/7 (100 %) questions regarding common acute breast symptoms when phrased both colloquially and using standard medical terminology.

title: Appropriateness of acute breast symptom recommendations provided by ChatGPT
outcome: Adherence of LLM breast symptom advice to ACR guidelines and clinical judgment, rated by breast radiologists
effect: Appropriate for 7/7 (100%) common symptom questions, but only 3/9 (33%) pregnancy-associated breast symptom questions and 3/4 (75%) palpable abnormality management/imaging questions.
quote: In contrast, ChatGPT-3.5 generated responses were appropriate for 3/9 (33 %) questions about pregnancy-associated breast symptoms and 3/4 (75 %) questions about management and imaging recommendations for a palpable breast abnormality.

title: Appropriateness of acute breast symptom recommendations provided by ChatGPT
outcome: Consistency of responses across three repeated submissions of each question
effect: Responses were scored 'unreliable' if inconsistent across three submissions; overall results were appropriate for 100% of common, 33% of pregnancy-related, and 75% of palpable abnormality questions.
quote: Questions were submitted three times to ChatGPT-3.5 and all responses were assessed by five fellowship-trained breast radiologists.

title: Agent-guided AI-powered interpretation and reporting of nerve conduction studies and EMG (INSPIRE)
venue: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
outcome: Accuracy detecting normal versus abnormal EDX tests, multi-agent INSPIRE versus one-shot Base-LLM
effect: INSPIRE accuracy 92.2% vs Base-LLM 62.6% (p < 0.001); INSPIRE also higher AIGERS scores in finding, clinical diagnosis, semantic concordance (p < 0.001).
quote: INSPIRE achieved an accuracy of 92.2 % for detecting normal versus abnormal tests, significantly outperforming the Base-LLM model, which achieved 62.6 % (p < 0.001).

title: Feasibility of Using ChatGPT to Generate Exposure Hierarchies for Treating Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
outcome: Expert-blinded ratings of ChatGPT vs expert clinician OCD exposure hierarchies
effect: Expert hierarchies rated significantly more appropriate, specific, variable, and useful than ChatGPT (ps < .05); safety/ethics not different (p = .24).
quote: However, expert human-generated hierarchies were still rated as significantly more appropriate, specific, variable, and useful, ps < .05, but not more or less safe and ethical than ChatGPT-generated hierarchies, p = .24.

title: Validation of an artificial intelligence-based algorithm for predictive performance and risk stratification of sepsis using real-world data from hospitalised patients: a prospective observational study
outcome: AUROC of AI sepsis prediction versus traditional scoring systems on same prospective cohort
effect: VC-SEPS AUROC 0.880, superior to traditional scoring systems; predicted sepsis on average 68.05 min before operational-definition diagnosis.
quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of VC-SEPS was 0.880, indicating its superiority over traditional scoring systems.

title: Online and ChatGPT-generated patient education materials regarding brain tumor prognosis fail to meet readability standards
venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT and website brain tumor prognosis materials
effect: Zero websites and ChatGPT responses met 6th or 8th grade benchmarks; 93.3% of ChatGPT responses were graduate level; ChatGPT less readable than websites across all metrics (p<0.001).
quote: Among ChatGPT responses, 93.3 % were graduate level.

title: Online and ChatGPT-generated patient education materials regarding brain tumor prognosis fail to meet readability standards
venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
outcome: Reading level of patient materials versus AMA/NIH recommended grade levels
effect: Zero websites and ChatGPT responses met the 6th grade or below (AMA) or 8th grade or below (NIH) benchmarks; 50.4% of websites at 9th-12th grade, 47.9% undergraduate, 1.7% graduate.
quote: Zero websites and ChatGPT responses met the readability benchmarks of 6th grade or below (AMA guideline) or 8th grade or below (NIH guideline).

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma on endoscopic images: a national, multicentre, model development and validation study
outcome: Otolaryngologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in multireader multicase study
effect: Primary care otolaryngologists' accuracy rose 7.9%, from 83.4% (95% CI 80.1-86.7) without AI to 91.2% (88.6-93.9) with AI (p<0.0001); reading time fell from 6.7 s to 5.0 s.
quote: In the multireader, multicase study, the artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategy enhanced otolaryngologists' diagnostic accuracy by 7·9%, increasing from 83·4% (95% CI 80·1-86·7, without AI assistance) to 91·2% (95% CI 88·6-93·9, with AI assistance; p<0·0001) for primary care otolaryngologists.
sample_unit: images read in multireader multicase study by 28 otolaryngologists

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma on endoscopic images: a national, multicentre, model development and validation study
outcome: Model performance on prospectively acquired external multisite validation images versus internal dataset
effect: Internal AUC 0.99 for NPC vs non-malignant; external validation on 1885 prospective images from ten hospitals gave AUC 0.95, sensitivity 91.6%, specificity 86.1%.
quote: In the external validation, the system had an AUC for the detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma of 0·95 (95% CI 0·94-0·96), a sensitivity of 91·6% (95% CI 89·3-93·5), and a specificity of 86·1% (95% CI 84·1-87·9).
sample_unit: images read in multireader multicase study by 28 otolaryngologists

title: Dental services use prediction among adults in Southern Brazil: A gender and racial fairness-oriented machine learning approach
outcome: Model AUC by gender and racial subgroups for dental service use prediction
effect: Consistent performance across gender; disparities across racial groups, with AUC = 0.57 for self-reported mixed (pardos) skin color versus overall AUC 0.77.
quote: Fairness estimations for the best model indicated consistent performance across gender categories. However, disparities were observed among racial groups, AUC = 0.57 for individuals who self-reported mixed ("pardos") skin color.

title: Development of the treatment prediction model in the artificial intelligence in depression - medication enhancement study
outcome: Model bias amplification across demographic subgroups
effect: The model was examined for biases and did not amplify potentially harmful biases; AUC on held-out test set was 0.65.
quote: The model did not amplify potentially harmful biases.
sample_unit: adults with moderate to severe major depression from antidepressant clinical trials

title: An adaptive AI-based virtual reality sports system for adolescents with excess body weight: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: Fat mass change in adolescents randomized to AI VR sports vs control
effect: REVERIE sports reduced fat mass by mean -4.28 kg (95% CI -6.35 to -2.22) relative to control, with no significant difference vs physical sports (-5.06 kg).
quote: REVERIE sports intervention was effective in reducing primary outcome fat mass (mean -4.28 kg (95% confidence interval (CI) -6.35 to -2.22), relative to control), with no significant difference compared with physical sports (mean -5.06 kg (95% CI -7.13 to -2.98), relative to control).

title: Forewarning Artificial Intelligence about Cognitive Biases
venue: Medical decision making : an international journal of the Society for Medical Decision Making
outcome: LLM bias under paired case variations (framing etc.), with and without forewarning
effect: Forewarning reduced cognitive biases by only 6.9% on average; no bias present in controls was eliminated; Occam's razor fallacy increased (77% v. 89%, P = 0.024).
quote: No bias present in the control group was eliminated after a forewarning ( Appendix §4, §5 ).
sample_unit: synthetic physician responses (100 per case version, 10 cases, 2 versions)

title: Subthalamic nucleus or globus pallidus internus deep brain stimulation for the treatment of parkinson's disease: An artificial intelligence approach
venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
outcome: Readability of AI responses on DBS for Parkinson's disease (Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG, Flesch Reading Ease)
effect: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level ranged 14.44 (Gemini) to 18.94 (Copilot); Gunning Fog 17.9 to 22.06; SMOG 16.54 to 19.67; all Flesch Reading Ease scores low, highest 30.91 (Gemini).
quote: The Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level scores ranged from 14.44 (Gemini) to 18.94 (Copilot), Gunning Fog Index scores varied between 17.9 (Gemini) and 22.06 (Copilot), SMOG Index scores ranged from 16.54 (Gemini) to 19.67 (Copilot), and all Flesch Reading Ease scores were low, with Gemini showing the highest score of 30.91.

title: Subthalamic nucleus or globus pallidus internus deep brain stimulation for the treatment of parkinson's disease: An artificial intelligence approach
venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated responses relative to appropriate user reading level
effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade levels of 14.44 to 18.94 and all low Flesch Reading Ease scores (max 30.91), indicating complex readability across all chatbots.
quote: All responses showcased complex readability.

title: Subthalamic nucleus or globus pallidus internus deep brain stimulation for the treatment of parkinson's disease: An artificial intelligence approach
venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
outcome: Concordance of LLM answers with CNS guideline recommendations on STN/GPi DBS

quote: ChatGPT 4o showcased 42.9% concordance, with non-concordant responses classified as 14.3% insufficient and 42.8% over-conclusive.

title: Clinical feasibility of AI Doctors: Evaluating the replacement potential of large language models in outpatient settings for central nervous system tumors
outcome: LLM accuracy versus neurosurgeons on differential diagnosis, main diagnosis, and treatment advice

quote: For treatment recommendations, all models showed reduced accuracy (ChatGPT-4o: 80.5 %; DeepSeek-R1: 79 %; Doubao: 71.3 %), significantly lower than doctors (Whether in Chinese or English: P < 0.05).

title: AI-based large-scale screening of gastric cancer from noncontrast CT imaging
outcome: AUC on internal validation versus independent multicenter external cohort
effect: Internal validation AUC 0.970 (1,298 cases); external cohort from 16 centers AUC 0.927 (18,160 cases), a modest drop but still strong performance.

title: Radiology Synthetic Confusion: How Generative Artificial Intelligence Amplifies Misunderstandings of Radiologists and Technologists in Patient-Facing Media

title: Diagnostic Performance of ChatGPT-4o in Detecting Hip Fractures on Pelvic X-rays
outcome: Missed hip fractures (false negatives) by ChatGPT-4o on pelvic X-rays, especially non-displaced fractures

quote: Among 22 false-negative cases, 68.2% were non-displaced fractures, suggesting the model had greater difficulty identifying subtle radiographic findings.

title: A Comparative Analysis of the Accuracy and Readability of Popular Artificial Intelligence-Chat Bots for Inguinal Hernia Management
outcome: Readability of LLM responses to inguinal hernia questions versus patient reading level
effect: Readability scores comparable across models; all responses at college to college-graduate reading levels, which may limit patient accessibility.
quote: Readability scores were comparable across models, with all responses at college to college-graduate reading levels.

title: A Comparative Analysis of the Accuracy and Readability of Popular Artificial Intelligence-Chat Bots for Inguinal Hernia Management
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient information on hernia repair
effect: All responses from the three chatbots were at college to college-graduate reading level, potentially limiting patient accessibility.
quote: However, the consistently high reading level of responses may limit accessibility for patients.

effect: Baseline ≤sixth FKGL was 5.8% English and 10.0% Spanish. After ChatGPT-4.0/Gemini, English 21.4%/60.2%; Spanish 52.5%/77.5% achieved ≤sixth FKGL.
quote: 21.4% and 60.2% of ChatGPT-4.0-converted and Google Gemini-converted English PEMs achieved ≤sixth FKGL, respectively.

title: Currently Available Large Language Models Are Moderately Effective in Improving Readability of English and Spanish Patient Education Materials in Pediatric Orthopaedics

title: Using a Multilingual AI Care Agent to Reduce Disparities in Colorectal Cancer Screening for Higher Fecal Immunochemical Test Adoption Among Spanish-Speaking Patients: Retrospective Analysis
outcome: AI outreach engagement (FIT opt-in, connect rate, call duration) stratified by patient language

title: The role of generative artificial intelligence in deciding fusion treatment of lumbar degeneration: a comparative analysis and narrative review
venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
outcome: Readability of LLM responses (Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, SMOG, Flesch Reading Ease)

title: Efficacy of an Automated Pulmonary Embolism (PE) Detection Algorithm on Routine Contrast-Enhanced Chest CT Imaging for Non-PE Studies
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

effect: Without CAD, ADR fell from 31.6% to 13.5% (p<0.001) and PDR from 39.8% to 18.2% (p<0.001) after CAD introduction, suggesting reliance on CAD and lapses in independent detection.
quote: ADR (31.6% vs. 13.5%, p < 0.001) and PDR (39.8% vs. 18.2%, p < 0.001) were significantly lower in the post-intervention non-CAD group than in the pre-intervention non-CAD group.

title: Integrated Care Coordination for Managing Chronic Conditions: Views of Health Staff on the Implementation of a Program Using an Algorithm to Identify People at Higher Risk of Hospitalisation in Sydney, Australia
venue: Global advances in integrative medicine and health
outcome: Staff views on whether the risk algorithm identified all suitable patients for care coordination
effect: Algorithm identified previously hospitalised patients but missed suitable community patients at increasing risk; clinician referrals were an important additional selection mechanism.
quote: While the algorithm effectively identified previously hospitalised patients, it did not identify all suitable patients in the community with an increasing risk of requiring acute health care intervention.

quote: The population-based recalibration method largely corrected the initial risk underestimation, yielding observed-to-expected (O:E) ratios of 1.080, 1.115, and 1.153 for recalibrated DeepSurv, age-specific DeepSurv, and DeepHit, achieving comparable calibration to individual-based recalibration method (O:E ratios: 1.040, 1.054 for DeepSurv and age-specific DeepSurv).

outcome: Calibration of UK-trained models when applied to a Chinese population

title: A population-based recalibration method for updating survival neural networks models for cardiovascular risk prediction in United Kingdom and China

title: A population-based recalibration method for updating survival neural networks models for cardiovascular risk prediction in United Kingdom and China

title: Using a Large Language Model for Postdeployment Monitoring of FDA-Approved Artificial Intelligence: Pulmonary Embolism Detection Use Case
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Whether LLM-based report classification compared against deployed AI outputs detects discrepancies and drift
effect: Of 11,999 studies, 373 (3.1%) had discrepant classifications between CVPED and LLM; a 2.5% drop in LLM specificity led to a 1.7-fold increase in discrepancies, detected in 22 days.
quote: A PDM framework combining LLM-based free-text classification with a human-in-the-loop alerting system can continuously track an image-based AI's performance, alert for performance drift, and provide incremental clinical value.

title: Using a Large Language Model for Postdeployment Monitoring of FDA-Approved Artificial Intelligence: Pulmonary Embolism Detection Use Case
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Ability of simulated daily monitoring framework to detect performance drift in deployed AI
effect: A 2% to 3% decline in model specificity caused a 2- to 3-fold increase in discrepancies; a 10% drop in sensitivity was required for a similar effect.
quote: A 2% to 3% decline in model specificity caused a 2- to 3-fold increase in discrepancies, and a 10% drop in sensitivity was required to produce a similar effect.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled ECGs for Atrial Fibrillation Identification and Enhanced Oral Anticoagulant Adoption: A Pragmatic Randomized Clinical Trial

title: Readability of AI-Generated Patient Information Leaflets on Alzheimer's, Vascular Dementia, and Delirium
outcome: Readability of LLM-generated patient leaflets across five readability metrics
effect: ChatGPT most readable; DeepSeek markedly more complex and less accessible; Gemini intermediate. Flesch Reading Ease differed significantly between models (H = 7.20, p = 0.027); other metrics approached significance.
quote: DeepSeek generated text that was markedly more complex and less accessible.
sample_unit: patient information leaflets (3 models x 3 topics)

title: Readability of AI-Generated Patient Information Leaflets on Alzheimer's, Vascular Dementia, and Delirium
outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated patient leaflets by model
effect: ChatGPT had the lowest grade-level indices and highest Flesch Reading Ease; DeepSeek was more complex; Gemini intermediate. Flesch Reading Ease differed significantly (H = 7.20, p = 0.027).
quote: ChatGPT consistently produced the most readable content, with the highest Flesch Reading Ease scores and the lowest grade-level indices.
sample_unit: patient information leaflets (3 models x 3 topics)

title: Impact of a computed tomography-based artificial intelligence software on radiologists' workflow for detecting acute intracranial hemorrhage
outcome: Reading order and early diagnosis rate of AIH cases before vs after AI prioritization
effect: Early diagnosis rate rose from 0.49 to 0.76 (P=0.013); median reading order of AIH cases fell from 7.25 to 1.5 (P<0.001); Kendall's Tau fell from 0.61 to 0.01.
quote: Additionally, the early diagnosis rate significantly increased [from 0.49 (0.34-0.63) to 0.76 (0.60-0.93), P = 0.013], and the daily median reading order of AIH cases significantly decreased [from 7.25 (Q1-Q3: 3-10.75) to 1.5 (1-3), P < 0.001] after the implementation.

title: Impact of a computed tomography-based artificial intelligence software on radiologists' workflow for detecting acute intracranial hemorrhage
outcome: Radiologist diagnostic performance with vs without AI assistance
effect: No significant differences in accuracy (0.99 to 0.99, P=0.343), sensitivity (1.00 to 1.00, P=0.859), or specificity (1.00 to 0.99, P=0.252) after AI implementation.
quote: There were no significant differences in accuracy [from 0.99 (95% confidence interval: 0.99-1.00) to 0.99 (0.98-1.00), P = 0.343], sensitivity [from 1.00 (0.99-1.00) to 1.00 (0.99-1.00), P = 0.859], or specificity [from 1.00 (0.99-1.00) to 0.99 (0.97-1.00), P = 0.252] following the implementation of the AI software.

title: Evaluating a Large Language Model in Translating Patient Instructions to Spanish Using a Standardized Framework
outcome: Translation quality (MQM score) of GPT-4o versus professional human translators on the same instructions
effect: Mean difference 1.6 MQM points (90% CI, 0.7-2.5), within equivalence margin of ±5; LLM had fewer mistranslation errors; 52% (SE 6%) of ratings preferred the LLM.
quote: Equivalence testing showed no significant difference in translation quality between GPT-4o and human translations, with a mean difference of 1.6 points (90% CI, 0.7-2.5), falling within a predefined equivalence margin of plus or minus 5 MQM points.
sample_unit: source files of pediatric patient instructions

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Google Gemini 2.0 Flash as Patient Education Resources for Upper Blepharoplasty Patients
outcome: Readability (Coleman-Liau and SMOG indices) of LLM patient education responses on upper blepharoplasty
effect: Claude 3.5 Sonnet was most complex (Coleman-Liau 17.34; SMOG 23.82); Gemini 2.0 Flash was most comprehensible (Coleman-Liau 13.27; SMOG 15.04), all well above typical patient reading levels.
quote: Claude 3.5 Sonnet generated the most complex responses (Coleman-Liau index: 17.34; SMOG index: 23.82 points), whereas Google Gemini 2.0 Flash produced the most comprehensible texts (Coleman-Liau index: 13.27; SMOG index: 15.04 points).

title: The potential utility of CHATGPT4.0 as an AI assistant in the education and management of patients with Barrett's esophagus
venue: Diseases of the esophagus : official journal of the International Society for Diseases of the Esophagus
outcome: Gastroenterologist-rated accuracy of ChatGPT responses on Barrett's esophagus questions
effect: Mean accuracy 4.01 out of 5; 79.3% of responses completely accurate or mostly accurate with minor errors, implying about one fifth had greater inaccuracies.
quote: Gastroenterologists rated ChatGPT responses as mostly accurate overall (4.01 out of 5) with 79.3% of responses completely accurate or mostly accurate with minor errors.

title: External validation of an artificial intelligence tool for fracture detection in children with osteogenesis imperfecta: a multireader study
outcome: Radiologist per-examination accuracy without versus with AI assistance
effect: Radiologist accuracy rose from 83.4% [95% CI 75.2, 89.8] unaided to 90.7% [83.5, 95.4] with AI, despite AI alone at 74.8%.
quote: Radiologists using AI assistance improved average radiologist accuracy per examination to 90.7% [95% CI: 83.5%, 95.4%].

title: External validation of an artificial intelligence tool for fracture detection in children with osteogenesis imperfecta: a multireader study
outcome: AI standalone accuracy compared with radiologists on the same images
effect: AI per-examination accuracy 74.8% vs average radiologist 83.4%; AI missed 80 fractures vs 41 for radiologists.
quote: AI produced a per-examination accuracy of 74.8% [95% CI: 65.4%, 82.7%], compared to average radiologist performance at 83.4% [95% CI: 75.2%, 89.8%].

title: External validation of an artificial intelligence tool for fracture detection in children with osteogenesis imperfecta: a multireader study
outcome: AI accuracy on a local/specific population versus radiologists
effect: AI standalone accuracy 74.8% in children with OI, below radiologists at 83.4%, with more false negatives (80 vs 41 missed fractures).
quote: AI gave more false negatives than radiologists, with 80 missed fractures versus 41, respectively.

title: GPT-4 as a Board-Certified Surgeon: A Pilot Study
outcome: GPT-4 exam-style MCQ score versus performance on oral board clinical scenarios
effect: MCQs: 197/250 (78.8%) correct, 92% probability of passing ABS QE; oral boards: critical failures in 3 of 4 (75%) cases, mainly incorrect timing of intervention and incorrect operation.
quote: While GPT-4's high performance on MCQs mirrored prior studies, the model struggled to generate accurate long-form content in our mock oral board examination.

title: Through a Glass Darkly: Perceptions of Ethnoracial Identity in Artificial Intelligence Generated Medical Vignettes and Images
outcome: Ethnoracial stereotyping in ChatGPT-generated vignettes and Bing images for genetic conditions
effect: Initial-prompt ChatGPT vignettes gave 100% conformity to the traditionally associated group for all five conditions; Bing images most often depicted Caucasian patients (47.4%). Self-prompting reduced conformity but gave inaccurate proportions.
quote: As seen in the results of this study, each of the five disorders had a 100% conformation with the single most commonly known ethnoracial identity: 100% African American for sickle cell, 100% Caucasian for cystic fibrosis, 100% Ashkenazi Jewish for Tay-Sachs disease, 100% Mediterranean for beta-thalassemia, and 100% East Asian for ALDH2 deficiency.
sample_unit: generated vignettes and images (10 ChatGPT regenerations per prompt per condition; MBIC image tiles)

title: Through a Glass Darkly: Perceptions of Ethnoracial Identity in Artificial Intelligence Generated Medical Vignettes and Images
outcome: Output variability across repeated runs, prompt changes, and time (March vs May 2024)
effect: Change in historically associated group share over time was significant (t(9)=2.63, p=0.027); between initial and self-prompts also significant (t(9)=2.80, p=0.021).
quote: Change over months, between March and May, was statistically significant ( t (9) = 2.63, p = 0.027) (Table 1 ).
sample_unit: generated vignettes and images (10 ChatGPT regenerations per prompt per condition; MBIC image tiles)

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT's performance in providing treatment recommendations for pediatric diseases
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT pediatric treatment recommendations by disease type, question type, and error category
effect: Overall accuracy 82.2% (95% CI 81.0%-83.4%); common diseases 84.4%; prone to errors in disease definitions, medications, and surgical treatment.
quote: However, it was prone to errors in disease definitions, medications, and surgical treatment.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT's performance in providing treatment recommendations for pediatric diseases
outcome: ChatGPT accuracy by response language (English vs Chinese)
effect: Accuracy was 93.0% (95% CI: 91.9%-94.1%) in English, notably higher than the 82.2% overall, implying substantially lower accuracy in Chinese.
quote: ChatGPT achieved an overall accuracy of 82.2% (95% CI: 81.0%-83.4%), with superior performance in addressing common diseases (84.4%, 95% CI: 83.2%-85.7%), offering general treatment advice (83.5%, 95% CI: 81.9%-85.1%), and responding in English (93.0%, 95% CI: 91.9%-94.1%).

title: Real-world performance evaluation of commercial autocontouring software for head and neck cancer radiotherapy
outcome: Differences between AI-generated contours and clinician-reviewed final contours, geometric and dosimetric
effect: Dosimetric comparison of AI-contours versus final reviewed contours showed clinically significant dose differences for larynx and elective nodal volumes, so clinician review altered contours; authors conclude final clinician review remains essential.
quote: Dosimetric evaluation demonstrated clinically significant dose differences for larynx and elective nodal volumes.

title: Real-world performance evaluation of commercial autocontouring software for head and neck cancer radiotherapy
outcome: Retrospective local comparison of AI contours to clinically used contours (VDSC, blinded preference)
effect: Median VDSC varied widely by structure (0.23-0.88); blinded preference was 31.4% clinician, 32.9% AI, 35.7% no difference, revealing local protocol differences.
quote: Retrospective median VDSC varied widely for different structures (0.23-0.88).

title: Toward Cross-Hospital Deployment of Natural Language Processing Systems: Model Development and Validation of Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for Disease Name Recognition in Japanese
outcome: F1 performance gap from in-domain case reports to out-of-domain progress notes
effect: Performance dropped out-of-domain for both models; LLM F1 gap ID-OOD = -8.6, MLM baseline gap = -13.9.
quote: The LLM demonstrated greater robustness, with a smaller performance gap in F1-scores (ID-OOD = -8.6) compared to the MLM baseline performance (ID-OOD = -13.9).
sample_unit: clinical documents (case reports and physician-written progress notes)

title: Improving the Readability of Institutional Heart Failure-Related Patient Education Materials Using GPT-4: Observational Study
outcome: Reading grade level of institutional heart failure patient education materials versus recommended level
effect: Median FKGL of institutional PEMs was 10.3 (IQR 7.9-13.1); only 13 (9.1%) of 143 were below sixth-grade level.
quote: For 143 institutional heart failure-related PEMs analyzed, the median FKGL was 10.3 (IQR 7.9-13.1; high school sophomore) compared to 7.3 (IQR 6.1-8.5; seventh grade) for GPT-4's revised PEMs (P<.001).

title: Improving the Readability of Institutional Heart Failure-Related Patient Education Materials Using GPT-4: Observational Study
outcome: Readability and accuracy of GPT-4 plain-language rewrites of patient education materials
effect: Median FKGL fell from 10.3 to 7.3 (P<.001); PEMs below sixth-grade level rose from 9.1% to 23.1%; none graded less accurate or less comprehensive.
quote: No revised GPT-4 PEMs were graded as less accurate or less comprehensive compared to institutional PEMs.

title: Comparison of Responses from ChatGPT-4, Google Gemini, and Google Search to Common Patient Questions About Ankle Sprains: A Readability Analysis
venue: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
outcome: Readability of chatbot answers to patient ankle sprain questions (Flesch-Kincaid grade level and reading ease)
effect: ChatGPT-4 answers were harder to read than Google Search answers: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level difference 3.2 ± 1.7 (P = 0.0012) and Reading Ease difference 22.2 ± 9.3 (P < 0.0001).
quote: ChatGPT-4's answers were more difficult to read based on the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (3.2 ± 1.7, P = 0.0012) and Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease Score (22.2 ± 9.3, P < 0.0001).

title: Evaluating accountability, transparency, and bias in AI-assisted healthcare decision- making: a qualitative study of healthcare professionals' perspectives in the UK
outcome: Clinician perceptions of accountability and liability for AI-assisted decisions
effect: Clinicians felt ultimately liable for patient outcomes yet relied on AI-generated insights, raising questions about liability if systems malfunctioned.
quote: Nevertheless, accountability surfaced as a pervasive concern: while clinicians felt ultimately liable for patient outcomes, they also relied on AI-generated insights, prompting questions about liability if systems malfunctioned.

title: Evaluating accountability, transparency, and bias in AI-assisted healthcare decision- making: a qualitative study of healthcare professionals' perspectives in the UK
outcome: Clinician trust in opaque black-box AI models lacking interpretability
effect: Clinicians emphasized difficulty trusting black box models lacking clear rationale or interpretability, particularly for rare or complex cases.
quote: Transparency emerged as another major theme, with clinicians emphasizing the difficulty of trusting “black box” models that lack clear rationale or interpretability—particularly for rare or complex cases.

title: Evaluating accountability, transparency, and bias in AI-assisted healthcare decision- making: a qualitative study of healthcare professionals' perspectives in the UK
outcome: Reported AI underperformance in minority patient groups or atypical presentations
effect: Bias was repeatedly cited, especially when algorithms underperformed in minority patient groups or in identifying atypical presentations (qualitative reports, no quantified metrics).
quote: Bias was repeatedly cited, especially when algorithms underperformed in minority patient groups or in identifying atypical presentations.

title: Applying Large Language Models for Surgical Case Length Prediction
outcome: LLM case length prediction error and accuracy versus current OR scheduling estimates on the same cases
effect: Fine-tuned GPT-4 MAE 47.64 min vs current scheduling 49.34 min (P = .10, matching); accuracy within 20% was 46.12% vs 40.92% (P < .001).
quote: Both GPT-4 fine-tuned and GPT-3.5 fine-tuned significantly outperformed current scheduling methods in accuracy (46.12% and 46.08% vs 40.92%, respectively; P < .001).
sample_unit: surgical cases (evaluation set; plus 500 external validation cases)

title: Applying Large Language Models for Surgical Case Length Prediction
outcome: Prediction error of fine-tuned versus non-fine-tuned LLMs using institutional case data
effect: Fine-tuned GPT-4 MAE 47.64 min vs best base model (GPT-4) MAE 59.20 min; fine-tuned GPT-4 also performed best in external validation (MAE 48.66 min).
quote: Base models demonstrated variable performance, with GPT-4 showing the highest performance among non-fine-tuned models (MAE, 59.20 minutes; 95% CI, 56.88 - 61.52).
sample_unit: surgical cases (evaluation set; plus 500 external validation cases)

title: External Validation of Mortality Prediction Models in Japanese Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Registry
venue: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery
outcome: Calibration of short-term mortality models before and after local intercept recalibration

quote: Among short-term MPMs, NHR (AU-ROC: 0.82) and STS-PRoM (0.78) showed the highest discrimination, though all models overestimated mortality risk, which improved after intercept recalibration.

title: External Validation of Mortality Prediction Models in Japanese Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Registry
venue: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery

effect: All five short-term models overestimated mortality risk in Japanese patients (30-day mortality 1.4%); long-term AU-ROC up to 0.75.
quote: Among short-term MPMs, NHR (AU-ROC: 0.82) and STS-PRoM (0.78) showed the highest discrimination, though all models overestimated mortality risk, which improved after intercept recalibration.

title: External Validation of Mortality Prediction Models in Japanese Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Registry
venue: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery
outcome: External validation of short-term mortality models
effect: All short-term MPMs overestimated mortality risk; NHR AU-ROC: 0.82 and STS-PRoM 0.78 had highest discrimination.
quote: Among short-term MPMs, NHR (AU-ROC: 0.82) and STS-PRoM (0.78) showed the highest discrimination, though all models overestimated mortality risk, which improved after intercept recalibration.

title: External Validation of Mortality Prediction Models in Japanese Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Registry
venue: European journal of cardio-thoracic surgery : official journal of the European Association for Cardio-thoracic Surgery

title: Language Models for Multilabel Document Classification of Surgical Concepts in Exploratory Laparotomy Operative Notes: Algorithm Development Study
outcome: Multilabel classification F1 of Llama 3.3 versus BoW, tf-idf, Clinical-Longformer on same notes
effect: Llama 3.3 micro F1 0.88 (HL 0.11) vs BoW 0.68, Clinical-Longformer 0.73, tf-idf 0.57 on the same 388 notes.
quote: Off-the-shelf autoregressive LLMs outperformed fined-tuned, encoder-only transformers and traditional natural language processing techniques in classifying operative notes.

title: Evaluation of the accuracy and safety of machine translation of patient-specific discharge instructions: a comparative analysis
outcome: Translation accuracy of ED discharge instructions by target language (Spanish, Chinese, Russian)
effect: Sentence-level accuracy: GPT 97%, 95%, 89% and Google Translate 96%, 90%, 80% for Spanish, Chinese, Russian; instruction sets with at least one inaccuracy: GPT 16%, 24%, 56%; Google 24%, 56%, 66%.
quote: At the instruction set level, 16%, 24% and 56% of Spanish, Chinese and Russian GPT-translated instruction sets contained at least one inaccuracy.

title: Challenges and Strategies for Deep Learning in Cardiovascular Imaging: Ejection Fraction and Heart Failure Management
outcome: Performance degradation of DL LVEF model on external versus internal data
effect: Performance degradation was observed compared with internal data when testing the model on external data; incorporating imaging domain knowledge helped recover performance and improve generalizability.
quote: For the generalization challenge, a performance degradation was observed compared with internal data when testing the model on external data.

title: Challenges and Strategies for Deep Learning in Cardiovascular Imaging: Ejection Fraction and Heart Failure Management
outcome: Reliability of AUC as evaluation metric for dichotomized heart failure diagnosis
effect: AUC varied from 0.71 to 0.98 owing solely to changes in population characteristics, showing significant unreliability of the AUC.
quote: Specifically, AUC varied from 0.71 to 0.98 owing solely to changes in population characteristics.

title: Population-scale cross-sectional observational study for AI-powered TB screening on one million CXRs
outcome: AI performance disparities across age, sex, HIV status, and region of origin
effect: Insignificant performance disparities across age, sex, HIV status, and region of origin; sputum tests for suspected TB strongly correlated with model predictions.
quote: Subgroup analysis revealed insignificant performance disparities across age, sex, HIV status, and region of origin, with sputum tests for suspected TB showing a strong correlation with model predictions.

title: Population-scale cross-sectional observational study for AI-powered TB screening on one million CXRs
outcome: Missed findings in CXRs the AI labeled as without findings (false negative rate)
effect: Overall FNR 1.57% versus radiologists 1.85%, with 0% TB-FNR; AUC 98.51%. Some non-TB findings are still missed.
quote: AIRIS-TB was evaluated on over one million CXRs, achieving an AUC of 98.51% and overall false negative rate (FNR) of 1.57%, outperforming radiologists (1.85%) while maintaining a 0% TB-FNR.

title: Real-world deployment of a fine-tuned pathology foundation model for lung cancer biomarker detection
outcome: Prospective silent-trial performance of EGFR biomarker on live primary samples (AUC)
effect: Prospective silent trial on primary samples achieved AUC of 0.890, consistent with retrospective internal 0.847 and external 0.870 performance.
quote: To evaluate real-world clinical translation, we conducted a prospective silent trial of the biomarker on primary samples, achieving an area under the curve of 0.890.
country: International (US, Europe, Asia; prospective trial at a single US cancer center)

title: Real-world deployment of a fine-tuned pathology foundation model for lung cancer biomarker detection
outcome: Performance on internal versus external out-of-center validation data (AUC)
effect: Mean AUC internal 0.847, external 0.870, showing out-of-center generalization with clinical-grade accuracy on primary and metastatic specimens.
quote: Our model fine-tunes an open-source foundation model, improving task-specific performance with out-of-center generalization and clinical-grade accuracy on primary and metastatic specimens (mean area under the curve: internal 0.847, external 0.870).
country: International (US, Europe, Asia; prospective trial at a single US cancer center)

title: Evaluation and comparison of large language models' responses to questions related optic neuritis
outcome: Readability of LLM chatbot responses to optic neuritis questions on four readability scales

quote: Note that all responses require at least a university-level reading proficiency.

outcome: Agreement between baseline and second-month ChatGPT-4o responses on complex EGM interpretation scenarios
effect: Accuracy was 30% (Scenario C) and 25% (Scenario D); baseline vs second-month agreement was fair (κ = 0.285 and 0.3), showing limited consistency.
quote: In Scenarios C (30%) and D (25%), accuracy was lower, and agreement between baseline and second-month responses remained fair (κ = 0.285 and 0.3, respectively), indicating limited consistency in complex decision-making tasks.

title: Leveraging AI to Drive Timely Improvements in Patient Experience Feedback: Algorithm Validation
outcome: Theme and sentiment accuracy before vs after local recoding/retraining with trust-specific coded data
effect: Theme accuracy rose after recoding: Trust A 57% to 76%, B 69% to 78%, C 84% to 90%, D 67% to 82%, GP/community 64% to 77%; sentiment also improved (e.g., A 76% to 82%).
quote: The accuracy for the theme improved in all the organizations demonstrating that while the algorithm may not initially be transferable, with some retraining and adaptations, it can easily be reused in different service settings.
sample_unit: NHS trusts (500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust for accuracy)

title: Leveraging AI to Drive Timely Improvements in Patient Experience Feedback: Algorithm Validation
outcome: Local performance against manually coded reference standard with a 75% acceptance threshold
effect: Accuracy was calculated on a 500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust against a 75% threshold; initial accuracy fell below threshold in some trusts and recoding brought all to at or above 75%.
quote: The acceptable threshold for overall accuracy for theme and sentiment for a supervised algorithm using patient feedback was determined at 75%.
sample_unit: NHS trusts (500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust for accuracy)

title: Leveraging AI to Drive Timely Improvements in Patient Experience Feedback: Algorithm Validation
outcome: Algorithm accuracy variation across care settings/sites
effect: Initial accuracy was notably lower in pediatrics and mental health/community trusts (theme accuracy 57% to 67% before recoding) than in adult inpatient settings; final accuracy was 75% or higher after recoding.
quote: However, the accuracy of the model was lower in organizations delivering different services, such as pediatrics and mental health.
sample_unit: NHS trusts (500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust for accuracy)

title: Leveraging AI to Drive Timely Improvements in Patient Experience Feedback: Algorithm Validation
outcome: Deployment script integration errors
effect: Common errors were “FileNotFoundError” from incorrect .pkl paths and “invalid column name” from SQL input-column mismatch before final deployment.
quote: The 2 most common errors encountered were “FileNotFoundError” which was a result of not specifying the correct path to a .pkl file, and “invalid column name,” as the code had not been adapted appropriately with the column names from the input table on the SQL server.
sample_unit: NHS trusts (500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust for accuracy)

title: Leveraging AI to Drive Timely Improvements in Patient Experience Feedback: Algorithm Validation
outcome: Transferability to different service settings
effect: Initial theme accuracy was 57% in community/mental health, 67% in pediatrics, and 64% in GP/community, below the 75% threshold.
quote: However, the accuracy of the model was lower in organizations delivering different services, such as pediatrics and mental health.
sample_unit: NHS trusts (500-comment stratified manually coded sample per trust for accuracy)

quote: GPT-3.5-Turbo showed the best overall readability, outperforming GPT-4 in two metrics.

title: Performance of open-source and proprietary large language models in generating patient-friendly radiology chest CT reports
outcome: Emotional sensitivity of LLM-generated patient-friendly reports rated by radiologists

quote: Claude-3-Opus and GPT-4 outperformed Llama-3-70b in emotional sensitivity (90.0 % vs 46.0 %, p < 0.001).

title: Evaluation of performance of generative large language models for stroke care

title: Evaluation of performance of generative large language models for stroke care

title: Evaluation of performance of generative large language models for stroke care

title: Evaluation of performance of generative large language models for stroke care

effect: Hallucination scores ranged from 27.82 to 35.87 across models and stages (scores below 60 indicating frequent hallucinations), demonstrating high rates of non-factual outputs.

title: [Preliminary exploration of the applications of five large language models in the field of oral auxiliary diagnosis, treatment and health consultation]
venue: Zhonghua kou qiang yi xue za zhi = Zhonghua kouqiang yixue zazhi = Chinese journal of stomatology

title: Optimizing Thyroid Nodule Management With Artificial Intelligence: Multicenter Retrospective Study on Reducing Unnecessary Fine Needle Aspirations
outcome: Malignant nodules misclassified as benign by AI (false-negative results)

quote: However, 123 malignant nodules (8.6% of malignant cases) were mistakenly identified as benign, with the majority of these being of low or intermediate suspicion.

title: Optimizing Thyroid Nodule Management With Artificial Intelligence: Multicenter Retrospective Study on Reducing Unnecessary Fine Needle Aspirations
outcome: AI benign-nodule identification compared with junior and senior radiologists on same cohort
effect: AI identified 81.4% (96/118) of benign nodules vs 40% (junior) and 55% (senior) radiologists; AUC 0.88 vs 0.43 (P=.002) and 0.63 (P=.003).

outcome: Zero-shot LLM accuracy on diagnosis, ICD-9 coding, and readmission risk using discharge summaries

title: The need for guardrails with large language models in pharmacovigilance and other medical safety critical settings
outcome: Whether token-level entropy uncertainty signals correlate with human-rated errors
effect: Significant differences found (e.g., clinical accuracy adj. p=0.0031), but higher entropy correlated with more accurate outputs, a counterintuitive direction; described as a 'useful, if subtle, signal'.
quote: More clinically accurate, less incorrect drugs/AEs trended towards a higher uncertainty score, implying that entropy correlates negatively with the model’s human evaluated performance.

title: The need for guardrails with large language models in pharmacovigilance and other medical safety critical settings
outcome: Document-level uncertainty detecting non-ICSR/anomalous documents before LLM processing

quote: Although not completely separated, the separation of the validation and extraneous samples corresponds to an AUROC in the validation data of 0.80.
sample_unit: Japanese individual case safety reports (ICSRs) translated to English and reviewed by experts

title: The need for guardrails with large language models in pharmacovigilance and other medical safety critical settings
outcome: Automated MISMATCH check on outputs catching drug hallucinations without human review
effect: MISMATCH hard guardrail flagged all hallucinated drug names in 20 cases; other drug error categories were not universally caught due to dictionary limits and misspellings.
quote: Our findings reveal that strategic guardrail applications effectively mitigate the risk of “never event” errors, with our MISMATCH guardrail successfully identifying every instance of hallucinated drug names in our translated texts from a carefully chosen case sample, although other drug error categories were not universally caught, such as wrong indications and due to dictionary limitations.
sample_unit: Japanese individual case safety reports (ICSRs) translated to English and reviewed by experts

title: The need for guardrails with large language models in pharmacovigilance and other medical safety critical settings
outcome: hallucinated drug-name flagging
effect: In 20 randomly selected cases, MISMATCH correctly identified all spontaneously hallucinated drug names; dictionary incompleteness and drug spelling issues still caused misses.
quote: As can be seen in Fig. 4 , all instances of the never event, “spontaneously hallucinated drug names”, were correctly identified by the MISMATCH guardrail.
sample_unit: Japanese individual case safety reports (ICSRs) translated to English and reviewed by experts

title: The need for guardrails with large language models in pharmacovigilance and other medical safety critical settings
outcome: LLM translation error rates

quote: The results (Table 4 ) showed the LLM translation had errors in categories including dates/times (60% error rate), drug names (59% error rate), AEs (66% error rate), and 62% had nonsensical phrases, including grammatical errors.
sample_unit: Japanese individual case safety reports (ICSRs) translated to English and reviewed by experts

title: The need for guardrails with large language models in pharmacovigilance and other medical safety critical settings
outcome: correlation between token entropy uncertainty scores and clinical accuracy or errors
effect: Entropy significantly differed for clinical accuracy (adj p=0.0031) and wrong drug mentions (adj p=0.028), with higher entropy in accurate cases.

title: Are clinical improvements in large language models a reality? Longitudinal comparisons of ChatGPT models and DeepSeek-R1 for psychiatric assessments and interventions

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence With Youth Codesign to Create Vaping Awareness Advertisements

outcome: Frequency of inaccurate content in GenAI replies to patient portal messages

title: Evaluating the Performance of State-of-the-Art Artificial Intelligence Chatbots Based on the WHO Global Guidelines for the Prevention of Surgical Site Infection: Cross-Sectional Study

title: A comprehensive multifaceted technical evaluation framework for implementation of auto-segmentation models in radiotherapy

quote: Expert evaluation revealed that 88% of automatically segmented structures were clinically acceptable with only minor adjustments needed.

title: AI Opportunistic Coronary Calcium Screening at Veterans Affairs Hospitals
outcome: Cardiologist review of sampled high-CAC AI outputs for appropriateness of lipid-lowering therapy

quote: Four cardiologists qualitatively reviewed a random sample of the >400 AI-CAC LDCT patients and verified that 527 of the 531 (99.2%) would benefit from lipid-lowering therapy.

title: Evaluating a predictive model of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy failure in a European-type cohort: a step towards population-specific tools

title: Evaluating a predictive model of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy failure in a European-type cohort: a step towards population-specific tools

effect: Model 2 recalibration gave HR 1.5 and 2.1; Model 3 gave HR 1.7 and 2.1, still below original 5.4 and 12.1; AUCs remained <0.68 with no significant improvement.

title: Evaluating a predictive model of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy failure in a European-type cohort: a step towards population-specific tools
outcome: Optimism bias from evaluating recalibrated models on the same dataset used to build them

title: Evaluating a predictive model of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy failure in a European-type cohort: a step towards population-specific tools

title: Evaluating a predictive model of tyrosine kinase inhibitor therapy failure in a European-type cohort: a step towards population-specific tools
outcome: Comparison of new models against existing ELTS score on same data
