title: Comparative Accuracy Assessment of Large Language Models in Cardiothoracic Anesthesia: A Performance Analysis of Claude and ChatGPT-4 on Subspecialty Board-Style Questions
outcome: Subspecialty benchmark accuracy of general LLMs versus their strong performance on general medical exams
effect: Both models scored well below the 80% clinical threshold on subspecialty questions (Claude 32%, ChatGPT-4 23%), despite prior proficiency on general medical licensing examinations.
quote: Both models performed below the threshold typically considered acceptable for clinical decision-making (≥80%).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Primary Care: Support or Additional Burden on Physicians' Healthcare Work?-A Qualitative Study
outcome: Physician-reported workflow disruption and burden from AI in primary care
effect: Physicians reported workflow disruption due to excessive system prompts and increased cognitive and emotional strain; qualitative, no quantitative effect sizes.
quote: Conversely, physicians reported concerns about workflow disruption due to excessive system prompts, lack of algorithmic transparency, increased cognitive and emotional strain, and perceived threats to clinical autonomy and accountability.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Primary Care: Support or Additional Burden on Physicians' Healthcare Work?-A Qualitative Study
outcome: Physician-reported lack of algorithmic transparency of AI systems
effect: Physicians raised concerns about lack of algorithmic transparency; transparent and explainable systems were named a crucial prerequisite for implementation.
quote: Conversely, physicians reported concerns about workflow disruption due to excessive system prompts, lack of algorithmic transparency, increased cognitive and emotional strain, and perceived threats to clinical autonomy and accountability.

title: Accuracy and Safety of ChatGPT-3.5 in Assessing Over-the-Counter Medication Use During Pregnancy: A Descriptive Comparative Study
outcome: Correctness, completeness, safety of ChatGPT-3.5 OTC pregnancy answers versus UpToDate
effect: Median correctness 5 (IQR 5-5), completeness 4 (IQR 4-5), safety 5 (IQR 5-5); safety errors in 9% of evaluations (n=8), including omissions risking serious complications.
quote: Despite high overall scores, the safety errors in 9% of the evaluations (n = 8), including omissions that pose a risk of serious complications, currently renders the chatbot an unsafe standalone resource for this purpose.

title: Misleading Results in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder Predictive Models Using Electronic Health Record Data: Algorithm Validation Study
outcome: Model performance predicting EHR-based diagnosis versus SCID-5 interview-based diagnosis (reference standard quality)
effect: EHR-diagnosis models AUC .85-.9, MCC .58-.69; interview-based models AUC .71-.76, MCC .24-.28. EHR vs SCID-5 concordance 73.3%, 17.8% false negatives, 8.9% false positives.
quote: Predictive models of PTSD built using only EHR data demonstrated inflated performance metrics relative to models predicting diagnosis from a rigorous structured clinical interview.
sample_unit: veterans with SCID-5 interviews and VA EHR visit data

title: Evaluating the Quality and Understandability of Radiology Report Summaries Generated by ChatGPT: Survey Study
outcome: Patient confidence, satisfaction with jargon and time to understand: original report vs ChatGPT plain-language summary
effect: Confidence in understanding 98% (116/118) with summary vs 26% (31/118) with report; jargon satisfaction 91% vs 8%; time to understand 97% vs 23%.
quote: After reading the summary, patient confidence in understanding (98%, 116/118 vs 26%, 31/118) and satisfaction regarding the level of jargon/terminology (91%, 107/118 vs 8%, 9/118) and time taken to understand the content (97%, 115/118 vs 23%, 27/118) substantially improved.
sample_unit: radiology reports (evaluated by 4 neuroradiologists and 4 patient volunteers)

title: Evaluating the Quality and Understandability of Radiology Report Summaries Generated by ChatGPT: Survey Study
outcome: Radiologist-rated omissions and over/underemphasis errors in AI-generated report summaries
effect: Missing relevant information in 5% (6/120) of responses; overemphasis of nonsignificant findings 12% (14/120); underemphasis of significant findings 18% (22/120); no fabricated findings.
quote: Five percent (6/120) of responses indicated there was missing relevant medical information in the summary, 12% (14/120) reported instances of overemphasis of nonsignificant findings, and 18% (22/120) reported instances of underemphasis of significant findings.
sample_unit: radiology reports (evaluated by 4 neuroradiologists and 4 patient volunteers)

title: Implementation of Passive Deterioration Index Alerts in an Intermediate Care Unit: A Failed Early Warning System Strategy
outcome: Alert-to-action time, mortality, length of stay, ICU transfer pre vs post
effect: No significant differences: alert-to-action 469 vs 359 min before alert (p=0.96); mortality 10.3% vs 13.1% (p=0.56); LOS 15.7 vs 12.8 days; ICU transfer 8.3% vs 6.2%.
quote: In this single-unit pilot, passive DTI-enabled EWS alerts did not improve time to intervention or clinical outcomes.

title: Implementation of Passive Deterioration Index Alerts in an Intermediate Care Unit: A Failed Early Warning System Strategy
outcome: Charge nurse documented acknowledgment of passive alerts
effect: Alert acknowledgment documented in 18.6% of cases; nurses preferred interruptive alerts and more prominent display locations.
quote: Charge nurses documented acknowledgment of the alert in 18.6% of cases, and acceptance was poor.

title: Implementation of Passive Deterioration Index Alerts in an Intermediate Care Unit: A Failed Early Warning System Strategy
outcome: Nurse acceptance and preferences for alert design
effect: Acceptance was poor; most nurses preferred interruptive alerts and more prominent DTI display locations.
quote: Most nurses expressed a preference for interruptive alerts and more prominent DTI display locations.

title: Implementation of Passive Deterioration Index Alerts in an Intermediate Care Unit: A Failed Early Warning System Strategy
outcome: Timeliness of deterioration alerts relative to provider actions
effect: Provider actions typically preceded alerts: 469 vs. 359 minutes before alert in pre- versus postimplementation periods; p = 0.96.
quote: High-risk DTI scores often occurred after clinical deterioration had already been recognized.

title: Implementation of Passive Deterioration Index Alerts in an Intermediate Care Unit: A Failed Early Warning System Strategy
outcome: alert acknowledgment and acceptance
effect: Charge nurses documented acknowledgment of alerts in only 18.6% of cases, and user acceptance was poor.
quote: Charge nurses documented acknowledgment of the alert in 18.6% of cases, and acceptance was poor.

title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
outcome: Adequacy of chatbot responses to simulated escalating suicidal risk scenarios (C-SSRS-based prompts)
effect: None of 29 agents met the adequate-response criteria; 51.72% gave marginal responses and 48.28% were inadequate. Common errors: no emergency contact information and lack of contextual understanding.
quote: None of the tested agents satisfied our initial criteria for an adequate response, 51.72% satisfied the relaxed criteria for a marginal response, while 48.28% were deemed inadequate.

title: Performance of mental health chatbot agents in detecting and managing suicidal ideation
outcome: Recognition and escalation of suicidal crisis in escalating simulated chatbot scenarios
effect: No agent gave an adequate response; 48.28% were inadequate. Common errors included failure to provide emergency contact information and poor contextual understanding.
quote: Common errors included the inability to provide emergency contact information and a lack of contextual understanding.

title: Quantifying device type and handedness biases in a remote Parkinson’s disease AI-powered assessment
outcome: Model fairness across sex, ethnicity, device type, and dominant hand subgroups
effect: No significant F1 differences across groups, but disparate impact and equalized odds showed bias by device type and dominant hand; sex and ethnicity had no statistically significant impact on PD predictions.
quote: While we find that sex and ethnicity have no statistically significant impact on PD predictions, biases exist regarding device type and dominant hand, as evidenced by disparate impact and equalized odds.

title: How Accurate Is AI? A Critical Evaluation of Commonly Used Large Language Models in Responding to Patient Concerns About Incidental Kidney Tumors
outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of LLM responses to patient questions
effect: ChatGPT FRE 48.5, FKGL 11.94; Gemini most complex, FRE 29.9, FKGL 13.3; reading levels above plain-language level.
quote: Readability varied between models: ChatGPT responses were easiest to understand (FRE = 48.5; FKGL = 11.94), while Gemini's were the most complex (FRE = 29.9; FKGL = 13.3).

title: How Accurate Is AI? A Critical Evaluation of Commonly Used Large Language Models in Responding to Patient Concerns About Incidental Kidney Tumors
outcome: Reading grade level of LLM patient-facing responses
effect: FKGL 11.94 (ChatGPT) to 13.3 (Gemini), FRE 29.9-48.5, well above typical patient reading level.
quote: Readability varied between models: ChatGPT responses were easiest to understand (FRE = 48.5; FKGL = 11.94), while Gemini's were the most complex (FRE = 29.9; FKGL = 13.3).

title: How Accurate Is AI? A Critical Evaluation of Commonly Used Large Language Models in Responding to Patient Concerns About Incidental Kidney Tumors
outcome: Rate of misleading or incomplete LLM responses rated by urologists
effect: 14% of responses flagged as potentially misleading or incomplete; Gemini accuracy 4.3, hallucination score 4.6.
quote: Overall, 14% of responses were flagged as potentially misleading or incomplete.

title: Standalone AI Versus AI-Assisted Radiologists in Emergency ICH Detection: A Prospective, Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of standalone AI vs AI-assisted radiologists for ICH
effect: Radiologists with AI outperformed standalone AI: sensitivity 98.91% vs 95.91%, specificity 99.83% vs 87.35%, accuracy 99.53% vs 90.11% (p<0.001); false positives 293 vs 4.
quote: Radiologists demonstrated statistically significant superiority across all main diagnostic metrics.

title: Standalone AI Versus AI-Assisted Radiologists in Emergency ICH Detection: A Prospective, Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
outcome: Radiologist review catching ICH cases missed (labeled negative) by AI
effect: All 45 ICH cases missed by AI were diagnosed by radiologists; AI missed 4.09% vs radiologists 1.09%.
quote: Conversely, in all 45 CT studies where AI services did not detect hemorrhages, pathology was identified by radiologists.

title: Clinical Failure of General-Purpose AI in Photographic Scoliosis Assessment: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of general-purpose LLMs assessing scoliosis from photographs versus radiographic reference
effect: ChatGPT specificity 0% (95% CI 0.0-14.8), misclassifying all non-AIS cases; Claude 2 78.3% false positives; ChatGPT thoracic Cobb overestimated by +10.74° (LoA -21.45° to +42.92°).
quote: The LLMs exhibited hazardous diagnostic inaccuracy: ChatGPT misclassified all non-AIS cases (specificity 0% [95% CI: 0.0-14.8]), while Claude 2 generated 78.3% false positives.
sample_unit: adolescents (74 with AIS, 23 with postural asymmetry)

title: Clinical decision support for pharmacologic management of treatment-resistant depression with augmented large language models
venue: Journal of mood and anxiety disorders
outcome: Change in LLM treatment rankings when vignette gender or race was permuted
effect: Results were not meaningfully different when gender or race of the vignette was permuted to examine risk for bias; optimal choice prioritized in 114/320 vignettes (35.6%).
quote: Results were not meaningfully different when gender or race of the vignette was permuted to examine risk for bias.
sample_unit: vignette evaluations (20 vignettes with gender and race permutations)

title: Clinical decision support for pharmacologic management of treatment-resistant depression with augmented large language models
venue: Journal of mood and anxiety disorders
outcome: Agreement of guideline-augmented LLM with expert-ranked optimal treatment
effect: Augmented model prioritized expert-designated optimal choice for 114/320 vignettes (35.6%, 95% CI 30.6%-41.0%; kappa 0.34); no contraindicated treatments chosen. No unaugmented comparison reported.
quote: The augmented model prioritized the expert-designated optimal choice for 114/320 vignettes (35.6 %, 95 % CI 30.6 %-41.0 %; Cohen's kappa = 0.34, 95 % CI 0.28-0.39).
sample_unit: vignette evaluations (20 vignettes with gender and race permutations)

title: Stability and reliability of artificial intelligence models in embryo selection for in vitro fertilization
outcome: Consistency of embryo rank ordering across replicate models and critical error rates
effect: Poor rank-order consistency (Kendall's W approximately 0.35) and critical error rates of approximately 15% across replicate models with identical architectures and similar AUC (~60%).
quote: The AI models demonstrated poor consistency in embryo rank ordering (Kendall's W approximately 0.35) and exhibited high critical error rates (approximately 15%), often ranking lower-quality embryos above viable ones.

title: Stability and reliability of artificial intelligence models in embryo selection for in vitro fertilization
outcome: Model stability when tested on data from a different fertility center
effect: Model instability increased on external center data (error variance delta: 46.07%^2), showing sensitivity to distribution shift.
quote: When tested on data from a different fertility center, model instability increased (error variance delta: 46.07%<sup>2</sup>), highlighting sensitivity to distribution shifts.

title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
outcome: ChatGPT status epilepticus recommendations' adherence to NCS/AES/EFNS guidelines and completeness
effect: Rarely recommended side positioning (25%) and neurological assessment (0-25%); dosing lacking when unprompted; non-established therapies suggested; GPT-5 not higher adherence than GPT-4o.
quote: However, it rarely recommended key measures such as side positioning (25%) to prevent potential aspiration and neurological assessments (0-25%).

title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
outcome: Output variation across prompt detail levels and repeated runs
effect: Guideline adherence rose with prompt detail: vital sign assessment 33 to 91%, second-line dosages 50 to 100%, third-line drugs 0 to 100%, complication screening 0 to 100%; repeated runs varied.
quote: More specific and detailed prompts increased guideline adherence most markedly regarding vital sign assessment (from 33 to 91%), correct dosages of second-line (from 50 to 100%), third-line drugs (from 0 to 100%), and screening for complications (from 0 to 100%).

title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
outcome: detailed prompting and guideline adherence
effect: Detailed prompts improved vital signs from 33 to 91%, second-line dosages from 50 to 100%, third-line dosages from 0 to 100%, complications from 0 to 100%.
quote: More specific and detailed prompts increased guideline adherence most markedly regarding vital sign assessment (from 33 to 91%), correct dosages of second-line (from 50 to 100%), third-line drugs (from 0 to 100%), and screening for complications (from 0 to 100%).

title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
outcome: Recognition of emergency management steps and context in status epilepticus scenario
effect: Missed that the patient was already intubated in 25% of 4th-prompt responses; rarely recommended neurological assessment and side positioning.
quote: In the fourth prompt, it missed the fact that the described patient was already intubated.

title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
outcome: autonomous treatment guidance safety
effect: Guideline gaps included side positioning 25% and neurological assessments 0-25%, with false statements; authors concluded not ready for safe autonomous practice.
quote: While the model shows promise in some areas and excels with the newer LLMs, the need for explicit, structured prompts, the occasional propagation of false statements, and gaps in guideline adherence indicate that such AI systems are not yet ready to be used safely and autonomously in clinical practice.

title: The impact of prompting on ChatGPT's adherence to status epilepticus treatment guidelines
outcome: guideline adherence across model versions
effect: GPT-4o outperformed GPT-3.5 and GPT-5; GPT-5 was superior to GPT-3.5.
quote: GPT-4o outperformed both GPT-3.5 and GPT-5, while GPT-5 was superior to GPT-3.5.

title: An eyecare foundation model for clinical assistance: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: Correct diagnostic rate and referral rate with versus without EyeFM copilot in RCT
effect: Correct diagnostic rate 92.2% vs 75.4% (P<0.001); referral rate 92.2% vs 80.5% (P<0.001); higher patient compliance with self-management (70.1% vs 49.1%) and referral (33.7% vs 20.2%).
quote: The primary endpoint indicated that ophthalmologists with EyeFM copilot achieved higher correct diagnostic rate (92.2% versus 75.4%, P < 0.001) and referral rate (92.2% versus 80.5%, P < 0.001).

title: An eyecare foundation model for clinical assistance: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: Ophthalmologist diagnostic performance with versus without AI copilot in intended deployment mode
effect: Ophthalmologists with EyeFM copilot had higher correct diagnostic rate (92.2% vs 75.4%, P<0.001) than standard care; overreliance not reported in the abstract.
quote: The primary endpoint indicated that ophthalmologists with EyeFM copilot achieved higher correct diagnostic rate (92.2% versus 75.4%, P < 0.001) and referral rate (92.2% versus 80.5%, P < 0.001).

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Utility in Biologic Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Comparative Study of ChatGPT and Google Web Search
outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of ChatGPT-4o answers on SLE biologic therapy
effect: ChatGPT-4o FKGL 11.7 (or 14.9) and FRE 17.3 (or 11.7) versus Google FKGL 16.2 and FRE 20; both required college graduate-level reading proficiency, far above sixth-grade level.
quote: These results indicate that both texts have a high level of reading difficulty, requiring readers to have a college graduate-level reading proficiency [ 41 ].

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Utility in Biologic Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Comparative Study of ChatGPT and Google Web Search
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient information text
effect: ChatGPT-4o and Google answers had high reading difficulty requiring college graduate-level proficiency; a sixth-grade prompt improved FKGL from 11.7 to 10.5 and FRE from 17.3 to 51.9.
quote: However, the content’s readability was low.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Utility in Biologic Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Comparative Study of ChatGPT and Google Web Search
outcome: Hallucination in ChatGPT-4o links and answers via two-step verification
effect: No hallucination found in links or answers after verifying links manually and checking accuracy scores (<3 = hallucination).
quote: No hallucination was found in the links or answers provided by ChatGPT after the 2-step verification.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Utility in Biologic Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Comparative Study of ChatGPT and Google Web Search
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4o answers rated by physicians on 6-point Likert scale
effect: ChatGPT-4o mean accuracy 5.83 (SD 0.49) vs Google 4.75 (SD 0.94); mean difference 1.08 (95% CI 0.61-1.54).
quote: In terms of accuracy, the accuracy scores indicate that ChatGPT-4o achieved a higher mean score (mean 5.83, SD 0.49) compared with Google Web Search responses (mean 4.75, SD 0.94), with a mean difference of 1.08 (95% CI 0.61‐1.54).

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Utility in Biologic Therapy for Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: Comparative Study of ChatGPT and Google Web Search
outcome: Comparison of ChatGPT-4o versus Google Web Search on accuracy and completeness
effect: ChatGPT-4o was more accurate (5.83 vs 4.75) and more complete (2.88 vs 1.68; difference 1.2, 95% CI 0.96-1.44) than Google Web Search.
quote: For completeness, ChatGPT-4o’s mean score was 2.88 (SD 0.32), significantly higher than Google Web Search’s 1.68 (SD 0.69), with a mean difference of 1.2 (95% CI 0.96‐1.44).

title: Rapidly Benchmarking Large Language Models for Diagnosing Comorbid Patients: Comparative Study Leveraging the LLM-as-a-Judge Method
outcome: Diagnostic hit rate of GPT-4o with versus without retrieval-augmented generation using ABIM reference ranges
effect: RAG significantly improved GPT-4o 05-13 hit rate by an average of 0.8% (P<.006)
quote: Finally, RAG significantly improved the hit rate of GPT-4o 05-13 by an average of 0.8% (P<.006).

title: Rapidly Benchmarking Large Language Models for Diagnosing Comorbid Patients: Comparative Study Leveraging the LLM-as-a-Judge Method
outcome: Sensitivity of diagnostic hit rate to prompt wording and temperature setting
effect: Significant variation in hit rates across the 3 prompts; temperature changes generally had little effect
quote: Significant variation in diagnostic hit rates was observed across different prompts, while changes in temperature generally had little effect.

title: Evaluating artificial intelligence chatbots' responses to gynecomastia inquiries: Comparative study of information quality, readability, and guideline consistency
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of chatbot answers versus European Association of Andology guidelines
effect: Overall accuracy of 85.71% for AI responses, but key guideline details were often omitted.
quote: Guideline consistency analysis revealed an overall accuracy of 85.71% for AI responses, but key details were often omitted.

title: Token Probabilities to Mitigate Large Language Models Overconfidence in Answering Medical Questions: Quantitative Study
outcome: Whether LLM self-expressed confidence predicts response accuracy on medical exam questions (AUROC)
effect: Chatbots expressed uniformly high confidence (90-100) yet self-rated confidence AUROC was only 0.52-0.68. Token probability AUROC was 0.71-0.87, and all models showed imperfect calibration with a trend toward overconfidence.
quote: However, expressed confidence failed to predict response accuracy (AUROC ranging from 0.52, 95% CI 0.50-0.53 for Phi-3-Mini to 0.68, 95% CI 0.65-0.71 for GPT-4o).

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Reducing Data Deluge From Cardiac Implantable Electronic Devices
outcome: AI classification accuracy versus blinded electrophysiologist adjudication on random ~15% sample of transmissions

quote: Considering electrophysiologist interpretation/adjudication as the gold standard, AI was 93.8% accurate with 99.1% sensitivity, 93% specificity, and an F1 score of 81%.

title: Development and Validation of a Large Language Model-Based System for Medical History-Taking Training: Prospective Multicase Study on Evaluation Stability, Human-AI Consistency, and Transparency
outcome: Run-to-run stability of LLM automated scoring (coefficient of variation) across 3 cases
effect: CVs were low for total scores (0.87%-1.12%) and item-level scoring (0.55%-0.73%); fully-processed system raised ICCs from 0.414/0.500 to 0.923/0.972 in moderate and complex cases versus baseline.
quote: Specifically, the coefficients of variation (CV) were low across total scores (0.87%-1.12%) and item-level scoring (0.55%-0.73%).

title: External validation of deep learning-derived 18F-FDG PET/CT delta biomarkers for loco-regional control in head and neck cancer
outcome: Performance of externally developed segmentation model on local retrospective PET/CT data for stratifying loco-regional control
effect: Higher AI-derived ΔPET-GTV stratified loco-regional control (log-rank p = 0.02); 2-year control 94.1% vs 53.6%; clinician found AI volumes acceptable in 78% of cases.
quote: Patients with higher ΔPET-GTV (i.e. greater tumour shrinkage) had significantly improved loco-regional control (log-rank p = 0.02).

title: A comprehensive evaluation of large language models for information extraction from unstructured electronic health records in residential aged care
outcome: Robustness of LLM information extraction and summarization from nursing notes
effect: Robustness was low: 4.00% for NER and 4.31% for summarization, despite fairness of 99.9% and bias of 0.11%.
quote: However, robustness remained low (4.00 % for NER, 4.31 % for summarization) despite excellent fairness (99.9 %) and minimal bias (0.11 %) in both tasks.

title: Can Large Artificial Intelligence-Based Linguistic Models Help to Obtain Information About Burning Mouth Syndrome?
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of LLM responses on burning mouth syndrome
effect: Average readability corresponded to 12th grade; ChatGPT required the highest proficiency.
quote: Average readability corresponded to 12th grade, with ChatGPT requiring the highest proficiency.

title: Feasibility of AI-powered assessment scoring: Can large language models replace human raters?
outcome: LLM scoring reliability and discrepancies before versus after public release of the model
effect: After public release, reliability decreased notably (ICC = -0.046 for BVMT-R Trial 3) and average scoring discrepancies rose (SDMT from 0.05 to 6.79).
quote: After ChatGPT-4.5 was publicly released, reliability decreased notably (e.g. ICC = -0.046 for BVMT-R Trial 3), and average scoring discrepancies per test increased (e.g. SDMT = 6.79).

title: Feasibility of AI-powered assessment scoring: Can large language models replace human raters?
outcome: Change in LLM scoring performance after model update/release
effect: Reliability fell and scoring discrepancies increased after the public release version replaced the early-access model (SDMT discrepancy 0.05 to 6.79).
quote: After ChatGPT-4.5 was publicly released, reliability decreased notably (e.g. ICC = -0.046 for BVMT-R Trial 3), and average scoring discrepancies per test increased (e.g. SDMT = 6.79).

title: Impact of Prognostic Notifications on Inpatient Advance Care Planning: A Cluster Randomized Trial
venue: Journal of pain and symptom management
outcome: ACP documentation by randomized physician after high-risk notification recommending ACP
effect: Intervention 34.7% vs control 19.6% (OR 2.04; 95% CI 1.16-3.59); no significant change in ACP documentation by any clinician (52.8% vs 42.8%, OR 1.31; 95% CI 0.81-2.13).
quote: Patients of physicians randomized to the intervention group were more likely to have a documented ACP conversation by the randomized physician compared to the control group (34.7% vs. 19.6%; OR 2.04; 95% CI 1.16-3.59).

title: Prompt Engineering and Follow-Up Questioning Improves the Readability of Spine Surgery Questions in Large Language Models
outcome: Readability of LLM spine surgery answers under different plain-language prompting strategies
effect: Phase 2 (sixth-grade level request) gave the most readable responses, with 51.11% meeting the sixth-grade level. Follow-up clarification and simple prompts beat complex rule-based prompts.
quote: Phase 2 yielded the most readable responses, with 51.11% meeting the sixth-grade level.

title: Performance of ChatGPT, Gemini and DeepSeek for non-critical triage support using real-world conversations in emergency department
outcome: LLM triage accuracy against nurse-assigned KTAS on real-world conversations across models
effect: Among 1,057 real triage cases, Gemini 2.5 flash reached 73.8% accuracy and Gemini 2.5 pro 90.9% sensitivity; performance varied widely across models and versions.
quote: Performance varied widely between models and even between different versions from the same vendor.

title: Performance of ChatGPT, Gemini and DeepSeek for non-critical triage support using real-world conversations in emergency department
outcome: Comparison of multiple LLMs against each other and nurse KTAS gold standard on same data
effect: Eight LLMs compared on identical cases; accuracy, sensitivity and specificity differed widely (e.g., Gemini 2.5 pro sensitivity 90.9% but specificity 23.3%; GPT-4.1 accuracy 70.6%).
quote: Gemini 2.5 pro demonstrated the highest sensitivity (90.9%) and F1-score (82.4%), though with lower specificity (23.3%).

title: The Impact of Access to Clinical Guidelines on LLM-Based Treatment Recommendations for Chronic Hepatitis B
venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
outcome: Guideline coherence of GPT-4 treatment recommendations with vs without attached guideline document
effect: Coherence with 2024 WHO guidelines rose from 51% without context to 91% with context (p = 0.017); textual correctness rose 2.60 to 2.91 (p = 0.029).
quote: without context, only 51% of the cases were assessed as coherent on average, whereas with context, this rose to 91%, representing an increase of 78% ( p = 0.017).

title: The Impact of Access to Clinical Guidelines on LLM-Based Treatment Recommendations for Chronic Hepatitis B
venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
outcome: Whether GPT-4 without context gave outdated guideline recommendations after guideline update
effect: Without context GPT-4 mostly adhered to the older 2015 WHO guidelines; only 51% of recommendations were coherent with the 2024 guidelines.
quote: Our findings showed that GPT-4, when enhanced with more context, aligns consistently with the latest WHO guidelines, whereas GPT-4 without additional context mostly adhered to the older 2015 WHO guidelines.

title: The Impact of Access to Clinical Guidelines on LLM-Based Treatment Recommendations for Chronic Hepatitis B
venue: Liver international : official journal of the International Association for the Study of the Liver
outcome: Currency of LLM clinical knowledge versus current guidelines
effect: GPT-4 without external context gave outdated treatment recommendations for chronic hepatitis B; coherence was 51%, and errors persisted (91%) even with context.
quote: Consequently, this setup allowed us to specifically isolate and demonstrate the impact of providing access to an up‐to‐date external document, effectively showcasing GPT‐4's vulnerability to providing outdated or incorrect treatment recommendations without immediate contextualisation.

title: Evaluating Retrieval Augmented Generation-enhanced Large Language Models for Question Answering On German Neurovascular Guidelines
outcome: Answer correctness of LLM with versus without RAG grounding in guidelines
effect: GPT-4o-mini without RAG performed significantly worse (20.0% correct, 32.9% wrong) than with RAG (57.6% correct, 15.3% wrong); RAG models ranged 56.6%-70.6% correct.
quote: GPT-4o-mini without RAG performed significantly worse (20.0%, 32.9% wrong).

title: Evaluating Retrieval Augmented Generation-enhanced Large Language Models for Question Answering On German Neurovascular Guidelines
outcome: Expert-graded output accuracy of guideline question answering against reference guidelines
effect: Best model Claude 3.5 Sonnet 70.6% correct, 10.6% wrong; other RAG models 56.6-64.7% correct with 15.3-17.6% wrong; retrieval errors caused 80% of incorrect answers.
quote: Claude Sonnet 3.5 achieved the highest answer correctness (70.6% correct, 10.6% wrong), followed by Llama 3.1 (64.7%, 15.3% wrong), GPT-4o-mini with RAG (57.6%, 15.3% wrong), and Mixtral (56.6%, 17.6% wrong).

title: Comparison of a Specialized Large Language Model with GPT-4o for CT and MRI Radiology Report Summarization
outcome: Report summarization F1 and expert-rated quality, specialized LLM versus general-purpose GPT-4o on same data

venue: Arquivos brasileiros de cirurgia digestiva : ABCD = Brazilian archives of digestive surgery

outcome: Rated quality and demographic bias of LLM explanations when prompt patient gender and age were varied

title: Performance of GPT-4o combined with retrieval-augmented generation on nutritionist licensing exam questions
outcome: Accuracy and response consistency of GPT-4o with vs without guideline retrieval grounding

quote: While the accuracy improvement of GPT-4o-RAG over GPT-4o was not statistically significant (p = 0.12), it exhibited significantly lower variance and higher response consistency (97.3% vs. 91.2-95.2%, p < 0.001).

title: Performance of GPT-4o combined with retrieval-augmented generation on nutritionist licensing exam questions
outcome: Model performance on numerical/calculation questions and association of errors with numerical terms
effect: GPT-4o-RAG showed limited performance on numerical questions; TF-IDF analysis linked incorrect answers more frequently to numerical terms.
quote: GPT-4o-RAG outperformed other models in applied and clinical nutrition categories but showed limited performance on numerical questions.

title: Implementing a Resource-Light and Low-Code Large Language Model System for Information Extraction from Mammography Reports: A Pilot Study
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Inter-rater agreement between two independent annotators establishing ground truth
effect: Cohen's kappa 0.83 overall between two independent physicians; lowest for Findings (0.71); disagreements resolved by study coordinators.
quote: A high level of IRA with a Cohen’s Kappa of 0.83 was observed between the two researchers performing the manual value assignment.

title: Implementing a Resource-Light and Low-Code Large Language Model System for Information Extraction from Mammography Reports: A Pilot Study
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Comparison of five candidate open-source LLMs on same data
effect: Rombos significantly outperformed other LLMs with default prompt (72.9% vs 59.2–68.5%, p<0.0001) and with adapted prompts (85.3%).
quote: The overall accuracy of Rombos was significantly higher compared to each of the other LLMs ( p < 0.0001; see also Supplementary Table 4).

title: Implementing a Resource-Light and Low-Code Large Language Model System for Information Extraction from Mammography Reports: A Pilot Study
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Accuracy and coverage when restricting to high model certainty classifications

quote: In the sub-analysis using a threshold for the relative probability (= “certainty” ), an increase in accuracy compared to the baseline was seen across all models and thresholds.

title: Implementing a Resource-Light and Low-Code Large Language Model System for Information Extraction from Mammography Reports: A Pilot Study
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine

effect: Few-shot prompting decreased all models: 1-shot accuracy 30.9–67.5%; 3-shot accuracy 32.3–58.5%.
quote: Few-shot prompting (both 1- and 3-shot prompts) decreased the overall accuracy for all models, with a range of 30.9–67.5% for the 1-shot prompt and 32.3–58.5% for the 3-shot prompt (see Table 2 for detailed results).

title: Customizing AI-based screening with real-world data: Practical insights from diabetic retinopathy
outcome: Sensitivity and missed moderate/severe DR after local referral threshold retuning
effect: Greifswald-modified RetCAD sensitivity for more-than-mild DR 93.63% vs 70.41% unmodified (diagnosable); specificity fell to 66.5%; missed severe DR 2 vs 13, moderate 13 vs 67. Threshold derived and evaluated on the same local data.
quote: Under this scenario, 2 severe DR cases and 13 moderate DR cases would be missed compared to 13 severe DR and 67 moderate DR cases with unmodified RetCAD screening.

title: Customizing AI-based screening with real-world data: Practical insights from diabetic retinopathy
outcome: Real-world local sensitivity versus pivotal trial performance
effect: IDx-DR sensitivity for more-than-mild DR 90.2% in diagnosable patients but 52.7% across all patients, versus 87.2% in the pivotal trial; 25.5% of patients rejected for image quality.
quote: The sensitivity for more than mild DR on this data set was 87.2%, which is comparable to our result of diagnosable patients (90.2%), but not for all patients in our study (52.7%) (Abràmoff et al., 2018 ).

title: Customizing AI-based screening with real-world data: Practical insights from diabetic retinopathy
outcome: Diagnostic sensitivity against ophthalmologists' dilated funduscopic examination
effect: Unmodified RetCAD sensitivity was 70.41% for more than mild DR and 62.86% for severe DR among analysable images, including images recommended for rejection.
quote: The diagnostic sensitivity of the RetCAD algorithm for detecting more than mild DR on analysable images (including the ones recommended to be rejected) was 70.41%, and the sensitivity for severe DR was 62.86%.

title: Customizing AI-based screening with real-world data: Practical insights from diabetic retinopathy
outcome: sensitivity in real-world clinical screening
effect: performance was substantially lower in real-world settings when missing or non-analysable images were included
quote: Real-world DR screening performance of AI algorithms, when including non-analysable patients, can be substantially lower than in controlled studies.

title: Artificial intelligence for detecting anaphylaxis in electronic medical records
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM diagnoses across repeated runs on different days

quote: Diagnoses: Most notably, 6 cases (0.65%) presented different diagnoses on at least 2 different days.

title: Artificial intelligence for detecting anaphylaxis in electronic medical records
outcome: Comparison of candidate GPT model configurations against expert physician labels on same data
effect: GPT 4 Turbo precision 90.6%, sensitivity 100%, kappa 0.95; GPT 3.5 precision 44.9%, kappa 0.59; GPT 3.5+4 precision 81.0%, kappa 0.88.
quote: The best results came using configuration 3, the GPT 4 Turbo.

title: Artificial intelligence for detecting anaphylaxis in electronic medical records
outcome: Effect of adding WAO criteria to prompt on LLM precision

title: Artificial intelligence for detecting anaphylaxis in electronic medical records

quote: Specificity went from 99.5% to 90.2%, and accuracy from 99.5% to 95%, still outstanding results.

title: Reducing Hallucinations and Trade-Offs in Responses in Generative AI Chatbots for Cancer Information: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: Hallucination rate with RAG on curated CIS source versus Google-based RAG versus no RAG
effect: Hallucination rates 0% (GPT-4) and 6% (GPT-3.5) with CIS RAG; conventional chatbots about 40%. OR vs CIS: Google 9.4 (95% CI 1.2-17.5), conventional 16.1 (95% CI 3.7-50.0).
quote: Similarly, conventional GPTs had an OR of 16.1 (95% CI 3.7‐50.0; P <.001) compared to those with RAG reference data from CIS.

title: Reducing Hallucinations and Trade-Offs in Responses in Generative AI Chatbots for Cancer Information: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: Effect of vetted versus unvetted retrieval corpus on hallucination rate
effect: Google-retrieval chatbots had 18% hallucinations among answered questions vs 2% for CIS chatbots; Google OR 9.4 (95% CI 1.2-17.5, P<.01) versus CIS.
quote: In multivariate analysis, adjusting for other factors, models with RAG reference data from Google search results were more likely to generate hallucinations compared with those with RAG reference data from CIS, with an OR of 9.4 (95% CI 1.2‐17.5; P <.01).

title: Reducing Hallucinations and Trade-Offs in Responses in Generative AI Chatbots for Cancer Information: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: Hallucination rate of conventional GPT chatbots on cancer questions against reference review
effect: Conventional GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 generated hallucinations in 37% and 40% of responses respectively.
quote: The conventional models generated hallucinations in approximately 40% of their responses.

title: Comparing clinical decision support systems for improving follow-up of abnormal cervical cancer screening test results
outcome: Completion of recommended follow-up at 120 days, CDSS alone vs usual care
effect: In a cluster RCT, CDSS alone versus usual care did not improve follow-up outcomes in either system.
quote: CDSS alone versus usual care did not improve outcomes in either system.

title: Comparing clinical decision support systems for improving follow-up of abnormal cervical cancer screening test results

title: Comparing clinical decision support systems for improving follow-up of abnormal cervical cancer screening test results
outcome: Completion of recommended follow-up within 120 days
effect: CDSS alone: no improvement. Outreach with/without navigation: System A, 38.2 % or 37.2 % vs 23.5 %, p < 0.001; System B, 25.4 % or 23 % vs. 19.7 %, p = 0.044.
quote: Both models with patient outreach with or without navigation - but not CDSS alone - increased recommended follow-up.

title: Comparing clinical decision support systems for improving follow-up of abnormal cervical cancer screening test results
outcome: CDSS true-positive identification assessed by manual chart review
effect: CDSS true positives were 61.3 % in System A and 70.4 % in System B.
quote: CDSS true positives were 61.3 % in System A and 70.4 % in System B.

title: Comparing clinical decision support systems for improving follow-up of abnormal cervical cancer screening test results
outcome: Completion of recommended follow-up
effect: CDSS with patient outreach increased follow-up to 38.2% vs 23.5% in System A, and 25.4% vs 19.7% in System B, whereas CDSS alone did not.
quote: CDSS with patient outreach with or without navigation versus usual care significantly increased follow-up rates in System A (38.2 % or 37.2 % vs 23.5 %, p < 0.001) and System B (25.4 % or 23 % vs. 19.7 %, p = 0.044).

title: Advancing Question-Answering in Ophthalmology With Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Benchmarking Open-Source and Proprietary Large Language Models
outcome: LLM multiple-choice accuracy with RAG versus zero-shot on ophthalmology questions
effect: RAG raised GPT-4-turbo accuracy by 11.54% on BCSC and 10.96% on OphthoQuestions; overall gains were 23.85% for Llama-3, 17.11% for Gemma-2 and 22.11% for Mixtral-8x7B.
quote: Using RAG, GPT-4-turbo's accuracy increased by 11.54% on BCSC and by 10.96% on OphthoQuestions.

title: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
venue: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
outcome: AUC of CNN versus simple MAP threshold for predicting intraoperative hypotension across datasets
effect: CNN beat MAP threshold in the ambiguous Karolinska data (64.41 vs 61.92) but only marginally in VDB datasets (80.29 vs 78.46; 80.64 vs 79.80); threshold metrics were comparable at 80% specificity.
quote: In the Karolinska dataset, characterized by narrow class separation ( = 2.44 mmHg), the CNN model performed better than MAP threshold method (MAPthr), achieving a higher (64.41 vs. 61.92 ).

title: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
venue: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
outcome: Performance inflation from selection bias excluding borderline MAP cases, tested by standardizing class separation
effect: Baseline AUCs differed (64.41 Karolinska vs ~80 VDB); after standardizing MAP difference to 5.01 mmHg, AUCs equalized (72.48, 71.79, 73.33), indicating selection bias inflated metrics.
quote: This standardization equalized performance ( for Karolinska, VDB Matched, and VDB Non-Matched), confirming that class separation bias inflates metrics in datasets with larger values (Table 5 ).

title: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
venue: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
outcome: Cross-center and cross-cohort AUC when training on one site and testing on another
effect: Trained on VDB Matched, tested on Karolinska AUC fell to 63.25 (vs 80.29 within-site); VDB Non-Matched to Karolinska 63.76; Karolinska-trained models generalized to VDB at 68.28-70.62.
quote: Cross-center validation exposed asymmetric generalizability: models trained on Karolinska–with a larger Gray Zone prevalence ( 49 versus 18–20 in VDB datasets; see Fig. 3 , right panels)–generalized moderately to VDB Matched ( = 68.28 ), while the reverse (VDB Matched Karolinska) showed significant degradation ( = 63.25 ).

title: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
venue: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
outcome: Performance degradation when applying models across datasets with different populations and class separation
effect: Models trained on well-separated VDB data degraded on Karolinska (AUC 63.25-63.76), while within-VDB transfer was consistent (79.16-80.63).
quote: These findings establish realistic expectations for AI-deployment in one hospital doesn’t guarantee success in another.

title: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
venue: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
outcome: age-subgroup model performance
quote: This suggest that age-related factors may introduce variability or complexity in the data for older patients, potentially making accurate prediction more challenging.

title: Towards reliable prediction of intraoperative hypotension: a cross-center evaluation of deep learning-based and MAP-derived methods
venue: Journal of clinical monitoring and computing
outcome: Predictive performance of CNN versus MAP threshold method across datasets
effect: In VDB cohorts, CNN was marginally better than MAPthr (AUC-ROC 80.29 vs 78.46, and 80.64 vs 79.80), but in Karolinska CNN was higher (64.41 vs 61.92); sensitivity, PPV, and F1 were comparable across all datasets.
quote: In contrast, for the VDB datasets–characterized by a wider class separation ( = 11.21–11.96 mmHg) and clearer hemodynamic patterns–the CNN model performed only marginally better than MAPthr ( = 80.29 vs. 78.46 for VDB Matched, and 80.64 vs. 79.80 for VDB Non-Matched).

title: New frontiers in radiologic interpretation: evaluating the effectiveness of large language models in pneumothorax diagnosis
outcome: Response consistency across three repeated runs of same radiograph (Fleiss' Kappa)
effect: Gemini 2.0 showed excellent reliability for large pneumothorax (Kappa = 1.00), while Claude 3.5 showed moderate consistency across both pneumothorax sizes.
quote: Regarding consistency, Gemini 2.0 demonstrated excellent reliability for large pneumothorax (Kappa = 1.00), while Claude 3.5 showed moderate consistency across both pneumothorax sizes.

title: New frontiers in radiologic interpretation: evaluating the effectiveness of large language models in pneumothorax diagnosis
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy by patient age group and pneumothorax size
effect: Adult overall accuracy: ChatGPT-4o 69.6%, Claude 3.5 64.9%, Gemini 2.0 57.4%; pediatric 20.8%, 12.5%, 20.8%. ChatGPT-4o large vs small pneumothorax 81.6% vs 42.2% (p<0.001).
quote: Performance was significantly poorer in pediatric patients across all models (20.8%, 12.5%, and 20.8%, respectively).

title: New frontiers in radiologic interpretation: evaluating the effectiveness of large language models in pneumothorax diagnosis

title: Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribes: A Pilot Survey of Perspectives on the Utility and Documentation Burden in Palliative Medicine
outcome: Documentation time savings with ambient AI scribe versus dictation, by resident

quote: One resident saw a statistically significant reduction (p < 0.025) in the time spent on clinical documentation, while a second resident saw essentially no improvement.

title: Evaluation of large language models in patient education for hyperthyroidism: A comparative study of chatgpt, gemini, and deepseek
outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of LLM patient education responses on hyperthyroidism

title: An end-to-end solution for out-of-hospital emergency medical dispatch triage based on multimodal and continual deep learning

quote: Compared with the Valencian Region's existing in-house triage protocol, E2eDeepEMC<sup>2</sup> achieved absolute F1-score gains of 18.46% for life-threatening level, 25.96% for response delay and 3.63% for jurisdiction.

title: Development, external validation and integration into clinical workflow of machine learning models to support pre-operative assessment in the UK

outcome: Reading grade level of LLM-generated patient-facing content

title: Pathology Made Simple: ChatGPT's Summarization of Pathology Reports

title: A Novel Playbook for Pragmatic Trial Operations to Monitor and Evaluate Ambient Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Practice

quote: However, when explicitly prompted, ChatGPT reliably adjusted the complexity of its responses to both a seventh-grade and a graduate-level reading standard.

title: Advancing patient education in PRRT through large language models: challenges and potential
venue: American journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
outcome: Rate of medically incorrect chatbot answers (accuracy ≤3) to PRRT patient questions
effect: Medically incorrect information (accuracy ≤3) appeared in 7-8% of responses, with no significant difference between ChatGPT 4o and DeepSeek V3 (P = 0.8005). Mean accuracy was 4.43 vs 4.56.
quote: However, the presence of medical inaccuracies highlights the need for physician oversight when using AI chatbots for patient education.

title: A Cross-Sectional Study Assessing the Suitability of ChatGPT and DeepSeek AI for Generating Patient Education Guides on Imaging Modalities in Stroke
outcome: Readability (grade level, ease score) of AI-generated stroke imaging patient education guides
effect: No significant differences between tools; ChatGPT often slightly higher grade levels, DeepSeek higher ease scores for some modalities; reliability uniformly high. Absolute grade levels not reported in abstract.
quote: ChatGPT often produced slightly higher grade levels, while DeepSeek AI had higher ease scores for some modalities.
sample_unit: AI-generated patient education guides (2 tools x 3 imaging modalities)

title: Integrating generative AI in perinatology: applications for literature review
outcome: Citation accuracy and hallucinated references in generative AI outputs
effect: Perplexity AI had the best citation accuracy; ChatGPT4 and Claude required manual verification of citations; hallucinated references persist as a risk.
quote: Perplexity AI demonstrated the best citation accuracy, while ChatGPT4 and Claude excelled in content summarization but required manual verification of citations.

title: Large Language Models in Neurological Practice: Real-World Study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLMs versus neurologists (concordance with discharge diagnoses)
effect: Neurologists achieved 75% diagnostic accuracy, outperforming ChatGPT (54%) and Gemini (46%); LLMs overprescribed diagnostic tests in 17%-25% of cases.
quote: Neurologists achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 75%, outperforming ChatGPT (54%) and Gemini (46%).

title: Large Language Models in Neurological Practice: Real-World Study
outcome: LLM clinical reasoning and test appropriateness on real-world neurology cases
effect: Both LLMs showed limitations in nuanced clinical reasoning and overprescribed diagnostic tests in 17%-25% of cases; accuracy 54% (ChatGPT) and 46% (Gemini).
quote: Both LLMs demonstrated limitations in nuanced clinical reasoning and overprescribed diagnostic tests in 17%-25% of cases.

title: Radiologist Interaction with Artificial Intelligence-Generated Preliminary Reports: A Longitudinal Multireader Study
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Reading time, acceptance, agreement and quality of radiologist reports using AI preliminary reports over batches
effect: Reading time fell from 25.8 s to 19.3 s; acceptance rose 54.6% to 60.2%; agreement and quality stable for normal but varied significantly for abnormal radiographs.
quote: However, agreement and quality scores showed variability, particularly in abnormal cases, emphasizing the need for oversight in the interpretation of complex chest radiographs.

title: Use, knowledge and perception of large language models in clinical practice: a cross-sectional mixed-methods survey among clinicians in Switzerland
outcome: Availability of workplace LLM guidelines reported by clinicians amid frequent LLM use
effect: 225 (32.8%) reported frequent LLM use, while only 42 (6%) reported availability of workplace LLM guidelines.
quote: Among 685 participants (response rate 29.0%), 225 (32.8%) reported frequent use of LLMs, 25 (3.6%) reported having used a specific medical LLM and 42 (6%) reported the availability of workplace LLM guidelines.

title: Large language models to develop evidence-based strategies for primary and secondary cardiovascular prevention
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease Score) of LLM cardiovascular prevention content
effect: Readability scores were low; median FRES indicated both primary and secondary prevention content were difficult to understand.
quote: Readability scores were low, with median FRES indicating that both primary and secondary prevention content were difficult to understand.

title: Large language models to develop evidence-based strategies for primary and secondary cardiovascular prevention
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education content
effect: Median FRES indicated difficult-to-understand content for primary and secondary prevention; specialized clinical topics had lower readability.
quote: Readability scores were low, with median FRES indicating that both primary and secondary prevention content were difficult to understand.

title: Deep learning for atrioventricular regurgitation diagnosis: an external validation study
outcome: Proportion of eligible echocardiograms for which the model could return a prediction
effect: Model returned predictions for 578 of 1541 eligible TTEs (38%); performance analysis limited to these cases, indicating mismatch between model input requirements and local acquisition practices.
quote: Among 1541 eligible TTEs, the model returned predictions for 578 studies (38%).
sample_unit: echocardiography studies with model predictions (of 1541 eligible)

title: Deep learning for atrioventricular regurgitation diagnosis: an external validation study
outcome: Model performance on local historical echocardiograms versus cardiologist reference interpretations
effect: MR AUC 0.98 (95% CI 0.97-0.99), 91% accuracy, 95% sensitivity, 89% specificity; TR AUC 0.96, 84% accuracy, 91% sensitivity, 80% specificity; only 38% of studies received predictions.
quote: For MR, the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.98 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.97-0.99], with 91% accuracy, 95% sensitivity, and 89% specificity.
sample_unit: echocardiography studies with model predictions (of 1541 eligible)

title: Including AI in diffusion-weighted breast MRI has potential to increase reader confidence and reduce workload
outcome: Reader performance with versus without AI-CAD: BI-RADS-like 3 calls, agreement, lesion detection
effect: AI-augmented reading reduced BI-RADS-like 3 calls by 29% (P=.019), raised interrater agreement (0.57 vs 0.49), preserved accuracy; two of three readers detected more malignant lesions (63/69 vs 59/69; 64/69 vs 62/69).
quote: The AI-augmented approach significantly reduced BI-RADS-like 3 calls in breast DWI by 29% (P =.019) and increased interrater agreement (0.57 ± 0.10 vs 0.49 ± 0.11), while preserving diagnostic accuracy.

title: Optimizing Order Sets With a Large Language Model-Powered Multiagent System
outcome: Hallucinated clinical content in RAG-grounded order set suggestions
effect: No suggestions were identified as hallucinations, although 11% were redundant (96 suggestions rated by 3 physicians).
quote: No suggestions were identified as hallucinations, although 11% were redundant.

title: Optimizing Order Sets With a Large Language Model-Powered Multiagent System
outcome: Postprocessing filter retention of useful suggestions while reducing total suggestions
effect: Threshold of 0.11 retained 453 suggestions (29% reduction) while preserving 92% of useful suggestions.
quote: Using this model as a filter, a threshold of 0.11 retained 453 suggestions (a 29% reduction) while preserving 92% of useful suggestions.

title: Optimizing Order Sets With a Large Language Model-Powered Multiagent System
outcome: hallucinations in RAG suggestions
effect: No hallucinations were identified; 11% of suggestions were redundant.
quote: No suggestions were identified as hallucinations, although 11% were redundant.

title: Optimizing Order Sets With a Large Language Model-Powered Multiagent System
outcome: context-specific usefulness
effect: Only 19% of suggestions were useful; many factually correct suggestions lacked needed clinical context.
quote: The modest useful suggestion rate (19%) highlights a key challenge: many suggestions, while factually correct, lacked the specific clinical context to be deemed useful.

title: Comparative Evaluation of a Medical Large Language Model in Answering Real-World Radiation Oncology Questions: Multicenter Observational Study
outcome: LLM answer quality vs experts on real-world clinical questions, rather than exam-style
effect: No significant quality difference between LLM and clinical experts (mean 3.38 vs 3.63; P=.26); harmful in 13% expert vs 16% LLM answers (P=.63).
quote: There were no significant differences between the quality of the answers between LLM and clinical experts (mean scores of 3.38 vs 3.63; median 4.00, IQR 3.00-4.00 vs median 3.67, IQR 3.33-4.00; P=.26; Wilcoxon signed rank test).

title: Comparative Evaluation of a Medical Large Language Model in Answering Real-World Radiation Oncology Questions: Multicenter Observational Study
outcome: LLM answer quality and harmfulness compared with senior radiation oncology experts on same questions
effect: Quality not significantly different (3.38 vs 3.63; P=.26); potentially harmful 16% LLM vs 13% experts (P=.63).
quote: The answers were deemed potentially harmful in 13% of cases for the clinical experts compared with 16% of cases for the LLM (P=.63; Fisher exact test).

title: Automated production of comparison tables for shared decision making: Comparing a human-generated table (Option Grid), a search engine process, and outputs from four large language models
outcome: Readability of LLM-generated comparison tables versus human Option Grid
effect: The human-generated Option Grid had superior readability; LLM tables may be less readable and require additional checking and editing.
quote: The human-generated Option Grid had superior readability.
sample_unit: comparison tables (one human Option Grid, four LLM tables, one Google search table)

title: Automated production of comparison tables for shared decision making: Comparing a human-generated table (Option Grid), a search engine process, and outputs from four large language models
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM-generated clinical content versus expert Option Grid
effect: Accuracy was 97% for the ChatGPT models and OpenBioLLM-70b and 95% for OpenBioLLM-8b and the Google search process; several tables omitted alternative interventions.
quote: Accuracy, compared to the human Option Grid, was 97 % for the ChatGPT models and the open-source OpenBioLLM-70b, and 95 % for OpenBioLLM-8b and the Google search process.
sample_unit: comparison tables (one human Option Grid, four LLM tables, one Google search table)

title: A collaborative large language model for drug analysis
outcome: Drug recommendation, dosage, adverse reaction, and interaction task performance of knowledge-grounded LLM versus generic LLMs
effect: Knowledge-grounded DrugGPT outperformed a wide range of existing LLMs and reached state-of-the-art performance across all metrics with fewer parameters than generic LLMs. No numbers are given in the abstract.
quote: DrugGPT outperforms a wide range of existing LLMs and achieves state-of-the-art performance across all metrics with fewer parameters than generic LLMs.

title: Detection of pneumonia in children through chest radiographs using artificial intelligence in a low-resource setting: A pilot study
outcome: AI performance on local prospective data versus internal test data
effect: Internal test: 86% accuracy, 0.93 AUC; external Nigerian test: 58% accuracy, 0.48 recall, 0.65 AUC.
quote: The model achieved 86% accuracy, 0.83 precision, 0.98 recall, 0.79 F1-score, and 0.93 AUC on the internal test, and 58% accuracy, 0.62 precision, 0.48 recall, 0.68 F1-score, and 0.65 AUC on the external test.
sample_unit: Nigerian pediatric chest radiographs (external test set)

title: Detection of pneumonia in children through chest radiographs using artificial intelligence in a low-resource setting: A pilot study
outcome: Performance gap between development population/setting and local deployment setting
effect: Large drop from internal to external test attributed to differences in imaging protocols and equipment between LMIC and high-income settings.
quote: This performance gap likely stems from differences in imaging protocols/equipment between LMICs and high-income settings.
sample_unit: Nigerian pediatric chest radiographs (external test set)

title: Leveraging Electronic Health Record Data and Up-to-Date Clinical Guidelines for High-Accuracy Clinical Diabetes Drug and Dosage Recommendation
outcome: Faithfulness of RAG-grounded recommendations to retrieved guideline sources
effect: Faithfulness of recommendations reached 0.850 with RAG over ADA and Taiwan NHI guidelines; no comparison without grounding reported in the abstract.
quote: Faithfulness of recommendations reached 0.850.
sample_unit: physicians (field validation); EHR patient sample size not reported

title: Interpreting psychiatric digital phenotyping data with large language models: a preliminary analysis
outcome: LLM accuracy across data quality levels and timeframes in interpreting phenotyping data
effect: GPT-4o accuracy declined with decreasing data quality (69% high-quality vs 39% low-quality) and shorter timeframes (60% for 3-month vs 43% for 3-week data).
quote: Accuracy declined with decreasing data quality (69% for high-quality data vs 39% for low-quality data) and shorter timeframes (60% for 3-month data vs 43% for 3-week data).

title: Interpreting psychiatric digital phenotyping data with large language models: a preliminary analysis
outcome: Comparison of candidate LLMs on the same test cases for pattern identification accuracy
effect: GPT-4o 52% accuracy (95% CI 46.5% to 57.6%) significantly outperformed GPT-3.5-turbo (12%, 95% CI 8.4% to 15.6%).
quote: GPT-4o demonstrated 52% accuracy (95% CI 46.5% to 57.6%) in identifying clinical patterns based on standard test cases, significantly outperforming GPT-3.5-turbo (12%, 95% CI 8.4% to 15.6%).

title: Expanding care coordination in an integrated health system through causal machine learning
outcome: 30-day readmission in randomized low-risk patients targeted by causal ML score, intervention vs usual care
effect: 30-day readmissions 7.7% vs 8.2% in intervention vs usual care, not statistically significant; observed-to-expected readmission ratio decline was statistically significant.
quote: While 30-day readmissions declined in the intervention group (7.7% vs. 8.2%), the difference was not statistically significant.

title: Evaluating the performance of five large language models in generating patient educational content for pediatric cardiothoracic procedures: a comparative study
outcome: Readability of LLM-generated pediatric cardiothoracic patient pamphlets across six readability metrics
effect: Readability differed by model; Gemini was most comprehensible, ChatGPT 4 and Perplexity AI had similar readability; authors conclude readability should be optimized for general public comprehension. No numeric grade levels in abstract.
quote: Readability analysis indicated that Gemini produced the most comprehensible content.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4's performance on pediatric dentistry questions: accuracy and completeness analysis
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT-4 pediatric dentistry answers by topic
effect: Mean accuracy 4.21 for FAQs and 4.16 for curricular questions; accuracy varied by topic (p=0.007), highest for fissure sealants (4.45), lowest for pulpal therapy (3.93).
quote: Accuracy scores for curricular questions varied significantly by topic (p = 0.007), with the highest score for fissure sealants (4.45 ± 0.62; median: 5) and the lowest for pulpal therapy (3.93 ± 0.93; median: 4).

title: Artificial intelligence-generated informed patient consent in various ophthalmological procedures: A comparative study of correctness, completeness, readability, and real-word application between Deepseek and Chatgpt 4o
outcome: Real-world applicability of AI-generated consent forms in the Indian setting, judged by ophthalmology faculty
effect: 40% of consents generated by both chatbots were not fit for use in Indian scenarios.
quote: However, 40% of the consents generated by both chatbots were not fit to be used in Indian scenarios.
sample_unit: AI-generated informed consent forms for ophthalmological procedures

title: Large language model as clinical decision support system augments medication safety in 16 clinical specialties
outcome: Performance of pharmacists using LLM-CDSS in workflow versus standalone LLM or pharmacist alone
effect: Co-pilot accuracy 61% vs human only 46%; serious errors caught 66% in co-pilot vs 52% by LLM alone.
quote: LLMs alone were capable of catching 52% of serious errors, while that improved with co-pilot mode to 66%.
sample_unit: simulated prescribing error scenarios (40 vignettes) reviewed by 6 pharmacists

title: Large language model as clinical decision support system augments medication safety in 16 clinical specialties
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM responses across repeated runs
effect: Claude 3.5 Sonnet averaged 0.84 BERTscore, 0.947 cosine similarity, and 0.570 BLEU across repeated prompts, indicating high reproducibility.
quote: Claude 3.5 Sonnet demonstrated high degree of semantic reproducibility, scoring an average of 0.84, 0.947, and 0.570 for BERT score, cosine similarity, and BLEU score, respectively.
sample_unit: simulated prescribing error scenarios (40 vignettes) reviewed by 6 pharmacists

title: Large language model as clinical decision support system augments medication safety in 16 clinical specialties
outcome: Accuracy of RAG-grounded vs native LLMs for detecting prescribing errors
effect: RAG improved accuracy and recall of all models except Claude 3.5 Sonnet, where accuracy fell 51% to 49%.
quote: Applying a RAG framework improved accuracy and recall of all models except for Claude 3.5 Sonnet.
sample_unit: simulated prescribing error scenarios (40 vignettes) reviewed by 6 pharmacists

title: Large language model as clinical decision support system augments medication safety in 16 clinical specialties
outcome: Comparison of five LLMs, LLM-alone, and pharmacists alone on same scenarios
effect: Claude 3.5 Sonnet best native model (accuracy 51%, F1 0.42) vs Gemini Flash 16%; co-pilot 61% vs pharmacist alone 46%.
quote: Of the native models, Gemini Flash scored the lowest while Claude 3.5 Sonnet performed the best on measures of recall (0.16 vs. 0.51), precision (0.15 vs. 0.35), F1 (0.16 vs. 0.42), and overall accuracy (16% vs. 51%).
sample_unit: simulated prescribing error scenarios (40 vignettes) reviewed by 6 pharmacists

title: Large language model as clinical decision support system augments medication safety in 16 clinical specialties
outcome: Serious-error detection
effect: LLM alone caught 52% of serious errors; co-pilot mode caught 66%.
quote: LLMs alone were capable of catching 52% of serious errors, while that improved with co-pilot mode to 66%.
sample_unit: simulated prescribing error scenarios (40 vignettes) reviewed by 6 pharmacists

title: Large language model as clinical decision support system augments medication safety in 16 clinical specialties
outcome: Error identification accuracy for pharmacists with vs without LLM CDSS vs LLM alone
effect: Co-pilot accuracy 61% (SD 17.7) vs human alone 46% (SD 21.1), a 32.6% increase; overall ANOVA across modes not significant (p=0.38).
quote: The mean accuracy in identifying DRPs increased by 32.6% in co-pilot mode when compared against human alone (61%, SD 17.7 vs. 46%, SD 21.1).
sample_unit: simulated prescribing error scenarios (40 vignettes) reviewed by 6 pharmacists

title: 'ChatGPT can make mistakes' warnings fail: A randomized controlled trial
outcome: Effect of 'ChatGPT can make mistakes' warning on students' diagnosis changes after AI advice
effect: Diagnostic changes 15.3% no-warning vs. 15.9% warning; OR = 1.09, 95% CI 0.46-2.59, p = 0.84. Warning did not alter advice-taking.
quote: The warning did not influence diagnostic changes (15.3% no-warning vs. 15.9% warning; OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 0.46-2.59, p = 0.84).

title: Quality safety and disparity of an AI chatbot in managing chronic diseases: simulated patient experiments
outcome: Differences in AI care intensity across simulated patient age and household economic status
effect: Disparities were observed by patient age and household economic status; older and wealthier patients received more intensive care.
quote: Disparities were observed based on patient age and household economic status, with older and wealthier patients receiving more intensive care.

title: AI-Generated Diet and Exercise Recommendations for Cardiovascular Health Compared to Established Cardiology Society Guidelines
outcome: LLM diet and exercise recommendations compliance with AHA/ACC and ESC guidelines
effect: 90% of responses from ChatGPT, Claude AI, and DeepSeek AI met guideline standards; Gemini 80%; all models struggled with precise quantitative carbohydrate and added sugar guidance.
quote: Ninety percent of responses from ChatGPT, Claude AI, and DeepSeek AI met established cardiovascular health standards, indicating superior performance among the language models.

title: Artificial Intelligence Versus Professional Standards: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study of GPT, Gemini, and ENT UK in Delivering Patient Information on ENT Conditions
outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of LLM-generated patient information versus ENT UK
effect: ENT UK FRE 64.6 and FKGL 7.4; ChatGPT FRE 38.8, FKGL 11.0; Gemini FRE 38.3, FKGL 11.9 (all p<0.001).
quote: ENT UK showed the highest readability (FRE: 64.6 ± 8.4) and lowest grade level (FKGL: 7.4 ± 1.5), significantly better than that of ChatGPT (FRE: 38.8 ± 10.5, FKGL: 11.0 ± 1.5) and Gemini (FRE: 38.3 ± 8.5, FKGL: 11.9 ± 1.2) (all p < 0.001).
sample_unit: patient information documents (6 laryngology conditions x 3 sources)

title: Artificial Intelligence Versus Professional Standards: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study of GPT, Gemini, and ENT UK in Delivering Patient Information on ENT Conditions
outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated patient materials relative to recommended literacy standards
effect: ChatGPT FKGL 11.0 and Gemini FKGL 11.9 versus ENT UK 7.4; AI text requires higher reading levels and falls short of recommended literacy standards.
quote: GPT and Gemini produce patient information of comparable quality and engagement to ENT UK but require higher reading levels and fall short of recommended literacy standards.
sample_unit: patient information documents (6 laryngology conditions x 3 sources)

title: AI-Generated Patient-Friendly MRI Fistula Summaries: A Pilot Randomised Study
outcome: Patient-rated readability and comprehensibility of AI plain-language MRI summaries versus original reports; Flesch-Kincaid score
effect: Patients rated AI summaries higher for readability (median 5 vs 2, p=0.011) and comprehensibility (5 vs 2, p=0.007); Flesch-Kincaid 54.6 vs 32.2 (p=0.005); no clinically significant inaccuracies.
quote: Patients rated AI summaries significantly higher in readability (median 5 vs. 2, p = 0.011), comprehensibility (5 vs. 2, p = 0.007), utility (5 vs. 3, p = 0.014), and overall quality (4.5 vs. 4, p = 0.013), with fewer follow-up questions (3 vs. 4, p = 0.018).

title: Benefit-Risk Reporting for FDA-Cleared Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices
outcome: Reporting of study design, training sample size, and demographics in FDA device summaries
effect: Summaries failed to report study designs (323 [46.7%]), training sample size (368 [53.3%]), and demographic information (660 [95.5%]).
quote: Device summaries often failed to report study designs (323 [46.7%]), training sample size (368 [53.3%]), and/or demographic information (660 [95.5%]).

title: Benefit-Risk Reporting for FDA-Cleared Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices
outcome: Proportion of cleared devices with randomized trial data or patient outcomes evidence
effect: Only 6 devices (1.6%) reported RCT data, 53 (7.7%) prospective studies, and patient outcomes in 3 (<1%).
quote: Only 6 devices (1.6%) reported data from randomized clinical trials and 53 (7.7%) from prospective studies.

title: Benefit-Risk Reporting for FDA-Cleared Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices
outcome: Reporting of sensitivity and specificity performance metrics in premarket summaries
effect: Sensitivity reported for 166 (24.0%) and specificity for 152 (22.0%) devices.
quote: Few premarket summaries contained data published in peer-reviewed journals (272 [39.4%]) or provided statistical or clinical performance, including sensitivity (166 [24.0%]), specificity (152 [22.0%]), and/or patient outcomes (3 [<1%]).

title: Benefit-Risk Reporting for FDA-Cleared Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices
outcome: Postmarket adverse events and recalls among AI/ML devices
effect: 489 adverse events involving 36 (5.2%) devices, including 458 malfunctions, 30 injuries, 1 death; 40 devices (5.8%) recalled 113 times, mostly software issues.
quote: A total of 40 devices (5.8%) were recalled 113 times, primarily due to software issues.

title: Enhancing the CAD-RADS™ 2.0 Category Assignment Performance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek Through "Few-shot" Prompting
outcome: CAD-RADS category assignment accuracy with structured few-shot prompt versus zero-shot prompt
effect: Zero-shot accuracy 14% (ChatGPT) and 8% (DeepSeek); few-shot improved to 98% and 93% (both P<0.001).
quote: Few-shot prompting significantly improved accuracy to 98% for ChatGPT and 93% for DeepSeek (both P <0.001) and eliminated hallucinations.

title: Enhancing the CAD-RADS™ 2.0 Category Assignment Performance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek Through "Few-shot" Prompting
outcome: Reproducibility of few-shot classifications across repeated runs on 50 reports
effect: Kappa 0.957 (0.900, 1.000) for ChatGPT and 0.873 (0.779, 0.967) for DeepSeek between repeated assignments.
quote: Reproducibility analysis yielded kappa values of 0.957 (0.900, 1.000) ( P <0.001) for ChatGPT and 0.873 [0.779, 0.967] ( P <0.001) for DeepSeek, indicating almost perfect and strong agreement between repeated assignments, respectively, with no significant difference between the models ( P =0.125).

title: Enhancing the CAD-RADS™ 2.0 Category Assignment Performance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek Through "Few-shot" Prompting
outcome: zero-shot CAD-RADS assignment accuracy
effect: Zero-shot accuracy was low: ChatGPT 14%, DeepSeek 8%; correct assignments almost exclusively in CAD-RADS 0 cases.
quote: Using zero-shot prompting, accuracy was low for both models (ChatGPT: 14%, DeepSeek: 8%), with correct assignments occurring almost exclusively in CAD-RADS 0 cases.

title: Enhancing the CAD-RADS™ 2.0 Category Assignment Performance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek Through "Few-shot" Prompting
outcome: repeated-run CAD-RADS agreement
effect: Kappa 0.957 (0.900, 1.000) for ChatGPT and 0.873 [0.779, 0.967] for DeepSeek; both P <0.001.
quote: Reproducibility analysis yielded kappa values of 0.957 (0.900, 1.000) ( P <0.001) for ChatGPT and 0.873 [0.779, 0.967] ( P <0.001) for DeepSeek, indicating almost perfect and strong agreement between repeated assignments, respectively, with no significant difference between the models ( P =0.125).

title: Utilizing artificial intelligence to increase the readability of patient education materials in pediatric neurosurgery
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of patient education materials before and after ChatGPT plain-language rewriting
effect: ChatGPT reduced mean reading level from 10.60 (SD 0.57) to 6.18 (SD 0.28; p < 0.05), reaching the 6th-grade target across all conditions.
quote: ChatGPT effectively reduced the mean reading level from 10.60 (SD 0.57) to 6.18 (SD 0.28; p < 0.05), achieving the target 6th-grade level across all conditions.

title: Utilizing artificial intelligence to increase the readability of patient education materials in pediatric neurosurgery
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level
effect: Mean reading level decreased from 10.60 (SD 0.57) to 6.18 (SD 0.28; p < 0.05).
quote: ChatGPT effectively reduced the mean reading level from 10.60 (SD 0.57) to 6.18 (SD 0.28; p < 0.05), achieving the target 6th-grade level across all conditions.

title: National indication protocol for proton radiotherapy in esophageal cancer patients in the Netherlands
venue: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
outcome: Performance of externally validated mortality model after local recalibration in esophageal cancer cohorts
effect: Model performed well after updates to the intercept (both cohorts) and slope (nCRT).
quote: The model performed well after updates to the intercept (both cohorts) and slope (nCRT).

title: Evaluating the clinical utility of multimodal large language models for detecting age-related macular degeneration from retinal imaging
outcome: Accuracy of general-purpose MLLMs on AMD detection and grading from fundus images
effect: Binary classification accuracy ranged from 0.301 (Claude 3.5 Sonnet) to 0.824 (ChatGPT-4o); severity grading accuracy at best 0.463 (Perplexity Sonar Large). Reliability judged insufficient for clinical application.
quote: In summary, while MLLMs show promise for automated AMD detection and grading from fundus images, their current reliability is insufficient for clinical application, highlighting the need for further model development and validation.
sample_unit: eyes (ultrawide field fundus images from 76 patients)

title: Concordance of an Artificial Intelligence Model (ChatGPT 4.0) with Physician Decisions in Smoking Cessation Clinics: A Comparative Evaluation
