outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT-4.0 smoking cessation treatment recommendations versus physician decisions, by case complexity
effect: Overall concordance 67.1%; 32.9% inappropriate. Inappropriate recommendations in 81.5% of chronic disease cases and 77.8% of regular medication cases (p=0.021, p=0.030).
quote: ChatGPT-4.0 provided inappropriate recommendations in 81.5% of cases involving chronic diseases and 77.8% of cases involving regular medication use (p = 0.021, p = 0.030, respectively).

title: Evaluating Deep Learning-Based Commercial Software for Detecting Ischemic Lesions on DWI in Stroke Patients
outcome: Lesion-level and patient-level sensitivity of commercial AI on local retrospective DWI data versus expert neurologist reference standard
effect: Lesion-level sensitivity 83.51% (95% CI 79.8-86.8%); patient-level sensitivity 95.31% (95% CI 91.8-97.6%); undetected lesions were smaller, covered fewer slices, and had higher ADC values.
quote: The software achieved a lesion-level sensitivity of 83.51% (95% CI, 79.8-86.8%) and a patient-level sensitivity of 95.31% (95% CI, 91.8-97.6%).

title: Human-in-the-Loop Performance of LLM-Assisted Arterial Blood Gas Interpretation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
outcome: Agreement with expert reference on primary and secondary acid-base disorders, LLM-S (user interpretation) vs LLM-I (LLM interpretation)
effect: APSD kappa rose from 0.61-0.65 with LLM interpretation (LLM-I) to 0.81-0.91 with user-supervised interpretation (LLM-S); AMA kappa from 0.48-0.76 to ≥0.85.
quote: In the LLM-S method, APSD agreement improved substantially, with κ = 0.91 for ChatGPT and κ = 0.81 for both Copilot and Gemini.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Performance of LLM-Assisted Arterial Blood Gas Interpretation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
outcome: LLM calculation and formula errors in acid-base compensation computations
effect: Errors under LLM-S were few: Copilot had two (chronic formula misapplied; arithmetic sign error); ChatGPT one and Gemini four failures to impute a primary disorder. No calculation issues in albumin-corrected anion gap.
quote: Errors in the LLM-S evaluations included a failure to impute a primary disorder in a mixed case for ChatGPT; two errors for Copilot (a misapplication of a chronic compensation formula to an acute metabolic alkalosis, and an incorrect directional change in bicarbonate for respiratory alkalosis due to an arithmetic sign error); and four failures to impute a primary disorder for Gemini (three mixed cases and one simple case).

title: Human-in-the-Loop Performance of LLM-Assisted Arterial Blood Gas Interpretation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
outcome: LLM behavior under input variation and prompt design during pilot testing (forced disorder detection, overinterpretation, hypoalbuminemia)
effect: Pilot testing showed LLMs forced detection of a disorder when 'no disorder' option was absent, overinterpreted mild electrolyte deviations, and misattributed hypoalbuminemia to liver disease and respiratory alkalosis.
quote: Furthermore, in the pilot testing we found that including cases with hypoalbuminemia prompted the LLM to attribute the finding to chronic liver disease and suggest the presence of respiratory alkalosis, even when the remaining data did not support such disorder.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Performance of LLM-Assisted Arterial Blood Gas Interpretation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
outcome: Agreement of three general-purpose LLMs against pathologist reference standard for ABG interpretation
effect: Primary disorder agreement κ ≥ 0.88 for all LLMs; secondary disorder agreement varied by model and method (ChatGPT LLM-S κ = 0.91 vs Copilot/Gemini 0.81).
quote: Agreement for identifying the primary acid-base (APD) disorder was strong across all approaches (Cohen's κ ≥ 0.88).

title: Human-in-the-Loop Performance of LLM-Assisted Arterial Blood Gas Interpretation: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
outcome: agreement on primary and secondary acid-base disorders
effect: APSD agreement was moderate for standalone LLM-I (ChatGPT κ=0.65, Copilot κ=0.61, Gemini κ=0.62) but strong for supervised LLM-S (ChatGPT κ=0.91, Copilot κ=0.81, Gemini κ=0.81).
quote: For identifying both primary and secondary disorders regardless of order (APSD), LLM-I showed moderate agreement (ChatGPT κ = 0.65, Copilot κ = 0.61, Gemini κ = 0.62), whereas LLM-S achieved strong agreement (ChatGPT κ = 0.91, Copilot κ = 0.81, Gemini κ = 0.81).

title: Evaluating the performance of ChatGPT in clinical multidisciplinary treatment: a retrospective study
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: ChatGPT etiology reasoning and diagnostic accuracy in complex MDT cases versus physicians
effect: ChatGPT median overall score 41.0/50 vs MDT physicians 43.5 (p = 0.001); lower accuracy (p < 0.001); higher comprehensiveness (p < 0.001); lacked ability to reason through etiologies of complex cases.
quote: Analysis of specific questions revealed that ChatGPT lacked the ability to reason through the etiologies of complex cases.

title: Evaluation of Nurses' Perceptions and Readiness for Artificial Intelligence Integration in Healthcare: A Cross-Sectional Study in Turkey
outcome: Nurses' knowledge of AI in healthcare and readiness for AI integration
effect: Nurses' knowledge of AI in healthcare was generally limited among 388 nurses, despite optimism about benefits; concerns about privacy and ethics were significant.
quote: Findings revealed that nurses' knowledge of AI in healthcare was generally limited, though many participants expressed optimism about its potential to improve efficiency, enhance patient care quality and alleviate nurse burnout.

title: Referential hallucination and clinical reliability in large language models: a comparative analysis using regenerative medicine guidelines for chronic pain
outcome: Reference hallucination scores of LLM responses on regenerative pain guideline questions
effect: Claude had lowest reference hallucinations (RHS 4.44 ± 3.18) vs. ChatGPT-4o (8.38 ± 1.86) and Gemini 2.5 (8.75 ± 1.73).
quote: Claude had the lowest reference hallucinations (RHS 4.44 ± 3.18) vs. ChatGPT-4o (8.38 ± 1.86) and Gemini 2.5 (8.75 ± 1.73).

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence-Generated Patient Education Materials for Bariatric Surgery: Comparative Analysis of Response Quality, Reliability, and Readability Across ChatGPT and DeepSeek Models
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease) of AI patient education responses
effect: ChatGPT FKGL 16.40 (SD 2.43) vs DeepSeek 13.48 (SD 2.35), P<0.001; FRE 26.11 vs 20.87 (P=0.110). Both models at college reading level.
quote: Both models produced responses at a readability level corresponding to college education.

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence-Generated Patient Education Materials for Bariatric Surgery: Comparative Analysis of Response Quality, Reliability, and Readability Across ChatGPT and DeepSeek Models
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient education materials relative to appropriate user level
effect: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 16.40 (ChatGPT) and 13.48 (DeepSeek); Flesch Reading Ease 26.11 and 20.87, both college-level text.
quote: ChatGPT yielded significantly higher Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level Scores (meaning its text was more complex) (mean [SD], 16.40 [2.43] vs. 13.48 [2.35]; P < 0.001).

title: Influence of head positioning errors on the accuracy of fully automated artificial intelligence-based cephalometric software
outcome: AI cephalometric measurement agreement under incorrect head positioning versus correct positioning
effect: Positional errors drastically reduced measurement accuracy; linear parameters such as Go-Me showed poorest agreement across all software; WebCeph and Ceph Assistant linear ICC < 0.50.
quote: Positional errors drastically reduced measurement accuracy, with linear parameters such as Go-Me showing the poorest agreement across all software.

title: Influence of head positioning errors on the accuracy of fully automated artificial intelligence-based cephalometric software
outcome: AI software accuracy variation across three products and measurement types
effect: AudaxCeph achieved excellent agreement (ICC > 0.90) for several skeletal parameters but failed on soft tissue; WebCeph and Ceph Assistant showed greater variability (ICC < 0.50 for linear measures).
quote: AudaxCeph demonstrated the most consistent accuracy, achieving excellent agreement (ICC > 0.90) for several skeletal parameters; however, it failed in detecting soft tissue accurately.

title: Readability and performance of AI chatbot responses to frequently asked questions in maxillofacial prosthodontics
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of chatbot answers to patient maxillofacial prosthodontics questions versus health literacy guidelines
effect: FKGL differed significantly among chatbots (P=.002); DeepSeek had the lowest FKGL (best readability) and ChatGPT the highest; none consistently met health literacy guidelines.
quote: Although the DeepSeek and ChatGPT platforms produced higher-quality content, none consistently met health literacy guidelines.

title: Evaluating the Accuracy and Efficiency of AI-Generated Radiology Reports Based on Positive Findings-A Qualitative Assessment of AI in Radiology
outcome: Whether radiologist review corrects errors in AI-drafted reports
effect: Minor formatting errors and occasional anatomical misinterpretations in AI reports were easily corrected by the radiologist during review; accuracy rated 4.65 vs 3.81 with dictation (p<0.0001).
quote: Minor formatting errors and occasional anatomical misinterpretations were observed in AI-generated reports, but could be easily corrected by the radiologist during review.
sample_unit: imaging cases (MRI knee, MRI lumbar spine, CT head, CT abdomen/pelvis)

title: Can ChatGPT provide responses to patients for orthopaedic-related questions? A comparison between ChatGPT and medical support staff
outcome: ChatGPT vs support staff response quality and empathy on the same patient questions
effect: No quality difference (p = 0.075); ChatGPT rated more empathetic (p < 0.001); no difference in risk of incorrect treatment (p = 0.377).
quote: No quality difference was found (p = 0.075) between ChatGPT and support staff, though ChatGPT was rated as more empathetic (p < 0.001).

title: Can ChatGPT provide responses to patients for orthopaedic-related questions? A comparison between ChatGPT and medical support staff
outcome: High-risk errors in ChatGPT-generated replies to patient questions
effect: Three ChatGPT responses showed high-risk errors among 50 compared, with no difference from support staff in risk of incorrect treatment (p = 0.377).
quote: Three ChatGPT responses showed high-risk errors.

title: AI‑Enhanced Smartwatch AHI Estimation and AI‑Scored Polysomnography for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Real‑World Validation
outcome: Smartwatch algorithm performance in a Korean cohort versus South-American training cohorts (inter-ethnic validation)
effect: eAHI correlated strongly with aiAHI (rho 0.88, ICC 0.87); sensitivity 92.3%, specificity 92.6% for moderate-to-severe OSA; systematic underestimation, especially in mild OSA.
quote: The model was trained in South‑American cohorts, allowing inter‑ethnic validation.
sample_unit: adults with valid simultaneous smartwatch and PSG recordings

title: Refining patient education on autologous chondrocyte implantation for chondral lesions of the knee: A fine-tuned ChatGPT-4o model improves readability and quality
outcome: Reading grade level (FKGL) of native ChatGPT-4o patient education responses
effect: Native ChatGPT-4o mean FKGL 13.45 (university sophomore level), FRES 35.68, exceeding the recommended 8th-9th grade level for patient materials.
quote: In contrast, the native ChatGPT‐4o generated content with a mean FKGL of 13.45 and a FRES of 35.68, indicating a reading difficulty equivalent to the university sophomore level, which substantially exceeds the accepted readability thresholds for patient educational materials.

title: Refining patient education on autologous chondrocyte implantation for chondral lesions of the knee: A fine-tuned ChatGPT-4o model improves readability and quality
outcome: Readability and quality of AI patient education responses, fine-tuned vs native model
effect: Fine-tuned ACI Guide FKGL 9.25 vs 13.45 native; FRES 49.59 vs 35.68 (p<0.001); DISCERN 43.18 vs 35.29 (p<0.001).
quote: The ACI Guide achieved a mean DISCERN score of 43.18 ± 3.92 (range: 34–53), reflecting moderate‐quality responses, while the native ChatGPT‐4o scored 35.29 ± 5.0 (range: 23–45; p < 0.001), indicating poor‐quality responses.

title: Refining patient education on autologous chondrocyte implantation for chondral lesions of the knee: A fine-tuned ChatGPT-4o model improves readability and quality
outcome: Reading grade level
quote: The ACI guide had a mean FKGL of 9.25 (range: 5.80–12.20, ±1.64), while the native ChatGPT‐4o had a significantly higher mean FKGL of 13.45 (range: 11.40–16.20, ±1.30) ( p < 0.001) (see Figure 2 ).

title: Mapping artificial intelligence adoption in hepatology practice and research: challenges and opportunities in MENA region
outcome: Reported barriers to AI adoption among hepatology clinicians, including inadequate AI training
effect: Inadequate training was reported by 60.6% of respondents, limited AI tool access by 53%, and insufficient infrastructure by 53%; 70.3% expressed strong interest in AI training.
quote: Major barriers included inadequate training (60.6%), limited AI tool access (53%), and insufficient infrastructure (53%).

title: Evaluation of the clinical reasoning of GPT-4o, a multimodal generative artificial intelligence model, in 18 public gastroenterology case studies
outcome: GPT-4o accuracy on Spanish gastroenterology board exam clinical case questions and error analysis
effect: GPT-4o answered 39 of 49 questions correctly (79.6%); errors included unawareness of contraindications and inappropriate therapeutic generalizations.
quote: GPT-4o answered 39 questions correctly (79.6 %).
sample_unit: multiple-choice questions from 18 board exam clinical cases

title: Evaluation of the clinical reasoning of GPT-4o, a multimodal generative artificial intelligence model, in 18 public gastroenterology case studies
outcome: Exam-style benchmark accuracy versus clinical reasoning quality
effect: 79.6% accuracy on board exam questions, yet reasoning errors showed omission of information already provided (clinical context, temporal criteria).
quote: the observed failures revealed that the model tends to omit information already provided (such as clinical context or temporal criteria), thereby compromising the quality of its reasoning.
sample_unit: multiple-choice questions from 18 board exam clinical cases

title: Amending AI Software Accuracy for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection Using Conditional Probability and the Appropriate Reference Standard
outcome: DART sensitivity and specificity corrected using the appropriate reference standard and conditional probability
effect: Corrected sensitivity and specificity were significantly lower than originally reported in all three scenarios (retinography sensitivity 90%, 80%, 70%). Retinography by an ophthalmologist outperformed DART on FN%, FP%, NPV and PPV.
quote: In all scenarios, corrected sensitivity and specificity values for DART were significantly lower than those reported in the original validation study.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's ability to simplify scientific abstracts for clinicians and the public
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of ChatGPT summaries versus original abstracts
effect: ChatGPT summaries scored higher on Flesch Reading Ease than original abstracts in 31 of 43 papers (p = 0.005), but technical terms usage scored below 7 out of 10.
quote: ChatGPT's summaries scored higher on the Flesch Reading Ease test than the original abstracts in 31 out of 43 papers, showing a significant improvement in readability (p = 0.005).

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's ability to simplify scientific abstracts for clinicians and the public
outcome: Hallucination presence in ChatGPT-generated abstract summaries rated by reviewers
effect: Hallucination presence scored below 7 out of 10; hallucination scores varied by study type, with case reports lowest.
quote: Despite its strengths, ChatGPT showed limitations in "Hallucination presence" and "Technical terms usage," scoring below 7 out of 10.

title: An infection prediction model developed from inpatient data can predict out-of-hospital COVID-19 infections from wearable data when controlled for dataset shift
outcome: AUROC of hospital model on wearable data with vs without local distribution adjustment
effect: Baseline AUROC 0.527; sleep-only 0.644; sleep-only plus unsupervised feature transformation from healthy local wearable data 0.740; 25 healthy subjects' data sufficed.
quote: Applying feature transformation on the sleep-only features resulted an additional 15% boosting of performance in terms of AUROC (0.740 versus 0.643, red solid line versus green dashed line in Fig. 5 A).
sample_unit: wearable-study subjects (301 COVID-19 positive, 2,111 negative) used to test the model

title: An infection prediction model developed from inpatient data can predict out-of-hospital COVID-19 infections from wearable data when controlled for dataset shift
outcome: Performance of hospital-trained model applied directly to wearable population with dataset shift
effect: Directly applied hospital model performed at chance: AUROC 0.527 (95% CI 0.498-0.566), AP 0.132; five sources of dataset shift identified.
quote: This performance was at chance level (95% confidence interval: [0.498, 0.566] for AUROC, [0.122, 0.153] for AP), suggesting that the hospital model failed to generalize when directly applied to wearable dataset.
sample_unit: wearable-study subjects (301 COVID-19 positive, 2,111 negative) used to test the model

title: An infection prediction model developed from inpatient data can predict out-of-hospital COVID-19 infections from wearable data when controlled for dataset shift
outcome: Generalization of inpatient predictive model to a new population and context (out-of-hospital wearables)
effect: Model applied to new population and setting without correction gave AUROC 0.527, near chance; improved to 0.740 only after both corrections.
quote: The model performed at chance level without these two corrections and performed at AUROC of 0.74 when and only when both corrections were used.
sample_unit: wearable-study subjects (301 COVID-19 positive, 2,111 negative) used to test the model

title: Readability versus accuracy in LLM-transformed radiology reports: stakeholder preferences across reading grade levels
outcome: readability and accuracy of generated reports
effect: Across reading grades 7-17, lower grades improved readability but increased errors; higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability.
quote: Lower reading grades improved readability but increased errors, while higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability.

title: Readability versus accuracy in LLM-transformed radiology reports: stakeholder preferences across reading grade levels
outcome: Trade-off between accuracy and readability of LLM-transformed reports across reading grade levels
effect: Lower reading grades improved readability but increased errors; higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability. Preferences peaked at grade 16 and declined at grade 17, particularly among laypersons.
quote: Lower reading grades improved readability but increased errors, while higher grades improved accuracy but reduced readability.

title: Can large language models follow guidelines? A comparative study of ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek AI in clavicle fracture management based on AAOS recommendations
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to guideline-based clavicle fracture questions, rated by orthopedic surgeons
effect: Binary accuracy ChatGPT 0.93 vs DeepSeek 0.89; weighted accuracy 0.83 vs 0.79 (p > 0.05); occasional inaccuracies and hallucinations observed.
quote: Both models demonstrated generally high accuracy levels.

title: Managing a "responsibility vacuum" in AI monitoring and governance in healthcare: a qualitative study
outcome: Presence of structured monitoring of deployed AI for degradation and drift in institutions
effect: Participants recognized that AI models degrade over time from data drift, practice changes and poor generalizability, but monitoring practices remain ad hoc and fragmented, with few institutions investing in structured oversight infrastructure.
quote: However, monitoring practices remain ad hoc and fragmented, with few institutions investing in structured oversight infrastructure.

title: Managing a "responsibility vacuum" in AI monitoring and governance in healthcare: a qualitative study
outcome: Clarity of responsibility for AI maintenance and monitoring tasks
effect: Maintenance and monitoring tasks were described as poorly defined, inconsistently performed, and undervalued across healthcare systems, a 'responsibility vacuum'.
quote: This study explores the phenomenon of a "responsibility vacuum" in AI governance, wherein maintenance and monitoring tasks are poorly defined, inconsistently performed, and undervalued across healthcare systems.

title: Evaluating the effectiveness of a risk prediction model (PERSARC) on improving treatment decisions quality for patients with soft-tissue sarcomas: the VALUE-PERSARC study
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Decision-making quality (knowledge, decisional conflict) and options discussed, PERSARC vs usual care
effect: No significant differences in adequate knowledge (82% vs 86%) or decisional conflict (23.1 vs 18.9); treatment choices did not differ; multiple options discussed more often (93% vs 35%).
quote: While PERSARC did not significantly improve patients’ knowledge or decisional conflict, it led to more frequent discussion of multiple treatment options by clinicians.

title: Ethical implications of using general-purpose LLMs in clinical settings: a comparative analysis of prompt engineering strategies and their impact on patient safety
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Differential LLM recommendations by patient age and gender in identical presentations
effect: Age bias in 8 of 30 elderly responses (26.7%; OR 2.34, p=0.02); gender bias in 6 of 15 cardiovascular scenarios (40%), delayed cardiac workup for women (2.3 vs 0.8 recommendations, p=0.003).
quote: Gender bias appeared in 6 of 15 cardiovascular scenarios (40%), with female presentations receiving delayed cardiac workup recommendations despite identical risk profiles (mean delay: 2.3 vs. 0.8 recommendations before cardiac evaluation, p = 0.003).
sample_unit: LLM responses (3 models x 6 prompt strategies x 5 scenarios)

title: Ethical implications of using general-purpose LLMs in clinical settings: a comparative analysis of prompt engineering strategies and their impact on patient safety
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Biased or population-specific knowledge gaps in generated content (cultural, age, gender, socioeconomic)
effect: Bias patterns in 17 of 90 responses (18.9%); cultural bias in 7 of 15 multicultural scenarios (46.7%); residual bias 11.7% with safety-first prompting.
quote: Cultural bias affected 7 of 15 multicultural scenarios (46.7%), particularly in end-of-life discussions where Western bioethical frameworks were assumed without consideration of alternative cultural approaches to family decision-making and advance directives.
sample_unit: LLM responses (3 models x 6 prompt strategies x 5 scenarios)

title: Ethical implications of using general-purpose LLMs in clinical settings: a comparative analysis of prompt engineering strategies and their impact on patient safety
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Total clinical performance score by prompt strategy (meta-cognitive vs zero-shot)
effect: Meta-cognitive prompts scored 73.2 vs 64.8 for zero-shot (p<0.001, d=0.62); safety-first 72.1; residual safety and bias concerns persisted.
quote: This approach demonstrated significant advantages over zero-shot reasoning (64.8 ± 15.3 points, 95% CI: 58.2–71.4, 58.9%; p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 0.62) and structured reasoning (67.9 ± 13.7 points, 61.7%; p = 0.02, Cohen’s d = 0.42), with effect sizes indicating moderate to large practical significance.
sample_unit: LLM responses (3 models x 6 prompt strategies x 5 scenarios)

title: Ethical implications of using general-purpose LLMs in clinical settings: a comparative analysis of prompt engineering strategies and their impact on patient safety
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: safety incidents by case complexity
effect: Level 5: 23.1% critical safety incidents vs Level 1: 2.3%; χ² = 15.7, p < 0.001.
quote: Level 5 ethical scenarios demonstrated 23.1% critical safety incidents, compared to only 2.3% in Level 1 cases (χ² = 15.7, p < 0.001).
sample_unit: LLM responses (3 models x 6 prompt strategies x 5 scenarios)

title: Ethical implications of using general-purpose LLMs in clinical settings: a comparative analysis of prompt engineering strategies and their impact on patient safety
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: critical safety concerns
effect: 11 of 90 responses (12.2%) had critical safety concerns.
quote: Critical safety concerns, as assessed through traditional clinical error evaluation criteria, were identified in 11 of 90 responses (12.2%), with notable disparities related to case complexity.
sample_unit: LLM responses (3 models x 6 prompt strategies x 5 scenarios)

title: Ethical implications of using general-purpose LLMs in clinical settings: a comparative analysis of prompt engineering strategies and their impact on patient safety
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: communication and empathy quality
effect: Communication/empathy overall mean 10.3 ± 2.5 points, 51.5% of maximum.
quote: Significant variations emerged across evaluation domains, with communication & empathy consistently representing the lowest-performing area across all prompt strategies (overall mean: 10.3 ± 2.5 points, 51.5% of maximum).
sample_unit: LLM responses (3 models x 6 prompt strategies x 5 scenarios)

title: The Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Providing Real-Time Aid in Emergency Dental Trauma: A Clinical Validation Study
venue: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
outcome: Time-critical safety flag (accurate immediate action and contraindication advice) in emergency dental avulsion responses
effect: Safety flag present in 81% and 89% of cases across two sessions (p = 0.009), leaving roughly one in eight potentially unsafe situations.
quote: The safety flag was present in 81% and 89% of cases (χ<sup>2</sup> = 6.73, p = 0.009), with one in eight potentially unsafe situations.
sample_unit: chatbot responses (78 avulsion vignettes x 2 sessions)

title: The Performance of Artificial Intelligence in Providing Real-Time Aid in Emergency Dental Trauma: A Clinical Validation Study
venue: Dental traumatology : official publication of International Association for Dental Traumatology
outcome: Reproducibility of chatbot responses across two sessions 14 days apart
effect: Safety flag differed between sessions (81% vs 89%, p = 0.009), though inter-rater reproducibility was near perfect (ICC = 0.94).
quote: The safety flag was present in 81% and 89% of cases (χ<sup>2</sup> = 6.73, p = 0.009), with one in eight potentially unsafe situations.
sample_unit: chatbot responses (78 avulsion vignettes x 2 sessions)

title: Impact of Artificial Intelligence Triage on Radiologist Report Turnaround Time: Real-World Time Savings and Insights From Model Predictions
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Report turnaround time for PE-positive CTPA exams before vs after AI worklist prioritization
effect: Work-hour time savings 22.2 min (95% CI 5.85-38.6), significant (P=.004). Off-hour savings 2.82 min (-11.1 to 16.7), not significant (P=.345).
quote: Clinically observed time savings during work hours (22.2 [95% confidence interval: 5.85-38.6] min) were significant (P = .004), while off-hour (2.82 [-11.1 to 16.7] min) were not (P = .345).

title: Evaluating large language models in answering patient questions about eye removal surgeries
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of LLM patient education responses versus recommended levels
effect: Gemini FRE 39.0 vs ChatGPT 31.3; FKGL 11.6 vs 14.0; both exceeded recommended readability levels for patient education.
quote: Gemini provided more consistent and readable responses, but both LLMs exceeded the recommended readability levels for patient education.

title: Evaluation of a commercial deep-learning-based contouring software for CT-based gynecological brachytherapy
outcome: Interobserver agreement and contouring time, AI-assisted versus manual contouring by radiation oncologists
effect: AI-assisted interobserver agreement was better than manual for all organs and metrics; median contouring time 14.8 vs 6.9 minutes/patient (p < 0.001).
quote: AI-assisted interobserver agreement was better than manual interobserver agreement for all organs and metrics.

title: Evaluation of a commercial deep-learning-based contouring software for CT-based gynecological brachytherapy
outcome: AI versus clinical contour agreement
effect: DSC was 0.92 bladder, 0.79 rectum, 0.62 sigmoid, and 0.66 bowel.
quote: Between clinical and AI contours, DSC was 0.92, 0.79, 0.62, 0.66, for bladder, rectum, sigmoid, and bowel, respectively.

title: Evaluation of a commercial deep-learning-based contouring software for CT-based gynecological brachytherapy
outcome: AI-assisted versus manual contouring time
effect: Median time was 14.8 minutes/patient manually versus 6.9 minutes/patient AI-assisted (p < 0.001).
quote: The median time to contour all organs for manual and AI-assisted approaches was 14.8 and 6.9 minutes/patient (p < 0.001), respectively.

title: Assessment of the validity of ChatGPT-3.5 responses to patient-generated queries following BPH surgery
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-3.5 post-BPH-surgery responses graded by urology residents against predefined criteria
effect: Of 216 graded responses, 78.2% comprehensive and correct, 9.3% incomplete or partially correct, 10.2% mixed accurate and inaccurate, 2.3% entirely incorrect.
quote: Among the 216 graded responses, 78.2% were comprehensive and correct, 9.3% were incomplete or partially correct, 10.2% contained a mix of accurate and inaccurate information, and 2.3% were entirely incorrect.

title: Clinical validation of an AI-based blood testing device for diagnosis and prognosis of acute infection and sepsis
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of TriVerity versus CRP, procalcitonin, WBC, and qSOFA comparators
effect: TriVerity Bacterial AUROC 0.83 and Viral AUROC 0.91 exceeded CRP, procalcitonin and WBC; Severity score AUROC 0.78 reclassified risk compared with qSOFA alone.
quote: The TriVerity Bacterial and Viral scores had higher accuracy than C-reactive protein, procalcitonin or white blood cell count for the diagnosis of bacterial infection with area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC) of 0.83, and viral infection (AUROC = 0.91).

title: Clinical validation of an AI-based blood testing device for diagnosis and prognosis of acute infection and sepsis
outcome: Whether AI improves patient outcomes in an interventional study versus standard care
effect: Study was non-interventional; potential 60-70% reduction in inappropriate antibiotic false positives/negatives was estimated, and benefit remains unproven pending interventional testing.
quote: Further clinical testing in an interventional setting is needed to prove actionability and clinical benefit of TriVerity.

title: Quality assessment of artificial intelligence-generated versus human-written hospital summaries evaluating detail, usefulness, and continuity of care
outcome: Rubric-rated quality of LLM-drafted vs human-written discharge summaries on same hospitalizations
effect: LLM summaries outperformed human summaries across all nine criteria (p < .05); comprehensiveness median 0.62 vs -0.23. LLM performance was consistent across medical and surgical services.
quote: LLM-generated summaries outperformed human-written summaries across all criteria (p < .05), with the greatest difference observed in comprehensiveness (LLM median 0.62 vs. human -0.23).

title: The quality, accuracy, and readability of information about hidradenitis suppurativa provided by artificial intelligence: Comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Copilot, and Perplexity
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses about hidradenitis suppurativa (FRES, FKGL) versus recommended patient reading level
effect: All three chatbots produced text at college or postgraduate reading level; none achieved the necessary readability level. Copilot had better readability scores (P < .001).
quote: All the AI models had difficult reading levels as college or postgraduate.

title: The quality, accuracy, and readability of information about hidradenitis suppurativa provided by artificial intelligence: Comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Copilot, and Perplexity
outcome: Reading grade level of chatbot patient information (FKGL, FRES) relative to appropriate level
effect: None of the chatbots achieved the necessary readability level; Perplexity had higher FKGL (P = .001) and lower FRES (P = .001) in the test/procedure & drug category; outputs at college or postgraduate level.
quote: Nevertheless, none of the chatbots achieved the necessary level of readability.

title: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Diagnose Diabetic Retinopathy from Fundus Photos? A Quantitative Evaluation
outcome: MLLM diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity for diabetic retinopathy detection and grading on fundus images
effect: Binary DR detection sensitivity: ChatGPT 0.539, Perplexity 0.488, Claude 0.179, Gemini 0.042. Severity grading accuracy 0.314-0.411, sensitivity 0.184-0.247. Performance short of clinical standards.
quote: Currently, however, there is variability in the accuracy of image analysis, and diagnostic performance falls short of clinical standards for safe implementation in DR diagnosis and grading.

title: Privacy-by-Design Approach to Generate Two Virtual Clinical Trials for Multiple Sclerosis and Release Them as Open Datasets: Evaluation Study
outcome: Protection against distance-based membership inference attacks and other privacy metrics in synthetic datasets
effect: Membership inference protection was hardest privacy metric to optimize but yielded robust privacy; selected datasets had hidden rates of 85.0% and 93.2%.
quote: Protection against membership inference attacks was the hardest privacy metric to optimize, but the technique yielded robust privacy and replication of the primary end points (in 72.5% and 80.8% of the 1080 generated datasets).
sample_unit: synthetic datasets generated from two multiple sclerosis RCTs (n=865 and 1516 patients)

title: Online patient information on temporomandibular disorders provided by UK NHS hospitals: assessment and improvement of readability standards using AI-chatbots
venue: The British journal of oral & maxillofacial surgery
outcome: Readability of UK NHS online TMD patient materials versus sixth-grade target
effect: Only 12/31 met target on FKGL and 1/31 on GFI/CLI; mean FRES 64.68 (6.79).
quote: Online patient information on TMD exceeds the recommended Year Six (sixth grade in the US) reading level.
sample_unit: hospital Trust TMD patient information materials

title: Online patient information on temporomandibular disorders provided by UK NHS hospitals: assessment and improvement of readability standards using AI-chatbots
venue: The British journal of oral & maxillofacial surgery
outcome: Readability of AI-revised patient materials versus original, at sixth-grade target
effect: After Gemini revision, 96.8% met target per FKGL, 54.8% per GFI, 29.0% per CLI; mean FRES improved to 82.59 (5.73), p<0.001.
quote: AI chatbots, particularly Gemini, can significantly enhance the readability of these materials, enabling them to meet health literacy standards according to certain readability tools.
sample_unit: hospital Trust TMD patient information materials

title: Machine learning model for differentiating xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis and gallbladder cancer in multicenter largescale study
outcome: AUC in internal validation versus external testing
effect: AUC 0.94 in internal validation dropped to 0.88 in external testing.
quote: LIDGAX achieved area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.94 (internal validation) and 0.88 (external testing), outperforming the other five ML models.

title: Machine learning model for differentiating xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis and gallbladder cancer in multicenter largescale study
outcome: AI diagnostic performance and time versus six radiologists on the same cases
effect: LIDGAX improved sensitivity by 1.2-8.5%, specificity by 0.0-4.6%, and balanced accuracy by 1.8-6.6% versus radiologists. It reduced diagnostic time by 30.44-35.76 s per patient.
quote: Compared to six radiologists, LIDGAX improved sensitivity (1.2-8.5%), specificity (0.0-4.6%), and balanced accuracy (1.8-6.6%), while reducing average diagnostic time per patient by 30.44-35.76 s.

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: AUROC after retraining model on local VHA data versus external validation
effect: Retraining increased AUROC in the target cohort from 0.70 to 0.82 (0.12 shift), improving most subgroups, though opioid-exposed disparities persisted.
quote: In Stage 3, retraining the model increased AUROC in the target cohort from 0.70 to 0.82 (0.12 shift).

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: Subgroup gaps masked by aggregate metrics
effect: Forest plots revealed subgroup-level disparities masked by overall cohort metrics; opioid-exposed subgroup had greatest performance and net benefit degradation.
quote: Forest plots revealed subgroup-level disparities in performance that were masked by overall cohort metrics.

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: Effect of development vs local population differences on performance
effect: Outcome prevalence rose from 14.65% to 34.34% (P < .001); higher VHA prevalence reduced AUROC and increased subgroup disparities.
quote: The higher prevalence of POU in the VHA population biased model predictions and contributed to reduced AUROC and increased subgroup disparities during external validation.

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: AUROC drop of prolonged opioid use model from internal to external VHA data
effect: AUROC dropped from 0.74 in Stage 1 to 0.70 in Stage 2 (6% reduction, P < .001); outcome prevalence rose from 14.65% to 34.34%.
quote: In Figure 2 , AUROC dropped from 0.74 in Stage 1 to 0.70 in Stage 2 (6% reduction, P < .001).

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: Subgroup performance disparities in external validation and after retraining
effect: Stage 2 disparities: opioid-naive 0.68 vs opioid-exposed 0.63, Hispanic 0.68 vs non-Hispanic 0.70; disparities persisted for opioid-exposed after retraining.
quote: Predictive performance in Stage 1 was equal across groups, but Stage 2 showed disparities: Hispanic 0.68 vs non-Hispanic 0.70 ( P < .001), opioid-naive 0.68 vs opioid-exposed 0.63 ( P < .001), depression 0.68 vs non-depression 0.69 ( P < .001), and mild comorbidity 0.71 vs severe comorbidity 0.69 ( P < .001).

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: Model performance when applied to new population (VHA) beyond development setting
effect: AUROC fell from 0.74 to 0.70, subgroup disparities increased, and net-benefit threshold range shifted from [0.1-0.5] to [0.2-0.6].
quote: This shows the model’s performance sensitivity to outcome distribution shifts in real-world settings.

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: Clinical utility via standardized net benefit across subgroups and thresholds
effect: Net benefit range shifted from [0.1-0.5] to [0.2-0.6]; opioid-exposed required threshold ~0.5 vs ~0.2 in the general cohort, revealing utility loss not seen in AUROC.
quote: For example, opioid-exposed patients required a threshold probability of ∼.5 to achieve net benefit from the model, compared to ∼.2 in the general cohort.

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: Calibration and subgroup miscalibration in external validation
effect: Model overestimates higher probabilities, and underestimates probabilities below 0.6 in opioid-exposed subgroup in Stage 2; depression and opioid-exposed showed most miscalibration.
quote: This situation varies in the opioid-exposed subgroup, where the model underestimates probabilities below 0.6 in Stage 2.

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: External validation AUROC
effect: AUROC dropped from 0.74 to 0.70 in Stage 2 (6% reduction, P < .001).
quote: In Figure 2 , AUROC dropped from 0.74 in Stage 1 to 0.70 in Stage 2 (6% reduction, P < .001).

title: Evaluating the impact of data biases on algorithmic fairness and clinical utility of machine learning models for prolonged opioid use prediction
outcome: AUROC drop on external validation
effect: AUROC dropped from 0.74 in Stage 1 internal validation to 0.70 in Stage 2 external validation, representing a 6% reduction (P < .001).
quote: In Figure 2 , AUROC dropped from 0.74 in Stage 1 to 0.70 in Stage 2 (6% reduction, P < .001).

title: eXplainable artificial intelligence-Eval: A framework for comparative evaluation of explanation methods in healthcare
outcome: Fidelity, stability and complexity of local and global explanation methods on healthcare datasets
effect: RuleFit and RuleMatrix gave robust, interpretable global explanations across tasks; local methods varied by evaluation dimension and dataset, with trade-offs between fidelity, stability and complexity. No numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: Our findings highlight important trade-offs between fidelity, stability, and complexity, offering critical insights into method suitability for clinical applications.

title: Evaluation of reliability, repeatability, and confidence of ChatGPT for screening, monitoring, and treatment of interstitial lung disease in patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT reliability across three repeated attempts
effect: GPT-4 showed significant variability in reliability across three attempts (P = .007); GPT-4o mini and GPT-4o showed no significant differences.
quote: GPT-4 demonstrated significant variability in reliability across the three attempts (P = .007).

title: Evaluation of reliability, repeatability, and confidence of ChatGPT for screening, monitoring, and treatment of interstitial lung disease in patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases
outcome: Overconfidence: high confidence scores assigned to incorrect answers
effect: Overconfidence percentage was 100% (22 of 22) for GPT-4o and 22.7% (10 of 44) for GPT-4o mini (P < .01).
quote: Furthermore, the overconfidence percentage (confidence score of ≥8 assigned to incorrect answers) was 100% (22 of 22) for GPT-4o and 22.7% (10 of 44) for GPT-4o mini, respectively (P < .01).

title: Assessing the validity of ChatGPT-4o and Google Gemini Advanced when responding to frequently asked questions in endodontics
venue: Journal of applied oral science : revista FOB
outcome: Expert-rated validity of chatbot answers to endodontic FAQs at lenient and strict thresholds
effect: Low threshold: both models 95% validity (95% CI 75.1%-99.9%). High threshold: ChatGPT-4o 35% (15.4%-59.2%), Gemini Advanced 40% (19.1%-63.9%), p=1.
quote: At the low threshold, both models obtained 95% validity (95% CI: 75.1%- 99.9%; p=.05).

title: Use of Ambient AI Scribes to Reduce Administrative Burden and Professional Burnout
outcome: Clinician burnout and after-hours documentation time before and after 30 days of ambient AI scribe use
effect: Burnout fell from 51.9% to 38.8% (OR 0.26; 95% CI 0.13-0.54). After-hours documentation time improved by a mean (SE) of 0.90 (0.19) hours.
quote: After 30 days with the ambient AI scribe, the proportion of participants experiencing burnout decreased significantly from 51.9% to 38.8% (odds ratio, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.13-0.54).

title: Accuratezza e affidabilità di GPT-4 nel rispondere alle domande dei pazienti su malattie dermatologiche: uno studio sul ruolo dell’intelligenza artificiale nell’assistenza digitale ai pazienti
outcome: Accuracy and safety of GPT-4o mini answers to dermatology patient questions versus specialists
effect: Some answers contained inaccuracies that could lead to risky patient management; authors suggest retrieval from reliable sources to improve safety and accuracy.
quote: While GPT-4o mini provided clearer and more updated information, some answers contained inaccuracies that could lead to risky patient management.

title: Evaluating the Reliability and Readability of AI Chatbot Responses for Microtia Patient Education
outcome: SMOG readability of chatbot responses to microtia patient questions
effect: Average SMOG 15.93 (SD=1.94), undergraduate reading level; OpenEvidence worst at 18.06, ChatGPT 16.32, Gemini 14.73, DeepSeek 14.63.
quote: Overall, the average DISCERN and SMOG scores across all platforms were 32.19 (SD=4.43) and 15.93 (SD=1.94), respectively, indicating a good quality and an undergraduate reading level.

title: Evaluating the Reliability and Readability of AI Chatbot Responses for Microtia Patient Education
outcome: Reading level of chatbot patient education responses versus appropriate user reading level
effect: Mean SMOG 15.93 across platforms (undergraduate level); all four platforms exceeded typical patient reading levels, OpenEvidence highest at 18.06.
quote: OpenEvidence had the worst readability (M=18.06, SD=1.12), followed by ChatGPT (M=16.32, SD=1.41).

title: Patient Perceptions on Operative Reports Written by Surgeons versus Versions Simplified by Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Patient preference and comprehension of AI-simplified versus original operative reports
effect: 55.4% preferred GPT-simplified reports; clearer (1.53 vs 1.98, P<0.001), more accessible terminology (1.50 vs 2.31, P<0.001), more understandable (86.40 vs 73.70, P<0.001).
quote: The primary outcome showed that 55.4% (95% CI: 48.6%-61.2%) of participants preferred the GPT-simplified reports for being significantly clearer (mean = 1.53 ± 0.83 vs. 1.98 ± 1.92, P < 0.001), terminology being more accessible (mean = 1.50 ± 0.70 vs. 2.31 ± 0.89, P < 0.001), and overall, more understandable (mean = 86.40 ± 18.07 vs. 73.70 ± 20.82, P < 0.001).

title: Evaluation of prostate cancer pathology reports generated by ChatGPT to enhance patient comprehension
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of AI-generated versus original pathology reports; patient and urologist ratings
effect: AI biopsy and surgical reports had higher Flesch Reading Ease Scores (49 ± 5; 50 ± 3) than originals (31 ± 15, p < 0.001; 41 ± 17, p = 0.02). 88% of patients found AI biopsy reports helpful for understanding diagnosis.
quote: The AI-generated biopsy and surgical pathology reports had higher mean Flesch Reading Ease Scores (49 ± 5; 50 ± 3) compared to the original reports (31 ± 15, p < 0.001; 41 ± 17, p = 0.02, respectively).

title: A longitudinal analysis of declining medical safety messaging in generative AI models
outcome: Presence of medical disclaimers warning of possible inaccuracy in LLM and VLM outputs across model generations
effect: LLM disclaimer presence fell from 26.3% (2022) to 0.97% (2025); VLM disclaimer rates fell from 19.6% (2023) to 1.05%. By 2025 most models displayed no disclaimers.
quote: Disclaimer presence in LLM outputs dropped from 26.3% in 2022 to 0.97% in 2025, while VLM disclaimer rates declined from 19.6% in 2023 to 1.05%.
sample_unit: inputs (500 mammograms, 500 chest X-rays, 500 dermatology images, 500 medical questions)

title: Quantifying Epistemic Uncertainty in Predictions for Safer Health AI Performance Under Dataset Shifts
venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
outcome: Whether uncertainty screening flags out-of-distribution samples that drive prediction errors
effect: Sample-level epistemic uncertainty threshold flagged potential OOD samples and captured most prediction errors, with no retraining required.
quote: Results across all training-test time pairs show that samples below this threshold exhibit consistently higher macro-F1 and render performance virtually invariant to temporal drift, while the flagged samples captured most prediction errors.

title: Quantifying Epistemic Uncertainty in Predictions for Safer Health AI Performance Under Dataset Shifts
venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
outcome: Flagging out-of-distribution prediction errors
effect: Using a 95% uncertainty threshold, below-threshold samples had consistently higher macro-F1, while flagged samples captured most prediction errors.
quote: Results across all training-test time pairs show that samples below this threshold exhibit consistently higher macro-F1 and render performance virtually invariant to temporal drift, while the flagged samples captured most prediction errors.

title: Quantifying Epistemic Uncertainty in Predictions for Safer Health AI Performance Under Dataset Shifts
venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
outcome: macro-F1 and prediction error capture under temporal drift
effect: samples below 95% uncertainty threshold had consistently higher macro-F1 and performance invariant to temporal drift, while flagged samples captured most errors
quote: Results across all training-test time pairs show that samples below this threshold exhibit consistently higher macro-F1 and render performance virtually invariant to temporal drift, while the flagged samples captured most prediction errors.

title: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4 Plus in Providing Information on Oral Cancer Management
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of ChatGPT-4 Plus answers to oral cancer diagnosis, treatment, recovery, prevention questions
effect: 63% of 65 responses were Score 1, none Score 4. Score 1 was 72% in Recovery, 62% Treatment, 60% Prevention, 55% Diagnosis. Scores 2 and 3 were highest in Diagnosis (45%). ICC 0.85 to 0.93.
quote: Among 65 questions, 63% of responses were Score 1, with none rated as Score 4.

title: Application of Large Language Models in TN Staging and Treatment Response Evaluation for Patients With Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Comparative Performance Analysis of ChatGPT-4o-Latest and DeepSeek-V3-0324
venue: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
outcome: Radiologist efficiency and performance with versus without LLM assistance
effect: Four radiologists assessed 68 cases with and without LLM assistance; significant time-efficiency improvements across all radiologists with LLM assistance (p < 0.001); diagnostic consistency may improve, especially for junior clinicians.
quote: Significant improvements in time efficiency were observed across all radiologists with LLM assistance (p < 0.001).
sample_unit: patients (831 reports) in test set; 68 cases in reader study

title: Application of Large Language Models in TN Staging and Treatment Response Evaluation for Patients With Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Comparative Performance Analysis of ChatGPT-4o-Latest and DeepSeek-V3-0324
venue: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
outcome: Accuracy comparison of two LLMs against radiologist reference standard for NPC staging
effect: DeepSeek-V3-0324 outperformed GPT-4o-latest in TRE-1 (96.5% vs. 82.9%, p < 0.001); no significant difference for T staging, N staging, or TRE-2.
quote: DeepSeek-V3-0324 significantly outperformed GPT-4o-latest in TRE-1 staging (96.5% vs. 82.9%, p < 0.001).
sample_unit: patients (831 reports) in test set; 68 cases in reader study

title: Quality and Readability Analysis of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Medical Information Related to Prostate Cancer: A Cross-Sectional Study of ChatGPT and DeepSeek
venue: The world journal of men's health
outcome: Readability of AI-generated prostate cancer patient information (ARI, Flesch, Gunning Fog, FKGL)
effect: DeepSeek ARI higher than ChatGPT (12.63±1.42 vs 10.85±1.93, p<0.001), indicating greater textual complexity and reading difficulty; both above typical patient reading levels.
quote: However, the ARI for DeepSeek was higher than that for ChatGPT (12.63±1.42 vs. 10.85±1.93, p<0.001), indicating greater textual complexity and reading difficulty.

title: Assessment of Preferences for Delivery of Spine Care Information: A ChatGPT and Survey-Based Study
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient materials relative to recommended 5th-6th grade level
effect: ChatGPT output exceeded intended reading levels; only 22.1% chose 8th-12th grade and 50.6% chose postgraduate-level text; authors recommend targeting 8th-12th grade or lower, above AMA 5th-6th grade guidance.
quote: Similar to previous work, we found that ChatGPT often generates content above the intended reading level.

title: Assessment of Preferences for Delivery of Spine Care Information: A ChatGPT and Survey-Based Study
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-generated spine care answers versus requested reading level
effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade levels were consistently higher than target levels (e.g., PreK-3rd prompts averaged FK 7.3; 8th-12th prompts averaged 13.4); FRE scores 73.7 to 4.1 across levels.
quote: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level scores, however, were consistently higher than the target levels ChatGPT was instructed to emulate ( Table 2 ).

title: Better understanding: can a large language model safely improve readability of patient information leaflets in interventional radiology?
outcome: Reading grade level of original versus LLM-simplified patient leaflets versus recommended grade 6
effect: LLM-modified PILs mean reading grade 9.5±0.5 vs original 11.1±0.1 (p<0.01); recommended grade 6 not achieved.
quote: However, the recommended reading grade of 6 (expected to be understood by 11- to 12-year-old children) was not achieved.

title: Better understanding: can a large language model safely improve readability of patient information leaflets in interventional radiology?
outcome: Readability of LLM-generated plain-language patient materials
effect: LLM-simplified leaflets reduced reading grade to 9.5±0.5 from 11.1±0.1 but remained above the recommended grade 6.
quote: However, the recommended reading grade of 6 (expected to be understood by 11- to 12-year-old children) was not achieved.

title: Better understanding: can a large language model safely improve readability of patient information leaflets in interventional radiology?
outcome: Factual accuracy of LLM-modified leaflets as rated by consultant radiologists
effect: Most LLM-modified PILs had minor factual accuracy concerns identified by three consultant radiologists; no errors that could cause serious patient harm detected.
quote: Human evaluation revealed that most LLM-modified PILs had minor concerns regarding factual accuracy, but no errors that could result in serious patient harm were detected.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Clinical Nutrition: A Descriptive Comparison of ChatGPT- and Dietitian-Planned Diets for Chronic Disease Scenarios
venue: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
outcome: Safety and nutritional adequacy of ChatGPT diet plans versus dietitian plans, including contraindicated foods
effect: ChatGPT diets had notable deficiencies in meeting energy and nutrient requirements, lacked personalization, and in several cases included contraindicated foods.
quote: In several cases, contraindicated foods were included.

title: Application of Large Language Models in Complex Clinical Cases: Cross-Sectional Evaluation Study
outcome: Hallucination rates of LLM clinical decision recommendations in complex cases
effect: Deepseek-R1 6/80 (8%) and GPTo1 5/80 (6%) lowest; GPT-4o 7/80 (9%), Kimi 10/80 (12%); Gemini and LLaMa3 13/80 (16%) to 25/80 (31%).
quote: Deepseek-R1 and GPTo1 demonstrated the lowest hallucination rates-6/80 (8%) and 5/80 (6%), respectively-significantly outperforming GPT-4o (7/80, 9%), Kimi (10/80, 12%), and the Gemini and LLaMa3 models, which exhibited substantially higher rates ranging from 13/80 (16%) to 25/80 (31%).

title: Evaluating AI-Generated Meal Plans for Simulated Diabetes Profiles: A Guideline-Based Comparison of Three Language Models
venue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
outcome: Hallucinated or ungrounded clinical content in LLM-generated diabetes meal plans
effect: Frequent hallucinations and lack of clinical contextualization were noted across the three LLMs; RAG integration was identified as a potential improvement but was not tested.
quote: Frequent hallucinations and lack of clinical contextualization were noted.

title: Evaluating AI-Generated Meal Plans for Simulated Diabetes Profiles: A Guideline-Based Comparison of Three Language Models
venue: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
outcome: Concordance of LLM dietary plans with T2DM guidelines and the nutrition care process
effect: None of the models fully matched the NCP framework, particularly diagnosis and monitoring. Energy alignment was 70.9% for ChatGPT-4.1 and 83.1% for Grok-3. There were fat overestimation, micronutrient shortfalls, and carbohydrate underdelivery.
quote: None of the models demonstrated full concordance with the NCP framework, particularly in the diagnosis and monitoring components.

title: Artificial intelligence in endocrine practice: comparing ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude for adrenal incidentaloma care
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of LLM responses on adrenal incidentaloma queries
effect: High text complexity across models, with Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 10.6-17.4.
quote: Readability analysis revealed high text complexity (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level: 10.6-17.4), and inter-rater reliability was excellent (intraclass correlation coefficient: 0.876-0.961, p < 0.001).
sample_unit: questions and case scenarios (34 guideline questions, 4 cases)

title: Invisible Bias in GPT-4o-mini: Detecting Disparities in AI-Generated Patient Messaging
outcome: Differences in LLM-scored message quality across synthetic patient history attributes
effect: Patient sex and religious preference had a statistically significant impact on scores for empathy, encouragement, accuracy, clarity, professionalism and respect. No numbers are given in the abstract.
quote: A patient's sex and religious preference were found to have a statistically significant impact on scores.

title: Large Language Models Versus Human Readers in CAD-RADS 2.0 Categorization of Coronary CT Angiography Reports
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Full CAD-RADS categorization accuracy of LLMs versus human readers on same reports
effect: O1 90.7% accuracy vs GPT-4o 73.8%, GPT-4 59.7%, GPT-3.5-turbo 25.8%, fellow 83.3%, resident 1 83.3%; no significant difference vs cardiac radiologist (86.1%; P = 0.12) and resident 2 (89.4%; P = 0.68).
quote: However, there was no significant difference in accuracy when compared to the cardiac radiologist (86.1%; P = 0.12) and resident 2 (89.4%; P = 0.68).

title: Large Language Models Versus Human Readers in CAD-RADS 2.0 Categorization of Coronary CT Angiography Reports
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: O1 accuracy on external validation dataset from two independent institutions
effect: O1 achieved 95.7% accuracy for full CAD-RADS categorization in the external validation dataset (n = 327).
quote: In the external validation dataset (n = 327) derived from two independent institutions, O1 achieved 95.7% accuracy for full CAD-RADS categorization.

title: AI-Based System for Analysis of Electron Microscope Images in Glomerular Disease
outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance on TEM images
effect: TEM-AID accuracy 0.886 (95% CI, 0.859-0.912) exceeded clinicians' unaided performance; clinicians' accuracy improved by a mean (SD) of 11.7% (5.2%) with TEM-AID.
quote: Clinicians' accuracy improved by a mean (SD) of 11.7% (5.2%) when they used TEM-AID.

title: AI-Based System for Analysis of Electron Microscope Images in Glomerular Disease
outcome: Classification accuracy in internal versus external multicenter test sets
effect: Accuracy 0.911 (95% CI, 0.904-0.918) internally and 0.895 to 0.914 across external tests; macro-AUC 0.972 to 0.989 across cohorts.
quote: Subtype classification accuracy was 0.911 (95% CI, 0.904-0.918) in internal validation and 0.895 to 0.914 in external tests.

title: Bias or Best Fit? A Comparative Analysis of the SEER and NCDB Data Sets in Single-model Machine Learning for Predicting Osteosarcoma Survival Outcomes
outcome: AUC on internal versus external validation across databases
effect: Internal AUC 0.90-0.93; external AUC fell to 0.56-0.67 (NCDB models on SEER 0.67/0.60; SEER models on NCDB 0.61/0.56).
quote: However, external validation revealed poor transferability: NCDB models tested on SEER data achieved an AUC of 0.67 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.68) and 0.60 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.62), while SEER models tested on NCDB data achieved 0.61 (95% CI 0.59 to 0.62) and 0.56 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.58).

title: Bias or Best Fit? A Comparative Analysis of the SEER and NCDB Data Sets in Single-model Machine Learning for Predicting Osteosarcoma Survival Outcomes
outcome: Generalization of models to a new population/data context
effect: External validation AUC <0.70 (0.56-0.67) vs internal 0.90-0.93, indicating failure to generalize.
quote: Cross-database application of models leads to poor predictive performance and should be avoided without revalidation.

title: Bias or Best Fit? A Comparative Analysis of the SEER and NCDB Data Sets in Single-model Machine Learning for Predicting Osteosarcoma Survival Outcomes
outcome: Performance of models on data from a different database/population than training
effect: Cross-database AUCs of 0.56-0.67 versus internal >0.90, described as poor and unsuitable for clinical decision-making.
quote: This dramatic performance drop demonstrates that models cannot be reliably transferred between different healthcare databases.

title: Bias or Best Fit? A Comparative Analysis of the SEER and NCDB Data Sets in Single-model Machine Learning for Predicting Osteosarcoma Survival Outcomes
outcome: external validation transferability
effect: Internal AUCs were 0.93/0.91 (NCDB) and 0.90/0.92 (SEER); external AUCs were 0.67/0.60 and 0.61/0.56.
quote: However, external validation revealed poor transferability: NCDB models tested on SEER data achieved an AUC of 0.67 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.68) and 0.60 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.62), while SEER models tested on NCDB data achieved 0.61 (95% CI 0.59 to 0.62) and 0.56 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.58).

title: Human-Machine Agreement in Medical Ethics: Patient Autonomy Case-Based Evaluation of Large Language Models
outcome: LLM answer agreement against physician-panel reference standard before improvement
effect: Before improvement, LLMs matched physician consensus on 27 (ChatGPT), 22 (Gemini), and 26 (LLaMA) of 44 cases; agreement slight to fair.
quote: There was slight agreement between the foundational Gemini and the physician consensus (κ=0), slight agreement between the foundational LLaMA and the physician consensus (κ=0.14), and fair agreement between the foundational ChatGPT and the physician consensus (κ=0.32).

title: A novel gradient inversion attack framework to investigate privacy vulnerabilities during retinal image-based federated learning
outcome: Identification of training participants from reconstructed retinal images via gradient inversion attack in federated learning
effect: Across all models, over 92% of training-set participants could be identified from reconstructed retinal vessel structure alone; with differential privacy, substantial information could still be extracted.
quote: Experimental results for the task of retinal age prediction demonstrate that, across all models, over 92 % of the participants in the training set could be identified from their reconstructed retinal vessel structure alone.

title: Evaluating a retrieval-augmented pregnancy chatbot: a comprehensibility-accuracy-readability study of the DIAN AI assistant
outcome: Women's vs clinicians' Likert ratings of comprehensibility, accuracy, readability of chatbot responses
effect: Differences concentrated in postpartum care: comprehensibility favored women (p=0.012), accuracy favored women (p=0.018), readability favored clinicians (p=0.008); other domains showed no significant differences after correction.
quote: Other domains showed no significant between-group differences after correction.
sample_unit: evaluators (119 women, 29 clinicians) rating chatbot responses

title: Incidental pulmonary embolism in abdominal CT: detection rate and characteristics with artificial intelligence
outcome: AI sensitivity for incidental pulmonary embolism in a randomly selected manually reviewed subset
effect: Sensitivity was 40% (95% CI 16-68) with 100% specificity; iPE prevalence in the subset was 1.7% (15/874). The AI missed most iPE cases in the reviewed subset.
quote: In the manually reviewed randomly selected subset, iPE prevalence was 1.7% (15/874, 95% confidence interval: 1.0-2.8%) with AI having 40% sensitivity (95% CI, 16-68) and 100% specificity (95% CI, 99.5-100).

title: The Potential of AI in Nursing Care: Multicenter Evaluation in Fall Risk Assessment
outcome: AI fall risk model AUROC versus rule-based clinical systems on same data
effect: AI models consistently outperformed rule-based systems in all setups; AUROC 0.735 (90% CI 0.727-0.744) geriatric hospital, 0.926 (90% CI 0.924-0.928) university hospital.
quote: Our findings demonstrate that AI models consistently outperform rule-based systems across all experimental setups, with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.735 (90% CI 0.727-0.744) for the geriatric hospital, and 0.926 (90% CI 0.924-0.928) for the university hospital.

title: The Potential of AI in Nursing Care: Multicenter Evaluation in Fall Risk Assessment
outcome: Generalization of models across hospitals with demographic and label distribution differences
effect: Demographic shifts and label distribution imbalances limited federated learning models' ability to generalize; FL did not improve fall risk prediction.
quote: However, it also reveals the challenges related to demographic shifts and label distribution imbalances, which limited the FL models' ability to generalize.

title: The Potential of AI in Nursing Care: Multicenter Evaluation in Fall Risk Assessment
outcome: Model fairness across sex and age subgroups
effect: No performance disparities between sex groups, but fairness infringements found across age groups.
quote: Our fairness analysis ruled out disparities in model performance between different sex groups, but we found fairness infringements across age groups.

title: InfoOOD: information bottleneck optimization for post hoc medical image out-of-distribution detection
outcome: OOD detection AUC for simulated CT artifacts, InfoOOD vs established OOD detectors
effect: InfoOOD AUC 0.93 vs 0.57 for embedded feature-based measures (strong rings artifact); AUC 0.75 vs 0.61 for reconstruction-based measure (weak sparse view artifact).
quote: TheInfoOODmeasure consistently outperformed the embedded feature-based measures in detecting OOD data (e.g. AUC = 0.93 vs. AUC = 0.57 for the strong rings artifact) and surpassed the reconstruction-based measure across weak magnitude artifacts (e.g., AUC = 0.75 vs. AUC = 0.61 for the weak sparse view artifact).
sample_unit: test CT images (40 with simulated artifacts plus 131 for correlation analysis)

title: InfoOOD: information bottleneck optimization for post hoc medical image out-of-distribution detection
outcome: Segmentation performance under simulated low-dose, sparse-view, and ring artifacts
effect: Artifact simulation significantly degraded segmentation performance across all artifact types and magnitudes (p<0.001), worsening as magnitude increased.
quote: Artifact simulation significantly degraded segmentation model performance across all artifact types and magnitudes (ρ< 0.001), with model performance worsening as artifact magnitude increased.
sample_unit: test CT images (40 with simulated artifacts plus 131 for correlation analysis)

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Algorithms Improve Care of Patients with AAA
outcome: Initial AAA evaluation after AI detection with defined referral workflow vs pre-AI
effect: Initial evaluation 42% vs. 18% (P < 0.001); evaluation timeline 22 vs. 83 days (P = 0.1); long-term follow-up 45% vs. 30% (P = 0.004)
quote: A greater proportion of patients underwent initial AAA evaluation after implementation of AI-assisted AAA care (42% vs. 18%, P < 0.001).

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Algorithms Improve Care of Patients with AAA
outcome: Long-term follow-up and scheduled monitoring for AI-detected AAA patients
effect: Long-term follow-up 45% vs. 30% (P = 0.004); scheduled monitoring appointments 99% vs. 65% (P < 0.001)
quote: A greater proportion of patients in the post-AI protocol group had long-term follow-up (45% vs. 30%, P = 0.004) and had scheduled appointments for long-term AAA monitoring (99% vs. 65%, P < 0.001).

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Algorithms Improve Care of Patients with AAA
outcome: initial AAA evaluation rate
effect: 42% of patients received initial evaluation post-AI compared to 18% pre-AI.
quote: A greater proportion of patients underwent initial AAA evaluation after implementation of AI-assisted AAA care (42% vs. 18%, P < 0.001).

title: Continuous predicted risks should be retained when deploying clinical prediction models
outcome: PPV, sensitivity, mean rank of true positives when ranking by predicted risk versus risk groups under resource constraints
effect: Ranking patients by predicted probabilities gave better performance than risk groups alone; benefits grew with discrimination and prevalence and were greatest when resource constraints were highest.
quote: Using predicted probabilities to rank patients by predicted risk led to model performance benefits when compared to risk groups alone.

title: Deep learning based semi-automated model can predict lineage in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
outcome: Lineage accuracy: fully automated vs routing low-confidence cases to IHC/pathologist review
effect: Fully automated model had a 16.1% accuracy decrease in the prospective cohort (p<0.001). Semi-automated routing gave 95.9% accuracy, comparable to full manual review (p=0.610), with 68.9% workload reduction.
quote: This significant decrease in manual labor was accompanied by 95.9% in overall accuracy (Fig. 3 ), which was statistically comparable ( p = 0.610) to that achieved through fully IHC staining and manual evaluation by pathologists.

title: Deep learning based semi-automated model can predict lineage in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
outcome: External-cohort accuracy after raising the confidence threshold
effect: Raising the cut-off from 0.8 to 0.9 improved accuracy from 86.0% to 95.1%, comparable to manual evaluation (p=0.293). Workload reduction fell to 39.3%.
quote: Under this scenario, although the workload reduction was only 39.3%, the accuracy significantly improved to 95.1%.

title: Deep learning based semi-automated model can predict lineage in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and workload reduction with confidence-based deferral to IHC and manual review
effect: In the prospective cohort, confidence-based deferral achieved 68.9% workload reduction and 95.9% overall accuracy; comparison with fully manual IHC-based evaluation: p = 0.610.
quote: In prospective validation, this approach achieved a 68.9% reduction in diagnostic workload while maintaining 95.9% overall accuracy.

title: Deep learning based semi-automated model can predict lineage in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
outcome: Classification accuracy in external institutions with heterogeneous histopathological protocols
effect: Prospective-cohort accuracy was 95.9%; external-cohort accuracy was 86.0% at a confidence cut-off of 0.8, among 206 patients from four external centers.
quote: In the external cohort comprising 206 patients from four external centers, the implementation of the semi-automated approach with a confidence cut-off of 0.8 yielded an accuracy of 86.0% (Fig. 3 ).

title: Deep learning based semi-automated model can predict lineage in patients with pituitary neuroendocrine tumors
outcome: diagnostic accuracy
effect: Using the fully automated model as a stand-alone diagnostic resulted in a 5.9% decrease in accuracy compared to standard-of-care manual review.
quote: However, it demonstrated a 5.9% decrease in accuracy and a 0.011 reduction in the AUC ( p < 0.001), compared to diagnoses based on IHC and manual review (Fig. 2 ).

title: The Utility of ChatGPT for Assisting Patients with Study Preparation and Report Interpretation of Myocardial Viability Scintigraphy: Exploring the Future of AI-driven Patient Comprehension in Nuclear Medicine
venue: Indian journal of nuclear medicine : IJNM : the official journal of the Society of Nuclear Medicine, India
outcome: Validity of references cited in ChatGPT responses
effect: Reference validity remained an issue, as only one response had a valid reference.
quote: Reference validity remained an issue, as only one response had a valid reference.
sample_unit: mock myocardial viability reports (plus 14 preparation questions and 2 report questions, each repeated twice)

title: The Utility of ChatGPT for Assisting Patients with Study Preparation and Report Interpretation of Myocardial Viability Scintigraphy: Exploring the Future of AI-driven Patient Comprehension in Nuclear Medicine
venue: Indian journal of nuclear medicine : IJNM : the official journal of the Society of Nuclear Medicine, India
outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT responses across repeated regenerations of the same prompt
effect: Consistency scored lower for preparation prompts (1.14 ± 0.66) than report prompts (1.67 ± 0.49); inconsistent responses mandate supervised use.
quote: However, empathy and consistency had lower scores in preparations (1.43 ± 0.76; 1.14 ± 0.66) than in report prompts (1.58 ± 0.51; 1.67 ± 0.49).
sample_unit: mock myocardial viability reports (plus 14 preparation questions and 2 report questions, each repeated twice)

title: OphthoACR (Ophthalmology Automated Chart Review): An AI-Powered Tool for Complete Automation of Ophthalmology Chart Reviews and Cohort Data Analysis
outcome: Accuracy of AI chart review versus manual review for extracting variables
effect: OphthoACR achieved 94% accuracy in extracting variables of interest, significantly outperforming manual review (83%); 97% specificity, 92% sensitivity, Cohen's κ 0.70.
quote: OphthoACR achieved 94% accuracy in extracting variables of interest, significantly outperforming manual review (83%).

title: Adversarial prompt and fine-tuning attacks threaten medical large language models
outcome: Vulnerability of medical LLMs to prompt injection with malicious instructions across prevention, diagnosis, treatment tasks
effect: Both open-source and proprietary LLMs were vulnerable to malicious manipulation across the three medical tasks; no numeric results in the abstract.
quote: Utilizing real-world patient data, we demonstrate that both open-source and proprietary LLMs are vulnerable to malicious manipulation across multiple tasks.

title: Adversarial prompt and fine-tuning attacks threaten medical large language models
outcome: Vulnerability of medical LLMs to fine-tuning with poisoned samples
effect: Poisoned fine-tuning data did not markedly degrade overall benchmark performance but produced noticeable shifts in fine-tuned model weights; models were vulnerable to manipulation.
quote: We discover that while integrating poisoned data does not markedly degrade overall model performance on medical benchmarks, it can lead to noticeable shifts in fine-tuned model weights, suggesting a potential pathway for detecting and countering model attacks.

title: Evaluation of large language model-generated medical information on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid) of LLM-generated IPF medical information
effect: Both ChatGPT-4 and Gemini 1.5 Pro responses were rated difficult to understand on readability evaluations.
quote: Readability analyses found that AI-generated medical information was difficult to understand, stressing the need to refine it.

title: Evaluation of large language model-generated medical information on idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
outcome: Concordance of LLM answers with ATS/ERS/JRS/ALAT IPF guidelines (0-4 scale)
effect: Gemini higher than ChatGPT-4: median 3.0 [3.0-3.5] vs 3.0 [2.5-3.0], p=0.0029; neither model fully concordant with guidelines.
quote: Nevertheless, neither model provided answers in full concordance with established clinical guidelines, and their readability remained a major challenge.

title: Performance of Large Language Models in Diagnosing Rare Hematologic Diseases and the Impact of Their Diagnostic Outputs on Physicians: Combined Retrospective and Prospective Study
outcome: Physician diagnostic accuracy with versus without LLM assistance, and effect of biased LLM outputs
effect: LLMs significantly improved diagnostic accuracy of less-experienced physicians; no significant benefit for specialists. When LLMs gave biased responses, physician performance often failed to improve or declined.
quote: In the prospective phase, LLMs significantly improved the diagnostic accuracy of less-experienced physicians; no significant benefit was observed for specialists.
sample_unit: nonpublic real-world admission records (retrospective phase); 28 physicians diagnosing 5 cases each (prospective phase)

title: Performance of Large Language Models in Diagnosing Rare Hematologic Diseases and the Impact of Their Diagnostic Outputs on Physicians: Combined Retrospective and Prospective Study
outcome: Ranking stability of LLM diagnoses across repeated runs (Jaccard similarity, entropy)
