effect: Higher accuracy often correlated with lower ranking stability across most LLMs.
quote: Interestingly, higher accuracy often correlated with lower ranking stability across most LLMs.
sample_unit: nonpublic real-world admission records (retrospective phase); 28 physicians diagnosing 5 cases each (prospective phase)

title: Performance of Large Language Models in Diagnosing Rare Hematologic Diseases and the Impact of Their Diagnostic Outputs on Physicians: Combined Retrospective and Prospective Study
outcome: Physician performance when LLM outputs were biased or incorrect
effect: When LLMs generated biased responses, physician performance often failed to improve or even declined.
quote: However, when LLMs generated biased responses, physician performance often failed to improve or even declined.
sample_unit: nonpublic real-world admission records (retrospective phase); 28 physicians diagnosing 5 cases each (prospective phase)

title: Novel Insights into the Application of Large Language Models in the Diagnosis and Treatment of Complex Cardiovascular Diseases: A Comparative Study
outcome: Comparative accuracy, comprehensiveness, and safety of two LLMs on same cardiovascular cases
effect: ChatGPT-4o outperformed Kimi on treatment accuracy (P=0.004) and comprehensiveness (P<0.001); high-risk outputs 1.5% vs 4.5%; diagnostic accuracy similar (P=0.663).
quote: For treatment recommendations, ChatGPT-4o outperformed Kimi in both accuracy (P = 0.004, r = 0.321) and comprehensiveness (P < 0.001, r = 0.644).

title: Use of an AI Scribe and Electronic Health Record Efficiency
outcome: Clinician EHR time, note time, after-hours documentation time, and encounter closure time after AI scribe use
effect: Users had 8.5% lower mean EHR time and 15.9% lower note time versus weighted nonusers; pre-post time to close encounters fell 7.1 hours. No significant difference in after-hours documentation time or appointment volume.
quote: In this retrospective cohort study, clinicians using an AI scribe spent significantly less time in the EHR and in notes in both pre-post and propensity score analyses.
sample_unit: ambulatory clinicians (125 AI scribe users, 478 weighted nonusers)

title: Head-to-Head Comparison of 2 Artificial Intelligence Tools for Detecting Lymph Node Metastases in Whole-Slide Pathology Images Within and Beyond Their Intended Use
venue: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
outcome: Sensitivity of AI tools on tumor types beyond their intended use
effect: Both tools showed excellent sensitivity for macrometastases across tumor types, including beyond intended use. DPL had slightly higher sensitivity for micrometastases and isolated tumor cells than VMD, particularly in lung cancer and melanoma.
quote: Our findings suggest that a single AI tool may be suitable for LN metastasis detection across multiple tumor types, even beyond its intended use.
sample_unit: patients with lymph node metastases (whole-slide images); plus 1012 tumor-negative slides for false-positive alerts

title: Head-to-Head Comparison of 2 Artificial Intelligence Tools for Detecting Lymph Node Metastases in Whole-Slide Pathology Images Within and Beyond Their Intended Use
venue: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
outcome: False-positive alert rates in tumor-negative slides
effect: FPA rates were substantial for both tools; VMD generally produced more alerts, especially in lung and breast cancer. High FPA rates, even in lung cancer within DPL's intended use, may limit practical use.
quote: FPA rates were substantial for both tools, with VMD generally producing more alerts, especially in lung and breast cancer.
sample_unit: patients with lymph node metastases (whole-slide images); plus 1012 tumor-negative slides for false-positive alerts

title: Robust comparative evaluation of 15 natural language processing algorithms to positively identify patients with inflammatory bowel disease from secondary care records
outcome: Fairness of NLP models across patient subgroups
effect: Bias was reported as a significant issue for all effective model types.
quote: Bias was a significant issue for all effective model types.

title: Robust comparative evaluation of 15 natural language processing algorithms to positively identify patients with inflammatory bowel disease from secondary care records
outcome: Comparison of 15 NLP algorithms, from simple to LLM, on the same labelled data
effect: Fine-tuned DistilBERT best (micro F1 93.54%), sBERT-Base 93.05%; LLMs 86.47-92.20% but slow (18-300 hours) and expensive; specificity 67.80-64.41% for top two.
quote: The fine-tuned DistilBERT_IBD model achieved the best performance overall (micro F1: 93.54%), followed by sBERT-Base (micro F1: 93.05%); however, specificity was an issue for both: (67.80-64.41%) respectively.

title: Evaluating the readability and quality of AI-generated scoliosis education materials: a comparative analysis of five language models
outcome: Reading level (FKGL, FKRE) of AI-generated scoliosis patient education content
effect: DeepSeek-R1 lowest FKGL (6.2), highest FKRE (64.5); ChatGPT-o1 and ChatGPT-o3 mini-high scored above FKGL 12.0, requiring college-level reading skills.
quote: In contrast, ChatGPT-o1 and ChatGPT-o3 mini-high scored above FKGL 12.0, requiring college-level reading skills.
sample_unit: AI-generated responses (5 models x 3 scoliosis types)

title: Evaluating the readability and quality of AI-generated scoliosis education materials: a comparative analysis of five language models
outcome: Presence of citations in AI-generated scoliosis responses
effect: All responses lacked citations, limiting reliability.
quote: However, all responses lacked citations, limiting reliability.
sample_unit: AI-generated responses (5 models x 3 scoliosis types)

title: Robustness of a convolutional neural network trained on dermoscopic images and challenged with close-up images
venue: Journal der Deutschen Dermatologischen Gesellschaft = Journal of the German Society of Dermatology : JDDG
outcome: Sensitivity of dermoscopy-trained CNN on close-up images, a setting it was not validated for
effect: Sensitivity fell from 88.2% (dermoscopic) to 60.5% (close-up, p < 0.001); specificity rose from 69.0% to 79.4% (p = 0.027); ROC-AUC 0.866 vs 0.780 (p = 0.003).
quote: For close-up images of the same lesions, sensitivity decreased to 60.5% (53.5%-67.1%, p < 0.001), while specificity increased to 79.4% (72.3%-85.0%, p = 0.027).

title: From digital assistants to clinical partners: revolutionizing pediatric urology through large language model-powered decision support and patient education
outcome: LLM accuracy on routine versus complex pediatric urology cases
effect: Accuracy 76% in routine vs 41% in complex cases; GPT-4o3 scored 61.4 vs 51.8 for other models in complex cases.
quote: LLMs demonstrated superior performance in routine clinical scenarios compared to complex cases (76% vs. 41% accuracy, respectively).

title: From digital assistants to clinical partners: revolutionizing pediatric urology through large language model-powered decision support and patient education
outcome: Correlation between LLM diagnostic confidence and actual performance
effect: Diagnostic confidence correlated strongly with actual performance (r = 0.82, p < 0.001).
quote: Diagnostic confidence demonstrated strong correlation with actual performance (r = 0.82, p < 0.001).

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4 responses on physical activity guidance in children with cystic fibrosis: reliability, quality, and readability
outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of ChatGPT-4 responses on physical activity in children with cystic fibrosis
effect: Readability mean scores varied from 29.99 (S5) to 46.31 (S3), with a total mean of 38.07; most responses were 'difficult' for the target age group.
quote: Low FRE scores showed most responses were "difficult" for the target age group.

title: Enhanced LLM-supported instructions for medication use through retrieval-augmented generation
outcome: Instruction adequacy and clarity
quote: RAG introduction significantly improved instructions adequacy: median (interquartile range) 93.0 (40.0) vs. 94 (53.3) vs 100 (15.0), p = 0.001, and clarity 90.0 (60.0) vs. 92 (55.0) vs 95.0 (24.0), p = 0.012, for model1, model2, and model3 respectively.

title: Understandability and Actionability of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Lymphedema Education Material in Patients Undergoing Breast Cancer Surgery: Expert Evaluation
outcome: Readability, understandability and actionability of AI-generated lymphedema education material
effect: Turkish readability index 67.3 ('easily understandable'); PEMAT understandability 92.10 ± 9.03; actionability 81.60 ± 18.47; Global Quality Scale 4.10 ± 0.87.
quote: It was determined that the Patient Education Materials Evaluation Tool understandability score average was 92.10 ± 9.03, and the actionability score average was 81.60 ± 18.47.

title: Assessing the accuracy and readability of ChatGPT 4.0's original and simplified responses to common patient questions regarding periacetabular osteotomy
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of original ChatGPT responses versus sixth-grade recommendation
effect: Original responses averaged FK grade 11.09 ± 1.47 and reading ease 39.12 ± 8.25; 28 of 30 (93.3%) required at least college-level education.
quote: Similar to other studies [ 15 , 32 , 40 ], the original responses generated by ChatGPT in our research were written at much higher educational levels than the sixth grade reading level recommended by the National Institutes of Health and the American Medical Association [ 13 , 29 ].

title: Assessing the accuracy and readability of ChatGPT 4.0's original and simplified responses to common patient questions regarding periacetabular osteotomy
outcome: Readability and accuracy of AI patient education responses after simplification prompts
effect: Simplify prompt lowered FK grade from 11.09 to 8.16; sixth-grade prompt gave 7.09. Accuracy remained high (no unsatisfactory responses) across prompt types.
quote: For simplified responses, the average Flesch‐Kincaid Grade Level for all responses was 8.16 ± 1.46 which correlates approximately to the reading level of an eighth grader.

title: Assessing the accuracy and readability of ChatGPT 4.0's original and simplified responses to common patient questions regarding periacetabular osteotomy
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid readability
effect: Grade level improved from 11.09±1.47 original to 8.16±1.46 simplified and 7.09±1.23 sixth-grade, but remained above sixth grade.
quote: Readability analysis revealed an average Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level corresponding to an 11th-grade reading level (11.09 ± 1.47) and a mean Reading Ease score requiring college level reading comprehension (39.12 ± 8.25) for original responses, 8th-grade reading level (8.16 ± 1.46) requiring high school to college level reading comprehension (51.53 ± 9.62) for simplified responses, and 7th-grade reading level (7.09 ± 1.23) requiring high school level reading comprehension (62.46 ± 7.48) for 6th grade responses.

title: Dementia risk prediction in the general population: external validation of a prediction model in the population-based LifeLines Cohort Study
outcome: Discrimination (c-statistic) and calibration of dementia risk model in external population cohort
effect: Overall c-statistic 0.62 (95% CI 0.48-0.70); 0.67 (0.57-0.78) at follow-up 2a; poor calibration with systematic overestimation of predicted risk; only 36 self-reported dementia cases.
quote: However, calibration of the model in this external validation cohort was poor, with systematic overestimation of the predicted risk.

title: Are Artificial Intelligence-generated Patient Leaflets Ready for Clinical Use? A Readability Comparison across Common Orthopaedic Procedures
outcome: Readability grade level of AI-generated leaflets versus professionally authored leaflets
effect: RCS England leaflets had Flesch-Kincaid Grade Levels 5.52-7.15 and Flesch Reading Ease above 70; AI leaflets often had Grade Levels above 12, with Gunning Fog and SMOG indicating post-secondary reading requirements.
quote: In contrast, AI-generated leaflets frequently exceeded recommended complexity thresholds, with Grade Levels often above 12 and Gunning Fog and SMOG scores indicating post-secondary reading requirements.

title: Are Artificial Intelligence-generated Patient Leaflets Ready for Clinical Use? A Readability Comparison across Common Orthopaedic Procedures
outcome: Comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education materials by readability metrics
effect: AI-generated leaflets did not consistently meet recommended readability standards; ChatGPT most complex, Gemini and DeepSeek intermediate but still suboptimal.
quote: While LLMs offer promising avenues for scalable health communication, current AI-generated PILs do not consistently meet recommended readability standards.

title: Oesophageal cancer multi-disciplinary tool: a co-designed, externally validated, machine learning tool for oesophageal cancer decision making
outcome: Model AUC on external Oxford cohort versus Southampton training cohort with differing baseline characteristics
effect: External AUCs for the primary treatment model stayed high (MLR 0.894, XGB 0.887, RF 0.891). The palliative classifier fell to MLR 0.711, XGB 0.742, RF 0.730, versus internal 0.793-0.815 (k=5 cross-validation).
quote: On external validation (OUH cohort), AUCs were MLR 0.894, XGB 0.887 and RF 0.891 for the primary treatment model and MLR 0.711, XGB 0.742 and RF 0.730 for the palliative treatment classifier.

title: Development of a multi-task deep learning system for classification of nine common knee abnormalities on MRI: a large-scale, multicentre, stepwise validation study
outcome: Radiologist accuracy and reading time with versus without DLS assistance (randomised comparative study)
effect: DLS-assisted junior and senior radiologists had higher accuracy (difference 4.8-8.8% and 4.2-8.2%, all p<0.05) and reduced reading time (by 35.5 and 30.7 s, all p<0.05) vs control.
quote: For step 3, the randomised comparative study demonstrated that the junior and senior radiologists in the DLS-assisted group achieved significantly higher accuracy (difference of 4.8-8.8% and 4.2-8.2%, all p < 0.05) and reduced reading time (by 35.5 and 30.7 s, all p < 0.05) compared to the control group for nine knee abnormalities.

title: Development of a multi-task deep learning system for classification of nine common knee abnormalities on MRI: a large-scale, multicentre, stepwise validation study
outcome: DLS accuracy compared with senior radiologists on the same data
effect: DLS showed comparable accuracy to senior radiologists for meniscal tear (79.6% vs 78.1%), ACL tear (89.3% vs 89.4%), and MCL injury (87.1% vs 85.7%).
quote: For step 1 of validation, the DLS demonstrated comparable accuracy to that of the senior radiologists in classifying meniscal tear (79.6% vs. 78.1%, p = 0.426), ACL tear (89.3% vs. 89.4%, p = 1.000), and MCL injury (87.1% vs. 85.7%, p = 0.565).

title: Development of a multi-task deep learning system for classification of nine common knee abnormalities on MRI: a large-scale, multicentre, stepwise validation study
outcome: DLS AUC on internal versus external test sets
effect: AUCs for primary abnormalities fell from 0.898 (internal) to 0.852 and 0.812 (external sets I and II); secondary abnormalities from 0.815 to 0.744 and 0.774.
quote: The DLS demonstrated areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of 0.898 (95% confidence intervals [CI], 0.890-0.905) and 0.815 (95% CI, 0.805-0.823), 0.852 (95% CI, 0.830-0.872) and 0.744 (95% CI, 0.721-0.766), and 0.812 (95% CI, 0.771-0.854) and 0.774 (95% CI, 0.733-0.816) for primary and secondary abnormalities on the internal test set, external test set I, and external test set II, respectively.

title: Multimodal large language models in ultrasound diagnosis of breast masses: a multicenter comparative analysis based on GPT-4o, radiologists, and convolutional neural network (CNN)
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Intra-model consistency (Fleiss kappa) of GPT-4o across repeated runs by input strategy
effect: Image-only kappa 0.25 (95% CI 0.07-0.43, fair); image-plus-text kappa 0.81 (95% CI 0.67-0.91, excellent).
quote: GPT-4o with image-strategy exhibited a fair consistency [0.25, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.07-0.43], whereas the agreement of image-combined-text-strategy was excellent (0.81, 95% CI: 0.67-0.91).

title: Multimodal large language models in ultrasound diagnosis of breast masses: a multicenter comparative analysis based on GPT-4o, radiologists, and convolutional neural network (CNN)
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4o versus radiologists and a CNN on the same breast ultrasound cases
effect: GPT-4o image-only 58% vs image+text 70% (P=0.031); image+text similar to moderately experienced radiologists 71% (P=0.450) and CNN 74% (P=0.701).
quote: Diagnostic accuracy improved when deploying the image-combined-text-strategy compared to only image [58% (46 of 80) vs. 70% (56 of 80), P=0.031], which resembled board-certified moderately experienced radiologists (70% [56 of 80] vs. 71% [57 of 80], P=0.450) and customized CNN [70% (56 of 80) vs. 74% (59 of 80), P=0.701].

title: Table-based language models for ophthalmology assessment in the emergency department
venue: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
outcome: Inter-grader agreement between two board-certified ophthalmologists on GPT-4o answer classification
effect: Inter-grader agreement kappa was 0.841 (P < 0.001) on a sample of encounters reviewed by a second ophthalmologist.
quote: The inter-grader agreement kappa was 0.841 (P < 0.001).

title: A rural-to-center artificial intelligence model for diagnosing Helicobacter pylori infection and premalignant gastric conditions using endoscopy images captured in routine practice
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy at rural implementation site versus development-phase accuracy
effect: Implementation accuracy: H. pylori 91.3% (development 92.8%), atrophic gastritis 79.9% (88.6%), intestinal metaplasia 63.4% (88.0%). Accuracy was maintained for H. pylori but dropped for premalignant conditions.
quote: Implementation-phase diagnostic accuracies were 91.3% (95%CI 88.0%–94.6%), 79.9% (95%CI 72.1%–86.3%), and 63.4% (95%CI 54.7%–71.6%), respectively.
sample_unit: rural residents with positive screening who underwent endoscopy (implementation phase)

title: Deep learning CT model for stratified diagnosis of pancreatic cystic neoplasms: multicenter development, validation, and real-world clinical impact
outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance in MRMC study
effect: AI assistance improved radiologists' AUC from 0.786 to 0.845 (p < 0.05), reduced interpretation time by 23.7% (5.28 vs. 4.03 min/case); radiologists accepted AI recommendations in 87.14% of cases.
quote: A multi-reader, multi-case (MRMC) study demonstrated that AI assistance significantly improved radiologists' diagnostic accuracy (AUC: 0.786 to 0.845; p < 0.05) and reduced interpretation time by 23.7% (5.28 vs. 4.03 minutes/case).

title: Deep learning CT model for stratified diagnosis of pancreatic cystic neoplasms: multicenter development, validation, and real-world clinical impact
outcome: AI performance versus radiologist double-reading in prospective real-world cohort
effect: PCN-AI outperformed radiologist double-reading, providing actionable diagnostic benefit to 45.45% of patients (5/11) by identifying missed malignant PCN cases, and reduced clinical workload by 39.3%.
quote: In a prospective real-world cohort, PCN-AI outperformed radiologist double-reading, providing actionable diagnostic benefits to 45.45% of patients (5/11) by correctly identifying missed malignant PCN cases, enabling timely intervention, and simultaneously reducing clinical workload by 39.3%.

title: YOLOv5 Attention Analysis for Anterior Eye Disease Classification: Grad-CAM++ Feature Importance and Cut-and-Paste Validation
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Model accuracy after swapping corneal region backgrounds (cut-and-paste perturbation)
effect: Accuracy was highly dependent on background context for certain diseases; accuracy for infectious keratitis and acute primary angle closure dropped significantly after background alteration.
quote: Cut-and-paste validation demonstrated that model accuracy was highly dependent on the background context for certain diseases; for instance, the accuracy for infectious keratitis and acute primary angle closure dropped significantly upon background alteration.

title: YOLOv5 Attention Analysis for Anterior Eye Disease Classification: Grad-CAM++ Feature Importance and Cut-and-Paste Validation
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Fidelity of Grad-CAM++ attention maps to expert lesion annotations (IoU) by prediction correctness
effect: IoU of attention maps against expert annotations was significantly higher for correct than for incorrect predictions, linking visual explanation to diagnostic reliability.
quote: Critically, the clinical relevance of the attention maps measured by the IoU against expert annotations was significantly higher for correct predictions than for incorrect predictions, linking the model's visual explanation to its diagnostic reliability.

title: Quality of patient information on interstitial cystitis from artificial intelligence chatbots
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid) of chatbot interstitial cystitis patient information
effect: Responses averaged 256 words with college-level readability (median Flesch-Kincaid 25.4 [IQR 20.89-28.50]) across all platforms, limiting accessibility.
quote: Responses averaged 256 words and college-level readability (median [IQR] Flesch-Kincaid score 25.4 [20.89-28.50]) across all platforms, limiting accessibility.

title: Quality of patient information on interstitial cystitis from artificial intelligence chatbots
outcome: Reading level of chatbot patient information versus typical patient comprehension
effect: Content generated at college-level readability (median Flesch-Kincaid 25.4), above typical patient comprehension.
quote: Artificial intelligence chatbots offer generally accurate and understandable information about interstitial cystitis but lack actionable guidance and generate content at reading levels above typical patient comprehension.

title: Artificial Intelligence Models for Dysphonia Patient Education
venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRES, GFI) of AI chatbot and DI patient education responses versus recommended levels
effect: All resources exceeded recommended FKGL and GFI and fell below FRES of 90 to 100; ChatGPT had higher FKGL than GAO (P < .01) and lower FRES than GAO and DI (P < .01).
quote: All resources exceeded the recommended FKGL and GFI scores as well as the FRES of 90 to 100.

title: Artificial Intelligence Models for Dysphonia Patient Education
venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses relative to recommended plain-language levels
effect: ChatGPT had a significantly higher FKGL than GAO (P < .01) and a lower FRES than both GAO and DI (P < .01), indicating a more difficult reading level; all resources exceeded recommendations.
quote: ChatGPT had a significantly higher FKGL than GAO (P < .01), and a lower FRES than both GAO (P < .01) and DI (P < .01), indicating a more difficult reading level.

title: Quality assessment of patient-facing urologic telesurgery content using validated tools
outcome: Understandability and actionability of chatbot patient information on urologic telesurgery (PEMAT-P)
effect: PEMAT-P understandability exceeded 70% for both (overall 79.7% Gemini vs 78.1% ChatGPT); actionability uniformly low, only Gemini met 70% in the prospective domain.
quote: PEMAT-P understandability uniformly exceeded 70% for both platforms: prospective 80.0% versus 71.7%; technical 80.1% versus 79.8%; recovery 79.2% versus 80.1%; other 79.2% versus 81.3%; overall 79.7% versus 78.1% (Fig. 2).

title: Comparing Generative Artificial Intelligence and Mental Health Professionals for Clinical Decision-Making With Trauma-Exposed Populations: Vignette-Based Experimental Study
outcome: Change in AI diagnosis/treatment ratings when trauma history was added to otherwise identical vignettes
effect: GAI showed some trauma-related diagnostic overshadowing (e.g., PTSD ratings with sexual trauma, P<.001), but bias varied by task and model and was generally less than that of mental health professionals.
quote: GAI models demonstrate some evidence of trauma-related diagnostic overshadowing bias, yet the degree of bias varied by task and model.
sample_unit: mental health professionals (plus GAI models, 20 runs per block per model)

title: Domain validation of the CRASH prognostic model for predicting 14-day mortality among patients and traumatic brain injury and intracranial hemorrhage in a Thai emergency department
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of CRASH model on local retrospective data against observed 14-day mortality
effect: AuROC 0.92 (Basic) and 0.93 (CT); calibration-in-the-large -0.916 and -1.257, slopes 1.69 and 1.86, showing overestimation of mortality locally.
quote: However, calibration metrics indicated a systematic overestimation of mortality, suggesting that recalibration of both the intercept and slope is necessary before the model can be implemented in local clinical practice.

title: Domain validation of the CRASH prognostic model for predicting 14-day mortality among patients and traumatic brain injury and intracranial hemorrhage in a Thai emergency department
outcome: Effect of logistic recalibration of intercept and slope on calibration in local population
effect: Recalibration reduced overestimation in high-risk groups and better aligned predictions with observed mortality (shown in plots; no numeric post-recalibration metrics in text).
quote: The recalibration process effectively reduced this overestimation, aligning predicted outcomes with observed mortality rates.

title: Domain validation of the CRASH prognostic model for predicting 14-day mortality among patients and traumatic brain injury and intracranial hemorrhage in a Thai emergency department
outcome: Differences between development and local validation populations (age, GCS, CT findings, mortality)
effect: 75% aged ≥55 vs 14.5% in development; mortality 9.1% vs 20.7%; non-evacuated hematoma 62.1% vs 27.3%; miscalibration followed.
quote: Patients in the validation dataset were predominantly older, with 75% aged 55 or above, compared to only 14.5% in the development cohort (STD = 1.940).

title: Domain validation of the CRASH prognostic model for predicting 14-day mortality among patients and traumatic brain injury and intracranial hemorrhage in a Thai emergency department
outcome: Generalization of CRASH model to new population (TBI with ICH in Thai ED)
effect: Discrimination retained (AuROC 0.92/0.93) but systematic overestimation of mortality (CITL -0.916 Basic, -1.257 CT).
quote: These results suggest that the models systematically predict higher risks of 14-day mortality than observed, particularly in higher-risk groups.

title: Domain validation of the CRASH prognostic model for predicting 14-day mortality among patients and traumatic brain injury and intracranial hemorrhage in a Thai emergency department
outcome: 14-day mortality discriminative ability and calibration
effect: Basic model had AuROC 0.92 (95% CI: 0.84, 1.00) and CT model 0.93 (95% CI: 0.86, 1.00), but both had significant miscalibration (Basic CITL -0.916; CT CITL -1.257).
quote: The original CRASH prediction model demonstrates strong discriminative ability for predicting 14-day mortality in TBI patients; however, significant miscalibration was observed.

title: GPT-4 as a source of patient information for cervical disc arthroplasty: a comparative analysis against Google web search
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade, Reading Ease) of GPT-4 initial responses versus recommended sixth-grade level
effect: GPT-4 initial responses had FK grade 13.06 and Flesch Reading Ease 36.87, similar to Google (12.24; 40.05), well above the recommended sixth-grade level.
quote: GPT-4’s initial responses had a Flesch-Kincaid grade level of 13.06, a Flesch Reading Ease score of 36.87, and a word count of 222.80.

title: GPT-4 as a source of patient information for cervical disc arthroplasty: a comparative analysis against Google web search
outcome: Agreement of GPT-4 numerical answers with Google answers for CDA FAQs
effect: 60% (6 of 10) of numerical responses differed between GPT-4 and Google, e.g., success rate 62.40% (Google) vs above 80% (GPT-4).
quote: In our study, 60% of numerical responses differed between GPT-4 and Google, underscoring the variability and potential inaccuracy in AI-generated health content.

title: GPT-4 as a source of patient information for cervical disc arthroplasty: a comparative analysis against Google web search
outcome: Readability of GPT-4 output after prompting to rewrite for low literacy versus initial output
effect: After the low-literacy rewrite prompt, FK grade fell from 13.06 to 6.58 and Reading Ease rose from 36.87 to 76.20 (P<0.001), with similar word count (218.6 vs 222.8).
quote: However, when GPT-4 was prompted to make its responses more readable, the Flesch-Kincaid grade level improved to 6.58, the Flesch Reading Ease score to 76.20, and the word count slightly decreased to 218.60.

title: GPT-4 as a source of patient information for cervical disc arthroplasty: a comparative analysis against Google web search
outcome: initial readability versus Google
effect: Initial GPT-4 vs Google: Flesch-Kincaid 13.06 vs. 12.24 (P=0.41); Reading Ease 36.87 vs. 40.05 (P=0.53).
quote: No significant differences were found in readability between GPT-4 and Google, displaying a similar Flesch-Kincaid grade level (13.06 vs. 12.24, P=0.41) and Flesch Reading Ease score (36.87 vs. 40.05, P=0.53).

title: Diagnostic accuracy of otitis media with and without a fictitious AI support among physicians in primary care and medical students
venue: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
outcome: Automation bias (misled by incorrect fictitious AI advice) by physician experience level
effect: Automation bias was 1.2 overall, 0.9 for the most experienced and 1.2 for the least experienced physicians. Less experienced participants were more often misled by the fictitious AI.
quote: Automation bias was 1.2 overall, 0.9 for the most experienced and 1.2 for the least experienced physicians.
sample_unit: participants (primary care physicians and medical students) diagnosing 21 eardrum images

title: Consistent performance of large language models in rare disease diagnosis across ten languages and 4917 cases
outcome: LLM differential diagnosis accuracy by prompt language (top-1 and top-3 rank)
effect: GPT-4o top-1 was 19.9% in English vs 16.9%-20.6% in nine non-English languages; top-3 was 27.0% in English vs 25.4%-28.6% in others. Performance largely consistent across languages.
quote: For English, GPT-4o placed the correct diagnosis at the first rank 19.9% and within the top-3 ranks 27.0% of the time.
sample_unit: clinical vignettes (rare disease cases) per language

title: Bridging generative AI and healthcare practice: insights from the GenAI Health Hackathon at Hospital Clínic de Barcelona
outcome: Prototype performance on multilingual tasks
effect: Lower scores (F1<0.52, Jaccard Index <0.4) were seen in complex reasoning or multilingual tasks.
quote: Lower scores (F1<0.52, Jaccard Index <0.4) were seen in complex reasoning or multilingual tasks.

title: The ethics of simplification: balancing patient autonomy, comprehension, and accuracy in AI-generated radiology reports
outcome: Accuracy and potential management-altering errors of LLM reports simplified to low reading grade levels
effect: Accuracy declined significantly below grade 11; at 7th-grade level 20% (20/100) of reports had potential changes in patient management (generalization 8/20, omission 7/20, incorrect conversion 7/20).
quote: Among the 100 reports transformed to a 7th-grade reading level, 20% (20/100) exhibited potential changes in patient management when compared to the original reports.
sample_unit: radiology reports (CT and MRI), each transformed into 17 reading-grade versions

title: The ethics of simplification: balancing patient autonomy, comprehension, and accuracy in AI-generated radiology reports
outcome: Omissions, incorrect conversions and generalizations in AI-simplified reports that could reach patients unverified
effect: At 7th grade, inaccuracies with potential to alter management: inappropriate generalization 40% (8/20), omission 35% (7/20), incorrect conversion 35% (7/20).
quote: The inaccuracy patterns identified within these 20 cases were as follows: inappropriate generalization occurred in 40% (8/20), omission in 35% (7/20), and incorrect conversion in 35% (7/20).
sample_unit: radiology reports (CT and MRI), each transformed into 17 reading-grade versions

title: Exploring AI's Potential in Papilledema Diagnosis to Support Dermatological Treatment Decisions in Rural Healthcare
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of GPT-4o versus fine-tuned ResNet and human ophthalmologists on same test images
effect: GPT-4o accuracy 85.9% (Kappa 0.72), specificity 78.9%, PPV 73.7%; ResNet 99.5% (Kappa 0.99); ophthalmologists 96.0% (Kappa ≈ 0.92). GPT-4o underperformed both.
quote: GPT-4o achieved moderate diagnostic accuracy and substantial agreement with the ground truth, but it underperformed compared to both a domain-specific ResNet model and human ophthalmologists.
sample_unit: fundus images (test set from 1094 total; test set size not reported)

title: Pilot Study of AI-Assisted ANA Immunofluorescence Reading-Comparison with Classical Visual Interpretation
outcome: Agreement of AI vs visual ANA positive/negative classification on local consecutive clinical samples
effect: At cut-off 80, kappa 0.69 but significantly different (McNemar p<0.0001); at cut-off ≥1/80 kappa 0.76 and no significant difference (p=1.0000). Pattern agreement moderate (kappa 0.54).
quote: Agreement of positive/negative ANA discrimination between AI-aided and VI-IIFT at the recommended cut-off of 80 was good (Cohen's kappa [κ] 0.69) but significantly different (McNemar test, p < 0.0001).

title: Pilot Study of AI-Assisted ANA Immunofluorescence Reading-Comparison with Classical Visual Interpretation
outcome: AI titer levels versus gold standard visual interpretation, indicating miscalibrated thresholds
effect: Titer levels in automated evaluations were frequently assessed at higher values than visual interpretation; agreement improved when cut-off was adjusted to ≥1/80 (kappa 0.69 to 0.76).
quote: Notably, titer levels in the automated evaluations were frequently assessed at higher values than in the gold standard interpretation.

title: Enhancing Patient Education with AI: A Readability Analysis of AI-Generated Versus American Academy of Ophthalmology Online Patient Education Materials
outcome: Reading grade level of LLM-generated patient education materials versus 6th-grade target
effect: Initial outputs averaged grade 10.8 (ChatGPT), 12.2 (Copilot), 13.2 (Llama); all exceeded the recommended 6th-grade level; AAO averaged 8.0 FKGL.
quote: For all 15 topics, ChatGPT, Copilot, and Llama successfully generated PEMs, though all exceeded the recommended 6th-grade reading level.
sample_unit: diagnoses (topics) for which patient education materials were generated per LLM

title: Enhancing Patient Education with AI: A Readability Analysis of AI-Generated Versus American Academy of Ophthalmology Online Patient Education Materials
outcome: Readability change after follow-up prompt to rewrite at 6th-grade level
effect: FRO prompting improved readability to 8.3 (ChatGPT), 11.2 (Copilot), 9.3 (Llama) (p<0.001), but still above 6th grade and not statistically easier than AAO (8.0).
quote: While initially prompted ChatGPT, Copilot, and Llama outputs were 10.8, 12.2, and 13.2, respectively, FRO prompting significantly improved readability to 8.3 for ChatGPT, 11.2 for Copilot, and 9.3 for Llama (p < 0.001).
sample_unit: diagnoses (topics) for which patient education materials were generated per LLM

title: Comparison of Accuracy in the Evaluation of Nutritional Labels on Commercial Ready-to-Eat Meal Boxes Between Professional Nutritionists and Chatbots
outcome: Reproducibility of chatbot nutrient estimates across repeated identical prompts (coefficient of variation)
effect: Calories and protein were consistent across models (CV <15%). Sodium was consistently underestimated, with CVs ranging from 20% to 70%. Fat and saturated fat were consistent only for ChatGPT-4o.
quote: Sodium values were consistently underestimated across all AI models, with CVs ranging from 20% to 70%.

title: Conceptualization of the Use of Artificial Intelligence by Clinical or Research Laboratory Professionals: Challenges for Its Implementation in Mexico
outcome: Formal AI training received and willingness to take AI courses among laboratory professionals
effect: Only 4.7% had received formal AI training; 84.8% were willing to take AI courses; 74% cited lack of knowledge and training as a major concern.
quote: Only 4.7% of respondents had received formal AI training, but 84.8% were willing to take AI courses.
sample_unit: clinical or research laboratory professionals (survey respondents)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models' Potential in Field Epidemiology Investigation Based on Chinese Context- Zhejiang Province, China, 2025
outcome: Accuracy of references and citations generated by LLMs
effect: LLMs may generate inaccurate or fabricated references, presenting substantial risks for inexperienced practitioners.
quote: Notably, LLMs may generate inaccurate or fabricated references, presenting substantial risks for inexperienced practitioners.

title: Large Language Models for Automating Clinical Trial Criteria Conversion to Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model Queries: Validation and Evaluation Study
outcome: Concept mapping accuracy of GPT-4 versus USAGI baseline on 357 clinical terms
effect: GPT-4 achieved 48.5% concept mapping accuracy versus USAGI's 32.0% (P<.001); llama3:8b had higher effective SQL rate (75.8%) than GPT-4 (45.3%).
quote: GPT-4 achieved a 48.5% concept mapping accuracy versus USAGI's 32.0% (P<.001), with domain-specific performance ranging from 72.7% (drug) to 38.3% (measurement).
sample_unit: SQL generation attempts (19 trials x 8 LLMs x 5 prompting strategies)

title: Large Language Models for Automating Clinical Trial Criteria Conversion to Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model Queries: Validation and Evaluation Study
outcome: Concordance of LLM-generated queries with reference concept sets in local OMOP CDM database
effect: Mixed: T1D Jaccard=0.81, pregnancy 0.00, T2D 0.03, uncontrolled hypertension 0.18.
quote: Clinical validation revealed mixed performance: high concordance for type 1 diabetes (Jaccard=0.81), complete failure for pregnancy (Jaccard=0.00), and minimal overlap for type 2 diabetes (Jaccard=0.03), despite perfect overlap coefficients in both diabetes cases.
sample_unit: SQL generation attempts (19 trials x 8 LLMs x 5 prompting strategies)

title: Large Language Models for Automating Clinical Trial Criteria Conversion to Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model Queries: Validation and Evaluation Study
outcome: Hallucination rate in LLM-generated SQL queries
effect: Overall hallucination rate 32.7%; wrong domain assignments 34.2% and placeholder insertions 28.7% most common; GPT-4 33.7% vs llama3:8b 21.1%.
quote: The overall hallucination rate was 32.7%, with wrong domain assignments (34.2%) and placeholder insertions (28.7%) being the most common.
sample_unit: SQL generation attempts (19 trials x 8 LLMs x 5 prompting strategies)

title: Automated real-time assessment of intracranial hemorrhage detection AI using an ensembled monitoring model (EMM)
outcome: Accuracy of the primary model stratified by case-level confidence from EMM agreement
effect: Accuracy was highest with high EMM agreement and lowest with low agreement, for both ICH-positive and ICH-negative predictions and at all prevalences.
quote: As expected, overall accuracy was highest for cases in which the primary model and EMM showed high agreement, and overall accuracy was lowest when EMM showed a lower agreement level with the primary model.

title: Automated real-time assessment of intracranial hemorrhage detection AI using an ensembled monitoring model (EMM)
outcome: EMM error-detection performance across gender, age and race subgroups
effect: Discrepancies in EMM performance were found in some gender, age and race subgroups, possibly from underrepresentation in the training data or distribution mismatch.
quote: Additionally, we analyzed EMM performance across gender, age and race groups and found discrepancies in some subgroups, potentially due to either underrepresentation in the EMM training data or the distribution mismatch between the EMM training data and our internal testing dataset for these subgroups (Supplementary Fig. 6 ).

title: Automated real-time assessment of intracranial hemorrhage detection AI using an ensembled monitoring model (EMM)
outcome: False confidence when the confidence estimator agrees with an incorrect primary AI prediction
effect: EMM showed full agreement with an incorrect primary prediction in 138 cases (4%), mainly subtle hemorrhages or hemorrhage mimics, which could instill false confidence.
quote: Of particular concern are instances where EMM fails simultaneously with the primary model while indicating complete consensus, as this could instill false confidence in clinicians and potentially increase misdiagnosis risk.

title: Automated real-time assessment of intracranial hemorrhage detection AI using an ensembled monitoring model (EMM)
outcome: Low-confidence deferral accuracy and false alarms
effect: ICH-positive: +4.66, +11.28, and +38.57% versus false alarms 0.89, 0.45, and 0.14%; ICH-negative net benefit only at 30%.
quote: However, this net benefit was only observed for cases with ICH-negative primary model predictions at 30% prevalence (false-alarm rate of 1.05% versus relative accuracy improvement of 3.35%).

title: A multimodal uncertainty-aware AI system optimizes ovarian cancer risk assessment workflow
outcome: Radiologist AUC and sensitivity with versus without AI assistance in reader study
effect: Human-AI collaboration increased radiologists' average AUC by 10.58% and sensitivity by 22.48% (n = 284 cases, six radiologists).
quote: Furthermore, a prospective reader study (n = 284 cases, six radiologists) demonstrated that UMORSS as a human-AI collaborative tool increased radiologists' average AUC by 10.58% and sensitivity by 22.48%.

title: A multimodal uncertainty-aware AI system optimizes ovarian cancer risk assessment workflow
outcome: Phase II AUC in internal testing versus external validation
effect: Phase II AUC was 0.955 in internal testing and 0.926 in external validation, a modest drop at external sites.
quote: Phase II achieved an AUC of 0.955 (internal testing) and 0.926 (external validation).

title: What does ChatGPT know about Migraine? A comparative-descriptive analysis
venue: Cephalalgia : an international journal of headache
outcome: Validity of references and citations in ChatGPT-4o migraine answers
effect: Reference-related AI hallucinations were among the most common limitations; 37.5% of 8 responses were partially satisfactory, 62.5% satisfactory, none unsatisfactory.
quote: The most common limitations included reference-related AI hallucinations and insufficient technical depth in selected answers.

title: Automated Esophageal Cancer Staging From Free-Text Radiology Reports: Large Language Model Evaluation Study
outcome: Overall esophageal cancer staging accuracy of LLMs versus clinicians on same reports
effect: INF-72B+IR achieved 61.5% accuracy and F1 0.60 versus clinicians' 39.5% and 0.39 (P<.001); Qwen2.5-72B+IR 46%; LLaMA3.1-70B not significantly different from clinicians.
quote: INF-72B+IR achieved a superior overall staging accuracy of 61.5% and an F1-score of 0.60, substantially higher than the clinicians' accuracy of 39.5% and F1-score of 0.39 (all P<.001).

title: Comparison of Japanese Mpox (Monkeypox) Health Education Materials and Texts Created by Artificial Intelligence: Cross-Sectional Quantitative Content Analysis Study
outcome: Understandability and readability of AI-generated versus web mpox education texts
effect: AI texts more understandable: 80% (24/30) scored ≥70% on PEMAT-P (P<.001). Readability higher for AI (mean 2.9, SD 0.4) than web pages (mean 2.4, SD 1.0; P=.009). Actionable guidance largely absent in AI content.
quote: AI-generated texts significantly outperformed web pages in understandability, with 80% (24/30) scoring ≥70% in PEMAT-P (P<.001).
sample_unit: texts (119 web pages and 30 ChatGPT-4o-generated texts)

title: Diagnosis and Triage Performance of Contemporary Large Language Models on Short Clinical Vignettes
outcome: triage escalation errors
effect: Safety of advice rose from 89.06% to 94.53%, while over-triage rose from 53.15% to 65.62%.
quote: Safety of advice nearly reached a ceiling (94.53%) while over-triage rose substantially (from 53.15% to 65.62%).

title: Diagnosis and Triage Performance of Contemporary Large Language Models on Short Clinical Vignettes
outcome: LLM performance versus physicians
effect: Best LLM diagnosis reached 93.75% versus physician benchmark 96%; triage remained lower than physicians, who correctly classified 91%.
quote: However, triage accuracy for these models remained lower than that of physicians, with systematic tendencies toward over-triage.

title: Automated review of spine surgery operative reports with large language models: a pilot study of GPT reasoning models
venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
outcome: Inter-reviewer agreement on human ground truth for extracted variables
effect: Reviewer agreement for presence of certain variables varied considerably (52%-99%); human agreement positively correlated with model accuracy (r = 0.67, p = 0.0003).
quote: Reviewer agreement for the presence of certain variables varied considerably (52 %-99 %).

title: Automated review of spine surgery operative reports with large language models: a pilot study of GPT reasoning models
venue: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
outcome: Sensitivity of model-expressed uncertainty for detecting its own errors
effect: Uncertainty from the model was highly sensitive for errors, ranging from 0.63 to 1.00.
quote: Human agreement was positively correlated with model accuracy (r = 0.67, p = 0.0003) and uncertainty from the model was highly sensitive for errors (ranging from 0.63 to 1.00).

title: ChatGPT answers patient questions about hallux rigidus: Is it satisfactory?
venue: Foot and ankle surgery : official journal of the European Society of Foot and Ankle Surgeons
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses to hallux rigidus patient questions (Flesch-Kincaid, Gunning Fog, Coleman-Liau, SMOG)
effect: Mean readability corresponded to 11.3 years of education; authors describe ChatGPT information as provided at a high reading level.
quote: The mean readability corresponded to 11.3 years of education.

title: Geographic prompting and content fidelity in generative Artificial Intelligence: A multi-model study of demographics and imaging equipment in AI-generated videos and images of Canadian medical radiation technologists
venue: Journal of medical imaging and radiation sciences
outcome: Demographic and equipment representation in AI-generated depictions of Canadian medical radiation technologists versus workforce data
effect: Visible minorities 39% vs 20.8%; males 41.4% vs 21.2%; women 58.5% vs 78.8% (all p<0.001); younger age skew; 26% of outputs showed inaccurate or fictional equipment.
quote: AI depictions included a higher proportion of visible minorities (as defined by Statistics Canada) (39% vs. 20.8%, p < 0.001) and males (41.4% vs. 21.2%, p < 0.001), while underrepresenting women (58.5% vs. 78.8%, p < 0.001).

title: Development and Validation of an Electronic Health Record-Derived Prediction Model for Preventing COVID-19 Hospitalization and Death
venue: Prevention science : the official journal of the Society for Prevention Research
outcome: Model performance across racial and ethnic subgroups
effect: Supplemental analyses confirmed strong model performance across racial and ethnic subgroups and over time.
quote: Supplemental analyses confirmed strong model performance across racial and ethnic subgroups and over time.

title: Utility and Safety of Artificial Intelligence for Patient-Initiated Contact After Functional Rhinoplasty
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level readability of chatbot responses to patient questions
effect: Perplexity most readable (median FK 13.2), ChatGPT least readable (16.8; P < .0001); all above typical patient reading levels.
quote: Perplexity was the most readable (median FK 13.2), and ChatGPT the least (16.8; P < .0001).

title: Utility and Safety of Artificial Intelligence for Patient-Initiated Contact After Functional Rhinoplasty
outcome: Expert approval of chatbot responses to red flag postoperative complication questions
effect: Experts unanimously approved ChatGPT responses 96% of the time overall and 100% for the 6 Red Flag Questions.
quote: Experts unanimously approved ChatGPT responses (mean EOQ = 1) 96% of the time, and 100% for Red Flag Questions.

title: Computational Pupillometry and the Pupil Reactivity (PuRe) Score in Neurocritical Care: Prospects for High-Accuracy, Lighting-Invariant Neuromonitoring
outcome: Stability of AI-derived PuRe Score versus standard pupil parameters across ambient light conditions (4-1,200 lux)
effect: Standard PLR parameters varied up to 133% with light (p<0.001); PuRe Scores were stable: median 2.64 in dim vs 2.42 in bright light (p=0.449; r=-0.026).
quote: Standard pupillary light reflex parameters showed high light dependence with variations up to 133% (p<0.001), whereas PuRe Scores remained stable with medians of 2.64 in dim light versus 2.42 in bright light (p=0.449; r=-0.026).

title: Evaluation and tuning of a commercial automated planning system for prostate radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Whether tuning the model on selected local cases improved plan quality
effect: Two further model iterations tuned on locally selected cases produced comparable rectum sparing (0.02 mean difference in rectum V50Gy) while keeping much of the improved consistency.
quote: Further iterations of the model resulted in comparable rectum sparing, a 0.02 mean difference in rectum V50 Gy, was achieved whilst maintaining much of the improved consistency.

title: Evaluation and tuning of a commercial automated planning system for prostate radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Ability of CUSUM-based monitoring to detect deviations in plan quality metrics
effect: Wald sequential mean and variance tests reached decisions in tens of cases (delta=0.5) using 18 validation cases; validated as a post-deployment monitoring method.
quote: Two process control metrics have been demonstrated to monitor the introduction of AI planning into routine practice to ensure that the real-world performance was consistent with that projected.

title: Evaluation and tuning of a commercial automated planning system for prostate radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Local historical plan quality of automated plans versus clinical plans, and effect of tuning
effect: Baseline model had inferior rectum sparing (mean rectum V40Gy 0.04 higher); after two tuning iterations, differences were small (mean difference -0.01 rectum V40Gy, -0.03 PTV48 D98%).
quote: The Bland–Altman plots, supplementary Material S4, showed little difference between the original and automated plans for the third iteration.

title: Evaluation and tuning of a commercial automated planning system for prostate radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Feasibility of control-chart (Wald sequential test) monitoring of plan quality on validation cases
effect: Monitoring null hypothesis rejected quickly: after 10, 13 and 12 cases for the tested metrics; more than the 18 validation cases were needed in many cases to accept or reject hypotheses.
quote: This was reflected in the rapid rejection of H1; after 10 cases for PTV60 Gy D 98 % , 13 cases for PTV60 Gy D 98 % and 12 cases for the MCS.

title: Evaluation and tuning of a commercial automated planning system for prostate radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Initial local rectum sparing
effect: Initial automated plans had rectum V40Gy 0.04 (σ = 0.04) greater than original plans.
quote: The mean rectum V 40 G y was 0.04 ( σ = 0 . 04 ) greater for the automated plans in the initial evaluation ( Fig. 1(a) ).

title: Evaluation and tuning of a commercial automated planning system for prostate radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: AI versus human plan quality
effect: Final iteration mean difference −0.03 for PTV48 Gy D98% and −0.01 for rectum V40Gy.
quote: PTV coverage and rectum sparing was almost identical between the two groups, with a mean difference −0.03 for PTV48 Gy D 98 % coverage and −0.01 for rectum V 40 G y .

title: Evaluation and tuning of a commercial automated planning system for prostate radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Performance after model update
effect: Iteration 2 caused some PTV48 Gy D98% results below mandatory D99% threshold; iteration 3 was produced.
quote: In some cases the PTV 48 Gy D 98 % fell below the mandatory D99% threshold and so iteration three of the model was produced.

title: A Retrospective Comparison of Artificial Intelligence and the Orthopaedic Multi-disciplinary Team in the Management of Intracapsular Neck of Femur Fractures
outcome: Agreement between ChatGPT and consultant decisions on retrospective hip fracture cases
effect: Initial agreement low (κ = 0.03, 95% CI -0.11 to 0.19); validation cohort agreement κ = 0.29 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.60), not significantly different from initial.
quote: ChatGPT did not reliably replicate orthopaedic consultant decision-making for intracapsular NOF fractures.

title: A Retrospective Comparison of Artificial Intelligence and the Orthopaedic Multi-disciplinary Team in the Management of Intracapsular Neck of Femur Fractures
outcome: Generalization of in-session-adjusted ChatGPT agreement to independent validation dataset
effect: After in-session adjustment κ = 0.93 (95% CI 0.84-1.00) in primary cohort; in validation cohort agreement fell to κ = 0.29 (95% CI -0.04 to 0.60, p = 0.06).
quote: Although in-session adjustments produced high superficial concordance, this effect did not generalize to an independent dataset.

title: Unlocking Potential of Generative Large Language Models for Adverse Drug Reaction Relation Prediction in Discharge Summaries: Analysis and Strategy
outcome: Generative LLMs vs in-house fine-tuned model on ADR relation prediction F1 and recall
effect: On MIMIC-Unrestricted, Gemini 1.5 Pro F1 0.724 to 0.863 and recall 0.675 to 0.943; Llama 3.1 405B F1 0.724 to 0.814 and recall 0.675 to 0.948 versus BioM-ELECTRA-Large.
quote: Notably, on the MIMIC-Unrestricted dataset, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Llama 3.1 405B outperform our in-house fine-tuned BioM-ELECTRA-Large, with Gemini 1.5 Pro showing a 19.2% (0.724-0.863) improvement in F1 score and a 39.7% (0.675-0.943) increase in recall, while Llama 3.1 405B exhibits a 12.4% (0.724-0.814) improvement in F1 and a 40.4% (0.675-0.948) boost in recall.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Adoption, Policies, and Goals in Family Medicine: A Survey of Department Chairs
venue: Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine : JABFM
outcome: Share of departments reporting formal written AI policies, strategic plans, or frameworks
effect: 37.6% (41/109) reported formal organizational policies, while 56.9% (62/109) reported current AI use.
quote: Current AI use was reported by 56.9% (62/109), while 37.6% (41/109) indicated formal organizational policies.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Adoption, Policies, and Goals in Family Medicine: A Survey of Department Chairs
venue: Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine : JABFM

outcome: Accuracy, F1, and calibration error of Gemini ICL versus fine-tuned RETFound on the same DR data

title: Can a Natural Image-Based Foundation Model Outperform a Retina-Specific Model in Detecting Ocular and Systemic Diseases?
outcome: Head-to-head AUC comparison of candidate foundation models on same ocular and systemic disease tasks
effect: DINOv2-Large DR AUCs 0.850-0.952 vs RETFound 0.823-0.944 (all P≤0.007); RETFound better for systemic incidence prediction (AUC 0.796 HF, 0.732 MI, 0.754 stroke vs DINOv2 0.663-0.771, P<0.001).
quote: Conversely, for systemic disease incidence prediction, RETFound achieved superior AUCs of 0.796 (heart failure), 0.732 (myocardial infarction), and 0.754 (ischemic stroke), outperforming DINOv2's best models' AUC (0.663-0.771, all P < 0.001).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Colonoscopy: A Tool, Not a Necessity for Experts
outcome: Adenoma detection rate and polyp detection rate with versus without AI-assisted colonoscopy
effect: ADR 35% pre-AI vs 31% with AI (p=0.2); PDR 42% vs 38% (p=0.22); adenomas per colonoscopy 0.62 vs 0.51 (p=0.22); withdrawal time shorter with AI (9.34 vs 10.44 min, p<0.0001).
quote: ADR was 151 (35%) in the pre-AIAC group and 116 (31%) in AIAC group, with no statistical significance (p = 0.2).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Colonoscopy: A Tool, Not a Necessity for Experts
outcome: Endoscopist detection performance with AI in intended workflow versus without AI
effect: No significant improvement in ADR (35% vs 31%, p=0.2) or PDR (42% vs 38%, p=0.22) for experienced endoscopist; withdrawal time significantly shorter with AI (9.34 vs 10.44 min; p<0.0001).
quote: AIAC may not significantly improve adenoma or PDRs when performed by an experienced endoscopist.

title: Comparison of GPT-4o With Human Performance in the Polish Vascular Surgery Specialty Examination
outcome: Correlation between model self-reported confidence rating and answer correctness on exam questions
effect: ChatGPT-4o answered 88 of 120 correctly (73.3%), but its self-reported confidence levels did not largely correlate with accuracy, so it could not consistently predict its own performance.
quote: The model's self-reported confidence levels did not largely correlate with its response accuracy.

title: The ABCs of PEMs: Using Artificial Intelligence to Enhance the Readability of Patient Educational Materials in Pediatric Orthopaedics
venue: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated versus OrthoInfo patient education materials
effect: ChatGPT average grade level 8.7, OpenEvidence 10.1, OrthoInfo 10.8, all above the 6th-grade target despite a prompt requesting sixth-grade level.
quote: ChatGPT-generated PEMs had the lowest average reading grade level (8.7) compared to OrthoInfo (10.8) and Open Evidence (10.1).

title: The ABCs of PEMs: Using Artificial Intelligence to Enhance the Readability of Patient Educational Materials in Pediatric Orthopaedics
venue: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
outcome: Reading level of patient education materials versus recommended 6th-grade level
effect: OrthoInfo PEMs averaged 10.8 grade level; AI outputs 8.7 (ChatGPT) and 10.1 (OpenEvidence), all above 6th-grade recommendation.
quote: While OrthoInfo remains the gold standard in content accuracy and completeness, it falls short of national readability guidelines.

title: The ABCs of PEMs: Using Artificial Intelligence to Enhance the Readability of Patient Educational Materials in Pediatric Orthopaedics
venue: Journal of the Pediatric Orthopaedic Society of North America
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of AI-generated pediatric orthopaedic PEMs rated by blinded surgeons
effect: Total accuracy: OrthoInfo 6.95, ChatGPT 6.15, OpenEvidence 3.25; total completeness: OrthoInfo 6.98, ChatGPT 5.90, OpenEvidence 3.05.
quote: OrthoInfo PEMs were rated highest for accuracy and completeness (total accuracy: 6.95; total completeness: 6.98), compared to Chat GPT (total accuracy: 6.15; total completeness: 5.90) and Open Evidence (total accuracy: 3.25; total completeness: 3.05), but ChatGPT approached OrthoInfo in several subdomains, including treatment descriptions, timeline, and follow-up recommendations.

title: An integrated and interpretable machine learning framework for Kawasaki disease diagnosis and risk prediction
outcome: Model accuracy versus pediatricians and ChatGPT for KD diagnosis, IVIG resistance, CAL prediction
effect: Model accuracies were 0.900, 0.800, and 0.757 for KD diagnosis, IVIG resistance, and CAL prediction, outperforming pediatricians with over 5 years of experience and ChatGPT.
quote: In a comparative study, our model achieved accuracies of 0.900, 0.800, and 0.757 for KD diagnosis, IVIG resistance, and CAL prediction, respectively, consistently outperforming pediatricians with over 5 years of experience and ChatGPT, highlighting its potential as a clinical decision support tool.
sample_unit: pediatric patients (typical and atypical Kawasaki disease cases)

title: Assessment of demographic bias in retinal age prediction machine learning models
outcome: Retinal age prediction error (MAE) and age gap differences by sex and ethnicity across imaging modalities
effect: Combined CFP+OCT MAE 3.01 years vs CFP 3.40 and OCT 4.37. Significant sex differences only in CFP model (p<0.001); significant ethnicity differences only in OCT model (p<0.001); none in combined model.
quote: Significant sex differences were observed only in the CFP model (p < 0.001), while significant ethnicity differences appeared only in the OCT model (p < 0.001).

title: Ambient AI-assited clinical documentation in surgical outpatient care: a preliminary study of usability, workflow, and patient experience
outcome: Billing metrics, pajama time, mental demand, and burnout after ambient AI scribe pilot
effect: Billing showed no significant changes, so no upcoding signal. Pajama time did not change (p=0.55). NASA-TLX mental demand fell 14 to 5 (p=0.08), and burnout fell from 67% to 33%.
quote: The billing metric showed no significant changes.
sample_unit: ambulatory providers (three surgeons in the surgical subgroup)

title: An AI-Powered Lifestyle Intervention vs Human Coaching in the Diabetes Prevention Program
outcome: Composite of weight loss, physical activity, and HbA1c outcomes for AI-led vs human-led DPP in a noninferiority RCT
effect: Primary outcome achieved by 58/183 (31.7%) AI-led vs 59/185 (31.9%) human-led; risk difference -0.2% (1-sided 95% CI, -8.2%), meeting the noninferiority criterion.
quote: The primary outcome was achieved by 58 of 183 participants (31.7%) in the AI-led DPP group and 59 of 185 (31.9%) in the human-led DPP group (risk difference, -0.2% [1-sided 95% CI, -8.2%]), meeting the criterion for noninferiority.

title: Compliance and factuality of large language models for clinical research document generation
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Regulatory compliance and factual accuracy of ICFs with retrieval-augmented pipeline vs baseline LLMs
effect: Baseline LLMs (e.g., GPT-4o) achieved 70%-80% compliance with factual errors in 18%-43% of cases; InformGen (retrieval-augmented, human-in-the-loop) achieved nearly 100% compliance and over 90% factual accuracy.
quote: In contrast, InformGen substantially improved outputs, achieving nearly 100% regulatory compliance and over 90% factual accuracy, as validated by 5 domain-expert annotators.

title: Compliance and factuality of large language models for clinical research document generation
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: LLM-generated consent form accuracy and compliance assessed against regulatory guidelines and templates with expert annotators

title: Compliance and factuality of large language models for clinical research document generation

outcome: Stereotyping or negative depictions of older adults and people with dementia in generated images
effect: Both models more often portrayed subjects with negative affect in response to dementia-related prompts than for control prompts. DALL-E 3 also generated more positive-affect personas. Chi-square tests showed significant disparities versus controls.
quote: Both models more often portrayed subjects in response to dementia-related prompts with negative affect, in less favorable emotional states.

title: Experimental investigation of real-time 3D beam's eye view image-guided radiotherapy for prostate SBRT
outcome: Localization accuracy across varying plan complexity, static and dynamic motion conditions
effect: Overall accuracy 0.1 ± 0.7 mm (SI), -0.1 ± 0.8 mm (AP), 0.1 ± 0.7 mm (LR); within ±2 mm in all individual tests; latency 300 ± 100 ms.

title: Barriers and enablers for generative artificial intelligence in clinical psychology: a qualitative study based on the COM-B and theoretical domains framework (TDF) models
outcome: Psychologists' perceived barriers and facilitators to GenAI adoption, including AI understanding
effect: Of 18 factors identified, 12 were barriers and 6 were facilitators. A lack of understanding of AI was a highlighted barrier, and training in AI skills was a main facilitator.
quote: Highlighted barriers included a lack of understanding of AI and concerns about the confidentiality and privacy of information shared in therapy, while the main facilitators were training in AI skills and the possibility of having a digital assistant.

title: Assessing the utility and challenges for implementation of a risk prediction system: a usability study with hospital pharmacists
venue: Journal of pharmaceutical health care and sciences
outcome: Pharmacist perceptions of usability and integration barriers of a paper-format prediction tool
effect: Some participants gave neutral feedback on ease of use (10/49, 20.4%); manual data input and paper format were identified as limitations, with EHR integration needed.
quote: One concern was the inconvenience of implementing a paper-format tool in clinical environments that primarily operate on electronic health records.

title: Evaluating the robustness of slide-level AI predictions on out-of-focus whole slide images: A retrospective observational study
outcome: AI slide-level prediction robustness to image blur perturbation
effect: Blur metrics did not differ between concordant and discordant slides (p>0.05 except one pair); performance stayed robust at blur radius 1 (top 8.6% and 12.15% of blurriness); slide embedding cosine similarity >0.99 up to ±3 μm.
quote: Model performance remained robust even at a high blur level (radius = 1), where the patch image had a Laplacian variance of 133.14 and a wavelet score of 1667.98, corresponding to the top 8.6% and 12.15% of blurriness, respectively, in our dataset.

title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for accurate detection of wrong blood in tube errors in hospitalized patients
outcome: Discrimination of ML model versus multivariate Mahalanobis and univariate delta checks on same internal data
effect: The model consistently outperformed both the multivariate Mahalanobis approach and univariate delta checks within the internal cohort.
quote: The model consistently outperformed both the multivariate Mahalanobis approach and univariate delta checks within the internal cohort.

title: Development and validation of a machine learning model for accurate detection of wrong blood in tube errors in hospitalized patients

title: Readability of Chatbot Responses in Prostate Cancer and Urological Care: Objective Metrics Versus Patient Perceptions

quote: Chatbot responses were objectively written at a difficult reading level, exceeding recommendations for optimized health literacy.

title: Readability of Chatbot Responses in Prostate Cancer and Urological Care: Objective Metrics Versus Patient Perceptions
outcome: Reading level of chatbot responses relative to recommended reading level

title: Diagnostic Performance of GPT-4o Compared to Radiology Residents in Emergency Abdominal Tomography Cases
outcome: GPT-4o diagnostic accuracy versus radiology residents on same emergency abdominal CT cases
effect: Overall accuracy 76% for R1-R2, 89% for R3, 82% for R4-R5, 84% for R6, and 82% for GPT-4o; no statistically significant differences between GPT-4o and residents (p > 0.05).
quote: No statistically significant differences in diagnostic accuracy were found between GPT-4o and the residents, regardless of the experience level or case difficulty (p > 0.05).

title: Diagnostic Performance of GPT-4o Compared to Radiology Residents in Emergency Abdominal Tomography Cases

effect: Online dermatology health information often exceeds the recommended sixth-grade reading level; LLMs reworded texts to a sixth-grade level and significantly improved readability (p<0.01).
quote: Online health information (OHI) in dermatology often exceeds the recommended sixth-grade reading level, hindering patient comprehension.
sample_unit: online web texts on generalized pustular psoriasis

title: Utility and Limitations of Large Language Models to Simplify Online Content on Generalized Pustular Psoriasis
outcome: readability and DISCERN quality
effect: All LLMs significantly improved readability/reduced reading level (p<0.01) but had lower DISCERN scores than original text (p<0.01).
quote: All LLMs significantly reduced readability (p<0.01) but scored lower on the DISCERN instrument compared to the original text (p<0.01).

title: Utility and Limitations of Large Language Models to Simplify Online Content on Generalized Pustular Psoriasis
outcome: plain-language patient education quality

quote: While LLMs improved readability, they did not preserve the original content's reliability and quality.

title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini in brain-computer interfaces patient education: A multi-dimensional analysis of reliability, accuracy, comprehensibility, and readability
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level and reading ease) of LLM patient education responses about BCI
effect: For 12 of 13 questions, Gemini text required a significantly lower reading grade level than ChatGPT (p < 0.05) with higher reading ease, implying ChatGPT text was harder to read.
quote: However, a clear significant disparity emerged in the dimension of readability: for 12 of the 13 questions, the text generated by Gemini required a significantly lower reading grade level than that of ChatGPT (p < 0.05) and had significantly higher reading ease scores.

title: Comparative Evaluation and Performance of Large Language Models in Clinical Infection Control Scenarios: A Benchmark Study
outcome: Clinical knowledge errors and incomplete differentials in LLM infection control recommendations, qualitatively reviewed
effect: Critical deficiencies in all models: DeepSeek V3 recommended TB treatment without considering NTM; GPT-4.1 wrongly advised against single-room isolation for MDRA; wrong C. auris screening sites.
quote: These findings, summarized in Table 6 , reveal that even the higher-performing models may generate clinically significant and potentially unsafe recommendations.

title: Comparative Evaluation and Performance of Large Language Models in Clinical Infection Control Scenarios: A Benchmark Study
outcome: Output quality after structured prompting
effect: Composite score improved overall (p = 0.019); evidence quality improved +0.765, +1.106, and +0.425 with p < 0.001.
quote: The analysis of the structured prompt’s effect revealed that this approach led to a small but statistically significant improvement in the composite score across all LLMs.
sample_unit: clinical infection control scenarios (165 outputs rated by 16 experts)

title: Comparative Evaluation and Performance of Large Language Models in Clinical Infection Control Scenarios: A Benchmark Study
outcome: Inaccurate LLM infection control recommendations versus expert panel corrections
effect: Qualitative review found factual inaccuracies and unsafe advice across all three models despite generally positive scores (composite means 36.77, 36.25, 33.22).
quote: These errors highlight potential safety risks and limited real-world applicability, despite generally positive scores.
sample_unit: clinical infection control scenarios (165 outputs rated by 16 experts)

title: Comparative Evaluation and Performance of Large Language Models in Clinical Infection Control Scenarios: A Benchmark Study
outcome: Reliability of LLM outputs for autonomous use versus adjunct use in infection control
effect: Critical errors found in all models; authors conclude LLMs are not reliable for autonomous use and should serve as adjuncts.
quote: While GPT-4.1 and DeepSeek V3 deliver useful IPC advice, they are not yet reliable for autonomous use.
sample_unit: clinical infection control scenarios (165 outputs rated by 16 experts)

title: Comparative Evaluation and Performance of Large Language Models in Clinical Infection Control Scenarios: A Benchmark Study
outcome: Incorrect recommendation requiring verification
effect: GPT-4.1 advised against single-room isolation for MDRA; Table 6 rated potential harm as High.
