title: ChatGPT in Oral Pathology: Bright Promise or Diagnostic Mirage
outcome: Diagnostic sensitivity of ChatGPT-4o for OSCC, oral leukoplakia and oral lichen planus from clinical photographs
effect: Sensitivity was 65% for OSCC, 60% for OL and 25% for OLP; specificity 96.1-100%; a significant proportion of true cases were missed, so it cannot serve as a standalone diagnostic tool.
quote: Nevertheless, its sensitivity remains insufficient, as a significant proportion of true cases were missed, underscoring that the model cannot be relied upon as a standalone diagnostic tool.

title: Language Models for Standardising Clinical Notes and Information Extraction in Addiction Psychiatry-An Empirical Study
outcome: Gold standard annotations by clinicians used to evaluate proofreading and extraction
effect: Annotations by a team of doctors and nurses provided the gold standard; fine-tuned model outperformed GPT-4o on both tasks; masked raters preferred model versions 62% of trials (p<0.001).
quote: Annotations by a team of doctors and nurses provided the gold standard.

title: AI-Enabled ECG Analysis Improves Diagnostic Accuracy and Reduces False STEMI Activations: A Multicenter U.S. Registry
outcome: AI ECG versus standard triage sensitivity, specificity, and false positive activation rate against angiographic reference
effect: Sensitivity 92.0% vs 71.0%; specificity 81.0% vs 29.0%; FPA rate 7.9% vs 41.8% (P<0.001 for all); AUROC 0.94.
quote: The AI ECG model outperformed standard triage, demonstrating higher index ECG sensitivity (553 of 601 [92.0%; 95% CI: 89.7%-94.1%] vs 427 of 601 [71.0%; 95% CI: 67.4%-74.6%]), reducing FPA rates (34 of 431 [7.9%; 95% CI: 6.4%-9.6%] vs 180 of 431 [41.8%; 95% CI: 38.9%-44.7%]), and improving specificity (431 of 531 [81.0%; 95% CI: 77.2%-84.5%] vs 154 of 531 [29.0%; 95% CI: 24.8%-33.4%]) (P < 0.001 for all).
sample_unit: patients with suspected STEMI triggering emergent CCL activation

title: Evaluating AI performance in infectious disease education: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Google Bard, Perplexity AI, Microsoft Copilot, and Meta AI
outcome: Reproducibility of answers when identical prompts were resubmitted 24 hours apart
effect: ChatGPT 3.5 showed a 7.5% accuracy decline on repeat testing; some models gave different antimicrobial recommendations for the same case; Microsoft Copilot was most stable.
quote: AI-generated responses were found to change over time, with some models giving different antimicrobial recommendations for the same case scenario upon repeated testing.

title: Evaluating AI performance in infectious disease education: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Google Bard, Perplexity AI, Microsoft Copilot, and Meta AI
outcome: Accuracy of antimicrobial selection and dosing recommendations
effect: Therapy-related questions had the lowest accuracy (57.1%); ChatGPT 3.5 antimicrobial treatment accuracy was 56.6%; Perplexity AI and Meta AI showed variability in drug selection and dosing adjustments.
quote: AI platforms offer potential in infectious disease education but demonstrate limitations in pharmacotherapy decision-making, particularly in antimicrobial selection and dosing accuracy.

title: Deploying machine learning models in clinical settings: a real-world feasibility analysis for a model identifying adult-onset type 1 diabetes initially classified as type 2
outcome: Performance of locally retrained model versus national model on regional HIE data (AUROC, precision at 5% recall)
effect: Localized model AUROC 0.774 vs national 0.751; precision at 5% recall 35.4% vs 25.5%; PR CIs overlap, so differences modest and localization is effort-intensive.
quote: Model localization involved retraining on the regional dataset and resulted in improved AUROC (increased from 0.751 to 0.774), AUPRC (from 5.48% to 6.88%), and precision on the highest scoring patients (from 25.5% to 35.4% at 5% recall).
sample_unit: adult type 2 diabetes patients in regional HIE dataset (2,564,877 patient cross-sections)

title: Deploying machine learning models in clinical settings: a real-world feasibility analysis for a model identifying adult-onset type 1 diabetes initially classified as type 2
outcome: Discrepancies between national development data and regional deployment data in demographics and data capture
effect: Regional data had lower capture of weight (65% vs 97.5%), BMI, HbA1c and insulin records; Caucasian share 60%/55% vs 84%/81% nationally; only 415 of 536 facilities share diagnoses.
quote: Moreover, records of vitals (weight and BMI), lab test results (HbA1c), and prescribed medications (insulin) were found more frequently overall in the national dataset compared to the regional one.
sample_unit: adult type 2 diabetes patients in regional HIE dataset (2,564,877 patient cross-sections)

title: Deploying machine learning models in clinical settings: a real-world feasibility analysis for a model identifying adult-onset type 1 diabetes initially classified as type 2
outcome: local input availability across HIE facilities
effect: Only 415/536 facilities shared diagnoses; among these, 87% shared medications, 87% vital signs, 68% labs, and 21% procedures.
quote: Out of 536 health facilities contributing to the HIE data pool, we found that only 415 share diagnoses records, which are crucial for identifying T2D patients and building cohorts for this study.
sample_unit: adult type 2 diabetes patients in regional HIE dataset (2,564,877 patient cross-sections)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for Accuracy and Completeness of Vitiligo Patient Education: A Comparative Analysis
outcome: Readability of LLM vitiligo patient education responses (Flesch Reading Ease)
effect: Elevated reading difficulty across all models; DeepSeek-R1 lowest readability (mean Flesch Reading Ease 19.7), significantly lower than OpenAI o1 and Grok 3 (both p < 0.01).
quote: Readability assessments revealed elevated reading difficulty across all models, with DeepSeek-R1 exhibiting the lowest readability (mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 19.7; pairwise comparisons showed DeepSeek-R1 scores were significantly lower than those of OpenAI o1 and Grok 3, both p < 0.01), potentially reducing accessibility for diverse patient populations.

title: Evaluating Web Retrieval-Assisted Large Language Models With and Without Whitelisting for Evidence-Based Neurology: Comparative Study
outcome: Correct-answer rate of web-RAG LLMs with vs without whitelisting retrieval to authoritative neurology domains
effect: Correct rates open vs whitelisted: Sonar 60% vs 78%, Sonar-Pro 80% vs 88%, Sonar-Reasoning-Pro 81% vs 89%; mean accuracy gains 0.23, 0.08, 0.08 on 0-2 scale.
quote: Restricting retrieval to authoritative neurology domains yielded a clinically meaningful 8 to 18 percentage-point gain in correctness and halved output variability, upgrading a consumer search assistant to a decision-support-level tool that at least performed on par with a specialized literature engine.

title: Hallucination in artificial-intelligence-assisted diagnosis of arthritis: a case report
outcome: Presence of hallucination in ChatGPT-4o interpretation of imaging, labs, and treatment recommendations
effect: In a single case of hand arthralgia, ChatGPT-4o fabricated unsupported or inaccurate information in radiologic and laboratory analysis and in treatment recommendations.
quote: The AI-generated interpretation demonstrated hallucination-namely, the fabrication of unsupported or inaccurate information-in the analysis of radiologic and laboratory findings, as well as in treatment recommendations.

title: Detecting Laterality Errors in Combined Radiographic Studies by Enhancing the Traditional Approach With GPT-4o: Algorithm Development and Multisite Internal Validation
outcome: Precision on real-world imbalanced data versus synthetic balanced data
effect: GPT-4o precision fell from 0.979 on synthetic Test-2 to 0.219 on real-world Test-1. ClinicalBERT precision fell from 0.984 to 0.047. Test-1 membership predicted false positives (GPT-4o OR 239.89).
quote: Both ClinicalBERT and GPT-4o exhibited notable declines in precision on TrainVal and Test-1 compared to Test-2.

title: Detecting Laterality Errors in Combined Radiographic Studies by Enhancing the Traditional Approach With GPT-4o: Algorithm Development and Multisite Internal Validation
outcome: Benchmark performance on synthetic balanced data versus real-world imbalanced reports
effect: Synthetic balanced data gave F1 of 0.966 for GPT-4o and 0.959 for rule-based+GPT-4o. On real-world Test-1, F1 was 0.352 for GPT-4o and 0.780 for rule-based+GPT-4o.
quote: A significant performance gap exists between balanced synthetic datasets and imbalanced real-world data.

title: Detecting Laterality Errors in Combined Radiographic Studies by Enhancing the Traditional Approach With GPT-4o: Algorithm Development and Multisite Internal Validation
outcome: Comparison of the candidate ensemble against GPT-4o, ClinicalBERT and RoBERTa on the same test data
effect: On Test-1, rule-based+GPT-4o had F1 0.780, versus 0.352 for GPT-4o, 0.088 for ClinicalBERT and 0.000 for RoBERTa.
quote: In experiment 2, on Test-1, rule-based+GPT-4o (precision=0.696; recall=0.889; F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.780) outperformed GPT-4o (precision=0.219; recall=0.889; F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.352), ClinicalBERT (precision=0.047; recall=0.667; F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.088), and RoBERTa (F<sub>1</sub>-score=0.000).

title: Performance of Large Language Models on the Acute Coronary Syndrome Guidelines Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation
outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to ACS guideline questions with versus without RAG grounding
effect: ChatGPT-4o rose from 71.1% without RAG to 92.1% with RAG (P = 0.017); DeepSeek R1 with RAG reached 94.7% versus 78.9% without RAG.
quote: ChatGPT-4o without RAG achieved 71.1% accuracy (95% CI: 55.2%-83.0%), which significantly improved with RAG (P = 0.017).

title: Evaluating the performance of large language models versus human researchers on real world complex medical queries
outcome: Hallucinated and unfaithful citations in LLM reports versus human reports
effect: Human reports contained no hallucinated (p < 0.001) or unfaithful (p < 0.001) citations, unlike LLM reports.
quote: Unlike LLMs, human reports contained no hallucinated (p < 0.001) or unfaithful (p < 0.001) citations.

title: Evaluating the performance of large language models versus human researchers on real world complex medical queries
outcome: LLM reports contain hallucinated citations that clinicians would need to verify before acting
effect: LLM reports contained hallucinated and unfaithful citations while human reports had none (p < 0.001 for both).
quote: Unlike LLMs, human reports contained no hallucinated (p < 0.001) or unfaithful (p < 0.001) citations.

title: Evaluating the performance of large language models versus human researchers on real world complex medical queries
outcome: Correlation between physician satisfaction and objective report quality
effect: No meaningful correlation between physician satisfaction and objective measures of report quality, so satisfaction is not a good quality measure.
quote: However, no meaningful correlation was identified between physician satisfaction and objective measures of report quality.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models in Explaining Radiology Reports: Expert Assessment of Readability, Understandability, and Communication Features
outcome: Readability (FRE, ARI, GFI) of LLM radiology report explanations relative to patient reading level
effect: ChatGPT most readable (FRE 60.33 ± 3.65; ARI 9.66 ± 1.01; GFI 9.1 ± 1.04), with ARI and GFI grade levels around 9-10 (above typical recommended patient reading level).
quote: ChatGPT produced the most readable (FRE: 60.33 ± 3.65; ARI: 9.66 ± 1.01; GFI: 9.1 ± 1.04) and understandable (PEMAT-U: 89.58 ± 3.90%) responses (p < 0.01).

title: [Assessing the accuracy and comprehensiveness of large language models in responding to patient inquiries on placenta accreta spectrum]
outcome: LLM answer accuracy and comprehensiveness rated by expert physicians against ratings
effect: Accuracy differed significantly across models (P=0.005). 25% (4/16) of Model A responses rated good vs 75% (12/16) for Models B and D.
quote: 25% (4/16) of Model A responses were rated as "good", which was lower than the 75% (12/16) for both Model B and Model D (both P<0.05).

title: Fully Automatic AI-Based Quantification of LV Mass in Echocardiography: A Multimodality Validation
outcome: AI vs expert manual echo LV mass measurement accuracy against CT reference
effect: AI reduced measurement error by ~20% vs expert; AUC for increased LV mass 0.78 vs 0.71 (linear) and 0.84 vs 0.77 (hybrid).
quote: Diagnostic accuracy for detecting increased LV mass was higher with AI echocardiography than with Expert echocardiography (AUC: 0.78 vs 0.71 for linear; 0.84 vs 0.77 for hybrid).

title: Automated Scan Region Classification and Patient-specific Dose Modeling for Enhanced Dose Management in Computed Tomography
outcome: Number of cases flagged for review by patient-specific outlier method versus fixed DRL exceedances
effect: Patient-specific models flagged 60 statistical outliers versus 170 DRL exceedances; all flagged cases manually confirmed as clinically justified.
quote: Crucially, the patient-specific models identified substantially fewer cases for review (60 statistical outliers) compared with the standard DRL-based method (170 exceedances).

title: Artificial intelligence in patient education: evaluating large language models for understanding rheumatology literature
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT-simplified summaries versus recommended sixth-grade level
effect: ChatGPT reduced reading level from about 15th grade (FKGL 15.06, SMOG 14.08) to 10th grade (FKGL 10.52, SMOG 9.48), still above the recommended sixth-grade level.
quote: However, the achieved 10th-grade reading level still exceeds the recommended sixth-grade level for patient education materials.

title: Artificial intelligence in patient education: evaluating large language models for understanding rheumatology literature
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education summaries
effect: Summaries improved readability (P < .0001) but remained at 10th-grade level (FKGL 10.52, SMOG 9.48), above the sixth-grade target for patients.
quote: However, the achieved 10th-grade reading level still exceeds the recommended sixth-grade level for patient education materials.

title: Medical Feature Extraction From Clinical Examination Notes: Development and Evaluation of a Two-Phase Large Language Model Framework
outcome: Calibration (ECE, Brier score, average confidence) after confidence-regularization fine-tuning for feature extraction
effect: ECE rose from 0.060 to 0.147 while Brier score improved from 0.087 to 0.036; average confidence stayed at 0.84 (SD 0.003) as F1 rose from 0.819 to 0.986.
quote: Calibration evaluation on few-shot training (100 patient notes) showed that the expected calibration error increased from 0.060 to 0.147, whereas the Brier score improved from 0.087 to 0.036.

title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok on familial mediterranean fever: are they trustworthy?
outcome: Reproducibility of chatbot responses when queries repeated 1 week later
effect: ChatGPT showed the greatest consistency (89.7% reproducibility); the abstract notes inconsistencies across chatbots.
quote: ChatGPT demonstrated the greatest consistency (89.7% reproducibility) and provided no misleading content.

title: ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok on familial mediterranean fever: are they trustworthy?
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of chatbot clinical knowledge on FMF, including diagnosis
effect: Comprehensive/correct responses: Gemini 87.7%, Grok 83.6%, ChatGPT 81.6%; Grok gave 4.0% misleading responses, mainly on diagnosis; diagnostic performance notably lower.
quote: Grok was the only model to produce misleading responses (4.0%), primarily in diagnosis-related answers.

title: Development and prospective evaluation of a machine learning model to predict vomiting among pediatric cancer and hematopoietic cell transplant patients
outcome: Prospective silent-trial AUROC versus retrospective AUROC for vomiting prediction
effect: AUROC 0.730 (95% CI 0.694-0.765) retrospective vs 0.716 (95% CI 0.649-0.784) in the prospective silent trial; performance was retained, with no notable degradation.
quote: This model retained satisfactory performance in a prospective silent trial.
sample_unit: admissions (7,408 retrospective plus 340 prospective silent trial)

title: Chatbots versus retina specialists in answering real-world retina questions
venue: International journal of retina and vitreous
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of chatbot versus specialist responses
effect: Retina specialists and Gemini produced more readable responses; ChatGPT 4.0, ConsensusGPT, and Claude 3 gave more detailed, accurate answers but required a higher reading level.
quote: In contrast, ChatGPT 4.0, ConsensusGPT, and Claude 3 delivered more detailed and accurate answers but required a higher reading level.

title: Evaluation of Alignment Between Large Language Models and Expert Clinicians in Suicide Risk Assessment
outcome: Whether chatbot direct vs. indirect responses to suicide queries matched clinician-rated risk levels
effect: Chatbots never answered very-high-risk queries directly, and ChatGPT and Claude answered very-low-risk queries directly 100% of the time. Intermediate risk levels were not distinguished (low, medium, high vs very low not significantly different). Claude AOR=2.01, Gemini AOR=0.09 vs ChatGPT.
quote: LLM-based chatbots' responses to queries aligned with experts' judgment about whether to respond to queries at the extremes of suicide risk (very low and very high), but the chatbots showed inconsistency in addressing intermediate-risk queries, underscoring the need to further refine LLMs.
sample_unit: chatbot responses (30 queries x 3 LLMs x 100 repetitions)

title: Can LLMs simplify operative notes? A comparative analysis in otorhinolaryngology
venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Readability of LLM-simplified operative notes across eight readability metrics and expert-rated clarity
effect: Claude 3.7 produced the most complex outputs; GPT-4o, Gemini, and DeepSeek produced the most readable texts. GPT-4o received the highest clarity ratings. Performance varied across subgroups.
quote: Claude 3.7 produced the most complex outputs, whereas GPT-4o, Gemini, and DeepSeek generated the most readable texts.

title: Performance of Large Language Models in Analyzing Common Hypertension Scenarios
outcome: Accuracy, safety, and guideline concordance of LLM hypertension management recommendations versus expert
effect: GPT-4 accuracy 83%, safety 86% vs expert 92%/93%; Gemini 64%/73%; MedLM 35%/39%. Guideline-concordant: GPT-4 46%, Gemini 35%, MedLM 14%, expert 68%.
quote: GPT-4 had the highest accuracy (83%) and safety (86%) scores among LLMs but remained inferior to expert responses (92% accuracy, 93% safety).

title: Performance of Large Language Models in Analyzing Common Hypertension Scenarios
outcome: LLM responses compared against hypertension expert responses on same vignettes
effect: All three LLMs scored below the expert on accuracy and safety; GPT-4 was closest (83% vs 92% accuracy), MedLM far lower (35%).
quote: Despite their potential, current LLM versions are inferior to expert recommendations.

title: Transcription Accuracy of Automatic Speech Recognition for Orthodontic Clinical Records
outcome: transcription hallucinations
effect: Whisper produced 57 hallucinations and DigitalTCO produced 1, while hallucinations were absent in other systems
quote: Hallucinations were absent except for Whisper (n = 57) and DigitalTCO (n = 1).
sample_unit: narrated orthodontic diagnostic and treatment planning summaries

title: Transcription Accuracy of Automatic Speech Recognition for Orthodontic Clinical Records
outcome: Comparative transcription accuracy across 10 ASR systems on same data
effect: GPT4oTranscribeCorrected best (DWER 3.5%; WER 3.7%); Heidi Health best commercial (DWER 6.2%); Dragon Professional Anywhere worst (WER 33.9%).
quote: Heidi Health was the highest-performing commercial system (DWER = 6.2%; WER = 5.4%), with Dragon Professional Anywhere being the worst (WER = 33.9%).
sample_unit: narrated orthodontic diagnostic and treatment planning summaries

title: Transcription Accuracy of Automatic Speech Recognition for Orthodontic Clinical Records
outcome: background noise effect on ASR errors
effect: Background noise increased DWER and WER (P < 0.001).
quote: Across systems, background noise increased DWER and WER (P < 0.001).
sample_unit: narrated orthodontic diagnostic and treatment planning summaries

title: Transcription Accuracy of Automatic Speech Recognition for Orthodontic Clinical Records
outcome: Clinically significant transcription errors that would require verification
effect: Clinically significant errors seen with all systems, ranging from 2% to 66% (GPT4oTranscribeCorrected clean; Dragon Medical One background noise).
quote: Importantly, clinically significant errors were seen with all systems, ranging from 2% to 66% (GPT4oTranscribeCorrected clean; Dragon Medical One background noise, respectively).
sample_unit: narrated orthodontic diagnostic and treatment planning summaries

title: Transcription Accuracy of Automatic Speech Recognition for Orthodontic Clinical Records
outcome: clinically significant transcription errors
effect: Clinically significant errors ranged from 2% to 66% across systems/conditions.
quote: Importantly, clinically significant errors were seen with all systems, ranging from 2% to 66% (GPT4oTranscribeCorrected clean; Dragon Medical One background noise, respectively).
sample_unit: narrated orthodontic diagnostic and treatment planning summaries

title: Appraisal of ChatGPT's responses to common patient questions regarding acromioclavicular joint dislocations
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses to AC joint dislocation patient questions using six metrics
effect: Readability scores showed moderate difficulty, suitable for a high school-level audience.
quote: Readability scores revealed moderate difficulty levels, suitable for a high school-level audience.

title: Appraisal of ChatGPT's responses to common patient questions regarding acromioclavicular joint dislocations
outcome: Surgeon-graded accuracy of ChatGPT clinical answers on 5-point Likert scale, by question category
effect: Average score 4/5 (good quality with minor inaccuracies); treatment questions scored lower than rehabilitation (P = .025).
quote: Treatment-related questions scored lower compared to other categories, with a significant difference observed between treatment and rehabilitation (P = .025).

title: ICU readmission and mortality risk prediction: Generalizability of a multi-hospital model
outcome: External-site AUROC of ICU readmission/mortality models versus internal performance
effect: Weighted AUROC on AUMC data: local MSZ 69.7%, OLVG 70.5%, AUMC (internal) 76.5%; pooled MSZ+OLVG model 71.1%. The internal-external gap shrank when cardiac surgery patients were excluded.
quote: Performance evaluation of the local models on AUMC data demonstrated weighted area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 69.7 %±0.8 %, 70.5 %±0.5 %, and 76.5 %±1.9 %, respectively, whereas the pooled model achieved a weighted area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 71.1 %±0.7 %.

title: ChatGPT in general surgery: a cross-sectional study assessing its response to patient questions
outcome: Readability (FKRE, SMOG) of ChatGPT responses to patient surgery questions
effect: Mean FKRE 24.3 ± 7.35 and mean SMOG 13.9 ± 1.22, indicating a difficult to very difficult reading level best suited for university graduates.
quote: The mean FKRE score was 24.3 ± 7.35 and the mean SMOG score was 13.9 ± 1.22, indicating a difficult to very difficult reading level best suited for university graduates.

title: ChatGPT in general surgery: a cross-sectional study assessing its response to patient questions
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education responses
effect: FKRE 24.3 and SMOG 13.9, a difficult to very difficult reading level suited to university graduates, i.e. not plain language.
quote: The mean FKRE score was 24.3 ± 7.35 and the mean SMOG score was 13.9 ± 1.22, indicating a difficult to very difficult reading level best suited for university graduates.

title: Reliability and Readability Assessment of Atrial Fibrillation Patient Information Delivered by Artificial Intelligence-Based Language Models (ChatGPT, YouChat, Gemini, and Perplexity AI) in English and Spanish
outcome: Readability of AI responses on atrial fibrillation (Flesch-Szigriszt) by model and language
effect: Significant readability differences between models (P < .01); ChatGPT performed best but its content was moderately challenging in Spanish and highly challenging in English.
quote: The ChatGPT demonstrated the highest performance, although its content was moderately challenging in Spanish and highly challenging in English.
sample_unit: standardised questions (posed in English and Spanish to each of 4 models)

title: Reliability and Readability Assessment of Atrial Fibrillation Patient Information Delivered by Artificial Intelligence-Based Language Models (ChatGPT, YouChat, Gemini, and Perplexity AI) in English and Spanish
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient information relative to patient needs
effect: Readability significantly differed between models (P < .01); even the best model, ChatGPT, was moderately challenging in Spanish and highly challenging in English.
quote: The ChatGPT demonstrated the highest performance, although its content was moderately challenging in Spanish and highly challenging in English.
sample_unit: standardised questions (posed in English and Spanish to each of 4 models)

title: A comparative study on the application of large language models: Deepseek-R1, GPT-4o, and Claude-Sonnet-4 in post-cardiac surgery rehabilitation-A cross-sectional study
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM responses under repeated prompting (five runs per question)
effect: DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest response stability (85.7%); GPT-4o showed lower reproducibility (62.9%). Differences were statistically significant (P < 0.05).
quote: GPT-4o outperformed the others in readability (FRE: 53.19) and linguistic fluency but showed lower reproducibility (62.9%).

title: A comparative study on the application of large language models: Deepseek-R1, GPT-4o, and Claude-Sonnet-4 in post-cardiac surgery rehabilitation-A cross-sectional study
outcome: Readability of LLM patient education responses (FRE, FKGL)
effect: GPT-4o had the best readability (FRE 53.19) among the three models. Differences were statistically significant. Grade-level results for the other models are not reported in the abstract.
quote: GPT-4o outperformed the others in readability (FRE: 53.19) and linguistic fluency but showed lower reproducibility (62.9%).

title: Large language models with retrieval-augmented generation enhance expert modelling of Bayesian network for clinical decision support
venue: International journal of computer assisted radiology and surgery
outcome: Faithfulness and retrieval accuracy of RAG-grounded LLM answers
effect: Recursive chunking with fine-tuned GTE-Large reached retrieval accuracy 0.9; query expansion raised semantic chunking accuracy from 0.75 to 0.85; faithfulness at least 0.9.
quote: Responses maintained high faithfulness ( ≥ 0.9).

title: Debunking Myths and Patient Education About Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Using Popular Generative Artificial Intelligence Chatbots
outcome: Readability of AI-generated and traditional CRPS patient education materials (Flesch Reading Ease)
effect: Gemini had the best readability (Flesch score 62); traditional PEMs and other AI-generated PEMs all scored <52, i.e., harder to read.
quote: Gemini had superior readability (Flesch score 62 as compared to Traditional PEMs and other AI generated PEMs all scoring <52) but lower specificity (66.67%) in debunking myths.
sample_unit: patient education materials (3 AI chatbots, 2 traditional sources, 15 myths)

title: Debunking Myths and Patient Education About Complex Regional Pain Syndrome Using Popular Generative Artificial Intelligence Chatbots
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of chatbot PEMs versus Cleveland Clinic and myth-debunking performance
effect: Cleveland Clinic accuracy 4.8 vs Gemini 3.4 (P=.004) and Llama 3.6 (P=.014); Gemini myth-debunking specificity 66.67%, ChatGPT 100%.
quote: Cleveland Clinic PEMs demonstrated the highest accuracy (4.8 ± 0.40 expressed as mean ± standard deviation, significantly outperforming Gemini (3.4 ± 0.49, P = .004) and Llama (3.6 ± 0.49, P = .014).
sample_unit: patient education materials (3 AI chatbots, 2 traditional sources, 15 myths)

title: Readability, linguistic complexity, and stigma in ChatGPT responses to opioid use disorder FAQs: A comparative analysis
outcome: Readability grade levels of ChatGPT responses versus health organization FAQs on OUD
effect: ChatGPT grade levels were consistently higher: Coleman-Liau +3.43, Gunning Fog +3.47, SMOG +2.96, Flesch-Kincaid +3.61, ARI +4.33, Flesch Reading Ease -20.4 (all p < .05).
quote: Readability grade levels were consistently higher: Coleman-Liau +3.43, Gunning Fog +3.47, SMOG + 2.96, Flesch-Kincaid +3.61, Automated Readability Index +4.33, and Flesch Reading Ease -20.4 (all p < .05).
sample_unit: FAQ questions paired with ChatGPT responses

title: Readability, linguistic complexity, and stigma in ChatGPT responses to opioid use disorder FAQs: A comparative analysis
outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated OUD patient education relative to FAQs
effect: ChatGPT responses were 3-4 grade levels higher across indices, longer (253.7 vs 76.6 words), with higher lexical density (+6.5 percentage points).
quote: ChatGPT produced more comprehensive but less readable content than FAQs, revealing a gap with health literacy standards.
sample_unit: FAQ questions paired with ChatGPT responses

title: Simulating a virtual tumor board with large language models: a pilot study in NSCLC patients receiving immunotherapy
outcome: LLM recommendation accuracy, consistency, applicability, and safety when grounded with in-context guidelines
effect: Mean scores 4.9/5.0 content accuracy, 5.0/5.0 internal consistency, 4.4/5.0 clinical applicability; no safety concerns identified in 10 cases (no ungrounded comparator).
quote: The combination of guideline injection and meticulous prompt engineering is a critical strategy for ensuring LLM reliability.

title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM treatment decisions across 10 repeated runs (ICC, entropy)
effect: Low reliability in raw experiment (ICC 0.0-1.0); GPT-3.5 and LLaMA-2 gave opposite answers to the identical prompt across runs; smaller models gave conflicting recommendations.
quote: Some LLMs gave indeterminate treatment recommendations in up to 54% of cases (eg, GPT-3.5) and showed low reliability as evidenced by low ICCs and high entropy values (eg, Mistral, LLaMA-2, and DeepSeek-R1).

title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
outcome: LLM agreement with heart team compared with a simple guideline-based non-LLM reference model
effect: Reference model outperformed LLMs on raw reports; only with summaries plus guideline text did GPT-4 models and DeepSeek-R1 draw level with it.
quote: The reference model outperformed the LLMs in the raw experiment regarding the metrics we assessed.

title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
outcome: LLM performance with lengthy unstructured raw reports versus curated case summaries
effect: Raw reports: Cohen kappa -0.47 to 0.22; with summaries plus guideline text kappa -0.02 to 0.63. Input representation was the most critical factor.
quote: This, along with the significant performance gains observed when providing case summaries instead of original medical reports, suggests that input data representation is the most critical factor in LLM performance.

title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
outcome: Effect of adding guideline summary to the prompt on agreement with heart team
effect: Adding guideline knowledge to raw reports did not substantially change performance (DeepSeek-R1 kappa 0.22 to 0.40); with summaries, sum+ peaked, giving the best results.
quote: The performance metrics of the other LLMs did not change substantially in the raw+ experiment.

title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
outcome: Whether a simple non-LLM model matches LLM performance on treatment decision
effect: Simple reference model performed comparably to GPT-4 and outperformed LLMs on raw reports, suggesting simpler models could suffice.
quote: In our study, as well as in the study by Salihu et al [ 8 ], simple reference models performed comparably to GPT-4, suggesting that non-LLM models could outperform LLMs if trained appropriately.

title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
outcome: Hallucinations in LLM treatment recommendations
effect: All LLMs produced hallucinations of varying severity and frequency in every experiment, including fabricated frailty and prior cardiac surgery and a fabricated surgery report.
quote: In each experiment, all LLMs produced hallucinations of varying severity and frequency.

title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
outcome: LLM treatment recommendation quality on real-world data
effect: LLMs gave poor agreement with the heart team on original reports and are deemed unsuitable as decision makers; some recommended heart transplantation, ignoring instructions.
quote: Overall, we conclude that LLMs are currently not suitable as decision makers for the treatment of patients with severe AS, as our results suggest that LLMs require elaborate preprocessing of patient data to make guideline-concordant treatment decisions.

title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
outcome: raw-report treatment decision performance
effect: Original medical reports: Cohen κ -0.47 to 0.22; ICC 0.0-1.0; FBI 0.95-1.51.
quote: When presented with original medical reports, LLMs showed poor performance (Cohen κ coefficient: -0.47 to 0.22; ICC: 0.0-1.0; FBI: 0.95-1.51).

title: Assessing the Limitations of Large Language Models in Clinical Practice Guideline-Concordant Treatment Decision-Making on Real-World Data: Retrospective Study
outcome: LLM decision performance compared with a simpler non-LLM reference model
effect: A simpler non-LLM guideline reference model outperformed all LLMs on raw medical reports, while LLMs only matched the reference model when given manually curated summaries.
quote: The reference model outperformed the LLMs in the raw experiment regarding the metrics we assessed.

title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases
outcome: Accuracy of adjuvant therapy recommendations, guideline-grounded RAG vs ungrounded LLMs vs tumor board consensus
effect: TSB (Claude-2 + NCCN RAG) accuracy 0.89 vs Claude-2 0.86 (P=.080) and GPT-4 0.78 (P<.001); GPT-4 much lower on genetic testing (OR 0.05).
quote: TSB achieved an overall accuracy of 0.89, compared with 0.86 for Claude-2 and 0.78 for GPT-4 across all seven modalities.

title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases
outcome: Whether AI flagged missing or anomalous input (menopausal status) that prevented valid output
effect: In a T2N1 case with unclear menopausal status, TSB recommended Oncotype testing, whereas MTB recommended chemotherapy; AI did not flag the missing variable.
quote: The AI did not identify the missing menopausal status as a critical variable.

title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases
outcome: Concordance of AI treatment recommendations with expert consensus and guidelines, discordant cases
effect: TSB recommended endocrine therapy for three low ER-positive DCIS cases where MTB withheld; also recommended redundant genetic testing and RT without considering margin status in two patients.
quote: Similarly, TSB automatically recommended RT after lumpectomy in two patients without considering margin status or the need for re-excision.

title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases
outcome: Recommendations reflecting available prior patient data (longitudinal recall)
effect: AI recommended genetic testing for a patient who had already undergone testing, reflecting limitation in longitudinal data recall.
quote: In another case, the AI recommended GT for a patient who had already undergone testing.

title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases
outcome: Candidate model comparison
effect: TSB accuracy 0.89, Claude-2 0.86, and GPT-4 0.78; GPT-4 was significantly lower than TSB (P < .001).
quote: TSB achieved an overall accuracy of 0.89, compared with 0.86 for Claude-2 and 0.78 for GPT-4 across all seven modalities.

title: Augmenting Large Language Models With National Comprehensive Cancer Network Guidelines for Improved and Standardized Adjuvant Therapy Recommendations in Postoperative Breast Cancer Cases
outcome: Uncertain-case deferral
effect: One T2N1 case with unclear menopausal status produced an Oncotype Dx recommendation instead of a flagged data gap needing clarification.
quote: The AI did not identify the missing menopausal status as a critical variable.

title: Universal black-box attacks against a third-party Alzheimer's diagnostic system
outcome: Diagnostic performance of third-party Alzheimer's system under universal black-box adversarial perturbations
effect: FGSM and DeepFool perturbations reliably degraded VolBrain diagnostic performance; DeepFool was more effective at comparable perturbation sizes; a simple Mean Attack also degraded performance. No numbers in the abstract.
quote: Our results show that these perturbations can reliably degrade the diagnostic performance of VolBrain, with DeepFool-based attacks being particularly effective for comparable perturbation sizes.

title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Responding to Patient Questions About Anterolateral Thigh Flap Surgery for Diabetic Foot Ulcers
outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT responses to patient FAQs on ALT flap surgery
effect: ChatGPT answered at a mean grade level of 19.8 ± 20.1, far above typical patient reading levels.
quote: ChatGPT answered at a mean grade level of 19.8 ± 20.1.

title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in Responding to Patient Questions About Anterolateral Thigh Flap Surgery for Diabetic Foot Ulcers
outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated patient materials
effect: Mean reading grade level of 19.8 ± 20.1 across 10 readability indexes, well above an appropriate patient reading level.
quote: ChatGPT answered at a mean grade level of 19.8 ± 20.1.

title: DietAI24 as a framework for comprehensive nutrition estimation using multimodal large language models
outcome: Nutrient estimation error (MAE) of MLLM grounded via RAG in FNDDS versus commercial and computer vision baselines
effect: 63% reduction in MAE for food weight and four key nutrients versus existing methods on real-world mixed dishes (p < 0.05); 65 nutrients estimated.
quote: DietAI24 demonstrates that integrating MLLMs with RAG and standardized nutrition databases can substantially improve dietary assessment accuracy while enabling comprehensive nutrient analysis.

title: Artificial intelligence meets medical rarity: evaluating ChatGPT's responses on post-orgasmic illness syndrome
outcome: Readability (Gunning Fog Index) of ChatGPT-4o patient-directed responses on POIS across two days

effect: Flesch Reading Ease scores ranged from 42.92 to 55.61, mean 47.79, indicating college-level reading required, which may limit accessibility.
quote: The Flesch Reading Ease scores ranged from 42.92 to 55.61, with a mean of 47.79.

title: Locally deployed context-aware chatbot outperforms generic large language models for guideline-concordant pediatric imaging recommendations
outcome: Proportion of 'Usually appropriate' ACR-concordant imaging recommendations with vs without RAG grounding
effect: ped-Llama (RAG) achieved 80% (40/50) 'Usually appropriate' vs 46% for Llama-3.1-8B without RAG, 54% GPT-4o, 46% Claude Opus.
quote: ped-Llama achieved 80% (40/50) "Usually appropriate" recommendations, outperforming Llama-3.1-8B (46%), GPT-4o (54%), and Claude Opus (46%), and matching the specialist radiologist (76%).

title: Locally deployed context-aware chatbot outperforms generic large language models for guideline-concordant pediatric imaging recommendations
outcome: Consistency of LLM recommendations across three independent runs
effect: Consistency across runs was 72% for ped-Llama versus 44-50% for generic LLMs, showing output nondeterminism.
quote: Consistency across runs was 72% for ped-Llama versus 44-50% for generic LLMs.

title: RAG-Enhanced Open SLMs for Hypertension Management Chatbots
outcome: G-Eval medical faithfulness of SLM answers with RAG versus role-playing or full-context prompts
effect: RAG outperformed or tied the best SLM-only approach for all models; significant for Gemma 3 (4.48 vs 3.48, p=0.0012) and Qwen 2.5 with Mxbai, and Gemma 3 and SmolLM2 with Nomic; no clear pattern in physician ratings.
quote: Overall, we can observe that the performance of SLMs are indeed positively affected by the RAG pipeline, and for some models the difference is statistically significant.

title: Can artificial intelligence (AI)-based software programs generate accurate clinical dictation?
outcome: Procedural accuracy of AI-generated clinical dental dictations
effect: All 5 AI software programs produced clinically accurate dictations across surgical and restorative procedures using structured prompts, with no substantial procedural accuracy differences.
quote: Across both surgical and restorative procedures, all 5 AI software programs (Copilot, ChatGPT-4, ChatGPT-5, Gemini, and OpenEvidence) produced clinically accurate dictations when using the SP format.

title: AI performance in emergency medicine fellowship examination: comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, Claude 3.5, and DeepSeek R1 models
outcome: Response consistency across repeated runs of same question (Fleiss' Kappa)
effect: Claude 3.5 Fleiss' Kappa 0.68 (highest); Gemini 2.0 0.49 (lowest). Inconsistent hallucinations more frequent in Gemini 2.0 and DeepSeek R1.
quote: In terms of response consistency, the Claude 3.5 model (Fleiss' Kappa = 0.68) showed the highest consistency, while Gemini 2.0 (Fleiss' Kappa = 0.49) showed the lowest.

title: The Great Scribe-Off: A Comparative Analysis of AI Scribes Versus Human Documentation in Simulated General Practice Consultations
venue: Studies in health technology and informatics
outcome: Blinded GP-rated note quality (PDQI-9) including accuracy and thoroughness for AI scribes versus human notes
effect: Top AI scribes scored 44.08/50 (SD 3.32) vs 37.42 (SD 9.78) for humans; thoroughness M=4.92, accuracy M=4.67. Only top scribes are reported; accuracy ICC 0.745.
quote: Top AI scribes scored a mean of 44.08/50 (SD = 3.32) vs. 37.42 (SD = 9.78) for humans, excelling in thoroughness (M = 4.92), accuracy (M = 4.67), and freedom from bias (M = 4.92).

title: ChatGPT-4 in Psychiatric Discharge Summaries: Toward a More Comprehensible and Emotionally Sensitive Clinical Communication
venue: The International journal of social psychiatry
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4 rewritten discharge summaries (Fernández-Huerta, INFLESZ) versus originals
effect: Significant readability improvement across all diagnostic groups (p < .001), with mean values above recommended thresholds; five summaries remained below thresholds.
quote: Significant improvements in readability were observed across all diagnostic groups (p < .001), with mean values surpassing recommended thresholds for general comprehension.

title: ChatGPT-4 in Psychiatric Discharge Summaries: Toward a More Comprehensible and Emotionally Sensitive Clinical Communication
venue: The International journal of social psychiatry
outcome: Psychiatrist-rated emotional risk and language appropriateness of AI-rewritten summaries
effect: Summaries were rated positively overall, but evaluators noted emotionally charged or stigmatizing language in a few cases.
quote: Evaluators also highlighted emotionally charged or stigmatizing language in a few cases.

title: Enhancing Large Language Models With AI Agents for Chronic Gastritis Management: Comprehensive Comparative Study
outcome: Answer quality of retrieval- and search-grounded agent versus plain LLM on high-complexity questions
effect: Embedding average score on high-complexity questions was 82.849 for AI agents vs 77.825 for LLMs; agents were particularly effective in clinical consultation tasks.
quote: Using a dual-evaluation framework comprising automated metrics and expert manual assessments, our results demonstrated that AI agents substantially outperformed LLMs in addressing high-complexity questions (embedding average score: 82.849 for AI agents vs 77.825 for LLMs) and were particularly effective in clinical consultation tasks.

title: Enhancing Large Language Models With AI Agents for Chronic Gastritis Management: Comprehensive Comparative Study
outcome: Output variability across 30 repeated runs of the agent
effect: Mean absolute deviation of 0.0167 (embedding average score) and 0.0387 (BERTScore) after 30 repeated experiments, indicating stable, minimally variable responses.
quote: After 30 repeated experiments, the mean absolute deviation of the AI agents in the embedding average score and BERTScore metrics were 0.0167 and 0.0387, respectively.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Patient Education for Androgenetic Alopecia: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Deepseek R1
outcome: Reading level of LLM answers to androgenetic alopecia patient questions (Flesch-Kincaid)
effect: All three models generated responses at a high school reading level.
quote: All models generated responses at a high school reading level.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Patient Education for Androgenetic Alopecia: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Deepseek R1
outcome: Presence of warnings about potential misinformation in Deepseek R1 responses
effect: Deepseek R1 lacked warnings about potential misinformation and frequently provided inaccurate content.
quote: It also lacked warnings about potential misinformation.

title: RadOncRAG: A Novel Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework Improves Large Language Model Benchmark Performance in Radiation Oncology
outcome: Exam accuracy of LLMs with versus without radiation oncology retrieval-augmented generation
effect: RAG improved nonreasoning models (Gemini-2.0 +6.7% to 79.2%, Llama-3-70b +8.4% to 75.8%, GPT-4o +5.7% to 85.6%); top reasoning models showed no improvement or detriment.
quote: Gemini-2.0 improved 6.7% (to 79.2%), Llama-3-70b 8.4% (to 75.8%), and GPT-4o 5.7% (to 85.6%) with RAG.

title: The human factor in explainable artificial intelligence: clinician variability in trust, reliance, and performance
outcome: Clinician gestational age error with versus without AI predictions and explanations
effect: Model predictions reduced clinician MAE from 23.5 to 15.7 days; explanations gave a further non-significant reduction to 14.3 days; effect of explanations varied across participants.
quote: Model predictions reduced clinician mean absolute error (MAE) from 23.5 to 15.7 days, and explanations had a further non-significant reduction to 14.3 days.

title: The human factor in explainable artificial intelligence: clinician variability in trust, reliance, and performance
outcome: Effect of AI explanations on clinician trust, reliance, confidence, and performance
effect: Explanations increased participant confidence but had no significant effect on trust or reliance; some participants performed worse with explanations than without.
quote: Additionally, although explanations increased participant confidence, they had no significant effect on trust or reliance on the model.

title: The human factor in explainable artificial intelligence: clinician variability in trust, reliance, and performance
outcome: clinician user testing of explanations
effect: Human testing found clinician variability: some worse with explanations; confidence increased but no significant trust or reliance effect.
quote: These counterintuitive results highlight potential pitfalls in deploying XAI, emphasising the need for human studies to capture clinician variability.

title: Large language model as a clinical decision support tool in the initial management of critically ill children: a pilot evaluation
outcome: Appropriateness, harm, and omissions of LLM diagnostic vs therapeutic recommendations in pediatric critical care
effect: Diagnostic recommendations appropriate 94% (ED) and 98% (PICU); therapeutic only 82%. Potentially harmful therapeutic suggestions 7% vs 2% (ED) and 10% vs 0% (PICU); 0.95 critically missing therapeutic recommendations per PICU case.
quote: Potentially harmful therapeutic suggestions were more common than diagnostic ones: 7% vs. 2% in the ED (p = 0.016) and 10% vs. 0% in the PICU (p < 0.00001).

title: Large language model as a clinical decision support tool in the initial management of critically ill children: a pilot evaluation
outcome: LLM performance on real-world clinical cases across diagnosis, triage, and therapy tasks
effect: Correct diagnosis in 100% of ED discharge and 95% of PICU 24-h differentials; triage accurate in all PICU cases; therapeutic recommendations appropriate in only 82%.
quote: Triage decisions were accurate in all PICU cases.

title: Application of AI-assisted magnifying colonoscopy system in the diagnosis of colorectal tumors: a multicenter exploratory diagnostic study
outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance, by experience level
effect: Junior endoscopists improved accuracy from 0.866 to 0.951 after AADM assistance (P < 0.01); AADM alone 0.938 vs junior 0.866 (P<0.05), comparable to senior 0.937.
quote: Additionally, junior endoscopists significantly improved their accuracy from 0.866 to 0.951 after receiving assistance from the AADM (P < 0.01).

title: Application of AI-assisted magnifying colonoscopy system in the diagnosis of colorectal tumors: a multicenter exploratory diagnostic study
outcome: AI model diagnostic accuracy compared with endoscopists of varying experience on same images
effect: AADM accuracy 0.938 was superior to junior endoscopists (0.866, P<0.05) and comparable to senior endoscopists (0.937, P>0.05).
quote: The diagnostic performance of the AADM was superior to that of junior endoscopists (accuracy: 0.938 vs. 0.866, P < 0.05) and comparable to senior endoscopists (accuracy: 0.938 vs. 0.937, P > 0.05).

title: Can general purpose large language models assist pediatricians in predicting infants with serious bacterial infection?
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy for infant SBI versus pediatricians, ML models, and rule-based methods
effect: LLMs performed comparably to ML models, rule-based methods, and pediatrician majority vote (MCC 0.41-0.43 vs 0.43); best individual pediatrician sensitivity 0.74, specificity 0.68, MCC 0.33.
quote: In comparison, the best-performing individual pediatrician achieved a higher sensitivity (0.74) but lower specificity (0.68), with an MCC of 0.33, while the pediatricians’ majority vote yielded sensitivity of 0.69, specificity of 0.81, and MCC of 0.43 — comparable to the top-performing LLMs.
sample_unit: patients (infants under 90 days admitted to the emergency department)

title: Enhancing predictive modeling for respiratory support with LLM-driven guideline adherence
outcome: Clinician chart review of LLM recommendations for guideline alignment, errors and harm risk
effect: 19/20 (95%) LLM recommendations aligned with guidelines; physicians agreed with 13/20 (65%); errors in 11/20 cases; 2/20 judged potentially severe harm.
quote: In a 20-case chart review, 19/20 (95%) LLM recommendations aligned with clinical guidelines and physicians agreed with 13/20 (65%) final recommendations.

title: Improving patient understanding of radiology reports using generative artificial intelligence: a vignette study of 2000 US adults
outcome: Patient comprehension of key findings and follow-up, AI plain-language vs original radiology reports
effect: AI plain language reports had higher comprehension (68.0% vs 58.0%; marginal difference 10.8% [95% CI 7.8%-13.8%]) and follow-up accuracy (64.5% vs 58.4%; 6.8% [4.1%-9.4%]). Larger gains among older and less-educated participants.
quote: Compared to original reports, participants shown AI-generated plain language reports had higher accuracy in comprehension (68.0% vs 58.0%; marginal difference 10.8% [95% CI, 7.8%-13.8%]) and follow-up (64.5% vs 58.4%; marginal difference 6.8% [95% CI, 4.1%-9.4%]).

title: Ctrl + Alt + Conceive: fertility awareness in the age of Artificial Intelligence, how do large language models compare?
outcome: Presence of warning or safety messages about potential inaccuracies across LLM platforms
effect: Not all platforms provided warning or safety messages regarding potential inaccuracies; content on assisted reproductive technologies was the least accurate.
quote: Not all platforms provided warning or safety messages regarding potential inaccuracies.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation for interpreting clinical laboratory regulations using large language models
outcome: Completeness and correctness of RAG answers versus pathologist-generated reference answers
effect: Raven's responses were totally complete and correct in 92.0% of 88 CFR-addressed questions; performance declined significantly on questions not addressed in the CFR, confirming grounding.
quote: Compared to answers generated manually by a board-certified pathologist, Raven's responses were judged to be totally complete and correct in 92.0% of those 88 cases, with little irrelevant content and a low potential for regulatory or medical error.

title: A comparative performance analysis of regular expressions and a large language model-based approach to extract the BI-RADS score from radiological reports
outcome: Accuracy of LLM vs simple Regex baseline for BI-RADS extraction on same reports
effect: Accuracy 89.20% Regex vs 87.69% LLM (P = .56, not significant); Regex 28,120 times faster (0.06 s vs 1687.20 s).
quote: For structured, standardized data like BI-RADS, traditional NLP techniques seem to be superior, though future work should explore hybrid approaches combining Regex precision for standardized elements with LLM contextual understanding for more complex information extraction tasks.

title: A comparative performance analysis of regular expressions and a large language model-based approach to extract the BI-RADS score from radiological reports
outcome: Whether LLM outperforms simpler non-AI method for structured extraction task
effect: LLM was no more accurate than Regex (87.69% vs 89.20%, P = .56) and far slower (1687.20 s vs 0.06 s).
quote: Compared to the LLM-based method, Regex processing was more efficient, completing the task 28 120 times faster (0.06 seconds vs 1687.20 seconds).

title: Hybrid Ambient Clinical Documentation and Physician Performance: Work Outside of Work, Documentation Delay, and Financial Productivity
outcome: After-hours work, documentation delay, and wRVU productivity after ambient scribe activation
effect: WOW rose 32.1% at day 10 then fell 41.7% by day 50; odds of delayed notes fell 66.0% at day 50; wRVUs rose 12.1% by day 50.
quote: ACD adoption was associated with reduced after-hours work, faster note completion, and improved financial productivity within 50 days of implementation.
sample_unit: clinicians (attending physicians and advanced practice clinicians)

title: Hybrid Ambient Clinical Documentation and Physician Performance: Work Outside of Work, Documentation Delay, and Financial Productivity
outcome: Documentation time, after-hours work, and financial productivity after ambient scribe deployment
effect: WOW decreased 41.7% (95% CI -51.8%, -29.4%) by day 50; wRVUs increased 12.1% (95% CI 5.7%, 18.9%) by day 50.
quote: Financial productivity increased steadily by 1.5% (95% CI -0.2%, 3.2%) on day 10 and 12.1% (95% CI 5.7%, 18.9%) by day 50.
sample_unit: clinicians (attending physicians and advanced practice clinicians)

title: Comparative analysis of artificial intelligence platforms in generating Post-Operative instructions for endoscopic transnasal skull base surgery
venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Readability, understandability and actionability of AI-generated postoperative instructions
effect: FKGL was 9.07 (Gemini), 9.82 (DeepSeek) and 10.87 (ChatGPT). Understandability was 63.30-76.45% and actionability 45.15-58.5%. None met optimal standards for patient education.
quote: FKGL was lowest in Gemini (9.07), compared to DeepSeek (9.82) and ChatGPT (10.87) (p = 0.469).

title: A Prospective Controlled Trial of Large Language Model-based Simplification of Oncologic CT Reports for Patients with Cancer
outcome: Patient comprehension, cognitive workload, perceived usefulness, reading time and readability of simplified versus standard CT reports
effect: Simplified reports gave lower cognitive workload (adjusted OR 0.18), better comprehension (adjusted OR 13.28) and better perceived usefulness (adjusted OR 5.46). Median reading time fell from 7 to 2 minutes. Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was 8.89 vs 13.69.
quote: LLM simplification of oncologic CT reports improved patient comprehension and reduced reading burden.

title: Ambient Artificial Intelligence Versus Human Scribes in the Emergency Department
outcome: Local ambient scribe evaluation of note quality (PDQI-9), EHR time, and physician note contribution versus human scribes
effect: PDQI-9 similar for adults, lower for pediatrics with AI (41.36 vs 42.25, aRR -1.89 [95% CI -3.58 to -0.20]); more EHR notes time with AI (adult 4.3 vs 1.8 min).
quote: PDQI-9 scores were similar for adults, but AI scribes scored lower for pediatric patients (41.36 versus 42.25, adjusted risk ratio [aRR] = -1.89 [95% confidence interval (CI) -3.58 to -0.20]).

title: Ambient Artificial Intelligence Versus Human Scribes in the Emergency Department
outcome: Blinded physician-rated quality of ambient scribe notes using PDQI-9 compared with human scribe notes
effect: Adult note quality similar; pediatric AI notes scored lower (41.36 vs 42.25, aRR -1.89 [95% CI -3.58 to -0.20]).
quote: PDQI-9 scores were similar for adults, but AI scribes scored lower for pediatric patients (41.36 versus 42.25, adjusted risk ratio [aRR] = -1.89 [95% confidence interval (CI) -3.58 to -0.20]).

title: Ambient Artificial Intelligence Versus Human Scribes in the Emergency Department
outcome: Side-by-side local pilot comparing AI scribe with human scribe on quality and EHR time
effect: AI scribes associated with more EHR notes time, more physician note contribution, and similar to lower quality notes versus human scribes.
quote: In comparison to human scribes, AI scribes were associated with more time spent in the electronic health record notes section, more physician note contribution, and similar to lower quality notes.

title: Comparative Accuracy, Stability, and Correctability of Large Language Models in Otolaryngology and Pharmacovigilance
venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM clinical outputs when all cases were re-queried one month later
effect: All three LLMs showed almost perfect clinical stability (Cronbach's α = 0.831-0.856); feedback did not significantly reduce misdiagnosis rates in subsequent interactions.
quote: All LLMs demonstrated an almost perfect clinical stability (α = 0.831-0.856), though human feedback did not significantly reduce misdiagnosis rates in subsequent interactions.

title: Evaluating the performance of Large language models in rheumatology for connective tissue Diseases: DeepSeek-R1, ChatGPT-4.0, Copilot, and Gemini-2.0
outcome: Readability of LLM responses to connective tissue disease questions (Flesch Reading Ease Score)
effect: Average FRES 80.46 (7.19), rated 'easy' to read across the four LLMs; readability was not a barrier in this evaluation.
quote: The answers provided by the LLMs were "easy" to read, with an average FRES score of 80.46 (7.19).

title: How accurately do large language models answer patient questions on anterior cruciate ligament tears? A comparative study
outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers to ACL questions rated by orthopedic consultants on 5-point Likert scale
effect: All models scored mean accuracy ≥3 (mostly accurate). DeepSeek 3.61 and Grok 3.59 were significantly higher than Llama 3.25 (P<0.05); ChatGPT 3.48, Gemini 3.52.
quote: DeepSeek (3.61) and Grok (3.59) demonstrated significantly higher mean accuracies than Llama (3.25; P < 0.05).

title: Evaluating online health information on PIFP: A cross-platform analysis of content quality and readability
outcome: Readability of online and AI-generated PIFP patient information (Flesch Reading Ease, SMOG)
effect: All sources, including ChatGPT and Gemini content, were rated as difficult to read; AI content was more understandable on PEMAT (83.31% vs 64.96%, p<0.001).
quote: All sources were rated as "difficult" to read.

title: A novel AI-powered radiographic analysis surpasses specialists in stage II–IV periodontitis detection: a multicenter diagnostic study
outcome: Periodontitis detection by dentists with versus without AI support across experience levels
effect: AI support significantly improved early periodontitis detection across training and experience levels; junior dentists matched specialist performance with AI support.
quote: The system significantly improved early periodontitis detection across training and experience levels, enabling junior dentists to match specialist performance with AI support.
sample_unit: orthopantomograms (382 clinically labeled + 760 radiographically labeled test OPGs)

title: A novel AI-powered radiographic analysis surpasses specialists in stage II–IV periodontitis detection: a multicenter diagnostic study
outcome: AI diagnostic accuracy consistency across four international centers
effect: Performance remained consistent in the multicenter evaluation, with >92.4% accuracy across all locations.
quote: Performance remained consistent in the multicenter evaluation, achieving >92.4% accuracy across all locations.
sample_unit: orthopantomograms (382 clinically labeled + 760 radiographically labeled test OPGs)

title: Uncertainty-aware large language models for explainable disease diagnosis
outcome: Expert uncertainty recognition and explanation with versus without ConfiDx assistance
effect: ConfiDx-assisted experts outperformed standalone experts by 10.7% in uncertainty recognition and 26% in uncertainty explanation.
quote: Moreover, ConfiDx-assisted experts outperformed standalone experts by 10.7% in uncertainty recognition and 26% in uncertainty explanation, underscoring its substantial potential to improve clinical decision-making.

title: Uncertainty-aware large language models for explainable disease diagnosis
outcome: Model identification and explanation of diagnostic uncertainty on real-world datasets
effect: ConfiDx excelled in identifying diagnostic uncertainties and generating trustworthy explanations for diagnoses and uncertainties (no numbers in abstract).
quote: Evaluating on real-world datasets demonstrated that ConfiDx excelled in identifying diagnostic uncertainties, achieving superior diagnostic performance, and generating trustworthy explanations for diagnoses and uncertainties.

title: Demographic biases in AI-generated simulated patient cohorts: a comparative analysis against census benchmarks
outcome: Demographic representation (age, sex, ethnicity) of LLM-generated patients versus 2021 census benchmarks
effect: Both models diverged from census on every variable (p<0.0001). Male patients were 64.7% (GPT-3.5) and 92.8% (GPT-4-mini). No patients under 25 were generated, and no one over 47 (GPT-3.5) or 56 (GPT-4-mini). Some ethnic groups were absent.
quote: Both cohorts diverged significantly from census benchmarks (p < 0.0001 for every variable).

title: Large Language Models for Dietary Advice to Patients With Irritable Bowel Syndrome: ChatGPT vs. Google Gemini
venue: Journal of human nutrition and dietetics : the official journal of the British Dietetic Association
outcome: Compliance of LLM dietary responses with IBS clinical guidelines (Guideline Compliance Score)
effect: ChatGPT 70% and Gemini 57.5% of responses guideline-compliant; no significant difference between models (p > 0.05), so a substantial share of responses were noncompliant.
quote: This study found that most responses from ChatGPT (70%) and Gemini (57.5%) were compliant with the guidelines, but there was no significant difference in guideline compliance, quality, understandability, actionability, or readability scores (p > 0.05).
sample_unit: LLM responses to IBS dietary questions

title: Exploring the prognostic utility of large language models versus traditional clinical models in heart failure: a pilot study
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM predicted probabilities across repeated runs (intraclass correlation)
effect: Repeated predictions showed significant variability for both ChatGPT and DeepSeek.
quote: Repeated predictions showed significant variability for both models.

title: Exploring the prognostic utility of large language models versus traditional clinical models in heart failure: a pilot study
outcome: AUC of LLMs versus conventional logistic regression model on same data
effect: Zigong: ChatGPT AUC 0.59, DeepSeek 0.56 vs clinical model 0.63. MIMIC-IV: ChatGPT 0.72 vs clinical model 0.74 (P=0.31); DeepSeek 0.67.
quote: In the MIMIC-IV cohort, ChatGPT achieved higher discrimination (AUC 0.72) than DeepSeek (AUC 0.67, P < 0.001) and comparable performance to the clinical model (AUC 0.74, P = 0.31).

title: Caught in the Web of Words: Do LLMs Fall for Spin in Medical Literature?
outcome: LLM susceptibility to spin in medical trial abstracts compared with humans
effect: 22 LLMs were across the board more susceptible to spin than humans, and implicitly incorporated spin into plain language summaries they generated.
quote: We evaluated 22 LLMs and found that they are across the board more susceptible to spin than humans.
sample_unit: not reported in text (22 LLMs evaluated on trial abstracts)

title: Artificial intelligence in anesthesia: comparison of the utility of ChatGPT v/s google gemini large language models in pre-anesthetic education: content, readability and sentiment analysis
outcome: Readability of LLM pre-anesthetic patient education responses (Flesch-Kincaid grade, Flesch Reading Ease)
effect: Gemini text was more readable than ChatGPT (lower Flesch-Kincaid Grade level p = 0.04; higher Flesch Reading Ease p = 0.04); ChatGPT was less readable.
quote: Gemini generated text with greater readability, demonstrated by a lower Flesch-Kincaid Grade level (p = 0.04) and higher Flesch Reading Ease score (p = 0.04).

title: What do the current popular artificial intelligence chatbots offer us regarding patient information? Comparison of responses from the ten most popular chatbots about bladder cancer
venue: Journal of cancer survivorship : research and practice
outcome: Readability (ARLC, FKGL, FKRE) and quality (mEQIP, DISCERN, QUEST) of chatbot bladder cancer patient information
effect: Readability differed significantly across chatbots (ARLC p=0.002, FKGL p=0.001, FKRE p=0.002). Google Palm was easiest to read and Llama most difficult. Overall quality and readability were moderate.
quote: AI chatbots can produce information on BC that is of moderate quality and readability, while there is significant variability among platforms.

title: Using ChatGPT-4 for Lay Summarization in Prostate Cancer Research to Advance Patient-Centered Communication: Large-Scale Generative AI Performance Evaluation
outcome: Readability (FKRE) of AI lay summaries with simple vs extended plain-language prompt vs original
effect: Median FKRE extended prompt 47 (IQR 42-56), simple prompt 36 (29-43), original 20 (9.5-29); P<.001. High-quality: 79.4% extended, 54.9% simple, 5.4% original.
quote: ChatGPT-4-generated lay summaries showed an improvement in readability compared to human-written versions, with the extended prompt achieving higher scores than the simple prompt (median FKRE: extended prompt 47, IQR 42-56; simple prompt 36, IQR 29-43; original 20, IQR 9.5-29; P<.001).
sample_unit: prostate cancer articles (lay summaries per prompt)

title: Using ChatGPT-4 for Lay Summarization in Prostate Cancer Research to Advance Patient-Centered Communication: Large-Scale Generative AI Performance Evaluation
outcome: Factual accuracy of AI lay summaries rated by 2 blinded experts on 5-point Likert scale
effect: Median accuracy 5 (IQR 5-5) for both prompts vs 5 (4-5) original; P<.001. Both raters <4: 1 (0.5%) extended, 1 (0.5%) simple, 12 (5.9%) original.
quote: Factual accuracy was higher for the AI-generated lay summaries compared to originals (median factual accuracy score: extended prompt 5, IQR 5-5; simple prompt 5, IQR 5-5; original 5, IQR 4-5; P<.001) in this dataset.
sample_unit: prostate cancer articles (lay summaries per prompt)

title: Using ChatGPT-4 for Lay Summarization in Prostate Cancer Research to Advance Patient-Centered Communication: Large-Scale Generative AI Performance Evaluation
outcome: Reading level of lay summaries with prompt targeting 6th-grade level vs simple prompt vs author-written
effect: Median FKGL 12 (extended), 14 (simple), 16 (original); reading age 19, 21, 23 years; all P<.001. Extended prompt targeted sixth-grade level but still did not reach it.
quote: Compared to the original lay summaries, those generated by ChatGPT-4 (using both simple and extended prompts) exhibited improved readability metrics, generally higher factual accuracy, and better adherence to the predefined correct word count.
sample_unit: prostate cancer articles (lay summaries per prompt)

title: Using ChatGPT-4 for Lay Summarization in Prostate Cancer Research to Advance Patient-Centered Communication: Large-Scale Generative AI Performance Evaluation
outcome: quality versus author-written summaries
effect: High-quality: extended prompt 79.4%, simple prompt 54.9%, original summaries 5.4%; P<.001.
quote: The proportion rated as high-quality was 79.4% for the extended prompt, 54.9% for the simple prompt, and 5.4% for original summaries (P<.001).
sample_unit: prostate cancer articles (lay summaries per prompt)

title: Using ChatGPT-4 for Lay Summarization in Prostate Cancer Research to Advance Patient-Centered Communication: Large-Scale Generative AI Performance Evaluation
outcome: Lay summary readability by Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease
effect: Extended prompt median FKRE was 47 (IQR 42-56) vs 36 (IQR 29-43) for simple prompt and 20 (IQR 9.5-29) for original (P<.001)
quote: ChatGPT-4-generated lay summaries showed an improvement in readability compared to human-written versions, with the extended prompt achieving higher scores than the simple prompt (median FKRE: extended prompt 47, IQR 42-56; simple prompt 36, IQR 29-43; original 20, IQR 9.5-29; P<.001).
sample_unit: prostate cancer articles (lay summaries per prompt)

title: Performance of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Large Language Models in Guideline-Concordant Prostate-Specific Antigen Testing: Comparative Study With Junior Clinicians
outcome: Guideline-concordant PSA testing recommendations by RAG-grounded LLM versus junior clinicians
effect: RAG-LLM concordant in 95.5% (210/220) of scenarios vs junior clinicians 62.3% (137/220) closed-book and 74.1% (163/220) open-book; both P<.001.
quote: The RAG-LLM tool provided guideline-concordant recommendations in 95.5% (210/220) of case scenarios, compared to junior clinicians, who were correct in 62.3% (137/220) of scenarios in a closed-book format and 74.1% (163/220) of scenarios in an open-book format.

title: AI-Powered Chest X-Ray for Diagnosing Pulmonary Tuberculosis in County and Township Health Care Facilities in Yichang: Retrospective, Real-World Study
outcome: CAD performance by health care facility tier (county vs township)
effect: CAD performed worse in county-level hospitals (DYD 62.5%, PPV 0.6%) than township facilities (DYD 86.7%, PPV 2%), P<.001.
quote: However, CAD showed significant variation in performance with respect to health care facility tier, performing poorer in the county-level group than in the township-level group ( P <.001; Table S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1 ).

title: AI-Powered Chest X-Ray for Diagnosing Pulmonary Tuberculosis in County and Township Health Care Facilities in Yichang: Retrospective, Real-World Study
outcome: AI score quartiles for prioritizing radiologist review of high-risk patients
effect: Scores >0.75 (34.2% of CAD-positive) contained 189/229 (82.5%) of confirmed PTB cases; P for trend <.001.
quote: Most confirmed patients (189/229, 82.5%) had CAD scores exceeding the 75% quantiles (Q75) threshold, which accounted for 34.2% (4618/13,515) of all CAD-positive patients ( Table 3 ).

title: AI-Powered Chest X-Ray for Diagnosing Pulmonary Tuberculosis in County and Township Health Care Facilities in Yichang: Retrospective, Real-World Study
outcome: CAD false positives and positive rate in low-prevalence symptomatic population
effect: CAD flagged 13,515 (14.5%) as positive with PPV 1.7% at 0.3% prevalence, versus radiologist positive rate 0.7%.
quote: However, excessive reliance on CAD-based diagnoses may potentially contribute to a higher volume of unnecessary follow-up procedures, leading to an inefficient allocation of medical resources.

title: AI-Powered Chest X-Ray for Diagnosing Pulmonary Tuberculosis in County and Township Health Care Facilities in Yichang: Retrospective, Real-World Study
outcome: CAD performance across subgroups (age, sex, region, patient category)
effect: CAD outperformed radiologists in all subgroups; age ≥80 less likely to have high PPV (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.10-0.44); no sex or inpatient/outpatient differences.
quote: Multivariate logistic regression also demonstrated that advanced age (≥80 y) groups were less likely to achieve high PPV (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.10‐0.44; P <.001).

title: AI-Powered Chest X-Ray for Diagnosing Pulmonary Tuberculosis in County and Township Health Care Facilities in Yichang: Retrospective, Real-World Study
outcome: CAD triage workload and yield
effect: Selective review reduced radiologist workload 85.5%, with minimum DYD 25.6% and potential DYD 83.9%.
quote: Strategy 5 enabled a radiologist workload reduction of 85.5% (1‐13,515/93,319) while maintaining a minimum system DYD of 25.6% (ie, finding all cases the radiologists originally found) and a potential DYD of 83.9% (if radiologists trusted the AI on all 229 positive cases; Table 2 ).

title: AI-Powered Chest X-Ray for Diagnosing Pulmonary Tuberculosis in County and Township Health Care Facilities in Yichang: Retrospective, Real-World Study
outcome: CAD PPV by age subgroup
effect: Age ≥80 had lower PPV: OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.10‐0.44; P <.001.
quote: Multivariate logistic regression also demonstrated that advanced age (≥80 y) groups were less likely to achieve high PPV (OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.10‐0.44; P <.001).

title: Evaluation of the accuracy and readability of large language model responses on menopause and hormone therapy
outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of LLM responses to patient-level menopause questions
effect: FRES differed significantly (P<0.001): Gemini 38.9±7.3 (difficult), ChatGPT 3.5 31.0±11.2 and ChatGPT 4.0 26.5±8.6 (both very difficult).
quote: FRES scores differed significantly ( P <0.001): Gemini scored 38.9±7.3 ("difficult"), ChatGPT 3.5 scored 31.0±11.2, and ChatGPT 4.0 scored 26.5±8.6 (both "very difficult").

title: Evaluation of the accuracy and readability of large language model responses on menopause and hormone therapy
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of LLM answers to menopause and hormone therapy questions
effect: Patient-level accuracy: ChatGPT 3.5 70%, ChatGPT 4.0 60%, Gemini 30%. Clinician-level: ChatGPT 4.0 67%, ChatGPT 3.5 and OpenEvidence 60%, Gemini 47%.
quote: LLMs demonstrated limited accuracy and frequent incorrect or incomplete responses to menopause-related queries, highlighting the need to improve model performance to ensure accurate and reliable information for both patients and clinicians.

title: Enhancing Large Language Models for Improved Accuracy and Safety in Medical Question Answering: Comparative Study
outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rates of LLMs with vs without retrieval-augmented grounding (Med-RISE)

title: Evaluating the clinical readiness of artificial intelligence in EEG-based epilepsy diagnosis

quote: Permitting subject overlap artificially elevated accuracy to 59%-96%, whereas strict patient separation reduced it to 41%-53% in 95% Confidence Interval.

title: Evaluating the clinical readiness of artificial intelligence in EEG-based epilepsy diagnosis

title: Evaluating the clinical readiness of artificial intelligence in EEG-based epilepsy diagnosis
