title: Evaluating the clinical readiness of artificial intelligence in EEG-based epilepsy diagnosis
outcome: diagnostic accuracy with data leakage versus strict patient separation
effect: subject overlap artificially elevated accuracy to 59%-96%, whereas strict patient separation reduced it to 41%-53% (95% CI)
quote: Permitting subject overlap artificially elevated accuracy to 59%-96%, whereas strict patient separation reduced it to 41%-53% in 95% Confidence Interval.

title: Incorporating information retrieval into AI chatbots for patient education on thyroid eye disease
outcome: Clinical quality ratings of RAG-grounded chatbot versus ungrounded general-purpose chatbot on TED questions
effect: ChatGPT-RAG mean clinical score 5.55 vs ChatGPT 4.94 (implied); OpenEvidence 5.96 outperformed both ChatGPT and ChatGPT-RAG (g = 0.53, P < 0.001). RAG was intermediate on clinical and non-clinical metrics.
quote: Across both domains, ChatGPT-RAG achieved intermediate performance, more closely trailing OpenEvidence clinically (g = 0.53) and ChatGPT with respect to non-clinical metrics (g = 0.44).

title: Incorporating information retrieval into AI chatbots for patient education on thyroid eye disease
outcome: empathy, understandability, and actionability
effect: ChatGPT outperformed specialized models: 18.4 vs 14.96 for OpenEvidence; g=1.25, P<0.001.

title: AI assistance improves reader agreement in digital mammography: A multireader crossover study of general and breast subspecialty radiologists
outcome: Reader agreement with gold standard with vs without AI assistance in multireader crossover

title: Readability of Professional Medical Content on Acute Appendicitis: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study of ChatGPT and UpToDate

quote: ChatGPT had a lower absolute difficult-word count (p = 0.002) but a higher difficult-word percentage (p = 0.002).

title: Identifying Bias at Scale in Clinical Notes Using Large Language Models
outcome: Prevalence of stigmatizing, judgmental, discrediting, stereotyping language in clinical notes
effect: Biased language appeared in 6.5% (3229 of 50,000) of Mount Sinai notes and 7.4% (37 of 500) of MIMIC-IV notes; elevated odds with substance use presentations (aOR 3.09) and frequent utilization (aOR 2.85).
quote: Biased language appeared in 6.5% (3229 of 50,000) of Mount Sinai notes and 7.4% (37 of 500) of Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV notes.

outcome: Proportion of surgical staff using DeepSeek who had received AI training

title: Evaluating sociodemographic bias in a deployed machine-learned patient deterioration model
outcome: Deployed model sensitivity and specificity by sociodemographic subgroup after deployment

title: Evaluating sociodemographic bias in a deployed machine-learned patient deterioration model

title: Evaluating sociodemographic bias in a deployed machine-learned patient deterioration model
outcome: Subgroup performance gaps in model specificity and sensitivity

title: Advancing Chinese Conversation-based Patient Guidance with a Benchmark and Knowledge-Evolvable Assistant

outcome: Department-guidance accuracy of LLMs with versus without retrieval augmentation from experience bank and medical knowledge base

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Decision-Making in Emergency Care

title: Unsupervised Characterization of Temporal Dataset Shifts as an Early Indicator of AI Performance Variations: Evaluation Study Using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV Dataset
outcome: Association between unsupervised temporal data shift clusters and clusters of yearly model performance

title: Unsupervised Characterization of Temporal Dataset Shifts as an Early Indicator of AI Performance Variations: Evaluation Study Using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV Dataset

title: Unsupervised Characterization of Temporal Dataset Shifts as an Early Indicator of AI Performance Variations: Evaluation Study Using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV Dataset
outcome: data coding change affecting performance

title: Unsupervised Characterization of Temporal Dataset Shifts as an Early Indicator of AI Performance Variations: Evaluation Study Using the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV Dataset

title: Evaluating the clinical utility of multimodal large language models in rare maculopathy

title: Evaluating the clinical utility of multimodal large language models in rare maculopathy

title: Artificial Intelligence Can Answer Postoperative Questions About Distal Radius Fractures-But Can Patients Understand the Answers?
venue: Journal of hand surgery global online

title: Artificial Intelligence Can Answer Postoperative Questions About Distal Radius Fractures-But Can Patients Understand the Answers?
venue: Journal of hand surgery global online

title: Artificial Intelligence Can Answer Postoperative Questions About Distal Radius Fractures-But Can Patients Understand the Answers?

title: What is Artificial Intelligence (AI) "Empathy"? A Study Comparing ChatGPT and Physician Responses on an Online Forum

title: Hemodialysis equipment malfunction incidence and risk profiling in clinical settings: a retrospective single-center cohort analysis
outcome: Discriminative performance compared with alternative models

title: Hemodialysis equipment malfunction incidence and risk profiling in clinical settings: a retrospective single-center cohort analysis
outcome: Alarm burden, response time, and treatment interruptions after model-guided interventions

quote: Implementation of model-guided interventions resulted in substantial improvements across all key performance indicators: 43% reduction in total alarm frequency ( P < 0.001), 56% reduction in false alarm rate ( P < 0.001), 38% improvement in response time ( P < 0.001), and 51% reduction in treatment interruptions ( P < 0.001).

title: Hemodialysis equipment malfunction incidence and risk profiling in clinical settings: a retrospective single-center cohort analysis
outcome: alarm metrics and interruptions
effect: Predictive model-guided interventions reduced total alarm frequency by 43%, false alarms by 56%, response time by 38%, and treatment interruptions by 51%.

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: CIN2+ calling with vs without AI assistance for the same pathologist
effect: EE + P2 identified 69 CIN2+ vs P2 alone 70; agreement with P2-digital 90.7% (κ 0.79) for EE+P2 vs 88.7% (κ 0.74) for EE alone; P1 sensitivity 83.8% vs AI-assisted reference; no significant shift (p=1.00).
quote: These findings indicate that, for the high-volume expert reader, the AI-assisted workflow (EE + P2) did not significantly alter the overall CIN2+ calling rate relative to unaided digital review, but rather redistributed a small number of borderline cases in both directions.

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: AI false negatives and overcalls that clinician review must catch
effect: EE had 4 false negatives and 11 false positives vs P1; under-called ACIS (13/20) with 3 downgraded to CIN1; pathologist review corrected most errors.
quote: EE alone under-called ACIS (13/20) and redistributed the remainder in both clinically unfavorable directions—downward to CIN1 (n = 3), which represents a potential false negative at the treatment threshold, and upward to SCC (n = 4), which represents a false positive invasive call ( Table 9 ).

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: Whether pathologist review corrects AI errors in ACIS and suspected SCC calls
effect: After adjudication (EE + P2), ACIS restored from 13/20 to 18/20 and SCC calls reduced from 4 to 1 of 20; 6 of 7 AI-flagged SCC in P1-CIN3 retained.
quote: After expert adjudication in the EE + P2 condition, ACIS was restored to 18/20 and SCC was reduced to 1/20, demonstrating that the human reviewer corrected virtually all high-consequence AI errors.

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: AI performance compared against original pathologist sign-out at CIN2+ threshold
effect: Using P1 as reference, EagleEye sensitivity 93.3% (56/60), specificity 71.8% (28/39); agreement with P1 κ=0.67.
quote: Against P1 as reference, EE identified 56/60 CIN2+ cases (sensitivity 93.3%) with specificity 71.8% (28/39), corresponding to 11 false positives (P1 <CIN2) and 4 false negatives.

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: Representativeness and generalizability of test data (single-centre, spectrum-balanced, prevalence-inflated)
effect: Single centre, one scanner, spectrum-balanced convenience sample with inflated CIN2+ prevalence (~60–70%); PPV/NPV would be lower at 5–10% prevalence; external validation needed.
quote: Second, the dataset was intentionally spectrum-balanced with a much higher CIN2+/ACIS prevalence than in routine screening or ordinary referral cohorts; this spectrum bias inflates PPV/NPV and may also influence κ, so predictive values reported here should be considered study-internal and would be lower at 5–10% CIN2+ prevalence.

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: Adequacy of reference standard for accuracy estimates
effect: No independent gold standard; P1 sign-out and AI-assisted EE+P2 used as references, the latter subject to incorporation/verification bias.
quote: Because EE + P2 incorporates the intervention under study, this comparison is subject to verification/incorporation bias and is presented strictly as an internal case-finding exploration rather than as a formal estimate of P1 diagnostic accuracy; all sensitivity/specificity estimates versus EE + P2 should therefore be interpreted as study-internal performance metrics, not as externally generalizable truth standards.

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: Justification of decision threshold for AI slide-level positivity
effect: The ≥15-tile operating point was chosen heuristically, not from ROC or decision-curve analysis; no continuous score or tunable operating point.
quote: The threshold was not derived from formal ROC or decision-curve calibration and is therefore reported as a methodological limitation.

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: Expert detection of incorrect AI outputs
effect: After adjudication, ACIS increased from EE-alone 13/20 to 18/20, and false invasive SCC calls decreased to 1/20.
quote: After expert adjudication in the EE + P2 condition, ACIS was restored to 18/20 and false invasive calls were largely removed (SCC 1/20).

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: CIN2+ agreement under human-in-the-loop review versus standalone AI
effect: Agreement with P2-digital increased from 88.7% (kappa 0.74) for EagleEye alone to 90.7% (kappa 0.79) for AI-assisted review (EE + P2).
quote: Relative to P2-digital, agreement with the algorithm increased from 88.7% (κ = 0.74) for EE alone to 90.7% (κ = 0.79) for EE + P2, indicating incremental value of human adjudication in a human-in-the-loop workflow, where the expert accepts or dismisses AI-suggested foci.

title: Digital Pathology with AI for Cervical Biopsies: Diagnostic Accuracy at the CIN2+ Threshold
outcome: clinician correction of high-consequence AI errors
effect: Clinician review of AI outputs restored ACIS from 13/20 to 18/20 and reduced false-positive squamous cell carcinoma calls from 4 to 1.
quote: After expert adjudication in the EE + P2 condition, ACIS was restored to 18/20 and SCC was reduced to 1/20, demonstrating that the human reviewer corrected virtually all high-consequence AI errors.

title: Benchmarking robustness of automated CT pancreas segmentation: achieving human-level reliability through human-in-the-loop optimization
outcome: Segmentation accuracy versus multi-reader human reference standard, including tail-case failures
effect: Best model DSC 0.88 ± 0.04 approached humans, but 3%-5% of cases (best model) and 7%-10% (benchmark) fell below human thresholds vs 1% for humans.
quote: Figure 2C-D confirm this trend—human readers had fewer low DSC and NSD cases (1%) compared to AI models (7%–10% for the benchmark, 3%–5% for the best model).
sample_unit: test CT scans (each with 4 independent human segmentations)

title: Benchmarking robustness of automated CT pancreas segmentation: achieving human-level reliability through human-in-the-loop optimization
outcome: Uncertainty-based triage identifying cases to defer to humans for revision
effect: Acquisition function (entropy + sphericity) inversely correlated with DSC/NSD; revising 6% of cases reduced error rate (1 – FT) to ~1%.
quote: Instead, an active learning approach proved effective in this case, reducing the error rate (1 – FT) to ∼1% with manual revision of only 6% of cases, leading to a 23-fold workload reduction.
sample_unit: test CT scans (each with 4 independent human segmentations)

title: Benchmarking robustness of automated CT pancreas segmentation: achieving human-level reliability through human-in-the-loop optimization
outcome: Robustness hidden by mean metrics
effect: Even best models lacked robustness: 5% to 7% of predictions fell below minimum performance threshold despite high mean metrics.
quote: Our multireader evaluation revealed that even the best-performing pancreas segmentation models lacked robustness: 5% to 7% of predictions fell below the minimum performance threshold in cases that human readers handled consistently.
sample_unit: test CT scans (each with 4 independent human segmentations)

title: Benchmarking robustness of automated CT pancreas segmentation: achieving human-level reliability through human-in-the-loop optimization
outcome: Failures in anatomical variants
effect: Annular pancreas case 79 and duodenal diverticulum case 53 led to segmentation inconsistencies; other errors involved fatty infiltration and low BMI.
quote: Additionally, rare anatomical variations, such as annular pancreas (case 79) and duodenal diverticulum (case 53), led to segmentation inconsistencies, likely because of their limited representation in training data.
sample_unit: test CT scans (each with 4 independent human segmentations)

title: Benchmarking robustness of automated CT pancreas segmentation: achieving human-level reliability through human-in-the-loop optimization
outcome: Automated outlier detection for segmentations
effect: High α was inversely correlated with DSC/NSD; 95th-percentile high-α cases were more likely to underperform and were triaged for revision.
quote: Figure 5A shows an inverse correlation between the acquisition function α and the DSC/NSD, confirming that cases with high α were more likely to underperform manual segmentation.
sample_unit: test CT scans (each with 4 independent human segmentations)

title: Next-generation multicenter studies: using artificial intelligence to automatically process unstructured health records of patients with lung cancer across multiple institutions
venue: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
outcome: Error rate reduction with targeted human review of low-confidence AI outputs
effect: Targeted human review of 30% of low-confidence AI outputs decreased error rates to 4.4%
quote: A hybrid approach with targeted human review of 30% of low-confidence AI outputs further decreased error rates to 4.4%.

title: Next-generation multicenter studies: using artificial intelligence to automatically process unstructured health records of patients with lung cancer across multiple institutions
venue: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
outcome: Interinstitutional variability in extraction error across 10 centers
effect: Interinstitutional variance lower with AI (0.12%) than manual abstraction (0.39%)
quote: Interinstitutional variance was lower with AI (0.12% versus 0.39%).

title: Next-generation multicenter studies: using artificial intelligence to automatically process unstructured health records of patients with lung cancer across multiple institutions
venue: Annals of oncology : official journal of the European Society for Medical Oncology
outcome: data extraction error rate
effect: error rate decreased from 7.0% to 4.4% with targeted human review of 30% low-confidence outputs
quote: A hybrid approach with targeted human review of 30% of low-confidence AI outputs further decreased error rates to 4.4%.

title: Evaluation of AI chatbot responses to brachytherapy frequently asked questions
outcome: Reading level of chatbot and gold-standard brachytherapy answers versus recommended level
effect: Both sources significantly exceeded recommended reading levels (>12th grade Flesch-Kincaid); AI responses substantially longer; simulated patients rated readability easy for 44% of AI vs 92% of GS responses.
quote: Objective analysis confirmed that both sources significantly exceeded the recommended reading levels (e.g., >12th grade Flesch-Kincaid), with AI responses being substantially longer.
sample_unit: expert response-pair ratings (4 experts x 10 FAQ x 2 sources)

title: Evaluation of AI chatbot responses to brachytherapy frequently asked questions
outcome: Chatbot helpfulness and readability for simulated patient personas of varying literacy
effect: Simulated patients preferred GS responses (62% vs 34%), particularly lower-literacy personas; readability easy/very easy 92% for GS vs 44% for AI.
quote: Simulated patients preferred GS responses (62% vs. 34%), particularly lower-literacy personas, citing better perceived readability (92% easy/very easy vs. 44% for AI) and a more reassuring tone (42% vs. 24% for AI).
sample_unit: expert response-pair ratings (4 experts x 10 FAQ x 2 sources)

title: Accuracy and efficiency of artificial Intelligence-Assisted three-dimensional liver volumetry in living donor evaluation based on real world prospective data
venue: HPB : the official journal of the International Hepato Pancreato Biliary Association
outcome: Graft-volume prediction accuracy versus conventional manual volumetry
effect: After exclusions, AI: R² = 0.818; median error 54.0 mL. Conventional methods: R² = 0.707; median error 65.0 mL.
quote: After exclusions, AI-based volumetry showed superior predictive performance (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.818; median error 54.0 mL) versus conventional methods (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.707; median error 65.0 mL).

title: The impact of language differences on the readability, quality, and reliability of information provided by artificial intelligence chatbots regarding vital pulp therapy: a cross-sectional study
outcome: Chatbot response readability, quality, and reliability differences across English and Turkish
effect: Significant differences between chatbots in readability, GQS, and JAMA in both languages (p<0.05); Perplexity most difficult to read in both languages, ChatGPT most readable. Quality leaders differed by language.
quote: Readability, GQS, and JAMA assessments revealed statistically significant differences between the chatbots in both English and Turkish responses (p < 0.05).
sample_unit: questions (each submitted to 6 chatbots in 2 languages over 7 days)

title: Detection of undiagnosed liver cirrhosis via AI-enabled electrocardiogram: a pragmatic, cluster-randomized clinical trial
outcome: New diagnosis of advanced CLD within 180 days, intervention vs usual care in cluster RCT
effect: Advanced CLD diagnoses 1.0% vs 0.5% overall (OR 2.09, 95% CI 1.22-3.55, P = 0.007); among ECG-ML-positive patients 4.4% vs 1.1% (OR 4.37).
quote: The intervention significantly increased new diagnoses of advanced CLD in the overall cohort (1.0% versus 0.5% in the control arm; odds ratio (OR) 2.09, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.22-3.55, P = 0.007).

title: Enhancing patient education in cataract surgery using a conversational artificial intelligence chatbot: pilot randomized controlled trial
venue: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery
outcome: Knowledge gain, anxiety change, and satisfaction, chatbot plus brochure vs brochure alone
effect: No significant differences in knowledge gain, anxiety change, or satisfaction (P > .05). 17 of 33 (52%) chatbot-group patients did not engage; SUS 83.1 ± 12.1. Only 35 of 64 completed postoperative questionnaires.
quote: No significant differences were detected in knowledge gain, anxiety change, or satisfaction ( P > .05).

title: Large Language Models for Psychiatric Diagnosis Based on Multicenter Real-World Clinical Records: Comparative Study
outcome: LLM diagnostic performance differences across 6 psychiatric centers
effect: Model performance remained stable across centers, with no significant intercenter differences.
quote: Across centers, model performance remained stable, with no significant intercenter differences.

title: Large Language Models for Psychiatric Diagnosis Based on Multicenter Real-World Clinical Records: Comparative Study
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy across age subgroups
effect: Accuracy varied by age group: highest in older adults (up to 79.5%), lower in adolescents.
quote: Diagnostic performance varied across age groups, with the highest accuracy observed in older adult patients (up to 79.5%) and lower accuracy in adolescents.

title: Comparing guideline adherence and readability: Artificial intelligence with deep learning versus specialized physicians in peripheral artery disease management
outcome: LLM adherence to 2024 ACC/AHA PAD guideline versus physicians, scored by three experts
effect: Adherence did not differ (physicians median 5.8 vs LLMs 7.3, p=0.169); CoT-LLMs highest (9.7). LLMs more often recommended supervised exercise (84.6% vs 30.0%) and revascularization for quality of life (69.2% vs 20.0%).
quote: LLM showed comparable guideline adherence to physicians although CoT models achieved the highest scores.
sample_unit: responses (30 physician, 13 LLM system) to a standardized PAD case

title: Performance of artificial intelligence large language models (LLMs) in answering frequently asked questions about isotretinoin
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading ease of chatbot answers about isotretinoin
effect: No significant difference between programs in Flesch Kincaid reading ease scores (p = 0.671); all three programs were at a difficult level of reading.
quote: No significant difference was found between the groups in terms of Flesch Kincaid reading ease scores (p = 0.671), and all three programs were found to be at a difficult level of reading.

title: When Jack of All Trades Is a Master of None: Comparing the Performance of GPT-4 Omni against Specialised Neural Networks in Identifying Malignant Dermatological Lesions from Smartphone Images and Structured Clinical Data
outcome: Comparison of GPT-4o against specialised neural networks on skin lesion malignancy triage
effect: Specialised neural networks significantly outperformed GPT-4o on most pairwise comparisons; GPT-4o balanced accuracies were 0.571, 0.602, 0.622 for clinical, image, multimodal inputs.
quote: Specialised neural networks significantly outperformed GPT-4o on most pairwise comparisons.
sample_unit: random skin lesion cases from PAD-UFES-20 (50 repeated trials each)

title: When Jack of All Trades Is a Master of None: Comparing the Performance of GPT-4 Omni against Specialised Neural Networks in Identifying Malignant Dermatological Lesions from Smartphone Images and Structured Clinical Data
outcome: GPT-4o discriminative performance across age, sex, and skin tone subgroups
effect: Poorer discriminative performance in younger patients versus middle-aged and elderly; no notable differences between sex and skin tone subgroups.
quote: Fairness evaluations showed poorer discriminative performance in younger patients compared to middle-aged and elderly patients but no notable differences between different sex and skin tone subgroups.
sample_unit: random skin lesion cases from PAD-UFES-20 (50 repeated trials each)

title: When Jack of All Trades Is a Master of None: Comparing the Performance of GPT-4 Omni against Specialised Neural Networks in Identifying Malignant Dermatological Lesions from Smartphone Images and Structured Clinical Data
outcome: GPT-4o output reproducibility across 50 repeated trials
effect: Mean agreement rates were >0.90, but Fleiss' kappa indicated only moderate consistency due to strong bias toward malignant classifications.
quote: Mean agreement rates were high (>0.90); however, Fleiss' κ indicated only moderate consistency due to a strong bias toward malignant classifications.
sample_unit: random skin lesion cases from PAD-UFES-20 (50 repeated trials each)

title: When Jack of All Trades Is a Master of None: Comparing the Performance of GPT-4 Omni against Specialised Neural Networks in Identifying Malignant Dermatological Lesions from Smartphone Images and Structured Clinical Data
outcome: GPT-4o triage performance for skin lesion malignancy
effect: Poor triage performance; balanced accuracy 0.571-0.622, sensitivity >0.95 but very low specificity.
quote: Sensitivity was consistently high (>0.95) with the trade-off of very low specificity.
sample_unit: random skin lesion cases from PAD-UFES-20 (50 repeated trials each)

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o as a Patient Information Tool for Common Orthopaedic Surgeries: Accuracy, Completeness, and Clinical Utility
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM clinical content on orthopaedic procedures, incl. risks and alternatives
effect: Factual accuracy >90%, but 36% of responses contained misleading or incomplete information; surgical risk responses performed worst; mean DISCERN 43.5 (fair).
quote: Factual accuracy was high (>90%), but 36% of responses contained some misleading or incomplete information.

title: AI-Based Gait Analysis System for Rehabilitation: Usability Evaluation of Human-Technology Interaction
outcome: System usability (SUS) and usability barriers found in scenario-based testing with end users
effect: Mean SUS score 57 (grade D), suboptimal usability. Testing with 5 physical therapists surfaced barriers: power button access, no battery indicator, burdensome manual calibration, insufficient report detail.
quote: The mean SUS score was 57 (grade D), indicating suboptimal usability and the need for iterative design refinements.

title: AI-Based Gait Analysis System for Rehabilitation: Usability Evaluation of Human-Technology Interaction
outcome: Clinician-reported need for EHR integration of the AI gait system
effect: Participants emphasized needing integration with hospital electronic medical record systems, plus wireless operation and improved portability. The prototype was not integrated.
quote: They also emphasized the need for wireless operation, improved portability, and integration with hospital electronic medical record systems.

title: A Rule-Based Automated Triage Model Using Natural Language Processing for Pain Medicine-Development and Implementation
outcome: Agreement between predicted accuracy and accuracy in live EHR deployment
effect: Post-processing model predicted 84.2% accuracy; the first 200 live cases showed 83.5%, consistent with prediction.
quote: The implementation accuracy of 200 cases for the first 3 months was consistent with our prediction at 83.5%, which concluded that the improvement over ML models (p-value = 0.018) was statistically significant at 95% significance level.

title: Mixed-methods evaluation of how a predictive model pilot intervention addresses patient non-attendance at outpatient services in an NHS Foundation Trust in England
outcome: Staff ability to act on model risk scores within defined workflow roles
effect: Many staff struggled to action the intervention workflow, especially when it was not seen to fall within their defined roles; low volumes of intervention calls were made in phase 1 and call rates were lower in phase 2.
quote: Thematic analysis of the qualitative data suggests that many staff delivering the intervention struggled with actioning the intervention workflow, especially when it was not seen to fall within their defined roles.

title: Mixed-methods evaluation of how a predictive model pilot intervention addresses patient non-attendance at outpatient services in an NHS Foundation Trust in England
outcome: Team capacity and prioritisation to act on predictive model outputs
effect: Differing prioritisation of the intervention amid long waiting lists and staff resourcing issues limited pilot success; only 3 of 9 services significantly reduced non-attendance in phase 1, and 1 in phase 2 (20.4% to 19.1%, p<0.05).
quote: Differing perceptions of how the intervention should be prioritised, especially in the context of long waiting lists and staff resourcing issues, offer some context to the limits of the pilot's success.

title: Personalizing prostate cancer education for patients using an EHR-Integrated LLM agent
outcome: Clinician review of real patient-chat histories for correctness, completeness, safety, and personalization
effect: Clinicians rated MedEduChat as highly correct (2.9/3), complete (2.7/3), and safe (2.7/3), with moderate personalization (2.3/3).
quote: Clinicians evaluated the patient-chat interaction history and rated MedEduChat as highly correct (2.9/3), complete (2.7/3), and safe (2.7/3), with moderate personalization (2.3/3).

title: Signal Fidelity Index-aware calibration for addressing distributional shift in predictive modeling across heterogeneous real-world data
outcome: F1 and AUC under heterogeneous target datasets
effect: F1 +4.2% to +34.9% and AUC +4.6 % to +40% versus uncalibrated predictions and baselines.
quote: Evaluation across six phenotypes and 3,550 synthetic datasets demonstrated consistent performance improvements (F1 score +4.2% to +34.9%, AUC +4.6 % to +40%) over uncalibrated predictions and established baseline methods.

title: Signal Fidelity Index-aware calibration for addressing distributional shift in predictive modeling across heterogeneous real-world data
outcome: expected calibration error
effect: ECE decreased in five phenotypes (−45.2% to −3.5%) but increased +7.7% for adult ADHD.
quote: Notably, ECE decreased for several phenotypes–indicating improved bin-level calibration–(hypertension: –45.2%, geriatric bipolar: –22.7%, type 2 diabetes: –15.4%, dementia: –14.2%, fibromyalgia: –3.5%), while adult ADHD showed a modest ECE increase (+7.7%).

title: Investigating How Clinicians Form Trust in an AI-Based Mental Health Model: Qualitative Case Study
outcome: Clinician-reported trust formation with uncertainty visualization in an AI mental health screening model
effect: Clinicians reported that violin-plot visualization of confidence and uncertainty supported trust and aligned with their expectations of decision ambiguity. Qualitative only, with no numeric effect.
quote: Trust formation was supported by the explainability of the model, particularly through (1) visualization of confidence and uncertainty through violin plots, aligning with the clinicians' expectations of decision ambiguity; (2) feature attribution for and against predictions, which mirrored clinical reasoning; and (3) use of pseudo-sumscores in the AI model, which increased interpretability by presenting explanations in familiar clinical formats.

title: Artificial intelligence for drug information: Evaluating its use in real-world pharmacy practice
venue: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
outcome: Accuracy of references and citations in chatbot drug information answers
effect: 15% of ChatGPT answers were completely inaccurate and included fake/unreliable references, versus 5% of Gemini's; only 19% of answers for each were fully accurate with reliable references.
quote: Fifteen percent of answers by ChatGPT were completely inaccurate and included fake/unreliable references, while 5% of Gemini's answers were categorized as such.

title: Artificial intelligence for drug information: Evaluating its use in real-world pharmacy practice
venue: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
outcome: Accuracy of chatbot responses against DI pharmacist answers on a 3-point scale
effect: ChatGPT and Gemini were completely accurate with reliable references 19% of the time; 66% (ChatGPT) and 76% (Gemini) were partially correct and/or had incomplete resources.
quote: ChatGPT and Gemini were both completely accurate, with reliable references provided 19% of the time.

title: Implementation of large language models in electronic health records
outcome: Volume of voluntary user feedback after pilot versus hospital-wide routine use
effect: Feedback volume decreased compared with the pilot as routine use grew (1,028 users, 14,910 conversations over five months), indicating voluntary reporting declines and automated monitoring is needed.
quote: Feedback volume decreased compared with the pilot, suggesting that routine use diminishes voluntary reporting and underscoring the need for complementary automated monitoring strategies.

title: Autonomous Analysis of Curated Patient Data Using a Large Language Model-Based Multiagent Framework
outcome: Accuracy replicating published primary outcomes versus reference results, multiagent versus ChatGPT 4o
effect: Multiagent framework replicated 53.3% (95% CI, 40.7 to 66.0) of primary outcomes vs ChatGPT 4o 35.0% (95% CI, 22.9 to 47.1); P = .04.
quote: The multiagent framework successfully replicated 53.3% (95% CI, 40.7 to 66.0) of primary outcomes, significantly outperforming ChatGPT 4o (35.0% [95% CI, 22.9 to 47.1]; P = .04).

title: Comparative validation of PREDICT versions 3.1 and 2.2 for overall survival in the Dutch breast cancer population
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of PREDICT versions on Dutch registry data versus observed 10-year survival
effect: Overall AUC 0.768 (v2.2) and 0.775 (v3.1); v3.1 overestimated OS by 1.9%, v2.2 underestimated by 1.6%; small differences varying by subgroup.
quote: Both PREDICT v2.2 and v3.1 accurately predict 10-year OS in Dutch breast cancer patients, with small differences between versions that vary by subgroup.

title: Comparative validation of PREDICT versions 3.1 and 2.2 for overall survival in the Dutch breast cancer population
outcome: Performance across 36 subgroups by ER, HER2, age and tumour stage
effect: v3.1 generally outperformed v2.2 except age >75, where v2.2 was more accurate; in ER-/HER2- aged 50-75, v3.1 overestimated 1.5-2.8% and v2.2 underestimated 2.8-5.3%.
quote: Across subgroups, v3.1 generally outperformed v2.2 except in patients aged >75 years, where v2.2 provided more accurate estimates.

title: Connecting algorithmic fairness and fair outcomes in a sociotechnical simulation case study of AI-assisted healthcare
outcome: Effect of error-rate parity mitigation on group mortality disparity and privileged group mortality
effect: EqOdds/EqOppTPR reduced mortality rate ratio from 3.77 to ~3.05-3.07 but raised privileged group mortality via leveling down; EqOppFPR slightly raised disparity (3.82).
quote: Although the reduced disparity in mortality rates implies a positive health equity outcome, it is notable that in the EqOppTPR and EqOdds scenarios, the privileged group's mortality rate increased (Fig. 2A ).
sample_unit: simulated women per run (100 simulation runs)

title: Connecting algorithmic fairness and fair outcomes in a sociotechnical simulation case study of AI-assisted healthcare
outcome: Simulated group-wise mortality and socioeconomic outcomes under fairness-constrained AI
effect: Stark mortality disparities persisted regardless of algorithmic fairness constraints; equalized odds reduced disparity by only ~12 per 100k versus ~57 per 100k from improving screening access.
quote: We observed stark differences in annual mortality rates between the privileged and unprivileged groups, regardless of the algorithmic fairness constraints imposed.
sample_unit: simulated women per run (100 simulation runs)

title: Connecting algorithmic fairness and fair outcomes in a sociotechnical simulation case study of AI-assisted healthcare
outcome: Fair distribution of AI-enabled care benefits when access barriers differ between groups
effect: Access barriers had greater impact on disparities than AI fairness; enforcing equalized odds reduced disparity ~12 per 100k vs ~57 per 100k with 93% screening access.
quote: The sensitivity analysis for parameters determining the likelihood of screening, treatment delays, and adjuvant treatment within the simulation showed that barriers to accessing appropriate healthcare had a greater impact on health disparities than AI-based interventions.
sample_unit: simulated women per run (100 simulation runs)

title: Connecting algorithmic fairness and fair outcomes in a sociotechnical simulation case study of AI-assisted healthcare
outcome: Impact of subgroup TPR/FPR disparities in AI on group-wise outcomes
effect: Lowering unprivileged TPR by 30% increased mortality rate ratio by over 15%; 30% higher privileged FPR reduced ratio by under 5%.
quote: For instance, at a given ΔFPR, lowering the TPR for the unprivileged group by 30% increased the mortality rate ratio by over 15%.
sample_unit: simulated women per run (100 simulation runs)

title: Connecting algorithmic fairness and fair outcomes in a sociotechnical simulation case study of AI-assisted healthcare
outcome: reliance and group misdiagnosis
effect: Naive FNR privileged/unprivileged: 27.11/26.74 at α=0.0; 22.94/30.01 at α=0.5; 18.79/33.33 at α=1.0.
quote: Here, it can be seen that the mortality rate disparity surged with a higher degree of reliance on the AI system under both the Naive and EqOppFPR scenarios.
sample_unit: simulated women per run (100 simulation runs)

title: An AI-powered tongue image model for home-based monitoring of liver fibrosis
outcome: AUC for liver fibrosis detection versus state-of-the-art image models on same data
effect: TongVMoe AUC 0.8061 versus DiffMIC-v2 0.6929, HorNet 0.7018, InceptionNeXt 0.7012, LSNet 0.6971, TransXNet 0.7062.
quote: The model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.8061, outperforming State-of-the-Art methods such as DiffMIC-v2 (0.6929), HorNet (0.7018), InceptionNeXt (0.7012), LSNet (0.6971), and TransXNet (0.7062).

title: Performance of large language models in reporting oral health concerns and side effects in head and neck cancer: a comparative study
venue: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
outcome: Readability (FRES) and actionability of LLM responses for head and neck cancer patient questions
effect: Median FRES ≤ 40.2 (complex language); median PEMAT-actionability ≤ 40; PEMAT-understandability median ≥ 75.0.
quote: LLMs were understandable (median PEMAT-understandability scores ≥ 75.0), but provided limited specific guidance (median PEMAT-actionability scores ≤ 40) and used complex language (median FRES ≤ 40.2).

title: Identifying eligible patients for the Australian national lung cancer screening program in primary care: A cross-sectional study using clinical decision support systems and evaluating PLCOm2012 data quality
outcome: Availability of PLCOm2012 input variables in general practice EMRs
effect: In 933 audited records, missing data were education 100%, ethnicity 58%, BMI 57%, daily cigarette consumption 33%; pack-years calculable for only 17.2% of 1,315 records.
quote: A subset of 933 records was assessed for PLCOm2012 variables, revealing substantial data gaps (% missing): education level (100 %), ethnicity (58 %), BMI (57 %), and daily cigarette consumption (33 %).

title: Physicians' perceptions of how digital-intelligent medical technology reshapes job characteristics: a qualitative study
outcome: Physician-perceived skill degradation and technical dependency from digital-intelligent medical technology
effect: Interviewed physicians described technical dependency and skill degradation risks as new job demands; no prevalence figures reported.
quote: Challenges such as technical dependency, operational complexity, and ethical responsibility arising from digital-intelligent medical technologies impose new job demands on physicians, exacerbating burnout and skill degradation risks.

title: Physicians' perceptions of how digital-intelligent medical technology reshapes job characteristics: a qualitative study
outcome: Physician-perceived job demands, burnout and efficiency effects of AI tools
effect: Technologies were perceived to improve efficiency and decision accuracy, but also added operational complexity and burnout risk; qualitative only, no quantified effects.
quote: Challenges such as technical dependency, operational complexity, and ethical responsibility arising from digital-intelligent medical technologies impose new job demands on physicians, exacerbating burnout and skill degradation risks.

title: Retrospective validation study of a large language model approach to screening for intraabdominal surgical site infections for quality and safety reporting
outcome: LLM screening PPV and NPV versus current EHR-based screening workflow for intra-abdominal SSI
effect: LLM flagged 104 cases high risk, PPV 53.8%, NPV 100%; EHR-based workflow flagged 288 cases, PPV 19.4%, NPV 100%.
quote: In contrast, the EHR-based workflow identified 288 cases for further review, with a PPV of only 19.4% and the same NPV of 100%.

title: Tele-ophthalmology-enabled and artificial intelligence-ready referral pathway for community optometry referrals of retinal disease: HERMES cluster randomised trial with a diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: AI processing rate and referral accuracy in real-world optometry settings
effect: Octane processed images from only 204 of 396 participants (51.5%); could not process 48.5%; generalisability challenges in real-world evaluation.
quote: The artificial intelligence model presented challenges relating to its generalisability in a real-world evaluation context.

title: Tele-ophthalmology-enabled and artificial intelligence-ready referral pathway for community optometry referrals of retinal disease: HERMES cluster randomised trial with a diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: AI referral decision accuracy versus hospital experts and community optometrists
effect: Octane showed inferior sensitivity and specificity versus human expert assessors (clinical reference standard); similar accuracy to community optometrists.
quote: Compared to hospital-based experts for referral decisions, Octane was less accurate at making routine and urgent referral decisions and of similar accuracy to community optometrists.

title: Tele-ophthalmology-enabled and artificial intelligence-ready referral pathway for community optometry referrals of retinal disease: HERMES cluster randomised trial with a diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Ability to process OCT images collected in community optometry practices
effect: Octane processed images from 204 of 396 participants (51.5%) and could not process images from 48.5% of study participants.
quote: The Octane artificial intelligence model could not process images from 48.5% of study participants.

title: Assessment of quality and readability of information provided by ChatGPT in relation to developmental dysplasia of the hip and periacetabular osteotomy
outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT 4 patient-education responses versus recommended sixth-grade level
effect: Average Reading Grade Level was 13.44, considerably higher than the recommended sixth-grade level for patient education materials.
quote: Readability tests showed that the average Reading Grade Level was 13.44, considerably higher than the recommended sixth-grade level for patient education materials, indicating a substantial barrier to comprehension for the general public.

title: Comparative evaluation of artificial intelligence platforms and drug interaction screening databases using real-world patient data
venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
outcome: LLM DDI identification accuracy against a database-derived reference standard (sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1)
effect: Against 204 reference DDIs, ChatGPT flagged 439, Gemini 1556, Copilot 1813. Gemini sensitivity 0.697; ChatGPT specificity 0.868; F1 0.2520 (ChatGPT), 0.1933 (Gemini), 0.1153 (Copilot); precision low.
quote: Our results suggest that no AI systems assessed achieve the required balance of precision and sensitivity for reliable clinical decision-making in DDI screening.

title: Comparative evaluation of artificial intelligence platforms and drug interaction screening databases using real-world patient data
venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
outcome: Incorrect or hallucinated LLM interaction outputs that clinicians would need to verify
effect: All three LLMs had low precision and flagged many more interactions than the 204 in the reference set (439, 1556, 1813), producing clinically inaccurate information from hallucinations.
quote: Although LLMs show promise as complementary tools in DDI screening, as they proved effective in identifying true interactions, they generate clinically inaccurate information due to hallucinations, which limits their reliability as standalone screening tools.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence models in childhood exanthematous diseases: a comparative analysis against clinical diagnosis
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI models vs consultant and resident physicians against definitive diagnosis
effect: Consultant 96.6%; ChatGPT with clinical data 86.9%, Copilot 81.4%, Gemini 78.7%; resident 72.5%. Consultant superior to all other interpreters and models (p < .001).
quote: The consultant's diagnostic performance was significantly superior to all other interpreters and models (p < .001 for all comparisons).

title: Multi-step retrieval and reasoning improves radiology question answering with large language models
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy with multi-step retrieval grounding versus zero-shot and conventional online RAG
effect: RaR improved mean diagnostic accuracy vs zero-shot (75% vs. 67%; P = 1.1e-7) and vs conventional online RAG (75% vs. 69%; P = 1.9e-6). Reduced hallucinations, with clinically relevant evidence in 46% of cases.
quote: RaR significantly improved mean diagnostic accuracy versus zero-shot prompting (75% vs. 67%; P = 1.1 × 10<sup>-7</sup>) and conventional online RAG (75% vs. 69%; P = 1.9 × 10<sup>-6</sup>).
sample_unit: radiology questions (104 expert-curated plus 65 board-exam questions)

title: Performance of large language model in cross-specialty medical scenarios
outcome: LLM diagnostic and therapeutic accuracy on clinical vignettes across 12 specialties
effect: Therapeutic recommendations were inconsistent: GPT-4o median 10 (IQR 0–10), GPT-3.5-Turbo median 0 (IQR 0–6.3; P=.0005), Claude-3-Sonnet median 5 (IQR 0–10); GPT-4o vs Claude P=.45.
quote: However, their inconsistent performance in generating therapeutic recommendations presents a major barrier to clinical adoption.

title: Artificial intelligence for procedural coding in cardiac critical care: Evaluating large language models for current procedural terminology accuracy
outcome: CPT code accuracy of six LLMs on cardiac ICU procedures, ECMO vs non-ECMO
effect: Non-ECMO accuracy ranged from 56% (GPT-4.0) to 88% (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Perplexity). ECMO accuracy ranged from 0% (GPT-4.0) to 86% (Perplexity), with Claude 3.7 Sonnet at 14%.
quote: For ECMO-related codes, Perplexity outperformed all models (86%), followed by Gemini 2.5 Pro (71%), Mistral (43%), DeepSeek (29%), Claude 3.7 Sonnet (14%), and GPT 4.0 (0%).

title: Artificial Intelligence's Capacity to Detect Subtle Medical Misinformation: A Novel Reverse Prompting Approach
outcome: Detection and correction of subtle medical misinformation embedded in prompts, by model
effect: GPT-4o corrected misinformation in 86% of prompts, GPT-5 in 74%, GPT-4.1-mini detected only 52% (complete failure 34%, hedging 14%).
quote: GPT-4.1-mini showed weaker performance, detecting dsmisinformation in only 52% of prompts, with complete failure in 34% and hedging in 14%.

title: Label Noise in Pathological Segmentation Is Overlooked, Leading to Potential Overestimation of Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Effect of annotation label noise on segmentation performance estimates against clean test data
effect: Models overfit label noise, especially boundary-dependent noise (dilation, shrinkage); apparent scores under noisy conditions overestimated true performance on clean test data, most for boundary-altering noise.
quote: Discrepancies were identified between apparent performance scores obtained under real-world conditions and true performance scores derived using clean test data.

title: ARTEMIS: a pilot study comparing AI-based and expert therapeutic decisions in simulated clinical cases of neuroendocrine neoplasms
outcome: Agreement with expert benchmark for systemic therapy: grounded (RAG, static corpus) vs baseline GPT
effect: RAG and GPTs 70.0% agreement vs baseline GPT 60.0%; RAG and GPTs met the -10% non-inferiority margin, baseline did not; neither met -5%.
quote: Based on the lower bound of the one-sided 95% bootstrap confidence interval, GPT did not meet non-inferiority, whereas GPTs and RAG satisfied the –10% but not the –5% margin (Fig. 1 ).

title: ARTEMIS: a pilot study comparing AI-based and expert therapeutic decisions in simulated clinical cases of neuroendocrine neoplasms
outcome: Reproducibility of outputs across repeated runs of the same cases
effect: RAG perfect stability (AC1 1.000); baseline GPT AC1 0.843; GPTs lower (about 0.766, 69.9% agreement); temperature 0.2 used.
quote: Baseline GPT was more reproducible than GPTs (AC1 0.843, 95% CI 0.687–0.961; 80.1%, 95% CI 60–95 vs 69.9%, 95% CI 50–90), yielding the ranking RAG > GPT > GPTs.

title: ARTEMIS: a pilot study comparing AI-based and expert therapeutic decisions in simulated clinical cases of neuroendocrine neoplasms
outcome: Agreement with expert systemic therapy benchmark

title: Factors Impacting the Performance of Deep Learning Detection of Pulmonary Emboli

quote: Multivariable analysis showed significant associations between decreased sensitivity and scanner manufacturer (odds ratio [OR] 0.25, 95% CI 0.14-0.46 and OR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.69, for different vendors versus reference, P < .003), increased slice thickness (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57-0.95 per 1-mm increase, P = .018), presence of imaging artifacts (OR 0.33, 95% CI 0.23-0.48, P < .001), heart failure (OR 0.58, 95% CI 0.38-0.88, P = .010), and pulmonary hypertension (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.25-0.77, P = .004).

title: Evaluating the appropriateness and safety of generative AI in delivering lifestyle guidance for atrial fibrillation patients

outcome: Comparison of LLM responses against electrophysiologist responses on ten dimensions

quote: For Evidence of Incorrect Comprehension, GPT-4o demonstrated a significantly lower error rate compared with the electrophysiologist (OR 3.41, 95% CI 1.40–8.30), whereas DB GPT and PubMed GPT showed comparable performance (OR 1.06 [0.49–2.29] and 0.64 [0.30–1.37], respectively).

title: Evaluating the appropriateness and safety of generative AI in delivering lifestyle guidance for atrial fibrillation patients

title: Accuracy and Readability of Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer-4 Omni in Answering Ophthalmology Patient Questions
outcome: Incomplete or unacceptable AI patient replies
effect: Standard ChatGPT-4o replies: 220/285 (77.2%) accurate and complete, 49 (17.2%) incomplete, 16 (5.6%) unacceptable.
quote: Overall, 220 (77%) responses were graded as accurate and complete, 49 (17%) as incomplete, and 16 (6%) as unacceptable.

title: Accuracy and Readability of Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer-4 Omni in Answering Ophthalmology Patient Questions
outcome: Accuracy of responses when prompted for sixth-grade reading level versus unrestricted
effect: Accurate and complete responses 242 (85%) at sixth-grade prompt vs 220 (77%) standard; unacceptable 5 (2%) vs 16 (6%); no quality loss, significant improvement in cornea (P=0.001).
quote: Prompting the LLM to respond at a sixth-grade reading level did not result in a loss of response quality.

title: Accuracy and Readability of Chat Generative Pre-Trained Transformer-4 Omni in Answering Ophthalmology Patient Questions
outcome: Sixth-grade prompt answer quality
effect: Accurate/complete increased from 220/285 (77.2%) to 242/285 (84.9%); unacceptable decreased from 16 (5.6%) to 5 (1.8%).
quote: When asked to respond at a sixth-grade reading level, 242 (85%) responses were graded as accurate and complete, 38 (13%) were incomplete, and 5 (2%) were graded as unacceptable.

title: Establishing prospective performance monitoring for real-world implementation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation in prostate cancer radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Detection of performance shifts using predefined 2σ and 3σ statistical process control limits
effect: Model A stayed within 3σ limits for 9-13 months per organ; model B shift (p < 0.001) exceeded both thresholds for all five organs across all 7 months; 2σ more sensitive to mild deviations.
quote: The 2 σx¯ thresholds were more sensitive in detecting mild deviations for model A, while both limits effectively identified the substantial drift of model B.

title: Establishing prospective performance monitoring for real-world implementation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation in prostate cancer radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Monthly monitoring of auto-segmentation agreement with clinical contours for drift
effect: Monthly monitoring detected model switch/practice change; no degradation trend or clinician overreliance observed over 20 months; authors recommend at least monthly QA.
quote: The monitoring system effectively detected out-of-distribution outliers and clinical practice changes, providing a reliable framework for early detection of monthly performance degradation.

title: Establishing prospective performance monitoring for real-world implementation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation in prostate cancer radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Flagging of out-of-distribution outlier cases (e.g., metal artifacts)
effect: Flagged prostate outliers included 5 cases with fiducials and 6 with hip implants; rectum, bladder, femoral head outliers attributed to metal artifacts and generalization limits.
quote: By employing statistical process control, our framework effectively identified out-of-distribution outliers, serving as an early warning mechanism to prevent performance degradation.

title: Establishing prospective performance monitoring for real-world implementation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation in prostate cancer radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Apparent accuracy differences associated with clinician-edited AI reference contours
effect: Mean DSC increased from 0.82–0.96 to 0.89–0.97; HD95 decreased from 5.0–9.6 mm to 2.5–5.7 mm. Clinical references were edited AI outputs; authors cautioned that improved agreement did not necessarily indicate intrinsically better performance.
quote: The mean DSC increased from a range of 0.82–0.96 during testing to 0.89–0.97 during clinical practice, while the HD95 decreased from 5.0–9.6 mm to 2.5–5.7 mm across all organs of interest.

title: Establishing prospective performance monitoring for real-world implementation of deep learning-based auto-segmentation in prostate cancer radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Segmentation outliers associated with image artifacts and implanted materials
effect: Among prostate outliers, five cases were associated with fiducials and six with hip implants. Many other patients with fiducials remained within acceptable thresholds; hip-prosthesis metal artifacts also contributed to femoral-head segmentation failures.
quote: Among the prostate outliers, five cases were associated with fiducials and six with hip implants.

title: GraphRAG-Enabled Local Large Language Model for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus: Development of a Proof-of-Concept
outcome: Response similarity to reference answers (BLEU, Jaccard, BERTScore) for GraphRAG-grounded LLM versus ungrounded LLMs
effect: GraphRAG local LLM scored BLEU 0.99, Jaccard 0.98, BERTScore 0.98, outperforming ChatGPT, Claude and BioMistral on simulated clinical and layperson prompts.
quote: It achieved a bilingual evaluation understudy score of 0.99, Jaccard similarity of 0.98, and BERTScore of 0.98, outperforming the benchmark LLMs.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 for Patient Education in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Radiotherapy: a Comparative Analysis
venue: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
outcome: Readability of LLM patient education responses (FRES, FKGL, CLI) for NPC radiotherapy
effect: DeepSeek-R1 had significantly higher readability than ChatGPT-4o, with a 25.6% reduction in FKGL and 27% decrease in mean sentence length; ChatGPT-4o was harder to read.
quote: DeepSeek-R1 demonstrated significantly higher readability compared with ChatGPT-4o, with a 25.6% reduction in FKGL and a 27% decrease in mean sentence length, making it more accessible for populations with limited health literacy.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 for Patient Education in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma Radiotherapy: a Comparative Analysis
venue: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
outcome: Currency of evidence and guideline references in LLM responses
effect: Both models scored DISCERN 51-62 (good), but had deficiencies in evidence currency, guideline references, and long-term side effects.
quote: However, deficiencies were noted in the areas of evidence currency, guideline references, and long-term side effects.

title: Improving In-person Interpreter Utilization in Complex Care: Findings from a Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial of Integrated Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Time from study entry to first in-person interpreter visit, intervention vs control
effect: Time to receiving interpreter did not differ between groups (HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.81-1.29, p=0.87); the abstract reports an OR and CI close to >1 for receiving an interpreter.
quote: Time to receiving interpreter did not differ between groups (HR = 1.02, 95% C.I. (0.81, 1.29), p = 0.87).

title: Comparative Performance of ChatGPT-4o, Grok-3, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet in Differentiating Cerebellopontine Angle Schwannomas and Meningiomas: A Pilot Study of Visual Versus Text-Based Diagnostic Prompting
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy versus radiologists across input types (raw images, expert or resident structured features)
effect: With expert features GPT-4o reached 94.3% vs expert 92.5% (p=1.000) and resident 79.2% (p=0.021); with raw images LLMs 18.9-52.8%, significantly worse than radiologists (p<0.05). Not tested as human-AI teams.
quote: With expert-derived structured features, LLMs achieved high accuracy (86.8-94.3%), with GPT-4o reaching 94.3% (95%CI 84.6-98.1%), matching the expert neuroradiologist (92.5%, 95%CI 82.1-97.0%, p = 1.000) and significantly outperforming the resident (79.2%, p = 0.021).

title: Comparative Performance of ChatGPT-4o, Grok-3, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet in Differentiating Cerebellopontine Angle Schwannomas and Meningiomas: A Pilot Study of Visual Versus Text-Based Diagnostic Prompting
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy compared with neuroradiologists, residents, and machine learning baselines on the same cases
effect: GPT-4o matched expert neuroradiologist with expert features (94.3% vs 92.5%) and beat resident (79.2%); with raw images all LLMs were significantly worse than radiologists (p<0.05).
quote: Performance was moderate with resident-derived structured features (71.7-73.6%), significantly better than raw image input (p < 0.05), but declined markedly with raw images alone (18.9-52.8%), where all LLMs performed significantly worse than radiologists (p < 0.05).

title: Comparative Performance of ChatGPT-4o, Grok-3, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet in Differentiating Cerebellopontine Angle Schwannomas and Meningiomas: A Pilot Study of Visual Versus Text-Based Diagnostic Prompting
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: LLM accuracy under varied input quality (expert vs resident structured features vs raw images)
effect: Accuracy fell from 86.8-94.3% (expert features) to 71.7-73.6% (resident features) to 18.9-52.8% (raw images), showing brittleness to input variation.
quote: Performance degrades moderately with resident-derived features and dramatically with raw image input, highlighting the critical importance of structured prompting for clinical LLM applications.

title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Automated Protocoling of Abdominal and Pelvic CT Scans: The Power of Context
outcome: Optimal protocol selection by LLM versus radiologists' human-selected protocols on the same cases
effect: GPT-4o with prompting only selected optimal protocols more often than humans (96.2% [527/548] vs 88.3% [484/548]; P < .001); inappropriate protocols 1.3% vs 2.4%, P = .21.
quote: GPT-4o with prompting only selected optimal protocols more frequently than humans (96.2% [527 of 548 patients] vs 88.3% [484 of 548 patients]; P < .001), but there was no evidence of a difference in inappropriate protocols (1.3% [seven of 548 patients] vs 2.4% [13 of 548 patients]; P = .21).

title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Automated Protocoling of Abdominal and Pelvic CT Scans: The Power of Context
outcome: Reference standard defined by radiologists and blinded radiologist review of protocol categories
effect: Reference standard protocols were set by radiologists with institutional guidelines; outputs were categorized by blinded radiologists. Effectiveness of the practice itself was not tested.
quote: Model-selected protocols and original human-selected protocols were categorized compared with the reference standard after review by blinded radiologists as follows: exact match, equal alternative, reasonable but inferior, or inappropriate.

title: Performance of a Small Language Model Versus a Large Language Model in Answering Glaucoma Frequently Asked Patient Questions: Development and Usability Study
outcome: Readability grade level of glaucoma answers from SLM and ChatGPT 4.0
effect: Both models' answers were difficult for the average layperson to read and judged unsuitable for health care-related information; readability assessed with 4 formulas.
quote: Both models provided answers considered unsuitable for health care-related information, as they were difficult for the average layperson to read.

title: Performance of a Small Language Model Versus a Large Language Model in Answering Glaucoma Frequently Asked Patient Questions: Development and Usability Study
outcome: Readability grade level of AI-generated patient answers versus lay reading level
effect: Answers from both models were challenging for the average layperson to understand, making them unsuitable for health care-related information.
quote: Both models generated accurate content, but the answers were considered challenging for the average layperson to understand, making them unsuitable for health care-related information.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o and Gemini for gout management: a comparative analysis based on EULAR guidelines
outcome: Readability of LLM responses for gout questions
effect: Both models generated content requiring college-level comprehension.
quote: Readability assessments indicated that both models generated content requiring college-level comprehension.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o and Gemini for gout management: a comparative analysis based on EULAR guidelines
outcome: Alignment of LLM gout answers with EULAR guidelines
effect: ChatGPT-4o fully aligned, complete and accurate for 76.0% of questions vs Gemini 48.0%; 8.0% of Gemini responses entirely contradictory to guidelines, ChatGPT-4o none.
quote: Regarding guideline alignment, ChatGPT-4o provided fully aligned, complete, and accurate responses to 76.0% of the questions, whereas Gemini achieved this in 48.0%.

title: Enhancing ocular sign detection: AI-based strategic segmentation for improved accuracy and privacy protection
outcome: Model performance on internal versus external multi-site test datasets for ocular sign detection
effect: Internal AUCs of 71.09%, 80.81%, 90.07%, and 82.86%; external AUCs ranged 55.58%-84.29% across two test datasets, showing variation across sites.
quote: SegmenView achieved internal Area Under the Curve (AUCs) of 71.09%, 80.81%, 90.07%, and 82.86%; external AUCs ranging 55.58%-84.29% across two test datasets, outperforming half-face and periocular models.

title: Ambient AI Scribes in Clinical Practice: A Randomized Trial
outcome: Local ambient scribe effect on time-in-note, burnout, task load, accuracy, and usability versus control
effect: Nabla reduced time-in-note 9.5% (95% CI -17.2% to -1.8%; P=0.02); DAX no significant change (-1.7%). Both scribes suggested improved Mini-Z, task load, and work exhaustion; occasional inaccuracies reported.
quote: Nabla users experienced a 9.5% (95% CI, -17.2% to -1.8%; P=0.02) decrease in time-in-note versus the control group, whereas DAX users exhibited no significant change versus the control group (-1.7%; 95% CI, -9.4% to +5.9%; P=0.66).

title: Ambient AI Scribes in Clinical Practice: A Randomized Trial
outcome: Clinician-reported clinically significant inaccuracies in ambient scribe notes
effect: Clinically significant inaccuracies noted 'occasionally' on five-point Likert questions (DAX 2.7 [95% CI 2.4 to 3.0]; Nabla 2.8 [95% CI 2.6 to 3.0]).
quote: One grade 1 (mild) adverse event was reported, while clinically significant inaccuracies were noted "occasionally" on five-point Likert questions (DAX 2.7 [95% CI, 2.4 to 3.0]; Nabla 2.8 [95% CI, 2.6 to 3.0]).

title: Ambient AI Scribes in Clinical Practice: A Randomized Trial
outcome: Documentation time and clinician burnout after AI scribe deployment using validated instruments
effect: Improvements in Mini-Z (DAX +2.83; Nabla +2.69), PTL (DAX -39.9), and PFI-WE (DAX -0.32; Nabla -0.23) versus control; Nabla reduced time-in-note 9.5%.
quote: Increases in total Mini-Z (scale 10-50; DAX 2.83 [95% CI, +1.28 to +4.37]; Nabla +2.69 [95% CI, +1.14 to +4.23]) and reductions in PTL (scale 0-400; DAX -39.9 [95% CI, -71.9 to -7.9]; Nabla -31.7 [95% CI, -63.8 to +0.4]), and PFI-WE (scale 0-4; DAX 0.32 [95% CI,-0.55 to -0.08]; Nabla -0.23 [95% CI, -0.46 to +0.01]) scores suggest improvement for users of either scribe versus the control.

title: Large Language Models in Patient Health Communication for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: Pilot Cross-Sectional Comparative Analysis
outcome: LLM answers to ASCVD treatment questions aligned with latest clinical guidelines
effect: None of the models consistently provided responses aligned with latest guidelines for the standard ASCVD treatment regimen; performance weaker for treatment and prevention than definitions and diagnosis.
quote: Specifically, none of the models consistently provided responses aligned with the latest clinical guidelines for the following key guideline-facing question "What is the standard treatment regimen for ASCVD?"

title: Evaluating few-shot prompting for spectrogram-based lung sound classification using a multimodal language model
outcome: Repeatability of GPT-4o lung sound classifications across repeated runs
effect: Cohen's kappa 0.76-0.88 and agreement 89-96% across repeated runs, indicating high consistency.
quote: Model repeatability analysis demonstrated high agreement (κ = 0.76-0.88; agreement: 89-96%), indicating excellent consistency.

title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Successfully Automates Data Extraction From Unstructured Magnetic Resonance Imaging Reports: Feasibility in Prostate Cancer Care
outcome: Output variability of GPT-4.0 across five repeated identical runs, by data element
effect: Response variability ranged from 0.14% to 3.61%, differed by data element (P < .001), and was inversely correlated with accuracy (P < .001).
quote: Response variability over five repeated runs ranged from 0.14% to 3.61%, differed based on the data element extracted (P < .001), and was inversely correlated with accuracy (P < .001).

title: Tumor Board-Inspired Multiagent Artificial Intelligence System for Interpreting Oncology Guidelines
outcome: Accuracy and hallucination of guideline-grounded multiagent system versus general LLMs on guideline questions
effect: Guideline-grounded system 90% accuracy vs GPT-4o 48%, Claude 3.7 49%, Gemini 2.5 50%, DeepSeek-R1 58%, ASCO Assistant 67% (all P<.01); no hallucinated answers observed.
quote: Most errors were due to incorrect guideline selection or misinterpretation; no hallucinated answers were observed.

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Responses to Patient Concerns About Axial Spondyloarthritis: Delphi-Based Evaluation
outcome: Rate of safety disclaimers in LLM responses
effect: Disclaimer rates were GPT-4.0 and DeepSeek-R1 100% and Kimi k1.5 88%; safety generally high, but hallucinations remain a critical barrier.
quote: GPT-4.0 and Kimi k1.5 demonstrated superior overall readability; safety remained generally high (disclaimer rates: GPT-4.0 and DeepSeek-R1 100%; Kimi k1.5 88%).
sample_unit: survey respondents (84 patients with axSpA and 26 rheumatologists); LLM responses to patient-identified concerns evaluated by 2 raters

title: Predicting emergency mortality risk in traumatic brain injury: comparative analysis of machine learning and large language model GPT-5
outcome: Compared LLM prompting strategies against SVM machine learning model on same TBI dataset
effect: SVM achieved best overall performance (AUC = 0.920); after threshold adjustment all LLMs reached comparable AUCs (0.902-0.919).
quote: The SVM model achieved the best overall performance (AUC = 0.920).

title: Predicting emergency mortality risk in traumatic brain injury: comparative analysis of machine learning and large language model GPT-5
outcome: mortality prediction AUC of LLM versus simpler ML model
effect: SVM achieved the best overall performance with AUC 0.920, outperforming all LLM prompting configurations which reached AUCs between 0.902 and 0.919 after threshold adjustment.
quote: The SVM model achieved the best overall performance (AUC = 0.920).

title: An autonomous agentic workflow for clinical detection of cognitive concerns using large language models
outcome: Sensitivity change from balanced refinement dataset to real-world-prevalence validation dataset
effect: Sensitivity decreased from 0.91 to 0.62 between datasets; F1 for expert-driven workflow 0.81 in validation vs 0.87 in refinement, agentic 0.74 vs 0.93, attributed to prevalence shift.
quote: Sensitivity decreased from 0.91 to 0.62 between datasets, demonstrating the impact of prevalence shift on generalizability.

title: An autonomous agentic workflow for clinical detection of cognitive concerns using large language models
outcome: Share of apparent false negatives that were actually correct on expert re-adjudication
effect: Expert re-adjudication found 44% of apparent false negatives reflected clinically appropriate reasoning, indicating the original reference labels understated model accuracy.
quote: Expert re-adjudication revealed 44% of apparent false negatives reflected clinically appropriate reasoning.

title: Comparative analysis of six large language models in perioperative decision support for geriatric patients with multimorbidity: a three-dimensional evaluation framework
outcome: Guideline compliance and completeness of perioperative recommendations, including omissions of protocols
effect: NYAAI omitted temperature management and delirium protocols; general-purpose models showed moderate guideline compliance (ChatGPT 4/5; Gemini 3/5) but produced contextually inappropriate recommendations.
quote: However, it exhibited selective guideline adherence, omitting temperature management and delirium protocols.
sample_unit: simulated clinical case (scored outputs from six LLMs)

title: Comparative analysis of six large language models in perioperative decision support for geriatric patients with multimorbidity: a three-dimensional evaluation framework
outcome: Addressing extreme-event or emergency protocols (aortic rupture management) in perioperative recommendations
effect: Safety redundancy was a universal failure: no model addressed extreme-event protocols such as aortic rupture management.
quote: Safety redundancy emerged as a universal failure—no model addressed extreme-event protocols (aortic rupture management).
sample_unit: simulated clinical case (scored outputs from six LLMs)

title: Readability and quality assessment of AI-powered chatbot responses to overactive bladder patient questions: a comparative study
outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot responses versus recommended 6th-8th grade
effect: Significant differences between chatbots (Gunning Fox p = 0.008, Flesch-Kincaid p < 0.001); all responses required education levels above the recommended 6th-8th grade.
quote: A significant difference was found between chatbots in terms of readability scores (Gunning Fox Index p = 0.008, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level p < 0.001), with all responses requiring education levels above the recommended 6th-8th grade.

title: Readability and quality assessment of AI-powered chatbot responses to overactive bladder patient questions: a comparative study
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility (readability) of chatbot patient education responses
effect: All chatbot responses required education levels above the recommended 6th-8th grade; readability differed across chatbots (FKGL p < 0.001).
quote: AI chatbots show potential for patient education but produce content with readability levels too complex for general audiences.

title: Artificial intelligence for personalized management of vestibular schwannoma: a multidisciplinary clinical implementation study
outcome: Preparation and discussion time in simulated multidisciplinary meetings with versus without AI-assisted reports
effect: AI reports lengthened neuroradiologist preparation (2 min 54 s vs 2 min 36 s per case) but shortened discussion (1 min 15 s vs 1 min 21 s per case, P < .01).
quote: However, the computer-assisted simulated MDTM approach significantly improved (P < .01) MDTM efficiency, with shorter discussion times per patient (1 min 15 s [ ± 0 min and 28 s] per case) compared to standard simulated MDTM (1 min 21 s [ ± 0 min and 44 s] per case).

title: A Large Language Model Assistant for Summarizing Hepatology Referral Documents
outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rate of AI summaries reviewed against source hepatology referral records
effect: AI summaries had high accuracy (median 94.6% [IQR 86.5%-97.3%]) with a low hallucination rate.
quote: AI summaries had high accuracy (median [interquartile range]: 94.6% [86.5%-97.3%]) with a low hallucination rate.

title: A Large Language Model Assistant for Summarizing Hepatology Referral Documents
outcome: Time to triage AI summary files versus original referral files
effect: 60% reduction in triage time; adjusted mean 37.2 seconds for AI files vs 94.2 seconds for original files, P < 0.001.
quote: Use of the AI summaries led to a 60% reduction in triage time (adjusted mean triage time of 37.2 seconds for AI files vs 94.2 seconds for original files, P < 0.001).

title: Assessment of microorganism detection in ThinPrep Papanicolaou tests utilizing the Hologic Genius Digital Diagnostics System
outcome: Microorganisms missed by AI-selected image galleries in Pap tests
effect: Sensitivity was 95.4% overall and 82.5% for HSV. Among 12 missed cases, 3 of 5 Candida and 3 of 7 HSV organisms were not shown in the 60 AI-selected images.
quote: Among the 12 cases with missed diagnoses, 3 of 5 Candida spp and 3 of 7 HSV organisms were not presented within the 60 images selected by HGDDS.

title: Liver cancer segmentator: Metadata-guided confidence scoring for reliable segmentation of colorectal liver metastases in CT
venue: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
outcome: Failure detection by confidence scoring, measured by area under the risk coverage curve
effect: Adding tumor volume and slice thickness to confidence scoring reduced the area under the risk coverage curve from 16.7 to 10.3 and improved failure detection.
quote: Incorporating tumor volume and slice thickness into the confidence scoring process improved failure detection, enhanced reliability, and provided valuable insights for refining clinical deployment of automated segmentation algorithms.
sample_unit: CT examinations (test set; 446 collected in total)

title: Large Language Models' Performances regarding logical observation identifiers names and codes mapping in laboratory medicine: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4.0, Gemini, and Perplexity
outcome: LLM LOINC mapping accuracy against expert consensus reference standard
effect: ChatGPT-4.0 highest complete match in clinical chemistry (58.2%); Perplexity best in hematology (55.0%); Gemini highest mismatch, hematology 80.0%.
quote: ChatGPT-4.0 achieved the highest CM rate in clinical chemistry (58.2%), whereas Perplexity AI performed best in hematology (55.0%).

title: ChatGPT-5 for drug-drug interaction detection in the intensive care unit: A real-world cohort study on large language model advances and implications for clinical pharmacists
venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT pDDI outputs across repeated runs on 50 patients
effect: Reproducibility was limited, with ChatGPT-5 achieving only 68% consistency across repeated runs.
quote: Reproducibility was also limited, with ChatGPT-5 achieving only 68% consistency across repeated runs.

title: ChatGPT-5 for drug-drug interaction detection in the intensive care unit: A real-world cohort study on large language model advances and implications for clinical pharmacists
venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
outcome: ChatGPT pDDI detection versus standard interaction checkers, discrimination and clinical utility
effect: ChatGPT identified fewer interactions than standard databases (8 and 10 vs. 22 total; 1 and 2 vs. 4 significant per patient); none outperformed standard tools in discrimination or clinical utility.
quote: None of the versions outperformed standard tools in discrimination or clinical utility.

title: Dosage adjustments in renal impairment among medical ward patients: ChatGPT® and DeepSeek® models' effectiveness in assessing those adjustments
venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
outcome: AI accuracy in renal dose adjustment assessment versus UpToDate
effect: DeepThink had 81.6% sensitivity, 29% specificity, 67.5% accuracy; ChatGPT 5.0 had 64.3% sensitivity, 54.8% specificity, 61.7% accuracy.
quote: DeepThink® showed the highest sensitivity (81.6 %) but low specificity (29 %) and 67.5 % accuracy.
