title: Artificial intelligence-based software to support mechanical thrombectomy transfer decision in low-volume primary stroke centers: a multicenter, retrospective study
outcome: AI LVO detection sensitivity by occlusion location
effect: Sensitivity for anterior circulation LVO was 83.5% [95% CI 76.5-90.5], significantly higher for M1 than for ICA occlusions (95.2% vs. 63.9%, p < 0.01).
quote: Artificial intelligence-based sensitivity for anterior circulation LVO detection was 83.5% [95% confidence interval (CI) 76.5-90.5], significantly higher for M1 than for internal carotid artery (ICA) occlusions (95.2% vs. 63.9%, p < 0.01).

title: PREDICTING POSTOPERATIVE OUTCOMES IN FULL-THICKNESS MACULAR HOLE REPAIR SURGERY: ChatGPT Versus Clinical Decision
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-5 versus retina specialists in predicting FTMH surgery outcomes on same cases
effect: Anatomical accuracy 72-86% (specialists) vs 90% (ChatGPT-5); functional accuracy 42-44% (specialists) vs 66% (ChatGPT-5), but ChatGPT missed all nonclosure cases and worsened cases (optimism bias).
quote: The anatomical prediction accuracy was 72% to 86% (specialists) and 90% (ChatGPT-5).

title: PREDICTING POSTOPERATIVE OUTCOMES IN FULL-THICKNESS MACULAR HOLE REPAIR SURGERY: ChatGPT Versus Clinical Decision
outcome: Optimism bias and missed adverse outcomes in ChatGPT-5 predictions
effect: ChatGPT-5 failed to identify nonclosure; 0% accuracy for worsened cases, <=13% for stable; mean BCVA error 11.4 ± 10.8 letters, ~60% within two lines.
quote: ChatGPT achieved perfect accuracy in closure cases but failed to identify nonclosure, reflecting optimism bias.

title: Effects of Image Degradation on Deep Neural Network Classification of Scaphoid Fracture Radiographs: Comparison Study of Different Noise Types
outcome: Classifier accuracy under perturbed inputs (blur, noise, JPEG, CLAHE, resizing, screenshots) versus clean images
effect: Accuracy fell from 92.03% clean as perturbation severity increased; Gaussian blur σ=3.0 gave 72.0%, resize_400 71.9%, CLAHE clip 5 77.0%, ImageJ screenshot 78.1%.
quote: However, as the perturbations increased in severity, image features deteriorated further, and model performance declined.
sample_unit: test radiographs (scaphoid crops), each perturbed across 44 degradation datasets

title: Effects of Image Degradation on Deep Neural Network Classification of Scaphoid Fracture Radiographs: Comparison Study of Different Noise Types
outcome: Silent performance loss from degraded or low-resolution input images
effect: Resolution reduction and screenshots cut accuracy (MicroDicom 900×1050 to 550×780: 86.3% to 82.8%; ImageJ 78.1%); no input quality check was tested.
quote: The only difference between the datasets Screenshot_MicroDicom_1 and Screenshot_MicroDicom_2 was the resolution; changing the resolution from 900×1050 to 550×780 pixels resulted in an accuracy reduction from 86.3% to 82.8%.
sample_unit: test radiographs (scaphoid crops), each perturbed across 44 degradation datasets

title: Effects of Image Degradation on Deep Neural Network Classification of Scaphoid Fracture Radiographs: Comparison Study of Different Noise Types
outcome: fracture classification accuracy under image perturbations
effect: Accuracy declined from 0.9203 on clean images to 0.7203 under Gaussian blur (sigma=3.0) and 0.7703 under CLAHE, where recall dropped to 0.5390, while Gaussian blur decreased accuracy by 5% to 12%.
quote: Model accuracy declined with increasing perturbation severity, but the extent varied across perturbation types.
sample_unit: test radiographs (scaphoid crops), each perturbed across 44 degradation datasets

title: Impact of patient communication style on agentic AI-generated clinical advice in E-medicine
outcome: Consistency of LLM triage and advice across equivalent messages varying in emotional tone
effect: Urgent, threatening and demanding framings raised same-day/urgent care from 14% to 37%-63% (V up to 0.69, P<0.001); emotional tone raised empathy responses from 62% to 70%-86%; similar shifts in real messages.
quote: Urgent, threatening, and demanding framings increased same-day or urgent care from 14% to 37%-63% (V up to 0.69, P < 0.001).

title: PEER: Towards reliable and efficient inference via Patience-Based Early Exiting with Rejection
outcome: Accuracy and abstention rate when uncertain samples are rejected for human review versus baseline
effect: On MIMIC-III, PEER reached 90.73% accuracy versus 89.48% baseline by rejecting only 2.79% of uncertain samples.
quote: For instance, on the MIMIC-III dataset, PEER achieves an accuracy of 90.73% (surpassing the baseline of 89.48%) by rejecting only 2.79% of uncertain samples.

title: Identifying facilitators and barriers to implementing the Feverkidstool, a clinical decision tool, in the emergency department: a qualitative study in the Netherlands
outcome: Clinician-perceived barriers to implementing the decision tool, including EHR integration
effect: Lack of integration with electronic health records was mentioned by respondents (n=18) as a barrier to implementation; user-friendliness was a facilitator.
quote: User-friendliness was seen as a facilitator, whereas the need for C reactive protein testing and lack of integration with electronic health records were mentioned as barriers.

title: Leveraging a large language model to support expansion of surveillance activities to include cardiovascular implantable device infections in a large, integrated national healthcare system
outcome: GenAI infection classification accuracy versus manual chart review reference standard
effect: Specificity 100% (50/50 uninfected correct); all 50 infections identified but timing/attribution incorrect in 7 of 50; sensitivity for timing and attribution 82%.
quote: The overall specificity of the GenAI-assisted process was 100% and the sensitivity for accurately classifying timing and attribution of CIED infection events was 82%.

title: Leveraging a large language model to support expansion of surveillance activities to include cardiovascular implantable device infections in a large, integrated national healthcare system
outcome: Errors in GenAI outputs requiring manual adjudication
effect: Timing and attribution to preceding procedure incorrect in 7 of 50 infection cases; authors conclude manual adjudication of output is needed.
quote: Among 50 infection cases, GenAI identified all CIED infections, but the timing of events and the attribution to a preceding procedure were incorrect in 7 of 50 cases.

title: Artificial intelligence implementation in automated heart chambers quantification during pharmacological stress echocardiography
outcome: Effect of echocardiographic image quality on ML measurement performance
effect: Poor-quality images reduced ML diagnostic yield; image quality significantly influenced performance. RA and RV agreement was moderate, worse under stress.
quote: Image quality significantly influenced ML performance, as poor-quality images reduced diagnostic yield.
country: Multiple (five sites in four countries; countries not named in text)

title: Artificial Intelligence in Craniosynostosis Surgery: A Comparison of Large Language Models in Answering Perioperative Care Questions
outcome: SMOG readability grade level of LLM responses to caregiver craniosynostosis questions
effect: SMOG: OpenEvidence 17.54 (graduate level); ChatGPT 14.45, DeepSeek 14.40, Gemini 15.17 (undergraduate level).
quote: By SMOG score, OpenEvidence produced responses at the highest reading level (17.54), indicating a graduate-level comprehension requirement.

title: Development and pilot testing of AYA-RISE, a risk information and screening education intervention for adolescents and young adults with cancer risk syndromes
outcome: Acceptability (AIM score) and distress after using the AYA-RISE chatbot
effect: Acceptability threshold exceeded, with post-test AIM score >4 by 80% of AYAs; no significant change in distress thermometer scores (pre 3.4, post 3.6, p=.34).
quote: Our threshold for acceptability was exceeded, with a post-test Acceptability of Intervention Measure (AIM) score of > 4 by 80% of AYAs.

title: Development and pilot testing of AYA-RISE, a risk information and screening education intervention for adolescents and young adults with cancer risk syndromes
outcome: Feasibility and acceptability of a chatbot developed with AYAs, family members, and clinicians
effect: Co-developed with 17 AYAs plus families and clinicians; in pilot, 100% used the intervention through risk information presentation and 80% had AIM >4.
quote: The intervention was developed together with AYAs with cancer risk syndromes, their family members, and clinicians, using Invitae’s Gia® chatbot (study Phase 1).

title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Improve the Readability of German Online Medical Texts: Evaluation Study
outcome: Readability (WSTF, FRE) of LLM-simplified German patient education texts versus originals and eighth-grade target
effect: Original WSTF 11.24, FRE 35.92. Copilot WSTF 8.99, GPT-3.5 9.96, GPT-4o 10.6 (significant improvement); Le Chat 11.71 (no improvement). No model significantly reached eighth-grade level.
quote: ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-40, and Microsoft Copilot showed a statistically significant improvement in readability. However, the t tests yielded no statistically significant results for the reduction of scores lower than the eighth grade level.

title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Improve the Readability of German Online Medical Texts: Evaluation Study
outcome: Reading level of original German online patient education materials
effect: Original texts averaged WSTF 11.24 (SD 1.29) and FRE 35.92 (SD 7.64), rated difficult to quite difficult, above the recommended eighth-grade level.
quote: Most of the original texts were rated as difficult to quite difficult (average WSTF 11.24, SD 1.29; FRE 35.92, SD 7.64).

title: Less time Coding, more time Caring: Performance evaluation of ChatGPT-5 for ICD-10 coding of radiology reports
outcome: ICD-10 coding concordance and coding time for non-English versus English radiology reports
effect: Non-English reports had significantly lower concordance (first character p=0.002; second/third characters p<0.001; last characters p=0.012) and longer coding times (p=0.002) than English reports.
quote: Coding non-English reports resulted in significantly lower concordance (first character: p = 0.002; second/third characters: p < 0.001; last characters: p = 0.012) and longer coding times than English reports (p = 0.002).
sample_unit: fictitious radiology reports (PARROT) plus 100 fictitious PET/CT reports

title: From Evidence-based Endodontics to Generative AI: A Comparative Study of 11 Large Language Models
outcome: Intra-model consistency of answers across 5 repeated rounds
effect: Consistency exceeded 90% for most models, peaking at 98.3% for top performers but falling to 75.0% for DeepSeek.
quote: Consistency exceeded 90% for most models, peaking at 98.3% for top performers but falling to 75.0% for DeepSeek.
sample_unit: LLM responses (60 multiple-choice questions x 11 models x 5 rounds)

title: Mobility functional status ascertainment in electronic health records using large language models
outcome: Cross-institution generalizability of LLM mobility extraction across three healthcare institutions
effect: Authors report the local deterministic setup demonstrated cross-institution generalizability across three institutions; overall patient-level micro-F1 was 0.876 for Mobility Extraction and 0.897 for Impairment Classification.
quote: A local, deterministic setup improved trustworthiness by ensuring consistent outputs, safeguarding privacy, and demonstrating cross-institution generalizability.

title: Comparative analysis of multimodal large language models GPT-4o and o1 versus clinicians in clinical case challenge questions: Retrospective cross-sectional study
outcome: Consistency of correct answers across 5 repeated runs
effect: GPT-4o and o1 answered correctly 5/5 times in 86.2% and 90.7% of cases, respectively, so a portion of cases varied across runs.
quote: Across 5 trials, GPT-4o and o1 provided the correct answer 5/5 times in 86.2% and 90.7% of the cases, respectively.

title: Characterising liver lesions from free-text computer tomography reports - A real-world multicentre analysis
outcome: Repeatability of LLM outputs across repeated runs, and effect of prompt (simple vs optimised)
effect: Repeatability varied widely from 12.7% (Med-LMop) to 39.0% (GPT-4sp); optimised prompts improved accuracy, e.g. Med-LM lesion-level LI-RADS accuracy 40.8% (sp) vs 61.3% (op).
quote: Repeatability varied widely from 12.7% (Med-LMop) to 39.0% (GPT-4sp).
country: Multi-institutional (five institutions; country not stated in text)

title: Characterising liver lesions from free-text computer tomography reports - A real-world multicentre analysis
outcome: Comparison of GPT-4 vs medically fine-tuned Med-LM on same CT reports against radiologist LI-RADS reference
effect: Med-LMop had the highest performance in all analyses and was statistically superior to other models (all p < 0.001); lesion-level LI-RADS accuracy 40.8%-61.3%.
quote: Med-LMop demonstrated the highest performance in all analyses and was statistically superior to other models (all p < 0.001).
country: Multi-institutional (five institutions; country not stated in text)

title: Characterising liver lesions from free-text computer tomography reports - A real-world multicentre analysis
outcome: report quality versus classification
effect: Lesion-information Likert scores differed significantly between correctly and incorrectly classified lesions (all p ≤ 0.04).
quote: Kappa values were weak to moderate between the two reviewers in different aspects of report quality (0.471-0.766), and Likert scores for lesion information differed significantly between correctly and incorrectly classified lesions (all p ≤ 0.04).
country: Multi-institutional (five institutions; country not stated in text)

title: Patterns of AI Use in Clinical Work by Hospitalists: Survey Study
outcome: Proportion of hospitalists using unsanctioned AI tools in clinical practice without institutional endorsement
effect: 36 of 54 respondents (66.7%; 95% CI 53.4%-77.8%) reported using AI in clinical practice; OpenEvidence used by 28/54 (51.9%), ChatGPT by 4/54 (7.4%), without institutional oversight.
quote: Two-thirds of hospitalists organically adopted AI despite the absence of institutional oversight.

title: Patterns of AI Use in Clinical Work by Hospitalists: Survey Study
outcome: AI adoption by hospitalists in absence of institutional oversight
effect: 66.7% (36/54) of hospitalists used AI in clinical work with no institutional oversight; use spanned differential diagnosis (86.1%) and management options (86.1%).
quote: Two-thirds of hospitalists organically adopted AI despite the absence of institutional oversight.

title: Comparative assessment of AI-generated responses to frequently asked questions by parents on space maintainers in pediatric dentistry
outcome: Readability of chatbot answers to parents' questions, measured by Flesch Reading Ease Score
effect: ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-5 and DeepSeek-V3 had higher readability; Gemini 2.5 Flash and Grok 3 had lower FRES scores. No numeric values reported in the abstract.
quote: In terms of FRES scores, ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-5, and DeepSeek-V3 demonstrated higher readability, whereas Google Gemini 2.5 Flash and Grok 3 obtained lower scores.

title: Analysis of AI-Generated Patient Education Guides for Urological Conditions: A Comparative Study Between ChatGPT and Gemini
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient education guides (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) versus recommended reading level
effect: Guides from both ChatGPT 5.1 and Gemini 3 Pro exceeded the recommended reading level; no statistically significant difference between chatbots on readability, reliability, or similarity.
quote: PEGs generated by both AI chatbots exceeded the recommended reading level, demonstrated limited originality, and showed moderate reliability, highlighting the need for professional oversight.
sample_unit: patient education guides (5 urological conditions x 2 chatbots)

title: Large Language Models Show Comparable Response Performance but Vary in Readability Regarding Patient Questions on Hip Arthroscopy
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, Reading Ease) of LLM answers to patient hip arthroscopy questions
effect: FKGL: ChatGPT 11.0 vs Microsoft 8.6 vs Gemini 6.6 (P=.003); Reading Ease: ChatGPT 36.6 vs Microsoft 57.7 vs Gemini 65.0 (P=.001). ChatGPT worst.
quote: ChatGPT responses were at a significantly worse reading level compared to Gemini and Microsoft outputs (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level mean ± SD: ChatGPT: 11.0 ± 2.2 grade reading level vs Microsoft: 8.6 ± 2.3 vs Gemini: 6.6 ± 2.2, P = .003; Flesch Reading Ease mean ± SD: ChatGPT: 36.6 ± 19.0 vs Microsoft: 57.7 ± 13.3 vs Gemini: 65.0 ± 4.7, P = .001).

title: Large Language Models Show Comparable Response Performance but Vary in Readability Regarding Patient Questions on Hip Arthroscopy
outcome: Reading grade level of LLM patient-facing responses
effect: ChatGPT mean grade level 11.0, Microsoft 8.6, Gemini 6.6 (P=.003); only Gemini approached a typical recommended patient reading level.
quote: ChatGPT responses were at a significantly worse reading level compared to Gemini and Microsoft outputs (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level mean ± SD: ChatGPT: 11.0 ± 2.2 grade reading level vs Microsoft: 8.6 ± 2.3 vs Gemini: 6.6 ± 2.2, P = .003; Flesch Reading Ease mean ± SD: ChatGPT: 36.6 ± 19.0 vs Microsoft: 57.7 ± 13.3 vs Gemini: 65.0 ± 4.7, P = .001).

title: Large Language Models Show Comparable Response Performance but Vary in Readability Regarding Patient Questions on Hip Arthroscopy
outcome: Expert-graded accuracy and incorrect response rate of LLM answers on hip arthroscopy
effect: Mean Likert grades 3.0 (ChatGPT), 2.9 (Microsoft), 2.6 (Gemini), P=.481; overall incorrect response rate among LLMs was 20%.
quote: The overall incorrect response rate among LLMs was 20%.

title: Widely Available Large Language Models Are Not a Reliable Source to Address Medical Treatment Recommendations of Patients After a First-Time Anteroinferior Shoulder Dislocation
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT treatment recommendations across two sessions on identical cases
effect: ChatGPT agreed with itself in 70.0% of cases across 2 sessions. Its inconsistent responses led the authors to judge it not reliable for therapy planning.
quote: The agreement between the ChatGPT responses in the 2 sessions was 70.0%.

title: MedAlign: A Clinician-Generated Dataset for Instruction Following with Electronic Medical Records
venue: Proceedings of the ... AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence. AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Clinician-judged error rates of LLM responses to EHR instructions
effect: High error rates ranging from 35% (GPT-4) to 68% (MPT-7B-Instruct); 8.3% drop in accuracy for GPT-4 moving from 32k to 2k context lengths.
quote: We found high error rates, ranging from 35% (GPT-4) to 68% (MPT-7B-Instruct), and 8.3% drop in accuracy moving from 32k to 2k context lengths for GPT-4.
sample_unit: clinician-generated instructions for EHR data (303 with clinician reference responses; 276 longitudinal EHRs)

title: Machine Learning-Enabled Automated Large Vessel Occlusion Detection Improves Transfer Times at Primary Stroke Centers
outcome: Door-in-door-out time and EVT receipt pre- vs post-AI implementation at primary stroke centers
effect: Multivariable regression: 106-minute reduction in DIDO (95% CI -165 to -48) post-AI; no difference in likelihood of EVT post-transfer (OR 2.13, 95% CI 0.88-5.13). Pre-post design, not randomized.
quote: In multivariable linear regression, patients evaluated with automated LVO detection AI software were associated with a 106-minute (95% CI, -165 to -48 minutes) reduction in DIDO time but no difference in likelihood of EVT post-transfer (odd ratio, 2.13 [95% CI, 0.88-5.13).

title: A comparative study on DeepSeek and ChatGPT for bone and soft tissue tumor clinical practice
outcome: Head-to-head accuracy of two LLMs on bone and soft tissue tumor questions versus expert answers
effect: DeepSeek outperformed ChatGPT in overall accuracy (74.7% vs 55.4%, p < 0.001); single-choice 86.9% vs 64.9%; Pathology & Genetics 72.5% vs 40.0%; Treatment 71.3% vs 51.2%.
quote: DeepSeek outperformed ChatGPT in overall accuracy (74.7% vs 55.4%, p < 0.001), excelling in single-choice questions (86.9% vs 64.9%, p < 0.001) and two key domains: Pathology & Genetics (72.5% vs 40.0%, p = 0.006) and Treatment (71.3% vs 51.2%, p = 0.015).

title: A comparative study on DeepSeek and ChatGPT for bone and soft tissue tumor clinical practice
outcome: LLM clinical knowledge accuracy on sarcoma diagnosis, imaging, pathology, staging, and treatment questions
effect: Overall accuracy 74.7% (DeepSeek) and 55.4% (ChatGPT); both models shared 51 errors, indicating gaps in clinical knowledge.
quote: Cross-model analysis revealed DeepSeek uniquely answered 60 questions correctly where ChatGPT erred, while both models shared 51 errors.

title: Assessing Generative AI Chatbots for Alcohol Misuse Support: A Longitudinal Simulation Study
outcome: Stigmatizing or judgmental language and support of self-efficacy in chatbot responses to alcohol misuse questions
effect: All seven chatbots avoided stigmatizing or judgmental language and supported self-efficacy; empathy was the highest-rated domain (mean 4.6/5).
quote: All avoided stigmatizing or judgmental language and supported self-efficacy.

title: Assessing Generative AI Chatbots for Alcohol Misuse Support: A Longitudinal Simulation Study
outcome: Clinician-rated quality of information and inappropriate or inaccurate guidance in chatbot responses
effect: Quality of information was the lowest-rated domain (mean 2.7/5). Every chatbot had one or more examples of inappropriate, over-stated, or inaccurate guidance.
quote: Across all chatbots, empathy was the highest-rated domain (mean score 4.6/5) while quality of information was the lowest (mean 2.7/5).

title: Evaluation of GPT-4o and Gemini Advanced on the Korean National Dental Licensing Examination: Accuracy, consistency, and question generation
outcome: Consistency of LLM answers across three repeated runs on Korean dental licensing questions
effect: GPT-4o accuracy 81.1% vs Gemini Advanced 76.6% (P=0.013); GPT-4o showed greater consistency across attempts. Consistency difference between models in cross-solving was not significant (P=0.578).
quote: GPT-4o achieved significantly higher average accuracy than Gemini Advanced (81.1 % vs. 76.6 %, P = 0.013) and showed greater consistency across attempts.

title: Diagnostic performance of large language models on the NEJM image challenge: a comparative study with human evaluators and the impact of prompt engineering
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of top LLM versus medical students and attending physician on same questions
effect: o4-mini-high achieved 94% accuracy; human accuracies ranged from 38.5% (three medical students) to 70.5% (attending physician), all significantly lower than the LLM.
quote: The human accuracies in this cohort ranged from 38.5% for three medical students to 70.5% for an attending physician-all significantly lower than OpenAI o4-mini-high.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Ability to Answer Common Parent Questions on Avascular Necrosis in Children
venue: HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses versus prompted sixth-grade reading level
effect: Only 3 of 15 responses (20%) were at or below sixth-grade level; mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 6.94, Gunning Fog 9.22 (seventh grade to early high school).
quote: Yet only 3 ChatGPT responses (20%) were at or below a sixth-grade reading level, as prompted.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Ability to Answer Common Parent Questions on Avascular Necrosis in Children
venue: HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated parent education answers
effect: Providers rated answers satisfactory and 100% agreed reading level was appropriate, but objective scores showed only 20% of responses at or below sixth grade.
quote: A majority of providers agreed that these responses would be sufficient for most parents (56%) and that the information was at the appropriate reading level (100%).

title: Augmenting Braden Scores With Predictive Modeling to Reduce Hospital-Acquired Pressure Injuries: A Clinical Pilot Study
outcome: HAPI events per 1000 census days and injury severity distribution on pilot vs control floors
effect: Significant shift from full-thickness PIs toward deep tissue injuries on pilot floors (OR 0.09; 95% CI 0.01-0.88; P=.03); HAPI census-day odds reduction not significant (OR 0.69; 95% CI 0.34-1.39; P=.38).
quote: A reduction in the odds of census days with HAPI events to those without was also observed but was not significant in the span of the pilot (odds ratio: 0.69; 95% CI, 0.34-1.39; P =.38).

title: Comparing Accuracy and Completeness of Google Search Versus ChatGPT-4 Responses to Questions Patients Have Regarding Common Craniofacial Conditions
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading level of ChatGPT and Google responses to craniofacial patient questions
effect: Cleft palate: Google 9.95 vs ChatGPT 13.22 (P=0.006); craniosynostosis: 14.66 vs 14.73 (P=0.467). ChatGPT responses were at roughly grade 13-15 reading levels.
quote: For cleft palate queries, Google responses had significantly lower reading levels than ChatGPT (9.95 vs 13.22, P  = 0.006).
sample_unit: responses (20 questions, each answered by Google and ChatGPT-4)

title: Multi-Evidence Clinical Reasoning With Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Emergency Triage: Retrospective Evaluation Study
outcome: Triage agreement (QWK) and accuracy with RAG grounding versus prompt-only LLM
effect: MECR-RAG mean QWK 0.902 vs 0.801 baseline; accuracy 0.802 vs 0.542 (both P<.001); overtriage 28.8% to 12.7%.
quote: Across 5 independent runs, MECR‑RAG achieved a mean QWK of 0.902 (SD 0.0021; 95% CI 0.901-0.904), compared with 0.801 (SD 0.004; 95% CI 0.798-0.804) for the baseline model (mean paired difference 0.101, SD 0.0058; 95% CI 0.097-0.106; P <.001).

title: Multi-Evidence Clinical Reasoning With Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Emergency Triage: Retrospective Evaluation Study
outcome: Sensitivity for high-severity patients, LLM versus initial nurse triage and baseline LLM
effect: MECR-RAG sensitivity for R1+R2 124/130 (95.4%) vs nurses 117/130 (90.0%) (P=.02) and baseline LLM 122/130 (93.8%); specificity similar to nurses.
quote: When high-severity outcomes were defined as R1+R2 (n=130) and triage “positive” as categories 1 - 3 versus 4 - 5, MECR‑RAG achieved the highest sensitivity for high-risk courses at 124/130 (95.4%), compared with 117/130 (90.0%) for initial nurse triage and 122/130 (93.8%) for the baseline LLM.

title: Multi-Evidence Clinical Reasoning With Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Emergency Triage: Retrospective Evaluation Study
outcome: Undertriage and overtriage of urgent cases by LLM triage
effect: MECR-RAG undertriage 3/236 (1.3%) vs baseline 4/236 (1.7%); overtriage fell from 68/236 (28.8%) to 30/236 (12.7%) (McNemar P<.001).
quote: Overtriage decreased from 68/236 (28.8%) with the baseline LLM to 30/236 (12.7%) with MECR‑RAG (McNemar P <.001).

title: Multi-Evidence Clinical Reasoning With Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Emergency Triage: Retrospective Evaluation Study
outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs and across LLM backends
effect: Five independent runs gave QWK SD 0.0021 for MECR-RAG; advantage robust to run-to-run variability; single-run gains on Claude 3.7 (0.840 to 0.890) and GPT-4o (0.778 to 0.890).
quote: Similar effect sizes were observed when analyses were repeated using single median‑run prediction sets, indicating that MECR‑RAG’s advantage was robust to run‑to‑run variability.

title: Multi-Evidence Clinical Reasoning With Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Emergency Triage: Retrospective Evaluation Study
outcome: Run-to-run performance variability
effect: Across five runs, MECR‑RAG QWK SD 0.0021 and accuracy SD 0.0082; advantage was robust.
quote: Similar effect sizes were observed when analyses were repeated using single median‑run prediction sets, indicating that MECR‑RAG’s advantage was robust to run‑to‑run variability.

title: External validation and logistic recalibration of POSSUM and P-POSSUM for predicting postoperative morbidity and mortality after elective hepatic resection
outcome: Calibration of POSSUM/P-POSSUM before and after local logistic recalibration
effect: Original models underestimated events; bootstrap-corrected recalibration gave slopes 0.837-0.907 and intercepts 0.16 to -0.34, improving calibration without materially changing AUC.
quote: Our findings support the notion that logistic recalibration can reduce systematic calibration errors without materially changing discrimination [ 13 , 25 ].

title: External validation and logistic recalibration of POSSUM and P-POSSUM for predicting postoperative morbidity and mortality after elective hepatic resection
outcome: Performance of POSSUM/P-POSSUM on local historical data against observed outcomes
effect: Local validation showed fair discrimination (AUC 0.696-0.755) and miscalibration, with observed event rates higher than median predicted risks, supporting local model updating.
quote: These observed rates were higher than the median predicted risks for both endpoints, indicating that the models tended to underestimate the event probability in this population.

title: External validation and logistic recalibration of POSSUM and P-POSSUM for predicting postoperative morbidity and mortality after elective hepatic resection
outcome: Net benefit of recalibrated models versus treat-all and operative severity proxy in decision curve analysis
effect: For any morbidity, no incremental benefit over treat-all or proxy; major morbidity exceeded treat-all in 76.3% of thresholds and proxy in 46.1%; mortality exceeded proxy in 85.2%.
quote: Compared with the operative severity proxy (mean net benefit 0.173), the recalibrated model was higher in 46.1% of the thresholds, suggesting a modest and threshold-dependent incremental advantage (Fig. 4 B).

title: External validation and logistic recalibration of POSSUM and P-POSSUM for predicting postoperative morbidity and mortality after elective hepatic resection
outcome: Performance of established generic risk models applied to a new specialized surgical population
effect: POSSUM/P-POSSUM showed fair discrimination and slopes below 1 in hepatic resection, needing recalibration.
quote: OOB bootstrap calibration showed slopes below 1 for all endpoints (clinically relevant morbidity: α 0.16, β 0.837, Brier 0.172; major morbidity: α − 0.051, β 0.907, Brier 0.215; mortality: α − 0.34, β 0.843, Brier 0.068), supporting the need for local model updating.

title: Linguistic Disparities in Artificial Intelligence-Generated Patient Education for Total Hip Arthroplasty: A Pilot Study of Cross-Language Analysis of Leading Large Language Models
outcome: Clinical reliability scores of LLM THA patient education responses, English vs Spanish
effect: Significant main effect of language (p = 0.014, η2 = 0.151); lower clinical reliability scores for Spanish responses in all 3 LLMs; within-model declines nonsignificant.
quote: A statistically significant main effect of language was found (p = 0.014, η2 = 0.151), indicating significantly lower clinical reliability scores for Spanish responses in all LLMs.
sample_unit: LLM responses (10 questions x 2 languages x 3 LLMs)

title: Subjective and objective impacts of ambulatory AI scribes
venue: The American journal of managed care
outcome: Perceived versus actual documentation time change after AI scribe adoption
effect: 86.5% perceived DocTime reductions, but no overall association between perceived and actual change (OR 0.975; P=.144); actual savings uneven, concentrated in physicians with higher baseline DocTime.
quote: Although the majority of physicians perceived reductions in DocTime (86.5%) following AI scribe adoption, there was no overall association between perceived reductions and actual changes in DocTime (OR, 0.975; P  = .144).

title: Subjective and objective impacts of ambulatory AI scribes
venue: The American journal of managed care
outcome: Whether baseline documentation time modifies DocTime reduction from AI scribe use
effect: Each additional 10% of encounters with scribe use cut DocTime by just over 30 seconds per scheduled hour (P<.001); less-efficient physicians with higher baseline DocTime realized most savings.
quote: This effect was modified by baseline DocTime, with less-efficient physicians realizing the majority of time savings.

title: Reproducing real-world clinical prediction models using the DIVE platform: A comparative validation study across three chronic diseases
outcome: Discrimination and precision of CKD model on temporally later data versus original
effect: CKD AUC 89.2% vs 89.3% and average precision 22.1% vs 22.4% on the extended 2013-2022 temporal validation; no performance drop.
quote: The CKD model achieved largely consistent discrimination (AUC: 89.2% vs. 89.3%) and average precision (22.1% vs. 22.4%) using GA<sup>2</sup>M.
sample_unit: patients (over one million in primary care data)

title: Safety and efficacy of privacy-preserving models to create Lay summaries of brain MRI reports
outcome: Overall error rate in LLM-generated lay summaries of brain MRI reports
effect: Overall error rate in LLM-generated lay summaries was 19.7% (62/315), warranting expert oversight.
quote: Overall error rate in LLM-generated lay summaries was 19.7% (62/315), warranting expert oversight.
sample_unit: brain MRI reports (radiologist evaluation); 30-report subset for non-physician evaluation

title: AI-Generated Antibiotic Therapies for Acute Periprosthetic Joint Infections with Implant Retention in Comparison with an Interdisciplinary Team
outcome: Agreement of AI antibiotic recommendations with interdisciplinary team, and therapy duration
effect: Agreement 0-33% in multidrug-resistant/complex cases; up to 57% (95% CI 0.47-0.67) in monomicrobial cases; AI consistently recommended 12 weeks vs 6 weeks by the team.
quote: Notably, in cases involving multidrug-resistant organisms and more complex clinical scenarios, the AI-generated recommendations were incongruent with those of the IT, with estimated percentage agreement ranging from 0-33%.

title: Automated Tumor and Node Staging from Esophageal Cancer Endoscopic Ultrasound Reports: A Benchmark of Advanced Reasoning Models with Prompt Engineering and Cross-Lingual Evaluation
outcome: LLM T/N staging accuracy versus expert consensus reference standard
effect: T-staging average accuracy DeepSeek-R1 91.4%, Qwen3 88.8%, GPT-4o 84.2%, Grok-3 81.3%; N-staging 84.2%, 68.4%, 65.0%, 51.9%.
quote: The N-staging task proved significantly more challenging than T-staging for all models.
sample_unit: endoscopic ultrasound reports (625 for T-staging, 579 for N-staging)

title: Automated Tumor and Node Staging from Esophageal Cancer Endoscopic Ultrasound Reports: A Benchmark of Advanced Reasoning Models with Prompt Engineering and Cross-Lingual Evaluation
outcome: T-staging accuracy with explicit prompts
effect: With explicit instructions, all models achieved > 90% T-staging accuracy; Chinese T all-model average was 92.8% with prompt versus 79.7% without.
quote: In our study, all models demonstrated high performance levels under ideal conditions with explicit instructions, achieving > 90% accuracy in T-staging tasks and indicating strong baseline capabilities.
sample_unit: endoscopic ultrasound reports (625 for T-staging, 579 for N-staging)

title: Automated Tumor and Node Staging from Esophageal Cancer Endoscopic Ultrasound Reports: A Benchmark of Advanced Reasoning Models with Prompt Engineering and Cross-Lingual Evaluation
outcome: Model accuracy under prompt and language variation (2x2 factorial design)
effect: Without-prompt and language changes caused large accuracy drops for some models, e.g. English without-prompt N-staging Qwen3 36.8% vs DeepSeek-R1 79.8%; with-prompt T-staging all models >91% (Q=4.97, p=0.174) in Chinese.
quote: In the challenging English without-prompt N-staging scenario, DeepSeek-R1 retained an accuracy of 79.8%.
sample_unit: endoscopic ultrasound reports (625 for T-staging, 579 for N-staging)

title: Automated Tumor and Node Staging from Esophageal Cancer Endoscopic Ultrasound Reports: A Benchmark of Advanced Reasoning Models with Prompt Engineering and Cross-Lingual Evaluation
outcome: Clinically consequential cross-stage misclassification errors in N-staging
effect: Grok-3 misclassified 30.3% of N3 cases as N1; Qwen3 classified 91.8% of N0, 89.8% of N1 and 92.7% of N3 as N2 in English without-prompt; DeepSeek-R1 errors mostly adjacent.
quote: Grok-3, for example, misclassified 30.3% of N3 cases as the distant N1 stage under identical conditions ( Supplementary Material , Figures S1–S4 ).
sample_unit: endoscopic ultrasound reports (625 for T-staging, 579 for N-staging)

title: Automated Tumor and Node Staging from Esophageal Cancer Endoscopic Ultrasound Reports: A Benchmark of Advanced Reasoning Models with Prompt Engineering and Cross-Lingual Evaluation
outcome: accuracy across language and prompt scenarios
effect: English without-prompt N-staging: DeepSeek-R1 79.8% vs GPT-4o 60.8%, Grok-3 43.7%, Qwen3 36.8%.
quote: For instance, in the English without-prompt condition, DeepSeek-R1 achieved a significantly higher accuracy of 79.8%, compared to 60.8% for GPT-4o, 43.7% for Grok-3, and 36.8% for Qwen3.
sample_unit: endoscopic ultrasound reports (625 for T-staging, 579 for N-staging)

title: Automated Tumor and Node Staging from Esophageal Cancer Endoscopic Ultrasound Reports: A Benchmark of Advanced Reasoning Models with Prompt Engineering and Cross-Lingual Evaluation
outcome: pairwise candidate model differences
effect: Chinese without-prompt N-staging: DeepSeek-R1 outperformed GPT-4o OR = 4.64, Qwen3 OR = 2.43, Grok-3 OR = 5.86; all p < 0.001.
quote: For instance, in the Chinese without-prompt N-staging condition, DeepSeek-R1′s superiority was substantial against GPT-4o (OR = 4.64, 95% CI [3.20–6.74], p < 0.001), Qwen3 (OR = 2.43, 95% CI [1.52–3.89], p < 0.001), and Grok-3 (OR = 5.86, 95% CI [4.29–8.00], p < 0.001).
sample_unit: endoscopic ultrasound reports (625 for T-staging, 579 for N-staging)

title: Diagnostic Performance of ChatGPT-5 for Detecting Pediatric Pneumothorax on Chest Radiographs: A Multi-Prompt Evaluation
outcome: Diagnostic performance and reproducibility across three prompt formulations
effect: Accuracy 0.77-0.79 and specificity 0.96-0.98 across all prompts with stable reproducibility; no significant differences among prompting strategies.
quote: No significant differences were observed among prompting strategies.

title: Diagnostic Performance of ChatGPT-5 for Detecting Pediatric Pneumothorax on Chest Radiographs: A Multi-Prompt Evaluation
outcome: Sensitivity for pediatric pneumothorax, especially small pneumothoraces
effect: Sensitivity 0.57-0.61 overall; small pneumothoraces ACCP 0.18-0.22 and BTS 0.41-0.46 versus large ACCP 0.75-0.79 and BTS 0.85-0.88.
quote: However, sensitivity was limited (0.57-0.61) and substantially lower for small pneumothoraces (American College of Chest Physicians [ACCP]: 0.18-0.22; British Thoracic Society [BTS]: 0.41-0.46) than for large pneumothoraces (ACCP: 0.75-0.79; BTS: 0.85-0.88).

title: Clinical Validation of a Deep Learning-Based 2D Ultrasound Steatosis Algorithm: Cutoff Transferability, Scanner Generalizability, and Comparison with FibroScan
outcome: AUROC on a new scanner (Philips Affiniti 70) not included in training
effect: On Affiniti 70 images, AUROCs remained high (0.838-0.896), supporting scanner generalizability.
quote: On Affiniti 70 images, AUROCs remained high (0.838-0.896), supporting scanner generalizability.

title: Real-World Integration of an Automated Tool for Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection in an Unselected Cohort of Emergency Department Patients-An External Validation Study
outcome: Local performance of RAPID ICH versus prior studies on consecutive ED NCCTs
effect: Sensitivity 87.3%, specificity 74%, PPV 21.3%, NPV 98.6%; 8 false negatives and 203 false positives among 844 NCCTs. Lower than prior RAPID ICH studies.
quote: RAPID ICH's sensitivity and specificity were lower than in prior studies performed using RAPID ICH, and there was a high number of false-positive RAPID ICH identifications, limiting the generalizability of the assessed version of this DL tool.

title: Real-World Integration of an Automated Tool for Intracranial Hemorrhage Detection in an Unselected Cohort of Emergency Department Patients-An External Validation Study
outcome: Comparison of AI tool with first-year radiology resident on the same CT scans
effect: Resident: 95.2% sensitivity, 90.8% specificity, 45.5% PPV, 99.6% NPV vs RAPID ICH 87.3%, 74%, 21.3%, 98.6%.
quote: RAPID ICH showed 87.3% sensitivity, 74% specificity, 21.3% PPV, and 98.6% NPV, while the first-year radiology resident achieved 95.2% sensitivity, 90.8% specificity, 45.5% PPV, and 99.6% NPV.

title: Evaluating the Accuracy, Usefulness, and Safety of ChatGPT for Caregivers Seeking Information on Congenital Muscular Torticollis
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT responses across two independent sessions (TF-IDF and embedding similarity)
effect: Moderate lexical consistency (mean TF-IDF similarity 0.75) and high semantic stability (mean embedding similarity 0.92) across two sessions.
quote: ChatGPT demonstrated moderate lexical consistency (mean TF-IDF similarity 0.75) and high semantic stability (mean embedding similarity 0.92).
sample_unit: caregiver-centered questions (each answered in two sessions and rated by 10 clinical experts)

title: Evaluating the Accuracy, Usefulness, and Safety of ChatGPT for Caregivers Seeking Information on Congenital Muscular Torticollis
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and safety of ChatGPT responses on congenital muscular torticollis
effect: Mean scores 3.0 accuracy, 3.1 safety, 3.1 overall quality (4-point scale); several responses omitted key cautions, oversimplified, or lacked clinical detail.
quote: However, several responses exhibited deficiencies, particularly due to omission of key cautions, oversimplification, or insufficient clinical detail.
sample_unit: caregiver-centered questions (each answered in two sessions and rated by 10 clinical experts)

title: Visual Large Language Models in Radiology: A Systematic Multimodel Evaluation of Diagnostic Accuracy and Hallucinations
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and hallucination rates of general-purpose VLLMs on radiology images against reference diagnoses
effect: Accuracy ranged 8.1% to 29.2% across models; hallucinations 74.4% overall (51.7-82.8% across models); models described as diagnostically unreliable.
quote: Current VLLMs remain diagnostically unreliable, heavily context-biased, and prone to generating false findings, which limits their clinical suitability.

title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbots in Peritoneal Dialysis Education: A Cross-Sectional Comparative Study of Quality, Readability, and Reliability
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease) of chatbot responses to peritoneal dialysis patient questions
effect: FRES was 32.6 ± 10.5 for Gemini Pro 2.5, 24.2 ± 11.7 for ChatGPT-5, and 16.2 ± 7.5 for LLaMA Maverick 4 (p < 0.001), all in the difficult-to-read range.
quote: Gemini Pro 2.5 achieved higher Flesch Reading Ease (FRES) scores (32.6 ± 10.5) compared with ChatGPT-5 (24.2 ± 11.7) and LLaMA Maverick 4 (16.2 ± 7.5; p < 0.001), as well as higher EQIP scores (75.4% vs. 59.4% and 61.5%, respectively; p < 0.001) and Modified DISCERN scores (4.0 [4.0-4.5] vs. 3.0 [3.0-3.5] and 3.0 [2.5-3.5]; p < 0.001).

title: Large Language Model-Assisted Point-in-Time Interpretation of Advanced Hemodynamics in Liver Transplant Recipients: A Pilot Evaluation of Content Quality and Safety
outcome: Expert-rated content quality and catastrophic risk of ChatGPT interpretations of intraoperative hemodynamic screenshots
effect: Median domain scores 4.6 to 4.8; more than 90% of ratings satisfactory; 86% of catastrophic Risk ratings scored 0, with only three isolated high-risk assessments.
quote: ChatGPT demonstrated consistently high performance across all content-quality domains, with median scores ranging from 4.6 to 4.8 and more than 90% of all ratings classified as satisfactory.
sample_unit: hemodynamic monitor screenshots (frames) from 5 liver transplant recipients, each rated by 5 anesthesiologists

title: Retrospective Validation of Clinical Decision Support Tools for Predicting Effectiveness Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease Patients Treated with Vedolizumab
outcome: Predictive performance of CDSTs on local retrospective data across remission outcomes at weeks 14, 30, 54
effect: UC CDST predicted outcomes at week 54 (CREM 33.3% vs 81.8%, p=0.003; CompREM 33.3% vs 86.4%, p<0.001; CSF-CREM 22.2% vs 77.3%, p=0.001). CD CDST showed no significant differences for any outcome.
quote: For CD patients treated with vedolizumab, the CDST could not predict effectiveness outcomes.
sample_unit: patients treated with vedolizumab (32 CD, 41 UC)

title: [Clinical value of AI-assisted cardiac auscultation in screening for congenital heart disease in neonates]
venue: Zhejiang da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Zhejiang University. Medical sciences
outcome: Consistency of screening performance across four high-volume hospitals
effect: Across four high-volume institutions the AI strategy consistently reduced missed-diagnosis rate and increased sensitivity, NPV and Youden index, with lower specificity, PPV and accuracy.
quote: Across the four high-volume institutions, the intelligent strategy consistently showed a significant reduction in missed-diagnosis rate and increased sensitivity, NPV and Youden index, along with decreased specificity, PPV and diagnostic accuracy, indicating robust and reproducible performance across diverse clinical settings.

title: Exploring the influence of endoscopist characteristics and artificial intelligence on adenoma detection in colonoscopy
outcome: Adenoma detection rate with vs without AI assistance by endoscopist sex, in real workflow
effect: AI improved ADR among male endoscopists (AOR 1.166, 95% CI 1.064 to 1.278; p = 0.001) but had no significant effect for females; male ADR rose to 28.77% vs female without AI 30.05%.
quote: AI assistance improved ADR among male endoscopists (AOR 1.166, 95% CI 1.064 to 1.278; p = 0.001) but had no significant effect for females.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT for 12-lead ECG-based localisation of ventricular ectopic foci prior to catheter ablation
outcome: Accuracy of ChatGPT-4o localising ventricular ectopic foci versus electroanatomical mapping
effect: ChatGPT correctly localised 17/50 cases (34%), Cohen's κ -0.02 (95% CI -0.18 to 0.14); no fascicular or epicardial origins correctly predicted.
quote: ChatGPT correctly localised 17/50 cases (34%), yielding an overall Cohen's κ of -0.02 (95% CI -0.18 to 0.14).

title: Improving medication error classification using a reasoning large language model
outcome: LLM concordance with reference classification established by two independent pharmacists
effect: LLM concordance 96.0% (192/200; 95% CI, 92.3-98.3) with expert classification; 8 disagreements
quote: The LLM achieved a concordance rate of 96.0% (192/200; 95% CI, 92.3-98.3) with expert classification.

title: Physiological foundation modeling for subclinical disease assessment: a prospective pilot
outcome: Spearman correlation with PDFF versus existing foundation models and clinical risk scores
effect: Bioprofile models achieved a Spearman coefficient of 0.65 against PDFF, outperforming existing foundation models (ρ = 0.361) and clinical risk scores (ρ = 0.522-0.542) in retrospective validation.
quote: Bioprofile models achieved a Spearman coefficient of 0.65 against PDFF, outperforming existing foundation models (ρ = 0.361) and clinical risk scores (ρ = 0.522-0.542) in retrospective validation.

title: Large Language Models Triage of Retina Patient Emergency Telephone Calls: A Pilot Study
outcome: Accuracy of LLM chatbot diagnosis and triage/follow-up recommendations for simulated retina emergency calls versus humans
effect: Humans more accurate than chatbots in diagnosis (95% vs 76.7%, P<.01) and follow-up (85% vs 70%, P=.03); ChatGPT and Claude noninferior, Gemini (50%) and Meta (46.7%) worse in follow-up.
quote: Human graders were significantly more accurate than chatbots in diagnosis (95% vs 76.7%, respectively; P < .01) and follow-up recommendations (85% vs 70%, respectively; P = .03).

title: Cross specialty evaluation of large language model responses on intentional replantation
venue: Journal of stomatology, oral and maxillofacial surgery
outcome: Specialist-perceived accuracy and completeness of two LLMs on intentional replantation questions
effect: LLM type had a significant main effect on perceived accuracy and completeness (p < 0.001), with OpenEvidence scoring higher than ChatGPT 4.0 on both.
quote: The LMM analyses demonstrated that LLM type had a significant main effect on both perceived accuracy and completeness (p < 0.001), with OpenEvidence receiving higher scores than ChatGPT 4.0 for both outcomes.

title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Cystoscopic Image Interpretation and Bladder Lesion Classification: Comparative Study
outcome: MM-LLM accuracy on clinician-defined cystoscopy stress-test tasks, including difficult differential diagnosis
effect: OpenAI-o3 satisfaction fell from 84.5% for anatomy to 52.5% for lesion reasoning and 48.2% for final diagnosis; 7-class malignancy accuracy was 62.8%, with performance in difficult differentials modest.
quote: OpenAI-o3 demonstrated strong reasoning, with high satisfaction for anatomy (339/401, 84.5%) and findings (305/401, 76%), but lower satisfaction for lesion reasoning (211/401, 52.5%) and final diagnosis (193/401, 48.2%), indicating increasing difficulty with higher-order synthesis.
sample_unit: cystoscopic images (free-text interpretation task; 113 images in classification task)

title: Diagnostic tests for ovarian cancer in premenopausal women with non-specific symptoms (ROCkeTS): prospective, multicentre, cohort study
outcome: Head-to-head sensitivity and specificity of candidate risk models versus current standard test (RMI1) on same patients
effect: Versus RMI1 at 250 (sensitivity 42.6%, specificity 96.5%), IOTA ADNEX at 10% had sensitivity 89.1% (P<0.001) and specificity 75.1% (P<0.001); other tests also had higher sensitivity and lower specificity.
quote: Compared to Risk of Malignancy Index 1 at 250 threshold-the test currently used in NHS secondary care to triage women to tertiary care-most tests improve sensitivity but reduce specificity.

title: Comparison of AI-generated renal diets by different large language models: a guideline-based evaluation with expert input
outcome: Diet plan energy content and expert accuracy scores compared across Turkish and English prompts
effect: Energy differed significantly across models and languages (Gemini-English 859.11 ± 151.35 kcal vs Copilot-English 1496.03 ± 249.71 kcal; p < 0.001). Expert accuracy median was 0.00 for ChatGPT-Turkish vs 4.00 for Gemini-English.
quote: Significant differences were observed in energy content across models and languages (lowest: Gemini-English: 859.11 ± 151.35 kcal vs. highest: Copilot-English:1496.03 ± 249.71 kcal; p < 0.001).

title: Comparison of AI-generated renal diets by different large language models: a guideline-based evaluation with expert input
outcome: Adherence of LLM-generated renal diets to TUBER 2022 and KDOQI guideline nutrient targets
effect: All models' energy fell below reference targets, some potassium outputs exceeded safe limits, and none of the models fully met the guideline requirements.
quote: None of the models fully met the guideline requirements.

title: Comparison of AI-generated renal diets by different large language models: a guideline-based evaluation with expert input
outcome: Suitability of standalone LLM dietary planning for kidney disease patients
effect: LLM diets were inconsistent in nutrient accuracy, guideline adherence, and personalization; authors conclude standalone clinical use is inappropriate and expert supervision is required.
quote: Their standalone use in clinical practice is therefore not appropriate; expert supervision and integration with clinical guidelines are required.

title: Evaluating the efficacy of large language models in cardio-oncology patient education: a comparative analysis of accuracy, readability, and prompt engineering strategies
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of LLM cardio-oncology patient education responses
effect: 63.3% correct, 35.0% partially correct, 1.7% incorrect across 240 responses; no significant accuracy difference between models (p=0.26).
quote: The distribution of accuracy ratings for the combined question set across all three models is as follows: 63.3% ( n = 152, 95% CI: 57.2–69.4%) of responses were rated as “correct,” 35.0% ( n = 84, 95% CI: 29.0–41.0%) as “partially correct,” and 1.7% ( n = 4, 95% CI: 0–3.3%) as “incorrect” ( Figure 1 ).

title: Evaluating the efficacy of large language models in cardio-oncology patient education: a comparative analysis of accuracy, readability, and prompt engineering strategies
outcome: Readability age of LLM patient education responses
effect: Average readability age of 13.3 ± 1.2 years, difficulty score 13.2 ± 1.2, sentence length 51.5 ± 12.5 words across three models without simplification prompt.
quote: For readability and complexity, the three models achieved an average readability age of 13.3 ± 1.2 years, a difficulty score of 13.2 ± 1.2, a total word count of 285.6 ± 128.5, and a sentence length of 51.5 ± 12.5 words.

title: Evaluating the efficacy of large language models in cardio-oncology patient education: a comparative analysis of accuracy, readability, and prompt engineering strategies
outcome: Response quality change when prompt asks for simple language versus no prompt
effect: Simplification prompt lowered accuracy (Kimi 70.0% vs 48.8%, p<0.01; DouBao 57.5% vs 7.5%, p<0.01; GPT-4 62.5% vs 51.2%, p=0.15) and comprehensiveness, helpfulness, practicality (p<0.01 all).
quote: In accuracy, GPT-4 exhibited the smallest decline (62.5% vs. 51.2%, p = 0.15), while Kimi (70.0% vs. 48.8%, p < 0.01) and DouBao (57.5% vs. 7.5%, p < 0.01) showed significant reductions.

title: Evaluating the efficacy of large language models in cardio-oncology patient education: a comparative analysis of accuracy, readability, and prompt engineering strategies
outcome: prompt sensitivity of accuracy
effect: Accuracy declined after prompt: GPT-4 62.5% to 51.2% (p=0.15), Kimi 70.0% to 48.8% (p<0.01), DouBao 57.5% to 7.5% (p<0.01).
quote: In accuracy, GPT-4 exhibited the smallest decline (62.5% vs. 51.2%, p = 0.15), while Kimi (70.0% vs. 48.8%, p < 0.01) and DouBao (57.5% vs. 7.5%, p < 0.01) showed significant reductions.

title: Evaluating the efficacy of large language models in cardio-oncology patient education: a comparative analysis of accuracy, readability, and prompt engineering strategies
outcome: plain-language prompt tradeoff
effect: DouBao readability age decreased from 12.9 ± 0.8 to 10.1 ± 1.2 years (p<0.01), but accuracy decreased 57.5% to 7.5% (p<0.01).
quote: While simplifying language improves readability, it risks compromising clinical relevance.

title: Evaluating the efficacy of large language models in cardio-oncology patient education: a comparative analysis of accuracy, readability, and prompt engineering strategies
outcome: accuracy of LLM responses after language-simplification prompt
effect: Accuracy dropped significantly with prompt engineering for Kimi (70.0% vs 48.8%, p<0.01) and DouBao (57.5% vs 7.5%, p<0.01), with non-significant decline for GPT-4 (62.5% vs 51.2%, p=0.15).
quote: In accuracy, GPT-4 exhibited the smallest decline (62.5% vs. 51.2%, p = 0.15), while Kimi (70.0% vs. 48.8%, p < 0.01) and DouBao (57.5% vs. 7.5%, p < 0.01) showed significant reductions.

title: Prospective Diagnostic Accuracy and Technical Feasibility of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Rib Fracture Detection on Chest Radiographs: Observational Study
outcome: Prospective performance of passive (silent) AI on live ED chest radiographs versus radiologist reports
effect: Passive deployment on 23,251 radiographs: sensitivity 74.5%, specificity 93.3%, PPV 24.2%, NPV 99.2%; 14-day GPU outage exposed infrastructure fragility; median inference 10.6 s vs 3.3 h.
quote: AI operated passively, without influencing clinical decision-making.

title: Prospective Diagnostic Accuracy and Technical Feasibility of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Rib Fracture Detection on Chest Radiographs: Observational Study
outcome: Error rates of AI rib fracture detection relevant to stand-alone diagnostic use
effect: Sensitivity 74.5%, PPV 24.2%; false-positive and false-negative rates indicate AI should be a supportive screening tool, not stand-alone diagnostic.
quote: Although the system showed high negative predictive value, the observed false-positive and false-negative rates indicate that it should be considered a supportive screening tool rather than a stand-alone diagnostic solution or a replacement for clinical judgment.

title: Ontology-grounded knowledge graphs for mitigating hallucinations in large language models for clinical question answering
outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rate of clinical QA with vs without ontology/knowledge-graph grounding
effect: GraphRAG achieved 98% accuracy (59/60) vs ChatGPT-4 37% and DeepSeek-R1 52%; hallucination rate fell from ~63% and ~48% to 1.7%.
quote: While ChatGPT-4 achieved 37% accuracy and DeepSeek-R1 achieved 52%, the ontology-grounded approach achieved 98% accuracy (59/60 questions).

title: Can ChatGPT compete with emergency medicine specialists? A two-stage assessment of ECG interpretation supported by clinical information
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of customized GPT on real ED ECGs versus emergency specialists
effect: ECG Reader-GPT achieved 24% accuracy (27% with clinical information) versus 77% (79%) for emergency medicine specialists.
quote: In Stage 1, specialists correctly interpreted 77% of ECGs, whereas ECG Reader-GPT achieved 24%.

title: Can ChatGPT compete with emergency medicine specialists? A two-stage assessment of ECG interpretation supported by clinical information
outcome: AI ECG interpretation compared against emergency medicine specialists on same ECGs
effect: Specialists outperformed ECG Reader-GPT in all diagnostic subgroups and both stages (77% vs 24%; 79% vs 27%), so the AI would not have been selected over clinicians.
quote: EMSs consistently outperformed ECG Reader-GPT under all conditions, indicating that the model is currently insufficient for real-world ECG interpretation.

title: Real-world evaluation of an automated EEG spike detection software in a tertiary centre compared to a clinical reference standard
outcome: Local accuracy of IED detection software versus clinical reference standard at default setting
effect: Sensitivity 81.1% (95% CI 77.6-84.6), specificity 59.9%, PPV 19.9%, NPV 96.3%; high NPV but low PPV with potential over-calling of IEDs.
quote: At P15's default sensitivity setting, sensitivity for IED detection was 81.1% (95% CI:77.6-84.6), specificity 59.9% (95% CI: 55.5-64.2), positive predictive value 19.9% (95% CI:16.3-23.5) and negative predictive value 96.3% (95% CI:94.6-98.0).

title: Real-world evaluation of an automated EEG spike detection software in a tertiary centre compared to a clinical reference standard
outcome: Predictive values at local prevalence of IEDs in routine EEGs
effect: With 53 of 484 records IED-positive, PPV was 19.9% and NPV 96.3%, showing utility differs from pre-selected IED-rich datasets.
quote: Previous evaluations of machine learning models have reported non-inferiority compared to human experts, but these studies predominantly use small datasets of pre-selected, 'IED rich' records, which are not representative of clinical practice.

title: AI-driven analysis of patient safety reports using large language models: an exploratory multiple methods study
outcome: Expert reviewer agreement with LLM problem extraction and taxonomy category labels on sampled reports
effect: 94% mean reviewer agreement on problem identification; 91.5% agreement on parent category labels and 83.3% on child category labels.
quote: The LLM had scores of 94% mean agreement among reviewers in identifying problems, and 91.5% and 83.3% agreement in assigning 'parent' and 'child' category labels, respectively.

title: Performance of an adult-trained AI tool for intracranial hemorrhage detection on head CT in children aged 6-17 years
outcome: Performance of adult-trained ICH AI tool applied to pediatric patients aged 6-17
effect: Sensitivity 94.2% (162/172), specificity 94.7%, accuracy 94.6%, PPV 62.5%, NPV 99.4%; performance comparable to adult performance, though false positives were common.
quote: An adult-trained AI tool demonstrated high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy for ICH detection in pediatric patients aged 6-17 years, comparable to its adult performance.

title: Performance of an adult-trained AI tool for intracranial hemorrhage detection on head CT in children aged 6-17 years
outcome: Generalization of adult-trained AI performance to a different (pediatric) population
effect: Sensitivity 94.2% (95% CI 89.6-97.2%), specificity 94.7% (93.6-95.7%), comparable to adult performance across 21 sites.
quote: An adult-trained AI tool demonstrated high sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy for ICH detection in pediatric patients aged 6-17 years, comparable to its adult performance.

title: Performance of an adult-trained AI tool for intracranial hemorrhage detection on head CT in children aged 6-17 years
outcome: Multi-site performance validation of AI for ICH detection
effect: Pooled analysis across 21 sites gave sensitivity 94.2% and specificity 94.7%; results were not reported separately by site or device.
quote: This retrospective, multi-institution study analyzed consecutive pediatric NCHCTs performed between January 2017 and November 2022 across 21 sites.

title: Performance of an adult-trained AI tool for intracranial hemorrhage detection on head CT in children aged 6-17 years
outcome: Performance when extending an adult-trained model to a new pediatric population
effect: Sensitivity 94.2%, specificity 94.7%, NPV 99.4%, but PPV only 62.5%; false positives from streak artifact (21.6%) and misclassified anatomy (18.6%).
quote: AI correctly identified ICH in cases missed by radiologists, but false positives were common, most often due to streak artifact (21.6%) and misclassified anatomy (18.6%).

title: Triple cardiovascular disease detection with an artificial intelligence-enabled stethoscope (TRICORDER) in the UK: a cluster-randomised controlled implementation trial
outcome: Incidence of newly coded heart failure diagnosis, AI stethoscope vs routine care, cluster RCT
effect: ITT analysis found no significant difference in heart failure detection (IRR 0·94 [95% CI 0·86-1·02]); no difference in community or hospital diagnoses (p>0·05). Per-use analysis showed higher detection.
quote: Intention-to-treat analysis found heart failure detection did not differ between groups (IRR 0·94 [95% CI 0·86-1·02]); with no difference in community-based or hospital-based diagnoses (p>0·05).

title: Interval cancer, sensitivity, and specificity comparing AI-supported mammography screening with standard double reading without AI in the MASAI study: a randomised, controlled, non-inferiority, single-blinded, population-based, screening-accuracy trial
outcome: Interval cancer rate versus standard screening
effect: Interval cancer rates were 1·55 versus 1·76 per 1000 participants; proportion ratio 0·88 (95% CI 0·65-1·18; p=0·41), meeting the 20% non-inferiority margin.
quote: Interval cancer rates were 1·55 (95% CI 1·23-1·92) and 1·76 (1·42-2·15) per 1000 participants in the intervention and control group respectively, a non-inferior proportion ratio of 0·88 (95% CI 0·65-1·18; p=0·41).

title: Interval cancer, sensitivity, and specificity comparing AI-supported mammography screening with standard double reading without AI in the MASAI study: a randomised, controlled, non-inferiority, single-blinded, population-based, screening-accuracy trial
outcome: Screening sensitivity with AI-supported radiologist reading versus standard double reading
effect: Sensitivity was 80·5% [95% CI 76·4-84·2] with AI versus 73·8% [68·9-78·3] without AI (p=0·031), consistent across age and breast density.
quote: Sensitivity was higher in the intervention group (80·5% [95% CI 76·4-84·2]) than the control group (73·8% [68·9-78·3]; p=0·031), an effect consistent across age and breast density, and for invasive cancer but not for in-situ cancer.

title: Interval cancer, sensitivity, and specificity comparing AI-supported mammography screening with standard double reading without AI in the MASAI study: a randomised, controlled, non-inferiority, single-blinded, population-based, screening-accuracy trial
outcome: screening sensitivity
effect: Sensitivity was higher in the intervention group (80.5%) than the control group (73.8%).
quote: Sensitivity was higher in the intervention group (80·5% [95% CI 76·4-84·2]) than the control group (73·8% [68·9-78·3]; p=0·031), an effect consistent across age and breast density, and for invasive cancer but not for in-situ cancer.

title: Effect of ChatGPT-Assisted Reflective Reasoning on Guideline-Concordant Procedural Decision-Making Among Early-Career Interventional Radiologists
outcome: Guideline-concordant decisions by radiologists with vs without ChatGPT assistance
effect: Mean detailed compliance score rose from 1.697 to 1.900; minimal compliance from 90.89% to 98.70%; 30 scenario-level corrections (McNemar χ² = 27.03; p < 0.0001).
quote: ChatGPT-assisted reflective reasoning significantly improved guideline-concordant decision-making.
sample_unit: simulated clinical scenarios (each completed twice by 3 early-career radiologists)

title: [Development and validation of PhenoRAG: A visualization tool for automated human phenotype ontology term annotation based on large language models and retrieval-augmented generation technology]
venue: Zhonghua yi xue yi chuan xue za zhi = Zhonghua yixue yichuanxue zazhi = Chinese journal of medical genetics
outcome: Hallucinated or invalid HPO terms in RAG-grounded LLM output, checked against official database
effect: 2,064 of 2,150 terms (96.0%) fully validated; hallucination rate 1.3%; HPO ID-name mismatch rate 2.7%. With GPT-5, no hallucinations on the new dataset.
quote: Across the 112 cases, a total of 2 150 HPO terms were generated; 2,064 (96.0%) were fully validated by the official database, with a hallucination rate of 1.3% and an HPO ID-name mismatch rate of 2.7%.

title: Generative pre-trained transformer reinforces historical gender bias in diagnosing women's cardiovascular symptoms
outcome: Change in GPT-4o differential diagnosis accuracy when patient gender was swapped in real notes
effect: Significant diagnostic accuracy differences in 11 of 50 cases (22%); female patients scored lower for coronary artery disease (P<0.01), abdominal aortic aneurysm (P<1.0×10^-9), atrial fibrillation (P<0.01).
quote: Diagnostic accuracy across genders was determined by comparing model outputs to actual discharge diagnoses via FDR-corrected Mann-Whitney U tests, revealing significant diagnostic accuracy differences in 11 cases (22%).
sample_unit: de-identified cardiovascular patient notes (gender-swapped; 10,000 prompts) plus 15,000 simulated cases per model

title: Generative pre-trained transformer reinforces historical gender bias in diagnosing women's cardiovascular symptoms
outcome: Gender representation in LLM-generated simulated cardiovascular cases versus US prevalence
effect: Significant deviation from prevalence (P<0.0001); in 14 of 15 GPT-4-generated conditions (93%), males were overrepresented by a mean of 30% (SD 8.6%).
quote: In 14 GPT-4-generated conditions (93%), male patients were overrepresented compared to females by a mean of 30% (SD 8.6%).
sample_unit: de-identified cardiovascular patient notes (gender-swapped; 10,000 prompts) plus 15,000 simulated cases per model

title: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial of Ambient Artificial Intelligence to Improve Health Practitioner Well-Being
outcome: Ambient scribe effects on well-being, note time, documentation quality, and billing codes in local randomized trial
effect: Work exhaustion/interpersonal disengagement -0.44 points (95% CI -0.62 to -0.25); time on notes -0.36 hours/day; PDSQI-9 mean scores 3.97 to 4.99 of 5; diagnostic billing codes improved (P<0.001).
quote: Documentation time decreased without compromising diagnosis, billing compliance, or note quality.

title: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial of Ambient Artificial Intelligence to Improve Health Practitioner Well-Being
outcome: Coding accuracy/intensity, documentation time, and burnout measured after AI scribe deployment
effect: Burnout measure (Stanford PFI) work exhaustion fell 0.44 points; note time fell 0.36 h/day; diagnostic billing codes improved (P<0.001); professional fulfillment +0.14 (P=0.04) nonsignificant.
quote: Diagnostic billing codes improved with ambient AI use (P<0.001).

title: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial of Ambient Artificial Intelligence to Improve Health Practitioner Well-Being
outcome: Detection of drift in ambient AI software performance during deployment
effect: No drift in software performance was detected during the 24-week trial.
quote: No drift in software performance was detected.

title: Discovery of an Artificial Intelligence Label Feedback Loop: How the Success of a Clinically Implemented Artificial Intelligence Algorithm Has Created an Unforeseen Challenge to Algorithm Retraining
outcome: Model concordance on AI-influenced vs human-only reference labels
effect: V2 had 10% lower concordance than V1 on AI-influenced production hold-out set, similar on pre-AI set, but outperformed V1 on human-only or human-corrected labels, especially for less-common stone types.
quote: These findings revealed an AI label feedback loop, confounding retraining and evaluation.

title: Artificial intelligence agent for delirium screening among patients in oncology and cardiac intensive care units: a proof-of-concept study
outcome: Accuracy of conclusions and care recommendations, grounded agent versus ungrounded LLM baselines
effect: Agent using guideline knowledge graph with retrieval-augmented generation achieved 90% overall accuracy in conclusions and care recommendations, compared with 45% for other LLM baselines (20 cases).
quote: The agent achieved 100% accuracy in selecting appropriate tools and 90% overall accuracy in generating conclusions and care recommendations, compared with 45% for other large language model baselines.

title: Benchmark evaluation of deepseek AI models in antibacterial clinical decision-making for infectious diseases
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Concordance and performance of DeepSeek and ChatGPT o1 antibacterial regimens versus ID specialists' effective regimens
effect: DeepSeek-V3 had the highest concordance with ID specialists, exceeding DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT o1. DeepSeek-R1, R1+WS, and ChatGPT o1 escalated to higher AWaRe tiers significantly more than ID specialists (P<0.005). DeepSeek was comparable to ChatGPT o1.
quote: Moreover, DeepSeek's antibacterial clinical decision-making is comparable to that of ChatGPT o1, with DeepSeek-V3 surpassing it in certain performance metrics.

title: Benchmark evaluation of deepseek AI models in antibacterial clinical decision-making for infectious diseases
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Independent pharmacist review of AI antibacterial outputs against specialist regimens
effect: Five independent clinical pharmacists evaluated all outputs; DeepSeek-V3 had the highest overall ID specialists' endorsed rate, while R1 variants and ChatGPT o1 escalated to broader-spectrum tiers more than specialists.
quote: Then, Five independent clinical pharmacists evaluated all outputs.

title: A comparative study of ChatGPT 4o and DeepSeek in addressing CIED infection-related questions: Accuracy and readability assessment
outcome: Comprehensive answer rate with vs without guideline-based prompts for CIED infection questions
effect: ChatGPT 4o comprehensive answers rose from 80.00% (24/30) to 93.33% (28/30); DeepSeek from 80.00% (24/30) to 90.00% (27/30) with guideline prompts.
quote: With guideline prompts, ChatGPT 4o's comprehensive answer rate increased to 93.33% (28/30), while DeepSeek's rate rose to 90.00% (27/30).

title: A comparative study of ChatGPT 4o and DeepSeek in addressing CIED infection-related questions: Accuracy and readability assessment
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade) of LLM responses about CIED infections
effect: ChatGPT 4o Flesch-Kincaid Grade 15.40 ± 1.18 vs DeepSeek 13.91 ± 1.42 (P <.01), indicating complex responses.
quote: The Flesch-Kincaid Grade Score for ChatGPT 4o (15.40 ± 1.18) was higher than that of DeepSeek's (13.91 ± 1.42), indicating more complex responses (P <.01).

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-5.0 in developmental dysplasia of the hip: A scenario-based validation study against AAOS and AAP guidelines
outcome: Guideline-concordant recommendations when radiology inputs were deliberately erroneous or discordant with the exam
effect: Guided ChatGPT 30% strict accuracy (3/10) in mismatch cases; non-logged-in 60% (6/10). Error-aware prompts did not change recommendations.
quote: Even after being explicitly cautioned about possible examiner or measurement error, ChatGPT continued to recommend the same treatment strategies, failing to redirect toward repeat imaging or urgent consultation.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-5.0 in developmental dysplasia of the hip: A scenario-based validation study against AAOS and AAP guidelines
outcome: Recognition of discordant findings and deferral via repeat imaging or urgent pediatric orthopedic referral
effect: In mismatch scenarios ChatGPT frequently overtreated and failed to recommend repeat ultrasound or urgent referral, even when prompted with error-aware adjustments.
quote: The guided model achieved only 30% strict accuracy in these cases, often suggesting overtreatment such as early surgical intervention, while failing to recommend repeat ultrasound, second-reader confirmation, or urgent referral to a pediatric orthopedist.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-5.0 in developmental dysplasia of the hip: A scenario-based validation study against AAOS and AAP guidelines
outcome: Concordance of LLM management recommendations with AAOS 2022 and AAP 2016 guidelines
effect: Concordant scenarios: guided 20/20 (100%) correct, non-logged-in 19/20 (95%). Mismatch scenarios: guided 3/10 correct, non-logged-in 6/10 correct.
quote: Guided ChatGPT: Achieved 100% accuracy.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-5.0 in developmental dysplasia of the hip: A scenario-based validation study against AAOS and AAP guidelines
outcome: Accuracy of LLM outputs against guideline reference standard, guided vs non-logged-in
effect: Concordant cases 100% (guided) vs 95% (non-logged-in); mismatch cases 30% vs 60% strict accuracy, 50% vs 80% including partially correct.
quote: Non-logged-in ChatGPT: Performed relatively better in this subgroup, with 60% strict accuracy (6/10 correct) and 80% if partially correct were included.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-5.0 in developmental dysplasia of the hip: A scenario-based validation study against AAOS and AAP guidelines
outcome: Need for human oversight given LLM errors in ambiguous cases
effect: ChatGPT overtreated or gave inappropriate recommendations without prompting for repeat imaging in mismatch cases; authors conclude human oversight is essential.
quote: This suggests that in real-world clinical environments, where measurement variability is frequent, ChatGPT should not be used without human oversight.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-5.0 in developmental dysplasia of the hip: A scenario-based validation study against AAOS and AAP guidelines
outcome: erroneous radiology input handling
effect: Guided model proposed overtreatment in discordance cases at 6, 10, and 12 months despite error-aware adjustments.
quote: The model frequently proposed overtreatment in cases of discordance (6, 10, and 12 months), despite being prompted with error-aware adjustments.

title: A Novel Multimodal Implementation of a Foundation Artificial Intelligence Model Using Optic Nerve Head Fundus Photographs and OCT Imaging for Glaucoma Detection
outcome: Glaucoma detection AUC stratified by race, age, and disease severity
effect: No significant differences by race or age in unimodal or multimodal models. All models performed better for moderate-to-severe than mild glaucoma, significant for CFP (P=0.002) and OCT (P=0.005) unimodal models.
quote: No significant differences based on race or age were found in either unimodal or multimodal glaucoma detection models.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Interventions in Pulmonology: What Factors Influence Patient Participation in This Type of Study?
outcome: Patient characteristics associated with refusing an AI virtual assistant telemonitoring program

quote: Refusal was significantly associated with lower sociocultural level, fewer electronic devices, higher anxiety and depression scores (HADS-A, HADS-D), and lower adherence to inhaled therapy (TAI).

outcome: model comparison across simplification metrics

title: A comparative evaluation of large language models for simplifying prostate cancer pathology reports: ChatGPT and Gemini
outcome: patient and clinician understandability

outcome: reading grade level variation across sites
