quote: Mean Reading Grade Level scores varied between internal and external datasets, with GPT-4o Few-Shot performing best overall.

title: A comparative evaluation of large language models for simplifying prostate cancer pathology reports: ChatGPT and Gemini
outcome: patient and clinician understandability
effect: Patient and clinician understandability ratings were consistently high across models
quote: Patient and clinician understandability ratings were consistently high across models.

title: Vulnerability of Large Language Models to Prompt Injection When Providing Medical Advice
outcome: Prompt-injection attack success at primary decision turn across commercial LLMs in simulated medical advice dialogues
effect: Attacks achieved 94.4% (102 of 108) success at turn 4 and persisted in 69.4% (75 of 108) of follow-ups; LLM 1 and LLM 2 100% susceptible, LLM 3 83.3%.
quote: Across 216 evaluations (108 injection vs 108 control), attacks achieved 94.4% (102 of 108 evaluations) success at turn 4 and persisted in 69.4% (75 of 108 evaluations) of follow-ups.

title: Vulnerability of Large Language Models to Prompt Injection When Providing Medical Advice
outcome: Vulnerability of LLMs to adversarial injected inputs causing unsafe clinical recommendations, including flagship models
effect: Extremely high-harm scenarios (FDA Category X pregnancy drugs) succeeded in 91.7% (33 of 36); flagship models 100% (LLM 4, LLM 5) and 80.0% (LLM 6) vulnerable.
quote: The proof-of-concept experiment demonstrated 100% vulnerability for LLM 4 and LLM 5 (5 of 5 dialogues each) and 80.0% (4 of 5 dialogues) for LLM 6.

title: Vulnerability of Large Language Models to Prompt Injection When Providing Medical Advice
outcome: Undiscovered vulnerabilities to prompt injection and manipulation in commercial LLMs giving medical advice
effect: Injection succeeded in 94.4% of evaluations at turn 4; even flagship models showed high susceptibility (80-100%).
quote: In this quality improvement study using a controlled simulation, commercial LLMs demonstrated substantial vulnerability to prompt-injection attacks that could generate clinically dangerous recommendations; even flagship models with advanced safety mechanisms showed high susceptibility.

title: Diagnostic Codes in AI Prediction Models and Label Leakage of Same-Admission Clinical Outcomes
outcome: Inflated mortality prediction performance from ICD code label leakage; prevalence in literature
effect: ICD-only models reached AUROC 0.971-0.976 for in-hospital mortality; 37 of 92 (40.2%) MIMIC same-admission studies used ICD codes as features.
quote: The literature review found that 37 of 92 studies (40.2%) using MIMIC to predict same-admission outcomes included ICD codes as features, even though both MIMIC publications and documentation clearly state that ICD codes are derived after discharge.

title: Behavioral Dynamics of AI Trust and Health Care Delays Among Adults: Integrated Cross-Sectional Survey and Agent-Based Modeling Study
outcome: Association of AI trust and usage frequency with delayed or cancelled care-seeking
effect: Higher AI trust associated with delay (adjusted OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.00-1.18); usage frequency OR 1.39; 11.6% (285/2460) deferred or cancelled care due to AI advice.
quote: In the fully adjusted model (model 4), AI trust remained a significant predictor (OR 1.09, 95% CI 1.00-1.18; P =.04; Figure 2 B).

title: Behavioral Dynamics of AI Trust and Health Care Delays Among Adults: Integrated Cross-Sectional Survey and Agent-Based Modeling Study
outcome: Over-trust in AI advice leading to delayed care, with false reassurance
effect: Predicted delay probability rose from 11.6% at baseline to 30.5% with high trust and high frequency, and 35.8% adding chronic illness.
quote: Combining high trust and high frequency led to a delay probability of 30.5%, and when all 3 factors—high trust, high frequency, and chronic illness—were present, the probability escalated to 35.8%.

title: Performance of large language models in preoperative and postoperative counselling for aesthetic facial procedures
venue: The British journal of oral & maxillofacial surgery
outcome: Proportion of fabricated or non-verifiable citations in LLM counselling responses
effect: GPT-4 produced the most hallucinated citations (36%) compared with Gemini (14%) and DeepSeek (8.8%) (p < 0.00001).

title: Performance of large language models in preoperative and postoperative counselling for aesthetic facial procedures

title: Effectiveness of AI-enhanced colonoscopy: A case-control study using real world evidence in a young screening age population

title: Impact of mydriasis on image gradability and automated diabetic retinopathy screening with a handheld camera. A real-world setting evaluation

title: Impact of mydriasis on image gradability and automated diabetic retinopathy screening with a handheld camera. A real-world setting evaluation

title: Detecting Pediatric Emergency Service Use for Suicide and Self-Harm: Multimodal Analysis of 3828 Encounters
outcome: Detection AUROC by demographic and diagnostic subgroups across structured, text, and hybrid methods

quote: Hybrid modality (aCS+Large Language Model Meta AI) achieved optimal performance (AUROC=0.977), with AUROC ≥0.90 for all 20 demographic and 12/15 diagnostic subgroups.

title: Artificial intelligence risk stratification from dynamic digital subtraction angiography radiomics predicts pulmonary embolism and associates with clinical outcomes in deep vein thrombosis: A retrospective cohort study
venue: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders

title: FDA-Cleared Artificial Intelligence Medical Devices in Orthopaedic Surgery
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
outcome: Share of FDA-cleared orthopaedic AI devices lacking clinical testing or validated prospectively
effect: 22.8% of 70 devices lacked clinical testing, 68.6% used retrospective data sets, and only 8.6% had a prospective clinical trial. Lack of clinical testing fell from 62.2% (2017-2019) to 19.7% (2022-2024).
quote: Overall, 22.8% of orthopaedic AIMDs lacked clinical testing and 68.6% were tested with retrospective data sets.

title: Enhancing readability and understandability of vascular surgery discharge summaries using artificial intelligence
outcome: Readability of AI-simplified versus original discharge summaries (Flesch-Kincaid grade level and ease score)
effect: 39.6% reduction in Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and 106.37% increase in Ease Score; mean PEMAT-P understandability 77.71, actionability 52.12.
quote: AI-generated summaries demonstrated significant improvements in readability, with a 39.6% reduction in Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and a 106.37% increase in Ease Score.

title: Enhancing readability and understandability of vascular surgery discharge summaries using artificial intelligence
outcome: Omissions and hallucinations in AI-simplified discharge summaries
effect: 10.8% of summaries had omissions and 7.5% had hallucinations, with corrections made in some cases; mean accuracy 5.21/6.
quote: However, 10.8% of summaries had omissions, and 7.5% had hallucinations, with corrections made in some cases.

title: Enhancing readability and understandability of vascular surgery discharge summaries using artificial intelligence
outcome: Omissions and hallucinations
effect: 10.8% of summaries had omissions; 7.5% had hallucinations.
quote: However, 10.8% of summaries had omissions, and 7.5% had hallucinations, with corrections made in some cases.

title: Enhancing readability and understandability of vascular surgery discharge summaries using artificial intelligence
outcome: omissions and hallucinations in AI-generated discharge summaries
effect: 10.8% of summaries had omissions, and 7.5% had hallucinations
quote: However, 10.8% of summaries had omissions, and 7.5% had hallucinations, with corrections made in some cases.

title: Clinical Impact of Artificial Intelligence-Augmented Lymph Node Evaluation in Metastatic Gastric, Colorectal, and Breast Cancer
outcome: Pathologist sensitivity, specificity, and review time with versus without AI assistance
effect: AI assistance increased sensitivity from 91.8%-93.9% to 95.9% for all pathologists; specificity remained 97.0%-98.9%; review time decreased by up to 78% for some cancer types.
quote: AI assistance increased sensitivity-which ranged from 91.8% to 93.9%-to 95.9% for all pathologists, while specificity remained high (97.0%-98.9%).
sample_unit: whole slide images (from 95 patients), read by 3 pathologists with and without AI

title: Measuring the Accuracy and Reproducibility of DeepSeek R1, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and GPT-4.1 on Complex Clinical Scenarios
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across repeated runs
effect: Reproducibility was DeepSeek 100%, GPT-4.1 97.5%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 92%.
quote: The reproducibility analysis indicated that the tests were very repeatable: DeepSeek (100%), GPT-4.1 (97.5%), and Claude 3.5 Sonnet (92%).

title: Reliability of LLMs as medical assistants for the general public: a randomized preregistered study
outcome: LLM standalone versus human-with-LLM accuracy in identifying conditions and disposition, compared with control
effect: LLMs alone identified conditions in 94.9% and disposition in 56.3%; participants using LLMs identified conditions in <34.5% and disposition in <44.2%, no better than control.
quote: However, participants using the same LLMs identified relevant conditions in fewer than 34.5% of cases and disposition in fewer than 44.2%, both no better than the control group.

title: Reliability of LLMs as medical assistants for the general public: a randomized preregistered study
outcome: Whether benchmark and licensing-exam performance predicts real-world performance with human users
effect: Standard medical knowledge benchmarks and simulated patient interactions did not predict the failures seen with human participants.
quote: Standard benchmarks for medical knowledge and simulated patient interactions do not predict the failures we find with human participants.

title: Colon-Pilot: A Generative AI Tool for Automated Colonoscopy Surveillance Recommendations and 2024 ACG/ASGE Quality Benchmarking
outcome: Deferral of cases to manual review via predefined safety criteria; accuracy of automated cases
effect: Colon-Pilot issued recommendations for 522 of 596 cases (87.6%) and flagged 12.4% for manual review. For automated cases, guideline-concordant accuracy was 97.5% (Cohen κ = 0.970) versus 69.7% for endoscopists.
quote: Colon-Pilot issued recommendations for 522 of 596 cases (87.6%) and flagged 12.4% for manual review.

title: Colon-Pilot: A Generative AI Tool for Automated Colonoscopy Surveillance Recommendations and 2024 ACG/ASGE Quality Benchmarking
outcome: Guideline-concordant surveillance accuracy of AI versus original endoscopist recommendations
effect: Guideline-concordant accuracy 97.5% (κ = 0.970) for AI versus 69.7% (κ = 0.781) for original endoscopist recommendations.
quote: For automated cases, guideline-concordant accuracy was 97.5% (Cohen κ = 0.970) versus 69.7% (κ = 0.781) for original endoscopist recommendations.

title: Utility of ChatGPT-4o in Creating Patient Handouts in Ophthalmology: A Comparison With American Academy of Ophthalmology Educational Materials
outcome: Readability and grade level of AI-generated handouts versus AAO handouts
effect: ChatGPT-4o English SMOG 7.86 vs AAO 7.49 (P=0.35); grade levels comparable; Spanish SPPI 60.26 vs 64.82 (P=0.04)
quote: ChatGPT-4o handouts had English readability similar to that of AAO (SMOG 7.86 ± 0.53 vs. 7.49 ± 0.76; P = 0.35) but significantly lower Spanish SPPI scores (60.26 ± 4.47 vs. 64.82 ± 2.97; P = 0.04).
sample_unit: patient education handouts per language (ChatGPT-4o vs AAO), rated by 3 ophthalmologists per language

title: Utility of ChatGPT-4o in Creating Patient Handouts in Ophthalmology: A Comparison With American Academy of Ophthalmology Educational Materials
outcome: Plain-language readability of AI-generated patient education materials
effect: ChatGPT-4o handouts at ~8th-grade level with readability similar to AAO in English; grade levels comparable; Spanish quality scores higher (15.83 vs 14.23; P<0.001)
quote: ChatGPT-generated materials matched or exceeded AAO handouts in readability and content quality, with Spanish versions being most preferred.
sample_unit: patient education handouts per language (ChatGPT-4o vs AAO), rated by 3 ophthalmologists per language

title: Optimizing Large Language Model Responses to Medical Queries: a Cross-sectional Study On the Effective Use of Chatgpt for Cancer-related Questions
outcome: Readability under a 6th-grade prompt
effect: 6th-grade prompt: ChatGPT-5 FKRE 64.92±8.56, FKGL 8.74±1.73, SMOG 6.97±1.26; ChatGPT-4o FKRE 65.44±7.43, FKGL 8.73±1.80, SMOG 6.86±1.53.
quote: The 6th-grade prompt markedly improved readability over other strategies (ChatGPT-5: FKRE:64.92 ± 8.56, GFI:8.10 ± 1.13, FKGL:8.74 ± 1.73, SMOG:6.97 ± 1.26; ChatGPT-4o:65.44 ± 7.43, GFI:8.04 ± 1.48, FKGL:8.73 ± 1.80, SMOG:6.86 ± 1.53).

title: Real-world use of PACS-integrated automated spine numbering in MRI
outcome: Reading time with vs without AI labeling by radiologist type
effect: Reading times were reduced for residents (p < 0.05) but not for specialists; overall reading times did not differ significantly (p = 0.0858).
quote: Integrating an AI-assisted spine labeling algorithm into the PACS significantly reduced reading times for residents (p < 0.05) but not for specialists.

title: Evaluating Large Language Model-Generated Clinical Summaries Through a Dual-Perspective Framework: Retrospective Observational Study
outcome: Differences between parent and clinician ratings of LLM-generated clinical summaries
effect: Parents and clinicians differed importantly on helpfulness; clinicians gave insight on clinical accuracy and parents on readability. No numeric results are reported in the abstract.
quote: There were important discrepancies between parents and clinicians in the realm of helpfulness, along with important insights by clinicians assessing clinical accuracy and parents assessing readability.
sample_unit: pediatric cardiac intensive care unit notes

title: Mechanistic interpretability of reinforcement learning in Medicaid care coordination
outcome: Residual harm rates among cleared decisions by race/ethnicity and sex subgroup
effect: Baseline residual harm varied from 1.03% (Hispanic) to 1.33% (non-Hispanic black, p=0.006); female 1.14% vs male 1.28%.
quote: Baseline residual harm varied from 1.03% (Hispanic) to 1.33% (non-Hispanic black, p=0.006).

title: Mechanistic interpretability of reinforcement learning in Medicaid care coordination
outcome: Subgroup disparity and policy value after constrained fairness optimisation
effect: Disparity reduced 37% (95% CI 22% to 48%) for race and 28% (95% CI 14% to 39%) for sex; policy value decreased 0.2%.
quote: Constrained fairness optimisation tightened harm rates to 1.10%–1.20% across race/ethnicity groups, reducing disparity by 37% (95% CI 22% to 48%) for race and 28% (95% CI 14% to 39%) for sex ( table 3 ).

title: Mechanistic interpretability of reinforcement learning in Medicaid care coordination
outcome: Whether conformal clearance separates low-harm decisions from those needing human review
effect: 89.5% of decisions cleared with 1.22% residual harm versus 6.67% harm among flagged decisions (81.7% relative reduction).
quote: Residual harm among cleared decisions was 1.22% (95% CI 1.14% to 1.30%) vs 6.67% (95% CI 6.02% to 7.32%) for flagged decisions, an 81.7% relative reduction ( table 2 ).

title: Mechanistic interpretability of reinforcement learning in Medicaid care coordination
outcome: explanation fidelity
effect: Auxiliary-original Q-value correlation Pearson r=0.94 (95% CI 0.93 to 0.95); TreeSHAP ranking Spearman ρ=0.71 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.77).
quote: We validated fidelity through three mechanisms: Q-value correlation between auxiliary and original models (Pearson r=0.94, 95% CI 0.93 to 0.95), comparison with TreeSHAP values 19 (Spearman ρ=0.71, 95% CI 0.65 to 0.77) and triangulation with permutation importance.

title: Mechanistic interpretability of reinforcement learning in Medicaid care coordination
outcome: appropriateness of human overrides
effect: In divergent cases, care teams better addressed patient needs in 77% of overrides.
quote: The 77% where care teams better addressed patient needs validates appropriate human oversight based on contextual information unavailable to the algorithm.

title: Evaluation of large Language models on pediatric asthma: a comparative study of Claude3-Opus, Gemini 2.0, ChatGPT-4o, and DeepSeek-a cross-sectional questionnaire study
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Readability (FKGL) of LLM pediatric asthma outputs versus recommended patient reading level
effect: Mean FKGL across models was 13.2–14.9, far exceeding recommended reading level for patient materials; DeepSeek least readable, ChatGPT-4o most comprehensible (FRE diff 12.41, p=.005).
quote: Critically, the mean readability level of all outputs (FKGL: 13.2–14.9) far exceeded the recommended reading accessibility level for patient materials.

title: Evaluation of large Language models on pediatric asthma: a comparative study of Claude3-Opus, Gemini 2.0, ChatGPT-4o, and DeepSeek-a cross-sectional questionnaire study
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of LLM outputs for patients
effect: All four LLMs failed to meet health-literacy standards; ChatGPT-4o was relatively more comprehensible; DeepSeek significantly worse than all other models (all p<.05).
quote: ChatGPT‑4o shows relative advantages in comprehensibility, yet none meet recommended health-literacy standards.

title: Evaluating the reliability and guideline concordance of ChatGPT-5 in the management of vascular diseases: a cross-sectional expert-based assessment
outcome: Expert-rated guideline concordance of ChatGPT-5 answers to vascular disease questions
effect: Mean score 4.74±0.27 on a five-point Likert scale; 40 of 70 questions (57%) received perfect agreement; inter-rater kappa 0.50 (95% CI 0.37-0.64).
quote: ChatGPT-5 achieved a mean score of 4.74±0.27, showing strong consistency with evidence-based recommendations.

title: Comparison of Artificial Intelligence and Guidelines in Answering Questions on Gestational Diabetes: a CLEAR Tool Analysis
outcome: Readability and required literacy level of AI answers versus guidelines for GDM questions
effect: Guideline answers were more accessible to the general audience and easiest to read; ChatGPT and Bard required higher literacy levels, with Bard the most challenging text.
quote: The medical guidelines provided more accessible answers for the general audience, while ChatGPT and Bard required higher literacy levels.

title: Design and Architecture of a Generative-AI-Supported, Nonphysician-Delivered Model for GDMT Optimization in HFrEF: The ASSIST-HF Trial
outcome: GDMT optimization, NT-proBNP levels, and hospitalizations versus standard care
effect: At 12 weeks, VA-guided care produced superior GDMT optimization across all medication classes, lower N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, and fewer hospitalizations than standard care. Numerical effect estimates were not reported.
quote: At 12 weeks, patients in the VA arm had superior GDMT optimization across all medication classes, lower N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide, and fewer hospitalizations.

title: Design and Architecture of a Generative-AI-Supported, Nonphysician-Delivered Model for GDMT Optimization in HFrEF: The ASSIST-HF Trial
outcome: Safety disagreements between AI GDMT recommendations and supervising cardiologist
effect: No safety disagreements between VA and clinician recommendations were reported across the 12-week VA arm (30 patients).
quote: Patient-reported acceptability, appropriateness and feasibility scores were high, with no safety disagreements between VA and clinician recommendations.

title: Design and Architecture of a Generative-AI-Supported, Nonphysician-Delivered Model for GDMT Optimization in HFrEF: The ASSIST-HF Trial
outcome: Safety disagreements between VA recommendations and supervising clinician judgment
effect: No safety disagreements between VA and clinician recommendations were reported. Counts of recommendations reviewed and numerical disagreement rates were not provided.
quote: Patient-reported acceptability, appropriateness and feasibility scores were high, with no safety disagreements between VA and clinician recommendations.

title: Training the diagnostic artificial intelligence in thyroid sonography: how well is deep learning truly learning?
outcome: Agreement of AI TI-RADS classification with surgeon before and after software training and update
effect: Agreement rose from 128/176 (73%) in the first phase to 210/227 (92.6%) after update; re-evaluating the initial 110 patients, 194 vs. 176 nodules were correctly assessed.
quote: First phase: AI-supported TI-RADS classification corresponded to the assessor's in 128/176 (73%) of examined nodules; second phase: correspondence in 210/227 (92.6%).

title: Impact of AI Scribes on Physician Productivity and Workflow in Medical Oncology
outcome: Diagnostic codes per visit after AI scribe deployment (coding intensity)
effect: No change in number of diagnostic codes per visit; mean visits rose (β = 3.35, P = .010) and billing per working day rose (β = $433.61, P = .007).
quote: There was no change in the number of diagnostic codes per visit.

title: Mapping the susceptibility of large language models to medical misinformation across clinical notes and social media: a cross-sectional benchmarking analysis
outcome: LLM susceptibility to false claims under neutral versus logical-fallacy rephrased prompts
effect: Base susceptibility was 31.7% (50,108/158,000). Fallacy framings changed it: appeal to popularity 11.9% (-19.8 points), slippery slope 33.9% (+2.2), appeal to authority 34.6% (+2.9); eight of ten framings reduced or did not change the rate.
quote: Eight of ten fallacy framings significantly reduced or did not change that rate, led by appeal to popularity (susceptibility 11·9%; difference of -19·8 percentage points; p<0·0001); only the slippery-slope prompt (33·9%; difference of 2·2 percentage points; p<0·0001) and the appeal-to-authority prompt (34·6%; difference of 2·9 percentage points; p<0·0001) increased it.
sample_unit: base prompts (of >3.4 million total prompts across 20 LLMs)

title: Mapping the susceptibility of large language models to medical misinformation across clinical notes and social media: a cross-sectional benchmarking analysis
outcome: Rate at which LLMs accept fabricated medical content in clinical notes, social media, and vignettes
effect: LLMs were susceptible in 50,108 (31.7%) of 158,000 base prompts; real hospital notes with an inserted false recommendation 46.1% (46,108/100,000); social media 8.9% (2,479/28,000); Gemma-3-4B-it 63.6% (5,023/7,900).
quote: Across all models and corpora, LLMs were susceptible to fabricated data in 50 108 (31·7%) of 158 000 base prompts.
sample_unit: base prompts (of >3.4 million total prompts across 20 LLMs)

title: Mapping the susceptibility of large language models to medical misinformation across clinical notes and social media: a cross-sectional benchmarking analysis
outcome: Model detection of misinformation and logical-fallacy rhetoric in prompts
effect: LLMs accepted fabricated claims in 31.7% of base prompts. GPT models were least susceptible and most accurate at fallacy detection; other models such as Gemma-3-4B-it were susceptible in 63.6% (5,023/7,900).
quote: Performance varied by model: GPT models were the least susceptible and most accurate at fallacy detection, whereas others, such as Gemma-3-4B-it, showed 63·6% (5023 of 7900) susceptibility.
sample_unit: base prompts (of >3.4 million total prompts across 20 LLMs)

title: ChatGPT-5 Matches Surgeon-Level Assessment of Facelift Candidacy: A Pilot Proof-of-Concept Study
outcome: Agreement of ChatGPT-5 with board-certified surgeon consensus on facelift candidacy and aging features
effect: Facelift candidacy agreement 95.5% (21/22; κ=0.91; McNemar P=1.00); binary aging features 81.8-90.9% (κ≈0.61-0.81); ordinal severity exact agreement 77.3%, weighted κ 0.74-0.86.
quote: For facelift candidacy, agreement was 95.5% (21/22; Cohen's κ = 0.91; McNemar P = 1.00).

title: Evaluating Large-Scale and Lightweight Large Language Models for Traditional Chinese Medicine Exam Questions: A Comparative Study
outcome: LLM accuracy on TCM exam questions by question type, model size, and prompt language
effect: Large-scale LLMs reached 69.01%-90.92% on single-choice but at most 8.40% on multiple-choice; evaluation was exam-style and not real-world clinical decision-making.
quote: While the current evaluation is based on examination-style tasks and does not involve real-world clinical decision-making, our findings provide insights to support the deployment of optimized models in resource-constrained healthcare environments.

title: A comparative accuracy study of multimodal LLMs, VLM and agent-based framework for pulmonary nodule detection on chest radiographs
outcome: Accuracy of multimodal LLMs detecting pulmonary nodules on chest radiographs
effect: Best accuracy 0.711 (95% CI 0.613-0.808) for MedRAX and BiomedCLIP; Claude 3.7 Sonnet 0.651; others 0.602. Accuracy insufficient for clinical implementation.
quote: Overall, accuracy values of evaluated models were insufficient for current clinical practice implementation.

title: Computer-Aided Colonoscopy Alert Fatigue and Its Effect on Adenoma Detection
outcome: Adenoma detection rate with versus without CADe in real-world colonoscopy, by procedure order
effect: CADe ADR 49.9% in first 3 procedures vs 39.4% unassisted; later procedures 39.9% vs 40.9%, so the benefit disappeared later in the day.
quote: CADe assistance significantly improved ADR during early-day colonoscopies, but this benefit disappeared in later-day procedures.

title: Computer-Aided Colonoscopy Alert Fatigue and Its Effect on Adenoma Detection
outcome: Clinician performance with AI in real workflow versus without, across the day
effect: Adenomas per colonoscopy rose +0.27 (95% CI 0.14-0.41) early with CADe but only +0.11 (95% CI -0.09 to 0.31, P=0.51) later.
quote: Similarly, adenomas per colonoscopy were significantly higher in early CADe-assisted procedures (mean increase +0.27, 95% CI [0.14-0.41], P < 0.001), but this benefit disappeared in later procedures (+0.11, 95% CI [-0.09 to 0.31], P = 0.51).

title: Computer-Aided Colonoscopy Alert Fatigue and Its Effect on Adenoma Detection
outcome: Performance of endoscopists with versus without AI in deployment, assessing reliance/fatigue
effect: Early CADe ADR 49.9% vs 39.4% unassisted; late CADe ADR 39.9% vs 40.9% unassisted, suggesting diminished responsiveness to CADe.
quote: By contrast, ADR in CADe-assisted procedures was markedly higher in the first 3 procedures (49.9%, 95% CI [45.5-54.3]) but dropped significantly to 39.9% (95% CI [33.8-46.3]) in later procedures.

title: Computer-Aided Colonoscopy Alert Fatigue and Its Effect on Adenoma Detection
outcome: Alert fatigue reducing CADe effectiveness through the day
effect: CADe-assisted ADR fell from 49.9% in first 3 procedures to 39.9% in later procedures; ADR gain per WT minute 10.5% early vs 10.1% late.
quote: This pattern suggests that alert fatigue may limit endoscopists' responsiveness to CADe prompts as the day progresses.

title: Simplifying radiology reports with large language models: privacy-compliant open- versus closed-weight models
outcome: Flesch reading ease and layperson understandability of LLM-simplified versus original radiology reports
effect: Flesch reading ease: GPT-4o 46±7, Llama-3-70b 44±6, Mixtral-8x22B 44±6 vs original 17±13 (p<0.001); understandability 4.1-4.4 vs 1.5 (p<0.001).
quote: All three LLM reports yielded markedly higher layperson-understandability ratings than the original reports (GPT-4o: 4.4 ± 0.1; Llama-3-70B: 4.3 ± 0.1; Mixtral-8x22B: 4.1 ± 0.1 vs. 1.5 ± 0.1; p < 0.001 for each), with no significant difference between GPT-4o and Llama-3-70B (p = 0.136).

title: Simplifying radiology reports with large language models: privacy-compliant open- versus closed-weight models
outcome: Errors with potential for patient harm in LLM-simplified radiology reports
effect: Mixtral-8x22B and Llama-3-70B produced more errors with potential for patient harm than GPT-4o (p = 0.005 and p = 0.025, respectively).
quote: Mixtral-8x22B and Llama-3-70B produced more errors with potential for patient harm than GPT-4o (p = 0.005 and p = 0.025, respectively).

title: Reinforcing the stereotype: an analysis of AI-generated images of patients with obstructive sleep apnea
venue: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine
outcome: Demographic representation (age, sex, race, weight) in AI-generated images of patients with OSA
effect: Images portrayed individuals as middle-aged (98.3%), male (99.8%), White (94.7%), and obese/overweight (97.2%), differing markedly from real-world prevalence.
quote: ChatGPT-4o consistently portrayed individuals as middle-aged (98.3%), male (99.8%), White (94.7%), and obese/overweight (97.2%)-a representation differing markedly and in all axes from real-world prevalence.

title: Development of retrieval-augmented generation-based large language model for drug-induced liver injury using Livertox data
outcome: Accuracy, completeness, and hallucination of RAG-grounded vs non-RAG LLM responses to DILI questions, rated by hepatologists
effect: RAG-LLMs outperformed non-RAG GPT-4o in accuracy (p<0.001) and completeness (p<0.01); d=0.778 and 0.526; no hallucinations in RAG outputs, while both non-RAG variants produced several.
quote: RAG-LLMs outperformed non-RAG GPT-4o variants in accuracy (p<0.001) and completeness (p<0.01).

title: Prompt Engineering for Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Status Extraction: Comparing Large Language Model Techniques
outcome: LLM ECOG extraction accuracy and hallucination against reference standard
effect: CoT and DFT achieved 94% accuracy vs rule-based 91% and simple prompting 86%; all methods sometimes hallucinated ECOG status.
quote: All methods sometimes hallucinated ECOG status.

title: Prompt Engineering for Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group Status Extraction: Comparing Large Language Model Techniques
outcome: Comparison of LLM prompting methods against rule-based NLP for ECOG extraction
effect: CoT and DFT achieved 94% accuracy, outperforming the rule-based method (91%) and simple prompting (86%).
quote: Both CoT and double filtering technique (DFT) achieved 94% accuracy, outperforming the rule-based method (91%) and simple prompting (86%).

title: Chatbot Outreach in Value-Based Preventive Care: Retrospective Analysis
outcome: Preventive care-gap closure with chatbot outreach versus phone, email, mail, and multichannel outreach
effect: Phone outreach achieved higher compliance than chatbot or multichannel outreach across most groups and years; chatbot beat phone only for diabetes care in 2023 (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.48-2.21).
quote: Phone outreach consistently achieved higher compliance than chatbot or multichannel outreach across most groups and years.

title: Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Reporting Variability and AI-Assisted Reproducibility: A Multicentre Analysis
outcome: Agreement between report-derived AI LVEF and standardized reassessment across centres
effect: ICC ≥ 0.86 overall and single-centre, but 95% limits of agreement all exceeded ±5%; 44.3% of cases differed >5% and 17.5% >10%.
quote: In 44.3% of cases > 5% differences between R-LVEF and M-LVEF were observed, and 17.5% showed > 10% differences.

title: Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Reporting Variability and AI-Assisted Reproducibility: A Multicentre Analysis
outcome: Reproducibility and time of AI-assisted versus fully manual LVEF analysis by operators
effect: AI-assisted mode reduced assessment time; interobserver ICCs 0.968, 0.974, 0.984 vs 0.913, 0.924, 0.971 manual; CV 2.5%, 3.8%, 4.4% vs 5.6%, 8.8%, 9.3%.
quote: The AI-assisted method not only significantly reduced LVEF assessment time compared with manual analysis, but also showed superior reproducibility.

title: Development and Evaluation of a Retrieval-Augmented Generation System for Radiology Guidelines
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Factual accuracy, completeness, usefulness of RAG vs standalone LLM on radiology guideline queries
effect: Both RAG systems significantly outperformed standalone LLM; enhanced RAG factual accuracy 0.89 vs 0.68, completeness 4.20 vs 3.05, usefulness 3.99 vs 3.09 (5-point Likert).
quote: Both RAG systems significantly outperformed the standalone LLM in all metrics, with the enhanced model achieving the highest scores: Factual accuracy (0.89 vs. 0.68), completeness (4.20 vs. 3.05 on a 5-point Likert scale), and usefulness (3.99 vs. 3.09 on a 5-point Likert scale).

title: Assessing the accuracy, reliability, quality, and readability of artificial intelligence chatbots in patient education: insights from zirconia crowns
outcome: Readability of chatbot answers to zirconia crown FAQs, measured by Flesch Reading Ease Score
effect: ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5 and DeepSeek showed superior readability; Microsoft Copilot scored lowest, particularly for readability. No numeric FRES values reported in the abstract.
quote: Gemini achieved the highest scores in accuracy, quality, and reliability (p < 0.001), while ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-5, and DeepSeek demonstrated superior readability.

title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in rheumatology: a comparative evaluation of the ChatGPT and DeepSeek application
outcome: Agreement between LLM answers and clinical findings in axSpA and PsA (Cohen's and Fleiss' Kappa)
effect: No agreement between clinical results and GPT-5 or DeepSeek-R1 by Cohen's Kappa; no satisfactory Fleiss' Kappa agreement; mean-value comparisons ranged from very good to large differences; overall moderate validity, reliability and utility.
quote: Regarding the results of the calculation of the Cohen’s Kappa coefficient, no agreement is indicated between the clinical results and the answers of ChatGPT and DeepSeek and specifically the GPT-5 and DeepSeek-R1 models.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Stability of Multimodal Large Language Models for Hand Fracture Detection: A Multi-Run Evaluation on Plain Radiographs
outcome: Reproducibility of fracture detection across five repeated runs per model (Fleiss' kappa)
effect: GPT-5 Pro κ = 0.71; Gemini 2.5 Pro κ = 0.57; Claude Sonnet 4.5 κ = 0.33 (instability); Mistral κ = 0.88 despite 38.5% accuracy (systematic error).
quote: Claude Sonnet 4.5 showed low accuracy (33.8%) and consistency (κ = 0.33), reflecting instability.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Stability of Multimodal Large Language Models for Hand Fracture Detection: A Multi-Run Evaluation on Plain Radiographs
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of MLLMs for hand fracture detection on plain radiographs
effect: Accuracy ranged from 33.8% to 64.3% (GPT-5 Pro highest at 64.3%); scaphoid fractures remained challenging; models not reliable standalone tools.
quote: At present, MLLMs should be regarded as experimental diagnostic reasoning systems rather than reliable standalone tools for clinical fracture detection.

title: Multimodal Large Language Model for Fracture Detection in Emergency Orthopedic Trauma: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study
outcome: LLM fracture detection accuracy against specialist reference in consecutive ED patients at a single center
effect: Concordance 808/1136 (71.1%; κ=0.634); sensitivity 76.9%, specificity 66.8%; 184 false negatives (16.2% of cohort), mostly non-displaced fractures (82.6%).
quote: Overall, the LLM showed good diagnostic agreement with orthopedic specialists, with concordant results in 808 of 1136 patients (71.1%; κ = 0.634; 95% CI: 68.4-73.7).

title: Multimodal Large Language Model for Fracture Detection in Emergency Orthopedic Trauma: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study
outcome: Missed fractures by LLM, indicating risk of standalone use as diagnosis
effect: False negatives were 184 patients (16.2% of cohort), 32.4% of LLM-negative assessments; 17.4% of FN cases required surgery; ankle and foot FN rates 30.4% and 17.4%.
quote: However, its limited ability to detect non-displaced fractures-especially in anatomically complex regions like the ankle and foot-carries direct patient safety implications and confirms that specialist review remains indispensable.

title: Multimodal Large Language Model for Fracture Detection in Emergency Orthopedic Trauma: A Diagnostic Accuracy Study
outcome: Fractures missed by AI negative assessments, showing risk if clinicians skip review of AI-negative cases
effect: 184 false-negative cases (16.2% of cohort; 32.4% of LLM-negative assessments); 82.6% non-displaced, 17.4% needed surgical treatment.
quote: False-negative cases accounted for 184 patients (16.2% of the total cohort), representing 32.4% of all LLM-negative assessments.

title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric otorhinolaryngology: Assessing readability, understandability, and actionability of postoperative instructions
outcome: Readability, understandability and actionability of AI-generated pediatric postoperative instructions against adequacy thresholds
effect: ChatGPT best readability (FKRE 64.57, FKGL 7.40); Gemini understandability 83.20%; DeepSeek actionability 71.10%. No platform met FKGL <6, FKRE >60 and PEMAT-P >80% at once.
quote: No AI platform met all the adequacy thresholds (FKGL <6, FKRE >60, PEMAT-P > 80%) at one time.

title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric otorhinolaryngology: Assessing readability, understandability, and actionability of postoperative instructions
outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated patient instructions relative to target level
effect: Best FKGL was 7.40 (±1.54) for ChatGPT, above the FKGL <6 adequacy threshold; no platform met all thresholds.
quote: No AI platform met all the adequacy thresholds (FKGL <6, FKRE >60, PEMAT-P > 80%) at one time.

title: Generative artificial intelligence for patient education material on gastric cancer prevention
outcome: Readability of AI-generated patient summary (FKGL, SMOG) versus guideline recommendations
effect: Readability failed to meet guideline recommendations for both ChatGPT-4o and DiCE summaries on both FKGL and SMOG scores.
quote: Readability failed to meet guideline recommendations for both summaries on both FKGL and SMOG scores.
sample_unit: rating panels (expert physicians and patient advisory committee members) rating two summaries

title: Generative artificial intelligence for patient education material on gastric cancer prevention
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient education material relative to recommended level
effect: Both ChatGPT-4o and DiCE summaries exceeded guideline-recommended readability on FKGL and SMOG.
quote: Readability failed to meet guideline recommendations for both summaries on both FKGL and SMOG scores.
sample_unit: rating panels (expert physicians and patient advisory committee members) rating two summaries

title: Can Artificial Intelligence Align with Evidence? Performance of ChatGPT-4o in Knee Osteoarthritis Surgical Guidelines
outcome: Textual consistency of ChatGPT-4o responses across three repeated independent sessions
effect: Internal text consistency across repeated trials was low, with several responses showing unacceptable similarity levels (<50%).
quote: Internal text consistency across repeated trials was low, with several responses showing unacceptable similarity levels (<50%).
sample_unit: guideline recommendations translated into clinical questions (each submitted 3 times)

title: Can Artificial Intelligence Align with Evidence? Performance of ChatGPT-4o in Knee Osteoarthritis Surgical Guidelines
outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-4o answers with AAOS knee arthroplasty guideline recommendations
effect: Overall concordance of 60% with CPG recommendations, fair agreement (κ = 0.392, p = 0.005); discrepancies persisted in functional outcomes and rehabilitation recommendations.
quote: ChatGPT-4o achieved an overall concordance of 60% with the CPG recommendations, representing fair agreement (κ = 0.392, p = 0.005).
sample_unit: guideline recommendations translated into clinical questions (each submitted 3 times)

title: [The Digital Lab: Practical digital workflow and integration of AI for routine in pathology, through the example of prostate cancer]
outcome: Rate of AI analysis failures caused by poor-quality inputs (pre-analytical artifacts)
effect: A 10% failure rate related to pre-analytical artifacts was observed in routine use of the prostate AI tool.
quote: A 10% failure rate related to pre-analytical artifacts was observed and is an area for improvement in our practices.

title: Large language models provide unsafe answers to patient-posed medical questions
outcome: Rate of problematic and unsafe chatbot responses to patient-posed medical questions
effect: Problematic responses ranged from 21.6% (Claude) to 43.2% (Llama); unsafe responses ranged from 5% (Claude) to 13% (GPT-4o, Llama).
quote: The rate of problematic responses varies from 21.6% (Claude) to 43.2% (Llama), with unsafe responses varying from 5% (Claude) to 13% (GPT-4o, Llama).

title: Large language models provide unsafe answers to patient-posed medical questions
outcome: Safety of consumer LLM chatbot medical advice that patients may over-rely on
effect: Unsafe advice rates of 5% to 13% across four public chatbots; qualitative results show potential for serious patient harm.
quote: This study suggests that millions of patients could be receiving unsafe medical advice from publicly available chatbots, and further work is needed to improve the clinical safety of these powerful tools.

title: Benchmark evaluation of video large language models in quality assessment of science popularization videos for dry eye
outcome: Agreement (ICC) between VideoLLM scores and expert ratings of dry eye video quality
effect: Across most metrics, VideoLLMs showed poor agreement with experts (ICC < 0.40); only PEMAT-A/V actionability reached ICC 0.50 (QwenVL) and 0.43 (InternVL).
quote: Across most metrics, VideoLLMs demonstrated poor agreement with expert annotations (ICC < 0.40), except for the actionability dimension of PEMAT-A/V, where QwenVL and InternVL achieved ICCs of 0.50 and 0.43, respectively, with the experts.

title: A fine-tuned large language model chatbot for multi-scenario radiology cancer care: randomized controlled trial on interaction optimization, emotional support, and provider burnout reduction
outcome: Dialogue quality, provider burnout and image quality with vs without chatbot in randomized sub-trials
effect: RHP+REC improved factuality in appointment triage (4.12 vs 3.39, P<0.001), satisfaction in pre-exam preparation (3.73 vs 3.19), and burnout exhaustion (1.85 vs 2.40, P<0.01), but underperformed on empathy in radiology clinic services.
quote: RHP + REC group demonstrated superior dialogue quality in AT (factuality: 4.12 ± 0.86 vs. 3.39 ± 1.21, P < 0.001) and PP (satisfaction: 3.73 ± 0.11 vs. 3.19 ± 0.18, P < 0.001), with reduced burnout (exhaustion: 1.85 ± 0.91 vs. 2.40 ± 1.22, P < 0.01).

title: A fine-tuned large language model chatbot for multi-scenario radiology cancer care: randomized controlled trial on interaction optimization, emotional support, and provider burnout reduction
outcome: Chatbot empathy and emotional regulation in emotionally complex radiology clinic services
effect: REC scored lower than providers on empathy (3.88 ± 0.67 vs 4.42 ± 0.53, P = 0.002) and emotional regulation (3.87 ± 0.19 vs 4.12 ± 0.27, P = 0.004) in radiology clinic services.
quote: However, REC underperformed in empathy and emotional regulation during emotionally complex RCS (3.88 ± 0.67 vs. 4.42 ± 0.53, P = 0.002; 3.87 ± 0.19 vs. 4.12 ± 0.27, P = 0.004).

title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
outcome: Sensitivity, NPV, specificity across operating thresholds 0.15, 0.125, 0.10 for triage
effect: Lowering threshold from 0.15 to 0.10 raised sensitivity 87.3% to 93.2% and NPV 87.0% to 91.3%, with specificity falling to 71.7%; trade-off deemed acceptable.
quote: By lowering the operating threshold, we increased sensitivity and NPV, at the cost of reduced specificity, a trade-off that was considered acceptable for a co-triage use case in primary care.

title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
outcome: Threshold selection with clinician input balancing operational value and false negatives
effect: Threshold 0.1 chosen collaboratively with physicians and radiologists; sensitivity 93.19%, operational improvement 35.85% retained.
quote: Hence, the 0.1 threshold was deemed to have an acceptable sensitivity for safety and still retain acceptable potential operational improvement to yield value in implementation.

title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
outcome: Local threshold tuning versus vendor default on representative polyclinic data
effect: Default 0.15 gave sensitivity 87.3%, NPV 87.0%; tuned 0.10 gave sensitivity 93.2%, NPV 91.3%, specificity 71.7%.
quote: We found that the threshold required for optimal performance of Lunit CXR as a co-triage tool was different from the default threshold of 0.15 set by Lunit.

title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
outcome: AI sensitivity and NPV compared with working radiologist reports on same data
effect: At 0.125, sensitivity 90.10% vs 80.7% and NPV 89.01% vs 81.66% for radiologist, with non-overlapping CIs.
quote: At threshold 0.125, Lunit-enabled workflow demonstrates superior performance compared with the radiologist report, with significantly higher sensitivity (90.10% (95% CI 87.19% to 92.86%) vs 80.7% (95% CI 76.83% to 84.42%)) and NPV (89.01% (95% CI 85.71% to 92.05%) vs 81.66% (95% CI 77.95% to 85.24%)), with non-overlapping CIs in both metrics confirming the statistical significance of these differences.

title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
outcome: Performance on representative local data against radiologist reference standard
effect: At 0.15, AI sensitivity 87.3% vs radiologist report 80.7%; specificity 85.0% vs 85.9%.
quote: At the default recommended threshold, Lunit INSIGHT CXR3 achieved greater sensitivity than the radiologist (87.3% vs 80.7%) with comparable specificity (85.0% vs 85.9%).

title: How threshold customisation affects the performance of a multiclass X-ray AI model for primary care triage: a retrospective study
outcome: AI-normal missed-abnormality risk
effect: At 0.10, reported sensitivity was 93.2% and NPV was 91.3%.
quote: Lowering the threshold to 0.10 increased sensitivity to 93.2% (95% CI 90.7% to 95.5%) and NPV to 91.3% (95% CI 88.2% to 94.3%), with specificity of 71.7% (95% CI 67.3% to 76.1%).

title: Success and failure of human-AI collaboration in clinical reasoning: An experimental study on challenging real-world cases
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of clinicians with vs without LLM collaboration compared with LLM-only accuracy
effect: Accuracy rose from 0.45 to 0.60 with HAC (P<0.001); 20% of participants declined; HAC mean stayed below LLM-only accuracy (0.70).
quote: HAC significantly improved mean accuracy compared to the human-only condition (from 0.45 to 0.60, P < 0.001), although 20% of participants showed a decline in performance and the mean remained below the LLM-only accuracy (0.70).
sample_unit: participants (10 ophthalmologists, 10 residents, 10 senior medical students), each completing 30 cases

title: Success and failure of human-AI collaboration in clinical reasoning: An experimental study on challenging real-world cases
outcome: Whether users accepted incorrect LLM insights in failed human-AI collaboration
effect: 58.6% of failed HAC involved the LLM presenting incorrect insight and the human accepting it; 92.6% of successes involved correct insight accepted.
quote: In successful HAC, 92.6% followed the pattern LLM presents correct insight/human accepts, while 58.6% of failures involved LLM presents incorrect insight/human accepts.
sample_unit: participants (10 ophthalmologists, 10 residents, 10 senior medical students), each completing 30 cases

title: Guideline-based, but not error-free: Multilingual risks in AI-powered patient counseling on gallstones
outcome: Guideline concordance of LLM gallstone answers in Turkish versus English
effect: ChatGPT performed better in English than Turkish (p = 0.008); Turkish outputs more often under-explained, English outputs amplified risk; Perplexity had the highest error burden.
quote: ChatGPT performed better in English than Turkish (p = 0.008).
sample_unit: LLM responses (14 questions x 2 languages x 3 models)

title: Assessing the performance of generative AI chatbots in preimplantation genetic testing: a comparative study of expert evaluations
outcome: Specialist-rated quality of chatbot answers to PGT questions, by model and question type
effect: ChatGPT simple 16.83±1.80/25, controversial 27.75±4.49/40; Gemini 14.92±2.02, 26.08±3.99; Llama 13.58±3.60, 16.92±4.96. ChatGPT and Gemini outperformed Llama; performance lower for controversial questions.
quote: Generative AI shows moderate reliability in addressing PGT-related enquiries, with ChatGPT and Gemini outperforming Llama.
sample_unit: expert evaluations per chatbot (12 specialists x 13 questions)

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted training for rib fracture interpretation: a prospective study in undergraduate medical students
venue: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
outcome: Reader diagnostic performance with vs without AI heatmap assistance, and overreliance assessment
effect: AI assistance (S2) improved accuracy 26.7%, sensitivity 41.0%, specificity 25.1%, F1 35.6%, precision 31.4% (all p<0.01); agreement with AI on AI-misclassified cases rose (S1 vs S2 p=0.037), suggesting automation bias.
quote: Significant improvements were observed during the S2 using AI heatmapping, with a 26.7% increase in accuracy, 25.1% in specificity, 41.0% in sensitivity, 35.6% in F1 score, and 31.4% in precision (all p-values < 0.01).

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted training for rib fracture interpretation: a prospective study in undergraduate medical students
venue: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
outcome: automation bias on AI-misclassified CXRs
quote: In AI-misclassified CXRs (false negatives and false positives), UGY showed significantly higher agreement with AI during S2, suggesting possible automation bias.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted training for rib fracture interpretation: a prospective study in undergraduate medical students
venue: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
outcome: Retention of diagnostic skill after AI withdrawal and overreliance concerns among trainees
effect: After AI withdrawal (S3) performance declined vs S2 but stayed above baseline for accuracy (+13.3%, p=0.010) and precision (+13.7%, p=0.010); 34.6% worried about over-reliance.
quote: However, slight improvements were still observed, with statistically significant improvements in accuracy (13.3%, p = 0.010) and precision (13.7%, p = 0.010).

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted training for rib fracture interpretation: a prospective study in undergraduate medical students
venue: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
outcome: skill retention after AI withdrawal
effect: S3 declined versus S2, but baseline-to-S3 accuracy +13.3%, p = 0.010 and precision +13.7%, p = 0.010.
quote: Performance in S3 declined compared to S2 but remained higher than baseline for accuracy (+ 13.3%, p = 0.010) and precision (+ 13.7%, p = 0.010) compared to baseline.

title: The impact of artificial intelligence scribes on physician and advanced practice provider cognitive load and well-being
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Clinician burnout and intent to leave after AI scribe deployment, by professional role
effect: Physicians reported reduced burnout and intent to leave; APPs had no significant reduction in burnout or intent to leave. Both groups showed reduced cognitive task load.
quote: Physicians reported reduced burnout and intent to leave; however, APPs did not have a significant reduction in burnout or intent to leave.
sample_unit: physicians and advanced practice providers (survey respondents)

title: Which bot is best? Accuracy and readability of generative artificial intelligence assistant responses on adrenal nodules
outcome: Reading grade level of chatbot responses to adrenal nodule questions versus recommended patient education level
effect: Mean Lexile reading level was 8th-10th grade; all responses exceeded recommended patient education levels.
quote: More accurate, reliable, and thorough answers contained excess jargon, but all responses exceeded recommended patient education levels.

title: Which bot is best? Accuracy and readability of generative artificial intelligence assistant responses on adrenal nodules
outcome: Jargon use and readability of chatbot responses to patient questions
effect: Jargon use differed significantly (p ≤ 0.05); Perplexity, the most accurate, used the most jargon; Gemini used the least. All responses exceeded recommended patient levels.
quote: More accurate, reliable, and thorough answers contained excess jargon, but all responses exceeded recommended patient education levels.

title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with vs without GPT-5 assistance
effect: R1/R2 accuracy rose from 73%/71% unassisted to 87%/86% with browser GPT-5 and 94%/94% with optimal-settings GPT-5 (P=0.001; P=0.031/0.028). Overreliance not assessed.
quote: With browser-based GPT-5 assistance, their accuracy significantly improved to 87% (75/86; 95% CI: 79%–94%) and 86% (74/86; 95% CI: 78%–93%), respectively ( P = 0.001, P = 0.001).

title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
outcome: repeat-run reproducibility
effect: Round 2 agreement was high: diagnosis κ 0.882 (95% CI: 0.80–0.96); differential κ 0.816.
quote: Agreement between GPT-5 responses generated with the optimal settings at baseline and in the Round 2 evaluation was high, with Cohen’s κ: 0.882 (95% CI: 0.80–0.96) for the most likely diagnosis and κ: 0.816 for differential diagnosis performance, indicating strong agreement.

title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
outcome: Clinician performance with AI assistance versus unassisted in the workflow, not standalone metrics
effect: Radiologists' accuracy improved with GPT-5 assistance (73%/71% to 87%/86% to 94%); differential Likert scores improved to 4.56 and 4.49; assisted juniors outperformed the abdominal radiologist on differentials.
quote: Using GPT-5 with the optimal settings further improved their accuracy to 94% (81/86; 95% CI: 88%–99%) ( P = 0.031, P = 0.028).

title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
outcome: GPT-5 performance across input formats, temperature/top-p settings, and repeat-run reproducibility
effect: Accuracy 12% image-only vs 58% with text; 53% to 73% across temperatures; Round 2 agreement kappa 0.882 for diagnosis, no significant difference (P=0.41). Temperature 2 outputs were unevaluable.
quote: Agreement between GPT-5 responses generated with the optimal settings at baseline and in the Round 2 evaluation was high, with Cohen’s κ: 0.882 (95% CI: 0.80–0.96) for the most likely diagnosis and κ: 0.816 for differential diagnosis performance, indicating strong agreement.

title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
outcome: GPT-5 and GPT-5-assisted radiologists compared against unassisted and expert abdominal radiologist
effect: Abdominal radiologist accuracy 92% exceeded unassisted juniors (P<0.001) but did not differ from assisted juniors; assisted juniors outperformed the abdominal radiologist on differentials (P=0.002, 0.001).
quote: Comparatively, AR achieved an accuracy of 92% (79/86; 95% CI: 85%–97%), which was superior to the accuracy of R1 and R2 without GPT-5 assistance ( P < 0.001) but not significantly different from their performances with both browser-based GPT-5 and GPT-5 with the optimal settings ( Table 4 ).

title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
outcome: accuracy with clinical context inputs
effect: Accuracy increased from 12% to 58% when imaging findings and clinical presentation were added; P<0.001.
quote: With the "only visual" input format, browser-based GPT-5 achieved a diagnostic accuracy of 12%, increasing to 58% when imaging findings and clinical presentations were provided (P < 0.001).

title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
outcome: accuracy across hyperparameter settings
effect: Optimal temperature 1.5/top-p 1 raised accuracy to 73%; mean differential score improved from 3.44 to 3.84.
quote: Hyperparameter optimization further improved GPT-5 performance, with diagnostic accuracy increasing to 73% at the optimal settings (temperature: 1.5, top-p: 1) and mean differential diagnosis scores improving from 3.44 to 3.84.

title: Prospective quantitative analysis of hyperparameter and input optimization in GPT-5: comparative contribution to radiologist performance in abdominal radiology
outcome: diagnostic accuracy with visual-only versus multimodal input
effect: Browser-based GPT-5 achieved diagnostic accuracy of only 12% (10/86; 95% CI: 6%-21%) with visual-only input, compared to 58% when clinical presentation and imaging findings were added.
quote: Browser-based GPT-5 demonstrated limited diagnostic accuracy in the “only visual” format, correctly answering 12% of cases [10/86; 95% confidence interval (CI), 6%–21%].

title: The Case for Local AI Development: Lessons From Computer‑Aided Detection of Tuberculosis and Silicosis in Southern Africa's Ex‑Miners
outcome: Distribution difference between local mineworker CXRs and international CXR datasets
effect: Dimensionality reduction showed local silica-exposed mineworker CXRs form a distinct cluster separate from international images, indicating dataset shift.
quote: Dimensionality reduction analysis produced visual mappings that demonstrate how local CXRs form a distinct cluster, separate from international images.

title: The Case for Local AI Development: Lessons From Computer‑Aided Detection of Tuberculosis and Silicosis in Southern Africa's Ex‑Miners
outcome: CAD detection performance under reduced image resolution, TB versus silicosis
effect: Reducing image resolution disproportionately degraded silicosis detection relative to TB; no numbers reported in abstract.
quote: We also found that, relative to TB, reducing image resolution disproportionately degraded silicosis detection.

title: Enhancing Preoperative Orthopaedic Communication: A Comparative Analysis of Large Language Model- and Clinician-Generated Clinic Letters
outcome: Readability grade level and PEMAT-P understandability of LLM vs clinician clinic letters
effect: LLM letters at seventh-eighth grade level; Flesch-Kincaid 6.850-8.517 vs clinician letters 10.6 ± 0.94; PEMAT-P 0.72-0.83 for LLMs vs 0.72 for human letters.
quote: All LLMs produced text at a seventh-eighth grade level; Flesch‑Kincaid 6.850-8.517, markedly simpler than human letters (10.6 ± 0.94).
sample_unit: LLM-generated clinic letters (4 LLMs x 6 procedures x 2 letters), plus clinician letters as benchmark

title: Evaluation of Large Language Models in the Diagnosis, Urgency Triage, and Initial Management of Ophthalmic Emergencies
outcome: Urgency recognition and red flag identification scores of LLMs on ophthalmic emergency vignettes
effect: Overall scores 6.88 (ChatGPT), 7.03 (Gemini), 6.93 (Claude) of 8; no significant differences in urgency triage or red flag recognition; diagnostic errors and suboptimal management noted.
quote: Additional comparison across diagnostic scores, urgency triage, red flag recognition, and management scores yielded no significant differences between any of the LLMs.

title: Comparative performance of GPT-4, GPT-o3, GPT-5, Gemini-3-Flash, and DeepSeek-R1 in ophthalmology question answering
venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
outcome: Inter-run response consistency (Fleiss' kappa) across three repeated runs per model
effect: GPT-o3 kappa 0.966, DeepSeek-R1 0.904, Gemini-3-Flash 0.860; GPT-5 lowest at 0.668, showing variable output reproducibility across models.
quote: GPT-5 exhibited the lowest stability (κ = 0.668).

title: Patient Education in Bariatric Surgery: Can Artificial Intelligence-Based Chatbots Bridge the Knowledge Gap?
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading level of chatbot responses to bariatric patient questions
effect: Most chatbot responses required reading levels between 11th grade and college level, exceeding recommended patient reading levels.
quote: The readability of chatbot responses was assessed using Flesch-Kincaid scores, revealing that most responses required reading levels between the 11th grade and college level.

title: Patient Education in Bariatric Surgery: Can Artificial Intelligence-Based Chatbots Bridge the Knowledge Gap?
outcome: Readability of chatbot-generated patient education responses
effect: Most responses required 11th grade to college reading level; readability often exceeds recommended levels.
quote: However, readability often exceeds recommended levels, performance varies by model, occasional inaccuracies occur, and medicolegal considerations remain unresolved.

title: Development and multicentre validation of an artificial intelligence electrocardiogram model for ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
outcome: AI-ECG discrimination and calibration variation across external sites
effect: AUROC ranged 0.69 to 0.88 across five sites (A 0.87, B 0.88, C 0.82, D 0.74, E 0.69); three of five sites met criteria for miscalibration.
quote: Notably, there was variation observed in AUROC across centres, which ranged from 0.69 to 0.88 (AUROC Site A: 0.87, B: 0.88, C: 0.82; D: 0.74, E: 0.69; see Supplementary material online , Figure S1 ).

title: Development and multicentre validation of an artificial intelligence electrocardiogram model for ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
outcome: Calibration after centre-specific Platt scaling at miscalibrated sites
effect: After within-centre calibration, model adequately calibrated with expected calibration error 6.1% (Spiegelhalter Z P=0.25); uncalibrated model showed negative net benefit across all centres.
quote: After within-centre calibration, the model was adequately calibrated with expected calibration error of 6.1% (Spiegelhalter Z test P = 0.25, Figure 2 ).

title: Development and multicentre validation of an artificial intelligence electrocardiogram model for ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
outcome: AI-ECG versus QRS duration model discrimination and net reduction in CMR
effect: AI-ECG AUROC 0.87 vs 0.78 for QRS duration; QRS model gave no net CMR reduction (-0.02) at 0.25 threshold.
quote: Artificial intelligence analysis of electrocardiograms outperformed QRS duration (AUROC 0.87 vs. 0.78, see Supplementary material online , Figure S3 ).

title: Development and multicentre validation of an artificial intelligence electrocardiogram model for ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
outcome: Calibration and net benefit of uncalibrated model across sites
effect: Miscalibration at one high-AUROC site (B); uncalibrated model showed negative net benefit when all centres considered.
quote: This shows that without proper consideration of calibration, a model may be harmful compared with the current standard of care when considered in the context of clinical risk tolerance.

title: Development and multicentre validation of an artificial intelligence electrocardiogram model for ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
outcome: Performance in external multisite validation versus expected generalizability
effect: External validation across five sites revealed two sites with suboptimal discrimination, indicating that standard external validation may not ensure generalizability.
quote: The current standards could be inadequate to ensure truly generalizable performance, which warrants further examination across the breadth of AI-ECG applications.

title: Development and multicentre validation of an artificial intelligence electrocardiogram model for ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
outcome: demographic and site performance
effect: No sex/race difference; age and site differences, with 2/5 sites lower AUROC and 3/5 miscalibrated.
quote: There was no difference by sex or race/ethnicity, but there were differences by age and site, with two of five sites with lower AUROC than the others, and three of five sites met criteria for miscalibration, which improved after centre-specific calibration.

title: Development and multicentre validation of an artificial intelligence electrocardiogram model for ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
outcome: Performance at local sites versus aggregate; need for local verification
effect: Two of five sites had lower AUROC and three of five miscalibrated; authors conclude local verification of discrimination and calibration is required.
quote: Based on the extensive external validation performed in this study, we conclude that local verification of discrimination and calibration is required.

title: Development and multicentre validation of an artificial intelligence electrocardiogram model for ventricular remodeling in repaired tetralogy of Fallot
outcome: AUROC across subgroups by sex, race/ethnicity, and age
effect: No difference by sex (P=0.18) or race/ethnicity (P=1.0); lower AUROC in <22 years vs older (0.73 vs 0.85; P=0.005).
quote: There was lower performance in children and young adults <22 years old vs. older adults (AUROC 0.73 vs. 0.85; P = 0.005).

title: Generating Job Recommendations for People With Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorder Using Gemini 2.0 Flash and Claude Sonnet 4: An Exploratory Analysis
outcome: Stereotyping and bias in LLM-generated job recommendations
effect: Both models showed little diversity and strong bias toward entry-level roles; demographic stereotypes such as age-based framing, gendered role allocation, and assumptions about language skills often shaped recommendations.
quote: Nor was there diversity in how roles were tailored to patient strengths, qualifications, or prior experience; instead, demographic stereotypes such as age-based framing, gendered role allocation, and assumptions about language skills often shaped the recommendations.
sample_unit: patient discharge summaries (450 schizophrenia spectrum, 50 controls), three recommendations each

title: AI-assisted interpretation of bone scans: Performance comparison between ChatGPT-4o and a TFDA-approved bone scintigraphy platform in AI-driven nuclear imaging interpretation
outcome: ChatGPT-4o vs domain-specific platform vs physician gold standard on same bone scans
effect: Binary accuracy 84.6% (ChatGPT-4o) vs 82.7% (platform); regional precision 32.5% vs 80.3%; regional sensitivity 13.3% vs 64.9%.
quote: In binary classification, ChatGPT-4o achieved an accuracy of 84.6%, similar to the performance of the BS platform's accuracy of 82.7%.

title: Artificial intelligence-generated patient information on shoulder instability remains suboptimal: DeepSeek outperforms ChatGPT in completeness of content while ChatGPT is more readable
venue: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
outcome: Reading level (FKGL, FRES) of LLM patient education responses on shoulder instability
effect: ChatGPT FKGL 7.78, FRES 52.44; DeepSeek FKGL 9.90, FRES 41.87; significant difference between models (FKGL p = 0.016; FRES p = 0.015).
quote: In terms of readability, ChatGPT had an average FKGL value of 7.78 and an FRES score of 52.44.

title: Artificial intelligence-generated patient information on shoulder instability remains suboptimal: DeepSeek outperforms ChatGPT in completeness of content while ChatGPT is more readable
venue: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of AI-generated patient education responses
effect: ChatGPT FKGL 7.78, FRES 52.44; DeepSeek FKGL 9.90, FRES 41.87 (harder to read); ChatGPT was more readable (FKGL p = 0.016; FRES p = 0.015).
quote: The DeepSeek model had an FKGL value of 9.90 and an FRES score of 41.87.

title: External validation of the PREVENT risk score: performance and clinical utility in an Iranian population
outcome: Effect of local recalibration-in-the-large on predicted risk, sensitivity, and net benefit
effect: Recalibration raised mean predicted risk in men from 4.2% to 7.6%, sensitivity from 62.4% to 79.9% at 5% threshold; net benefit rose modestly (0.0356 to 0.040 in men); NRI +61% men, +79% women.
quote: Calibration-in-the-large improved model performance in both sexes, most notably in men, increasing mean predicted risks to 7.6% in men and 4.3% in women.
sample_unit: adults in a community-based cohort (Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study)

title: External validation of the PREVENT risk score: performance and clinical utility in an Iranian population
outcome: Calibration of PREVENT on a local cohort versus developer evidence
effect: Original model underestimated risk in men (mean predicted 4.2% vs observed ASCVD incidence higher) while well calibrated in women; AUC 0.84 women, 0.76 men.
quote: The basic model was well calibrated for women, particularly at low-to-intermediate risk levels, but underestimated risk in men.
sample_unit: adults in a community-based cohort (Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study)

title: External validation of the PREVENT risk score: performance and clinical utility in an Iranian population
outcome: Sex-specific discrimination and calibration performance
effect: AUC 0.84 (0.82-0.86) in women vs 0.76 (0.74-0.78) in men; risk underestimated in men but not women.
quote: Using the published 10-year logistic PREVENT equations, discrimination was higher in women (AUC 0.84 [0.82–0.86]) than in men (AUC 0.76 [0.74–0.78]) (Fig. 1 ).
sample_unit: adults in a community-based cohort (Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study)

title: External validation of the PREVENT risk score: performance and clinical utility in an Iranian population
outcome: Generalization of US-developed model to a new Iranian population
effect: PREVENT underestimated risk in Iranian men, needing recalibration; sensitivity 62.4% in men at 5% threshold before recalibration.
quote: However, the original model underestimated risk in Iranian men, indicating the need for recalibration to improve alignment with the local risk profile.
sample_unit: adults in a community-based cohort (Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study)

title: External validation of the PREVENT risk score: performance and clinical utility in an Iranian population
outcome: Dataset shift between US development and Iranian population affecting calibration
effect: Model developed in US underestimated risk in Iranian men; authors attribute differences to age distribution, baseline risk, follow-up, and population differences.
quote: Differences in discrimination across studies are likely attributable to variations in the age distribution, baseline risk, and follow-up duration of the study population.
sample_unit: adults in a community-based cohort (Tehran Lipid and Glucose Study)

title: Impact of Test Set Composition on AI Performance for Pediatric Radiograph Appendicular Skeleton Fracture Detection
outcome: AI fracture detection performance on difficult versus matched internal test sets
effect: Difficult set associated with 40% decreased odds of correct classification (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.53-0.68) for EfficientNet and 80% decreased odds of detection (OR 0.20, 95% CI 0.17-0.25) for YOLOv8.
quote: The difficult internal test set (392 patients, 786 radiographs) was associated with a 40% decrease in odds of a correct classification compared with the matched internal test set (526 patients, 786 radiographs) for EfficientNet variants (OR, 0.60 [95% CI: 0.53, 0.68]; P < .001).

title: Artificial intelligence-based smartphone application for skin cancer detection: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Diagnostic performance across smartphone models and image capture in user hands
effect: Image-capture success in user hands was 28.9%; diagnostic performance varied between smartphone models.
quote: A substudy demonstrated low image-capture success in user hands (28.9%) and variation in diagnostic performance between smartphone models.

title: Artificial intelligence-based smartphone application for skin cancer detection: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Image capture failure under real-world clinical conditions
effect: Image capture failed for 16.6% of lesions (317/1904) despite optimal conditions.
quote: Image capture was unsuccessful in 16.6% of lesions (n = 317/1904), despite optimal conditions.

title: Artificial intelligence-based smartphone application for skin cancer detection: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of CNN alone vs CNN plus teledermatology review
effect: CNN alone: sensitivity 82.5%, specificity 76.8%. With teledermatology review: specificity rose to 86.8% (P < 0.001) but sensitivity fell to 75.3%.
quote: Combined CNN and teledermatology review resulted in increased specificity (86.8%; P < 0.001), with a sensitivity of 75.3%.

title: Artificial intelligence-based smartphone application for skin cancer detection: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Image-capture success under patient-user conditions
effect: Image-capture success in user hands was 28.9%.
quote: A substudy demonstrated low image-capture success in user hands (28.9%) and variation in diagnostic performance between smartphone models.

title: Artificial intelligence-based smartphone application for skin cancer detection: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Skin cancer detection sensitivity and specificity after teledermatology review
effect: Adding teledermatology review increased specificity from 76.8% to 86.8% (P < 0.001), while sensitivity decreased from 82.5% to 75.3%.
quote: Combined CNN and teledermatology review resulted in increased specificity (86.8%; P < 0.001), with a sensitivity of 75.3%.

title: Artificial intelligence-based smartphone application for skin cancer detection: a prospective diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: diagnostic accuracy of combined human-AI team
effect: Adding teledermatology review to the AI output increased specificity to 86.8% but resulted in a lower sensitivity of 75.3% compared to standalone metrics.
quote: Combined CNN and teledermatology review resulted in increased specificity (86.8%; P < 0.001), with a sensitivity of 75.3%.

title: AI- vs Human-Based Assessment of Medical Interview Transcripts in a Generative AI-Simulated Patient System: Cross-Sectional Validation Study
outcome: Repeatability of AI scores across 5 runs with different random seeds
effect: ABA ICC(3,1) 0.77 (o1) and 0.82 (GPT-5); coefficient of variation 6.6% for ABA vs 13.9% for human raters; ICC(2,1) 0.38 for humans.
quote: The coefficient of variation for ABA was approximately half that of HBA (6.6% vs 13.9%).

title: Assessing large language models as assistive tools in selecting first trial lens parameters for orthokeratology
outcome: Feasibility errors and systematic bias in LLM-suggested first trial lens parameters
effect: Feasibility errors decreased across two correction rounds; outputs showed systematic bias toward smaller BC radius and larger RZD, with most Bland-Altman observations within 95% limits of agreement.
quote: However, first trial-lens parameter selection required feasibility constraints and clinician verification, with systematic parameter bias mainly involving BC and RZD.

title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
outcome: Consistency of LLM outputs across 3 repeated sessions on 15 cases
effect: Percentage agreement varied widely; e.g., HAS-BLED agreement 26.67% (DeepSeek-R1), 40% (ChatGPT-4o Deep Research), 46.67% (DeepSeek-V3); regimen agreement 60-80%.
quote: The consistency levels of the 3 models varied across tasks; although ChatGPT-4o Deep Research demonstrated relatively stable performance in most domains, its consistency was comparatively lower in the anticoagulation regimen task.
sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
outcome: LLM HAS-BLED scoring accuracy against multidisciplinary team reference standard
effect: HAS-BLED accuracy was low across all models (8%-51%); best model ChatGPT-4o Deep Research reached only 51%.
quote: In contrast, performance of the HAS-BLED scoring task was suboptimal for all models; even the best-performing model (ChatGPT-4o Deep Research) achieved an accuracy of only 51%.
sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
outcome: Comparison of 9 LLMs against each other on NVAF anticoagulation tasks
effect: Models varied substantially across 6 tasks; ChatGPT-4o Deep Research ranked first overall, DeepSeek-V3 lowest; no single model best across all tasks.
quote: The results showed that no single model performed optimally across all tasks.
sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
outcome: Errors in risk score calculation and dosing regimen accuracy
