effect: Anticoagulation regimen (drug, dose, frequency) accuracy ranged 33%-89%; CHA2DS2-VASc accuracy 20%-100%; errors included double-counting and self-contradiction.
quote: In contrast, performance of the HAS-BLED scoring task was suboptimal for all models; even the best-performing model (ChatGPT-4o Deep Research) achieved an accuracy of only 51%.
sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
outcome: HAS-BLED accuracy after adding guideline criteria to prompt
effect: After prompt modification, DeepSeek-R1 increased 24% to 89%; ChatGPT-4o Deep Research increased 51% to 95%; P < .001.
quote: Specifically, the accuracy of DeepSeek-R1 increased from 24% to 89%, while that of ChatGPT-4o Deep Research improved from 51% to 95%.
sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
outcome: HAS-BLED scoring accuracy before vs after prompt optimization with guideline criteria
effect: DeepSeek-R1 accuracy rose from 24% to 89%, ChatGPT-4o Deep Research from 51% to 95% (P < .001).
quote: Specifically, the accuracy of DeepSeek-R1 increased from 24% to 89%, while that of ChatGPT-4o Deep Research improved from 51% to 95%.
sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
outcome: Reliability of LLMs as stand-alone anticoagulation decision-makers
effect: Accuracy varied widely and HAS-BLED accuracy was low (8%-51%); authors conclude LLMs remain unsuitable as stand-alone decision-makers.
quote: At the current stage, LLMs are better suited as auxiliary tools for medical tasks rather than as independent decision-makers.
sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

title: Performance evaluation of 9 large language models in anticoagulation decision-making for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation
venue: Research and practice in thrombosis and haemostasis
outcome: Stand-alone anticoagulation decision-making
effect: No single model was optimal; HAS-BLED accuracy 8%-51%, regimen selection 33%-89%, monitoring mean 2.55-4.98.
quote: At present, LLMs may serve as valuable adjuncts to clinical practice but remain unsuitable for use as stand-alone decision-makers.
sample_unit: LLM responses (100 virtual NVAF patient cases x 9 LLMs)

title: Examining Artificial Intelligence Chatbots' Responses in Providing Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Information for Young Adults: Qualitative Content Analysis
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and Reading Ease) of chatbot HPV vaccine responses
effect: Mean FKGL: ChatGPT 10.7, Claude 13.2, DeepSeek 11.3, Docus 12.2; Reading Ease means 32.5-46.8. Some responses included medical jargon.
quote: Improvements in readability, personalization, and link accuracy are still needed.

title: Examining Artificial Intelligence Chatbots' Responses in Providing Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Information for Young Adults: Qualitative Content Analysis
outcome: Whether chatbots defer complex questions to health care professionals
effect: All 4 chatbots appropriately deferred complex questions to health care professionals' suggestions.
quote: For complex questions, all AI chatbots appropriately deferred to health care professionals' suggestions.

title: Examining Artificial Intelligence Chatbots' Responses in Providing Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Information for Young Adults: Qualitative Content Analysis
outcome: Accuracy and validity of sources and citations in chatbot responses
effect: All chatbots cited reputable sources with no fabricated information, but some responses included broken or irrelevant links.
quote: Occasionally, some responses included broken or irrelevant links and medical jargon.

title: The understandability and actionability of AI-generated information for patients with chronic kidney disease
outcome: PEMAT understandability and actionability of AI-generated CKD patient information versus expert webpages
effect: Understandability was similar for AI and expert information (67.2% vs 63.4%, P=0.06). Actionability was lower for AI (27.9% vs 37.1%, P<0.01). Gemini scored higher than ChatGPT and Copilot on both measures.
quote: There was no significant differences between AI responses and expert information in terms of understandability (mean±SD: AI vs expert, 67.2%±14.0% vs 63.4%±15.9 %, P = 0.06).

title: Assessing multimodal large language models for localizing dental implant fixtures on panoramic radiographs
outcome: Run-to-run reproducibility of implant fixture detection across five independent runs
effect: Fixtures detected in all five runs were 1.01% (GPT-4o), 22.22% (OpenAI o3), and 25.93% (GPT-5T).
quote: The fixtures detected in all five runs were 1.01 % (GPT-4o), 22.22 % (OpenAI o3), and 25.93 % (GPT-5T).
sample_unit: panoramic radiographs (82 implant-present with 297 fixtures, 82 implant-absent), five runs each

title: Assessing multimodal large language models for localizing dental implant fixtures on panoramic radiographs
outcome: Zero-shot localization performance of general-purpose multimodal LLMs on dental radiographs
effect: Micro sensitivity was 16.97% for GPT-4o, 68.82% for o3, and 65.66% for GPT-5T; specificity on implant-absent images 32.68%, 65.85%, 68.54%.
quote: Reasoning-focused multimodal LLMs outperformed GPT-4o in zero-shot implant fixture localization and reduced false positives, but moderate sensitivity, restoration-driven errors, and run-to-run variability limit autonomous clinical use.
sample_unit: panoramic radiographs (82 implant-present with 297 fixtures, 82 implant-absent), five runs each

title: Addressing the balance between fairness and performance in glioma grade prediction using bias mitigation techniques
outcome: Fairness metrics and prediction performance after reweighting and equalized-odds mitigation across race and gender groups
effect: For race, reweighting with logistic regression worsened outcomes for the under-represented group and increased unfairness, while equalized-odds post-processing improved results for the under-represented group and significantly improved fairness.
quote: For the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant improvements in fairness.
sample_unit: patients (TCGA glioma dataset; count not reported in text)

title: Addressing the balance between fairness and performance in glioma grade prediction using bias mitigation techniques
outcome: Performance and fairness disparities by race and gender in glioma grade prediction
effect: Demographic bias, most severe for race, was found in glioma grading classifiers; disparate impact, equal opportunity difference and error rate difference were evaluated by group.
quote: For the most severe bias (race), the pre-trained logistic regression model using the reweighting algorithm shows some deterioration in prediction outcomes for the under-represented group and even an increase in unfairness, while the post-processing approach improves results for the under-represented group and provides significant improvements in fairness.
sample_unit: patients (TCGA glioma dataset; count not reported in text)

title: Benchmarking large language model-based agent systems for clinical decision tasks
outcome: Agent system accuracy versus baseline LLMs on the same clinical benchmarks, plus token and latency cost
effect: Agent systems gave only modest accuracy gains over baseline LLMs (60.3% AgentClinic MedQA, 28.0% MIMIC, 30.3% MedAgentsBench, 8.6% HLE text), with >10x token usage and >2x latency.
quote: Despite access to advanced tools (e.g., web browsing, code development and execution, and text file editing) agent systems yielded only modest accuracy gains over baseline LLMs, reaching 60.3% and 28.0% in AgentClinic MedQA and MIMIC, 30.3% on MedAgentsBench, and 8.6% on HLE text.

title: Benchmarking large language model-based agent systems for clinical decision tasks
outcome: Share of hallucinations filtered by in-agent safeguards
effect: 89.9% of hallucinations were filtered by in-agent safeguards, but hallucinations remained prevalent.
quote: Although 89.9% of hallucinations were filtered by in-agent safeguards, hallucinations remained prevalent.

title: Diagnosing growth in low-grade gliomas with and without artificial intelligence-measured longitudinal volume measurements: A retrospective observational study
outcome: False positive and false negative rates of AI volumetry with versus without physician review
effect: AI without human review had 25% false positives (4/16) and 8.33% false negatives (4/48); with physician review all 7 negative controls were correctly identified as stable.
quote: The performance of the volumetric analysis using the change-point method varied significantly depending on whether human review was involved.

title: Diagnosing growth in low-grade gliomas with and without artificial intelligence-measured longitudinal volume measurements: A retrospective observational study
outcome: Time to tumor growth detection by AI volumetry versus radiologist visual inspection
effect: AI with human review detected growth a median of 21 months earlier than visual inspection in the clinical progression group, and 23 months earlier than last MRI in 13/22 clinically stable cases.
quote: The results demonstrate that volumetric analysis calculated by AI segmentation followed by human review detects tumor growth significantly earlier than traditional visual inspection by radiologists (median of 21 months, Table 1 , and Figure 1 ).

title: Diagnosing growth in low-grade gliomas with and without artificial intelligence-measured longitudinal volume measurements: A retrospective observational study
outcome: Accuracy of AI-only versus AI with physician oversight for detecting tumor growth
effect: AI alone yielded 25% false positive and 8.33% false negative rates, including 3/7 negative controls wrongly flagged; with physician review all 7 controls were correctly stable.
quote: In contrast, without human oversight, 3 out of 7 cases were incorrectly flagged as tumor growth.

title: Diagnosing growth in low-grade gliomas with and without artificial intelligence-measured longitudinal volume measurements: A retrospective observational study
outcome: Standalone AI growth-call errors
effect: AI without human review had 25% (4/16) false positives and 8.33% (4/48) false negatives.
quote: AI without human review generated similar results but with a 25% false positive and an 8.33% false negative rate.

title: A Therapeutic Conversational Agent (Solace) for Management of Chronic Pain: Acceptability and Usability Study
outcome: Whether safety guardrails identified and managed suicidal ideation, injury, and medication recommendation requests
effect: Guardrails for suicidal ideation, injury, and medication recommendation requests performed appropriately during the study; no counts reported in the abstract.
quote: Safety guardrails designed to identify and manage instances of suicidal ideation, injury, or requests for medication recommendations performed appropriately during the study.

title: Vision transformer-based diagnosis of psoriasis and eczema in whole-slide histology
venue: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
outcome: AI accuracy versus dermatopathologists and baseline CNNs on same external cohort
effect: Virchow + CLAM 85% accuracy on external cohort vs individual readers 47.5-70.0%, consensus 62.5%, baseline CNNs 61%.
quote: In a reader study on the same external cohort, individual dermatopathologist accuracies ranged from 47.5 to 70.0%, with a majority-vote consensus accuracy of 62.5%; our method outperformed both the average individual reader and the consensus under histology-only conditions.

title: Vision transformer-based diagnosis of psoriasis and eczema in whole-slide histology
venue: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
outcome: Performance on an independent external validation cohort
effect: Best configuration achieved 85% accuracy, macro-F1 0.80, AUC 0.81 on the external cohort (n=40).
quote: Using an internal dataset (n = 40) and an external validation cohort (n = 40), equally balanced between both conditions and annotated by board-certified dermatopathologists, our best-performing configuration (Virchow + CLAM) achieved 85% accuracy, a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.80, and an AUC of 0.81 on the external cohort.

title: Evaluating the Clinical Decision-Making Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence in Common Geriatric Syndromes Using Evidence-Based Guidelines
outcome: Completeness and guideline alignment of ChatGPT clinical responses to geriatric vignettes, including omissions
effect: Completeness 55/70, accuracy 59/70, guideline alignment 61/70; reviewers identified key omissions such as missing assessments or guideline-recommended tools in multiple vignettes; urinary incontinence scored lowest.
quote: Reviewers identified key omissions, such as missing assessments or guideline-recommended tools, in multiple vignettes.
sample_unit: standardized geriatric vignettes (each rated by 5 geriatricians)

title: A Longitudinal Analysis of the Usefulness, Readability, Consistency, and Capacity of Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Responses Regarding the Reality of Chronic Pain in Children
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of chatbot responses to pediatric chronic pain prompt
effect: With explicit scoring criteria, all chatbots attained readability below 7th grade; January 2025 responses showed substantial readability improvements versus January 2024.
quote: When provided with explicit scoring criteria, all systems achieved maximum usefulness scores (10/10) and attained a readability level below the 7th grade.
sample_unit: chatbot responses (4 chatbots x 10 prompts) in January 2025

title: Evaluation of validity, reliability, and readability of AI chatbots for gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-model comparative study
outcome: Readability of chatbot GDM patient education text versus recommended sixth-grade level
effect: All models produced text above the recommended sixth-grade reading level; ChatGPT-5 best (FKGL 7.43 ± 2.42, FRES 62.47 ± 13.51) but still did not meet guideline targets.
quote: All models produced text above the recommended sixth-grade reading level; ChatGPT-5 showed the most favorable readability profile (for example, FKGL 7.43 ± 2.42, FRES 62.47 ± 13.51) but still did not meet guideline targets.

title: Evaluation of validity, reliability, and readability of AI chatbots for gestational diabetes mellitus: a multi-model comparative study
outcome: Readability of chatbot-generated patient education content
effect: All four chatbots exceeded the sixth-grade reading level; even the best (ChatGPT-5) had FKGL 7.43 and did not meet guideline targets.
quote: All models produced text above the recommended sixth-grade reading level; ChatGPT-5 showed the most favorable readability profile (for example, FKGL 7.43 ± 2.42, FRES 62.47 ± 13.51) but still did not meet guideline targets.

title: Large language models with image processing in automated Cobb angle
venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
outcome: Accuracy of general-purpose multimodal LLMs in Cobb angle measurement versus radiologist reference standard
effect: Gemini produced no Cobb angles; ChatGPT failed on 90 radiographs (MAE 58.6°±45.9°); Perplexity and Grok mean differences 18.8° and 24.2°; all exceeded the clinically accepted ≤10% difference.
quote: All AI models demonstrated a difference greater than the clinically accepted difference (≤ 10%).

title: AI decision support for increasing prostate biopsy efficiency: a retrospective multicentre, multiscanner study
outcome: AI-DSS performance validated across multiple centres and scanners
effect: Independent validation cohort of 252 men from six UK centres (multiscanner); AI-DSS at 31% CDR avoided 28 biopsies while missing one ≥GG2 cancer.
quote: An AI-DSS integrating PI-RADS scores, automated prostate-specific antigen density (PSAd), and deep-learning imaging risk scores was developed on 770 cases and validated on an independent cohort of 252 men from six UK centres.

title: Self-supervised out-of-distribution detection-Metal implants and other anomaly
outcome: Detection of anomalous/out-of-distribution CT inputs in prospective and external test sets
effect: Prospective TP rate 86.11% despite under-documentation of anomalies in reports; external AbdominalCT-1k TP rate 75.26% with 24.7% FP rate, mostly from anomalies outside the body.
quote: Prospective analysis showed the model was able to handle the under-documentation of anomaly in radiology reports with 86.11% true positive (TP) rate.

title: Self-supervised out-of-distribution detection-Metal implants and other anomaly
outcome: Performance drop from internal to external validation due to artifacts and implants
effect: Model performance often drops on external validation because of artifacts from motion and implants not accounted for in curated training data.
quote: Despite the high precision of deep learning models on internal tests on CT, their effectiveness often drops on external validation due to artifacts caused by patient motion and implants like metal or silicone that were not accounted for in the carefully curated training data.

title: Performance of Large Language Models Under Input Variability in Health Care Applications: Dataset Development and Experimental Evaluation
outcome: LLM performance under redaction, homophone, and typo perturbations at varying levels
effect: Performance stable or improved in 151/270 (55.92%) cases; improved in 38/270 (14.07%); redactions were more detrimental than other variations.
quote: Contrary to expectations, LLMs demonstrate notable robustness to common variations, and in more than half of the cases (151/270, 55.92%), the performance was stable or improved.

title: Generative AI in preanesthetic consultations: Effects on efficiency, documentation workload, quality, and physician-patient interaction: A simulation trial
outcome: External rater documentation quality (PDQI-9) of AI-generated versus manual preanesthetic reports
effect: External raters judged documentation quality higher for manual reports (+4 PDQI-9 points; p = 0.004); clinicians less confident in AI-generated formatting.
quote: However, external raters judged documentation quality to be higher for manual reports (+4 PDQI-9 points; p = 0.004), and clinicians expressed less confidence in AI-generated formatting.

title: Large Language Models for Accurate Medical Chart Abstraction: Enabling Scalable and Secure Artificial Intelligence Deployment in Stroke
outcome: Accuracy of nonexpert staff annotations versus expert adjudication as reference standard
effect: Nonexpert staff annotations, used as the reference standard, were outperformed by LLaMA3.3-70B in 7 of 8 variables on expert adjudication; annotation accuracy rose with clinical experience.
quote: Expert adjudication confirmed that LLaMA3.3-70B outperformed nonexpert annotations in 7 of 8 variables and matched junior medical students.

title: Hallucination filtering in radiology vision-language models using discrete semantic entropy
outcome: Accuracy of VLM answers after deferring/excluding high-semantic-entropy questions
effect: Filtering DSE > 0.3 raised accuracy from 51.7% to 76.3% for GPT-4o (334/706 retained) and 54.8% to 63.8% for GPT-4.1 (499/706 retained), both p < 0.001.
quote: After filtering out high-entropy questions (DSE > 0.3), accuracy on the remaining questions was 76.3% (retained questions: 334/706) for GPT-4o and 63.8% (retained questions: 499/706) for GPT-4.1 (both p < 0.001).

title: Hallucination filtering in radiology vision-language models using discrete semantic entropy
outcome: Uncertainty-based filtering of hallucination-prone questions improving answer accuracy
effect: DSE filtering at a 0.3 threshold increased GPT-4o accuracy from 51.7% to 76.3% and GPT-4.1 from 54.8% to 63.8%, while answering fewer questions.
quote: DSE filtering at a 0.3 threshold increased GPT-4o accuracy from 51.7% to 76.3% and GPT-4.1 from 54.8% to 63.8%, while answering fewer questions.

title: Defining operational safety in clinical artificial intelligence systems
outcome: Head-to-head comparison of two FDA-cleared mammography AIs on same data for operational safety
effect: AI #1 had higher AUC (0.928 vs 0.882), but at alpha=100% AI #2 ruled out 290 true negatives (29.0%) vs 167 (16.7%) for AI #1; difference 123 cases (95% CI 87.0–150.0).
quote: This represents a substantial improvement over AI #1, which cleared only 167 cases (16.7% of the cohort), with a difference of 123 cases in the Rule-out Safe Zone in favor of AI #2 (95% confidence interval: 87.0–150.0).

title: Defining operational safety in clinical artificial intelligence systems
outcome: Deriving decision thresholds from clinician-defined PPV/NPV targets or utility maximization
effect: Different policies (balanced, high-precision referral, high-volume screening, strictly non-negligent, minimize FP harm) produced different thresholds and Gray Zone workloads on the same model; demonstrated, not tested against a comparator.
quote: Beyond direct rules, the framework navigates more complex scenarios by maximizing a clinical utility function that weighs the nuanced costs of errors against the benefits of correct decisions.

title: Defining operational safety in clinical artificial intelligence systems
outcome: AUC concealed operational safety
effect: AI #1 had higher AUC than AI #2 (0.928 vs. 0.882) but at α=100% cleared 167 cases (16.7%) versus AI #2's 290 (29.0%).
quote: Although AI Solution #1 demonstrated a higher AUC than AI Solution #2 (0.928 vs. 0.882; Fig. 3a , b ), this advantage translated to better operational efficiency only for less stringent tasks, as evidenced by its more rapid Gray Zone reduction at moderate safety levels ( α < 95%; Fig. 3c ).

title: Defining operational safety in clinical artificial intelligence systems
outcome: Whether AUC alone versus reliability-based operational metrics distinguishes model safety
effect: Models with nearly identical AUC 0.960 had Gray Zone Areas of 0.709 vs 0.344; the higher-AUC FDA-cleared model was less safe for high-confidence rule-out.
quote: This result shows that the AUC can be misleading and that models should be evaluated for their operational safety to understand their true clinical utility.

title: Guidelines vs. generative AI in CKD patient education: the role of prompt engineering and expert blinded evaluation
outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of LLM CKD responses with structured plain-language prompt vs unstructured prompt
effect: Structured prompt lowered FKGL from 11.34 to 7.87 (ChatGPT) and 9.62 to 7.13 (Gemini); FRE rose to 64.23 and 61.45; p < 0.001.
quote: Providing a structured prompt made the responses of both models significantly easier to read and reduced the required educational level to below high school (7th grade level).

title: Guidelines vs. generative AI in CKD patient education: the role of prompt engineering and expert blinded evaluation
outcome: Reading grade level of AI patient education responses with reading-level-targeted prompt vs default
effect: Prompt specifying elementary-school comprehension reduced FKGL by over 3 grade levels to about 7th grade; unstructured ChatGPT was 11.34 (high school senior).
quote: The reduction in FKGL by over 3 grade levels underscores prompt engineering’s potential as a low-cost intervention to enhance health accessibility.

title: Guidelines vs. generative AI in CKD patient education: the role of prompt engineering and expert blinded evaluation
outcome: expert rating agreement
effect: Total-score ICC was 0.55, indicating moderate inter-rater agreement among evaluators.
quote: The ICC value was 0.55, indicating moderate agreement among the evaluators.

title: Guidelines vs. generative AI in CKD patient education: the role of prompt engineering and expert blinded evaluation
outcome: output reproducibility across sessions
effect: Each prompt ran in two independent sessions; qualitative review found semantic consistency and no significant medical-accuracy or core-recommendation deviations.

title: Evaluating the Accuracy and Diagnostic Reasoning of Multimodal Large Language Models in Interpreting Neuroradiology Cases From RadioGraphics
outcome: LLM performance and reasoning when textual clinical history was absent, and across temperature settings
effect: GPT-4V (T1) identified both lesion location and imaging findings in 30.7% (123 of 401) and 12.9% (16 of 124) of cases without textual clinical history; performance declined without clinical history text.
quote: LLMs remarkably underperformed compared with neuroradiologists and showed unsatisfactory reasoning for their differential diagnoses, with performance declining further in cases without textual input of clinical history.

title: Simulated evaluation of large language model stepwise diagnostic reasoning with real-world chest pain encounters and Bayesian networks
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Suitability of LLM diagnostic output for autonomous use
effect: Configuration miscalibrated and not suitable for clinical deployment; authors support cautious stance against autonomous diagnostic use and recommend clinician oversight.
quote: More broadly, our findings suggest that current diagnostic LLMs remain highly sensitive to prompt context and struggle with real-world clinical probabilities, supporting a cautious stance toward autonomous or patient-facing diagnostic use.

title: Simulated evaluation of large language model stepwise diagnostic reasoning with real-world chest pain encounters and Bayesian networks
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: emergent diagnosis recognition
effect: No-category prompt: 19 TP, 198 FN; sensitivity 8.8% (5.7–13.3), specificity 94.7% (91.4–96.8).
quote: Removing diagnostic category constraints further increased specificity (94.7%, 95% CI 91.4–96.8) with minimal sensitivity (8.8%, 95% CI 5.7–13.3).

title: Simulated evaluation of large language model stepwise diagnostic reasoning with real-world chest pain encounters and Bayesian networks
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: LLM diagnostic performance in stepwise simulation with real ED data versus static vignette expectations
effect: In simulated stepwise setting with real data, GPT-4o over-predicted rare conditions (sensitivity 79.3%, specificity 45.2%) and diverged from physicians and BN-optimal pathways (RBO 0.060-0.097).
quote: The relatively low diagnostic accuracy we observed may partly reflect this closer adherence to real-world complexity.

title: Simulated evaluation of large language model stepwise diagnostic reasoning with real-world chest pain encounters and Bayesian networks
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Accuracy of LLM differential/diagnosis selection for emergent chest pain conditions
effect: Baseline over-called emergent conditions (specificity 45.2%); with prevalence cues or no categories, sensitivity fell to 30.4% and 8.8%, missing emergent diagnoses.
quote: With baseline prompting, GPT-4o systematically over-predicted rare conditions (sensitivity 79.3%; specificity 45.2%); adding prevalence cues or removing diagnostic category constraints respectively increased specificity (83.0% and 94.7%) while reducing false alarms by 107 and 140 per 500, but at the cost of poor sensitivity (30.4% and 8.8%).

title: Simulated evaluation of large language model stepwise diagnostic reasoning with real-world chest pain encounters and Bayesian networks
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: diagnostic stability under prompt changes
effect: Prevalence cues/no-category prompts raised specificity to 83.0%/94.7% but reduced sensitivity to 30.4%/8.8%, from baseline 79.3% sensitivity and 45.2% specificity.
quote: With baseline prompting, GPT-4o systematically over-predicted rare conditions (sensitivity 79.3%; specificity 45.2%); adding prevalence cues or removing diagnostic category constraints respectively increased specificity (83.0% and 94.7%) while reducing false alarms by 107 and 140 per 500, but at the cost of poor sensitivity (30.4% and 8.8%).

title: Simulated evaluation of large language model stepwise diagnostic reasoning with real-world chest pain encounters and Bayesian networks
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: diagnostic output accuracy
effect: Baseline sensitivity 79.3%, specificity 45.2%; prevalence/no-category prompts reduced false alarms by 107/140 per 500 but sensitivity fell to 30.4%/8.8%.
quote: With baseline prompting, GPT-4o systematically over-predicted rare conditions (sensitivity 79.3%; specificity 45.2%); adding prevalence cues or removing diagnostic category constraints respectively increased specificity (83.0% and 94.7%) while reducing false alarms by 107 and 140 per 500, but at the cost of poor sensitivity (30.4% and 8.8%).

title: Accuracy of the GPT-5 Mini in Predicting Six-Week Postoperative Knee Flexion Following Total Knee Replacement: A Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: GPT-5 mini prediction error in knee flexion across patient subgroups (age, ASA grade, diabetes, smoking, BMI)
effect: Median actual flexion 95° vs predicted 103°; median absolute error 10°. Absolute error differed by ASA grade (I: 17°, II: 9°, III: 6°, p < 0.001). BMI showed no association with error.
quote: Absolute error differed significantly by ASA grade (I: 17°, II: 9°, III: 6°, p < 0.001).

title: Emily vs. Lakisha: Quantifying socioeconomic and structural disparities in AI-generated ovarian cancer care plans
outcome: Change in LLM output when patient race proxy name and geography varied in vignettes
effect: Models were 16.8 times more likely (OR: 16.80) to introduce unprompted cost warnings for 'Lakisha' compared to 'Emily,' regardless of location; clinical guideline adherence remained high across demographics.
quote: Sensitivity analysis revealed that 'Financial Fixation' was driven almost exclusively by Race (p < 0.001), with models being 16.8 times more likely (OR: 16.80) to introduce unprompted cost warnings for 'Lakisha' compared to 'Emily,' regardless of location.

title: Emily vs. Lakisha: Quantifying socioeconomic and structural disparities in AI-generated ovarian cancer care plans
outcome: Population-specific biased or stereotyped content in LLM-generated ovarian cancer care plans
effect: Models hallucinated financial scarcity from onomastic signals and failed to prioritize logistical solutions for rural patients; severe structural incompetence for the Black/Rural intersectional phenotype.
quote: By hallucinating financial scarcity based on onomastic signals and failing to prioritize logistical solutions for rural patients, these models risk imposing a cognitive burden on physicians and inducing "algorithmic redlining."

title: A Novel Hybrid Large Language Model Approach for Reporting Panoramic Radiographs and Performance Comparison with Current Large Language Models
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Hallucination rate in radiograph reports, grounded hybrid LLMs versus ungrounded commercial LLMs
effect: Hybrid LLMs grounded in structured image-derived findings had 30 (DeepSeek R1) to 60 (Gemma 3) hallucinations; commercial LLMs hallucinated in 100% of reports.
quote: Commercial LLMs (ChatGPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek R1-cloud) exhibited hallucinations in 100% of reports.

title: Evaluating large language models for clinical note processing: local fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Change in concept extraction F1 and QA ROUGE-L/BLEU after fine-tuning on local EHR data
effect: Local fine-tuning yielded a 7.5% to 15% increase in F1 for MCE and a 27% to 53% increase in ROUGE-L and BLEU for MQA.
quote: However, fine-tuning the LLMs with local EHR data significantly improved model performance across both tasks, yielding a 7.5% to 15% increase in the F1 score for MCE and a 27% to 53% increase in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA.
sample_unit: clinical notes (50 discharge summaries, 150 SOAP notes)

title: Evaluating large language models for clinical note processing: local fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Performance of models fine-tuned on public data when externally validated on local Pakistani EHR data
effect: External validation on local data was poorer than internal validation, with reductions of at least 15% in F1 for MCE and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU for MQA.
quote: When clinical LLMs were not fine-tuned on the local EHR dataset, their performance during external validation on local data was notably poorer compared to internal validation on the dataset used for fine-tuning, with reductions of at least 15% in F1 scores for MCE and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA tasks.
sample_unit: clinical notes (50 discharge summaries, 150 SOAP notes)

title: Evaluating large language models for clinical note processing: local fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Dataset shift between US-derived development data and local Pakistani EHR data degrading performance
effect: Performance of models fine-tuned on public data dropped significantly on SKMCH&RC data, and vice versa, indicating performance incompatibility across datasets.
quote: In general, for open-source LLMs, including GatorTron, BioMegatron, ClinicalBERT, and BioBERT, when we fine-tuned the models on publicly accessible data for the purpose of our NLP tasks, their performance significantly reduced when tested on SKMCH&RC, and vice versa in both NLP tasks.
sample_unit: clinical notes (50 discharge summaries, 150 SOAP notes)

title: Evaluating large language models for clinical note processing: local fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Benchmark performance versus performance on real-world local clinical notes
effect: Models scored highly on public benchmarks (e.g., F1 0.83-0.96) but dropped on local notes (e.g., 3-label F1 0.58-0.71); benchmark-only evaluation is limited.
quote: These findings highlight the sensitivity of LLM performance to data distribution and underscore the limitations of relying solely on benchmark-based evaluations to assess real-world reliability.
sample_unit: clinical notes (50 discharge summaries, 150 SOAP notes)

title: Evaluating large language models for clinical note processing: local fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Translation of benchmark performance to real local EHR data conditions
effect: Models fine-tuned on public benchmarks performed notably worse on real-world local EHR notes; ChatGPT was an exception, performing better locally.
quote: Publicly available LLMs, predominantly trained on data from high-income regions, were found to be unreliable when applied in a real-world clinical setting in Pakistan.
sample_unit: clinical notes (50 discharge summaries, 150 SOAP notes)

title: Evaluating large language models for clinical note processing: local fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: External validation performance on local EHR data
effect: External local validation showed reductions of at least 15% in MCE F1 and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU for MQA versus internal validation.
quote: RESULTS: When clinical LLMs were not fine-tuned on the local EHR dataset, their performance during external validation on local data was notably poorer compared to internal validation on the dataset used for fine-tuning, with reductions of at least 15% in F1 scores for MCE and 35% in ROUGE-L and BLEU scores for MQA tasks.
sample_unit: clinical notes (50 discharge summaries, 150 SOAP notes)

title: Evaluating large language models for clinical note processing: local fine-tuning and internal-external validation using electronic health records from South Asia
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Performance in Pakistani versus Global North settings
effect: Models pretrained/fine-tuned on high-income public datasets underperformed in Pakistan, with at least 15% F1 and 35% ROUGE-L/BLEU reductions.
quote: In conclusion, our findings highlight the underperformance of medical LLMs in a local Pakistani setting compared to those in Global North settings revealing the data-driven biases in existing publicly available medical LLMs, which are predominantly pre-trained on data from high-income settings.
sample_unit: clinical notes (50 discharge summaries, 150 SOAP notes)

title: Tests of large language models' medical competence and application for clinical decision support of musculoskeletal rehabilitation
outcome: LLM accuracy on musculoskeletal rehabilitation exam questions
effect: Only ERNIE Bot X1 Turbo and Doubao 1.5 pro exceeded 90% accuracy; other LLMs performed lower, so exam-style benchmark performance varied widely across models.
quote: In the first test, only ERNIE Bot X1 Turbo and Doubao 1.5 pro had accuracy rates of over 90%, and Chinese LLMs had significantly fewer incorrect questions than English LLMs (9.6% vs. 14.8%, P < 0.001).
sample_unit: LLMs tested on musculoskeletal rehabilitation exam questions and two clinical cases

title: Artificial Intelligence Simplification of English and Spanish Surgical Consent Forms: 1-Size Does Not Fit All
venue: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
outcome: Readability grade level of AI-simplified surgical consent forms versus originals (English)
effect: Custom GPT reduced median Fry from 12.0 to 7.0, SMOG 12.3 to 9.3, Flesch-Kincaid 9.6 to 5.9 (all p < 0.001); ChatGPT-4.0 gains were modest (Fry 12.0 to 10.0).
quote: Our custom GPT improved English readability, reducing median Fry from 12.0 to 7.0, SMOG 12.3 to 9.3, and Flesch-Kincaid 9.6 to 5.9 (all p < 0.001).

title: Artificial Intelligence Simplification of English and Spanish Surgical Consent Forms: 1-Size Does Not Fit All
venue: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
outcome: Readability of AI-simplified consent forms in English and Spanish
effect: English improved modestly with ChatGPT-4.0 and more with custom GPT; Spanish direct simplification did not significantly improve (GPM 9.5 to 10.0; SOL 9.6 to 9.1; both p > 0.05).
quote: Spanish readability did not significantly improve (median GPM 9.5 to 10.0; SOL 9.6 to 9.1; both p > 0.05).

title: Artificial Intelligence Simplification of English and Spanish Surgical Consent Forms: 1-Size Does Not Fit All
venue: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
outcome: Spanish versus English readability performance
effect: ChatGPT-4.0 improved English, Fry 12.0 to 10.0, all p < 0.05; Spanish GPM 9.5 to 10.0 and SOL 9.6 to 9.1 were nonsignificant.
quote: Spanish readability did not significantly improve (median GPM 9.5 to 10.0; SOL 9.6 to 9.1; both p > 0.05).

title: Assessing Impact of Data Quality in Early Post-Operative Glioblastoma Segmentation
outcome: Model generalization from high-quality training images to low-quality test images
effect: Models trained on exclusively high-quality images did not generalize to low-quality images; including low-quality images in training did not deteriorate performance on high-quality images.
quote: However, models trained on exclusively high-quality images did not generalize to low-quality images.

title: Impact of GPT-4-Generated Discharge Letters on Patients' Medical Comprehension: Prospective Crossover Study
outcome: Comprehension of safety-relevant discharge information: GPT-4 patient-centered letters versus standard discharge letters
effect: OR 1.74 (95% CI 1.45-2.08; P<.001). Learning objectives fully stated 45.7% vs 38.5%; omissions 24.3% vs 34.8%. Gains were largest for medication and organization, smaller for higher-order understanding.
quote: The letter type significantly influenced comprehension (odds ratio [OR] 1.74, 95% CI 1.45-2.08; P<.001).

title: CPGPrompt: translating clinical guidelines into large language model-executable decision support
outcome: Missed specialty referrals (recall) on binary referral decisions in synthetic vignettes
effect: Binary specialty referral classification F1 0.85-1.00 across domains, with recall 1.00 ± 0.00 (no missed referrals).
quote: The binary specialty referral classification achieved consistently strong performance across all domains (F1: 0.85-1.00), with high recall (1.00 ± 0.00).

title: A Blinded Analysis of Quality and Fidelity in Orthopaedic Patient Education Materials Simplified by ChatGPT and Humans
venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
outcome: Reading grade level of original orthopaedic PEMs versus recommended sixth-grade level
effect: Original Epic Elsevier orthopaedic PEMs exceeded the sixth-grade level, mean grade 8.6 in English and 5.8 in Spanish.
quote: Orthopaedic patient education materials (PEMs) within Epic's Elsevier library often exceed the recommended sixth-grade reading level, with a mean grade of 8.6 in English and 5.8 in Spanish, risking poor patient comprehension and adherence.
sample_unit: orthopaedic patient education documents (86 with human easy-to-read versions used for fidelity analysis)

title: A Blinded Analysis of Quality and Fidelity in Orthopaedic Patient Education Materials Simplified by ChatGPT and Humans
venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
outcome: Reading grade level of PEMs after ChatGPT-4o plain-language simplification
effect: ChatGPT-4o-simplified PEMs had mean reading grade levels of 6.1 in English and 3.5 in Spanish, with acceptable fidelity.
quote: ChatGPT-4o-simplified PEMs showed mean reading grade levels of 6.1 in English and 3.5 in Spanish.
sample_unit: orthopaedic patient education documents (86 with human easy-to-read versions used for fidelity analysis)

title: A Blinded Analysis of Quality and Fidelity in Orthopaedic Patient Education Materials Simplified by ChatGPT and Humans
venue: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
outcome: Hallucinations, omissions, and inconsistencies
effect: ChatGPT-4o had fewer English omissions, similar Spanish omissions, fewer inconsistencies, comparable English hallucinations, but higher Spanish hallucinations than humans.
quote: Compared with human simplifications, ChatGPT-4o showed fewer English omissions, similar Spanish omissions, fewer inconsistencies in both languages, and comparable English hallucinations, but higher Spanish hallucinations.
sample_unit: orthopaedic patient education documents (86 with human easy-to-read versions used for fidelity analysis)

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical Question Answering on a Heart Failure Dataset: Performance Analysis
outcome: LLM classifier accuracy in identifying answerable, deferral, and nonanswerable heart failure queries
effect: Classifier achieved 65% accuracy for answerable and helpful deferral queries and 100% accuracy for identifying nonanswerable queries.
quote: The pipeline first uses an LLM-based classifier, achieving 65% accuracy for answerable and helpful deferral queries and 100% accuracy for identifying nonanswerable queries.

title: Clinical utility assessment framework for machine learning-based fetal health classification in cardiotocography: an observational study
outcome: False negative rate for pathological fetal cases (missed safety-critical cases)
effect: 35.3% false negative rate for pathological cases, described as a significant safety concern requiring physician oversight.
quote: The 35.3% false negative rate for pathological cases represents a significant safety concern and requires physician oversight.

title: Vision-Enabled AI scribes reduce omissions in clinical conversations: evidence from simulated medication histories
outcome: Ambient scribe documentation accuracy and omission errors, video input vs audio-only
effect: Vision-enabled scribe achieved 98% accuracy (2114/2,160 data points); video outperformed audio-only (98% vs 81%, P < 0.001), mainly via fewer omissions (10 vs 358 errors).
quote: Video input significantly outperformed audio-only processing (98% vs 81%, P < 0.001), primarily through reduced omissions (10 vs 358 errors).
sample_unit: simulated medication history test recordings (2160 data points)

title: Patient perspective on large-language model responses to questions about Moyamoya
outcome: Physician-rated failure of LLM answers to address urgent symptoms warranting referral
effect: Physicians reported answers failed to address urgent symptoms warranting referral to higher levels of care (ChatGPT 70.0%, Gemini 70.0%).
quote: Physicians evaluating the same LLM outputs reported the answers failed to address recent advances and research within the field (ChatGPT 57.5%, Gemini 62.5%) and failed to address urgent symptoms warranting referral to higher levels of care (ChatGPT 70.0%, Gemini 70.0%).
sample_unit: community respondent survey sets (27 ChatGPT, 20 Gemini)

title: Patient perspective on large-language model responses to questions about Moyamoya
outcome: Physician-rated omission of recent advances and research in LLM answers
effect: Answers failed to address recent advances and research within the field (ChatGPT 57.5%, Gemini 62.5%).

title: Patient perspective on large-language model responses to questions about Moyamoya
outcome: LLM omission of risks and of when to seek professional care, alongside high perceived quality
effect: Failed to address risks of mentioned procedures/medications (ChatGPT 38%, Gemini 28.6%); omitted when to consult professional (ChatGPT 27.2%, Gemini 40.8%); respondents rated quality similar or better than physicians.
quote: The LLMs failed to address potential risks for procedures and medications it mentioned (ChatGPT 38%, Gemini 28.6%).

title: Explainable deep learning framework incorporating medical knowledge for insulin titration in diabetes
outcome: Expert-rated correctness and alignment of AI explanations after doctor-in-the-loop refinement
effect: Final XAI system explanations showed strong alignment with experts' explanations and increased correctness by expert evaluation; unreasonable explanations were reduced versus other explanation models.
quote: The final XAI system explanations demonstrated strong alignment with experts' explanations and increased correctness by expert evaluation
sample_unit: inpatients with T2DM (1,275 internal, 292 external EHR cohort)

title: Explainable deep learning framework incorporating medical knowledge for insulin titration in diabetes
outcome: Clinician insulin titration accuracy and confidence with versus without STII-DIL assistance
effect: Accuracy significantly improved for junior clinicians with STII-DIL assistance, while senior clinicians showed minimal change; both groups reported increased confidence.
quote: An AI-human collaboration study revealed that insulin titration accuracy significantly improved for junior clinicians with STII-DIL assistance, while senior clinicians showed minimal change.
sample_unit: inpatients with T2DM (1,275 internal, 292 external EHR cohort)

title: Continuous Evaluation Frameworks for Retrospective Evaluation of Clinical Machine Learning Models
outcome: Whether continuous evaluation frameworks reveal performance differences missed by single time point metrics such as AUROC
effect: Models with high AUROC showed markedly different performance under continuous evaluation across both datasets; no numbers reported in the abstract.
quote: Across both datasets, models with high AUROC demonstrate markedly different performance when continuously evaluated.

title: Revisiting AI Interpretability in Precision Oncology: Why Predictive Accuracy Does Not Ensure Stable Feature Importance
outcome: Stability of top-20 feature importance rankings after removing the top-ranked feature
effect: Supervised models had unstable feature rankings even under minimal perturbation (<0.1% feature removal). Highly Variable Gene Selection and Spearman correlation gave stable feature sets with competitive predictive performance.
quote: Supervised models exhibited unstable feature importance rankings even under minimal perturbations (<0.1% feature removal), suggesting that high predictive accuracy may obscure fragile or misleading explanations.

title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3 in Patient-Facing Information on Chest Wall Deformities: A Comparative Evaluation of Accuracy, RELIABILITY, and Reproducibility
outcome: Hallucination rate of LLM responses to patient questions on chest wall deformities
effect: ChatGPT-4o had the lowest hallucination rate (5.0%); DeepSeek-V3 had the highest (11.25%); treatment-related questions showed the most errors.
quote: ChatGPT-4o achieved the highest overall accuracy (median score: 1.20), the greatest proportion of fully accurate responses, and the lowest hallucination rate (5.0%).

title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Pro, and DeepSeek-V3 in Patient-Facing Information on Chest Wall Deformities: A Comparative Evaluation of Accuracy, RELIABILITY, and Reproducibility
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM outputs across repeated submissions on two days
effect: Reproducibility was highest for ChatGPT-4o (weighted kappa almost perfect), followed by Gemini and DeepSeek-V3.
quote: Reproducibility was highest for ChatGPT-4o (weighted κ = almost perfect), followed by Gemini and DeepSeek-V3.

title: Development and Clinical Validation of an Artificial Intelligence-Based Automated Visual Acuity Testing System
outcome: Speech recognition word error rate before vs after fine-tuning on local Singaporean English data
effect: Word error rate fell from 17.83% to 9.81% for letters and from 2.76% to 1.97% for numbers after fine-tuning on local data.
quote: The fine-tuned model reduced word error rates from 17.83% to 9.81% for letters and 2.76% to 1.97% for numbers.

title: Predicting Anticipated Telehealth Use: Development of the CONTEST Score and Machine Learning Models Using a National U.S. Survey
outcome: Group fairness metrics (Disparate Impact, Equal Opportunity) across sex and race/ethnicity
effect: Group fairness metrics revealed disparities across sex and race/ethnicity; individual counterfactual flip rates were low (sex CFR 0.024; race/ethnicity CFR 0.013).
quote: Group fairness metrics revealed disparities across sex and race/ethnicity, whereas individual counterfactual analyses indicated low flip rates (sex CFR: 0.024; race/ethnicity CFR: 0.013).
sample_unit: survey respondents with at least one telehealth visit in prior 12 months (HINTS 7)

title: Predicting Anticipated Telehealth Use: Development of the CONTEST Score and Machine Learning Models Using a National U.S. Survey
outcome: Counterfactual flip rate when sex or race/ethnicity attribute is changed
effect: Low counterfactual flip rates: sex CFR 0.024; race/ethnicity CFR 0.013.
quote: Group fairness metrics revealed disparities across sex and race/ethnicity, whereas individual counterfactual analyses indicated low flip rates (sex CFR: 0.024; race/ethnicity CFR: 0.013).
sample_unit: survey respondents with at least one telehealth visit in prior 12 months (HINTS 7)

title: Deep Learning for Freezing of Gait Detection: Cross-Dataset Validation Reveals Critical Deployment Gaps Between Laboratory and Daily Living Wearable Monitoring
outcome: Performance gap between laboratory-trained and daily-living datasets (dataset shift) in FoG detection F1
effect: Laboratory F1 reached 0.9999 ± 0.0002, whereas daily living F1 dropped to 0.55 ± 0.26 (p < 0.0001), an 83% gap with a 1299-fold increase in variance.
quote: Most importantly, cross-dataset validation revealed an 83% performance gap: laboratory F1 reached 0.9999 ± 0.0002, whereas daily living F1 dropped to 0.55 ± 0.26 (p < 0.0001), with a 1299-fold increase in variance.
sample_unit: patients (Parkinson's disease participants across two public datasets: Figshare n=35, DAPHNET n=10)

title: Deep Learning for Freezing of Gait Detection: Cross-Dataset Validation Reveals Critical Deployment Gaps Between Laboratory and Daily Living Wearable Monitoring
outcome: Overestimated performance on laboratory data versus real-world data
effect: Laboratory F1 0.9999 versus daily living F1 0.55; laboratory success does not guarantee real-world utility.
quote: These findings demonstrate that laboratory success does not guarantee real-world utility.
sample_unit: patients (Parkinson's disease participants across two public datasets: Figshare n=35, DAPHNET n=10)

title: Evaluating large language model responses to patient questions on ulnar collateral ligament repair
outcome: Reading grade level of LLM responses versus 6th grade AMA/NIH recommendation
effect: All responses exceeded the 6th grade threshold (FKGL >6). Gemini FKGL 16.2±2.2, ChatGPT 14.4±1.6, Grok 14.6±1.7.
quote: All responses exceeded the AMA/NIH 6th grade reading level threshold (FKGL >6).

title: Evaluating large language model responses to patient questions on ulnar collateral ligament repair
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient education responses versus recommended level

title: Evaluating large language model responses to patient questions on ulnar collateral ligament repair
outcome: Surgeon-rated accuracy of LLM answers to UCL repair patient questions (CRRS, AIRM)
effect: More than minimal clarification needed for 15% ChatGPT, 5% Gemini, 40% Grok responses; Gemini CRRS 1.5±0.5 vs ChatGPT 2.0±0.4 and Grok 2.1±0.7.
quote: More than minimal clarification was required for 15% (3/20) of ChatGPT, 5% (1/20) of Gemini, and 40% (8/20) of Grok responses.
