title: Agent-based large language model system for extracting structured data from breast cancer synoptic reports: a dual-validation study
outcome: Performance gap between synthetic validation and real-world annotated pathology reports
effect: Synthetic accuracy 93.8%-99.0% versus real-world field extraction recall 61.8%-87.7%, a performance drop of 11-32 percentage points.
quote: Real-world evaluation revealed field extraction recall ranging from 61.8% to 87.7%, demonstrating a substantial "reality gap" with performance drops of 11-32 percentage points.
sample_unit: pathology reports (6651 annotated fields) plus 864 synthetic test cases

title: Agent-based large language model system for extracting structured data from breast cancer synoptic reports: a dual-validation study
outcome: Benchmark or synthetic performance translating to real-world documents
effect: Synthetic validation showed 93.8%-99.0% accuracy, but real-world recall was 61.8%-87.7%, so synthetic validation gave false confidence.
quote: While LLM-based extraction systems show promise for pathology data extraction, synthetic validation alone provides false confidence.
sample_unit: pathology reports (6651 annotated fields) plus 864 synthetic test cases

title: Improving Trauma Triage Accuracy with Large Language Models: A Comparison to Human Expert Decisions
venue: Journal of the American College of Surgeons
outcome: Trauma surgeon triage accuracy before vs after LLM exposure, compared with standalone LLM accuracy
effect: Human accuracy rose from 73.7% to 75.8% after LLM exposure (p = 0.04, Bonferroni p = 0.12); odds ratio 2.57 (95% CI 1.39 to 6.83). Standalone LLM accuracy was 83.5% vs 78.9% for humans.
quote: In prospective evaluation, human triage accuracy improved after LLM exposure (73.7% [69.8 to 77.2]) to 75.8% ([71.9 to 79.2], p = 0.04, Bonferroni p = 0.12), significantly improving the odds of a correct triage decision (odds ratio 2.57, 95% CI 1.39 to 6.83, p < 0.01).

title: Automatic acromegaly detection using deep learning on hand images: a multicenter observational study
venue: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
outcome: Model performance versus endocrinologists (F1-score) for acromegaly detection on hand images
effect: Model achieved sensitivity 0.89, specificity 0.91, AUC 0.96, outperforming specialists (F1-score range: 0.43-0.63).
quote: The model achieved a sensitivity of 0.89, specificity of 0.91, positive predictive value of 0.88, negative predictive value of 0.93, F1-score of 0.89, and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.96, outperforming specialists (F1-score range: 0.43-0.63).

title: Deep Learning and Fluid Dynamics On-Site CT-FFR Solution Compared to Off-Site FFRct and Invasive FFR
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of on-site xFFR versus off-site FFRct against invasive FFR on the same patients
effect: xFFR AUC 0.91 vs FFRct AUC 0.89 (P = 0.274); superior only for LAD (AUC 0.96 vs 0.84, P = 0.001).
quote: The overall diagnostic accuracy was comparable to FFRct (AUC: 0.91 vs AUC: 0.89; P = 0.274), superior only for left anterior descending coronary artery assessment (AUC: 0.96 vs AUC: 0.84; P = 0.001).

title: Evaluation of Large Language Models as Emergency Department Revisit Predictors
venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
outcome: F1 of LLM approaches vs traditional LightGBM structured-data model on 30-day ED revisit prediction
effect: All LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed LightGBM on structured data (F1=0.4614, 95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789]); benchmarking against simpler model showed no LLM advantage.
quote: Despite having access to comprehensive structured and unstructured clinical data, all LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed a traditional LightGBM model using only structured data (F1=0.4614 (95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789]))).

title: Evaluation of Large Language Models as Emergency Department Revisit Predictors
venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
outcome: Effect of retrieval augmentation with 10 similar cases on LLM direct prediction F1
effect: RAG improved all direct-prediction models, e.g., Claude 3.7 F1 from 0.3755 to 0.4160; GPT-4o from 0.3403 to 0.3867.
quote: The most significant gains were observed in GPT-4o (from F1=0.3403 to 0.3867) and Claude 3.7 (standard), with the latter achieving the highest overall F1 score of 0.4160 (95% CI [0.4024, 0.4294]) among direct prediction methods.

title: Evaluation of Large Language Models as Emergency Department Revisit Predictors
venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
outcome: Whether complex LLM approaches outperform simpler non-LLM model for the task
effect: Simple LightGBM on structured EHR features (F1=0.4614) exceeded all LLM-based methods (F1=0.3022-0.4505).
quote: However, we also found that a structured EHR baseline achieved performance (F1=0.4614 (95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789])) that exceeded LLM-based methods (F1=0.3022–0.4505).

title: Evaluation of Large Language Models as Emergency Department Revisit Predictors
venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
outcome: Precision-recall tradeoff of LLM predictions, over-prediction of high risk
effect: Deepseek R1 and Claude 3.7 (reasoning) favored high recall (>85%) at expense of precision (<20%), producing excessive false positives.
quote: The precision-recall breakdown reveals that models exhibited different operational characteristics, with Deepseek R1 and Claude 3.7 (reasoning) favoring high recall ( > 85%) at the expense of precision ( < 20%), while GPT-4o and Claude 3.7 (standard) achieved a more balanced precision-recall profile.

title: Evaluation of Large Language Models as Emergency Department Revisit Predictors
venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
outcome: 30-day ED revisit prediction F1 score compared to traditional LightGBM baseline
effect: All LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed a traditional LightGBM model using only structured data (F1=0.4614, 95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789])
quote: Despite having access to comprehensive structured and unstructured clinical data, all LLM approaches (F1=0.3022-0.4505) failed to exceed a traditional LightGBM model using only structured data (F1=0.4614 (95% CI [0.4496, 0.4789])).

title: Retrieval-Augmented Guardrails for AI-Drafted Patient-Portal Messages: Error Taxonomy Construction and Large-Scale Evaluation
venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
outcome: Error checking agreement and F1
effect: Concordance = 50% vs. 33%; F1 = 0.500 vs. 0.256 for context-enhanced labels vs. baseline.
quote: Human validation on 100 messages demonstrated superior agreement (concordance = 50% vs. 33%) and performance (F1 = 0.500 vs. 0.256) of context-enhanced labels vs. baseline, supporting the use of our RAEC pipeline as AI guardrails for patient messaging.

title: MedFactEval and MedAgentBrief: A Framework and Workflow for Generating and Evaluating Factual Clinical Summaries
venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
outcome: Agreement of LLM Jury with seven-physician majority vote on key-fact inclusion in generated summaries
effect: LLM Jury achieved Cohen's κ = 81% with the physician panel, statistically non-inferior to a single human expert (κ = 67%, P < 0.001).
quote: The MedFactEval LLM Jury achieved almost perfect agreement with this panel (Cohen's κ = 81%), a performance statistically non-inferior to that of a single human expert (κ = 67%, P < 0.001).
sample_unit: inpatient cases with clinician-defined key facts

title: From Detection to Mitigation: Addressing Bias in Deep Learning Models for Chest X-Ray Diagnosis
venue: Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing. Pacific Symposium on Biocomputing
outcome: Subgroup fairness and overall predictive performance after bias mitigation (XGBoost retraining, active learning) across sex, age, race
effect: XGBoost final layer improved subgroup fairness while maintaining or improving overall performance; combining XGBoost retraining with active learning gave the largest bias reduction across all subgroups, in and out of distribution.
quote: We show that replacing the final layer of CNN with an eXtreme Gradient Boosting classifier improves the fairness of the subgroup while maintaining or improving the overall predictive performance.
sample_unit: chest X-ray images (CheXpert and MIMIC datasets)

title: When AI joins the table: evaluating large language model performance in soft tissue sarcoma tumor board decisions
venue: Journal of cancer research and clinical oncology
outcome: Expert-rated ChatGPT-4o tumor board recommendation quality across five domains versus maximum score
effect: Scores were significantly lower than the maximum of 1.0 across all five criteria (all p < 0.0001); discrepancies in treatment sequencing and chemotherapy selection.
quote: ChatGPT-4o scores were significantly lower than the maximum achievable value of 1.0 across all five criteria (all p < 0.0001).

title: Multicenter Prospective Validation of an Updated Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model
outcome: Site-level variation in sepsis model discrimination (AUROC) across 4 health systems
effect: Encounter-level AUROC ranged from 0.82 (95% CI, 0.81-0.83) to 0.92 (95% CI, 0.92-0.93) across sites; prediction-level 12-hour AUROC ranged from 0.75 to 0.85; authors note high institutional variability.
quote: At the encounter level, the AUROC ranged from 0.82 (95% CI, 0.81-0.83) to 0.92 (95% CI, 0.92-0.93) across study sites.

title: Multicenter Prospective Validation of an Updated Proprietary Sepsis Prediction Model
outcome: Positive predictive value and alert burden of sepsis model alerts
effect: PPV was low, 0.13 (95% CI, 0.13-0.14) to 0.26 (95% CI, 0.25-0.27), with a high number needed to evaluate and high alert burden.
quote: Positive predictive values remained low, from 0.13 (95% CI, 0.13-0.14) to 0.26 (95% CI, 0.25-0.27), with a high number needed to evaluate and high alert burden.

title: Financial impact of deep learning reconstruction in magnetic resonance imaging: experiences after widespread deployment
outcome: Radiologist review of DLR image quality for clinical limitations
effect: Radiologists observed artifacts in T2-weighted neuroimaging sequences and reduced quality in contrast-enhanced studies, described as unpredictable performance limiting DLR applicability.
quote: Nevertheless, unpredictable performance, particularly in neuroimaging, where artifacts in T2-weighted sequences and reduced quality in contrast-enhanced studies were observed, limits the applicability of DLR and underscores the need for rigorous quality assurance.
sample_unit: scanner log data (examinations and sequences); 4 radiologists rated image quality

title: The Effect of Ambient Listening Technology on the Patient Experience
outcome: Patient-reported satisfaction across six domains with vs without ambient scribe use
effect: Ambient scribe use associated with higher odds of satisfaction with perceived time spent with provider (OR 1.13, 95% CI 1.01-1.26, p=0.033); no detectable differences in other domains.
quote: Patients whose provider used an ambient scribe had higher odds of reporting satisfaction with the perceived duration of time spent with the provider (OR = 1.13, 95% CI: 1.01-1.26, p = 0.033).

title: Comparative analysis of large language models as decision support tools in oral pathology
outcome: LLM performance variation by patient age and sex subgroups
effect: Increasing patient age was associated with mild but significant reduction in performance for ChatGPT-4.0, Meta AI, and Gemini; no age effect for ChatGPT o1-preview; sex had no significant impact.
quote: Increasing patient age was associated with a mild but statistically significant reduction in model performance for ChatGPT-4.0, Meta AI, and Gemini, while no significant age effect was observed for ChatGPT o1-preview; patient sex had no significant impact.

title: Do Large Language Models Perform Equally Across Languages? A Comparison of Responses to Frequently Asked Questions in Anesthesiology
venue: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research
outcome: LLM response quality in Turkish versus English for anesthesia patient questions
effect: English responses of ChatGPT 4.0 and DeepSeek V3 were rated superior to Turkish responses in overall, content, and communication quality (P<0.001 for most comparisons; P=0.001 for DeepSeek communication).
quote: English responses of ChatGPT 4.0 were superior to the Turkish responses in the terms of overall, content, and communication quality (P<0.001 each) and English responses of DeepSeek V3 were superior to the Turkish responses in the terms of overall (P<0.001), content (P<0.001) and communication (P=0.001) quality.
sample_unit: expert anesthesiologist raters evaluating responses to 10 FAQs

title: Evaluation of Information Generated by ChatGPT on Preventing Peripheral Venous Catheter-Related Infections
outcome: LLM correctness on peripheral IV catheter infection prevention guideline questions
effect: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o scored 5/10, GPT-4 scored 3/10; struggled with hand hygiene, aseptic technique, and dressing type. Accuracy averaged 3.9, 3.5, 3.4.
quote: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o each scored 5 out of 10 on the Information Form for Preventing Peripheral Venous Catheter-Related Infections, while GPT-4 scored 3 out of 10.

title: Evaluation of Information Generated by ChatGPT on Preventing Peripheral Venous Catheter-Related Infections
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of ChatGPT information on infection prevention, implying need for verification
effect: Accuracy averaged 3.9 (GPT-3.5), 3.5 (GPT-4), 3.4 (GPT-4o); completeness 1.8, 1.6, 1.8; no significant differences between models (p > 0.05).
quote: The findings highlight that although ChatGPT models can provide supportive information, their limitations in accuracy and completeness may pose risks for patient safety, particularly in critical domains such as aseptic technique and hand hygiene.

title: Human medical documentation significantly outperforms ChatGPT-4o in critical clinical dimensions: A blinded comparative assessment in paediatric orthopaedics
venue: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
outcome: AI-generated summary quality: temporal consistency, omissions of accident details versus human documentation
effect: Human overall 5.2 vs ChatGPT 4.5 (p<0.001); temporal inconsistencies in 14/60 (23%) evaluations; omission of accident details in 21/60 (35%).
quote: ChatGPT demonstrated frequent temporal inconsistencies (14 of 60 evaluations, 23%) and omission of relevant accident details (21 of 60 evaluations, 35%).

title: Improving reliability and accuracy of structured data extraction using a consensus large-language model approach-a use case description in multiple sclerosis
outcome: LLM consensus extraction accuracy compared with neurology specialists and trained medical personnel on same reports
effect: LLM consensus true-error rate 1.48% vs NSP ~2%; difference not significant (p=0.6447; OR 1.38; 95% CI 0.57–3.31).
quote: The difference between the LLM consensus evaluation and the NSPs was not significant ( p = 0.6447; odds ratio = 1.38; 95% CI 0.57–3.31).

title: Improving reliability and accuracy of structured data extraction using a consensus large-language model approach-a use case description in multiple sclerosis
outcome: LLM structured-extraction content errors against human consensus reference, comparing single LLMs to multi-LLM consensus
effect: Consensus reduced errors ~30% versus best single LLM to 6.7% (36 errors, 93.30% accuracy); true-error rate 1.48% vs neurologists ~2% (p=0.6447).
quote: Using this method, we were able to decrease the error rate by around another 30% compared to the best performing LLM.

title: Alignment of large language models in solving medical ethical dilemmas
outcome: Model endorsement of impermissible medical actions in forced-choice ethical vignettes (boundary violations)
effect: Seven of 14 models recommended impermissible medical actions (nonconsensual amputation, killing a healthy person for organ harvesting, hospice transfer against wishes) in 44 of 700 outputs (6.3%).
quote: Seven of the fourteen models tested recommended impermissible medical actions, including nonconsensual limb amputation, killing a healthy person for organ harvesting, and transferring a patient to hospice against their wishes, in 44 of 700 outputs (6.3 %).
sample_unit: LLM responses (14 models x 5 dilemmas x 10 responses)

title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence-based electrocardiogram analysis tools in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
outcome: AI-ECG HCM probability scores in confirmed HCM patients, a population differing from general-population development
effect: Median HCM probability 38.8% (IQR 12.8-63.4%); only 41.2% scored >50% and 12.5% >75% despite all patients having confirmed HCM.
quote: Despite all patients having confirmed HCM, the AI-calculated HCM probabilities showed a relatively uniform distribution [median 38.8% (IQR: 12.8-63.4%)], with only 41.2% and 12.5% of patients receiving a probability score >50% and >75%.

title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence-based electrocardiogram analysis tools in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
outcome: AI-ECG tool performance on a specific disease cohort versus confirmed diagnosis
effect: Modest performance in the HCM cohort; only 41.2% of confirmed HCM patients scored >50% HCM probability; SHD probabilities >50% in 51.2%.
quote: AI-based ECG analysis tools demonstrated modest performance in our HCM cohort.

title: Assessing the robustness and clinical evaluation of a deep-learning segmentation model for head and neck cancer
outcome: Segmentation Dice and clinician-rated usability under synthetic image perturbations (noise, blur, ghosting, bias-field, spike, motion)
effect: Baseline Dice 0.766 (GTVp) and 0.698 (GTVn); performance dropped significantly under spike noise and bias-field, especially GTVn; usability for GTVn fell to 27.9% under severe perturbations vs 77.8% for GTVp.
quote: Performance dropped significantly under spike noise and bias-field artifacts, especially for GTVn.
sample_unit: test cases (HECKTOR 2022 PET/CT), each with 36 perturbed variants

title: Epistemic compression in large language model explanations of the gut-liver axis
venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
outcome: Under-signaling of uncertainty and source attribution in LLM gut-liver axis explanations
effect: Item-level analysis showed consistently high narrative clarity but systematic under-signaling of source attribution and uncertainty, yielding over-coherent explanations that compressed conditional associations into mechanism-like claims.
quote: Item-level analysis revealed consistently high narrative clarity but systematic under-signaling of source attribution and uncertainty, resulting in over-coherent explanations that compressed conditional associations into mechanism-like claims.

title: Improving Nurses' Management of Uterine Tachysystole
venue: MCN. The American journal of maternal child nursing
outcome: Tachysystole incidence and oxytocin management after AI alert implementation
effect: No significant difference in tachysystole events (p = .626) or management with oxytocin decrease/discontinuance (p = .603) after alert system implementation.
quote: Phase I found no significant difference in the number of tachysystole events ( p = .626) or management of tachysystole with the decrease or discontinuance of oxytocin after implementation ( p = .603).

title: Improving Nurses' Management of Uterine Tachysystole
venue: MCN. The American journal of maternal child nursing
outcome: Timely evidence-based nurse management of tachysystole after education added to AI alerts
effect: Significant improvement in timely management with Category II/III FHR pattern (p < .001); no change in tachysystole incidence (p = .945) or prolonged alerts (p = .377); only 31.4% of nurses completed module.
quote: Phase II found a significant improvement in the timely management of tachysystole with evidence-based intervention in the presence of Category II/III fetal heart rate pattern ( p < .001).

title: Improving Nurses' Management of Uterine Tachysystole
venue: MCN. The American journal of maternal child nursing
outcome: Timely tachysystole management, tachysystole incidence, and prolonged alerts after nurse education
effect: Education improved timely management with Category II/III fetal heart rate patterns (p < .001), but not tachysystole incidence among all births (p = .945), incidence with Category II/III patterns (p = .070), or prolonged alerts (p = .377).
quote: Phase II found a significant improvement in the timely management of tachysystole with evidence-based intervention in the presence of Category II/III fetal heart rate pattern ( p < .001).

title: Improving Nurses' Management of Uterine Tachysystole
venue: MCN. The American journal of maternal child nursing
outcome: timely management of tachysystole
effect: Timely management with evidence-based intervention significantly improved after targeted retraining via an educational intervention (p < .001).
quote: Phase II found a significant improvement in the timely management of tachysystole with evidence-based intervention in the presence of Category II/III fetal heart rate pattern ( p < .001).

title: Fairness analysis of machine learning predictions of aggression in acute psychiatric care
outcome: Disparities in false positive and true positive rates of aggression prediction across demographic and social subgroups
effect: Random forest ROC-AUC 0.81 overall; significant FPR and TPR disparities across subgroups, with higher FPR for Middle Eastern and Black patients, men, police-admitted patients, and those with unstable or supportive housing.
quote: Fairness analyses revealed significant disparities in FPR and TPR across subgroups: FPR was higher for Middle Eastern and Black patients, men, those admitted into emergency care by the police, and those with unstable or supportive forms of housing.

title: Accent related errors in clinical speech transcription and a LLM-based remedy
outcome: ASR transcription error (WER) for native vs non-native English accented speech
effect: Non-native speakers had higher WER across all models; Whisper disparity β = 11.0 (95% CI 1.0–21.0, p = 0.031); WhisperX β = 3.4 (p = 0.07).
quote: The greatest disparity was observed in Whisper ( β = 11.0, 95% CI [1.0, 21.0], p = 0.031), while WhisperX showed a smaller, marginally significant difference ( β = 3.4, p = 0.07).

title: Accent related errors in clinical speech transcription and a LLM-based remedy
outcome: Speech transcription error rates stratified by speaker language background (native vs non-native)
effect: Language-stratified analysis showed higher WER for non-native speakers across Whisper, WhisperX and WhisperX-GPT; disparity largest for Whisper (β = 11.0).
quote: Across all three ASR systems (Whisper, WhisperX, and WhisperX-GPT) non-native speakers consistently demonstrated higher WER, with the effect size varying by model.

title: Accent related errors in clinical speech transcription and a LLM-based remedy
outcome: subgroup transcription performance gap
effect: Non-native speakers consistently had higher WER; effect sizes varied by model, with Whisper β = 11.0 and WhisperX β = 3.4.
quote: Across all three ASR systems (Whisper, WhisperX, and WhisperX-GPT) non-native speakers consistently demonstrated higher WER, with the effect size varying by model.

title: Accent related errors in clinical speech transcription and a LLM-based remedy
outcome: bias mitigation with LLM correction
effect: GPT-4o correction attenuated the non-native penalty to 1.7 percentage points (p = 0.057); WER reductions ranged 4.52 to 6.89 (p < 0.001).
quote: Notably, applying GPT-4o correction to WhisperX output reduced the mean WER overall and attenuated the non-native penalty to 1.7 percentage points ( p = 0.057), effectively eliminating speaker-level variability.

title: Advancing trauma scoring through large language models: automated estimation of injury severity
outcome: LLM-estimated ISS agreement with human-assigned ISS on local retrospective data
effect: Weighted Kappa 0.91 (Grok-3), 0.88 (GPT-4), 0.54 (Perplexity); ICC 0.97 GPT-4, 0.92 Grok-3, 0.84 Perplexity; LoA ±5.2, ±7.0, ±9.7.
quote: Categorical agreement was high in Grok-3 (weighted Kappa = 0.91), and GPT-4 (weighted Kappa = 0.88), but adequate in Perplexity (weighted Keppa = 0.54).

title: Advancing trauma scoring through large language models: automated estimation of injury severity
outcome: Comparison of three candidate LLMs against human-assigned ISS on the same data
effect: GPT-4 and Grok-3 showed high agreement (weighted Kappa 0.88, 0.91) while Perplexity was lower (0.54); ICCs 0.97, 0.92, 0.84.
quote: ICCs were 0.97 (GPT-4, CI 95% = 0.94–0.98), 0.92 (Grok-3, CI 95% = 0.86–0.95), and 0.84 (Perplexity, CI 95% = 0.73–0.91), demonstrating near-expert-level consistency.

title: Large language models for structuring knee ultrasound reports-A comparative evaluation of DeepSeek R1, gemini 2.5 flash, and GPT-4o
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Run-to-run repeatability of LLM outputs across repeated runs (percent agreement, Cohen's kappa)
effect: DeepSeek R1 showed repeatability of 3.41 ± 0.06 with stable schema compliance and run-to-run consistency; GPT-4o showed superior objective repeatability versus the other models.
quote: DeepSeek R1 showed competitive performance in structured reporting (4.0 ± 0.5) and repeatability (3.41 ± 0.06), with stable schema compliance and run-to-run consistency.

title: Large language models for structuring knee ultrasound reports-A comparative evaluation of DeepSeek R1, gemini 2.5 flash, and GPT-4o
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Comparison of three candidate LLMs on the same reports for extraction, impression, recommendation
effect: GPT-4o had the best diagnostic F1 (0.79 vs 0.54 DeepSeek R1 and 0.45 Gemini 2.5 Flash), highest balanced accuracy and MCC; Gemini 2.5 Flash consistently underperformed.
quote: GPT-4o consistently outperformed DeepSeek R1 and Gemini 2.5 Flash, supporting its potential to improve knee ultrasound report consistency and clinical utility.

title: Benchmarking large language models against human experts in rehabilitation medicine: a multidimensional evaluation
outcome: LLM-generated rehabilitation plan quality versus senior physiatrist plans, blinded expert ratings
effect: Grok-4 (mean 4.31), Gemini-2.5-pro (4.14) and Deepseek-r1 (3.69) significantly outperformed human benchmark (3.56); Claude-opus-4 (3.50) did not differ significantly.
quote: Quantitative analysis revealed that Grok-4 (mean 4.31) and Gemini−2.5-pro (mean 4.14) significantly outperformed the human benchmark (derived from standardized expert solutions) (mean 3.56; [Formula: see text]).

title: Comparison of GPT-5 and GPT-4o in Solving the Polish Centre for Medical Examinations (CEM) Gastroenterology Examination
outcome: Correlation between model self-reported confidence and answer correctness on specialty exam questions
effect: GPT-4o confidence-accuracy correlation weak and non-significant (r = 0.14); GPT-5 significant positive correlation (r = 0.28), surviving Bonferroni correction; mean confidence high for both models.
quote: The confidence-accuracy correlation was weak and non-significant for GPT-4o (r = 0.14), whereas GPT-5 demonstrated a statistically significant positive correlation (r = 0.28), which remained significant after correction for multiple testing.

title: Evaluating GPT-4 Responses on Scars or Keloids for Patient Education: Large Language Model Evaluation Study
outcome: Readability of GPT-4 patient education responses (Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog)
effect: Flesch Reading Ease 50.13; Gunning Fog 12.68, corresponding to a 12th-grade reading level, above the recommended sixth to eighth grade.
quote: Readability analyses indicated moderate complexity (Flesch Reading Ease Score: 50.13; Gunning Fog Index: 12.68), corresponding to a 12th-grade reading level.

title: Evaluating GPT-4 Responses on Scars or Keloids for Patient Education: Large Language Model Evaluation Study
outcome: Rate of hallucinated and real references in GPT-4 responses
effect: 11.8% (383/3250) of references hallucinated; 88.2% (2867/3250) real, with 95.1% (2724/2867) from authoritative sources.
quote: Reference Evaluation for Artificial Intelligence identified 11.8% (383/3250) hallucinated references, while 88.2% (2867/3250) of references were real, with 95.1% (2724/2867) from authoritative sources (eg, government guidelines and the literature).

title: ChatGPT Versus DeepSeek for Breast Cancer Information Retrieval: Quantitative Comparative Study
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of AI-generated breast cancer patient information versus expert reference materials
effect: AI text was 2.60 grade levels lower than expert references (P<.001), but median FKGL was still 10.66 (ChatGPT-4.0) and 10.17 (DeepSeek-V3).
quote: AI models produced significantly more readable content than expert references (mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level difference -2.60; P<.001).

title: Sport-Specific Craniofacial Injury Risk Stratification in Squash, Badminton, and Tennis Using NEISS and ChatGPT: A Structured Vignette Study
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT-4o patient education output
effect: Readability averaged an 11th-grade level across sports, above AMA recommendations.
quote: Readability averages an 11th-grade readability across sports.

title: Sport-Specific Craniofacial Injury Risk Stratification in Squash, Badminton, and Tennis Using NEISS and ChatGPT: A Structured Vignette Study
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient education content
effect: Average 11th-grade reading level across sports, above AMA recommended level.
quote: Readability averages an 11th-grade readability across sports.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT in Pediatric Craniofacial Surgery Counseling: A Vignette-Based Assessment of Educational Quality, Specificity, Readability, and Emotional Content
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of ChatGPT-4o responses versus recommended 6th-8th grade
effect: Average FKGL was 9.5 (10th-grade level), exceeding the recommended sixth to eighth grade patient education standard.
quote: Reading level exceeds recommended patient education standards of sixth to eighth grade.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT in Pediatric Craniofacial Surgery Counseling: A Vignette-Based Assessment of Educational Quality, Specificity, Readability, and Emotional Content
outcome: Readability and actionability of AI-generated patient education responses
effect: Average FKGL 9.5; PEMAT understandability averaged 62% and actionability 27%.
quote: PEMAT scores averaged 62% for understandability and 27% for actionability.

title: Performance of next-generation AI chatbots in gynecological knowledge assessment: a comparative pilot study of ChatGPT-5, Gemini-3, DeepSeek-V3.2, and Claude-4.5-Opus
outcome: LLM accuracy on gynecology MCQs from USMLE-style questions under zero-shot constrained prompts
effect: Overall accuracy unsatisfactory: Gemini-3 32.86%, DeepSeek-V3.2 30.00%, ChatGPT-5 25.71%, Claude-4.5-Opus 21.43%; ChatGPT-5 scored 0.00% in Infertility.
quote: Contrary to expectations for advanced models, overall accuracy was unsatisfactory: Gemini-3 (32.86%), DeepSeek-V3.2 (30.00%), ChatGPT-5 (25.71%), and Claude-4.5-Opus (21.43%).

title: Performance of next-generation AI chatbots in gynecological knowledge assessment: a comparative pilot study of ChatGPT-5, Gemini-3, DeepSeek-V3.2, and Claude-4.5-Opus
outcome: Clinical knowledge errors and failure patterns in gynecological diagnosis
effect: Three failure patterns found: semantic association bias, spatial anatomy confusion, and genetic logic reversal; theoretically dangerous errors such as misdiagnosing adrenal enzymes.
quote: Qualitative analysis revealed three critical failure patterns: (1) semantic association bias (confusing high-probability diseases with symptom-specific diagnoses), (2) spatial anatomy confusion, and (3) genetic logic reversal.

title: AI-Powered Ambient Scribe Technology Experiences Among Emergency Physicians: Cross-Sectional, Mixed Methods Pilot Survey Study
outcome: Emergency physician trust in ambient scribe note accuracy, efficiency, usefulness by note component
effect: Trust in accuracy 6/14 (42.9%) vs 6/8 (75%) for in-person scribes; efficiency improved 10/14 (71.4%); helpful for physical exam 3/13 (23.1%), MDM documentation 5/14 (35.7%).
quote: However, only 42.9% (6/14; 95% CI 22.3%-69.2%) of respondents trusted the accuracy of ambient scribe-generated notes, compared with 75% (6/8; 95% CI 40.9%-92.9%) who trusted in-person scribes.

title: Reducing Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury: A Regional Quality Improvement Initiative of 26 Community-Based Hospitals
venue: Joint Commission journal on quality and patient safety
outcome: Postoperative AKI incidence across phased rollout of CDS tools at 26 sites
effect: PO-AKI fell from a baseline average of 1,031 cases per month to 400 per month after full Phase 3 implementation; intraoperative hypotension episodes fell 33% in Phase 1.
quote: With the full implementation of risk tools, alerts, and order sets in Phase 3, AKI incidence declined to 400 cases per month.

title: Large language model-based scribing tools for ophthalmology: performance and safety evaluation using simulated clinical encounters
outcome: Ambient scribe documentation accuracy and quality across six tools
effect: Heidi AI highest PDQI-9 (38.524), then Whisper GPT-4o (38.048); all tools produced errors, especially omissions of critical details.
quote: However, persistent errors, particularly omissions of critical details, were observed across all tools and could compromise patient care.

title: Predicting the Value of Radiology Artificial Intelligence Applications: Large-Scale Predeployment Evaluation of a Portfolio of Models
outcome: Augmentation metrics (AI-detected radiologist-missed cases) predicting postdeployment perceived value
effect: Absolute and relative enhanced detection rates ranged 0.03-2.27% and 4.5-60.5%; predicted value categories agreed with postdeployment radiologist survey for 10 of 12 tasks (response rate 43.2%, 54/125).
quote: Perceived value categories agreed between survey respondents and workgroup predictions for 10 of 12 tasks.

title: Predicting the Value of Radiology Artificial Intelligence Applications: Large-Scale Predeployment Evaluation of a Portfolio of Models
outcome: Predeployment comparison of AI versus radiologist performance on the same examinations

title: Autonomous AI-assisted diabetic retinopathy screening at primary care is associated with increased presentation to eye care by at risk patients
outcome: Presentation to eye specialist care by African-American patients after AI screening

quote: An inverse-probability-weighted regression, which incorporated propensity score matching on social determinants of health and relevant clinical variables, showed that implementation of an autonomous AI-assisted diabetic screening program in a primary care clinic was associated with increased presentation to eye care specialist care by African-Americans (p = 0.02).

title: Autonomous AI-assisted diabetic retinopathy screening at primary care is associated with increased presentation to eye care by at risk patients
outcome: Presentation to specialist eye care among African-American patients

quote: An inverse-probability-weighted regression, which incorporated propensity score matching on social determinants of health and relevant clinical variables, showed that implementation of an autonomous AI-assisted diabetic screening program in a primary care clinic was associated with increased presentation to eye care specialist care by African-Americans (p = 0.02).

title: Autonomous AI-assisted diabetic retinopathy screening at primary care is associated with increased presentation to eye care by at risk patients

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled ultrasound diagnosis and stratification of follicular thyroid neoplasms: a multi-center study
outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance, and AI versus radiologists
effect: AI consistently outperformed radiologists and improved diagnostic accuracy as an assistive tool; no numeric effect or overreliance assessment reported in the abstract.
quote: It consistently outperformed radiologists and improved diagnostic accuracy as an assistive tool.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled ultrasound diagnosis and stratification of follicular thyroid neoplasms: a multi-center study
outcome: Model AUC across three external test sets from multiple hospitals
effect: AUCs of 0.816-0.847 for FTC vs FTA across external test sets; subtype AUC range 0.754-0.910; generalized well to varied clinical settings.
quote: The model demonstrated high diagnostic performance, with AUCs of 0.816-0.847 for FTC vs FTA discrimination across external test sets and robust performance across subtypes (AUC range 0.754-0.910), and generalized well to varied clinical settings.

title: Evaluation of large language models in emergency medicine scenarios: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-o3mini, Gemini 2.0-pro, and DeepSeek-R1
outcome: LLM errors in emergency triage across simulated cases, rated by emergency physicians
effect: Triage was the most error-prone domain across all four models; re-prompting after misleading outputs significantly improved applicability for ChatGPT-o3mini, Gemini 2.0-Pro, and DeepSeek-R1, particularly in triage.
quote: Triage emerged as the most error-prone domain across all models.

title: Accuracy, quality, and readability analyses of responses from large language models to questions on pediatric dental sedation
outcome: Accuracy of chatbot responses on pediatric dental sedation against clinical guidelines
effect: Gemini and ChatGPT-4o highest accuracy; Copilot lowest with highest guideline deviation; none of the chatbots fully aligned with clinical guidelines or consistently achieved high accuracy across all phases.
quote: Despite the fact that ChatGPT-4o and Gemini exhibited superior performance in general, none of the evaluated chatbots fully aligned with clinical guidelines or consistently achieved high accuracy across all phases.

title: Should we leave paediatric emergency triage to artificial intelligence? A comparison of ChatGPT 4o and Grok 3
outcome: ESI triage accuracy of LLMs versus nurses, against paediatric specialist gold standard, on same patients
effect: Accuracy: nurses 53.1%, ChatGPT 4o 76.1%, Grok 3 47.0% (Cochran's Q = 275.68, p < 0.001). ChatGPT 4o outperformed nurses; Grok 3 did not.
quote: Nurses achieved 53.1% (95% CI: 50.6-55.6) accuracy in triage assessments, while ChatGPT 4o achieved 76.1% (95% CI: 73.9-78.2) and Grok 3 achieved 47.0% (95% CI: 44.5-49.6) accuracy (Cochran's Q = 275.68, p < 0.001).

title: Should we leave paediatric emergency triage to artificial intelligence? A comparison of ChatGPT 4o and Grok 3
outcome: Sensitivity for critical (ESI-2) patients and over-triage rates
effect: Critical-patient sensitivity: nurses 37.2%, ChatGPT 4o 82.9%, Grok 3 97.7%; Grok 3 over-triage 36.3% with PPV 37.2%.
quote: For critical patient identification, sensitivity was 37.2% for nurses, 82.9% for ChatGPT 4o, and 97.7% for Grok 3; however, Grok 3 demonstrated substantial over-triage (36.3%) and low positive predictive value (37.2%).

title: Evaluating the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence-assisted decision-making software for pulmonary nodules in a resource-limited setting
outcome: Reader diagnostic performance (AUC) with versus without AI assistance
effect: Average AUC rose from 0.78 to 0.89 (mean difference 0.11, 95% CI 0.08, 0.14) with AI-assisted DMS; improvements consistent across experience levels and specialties.
quote: AI-assisted DMS significantly improved readers' diagnostic performance, with the average AUC increasing from 0.78 to 0.89 (mean difference: 0.11, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.08, 0.14).
sample_unit: chest CT scans (enriched; read by 6 physicians)

title: Real-World Testing of an Artificial Intelligence Conversational Agent as an Early Intervention and Support Tool in the Mental Health Referral Care Pathway: A Mixed-Methods Study
venue: The International journal of social psychiatry
outcome: Change in depression severity over 12 weeks, Wysa versus waitlist control
effect: Mean depression change was similar between arms (Wysa M=2.62 vs control M=2.59) with large SDs; no evidence Wysa treats depression, though the sample was small (76 randomized, 30 lost to follow-up).
quote: Our study findings suggest that the change of depression score is similar in both arms thus indicating that there is no evidence that Wysa treats depression in this study.

title: Enhancing pancreatic cancer staging with large language models: the role of retrieval-augmented generation

effect: REK+/RAG+ 70% staging accuracy vs REK+/RAG− 38% and REK−/RAG− 35%; difference 0.32 (95% CI 0.17-0.45), p<0.001; TNM 80% vs 55% and 50%.
quote: The REK+/RAG+ group achieved 70% staging accuracy, outperforming REK+/RAG− (38%) and REK−/RAG− (35%).

title: Enhancing pancreatic cancer staging with large language models: the role of retrieval-augmented generation

quote: Unlike Gemini 2.0 Flash with REK (REK+/RAG−) and without REK (REK−/RAG−), NotebookLM (REK+/RAG+) presented retrieved excerpts from REK as the basis for its classifications, achieving a retrieval accuracy of 92% (Fig. 2 ).

title: Enhancing pancreatic cancer staging with large language models: the role of retrieval-augmented generation
outcome: LLM output accuracy against radiologist-defined ground-truth staging
effect: Best configuration reached only 70% staging accuracy; most errors (e.g., resectability 9/14, T 13/15) occurred despite sufficient retrieval, indicating generation errors.
quote: Consequently, retrieval failures accounted for a minority of misclassifications (resectability: 5/14, T category: 2/15, local invasion: 1/7), whereas most errors occurred despite sufficient retrieval, indicating generation-related failures (see Figs. 3 and 4 for reference).

title: Enhancing pancreatic cancer staging with large language models: the role of retrieval-augmented generation
outcome: Reproducibility of staging outputs across repeated runs
effect: Identical inputs submitted twice per case under each setting gave consistent staging classifications (temperature zero for Gemini).
quote: To assess potential variability in staging results, identical inputs were submitted twice for each of the 100 cases under each LLM setting across independent runs, and the resulting staging classifications were consistent.

title: Factors for Patient Trust and Acceptance of Medical Artificial Intelligence

title: Factors for Patient Trust and Acceptance of Medical Artificial Intelligence

outcome: Association between hospital AI usage intensity and misdiagnosis rate for acute imaging-dependent tracer condition
effect: Higher AI usage intensity was positively associated with misdiagnosis rates (β = 0.28, p < 0.001), suggesting automation bias in time-sensitive acute triage; attenuated by high public trust and remoteness.
quote: Within the specific context of the tracer condition, higher AI usage intensity was positively associated with misdiagnosis rates (β = 0.28, p < 0.001), suggesting a pattern of "automation bias" in time-sensitive acute triage.

title: Effect of a Computer-Aided Device for Detecting Gastric Neoplasms: A Multicenter, Randomized Controlled Trial
outcome: Gastric neoplasm detection rate with vs without AI-assisted endoscopy in randomized trial
effect: Primary outcome after pathologic review not improved (RR 1.13; 0.92-1.38; 1.42 vs 1.25%; P=.25); original pathology showed improvement (RR 1.14; 4.06 vs 3.57%; P=.03); blind spots fell from 2.52 to 1.07.
quote: AI did not improve detection rate of gastric neoplasm after pathological review (RR, 1.13; 0.92-1.38; 1.42 vs 1.25%; P = .25).

title: Benchmarking a deep learning model against healthcare practitioners for hip fracture detection in the emergency department
outcome: DL model AUROC and AUPRC on external validation versus development metrics
effect: External validation AUROC 0.96 and AUPRC 0.91, reduced versus development metrics (AUROC 0.99, AUPRC 0.95).
quote: The DL model trained on 512 by 512 images achieved an AUROC of 0.96 and AUPRC of 0.91, showing reduced performance compared with development metrics (AUROC 0.99, AUPRC 0.95).

title: Benchmarking a deep learning model against healthcare practitioners for hip fracture detection in the emergency department
outcome: DL model performance compared with radiographers and junior doctors on same radiographs
effect: Radiographers significantly outperformed the DL model (P<0.001; sensitivity 99% vs 85%); no significant difference between DL model and ED junior doctors.
quote: On original high-resolution images, radiographers significantly outperformed the DL model (McNemar's test: P < 0.001), achieving a sensitivity of 99% compared to the model's sensitivity of 85%.

title: Benchmarking a deep learning model against healthcare practitioners for hip fracture detection in the emergency department
outcome: Junior doctor performance with versus without DL model outputs
effect: No significant difference in performance between DL model and ED junior doctors reading independently or with DL support.
quote: There was no significant difference in performance between the DL model and ED junior doctors, who read the original radiographs independently or with support from the DL model.

title: Medical Student Experiences With ChatGPT: National Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Proportion of ChatGPT-using students who used it to help write clinical notes
effect: 21.0% (33/157) of ChatGPT users reported using it to help write clinical notes, and 46.5% (73/157) used it for assignments; the authors flag patient confidentiality concerns.
quote: Notably, 21.0% (33/157) of participants responded having used ChatGPT to help write clinical notes.

title: Medical Student Experiences With ChatGPT: National Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Association between baseline AI understanding and cross-checking or editing of ChatGPT output
effect: Moderate or advanced AI understanding was associated with cross-checking (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.08-4.97) and editing (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.05-5.71) versus basic or limited understanding.
quote: Students who reported moderate or advanced baseline understanding of AI were more likely to practice conscientious use habits, such as cross-checking (odds ratio [OR] 2.31, 95% CI 1.08-4.97) and editing (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.05-5.71) ChatGPT output before using it, than those who reported a basic or limited understanding.

title: Large Language Model-Driven Analysis and Report Generation of Endoscopy Videos-A Pilot Study
venue: Digestive endoscopy : official journal of the Japan Gastroenterological Endoscopy Society
outcome: Adequacy of MLLM-generated EGD report completeness, visualization, and lesion characteristics rated by blinded endoscopists
effect: Completeness adequate in 56.0% (14/25) clean vs 48.0% (12/25) overlay; visualization 36.0% both; lesion characteristics 16.0% both. Authors conclude performance was inadequate for clinical EGD reporting.
quote: In this pilot study, Gemini 2.5 Pro demonstrated inadequate performance for clinical EGD reporting.
sample_unit: complete EGD videos (from 5 patients), each analyzed in clean and CAD-overlay versions

title: Large Language Model-Driven Analysis and Report Generation of Endoscopy Videos-A Pilot Study
venue: Digestive endoscopy : official journal of the Japan Gastroenterological Endoscopy Society
outcome: MLLM landmark detection accuracy on full-length EGD videos against expert annotations
effect: Landmark accuracy 0.55 [95% CI 0.43-0.67] clean vs 0.33 [0.23-0.46] with CAD overlay, p = 0.029; specificity 0.67 vs 0.22.
quote: For the Landmark agreement, the overall accuracy of the MLLM with Clean-Video vs. Overlay-Video was: 0.55 [95% CI 0.43-0.67] vs. 0.33 [0.23-0.46], p = 0.029; sensitivity 0.53 [0.40-0.66] vs. 0.35 [0.24-0.49], p = 0.122; specificity 0.67 [0.35-0.88] vs. 0.22 [0.06-0.55], p = 0.125.
sample_unit: complete EGD videos (from 5 patients), each analyzed in clean and CAD-overlay versions

title: Clinical Validation of AI-Assisted Evaluation of Indeterminate Biliary Strictures in Digital-Single Operator Cholangioscopy: A Transcontinental Multicentric Study
outcome: AI performance validated across 14 centers and devices, reported by center
effect: Patient-level accuracy 86.0%, sensitivity 84.1%, specificity 85.7%, AUC 0.904; performance maintained across demographic variables and centers.
quote: Performance was maintained across demographic variables and centers.
country: Multinational (United States, Brazil, Spain, Colombia, Australia, Saudi Arabia)

title: Barriers and Enablers for Sustaining Nurse-Led Use of Clinical Decision Support Tools for Antibiotic Stewardship: Qualitative Study
outcome: Nurse-perceived barriers and enablers to sustaining CDS tool use, including training needs
effect: Ongoing need for training and support emerged as one of five themes among 22 nurses and nurse leaders interviewed about sustaining the CDS tool.
quote: Five themes emerged: (1) importance of staffing stability and capacity, (2) impact of dedicated clinic resource availability, (3) variable nurse readiness with CDS-guided clinical care, (4) influence of openness to change and a nurse-supportive clinic culture, and (5) ongoing need for training and support.

title: Accuracy and reproducibility of tumor size measurement using a deep-learning-based CDSS in resected lung cancer
outcome: Tumor size measurement agreement of CDSS versus radiologists against pathologic size
effect: CDSS and radiology reports both showed ICC 0.869 with pathology; no significant difference between radiologists and CDSS; CDSS detected 162/176 (92%) tumors; interobserver ICC 0.907 vs CDSS 1.000
quote: No significant differences were found in the measurement of tumor size between radiologists and the CDSS.

title: RAPID CTA versus JLK LVO for large vessel occlusion detection: a pragmatic comparison of performance and common pitfalls
outcome: Head-to-head LVO detection performance of two commercial AI tools versus neuroradiologist consensus
effect: AUROC 0.93 for both tools (p = 0.64); at matched 83% sensitivity, JLK LVO specificity 0.96 vs RAPID CTA 0.89.
quote: Both tools demonstrated high and comparable overall performance (AUROC 0.93 for both, p = 0.64).

title: RAPID CTA versus JLK LVO for large vessel occlusion detection: a pragmatic comparison of performance and common pitfalls
outcome: Local retrospective validation of AI LVO detection against expert reference standard
effect: In 176 consecutive local patients, both tools achieved AUROC 0.93 against neuroradiologist consensus; misclassification causes reviewed.
quote: The performance of RAPID CTA and JLK LVO was compared against expert neuroradiologist consensus using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC).

title: Educational Impact of a National Training Webinar on AI-based Automatic Contouring in Radiation Oncology
venue: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education
outcome: Pre- vs post-webinar knowledge score on AI auto-contouring (5-item MCQ)
effect: Median score rose from 3.5 (IQR 2–4) to 5.0 (IQR 4–5), p < 0.0001, among 28 participants.
quote: The median questionnaire score increased from 3.5 (IQR: 2–4) before training to 5.0 (IQR: 4–5) after training, corresponding to a statistically significant improvement (p < 0.0001).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Military Graduate Medical Education: Trainee Perceptions and Current Use
outcome: Trainee AI use in daily work without prior formal AI training
effect: Only 10 of 83 respondents reported prior formal AI training; 73% disagreed their curriculum had enough. 30% used AI for diagnosis, 27% for treatment, 28% for teaching.
quote: Importantly, trainees reported utilizing AI in daily practice without training.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Military Graduate Medical Education: Trainee Perceptions and Current Use
outcome: Trainee AI literacy training gap and desire for formal AI education
effect: 84% agreed a need for formal AI training exists; 73% disagreed that their current curriculum contained enough; only 10 had prior formal AI training.
quote: Eighty-four percent of trainees agreed with a need for formal AI training, while 73% disagreed that their current curriculum contained enough.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models-Generated Health Education Materials for Discharged Patients with Diabetes: A Comparative Analysis
venue: Journal of diabetes science and technology
outcome: Accuracy of LLM-generated discharge education materials rated by nursing experts
effect: Accuracy scores for all three models were ≥98%, with no significant differences (P > .01).
quote: Accuracy scores for all models were ≥98%, and there were no significant differences in accuracy (P > .01).
sample_unit: de-identified discharge records of patients with diabetes (each yielding LLM-generated education materials)

title: Diagnostic accuracy, fairness and clinical implementation of AI for breast cancer screening: results of multicenter retrospective and prospective technical feasibility studies
outcome: Whether noninterventional prospective deployment revealed problems missed by retrospective validation
effect: Prospective deployment at 12 sites (9,266 cases) confirmed technical feasibility but revealed a distribution shift requiring threshold recalibration.
quote: Prospective deployment confirmed technical feasibility but revealed a distribution shift requiring threshold recalibration.

title: Diagnostic accuracy, fairness and clinical implementation of AI for breast cancer screening: results of multicenter retrospective and prospective technical feasibility studies
outcome: Distribution shift between retrospective development/validation data and prospective deployment data
effect: A distribution shift was revealed in prospective deployment, requiring threshold recalibration.
quote: Prospective deployment confirmed technical feasibility but revealed a distribution shift requiring threshold recalibration.

title: Diagnostic accuracy, fairness and clinical implementation of AI for breast cancer screening: results of multicenter retrospective and prospective technical feasibility studies
outcome: Demographic subgroup performance disparities of the AI system
effect: No systematic demographic disparities were observed in the retrospective analysis.
quote: No systematic demographic disparities were observed.

title: Accuracy of large language model transcription of simulated physician-patient verbal interactions
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: LLM transcription errors: omissions, substitutions, speaker misattribution, medical terminology errors
effect: Mean 73 target word errors (3.3%), 51 deletions (2.3%), 19 semantic errors, 8 medical terminology semantic errors; 15 turn-taking errors (7.3% of turns); 48 mis-attributed speaker word errors (2.2%).
quote: The LLM produced a mean of 73 ± 26 target word errors (3.3% of all target words), comprising 22 ± 13 substitutions (1.0%) and 51 ± 22 deletions (2.3%).

title: Accuracy of large language model transcription of simulated physician-patient verbal interactions
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Errors in AI-generated transcripts that could enter clinical notes if unreviewed
effect: Even modest error rates (3.3% target word errors, 19 semantic errors per interaction) could undermine documentation accuracy; authors caution against autonomous note generation.
quote: Our study found modest error rates, yet meaningful errors persisted that could undermine documentation accuracy, confuse clinicians, and cause patient harm.

title: Accuracy of large language model transcription of simulated physician-patient verbal interactions
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Competing transcription tools' word error rates
effect: NotebookLM: 96 errors, 4.0%; AssemblyAI: 252, 10.4%; Otter.ai: 448, 18.5%.
quote: Across the two interactions with a mean 2416 target words, NotebookLM demonstrated substantially lower overall word error rates (96 total word errors; 4.0% of target words) compared with AssemblyAI (252; 10.4%) and Otter.ai (448; 18.5%).

title: Accuracy of large language model transcription of simulated physician-patient verbal interactions
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Errors associated with overlapping speech
effect: Overlapping speech was associated with 16 ± 12 word errors and 8 ± 7 mis-attributed speaker word errors, 19.1% and 16.3% respectively.
quote: Out of all total word errors (substitutions, deletions, and insertions) and mis-attributed speaker word errors, 16 ± 12 total word errors and 8 ± 7 mis-attributed speaker word errors were associated with overlapping speech, representing 19.1% of total word errors and 16.3% of mis-attributed speaker word errors.

title: Accuracy of large language model transcription of simulated physician-patient verbal interactions
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Audio fidelity and transcription errors
effect: HFA had fewer target word errors than OFA: 23 ± 10, 1.0% vs. 71 ± 25, 3.2%, p = 0.001.
quote: Recordings obtained using higher-fidelity audio (HFA) (Supplemental Table 2 ) demonstrated significantly fewer total target word errors than original-fidelity audio (OFA) (23 ± 10, 1.0% vs. 71 ± 25, 3.2%, respectively, p = 0.001), primarily due to reduced deletions (8 ± 5, 0.4% vs. 56 ± 25, 2.5%, respectively, p = 0.001).

title: Can large language models be trusted? Reliability and readability of responses to perinatal depression FAQs
outcome: Readability of LLM responses versus NIH sixth-grade benchmark
effect: All models exceeded the sixth-grade level on grade-based indices (ARI 13.49 ± 2.92 to 15.81 ± 3.25); OLWF 61.44 to 72.96 versus benchmark 94.
quote: All models exceeded the NIH recommended sixth grade level on grade-based indices (for example, ARI ranged from 13.49 ± 2.92 to 15.81 ± 3.25).

title: Can large language models be trusted? Reliability and readability of responses to perinatal depression FAQs
outcome: Readability of LLM patient-facing answers relative to public health literacy
effect: All five LLMs exceeded sixth-grade level; ARI 13.49 to 15.81; OLWF 61.44 to 72.96 versus benchmark 94, so outputs may be challenging for lower health literacy.
quote: However, readability levels above recommended benchmarks suggest that current outputs may remain challenging for individuals with lower health literacy.

title: Automated Tumor International Classification of Diseases Coding of Real-World Pathology Reports Using Self-Hosted Large Language Models
outcome: LLM ICD-O-3 coding performance on real-world pathology reports versus need for deployment competence
effect: Best exact topography micro-F1 71.6% (Qwen3-235B-A22B); best exact morphology micro-F1 34.7% (DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B); performance not sufficient for fully automated use.
quote: Although LLMs demonstrate promising capabilities as support systems for expert-guided pathology coding, their performance is not yet sufficient for fully automated, unsupervised use in routine clinical workflows.

title: Automated Tumor International Classification of Diseases Coding of Real-World Pathology Reports Using Self-Hosted Large Language Models
outcome: Generalization to rare conditions measured by micro- vs macro-average F1 gap
effect: Large disparities between micro- and macroaverage F1-scores indicated poor generalization to rare conditions.
quote: Large disparities between micro- and macroaverage F1-scores indicated poor generalization to rare conditions.

title: Performance Evaluation of Large Language Models in Multilingual Medical Multiple-Choice Questions: Mixed Methods Study
outcome: LLM accuracy on medical MCQs across input question languages and prompt languages
effect: Accuracy ranged 64%-87%; input language effect significant (P<.01), best on German; English prompts generally better than language-matched, though top models showed comparable results.
quote: The effect of input question language was significant (P<.01) with models performing best on German questions.

title: Knowledge-Guided Explainable Recommendation Tool for Cancer Risk Prediction Models Using Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models: Development and Validation Study
outcome: Expert-rated relevance, reliability and authenticity of RAG-grounded recommendations versus ungrounded LLMs and PubMed
effect: CanRisk-RAG had highest relevance (8.30 [SD 0.59]) and reliability (7.62 [SD 0.76]) on a 10-point scale (P<.05) versus 4 baselines, which often returned incomplete or fabricated results.
quote: Baseline applications frequently returned incomplete, inconsistent, or fabricated results, especially for complex, multifactorial queries, whereas CanRisk-RAG delivered accurate and structured recommendations grounded in validated evidence.

title: Digitally Assisted Clinical Decision-Making in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Comparative Study of 5 Large Language Models
outcome: Decision quality and time for physicians with vs without LLM assistance
effect: Human-AI collaboration scored 33.62 vs physician-only 28.97 (P<.001), 66.1% time reduction (162.6 s vs 479.2 s); AI-only 33.80, not different from collaboration (P=.79).
quote: Pairwise comparisons revealed that human-AI collaboration significantly outperformed physician-only decision-making (paired t 49 =6.603, Cohen d =0.943; P< .001), representing a 116.1% quality improvement.
sample_unit: TCM practitioners (plus 160 exam questions, 30 cases, 5 clinical cases for human-AI comparison)

title: Digitally Assisted Clinical Decision-Making in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Comparative Study of 5 Large Language Models
outcome: Comparison of five LLMs against each other on TCM knowledge and case analysis for model selection
effect: DeepSeek-R1 had 96.7% knowledge accuracy vs 50.6-66.3% for others, and 17.31/20 case score vs 10.02-16.16; chosen as optimal model (P<.001).
quote: Based on superior performance across both evaluation domains and a significant advantage of 15.89 points over the second-ranked model, DeepSeek-R1 was selected as the optimal model for phase 4 clinical application and human-AI collaboration assessment.
sample_unit: TCM practitioners (plus 160 exam questions, 30 cases, 5 clinical cases for human-AI comparison)

title: Digitally Assisted Clinical Decision-Making in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Comparative Study of 5 Large Language Models
outcome: Physician adoption, modification, and rejection of AI-generated plans after review
effect: Of 400 decisions, 74.25% adopted, 24% modified, 1.75% rejected; medication recommendations had 32% adoption and 62% modification.
quote: Collaboration pattern analysis across 400 total decisions revealed high acceptance rates—74.25% (297/400) adoption, 24% (96/400) modification, and 1.75% (7/400) rejection.
sample_unit: TCM practitioners (plus 160 exam questions, 30 cases, 5 clinical cases for human-AI comparison)

title: Digitally Assisted Clinical Decision-Making in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Comparative Study of 5 Large Language Models
outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs and model consistency
effect: Triple repetition; Fleiss kappa 0.969 DeepSeek-R1, 0.953 Gemini, 0.764 Claude, 0.803 GPT-4.5, 0.614 Grok3; case-score SDs across attempts 0.55-2.04.
quote: Internal consistency analysis using Fleiss κ demonstrated excellent reliability for DeepSeek-R1 (κ=0.969) and Gemini 2.0 (κ=0.953), with moderate to good reliability for other models—Claude 3.7 (κ=0.764), GPT-4.5 (κ=0.803), and Grok3 (κ=0.614).
sample_unit: TCM practitioners (plus 160 exam questions, 30 cases, 5 clinical cases for human-AI comparison)

title: Digitally Assisted Clinical Decision-Making in Traditional Chinese Medicine: Comparative Study of 5 Large Language Models
outcome: repeated-run output stability
effect: Stability varied: SD 0.55 Gemini, 0.69 DeepSeek, 1.13 Claude, 1.99 GPT-4.5, 2.04 Grok3.
quote: Model output stability analysis across multiple attempts revealed varying degrees of consistency, with Gemini 2.0 demonstrating the highest stability (mean 16.16, SD 0.55), followed by DeepSeek-R1 (mean 17.31, SD 0.69), Claude 3.7 (mean 14.57, SD 1.13), GPT-4.5 (mean 10.02, SD 1.99), and Grok3 (mean 12.40, SD 2.04).
sample_unit: TCM practitioners (plus 160 exam questions, 30 cases, 5 clinical cases for human-AI comparison)

title: Cardiology knowledge assessment of retrieval-augmented open versus proprietary large language models
outcome: Multiple-choice accuracy on cardiology board questions with versus without RAG over guideline and textbook documents
effect: All 14 models improved after RAG; open-weight Mistral Large 2 reached 78.0% (95% CI 73.9-81.5), comparable to GPT 4o. RAG was particularly beneficial for smaller models.
quote: After RAG, all models improved, and open-weight models like Mistral Large 2 (78.0%, 95% CI: 73.9-81.5) performed comparably to proprietary alternatives like GPT 4o.

title: REAL-WORLD PRACTICE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEM FOR DIABETIC RETINOPATHY IN TAIWAN
outcome: AI diagnostic performance for referable diabetic retinopathy across age and sex subgroups
effect: Overall sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.86, AUC 0.87; performance declined with increasing age, while sex distribution remained consistent across age groups.
quote: Performance declined with increasing age, whereas sex distribution remained consistent across age groups.

title: Strategic Governance of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Clinical Algorithm Development: Formative Evaluation of the Semiautomatic Clinical Algorithm Development Framework
outcome: Whether human expert verification of AI outputs caught errors versus a fully autonomous AI workflow
effect: S-ACAD with 19 human interventions: no critical safety errors found by 2 external specialists; F-ACAD without human review produced 17 issues (9 high-priority). Expert changed AI-generated diazepam pathway to require calling 911. Single case.
quote: Although F-ACAD reviewed more sources and produced a more complex algorithm, its own AI critics identified 17 issues requiring correction, including 9 high-priority concerns related to US standard-of-care compliance, emergency-response clarity, and parent-friendly communication.
sample_unit: algorithm development executions (single expert, single clinical topic: pediatric febrile seizures)

title: Strategic Governance of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Clinical Algorithm Development: Formative Evaluation of the Semiautomatic Clinical Algorithm Development Framework
outcome: Independent clinician review of AI-generated clinical content before deployment
effect: External pediatric emergency physician and pediatrician reviewed the algorithm; none identified critical safety errors; both rated it usable after minor revisions, pending usability testing.
quote: Neither reviewer identified critical safety errors requiring mandatory correction, providing some reassurance that execution bias did not compromise clinical safety in this single-case run.
sample_unit: algorithm development executions (single expert, single clinical topic: pediatric febrile seizures)

title: Strategic Governance of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Clinical Algorithm Development: Formative Evaluation of the Semiautomatic Clinical Algorithm Development Framework
outcome: Whether AI critic (AI sparring) surfaced gaps in AI drafts for expert scrutiny
effect: Claude critic identified 16 improvement suggestions for the Gemini draft; 14 (88%) adopted after expert review (logic gaps 3/3, UX 5/7, missing scenarios 4/4, safety 2/2).
quote: Of these, 14 (88%) were adopted into the final algorithm after expert review.
sample_unit: algorithm development executions (single expert, single clinical topic: pediatric febrile seizures)

title: Strategic Governance of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Clinical Algorithm Development: Formative Evaluation of the Semiautomatic Clinical Algorithm Development Framework
outcome: Comparison of human-checkpointed workflow versus fully autonomous multi-agent workflow on quality issues
effect: Fully autonomous 14-agent system finished in ~68 min vs 245 min but its critics flagged 17 issues (9 high, 8 medium); human-in-loop version had 19 interventions and no critical safety errors identified by external review.
quote: However, this substantial reduction in time was accompanied by notable quality trade-offs.
sample_unit: algorithm development executions (single expert, single clinical topic: pediatric febrile seizures)

title: Strategic Governance of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Clinical Algorithm Development: Formative Evaluation of the Semiautomatic Clinical Algorithm Development Framework
outcome: domain-expert governance versus automation
effect: Expert-governed S-ACAD had no mandatory critical safety corrections; fully automated F-ACAD was 3.6× faster but generated 17 issues, 9 high priority.
quote: The fully automated comparator (F-ACAD), although approximately 3.6 times faster, generated 17 issues (9 high priority) that overlapped with the categories in which human oversight was concentrated in S-ACAD.
sample_unit: algorithm development executions (single expert, single clinical topic: pediatric febrile seizures)

title: Strategic Governance of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Clinical Algorithm Development: Formative Evaluation of the Semiautomatic Clinical Algorithm Development Framework
outcome: standard-of-care and emergency-response errors
effect: F-ACAD had 17 issues requiring correction, including 9 high-priority concerns about US standard-of-care compliance, emergency-response clarity, and communication.
quote: Although F-ACAD reviewed more sources and produced a more complex algorithm, its own AI critics identified 17 issues requiring correction, including 9 high-priority concerns related to US standard-of-care compliance, emergency-response clarity, and parent-friendly communication.
sample_unit: algorithm development executions (single expert, single clinical topic: pediatric febrile seizures)

title: CALM-RAD: Calibrated GPT-4o Confidence-Based Triage Enables 96-100% Accuracy in Automated TNM Staging of Head and Neck Cancer Reports
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Accuracy of GPT-4o TNM labels when uncertain cases are deferred via calibrated confidence triage
effect: Accepting 37% (simple) and 34% (structured) of T-stage predictions raised accuracies to 0.89 and 1.00; accepting 55% of N-stage cases achieved up to 1.00 accuracy.
quote: Triage thresholds accepting 37% (simple) and 34% (structured) of T-stage predictions raised accuracies to 0.89 and 1.00, respectively; accepting 55% of N-stage cases achieved up to 1.00 accuracy.

title: CALM-RAD: Calibrated GPT-4o Confidence-Based Triage Enables 96-100% Accuracy in Automated TNM Staging of Head and Neck Cancer Reports
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Whether calibrated confidence scores separate correct from incorrect LLM predictions
effect: Correct predictions showed higher TLPs than errors (e.g., N-stage U = 1302.5, P < 0.001); calibrated confidence enabled selective triage.
quote: Correct predictions showed higher TLPs than errors (e.g., N-stage U = 1302.5, P < 0.001).

title: PAIR: Evaluating the Limits of Agreement Among Non-Retinal Specialist Using PathFinder Artificial Intelligence Tool for Retinal Disease Referrals: A Prospective Observational Study
outcome: Agreement and sensitivity of AI-assisted non-retina specialists versus retina specialist gold standard
effect: NRS diagnostic kappa 0.78, 0.64, 0.54; specificity >90%; sensitivity 0.57-0.89, lower for AMD and macular hole; referral kappa 0.68, 0.24, 0.34.
quote: Sensitivity varied across raters and diagnoses (0.57-0.89), with comparatively lower sensitivity observed for certain vision-threatening conditions such as age-related macular degeneration and macular hole.

title: Community medical centers struggle to produce well-calibrated clinical prediction models: Data augmentation can help
outcome: Calibration after local recalibration using real and synthetic-data-augmented local samples
effect: Urban center met sample guideline (Required 14,224, Available 42,303) and was best calibrated (α=0.1, β=1.05). Neither smaller site had enough samples (Site 1: 3187 of 16461; Site 2: 905 of 15299). Deep learning SDG most improved calibration.
quote: In the simulation study, deep learning-based SDG was most effective at improving calibration performance.

title: Community medical centers struggle to produce well-calibrated clinical prediction models: Data augmentation can help
outcome: Recalibration sample availability at smaller sites
effect: Site 1 required 16461, available 3187; Site 2 required 15299, available 905.
quote: For the smaller sites, neither site had the samples required for recalibration (Site 1: Required: 16461, Available: 3187; Site 2: Required: 15299, Available: 905).

title: Opportunities and Challenges of Visual Large Language Models in Imaging Diagnostics: Lessons from Brain Metastasis Detection in Clinical MRI
outcome: Specificity and hallucinated lesions in vLLM brain metastasis MRI reports
effect: Sensitivity 100% for both; specificity GPT-4o 8%, Sonnet 3.5 4%; accuracy 54% and 52%; both models hallucinated additional lesions in 12% of cases.
quote: Both models hallucinated additional lesions in 12% of cases.

title: Opportunities and Challenges of Visual Large Language Models in Imaging Diagnostics: Lessons from Brain Metastasis Detection in Clinical MRI
outcome: Real-world clinical MRI performance of general-purpose vLLMs for brain metastasis detection
effect: Very low specificity (8% and 4%) and low accuracy (54% and 52%) on routine clinical MRI; authors state this precludes clinical application.
quote: GPT-4o and Claude Sonnet 3.5 can generate radiological reports and detect brain metastases with excellent sensitivity, but their very low specificity, frequent hallucinations, and limited spatial reliability currently preclude clinical application.

title: PHENO-RAG: An artificial intelligence tool for guideline-informed management decisions in hepatocellular carcinoma
outcome: Exact-match accuracy of LLM treatment decisions with vs without guideline retrieval (RAG) grounding
effect: Accuracy increased with structured inputs, few-shot exemplars, and RAG across all models; best configuration (few-shot+RAG, structured notes) gave GPT-oss-120B 86.5% treatment allocation exact match; zero-shot unstructured baseline substantially lower.
quote: For decision support, accuracy increased with structured inputs, few-shot exemplars, and RAG across all models.

title: Cross-Institutional Five-Class Kellgren-Lawrence Grading of Knee Osteoarthritis via Multitask Deep Learning
venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
outcome: External test accuracy/QWK before vs after fine-tuning on local site data
effect: Zero-shot accuracy 0.661, QWK 0.907; after fine-tuning accuracy 0.800, QWK 0.950, macro-F1 0.634 to 0.783, MAE 0.348 to 0.206.
quote: After fine‐tuning on the external training/validation partitions ( n = 1606 + 344), the same held‐out test ( n = 345) achieved QWK 0.950 (0.903–0.960), accuracy 0.800 (0.708–0.831), macro‐F1 0.783 (0.712–0.811), and MAE 0.206 (0.172–0.306); multiclass ROC AUC rose to 0.946 and KL≥2 ROC AUC rose to 0.984 (Figure 6C ).

title: Cross-Institutional Five-Class Kellgren-Lawrence Grading of Knee Osteoarthritis via Multitask Deep Learning
venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
outcome: Performance variation across sites and scanners
effect: Internal OAI accuracy 0.703 vs external zero-shot held-out 0.661 and macro-F1 0.724 vs 0.634 on a different scanner and site.
quote: On the held‐out 15% external test partition ( n = 345), zero‐shot performance was QWK 0.907 (95% CI 0.869–0.915), accuracy 0.661 (0.605–0.693), macro‐F1 0.634 (0.598–0.692), and MAE 0.348 (0.314–0.402); multiclass ROC AUC was 0.895 and KL≥2 ROC AUC 0.981 (Figure 5D − F ).

title: Cross-Institutional Five-Class Kellgren-Lawrence Grading of Knee Osteoarthritis via Multitask Deep Learning
venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
outcome: Performance drop when model applied to new institution/scanner/population without adaptation
effect: Zero-shot external held-out accuracy 0.661 vs internal 0.703; macro-F1 0.634 vs 0.724; authors describe a 10.7-point macro-F1 domain gap.

title: Comparison of proprietary and fine-tuned large language models for multi-label classification of billing codes from radiology reports
