outcome: Functional stratification accuracy in internal versus real-world cohorts
effect: Functional stratification accuracy was 0.91 in the internal cohort and 0.89 in the real-world cohort; AUC for levator dysfunction was 0.993.
quote: The functional module identified levator dysfunction with an area under the curve of 0.993, achieving robust functional stratification accuracy in both internal (0.91) and real-world (0.89) cohorts.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Lung Nodule Evaluation on Low-Dose Chest CT in Asymptomatic Individuals: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial
outcome: Interpretation time, nodule detection rates, follow-up recommendations, and lung cancer diagnoses with vs without AI in randomized trial
effect: No significant difference in interpretation time (187 vs 172 s, p=.23); higher Lung-RADS-positive detection (16.9% vs 10.3%), all-nodule detection (52.9% vs 32.6%), follow-up LDCT recommendations (15.3% vs 7.4%); no lung cancers diagnosed in either group.
quote: Use of an AI-based nodule evaluation tool integrated into PACS during real-world clinical workflows was not associated with a significant difference in interpretation times.

title: Automated Flow and local LLM-Driven clinical Context Engineering: Precision colorectal cancer recurrence registry
outcome: Accuracy of rule-based LLM versus standard Taiwan Cancer Registry process against manual reference
effect: Rule-Based LLM achieved 90.7% accuracy, comparable to standard TCR processes (92.0%), with 77.2% sensitivity.
quote: Under a strict 60-day temporal tolerance, the Rule-Based LLM achieved 90.7% accuracy, comparable to standard TCR processes (92.0%), and 77.2% sensitivity.
sample_unit: patients (20% manual reference standard subset of 3053 CRC patients)

title: Automated Flow and local LLM-Driven clinical Context Engineering: Precision colorectal cancer recurrence registry
outcome: specificity after validation rules
effect: Specificity improved from 87.7% (Raw LLM) to 93.9% (Rule-Based LLM).
quote: The application of clinical validation rules significantly improved specificity from 87.7% (Raw LLM) to 93.9% (Rule-Based LLM).
sample_unit: patients (20% manual reference standard subset of 3053 CRC patients)

title: Automated Flow and local LLM-Driven clinical Context Engineering: Precision colorectal cancer recurrence registry
outcome: Specificity of raw LLM versus LLM with clinical validation rules against manual reference standard
effect: Clinical validation rules significantly improved specificity from 87.7% (Raw LLM) to 93.9% (Rule-Based LLM).
quote: The application of clinical validation rules significantly improved specificity from 87.7% (Raw LLM) to 93.9% (Rule-Based LLM).
sample_unit: patients (20% manual reference standard subset of 3053 CRC patients)

title: Pediatric nurses' use of generative artificial intelligence and their competency levels
outcome: Proportion of pediatric nurses with AI training and self-perceived competence using generative AI
effect: Only 9.3% (n = 51) had received AI training; 77.2% (n = 27) of generative AI users did not feel competent; mean scale score 48.97 ± 10.07.
quote: It was determined that very few nurses had received training related to artificial intelligence (9.3%, n = 51), used generative artificial intelligence applications, and that the majority of those who used them (77.2%, n = 27) did not feel competent while using the applications.

title: From tool to teammate in a randomized controlled trial of clinician-AI collaborative workflows for diagnosis
outcome: Clinician diagnostic score with AI first, AI second, versus conventional resources; AI alone
effect: Conventional 75% vs AI first 85% (mean diff 9.9%, p=0.00039) and AI second 82% (6.8%, p=3.3e-6); clinicians with AI not significantly different from AI alone.
quote: Clinicians using conventional resources only had a significantly lower overall score (75%) than either AI arm, with the clinicians’ using AI as a first opinion (85%, p = 0.00039, mean difference=9.9%, 95% CI = 4.7–15%), or AI as a second opinion (82%, p = 3.3e−6, mean difference=6.8%, 95% CI = 4.0–9.6%).

title: From tool to teammate in a randomized controlled trial of clinician-AI collaborative workflows for diagnosis
outcome: Anchoring and automation bias in AI-assisted diagnosis; score decreases after AI
effect: Actionable scores decreased after AI engagement in 8% of cases; AI second-opinion outputs overlapped fully with clinician input in 48% of cases vs 3% for AI first, suggesting anchoring.
quote: Scores on clinically actionable decisions decreased after engagement with the AI in 8% of cases, highlighting the possibility that AI recommendations can interfere with performance.

title: From tool to teammate in a randomized controlled trial of clinician-AI collaborative workflows for diagnosis
outcome: Nondeterminism of LLM output across participants for the same vignette
effect: AI generated different recommended diagnostic assessments across participants for the same vignette input; also omitted the joint analysis in 10% of second-opinion cases.
quote: We also observed non-determinism, whereby the AI system could generate different recommended diagnostic assessments across participants for the same vignette input, raising concerns about reliability and replicability in clinical decision support.

title: From tool to teammate in a randomized controlled trial of clinician-AI collaborative workflows for diagnosis
outcome: Incorrect LLM output that clinicians would need to verify (hallucinated facts)
effect: The AI claimed a patient had a fever at 99.6 F; a participant caught the error; AI omitted the synthesis view in 10% of second-opinion cases.
quote: For example, one participant in the AI-as-first-opinion group noticed that the AI system claimed the patient in Case 1 (Supplementary Fig. 3 ) had a fever when they had a temperature of 99.6 F (a fever is defined by the CDC as ≥100.4 °F).

title: From tool to teammate in a randomized controlled trial of clinician-AI collaborative workflows for diagnosis
outcome: Human-AI team performance in intended workflow versus conventional resources and AI alone
effect: Both collaborative workflows improved clinician scores over conventional resources (85% and 82% vs 75%); the two workflows did not differ overall (p=0.22), and actionable-decision scores were 8.9% higher with AI first (p=0.026).
quote: Clinicians in the AI-as-first-opinion arm scored 8.9% better than the AI-as-second-opinion arm ( p = 0.026, 95% CI 1.1–16%).

title: Quality assessment of large language model-generated prior authorization letters in nephrology
outcome: Validity of references and citations in LLM-generated prior authorization letters
effect: 27 of 29 letters (93.1%) cited valid references; one letter cited an incorrect trial and another cited a correct KDIGO guideline with an inaccessible link.
quote: 27 letters (93.1%) cited valid references, with one letter citing an incorrect trial and another one citing a correct KDIGO guideline with inaccessible link.

title: Quality assessment of large language model-generated prior authorization letters in nephrology
outcome: Correctness of ICD-10 diagnosis coding in LLM-generated letters
effect: ICD-10 code correct in 23 of 29 letters (79.3%); errors mostly involved CKD staging or internal diagnostic inconsistencies.
quote: The ICD-10 diagnosis code was correct in 23 letters (79.3%), most errors were related to chronic kidney disease (CKD) staging or internal diagnostic inconsistencies.

title: Advancing clinical utility of artificial intelligence: lessons from developing a model to predict cochlear implant eligibility
outcome: Model sensitivity and PPV versus existing referral heuristics for CI candidacy
effect: Binary classification models achieved sensitivity of 90.4% with PPV 80.2% at CNC 50/AzBio 60, outperforming referral heuristics (60/60 and 75/40).
quote: Binary classification models achieved sensitivity of 90.4% with PPV 80.2% at CNC 50/AzBio 60, outperforming referral heuristics (60/60 and 75/40).

title: Advancing clinical utility of artificial intelligence: lessons from developing a model to predict cochlear implant eligibility
outcome: Effect of test-retest noise in predictor inputs on attainable model precision
effect: Variability analyses indicated that attainable precision is bounded by noise in key predictors.
quote: Variability analyses indicated that attainable precision is bounded by noise in key predictors.

title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease
outcome: Discrimination before and after refitting model on representative provincial data with site-level calibration and thresholds
effect: Provincial refit AUROC 0.794 vs 0.714 for local model on other sites; ICAs avoided 27 of 39 vs 21 of 36; performance recovered across all sites.
quote: Following updating, model AUROC recovered almost entirely at 0.794 (95% CI: 0.794, 0.795) compared with 0.807 (95% CI: 0.806, 0.808) for the original local test set.

title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease

quote: AUROC across individual sites ranged from a high of 0.851 (95% CI: 0.850, 0.852) to a low of 0.608 (95% CI: 0.607, 0.609).

title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease

quote: The local model performed best for Asian patients (AUROC = 0.704 [95% CI: 0.702, 0.705]) and worst for Black patients (AUROC = 0.612 [95% CI: 0.609, 0.614]).

title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease

title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease
outcome: Temporal drift in AUROC using sliding-window annual updating simulation

title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease
outcome: Model performance and impact across sex, age, ethnicity and marginalization subgroups

quote: The local model performed best for Asian patients (AUROC = 0.704 [95% CI: 0.702, 0.705]) and worst for Black patients (AUROC = 0.612 [95% CI: 0.609, 0.614]).

title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease
outcome: Fairness metrics across demographic subgroups and sites beyond aggregate results
effect: Aggregate AUROC hid subgroup and site gaps: local model AUROC 0.608-0.851 across sites; ICA avoided 13/29 for men vs 34/47 for women; updating narrowed ethnic gaps.

title: An artificial intelligence prediction model for optimizing patient selection for cardiac imaging for the investigation of suspected coronary artery disease
outcome: Distribution of benefit (unnecessary ICAs avoided) across sex, age and ethnic groups

quote: Benefits, however, were skewed heavily towards females, with 42 out of every 50 unnecessary ICAs avoided (specificity: 83.3%) compared with only 18 out of every 32 (specificity: 56.5%) for males (see Supplementary material online , Figure S4 ).

title: A Pilot Study to Evaluate Artificial Intelligence-Driven Early Retrieval of Medical Histories in the Emergency Department
outcome: Hallucinations in AI-generated histories of present illness, as reviewed by pediatric emergency physicians
effect: Physician reviewers noted no hallucinations in the final transcripts, though summaries sometimes lacked important features of prior visits.
quote: They noted no hallucinations in the final transcripts.

title: AI-based triage and decision support in mammography and digital tomosynthesis for breast cancer screening: a paired, noninferiority trial
outcome: Workload, cancer detection, and recall when AI-classified low-risk exams skip radiologist reading
effect: Compared with standard double reading of all exams, the AI strategy cut workload 63.6%. Cancer detection rose 15.2% (6.3 to 7.3 per 1,000). Recall rose 14.8%, failing noninferiority.
quote: In the AI strategy, radiologist workload was 63.6% lower; the cancer detection rate was 15.2% higher (95% confidence interval 6.6%, 24.4%), increasing from 6.3 of 1,000 to 7.3 of 1,000, P < 0.001; and the recall rate was not noninferior and was 14.8% higher (95% confidence interval 9.0%, 20.6%).

title: AI-based triage and decision support in mammography and digital tomosynthesis for breast cancer screening: a paired, noninferiority trial
outcome: Radiologist workload by imaging modality
effect: Radiologist workload decreased in digital mammography (-62.1%) and digital breast tomosynthesis (-65.5%).
quote: Subanalyses by modality highlighted a similar workload reduction in digital mammography (-62.1%) and digital breast tomosynthesis (-65.5%).

title: AI-based triage and decision support in mammography and digital tomosynthesis for breast cancer screening: a paired, noninferiority trial
outcome: workload and cancer detection
effect: Automating low-risk case review while routing other cases to humans lowered workload by 63.6% and increased cancer detection by 15.2%.
quote: In the AI strategy, radiologist workload was 63.6% lower; the cancer detection rate was 15.2% higher (95% confidence interval 6.6%, 24.4%), increasing from 6.3 of 1,000 to 7.3 of 1,000, P < 0.001; and the recall rate was not noninferior and was 14.8% higher (95% confidence interval 9.0%, 20.6%).

title: AI-based triage and decision support in mammography and digital tomosynthesis for breast cancer screening: a paired, noninferiority trial
outcome: performance by acquisition modality
effect: The AI strategy's impact on cancer detection and recall rates differed depending on whether digital mammography or digital breast tomosynthesis was used.
quote: However, in digital mammography, the cancer detection rate increased by 1.6 of 1,000 and the recall rate by 1.3%, while both remained stable in digital breast tomosynthesis.

title: Advancing diagnostic equity through artificial intelligence chest radiograph screening for osteoporosis in Asian populations
outcome: AI performance across BMI and sex subgroups versus aggregate performance
effect: Population-level AUC 0.95 and sensitivity 79.7%; intersectional subgroup analyses were exploratory because of small event counts. Decision curve net benefit was highest for women with normal BMI.
quote: Although BMI distributions paralleled East Asian regional trends, intersectional subgroup analyses remain exploratory due to small event counts.

title: Effect of Emotional Prompt on the Quality of ChatGPT Based Discharge Instructions After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Using ERAS Derived Benchmarks
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM discharge instructions against ERAS-derived 43-item benchmark
effect: No factual inaccuracies or harmful statements found in any output; completeness gaps, e.g., full antibiotic details in 25.0%, fibre reintroduction 41.7%, adaptation period 30.0%.
quote: An expert review, conducted using a structured benchmark form to record any concerns, revealed no factual inaccuracies, recommendations inconsistent with evidence-based guidelines, or potentially harmful instructions in any of the ChatGPT-generated outputs, regardless of the prompt type.
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated discharge instruction outputs (30 per prompt type)

title: Effect of Emotional Prompt on the Quality of ChatGPT Based Discharge Instructions After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Using ERAS Derived Benchmarks
outcome: Completeness of LLM clinical content against ERAS guidelines
effect: Core domains 100% present, but full antibiotic details only 25.0%, fibre reintroduction 41.7%, adaptation period 30.0%, GI symptom monitoring 33.3%.
quote: Only 25.0% of outputs addressed full antibiotic prescription details, while specific dietary components (eg, vegetables, fruits, cereals) were each covered in fewer than 25.0% of cases.
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated discharge instruction outputs (30 per prompt type)

title: Effect of Emotional Prompt on the Quality of ChatGPT Based Discharge Instructions After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Using ERAS Derived Benchmarks
outcome: Effect of emotional prompt framing on completeness and accuracy of generated instructions
effect: No significant differences in completeness for any of 43 features (all p ≥ .05); relative effects near 0.50; tone changed markedly (CRI up to 5.28 vs 0 in 26/30 PP outputs).
quote: No statistically significant differences in completeness were found between outputs generated with EP-type prompts and those generated with PP-type prompts for any feature (all p ≥.05, Fisher’s exact test).
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated discharge instruction outputs (30 per prompt type)

title: Effect of Emotional Prompt on the Quality of ChatGPT Based Discharge Instructions After Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy Using ERAS Derived Benchmarks
outcome: overall completeness by emotional prompt
effect: Overall EP 29.03 (SD 2.312) vs PP 28.50 (SD 2.446), p=0.414; relative effect 0.44 (95% CI 0.29–0.59).
quote: Importantly, the Brunner Munzel analysis of domain level completeness did not reveal statistically significant differences between PP and EP outputs, with relative effect estimates close to 0.50 across domains.
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated discharge instruction outputs (30 per prompt type)

title: Feasibility of a Large Language Model Chatbot to Support Parental Understanding in the PICU
outcome: Accuracy of EHR-grounded chatbot sentences rated by clinicians; error severity
effect: Of 1225 sentences, 99.3% accurate; eight errors, all minor; Gwet's AC2 = 0.98 (95% CI 0.97-0.99).
quote: Of 1225 chatbot-generated sentences evaluated, 99.3% were accurate with all eight errors classified as minor (inter-rater reliability: Gwet's AC2, a chance-corrected inter-rater agreement coefficient, = 0.98; 95% CI, 0.97-0.99).

title: Radiographers' role in the age of AI: A qualitative comparative multi case study
outcome: Radiographers' formal AI training availability
effect: Participants reported a lack of training; formal AI training is absent in Sweden and remains limited despite AI in workflows such as image reconstruction, protocol optimisation and patient positioning.
quote: Participants reported a lack of training and uncertainty about the future, as radiographers' roles are rarely considered in technology implementation.
sample_unit: interview participants (section leaders, researchers, department managers)

title: Radiographers' role in the age of AI: A qualitative comparative multi case study
outcome: Radiographer concerns about deskilling and loss of identity from AI
effect: Participants viewed AI as both a facilitator and a potential threat to core tasks, raising concerns about deskilling and loss of identity; maintaining competence was highlighted as critical.
quote: Participants viewed AI as both a facilitator of daily work and a potential threat to core tasks, raising concerns about deskilling and loss of identity.
sample_unit: interview participants (section leaders, researchers, department managers)

title: DeepSeek-R1 performance in fusion planning of adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: A preliminary study
outcome: Rate of surgically reasonable fusion levels by Lenke curve subtype
effect: Overall 70.9% (144/203) reasonable; varied significantly by Lenke subtype: high for 1A (87.0%), 1B (82.9%), 5C (81.1%), 6C (87.5%), low for 1C (19.0%), 2A (42.9%), 2C (25.0%).
quote: Performance varied significantly by Lenke subtype, demonstrating high reasonable rates for types 1A (87.0%), 1B (82.9%), 5C (81.1%), and 6C (87.5%).

title: High-sensitivity pan-cancer AI assessment of lymph node metastasis via uncertainty quantification
outcome: uncertainty-based deferral of potential false negatives
effect: Flagging potential false-negative predictions intercepted all missed diagnoses; 100% conditional sensitivity in development and independent test cohorts.
quote: Crucially, the uncertainty module functioned as a decisive fail-safe: by flagging potential false-negative predictions for mandatory pathologist review, it intercepted all missed diagnoses, securing 100% conditional sensitivity across both the development and independent test cohorts-even for tumors from seven unseen primary origins.

title: High-sensitivity pan-cancer AI assessment of lymph node metastasis via uncertainty quantification
outcome: uncertainty fail-safe sensitivity
effect: The uncertainty module intercepted all missed diagnoses and secured 100% conditional sensitivity across development and independent test cohorts.
quote: Crucially, the uncertainty module functioned as a decisive fail-safe: by flagging potential false-negative predictions for mandatory pathologist review, it intercepted all missed diagnoses, securing 100% conditional sensitivity across both the development and independent test cohorts-even for tumors from seven unseen primary origins.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o as a text-based clinical decision support tool for junior otolaryngology residents: A randomized controlled trial
venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: AIPI scores of ChatGPT-4o versus board-certified otolaryngologist on same PGY1 consultation outputs
effect: Mean AIPI score for ChatGPT-4o was higher than otolaryngologist (14.20 ± 2.24 versus 12.34 ± 1.91; p = 0.001); comparable on history, clinical presentation, primary diagnosis, management plan.
quote: The mean AIPI score for ChatGPT-4o was significantly higher than the otolaryngologist score (14.20 ± 2.24 versus 12.34 ± 1.91; p = 0.001).

title: AI-assisted tumor board decision-making in pancreatic oncology

effect: Best accuracy 78.6% (micro-F1 0.786) for advanced zero-shot and CoT, but Recall NEO = 0.00 (0/7); few-shot Recall NEO = 1.00 with overall accuracy 56.7%.
quote: Crucially, both high-accuracy strategies failed to identify any of the neoadjuvant therapy candidates (Recall NEO = 0.00; 0/7 cases), systematically misclassifying them as palliative or surgical.

title: AI-assisted tumor board decision-making in pancreatic oncology
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Whether aggregate accuracy conceals poor category-specific performance

title: Performance validation of large language models for drug-drug interaction consultations: Potential pharmacist assistant in outpatient pharmaceutical services
venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA

title: Performance validation of large language models for drug-drug interaction consultations: Potential pharmacist assistant in outpatient pharmaceutical services
venue: Journal of the American Pharmacists Association : JAPhA
outcome: LLM responses compared against pharmacist answers on the same queries

title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of fetal hypoxia: a multicenter model development and nationwide AI-human comparison
outcome: AUROC of AI models versus human experts on same held-out CTG cases
effect: All CAP models achieved higher AUROC than 10,571 expert responses (0.757-0.789 vs. 0.715, DeLong P < 0.05).
quote: In comparison with 10,571 expert responses, all CAP models achieved higher AUROC (0.757-0.789 vs. 0.715, P values in Delong test < 0.05).

title: Artificial intelligence-based prediction of fetal hypoxia: a multicenter model development and nationwide AI-human comparison

title: Concordance of ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and OpenEvidence with the 2024 AAOS guidelines on acute isolated meniscal pathology
outcome: Concordance with AAOS meniscal guidelines: evidence-grounded OpenEvidence versus general LLMs

title: Concordance of ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and OpenEvidence with the 2024 AAOS guidelines on acute isolated meniscal pathology

title: Challenges of using generative AI for patient education in chronic heart failure: an evaluation of content quality, readability, and actionability in cross-platform LLM-generated texts
outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of LLM-generated CHF patient education texts
effect: DeepSeek-R1 lowest readability (FRES 19.32, FKGL 14.28); ERNIEBot and Qwen most readable (FRES ≈ 59; FKGL ≈ 8), still above typical patient reading levels for some platforms.

title: Challenges of using generative AI for patient education in chronic heart failure: an evaluation of content quality, readability, and actionability in cross-platform LLM-generated texts
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility and actionability of LLM patient education outputs
effect: Overall quality high (GQS median 5.00), but readability varied widely across platforms and PEMAT-P actionability was limited overall at 20.00% (0.00-40.00).
quote: Actionability was limited overall [PEMAT-P actionability 20.00% (0.00-40.00); χ2 = 26.40, P < 0.001] and varied by topic, with daily management and prevention outperforming disease knowledge and diagnosis/classification (χ2 = 20.86, P < 0.001).

title: Assessing the accuracy of 4 generative AI tools to guide dosing of long-acting injectable antipsychotics
venue: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
outcome: Accuracy of AI dosing recommendations for long-acting injectable antipsychotics initiation and missed doses
effect: OpenEvidence 95% accurate (one inaccurate response); ChatGPT 40% accurate; 62% of inaccuracies occurred in missed-dose scenarios.
quote: OpenEvidence was the most accurate, providing an inacurate response to only one query (a 95% accuracy rate). ChatGPT was the least accurate, with a 40% accuracy rate.
sample_unit: queries per AI tool (LAIA initiation and missed-dose dosing scenarios)

title: Assessing the accuracy of 4 generative AI tools to guide dosing of long-acting injectable antipsychotics
venue: American journal of health-system pharmacy : AJHP : official journal of the American Society of Health-System Pharmacists
outcome: Incorrect AI dosing outputs that clinicians might act on without verification
effect: Accuracy varied significantly across tools; ChatGPT 40% accurate; most inaccuracies (62%) in missed-dose scenarios, supporting need to verify against package inserts.
quote: Most of the inaccuracies (62%) occurred when the AI tools provided recommendations related to missed-dose scenarios.
sample_unit: queries per AI tool (LAIA initiation and missed-dose dosing scenarios)

title: Comparative Evaluation of Advanced Reasoning Models for Clinical Decision Support in Urology
outcome: Accuracy of LLMs versus experienced urologists and medical students on the same urology questions
effect: All five AI models had significantly higher odds of correct answers than experienced urologists (all p < 0.001, Dunnett-adjusted); medical students did not differ significantly from urologists.
quote: In the model-adjusted analysis, all five AI models showed significantly higher odds of correct answers than experienced urologists (all p < 0.001, Dunnett-adjusted), while medical students did not differ significantly from urologists.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT-4o's Quality and Readability in Preoperative Facial Plastic Surgery Counseling: A Vignette-Based Analysis
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of ChatGPT-4o preoperative counseling responses
effect: Average Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 8.4, within the recommended range, suitable for most patient populations.
quote: Readability remained within the recommended range, with an average Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 8.4, suitable for most patient populations.
sample_unit: ChatGPT responses to vignette prompts for 5 aesthetic procedures

title: Harnessing Large Language Models in Neonatal Intraventricular Hemorrhage: Exploring Retrieval Augmented Generation Methodology for Prognostic Variable Discovery
outcome: Hallucinated or unverifiable references among LLM-identified studies
effect: LLMs initially identified 39 studies; 28 met some or all validation criteria after excluding hallucinated references (about 11 excluded).
quote: LLMs initially identified 39 studies, with 28 meeting some or all the validation criteria after excluding references that were hallucinated.

title: Harnessing Large Language Models in Neonatal Intraventricular Hemorrhage: Exploring Retrieval Augmented Generation Methodology for Prognostic Variable Discovery
outcome: Whether manual validation of LLM outputs catches hallucinated or incomplete content
effect: Manual validation excluded hallucinated references from 39 LLM-identified studies (28 retained); authors conclude LLM outputs were susceptible to hallucinations and incomplete synthesis, requiring human validation.
quote: However, LLM outputs were susceptible to hallucinations and incomplete data synthesis, underscoring the need for rigorous clinical oversight and human validation to ensure reliability.

title: Engineering framework for curiosity-driven and humble AI in clinical decision support
outcome: Clinical response quality, hedging (humility) and context-seeking with vs without BODHI uncertainty framework
effect: Overall quality +16.6 pp (GPT-4.1-mini, d=11.56) and +2.2 pp (GPT-4o-mini, d=1.56); hedging d=5.80 for GPT-4.1-mini; context seeking d=16.38 and 19.54.
quote: BODHI improved overall clinical response quality (GPT-4.1-mini: +16.6 pp, p<0.0001, Cohen's d=11.56; GPT-4o-mini: +2.2 pp, p<0.0001, Cohen's d=1.56) and achieved very large effect sizes on curiosity (context seeking rate: Cohen's d=16.38 and 19.54) and humility (hedging: d=5.80 for GPT-4.1-mini) metrics.
sample_unit: clinical vignettes (HealthBench Hard), 5 random seeds, 2000 observations

title: Comparative evaluation of multimodal large language models for diagnostic accuracy in pediatric electrocardiography: a prospective comparative diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Emergency arrhythmia detection and overcalling by multimodal LLMs on pediatric ECGs
effect: Gemini had 100% sensitivity (95% CI 85.1-100.0) for emergency abnormality, -LR 0.07, in n=22, but specificity 30.2% and +LR 1.40, indicating overcalling (unnecessary escalation).
quote: For the emergency endpoint, Gemini achieved 100% sensitivity (95% CI = 85.1-100.0) with - LR 0.07 (95% CI = 0.00-1.12) in a small subgroup (n = 22); however, specificity of 30.2% and + LR of 1.40 indicate overcalling rather than diagnostic precision.

title: Comparative evaluation of multimodal large language models for diagnostic accuracy in pediatric electrocardiography: a prospective comparative diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Diagnostic performance of LLMs on prospectively collected real pediatric ECGs
effect: AUC ranged from 0.550 to 0.623 (modest discrimination); +LR 2.05, 1.26, 1.21 and -LR 0.68, 0.55, 0.81 for clinically significant abnormality; no model achieved meaningful rule-in utility.
quote: No model achieved clinically meaningful rule-in utility for either endpoint.

title: Comparative evaluation of multimodal large language models for diagnostic accuracy in pediatric electrocardiography: a prospective comparative diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Suitability of multimodal LLM outputs as standalone diagnosis of pediatric ECG
effect: +LR values near 1.0 across both endpoints; authors conclude standalone deployment is not supported and tools may only serve as adjunctive screening aids under clinician oversight.
quote: Standalone deployment is not supported; these tools may at most serve as adjunctive screening aids under clinician oversight.

title: From Guidelines to Clicklists: GPT-5-Generated ERAS Checklists Improve Guideline Coverage for Bariatric and Gastrointestinal Cancer Surgery-A STROBE-Compatible Cross-Sectional Evaluation
outcome: Guideline-item coverage and clarity of GPT-5 checklists versus guideline-derived traditional checklists
effect: AI coverage 97.0% ± 2.1% vs 89.0% ± 3.2% for traditional; clarity 4.8 ± 0.2 vs 4.2 ± 0.3 (p = 0.021).
quote: AI-generated checklists demonstrated higher mean guideline-item coverage than traditional checklists (97.0% ± 2.1% vs. 89.0% ± 3.2%) and higher clarity scores (4.8 ± 0.2 vs. 4.2 ± 0.3; p = 0.021).

title: The Impact of Evaluation Strategy on Sepsis Prediction Model Performance Metrics in Intensive Care Data: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: AUROC drop when applying MIMIC-IV-trained sepsis model to German ICU data
effect: Continuous evaluation, 6-hour horizon: AUROC 0.67 (95% CI 0.66-0.68) on BerlinICU versus 0.84 (95% CI 0.83-0.85) on MIMIC-IV test set.
quote: Application of a temporal convolutional network model to BerlinICU yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.67 (95% CI 0.66-0.68) for continuous evaluation with a 6-hour prediction horizon, compared with 0.84 (95% CI 0.83-0.85) on the test set of Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV.

title: The Impact of Evaluation Strategy on Sepsis Prediction Model Performance Metrics in Intensive Care Data: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: Variation in AUROC across evaluation strategies for the same model and dataset
effect: Fixed horizon AUROC 0.61 (95% CI 0.60-0.62) versus about 0.67 for continuous and peak score evaluation; metrics improved with shorter horizons.
quote: The same model applied to the same dataset yields markedly different performance metrics depending on the evaluation approach.

title: Integrated Implementation Strategies to Promote the Use of AI-Assisted Diagnostic Software for Lung Nodule Screening in China: Process Evaluation Based on the RE-AIM Framework
outcome: Clinician burden and workflow disruption associated with a separate referral-data platform
effect: ESDR-related burden was reported by 55.6% (5/9) of secondary-hospital respiratory physicians; 62.5% (5/8) at the tertiary hospital reported workflow disruptions associated with external platform access.
quote: However, 55.6% (5/9) of respiratory physicians indicated that the ESDR tool imposed a substantial burden on daily tasks.

title: Integrated Implementation Strategies to Promote the Use of AI-Assisted Diagnostic Software for Lung Nodule Screening in China: Process Evaluation Based on the RE-AIM Framework
outcome: Perceived workflow disruption of PACS-integrated AI vs non-integrated ESDR tool
effect: 93.3% (14/15) said PACS-integrated AI did not interfere with practice; 55.6% (5/9) said the non-integrated ESDR tool imposed substantial burden; only 28% complete referral records and 44.4% reviewed feedback.
quote: However, 55.6% (5/9) of respiratory physicians indicated that the ESDR tool imposed a substantial burden on daily tasks.

title: Integrated Implementation Strategies to Promote the Use of AI-Assisted Diagnostic Software for Lung Nodule Screening in China: Process Evaluation Based on the RE-AIM Framework
outcome: Completion and timeliness of structured referral following AI-assisted screening
effect: Referral completion was 88% (22/25); the median interval from referral submission to hospital visit was 3 (IQR 2‐4) days. Referral outcomes lacked a historical comparison.
quote: At the patient level, of the 25 individuals who consented to referral, 22 successfully completed the referral process by visiting the tertiary hospital, yielding a referral completion rate of 88%.

title: Integrated Implementation Strategies to Promote the Use of AI-Assisted Diagnostic Software for Lung Nodule Screening in China: Process Evaluation Based on the RE-AIM Framework
outcome: Successful automated transfer of CT images and AI results between hospitals
effect: CT image transmission succeeded for 90.9% (20/22); two patients experienced PACS-related transmission failures and were required to carry physical CT films to the tertiary hospital.
quote: Despite a relatively high CT image transmission success rate of 90.9% (20/22), system-level failures persisted.

title: Integrated Implementation Strategies to Promote the Use of AI-Assisted Diagnostic Software for Lung Nodule Screening in China: Process Evaluation Based on the RE-AIM Framework
outcome: data transmission failures
effect: Two of the 22 successfully referred patients experienced data transmission failures that prevented the upload of AI-generated results and images.
quote: Among the 22 patients who successfully completed the referral process, two experienced data transmission failures due to PACS system malfunctions at the secondary hospital, which prevented the upload of AI-generated results and CT images to the ESDR platform.

title: A Bilingual Arabic-English Ambient AI Scribe for Clinical Documentation: Prospective Evaluation Study
outcome: Ambient scribe note accuracy compared between Arabic and English encounters
effect: Accuracy mean 4.53 (SD 0.46) out of 5 for Arabic vs 4.77 (SD 0.37) for English (P=.06); Arabic slightly lower but not significant.
quote: On the Likert scale, for the accuracy domain, the mean score was 4.53 (SD 0.46) out of 5 for Arabic compared with 4.77 (SD 0.37) out of 5 for English (P=.06).

title: Using ChatGPT‑4.0 to Address Nurse Scheduling Challenges in a Cardiology Clinic
outcome: Whether human review corrected gaps in ChatGPT-generated nurse schedules
effect: Hybrid 4×10/5×8 schedule met daily coverage and maintained equity but gave no redundancy for absences; human review resolved role-specific gaps.
quote: A hybrid 4×10/5×8 model met daily coverage 5 Outpatient Care Center (OCC), 1 Heart Center (HC), and maintained equity, but provided no redundancy for absences; human review resolved role‑specific gaps.

title: Large Language Model-Powered Diagnostic Co-Pilot ("CapyEngine") for Mental Disorders: Development, Evaluation, and Future Optimization Study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of candidate LLM tools versus clinicians and general LLM on same questions
effect: ChatGPT-4o outperformed CapyEngine and clinicians at top 10 and top 5 (all P<.03); clinicians beat CapyEngine at top 5 (OR 0.26, P=.02); top 1 no significant differences.
quote: Across diagnostic accuracy thresholds, ChatGPT-4o consistently outperformed both CapyEngine and clinicians in broader rankings (top 10 and top 5 benchmarks; all P<.03).

title: Evaluating Patient and Professional Satisfaction and Documentation Time Reduction Through AI-Driven Automatic Clinical Note Generation in Primary Care: Proof-of-Concept Study
outcome: Clinician-reported errors in AI-generated consultation notes, including hallucinations, and edit burden
effect: Context or meaning errors were most frequent; unsupported additions or hallucinations were uncommon; 26% of drafts required no edits; most reviews were <24 corrected words per minute.
quote: A qualitative analysis of clinician feedback showed that context or meaning errors were the most frequent, while unsupported additions or hallucinations were uncommon.

title: Investigation of Bias Using ChatGPT-4 in Pain Management and Patient Profiling
outcome: Whether LLM pain recommendations change when patient demographic attributes in prompts are varied
effect: Race, language, and socioeconomic status often did not alter recommendations; opioid use disorder history consistently changed suggestions (opioid-sparing). Overall agreement 82% for ED medications, 78% for discharge medications.
quote: When using cGPT, demographic factors such as race, language, and socioeconomic status often did not alter recommendations.

title: Towards fair and trustworthy heart rate estimation from wrist-worn photoplethysmography: a multi-wavelength dataset and uncertainty-aware deep learning approach evaluated across skin tones, sexes, and motion conditions
outcome: MAE and skin-tone parity gap
effect: Uncertainty-guided rejection reduced MAE and skin-tone parity gap from 1.2 BPM to 0.0 BPM.
quote: Baseline error was higher for participants with darker skin tones and for females; uncertainty-guided rejection reduced MAE and effectively eliminated these gaps (reducing parity gaps from 1.2 BPM to 0.0 BPM for skin tone).

title: Towards fair and trustworthy heart rate estimation from wrist-worn photoplethysmography: a multi-wavelength dataset and uncertainty-aware deep learning approach evaluated across skin tones, sexes, and motion conditions
outcome: Heart rate MAE parity gaps across skin tone and sex before and after uncertainty-guided rejection
effect: Baseline error was higher for darker skin tones and females; uncertainty-guided rejection reduced MAE and effectively eliminated gaps (skin tone parity gap from 1.2 BPM to 0.0 BPM).
quote: Baseline error was higher for participants with darker skin tones and for females; uncertainty-guided rejection reduced MAE and effectively eliminated these gaps (reducing parity gaps from 1.2 BPM to 0.0 BPM for skin tone).

title: Towards fair and trustworthy heart rate estimation from wrist-worn photoplethysmography: a multi-wavelength dataset and uncertainty-aware deep learning approach evaluated across skin tones, sexes, and motion conditions
outcome: Baseline subgroup error
effect: Baseline error was higher for darker skin tones and females; skin-tone parity gap was 1.2 BPM before rejection.
quote: Baseline error was higher for participants with darker skin tones and for females; uncertainty-guided rejection reduced MAE and effectively eliminated these gaps (reducing parity gaps from 1.2 BPM to 0.0 BPM for skin tone).

title: Towards fair and trustworthy heart rate estimation from wrist-worn photoplethysmography: a multi-wavelength dataset and uncertainty-aware deep learning approach evaluated across skin tones, sexes, and motion conditions
outcome: Uncertainty calibration
effect: Concrete dropout had lowest average miscalibration area (MA=0.12) with competitive MAE.
quote: Concrete dropout provided the best calibration-accuracy-efficiency trade-off, achieving the lowest average miscalibration area (MA=0.12) while maintaining competitive MAE.

title: AI chatbots for patient education in localized prostate cancer radiotherapy: A comparative quality and readability analysis
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on prostate cancer radiotherapy (Coleman-Liau Index)
effect: All chatbot responses required college-level literacy, limiting accessibility for many patients.
quote: Although several chatbots achieved acceptable understandability scores, all responses required college-level literacy, limiting accessibility for many patients.

title: AI-based chest X-ray prioritization in the lung cancer diagnostic pathway: the LungIMPACT randomized controlled trial
outcome: Time to CT and lung cancer diagnosis with vs without AI worklist prioritization
effect: Median time to CT 53 vs 53 days (ratio of geometric means 0.97, 95% CI 0.93-1.02; P=0.31); time to diagnosis 44 vs 46 days (ratio 0.98, 95% CI 0.83-1.16; P=0.84); no stage difference (P=0.34).
quote: AI prioritization of CXR requested by UK primary care has no significant impact on the lung cancer pathway.

title: AI-based chest X-ray prioritization in the lung cancer diagnostic pathway: the LungIMPACT randomized controlled trial
outcome: time to lung cancer diagnosis
effect: Median times to diagnosis were 44 days with and 46 days without AI prioritization (P = 0.84), showing no clinical benefit.
quote: Median times to diagnosis were 44 days (26-90) and 46 days (24-105) respectively, with a ratio of geometric means of 0.98 (95% CI = 0.83-1.16; P = 0.84).

title: Lightweight and interpretable edge intelligence AI with intrusion detection for trustworthy cardiac arrhythmia in medical IoT
outcome: Detection of unreliable or attacked ECG inputs via attack probability and trust score
effect: Intrusion detection module outputs an attack probability and trust score flagging unreliable inputs; generalization under dataset shift reported as AUC 0.940 on PTB-XL and 0.915 on Chapman (zero-shot).
quote: To improve trust under hostile network conditions, an intrusion detection module outputs an attack probability and a trust score that flags unreliable inputs.

title: Large language models enhance diagnostic reasoning of medical students in rheumatology: a randomized controlled trial
outcome: Correct top diagnosis: students with LLM vs without, and vs LLM alone
effect: LLM group 77.5% vs controls 32.4% (aOR 7.0, 95% CI 3.8–14.4; P<.001); also exceeded LLM-only performance (77.5% vs. 71.6%).
quote: The LLM group identified the correct top diagnosis more often than controls (77.5% vs. 32.4%), yielding an adjusted odds ratio of 7.0 (95% CI 3.8–14.4; P<.001), and also exceeded LLM-only performance (77.5% vs. 71.6%).

title: Development of a generative AI agent for family support in implementing family-based treatment for children and adolescents with anorexia nervosa
outcome: Escalation insufficiency rate in clinician-evaluated responses from safety-gated RAG system
effect: Escalation insufficiency (0.6% of all dialogs) rarely occurred; 91.6% (437/477) of responses clinically appropriate.
quote: Clinically inappropriate responses (8.4%) were mainly attributable to information insufficiency; not FBT concordant (1.8% of FBT-related responses) and escalation insufficiency (0.6% of all dialogs) rarely occurred.

title: Development of a generative AI agent for family support in implementing family-based treatment for children and adolescents with anorexia nervosa
outcome: Clinician review of AI responses for clinical appropriateness and safety
effect: Six clinicians rated 91.6% (437/477) of responses clinically appropriate; 8.4% inappropriate, mainly information insufficiency.
quote: The clinically appropriate response rate was 91.6% (437/477), including 92.3% for FBT-related questions, 88.0% for general knowledge, 93.7% for psychological distress, and 100.0% for other questions.

title: Evaluation of large language models in supporting autoimmune liver disease diagnosis and clinical decision-making: advantages of reasoning-based models
outcome: LLM accuracy, safety, and diagnostic performance on AILD questions and real-world cases, by model
effect: o1-preview had the greatest proportion of accurate responses (78.3%), highest mean safety score; diagnostic accuracy 81.0%, outperforming GPT-4o and GPT-3.5-Turbo.
quote: In diagnostic testing, the o1-preview achieved an overall accuracy of 81.0%, outperforming GPT-4o and GPT-3.5-Turbo, particularly in single-entity AILD diagnoses.

title: Evaluation of large language models in supporting autoimmune liver disease diagnosis and clinical decision-making: advantages of reasoning-based models
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLMs on confirmed AILD cases, including overlap syndrome
effect: o1-preview overall diagnostic accuracy 81.0%; all models showed reduced diagnostic accuracy for AIH-PBC overlap syndrome.
quote: All models demonstrated reduced diagnostic accuracy for autoimmune hepatitis-primary biliary cholangitis overlap syndrome.

title: Grounding large language models in clinical diagnostics
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy and efficiency of physicians with AI versus physicians or AI alone
effect: Collaboration between physicians and ClinDiag-GPT yields higher diagnostic accuracy and efficiency compared to either working alone.
quote: Furthermore, a comparative analysis reveals that collaboration between physicians and ClinDiag-GPT yields higher diagnostic accuracy and efficiency compared to either working alone, demonstrating the utility of ClinDiag-GPT as a clinical assistant.

title: Grounding large language models in clinical diagnostics
outcome: LLM performance on dynamic diagnostic workflows versus static tasks
effect: Existing LLMs proficient in static tasks fall short in dynamic diagnostic workflows and frequently commit clinical errors.
quote: Our evaluation shows that existing LLMs, including GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Claude-3-Haiku, Qwen2.5-72b, Qwen2.5-32b, and Qwen2.5-14b, while proficient in static tasks, fall short in dynamic diagnostic workflows and frequently commit clinical errors.

title: Assessing ChatGPT and Gemini Responses to Common Patient Questions Regarding Augmentation Mammaplasty
outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of LLM answers to patient questions
effect: FKGL 9.71 (ChatGPT) vs 11.43 (Gemini), p=0.002; FRE 46.53 vs 43.70, p=0.243. Both outputs above a plain-language level.
quote: ChatGPT produced more readable outputs (FRE: 46.53 vs 43.70, p = 0.243; FKGL: 9.71 vs 11.43, p = 0.002), indicating approximately two US grade levels of easier reading.

title: Accuracy and Knowledge Base Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.0-Flash, and DeepSeek-V3 in Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: an Expert-Rated Blinded Study
outcome: Expert-rated guideline concordance of LLM answers to bariatric surgery questions (0-3 scale)
effect: DeepSeek-V3 2.44±0.40, ChatGPT-4o 1.79±0.46, Gemini 2.0 Flash 1.63±0.47 (p<0.001); fully concordant (score 3) in 80% DeepSeek vs 0% ChatGPT and 3.3% Gemini.
quote: Fully guideline-concordant ratings (score = 3) were most frequent for DeepSeek (80%) vs. ChatGPT (0%) and Gemini (3.3%).

title: Accuracy and Knowledge Base Evaluation of ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.0-Flash, and DeepSeek-V3 in Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery: an Expert-Rated Blinded Study
outcome: LLM performance on guideline-based specialty questions, showing need for domain validation
effect: Models differed significantly in guideline concordance; ChatGPT and Gemini rarely fully concordant, indicating general-purpose performance may not reflect specialty competence.
quote: These results highlight the need for ongoing, domain-focused validation before clinical use.

title: WiseMind: a knowledge-guided multi-agent framework for accurate and empathetic psychiatric diagnosis
outcome: Hallucination rate with DSM-5 knowledge-graph grounding versus standard prompting
effect: The DSM-5-guided structured knowledge graph significantly reduced hallucinations compared to standard prompting. Top-1 diagnostic accuracy was 85.6%, 15-54 percentage points above knowledge-enhanced single-agent baselines.
quote: Our framework utilizes a Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5)-guided Structured Knowledge Graph to steer diagnostic inquiries, significantly reducing hallucinations compared to standard prompting methods.

title: The reliability and readability of large language models in answering patient questions on maintenance hemodialysis: A comparative study
outcome: Readability of LLM answers to hemodialysis questions versus recommended sixth-grade level
effect: All five models produced texts exceeding the sixth-grade reading level; ARI, GFI, FKGL, CLI, SMOG notably higher than recommended; FRES substantially below the 80-90 range.
quote: In terms of readability, all models produced texts exceeding the sixth-grade reading level.

title: The reliability and readability of large language models in answering patient questions on maintenance hemodialysis: A comparative study
outcome: Reading level of LLM patient education content relative to recommended level
effect: All models exceeded sixth-grade reading level; FRES scores substantially below the 80-90 range recommended for patient materials.
quote: In terms of readability, all models produced texts exceeding the sixth-grade reading level.

title: The reliability and readability of large language models in answering patient questions on maintenance hemodialysis: A comparative study
outcome: Source attribution and transparency in LLM responses on hemodialysis
effect: All models showed limitations in information quality and transparency; persistent deficiencies in source attribution, with Perplexity performing relatively better on DISCERN, EQIP, JAMA.
quote: However, persistent deficiencies in source attribution, language accessibility, and response consistency limit their immediate clinical and educational utility.

title: Improving Fairness and Mitigating Bias in Multicenter Electronic Health Records Models to Predict Glaucoma Outcomes
outcome: fairness-performance after mitigation
effect: IPW FairOdds-AUC 0.574–0.600 and AFC 0.573–0.613 exceeded baseline 0.547–0.562; both p < 1e-12.
quote: FairOdds-AUC heatmaps show that IPW (0.574 [0.556, 0.593] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.600 [0.575, 0.629]) and AFC (0.573 [0.559, 0.588] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.613 [0.595, 0.629]) were bias mitigation techniques that consistently performed significantly better than the baseline approach without bias mitigation (0.547 [0.512, 0.570] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.562 [0.544, 0.578]) across modeling architecture backbones and evaluation sets, striking a balance between AUC performance and fairness (p < 1e-12 [IPW, baseline], p < 1e-12 [AFC, baseline]), while ColRm (0.549 [0.533, 0.559] < FairOdds-AUC< 0.559 [0.543, 0.580]) and ThreshOpt (0.546 [0.524, 0.563] < FairOdds-AUC < 0.568 [0.546, 0.592]) performed similarly to baseline ( P < 0.0083 [ColRm, baseline], P < 0.203 [ThreshOpt, baseline]).

title: Improving Fairness and Mitigating Bias in Multicenter Electronic Health Records Models to Predict Glaucoma Outcomes
outcome: Subgroup fairness gaps (equalized odds by sex and race/ethnicity) across internal and external sites
effect: Baseline and column remover had sex EO >0.298; a trade-off was seen between AUROC and equalized odds gaps across sites, with no method excelling on both.
quote: For sex EO, baseline and column remover performed poorly (EO > 0.298 [0.276, 0.322]), while adversarial classifier (EO < 0.220 [0.191, 0.257]) and, to some extent, threshold optimization performed better across test sets (EO < 0.243 [0.213, 0.299]).

title: Improving Fairness and Mitigating Bias in Multicenter Electronic Health Records Models to Predict Glaucoma Outcomes
outcome: Fairness and performance generalization of mitigation methods across two external sites
effect: Inprocessing methods (IPW, AFC) generalized consistently across internal and two external sites; pre/postprocessing methods showed weaker generalizability and dataset-dependent effects.
quote: Postprocessing and preprocessing bias mitigation strategies yielded more variable FairOdds-AUC changes (-0.009 to +0.021) and showed weaker generalizability across external sites.

title: Evaluating ChatGPT's Triage and Diagnostic Capabilities in Patients Presenting With Common Causes of Foot and Ankle Pain
outcome: Agreement of AI triage destination (PCP, specialist, ED/urgent care) with surgeon decisions
effect: Triage recommendations matched surgeons in 6 of 12 cases (50%); differential diagnoses were clinically appropriate for all triage conditions.
quote: ChatGPT-4o's triage recommendations matched the surgeons' decisions in 6 cases (50%).

title: When Artificial Intelligence Fails the Future: How Unchecked Artificial Intelligence Could Amplify Inequality in Medical Education
venue: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
outcome: LLM specialty competitiveness and surgical recommendations varying with synthetic applicant race and gender
effect: Male applicants rated more competitive than female (P<0.0001); Black and Hispanic less competitive than White (P=0.0019, 0.0108); male surgical recommendation OR 10.23; Black and Hispanic females needed 95 and 88 extra Step 2 points vs 56 for White females.
quote: Compensatory scoring revealed that White female applicants needed 56 additional Step 2 Clinical Knowledge points to match perceived competitiveness, whereas Black and Hispanic female applicants required 95 and 88 additional points, respectively.

title: Bridging the Gap: A Pilot Study Using Artificial Intelligence to Make Plastic Surgery Research Accessible
venue: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
outcome: Readability of LLM-generated plain-language summaries of plastic surgery research versus original articles
effect: Grok reached 7th-9th grade level (FRE M=63.06, FKGL M=7.69) and significantly outperformed others; ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek stayed at 10th-12th grade, not significantly different from originals (P>0.05).
quote: ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek showed moderate improvements but did not achieve statistically significant differences from the original articles (P > 0.05), with average grade levels between the 10th and 12th grades.

title: Bridging the Gap: A Pilot Study Using Artificial Intelligence to Make Plastic Surgery Research Accessible
venue: Plastic and reconstructive surgery. Global open
outcome: Whether generative AI output matched lower health literacy targets while preserving accuracy
effect: Only Grok met sixth- to eighth-grade health literacy benchmarks with accuracy preserved; other three models fell short with 10th-12th grade outputs.
quote: Grok demonstrated superior readability while preserving accuracy, making it the only LLM to meet health literacy benchmarks.

title: Improving support and self-management of ophthalmic patients using an artificial intelligence health coach
outcome: Independent glaucoma consultant validation of AI question-answer pairs across assessed domains
effect: Human expert validation scores exceeded 95% across all assessed domains.
quote: Human expert validation scores exceeded 95% across all assessed domains.
sample_unit: patients who interacted with the AI health coach (446 chat sessions analyzed)

title: Performance of clinical breast cancer risk prediction models vs a mammography-based artificial intelligence risk model
venue: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
outcome: Local calibration (observed-to-expected ratio) of AI risk model versus clinical models in a Mayo Clinic cohort
effect: MIRAI overall breast cancer O/E 0.96 (95% CI 0.85-1.08) but invasive cancer O/E 0.68 (95% CI 0.58-0.78), overestimating risk; clinical models O/E 0.86-0.99.
quote: MIRAI also overestimated risk of invasive breast cancer across the risk spectrum (observed-to-expected ratio = 0.68, 95% CI = 0.58 to 0.78), whereas clinical models had good calibration (observed-to-expected ratio = 0.86-0.99).
sample_unit: women in a screening mammography cohort

title: Performance of clinical breast cancer risk prediction models vs a mammography-based artificial intelligence risk model
venue: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
outcome: Discrimination versus calibration of AI risk model, including calibration by risk stratum
effect: MIRAI C-index 0.71 for overall and invasive cancer, higher than clinical models (0.59-0.68), yet it overestimated risk in low-risk women (about 50%) and for invasive cancer.
quote: However, for low-risk women (approximately 50%), MIRAI overestimated risk of overall breast cancer.
sample_unit: women in a screening mammography cohort

title: Quality, Empathy, and Readability of AI Chatbot Responses to the Survivorship Needs of Adolescents and Young Adults With Melanoma: Evaluation Study
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses (Flesch Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease) versus recommended reading level

title: Quality, Empathy, and Readability of AI Chatbot Responses to the Survivorship Needs of Adolescents and Young Adults With Melanoma: Evaluation Study
outcome: Reading level of chatbot health information relative to recommended level

title: Effect of large language model on diagnostic accuracy and clinical completeness among nephrology fellows managing transplant infection

quote: Median accuracy increased from 72% (65·5-78·5) in the unaided arm to 85·5% (79·0-91·0) in the aided arm with Δ =  + 13·0%, p-value < 0·001.

title: Effect of large language model on diagnostic accuracy and clinical completeness among nephrology fellows managing transplant infection
outcome: Clinically significant hallucination and niche dose-duration knowledge gaps in LLM-aided responses
effect: Only a single clinically significant hallucination (3.3%) occurred; minimal or no benefit in dual infection scenarios and niche dose-duration knowledge.
quote: Only a single clinically significant hallucination (3·3%) occurred.

title: Machine learning predicts sepsis deterioration trajectories
outcome: Model AUROC across development, internal, and external sites
effect: AUROC 0.92 (development), 0.89 (internal), 0.84 (MIMIC-III) and 0.77 (eICU), showing performance decline at external sites.
quote: In the final binary classification task, AUROC was 0.92 (development), 0.89 (internal), 0.84 (MIMIC-III) and 0.77 (eICU); median warning time before deterioration was 17.6 h (Overall pooled across all cohorts).

title: External validation of a commercial AI system for pulmonary embolism detection on chest CTPA: a multicenter study
outcome: Radiologist performance with AI in intended workflow versus standalone AI metrics
effect: Standalone AI AUC 0.807-0.810 was below radiologists (0.888-0.914); combined reading reached 0.928-0.934, significantly above AI alone in all centers.
quote: DeLong test comparisons revealed statistically significant improvements in AUC for the combined approach compared to either AI-only or radiologist-only interpretation across all centers (P < 0.05 for all comparisons).

title: External validation of a commercial AI system for pulmonary embolism detection on chest CTPA: a multicenter study
outcome: Adjunct (radiologist plus AI) versus AI standalone diagnostic accuracy
effect: AI alone had 43 errors (36 false positives); radiologist plus AI had 7 errors and higher AUC 0.928-0.934 than AI alone 0.807-0.810.
quote: The superior performance of the combined approach suggests that AI systems function most effectively as assistive tools rather than replacement technologies, augmenting human expertise rather than superseding it.

title: External validation of a commercial AI system for pulmonary embolism detection on chest CTPA: a multicenter study
outcome: Diagnostic AUC and errors for radiologists with vs without AI, and AI alone
effect: Combined AUC 0.928-0.934 vs manual 0.888-0.914 and AI alone 0.807-0.810; errors 7 combined vs 29 manual vs 43 AI alone; overall manual vs combined P=0.0427.
quote: The combined radiologist + AI approach resulted in only 7 diagnostic errors (2 false-negative and 5 false-positive cases), representing a 75.9% reduction in errors compared to AI alone and a 75.9% reduction compared to radiologists alone.

title: External validation of a commercial AI system for pulmonary embolism detection on chest CTPA: a multicenter study
outcome: AI compared with radiologists on the same data for PE detection
effect: AI alone AUC 0.807-0.810 was lower than manual reading AUC 0.888-0.914; AI had 43 errors versus 29 for radiologists.
quote: The findings of our comprehensive analysis reveal a persistent performance gap between standalone AI systems and experienced radiologists in PE detection.

title: External validation of a commercial AI system for pulmonary embolism detection on chest CTPA: a multicenter study
outcome: Interrater reliability of consensus reference standard
effect: Pairwise Cohen's kappa 0.867-0.894 and Fleiss' kappa 0.884 among three senior radiologists.
quote: The overall interrater agreement among the three radiologists was also excellent, with a Fleiss’ Kappa value of 0.884 (P < 0.001).

title: External validation of a commercial AI system for pulmonary embolism detection on chest CTPA: a multicenter study
outcome: False-positive and false-negative diagnostic errors
effect: Combined had 7 errors (2 FN, 5 FP), reported as 75.9% reduction vs AI alone and radiologists alone; AI alone had 43 errors, manual 29.
quote: The combined radiologist + AI approach resulted in only 7 diagnostic errors (2 false-negative and 5 false-positive cases), representing a 75.9% reduction in errors compared to AI alone and a 75.9% reduction compared to radiologists alone.

title: Efficacy of ChatGPT in personalized glucose-lowering strategy development: a clinician-based comparative study

quote: However, its accuracy in complex cases, especially concerning medication contraindications, requires improvement.

title: Unlocking electronic health records: a hybrid graph RAG approach to safe clinical AI for patient QA
outcome: Expert-rated quality and safety violations of graph-grounded LLM answers on complex inference queries

quote: Complex inference tasks achieved a mean expert quality score of 4.25/5 with zero safety violations across all evaluated cases.

title: Adherence of Free-Tier Large Language Models to the 2024 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) Guidelines for the Management of Elevated Blood Pressure and Hypertension: A Comparative Study
outcome: LLM adherence to 2024 ESC hypertension guideline knowledge on 40 questions
effect: Correct on 33/40 (82.5%) Claude, 32/40 (80.0%) ChatGPT-5.2 and Gemini 3 Flash; no significant difference (p>0.99); tendency toward overly aggressive management in complex scenarios.
quote: Claude 4.5 Sonnet achieved the highest numerical accuracy, providing correct responses to 33 out of 40 questions (82.5%).

title: AI-generated explanations in kidney transplantation: accuracy vs. readability and implications for patient education
outcome: Reading level of LLM patient explanations with generic vs explicit 8th-grade-level prompt

title: AI-generated explanations in kidney transplantation: accuracy vs. readability and implications for patient education

outcome: Clinician confidence in understanding AI bias sources and ethical issues

title: Artificial intelligence in emergency skeletal X-ray: post-deployment monitoring and clinical impact of incorrect AI results

title: Artificial intelligence in emergency skeletal X-ray: post-deployment monitoring and clinical impact of incorrect AI results
outcome: Premature discharge caught by subsequent radiologist report

title: Artificial intelligence in emergency skeletal X-ray: post-deployment monitoring and clinical impact of incorrect AI results

title: A prospective multicenter trial of deep learning auto-segmentation for organs at risk in thoracic radiotherapy

title: A prospective multicenter trial of deep learning auto-segmentation for organs at risk in thoracic radiotherapy
