title: Performance of a Screening Mammography AI Algorithm Repurposed for Symptomatic Mammography in a Tertiary Outpatient Clinic
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy (AUC) of a screening-trained AI applied to a new symptomatic population
effect: AUC 0.96 (95% CI 0.86-1.00) overall in 156 breasts with 15 malignancies; performance did not fail to generalize, though single-center and small.
quote: In the overall cohort (156 breasts, including 15 breasts with malignancies), the AI algorithm achieved an AUC of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.86-1.00).

title: Performance of a Screening Mammography AI Algorithm Repurposed for Symptomatic Mammography in a Tertiary Outpatient Clinic
outcome: AI AUC stratified by breast density subgroup
effect: Non-dense AUC 0.96 (0.88-1.00), dense AUC 0.99 (0.93-1.00); no significant difference (DeLong p = 0.36), but subgroup comparisons were underpowered.
quote: Performance remained high in non-dense breasts (AUC = 0.96; 95% CI: 0.88-1.00) and dense breasts (AUC = 0.99; 95% CI: 0.93-1.00)

title: Identifying a Critical Blind Spot: How Commercial AI (CAD) Systems Fail to Detect Faint Ground-Glass Opacities at -730 HU on Low-Dose CT
outcome: AI/CAD false negative rate versus expert reference standard on LDCT nodules
effect: Combined cohort false negative rates were 12.7% for Vendor A and 14.7% for Vendor B; missed nodules were mostly GGOs (92.3% and 78.6% in the primary cohort).
quote: The AI systems demonstrated significant and comparable false negative rates in the combined cohort: 12.7% for Vendor A and 14.7% for Vendor B.

title: Identifying a Critical Blind Spot: How Commercial AI (CAD) Systems Fail to Detect Faint Ground-Glass Opacities at -730 HU on Low-Dose CT
outcome: Nodules missed by AI/CAD that experts confirmed
effect: AI missed expert-confirmed nodules (12.7% Vendor A, 14.7% Vendor B), mostly faint GGOs with mean attenuation around -730 HU, showing cases AI overlooks would be missed without clinician review.
quote: The vast majority of missed nodules were GGOs (92.3% and 78.6%, respectively, in the primary cohort).

title: From ABCD to AI: Assessing the Diagnostic Reliability of MLLMs in Cutaneous Melanoma Screening-A Head-to-Head Comparison
outcome: Model confidence calibration during incorrect diagnoses (false negatives)
effect: Gemini 3 kept high confidence (84.62%) during false-negative predictions; GPT-5 and Grok 4 showed better calibration with a significant confidence drop upon incorrect diagnosis.
quote: Notably, Gemini 3 exhibited severe overconfidence, maintaining a high CI (84.62%) even during false-negative predictions, whereas GPT-5 and Grok 4 showed better calibration with a significant drop in confidence upon incorrect diagnosis.

title: From ABCD to AI: Assessing the Diagnostic Reliability of MLLMs in Cutaneous Melanoma Screening-A Head-to-Head Comparison
outcome: Sensitivity of MLLMs for melanoma screening when used as standalone tools
effect: All models missed about half of malignant lesions; Grok 4 sensitivity 52%; Gemini 3 accuracy 71%, specificity 94%.
quote: All models exhibited a critical deficit in sensitivity, missing approximately half of the malignant lesions.

title: Assessing the "Optimism-Knowledge Gap": An Exploratory Study of AI Awareness, Application, and Educational Needs Among a Sample of Italian Clinicians
outcome: Clinician AI familiarity, practical use, knowledge of limitations, and interest in training
effect: 89.9% moderately/very interested in learning about AI; 44.1% of GPs never used AI vs 34.9% of hospital clinicians (p=0.045); 32.6% of GPs understand some benefits but not limitations.
quote: Furthermore, 32.6% of GPs admitted that they "understand some benefits but not the limitations."

title: Real-Time Integration of an AI-Based ECG Interpretation System in the Emergency Department: A Pragmatic Alternating-Day Study of Diagnostic Performance and Clinical Process Metrics
outcome: STEMI sensitivity and reperfusion time metrics on AI-disclosure days versus physician-only days
effect: AI sensitivity 96.7% vs physician 68.3% (p=0.027); specificity 75.9% vs 84.5%; door-to-balloon 40.0 vs 47.34 min (p=0.001); mortality 17.0% vs 16.77% (p=0.191)
quote: Real-time AI-ECG integration in the ED was associated with improved STEMI detection sensitivity and shorter reperfusion-related time metrics, particularly in atypical presentations, and with reduced hospital LOS among admitted patients.

title: Real-World Evaluation of an AI-Assisted Diagnostic Support System for Early Gastric Cancer: Diagnostic Performance, Confidence Stratification, and Determinants of False-Positive Diagnosis
outcome: Local diagnostic performance of AI against pathology reference standard
effect: Sensitivity 97.6%, NPV 95.7%, specificity 45.8% on local real-world lesions; false positives remained common.
quote: The AI system demonstrated a sensitivity of 97.6% and an NPV of 95.7%, with a specificity of 45.8%.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Plastic Surgery Education: A Global Multimodel Benchmark of Large Language Models on the Plastic Surgery In-Service Training Examination
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across 5 repeated runs (Fleiss' kappa, coefficient of variation)
effect: Proprietary models kappa 0.84 vs open-source 0.70; stability varied from CV 0.00% (Falcon H1) to CV 32.2% (Mistral Medium).
quote: Stability varied, ranging from consistent error in Falcon H1 (CV = 0.00%) to erratic instability in Mistral Medium (Mistral AI, Paris, France) (CV = 32.2%).
sample_unit: model evaluations (14 LLMs x 100 questions x 5 runs)

title: Artificial Intelligence in Plastic Surgery Education: A Global Multimodel Benchmark of Large Language Models on the Plastic Surgery In-Service Training Examination
outcome: LLM accuracy on PSITE exam questions, as a proxy for clinical competence
effect: Claude Opus 4.5 90.2% and GPT-5.2 Pro 87.0%; proprietary mean 76.1% vs open-source 60.2%. Authors state accuracy alone is insufficient to judge clinical utility.
quote: Accuracy alone is insufficient to judge clinical utility; stability metrics are essential for selecting AI tools in surgical education.
sample_unit: model evaluations (14 LLMs x 100 questions x 5 runs)

title: Performance of PREVENT Cardiovascular Risk in Electronic Health Record-Based Clinical Practice
outcome: Effect of local retraining and recalibration on discrimination and calibration
effect: Local retraining and recalibration yielded similar C-indices; recalibration modestly improved calibration but risk remained underestimated for most subgroups.
quote: Recalibration modestly improved calibration, but risk remained underestimated for most subgroups, particularly Black patients, higher ADI quartiles, and those with Medicaid or no insurance (eFigure 12, eFigure 13, and eTable 4 in Supplement 1 ); decile-based calibration plots are shown in eFigure 14 and eFigure 15 in Supplement 1 .

title: Performance of PREVENT Cardiovascular Risk in Electronic Health Record-Based Clinical Practice
outcome: Subgroup discrimination and calibration by race, ADI, and insurance
effect: C-index lowest in Black individuals, highest ADI quartile, and Medicare patients; calibration worse for disadvantaged subgroups.
quote: Asian males showed the highest C-index, and Black individuals showed the lowest.

title: Performance of PREVENT Cardiovascular Risk in Electronic Health Record-Based Clinical Practice
outcome: Model performance across demographic and socioeconomic subgroups
effect: Discrimination declined with increasing neighborhood disadvantage; Black patients had lowest C-index in both Duke cohorts, unlike in PREVENT cohorts.
quote: Model performance declined with increasing neighborhood disadvantage, with the poorest discrimination in the highest ADI quartile.

title: Performance of PREVENT Cardiovascular Risk in Electronic Health Record-Based Clinical Practice
outcome: Calibration under missing laboratory and vital sign data across subgroups
effect: Missingness was greater among underserved groups (TC missing 52.2%); calibration was worse in the relaxed cohort especially among disadvantaged subgroups.
quote: However, calibration was worse in the relaxed cohort, especially among disadvantaged subgroups (Black patients, higher ADI quartiles, and those with Medicaid or no insurance), suggesting missingness is associated with poorer calibration even when discrimination is preserved.

title: Performance of PREVENT Cardiovascular Risk in Electronic Health Record-Based Clinical Practice
outcome: Local discrimination and calibration of published PREVENT equations in Duke EHR data
effect: Discrimination strong (C-index 0.75-0.77 vs 0.76-0.79 in validation cohort), but risk was underestimated in the relaxed cohort, especially for Black, high-ADI, and Medicaid/uninsured patients.
quote: Calibration ratios were higher in the strict cohort, indicating greater underestimation of CVD risk in the broader relaxed cohort, especially among Black patients, those in more disadvantaged ADI quartiles, and those with Medicaid or no insurance (eFigure 8, eFigure 9, and eTable 2 in Supplement 1 ).

title: Performance of PREVENT Cardiovascular Risk in Electronic Health Record-Based Clinical Practice
outcome: robustness to missing inputs
effect: C-index remained similar, but calibration was worse in the relaxed cohort, especially Black, higher ADI, Medicaid, or uninsured subgroups.
quote: However, calibration was worse in the relaxed cohort, especially among disadvantaged subgroups (Black patients, higher ADI quartiles, and those with Medicaid or no insurance), suggesting missingness is associated with poorer calibration even when discrimination is preserved.

title: Error Detection in Emergency Radiology Reports Using a Large Language Model: Multistage Evaluation Study
outcome: Error detection rate of LLM versus radiologists of different seniority on same reports
effect: DeepSeek-R1 few-shot 84.4% vs residents 51.6% and 53.1% (both P<.05); no significant difference vs senior/attending radiologists (68.8%-93.8%, P=.26 to ≥.99).
quote: Its performance exceeded that of radiology residents (84.4% vs 51.6% and 53.1%, respectively; both P<.05) and showed no statistically significant difference compared with senior radiologists and attending radiologists (84.4% vs 68.8%-93.8%, P=.26 to ≥.99).
sample_unit: emergency radiology reports (dataset 1); 200 reports stage 1, 100 stages 2-3, 800 stage 4

title: Error Detection in Emergency Radiology Reports Using a Large Language Model: Multistage Evaluation Study
outcome: Real-world validation of LLM error detection on verified reports
effect: In real-world validation on 800 reports, DeepSeek-R1 identified 117 true reporting errors, positive predictive value 56.5%.
quote: In real-world validation, DeepSeek-R1 identified 117 true reporting errors, yielding a positive predictive value of 56.5%.
sample_unit: emergency radiology reports (dataset 1); 200 reports stage 1, 100 stages 2-3, 800 stage 4

title: Error Detection in Emergency Radiology Reports Using a Large Language Model: Multistage Evaluation Study
outcome: Detection rate in independent-institution dataset
effect: In dataset 2 from independent institutions, DeepSeek-R1 achieved a detection rate of 95% under the few-shot setting.
quote: In dataset 2, collected from independent institutions, DeepSeek-R1 achieved a detection rate of 95% under the few-shot setting.
sample_unit: emergency radiology reports (dataset 1); 200 reports stage 1, 100 stages 2-3, 800 stage 4

title: Comparative evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini artificial intelligence in patient education on clear aligner therapy
outcome: Readability of LLM patient education responses (FKGL, SMOG) versus general audience comprehension
effect: Both models produced content with FKGL scores indicating university-level reading and SMOG scores suggesting high school-level comprehension; no significant differences between models in readability.
quote: Both produced content with FKGL scores indicating university-level reading and SMOG scores suggesting high school-level comprehension.

title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
outcome: ICD-10-CM coding performance at external hospital versus development site
effect: All models declined at TMMH; BioMistral full-code F-score 0.754 at KMUH vs 0.620 at TMMH; BERT precision dropped from 0.875 to 0.137.
quote: Performance declined for all models on the TMMH dataset, reflecting the expected impact of institution-specific documentation variability, including differences in documentation conventions and section availability.
sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
outcome: Coder satisfaction with AI-assisted workflow by model and coder subgroup
effect: 1947 satisfaction responses; BioMistral rated most favorably; lower satisfaction among coders with <10 years experience, clinical backgrounds, Gen Y (χ², p < 0.001); one late-career coder withdrew.
quote: Satisfaction also varied by CCS background: higher satisfaction was reported among CCSs with healthcare administration training, advanced certification, 10–24 years of experience, and members of Gen X, whereas lower satisfaction was more common among CCS with medical-related academic backgrounds, those with <10 years of experience, and members of the Gen Y cohort ( χ ², p < 0.001).
sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
outcome: Agreement between candidate-model screening ranks and downstream coding performance
effect: Intrinsic screening ranked BioMistral highest (44.1% selection probability). Downstream fine-tuning preserved model ordering, with BioMistral achieving F 1 -score = 0.78 and win rate = 69.2%.
quote: As shown in Fig. 4 , the relative ordering of models was preserved after fine-tuning: BioMistral achieved the highest downstream performance (F 1 -score = 0.78; win rate = 69.2%), followed by MedLlama2 and Mistral.
sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
outcome: Cross-institutional coding performance under documentation and population distribution differences
effect: From KMUH RCT to TMMH, BioMistral full-code F-score declined from 0.754 to 0.620; BERT precision declined from 0.875 to 0.137. External evaluation used no additional retraining.
quote: Performance declined for all models on the TMMH dataset, reflecting the expected impact of institution-specific documentation variability, including differences in documentation conventions and section availability.
sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
outcome: Coding robustness to heterogeneous or missing clinical sections
effect: Section-specific models performed optimally only when input structure matched training; the universal model was more robust to missing or inconsistently populated sections.
quote: On the full test, the universal model exhibited consistent, monotonic improvements in both precision and recall as more sections were included in the input, whereas section-specific models tended to perform optimally only when the input structure exactly matched their training configuration.
sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
outcome: Coding time with AI-assisted versus manual workflows
effect: Across 10,688 coded summaries, all three AI-assisted workflows were faster than manual coding (Games-Howell, all p < 0.001). PubMedGPT-2 produced the largest average time reduction, followed by BioMistral and HAN.
quote: All three AI-assisted workflows yielded faster completion times than manual coding (Games-Howell, all p < 0.001).
sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
outcome: Coding F-score with more complete clinical-section inputs
effect: Full-section inclusion increased F-score from 0.786 after deduplication to 0.798. External full-code F-scores increased from 0.764 to 0.779 at KMUH RCT and from 0.626 to 0.636 at TMMH.
quote: Finally, comparing these results from redundancy-aware sampling revealed complementary effects on downstream performance: the F-score increased from 0.780 (baseline) to 0.786 ( + deduplication) and 0.798 ( + full section inclusion).
sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

title: Evaluating real-world deployment of an HL7-CDA-aligned LLM for ICD-10-CM coding
outcome: AI-assisted coding time
effect: In a prospective RCT pilot, AI assistance significantly accelerated the coding workflow for real users compared to manual coding.
quote: All three AI-assisted workflows yielded faster completion times than manual coding (Games-Howell, all p < 0.001).
sample_unit: discharge summaries coded in RCT (10 certified coding specialists)

title: Challenges of using generative artificial intelligence for diabetes patient education: a cross-platform analysis of the quality, readability, and actionability of text generated by large language models
outcome: Readability and understandability of LLM-generated diabetes education texts
effect: Readability indices varied by platform (most p<0.001); greater reading burden tended to co-occur with lower GQS, PEMAT-P, and EQIP-36 scores; PEMAT-P actionability differed by topic (p<0.001).
quote: Exploratory regression analyses suggested that greater reading burden tended to co-occur with lower GQS, PEMAT-P, and EQIP-36 scores.

title: Risk-Guided Atrial Fibrillation Screening With Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Electrocardiogram Models: A VITAL-AF Trial Analysis
venue: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
outcome: AF screening effect (incident AF diagnosis rate difference) across AI risk deciles
effect: Screening effect seen only in top CH-AI decile: 10.07 vs 7.76/100 person-years, difference 2.32 (95% CI 0.01-4.63), number-needed-to-screen 43 per year; trade-off with reduced population coverage.
quote: An AF screening effect was observed in the top decile of CH-AI (AF diagnosis rate in screening 10.07/100 person-years [95% 8.28-11.87] vs 7.76 [95% 6.30-9.21] in control, P < 0.05), corresponding to a difference in AF diagnosis rate of 2.32/100 person-years (95% CI: 0.01-4.63) and number-needed-to-screen of 43 per year.

title: Cognitively Biased Prompt Effects on Large Language Model Accuracy for Radiology Board–style Examination Questions
outcome: LLM accuracy on radiology board-style questions under cognitively biased prompt variations
effect: Biased prompts reduced accuracy, especially on image-based tasks; prompt-level mitigations were effective but only partially restored accuracy (no numbers in available text).
quote: Large language model accuracy for radiology board–style questions was reduced by prompts that mimicked cognitive biases, especially on image-based tasks, and prompt-level mitigations, although effective, only partially restored accuracy.

title: AI Assessment and Management of Visceral Aneurysms Using ChatGPT-4o-mini: A Pilot Study Examining the Feasibility of Automating the AI Validation Process
outcome: Accuracy of LLM clinical responses against expert human evaluation
effect: Human evaluators rated 67% of responses correct; AI self-assessment overestimated correctness (89%).
quote: However, the 67% correctness rate and systematic AI self-overestimation indicate that current LLMs remain unsuitable for independent clinical use, reinforcing the need for expert oversight.
sample_unit: AI-generated visceral aneurysm clinical scenarios and responses

title: AI Assessment and Management of Visceral Aneurysms Using ChatGPT-4o-mini: A Pilot Study Examining the Feasibility of Automating the AI Validation Process
outcome: Guideline-based management correctness
effect: Human evaluators rated 67% correct; AI self-assessed 89% correct (scores 1-2).
quote: ChatGPT-4o-mini self-assessed 89% of responses as correct (scores 1-2), compared to 67% by human evaluators (chi-square, P < 0.0001), with the greatest discrepancy in the partially correct category.

title: AI Assessment and Management of Visceral Aneurysms Using ChatGPT-4o-mini: A Pilot Study Examining the Feasibility of Automating the AI Validation Process
outcome: Agreement between LLM self-assessment and human evaluator grading of correctness
effect: LLM self-assessed 89% of responses as correct (scores 1-2) versus 67% by human evaluators (P < 0.0001), with the greatest discrepancy in the partially correct category.
quote: ChatGPT-4o-mini self-assessed 89% of responses as correct (scores 1-2), compared to 67% by human evaluators (chi-square, P < 0.0001), with the greatest discrepancy in the partially correct category.

title: AI Assessment and Management of Visceral Aneurysms Using ChatGPT-4o-mini: A Pilot Study Examining the Feasibility of Automating the AI Validation Process
outcome: AI self-assessment calibration
effect: Self-assessed 89% correct versus 67% by human evaluators; chi-square, P < 0.0001.
quote: ChatGPT-4o-mini self-assessed 89% of responses as correct (scores 1-2), compared to 67% by human evaluators (chi-square, P < 0.0001), with the greatest discrepancy in the partially correct category.
sample_unit: AI-generated visceral aneurysm clinical scenarios and responses

title: Evaluation of the reliability of large language models for ASA-PS classification in cardiovascular surgery: a pilot study
outcome: Exact-match agreement with specialist consensus, LLMs versus residents on same cases
effect: Exact-match to five-specialist consensus was 42.2% for residents versus 59.4–75.0% for LLMs; LLM–specialist ICC 0.61–0.65.
quote: Exact-match to a five-specialist consensus was 42.2% for residents versus 59.4–75.0% for LLMs; classifications outside the range of ratings assigned by individual specialists were rare (0–3.1%).

title: Augmenting Large Language Model With Prompt Engineering and Supervised Fine-Tuning in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Tumor-Node-Metastasis Staging: Framework Development and Validation
outcome: TNM staging accuracy of optimized GLM-4-Air versus GPT-4o on held-out test set
quote: It achieved higher staging accuracies on the black-box test set: 92% (95% CI 0.850-0.959) for T, 86% (95% CI 0.779-0.915) for N, 92% (95% CI 0.850-0.959) for distant metastasis status (M), and 90% for overall clinical staging; by comparison, GPT-4o attained 87% (95% CI 0.790-0.922), 70% (95% CI 0.604-0.781), 78% (95% CI 0.689-0.850), and 80%, respectively.

title: Fact-Checking Large Language Model Responses to a Health Care Prompt: Comparative Study
outcome: Whether LLM fact-checking of its own response catches errors versus expert verification
effect: GPT-4o and OpenBioLLM-70B had 86% agreement with experts on the acne scenario. Both LLM fact-checks missed the understated urgency of stopping isotretinoin and the folic acid issue. Experts identified 3 mostly-true claims that the LLMs called true.
quote: The experts disagreed with the LLM classification of the claim about the use of folic acid because the response understated the importance of taking folic acid during pregnancy.
sample_unit: clinical claims (plus one acne scenario with 16 expert-identified claims)

title: Fact-Checking Large Language Model Responses to a Health Care Prompt: Comparative Study
outcome: Accuracy and speed of LLM fact-checking of generated medical claims versus expert pharmacists
effect: On 20 claims, GPT-4o agreed 100% and OpenBioLLM-70B 95% with experts. For the acne response both agreed 86%, but the LLM consistency check missed an internal inconsistency about stopping isotretinoin. GPT-4o took 42 seconds versus 18 minutes for experts.
quote: This inconsistency was not detected by the consistency check ( Textbox 3 ).
sample_unit: clinical claims (plus one acne scenario with 16 expert-identified claims)

title: Fact-Checking Large Language Model Responses to a Health Care Prompt: Comparative Study
outcome: Completeness and urgency of LLM clinical advice on isotretinoin during suspected pregnancy
effect: LLM responses did not consistently convey the urgency of discontinuing isotretinoin when pregnancy is suspected, nor adequately convey folic acid importance. One response recommended stopping only after a positive pregnancy test.
quote: However, the LLMs did not consistently recommend immediately stopping isotretinoin or sufficiently guide the patient to take folic acid.
sample_unit: clinical claims (plus one acne scenario with 16 expert-identified claims)

title: Fact-Checking Large Language Model Responses to a Health Care Prompt: Comparative Study
outcome: elicitation of missing medication details
effect: GPT-4o asked for acne medication details; OpenBioLLM-70B did not, despite a shorter 75-word response versus 279 words.
quote: However, OpenBioLLM-70B did not mention the risk of acne medication during pregnancy and did not ask the patient to provide more information on her medication.
sample_unit: clinical claims (plus one acne scenario with 16 expert-identified claims)

title: Fact-Checking Large Language Model Responses to a Health Care Prompt: Comparative Study
outcome: teratogenic medication exposure escalation
effect: Both LLMs had 86% agreement with experts but did not consistently communicate urgent isotretinoin discontinuation when pregnancy was suspected.
quote: The large language models did not consistently convey the urgency of discontinuing isotretinoin treatment when pregnancy is suspected.
sample_unit: clinical claims (plus one acne scenario with 16 expert-identified claims)

title: Impact of automated and manual segmentation errors on knee osteoarthritis classification using MRI-registered data on CT scans
venue: Computerized medical imaging and graphics : the official journal of the Computerized Medical Imaging Society
outcome: Classifier robustness to simulated segmentation errors (erosion, dilation, closing) in cartilage masks
effect: Linear and RBF SVC and Logistic Regression under error-modified datasets: F1 0.80-0.86, ROC AUC 0.86-0.92; tree-based models more sensitive to dilation errors, most models kept weighted F1 ≥ 0.75.
quote: While tree-based models were more sensitive to dilation errors, most models maintained weighted F1 scores ≥ 0.75.

title: Comparative Performance of Prostate Cancer Risk Prediction Tools in Gay, Bisexual, and Other Men Who Have Sex With Men vs Heterosexual Men
outcome: Prostate cancer risk calculator AUC and calibration in MSM vs heterosexual men
effect: MRI-based calculators had higher AUCs in MSM, best for PLUM and UCLA; PI-RADS ≥3 sensitivity 94% in MSM vs 87% in heterosexual men; no recalibration needed.
quote: MRI-based calculators showed higher AUCs in MSM, with best performance for PLUM and UCLA.
sample_unit: men undergoing prostate biopsy (243 MSM, 243 heterosexual men)

title: AI triage of duodenal biopsies improves workflow
outcome: Reporting turnaround time with AI-prioritised queue vs routine pathway
effect: Coeliac disease reported in 6 vs 10 days; non-neoplastic abnormalities 7 vs 10 days (both p<0.005); neoplastic lesions not reported quicker.
quote: In the AI triage workstream coeliac disease, and non-neoplastic abnormalities as a group, were reported quicker than in the standard workstream (6 days vs 10 days and 7 days vs 10 days, respectively, both p<0.005), but neoplastic lesions were not reported quicker.

title: Multidisciplinary blinded randomized expert evaluation of large language models for clinical diagnosis and management
outcome: Rate of incompetent responses and hallucinations in LLM clinical answers
effect: 3-19% of LLM responses were rated as incompetent and 40 instances of LLM hallucination were identified.
quote: Despite these strengths, 3-19% LLM responses were rated as incompetent and 40 instances of LLM hallucination were also identified.

title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
outcome: Physician accuracy with vs without LLM assistance, including poor-LLM assistance (overreliance)
effect: Optimal LLM raised physician accuracy (community 73.4% to 82.5%; county 84.0% to 87.9%; teaching 91.5% to 92.0%); worst LLM lowered accuracy below baseline, inappropriate regimens 26.6% to 35.2%.
quote: The worst LLM configurations decreased physician performance below baseline, increasing inappropriate regimen rates from 26.6% to 35.2% across all levels.

title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
outcome: Whether physicians detected incorrect AI outputs / automation bias
effect: With the worst model, accuracy declined for all six physicians (e.g., Physician 2 to 62.3%); case review showed automation bias with unnecessary escalation to drug therapy or downgrading of combination therapy.
quote: Furthermore, a case-level review revealed classic automation bias: lifestyle-only strategies were unnecessarily escalated to drug therapy based on erroneous LLM suggestions, while guideline-concordant initial dual therapy was sometimes downgraded to monotherapy for patients who clearly qualified for combination treatment.

title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
outcome: Human-AI team performance versus unassisted physicians in intended workflow
effect: Optimal LLM assistance improved accuracy for five of six physicians (e.g., Physician 1 to 84.3%, Physician 2 to 80.7%); worst-model assistance reduced accuracy for all participants.
quote: When the optimal model was integrated into physicians’ decision-making workflows, five physicians demonstrated improved accuracy compared with their standalone performance.

title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
outcome: LLM accuracy compared against physicians and across models/prompts on same cases
effect: Best configuration (GPT-4.1 Guidance-Self-Consistency, 91.3%) matched top physicians (92.7%) and exceeded community physicians; zero-shot DeepSeek 62.6%.
quote: Overall, GPT-4.1 with the Guidance-Self-Consistency prompt proved to be the most effective model-prompt configuration, achieving the optimal accuracy of 91.3% across the main decision-making dimensions; thus, it was selected as the optimal model.

title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
outcome: Task 1 accuracy by prompt strategy
effect: ChatGPT-4.1 accuracy was 91.3% with Guidance-Self-Consistency versus 64.0% zero-shot.
quote: Specifically, with the Guidance-Self-Consistency strategy, ChatGPT-4.1 achieved an accuracy of 91.3% for Task 1, while it only reached 64.0% under zero-shot prompting.

title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
outcome: decision accuracy with worst LLM advice
effect: Accuracy fell to 67.3%, 62.3%, 71.7%, 73.7%, 87.3%, and 83.3% for Physicians 1-6.
quote: Accuracy decreased to 67.3% for Physician 1, 62.3% for Physician 2, 71.7% for Physician 3, 73.7% for Physician 4, 87.3% for Physician 5, and 83.3% for Physician 6.

title: The effects of multitype prompt engineering for large language models in hypertension treatment decisions
outcome: initial hypertension treatment decision accuracy
effect: Guidance-based prompt strategies improved ChatGPT-4.1 accuracy from 64.0% (zero-shot) to 91.3% (Guidance-Self-Consistency), Claude-4 from 65.0% to 88.3%, Gemini-2.5 Pro from 64.33% to 87.7%, and DeepSeek-V3 from 62.7% to 86.3%.
quote: Guidance-based prompt engineering strategies significantly enhanced model accuracy on Task 1 compared to zero-shot prompting.

title: An agentic AI system for automated pharmacogenomic recommendation generation
outcome: Expert-rated clinical clarity and guideline concordance of evidence-grounded pipeline versus LLM baselines
effect: Evidence-grounded agentic system significantly outperformed GPT-5, Claude, and Grok in clinical clarity and guideline concordance on 24 random recommendations.
quote: In expert evaluations of 24 random recommendations, our system significantly outperformed leading LLM baselines (GPT-5, Claude, Grok) in clinical clarity and guideline concordance.

title: Comparing physician and artificial intelligence chatbot responses to preterm infant care questions posted to a public medical consultation forum: evaluation study
venue: Journal of perinatology : official journal of the California Perinatal Association
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT versus physician responses to preterm infant care questions
effect: ChatGPT responses exhibited higher semantic richness and were more difficult to read than human experts' responses, although understandability ratings were higher (4.12 vs 3.70).
quote: ChatGPT provided more comprehensive and elaborative information, though its responses exhibited higher semantic richness and were more difficult to read.

title: Comparative performance of risk prediction models for kidney disease: an external validation using 0.5 million UK Biobank participants
outcome: Calibration of published kidney risk models on an external population
effect: Severe miscalibration for many models; most substantially overpredicted CKD risk while underpredicting kidney failure risk, so recalibration is warranted before clinical application.
quote: Calibration performance was frequently suboptimal; most models substantially overpredicted CKD risk while underpredicting kidney failure risk, indicating that recalibration is warranted prior to clinical application.

title: Comparative performance of risk prediction models for kidney disease: an external validation using 0.5 million UK Biobank participants
outcome: Model discrimination across subgroups (age, sex, ethnicity, diabetes, hypertension)
effect: Discriminative performance was poorer for people with diabetes or hypertension.
quote: Discriminative performance was poorer for people with diabetes or hypertension.

title: Performance of large language models in endodontics: accuracy, consistency, and benchmarking with consensus guidelines
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across repeated weekly sessions (Fleiss' and Cohen's kappa)
effect: ChatGPT showed near-perfect reproducibility (kappa = 0.95); Gemini showed only fair agreement (kappa = 0.38). Accuracy was 92.8% vs. 84.8%.
quote: ChatGPT demonstrated significantly higher overall accuracy than Gemini (92.8% vs. 84.8%; OR = 2.37; p = 0.004) and near-perfect reproducibility (κ = 0.95), whereas Gemini showed fair agreement (κ = 0.38).
sample_unit: structured yes/no questions (600 responses per model over three weekly sessions)

title: Performance of large language models in endodontics: accuracy, consistency, and benchmarking with consensus guidelines
outcome: LLM accuracy on guideline-derived endodontic yes/no items, by clinical domain
effect: Overall accuracy was 92.8% (ChatGPT) and 84.8% (Gemini). Both models performed well in structured domains but had reduced accuracy in restoration and pulpal disease management.
quote: Both models performed well in structured clinical domains but showed reduced accuracy in areas related to restoration and pulpal disease management.
sample_unit: structured yes/no questions (600 responses per model over three weekly sessions)

title: Large Language Model Use and Training Needs Among Rheumatologists: An APLAR Young Rheumatologists International Survey
outcome: Prevalence of LLM use and presence of institutional LLM policies among rheumatologists
effect: 89.6% reported prior LLM use, while only 9.9% reported established institutional policies on LLM use.
quote: While usage is widespread, only 9.9% reported established institutional policies on LLMs use.

title: Large Language Model Use and Training Needs Among Rheumatologists: An APLAR Young Rheumatologists International Survey
outcome: Concern about loss of traditional clinical skills from LLM reliance
effect: 81.1% of both users and nonusers shared concerns regarding potential loss of traditional clinical skills.
quote: Although both groups shared concerns regarding the potential loss of traditional clinical skills (81.1%), active users significantly favored the integration of mandatory LLMs training into core rheumatology curricula.

title: Scenario-based evaluation of large language models for reference accuracy in dermatology: literature retrieval on latent tuberculosis in psoriasis patients on anti-IL-17/23 therapy
outcome: Proportion of fabricated or false references in LLM-generated citation lists
effect: ChatGPT 80.0% (12/15) correct and relevant with no hallucinations; Gemini 80.0% (12/15) hallucinations; Deepseek-V3.2 100.0% fictional references; significant difference between models (p<0.010).
quote: Gemini produced 80.0% (12/15) hallucinations, while Deepseek-V3.2 generated 100.0% fictional references.

title: Evaluating privacy leakages in LLM-driven ambient clinical documentation
outcome: Third-party information leakage in LLM-generated notes with a separate privacy-editing step versus single-step generation
effect: Separating generation and privacy editing further reduced leakage, but only with contextually specific privacy definitions; no single mitigation eliminated leakage, and combined approaches gave the greatest reductions.
quote: Decomposing generation and privacy editing into separate steps could further reduce leakage, but only when privacy was defined with contextual specificity.

title: Assessing ChatGPT vs. evidence-based online responses for polycystic ovary syndrome self-management and education: an international cross-sectional blinded survey of healthcare professionals
outcome: Readability of original ChatGPT and evidence-based patient responses versus recommended patient reading levels
effect: Original ChatGPT median FKGL 12.60, ARI 15.35, FRE 41.95; evidence-based FKGL 11.50, ARI 14.15; both above the 11-12 year-old recommended level; differences not significant (FRE p=0.053).
quote: Since, based on these scores, both evidence-based responses and the initial ChatGPT responses appear to be at a complexity level which is generally challenging for the average reader, we prompted ChatGPT to simplify the provided responses.
country: International (14 countries: Italy, Austria, Germany, UK, Switzerland, Canada, USA, Australia, and others)

title: Assessing ChatGPT vs. evidence-based online responses for polycystic ovary syndrome self-management and education: an international cross-sectional blinded survey of healthcare professionals
outcome: Change in readability scores after prompting ChatGPT to simplify responses
effect: Simplified answers improved: FRE 41.95 to 57.77, FKGL 12.60 to 8.55, GFI 12.93 to 10.63, ARI 15.35 to 11.20 (p<0.01 for all versus evidence-based).
quote: Accordingly, all readability scores improved significantly for the ChatGPT simplified answers ( p < 0.01 for all analyses) ( Table 4 ).
country: International (14 countries: Italy, Austria, Germany, UK, Switzerland, Canada, USA, Australia, and others)

title: Assessing ChatGPT vs. evidence-based online responses for polycystic ovary syndrome self-management and education: an international cross-sectional blinded survey of healthcare professionals
outcome: Ratings versus evidence-based online responses
effect: ChatGPT higher for 11/12 questions; r_rb=-0.46 to -1.00; all p<0.05; +0.824 units average.
quote: ChatGPT responses were rated significantly higher than the evidence-based responses for 11 of the 12 study questions, with moderate to large effect sizes (r r b  = -0.46 to -1.00; all p-values <0.05), with ChatGPT answers being rated on average 0.824 units higher.
country: International (14 countries: Italy, Austria, Germany, UK, Switzerland, Canada, USA, Australia, and others)

title: Assessing ChatGPT vs. evidence-based online responses for polycystic ovary syndrome self-management and education: an international cross-sectional blinded survey of healthcare professionals
outcome: Agreement among healthcare professional raters
effect: Weighted κ ranged from −0.03 to 0.37; agreement was poor to fair.
quote: Weighted Kappa ( κ ) with quadratic weights computed for each of the 12 study questions showed that the level of agreement varied across questions, ranging from poor to fair agreement ( Figure 3 ).
country: International (14 countries: Italy, Austria, Germany, UK, Switzerland, Canada, USA, Australia, and others)

title: Comparative Evaluation of Machine Translation Accuracy of Emergency Department Discharge Instructions: A Non-Inferiority Study
venue: Academic emergency medicine : official journal of the Society for Academic Emergency Medicine
outcome: Translation accuracy by language (fluency, adequacy, meaning, severity) versus professional interpreters
effect: Machine translation non-inferior for adequacy, meaning, severity in Spanish and Portuguese and all four domains in Chinese; fluency inferior in Spanish and Portuguese. Clinically significant error frequency did not differ by method.
quote: For fluency, Google Translate and ChatGPT-4o were inferior in Spanish and Portuguese but non-inferior in Chinese.

title: Expert Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Central Auditory Processing Disorder Information
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and completeness of chatbot CAPD answers by question difficulty
effect: Mean accuracy below 4.0 and completeness about 3.5; complex questions often scored below 3.0; only 3 of 44 questions consistently rated >=4 across all three chatbots.
quote: Current AI chatbots provided generally accurate CAPD information but fell short of clinical standards, particularly on specialized questions.

title: Speaking Patient's Language: Assessment of Readability and Fidelity of Artificial Intelligence-Optimized Consent Forms
outcome: Baseline readability grade level of institutional consent forms versus recommended sixth grade
effect: Original forms averaged 14.1 ± 1.3 grade levels, far above the recommended sixth-grade level.
quote: Original forms averaged 14.1 ± 1.3 grade levels.

title: Speaking Patient's Language: Assessment of Readability and Fidelity of Artificial Intelligence-Optimized Consent Forms
outcome: Readability of LLM-rewritten consent forms versus originals
effect: First LLM revision improved readability to an 8.8 ± 1.2 grade level (P < 0.01), a five-grade reduction; second revision showed no further improvement (9.9 ± 1.2; P = 0.87).
quote: First LLM revision significantly improved readability to an 8.8 ± 1.2 grade level (P < 0.01), a five-grade reduction.

title: Speaking Patient's Language: Assessment of Readability and Fidelity of Artificial Intelligence-Optimized Consent Forms
outcome: Content omissions in LLM-edited consent forms requiring human review
effect: LLM editing caused substantial content omissions; greater reading-level reductions associated with decreased fidelity (r = 0.73, P < 0.01).
quote: LLM-based editing significantly improved consent form readability but resulted in substantial content omissions.

title: Speaking Patient's Language: Assessment of Readability and Fidelity of Artificial Intelligence-Optimized Consent Forms
outcome: content fidelity of LLM-edited consent forms
effect: Mean F1 0.71 ± 0.26; precision 0.95 ± 0.06; recall 0.62 ± 0.16, indicating few hallucinations but frequent content omissions.
quote: The mean F1 score was 0.71 ± 0.26, with high precision (0.95 ± 0.06) but lower recall (0.62 ± 0.16), indicating few hallucinations but frequent content omissions.

title: Comparative performance analysis of AI-based large language models in assessing cervical vertebral maturation stages on lateral cephalometric radiographs
outcome: LLM accuracy in classifying cervical vertebral maturation stage versus orthodontist consensus
effect: Exact-match accuracy 14% to 28%; within ±1 stage 55% to 64%; correlations ρ 0.3–0.616; wide limits of agreement.
quote: Current LLMs did not exhibit clinically acceptable agreement with expert CVM assessments, showing wide error margins that limit their clinical utility.

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence-generated Patient Education Guides on Cardiomyopathies: A Cross-sectional Comparison of ChatGPT and DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level and reading ease) of AI-generated cardiomyopathy patient education brochures
effect: No significant differences between tools on ease, grade, or reliability scores; ChatGPT generally produced higher grade levels and longer text; DeepSeek showed superior readability in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
quote: ChatGPT generally produced content with higher grade levels and longer text, while DeepSeek AI demonstrated higher originality in restrictive cardiomyopathy and superior readability in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
sample_unit: AI-generated patient education brochures (3 cardiomyopathies x 2 tools)

title: Assessing nurses' attitudes toward artificial intelligence in Kazakhstan: psychometric validation of a nine-item scale
outcome: Nurses' general awareness and understanding of AI in nursing
effect: About one third reported no general awareness of AI; 45.8% (n=183) reported little to no understanding of AI use in nursing; 38.8% were reluctant to adopt AI personally.
quote: About one third of the participants reported having no general awareness of AI, and nearly half (45.8%, n = 183) reported little to no understanding of the use of AI in nursing.

title: Large language models as clinical decision-support tools in multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders: A comparative study of ChatGPT-4o and neurologists
venue: Multiple sclerosis journal - experimental, translational and clinical
outcome: Guideline-adherent responses with vs without RAG grounding on curated clinical documents
effect: ChatGPT-4o with RAG 80.5% correct vs 72.9% without context; vs neurologists 66.5% (p=0.001 with RAG; p=0.038 without). GEE OR 3.17 with RAG vs 1.55 without.
quote: Without context (mean: 72.9% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.038) and with context (mean: 80.5% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.001)
sample_unit: neurologists (responses to 21 clinical vignettes; ChatGPT-4o run 10 times per case)

title: Large language models as clinical decision-support tools in multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders: A comparative study of ChatGPT-4o and neurologists
venue: Multiple sclerosis journal - experimental, translational and clinical
outcome: AI versus neurologist correct responses
effect: ChatGPT higher overall: without context 72.9% vs. 66.5% (p = 0.038); with context 80.5% vs. 66.5% (p = 0.001).
quote: When analyzing results across all studies combined, ChatGPT-4o demonstrated a significantly higher percentage of correct responses than neurologists in both conditions: Without context (mean: 72.9% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.038) and with context (mean: 80.5% vs. 66.5%; p = 0.001) ( Figure 1A ).
sample_unit: neurologists (responses to 21 clinical vignettes; ChatGPT-4o run 10 times per case)

title: Large language models as clinical decision-support tools in multiple sclerosis and neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders: A comparative study of ChatGPT-4o and neurologists
venue: Multiple sclerosis journal - experimental, translational and clinical
outcome: Reproducibility of ChatGPT responses across 10 repeated runs per case
effect: Responses highly consistent across 10 repetitions, identical in most scenarios or showing minimal variability, typically two response patterns; some cases at 60-90% correct.
quote: In general, ChatGPT's responses were highly consistent across the 10 repetitions per case, with the model producing identical answers in most scenarios or showing minimal variability, typically limited to two different response patterns.
sample_unit: neurologists (responses to 21 clinical vignettes; ChatGPT-4o run 10 times per case)

title: Evaluating large language models for glaucoma counseling: A pilot study of ChatGPT and Google Gemini responses in Traditional Chinese
outcome: Appropriateness of LLM glaucoma answers in Traditional Chinese, rated by ophthalmologists on 5-point Likert
effect: ChatGPT 4.32 ± 0.65 vs Gemini 4.03 ± 0.66 (P = 0.004); both reasonably appropriate, lower on lifestyle questions; no language-stratified comparison with English.
quote: ChatGPT achieved a higher overall appropriateness score (4.32 ± 0.65) than Google Gemini (4.03 ± 0.66), with a statistically significant difference (P = 0.004).

title: Comparative performance of large language models and Drugs.com versus Lexicomp for antiseizure medication drug-drug interactions: A cross-sectional study with iterative prompting analysis
venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of LLMs versus Drugs.com against Lexicomp reference for ASM interactions
effect: Drugs.com sensitivity 0.870, specificity 0.629, accuracy 0.709; ChatGPT sensitivity 0.842, specificity 0.358; DeepSeek sensitivity 0.877, specificity 0.200. LLMs overpredicted interactions.
quote: Drugs.com demonstrated the best overall performance, with sensitivity 0.870, specificity 0.629, and accuracy 0.709.

title: Comparative performance of large language models and Drugs.com versus Lexicomp for antiseizure medication drug-drug interactions: A cross-sectional study with iterative prompting analysis
venue: Exploratory research in clinical and social pharmacy
outcome: Specificity of LLMs under single-prompt versus iterative prompting for false positive cases
effect: Iterative prompting improved specificity for ChatGPT (0.77) and DeepSeek (0.42), correcting many false positive classifications; single-prompt specificity was 0.358 and 0.200.
quote: Iterative prompting substantially improved specificity for ChatGPT (0.77) and DeepSeek (0.42), correcting many false positive classifications.

title: Evaluation of AI-Generated Surgical Decision Aids for Pelvic Floor Disorders
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease) of ChatGPT-generated decision aids
effect: The reading level required to read the decision aid tools was high overall, despite high patient and physician understandability ratings.
quote: Accuracy was <4 (unfavorable) on 2 of the decision aid tools, and the reading level required to read them was high overall.
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated decision aid tools (one per question)

title: Evaluation of AI-Generated Surgical Decision Aids for Pelvic Floor Disorders
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient decision aids relative to appropriate level
effect: Reading level required was high overall; all tools could benefit from improved readability.
quote: Accuracy was <4 (unfavorable) on 2 of the decision aid tools, and the reading level required to read them was high overall.
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated decision aid tools (one per question)

title: Evaluation of AI-Generated Surgical Decision Aids for Pelvic Floor Disorders
outcome: Physician-rated accuracy of ChatGPT decision aids on 5-point Likert scale
effect: Accuracy was <4 (unfavorable) on 2 of 6 decision aid tools; approximately 30% of topics require accuracy improvements.
quote: However, approximately 30% of the topics require improvements to accuracy, while all tools could benefit from improved reliability and readability.
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated decision aid tools (one per question)

title: Digital experts for fibromyalgia: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek in addressing patient questions with focus on readability and medical accuracy
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of chatbot fibromyalgia responses
effect: ChatGPT responses required lower reading grade levels; Gemini produced more complex responses requiring higher reading levels; DeepSeek fell mid-range. No numeric grade levels reported in abstract.
quote: Readability analysis using the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level revealed that ChatGPT's responses generally required lower reading grade levels, making them more accessible.

title: Rapid Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Technology Used for Ambient Dictation in Primary Care: Comparing the Quality of Documentation of Artificial Intelligence-Generated and Human-Produced Clinical Notes
outcome: Ambient scribe note quality (modified PDQI-9) versus human-produced notes, blinded raters
effect: Human notes scored higher than AI in all 5 cases; low back pain case human 43.8 vs AI 20.3, difference -23.5 (CI -29.2 to -17.9); AI lower in all 10 domains.
quote: Notes generated by AI had lower-quality scores than human-generated notes across 5 standardized care cases.
sample_unit: AI scribe tools (notes rated by 30 blinded raters across 5 standardized cases, compared with 18 human note takers)

title: Rapid Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Technology Used for Ambient Dictation in Primary Care: Comparing the Quality of Documentation of Artificial Intelligence-Generated and Human-Produced Clinical Notes
outcome: AI scribe note quality across domains including thoroughness, organization, and usefulness
effect: Pooled domain analysis showed lower AI scores across all 10 domains, largest deficits: thorough -1.23, organized -1.06, useful -1.03.
quote: Pooled domain analysis showed lower AI scores across all 10 domains, with the largest deficits in domains related to being thorough (-1.23 [CI, -1.82 to -0.65]), organized (-1.06 [CI, -1.65 to -0.47]), and useful (-1.03 [CI, -1.61 to -0.44]).
sample_unit: AI scribe tools (notes rated by 30 blinded raters across 5 standardized cases, compared with 18 human note takers)

title: Rapid Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence Technology Used for Ambient Dictation in Primary Care: Comparing the Quality of Documentation of Artificial Intelligence-Generated and Human-Produced Clinical Notes
outcome: Variation in note quality across competing vendor AI scribe products
effect: 11 vendor AI scribe tools were compared side by side on standardized cases; all scored below human notes, with wide CIs (e.g., AI 20.3 [15.4 to 25.2] in back pain case).
quote: Prior evaluations have been vendor specific and not focused on measures of documentation quality.
sample_unit: AI scribe tools (notes rated by 30 blinded raters across 5 standardized cases, compared with 18 human note takers)

title: Quality of Clinical Notes Created by Ambient Listening Generative AI: Pragmatic Prospective Pilot Study
outcome: Errors in AI drafted notes with potential for serious harm if not corrected
effect: 19 (5.3%) notes contained errors rated serious or imminent risk (severity 4-5); 14.9% (143/960) of notes left entirely unedited.
quote: However, because a small number contained errors that carried the risk of serious harm if not corrected, careful clinician review of notes remains imperative.
sample_unit: AI-generated clinic notes evaluated by physicians

title: Quality of Clinical Notes Created by Ambient Listening Generative AI: Pragmatic Prospective Pilot Study
outcome: Local assessment of ambient scribe documentation accuracy and quality via physician review of notes
effect: Local pilot review of 356 notes identified error types and severity; 94.7% (337/356) free from significant errors, showing feasibility of local evaluation.
quote: Prior to deploying an AI scribe, organizations should pilot the technology and include an efficient review process to understand the nature and type of errors common at their organization.
sample_unit: AI-generated clinic notes evaluated by physicians

title: Quality of Clinical Notes Created by Ambient Listening Generative AI: Pragmatic Prospective Pilot Study
outcome: Physician editing rates of AI-generated notes as a reliance signal
effect: Median 9.0% (IQR 2.5%-21.9%) of AI words changed; 14.9% (143/960) notes unedited; physician average edit ranged 1.9% to 69.3%.
quote: Physician editing practices varied widely, with average percentages of AI-generated words changed ranging from 1.9% to 69.3% (median 9.0%, IQR 2.5%-21.9%).
sample_unit: AI-generated clinic notes evaluated by physicians

title: Input structure-driven instability and convergence in large language model clinical reasoning: a formative study using pediatric residency-level MCQs
outcome: LLM accuracy and inter-model variability under simultaneous versus batch question delivery
effect: Simultaneous delivery: accuracy 38%-90% with significant inter-model differences; batches of ten: 83%-88% with no significant inter-model differences.
quote: When all questions were presented simultaneously, model accuracy varied widely (38%-90%), with significant inter-model differences, indicating poor reproducibility.

title: Assessment of AI-Generated Patient Education Materials for Bladder Training and Pelvic Floor Muscle Therapy: Comparison with an International Society Leaflet
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of LLM-generated patient leaflets versus society leaflet
effect: GPT-4 grade ≈ 6.6, Gemini ≈ 7.4; Sonnet4 ≈ 15; Llama-4 ≈ 17; IUGA leaflets around 9-10.
quote: Readability varied greatly: GPT-4 had an average Flesch-Kincaid grade level ≈ 6.6, Gemini ≈ 7.4; Sonnet4 ≈ 15; Llama-4 ≈ 17.

title: Assessment of AI-Generated Patient Education Materials for Bladder Training and Pelvic Floor Muscle Therapy: Comparison with an International Society Leaflet
outcome: Understandability (PEMAT-U) and readability of AI-generated patient education materials
effect: PEMAT-U showed a trend (p = 0.063); Sonnet4 outperformed Llama-4 on PEMAT-U; readability grade levels ranged from ≈6.6 to ≈17.
quote: PEMAT-U showed a trend (p = 0.063)

title: Evaluating open-source LLMs for dental EMR generation
outcome: AI-generated dental EMR quality
effect: CRISPE improved total 7DI: 28.86 ± 2.12 vs. 26.91 ± 2.36; p < .001; d = 0.57.
quote: As detailed in Table 3 , the CRISPE framework yielded a highly significant improvement in overall 7DI scores (28.86 ± 2.12 vs. 26.91 ± 2.36; p < .001, Cohen’s d = 0.57).
sample_unit: de-identified dental EMRs converted to synthetic Mandarin dialogues (50-case expert-rated subset)

title: Evaluating open-source LLMs for dental EMR generation
outcome: Between-model EMR quality differences
effect: Automated metrics differed significantly; expert 7DI found no significant between-model differences: F = 0.21, p = .957, η² = 0.009.
quote: ANOVA detected no statistically significant differences among models (F = 0.21, p = .957, η² = 0.009), and all post-hoc Tukey HSD pairwise comparisons were non-significant (all p > .05).
sample_unit: de-identified dental EMRs converted to synthetic Mandarin dialogues (50-case expert-rated subset)

title: Transforming adnexal mass assessment: how large language model improve ovarian-adnexal reporting and data system interpretation and sonographer performance
outcome: Reader diagnostic performance (AUC) and agreement with vs without LLM assistance, junior vs senior
effect: Juniors with LLM: weighted κ ≥ 0.85, mean ΔAUC = 0.10 (p = 0.06, non-significant); seniors ΔAUC = 0.01 (p = 0.22). Gains reflect reliance on LLM rather than independent skill.
quote: In contrast, senior readers showed stable performance (mean ΔAUC = 0.01; p = 0.22).
sample_unit: lesions (302 patients); 150-lesion subset read by 4 readers

title: Transforming adnexal mass assessment: how large language model improve ovarian-adnexal reporting and data system interpretation and sonographer performance
outcome: Acceptance of LLM suggestions in discordant cases by reader experience level
effect: Junior readers accepted LLM suggestions in 60.78%-72.34% of discordant cases versus 2.04%-2.33% among seniors.
quote: In discordant cases, junior readers accepted LLM suggestions in 60.78%-72.34% of instances, compared with only 2.04%-2.33% among seniors.
sample_unit: lesions (302 patients); 150-lesion subset read by 4 readers

title: Evaluating and enhancing the performance of large language models in thyroid eye disease through customization and Chain-of-Thought strategies
outcome: Accuracy of customized deployed LLM configurations on TED multiple-choice questions versus base models
effect: GPT-4 76.2% and Claude 3.5 83.2%; customized TED-GPT 86.1% and TED-Claude 89.1%, outperforming newer LLMs.
quote: The addition of CoT, along with customization into GPT-4 and Claude 3.5, led to improvement in the accuracy (CoT-GPT 86.1%, CoT-Claude 87.1%, TED-GPT 86.1%, TED-Claude 89.1%), outperforming all other newer LLMs.

title: Development and prospective shadow evaluation of a domain-specific large language model for emergency neurological diagnosis
outcome: Change in LLM health education recommendations when demographic information was included
effect: Adding demographic information altered the model's health education recommendations, suggesting sensitivity to sociodemographic factors. No magnitude is reported in the abstract.
quote: Moreover, the inclusion of demographic information altered the model's recommendations for health education, suggesting a sensitivity to sociodemographic factors.

title: Patch-to-slide fusion deep learning model for histological diagnosis of early pregnancy loss including hydatidiform mole
outcome: Pathologist diagnostic performance with versus without AI assistance
effect: AI-assisted diagnosis significantly improved pathologist performance (p < 0.05).
quote: AI-assisted diagnosis significantly improved pathologist performance (p < 0.05).

title: Radiomics Applicability Domain Analysis Classification Framework (RADAN-CF): A method for evaluating prediction reliability in radiomics
venue: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
outcome: Association between per-prediction out-of-distribution/reliability category and prediction error
effect: Prediction error significantly associated with RADANCF category (ANOVA p < 10^-12), though non-monotonic; correct predictions appeared in all traffic-light categories in external validation.
quote: Prediction error was significantly associated with RADANCF category, although the relationship was not strictly monotonic, with intermediate categories showing the largest error contributions.
sample_unit: model configurations (6 datasets x 5 classifiers, plus external cohort of 2689 prostate cancer patients)

title: [The use of artificial intelligence tools in the perception of electroradiologists]
outcome: Electroradiologists' AI knowledge and training adequacy
effect: Most respondents know the general concept of AI but lack detailed knowledge. Insufficient education and a need for training were reported. Lack of training limits readiness for implementation.
