quote: Models adapted to training-time imperfections but remained sensitive to previously unseen degradations at deployment.

title: Integrating AI Scribe Technology into Public Health Workflows: Simulation and Field Evaluation in Disease Case Management

quote: At SMDHU, scribe use was associated with a mean reduction of 12.9 minutes in documentation time compared with usual practice (p < 0.05), whereas at WDGPH it was associated with a mean increase of 10.4 minutes (p < 0.05).

title: Med-KAG: Preliminary Results of a Medical Knowledge-Augmented Generation Approach

title: Evaluating a Consumer LLM for Suicide Risk Response Calibration: A Pilot Study

title: Evaluating a Consumer LLM for Suicide Risk Response Calibration: A Pilot Study
venue: Studies in health technology and informatics

title: Generative-AI as a source of caregiving guidance for medical tourists: A content and readability analysis
outcome: Readability of GenAI medical tourism caregiving guidance versus recommended general-audience levels

title: Evaluation of segmentation accuracy and the improvement of time effectiveness using deep learning-based segmentation in 177Lu-DOTATATE dosimetry
outcome: AI segmentation compared with manual contouring by physicists/technologists on accuracy, dose and time
effect: AI-seg median DSC liver 0.988, spleen 0.965, kidneys 0.994 vs manual 0.955, 0.929, 0.929; AI with correction faster (47.0 vs 54.3 min, p=0.014).
quote: Further, the total required time for the reference contour, including the corrections after AI segmentation, was significantly shorter than that for manual contouring ( p = 0.014).

title: Evaluation of segmentation accuracy and the improvement of time effectiveness using deep learning-based segmentation in 177Lu-DOTATATE dosimetry
outcome: Output-appropriate contour metrics
effect: DSC and MDA met thresholds, but HD was approximately 20.0 mm in liver and spleen.
quote: In our study, DSC and MDA met the tolerance threshold in the liver and spleen, but HD was approximately 20.0 mm.

title: Evaluation of segmentation accuracy and the improvement of time effectiveness using deep learning-based segmentation in 177Lu-DOTATATE dosimetry
outcome: Performance under hepatomegaly
effect: AI outlier HD >30.0 mm occurred in liver 3/23 and spleen 2/23 due to hepatomegaly.
quote: Cases in which AI segmentation showed outlier liver (3/23) and spleen (2/23) HD (HD > 30.0 mm) were due to hepatomegaly caused by metastatic whole liver tumors.

title: Evaluation of segmentation accuracy and the improvement of time effectiveness using deep learning-based segmentation in 177Lu-DOTATATE dosimetry
outcome: AI-corrected versus manual dosimetry time
effect: Reference/AI-corrected method: 47.0 [30.0-58.0] min vs manual 54.3 [49.5-67.0] min, p = 0.014.
quote: Dosimetry using the reference method took significantly less time than the manual approach (47.0 [30.0-58.0] min vs. 54.3 [49.5-67.0] min, p = 0.014).

title: Evaluation of segmentation accuracy and the improvement of time effectiveness using deep learning-based segmentation in 177Lu-DOTATATE dosimetry
outcome: contouring accuracy of AI segmentation versus manual clinician contouring
effect: Manual contouring had significantly lower spleen HD (7.1 vs 12.5 mm, p=0.027), while AI had significantly higher kidney DSC (0.993-0.994 vs 0.926-0.935, p<0.001) and lower MDA
quote: For HD in the spleen, manual contouring showed significantly lower values than those of AI segmentation ( p = 0.027).

title: Accuracy of large language models in head and neck cancers: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT and Gemini in TNM staging and clinical decision support
outcome: LLM TNM staging and treatment plan accuracy versus AJCC 8th edition and tumor board decisions
effect: TNM staging accuracy ChatGPT 75.6%, Gemini 75.0%; treatment planning accuracy Gemini 78.9% vs ChatGPT 71.7% (p=0.043); staging error rate of 25% remains.
quote: However, a staging error rate of 25% remains a critical concern, potentially leading to inappropriate clinical pathways.

title: Accuracy of large language models in head and neck cancers: a comparative analysis of ChatGPT and Gemini in TNM staging and clinical decision support
outcome: Incorrect LLM staging and treatment outputs that could be acted upon without verification
effect: About 25% staging error rate for both models; treatment accuracy 71.7% (ChatGPT) and 78.9% (Gemini), so incorrect outputs would reach clinical pathways without supervision.
quote: Strict expert supervision is mandatory to prevent subsite-specific errors from impacting surgical and oncological outcomes.

title: A centralized decision-making support consultation response for fertility preservation in breast cancer patients: benchmark performance of generative large language models in terms of reliability and readability
outcome: Readability of LLM responses on fertility preservation for breast cancer patients

quote: The responses generated by all LLMs are too complex for the general public and fail to meet the recommended reading comprehension standards for years 6 to 8; the writing standards of most outputs are equivalent to those of secondary school education, or the reading level required for legal documents.

title: Performance evaluation of large language models in the diagnosis of emergency internal medicine diseases: a retrospective study
outcome: Main diagnostic accuracy of LLMs versus emergency junior physicians on same real cases
effect: DeepSeek-V3 (90.0%), ChatGPT-4o (86.0%), Grok3 (86.0%) significantly higher than EDJP (77.5%, p<0.05); LLM comprehensiveness scores all higher than EDJP; LLMs faster (6.3-14.0 s vs 360.2 s).

title: Identification of quality and safety concerns in AI chatbot responses to procedural sedation: a comparative evaluation of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot
outcome: Quality, safety omissions, and confabulation in chatbot answers to procedural sedation patient questions

quote: The results demonstrated variability in response quality across chatbots, with several answers containing incomplete information, safety omissions, or potentially misleading statements.

title: Utility of large language models as information tools for nursing care in gout: a comparative study of DeepSeek and ChatGPT
outcome: Validity of reference links cited by LLM answers

quote: In addition, DeepSeek-R1 provided 4 reference links were invalid.

title: Low-energy small language models with retrieval-augmented generation can surpass large-model performance in rheumatology
outcome: Diagnostic and therapeutic F1 and RAGAS with vs without guideline retrieval grounding
effect: RAG generally improved diagnostic and therapeutic accuracy, magnitude varied by model; SLMs benefited most consistently; Mixtral with RAG had top F1 (72% Dx, 73% Tx) and RAGAS 81%.
quote: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) generally improved diagnostic and therapeutic accuracy, although the magnitude of improvement varied considerably depending on model architecture ( Table 1 ).

title: Low-energy small language models with retrieval-augmented generation can surpass large-model performance in rheumatology
outcome: Proportion of responses unsuitable for clinical use due to unsafe or hallucinated recommendations

title: Low-energy small language models with retrieval-augmented generation can surpass large-model performance in rheumatology
outcome: LLMs generating treatment recommendations with unsafe content
effect: 9% of responses were unsuitable for clinical use, partly from unsafe or hallucinated therapeutic recommendations; authors state no model should be used without expert supervision.

title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm to Increase Productivity in Implantable Loop Recorder Monitoring: A Multicentre Observational Study
outcome: Site-level alert reduction after AI activation

quote: The magnitude of reduction varied between sites, suggesting heterogeneity in real-world implementation and warranting further evaluation of local workflow and programming factors (Table 1 ).

title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Algorithm to Increase Productivity in Implantable Loop Recorder Monitoring: A Multicentre Observational Study
outcome: Clinician-facing alert burden and estimated physiologist review workload
effect: Clinician-facing alerts decreased from 4,261 to 2,509 (41.1%). Suppression of 1,007 alerts corresponded to estimated savings of 185-218 hours annually (3.6-4.2 hours per week); review time was not directly measured.
quote: Applying published time-and-motion estimates for remote transmission review (11-13 minutes per alert), suppression of 1,007 alerts by the AI algorithm was estimated to release approximately 185-218 hours of physiologist review time annually, equivalent to 3.6-4.2 hours per week of re-deployable service capacity.

title: Persona Routing Associated With Fewer Safety and Monotonicity Violations in Simulated Emergency Large Language Model (LLM) Reasoning
outcome: Safety violations and under-triage with escalation routing from lean to safe persona versus lean baseline
effect: Lean baseline had safety violations in 8/56 (14.3%); routed strategies 0/56. Monotonicity violations fell from 10/16 (62.5%) to 2/16 (ROUTER_R1) and 0/16 (ROUTER_R2_CF); simulated calls 1.21 for R1.
quote: Routing strategies eliminated safety violations while keeping test counts near the lean baseline (ROUTER_R1 mean: 2.14; ROUTER_R2 mean: 2.20; ROUTER_R3 mean: 2.21).

title: Persona Routing Associated With Fewer Safety and Monotonicity Violations in Simulated Emergency Large Language Model (LLM) Reasoning

effect: mAP declined from 0.82 (95% CI: [0.79, 0.84]) on seen injuries to 0.70 (95% CI: [0.67, 0.73]) on unseen injuries; recall 0.84 to 0.73.
quote: These findings demonstrate that image-level partitioning, particularly under controlled acquisition conditions, can yield inflated generalization estimates.

title: Evaluation Framework for Bruise Detection: Systematic ALS/White-Light Training and Skin-Tone Balancing with Deep Learning
outcome: Lighting-distribution robustness
effect: FCOS mAP@0.5 dropped from 0.931 for ALS→ALS to 0.805 for ALS+W→ALS; higher W ratios raised CUM FP from 1804 (0/100) to 2582 (100/0).
quote: Cross-dataset evaluation reveals a decline in model performance when tested on a dataset different from its training distribution.

title: Evaluation Framework for Bruise Detection: Systematic ALS/White-Light Training and Skin-Tone Balancing with Deep Learning
outcome: Poor-quality imaging failures
effect: White light Invalid Failed Consistent/Inconsistent were 15.29%/10.59%; 450 nm orange was 5.44%/0%, and 415 nm yellow was 6.01%/4.37%.
quote: Several factors contribute to detection failures and underprediction, including low contrast (faded bruises), label inaccuracies, blurriness, camera shift, and shadows.

title: Marker-Free, Automated Eyelid Assessment in Thyroid Eye Disease Using Artificial Intelligence: A Multicenter Validation Study
outcome: Eyelid measurement error by site and imaging device (DSLR internal vs smartphone external)
effect: Internal (DSLR): MRD1 PCC 0.98, MAPE 5.69%; MRD2 PCC 0.94, MAPE 4.57%. External (smartphone): MRD1 PCC 0.94, MAPE 9.06%; MRD2 PCC 0.93, MAPE 15.07%.
quote: Although MRD2 showed a slightly higher MAPE (15.07%), likely due to manual measurement variability in clinical records, the correlation remained strong (PCC 0.93).

title: Clinical validation of an artificial intelligence model for thyroid fine-needle aspiration biopsy indication: comparison with TI-RADS systems and human specialists in a Chilean public hospital
outcome: AI FNA recommendation sensitivity/specificity versus specialists using ACR and Horvath TI-RADS on same patients
effect: AI sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.41; Horvath TI-RADS by expert radiologist sensitivity 0.82, specificity 0.69; concordance between AI and TI-RADS methods moderate.
quote: The AI model showed a sensitivity of 0.88 and a specificity of 0.41.

title: Clinical validation of an artificial intelligence model for thyroid fine-needle aspiration biopsy indication: comparison with TI-RADS systems and human specialists in a Chilean public hospital
outcome: AI performance on local retrospective data against cytology reference standard
effect: On 101 local patients using Bethesda ≥ III as reference, AI sensitivity was 0.88 and specificity 0.41, described as comparable to human specialists.
quote: In a real-world clinical setting, the AI model demonstrated performance comparable to that of human specialists for recommending FNA in thyroid nodules.

title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
outcome: Plain-language readability, practicality and structure of AI patient education responses with instruction configuration
effect: CSA-GPT had lower FKGL (6.07 vs 9.12), higher practicality (4.92 vs 4.45) and structural clarity (4.50 vs 3.19), all p < 0.001.
quote: Mean structural clarity scores were 4.50 ± 0.69 (95% CI: 4.35–4.65) for CSA-GPT and 3.19 ± 0.81 (95% CI: 3.01–3.37) for ChatGPT5.2 (all p < 0.001).

title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
outcome: Major factual errors or critical omissions
effect: Safety audit errors were 1.25% for CSA-GPT vs 3.75% for ChatGPT5.2; p=0.25.
quote: Safety audit error rates were low and did not differ significantly between models (1.25% vs. 3.75%, p = 0.25).

title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
outcome: Reading grade level (FKGL) of patient-facing LLM responses with vs without instruction configuration
effect: Mean FKGL 6.07 ± 1.28 for CSA-GPT vs 9.12 ± 1.71 for ChatGPT5.2 (p < 0.001); in-target (6–8) 37.5% vs 25.0%.
quote: Mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was 6.07 ± 1.28 (95% CI: 5.79–6.36) for CSA-GPT and 9.12 ± 1.71 (95% CI: 8.74–9.50) for ChatGPT5.2 ( p < 0.001).

title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
outcome: Empathetic tone and linguistic appropriateness of generative AI patient communications rated by specialists
effect: Empathy scores 4.45 ± 0.69 for CSA-GPT vs 3.39 ± 0.77 for ChatGPT5.2 (p < 0.001).
quote: Mean empathetic tone scores were 4.45 ± 0.69 (95% CI: 4.30–4.60) and 3.39 ± 0.77 (95% CI: 3.22–3.56), respectively.

title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
outcome: Empathetic tone and communication quality
effect: ChatGPT5.2 empathy averaged 3.39±0.77 versus CSA-GPT 4.45±0.69; all patient-centered submetrics p<0.001.
quote: Practicality, empathetic tone, and structural clarity were all significantly higher for CSA-GPT (all p < 0.001).

title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
outcome: communication quality total score
effect: Mean score was 17.95 ± 1.62 for configured model vs 9.55 ± 1.94 for baseline (p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 3.22); 97.5% vs 0% met high quality criteria
quote: CSA-GPT achieved higher total rubric scores than ChatGPT5.2 (17.95 ± 1.62; 95% CI: 17.59–18.31 vs. 9.55 ± 1.94; 95% CI: 9.12–9.98; p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 3.22), noting that the rubric is a theory-informed, exploratory benchmarking instrument.

title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
outcome: reading level above target
effect: Baseline model mean FKGL was 9.12 ± 1.71 (grade 9) with only 25.0% within the target 6-8 grade level range
quote: Mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level was 6.07 ± 1.28 (95% CI: 5.79–6.36) for CSA-GPT and 9.12 ± 1.71 (95% CI: 8.74–9.50) for ChatGPT5.2 ( p < 0.001).

title: Benchmarking the readability, quality, and educational suitability of large language models in communicating pertussis
outcome: Factual accuracy and guideline concordance of LLM pertussis answers against Chinese guidelines
effect: No harmful advice or direct guideline contradictions were identified in any model output; ChatGPT achieved the highest mean accuracy/concordance score.
quote: No harmful advice or direct guideline contradictions were identified in any model output.

title: Benchmarking the readability, quality, and educational suitability of large language models in communicating pertussis
outcome: Understandability and actionability (C-PEMAT) and quality (GQS) of LLM patient education content
effect: Median C-PEMAT generally acceptable across models; ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Doubao scored significantly higher than Wenxin Yiyan and Gemini on C-PEMAT and GQS (p<0.001).
quote: Median C-PEMAT scores across all models suggested generally acceptable accessibility for patient education.

title: Improving Clinical Efficiency Using Artificial Intelligence Scribe for Documentation (ICE-AID Study): A Retrospective-Prospective Cohort Study at a Quaternary Children's Hospital and Health Service
venue: Journal of paediatrics and child health
outcome: Clinician-rated document quality of AI scribe notes (modified PDQI-9 domains)
effect: Median score 4 on a 1-5 scale in 9 of 10 survey domains (n = 77), indicating acceptable quality; mean SUS 74.
quote: The document quality survey showed acceptable document quality with median score 4, in 9 of the 10 survey domains (scale 1-to-5, n = 77).

title: AI as a Safety Net Reader for Mammograms Classified as Normal or Benign in the French Screening Program
outcome: Missed cancers and second-reading workload
effect: Approximately 77% second-reading workload reduction, with small but measurable risk of missed cancers.
quote: Artificial intelligence triage could potentially reduce second reading workload by approximately 77% in the French breast cancer screening program, despite a small but measurable risk of missed cancers and the need for governance.

title: Responsible AI for Personalized Patient Education and Engagement Across Medical Conditions: Leveraging Multi-Agent LLMs, Ambient Technology, and NotebookLM-A Case Study in Diabetes Education and Limb Preservation
venue: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association
outcome: Expert evaluation of ambient scribe SOAP notes and summaries for hallucinations, accuracy, completeness
effect: Three outcomes passed validation criteria including accuracy, completeness, comprehensiveness, absence of potential harm, and no hallucination; no hallucinations were found.
quote: Three outcomes successfully passed the validation criteria, including accuracy, completeness, comprehensiveness, absence of potential harm, and no hallucination.

title: Comparison of ChatGPT-5 and DeepSeek V3 for Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Patient Education in Foot and Ankle Disorders
venue: Journal of the American Podiatric Medical Association
outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of AI-generated patient education texts for foot and ankle disorders
effect: DeepSeek V3 texts were easier to read (lower FKGL, higher FRE) than ChatGPT-5 texts; the abstract reports no numeric scores and no comparison against a target patient reading level.
quote: DeepSeek V3 demonstrated better readability, producing simpler and more understandable content, as reflected in its lower FKGL score and higher FRE score.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
outcome: AI performance as used by clinicians in workflow versus standalone model metrics
effect: Surgeon-plus-segmentation-map accuracy 94% and sensitivity 98% exceeded standalone SVM (84%, 83%) and Gemini (90%, 86%); sensitivity edge over Gemini significant, accuracy not.
quote: The human–model fusion significantly improves overall performance above both the autonomous ML output and human-only assessments of raw scans.
sample_unit: intraoperative OCT scans (27 patients; 5 neurosurgeon raters)

title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
outcome: Whether clinicians detect incorrect AI outputs rather than passively accepting them
effect: Surgeons rejected 9 of 13 (69%) AI false-positive cases; HITL accuracy exceeded SVM baseline, indicating no blind adherence. Limitation: 4 of 13 errors were still confirmed.
quote: Relying on their domain knowledge of tissue topology, the surgeon rejects the AI’s suggestion in 9 of these cases and overrides the machine.
sample_unit: intraoperative OCT scans (27 patients; 5 neurosurgeon raters)

title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
outcome: Clinician verification of AI segmentation outputs catching AI errors
effect: Surgeons overrode algorithmic false positives in 69% (9/13) of cases; HITL accuracy 94% vs SVM 84%.
quote: They successfully override algorithmic noise in 69% (9 out of 13) of false-positive cases because tissue topology and signal margins provide vital contextual cues that the algorithm currently lacks.
sample_unit: intraoperative OCT scans (27 patients; 5 neurosurgeon raters)

title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
outcome: Comparison of AI (SVM, Gemini) against clinician-in-the-loop on same scans
effect: On same 86 scans, HITL accuracy 94% vs SVM 84% and Gemini 90%; sensitivity 98% vs 83% and 86%.
quote: While advanced reasoning models like Gemini exhibit powerful contextual capabilities, the direct integration of human domain knowledge proved superior, firmly establishing the value of HITL over fully autonomous “models-only” pipelines.
sample_unit: intraoperative OCT scans (27 patients; 5 neurosurgeon raters)

title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
outcome: HITL adjunct versus standalone model diagnosis
effect: HITL sensitivity 98% [92–100] versus Gemini 86% [74–95].
quote: When compared to the advanced Gemini 3.1 Pro baseline, the human inference on Segmentation maps maintained a pronounced and significant edge in sensitivity (98% [92–100] vs. 86% [74–95]).
sample_unit: intraoperative OCT scans (27 patients; 5 neurosurgeon raters)

title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy/sensitivity of surgeons with AI segmentation maps versus AI alone and surgeons without AI
effect: HITL accuracy 94% [88-98], sensitivity 98% vs SVM alone accuracy 84%, sensitivity 83%; Gemini accuracy 90%, sensitivity 86%; structural scans without ML 80%. Surgeons overrode 9 of 13 AI false positives.
quote: Yet, human inference on the segmented scans achieved a superior, statistically significant accuracy of 94% [95% CI: 88–98%].
sample_unit: intraoperative OCT scans (27 patients; 5 neurosurgeon raters)

title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
outcome: Clinician-controlled HITL diagnostic inference
effect: HITL achieved accuracy 94% [88–98%] and sensitivity 98% [92–100%], exceeding model-only baselines.
quote: This HITL synergy not only improves overall diagnostic performance by optimally utilizing human contextual intelligence over purely algorithmic reasoning, but also ensures that the ultimate decision-making responsibility remains safely with the clinician.
sample_unit: intraoperative OCT scans (27 patients; 5 neurosurgeon raters)

title: Human-in-the-Loop Enhances Machine Learning Inference in Intraoperative Optical Coherence Tomography Glioma Imaging
outcome: Clinician override of incorrect AI suggestions
effect: Surgeons rejected AI suggestions in 9 of 13 algorithmic false-positive cases.
quote: Relying on their domain knowledge of tissue topology, the surgeon rejects the AI’s suggestion in 9 of these cases and overrides the machine.
sample_unit: intraoperative OCT scans (27 patients; 5 neurosurgeon raters)

title: Feasibility study of an AI-powered mobile app to support cutaneous leishmaniasis diagnosis in the Brazilian Amazon
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of AI pipeline in ideal-world versus real-world conditions

title: Knowledge and Use of Artificial Intelligence Among Oncology Faculty and Trainees at a Comprehensive Cancer Center in 2025
outcome: Staff need for AI training and knowledge of learning resources
effect: Nearly 93% of respondents endorsed the need for dedicated AI training, and approximately half reported not knowing where to find reliable learning resources.
quote: Nearly 93% of respondents endorsed the need for dedicated AI training, and approximately half reported not knowing where to find reliable learning resources.

title: Multimodal GPT-5 for Predicting Poor Functional Outcomes After Intracerebral Hemorrhage in the Emergency Department: Validation Study
outcome: GPT models vs conventional ML model on same data: discrimination, calibration, overall performance, net benefit
effect: Zero-shot GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 AUROC 0.84 and 0.85 vs ML 0.85, but lower scaled Brier scores, low or negative Nagelkerke R², and no superior clinical utility on decision curve analysis.
quote: Zero-shot GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 demonstrated discrimination comparable to the ML model (AUROC 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.91 and 0.85, 95% CI 0.78-0.91, respectively) with high reproducibility (ICC 0.91 and 0.95, respectively) but inferior overall performance, as reflected by lower scaled Brier scores and low or negative Nagelkerke R² values.

title: Multimodal GPT-5 for Predicting Poor Functional Outcomes After Intracerebral Hemorrhage in the Emergency Department: Validation Study
outcome: Reproducibility of GPT predictions across repeated runs (ICC)
effect: Zero-shot ICC 0.91 (GPT-4.1) and 0.95 (GPT-5); with ML-informed prompts ICC 0.97 and 0.96, indicating high reproducibility.
quote: Zero-shot GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 demonstrated discrimination comparable to the ML model (AUROC 0.84, 95% CI 0.77-0.91 and 0.85, 95% CI 0.78-0.91, respectively) with high reproducibility (ICC 0.91 and 0.95, respectively) but inferior overall performance, as reflected by lower scaled Brier scores and low or negative Nagelkerke R² values.

title: Usability and Usefulness of Machine Learning-Based Clinical Decision Support Software in Primary Care: Survey of Users in a Prospective Observational Study
outcome: User-reported workflow integration, usability and acceptance of the CDSS after a 4-month implementation
effect: 48% found the software easy to integrate into workflow; 67% trusted output; 52% agreed it supported decisions; 9% of practices dropped out in first 8 weeks; assistants under-involved in design.
quote: Forty-eight percent of respondents found the software easy to integrate into their clinical workflow.
sample_unit: practices submitting at least one survey response (survey sent to 263 general practitioners and assistants)

title: Guideline-Integrated Large Language Models Improve Decision Support for Acute Ear, Nose and Throat Emergencies
outcome: Guideline adherence, accuracy, and misleading recommendations with vs without guideline RAG
effect: RAG-enabled models showed significantly improved diagnostic accuracy, workup, management, referral appropriateness, and guideline adherence; RAG reduced misleading recommendations.
quote: Compared with baseline models, RAG-enabled models demonstrated significantly improved diagnostic accuracy, diagnostic workup quality, management planning, referral appropriateness, and guideline adherence.

title: Reliability and readability of AI platforms for pediatric health advice: a comparative analysis
outcome: Readability of LLM responses to pediatric caregiver questions versus health-literacy targets
effect: None of the models consistently met health-literacy targets (approx. 6th-8th grade); Grok often college level, while DeepSeek and Gemini were simpler and more concise.
quote: None of the models consistently met health-literacy targets for patient materials (approximately 6th-8th grade reading level).

title: Automated RECIST tumor response classification through prompt-guided large language models
outcome: Prompt-strategy sensitivity of RECIST classification
effect: k=2 few-shot micro-F1 0.652 versus zero-shot 0.716; CoT+SC reached 0.811.
quote: Adding just two examples per class (k = 2) led to a decrease in performance (micro-F1 = 0.652), indicating that limited contextual examples may introduce overfitting or noise, especially in a setting with imbalanced class distributions and variable linguistic structure in clinical texts.

title: Consistency in causal reasoning for large language models in scenarios of HIV antiretroviral treatment, drug interactions, and side effects
outcome: Fabricated or inaccessible references/citations in LLM outputs
effect: References to inaccessible online content were produced by the LLMs when provided extra documentation that was inaccessible, testing hallucination.
quote: References to inaccessible online content were produced.

title: Consistency in causal reasoning for large language models in scenarios of HIV antiretroviral treatment, drug interactions, and side effects
outcome: Intra- and inter-model consistency of LLM answers across repeated runs and models
effect: Moderate to high intra-model agreement, decreasing from associational to counterfactual queries; inter-model agreement notably lower.
quote: LLMs exhibited moderate to high intra-model agreement, decreasing from associational to counterfactual queries, whilst inter-model agreement was notably lower.

title: Detecting Citation Veneer in Guideline-Grounded Clinical and Public Health Large Language Model (LLM) Outputs: A Clinical Evidence Audit Grid Using CENHOV Tags
outcome: Supported-error citation veneer (evidential support present but clinically incorrect) by response regime
effect: Synthetic: RUSH 93.3% evidential support, 73.3% correctness, 25.8% veneer. Public check (n=12): RUSH 66.7% veneer (95% CI 39.1%-86.2%); VERIFY and POSTER none.
quote: In the 12-case public check, RUSH produced 66.7% CEAG-V veneer (95% CI 39.1%-86.2%), whereas VERIFY and POSTER produced none; because n=12, these public-case rates are descriptive pilot data only.
sample_unit: synthetic questions per condition (plus a 12-case public check)

title: Extracting Cardiorespiratory Symptoms From Clinical Notes Using Open-Weight Large Language Models: Method Development and Validation Study
outcome: Precision/recall of symptom extraction across four prompt strategies (constraints, overinference)
effect: Instruction-only prompting gave high recall but poor precision; adding structure and constraints improved performance. On test set, Llama 3.3-70B precision 0.63 vs gpt-oss-120B 0.89 for S&S extraction.
quote: Instruction-only prompting demonstrated high recall but poor precision.

title: Adaptive Fast-Slow Large Language Model Framework for Multidimensional Classification of Prenatal Ultrasound Reports: Comparative Study
outcome: Severity classification accuracy before vs after RAG grounding on retrieval and unseen test sets
effect: RAG improved accuracy on retrieval set (V3.2-B 56% to 70%, P=.002; V3.2-R 83% to 99%, P<.001) but not on unseen test set (V3.2-B 57% vs 59%, P=.61; V3.2-R 86% vs 81%, P=.33).
quote: Crucially, the performance gains observed in the retrieval set did not translate to the external test set, revealing a critical limitation in the generalizability of RAG for this specific task.

title: Adaptive Fast-Slow Large Language Model Framework for Multidimensional Classification of Prenatal Ultrasound Reports: Comparative Study
outcome: LLM severity grading errors, missing serious/lethal anomalies
effect: Lethal malformation recall 0.40 with V3.2-R; base model missed all minor anomalies; overall severity accuracy 84.6%.
quote: it achieved perfect precision for “lethal malformation” but with low recall (0.40), while for “major malformation,” it achieved perfect recall at the cost of lower precision (0.53).

title: Adaptive Fast-Slow Large Language Model Framework for Multidimensional Classification of Prenatal Ultrasound Reports: Comparative Study
outcome: candidate model comparison for severity
effect: On test set, V3.2-R 86% vs V3.2-B 57%; minor anomalies V3.2-B F1=0 vs V3.2-R F1=0.83.
quote: On the test set, V3.2-R achieved an accuracy of 86%, significantly outperforming V3.2-B, which achieved only 57%.

title: Adaptive Fast-Slow Large Language Model Framework for Multidimensional Classification of Prenatal Ultrasound Reports: Comparative Study
outcome: seen versus unseen validation performance
effect: RAG retrieval-set gains did not generalize: V3.2-R retrieval 83%→99%, but unseen test 86%→81% after RAG.
quote: These data indicate that while RAG can effectively guide LLMs to memorize or retrieve specific patterns within the knowledge base, it fails to significantly enhance—and may potentially hinder—performance on unseen, heterogeneous clinical data.

title: Ambient AI Scribes to Create Educational Feedback Notes for Medical Students: Randomized Trial
outcome: Factual accuracy of unedited AI feedback summaries: mischaracterization and hallucination rates

quote: Review of 117 AI-generated feedback elements showed a 6.8% (n=8) mischaracterization and 1.7% (n=2) hallucination rate, with most errors corrected during editing.

title: Ambient AI Scribes to Create Educational Feedback Notes for Medical Students: Randomized Trial
outcome: Whether instructor editing of AI-drafted feedback notes corrected AI errors

title: Evaluation of the accuracy, quality, and readability of large language models on local anesthesia and general anesthesia-sedation in dentistry

title: Demographic prompt cues shift clinical recommendations in multimodal large language models: a multi-model audit of 25,380 dental radiograph assessments

title: Demographic prompt cues shift clinical recommendations in multimodal large language models: a multi-model audit of 25,380 dental radiograph assessments

title: Large language models approach clinician performance in ESC cardiovascular risk stratification: a vignette-based benchmark study

title: Beyond Diagnosis: Evaluating Multimodal LLMs for Pathology Localization in Chest Radiographs
outcome: Localization accuracy of MLLMs versus task-specific CNN and radiologist benchmark
effect: GPT-5 49.7%, GPT-4 39.1%, MedGemma 17.7%, all lower than task-specific CNN (59.9%) and radiologist benchmark (80.1%).
quote: Averaged across nine pathologies in the CheXlocalize dataset, GPT-5 exhibited a localization accuracy of 49.7%, followed by GPT-4 (39.1%) and MedGemma (17.7%), all lower than a task-specific CNN baseline (59.9%) and a radiologist benchmark (80.1%).

title: Prospective blinded clinical evaluation of a fully automated workflow for prostate radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Blinded board-certified oncologist ratings of real patient AI-generated plans and structure sets as good/acceptable/unacceptable
effect: Clinically acceptable results in 86% of fully automated cases vs 95% conventional; automated plans rated 'good' less often (12/22 vs 17/22), mainly due to smaller target delineation.
quote: Clinically acceptable results were achieved in 86% of fully automated cases compared with 95% in the conventional workflow.

title: Prospective blinded clinical evaluation of a fully automated workflow for prostate radiotherapy
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Fully automated AI workflow compared with conventional clinical workflow on acceptability and processing time
effect: Acceptability 86% vs 95%; 'good' ratings 12/22 vs 17/22; median time 9 min vs 87 min; automated CTVs smaller (54.2 vs 68.3 cm3, p<0.001).
quote: The fully automated workflow required a median of 9 min (range 8-10) compared with 87 min (range 70-130) for the conventional workflow.

title: Large Language Model Hallucinations in Spine Surgery: A Comparative Analysis of Clinician vs Patient-Level Prompts
outcome: Accuracy of citations in LLM outputs (accurate, misrepresented, fabricated) on spine surgery questions
effect: Gemini average score 0.97 with 26.2% fabrications; ChatGPT fabrication rose from 2.1% to 20.0% on patient questions; Copilot 55.1% score-1 citations and 31.6% non-peer-reviewed websites; OpenEvidence perfect accuracy.
quote: General purpose LLMs exhibit substantial and variable citation errors when queried on spine surgery topics.

title: Large Language Model Hallucinations in Spine Surgery: A Comparative Analysis of Clinician vs Patient-Level Prompts
outcome: Citation accuracy of retrieval-grounded OpenEvidence versus general-purpose LLMs
effect: OpenEvidence, indexing PubMed directly, achieved perfect accuracy; general purpose LLMs had substantial fabrications (e.g., Gemini 26.2%).
quote: OpenEvidence, which directly indexes PubMed and requires user verification as a healthcare professional, achieved perfect accuracy.

title: Large Language Model Hallucinations in Spine Surgery: A Comparative Analysis of Clinician vs Patient-Level Prompts
outcome: LLM citation accuracy for patient-level versus clinician-level prompts
effect: All general purpose LLMs performed worse on patient-level queries; ChatGPT score fell from 1.83 to 1.08 and fabrication rate rose from 2.1% to 20.0%.
quote: All general purpose LLMs performed worse on patient-level queries.

title: Deep learning guided propofol ketamine dosing and inflammation trajectories in elderly burns
outcome: External validation of the forecasting model on independent episodes from a separate database
effect: Model developed on 614 episodes and externally validated on 206 independent episodes; 12-h IL-6 MAE 6.82 pg/mL, spike AUROC 0.814, 90% PI coverage 87.2%.
quote: External validation was performed on 206 independent episodes.

title: Operational Integration and Temporal Validation of a Continuously Deployed ICU Prediction Model
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of deployed ICU model on forward-in-time temporal validation cohort
effect: AUROC 0.856 to 0.960 and AUPRC 0.302 to 0.786 across six tasks; good overall calibration, with lower discrimination and worse calibration for intubation and slight hospital mortality overestimation at high probabilities.
quote: A continuously deployed, EMR-integrated ICU prediction system achieved strong temporal discrimination and generally good calibration.

title: ReclAIm: A Multiagent Framework for Monitoring and Correcting Performance Decline in Medical Imaging AI
outcome: Detection of performance decline in deployed imaging models via automated monitoring
effect: Performance discrepancies between test and inference data were detected in eight of 18 models, prompting fine-tuning workflows that reduced performance gaps.
quote: Performance discrepancies between test and inference data were detected in eight of 18 models, prompting fine-tuning workflows that reduced performance gaps.

title: ReclAIm: A Multiagent Framework for Monitoring and Correcting Performance Decline in Medical Imaging AI
outcome: Performance restoration after fine-tuning models with declined performance
effect: In cases with declines of up to 40.6% (cardiomegaly dataset, InceptionV3), fine-tuning restored performance metrics to within ±2% of baseline values.
quote: In cases with declines of up to 40.6% (cardiomegaly dataset, InceptionV3), fine-tuning restored performance metrics to within ±2% of baseline values.

title: Limits of Artificial Intelligence Models for Skin Cancer Diagnosis in Realistic Settings
outcome: Multiclass skin lesion diagnostic accuracy of AI models versus physician readers by experience level
effect: Experts with >10 years achieved 74.2% accuracy versus 56.7% CNN, 72.2% unimodal, 66.3% multimodal; AI did not beat the most experienced clinicians.
quote: With a mean (SD) accuracy of 74.2% (5.7%), experts with more than 10 years of experience achieved the highest multiclass diagnostic accuracy, outperforming all AI models on this primary end point, which included 56.7% (3.9%) for CNN, 72.2% (3.5%) for the unimodal model, and 66.3% (3.8%) for the multimodal model.
sample_unit: cases (clinical and dermoscopic images with metadata)

title: Uncertainty quantification framework for AI-based survival models: Application to lung cancer prognosis in older adults for informed decision-making
outcome: Uncertainty in individual predictions despite high aggregate AUC across survival models
effect: Mean AUCs 0.840 to 0.851, yet 26% of test-set patients were assigned to conflicting risk groups depending on the model used.
quote: Although the survival models achieved high mean areas under the receiver operating characteristics curve ranging from 0.840 to 0.851, 26% of patients in the test set were assigned to conflicting risk groups depending on the model used, indicating considerable variability in model-predicted prognosis.

title: Quality assessment of radiographs through AI-driven feedback: A randomized comparative study on radiographer response in lateral knee radiographs
outcome: Radiographer accept/reject performance with versus without AI annotations; overreliance on incorrect AI
effect: Sensitivity identical with and without AI (0.64); no significant differences in specificity, PPV, NPV; inter-reader agreement lower with AI (AC 0.233 vs 0.374); false AI feedback reduced sensitivity and specificity in repeated cases.
quote: Radiographers' sensitivity was identical with and without AI support (0.64), with no significant differences in specificity, PPV, or NPV.

title: Quality assessment of radiographs through AI-driven feedback: A randomized comparative study on radiographer response in lateral knee radiographs
outcome: Susceptibility of radiographers to incorrect AI advice (automation bias)
effect: False AI feedback reduced sensitivity and specificity in repeated cases, indicating susceptibility to incorrect AI advice.
quote: False AI feedback reduced sensitivity and specificity in repeated cases, indicating susceptibility to incorrect AI advice.

title: Quality assessment of radiographs through AI-driven feedback: A randomized comparative study on radiographer response in lateral knee radiographs
outcome: Human-AI team performance versus unaided readers in the workflow
effect: AI feedback did not improve overall performance (sensitivity 0.64 in both arms) and lowered inter-reader agreement (AC 0.233 vs 0.374).
quote: AI feedback did not improve overall performance in assessing lateral knee positioning and may reduce consistency, particularly among users without AI experience.

title: Performance of Vision-Enabled Large Language Models in Image-Based Electrocardiogram Interpretation: Exploratory Evaluation
outcome: Generalist VE-LLM diagnostic accuracy on real-world ECG images versus expert consensus
effect: Overall balanced accuracy 50.1% to 61.8% across generalist models; AF sensitivity ≤11.1%; QTc sensitivity 0%-45.5%; ST deviation sensitivity <25%; Cohen κ ≤0.39.
quote: VE-LLMs showed moderate overall performance but mostly low sensitivity and limited agreement with expert ECG interpretation.

title: Performance of Vision-Enabled Large Language Models in Image-Based Electrocardiogram Interpretation: Exploratory Evaluation
outcome: Comparison of generalist versus ECG-specialized LLMs on same ECG images
effect: Specialized models achieved overall balanced accuracy of 56.5% (ECG-Instruct) and 64.4% (PULSE-7B) versus 50.1%-61.8% for generalist models; PULSE-7B better on rhythm and ectopic beats.
quote: Specialized models achieved overall balanced accuracy of 56.5% (ECG-Instruct-Llama-3.2-11B-Vision) and 64.4% (PULSE-7B), with PULSE-7B showing higher task-specific balanced accuracy in rhythm classification and ectopic beats detection (up to 86.3% and 89.2%, respectively).

title: Using large language models to enhance clinically-driven missing data recovery algorithms in electronic health records
outcome: Clinician validation of LLM-generated clinical knowledge (search terms) before use
effect: Clinicians removed 18% of LLM (context) matched codes not clinically relevant; the clinician-approved roadmap recovered 73 (18%) missing values vs 83-89 (20-22%) for unreviewed LLM roadmaps.
quote: Large language models (context + clinicians) recovered more than the experts but less than the LLMs alone (73, 18 % ), suggesting that the enhancements successfully broadened the search terms but not all were clinically relevant.

title: Using large language models to enhance clinically-driven missing data recovery algorithms in electronic health records
outcome: AI versus chart-review recovery
effect: LLM-enhanced roadmaps recommended 83-89 (20%-22%) versus expert chart reviews 49 (12%).
quote: The expert chart reviews recovered 49 (12%), while the algorithms using LLMs-enhanced roadmaps recommended almost twice as many (83-89, 20%-22%).

title: Using large language models to enhance clinically-driven missing data recovery algorithms in electronic health records
outcome: Clinician review of LLM additions
effect: Clinicians endorsed 421 of 514 (82%) LLM-context ICD-10 code matches.
quote: Of the 514 ICD-10 codes matching patients in our sample based on LLMs (context), at least 1 clinician endorsed 421 of them ( 82 % ).

title: Using large language models to enhance clinically-driven missing data recovery algorithms in electronic health records
outcome: Missing EHR inputs for ALI
effect: 4009 ALI components were missing; 789 (20%) were recovered by the algorithm.
quote: Of 4009 missing ALI components, 789 ( 20 % ) were recovered.

title: A Clinical Quality-Assurance Panel for Patient-Facing Black-Box Large Language Models in Healthcare: Anchored Forced-Choice Drift Monitoring for Sensitive Communication
outcome: Agreement of pairwise winners across repeated pairs, wrappers, and prompt-family changes
effect: All 64 repeated pairs gave identical winners; wrapper changes 100% agreement; prompt-family change gave 3 reversals among 36 pairs (91.7% agreement); local model repeat agreement 90.6%.
quote: Within-session repeatability was complete: all 64 repeated unordered pairs yielded identical winners.

title: A Clinical Quality-Assurance Panel for Patient-Facing Black-Box Large Language Models in Healthcare: Anchored Forced-Choice Drift Monitoring for Sensitive Communication
outcome: prompt-family change sensitivity
effect: 3 reversals among 36 hardness pairs; 91.7% agreement.
quote: In contrast, changing prompt families yielded three reversals among 36 hardness pairs (91.7% agreement), indicating that the prompt family functions as the measurement instrument and should be version-controlled in governance workflows [ 17 - 19 ].

title: A Clinical Quality-Assurance Panel for Patient-Facing Black-Box Large Language Models in Healthcare: Anchored Forced-Choice Drift Monitoring for Sensitive Communication
outcome: model version/build traceability
effect: No stable build identifier beyond product label; temperature and seed not controllable.
quote: The interface did not expose a stable build identifier beyond the product label, and temperature and random seed were not user-controllable.

title: ChatGPT response consistency to the 2025 ESC/EACTS guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease: A test-retest study using binary and multiple-choice questions
outcome: Test-retest reproducibility of ChatGPT answers to identical questions 14 days apart
effect: Cohen's kappa showed moderate agreement for binary questions and low agreement for multiple-choice questions. Overall accuracy changed from 88.0% to 93.0% (p>0.05).
quote: Cohen's kappa analysis indicated moderate agreement for binary questions and low agreement for multiple-choice questions.

title: ChatGPT response consistency to the 2025 ESC/EACTS guidelines for the management of valvular heart disease: A test-retest study using binary and multiple-choice questions
outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers against current 2025 ESC/EACTS valvular heart disease guidelines
effect: Binary accuracy was 96.7% at both time points. Multiple-choice accuracy rose from 75.0% to 87.5%. Overall accuracy rose from 88.0% to 93.0%.
quote: However, the relatively high initial error rate in multiple-choice questions represents a limitation for clinical reliability.

title: Artificial intelligence and ChatGPT literacy among surgical healthcare professionals: knowledge, attitudes, and perceived clinical utility
outcome: Proportion of surgical trainees and specialists with formal AI training and AI/ChatGPT literacy
effect: 93.2% of participants lacked formal AI training; 80.9% had prior ChatGPT experience; consultants reported lower familiarity than trainees; lack of training was a reported barrier.
quote: Most participants lacked formal AI training (93.2%), but 80.9% had prior ChatGPT experience.
sample_unit: surgical medical students, residents, and consultants/specialists

title: ChatGPT Versus Custom-Trained Chatbot for Urogynecology Surgery Counseling
outcome: Readability of chatbot surgical counseling text versus health literacy recommendations
effect: FFHA Assistant responses had better readability scores and aligned more closely with health literacy recommendations than ChatGPT-4.0. Both chatbots produced longer responses than IUGA leaflets. No readability numbers reported in abstract.
quote: The FFHA Assistant responses had better readability scores, aligning more closely with health literacy recommendations.
sample_unit: IUGA surgical handout prompts (each response rated by 7 blinded experts)

title: Predicting Treatment Response After Total Neoadjuvant Therapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer
outcome: Brier score in external cohort before and after local recalibration
effect: External validation Brier score 0.30 (95% CI 0.26-0.33), improving to 0.17 with recalibration.
quote: At external validation in a cohort of 83 patients that are being managed with TNT+W/W (median age 57; 37% female), the model predicted pcCR with an AUROC 0.69 (95% CI 0.57-0.82), AUPRC 0.90 (95% CI 0.82-0.96), and Brier score of 0.30 (95% CI 0.26-0.33), improving to 0.17 with recalibration.

title: Predicting Treatment Response After Total Neoadjuvant Therapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer
outcome: Calibration when model applied to a new target population and outcome (pcCR in W/W patients)
effect: Brier score worsened to 0.30 in the new W/W population and AUROC was 0.69; recalibration was needed to reach 0.17.
quote: At external validation in a cohort of 83 patients that are being managed with TNT+W/W (median age 57; 37% female), the model predicted pcCR with an AUROC 0.69 (95% CI 0.57-0.82), AUPRC 0.90 (95% CI 0.82-0.96), and Brier score of 0.30 (95% CI 0.26-0.33), improving to 0.17 with recalibration.

title: Humans vs. large language models in neurology board examination: performance, limitations, and reference reliability
outcome: Reference validity of LLM-cited sources for incorrectly answered neurology questions, rated by neurologists
effect: ChatGPT insufficient citations 39.6%; fabricated references predominated in Gemini (53.0%) and Copilot (42.1%).
quote: Reference evaluation revealed substantial limitations: ChatGPT frequently provided insufficient citations (39.6%), while fabricated references predominated in Gemini (53.0%) and Co-pilot (42.1%).

title: Humans vs. large language models in neurology board examination: performance, limitations, and reference reliability
outcome: LLM exam accuracy versus visual-question performance and reference reliability as competence indicators
effect: Accuracy 85-87% vs examinee 65%, but no advantage on visual items and high rates of fabricated or insufficient references.
quote: On visually based questions, accuracy was lower than for non-visual items, and the performance advantage over examinees disappeared.

title: Readability, quality, and reliability of AI-generated ınformation on myofascial pain syndrome: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on myofascial pain syndrome versus 6th-grade reading level
effect: Responses from all three models were significantly more complex than the recommended 6th-grade level (p < 0.001); ChatGPT was the most readable and Perplexity the least readable but highest in quality and reliability.
quote: The responses generated by all AI models examined were found to be statistically significantly more complex than the suggested 6th-grade reading level (p < 0.001).

title: Performance and safety of a fine-tuned small language model for pediatric emergency triage: A benchmark study
outcome: Strict under-triage of KTAS 1-2 cases predicted as levels 4-5, and over-triage
effect: Fine-tuned model strict under-triage 0.65%; within-one-level agreement 97.13%; fewer extreme errors and lower under-triage than XGBoost in selected high-acuity groups, at the cost of higher over-triage.
quote: However, the fine-tuned model showed fewer extreme errors and lower strict under-triage in selected high-acuity groups, at the cost of higher over-triage.

title: Performance and safety of a fine-tuned small language model for pediatric emergency triage: A benchmark study
outcome: Overall triage performance of fine-tuned LLM versus structured-data XGBoost comparator
effect: LLM accuracy 58.60%, macro-F1 0.417, QWK 0.535 vs XGBoost accuracy 69.40%, macro-F1 0.618, QWK 0.651; LLM had a safer error profile.
quote: The structured-data comparator showed higher overall performance, with an accuracy of 69.40%, a macro-F1 score of 0.618, and a quadratic weighted kappa of 0.651.

title: Performance and safety of a fine-tuned small language model for pediatric emergency triage: A benchmark study
outcome: Lack of external and prospective validation of the model
effect: Single-center retrospective benchmark; authors state external and prospective validation are necessary before clinical implementation.
quote: External and prospective validation will be necessary before clinical implementation.

title: Comparing the Readability and Usability of Patient Education Materials Generated by Different Large Language Models: ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini
outcome: Reading grade level of LLM-generated colorectal patient education materials versus baseline
effect: Gemini grade level 5.9 vs baseline 7.7 (P<0.001); ChatGPT 12.5 and Copilot 8.8 worse than baseline (both P<0.001).
quote: Gemini-generated materials demonstrated improved readability (grade level 5.9; P < 0.001) from baseline (7.7), whereas ChatGPT (12.5) and Copilot (8.8) performed worse (both P < 0.001).

title: Comparing the Readability and Usability of Patient Education Materials Generated by Different Large Language Models: ChatGPT, Copilot, and Gemini
outcome: Reading grade level of LLM-generated patient materials relative to appropriate patient reading level
effect: Gemini 5.9 grade level; ChatGPT 12.5 and Copilot 8.8, worse than baseline 7.7 (P<0.001).
quote: Gemini-generated materials demonstrated improved readability (grade level 5.9; P < 0.001) from baseline (7.7), whereas ChatGPT (12.5) and Copilot (8.8) performed worse (both P < 0.001).

title: Urgent Need for Artificial Intelligence Readiness: Insights From a Multicenter Cross-Sectional Study on Medical Undergraduates and Radiology Trainees in Central and Western China
outcome: Medical undergraduates' exposure to formal AI training and hands-on AI experience
effect: Most medical undergraduates reported limited exposure to formal AI training or hands-on experience; radiology trainees reported higher AI education and tool use. The abstract reports no numbers.
quote: Most medical undergraduates reported limited exposure to formal AI training or hands-on experience yet expressed general support for its clinical use.
sample_unit: respondents (5043 medical undergraduates and 190 radiology trainees)

title: Development, validation, and user-centric evaluation of an interpretable machine learning decision support tool for the preoperative prediction of mild bleeding disorders (MBD-Check): a prospective diagnostic prediction study
outcome: Usability (System Usability Scale) and completion time among surgeons, anaesthesiologists, and haematologists using case vignettes
effect: 86 clinicians assessed the tool; median completion time 72 s (IQR 49·0-79·5); median SUS score 82·5 (IQR 72·5-90·0), indicating excellent usability.
quote: The median SUS score was 82·5 (IQR 72·5-90·0), indicating excellent usability.

title: Towards a clinically integrated artificial intelligence tool for triage of skin cancer
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of professionals with versus without AI assistance for skin lesion triage
effect: Phase 1: sensitivity and specificity improved from 0.64 and 0.90 (without AI) to 0.80 and 0.92 (with AI), matching standalone model performance.
quote: In Phase 1, sensitivity and specificity improved from 0.64 and 0.90 (without AI) to 0.80 and 0.92 (with AI), matching the model's standalone performance.

title: Towards a clinically integrated artificial intelligence tool for triage of skin cancer
outcome: Triage effectiveness and unnecessary referrals with AI assistance among rural community health workers in pilot
effect: Phase 2 (57 community health workers): AI assistance increased triage effectiveness by 17% and reduced unnecessary referrals by 30%; participant feedback positive.
quote: In Phase 2, with 57 community health workers in rural areas, AI assistance increased triage effectiveness by 17% and reduced unnecessary referrals by 30%.

title: Demographic-aware temporal graph attention for fair and accurate cardiac abnormality detection in 12-lead ECG
outcome: Male-female diagnostic performance gap and equalized odds difference after fairness-aware model design
effect: Male-female performance gap reduced from 15.42% to 1.75%; equalized odds difference 0.0423, below the 0.10 acceptance threshold.
quote: The male-female diagnostic performance gap is reduced from 15.42% to 1.75%, with an equalized odds difference (EO) of 0.0423-well within the clinical acceptance threshold of 0.10.

title: Demographic-aware temporal graph attention for fair and accurate cardiac abnormality detection in 12-lead ECG
outcome: Effect of fairness regularization on subgroup disparity and overall accuracy
effect: Gap reduced from 15.42% to 1.75% while macro F1 0.8952 and AUROC 0.9762 surpassed all baselines.
quote: Evaluated on PTB-XL (21,507 recordings), DA-GAT-v2 achieves macro F1 of 0.8952 and AUROC of 0.9762, surpassing all compared baselines.

title: Substance-induced manic psychosis in which delusions were corroborated by a chatbot - case report
outcome: Chatbot response to a user with acute manic psychosis, including risk recognition
effect: In one patient, ChatGPT reportedly affirmed a 'spiritual awakening', minimised the possibility of mania, and discouraged antipsychotic medication. Causal contribution to the presentation could not be determined.
quote: This case demonstrates that, in patients with psychotic symptoms, AI chatbots may reinforce delusional beliefs and impair the development of insight, and may also interfere with engagement with treatment by providing advice that conflicts with clinical recommendations.

title: Substance-induced manic psychosis in which delusions were corroborated by a chatbot - case report
outcome: Whether a general-purpose chatbot gave medical advice beyond appropriate scope
effect: Single case: the chatbot gave medical advice, including discouragement of prescribed antipsychotic medication, conflicting with clinical recommendations.
quote: This case demonstrates that, in patients with psychotic symptoms, AI chatbots may reinforce delusional beliefs and impair the development of insight, and may also interfere with engagement with treatment by providing advice that conflicts with clinical recommendations.

title: Bilateral disease in the classic subtype of papillary thyroid carcinoma: clinical significance and development of an artificial intelligence-based multimodal prediction model
outcome: Radiologist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI model assistance across experience levels
effect: In the external validation group of 120 patients, Model D significantly improved diagnostic accuracy across all radiologist experience levels, with junior radiologists improving most (+20.9%).
quote: In the external validation group of 120 patients, Model D's implementation significantly improved diagnostic accuracy across all radiologist experience levels, with junior radiologists benefiting most substantially (+20.9% improvement).

title: Bilateral disease in the classic subtype of papillary thyroid carcinoma: clinical significance and development of an artificial intelligence-based multimodal prediction model
outcome: Performance drop from training to internal validation to external validation cohort
effect: Model D AUC was 0.970 in training, 0.932 in validation, and 0.848 in the external validation set.
quote: The integrated Model D achieved superior performance with AUC of 0.970 in the training set, 0.932 in the validation set, and 0.848 in the external validation set.

title: Comparative performance of ChatGPT and DeepSeek in interpreting the 2025 ESICM guidelines on sepsis fluid therapy
outcome: Calibrated uncertainty expression in guideline-defined uncertainty domains
effect: Models gave consistently overconfident responses in domains where the guidelines define evidence as uncertain, described as an important safety limitation.
quote: Advanced LLMs show potential for supporting sepsis fluid therapy guideline interpretation, but consistent overconfident responses in guideline-defined uncertainty domains highlight important safety limitations.
sample_unit: guideline-derived clinical questions (each queried in English and Chinese, 3 responses per model)

title: Validation, implementation, and impact of an AI model in routine practice for pathologic diagnosis of prostate cancer in an academic medical center
outcome: Local validation performance against predefined acceptance criteria, with pathologist diagnoses as ground truth
effect: Validation cohort met all predefined acceptance criteria: sensitivity 91-100%, specificity 99%, PPV 98%, NPV 96%, AUC 0.97.
quote: The validation cohort met all predefined acceptance criteria, demonstrating high AI performance (sensitivity 91-100%, specificity 99%, positive-predictive value 98%, negative-predictive value 96%, area under the curve 0.97).

title: AI-Guided Surgical Blood Readiness: Overcoming Real-World Challenges in Prospective Validation for Safer, More Efficient Blood Preparation
outcome: Prospective silent-mode performance versus retrospective test performance, MSBOS, and clinician preordering
effect: Silent prospective validation (n=24,003) maintained AUROC 0.94 and AUPRC 0.55 (test: 0.94, 0.57); sensitivity 0.72 and PPV 0.34, surpassing MSBOS and clinician behavior.
quote: Silent prospective validation (n=24,003, transfusion rate 2.18%, 95% CI, 2.07 to 2.46) maintained a 0.94 (95% CI, 0.92 to 0.95) AUROC and a 0.55 (95% CI, 0.51 to 0.60) AUPRC.

title: AI-Guided Surgical Blood Readiness: Overcoming Real-World Challenges in Prospective Validation for Safer, More Efficient Blood Preparation
outcome: Model performance compared with MSBOS and clinician RBC preordering on same cases
effect: Prospective sensitivity 0.72 and PPV 0.34, surpassing both MSBOS and clinician behavior; hybrid model MAE 12.86 vs 13.34 for MSBOS on daily RBC needs.
quote: Prospectively, the model's sensitivity was 0.72 (95% CI, 0.67 to 0.75) and its positive predictive value was 0.34 (95% CI, 0.31 to 0.37), surpassing both MSBOS and clinician behavior.

title: The efficacy of ChatGPT as a student resource for the diagnosis and treatment of neck pain
outcome: Reading level and understandability versus actionability of chatbot neck pain responses
effect: Both chatbots produced responses around a 12th-grade reading level; the abstract concludes reading level and understandability likely make them learner-friendly, while actionability scores were far lower than understandability scores.
quote: Both chatbots produced responses around a 12th grade reading level.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Language Models for Clinical Decision Support in the Classification of Inborn Errors of Immunity
outcome: IEI class classification AUC with vs without retrieval-augmented grounding (R1+R2)
effect: AUC rose with RAG (R1+R2) across all models, e.g., Deepseek minimal 0.64 to 0.74, Gemini full 0.62 to 0.70; F1 also improved on average.
quote: The results also showed that retrieval strategies improved the average classification performance, increasing the F1 score from [Formula: see text] to [Formula: see text] across all models.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Language Models for Clinical Decision Support in the Classification of Inborn Errors of Immunity
outcome: LLM expression of uncertainty via 'I don't know' responses
effect: Only DeepSeek expressed uncertainty (once in Prompt 1, twice in Prompt 4, same patient record); other models never abstained despite modest accuracy.
quote: However, only Deepseek demonstrated even limited capability in expressing uncertainty.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Language Models for Clinical Decision Support in the Classification of Inborn Errors of Immunity
outcome: Reproducibility of class assignments across repeated runs (Fleiss' kappa)
effect: Average kappa 0.86 (minimal input) and 0.91 (full input); DeepSeek lowest (0.62-0.79), Gemini best (0.98 full).
quote: The models exhibited consistently high agreement across prompts, with the average Fleiss’s kappa values of 0.86 under minimal and 0.91 under full-form input.

title: Assessing and mitigating demographic bias in large language models for diagnostic radiology
outcome: Significant race- or sex-related differences in LLM diagnostic accuracy under counterfactual demographic prompts
effect: Ten significant race-related and four significant sex-related differences in diagnostic accuracy were observed across models and conditions; Black patients most often had significantly lower accuracy (4/10 race comparisons).
quote: Across models and conditions, ten significant race-related and four significant sex-related differences in diagnostic accuracy were observed.

title: Assessing and mitigating demographic bias in large language models for diagnostic radiology
outcome: Effect of prompting strategies on demographic bias and diagnostic accuracy
effect: No significant accuracy differences across prompting strategies (p = 0.78 text-only, 0.95 vision); basic and self-consistency gave ten and four significant race- or sex-related differences, chain-of-thought none.
quote: Text-only and vision models showed no statistically significant differences in diagnostic accuracy across prompting strategies (p = 0.78 and 0.95, respectively); basic and self-consistency prompting produced ten and four significant race- or sex-related differences, respectively, whereas no significant differences were observed with chain-of-thought prompting.

title: Assessing and mitigating demographic bias in large language models for diagnostic radiology
outcome: Subgroup diagnostic accuracy differences by race and sex across LLMs
effect: Black patients had significantly lower accuracy in 4 of 10 significant race-related comparisons; vision models with female patients under basic prompting showed 6/10 significant race-related differences.
quote: Vision models with female patients under basic prompting showed a higher number of significant race-related differences (6/10 [60%]) than vision models with male patients and all text-only models.

title: Assessing and mitigating demographic bias in large language models for diagnostic radiology
outcome: Subgroup diagnostic accuracy differences
effect: Ten race-related and four sex-related significant accuracy differences were observed across models and conditions.
quote: Across models and conditions, ten significant race-related and four significant sex-related differences in diagnostic accuracy were observed.

title: Assessing and mitigating demographic bias in large language models for diagnostic radiology
outcome: demographic bias in diagnostic accuracy
effect: Ten significant race-related and four significant sex-related differences in diagnostic accuracy were observed across models and conditions; Black patients had lower accuracy in 4/10 race-related comparisons (40%) and higher accuracy in 1/10 (10%).
quote: Across models and conditions, ten significant race-related and four significant sex-related differences in diagnostic accuracy were observed.

title: Evaluation of the quality of information provided by ChatGPT on distal biceps repair surgery
outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT answers (FRES, FKGL) about distal biceps repair
effect: FRES was 38.5 and FKGL was at a college reading level; a high reading level was required to comprehend the information.
quote: The FRES was 38.5, and the FKGL was at a college reading level.

title: Evaluation of the quality of information provided by ChatGPT on distal biceps repair surgery
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT patient education answers
effect: FRES 38.5 and college-level FKGL; high reading level required to comprehend ChatGPT information.
quote: A high reading level was required to comprehend the information provided by ChatGPT about distal biceps repair, and the evidence supplied was of fair quality.

title: Evaluation of the quality of information provided by ChatGPT on distal biceps repair surgery
