title: Assessment of OpenEvidence responses to American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
venue: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
outcome: Rate of hallucinated or irrelevant citations in OpenEvidence responses to guideline prompts
effect: 127 PubMed-indexed citations across 15 prompts; zero hallucinated; 2.4% irrelevant.
quote: Across 15 prompts, OE generated 127 PubMed-indexed citations (mean, 8.5 per response; range 6-11) with zero hallucinated and only 2.4% irrelevant citations.

title: Assessment of OpenEvidence responses to American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
venue: Journal of ISAKOS : joint disorders & orthopaedic sports medicine
outcome: Accuracy, evidence-basis and hallucination rate of a retrieval-grounded (RAG) tool's guideline answers
effect: Median scores exceeded 4.0 in all domains, evidence-based 5.0 (5.0-5.0); zero hallucinated citations; no comparator without grounding.
quote: OE produced highly relevant, accurate, clear, complete, and evidence-based responses to AAOS ACLR CPG prompts, with trustworthy PubMed-indexed citations and no hallucinations.

title: Enhancing Patient Understanding of Radiology Reports Through Large Language Model-Generated Summaries, Clickable Terms, and Artificial Intelligence Videos
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Extent of clinician edits required to LLM-generated radiology report summaries before release
effect: Summaries required manual clinician edits: average 24.75 words removed, 0.13 words added per summary; lexical similarity 84.63%, semantic similarity 98.25%.
quote: However, LLM-summaries required manual clinician edits (average per summary: 24.75 words removed; 0.13 words added, lexical similarity = 84.63%; semantic similarity = 98.25%).

title: Prompt-Induced Diagnostic Bias in Large Language Model Classification of Echocardiography Reports
outcome: LVEF classification shifts under biased prompts
effect: Bias prompts significantly altered LVEF classifications across all 3 classes, directionally consistent with the referenced category.
quote: Bias prompts significantly altered LVEF classifications across all 3 classes, with shifts directionally consistent with the referenced category.

title: Improving structural heart disease screening: AI-ECG and novice AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound
outcome: Two-step AI-ECG-gated FoCUS versus FoCUS for all: utilization and accuracy
effect: Two-step strategy kept PPV/NPV 96.1%/95.6% and limited FoCUS imaging to 47%, but lowered sensitivity versus AI-FoCUS for all (PPV 95.4%, NPV 98.0%).
quote: A two-step AI-ECG then AI-FoCUS strategy reduced FoCUS utilization, but lowered sensitivity compared with AI-FoCUS for all.

title: Improving structural heart disease screening: AI-ECG and novice AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound
outcome: Standalone AI-ECG screening accuracy for structural heart disease
effect: AI-ECG alone had NPV 95.8% but PPV 29.6%, limiting standalone screening; FoCUS-based strategies were superior.
quote: AI-ECG alone yielded NPV 95.8% but PPV 29.6%, limiting standalone screening.

title: Improving structural heart disease screening: AI-ECG and novice AI-guided focused cardiac ultrasound
outcome: Positive and negative predictive values of sequential AI-ECG and AI-FoCUS screening
effect: AI-ECG alone: PPV 29.6%, NPV 95.8%; positive AI-ECG followed by AI-FoCUS: PPV/NPV 96.1%/95.6%, with FoCUS imaging limited to 47%.
quote: A two-step strategy (positive AI-ECG followed by AI-FoCUS) maintained high PPV/NPV (96.1%/95.6%) but limited FoCUS imaging to 47%.

title: An expert-led benchmark using common patient questions: evaluating large language models for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis education
venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
outcome: Clarity and understandability of LLM responses to AIS patient questions, rated by experts
effect: Only one-third of responses were rated sufficiently understandable, despite 91% factual accuracy for both models.
quote: However, clarity was limited, with only one-third of responses rated as sufficiently understandable.

title: Development and external validation of a machine learning model for predicting post-CABG acute kidney injury: insights from MIMIC database and real-world cardiac surgery cohort
outcome: Performance drop when comparing development population to external cohort, attributed to population heterogeneity
effect: Performance decay attributed to significant population heterogeneity (e.g. BMI differences) and specific cardiac surgery pathophysiology not captured by general ICU variables.
quote: The performance decay was attributed to significant population heterogeneity (e.g. BMI differences) and the specific pathophysiological milieu of cardiac surgery not fully captured by general ICU variables.
sample_unit: patients (external validation cohort; 6,347 in MIMIC development cohort)

title: Development and external validation of a machine learning model for predicting post-CABG acute kidney injury: insights from MIMIC database and real-world cardiac surgery cohort
outcome: Model discrimination on external local cohort versus internal test set
effect: PR-AUC fell from 0.888 (MIMIC internal) to 0.309 in the external AHXY cohort; AUC fell from 0.709 to 0.548, near-random.
quote: However, upon deployment in the external AHXY cohort, the model exhibited significant performance attenuation, with the PR-AUC dropping to 0.309 and the AUC decreasing to 0.548.
sample_unit: patients (external validation cohort; 6,347 in MIMIC development cohort)

title: Development and external validation of a machine learning model for predicting post-CABG acute kidney injury: insights from MIMIC database and real-world cardiac surgery cohort
outcome: Model unsuited to local population without adaptation
effect: Near-random predictive performance externally (AUC 0.548), indicating lack of generalizability without further adaptation; recalibration or transfer learning recommended.
quote: This near-random predictive performance indicates a lack of direct real-world generalizability without further adaptation.
sample_unit: patients (external validation cohort; 6,347 in MIMIC development cohort)

title: Development and external validation of a machine learning model for predicting post-CABG acute kidney injury: insights from MIMIC database and real-world cardiac surgery cohort
outcome: Generalization of ICU-trained model to a specialized cardiac surgery population
effect: General ICU model showed substantial cross-domain transferability gap; AUC 0.548 and PR-AUC 0.309 in cardiac surgery cohort.
quote: General-purpose ICU models may face a substantial cross-domain transferability gap without local adaptation when applied to specialized sub-specialties like cardiac surgery across different demographic populations.
sample_unit: patients (external validation cohort; 6,347 in MIMIC development cohort)

title: Wave-aware mortality prediction in COVID-19: a multi-stage feature selection and explainable machine-learning framework
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Cross-wave model performance degradation from temporal drift in COVID-19 mortality prediction
effect: Cross-wave AUC declined moderately (RF: 0.87 within-wave to 0.80 early→Wave-5), while F1 collapsed due to miscalibration (RF F1: 0.68 → 0.13 → 0.07).
quote: However, early-wave models showed marked degradation when applied to later waves: cross-wave AUC declined moderately (e.g., RF: 0.87 within-wave → 0.80 early→Wave-5), whereas F1 collapsed due to pronounced miscalibration (e.g., RF F1: 0.68 → 0.13 → 0.07).

title: Wave-aware mortality prediction in COVID-19: a multi-stage feature selection and explainable machine-learning framework
venue: BMC medical informatics and decision making
outcome: Variation of optimal decision threshold across models and waves under temporal drift
effect: The F1-optimal probability threshold varied widely across models and waves, showing threshold-dependent performance is affected by temporal drift.
quote: Threshold-sweep analyses suggested that the F1-optimal probability threshold varied widely across models and waves, underscoring the impact of temporal drift on threshold-dependent performance.

title: Deficiencies in clinical reasoning of LLMs in low back pain management and remediation via prompt engineering: from performance evaluation to error diagnosis
outcome: Output stability (score variance) across three repeated generations for each model
effect: GPT-4o had lowest variance; Deepseek-V2.5 highest and most unstable. GPT-4o variance significantly lower than others in accuracy, completeness, safety, practicality (corrected p<0.005).
quote: Among all five models, GPT-4o exhibited the lowest overall variance, indicating the most consistent output. Deepseek-V2.5 exhibited the highest variance, reflecting the most unstable performance.
sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (plus 103 multiple-choice questions; 7 questions in prompt phase)

title: Deficiencies in clinical reasoning of LLMs in low back pain management and remediation via prompt engineering: from performance evaluation to error diagnosis
outcome: Gap between exam-style MCQ accuracy and clinical scenario response quality/safety
effect: All models exceeded 90% MCQ accuracy, but clinical scenarios yielded low-scoring responses (Deepseek-V2.5 n=51) with hallucinations and omitted safety warnings.
quote: These discrepancies highlight a critical gap between knowledge possession and clinically reliable knowledge application, with direct implications for safe deployment.
sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (plus 103 multiple-choice questions; 7 questions in prompt phase)

title: Deficiencies in clinical reasoning of LLMs in low back pain management and remediation via prompt engineering: from performance evaluation to error diagnosis
outcome: Reading difficulty and jargon in LLM outputs
effect: Excessive jargon was a near-universal error (e.g., GPT-5 23%, GPT-4o 20%); Deepseek-V2.5 highest reading difficulty score (16.871); outputs at secondary-school level.
quote: A near-universal pattern was the overuse of technical terminology, likely reflecting training biases toward guideline texts and specialist corpora during training.
sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (plus 103 multiple-choice questions; 7 questions in prompt phase)

title: Deficiencies in clinical reasoning of LLMs in low back pain management and remediation via prompt engineering: from performance evaluation to error diagnosis
outcome: Safety-oriented prompt correction
effect: Deepseek-V2.5 improved all five dimensions (p<0.001), largest in Safety B=0.91 (3.33 to 4.24) and Completeness B=0.86 (2.91 to 3.76).
quote: Linear mixed model estimates of marginal means ( Figure 5 and Table 4 ) showed that the corrected prompt significantly improved Deepseek-V2.5 across all five dimensions ( p < 0.001), with the largest gains in Safety ( B = 0.91, from 3.33 to 4.24) and Completeness ( B = 0.86, from 2.91 to 3.76).
sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (plus 103 multiple-choice questions; 7 questions in prompt phase)

title: Deficiencies in clinical reasoning of LLMs in low back pain management and remediation via prompt engineering: from performance evaluation to error diagnosis
outcome: Clinical knowledge errors, omissions, and missing safety warnings in guideline-based LBP responses
effect: Deepseek-V2.5 low-scoring responses: lack of safety warnings 16% (8/51), factual errors/hallucinations 12% (6/51); GPT-o3 harmful recommendations 7% (1/14).
quote: The most prominent causes of errors included: lack of safety warnings (Category 14: 16%, 8/51), factual errors/hallucinations (Category 1: 12%, 6/51), and incomplete or excessive content (Category 6: 10%, 5/51).
sample_unit: clinical scenario questions (plus 103 multiple-choice questions; 7 questions in prompt phase)

title: Analytical validation of Smilo.ai: evaluating an AI-driven platform for automated oral health screening and global diagnostic accessibility
outcome: AI oral condition detection versus dentist reference on local participant photographs; agreement and accuracy
effect: Overall sensitivity 73.6%, precision 46.0%, accuracy 47.3%, macro Cohen's kappa 0.010; near-zero specificity for decay, tooth wear, discoloration; optimization needed before screening workflow integration.
quote: Smilo.ai demonstrated an overall sensitivity of 73.6%, precision of 46.0%, accuracy of 47.3%, and a macro-level Cohen's κ of 0.010 relative to dentist assessments.

title: External validation of machine learning models for estimation of mortality 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after hip fracture on 5,055 consecutive patients
outcome: Calibration of XGB predicted mortality risk before vs after local recalibration with isotonic regression
effect: Average predicted 12-month risk 0.38 vs observed 0.27 before recalibration; 0.24 after. Predicted risks after recalibration were 0.07, 0.12, 0.17, 0.24 vs observed 0.08, 0.15, 0.20, 0.27. AUC unchanged.
quote: The calibration at large and the flexible calibration curves were initially slightly off but were greatly improved by recalibration with bootstrapped isotonic regression.

title: External validation of machine learning models for estimation of mortality 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after hip fracture on 5,055 consecutive patients
outcome: Differences between development and external validation cohort characteristics and mortality
effect: Mortality lower in validation cohort (27% vs 32% at 1 year); differences in sex, ASA, cardiac medication, and admission source; models overestimated mortality.
quote: Mortality across all timepoints was lower in the external validation cohort compared with the original development cohort (27% vs 32% at 1 year).

title: External validation of machine learning models for estimation of mortality 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after hip fracture on 5,055 consecutive patients
outcome: Whether AUC alone concealed poor calibration in mortality models
effect: Uncalibrated models had acceptable AUC but overestimated risk; calibration slope and intercept revealed miscalibration (e.g., 1-month XGB intercept -0.80), improved after recalibration.
quote: This is also evident by comparing the results and calibration curves in the present study before and after recalibration.

title: External validation of machine learning models for estimation of mortality 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after hip fracture on 5,055 consecutive patients
outcome: Generalization of a predictive model to a new independent cohort
effect: XGB discrimination held (AUC 0.72, 0.74, 0.75, 0.77) but risks were overestimated (12-month predicted 0.38 vs observed 0.27), requiring recalibration.
quote: Given the diversity in populations, treatment protocols, mortality rates, and outcome reporting across studies, it is unlikely that a single model will be applicable to all hip fracture populations without recalibration or updating during external validation before clinical use.

title: External validation of machine learning models for estimation of mortality 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after hip fracture on 5,055 consecutive patients
outcome: external validation discrimination
effect: XGB AUCs were 0.72, 0.74, 0.75, and 0.77 for 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month mortality.
quote: The XGB model had AUC values of 0.72 (CI 0.70–0.74), 0.74 (CI 0.72–0.76), 0.75 (CI 0.73–0.76), and 0.77 (CI 0.75–0.78) for 1-, 3-, 6-, and 12-month mortality respectively, while the RF model had slightly lower scores except for the 1-month model that had an AUC of 0.74.

title: External validation of machine learning models for estimation of mortality 1, 3, 6, and 12 months after hip fracture on 5,055 consecutive patients
outcome: model comparison performance
effect: XGB was best overall; RF was slightly lower except 1-month AUC 0.74 versus XGB 0.72.
quote: In accordance with the results from the original development of the models, the best performance overall was from the XGB model, with the exception of the AUC for 1-month mortality.

title: Evaluating the quality of artificial intelligence responses to psoriasis-related clinical and patient questions: a comparative study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy, evidence consistency, completeness and safety of chatbot psoriasis responses (max 8)
effect: Mean scores 7.36±0.97 (ChatGPT), 7.77±0.77 (Gemini), 7.05±1.09 (Copilot); differed significantly (Friedman P<0.001); all models showed high clinical safety but incomplete responses.
quote: The observation that models may provide accurate yet clinically incomplete responses, particularly for treatment content, emphasizes the need for physician oversight when AI-generated information is used in dermatological practice.

title: Comparative evaluation of generative AI models for chest radiograph report generation in the emergency department
outcome: VLM-generated CXR report quality versus radiologist-written reports on same cases
effect: AIRead had lower RADPEER 3b rate (5.3% vs 13.9%) and higher acceptability (84.5% vs 74.3%) than radiologists; other VLMs showed higher disagreement (16.8-43.0%) and lower acceptability (41.1-71.4%).
quote: Other VLMs showed higher disagreement (16.8-43.0%; p < 0.05), lower acceptability (41.1-71.4%; p < 0.05), and more frequent hallucinations (5.4-17.4%; p < 0.05).

title: Comparative evaluation of generative AI models for chest radiograph report generation in the emergency department
outcome: Hallucination rates in AI-generated chest radiograph reports
effect: AIRead hallucination 0.3% (4/1425) vs radiologists 0.1% (1/1425), p=0.21; other VLMs had hallucination rates of 5.4-17.4%.
quote: Other VLMs showed higher disagreement (16.8-43.0%; p < 0.05), lower acceptability (41.1-71.4%; p < 0.05), and more frequent hallucinations (5.4-17.4%; p < 0.05).

title: Pre-implementation safety evaluation of an AI decision-support system for surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis
outcome: Guideline concordance and clinically significant prescribing risk of LLM surgical prophylaxis recommendations
effect: Clinically significant risk in 10% (2/20) of scenarios, including omitted anaerobic coverage and failure to redose in prolonged procedures; overall concordance 4/5, perfect dose accuracy, timing 70%.
quote: Clinically significant antimicrobial prescribing risk was identified in 10% of simulated scenarios (2/20), recognising wide confidence intervals due to the small sample size.

title: Pre-implementation safety evaluation of an AI decision-support system for surgical antimicrobial prophylaxis
outcome: Accuracy of guideline citations in LLM outputs
effect: Guideline citation accuracy was 45%, the lowest-scoring domain.
quote: Overall guideline concordance was 4/5, with perfect dose accuracy but lower performance for timing (70%) and guideline citation (45%).

title: Large-Scale Evaluation of Five Large Language Models in Anesthesia Decision-Making for Hip Fracture Surgery
outcome: Change in LLM anesthesia recommendations across patient sociodemographic variables (e.g., sex) in vignettes
effect: Limited sociodemographic bias: only one significant and clinically meaningful effect across 150 comparisons.
quote: We identified limited sociodemographic biases, with only one significant and clinically meaningful effect across 150 comparisons.
sample_unit: LLM responses to standardized hip fracture surgery vignettes

title: Large-Scale Evaluation of Five Large Language Models in Anesthesia Decision-Making for Hip Fracture Surgery
outcome: Consistency of LLM justifications and recommendations with current clinical evidence for anesthesia choice
effect: Free-text justifications frequently cited neuraxial benefits unsupported by recent randomized trials; most models issued strong neuraxial recommendations without clinical justification.
quote: However, free-text justifications frequently cited neuraxial benefits unsupported by recent randomized trials, and most models issued strong neuraxial recommendations despite a lack of clinical justification.
sample_unit: LLM responses to standardized hip fracture surgery vignettes

title: Large Language Model-Based Simplification of Digital Therapeutics Explanations for Insomnia and Nicotine Dependence: Two Randomized Online Experiments
outcome: Perceived understanding and ease, clarity, comprehensibility ratings of LLM-simplified vs original DTx materials
effect: Group×time interaction on perceived understanding: insomnia F=24.8, nicotine F=14.1 (both P<.001), greater gains with LLM-simplified text; ease/clarity/comprehensibility rated higher (r=0.11-0.24). Self-reported outcomes only.
quote: A significant group×time interaction was observed in both experiments.

title: Large Language Model-Based Simplification of Digital Therapeutics Explanations for Insomnia and Nicotine Dependence: Two Randomized Online Experiments
outcome: Effect of simplifying patient materials to a 10-11-year-old reading level on perceived understanding and ratings
effect: LLM-simplified materials targeted at a 10- to 11-year-old reading level yielded greater perceived understanding gains (P<.001) and higher ease, clarity, comprehensibility ratings (all P<.05, r=0.11-0.24) than originals.
quote: In the insomnia experiment, the LLM-simplified explanations were rated significantly higher for ease ( U =27,281; P =.008; r =0.127), clarity ( U =27,803; P =.02; r =0.110), and comprehensibility ( U =25,125; P <.001; r =0.196).

title: Influence of Artificial Intelligence Assistance on Gleason Grading and Prostate Cancer Detection by Uropathologists in Daily Practice: A Prospective Multicenter Study
outcome: AI-assisted versus unassisted grade-group assessments and tumor detection agreement
effect: GG assessments differed in 16.5% (30/182); 36.7% (11/30) of discrepancies shifted between GG1 and GG2. Tumor detection agreement was 98.6% (279/283), with differences limited to GG1 tumors.
quote: GG assessments differed in 16.5% (30/182) of entries when comparing AI-assisted with unassisted evaluations.

title: Artificial intelligence in health systems of the WHO European region: implementation, applications, opportunities, and barriers
outcome: Member States offering AI training to the health workforce (in-service and pre-service)
effect: Only 24% (12/50) of Member States offered in-service AI training for the health workforce, and 20% (10/50) offered pre-service training.
quote: Finally, with regard to health workforce education and AI literacy, the study highlights a significant gap in preparedness, where only 24% of Member States (12/50) reported offering in-service AI training for the health workforce, and 20% (10/50) offered pre-service training.
country: WHO European Region (50 of 53 Member States)

title: Artificial intelligence in health systems of the WHO European region: implementation, applications, opportunities, and barriers
outcome: Stakeholder groups engaged by Member States on AI, including patients and the public
effect: Of 36 Member States reporting engagement, patient associations were engaged by 42% (15/36) and the general public by 22% (8/36). Government actors (81%), providers (75%), and developers (75%) were engaged more often.
quote: Of the 36 Member States reporting at least one form of engagement, the stakeholders most frequently engaged were government actors (81%; 29/36), healthcare providers (75%; 27/36), and AI developers (75%; 27/36), whereas patient associations (42%; 15/36) and the general public (22%; 8/36) were less commonly involved.
country: WHO European Region (50 of 53 Member States)

title: Large language models and retrieval-augmented platforms for dental implant complications: A blinded, expert-rated benchmarking study
outcome: Expert-rated safety and hallucination-free rates for retrieval-augmented versus general-purpose LLMs
effect: OpenEvidence (medical RAG) had 100% safe and 100% hallucination-free responses; general-purpose safe rates 56.7%-86.7% and hallucination-free rates 36.7%-93.3% (Cochran's Q p<0.01).
quote: Across 330 responses (1320 ratings), OpenEvidence achieved 100% safe and 100% hallucination-free responses.

title: Large language models and retrieval-augmented platforms for dental implant complications: A blinded, expert-rated benchmarking study
outcome: Hallucinations in general-purpose LLM outputs on dental implant complications rated by blinded experts
effect: Hallucination-free rates among general-purpose platforms ranged from 36.7% (Claude 4.5 Haiku) to 93.3% (GPT-5.4 Thinking; Qwen 3.5-Plus), a significant difference.
quote: Among general-purpose platforms, safe rates ranged from 56.7% (Claude 4.5 Haiku) to 86.7% (Perplexity) and hallucination-free rates from 36.7% (Claude 4.5 Haiku) to 93.3% (GPT-5.4 Thinking; Qwen 3.5-Plus), both significant (Cochran's Q, p < 0.01).

title: Evaluating reasoning in multimodal large language models for ophthalmology: a bilingual benchmark study using clinical vignettes and imaging
outcome: Multimodal LLM accuracy and reasoning on ophthalmology vignette-plus-image benchmark questions
effect: Reasoning-enabled scores rose (e.g., ChatGPT-5 English 20.77 to 23.97; CLM-V Chinese 9.03 to 10.27), but limitations in subspecialty robustness and image interpretation remained; benefit was model- and dataset-dependent.
quote: However, limitations in subspecialty robustness and image interpretation necessitate rigorous reasoning evaluation for safe educational and clinical applications.

title: Evaluating large language models on multilingual vaccine knowledge: a benchmark study
outcome: LLM accuracy on vaccine questions by language
effect: Mean accuracy across models was 86.0% in English, 83.7% in Spanish, and 80.0% in Chinese; performance also varied by vaccine type and question category.
quote: Mean accuracy across models was 86.0% in English, 83.7% in Spanish, and 80.0% in Chinese.

title: Natural language processing models for patient-centered summaries of prostatectomy pathology reports
outcome: Accuracy on external test set of differently formatted pathology reports from a separate institution
effect: LLM maintained high accuracy without additional training; rules-based NLP achieved similarly high accuracy only after minimal refinement.
quote: In an external test set of differently formatted RP pathology reports from a separate institution, the LLM maintained high accuracy without additional training, while the rules-based NLP model achieved similarly high accuracy after minimal refinement.

title: AI-assisted improvement of endoscopic diagnosis of ampullary lesions
outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic accuracy with versus without AI assistance for ampullary lesions
effect: With AI assistance, accuracy improved for fellows (63.5%-75.8%, P<0.001) and GI endoscopists (68.4%-76.5%, P=0.012); no significant difference for pancreatobiliary endoscopists (70.8%-73.1%, P=1.000).
quote: With AI assistance, mean diagnostic accuracies significantly improved for endoscopy fellows (63.5%-75.8%, P < 0.001) and gastrointestinal endoscopists (68.4%-76.5%, P = 0.012), while no significant difference was observed for pancreatobiliary endoscopists (70.8%-73.1%, P = 1.000).

title: Head-to-head evaluation of ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Perplexity on acid-base disorder case clinical management and drug treatment: Accuracy, domain performance, and response consistency assessment
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across two independent phases
effect: Identical answers across phases in 81.7% (ChatGPT), 81.1% (DeepSeek), 76.1% (Perplexity) of items; reproducibly correct only 52.1%, 48.8%, 43.2%.
quote: Identical answers across phases occurred in 81.7% of items for ChatGPT, 81.1% for DeepSeek, and 76.1% for Perplexity, but reproducibly correct answers were 52.1%, 48.8%, and 43.2%.

title: Head-to-head evaluation of ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Perplexity on acid-base disorder case clinical management and drug treatment: Accuracy, domain performance, and response consistency assessment
outcome: LLM accuracy on acid-base management and drug treatment MCQs
effect: Overall accuracy was 59.8% (305/510) ChatGPT, 58.8% (300/510) DeepSeek, 53.7% (274/510) Perplexity; only moderate performance.
quote: Overall accuracy was 59.8% (305/510) for ChatGPT, 58.8% (300/510) for DeepSeek, and 53.7% (274/510) for Perplexity (Cochran's Q p = 0.16); ChatGPT and DeepSeek each outperformed Perplexity (p = 0.0086 and p = 0.0374).

title: Head-to-head evaluation of ChatGPT, DeepSeek, and Perplexity on acid-base disorder case clinical management and drug treatment: Accuracy, domain performance, and response consistency assessment
outcome: LLM clinical knowledge accuracy on acid-base management and drug treatment questions
effect: Accuracy was lowest for metabolic acidosis subtypes (52.5%, 42.4%, 32.2%) and highest for compensation (70.7%, 70.7%, 62.1%); overall about 54-60%.
quote: Accuracy was highest for compensation/expected response (116 items; 70.7% for ChatGPT and DeepSeek, 62.1% for Perplexity) and lowest for metabolic acidosis subtypes (59 items; 52.5%, 42.4%, 32.2%).

title: Assessing the understandability, actionability, reliability, and readability of ChatGPT-4o in providing patient education on urinary incontinence
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4o urinary incontinence patient education responses (Çetinkaya-Uzun formula, Turkish)

title: Safety of a large language model-based clinical decision support system in African primary healthcare

effect: Actively harmful recommendations in 115 encounters (7.8%, 95% CI 6.5-9.3), with 67 appearing in the final documentation; clinicians did not modify documentation in 917 encounters (62%).
quote: Safety assessments identified actively harmful recommendations from the large language model in 115 encounters (7.8%, 95% CI 6.5-9.3), with 67 such recommendations appearing in the final documentation.

title: Clinical Implications of ChatGPT-assisted Multimodal Pre-operative Assessment in Elderly Pertrochanteric Fracture Patients: An Exploratory Study
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM mortality risk estimates across two repeated runs (Bland-Altman bias)

quote: Agreement analysis showed a mean difference (bias) of 1.28% (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.09-2.47) for GPT-4o and 0.18% (95% CI, -0.41-0.76) for GPT-5.

title: Clinical Evidence and FDA Recalls of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices
outcome: Hazard of FDA recall by availability of published clinical studies at authorization
effect: Devices with missing clinical study information had higher recall hazard than devices with published clinical studies (HR, 1.39; 95% CrI, 0.84-3.52); the credible interval includes 1.
quote: Devices with missing information regarding clinical studies had a higher hazard of recall than devices with published clinical studies (HR, 1.39; 95% CrI, 0.84-3.52).

title: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation Study of Mental Health Crisis Handling by Large Language Models
outcome: Appropriateness of LLM responses to suicidal ideation, self-harm, and violence crisis inputs (5-point Likert)
effect: Some models (gpt-5-nano, deepseek-v3.2-exp) had very low harmful response rates; others (gpt-4o-mini, Llama-4-Scout, grok-4-fast) had markedly higher unsafe output rates, especially in self-harm and suicidal ideation categories.
quote: A nonnegligible proportion of responses was rated as inappropriate or harmful, particularly in the self-harm and suicidal ideation categories.

title: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation Study of Mental Health Crisis Handling by Large Language Models
outcome: Recognition of indirect or ambiguous crisis signals by LLMs
effect: All models showed systemic weaknesses including poor handling of indirect or ambiguous risk signals, formulaic responses, and frequent misalignment with user context.

title: Augmenting large language models with clinical knowledge graph for personalized perioperative fluid therapy question answering
outcome: Accuracy of LLM answers with vs without retrieval grounding (GraphRAG/DocRAG vs Vanilla) on fluid therapy questions
effect: GraphRAG accuracy 96.89% MCQ / 66.44% open-ended vs Vanilla 69.44%/27.56%; case-based 71.12% GraphRAG, 62.47% DocRAG vs 52.67% Vanilla.
quote: On the retrospective case-based question set, GraphRAG also showed the strongest overall performance, with an average accuracy of 71.12%, compared with 62.47% for DocRAG, 54.20% for CoT, 52.67% for Vanilla, and 52.54% for RoT.

title: Augmenting large language models with clinical knowledge graph for personalized perioperative fluid therapy question answering
outcome: Rate of explicit uncertainty acknowledgment ('Don't Know') with option added and with RAG
effect: Adding a 'Don't Know' option raised abstention from 2.68% to 20.01%; GraphRAG raised 'Don't Know' rate from 17.86% to 35.00%.
quote: As shown in Fig 4 , adding a “Don’t Know” option substantially increased the proportion of honest abstention responses from 2.68% to 20.01%, suggesting that explicit uncertainty choices reduced the tendency to guess when the model was unsure.

title: Augmenting large language models with clinical knowledge graph for personalized perioperative fluid therapy question answering
outcome: Representativeness and independence of test data from retrieval knowledge base
effect: Knowledge-based questions and retrieval used the same PFTKG knowledge space, limiting external generalization; case-based set from a single hospital.
quote: In the knowledge-based evaluation setting, question construction and retrieval were both based on the same PFTKG knowledge space.

title: Augmenting large language models with clinical knowledge graph for personalized perioperative fluid therapy question answering
outcome: LLM strategies compared against each other and an exploratory nurse baseline
effect: Nurse achieved 93% MCQ and 90% open-ended; GraphRAG comparable on MCQ (96.89%) but nurse exceeded all LLM configurations on open-ended (best 66.44%).
quote: Her multiple-choice performance was comparable to the best-performing LLM strategy, whereas her open-ended performance exceeded all tested LLM configurations.

title: Augmenting large language models with clinical knowledge graph for personalized perioperative fluid therapy question answering
outcome: incorrect clinical answers
effect: Average accuracy was 75.16% for multiple-choice and 35.71% for open-ended questions.
quote: Across all LLMs and prompting strategies, accuracy was markedly higher for multiple-choice questions than for open-ended questions (average 75.16% vs. 35.71% ).

title: Patient Cognitive Bias in Large Language Model-Supported Health Consultations: Simulation-Based Comparative Study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy under biased patient framing versus standard multiturn consultations
effect: Biased consultations reduced accuracy by about 7 to 39 pp across 6 LLMs; ChatGPT-3.5-Turbo fell from 64.0% to 25.0%; bias-influenced error proportion exceeded one-third in all models.
quote: ChatGPT-3.5-Turbo declined from 64.0% (SD 0.6%) accuracy in standard consultations to 25.0% (SD 0.9%) under bias (−39.0 pp), and Gemini 1.5 Flash-8B declined from 61.3% (SD 0.7%) to 35.5% (SD 0.6%; −25.8 pp), with both models approaching the 25% random-guess baseline.

title: Transformer imputation in CTG: a length-dependent evaluation of reconstruction methods
outcome: Imputation accuracy (RMSE, correlation) as artificially removed FHR gap length increased
effect: Performance systematically degraded for all methods as gap lengths increased; reliability declined beyond 30 s; spline had significantly worse RMSE than the other methods.
quote: However, performance systematically degraded for all methods as gap lengths increased.

title: Disparities in engagement with an artificial intelligence-based chat intervention post-appendectomy
outcome: Engagement with AI chat by insurance, socioeconomic vulnerability, age, race
effect: Decreasing engagement associated with older patient age (OR 0.96 [0.93-0.99]), higher SVI socioeconomic score (0.28 [0.16-0.49]), and Medicaid insurance (0.68 [0.52-0.88]); higher SVI housing & transportation score increased engagement (2.08 [1.26-3.43]).
quote: Lower chat engagement was observed among non-White patients and those with lower socioeconomic status.

title: AIDx: a locally deployable AI system for physician clinical decision support
outcome: Benchmark accuracy with vs without retrieval-augmented generation grounding in open medical references
effect: RAG gave a modest additional accuracy gain of +0.4 points on average, varying by dataset. EHR fine-tuning gave +17.8 points over the base model.
quote: EHR-based fine-tuning accounts for the majority of the performance gain (+17.8 percentage points over the base model on average), while RAG provides a modest additional benefit (+0.4 points on average) that varies by dataset.

title: Physician adoption patterns of AI-driven clinical decision support systems in urinary tract infection management
outcome: Physician non-adherence to AI recommendations and physician characteristics associated with following them
effect: ~33% of physicians did not follow UTIS recommendations; older physicians (OR 1.034/yr), Arabic sector (OR 3.474), and higher patient volume (OR 1.027 per 100) were less likely to follow.
quote: UTIS reduced antibiotic mismatch-defined as pathogen resistance to prescribed empiric antibiotic based on culture-by ~ 30%, yet ~ 33% of physicians did not follow its recommendations.

title: Performance of a large language model in the informed consent process for participation in a clinical trial
outcome: Readability grade level of LLM consent answers

title: Performance of a large language model in the informed consent process for participation in a clinical trial
outcome: Semantic consistency of consent LLM answers across repeated runs

quote: Readability was appropriate (human: grade 7.5, 7.0-8.0; LLM: grade 6.4, 6.0-6.9) and there was near identical semantic consistency (human: 0.91, 0.89-0.92; LLM: 0.91, 0.89-0.92).

title: Performance of a large language model in the informed consent process for participation in a clinical trial
outcome: Inter-rater reliability of accuracy ratings for human raters versus moderator LLM

title: Revenue-sensitive evaluation of AI-assisted ICD-10-CM coding and human-AI collaboration under dual DRG payment systems
outcome: CRS reduction from human review queue prioritized by revenue risk versus random or confidence-based prioritization
effect: At 20% review rate, revenue-targeted prioritization achieved 43.2% CRS reduction vs 20.0% random and 19.7% confidence-based; 91% of oracle bound (47.4%). Simulation assumed perfect correction.
quote: At the practically relevant 20% review rate: S3 achieved F1-micro of 0.7423 with 43.2% CRS reduction; S3-TW (Tw-DRG targeting) achieved similar F1 of 0.7435 with 43.1% CRS reduction; while S2 (confidence-based) achieved only 19.7% and S1 (random) achieved 20.0% CRS reduction.

title: Revenue-sensitive evaluation of AI-assisted ICD-10-CM coding and human-AI collaboration under dual DRG payment systems
outcome: Metric sensitivity to operational performance
effect: AUC-micro 0.976–0.993 despite F1-micro range 0.481–0.593.
quote: Uniformly high AUC-micro scores (0.976–0.993) coexist with a wide F1-micro range (0.481–0.593): with 7942 codes per admission, the vast majority of code-admission pairs are true negatives that all models correctly identify.

title: Revenue-sensitive evaluation of AI-assisted ICD-10-CM coding and human-AI collaboration under dual DRG payment systems
outcome: Truncation impact on coding accuracy
effect: BioClinicalBERT F1-micro 0.4645 vs TF-IDF 0.5528; 99.7% exceeded 512 tokens.
quote: The self-trained TF-IDF baseline achieved F1-micro of 0.5528 on the restricted top-50 label space, while BioClinicalBERT reached only 0.4645, underperforming the simpler baseline because its 512-token limit discards most of each discharge summary (99.7% exceeded this length).

title: Large language models for optimizing clinical trial recruitment in ICUs: application to ventilator-induced diaphragm dysfunction
outcome: Expert adjudication of LLM-flagged potentially eligible ICU stays; positive predictive value

quote: Expert review confirmed 133 patients as eligible, resulting in a positive predictive value of 72% (95% CI 65-78).

title: Edge-Hosted LLM-Assisted NICU Discharge Summary Generation: Field-Level Evaluation Using a Clinician-Defined Rubric
outcome: Rubric-based quality of AI vs clinician-authored NICU discharge summaries on same admissions

quote: Error taxonomy analysis demonstrated fewer omissions, unsupported assertions, and contradictions in AI-generated summaries than in clinician-authored summaries.

title: Patient-Facing Radiology Communication with LLMs: Calibration Deficit and the Metadata Paradox
outcome: Self-reported confidence among safety-critical (Score 1) LLM errors

title: Patient-Facing Radiology Communication with LLMs: Calibration Deficit and the Metadata Paradox

outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT-4o responses versus recommended thresholds

title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o in Providing Information on Pediatric Inborn Errors of Immunity: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation

title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o in Providing Information on Pediatric Inborn Errors of Immunity: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation
outcome: Presence of medical disclaimers in ChatGPT-4o responses

title: Performance of ChatGPT-4o in Providing Information on Pediatric Inborn Errors of Immunity: A Cross-Sectional Evaluation

title: Language-Specific Differences in Large Language Model Diagnostic Reasoning: A Translation-Controlled Clinical Vignette Study
outcome: LLM diagnostic reasoning score in English versus Polish across six models

outcome: Sensitivity and agreement across prompt variants and repeated inference runs

title: Performance of Multimodal Large Language Models in Detection and Position Assessment of Thoracic Devices on Chest Radiographs

title: Digital Registrar: A Schema-First Framework for Multi-Cancer Privacy-Preserving Pathology Abstraction via Local LLMs
outcome: Accuracy on external TCGA cohort versus internal test data

title: Digital Registrar: A Schema-First Framework for Multi-Cancer Privacy-Preserving Pathology Abstraction via Local LLMs

title: Evaluating the Pediatric Behavior Guidance of Students Based on Actual Clinical Transcripts Scored by Faculty and Large Language Models: Pilot Comparative Study
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM scores across repeated runs with the same prompt
effect: Free and paid versions produced the same score for all 3 runs in only 7 (18%) and 4 (10%) of 40 encounters, respectively.
quote: The free-to-use and paid versions produced the same score for all 3 runs in only 7 (18%) and 4 (10%) of the 40 clinical encounters, respectively.

title: Evaluating the Pediatric Behavior Guidance of Students Based on Actual Clinical Transcripts Scored by Faculty and Large Language Models: Pilot Comparative Study
outcome: Agreement of LLM scores with human assessor reference scores
effect: Absolute agreement ICC vs human transcript scores was 0.729 (95% CI 0.475-0.859) for free LLM and 0.670 (95% CI 0.377-0.825) for paid LLM, moderate agreement.
quote: Comparing transcript scores with the free-to-use LLM's and paid LLM's scores yielded an absolute agreement intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.729 (95% CI 0.475-0.859; P<.001) and 0.670 (95% CI 0.377-0.825; P<.001), respectively, demonstrating moderate agreement.

title: From Burden to Balance: Trends in Documentation Workload with Ambient Artificial Intelligence Scribe Adoption
outcome: Clinician documentation time, workload, and burnout after ambient AI scribe deployment using validated instruments
effect: Reduced mental demand, time pressure, documentation effort (p<0.05); more clinicians reporting <2 hours/day outside-clinic documentation; burnout increased across follow-up (p<0.05).
quote: Clinicians reported statistically significant reductions in mental demand, time pressure, and documentation effort at postimplementation intervals (p < 0.05).
sample_unit: clinician survey respondents at baseline (172, 117, 101 at 1-, 3-, 6-month follow-up)

title: Reproducibility of AI-generated antibiotic recommendations in standardised clinical scenarios: A proof-of-concept experimental study
outcome: Reproducibility of antibiotic recommendations across 100 repeated identical submissions
effect: Entropy ranged from 0 to 2.53; ChatGPT fully consistent in 5/12 cases vs 1/12 for OpenEvidence; probability two responses differed reached 81% in some scenarios.
quote: For antibiotic selection, entropy ranged from complete agreement (H = 0) to high heterogeneity (H up to 2.53).
sample_unit: model interactions (12 scenarios x 100 submissions x 2 tools)

title: Reproducibility of AI-generated antibiotic recommendations in standardised clinical scenarios: A proof-of-concept experimental study
outcome: Clinical correctness of antibiotic and duration recommendations rated by blinded infectious diseases specialists
effect: OpenEvidence correct antibiotic recommendations 54.8% vs ChatGPT 35.7% (P<0.001); fully correct combined responses 33.4% vs 19.0% (P<0.001).
quote: Despite lower reproducibility, OpenEvidence generated more correct antibiotic recommendations (54.8% vs 35.7%; P < 0.001) and more fully correct combined responses (33.4% vs 19.0%; P < 0.001).
sample_unit: model interactions (12 scenarios x 100 submissions x 2 tools)

title: Performance of GPT-based large language models in hepatocellular carcinoma stratification: liver function assessment, BCLC staging, and treatment recommendations
outcome: GPT accuracy on local retrospective HCC patient data vs expert consensus and tumor board decisions
effect: Liver function accuracy >85% across versions; BCLC staging 46.2% (GPT-4) to 84.0% (o3); treatment recommendation overall accuracy up to 90.6%.
quote: BCLC staging accuracy ranged from 46.2% (version 4) to 84.0% (o3), with misclassification of radiological reports as the main error source.

title: Performance of GPT-based large language models in hepatocellular carcinoma stratification: liver function assessment, BCLC staging, and treatment recommendations
outcome: GPT recommendations compared against tumor board decisions and expert consensus, plus time and cost versus staff
effect: In 9-14% of cases GPT suggestions were retrospectively more guideline-concordant than tumor board decisions; GPT reduced costs approximately 300- to 1300-fold versus clinical staff.
quote: In 9-14% of cases, GPT suggestions were retrospectively more guideline-concordant than tumor board decisions.

title: General-purpose large language models outperform specialized clinical AI tools on medical benchmarks
outcome: Specialized clinical AI tools versus frontier LLMs on same benchmarks and real clinical queries
effect: Frontier LLMs outperformed clinical AI tools in all three evaluations (MedQA, HealthBench, RCQ); clinical AI tools performed comparably to Google Search AI Overview on the RCQ.
quote: Frontier LLMs outperformed clinical AI tools in all three evaluations.
sample_unit: model-question annotations by clinicians (RCQ benchmark; plus 500 MedQA and 500 HealthBench items)

title: An exploratory study of large language models in preoperative anesthesia assessment and planning for cardiac patients undergoing noncardiac surgery
outcome: LLM preoperative risk classification accuracy versus expert consensus (ASA, NYHA, RCRI, pulmonary risk)
effect: ASA accuracy: DeepSeek 73.2%, Grok 70.7%, ChatGPT 58.5%. NYHA and RCRI: Grok 75.6%, ChatGPT 46.3%. Pulmonary risk: Grok 80.5%, DeepSeek 78.0%, ChatGPT 51.2%.
quote: This exploratory study reveals that current LLMs exhibit suboptimal concordance with expert consensus in preoperative planning for complex cardiac cases.

title: Psychotic episode concurrent with interaction with a large language model (llm): a case report
outcome: Patient with schizophrenia misattributing intent to LLM chatbot output, preceding psychotic relapse
effect: Single case: generic safety tips were read as personalized 'signals', leading to checking behaviors, stopping paliperidone, and relapse (PANSS 102, BPRS 58).
quote: In this case, neutral safety statements produced by an LLM were seemingly reinterpreted as personally targeted messages, likely through the combined influence of anthropomorphic attributions, aberrant salience, and reasoning biases.

title: Performance of artificial intelligence chatbots in providing feeding management and oral health guidance for children with cleft lip and palate: ChatGPT 5.2 vs Gemini 3 Pro
outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of chatbot responses on cleft lip/palate feeding and oral health
effect: FRES 49.50 ± 10.33 (Gemini 3 Pro) vs 23.60 ± 14.48 (ChatGPT 5.2); FKGL 9.77 ± 1.54 vs 13.44 ± 2.81; both above plain-language levels, ChatGPT worse
quote: The FRES values were significantly higher for Gemini 3 Pro compared with ChatGPT 5.2 (49.50 ± 10.33 vs. 23.60 ± 14.48; p < 0.001), whereas the FKGL values were significantly lower (9.77 ± 1.54 vs. 13.44 ± 2.81; p < 0.001).

title: Breast cancer patients' questions about radiotherapy-induced skin toxicity: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4.0 and Gemini 2.5 flash
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid readability grade level of LLM answers to patient radiotherapy questions
effect: ChatGPT aligned with an 8th-grade level, whereas Gemini operated at an 11th-grade level.
quote: Readability analysis revealed that ChatGPT aligned with an 8th-grade level, whereas Gemini operated at an 11th-grade level.

title: AI in respiratory care: findings from the GOLD report
outcome: LLM accuracy on 2025 GOLD COPD guideline questions, binary and open-ended
effect: Binary accuracy ranged from 89.5% (Gemini 3) to 97.1% (Kimi K1.5); binary error rates 2.9% to 10.5%; open-ended weighted-score deficits 3.5% to 8.2%.
quote: Residual performance gaps persisted across both domains, with binary error rates ranging from 2.9% (Kimi K1.5) to 10.5% (Gemini 3), and open-ended weighted-score deficits ranging from 3.5% (Gemini 3) to 8.2% (DeepSeek-V3.2).

title: AI in respiratory care: findings from the GOLD report
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across repeated daily runs over 7 days
effect: All platforms showed statistical stability across the seven-day study period (p > 0.05 for all models).
quote: All platforms exhibited statistical stability across the seven-day study period (p > 0.05 for all models).

title: Intelligent fall risk prediction and real-time warning system for elderly care based on multimodal deep learning and wearable sensor fusion
outcome: Overall accuracy masking poor high-risk classification under extreme class imbalance
effect: Reported accuracy was 94.2%, versus 97.98% for always-low-risk predictions. High-risk PPV was 6.25%; sensitivity was 83.3% (5/6), with one misclassification shifting sensitivity by approximately 17% points.
quote: A classifier that predicted “low risk” for every window would achieve 97.98% accuracy, which is actually higher than our model’s overall figure—the difference being that our model trades some majority-class accuracy for improved sensitivity to minority-class events, as intended by the focal loss objective.

title: Intelligent fall risk prediction and real-time warning system for elderly care based on multimodal deep learning and wearable sensor fusion
outcome: Fall incidence with active warnings versus passive monitoring
effect: Falls/person-month: 0.82 ± 0.35 versus 2.14 ± 0.61; RR = 0.38 (95% CI: 0.24–0.62). Non-randomized, bundled intervention; exploratory association rather than causal efficacy evidence.
quote: During a three-month field deployment involving 80 participants, the group receiving active alerts recorded 62% fewer falls than the passive-monitoring control group, but we cannot attribute this outcome to the real-time warning mechanism alone given the non-randomized design and the additional intervention components (daily risk summaries, caregiver notifications) that could independently alter behavior; this finding is strictly exploratory.

title: Intelligent fall risk prediction and real-time warning system for elderly care based on multimodal deep learning and wearable sensor fusion
outcome: User satisfaction, usability, and wearing adherence during the pilot
effect: User satisfaction averaged 4.3/5; wearing compliance reached 91.3% of waking hours. The System Usability Scale score was 82.5 ± 7.8.
quote: User satisfaction averaged 4.3/5 on a Likert scale, and wearing compliance reached 91.3% of waking hours.

title: Intelligent fall risk prediction and real-time warning system for elderly care based on multimodal deep learning and wearable sensor fusion
outcome: usability and wearing compliance
effect: user satisfaction averaged 4.3/5 and wearing compliance reached 91.3% of waking hours
quote: User satisfaction averaged 4.3/5 on a Likert scale, and wearing compliance reached 91.3% of waking hours.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Bladder Cancer: Comparative Knowledge Retrieval and Clinical Reasoning of DeepSeek and ChatGPT
outcome: LLM performance compared against urologists on the same reconstructed clinical cases
effect: Human urologists significantly outperformed both AI models in diagnostic test appropriateness (P < 0.01); DeepSeek-R1 comparable to humans and ChatGPT-5 Pro on logical coherence (P > 0.05).
quote: Notably, human urologists significantly outperformed both AI models in diagnostic test appropriateness (P < 0.01), primarily because DeepSeek-R1 struggled with "test avoidance," tending to recommend redundant investigations (P < 0.0001).

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Bladder Cancer: Comparative Knowledge Retrieval and Clinical Reasoning of DeepSeek and ChatGPT
outcome: Reproducibility of accuracy across three independent runs
effect: All models achieved >92% accuracy; ChatGPT-5 Pro 97.52% and DeepSeek-R1 95.04%, both displaying superior stability.
quote: ChatGPT-5 Pro ranked first (97.52%), followed closely by DeepSeek-R1 (95.04%), with both displaying superior stability.

title: Assessing GPT-4o in cataract surgery decision-making: appropriateness, consistency, and clinical implications
outcome: Reproducibility of GPT-4o IOL recommendations across repeated runs
effect: Repeated testing showed significant instability in the model's responses (P = 0.026); GPT-4o ICC 0.378 versus human surgeons 0.359.
quote: However, repeated testing showed significant instability in the model's responses (P = 0.026).

title: Assessing GPT-4o in cataract surgery decision-making: appropriateness, consistency, and clinical implications
outcome: GPT-4o IOL selection appropriateness versus high- and low-volume cataract surgeons
effect: Overall appropriateness of GPT-4o was significantly lower than that of human surgeons (37.84% vs. 72.14%, P = 0.001).
quote: The overall appropriateness rate of GPT-4o for IOL selection was significantly lower than that of human surgeons (37.84% vs. 72.14%, P = 0.001).

title: Accuracy, readability, and health information quality of AI chatbot responses for patient education on intermittent fasting in chronic kidney disease: a prospective structured evaluation
outcome: Flesch-Kincaid reading grade level of chatbot responses versus US adult health literacy benchmark
effect: ChatGPT-5 responses at middle school level, aligned with US adult health literacy benchmark; Claude 4.5 Sonnet responses at high school level, above the benchmark.
quote: ChatGPT-5 produced responses at the middle school level, better aligned with the US adult health literacy benchmark, while Claude 4.5 Sonnet generated responses at the high school level.

title: Accuracy, readability, and health information quality of AI chatbot responses for patient education on intermittent fasting in chronic kidney disease: a prospective structured evaluation
outcome: Consistency of chatbot responses across repeated identical prompts
effect: Both models demonstrated identical internal consistency of 90%; accuracy improved on re-prompting after 24 hours.
quote: Both models demonstrated an identical internal consistency at 90%.

title: The Effect of Structured Context on Chest Radiograph Interpretation by a Multimodal Large Language Model: A Pilot Comparative Study
outcome: Multimodal LLM chest radiograph diagnostic accuracy against reference diagnoses
effect: Overall accuracy was 28% at baseline and 62% with structured context; lung cancer 20%, feeding tube placement 40%, rib fractures not identified in either condition; overall reliability inadequate for independent clinical use.
quote: Structured contextual guidance improved performance on selected chest radiograph tasks, but overall diagnostic reliability remained inadequate for independent clinical use.

title: Prompt-Induced Output Variability and Structured-Output Integrity in Local Open Large Language Models: A Multi-model In Silico Benchmark Using Synthetic Acute-Care Scenarios
outcome: prompt-induced distribution divergence
effect: Mean total Jensen-Shannon distance ranged from 0.126 to 0.306 across nine model-condition cells.
quote: Across the nine model-condition cells, the mean total Jensen-Shannon distance ranged from 0.126 to 0.306.
sample_unit: synthetic acute-care cases (3 timepoints, 21 prompt variants, 3 runs, 3 models)

title: Prompt-Induced Output Variability and Structured-Output Integrity in Local Open Large Language Models: A Multi-model In Silico Benchmark Using Synthetic Acute-Care Scenarios
outcome: top-action switching under prompt variation
effect: T3 top-action switching ranged 0.253 for Gemma STABLE to 0.584 for gpt-oss BASE.
quote: At the terminal timepoint, top-1 action switching remained appreciable across all cells, ranging from 0.253 for Gemma 3 12B under STABLE to 0.584 for gpt-oss 20B under BASE.
sample_unit: synthetic acute-care cases (3 timepoints, 21 prompt variants, 3 runs, 3 models)

title: Prompt-Induced Output Variability and Structured-Output Integrity in Local Open Large Language Models: A Multi-model In Silico Benchmark Using Synthetic Acute-Care Scenarios
outcome: cross-field structured-output inconsistency
effect: Gemma had 0 invalid outputs, but T3 top-action argmax agreement fell to 0.389-0.397.
quote: Gemma 3 12B produced no invalid outputs in the primary analysis set, but its agreement between the self-declared top action and the argmax of action probabilities deteriorated over time, falling to 0.389-0.397 at the terminal timepoint.
sample_unit: synthetic acute-care cases (3 timepoints, 21 prompt variants, 3 runs, 3 models)

title: A Reproducible Protocol and Framework for Large Language Model (LLM)-Assisted Estrogen and Progesterone Receptor (ER/PR) Scoring
outcome: Misclassification driven by poor-quality image inputs (compression, exposure, white balance, artifacts)
effect: Image quality, compression, improper brightness, and absent white-balance adjustment led LLMs to misclassify borderline images, e.g., misreading background hues as staining.
quote: In the critical 0% to 1% threshold, the primary drivers of error were image quality and pre-analytical slide preparation, low image resolution/compression, and improper brightness settings (over- or underexposure).

title: A Reproducible Protocol and Framework for Large Language Model (LLM)-Assisted Estrogen and Progesterone Receptor (ER/PR) Scoring
outcome: Overlap of prompt-optimization cases with final test set; lack of held-out validation
effect: The 10 cases used for iterative prompt optimization were included in final concordance analysis; no independent held-out validation cohort was employed, risking overestimated performance.
quote: The 10 cases used for iterative prompt optimization were drawn from the larger 80-case pool and were included in the final concordance analysis.

title: A Reproducible Protocol and Framework for Large Language Model (LLM)-Assisted Estrogen and Progesterone Receptor (ER/PR) Scoring
outcome: Use of confidence intervals and appropriate metrics in reporting concordance
effect: Only simple percentage agreement reported; no Cohen's kappa, confidence intervals, or sensitivity/specificity per tier were calculated.
quote: Formal statistical measures, such as Cohen's kappa or confidence intervals, were not calculated given the feasibility study design and sample size.

title: A Reproducible Protocol and Framework for Large Language Model (LLM)-Assisted Estrogen and Progesterone Receptor (ER/PR) Scoring
outcome: Concordance of three LLMs with CAP consensus for ER/PR scoring
effect: Claude 90-98%, Gemini 85-100%, Gemma 73-93% concordance across qualitative and semi-qualitative approaches; models compared with each other against CAP consensus, not against clinicians.
quote: Performance varied across models and scoring approaches, with Claude achieving the highest concordance (90-98%), followed by Gemini (85-100%) and Gemma (73-93%), reflecting differences in multimodal reasoning capacity that should be considered when selecting a model for implementation.

title: A Reproducible Protocol and Framework for Large Language Model (LLM)-Assisted Estrogen and Progesterone Receptor (ER/PR) Scoring
outcome: Prompt/session protocol concordance
effect: Systematic RPE plus ZSR elevated CAP concordance from 70-80% baseline to over 95%.
quote: The key insight is that diagnostic accuracy is driven not by model size or architecture, but by systematic RPE and the ZSR protocol, the latter proving essential for eliminating conversational bias and elevating concordance with CAP consensus from a baseline of 70-80% to over 95%.

title: TotalSegmentator-AI for aortic segmentation in CT: Reliable performance in normal anatomy but limited utility in pathological aortic disease
outcome: Segmentation quality across normal versus pathological aortic anatomy categories
effect: Quality varied by category (p<0.001): best in young patients (median 5), poorest in dissections (median 3) and aneurysms (median 4); overall median 4, 77% good or excellent.
quote: Performance was consistent across segments (p = 0.16) but varied by category (p < 0.001): best in young patients (5 [IQR 4-5]) and adequate in non-contrast and venous-phase scans (4 [IQR 4-5]), poorest in dissections (3 [IQR 3-4]) and aneurysms (4 [IQR 3-4]).

title: Performance comparison of large language models for medication counseling in people living with HIV
outcome: Expert-rated quality of five LLMs on real-world HIV medication questions
effect: Composite scores: DeepSeek 4.47, Qwen 4.33, Kimi 4.24, Doubao 4.13, ChatGPT 3.41 (H=182.14, p<0.001); all models showed significant limitations on complex pharmaceutical inquiries.
quote: All models demonstrated significant limitations when handling complex pharmaceutical inquiries and cannot fully replace professional clinical pharmacists.

title: Comparative evaluation of the quality, reliability, and readability of five large language model responses to frequently asked questions on gestational hypertension
outcome: Readability and patient-education appropriateness of LLM texts on gestational hypertension
effect: GPT-5 highest C-PEMAT (11.10 ± 2.40); readability varied by content category, with etiology and risk factor texts showing weaker reading fluency; quality and readability largely independent.
quote: Content categories exhibited differentiated readability but stable quality: texts on "Prevention and Prognosis" and "Treatment and Management" yielded the highest C-PEMAT scores, whereas "Etiology and Risk Factors" texts showed weaker reading fluency.
sample_unit: LLM-generated texts (20 per model, 20 per theme)

title: Comparative evaluation of the quality, reliability, and readability of five large language model responses to frequently asked questions on gestational hypertension
outcome: Factual accuracy of LLM responses on gestational hypertension
effect: 19.0% of responses contained factual inaccuracies; none judged potentially clinically harmful; significant between-model differences in factual accuracy scores.
quote: In the factual-accuracy assessment, 19.0% of responses contained factual inaccuracies, while no response was judged to contain potentially clinically harmful misinformation.
sample_unit: LLM-generated texts (20 per model, 20 per theme)

title: AI dialogues in cartilage repair: which guides evidence-based decisions better?
venue: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of LLM and Google answers to cartilage repair questions
effect: Grade Level 12.6-13.2 for Google vs. 15.7-17.4 for LLMs, far above typical patient reading levels; Google's lower score attributed to snippet brevity.
quote: Readability analysis paradoxically favored Google (Grade Level 12.6-13.2 vs. 15.7-17.4 for LLMs), attributable to extreme snippet brevity inflating formulaic scores rather than genuine comprehensibility.
sample_unit: questions (top-10 Google FAQs per domain across two domains, each answered by 3 platforms)

title: Blinded two-phase evaluation of large language models in complex cardiac surgery: task-specific performance and human-AI collaboration
outcome: Evaluator detection of incorrect LLM outputs; overacceptance vs underrecognition rate between rounds
effect: Overacceptance 7.57% vs underrecognition 2.59% (net gap +4.98%, p<0.001); in five highest-weighted dimensions 10.16% vs 3.68% (net +6.48%).
quote: The overall overacceptance rate (affirmative-to-negative revisions) was 7.57%, whereas the underrecognition rate (negative-to-affirmative revisions) was 2.59%, yielding a net trust calibration gap of +4.98% (McNemar's test, p < 0.001).
sample_unit: cardiac surgery scenarios (rated by 5 surgeons; 3,750 binary ratings)

title: Blinded two-phase evaluation of large language models in complex cardiac surgery: task-specific performance and human-AI collaboration
outcome: Inter-evaluator agreement (Fleiss' kappa) before and after viewing expert reference answers
effect: Kappa rose from 0.0834 (round 1) to 0.1298 (round 2) after reviewing reference answers.
quote: Agreement improved after the second-round review incorporating suggested answers ( κ = 0.1298; 95% CI: 0.0981–0.1615; p < 0.0001).
sample_unit: cardiac surgery scenarios (rated by 5 surgeons; 3,750 binary ratings)

title: Blinded two-phase evaluation of large language models in complex cardiac surgery: task-specific performance and human-AI collaboration
outcome: Experts failing to recognize incorrect or hallucinated LLM output on first-pass review
effect: Experienced surgeons often missed LLM errors at first glance; 10.16% of ratings in top-weighted dimensions revised affirmative to negative after seeing reference answers.
quote: Notably, even experienced experts often failed to recognize LLM errors at first glance
sample_unit: cardiac surgery scenarios (rated by 5 surgeons; 3,750 binary ratings)

title: Blinded two-phase evaluation of large language models in complex cardiac surgery: task-specific performance and human-AI collaboration
outcome: Automation bias from fluent, well-structured LLM outputs suppressing clinician scrutiny
effect: Overacceptance concentrated in safety-critical dimensions; overacceptance rate 10.16% nearly three times underrecognition 3.68%, net gap +6.48%.
quote: This indicates that expert trust miscalibration was concentrated in precisely the dimensions where errors carry the greatest clinical consequence—a finding consistent with automation bias, whereby plausible and fluently structured outputs reduce the likelihood of critical human scrutiny.
sample_unit: cardiac surgery scenarios (rated by 5 surgeons; 3,750 binary ratings)

title: Blinded two-phase evaluation of large language models in complex cardiac surgery: task-specific performance and human-AI collaboration
outcome: Whether benchmark/exam performance predicts competence in complex clinical decision-making
effect: Top models scored well overall, but even O1 showed deficits in patient safety (0.600) and hallucination avoidance (0.667) on expert-designed scenarios.
quote: Our results highlight that strong performance by LLMs on standardized exams does not ensure safe or reliable application in complex, high-stakes clinical decision-making.
sample_unit: cardiac surgery scenarios (rated by 5 surgeons; 3,750 binary ratings)

title: Assessing Eligibility for Anticancer Drug Health Insurance Reimbursement Using Large Language Models: Benchmark Development and Comparative Study
outcome: Recall on undeterminable cases (whether LLMs withhold judgment) versus eligible/ineligible cases
effect: Eligible/ineligible recall 86.5%-98.6%; undeterminable recall 44.6%-70.3%; information gap-filling was 83.4% of 235 errors, and undeterminable cases were mostly misclassified as eligible.
quote: Eligible and ineligible cases were classified with high recall (86.5%-98.6%), but undeterminable cases showed a marked decline across all models (44.6%-70.3%).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Patient Education: A Comparative Evaluation of Chatbot Reliability After Total Hip Arthroplasty
venue: American journal of physical medicine & rehabilitation
outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease Score) of LLM responses to post-THA patient questions
effect: Best readability was ChatGPT 3.5 with median FRES = 55; the other models scored lower. Significant differences in readability were found among models.
quote: Gemini scored significantly higher in reliability (P < 0.001), whereas ChatGPT 3.5 achieved the greatest readability (median FRES = 55).

title: Intravitreal anti-VEGF therapy: Comparative evaluation of appropriateness and readability of large language model chatbots' responses to frequently asked patient questions
outcome: Readability of chatbot answers to anti-VEGF patient questions across five readability indices
effect: Significant differences across all readability indices (P<0.001); Gemini 3 had the highest Flesch Reading Ease, while Grok 4 produced more complex texts requiring higher educational levels.
quote: Gemini 3 achieved the highest Flesch Reading Ease scores, indicating better patient accessibility, whereas Grok 4 produced more complex texts requiring higher educational levels.

title: Embedding LLMs in the patient portal to summarize acute minor illness information: a three-arm experimental study
outcome: Patient comprehension of acute minor illness information at Day 14 with vs without LLM plain-language summaries
effect: Comprehension at Day 14 was higher with LLM summaries (Claude M=81.4, GPT-5.1 M=79.6) than control (M=63.2); F(2,169)=47.34, p<0.001, partial η2=0.36.
quote: LLM-embedded patient portal summaries significantly improved comprehension of acute minor illnesses and reduced unnecessary healthcare utilization in a primary care setting.

title: Embedding LLMs in the patient portal to summarize acute minor illness information: a three-arm experimental study
outcome: Accuracy and safety of LLM summaries in clinician audit of 20% of summaries
effect: Minor factual imprecision in 5.7% (Claude) and 11.8% (GPT-5.1) of audited summaries; zero clinically significant hallucinations.
quote: Minor factual imprecision rates in audited summaries were 5.7% (Claude) and 11.8% (GPT-5.1), with zero clinically significant hallucinations across all audited summaries.

title: Cross-anatomical evaluation of a deep-learning auto-contouring system: qualitative, geometric, and dosimetric validation
venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
outcome: Local retrospective validation of auto-contours against manual contours: usability, geometric agreement, dosimetric impact
effect: 76.1% of auto-contours clinically usable (score ≥3); DSC >0.8 in 54.8%, MDA <2.5 mm in 71.5%, max HD <12.5 mm in 50%; 88.1% of organs within ±5% dose-volume difference.
quote: Overall, 76.1% of auto-contours were qualitatively judged to be clinically usable (score ≥3).

title: Cross-anatomical evaluation of a deep-learning auto-contouring system: qualitative, geometric, and dosimetric validation
venue: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
outcome: Variation in auto-contouring performance across anatomical sites and organs
effect: Performance showed organ-dependent variability across six anatomical sites, with 8/29 structures being major geometric outliers.
quote: The SYNAPSE Radiotherapy system showed high overall clinical usability with organ-dependent variability.

title: Impact of acute kidney injury labeling strategies in hospitalized patients: suggestion for a dual-alert clinical decision support system
outcome: Ambiguous AKI labels
effect: 978/5,115 (19.1%) standard KDIGO-labeled patients were considered ambiguous; 4,137 (80.9%) met refined criteria.
quote: Among 5,115 patients labeled by the standard KDIGO, 4,137 (80.9%) met the refined criteria, and 978 (19.1%) were considered ambiguous.
sample_unit: hospitalized patients labeled with AKI by standard KDIGO criteria

title: Benchmarking reliability and calibration of LLMs for multi-cancer early detection test communication
outcome: Confidence calibration of LLM answers on MCED multiple-choice questions, including high-confidence errors
effect: Brier scores were low across models, but several models made high-confidence errors (confidence ≥80 yet incorrect), mainly on precise numerical estimates.
quote: Despite low Brier scores across models, several models made high-confidence errors.
sample_unit: questions (94 multiple-choice, 13 free-response), each answered three times by five LLMs

title: Comparative Accuracy and Safety of 4 Large Language Models on Cornea and External Disease Multiple-Choice Questions
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answers across 5 repeated runs
effect: Five-run retesting showed similar ranking but imperfect stability, particularly for DeepSeek-V3.2.
quote: Five-run retesting showed similar ranking but imperfect stability, particularly for DeepSeek-V3.2.

title: Prospective validation and implementation of a model to identify patients with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) carriage on admission to acute care hospitals
outcome: Screening workload and diagnostic performance across alternative risk thresholds
effect: Raising the threshold from 0.16% to 0.36% reduced screening from 20 to 5 patients/week; PPV increased from 10.3% to 18.8%, while sensitivity decreased from 54.5% to 27.3%.
quote: For example, using a higher cutoff (≥0.36%) may be more practical as it would require screening fewer patients (∼5/week) with a higher PPV (19%), while only sacrificing a small decrease in NPV (98.2% to 97.5%).

title: Prospective validation and implementation of a model to identify patients with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) carriage on admission to acute care hospitals
outcome: Prospective discrimination on live EHR data versus derivation cohort
effect: AUC 0.66 prospectively vs 0.73 (95% CI 0.60–0.87) in derivation cohort; authors describe it as comparable, with moderate discrimination.
quote: The model demonstrated moderate discriminative performance (AUC of 0.66) under real-world conditions, comparable to that in the original derivation cohort (AUC, 0.73; 95% CI, 0.60–0.87).

title: Prospective validation and implementation of a model to identify patients with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) carriage on admission to acute care hospitals
outcome: resource and predictive yield trade-offs
effect: Raising the threshold to 0.36% would reduce screening volume to 5 patients per week and increase PPV to 19%, while minimally reducing NPV.
quote: For example, using a higher cutoff (≥0.36%) may be more practical as it would require screening fewer patients (∼5/week) with a higher PPV (19%), while only sacrificing a small decrease in NPV (98.2% to 97.5%).

title: Zero-shot Thoracic Oncologic History Generation for Radiologists Using Retrieval-augmented Large Language Model Pipeline
outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM oncologic summaries grounded via retrieval-augmented generation
effect: RAG pipeline summaries achieved mean accuracy of 97.9% (95% CI: 96.8, 99.1) for the best models and GPT-5-mini completeness of 95.5% (95% CI: 94.2, 96.7); no comparison without retrieval.
quote: The GPT-5-mini pipeline achieved the highest mean completeness score of 95.5% (95% CI: 94.2, 96.7) and was similar to o3-mini for a mean accuracy of 97.9% (95% CI: 96.8, 99.1).

title: High performance deep-learning model for the diagnosis of auto-immune hepatitis based on histological whole slide images
venue: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
outcome: AUC on development data versus external dataset for AIH diagnosis from whole slide images
