title: Evaluating accuracy and reasoning capabilities of large language models for acute ischemic stroke management
outcome: Treatment decision accuracy of LLMs versus stroke experts on the same vignettes
effect: DeepSeek R1 had highest MT accuracy (87%) and IVT accuracy of 78%; neurologists 81% MT and 80% IVT; neuroradiologists 84% MT and 76% IVT.
quote: DeepSeek R1 achieved the highest MT accuracy among all models and clinicians (MT 87%), with IVT accuracy of 78%.

title: Ambient AI Scribe Implementation in an Ambulatory Setting in a Single Medical Group: Prospective Study
outcome: Documentation time, after-hours EMR time, and provider burnout after ambient scribe deployment
effect: High users: 21% decrease in daily note time (-13.6 min), 13% decrease in pajama time (-3.6 min). Providers with no burnout symptoms rose 22% (49.4%), but the burnout difference was not significant.
quote: This ambient AI scribe decreased the time providers spent writing notes in the clinic and decreased time spent in the EMR outside of work hours.

title: Ambient AI Scribe Implementation in an Ambulatory Setting in a Single Medical Group: Prospective Study
outcome: Patient experience ('provider listened to me' satisfaction scores) after ambient AI use
effect: No significant effect on patient satisfaction scores (P=.39).
quote: Patient experience, as measured by "provider listened to me" scores on patient satisfaction surveys, was not significantly affected by ambient AI use (P=.39).

title: Comparative evaluation of traditional versus generative AI patient education material on prehabilitation
outcome: Readability and understandability of AI-generated prehabilitation patient education versus NHS leaflet
effect: ChatGPT readability comparable to NHS leaflet; PEMAT-P understandability >75% for all materials; actionability highest for NHS (93.3%). Expert accuracy lower for all AI models than NHS (9.8 ± 0.3).
quote: For readability, ChatGPT and the National Health Service were comparable.
sample_unit: expert raters (4 patient education materials evaluated)

title: Application of LLMs in CAD-RADS Classification and Patient Management
outcome: LLM CAD-RADS scoring and management agreement with human reference standard
effect: Scoring agreement ranged from κ=0.637 (DeepSeek, radiologist) to 0.997 (Claude); management recommendation accuracy was considerably lower than scoring accuracy.
quote: The LLMs' accuracy in proposing further management was considerably lower than their scoring accuracy, with CAD-RADS 3 showing the greatest variability in management recommendations across models and between human specialists.

title: Application of LLMs in CAD-RADS Classification and Patient Management
outcome: Output variation with prompt professional identity (cardiologist vs radiologist)
effect: ChatGPT κ=0.896 as radiologist vs 0.715 as cardiologist; DeepSeek 0.637 vs 0.768; scoring and management varied by prompt identity.
quote: Furthermore, both CAD-RADS scoring and management recommendations varied depending on the professional identity specified in the prompt.

title: Development and evaluation of a large language model-based, retrieval-augmented generation application for query response in early oncology clinical trials
venue: ESMO real world data and digital oncology
outcome: Response time and SME-rated accuracy with vs without RAG assistant for protocol queries
effect: Mean response time 14.9 vs 26.5 minutes (43.8% reduction, P = 0.0347); median SME accuracy ~3 (Mostly Correct) in both arms, no significant difference.
quote: Accuracy, measured as the median SME score (scale 1-4), was ∼3 ("Mostly Correct") for both arms, with no statistically significant difference.
sample_unit: sponsor clinical study team members (10 per arm)

title: Assessing Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Patient Education: Evaluating Accuracy and Readability of Responses on Surgical Procedures for Patellar Tendon Rupture
outcome: Readability of chatbot patient education responses relative to average American reading level
effect: No significant readability differences among four chatbots; all responses averaged above the average American reading level.
quote: There were no significant differences in readability among the four different chatbots and they all provided responses that averaged above the average American reading level.

title: Evaluating chat generative pre-trained transformer responses to common patient questions on temporomandibular disorders
outcome: Readability grade level of ChatGPT responses on temporomandibular disorders
effect: Flesch-Kincaid grade 6.2-10.7 (mean 8.0), middle-to-high school comprehension; some responses above typical patient reading levels.
quote: Readability levels ranged from grade 6.2-10.7 (mean 8.0), corresponding to middle-to-high school comprehension.

title: Impact of Exposure Parameters on Deep Learning Models in Chest Radiography and Implications for Deployment
outcome: AUC under mismatched exposure parameter distributions (pneumothorax, COVID-19, race classification)
effect: Pneumothorax AUC fell from 0.94 (95% CI 0.94, 0.95) to 0.56 (0.55, 0.58), ΔAUC -0.38; COVID-19 ΔAUC -0.33; race classification ΔAUC -0.09 (all P<.001).
quote: For pneumothorax detection, AUC decreased from 0.94 (95% CI: 0.94, 0.95) to 0.56 (95% CI: 0.55, 0.58) on mismatched exposure distributions (ΔAUC, -0.38; P < .001).

title: Impact of Exposure Parameters on Deep Learning Models in Chest Radiography and Implications for Deployment
outcome: Model performance in high-risk exposure regimes within natural distribution versus typical exposures
effect: A priori exposure-regimen screening found high-risk regimes within the natural distribution associated with reduced model performance compared with typical exposures.
quote: The a priori exposure-regimen screening revealed high-risk regimes within the natural distribution that were associated with reduced model performance compared with typical exposures.

title: Real-World Generalizability of Alzheimer's Volumetric MRI Machine-Learning Models: External Validation with British Data
outcome: Performance drop of CN vs AD model on external real-world clinical dataset
effect: Volume-normalized 'CN vs. AD' model BAC fell from 87.7% internally to 81.5% in SLaM-BRC due to misclassification of non-AD subjects with hippocampal atrophy.
quote: The volume-normalized 'CN vs. AD' model (87.7% balanced accuracy [BAC]) led to decreased performance in the SLaM-BRC (81.5% BAC) due to misclassifications of non-AD subjects with evidence of hippocampal atrophy.

title: Real-World Generalizability of Alzheimer's Volumetric MRI Machine-Learning Models: External Validation with British Data
outcome: Model performance across magnetic field strengths (1.5T vs 3.0T) and external site
effect: 87.1% of 93 subjects had the same class assignment at 1.5T vs 3.0T; CN vs MCI vs AD model BAC stayed similar (55.3% vs 54.6%).
quote: Our 'CN vs. AD' model showed similar performance when tested at different magnetic fields (1.5T vs. 3.0T: 87.1% of 93 subjects had the same class assignment).

title: Real-World Generalizability of Alzheimer's Volumetric MRI Machine-Learning Models: External Validation with British Data
outcome: real-world clinical dataset performance
effect: Volume-normalized CN vs. AD BAC decreased from 87.7% to 81.5% in the UK SLaM-BRC cohort.
quote: The volume-normalized 'CN vs. AD' model (87.7% balanced accuracy [BAC]) led to decreased performance in the SLaM-BRC (81.5% BAC) due to misclassifications of non-AD subjects with evidence of hippocampal atrophy.

title: Real-World Generalizability of Alzheimer's Volumetric MRI Machine-Learning Models: External Validation with British Data
outcome: generalization to UK clinical context
effect: Volume-normalized CN vs. AD BAC decreased from 87.7% to 81.5% when evaluated in SLaM-BRC.
quote: The volume-normalized 'CN vs. AD' model (87.7% balanced accuracy [BAC]) led to decreased performance in the SLaM-BRC (81.5% BAC) due to misclassifications of non-AD subjects with evidence of hippocampal atrophy.

title: Performance of multimodal Large Language Models in misdiagnosed dermatologic cases: a pilot study on diagnostic accuracy and human error replication
outcome: Multimodal LLM top-1 diagnostic accuracy on misdiagnosed dermatology cases
effect: Multimodal Top-1 accuracy: Gemini 3 60.0% (18/30), ChatGPT-5.2 56.7% (17/30), Claude 4.5 Sonnet 33.3% (10/30); limited accuracy for malignant lesions using macro-images.
quote: Gemini 3 achieved the highest multimodal Top-1 accuracy (60.0% (18/30), followed by ChatGPT-5.2 at 56.7% (17/30) and Claude 4.5 Sonnet at 33.3% (10/30).

title: Preclinical Dialogue Simulation: Evaluating Response Accessibility in Conversational Artificial Intelligence for Aphasia Therapy
venue: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
outcome: Readability of LLM clinician language measured with Flesch Reading Ease, Dale-Chall and composite score
effect: LLMs differ systematically in adapting clinician language to impaired speech; accessibility depended on model, prompting, and reasoning mode.
quote: LLMs differ systematically in their capacity to adapt clinician language to impaired speech.

title: Preclinical Dialogue Simulation: Evaluating Response Accessibility in Conversational Artificial Intelligence for Aphasia Therapy
venue: Journal of speech, language, and hearing research : JSLHR
outcome: clinician language accessibility during simulated aphasia therapy
effect: LLMs differed systematically in adapting language to impaired speech; few-shot prompting and advanced reasoning generally yielded more accessible clinician responses, whereas Gemini had superior accessibility under zero-shot, standard reasoning.
quote: LLMs differ systematically in their capacity to adapt clinician language to impaired speech.

title: Evaluation of six cutting-edge large language models in answering a set of open-ended questions in dental case reports
outcome: Expert-rated quality of six candidate LLMs compared on identical dental case questions
effect: Significant differences across all metrics; DeepSeek median 4.5/5 vs GPT 4.0, Gemini 4.0, Copilot 4.0, MedGemma 3.75, Llama 3.5.
quote: DeepSeek achieved the highest expert ratings, with a median score of 4.5/5, outperforming other models such as GPT (4.0/5), Gemini (4.0/5), Copilot (4.0/5), MedGemma (3.75/5), and Llama (3.5/5).

title: Leveraging simulation to provide a practical framework for estimating the novel scope of risk of large language models in healthcare
outcome: Model false-negative rates in detecting suicidal ideation, therapy-request and therapy-like interactions
effect: Estimated P1 ranged from 1.1×10⁻⁸ to 1.6×10⁻⁴ and P2 from 4.9×10⁻⁵ to 5.1×10⁻³, spanning four orders of magnitude; performance generally improved with model size.
quote: Estimated P<sub>1</sub> values ranged from 1.1×10⁻⁸ to 1.6×10⁻⁴ and P<sub>2</sub> from 4.9×10⁻⁵ to 5.1×10⁻³, spanning four orders of magnitude.
sample_unit: open-source LLMs evaluated on synthetic datasets

title: Performance of multivariable risk prediction algorithms in predicting COPD exacerbations: a population-based study
outcome: Discrimination of ACCEPT versus exacerbation history (standard of care) for predicting moderate/severe exacerbations
effect: ACCEPT 2.0 AUC 0.77 outperformed any and frequent exacerbator categories (AUC 0.69 and 0.67); ACCEPT 3.0-UK net beneficial and superior to exacerbation history across wide range of thresholds.
quote: ACCEPT 2.0 achieved an AUC of 0.77 for predicting moderate/severe exacerbations, outperforming both any and frequent exacerbator categories (AUC: 0.69 and 0.67, respectively).

title: Performance of multivariable risk prediction algorithms in predicting COPD exacerbations: a population-based study
outcome: Calibration (O/E ratio) before and after local recalibration of ACCEPT
effect: ACCEPT 2.0 overpredicted (O/E 0.81, 95% CI 0.80 to 0.81); recalibration gave O/E 1.00 (0.99 to 1.00) while maintaining AUC 0.77.
quote: Recalibration resolved this overprediction, yielding O/E ratio of 1.00 (95% CI 0.99 to 1.00), while maintaining discrimination (AUC: 0.77).

title: Performance of multivariable risk prediction algorithms in predicting COPD exacerbations: a population-based study
outcome: calibration of ACCEPT 2.0
effect: ACCEPT 2.0 overpredicted: O/E ratio 0.81 (95% CI 0.80 to 0.81).
quote: However, it overpredicted exacerbation events (observed-to-expected (O/E) ratio: 0.81 (95% CI 0.80 to 0.81)).

title: Automatic diagnosis of osteonecrosis of the femoral head and segmentation of necrotic regions using deep learning at computed tomography: a real-world multicenter study
outcome: Diagnostic AUC in internal versus external test hospital, generalizability across sites
effect: Slice-level AUC 0.98 internal vs 0.97 external; sensitivity 98.91% vs 99.61%; Dice 72.64% vs 69.11%; patient-level AUC 0.98 and 0.97.
quote: At the patient level, diagnostic performance remained high, with AUCs of 0.98 and 0.97 in the internal and external test sets, respectively.

title: Automatic diagnosis of osteonecrosis of the femoral head and segmentation of necrotic regions using deep learning at computed tomography: a real-world multicenter study
outcome: Model diagnostic and segmentation performance compared against three orthopaedic surgeons
effect: Model outperformed surgeons in diagnosis and matched a 10-year-experienced attending in segmentation.
quote: It outperformed surgeons in diagnosis and matched a 10-year-experienced attending in segmentation.

title: Performance of large language models in delivering accurate and comprehensible patient information on heart failure and cardiomyopathy
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid grade level) of LLM responses to patient heart failure and cardiomyopathy questions
effect: Most readable model (Gemini) still scored Flesch-Kincaid Grade 11.3 ± 1.9 with 668.7 ± 116.1 words; linguistic complexity and length varied substantially across models.
quote: Gemini provided the most readable responses (Flesch-Kincaid Grade 11.3 ± 1.9) but was among the most verbose (668.7 ± 116.1 words).

title: Performance of large language models in delivering accurate and comprehensible patient information on heart failure and cardiomyopathy
outcome: Hallucination and confabulation frequency in LLM patient-information responses
effect: Confabulation avoidance scored consistently high across models (4.49 ± 0.02 on 1-5 scale); major errors or hallucinations rare but not absent.
quote: While major factual errors or hallucinations were rare in our blinded evaluation, they were not entirely absent.

title: Diagnostic performance of real-time characterization in artificial intelligence-assisted colonoscopy
outcome: Local diagnostic accuracy of CADx for diminutive rectosigmoid polyps against histopathology
effect: Sensitivity 93% (95% CI 87%-97%), specificity 33% (95% CI 22%-46%), PPV 70%, NPV 74%, accuracy 71%; specificity significantly lower than prior studies.
quote: The CADx-system demonstrated high sensitivity, but significantly lower specificity compared with prior studies, driven by a high false-positive rate.

title: Generative AI-Assisted Indication of Anatomical Landmarks to Enhance Safety under Intraoperative Bleeding in Laparoscopic Gastrectomy for Gastric Cancer
venue: Annals of surgery open : perspectives of surgical history, education, and clinical approaches
outcome: AI landmark indication performance under intraoperative bleeding (perturbed input) in massive bleeding cases
effect: Baseline gAI performed poorly under massive bleeding: pancreas Dice 0.36 ± 0.26, rising to 0.65 ± 0.17 with GAN-based bleeding removal (P < 0.05).
quote: Dice coefficients for the pancreas increased from 0.36 ± 0.26 to 0.65 ± 0.17 (P < 0.05).

title: AI-Driven Dental Procedure Coding: A Multi-Model Framework for CDT Extraction from Clinical Text
outcome: Code extraction accuracy against reference labels across four model approaches
effect: Zero-shot LLM micro-F1 0.9614 with perfect recall for frequent codes; Bi-GRU micro-F1 0.9362, macro-F1 0.9377; LoRA outperformed QLoRA across all metrics.
quote: The zero-shot LLM achieved the highest micro-F1 score (0.9614) and perfect recall for frequent CDT codes, demonstrating strong baseline reasoning without task-specific training; however, performance declined for rare procedures and diagnostic code hallucinations were common.

title: Assessment of Large Language Models in Colorectal Cancer Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making: A Retrospective Single-Center Comparison of Guideline-Integrated General-Purpose vs. Domain-Specialized Models
outcome: Concordance and safety of LLM recommendations with vs without in-context guideline grounding (non-equivalent comparison)
effect: Guideline-integrated Gemini 2.5: kappa 0.792, exact concordance 85.0%, safe 83.7%; MedGemma without guidelines: kappa 0.566-0.610, safe 62.3-62.7% (p<0.001). Confounded by model differences.
quote: Guideline-integrated general-purpose LLMs, exemplified by Gemini 2.5, demonstrated higher concordance with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions compared with a domain-specialized model without external retrieval.
sample_unit: colorectal cancer cases discussed at MTB

title: Assessment of Large Language Models in Colorectal Cancer Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making: A Retrospective Single-Center Comparison of Guideline-Integrated General-Purpose vs. Domain-Specialized Models
outcome: Accuracy and safety of LLM treatment recommendations against MTB reference standard with blinded expert adjudication
effect: Gemini 2.5 safe in 83.7% of cases; MedGemma 62.3% (T=0) and 62.7% (T=1); weighted kappa 0.792 vs 0.566/0.610.
quote: In the safety assessment, Gemini 2.5 demonstrated the highest proportion of safe recommendations (83.7%), whereas MedGemma (T = 0.0: 62.3% and T = 1.0: 62.7%) showed higher rates of potentially risky and harmful recommendations.
sample_unit: colorectal cancer cases discussed at MTB

title: Assessment of Large Language Models in Colorectal Cancer Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making: A Retrospective Single-Center Comparison of Guideline-Integrated General-Purpose vs. Domain-Specialized Models
outcome: Comparison of two candidate LLMs against tumor board decisions on the same cases
effect: Gemini 2.5 (guideline-integrated) outperformed MedGemma 27B on concordance and safety (p<0.001); full concordance 81.7% vs 57.0% (T=0) and 62.3% (T=1).
quote: Comparisons of the three-category concordance distributions showed significant differences between Gemini and MedGemma (T = 0.0) ( p < 0.001) and between Gemini and MedGemma (T = 1.0) ( p < 0.001).
sample_unit: colorectal cancer cases discussed at MTB

title: Assessment of Large Language Models in Colorectal Cancer Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Decision-Making: A Retrospective Single-Center Comparison of Guideline-Integrated General-Purpose vs. Domain-Specialized Models
outcome: Unsafe or discordant treatment recommendations
effect: Gemini safe 83.7%; MedGemma safe 62.3% (T=0.0) and 62.7% (T=1.0), with higher potentially risky/harmful rates.
quote: In the safety assessment, Gemini 2.5 demonstrated the highest proportion of safe recommendations (83.7%), whereas MedGemma (T = 0.0: 62.3% and T = 1.0: 62.7%) showed higher rates of potentially risky and harmful recommendations.
sample_unit: colorectal cancer cases discussed at MTB

title: Fracture Detection on Bone Radiographs: The Impact of an AI Tool on Orthopaedic Night Shifts
outcome: Recall rates and missed fractures before vs after AI fracture detection implementation
effect: Recalls 31/13,813 (0.22%) pre vs 27/14,842 (0.18%) post, p=0.42; fracture-related recalls 0.19% vs 0.17%, p=0.63; management change 0.0006% vs 0.0005%, p=0.551.
quote: Gleamer BoneView<sup>®</sup> use was linked to a non-significant decrease in missed fractures by orthopaedists working without on-site radiologists.

title: Fracture Detection on Bone Radiographs: The Impact of an AI Tool on Orthopaedic Night Shifts
outcome: Orthopaedist fracture misdiagnosis with versus without AI assistance in deployed setting
effect: Missed fractures 16 pre-implementation vs 13 post; fracture-related recall rate 0.19% vs 0.17% (p=0.63), non-significant.
quote: Statistical analyses measured the rates of fracture misdiagnosis before and after implementation of Gleamer BoneView<sup>®</sup>.

title: Towards Automated Spine Fracture Detection on Whole-Body CT of Polytraumatized Patients
outcome: Sensitivity and false positives of v2.0 on prospectively collected real-world WBCTs
effect: v2.0 sensitivities 77%-85% on Cohort 2 (n=712 WBCTs) but generated an abundance of false positives, including from trabecular structure.
quote: Version 2.0 also achieved decent sensitivities for Cohort 2 (sensitivities ranging between 77% and 85%) but generated an abundance of false positives.

title: Towards Automated Spine Fracture Detection on Whole-Body CT of Polytraumatized Patients
outcome: Generalization of v1.0 (trained on cervical spine) to thoracic and lumbar spine fractures
effect: v1.0 generalized to thoracic and lumbar spine with sensitivities between 60% and 87%.
quote: Version 1.0 showed promising performance not only for the cervical but also the thoracic and lumbar spine due to generalization (sensitivities ranging between 60% and 87%).

title: The Role of AI-Based Software BrainScan in the Interpretation of Non-Contrast Head CT in Acute Ischemic Stroke: An External Validation Study
outcome: Ischemia sensitivity after threshold recalibration to Youden-optimal cutoff
effect: Default threshold sensitivity 59.2%; Youden-optimal threshold (0.055) recovered sensitivity to 86.1% with negligible specificity loss
quote: The Youden-optimal threshold (0.055) recovered sensitivity to 86.1% with negligible specificity loss, reflecting a markedly bimodal score distribution.

title: The Role of AI-Based Software BrainScan in the Interpretation of Non-Contrast Head CT in Acute Ischemic Stroke: An External Validation Study
outcome: Ischemia detection sensitivity of AI as stand-alone reader
effect: Ischemia sensitivity 59.2% (95% CI 52.1-66.1), specificity 99.8%, AUC 0.930; lower sensitivity in infratentorial structures; authors recommend rule-in adjunct not stand-alone
quote: Ischemia sensitivity was 59.2% (95% CI 52.1-66.1) and specificity was 99.8% (99.4-100), with an AUC of 0.930 (0.906-0.954).

title: Medical Record Abstraction for Quality Improvement in Sepsis Care Using Artificial Intelligence: A Cluster Randomized Trial
outcome: Effect of LLM-based SEP-1 feedback on compliance, 30-day mortality, and ICU admission in a randomized trial
effect: SEP-1 compliance 82.9% vs 70.1% (absolute +13.0%, OR 2.10, 95% CI 1.15-3.81, P=.02); no significant differences in ICU admissions or 30-day mortality.
quote: No significant differences existed in intensive care unit admissions or 30-day mortality.
sample_unit: patients meeting SEP-1 criteria (treated by 66 attending physicians)

title: Artificial Intelligence in Caries Risk Assessment: Evaluating the Current Status of Caries Management by Risk Assessment and Cariogram with Large Language Models
outcome: MAE, quality and accuracy of LLM caries risk classification under guideline-informed versus unguided prompting
effect: Guideline-informed and guideline-only prompting significantly reduced MAE and improved quality and accuracy versus unguided (p < 0.001).
quote: Guideline-informed and guideline-only prompting significantly reduced MAE and improved quality and accuracy compared with the unguided condition (p < 0.001).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Caries Risk Assessment: Evaluating the Current Status of Caries Management by Risk Assessment and Cariogram with Large Language Models
outcome: LLM caries risk output agreement with expert-panel reference classifications
effect: MAE differed significantly across model-prompting combinations for both tools (p < 0.001); ChatGPT had lower MAE than Gemini for Cariogram (p = 0.002); inter- and intra-rater ICC 0.89-0.93.
quote: MAE differed significantly across AI model-prompting condition combinations for both tools (p < 0.001).

title: Artificial Intelligence in Caries Risk Assessment: Evaluating the Current Status of Caries Management by Risk Assessment and Cariogram with Large Language Models
outcome: Effect of structured guideline-based prompts versus unguided prompts on LLM output accuracy
effect: Guideline-informed and guideline-only prompting significantly reduced MAE and improved quality and accuracy compared with unguided prompting (p < 0.001).
quote: Guideline-informed and guideline-only prompting significantly reduced MAE and improved quality and accuracy compared with the unguided condition (p < 0.001).

title: Foundation Model-Driven Regions of Interest Classification and Renaming in Cancer Radiotherapy: A Customizable, Retraining-Free Workflow Across Institutions
outcome: ROI classification and renaming accuracy across institutions and disease sites
effect: Overall ROI type classification accuracy 99.12% and renaming accuracy 97.92%; classification consistently high across institutions and sites, renaming showed minor variation.
quote: Classification performance was consistently high across all institutions and sites; renaming accuracy showed minor variation driven by protocol omissions, compound suffix ambiguity, and institution-specific naming conventions.

title: Large Language Model Summarization of Physician-to-Physician Calls for Interhospital Transfer of Patients With ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction: Observational Study
outcome: Physician-rated hallucination-free and thoroughness of LLM call summaries (1-5 Likert)
effect: Hallucination free mean 4.4/5 (SD 0.9) and thorough 4.4/5 (SD 1.0) were the lowest-rated domains; accuracy mean 4.6/5 (SD 0.7); raters penalized inferential hallucinations.
quote: The "useful" (mean 4.8/5, SD 0.5) and "consistent" (mean 4.9/5, SD 0.6) domains were the highest rated, and the "thorough" (mean 4.4/5, SD 1.0) and "hallucination free" (mean 4.4/5, SD 0.9) domains were the lowest rated.

title: When Wrong Answers Matter: Consequence-Weighted Evaluation of Large Language Models for ERCP Triage
outcome: LLM guideline-based ERCP triage accuracy and under-triage errors on synthetic vignettes
effect: Accuracy 96.0% GPT-5.5, 90.0% Gemini 3.0 Pro, 84.0% Claude 4 Opus; Claude produced 9 under-triage errors and 163.8 simulated delay hours per 100 vignettes (P = .007).
quote: Claude 4 Opus produced the most under-triage errors (n = 9) and the largest simulated delay burden (163.8 hours per 100 vignettes; Kruskal-Wallis P = .007).

title: Empowering digital health management with on-device large language models for glucose prediction: a model development and validation study
outcome: Glucose prediction performance on external validation cohort versus development dataset
effect: GluLLM had lower 30-min RMSE than the strongest baseline on REPLACE-BG and on the external Móstoles cohort (20.6 ± 3.5 and 9.6 ± 2.9 mg/dL; p < 0.001); hypoglycaemia AUROC 0.79 and 0.84.
quote: We trained and evaluated GluLLM on the REPLACE-BG dataset, which includes 226 individuals with type 1 diabetes, and validated it on an external cohort comprising 207 individuals with type 2 diabetes or without diabetes.
sample_unit: individuals (226 with type 1 diabetes in REPLACE-BG; 207 in external cohort)

title: A S.C.O.R.E. framework for evaluating open-ended responses from large language models in healthcare
outcome: Structured expert rubric evaluation versus BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore in classifying clinically appropriate LLM responses
effect: Quantitative metrics frequently misclassified clinically appropriate responses as inaccurate; S.C.O.R.E. showed Cronbach's α 0.745 in the optimized domain and Cliff's δ 0.68-0.92 for optimization status.
quote: While quantitative metrics frequently misclassified clinically appropriate responses as inaccurate, S.C.O.R.E. demonstrated acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α 0.745) in the hyperparameter-optimized domain and detected large effect sizes (Cliff's δ 0.68-0.92) reflecting optimization status.

title: The importance of clinical context in evaluating algorithmic fairness: insights from a medication adherence prediction algorithm
outcome: Subgroup accuracy, false positive and false negative rates by nSES and race
effect: Accuracy was similar across nSES and racial subgroups, but false positives were higher for low vs high nSES (RR 1.50 [1.44-1.56]) and Black vs White (2.05 [1.92-2.19]); false negatives lower for Black vs White (0.63 [0.59-0.67]).
quote: The algorithm assigned more false positives for medication nonadherence among low vs high nSES (RR [95%CI] 1.50 [1.44-1.56]) and Black vs White (2.05 [1.92-2.19]) subgroups.

title: The importance of clinical context in evaluating algorithmic fairness: insights from a medication adherence prediction algorithm
outcome: Whether fairness assessment tied to clinical use case reveals disparity worsening
effect: Applied to 3 hypothetical use cases, worsening of disparities was pertinent where false positives could be particularly harmful, e.g., if nonadherence predictions prompted lower treatment priority.
quote: When applied to 3 hypothetical use cases, worsening of existing disparities was pertinent for clinical applications where false positives could be particularly harmful (e.g, if predictions of nonadherence prompted lower treatment priority).

title: The importance of clinical context in evaluating algorithmic fairness: insights from a medication adherence prediction algorithm
outcome: Risk flags potentially driving lower treatment priority for groups with more false positives
effect: More false positives in low nSES and Black patients could worsen disparities if nonadherence predictions prompted lower treatment priority.
quote: When applied to 3 hypothetical use cases, worsening of existing disparities was pertinent for clinical applications where false positives could be particularly harmful (e.g, if predictions of nonadherence prompted lower treatment priority).

title: Using an Ambient Artificial Intelligence Tool to Document Clinical Pharmacist Patient Encounters: Real-World Evidence From a Federally Qualified Health Center
venue: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
outcome: Documentation time and clinical productivity after ambient scribe implementation among pharmacists
effect: 31.17% reduction in median time documenting notes per day (38.5 vs. 26.5 min, p = 0.04); visit increases not statistically significant.
quote: Nine ambient AI documentation tool users demonstrated a 31.17% reduction in median time spent documenting notes per day (38.5 vs. 26.5 min, p = 0.04).

title: Zero-shot detection of apical periodontitis on periapical radiographs using multimodal large language models: diagnostic accuracy and error patterns
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of zero-shot MLLMs for apical periodontitis detection, relevant to standalone diagnostic use
effect: Accuracy up to 71.67% (Gemini). Claude sensitivity 95.00%, specificity 13.33%; GPT-5.2 sensitivity 20.00%, specificity 98.33%. None reliable enough for independent clinical use.
quote: Although diagnostic performance varied among models, none achieved a level of diagnostic performance sufficient for independent clinical use.

title: Zero-shot detection of apical periodontitis on periapical radiographs using multimodal large language models: diagnostic accuracy and error patterns
outcome: Comparison of three candidate MLLMs against each other and a clinician reference standard on same images
effect: Gemini 3.0 Pro accuracy 71.67%, significantly superior to Claude 4.5 Sonnet (Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.0015); models differed in sensitivity and specificity trade-offs.
quote: This performance was significantly superior to that of Claude 4.5 Sonnet (Bonferroni-adjusted p = 0.0015).

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Quantification of Longitudinal HRCT Changes During Treatment of Pulmonary Tuberculosis: An Exploratory Proof-of-Concept Study
outcome: Fit of a general lung-texture tool to tuberculosis HRCT, including cavity classification
effect: The software has no dedicated cavity class. Tuberculous cavities and post-destructive abnormalities were frequently labeled as emphysema. The abstract reports no quantitative error rate.
quote: As a result, emphysema-labeled low-attenuation areas should not be interpreted as conventional emphysema alone, because tuberculous cavities and post-destructive abnormalities were frequently included in this category.

title: Explainability Methods for AI-Assisted Diagnosis of Lymph Node Metastases in Digital Pathology: A Quantitative Comparative Study

effect: Domain adaptation improved AUPRC in 8/12 combinations (4 significant; best ΔAUPRC +0.1474, P<.001) and Brier in 11/12; zero-shot reduced AUPRC in most settings.
quote: The domain adaptation model showed ΔAUPRC>0 in 8 out of 12 combinations, with significant improvement over the baseline model observed in 4 combinations.
sample_unit: patients (hospital external validation cohort; 375 in held-out test set)

title: Evaluation of the Applicability of Synthetic Data in the Development of Colorectal Cancer Survival Prediction Models: External Validation of Advanced Machine Learning Models Based on National Cancer Data Center Data
outcome: Distribution differences between synthetic development data and local hospital population
effect: Statistically significant differences for all variables (P<.05); adenocarcinoma 97.2% vs 55.6%; perineural invasion 29.4% vs 0.7%; zero-shot models degraded performance.
quote: A clear domain shift was observed between synthetic and hospital data, necessitating the use of domain adaptation techniques to ensure model performance in real-world settings.
sample_unit: patients (hospital external validation cohort; 375 in held-out test set)

title: Evaluation of the Applicability of Synthetic Data in the Development of Colorectal Cancer Survival Prediction Models: External Validation of Advanced Machine Learning Models Based on National Cancer Data Center Data
outcome: Zero-shot performance of synthetic-trained models on local hospital data versus hospital-only baseline
effect: Zero-shot only 2 of 12 combinations had ΔAUPRC>0, none significant; 3 significantly degraded; AUPRC 0.2706-0.4171 vs baseline 0.3576-0.4663.
quote: Only 2 of 12 combinations exhibited ΔAUPRC>0, and none of these improvements were statistically significant.
sample_unit: patients (hospital external validation cohort; 375 in held-out test set)

title: Evaluation of the Applicability of Synthetic Data in the Development of Colorectal Cancer Survival Prediction Models: External Validation of Advanced Machine Learning Models Based on National Cancer Data Center Data
outcome: generalization to external hospital data
effect: 10/12 zero-shot combinations showed no improvement, including 3 statistically significant degradations.
quote: The remaining 10 combinations showed no improvement, including 3 with statistically significant degradation.
sample_unit: patients (hospital external validation cohort; 375 in held-out test set)

title: A Comparative Study of Generative Artificial Intelligence Versus Clinical Experts for Evidence-Based Decision-Making in Austere Environments
outcome: Validity of AI recommendation for surgical instrument reprocessing versus expert recommendation and literature
effect: Only ChatGPT matched the experts' chlorine dioxide recommendation; GenAI.mil and Gemini recommended OPA and NIPRGPT recommended glutaraldehyde, prioritizing processing speed over sterility assurance.
quote: Clinical experts recommended chlorine dioxide (ClO2) due to its sporicidal properties, which ensure sterility assurance. Only ChatGPT matched this recommendation.
sample_unit: query responders (4 AI platforms and 2 clinical experts)

title: Diagnostic accuracy of ChatGPT-5 in evaluating root canal treatment and periapical pathosis on periapical radiographs

quote: In the augmented and open-access external validation cohort, a sensitivity of 81.4% (95% CI: 73.7%-89.1%) and 85.2% (95% CI: 83.0%-87.4%) with an average number of 0.22 and 1.19 FP lesions and DSCs of 0.70 (95% CI: 0.66-0.73) and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.77-0.78) were calculated, respectively.

title: Comprehensive Performance Testing and External Validation of an AI Algorithm to Detect and Segment Brain Metastases
outcome: AI performance across multiple datasets and institutions
effect: Performance varied across three datasets: sensitivity 90.0% (FDA multi-institutional), 81.4% (augmented), 85.2% (open-access UCSF-BMSR); DSC 0.86, 0.70, 0.78.
quote: This AI algorithm demonstrated promising performance via three unique datasets.

title: Comprehensive Performance Testing and External Validation of an AI Algorithm to Detect and Segment Brain Metastases
outcome: Physician qualitative rating of AI contours needing revision

title: Comprehensive Performance Testing and External Validation of an AI Algorithm to Detect and Segment Brain Metastases
outcome: Rate of AI contours requiring major physician revision
effect: 46.3% of contours in augmented external validation required major revisions, so authors conclude the tool needs physician oversight rather than autonomous use.
quote: However, given the notable rate of contour revisions, these findings support its clinical role not as an autonomous system, but as a human-in-the-loop tool requiring physician oversight.

title: Image-Quality-Aware Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Automated Structured OCT Report Generation in Glaucoma Evaluation
outcome: Performance stratified by glaucoma severity
effect: RNFL thinning detection was better in moderate-to-advanced glaucoma, especially temporal sectors, while nasal performance was better for mild cases; not stratified by site or device.
quote: Stratified analysis revealed better RNFL thinning detection in moderate-to-advanced glaucoma cases, especially in temporal sectors, while performance in nasal regions was better for mild cases.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Generated Versus Professional Society Patient Education Materials in Gastroenterology, Surgery, Ophthalmology, and Anesthesiology: A Comparative Analysis of Readability and Health Literacy Metrics
outcome: Readability (Flesch-Kincaid), quality, understandability, actionability of AI vs society patient materials by specialty
effect: Surgery: AI lower reading level and higher quality/understandability/actionability (p<0.001). Anesthesiology: AI more readable (p<0.001). Ophthalmology: AI more readable but society higher quality/understandability. Gastroenterology: AI higher reading level (p<0.001).
quote: In gastroenterology, AI materials had higher reading levels (p<0.001) with no differences in quality or usability.

title: Performance stability despite iteration: evaluating DeepSeek and ChatGPT on Chinese medical licensing examinations
outcome: Exam-style benchmark accuracy versus clinical risk of errors
effect: High exam accuracy (DeepSeek-V3.2 94.7%, ChatGPT-5.2 89.3% on 2025 CNMLE), yet error analysis found a substantial proportion of high-risk clinical errors across model versions.
quote: Error analysis showed no significant differences across model versions in error type classification or clinical risk rating, despite a substantial proportion of high-risk clinical errors.

title: Bedside Triage by Large Language Models in Acute Pancreatitis: A Scenario-Based Comparative Evaluation of GPT-4, GPT-5, and Gemini
outcome: Output reproducibility across three repeated runs at temperature 0.0
effect: Internal consistency across three repeated runs was 100% with deterministic settings.
quote: With deterministic settings, internal consistency across three repeated runs was 100%.

title: Bedside Triage by Large Language Models in Acute Pancreatitis: A Scenario-Based Comparative Evaluation of GPT-4, GPT-5, and Gemini
outcome: Unwarranted certainty in outputs under missing data
effect: Unwarranted certainty under missing data occurred in 12/20 GPT-4, 7/20 GPT-5, and 15/20 Gemini outputs.
quote: All models demonstrated clinically relevant failure modes, particularly unwarranted certainty under missing data; this occurred in 12/20 GPT-4, 7/20 GPT-5, and 15/20 Gemini outputs.
sample_unit: acute pancreatitis scenarios (15 hypothetical vignettes, 5 de-identified real-case patterns)

title: Performance of next-generation AI chatbots in colorectal cancer knowledge assessment: a comparative pilot study of ChatGPT-5.1, Gemini-3Pro Preview, DeepSeek-V3.2, Kimi K2 Thinking, Qwen3-Max and Claude Opus 4.5
outcome: Accuracy of LLM chatbots on colorectal cancer guideline MCQs under zero-shot constrained prompting
effect: Overall accuracy was low: Kimi K2 Thinking 27.74%, Claude Opus 4.5 26.28%, Gemini 3 Pro 16.06%, DeepSeek V3.2 15.33%, GPT-5.1 14.60%, Qwen3-Max 13.87%.
quote: Overall accuracy was low: Kimi K2 Thinking 27.74%, SD = 0.45, Claude Opus 4.5 26.28%, SD = 0.44, Gemini 3 Pro 16.06%, SD = 0.37, DeepSeek V3.2 15.33%, SD = 0.36, GPT-5.1 14.60%, SD = 0.35, and Qwen3-Max 13.87%, SD = 0.34.

title: Performance of next-generation AI chatbots in colorectal cancer knowledge assessment: a comparative pilot study of ChatGPT-5.1, Gemini-3Pro Preview, DeepSeek-V3.2, Kimi K2 Thinking, Qwen3-Max and Claude Opus 4.5
outcome: LLM clinical knowledge accuracy against current colorectal cancer guidelines
effect: Accuracy 13.87%-27.74% on 137 guideline-based MCQs; four failure patterns including fact retrieval error and hallucinations; module-wise disparities (Kimi 37.04% vs Qwen3-Max 7.41% in Endoscopic Imaging).
quote: Qualitative analysis revealed four failure patterns: semantic association bias, hierarchical logic failure, fact retrieval error, and hallucinations.

title: Generalization of AI-Based Gestational Age Assessment Using Blind Sweep Ultrasonography
outcome: Gestational age MAE reported separately by site (Chicago vs Nairobi) and probe
effect: Adapted model MAE 4.1 days (95% CI 3.5-4.7) in Chicago and 4.3 days (95% CI 3.8-4.8) in Nairobi; overall noninferior to clinical standard (4.2 vs 4.5 days).
quote: The adapted model achieved an MAE of 4.1 days (95% CI, 3.5-4.7) in Chicago and 4.3 days (95% CI, 3.8-4.8 days) in Nairobi.
sample_unit: participants (pregnant women) in the primary evaluation set

title: Large language model-generated clinical summaries in emergency departments: A blinded comparison study
outcome: Blinded physician ratings of LLM vs physician-authored ED one-liner summaries on accuracy, completeness, utility
effect: LLM summaries rated higher: accuracy 4.18 vs 3.40 (β=0.78; 95% CI 0.50-1.07); completeness 3.69 vs 3.25 (β=0.44); clinical utility 3.88 vs 3.21 (β=0.67).
quote: We found that across all dimensions, LLM-generated summaries received higher ratings than physician-authored summaries.

title: Effectiveness of Humanized AI Avatars and Messenger Gender for Dental Postprocedure Instructions: Two Randomized Experiments
outcome: Effect of AI-identity disclosure on intention to comply and return to same dentist
effect: Disclosure did not change intention to follow instructions but lowered likelihood of returning to same dentist (P<.01; Cohen d 0.35 and 0.37 for disclosed humanized and disclosed animated AI vs real person).
quote: Prior disclosure that the video was AI generated resulted in a lower willingness to return to the same dentist than the real-person condition ( P <.01; Cohen d =0.35 and 0.37 for the disclosed humanized AI and disclosed animated AI conditions, respectively).

title: Effectiveness of Humanized AI Avatars and Messenger Gender for Dental Postprocedure Instructions: Two Randomized Experiments
outcome: AI disclosure effects on trust and compliance
effect: Disclosure effects on following instructions were non-significant; return-to-dentist willingness lower, P<.01, Cohen d=0.35 and 0.37.
quote: Prior disclosure that the video was AI generated resulted in a lower willingness to return to the same dentist than the real-person condition ( P <.01; Cohen d =0.35 and 0.37 for the disclosed humanized AI and disclosed animated AI conditions, respectively).

title: Effectiveness of Humanized AI Avatars and Messenger Gender for Dental Postprocedure Instructions: Two Randomized Experiments
outcome: gender subgroup effect on compliance intention
effect: Women: female avatar 6.37 vs male avatar 6.69; 95% CI −0.66 to 0.00; P=.05; Cohen d=−0.35.
quote: However, women reported a significantly lower intention to comply when the video featured a female-presenting humanized avatar (mean 6.37, SD 1.24) than when it featured the man version (mean 6.69, SD 0.50; 95% CI −0.66 to 0.00; P =.05; Cohen d =−0.35).

title: Effectiveness of Humanized AI Avatars and Messenger Gender for Dental Postprocedure Instructions: Two Randomized Experiments
outcome: intention to comply and likelihood of returning to dentist
effect: AI disclosure did not affect intention to comply (non-significant at 95% CI) but reduced likelihood of returning to same dentist vs real person (P<.01; Cohen d=0.35 disclosed humanized, d=0.37 disclosed animated).
quote: AI disclosure did not affect intention to comply but reduced the reported likelihood of returning to the same dentist.

title: Evaluating the human-artificial intelligence interaction in optical diagnosis of early colorectal carcinoma through endoscopist responses to simulated artificial intelligence: a multinational online study
outcome: Endoscopist diagnostic performance decreased after receiving simulated AI diagnosis (inappropriate response to AI)

title: Evaluating the human-artificial intelligence interaction in optical diagnosis of early colorectal carcinoma through endoscopist responses to simulated artificial intelligence: a multinational online study
outcome: Human-AI team performance versus endoscopists alone, including inappropriate reliance on AI

quote: Inappropriate response to AI was observed in 28.2 % of endoscopists.

title: Chatbot Use by Patients Seeking Urogynecologic Consultation: A Randomized Trial
outcome: Readability of chatbot responses to patients

title: Chatbot Use by Patients Seeking Urogynecologic Consultation: A Randomized Trial
outcome: Patient visit satisfaction following peri-visit chatbot use

title: Treatment effects prediction and clinical decision-making system for retinal vein occlusion by artificial intelligence
outcome: Clinician predictive performance with versus without AI assistance in reader study

title: Treatment effects prediction and clinical decision-making system for retinal vein occlusion by artificial intelligence
outcome: AI retreatment prediction accuracy compared with retinal specialists on same data

title: Treatment effects prediction and clinical decision-making system for retinal vein occlusion by artificial intelligence
outcome: Retreatment prediction AUC in internal versus external test datasets

title: Automated risk scoring for venous thromboembolism using large language models with expert knowledge-augmented prompting: a multicenter validation study
outcome: VTE scoring accuracy

title: Automating clinical history extraction for flow cytometry panel selection using an EHR-integrated large language model

title: Automating clinical history extraction for flow cytometry panel selection using an EHR-integrated large language model
outcome: Comparison of LLM against current CLS workflow on same cases
effect: ChatEHR matched CLS on history extraction (78% vs 78%) but was worse on panel selection (47% vs 78%); processing time 20.3 s vs 41 s.
quote: ChatEHR achieved comparable accuracy to CLS in extracting and categorizing prior hematologic diagnoses (78% vs. 78%).

title: K-anonymity decay in multi-turn clinical large language model conversations

title: K-anonymity decay in multi-turn clinical large language model conversations
outcome: Cumulative quasi-identifier disclosure across multi-turn LLM prompts eroding anonymity beyond the minimum necessary

sample_unit: simulated patients sampled from 133,262 synthetic patients

quote: Of 5,000 randomly sampled patients, 79.9% (3,994; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 78.8% to 81.0%) reached k < 5 at some point during their disclosure sequence, while 86.2% (4,311; 95% CI: 85.2 to 87.2%) reached k < 11 .

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based CTA Software for Real-World Detection of Large-Vessel Occlusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based CTA Software for Real-World Detection of Large-Vessel Occlusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke
outcome: Time to diagnostic conclusion with versus without AI assistance across reader experience levels

title: Evaluation of an AI Medical Scribe After 236,153 Notes Generated Across Care Levels in a European Health System: Mixed Methods Retrospective Observational Study

quote: Following the introduction of the AI medical scribe, the estimated time spent on documentation per note was lower than before (4.72 vs 6.69 minutes; -29%, P<.001).

title: Simulation of covariate and concept drift in machine learning hospital admission prediction from emergency triage

title: Psychometric characterization of human and artificial intelligence performance on cardiology residency in-service examination items

title: Psychometric characterization of human and artificial intelligence performance on cardiology residency in-service examination items

effect: ChatGPT-4.5-preview (77% accuracy, mean weight 377.5/550) and Gemini-2.5_05-06 (74%, 365/550) outperformed human experts (64%, 253.5/550); p<0.05, Cohen's D 2.18 and 1.98.

title: Cross-model consistency of AI-generated exercise prescriptions: A repeated generation study across three large language models

title: Triage safety of patient-facing AI chatbots for nipple discharge: A guideline-informed assessment of red-flag recognition and patient actionability

effect: 46 of 77 PROMs (59.7%) contained at least one content-related error; response scales altered in 23%, recall timeframes omitted in 18%, items combined in 16%.
quote: Despite improvements in readability, 46 of the 77 PROMs (59.7%) contained at least one content-related error following ChatGPT revision ( Table 2 ).

title: ChatGPT improves readability in validated spine patient-reported outcome measures
outcome: readability after sixth-grade rewriting
effect: Word count decreased by 18% and all readability indices improved (p < .001), but 46/77 PROMs (59.7%) had ≥1 content error.
quote: ChatGPT 4.0 substantially improved the readability of validated spine PROMs but frequently introduced structural modifications affecting validated content.

title: Assessing the concordance between ChatGPT-4 and EAU guidelines indications in bladder cancer management: a real-world study
outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT-4 therapeutic recommendations with EAU guidelines-based urologist plans
effect: Overall agreement poor (Cohen's K=-0.06); first-time BCa K=0.23; MIBC K=0.88; recurrent K=-0.24; II look TURBT K=-0.6; aligned with guidelines for early radical cystectomy in only 3 of 21 cases.
quote: Overall agreement between urologist and ChatGPT recommendations was poor (Cohen's K=-0.06).

title: Examining explainable artificial intelligence in TNM staging with PET-CT: a user-centred observation study
outcome: Radiologists' adoption likelihood and usefulness of explanations for confirming or challenging AI staging recommendations
effect: All explanation approaches significantly increased willingness to adopt versus black-box (p < 0.05); explanations useful for confirming or challenging AI staging (p < 0.001).
quote: All explanation approaches significantly increased radiologists' willingness to adopt the AI system compared to a black-box model (p < 0.05).

title: Examining explainable artificial intelligence in TNM staging with PET-CT: a user-centred observation study
outcome: Explanation usefulness for clinician scrutiny
effect: Explanations were useful for confirming or challenging AI staging recommendations, p < 0.001.
quote: Explanations were consistently considered useful in enabling participants to confirm or challenge AI staging recommendations (p < 0.001).

title: Design and Preliminary Testing of the CardioCare System in Health Checkup Centers: Implementation Report
outcome: Attendance at follow-up clinic among high-risk individuals invited after risk flagging
effect: 181 of 2069 invited high-risk individuals (8.7%) attended at least 1 in-person visit; engaged patients gave positive feedback, but low uptake indicated significant barriers.
quote: However, patient engagement was low: of the 2069 high-risk individuals invited for follow-up care, 181 (8.7%) attended at least 1 in-person visit at the clinic.
sample_unit: high-risk older adults invited for follow-up

title: Large Language Models to Extract Cancer Staging Data From Clinical Documentation at Scale
outcome: Precision on two cancer types not used in training, versus trained cancer types
effect: Relation-level precision ranged 0.77 to 1.0 for the three trained cancers and 0.83 to 1.0 for breast and prostate cancers without further training.
quote: Relation-level precision across the six attributes ranged from 0.77 to 1.0 for the first three cancers and, without further training, 0.83 to 1.0 for two additional cancers.

title: fAI-BRO: a multimodal AI decision-support system to address diagnostic delay in fibromyalgia syndrome
outcome: Overestimated performance from post hoc thresholds without external validation
effect: Thresholds were optimised post hoc via Youden's J on the same 100 patients (91% accuracy, AUC 0.96); authors state external validation is needed before clinical deployment.
quote: Post hoc optimised thresholds require external validation before clinical deployment.

title: Impact of an AI algorithm for multi-day prediction of incident atrial fibrillation on clinical decision-making: PROVISION-AF study
outcome: Physician AF risk discrimination with versus without AI assistance in simulated cases
effect: AI assistance improved physicians' AF risk discrimination (AUROC 0.573 to 0.650) and NPV (0.764 to 0.839); NRI 0.127 for non-AF cases, p < 0.001.
quote: AI assistance significantly improved physicians' AF risk discrimination (AUROC 0.573 to 0.650) and negative predictive value (0.764 to 0.839), with significant net reclassification improvement for non-AF cases (NRI 0.127, p < 0.001).

title: Impact of an AI algorithm for multi-day prediction of incident atrial fibrillation on clinical decision-making: PROVISION-AF study
outcome: Model AUROC internal versus external cohort performance
effect: ECG-labeled AUROC 0.79 in internal EUMC cohort versus 0.74 in external BIDMC cohort; Holter-labeled 0.87 internal versus 0.75 prospective.
quote: For ECG-labeled outcomes, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.79 in the internal EUMC cohort and 0.74 in the external BIDMC cohort.

title: Clinical evaluation of large language model recommendations in melanoma: comparison with multidisciplinary tumor board decisions in a real-world cohort
outcome: LLM melanoma treatment recommendations rated against real MDT decisions across five domains
effect: ChatGPT-5 Thinking performed best, followed by ChatGPT-4o; Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2 rated less favorably; differences significant across all domains, largest in adjuvant/systemic treatment scenarios.
quote: ChatGPT-5 Thinking showed the strongest and most consistent overall performance, followed by ChatGPT-4o, while Gemini 2.5 Pro and DeepSeek-V3.2 were rated less favorably.

title: Artificial intelligence meets pediatric orthopedics: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, and Claude 3.5 in detecting supracondylar humeral fractures
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM fracture detection responses across three repeated runs (Fleiss' kappa)
effect: Consistency was very good for ChatGPT-4o (κ = 0.69) and Gemini 2.0 (κ = 0.61), and good for Claude 3.5 (κ = 0.44).
quote: Response consistency was very good for ChatGPT-4o (κ = 0.69) and Gemini 2.0 (κ = 0.61), good for Claude 3.5 (κ = 0.44).

title: Artificial intelligence meets pediatric orthopedics: A comparative analysis of ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, and Claude 3.5 in detecting supracondylar humeral fractures
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of LLMs as standalone diagnostic tools for supracondylar fractures
effect: Sensitivity was 68.4% (Gemini 2.0), 58.7% (Claude 3.5), and 19.3% (ChatGPT-4o); specificity was low (33.1-36.0%), giving many missed fractures and false positives.
quote: Current LLMs demonstrate limited capability as independent diagnostic tools for pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures.

title: Frontline Health Workers' Perspectives of the World Health Organization Skin Neglected Tropical Diseases App in Kenya: Qualitative Study on AI-Embedded mHealth Implementation
outcome: FHW reliance on or deferral to AI diagnostic output
effect: Most FHWs used the app as an assistive tool, but a minority reported diagnostic deferral to the AI output, raising clinical autonomy concerns.
quote: While most FHWs used the app in line with its intended role as an assistive tool, a minority reported situations of diagnostic deferral to the AI output, highlighting potential considerations of clinical autonomy.

title: The pediatric transfer gap: How adult-ICU-trained machine-learning models degrade on pediatric intensive care patients
outcome: Discrimination and calibration recovery after target-domain retraining on local data
effect: RF ROC-AUC fell from 0.940 to 0.725 in younger children; retraining recovered 0.867; ECE rose from ≤0.010 to 0.142 and was restored below 0.01. Retraining on 5% (~180 patients) recovered most of the gap.
quote: Random Forest ROC-AUC fell from 0.940 (95% CI 0.912-0.968) on older children to 0.725 (0.703-0.746) on younger children, and target-domain retraining recovered 0.867 (0.842-0.890); ECE rose from ≤0.010 to 0.142 and was restored below 0.01.

title: The pediatric transfer gap: How adult-ICU-trained machine-learning models degrade on pediatric intensive care patients
outcome: Model performance when transferred from adult/older-child cohorts to a new younger population
effect: Discrimination fell from 0.940 to 0.725 in younger children; adult-ICU models became severely miscalibrated (ECE up to 0.285); neonates AUC 0.587 (ECE 0.249).
quote: Vital-sign-based mortality models trained on older children or directly observed adult-ICU data lose discrimination and become severely miscalibrated when applied to younger children, with neonates worst affected.

title: The pediatric transfer gap: How adult-ICU-trained machine-learning models degrade on pediatric intensive care patients
outcome: Performance across age-band subgroups hidden by aggregate metrics
effect: Performance fell monotonically with age, from 0.992 in preschool children to 0.587 in neonates (ECE 0.249).
quote: Performance fell monotonically with age, from 0.992 in preschool children to 0.587 in neonates (ECE 0.249).

title: The pediatric transfer gap: How adult-ICU-trained machine-learning models degrade on pediatric intensive care patients
outcome: Dataset shift between development and deployment populations degrading performance
effect: Adult vs pediatric vitals showed large shifts (heart-rate d=+2.75, respiratory-rate d=+3.06) with ECE rising to 0.285 and discrimination loss in younger children.
quote: In the directly observed adult-ICU Experiment B the domain shift was confirmed with directly observed vitals (heart-rate Cohen's d=+2.75, respiratory-rate d=+3.06) and manifested mainly as severe miscalibration (ECE rising to 0.285) with a smaller, model-dependent discrimination change, again removed by target-domain retraining.

title: The pediatric transfer gap: How adult-ICU-trained machine-learning models degrade on pediatric intensive care patients
outcome: Model performance when applied outside validated population
effect: Models trained on adults or older children lost discrimination and were miscalibrated in younger children, worst in neonates.
quote: Vital-sign-based mortality models trained on older children or directly observed adult-ICU data lose discrimination and become severely miscalibrated when applied to younger children, with neonates worst affected.

title: Ambient AI scribe in pediatric outpatient visits: documentation burden, quality, and scale-up limits
outcome: Ambient scribe documentation quality, usability, corrections needed, time, and uneven adoption across clinicians
effect: Documentation quality improved (overall median 23 vs 17; p=0.008), but 67% reported technical issues, 33% needed extensive corrections, and adoption was under one-third of trained clinicians.
quote: Fifty-five percent of users reported being satisfied or very satisfied, although 67% reported technical issues and 33% reported requiring extensive corrections.

title: Real-time hallucination detection and intervention in medical LLMs via calibrated hidden-state probes
outcome: Hallucination detection and flagging of generated medical answers under false-positive-rate caps
effect: EDR@5 up to 0.390 (PubMedQA) and 0.352 (MedHallu) at strict cap γ≤0.10, rising to 0.587 with 29%-59% hallucination reduction at monitoring cap γ≤0.20.
quote: The trigger fires roughly 10-35 tokens before error onset, whereas a post-hoc check has zero lead time by construction.

title: Real-time hallucination detection and intervention in medical LLMs via calibrated hidden-state probes
outcome: Automated real-time hidden-state probe detecting erroneous LLM outputs without human review, with latency
effect: Probe gives viable detection across all backbone-dataset combinations, 29%-59% hallucination reduction at γ≤0.20, ~10ms latency per answer versus ~10s for multi-sample baselines.
quote: Probe latency is ∼10ms per answer versus ∼10s for multi-sample baselines.

title: The Illusion of Precision: Artificial Intelligence Cannot yet Reliably Predict Individual Outcomes in Infrapopliteal Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs and stability across prompt formats (naive vs structured)
effect: Internal reproducibility (ICC >0.500) and distributional stability across prompts were high, but this consistency was based on nondiscriminatory safety biases, masking failure to identify high-risk patients.
quote: While internal reproducibility (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICCs] >0.500) and distributional stability across prompts were surprisingly high, this consistency proved deceptive, based entirely on nondiscriminatory safety biases.

title: The Illusion of Precision: Artificial Intelligence Cannot yet Reliably Predict Individual Outcomes in Infrapopliteal Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia
outcome: Calibration (Brier score) versus discrimination (sensitivity) of LLM outcome predictions
effect: DS naive Brier score 0.068 at 6 months suggested high probabilistic accuracy, but all models had sensitivity 0.00 at 6-month and 1-year horizons; calibration masked discriminatory failure.
quote: However, this mathematical precision masked a failure in clinical utility: all models exhibited a sensitivity of 0.00 at 6-month and 1-year horizons.

title: Safety boundary maintenance in consumer AI systems responding to pediatric health queries: a cross-platform benchmark evaluation under naturalistic and adversarially pressured conditions
outcome: Safety-appropriate rate with versus without safety-oriented system prompt under adversarial caregiver pressure
effect: Safety-oriented system prompt deployment improved safety-appropriate rates by 5.9 percentage points across all four models; overall safety-appropriate rate was 95.5%.
quote: Safety-oriented system prompt deployment improved safety-appropriate rates by 5.9 percentage points across all four models.
sample_unit: pediatric health queries (300 authentic caregiver queries and 300 matched adversarial variants)

title: Safety boundary maintenance in consumer AI systems responding to pediatric health queries: a cross-platform benchmark evaluation under naturalistic and adversarially pressured conditions
outcome: Safety Composite Score under adversarial caregiver pressure patterns versus authentic queries
effect: Adversarial pressure was associated with higher, not lower, scores for all four models; false expertise claims were the most vulnerability-inducing pattern.
quote: False expertise claims were the most vulnerability-inducing pressure pattern, whereas emotional escalation was associated with the highest scores.
sample_unit: pediatric health queries (300 authentic caregiver queries and 300 matched adversarial variants)

title: Detecting Performance Drift in AI Models for Medical Image Analysis Using CUSUM Chart
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Detection delay and false alarm interval of CUSUM monitoring for simulated abrupt data drift
effect: With drift of 1.5 SD, CUSUM detected changes in test negativity rate within an average of 5 days, with ~293 days between false alarms.
quote: Our results indicate that, when the magnitude of the drift is 1.5 times the standard deviation of the performance metric, CUSUM is able to detect changes in the test negativity rate of an AI model within an average of 5 days following the onset of performance drift, with a long duration ( ∼ 293 days) between false alarms.
sample_unit: mammography examinations (EMBED dataset), simulated daily samples

title: Detecting Performance Drift in AI Models for Medical Image Analysis Using CUSUM Chart
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Tuning CUSUM alarm thresholds to balance false alarms against detection delay
effect: CUSUM sensitivity can be controlled to balance mean time between false alarms and delay in detecting a true performance change; almost no false alarms in 60 days at 40 samples/day.
quote: We demonstrate that the sensitivity of CUSUM can be controlled to balance the mean time between false alarms and the delay in detecting a true change in performance.
sample_unit: mammography examinations (EMBED dataset), simulated daily samples

title: Diagnostic capability of large language models in critically ill patients: a prospective single-centre study comparing ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini with emergency physicians
outcome: Reference diagnosis inclusion in preliminary and differential lists, LLMs versus emergency physicians
effect: Physicians included the reference diagnosis in 83.9% (top-5 preliminary) and 98.3% (top-3 differential) of cases, significantly exceeding every LLM (all p < 0.001).
quote: Physicians contained the reference diagnosis within their top-5 preliminary and top-3 differential lists in 83.9% and 98.3% of cases, respectively, significantly exceeding every LLM (all p < 0.001).

title: Clinical Safety and Reliability of Large Language Models in Answering Hemorrhoid-Related Patient Questions: A Comparative Study of ChatGPT, Gemini, and DeepSeek
outcome: Recognition and communication of risk in high-risk hemorrhoid scenarios (alarm symptoms, bleeding, acute pain)
effect: No model gave harmful recommendations or guidance likely to cause substantial diagnostic delay; DeepSeek showed disproportionately urgent or alarmist language in some higher-risk scenarios; model divergence larger in clinically significant scenarios.
quote: No model generated directly harmful medical recommendations or explicit guidance likely to result in substantial diagnostic delay.

title: Between Accessibility and Reliability: High Confidence, Low Control in General-Purpose Multimodal Models for Hip Fracture Radiograph Interpretation
outcome: Model performance when prompts contained incorrect laterality cues versus correct cues
effect: Incorrect laterality cues degraded performance from 90.7% to 66.4% in GPT-5.4 and from 97.7% to 57.0% in Gemini.
quote: Incorrect laterality cues markedly degraded performance, from 90.7% to 66.4% in GPT-5.4 and from 97.7% to 57.0% in Gemini.
sample_unit: surgically confirmed hip fracture AP pelvis radiographs

title: Between Accessibility and Reliability: High Confidence, Low Control in General-Purpose Multimodal Models for Hip Fracture Radiograph Interpretation
outcome: Whether self-reported confidence distinguished correct from incorrect outputs
effect: Both models frequently remained highly confident when wrong; self-reported confidence did not reliably distinguish correct from incorrect outputs.
quote: Both models frequently remained highly confident when wrong, and self-reported confidence did not reliably distinguish correct from incorrect outputs.
sample_unit: surgically confirmed hip fracture AP pelvis radiographs

title: Potential and Pitfalls of Multimodal Large Language Models in Cerebral Palsy Hip Surveillance: A Radiographic Interpretation Study Assessing Educational Utility
outcome: Radiographic interpretation accuracy and management recommendation specificity of MLLMs for CP hip displacement
effect: Diagnostic hallucinations observed (Claude misidentified non-operative cases as bilateral hip replacements); recommendations were generic and failed to measure or apply migration percentage thresholds.
quote: While management recommendations were clinically relevant, they remained generic rather than patient-specific, failing to measure or apply migration percentage thresholds.
sample_unit: deidentified pediatric pelvic radiographs (with 9 caregiver prompts each; ~95 responses per model)

title: Potential and Pitfalls of Multimodal Large Language Models in Cerebral Palsy Hip Surveillance: A Radiographic Interpretation Study Assessing Educational Utility
outcome: Whether MLLM diagnostic accuracy supports use as stand-alone diagnostic tool
effect: Significant radiographic hallucinations and lack of specific evidence-based guidance preclude standalone diagnostic use; MLLMs suggested as educational adjuncts requiring expert oversight.
quote: However, significant radiographic hallucinations and a lack of specific, evidence-based guidance preclude their use as standalone diagnostic tools.
sample_unit: deidentified pediatric pelvic radiographs (with 9 caregiver prompts each; ~95 responses per model)

title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Stage CNN Framework with External Validation
outcome: Performance drop from internal to external knee X-ray dataset under domain shift
effect: External AUC 0.72–0.89 but accuracy only 31–44%, indicating calibration drift and domain shift between internal and external datasets.
quote: Although most models achieved relatively high AUC values (0.72–0.89), the corresponding external test accuracy remained substantially lower (31–44%), suggesting the presence of calibration drift and domain shift between the internal and external datasets.
sample_unit: knee radiographs (116 patients internal; 150 external Kaggle images)

title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Stage CNN Framework with External Validation
outcome: Osteopenia recall and balanced accuracy after class-prior boosting and recalibration on external data
effect: Class-prior boosting raised balanced accuracy from 38.0% to 48.0%, macro F1 from 0.259 to 0.416, and Osteopenia recall from 2% to 78%; Normal recall fell from 22% to 6%. Recalibration alone was insufficient.
quote: Most importantly, Osteopenia recall improved dramatically from 2% to 78%, transforming the model from effectively blind to the intermediate disease stage into a clinically meaningful early-detection screening system.
sample_unit: knee radiographs (116 patients internal; 150 external Kaggle images)

title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Stage CNN Framework with External Validation
outcome: Overestimated performance from internal versus external validation
effect: Internal test accuracy about 67–75% versus external accuracy 31–44%; external set was isolated and used once, revealing a performance gap.
quote: This limitation is reflected in the observed performance gap between internal and external validation, highlighting the challenges of generalization across different imaging domains.
sample_unit: knee radiographs (116 patients internal; 150 external Kaggle images)

title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Stage CNN Framework with External Validation
outcome: Discrimination (AUC) masking poor calibration and threshold-based performance
effect: High external AUC (0.87–0.89) masked poor threshold-based accuracy (~42–43%); subgroup/class-specific Osteopenia sensitivity was near zero.
quote: Importantly, high discrimination performance should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical readiness.
sample_unit: knee radiographs (116 patients internal; 150 external Kaggle images)

title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Stage CNN Framework with External Validation
outcome: Calibration drift under external domain shift
effect: Osteopenia predicted probabilities collapsed below 0.30 externally, with baseline Osteopenia recall of 2%; Osteoporosis class overconfident.
quote: From Table 10 , reliability analysis revealed that the Osteopenia class experienced near-complete probability collapse, with predicted probabilities consistently remaining below 0.30 during external testing.
sample_unit: knee radiographs (116 patients internal; 150 external Kaggle images)

title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Stage CNN Framework with External Validation
outcome: External validation detected calibration/domain shift
effect: AUC 0.72–0.89 but external accuracy 31–44%, revealing calibration drift and domain shift.
quote: Although most models achieved relatively high AUC values (0.72–0.89), the corresponding external test accuracy remained substantially lower (31–44%), suggesting the presence of calibration drift and domain shift between the internal and external datasets.
sample_unit: knee radiographs (116 patients internal; 150 external Kaggle images)

title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Stage CNN Framework with External Validation
outcome: Dataset provenance incompleteness
effect: External dataset lacked acquisition protocols, equipment, DXA procedures, quality control, and label generation details.
quote: As the dataset was collected and curated by an independent source, detailed information regarding image acquisition protocols, imaging equipment, DXA procedures, image quality control, and label generation was not fully available.
sample_unit: knee radiographs (116 patients internal; 150 external Kaggle images)

title: Opportunistic Osteoporosis Screening from Routine Knee Radiographs Using a Multi-Stage CNN Framework with External Validation
outcome: Isotonic recalibration external recall
effect: Normal recall improved 14% to 22%, but Osteopenia recall remained 2%.
quote: Although recalibration improved Normal recall from 14% to 22%, Osteopenia recall remained unchanged at only 2%, indicating that probability recalibration alone was insufficient to recover the suppressed Osteopenia decision region under external domain shift (see Table 9 ).
sample_unit: knee radiographs (116 patients internal; 150 external Kaggle images)

title: Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model for Angiographic Prediction of Coronary Physiology
outcome: iFR agreement and ischemia discrimination
effect: RAG improved MAE 0.064 to 0.029, r 0.205 to 0.830, limits ±0.156 to ±0.075, and AUC 0.58 to 0.93.
quote: Within this selected cohort, several key findings emerged: (1) continuous agreement with invasive iFR improved, with reduced absolute error (MAE 0.064 to 0.029) and stronger correlation (r = 0.205 to 0.830, p < 0.001), accompanied by narrower limits of agreement (±0.156 to ±0.075); (2) discrimination for ischemia (iFR ≤ 0.89) also improved (AUC 0.58 to 0.93, p = 0.010); (3) qualitative analysis demonstrated a systematic shift from morphology-dominant procedural framing toward earlier integration of physiologic thresholds, guideline references, and graded uncertainty.

title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
outcome: Hallucination and faithfulness scores of RAG vs baseline LLM, expert and LLM-judge rated
effect: RAG hallucination mean 1.4 vs baseline 2.3 (P<.001); faithfulness 4.5 vs 3.7 (P<.001); overall accuracy 91.3% vs 68%. Confounded by prompt instruction differences.
quote: Pairwise comparisons confirmed that all 3 enhanced models significantly reduced hallucinations relative to the baseline ( P <.001 for all), while no statistically significant differences were observed among the fine-tuned, RAG, and hybrid approaches ( Figure 12 ).
sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
outcome: Reading grade level (FKGL) of LLM patient-facing postoperative responses vs 6th-8th grade recommendation
effect: Mean FKGL 9.7 baseline, 11.3 FT, 11.8 RAG, 10.6 hybrid; only 10 FT and 7 RAG/hybrid responses met the ≤8th-grade threshold (25 baseline).
quote: Only 10 responses in the fine-tuned model and 7 responses each in the RAG and RAG+fine-tuning models met the ≤8th-grade FKGL benchmark.
sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
outcome: Refusal of out-of-scope queries with vs without scope/refusal instructions
effect: Baseline refused 0/30 out-of-scope queries; FT 30/30, RAG 27/30, hybrid 30/30 with explicit refusal instructions. Authors note this reflects prompt compliance on previewed queries, not generalizable boundary recognition. Single-turn only.
quote: Accordingly, these findings primarily reflect compliance with predefined refusal instructions on previewed safety-query types rather than intrinsic or generalizable boundary-recognition ability.
sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
outcome: Refusal of out-of-scope requests by configurations with vs without refusal instructions
effect: Baseline 0/30 correct refusals vs 100% (FT), 90% (RAG), 100% (hybrid) with refusal instructions; safety queries were in validation set, single-turn, no adversarial prompting.
quote: The fine-tuning model appropriately refused 30 of 30 (100%) out-of-scope questions, whereas RAG refused 27 of 30 (90%), and RAG+fine-tuning again achieved 100% (30/30).
sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
outcome: Readability of AI-generated postoperative patient education outputs relative to recommended reading levels
effect: Enhanced models had FKGL 10.6-11.8 and lower FRE (35.1-40.0), exceeding AMA/NIH 6th-8th grade recommendations; baseline FKGL 9.7 also above.
quote: Although the enhanced models, particularly the hybrid configuration, achieved the highest accuracy, they also generated responses exceeding AMA and NIH-recommended patient education reading levels (sixth to eighth grade level) [ 39 ].
