title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
outcome: Recognition of emergency escalation and out-of-scope queries by configurations with vs without escalation/deferral instructions
effect: Enhanced configurations with predefined escalation/deferral prompts scored higher on safety/refusal (baseline 0/30 vs 90-100%); clinical accuracy including 20 emergency scenarios 85% baseline vs 96.7% hybrid; authors say partly scripted compliance; missed/unnecessary escalation not separately measured.
quote: Importantly, the emergency escalation scenarios were associated with predefined safety prompting and prior exposure within the validation set for the enhanced configurations; therefore, a portion of the observed Clinical Medical Accuracy likely reflects compliance with scripted escalation behavior in addition to clinical reasoning performance.
sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
outcome: Accuracy of candidate LLM configurations (fine-tuned, RAG, hybrid) compared against baseline LLM on same queries
effect: Overall accuracy baseline 68% vs FT 92.7%, RAG 91.3%, hybrid 97.3% (P<.001); pairwise all enhanced significantly better than baseline.
quote: Pairwise comparisons demonstrated that all 3 knowledge-enhanced approaches significantly outperformed the baseline model.
sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
outcome: evaluation-set leakage
effect: 50 safety-category queries were verbatim in validation; 0/100 in-domain queries were exact duplicates.
quote: However, the 50 safety-category queries (emergency and out-of-scope prompts) were present verbatim in the validation set.

title: Fine-Tuning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and Hybrid Large Language Models for Postoperative Decision Support: Comparative Analysis
outcome: out-of-scope refusal accuracy
effect: Baseline 0/30; FT 30/30; RAG 27/30; RAG+FT 30/30; overall P≤.001.
quote: Enhanced models also demonstrated higher safety or refusal accuracy than baseline; however, the baseline configuration did not receive equivalent safety or deferral instructions, which likely influenced these findings.
sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

title: Benchmarking of radiobiological NTCP models in head and neck radiotherapy using independent computational pipelines: an institutional validation study with machine learning augmentation
outcome: Institution-specific recalibration of NTCP model parameters versus published QUANTEC values
effect: Institutional parotid TD50 34.1 Gy vs QUANTEC 39.0 Gy (m 0.11 vs 0.18); traditional models performed acceptably after local calibration (LKB AUC 0.88-0.91).

title: Benchmarking of radiobiological NTCP models in head and neck radiotherapy using independent computational pipelines: an institutional validation study with machine learning augmentation
outcome: ANN and XGBoost versus best traditional NTCP model (LKB) discrimination on hold-out test set
effect: ANN AUC 0.93 vs LKB 0.89 (p=0.420) parotid; 0.95 vs 0.91 (p=0.380) oral cavity; 0.91 vs 0.88 (p=0.150) larynx; no significant differences; XGBoost overfit (test AUC 0.67-0.82).
quote: No statistically significant differences were observed between ANN and the best traditional model (LKB) for any organ.

title: Benchmarking of radiobiological NTCP models in head and neck radiotherapy using independent computational pipelines: an institutional validation study with machine learning augmentation
outcome: Agreement between two independent NTCP computational pipelines against predefined acceptance criteria
effect: Mean bias 0.8%, 95% limits of agreement -1.9% to +3.5%, meeting predefined criteria (bias <3%, limits within ±5%); max deviation 2.4%.
quote: The mean bias was 0.8%, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from −1.9% to +3.5%, meeting the predefined acceptability criteria (mean bias <3% and limits within ±5%).

title: Benchmarking of radiobiological NTCP models in head and neck radiotherapy using independent computational pipelines: an institutional validation study with machine learning augmentation
outcome: Training versus hold-out test AUC
effect: XGBoost training AUC 0.98–1.00 fell to test AUC 0.67–0.82, showing overfitting.
quote: Extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) models showed lower generalisation performance compared with ANN across all endpoints, with evidence of overfitting despite regularisation (training AUC 0.98–1.00; test AUC 0.67–0.82).

title: Benchmarking of radiobiological NTCP models in head and neck radiotherapy using independent computational pipelines: an institutional validation study with machine learning augmentation

outcome: Local performance of vendor AI against neuroradiologist reference standard on emergency CT data
effect: High AUROC (0.96-0.99) and sensitivity (0.85-0.92) locally across four solutions, but precision, specificity and volumetric agreement differed by vendor.
quote: However, meaningful differences emerged in confirmatory performance and volumetric agreement.

title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
outcome: Expert-rated dialogue quality with guideline knowledge base (V2/V3) vs role-only prompt (V1)
effect: V3 (knowledge base plus structured prompt) scored higher than V1 across all 6 dimensions (adjusted P<.05); Kruskal-Wallis all P<.001. Knowledge base confounded with slot-filling and formatting changes.
quote: Post hoc analyses using Dunn test with Bonferroni correction showed that prompt V3 scored higher than prompt V1 across all dimensions (adjusted P <.05).

title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
outcome: Expert-rated dialogue quality across iteratively refined prompt versions V1-V3
effect: Significant differences across all 6 dimensions (all P<.001); medians increased progressively from V1 to V3 with reduced dispersion.
quote: Overall differences among prompt versions were statistically significant across all 6 dimensions (Kruskal-Wallis test, all P values <.001).

title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
outcome: Personalization and clarity after adding simplified language and standardized formatting (V3 vs V2)
effect: V3 improved personalization and clarity (adjusted P=.02) and safety and fairness (adjusted P<.001) vs V2; other dimensions not significant.
quote: Compared with prompt V2, prompt V3 demonstrated statistically significant improvements only in personalization and clarity (adjusted P =.02) and safety and fairness (adjusted P <.001), whereas differences in the remaining dimensions did not reach statistical significance (adjusted P >.05).

title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
outcome: Unsafe or inappropriate outputs in real participant interactions reviewed by gastroenterologists
effect: 0/50 unsafe or inappropriate outputs; 50/50 (100%) guideline-concordant recommendations; 46/50 (92%) concordance with APCS risk stratification.
quote: Expert review confirmed that all chatbot-generated screening recommendations were consistent with current screening guidelines, and no inappropriate or unsafe outputs were identified during the study period.

title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
outcome: Screening recommendation concordance with current guidelines
effect: Guideline-concordant screening recommendations: 50 (100); unsafe or inappropriate outputs: 0 (0). Safety was assessed through expert review rather than downstream patient outcomes.
quote: Expert review confirmed that all chatbot-generated screening recommendations were consistent with current screening guidelines, and no inappropriate or unsafe outputs were identified during the study period.

title: A Guideline-Concordant Chatbot Framework for Structured Colorectal Cancer Screening: Multistage Feasibility Study
outcome: feasibility, safety, and guideline concordance
effect: During a limited clinical deployment, the chatbot collected complete risk information and generated guideline-concordant recommendations for 100% of the 50 participants.
quote: In phase 3, the optimized chatbot successfully collected complete CRC screening risk information and generated guideline-concordant screening recommendations for all participants (N=50).

title: Artificial Intelligence Large Language Models for Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation: Readabilty, Usability and Consistency
outcome: Readability of LLM answers (FRE, FKRGL, SMOG) for pelvic floor rehabilitation questions
effect: Significant SMOG differences among models at both evaluations (p<0.001), and for FKGL at the second evaluation only (p=0.006). Authors concluded that the answers were readable.
quote: ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Gemini provided readable, useful and repeatable answers to questions related to pelvic floor rehabilitation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Large Language Models for Pelvic Floor Rehabilitation: Readabilty, Usability and Consistency
outcome: Consistency of LLM responses across two evaluation time points
effect: Responses were evaluated at two separate time points. Authors concluded the answers were repeatable, and no numeric repeatability statistic is reported in the abstract.
quote: ChatGPT, DeepSeek and Gemini provided readable, useful and repeatable answers to questions related to pelvic floor rehabilitation.

title: DETERIO-LLM: enhancing traditional deterioration risk scores with clinical context and advanced reasoning
outcome: PPV and F1 of DETERIO-LLM versus comparators including eCART on same cohort
effect: DETERIO-LLM achieved PPV 30.6% and F1 37.3%, outperforming eCART and all comparators, with comparable sensitivity.
quote: DETERIO-LLM significantly improved predictive precision over all comparators.

title: Human perception of AI-generated post-treatment orthodontic facial images: factors associated with misclassification
outcome: Participants' ability to distinguish AI-enhanced from real post-treatment orthodontic images
effect: 63.2% misclassified AI-enhanced images as real; 18.5% misclassified real images as AI-generated; higher trust in AI content increased odds of misclassification (OR 1.38).
quote: A total of 63.2% of participants misclassified AI-enhanced images as real, whereas 18.5% misclassified real images as AI-generated.

title: Current Landscape of Generative AI Use as a Search Engine Among Resident Physicians: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Association of GenAI use with self-reported behaviors indicative of knowledge collapse or deskilling
effect: GenAI use was independently associated with favorable behaviors: thorough examination (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.18-1.70) and appropriate antimicrobial use (aOR 1.57, 95% CI 1.32-1.87). Only 13% (144/1110) of users relied on GenAI as primary reference for differential diagnoses.
quote: Although GenAI use was not associated with self-reported behaviors indicative of knowledge collapse at this stage, GenAI literacy among resident physicians in Japan remains limited, particularly among nonusers.

title: Current Landscape of Generative AI Use as a Search Engine Among Resident Physicians: Cross-Sectional Study
outcome: Resident physicians' GenAI literacy, including understanding of confabulation and ethical considerations
effect: Understanding of confabulation: 74.1% of users vs 58.4% of nonusers. Fairness examined by 47.3% and transparency by 49.8% overall; awareness lower among nonusers (41.5% and 43.8%).
quote: Although GenAI use was not associated with self-reported behaviors indicative of knowledge collapse at this stage, GenAI literacy among resident physicians in Japan remains limited, particularly among nonusers.

title: Multi-centre generalisability of deep learning-based dose prediction for head and neck radiotherapy using DAHANCA real-world data
venue: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
outcome: Dose prediction accuracy on external multi-centre data versus internal test data
effect: Model trained on single-centre data (388 plans) was tested on 560 external plans from six institutions. Median Dmean differences were -0.1 Gy for PTVs and 1.1 Gy for OARs across cohorts, supporting generalisability.
quote: Predictions closely matched clinically applied dose distributions with median D<sub>mean</sub> differences of -0.1 Gy [interquartile range -0.5, 0.3] for PTVs and 1.1 Gy [-0.6, 3.7] for OARs across cohorts.
sample_unit: treatment plans (42 internal test plans plus 560 national DAHANCA plans)

title: Multi-centre generalisability of deep learning-based dose prediction for head and neck radiotherapy using DAHANCA real-world data
venue: Radiotherapy and oncology : journal of the European Society for Therapeutic Radiology and Oncology
outcome: Deep learning dose prediction versus a simpler median-based model on the same data
effect: The deep learning model outperformed the median model. OAR Dmean difference was 1.1 Gy [-0.6, 3.7] versus -4.6 Gy [-14.6, 3.9] for the median model, which had larger interquartile ranges.
quote: The dose prediction model outperformed the median-based model, with prediction-plan differences within interquartile ranges observed across cohorts, supporting generalisability.
sample_unit: treatment plans (42 internal test plans plus 560 national DAHANCA plans)

title: Development and external validation of AI-ECG models in athlete pre-participation screening: Performance, limitations, and clinical implications
outcome: External validation AUROC of hospital-trained AI-ECG models in athlete screening population versus internal validation
effect: AUROC fell to 0.70 (95% CI 0.64-0.75) for VHD and 0.69 (95% CI 0.60-0.78) for CM; NPV ~99%, PPV ≤8%.
quote: External validation demonstrated substantial performance degradation compared with hospital-based internal validation.

title: Development and external validation of AI-ECG models in athlete pre-participation screening: Performance, limitations, and clinical implications
outcome: Performance transportability from hospital development population to low-prevalence athlete screening population
effect: Substantial degradation on external validation; AUROC 0.70 for VHD and 0.69 for CM; PPV ≤8% reflecting limited disease enrichment and prevalence dependence.
quote: Hospital-trained AI-ECG models demonstrated limited transportability to real-world athlete screening populations.

title: Development and external validation of AI-ECG models in athlete pre-participation screening: Performance, limitations, and clinical implications
outcome: Predictive values at local screening prevalence versus hospital-based performance
effect: NPV ~99% but PPV ≤8% at low prevalence (VHD 4.3%, CM 2.7%), showing strong prevalence dependence.
quote: Threshold analyses showed high negative predictive values (∼99%) but persistently low positive predictive values (≤8%), reflecting limited disease enrichment and strong prevalence dependence.

title: An explainable real-time artificial intelligence -assisted system to reduce intradialytic hypotension
venue: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi
outcome: Incidence of intradialytic hypotension with versus without AI assistance
effect: IDH incidence decreased from 16.42% to 13.09% after implementation of the AI system (P = 0.03).
quote: The incidence of IDH decreased significantly from 16.42% to 13.09% after implementation of the AI system (P = 0.03).

title: Evaluation of the performance and temporal variability of large language models in patient education regarding pneumothorax: a seven-day analysis
outcome: Quality and consistency of LLM outputs with optimized structured prompt (PROMPORT) versus zero-shot
effect: PROMPORT stabilized mDISCERN and JAMA profiles over time and reduced linguistic variance versus unprompted models, which showed significant temporal volatility (p < 0.05).
quote: In conclusion, while unprompted models exhibit marked baseline linguistic and quality variations, the strategic integration of robust prompt engineering successfully enforces the temporal stability and clarity required for reliable digital public health communication.

title: Evaluation of the performance and temporal variability of large language models in patient education regarding pneumothorax: a seven-day analysis
outcome: Reading level of chatbot pneumothorax patient education outputs
effect: Unprompted configurations consistently generated complex, high-school-level outputs; PROMPORT prompting compressed linguistic variance.
quote: Unprompted configurations consistently generated complex, high-school-level outputs, whereas the PROMPORT strategy successfully compressed linguistic variances and neutralized chronological algorithmic drift (p > 0.05).

title: Evaluation of the performance and temporal variability of large language models in patient education regarding pneumothorax: a seven-day analysis
outcome: temporal reproducibility of clinical quality
effect: Readability was stable (p > 0.05), but unprompted mDISCERN and JAMA profiles showed temporal volatility (p < 0.05), stabilized by optimized prompt constraints.
quote: Conversely, unprompted architectures exhibited significant temporal volatility in mDISCERN and JAMA profiles (p < 0.05), which was successfully stabilized by optimized prompt constraints.

title: Evaluation of the performance and temporal variability of large language models in patient education regarding pneumothorax: a seven-day analysis
outcome: readability of patient education outputs
effect: Unprompted configurations consistently generated complex, high-school-level outputs; PROMPORT compressed linguistic variances and neutralized drift (p > 0.05).
quote: Unprompted configurations consistently generated complex, high-school-level outputs, whereas the PROMPORT strategy successfully compressed linguistic variances and neutralized chronological algorithmic drift (p > 0.05).

title: Evaluating the quality, understandability, actionability, and readability of ChatGPT-generated patient information on overactive bladder: A cross-sectional study
outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-4o OAB patient information (FKGL, SMOG) versus recommended patient education standards
effect: Responses exceeded recommended standards; overall median FKGL 14.00 (range 7.61-17.11) and SMOG 12.34 (range 5.01-14.93).
quote: Readability analysis revealed that the responses exceeded recommended patient education standards, with overall median Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook scores of 14.00 (range: 7.61-17.11) and 12.34 (range: 5.01-14.93), respectively.

title: Evaluating the quality, understandability, actionability, and readability of ChatGPT-generated patient information on overactive bladder: A cross-sectional study
outcome: Reading grade level of AI-generated patient materials relative to recommended level
effect: Overall median FKGL 14.00 and SMOG 12.34, exceeding recommended patient education standards.
quote: Readability analysis revealed that the responses exceeded recommended patient education standards, with overall median Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level and Simple Measure of Gobbledygook scores of 14.00 (range: 7.61-17.11) and 12.34 (range: 5.01-14.93), respectively.

title: MAGMED: A clinically grounded LLM-guided synthetic augmentation framework for admission-time ICU mortality prediction
outcome: Cross-institutional performance degradation of mortality prediction under distribution shift
effect: Framework reported to demonstrate robust generalization under cross-institutional distribution shifts, mitigating performance degradation; no numbers given in abstract.
quote: Moreover, the proposed framework demonstrated robust generalization under cross-institutional distribution shifts, effectively mitigating the performance degradation commonly observed in multicenter settings.

title: Federated TinyML and digital twin framework for secure and resilient IoMT-based ICU monitoring
outcome: Critical-class recall under label-flipping poisoning attack, PBF versus FedAvg, Krum, Trimmed Mean, Coordinate Median
effect: Under a targeted label-flipping attack, PBF achieved 86.79% accuracy and 0.904 critical-class recall; PBF gave stronger protection of critical-class recall than the comparison aggregation methods.
quote: Comparative evaluation against FedAvg, Krum, Trimmed Mean, and Coordinate Median shows that PBF provides stronger protection of critical-class recall under adversarial conditions, although full prospective clinical validation remains outside the scope of this study.
sample_unit: synthetic ICU records across three non-IID hospital clients plus PhysioNet-based external dataset

title: Automating Case-Based Learning in Obstetrics and Gynecology: Validation of a Locally Deployed Large Language Model
outcome: LLM extraction accuracy and hallucination rate versus expert ground truth
effect: 96.0% accuracy for primary diagnoses, 92.0% for core teaching points; overall hallucination incidence 3.0%
quote: The LLM demonstrated high precision in extracting objective clinical data, achieving a 96.0% accuracy rate for primary diagnoses and 92.0% for core teaching points.
sample_unit: case abstracts (randomly selected subset of 3678 PubMed OB/GYN case abstracts rated by two educators)

title: Comparative Evaluation of ChatGPT and Gemini in Approximating Clinically Confirmed Diagnoses From Structured Numerical Pure-Tone Audiogram Data
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of two LLMs versus expert clinical diagnosis on same audiogram data
effect: ChatGPT-4o accuracy 60.8% (kappa 0.578) vs Gemini 1.5 Pro 86.1% (kappa 0.848); Gemini significantly higher, showing candidate performance differs on the same data.
quote: The findings suggest that Gemini 1.5 Pro demonstrated stronger performance, achieving an accuracy of 86.1%, whereas ChatGPT-4o achieved 60.8% in interpreting real-world pure-tone audiograms.

title: Quality of Tinnitus Information From Generative AI Systems and Web Search: An Expert‑Rated Comparative Study
venue: Otology & neurotology : official publication of the American Otological Society, American Neurotology Society [and] European Academy of Otology and Neurotology
outcome: Readability of AI responses to tinnitus questions (Flesch-Kincaid grade level)
effect: OpenEvidence had the lowest readability (FKGL 17.5; FRE 2.2, postgraduate level); general-purpose LLMs produced responses at a sixth-seventh grade reading level.
quote: OpenEvidence demonstrated the lowest readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 17.5; Flesch Reading Ease 2.2), corresponding to a postgraduate reading level, whereas general-purpose LLMs produced more accessible responses at a sixth-seventh grade reading level.

title: Moderate-to-substantial agreement of ChatGPT-5 for Kellgren-Lawrence grading on synthetic knee radiographs: a controlled cross-sectional observer agreement study
outcome: Agreement with expert reference on curated synthetic radiographs, not real-world prevalence data
effect: ChatGPT-5 weighted κ = 0.680, 60.9% exact five-grade agreement; authors state results preclude inference of real-world performance without validation on real-world, multicenter, prevalence-based datasets.
quote: However, the curated synthetic dataset, limited technical reproducibility of web-based inference, systematic grading tendencies, exploratory nature of the secondary-model analysis, and limited ecological validity preclude any inference of clinical readiness or real-world diagnostic performance without validation on real-world, multicenter, prevalence-based knee radiograph datasets.

title: Moderate-to-substantial agreement of ChatGPT-5 for Kellgren-Lawrence grading on synthetic knee radiographs: a controlled cross-sectional observer agreement study
outcome: Comparison of two AI models against expert consensus
effect: Gemini 2.5 Flash weighted κ = 0.23 vs expert reference and 0.06 vs ChatGPT-5; ChatGPT-5 weighted κ = 0.680; Gemini specificity 0%.
quote: In the 112-image exploratory subset, Gemini 2.5 Flash showed limited agreement with the expert reference standard (weighted κ = 0.23, MAE = 0.66, exact agreement = 50.0%) and poor agreement with ChatGPT-5 (weighted κ = 0.06).

title: Comparison of large language models in the management of pediatric ureteropelvic junction obstruction: a comparative analysis of 125 clinical scenarios
outcome: LLM clinical accuracy against international guidelines for pediatric UPJO management, by model
effect: ChatGPT clinical accuracy 4.13 +/- 1.31 and reliability 4.08 +/- 1.30, closest to guidelines; Copilot accuracy 3.49 +/- 1.67 with frequent clinical inaccuracies despite the highest readability.
quote: ChatGPT demonstrated significantly higher scores in clinical accuracy (4.13 +/- 1.31) and reliability (4.08 +/- 1.30) compared to its counterparts, showing the closest alignment with international guidelines.

title: Comparison of large language models in the management of pediatric ureteropelvic junction obstruction: a comparative analysis of 125 clinical scenarios
outcome: Overconfident presentation masking clinical inaccuracies in LLM outputs
effect: Copilot had highest readability (4.13 +/- 0.65) but lower accuracy (3.49 +/- 1.67); authors describe a 'readability-accuracy paradox' and 'deceptive confidence' posing misinformation risk.
quote: However, the "deceptive confidence" of models like Copilot poses a risk of misinformation.

title: A Secure User Interface for Preclinical Evaluation of AI in Patient Portal Message Management: Tutorial
outcome: Deidentification pipeline sensitivity and precision against manually adjudicated entities
effect: Validated against 110 manually adjudicated entities: sensitivity 95.1%, precision 82.1%, so some identifiers were missed.
quote: Personal health information partial masking was applied across the corpus using a deidentification pipeline validated against 110 manually adjudicated entities (sensitivity 95.1%, precision 82.1%).

title: Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Communication Platform for Racial Biases in Pretest Education About Prostate Cancer Germline Testing
outcome: Differences in chatbot response quality across Black, White, and race-agnostic vignettes
effect: No significant racial differences in comprehensiveness (mean 67%), inaccuracies (32%), readability, actionability (92%), or DISCERN (14/18); question-1 comprehensiveness lower for Black vs race-agnostic vignette (60% vs 93%, P<.01).
quote: We identified no statistically significant racial disparities across the five evaluation domains in ProGene.
sample_unit: chatbot responses (7 questions x 3 vignettes x 3 repetitions)

title: Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Communication Platform for Racial Biases in Pretest Education About Prostate Cancer Germline Testing
outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot patient education responses
effect: Mean readability was 10th grade (SMOG) and 13th grade (Flesch-Kincaid); none varied by race.
quote: The mean readability were 10th (SMOG) and 13th (Flesch-Kincaid) grades, actionability 92%, and DISCERN score 14/18 (good quality); none varied by race.
sample_unit: chatbot responses (7 questions x 3 vignettes x 3 repetitions)

title: [Would artificial intelligence pass a Geriatrics exam?: evaluating conversational responses and their accuracy]
venue: Revista espanola de geriatria y gerontologia
outcome: Readability (INFLESZ index) of AI models' justified explanatory responses
effect: Overall INFLESZ index ranged between 44.63 and 49.26, classifying the explanatory texts as 'somewhat difficult'.
quote: The overall INFLESZ index ranged between 44.63 and 49.26, classifying the explanatory texts as «somewhat difficult».

title: A multicentre evaluation of cardiovascular risk prediction tools in people living with HIV across England (ECARTH study)
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of seven CVD risk scores against observed 5-year MACE in local HIV cohort
effect: All seven scores showed moderate discrimination. QRISK3 was best calibrated (O:E 1.169, 95% CI 0.950-1.439). Framingham Office overpredicted; WHO scores and D:A:D underpredicted.
quote: Framingham Office generally overpredicted risk, while WHO scores and D:A:D generally underpredicted risk.

title: Generating guideline-concordant and safe recommendations for diabetic kidney disease management via a hierarchical retrieval-augmented large language model
outcome: Accuracy, guideline compliance, and safety-critical errors of RAG-grounded vs unaugmented LLM recommendations, blinded physician review
effect: RAG-enhanced system significantly outperformed unaugmented models in accurate, guideline-compliant recommendations and substantially reduced safety-critical errors, particularly renal-stage medication contraindications.
quote: Our evaluation reveals that the RAG-enhanced system significantly outperforms unaugmented models in providing accurate, guideline-compliant recommendations.

title: A multimodal evidence-driven framework for clinical decision support in cognitive impairment
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy with retrieval-grounded LLM reasoning added to classifier
effect: RAG-LLM integration improved all metrics; overall accuracy rose from 0.706 ± 0.038 to 0.753 ± 0.032 in external validation.
quote: In external validation on a heterogeneous cohort with primary labels, integrating RAG-LLM with the mHC improved all evaluation metrics, increasing overall accuracy from 0.706 ± 0.038 to 0.753 ± 0.032.

title: A multimodal evidence-driven framework for clinical decision support in cognitive impairment
outcome: Performance under progressive feature masking
effect: Performance declined with increasing missingness; RAG-LLM correction mitigated this effect, especially under severe sparsity.
quote: When the mHC was evaluated under progressive feature masking, performance declined with increasing missingness, whereas RAG-LLM correction mitigated this effect, especially under severe sparsity.

title: A multimodal evidence-driven framework for clinical decision support in cognitive impairment
outcome: Model performance under progressive feature masking with and without RAG-LLM correction
effect: mHC performance declined with increasing missingness, whereas RAG-LLM correction mitigated this effect, especially under severe sparsity.
quote: When the mHC was evaluated under progressive feature masking, performance declined with increasing missingness, whereas RAG-LLM correction mitigated this effect, especially under severe sparsity.

title: A multimodal evidence-driven framework for clinical decision support in cognitive impairment
outcome: mHC versus flat multimodal baselines
effect: mHC outperformed flat multimodal baselines across 15 diagnostic labels.
quote: Across 15 diagnostic labels, mHC outperformed flat multimodal baselines, supporting hierarchical diagnostic modeling.

title: A knowledge-enhanced domain-aware large language model agent for atrial fibrillation management
outcome: Blinded expert ratings of accuracy, integrity, utility, safety with vs without knowledge-enhanced RAG agent
effect: PULSE improved clinical accuracy, content integrity, utility, and safety (P < 0.05) across all tested models versus base LLMs.
quote: The results demonstrated that PULSE improved clinical accuracy, content integrity, utility, and safety (P < 0.05) across all tested models.

title: A knowledge-enhanced domain-aware large language model agent for atrial fibrillation management
outcome: empathy, clarity, and conciseness
effect: Substantially enhanced empathy and clarity while maintaining comparable conciseness.
quote: Furthermore, it substantially enhanced empathy and clarity while maintaining comparable conciseness.

title: Human evaluators vs. LLM-as-a-Judge: toward scalable evaluation of GenAI in global health
outcome: Kinyarwanda performance and cost-effectiveness
effect: Performance and cost-effectiveness fell moving from English to Kinyarwanda; no numeric estimate reported.
quote: Notably, performance and cost-effectiveness fell when moving from English to Kinyarwanda.

title: Quality of AI-generated exercise awareness messages for older adults aligned with the ICFSR consensus: a comparative study of three LLMs
venue: European review of aging and physical activity : official journal of the European Group for Research into Elderly and Physical Activity
outcome: Readability (FKGL, GFI, SMOG) of LLM messages versus recommended level for older adults
effect: Median FKGL 10.84 to 10.93 across LLMs (10th-11th grade), exceeding recommended levels for older populations.
quote: Readability indices revealed high complexity across all LLMs, with median FKGL values ranging from 10.84 to 10.93, corresponding to 10th-11th grade reading level, exceeding recommended levels for older populations.
sample_unit: LLM-generated exercise messages (13 chronic conditions x 3 LLMs)

title: Quality of AI-generated exercise awareness messages for older adults aligned with the ICFSR consensus: a comparative study of three LLMs
venue: European review of aging and physical activity : official journal of the European Group for Research into Elderly and Physical Activity
outcome: Reading grade level of LLM-generated messages for older adults
effect: Median FKGL 10.84-10.93 (10th-11th grade), above recommended reading level for older populations.
quote: Readability indices revealed high complexity across all LLMs, with median FKGL values ranging from 10.84 to 10.93, corresponding to 10th-11th grade reading level, exceeding recommended levels for older populations.
sample_unit: LLM-generated exercise messages (13 chronic conditions x 3 LLMs)

title: Quality of AI-generated exercise awareness messages for older adults aligned with the ICFSR consensus: a comparative study of three LLMs
venue: European review of aging and physical activity : official journal of the European Group for Research into Elderly and Physical Activity
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy and safety of LLM exercise messages against ICFSR consensus
effect: Overall scores Claude 4.63, ChatGPT-4 4.55, Deepseek 4.15 on 5-point scale; Claude accuracy 4.58 ± 0.64; Deepseek lower and more variable.
quote: Claude achieved the overall scores from both evaluators at 4.63 ± 0.55 and 4.60 ± 0.55, followed by ChatGPT-4 at 4.55 ± 0.50 and 4.48 ± 0.53 and Deepseek at 4.15 ± 0.87 and 4.17 ± 0.86.
sample_unit: LLM-generated exercise messages (13 chronic conditions x 3 LLMs)

title: Language-dependent performance variation in large language models for dental trauma management: a comparative evaluation of ChatGPT-5.2, Gemini 3.0, and Claude 4.5 Sonnet
outcome: LLM performance on dental trauma scenarios by query language (English vs Turkish)
effect: ChatGPT 9.14% higher in English (p<0.001); Gemini 5.69% English advantage (p=0.003); Claude language-independent (-0.02%, p=0.220).
quote: ChatGPT showed the strongest language effect with 9.14% higher performance in English (p < 0.001, r = 0.874).
sample_unit: LLM responses (27 scenarios x 3 models x 2 languages)

title: Can AI speak endo? A multi-platform evaluation of large language models against ESHRE endometriosis guidelines
outcome: Consistency of LLM responses across repeated identical queries in independent sessions
effect: Reproducible responses: model C 92.0%, model A 72.0% (P=0.028 vs C), model B 68.0% (P=0.008 vs C); non-reproducible answers in 8-32% of questions.
quote: For consistency, model C demonstrated a significantly higher rate of reproducible responses (92.0%) compared with model A (72.0%, P = 0.028) and model B (68.0%, P = 0.008).

title: Can AI speak endo? A multi-platform evaluation of large language models against ESHRE endometriosis guidelines
outcome: Concordance of LLM answers with the 2022 ESHRE endometriosis guideline (reliability)
effect: Reliability 76.0% model C, 68.0% model A, 68.0% model B (no significant difference, P=0.598); none reached reliability required for unsupervised clinical use.
quote: No significant between-model differences were found for reliability (χ2 = 1.029, P = 0.598), with rates of 76.0% for model C, 68.0% for model A, and 68.0% for model B.

title: Can AI speak endo? A multi-platform evaluation of large language models against ESHRE endometriosis guidelines
outcome: LLM answer accuracy (Global Quality Score) against guideline-based expert rating
effect: Median GQS: model A 5 (IQR 4-5), model C 4 (3-5), model B 3 (3-4); Kruskal-Wallis H=37.10, P<0.001; converged to 4 on API/May 2026 free tier.
quote: Model A achieved the highest median GQS (5, interquartile range [IQR] 4-5), followed by model C (4, IQR 3-5) and model B (3, IQR 3-4).

title: Innovative AI-based system for precision diagnosis of childhood strabismus incorporating gaze tracking and real-time correction feedback
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI versus pediatric ophthalmologists and existing AI methods on same data
effect: AI achieved binary accuracy 96.8% (AUC 0.992) and multi-class accuracy 92.5% (AUC 0.983), with agreement with gold standard κ = 0.931; comparable to specialist evaluation.
quote: The diagnostic performance was compared against pediatric ophthalmologists and existing AI methods.

title: Zero-Shot Large Language Models for Preliminary Prediction of PTSD Symptoms From Clinical Interview Transcripts: Grands modèles de langage sans exemple pour la prédiction préliminaire des symptômes de TSPT à partir de transcriptions d'entrevues cliniques
venue: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie
outcome: Zero-shot LLM accuracy predicting PTSD item scores from interview transcripts versus PCL-C
effect: Binary accuracy best 0.705 (Claude 4); Likert accuracy best 0.438 (DeepSeek 3.1), only modestly above majority-class baseline 0.399; deemed insufficient for clinical application.
quote: Zero-shot LLMs' performance was insufficient for clinical application in predicting PTSD symptoms from semi-structured interview transcripts.

title: Structured Clinical Input-Guided Large Language Model Workflow for Acute Ischemic Stroke Discharge Education: A Multicenter Feasibility Study
outcome: Blinded senior neurologist review of LLM discharge education drafts for hallucinations and acceptability
effect: No clear hallucinations identified during expert review, and LLM drafts had fewer unacceptable ratings than physician-written instructions.
quote: No clear hallucinations were identified during expert review, and LLM drafts had fewer unacceptable ratings.
sample_unit: patients with acute ischemic stroke (discharge education drafts)

title: A Locally Executable AI System for Improving Preoperative Patient Communication: Multidomain Clinical Evaluation
outcome: Accuracy of routing clinical questions to vetted FAQ answers versus cloud LLMs
effect: E5-large-instruct routed with 98.3% accuracy (393/400), AUC 0.996, 7/400 misclassifications; not statistically different from ChatGPT GPT-4o (6/400 errors; P>.99).
quote: Across both domains (N=400), E5-large-instruct achieved an accuracy of 98.3% (393/400; 95% CI 96.4%-99.1%) and an area under the curve of 0.996, with only 7 out of 400 (1.8%) misclassifications.
sample_unit: test utterances (200 per domain: 100 clinical, 100 casual)

title: Closing the Performance Gap between Generalists and Breast Imaging Specialists Using a Nationally Deployed AI Workflow for Screening Mammography
outcome: Radiologist cancer detection rates before and after introduction of the AI workflow
effect: Generalists improved from 3.76 to 4.99 cancers per 1000 examinations (P < .001); specialists showed no significant change, from 4.47 to 4.76 (P = .33).

title: GENERALIZABILITY OF DEEP LEARNING MODELS FOR REFERABLE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY DETECTION: A CROSS-POPULATION STUDY

title: GENERALIZABILITY OF DEEP LEARNING MODELS FOR REFERABLE DIABETIC RETINOPATHY DETECTION: A CROSS-POPULATION STUDY
outcome: dataset-shift performance

title: Benchmarking large language models for de-identification of electronic health record notes
outcome: Strict F1 of de-identification methods for detecting sensitive health information across datasets and settings

quote: Our findings indicate that while fine-tuned LLMs offer superior accuracy, the observed performance variability across heterogeneous electronic health record sources poses significant technical challenges.

title: Benchmarking large language models for de-identification of electronic health record notes
outcome: Cross-dataset generalization of de-identification performance across training/testing combinations
effect: Nine training/testing settings assessed; the model trained on the combined corpus of all five datasets performed best, while performance varied across heterogeneous EHR sources.

title: Benchmarking deep learning pipelines for surgical instrument segmentation in endoscopic spine surgery: cross-dataset evaluation under deployment-realistic conditions
venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
outcome: Segmentation DSC on internal, temporal external, and cross-dataset external test sets with patient-level splits

quote: With biportal-only training, the fully automatic foundation-model pipeline ranked last on cross-dataset external testing (DSC 0.776; 0.737 under a strict empty-mask convention), about 9% points below DeepLabV3+ (0.865).

title: Benchmarking deep learning pipelines for surgical instrument segmentation in endoscopic spine surgery: cross-dataset evaluation under deployment-realistic conditions
venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
outcome: Effect of adding uniportal data to training on external segmentation accuracy

quote: With combined training, all seven pipelines exceeded DSC 0.94; nnU-Net was highest (0.978), and the foundation-model pipeline (0.962) was not significantly different from SegFormer-B0 (0.960) or DeepLabV3+ (0.958) after Bonferroni correction, although the small external sample does not establish equivalence.

title: Benchmarking deep learning pipelines for surgical instrument segmentation in endoscopic spine surgery: cross-dataset evaluation under deployment-realistic conditions
venue: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
outcome: Deployment-mode (automatic detector-prompted) versus oracle bounding-box-prompted performance

quote: The same MedSAM2-Tiny segmentor reached DSC 0.946 with ground-truth bounding-box prompts, leaving a 16.9-point oracle-to-deployment gap driven by detector domain mismatch: 61% missed detections and 39% box-localization error.

title: Multi-Axial Analysis of Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Models: Inter-Verifier Disagreement and Its Implications for Automated Evaluation
outcome: Inter-verifier agreement on evidence-conclusion coherence judgments across three LLM verifiers
effect: Fleiss' κ 0.087-0.223; disagreement 62.2%-74.3%; same rationale judged supported or unsupported depending on verifier; agreement with physician varied across verifiers (50 cases).
quote: Second, inter-verifier agreement on coherence is consistently low (Fleiss' κ 0.087-0.223; disagreement 62.2%-74.3%), so the same rationale can be judged supported or unsupported depending on the verifier.

title: "Hallucinations" of artificial intelligence tools misleading patients and families
venue: Journal of family medicine and primary care
outcome: Occurrence of hallucinated false information from LLM tools given to patients and families

title: TNM-Accountable Whole-Body 3-Dimensional Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography Report Drafting in Lung Cancer Cohorts via Structured Impressions and Organ-wise Exemplar Synthesis
outcome: Performance on external-site test cases versus internal cases, including clinician Likert ratings

title: AI-based synthetic CT angiography from non-contrast CT for cerebrovascular disease screening
venue: International journal of stroke : official journal of the International Stroke Society
outcome: Consistency of synthetic CTA performance across internal and four external validation sets
effect: Performance remained consistent across four external validation sets; internal validation MAE 0.0416, MSE 0.0178, PSNR 25.59 dB, SSIM 85.41%.
quote: Performance remained consistent across four external validation sets.

title: Simulation of AI-driven CT Queue Prioritization in the Emergency Department
outcome: Wait times for actionable vs nonactionable CT studies under AI prioritization vs first-in-first-out
effect: Median wait for actionable studies reduced by 10.75 min; 90th percentile by 43.36 min; actionable findings within 1 hour rose from 48.33% to 57.30%; nonactionable 90th percentile wait increased 14.46 min.
quote: Compared with the first-in, first-out policy, the AI-based dispatch policy reduced median wait times for actionable studies in the internal test set (7637 of 20 795 [36.73%]) by 10.75 minutes (95% CI: -12.40, -9.10) and 90th-percentile wait times by 43.36 minutes (95% CI: -50.58, -36.80).

title: Comparative performance of chatgpt and gemini in diagnostic classification and clinical reasoning for open-angle glaucoma: a standardized scenario-based study
outcome: Head-to-head comparison of two LLMs on diagnostic accuracy, classification and reasoning on the same cases
effect: Accuracy 85.4% GPT-5.3 vs 75.0% Gemini (P=0.306); reasoning 4.4±0.6 vs 3.9±0.7 (P=0.011); kappa 0.675 vs 0.628.
quote: GPT-5.3 scored higher than Gemini in overall clinical reasoning (4.4 ± 0.6 vs. 3.9 ± 0.7, P = 0.011).

title: Comparative performance of chatgpt and gemini in diagnostic classification and clinical reasoning for open-angle glaucoma: a standardized scenario-based study

title: Reliability and readability of AI chatbot responses to patient questions about robot-assisted radical cystectomy

title: Reliability and readability of AI chatbot responses to patient questions about robot-assisted radical cystectomy
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of chatbot patient education responses (readability indices)

quote: However, all models exceeded the recommended sixth-grade reading level, and FRES scores remained below the recommended threshold.

title: AI-ECG Risk Stratification for Atrial Fibrillation: Real-World Performance and Explainability
outcome: AUC of AI-ECG alone versus models incorporating clinical risk scores on same patients

quote: AI-ECG provides rapid, low-cost AF risk estimation from a single sinus rhythm ECG; however, its predictive performance is modest compared with clinical scores.

title: Safety-aware AI for NSCLC trial pre-screening: a comparative proof-of-concept study of rule-based, single-agent, and multi-agent approaches

quote: Safety Agent gating reduced the false inclusion rate from 11.63% to 1.16% in the combined 120-pair cohort (McNemar's test, p = 0.002) and from 12.12% to 1.52% in the held-out set, accompanied by an increase in uncertain rate.

title: Safety-aware AI for NSCLC trial pre-screening: a comparative proof-of-concept study of rule-based, single-agent, and multi-agent approaches

title: CLEAR: an auditable foundation model for radiology grounded in clinical concepts
outcome: Classification performance of a concept-decomposable (interpretable) chest X-ray model on external datasets

quote: External validation on four large, physician-annotated datasets from the United States, Europe and Asia shows that CLEAR not only achieves state-of-the-art classification performance but also enables applications: auditable zero-shot pathology detection, systematic identification of radiological confounders and the creation of expert-level concept bottleneck models from data-driven concepts.

title: Opportunities and challenges in automated coding of electronic health records: a pilot study for rare disease registries
outcome: Generation of details not present in source reports during automated ICD-9-CM coding
effect: Authors report a tendency to generate details not present in reports; diagnosis accuracy 70.53%, procedure accuracy 78.28% against expert panel gold standard.
quote: Key challenges include limited ICD-9-CM codes, particularly for rare diseases, overreliance on nonspecific residual codes, and tendency to generate details not present in reports.

title: Automated MoCA scoring for Arabic speakers using hybrid AI of multimodal speech, vision, and LLM integration

title: Large language models as a screening tool for the qualification of patients with Parkinson's disease for device-aided therapies
outcome: Agreement of LLM screening versus MANAGE-PD with specialist decisions for device-aided therapy eligibility

quote: Agreement with specialist decisions was similar for LLM-based screening and MANAGE-PD (κ ≈ 0.575 vs. 0.567), with no significant differences in Cohen's kappa (p = 0.81) or discordant classifications (McNemar p = 1.0).

title: Model and Task-Aware Test-Time Scaling Strategies for Large Language and Vision-Language Models in Medicine: Evaluation Study
outcome: Model robustness to misleading clinical authority hints embedded in prompts

title: Implementation outcomes of AI documentation support in routine clinical practice: A non-randomized controlled trial

title: Implementation outcomes of AI documentation support in routine clinical practice: A non-randomized controlled trial

effect: Revision frequency decreased within intervention group (1.36 ± 0.14 to 1.26 ± 0.08 per document); no significant interaction for revision count, so standards were maintained under supervision.
quote: This real-world evaluation suggests that AI documentation assistance is associated with improved documentation efficiency under routine clinical conditions, while maintaining documentation standards under established supervision processes.

title: Identifying risk factors for drug use recurrence with ecological momentary assessment, wearable technologies, and machine learning: a feasibility trial of peer recovery support specialist intervention

title: Identifying risk factors for drug use recurrence with ecological momentary assessment, wearable technologies, and machine learning: a feasibility trial of peer recovery support specialist intervention

title: Identifying risk factors for drug use recurrence with ecological momentary assessment, wearable technologies, and machine learning: a feasibility trial of peer recovery support specialist intervention
outcome: Anxiety, depression, stress, angst composite, and maximum craving following alert-linked peer outreach
effect: Adding PRSS calls to participant alerts modestly reduced anxiety, stress, depression, and angst composite (all p's < 0.001) and maximum craving (p = 0.011). Calls included random as well as anomaly-triggered alerts.
quote: Statistically significant reductions were noted in anxiety, depression, stress, angst, and cravings in the PRSS intervention arm relative to the SoC arm, though the extent of the differences was modest, therefore likely tempering the clinical significance.

title: Identifying risk factors for drug use recurrence with ecological momentary assessment, wearable technologies, and machine learning: a feasibility trial of peer recovery support specialist intervention
outcome: Data-collection compliance and participant and staff workflow burden

title: Identifying risk factors for drug use recurrence with ecological momentary assessment, wearable technologies, and machine learning: a feasibility trial of peer recovery support specialist intervention

title: Identifying risk factors for drug use recurrence with ecological momentary assessment, wearable technologies, and machine learning: a feasibility trial of peer recovery support specialist intervention

title: Bridging algorithmic prediction and clinical agency: an exploratory pilot study of AI-augmented physician antidepressant choice
outcome: Clinician-adjustable weights versus fixed expert weights: perceived utility and decision change
effect: Adjustable clinician-determined weighting rated most useful (4.18 vs 3.41 static) and led to most treatment revisions (33.3% vs 15.8% static); psychiatrists resisted static weights.

title: Strategies for Deploying Large Language Models for Ascertaining Clinical Outcomes and Sites of Metastases From Radiology Impressions in Patients With Cancer
outcome: Performance of zero/one-shot versus fine-tuned open-source LLMs on local labeled data, by training data size

title: Strategies for Deploying Large Language Models for Ascertaining Clinical Outcomes and Sites of Metastases From Radiology Impressions in Patients With Cancer

effect: GPT4-turbo/GPT4o outperformed open-source LLMs zero/one-shot; fine-tuned Mistral0.2 had OR 0.27 (95% CI 0.20-0.36) versus best GPT4 for progression, favoring the fine-tuned models.
quote: In zero-/one-shot settings, GPT4-turbo/GPT4o outperformed open-source LLMs.

title: Performance of GPT-4o and Claude in Medical Ethics Scenarios: Comparative Study
outcome: Output variability across 3 identical repeated runs of ethics questions
effect: GPT-4o varied on 27/130 (21%) general vs 3/70 (4%) orthopedic questions (P=.002); Claude varied on 16/130 (12%) vs 3/70 (4%) (P=.06).
quote: GPT-4o provided different responses to identically worded trials for 27 (21%) of 130 general questions and 3 (4%) of 70 orthopedic questions (P=.002), while Claude did not have a significant difference in variability between these 2 groups (general: 16/130, 12% vs orthopedic: 3/70, 4%; P=.06).

title: Evaluating the Google CT Foundation model for central pulmonary embolism detection on computed tomography pulmonary angiograms

title: Evaluating the Google CT Foundation model for central pulmonary embolism detection on computed tomography pulmonary angiograms
outcome: Whether simple global threshold recalibration restores external-site performance

title: Decision Support Framework for Quality Assurance and Enhancement of Therapeutic Artificial Intelligence Systems: Mixed Methods Pilot Study
outcome: Therapeutic quality of chatbot before versus after expert-guided enhancement, rated by participants

title: Multimodal foundation model assistance for differentiating primary open-angle glaucoma in highly myopic eyes

title: Optimizing GPT-5 for Operation-Procedure-Code-Extraction from Operative Reports in Meningioma Surgery: Feasibility and Comparison of Context-Enhancements
outcome: Correct OPS coding and hallucination counts with versus without retrieved/curated context files

quote: Our data strongly support the thesis that contextualization significantly reduces hallucinations and thus leads to a great increase in quality.

title: Optimizing GPT-5 for Operation-Procedure-Code-Extraction from Operative Reports in Meningioma Surgery: Feasibility and Comparison of Context-Enhancements
outcome: Inaccurate GPT-5 OPS code output versus in-hospital ground-truth coding

title: Effect of CT Acquisition Parameters on RetinaNet-Based Lung Nodule Detection: A Physics-Guided Validation Study Across Dose, Slice Thickness, and Reconstruction Kernel
outcome: Detection sensitivity under simulated CT acquisition variation (dose, slice thickness, kernel)

quote: Soft kernel and 5 mm slice thickness produced the largest decreases: 74.3% (-10.5 pp, p < 0.05) and 71.6% (-13.2 pp, p < 0.05), respectively.

title: Effect of CT Acquisition Parameters on RetinaNet-Based Lung Nodule Detection: A Physics-Guided Validation Study Across Dose, Slice Thickness, and Reconstruction Kernel

title: End-to-End Pipeline Integrating Local Small Language Models and Machine Learning for Data Extraction and Stroke Outcome Prediction in Emergency Department
outcome: Error-detection yield of human review by flag tier and random sample of unflagged records

quote: Among these, 93 records were flagged by cosine similarity (58 contained at least one extraction error, 62.4%), 14 by the RAG fallback mechanism (11 contained errors, 78.6%), and 182 were randomly sampled nonflagged records (7 contained errors, 3.8%).

title: End-to-End Pipeline Integrating Local Small Language Models and Machine Learning for Data Extraction and Stroke Outcome Prediction in Emergency Department
outcome: Extraction accuracy before and after RAG-based verification against source text
effect: Accuracy increased from 74.8% (rule-based) to 86.0% after RAG validation; grounding accuracy 91.5%; improvement significant (P<0.001).
quote: After RAG-based contextual validation, accuracy increased further to 86.0% (95% CI, 83.6% to 88.4%), with F1 score and variable-level F1 both 0.813 (95% CI, 0.791 to 0.835).

title: End-to-End Pipeline Integrating Local Small Language Models and Machine Learning for Data Extraction and Stroke Outcome Prediction in Emergency Department
outcome: Accuracy gains from automated rule-based and similarity-based checks on LLM outputs

quote: With the addition of rule-based verification, performance improved to an accuracy of 74.8% (95% CI, 72.1% to 77.5%), F1 score of 0.701 (95% CI, 0.670 to 0.732), and variable-level F1 of 0.662 (95% CI, 0.631 to 0.693).

title: End-to-End Pipeline Integrating Local Small Language Models and Machine Learning for Data Extraction and Stroke Outcome Prediction in Emergency Department
outcome: Extraction accuracy after clinician review

quote: The final HITL review achieved the highest data fidelity, yielding an accuracy of 97.0% (95% CI, 95.7% to 98.3%), F1 score of 0.920 (95% CI, 0.879 to 0.961), and variable-level F1 of 0.902 (95% CI, 0.841 to 0.962), with grounding accuracy increasing to 93.2% (95% CI, 91.7% to 94.7%).

title: End-to-End Pipeline Integrating Local Small Language Models and Machine Learning for Data Extraction and Stroke Outcome Prediction in Emergency Department
outcome: Stroke outcome model discrimination

quote: While all models exhibited acceptable discrimination, the TabPFN model demonstrated the highest AUROC (0.816; 95% CI, 0.784 to 0.847), followed by CatBoost (0.789; 95% CI, 0.756 to 0.822) and logistic regression (0.700; 95% CI, 0.665 to 0.735).

title: End-to-End Pipeline Integrating Local Small Language Models and Machine Learning for Data Extraction and Stroke Outcome Prediction in Emergency Department
outcome: Extraction accuracy and F1 score after clinician human-in-the-loop review

title: LLM-Generated Lay-Language Protocols for Molecular Tumor Board Patients: Evaluation of Quality and Clinical Usability

sample_unit: generated patient protocols (25 MTB cases x 2 prompting approaches) expert-annotated

title: CATalyze-AI: accelerating referral for thrombectomy in acute stroke patients using an AI-based software. A prospective, multicentre, quasi-experimental cohort study

quote: Secondary case-level analyses using the >50% threshold showed improvement from 40% (16/40) to 67.5% (27/40) for intermediate physicians and from 57.5% (23/40) to 82.5% (33/40) for senior physicians, with similar findings using the ≥2/3 threshold.

title: Bigger Is Not Always Better: Computational Efficiency in Lexical Prehospital Triage Modeling
outcome: Compared simple ML model versus transformer models on the same data for predicting lifesaving intervention
effect: AUROC .793 for MLM vs .803 for BioBERT and DistilBERT; AP .670 vs .674 and .673. Performance was equivalent, and the LLMs needed far more computation, so the simpler model was sufficient.
quote: MLMs and LLMs produced broadly equivalent performance in predicting LSI (MLM: AUROC = .793 [.776, .810]; AP = .670 [.643, .695] vs. BioBERT: AUROC = .803 [.796, .816]; AP = .674 [.649, .698]) vs. DistilBERT: AUROC = .803 [.785, .811]; AP = .673 [.651, .688]).

title: Bigger Is Not Always Better: Computational Efficiency in Lexical Prehospital Triage Modeling
outcome: Whether complex transformer models outperform simpler models and at what computational cost
effect: Transformers gave no meaningful performance gain (AUROC .803 vs .793). Training took 7:14 (BioBERT) and 3:57 (DistilBERT) vs 9.42 s for MLM. Prediction took 13.36 s and 7.37 s vs .048 s.
quote: Our findings counter the "bigger is better" paradigm in medical AI: MLMs performed equivalently to LLMs in task mirroring on-scene triage while requiring a fraction of the computational resources.

title: AI-assisted VMAT planning incorporating deep learning-based dose prediction for head and neck cancer: feasibility of quality standardization and human intervention for irregular cases

title: AI-assisted VMAT planning incorporating deep learning-based dose prediction for head and neck cancer: feasibility of quality standardization and human intervention for irregular cases

effect: Relative inter-rater sensitivity between experts ranged from 68.4% to 88.3%; relative FPs/day ranged from 0.16 to 0.79, showing experts disagree on what constitutes a seizure.
quote: Relative inter-rater sensitivity between the experts ranged from 68.4% (95% confidence interval [CI[Formula: see text]]=[48.8%, 84.5%]) to 88.3%, [77.5%, 94.7%], while relative FPs/day ranged from 0.16, [0.02, 0.47] to 0.79, [0.14, 2.48].
sample_unit: EEG records (mean 67 hours each; 4,036 hours total)

title: Qualitative and Quantitative Assessment of Four Artificial Intelligence Systems for Nasal Deformity Analysis in Rhinoplasty
outcome: Chatbot MIRA sub-score agreement with expert surgeons on nasal deformity photographs
effect: All four models differed significantly from experts on MIRA sub-scores (p<0.05); Grok 2 worst (p<0.001); only Claude 3.7 matched total MIRA score; ChatGPT 4o 70% accuracy on nose type.
quote: Detailed analysis of MIRA sub-scores showed a significant difference between chatbots and experts across all models (p < 0.05), including Claude.

title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Breast Ultrasound Report Auditing: Workflow-Error Detection, False-Positive Burden, and Limits of Key-Image Interpretation
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: LLM vs physician reader performance in report auditing; no human-with-AI arm
effect: Physician reader achieved 91.7% report-level sensitivity and 83.0% error-level recall without false positives; Gemini multimodal sensitivity 96.2% but false positives in 18/60 error-free reports.
quote: The physician reader achieved 91.7% report-level sensitivity and 83.0% error-level recall without false positives.
sample_unit: breast ultrasound examinations (300-report error-enriched subset for report auditing)

title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Breast Ultrasound Report Auditing: Workflow-Error Detection, False-Positive Burden, and Limits of Key-Image Interpretation
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Comparison of LLMs against physician reader and physician-interpreted findings input
effect: Key-image input underperformed physician-interpreted findings input for malignancy (AUC 0.879 vs 0.971) and BI-RADS (AUC 0.887 vs 0.984).
quote: In the full cohort, key-image input underperformed physician-interpreted findings input for malignancy classification (AUC, 0.879 vs 0.971) and BI-RADS risk classification (AUC, 0.887 vs 0.984).
sample_unit: breast ultrasound examinations (300-report error-enriched subset for report auditing)

title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Breast Ultrasound Report Auditing: Workflow-Error Detection, False-Positive Burden, and Limits of Key-Image Interpretation
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: False-positive outputs from body-marker misinterpretation under multimodal input
effect: Gemini with multimodal input produced false-positive outputs in 18/60 error-free reports and 12/240 error-enriched reports, mainly from body-marker misinterpretation.
quote: Gemini with multimodal input produced false-positive outputs in 18/60 error-free reports and 12/240 error-enriched reports, mainly from body-marker misinterpretation.

title: Impact of guideline-based prompting on the large language model performance in dental trauma management clinical decision-making
outcome: LLM guideline concordance and scores on dental trauma questions with vs without uploaded guideline grounding
effect: With guideline support, OEQ median scores were 32 (DeepSeek) and 30 (ChatGPT, Gemini) vs 26, 20, 23 without; MCQ accuracy 100% with guideline vs 81.2% to 100% without.
quote: Guideline-based prompting substantially improved performance and guideline concordance on open-ended questions.
sample_unit: questions (16 MCQs and 16 open-ended questions), each asked repeatedly

title: Quality of AI-Generated Patient Education for Pre- and Post-Operative Tracheostomy Care
venue: Otolaryngology--head and neck surgery : official journal of American Academy of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Readability grade level of AI and physician tracheostomy patient education responses versus NIH 6th-grade recommendation
effect: All AI and expert responses exceeded the NIH-recommended 6th-grade reading level, ranging from 10th-13th grade (P < .001).
quote: All AI and expert responses exceeded the NIH-recommended 6th-grade reading level, ranging from 10th-13th grade (P < .001).

title: Accuracy of Artificial Intelligence based chatbots in reporting jaw lesions from multimodal radiographic images: A cross-sectional study
outcome: Chatbot lesion detection and correct diagnosis accuracy on jaw lesion images
effect: Manus CBCT 95% detected and correctly diagnosed; Gemini 2.5 Pro 80% detected, 56% correctly diagnosed; Copilot and Claude least accurate; significant differences between chatbots.
quote: Significant discrepancies exist among artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots regarding their diagnostic accuracy in reporting jaw lesions.

title: Large Language Model-Based Clinical Decision Support for Antibiotic Selection and Dose Recommendation in Hospitalized Patients With Pneumonia: Multicenter Retrospective Study
outcome: Antibiotic selection and dosing agreement (F1, Jaccard) of full retrieval-grounded pipeline versus alternatives
effect: Full pipeline with DeepSeek-V3 performed best: internal F1 0.8110 for selection and 0.7538 for selection plus dosing; external F1 0.8605 and 0.8503.
quote: On the internal test set, the full pipeline using DeepSeek-V3 achieved the best performance, with an F1-score of 0.8110 (95% CI 0.7371-0.8762) and Jaccard accuracy of 0.7624 (95% CI 0.6810-0.8386) for antibiotic selection and an F1-score of 0.7538 (95% CI 0.6671-0.8329) and Jaccard accuracy of 0.7076 (95% CI 0.6145-0.7938) for joint antibiotic selection plus dosing recommendation.

title: Correctness, Harmfulness, and Diversity of Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Comparative Evaluation Study
outcome: AI Coach response correctness and harmful errors vs prep instructions reference standard
effect: Human-rated turn-level accuracy: o3 93.5%, GPT-4.1 90.8%, Llama 78.1%, Mistral 68.1%; all models produced harmful errors (o3 11/17 errors harmful).
quote: All models produced harmful errors, primarily due to omissions or misinterpretations of prep instructions.
sample_unit: synthetic dialogues per model (50 per model human-rated)

title: Correctness, Harmfulness, and Diversity of Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Comparative Evaluation Study
outcome: Safety filter effect on harm
quote: Applying an automated safety filter reduced overall error rates but failed to eliminate harmful responses.
sample_unit: synthetic dialogues per model (50 per model human-rated)

title: Correctness, Harmfulness, and Diversity of Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Comparative Evaluation Study
outcome: Error and harmfulness rates before vs after LLM-judge filter replacing incorrect responses with provider deferral
effect: Filter reduced error rates (Mistral 31.9% to 10.8%; o3 6.5% to 5.2%) but harmful errors persisted (o3 4.3% to 3.9%; Llama 12.7% to 7.6%); little benefit for stronger models.
quote: Most importantly, the filter failed to eliminate a sufficient number of harmful errors, making it impractical as a safety mechanism.
sample_unit: synthetic dialogues per model (50 per model human-rated)

title: Correctness, Harmfulness, and Diversity of Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Comparative Evaluation Study
outcome: Deferral of incorrect responses to provider via automated filter, and cost of excessive deferral
effect: Filter cut error rates but did not penalize false deferrals; would likely be counterproductive if patients were redirected on answerable questions; harmful errors remained.
quote: If such a filter were deployed in patient interactions, it would likely be counterproductive: if patients are redirected to contact a provider for questions that could have been answered from the prep instructions, the usefulness of the AI Coach as an assistant for colonoscopy prep is undermined.
sample_unit: synthetic dialogues per model (50 per model human-rated)

title: Correctness, Harmfulness, and Diversity of Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Comparative Evaluation Study
outcome: Diversity of simulated patient questions under multiprompt vs single-prompt generation
effect: Multiprompt 10-question strategy increased Distinct-1/2 and entropy for all models (e.g., GPT-5.1 Distinct-2 0.25 to 0.47).
quote: Automatic diversity metrics, such as entropy and Distinct-1 or Distinct-2 ( Table 4 ), indicated that the multiprompt, multiquestion generation strategy produced more diverse patient questions than the single-prompt, single-question baseline for all models.
sample_unit: synthetic dialogues per model (50 per model human-rated)

title: Correctness, Harmfulness, and Diversity of Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Comparative Evaluation Study
outcome: Models' handling of ambiguous patient inputs such as weekday-phrased questions
effect: Even stronger models failed to detect ambiguity in questions phrased with weekdays rather than days before procedure.
quote: Such questions create ambiguity that a robust system should detect, but even stronger models were not able to do so.
sample_unit: synthetic dialogues per model (50 per model human-rated)

title: Correctness, Harmfulness, and Diversity of Large Language Models for Colonoscopy Preparation Assistance: Comparative Evaluation Study
outcome: Harmful patient-facing responses
effect: Human harmfulness rates before filtering: Mistral 33/251 (13.1%), Llama 30/237 (12.7%), GPT-4.1 9/250 (3.6%), o3 10/231 (4.3%).
quote: All models produced harmful errors, primarily due to omissions or misinterpretations of prep instructions.
sample_unit: synthetic dialogues per model (50 per model human-rated)

title: Quality and readability of AI Chatbot responses to frequently asked questions from patients undergoing progressive collapsing foot deformity surgery: a comparative study of ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini
outcome: Readability (FRE, FKGL) of chatbot responses versus recommended patient education thresholds
effect: No platform reached FRE ≥ 60 or FKGL ≤ 6; median FKGL ranged from 13.1 (ChatGPT) to 21.4 (Perplexity), p < 0.001.
quote: No platform reached the recommended FRE ≥ 60 or FKGL ≤ 6 thresholds: median FKGL ranged from 13.1 (ChatGPT) to 21.4 (Perplexity), with ChatGPT producing the most readable and Perplexity the least readable content (p < 0.001).

title: Quality and readability of AI Chatbot responses to frequently asked questions from patients undergoing progressive collapsing foot deformity surgery: a comparative study of ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Gemini
outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient education content relative to recommended grade level
effect: All three chatbots exceeded the FKGL ≤ 6 threshold; median FKGL 13.1 to 21.4.
quote: No platform reached the recommended FRE ≥ 60 or FKGL ≤ 6 thresholds: median FKGL ranged from 13.1 (ChatGPT) to 21.4 (Perplexity), with ChatGPT producing the most readable and Perplexity the least readable content (p < 0.001).

title: [Creation of Patient Summaries from Electronic Medical Records and Integration of Medical Knowledge via Large Language Models-Next-Generation Medical DX and Drug Discovery Support Opened Up by Natural Language Processing]
venue: Gan to kagaku ryoho. Cancer & chemotherapy
outcome: Hallucination risk in LLM-generated summaries from EMR text
effect: Risk of hallucinations was confirmed in generated summaries; authors conclude human-in-the-loop oversight is indispensable for clinical implementation. No rates reported.
quote: However, the risk of hallucinations inherent in generative AI was also confirmed, making human oversight (human-in-the-loop) indispensable for clinical implementation.

title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
outcome: Human accuracy with vs without AI assistance, including when AI was wrong
effect: Lay accuracy rose from 69.7% to 75.8% with AI; incorrect AI predictions reduced lay accuracy (β=-0.233), while PCPs' top-1 accuracy rose +21.5% and was little affected by wrong AI.
quote: We found that AI improved average accuracy of the nevus versus melanoma detection task from 69.7 ± 0.8% to 75.8% ± 0.7% (effect of AI assistance: β = 0.061, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.049−0.074, P < 0.001, linear mixed model on accuracy, with AI assistance, XAI methods and their interaction as the main factor, controlling gender, age, race, skin disease experience and the covariate of self-reported human−AI collaboration experience; see Supplementary Table 7 for details).

title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
outcome: Automation bias and detection of incorrect AI outputs in lay people vs PCPs
effect: Lay users' accuracy fell when AI was wrong (LLM -21.1%, basic -14.6%); PCPs were minimally affected (β=0-0.021, P=0.328-1.000). Medical students deferred more than PCPs.
quote: In contrast to the general public, incorrect AI predictions had minimal impact on the final decisions of PCPs across all XAI methods (Fig. 3f and Extended Data Fig. 2d−f ; β = 0−0.021, P = 0.328−1.000).

title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
outcome: Performance of users with vs without AI and overreliance assessment
effect: AI assistance improved lay accuracy 69.7% to 75.8% and PCP top-1 accuracy +21.5%; overreliance appeared in lay users when AI erred (−23.3 points, β=-0.233).
quote: However, the general publicʼs diagnostic accuracy improved when AI provided correct predictions, whereas incorrect predictions reduced the performance significantly ( β = −0.233, 95% CI: −0.307 to −0.158, P < 0.001; Fig. 2d and Supplementary Table 12 ).

title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
outcome: Effect of fairness-constrained training on subgroup disparity and overall accuracy
effect: CDANN model achieved AUROC 0.930 with balanced accuracy skin-tone gap Δ=0.021 versus ERM 0.091, narrowing gap by 76.9% while maintaining strong overall performance.
quote: Our fairness-constrained models (final architectures and hyperparameters reported in Methods ) achieved strong overall performance with substantially reduced disparities across skin tones.

title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
outcome: Effect of different explanation formats (basic, GradCAM, CBIR, LLM) on user accuracy and deference
effect: LLM explanations gave largest lay gain (+7.7%) but largest loss when wrong; for PCPs LLM was least helpful (+17.7%) though improving confidence calibration (r=0.494).
quote: Interestingly, for PCPs, LLM explanations were the least helpful method (+17.7%) and were 8.1% lower than the best improvement from the basic explanations ( β = −0.081, 95% CI: −0.207 to 0.044, P = 0.268; Fig. 3b and Supplementary Table 16 ).

title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
outcome: AI deference by medical expertise
effect: Medical students were more deferential than PCPs: role β = 0.067, P = 0.037; skin expertise β = 0.073, P = 0.005.
quote: We observed that the proportion of deferential participants was higher among medical students than PCPs (linear mixed model on the proportion of deferential participants, with medical role and medical expertise in skin as the main factor, controlling other confounders: main effect of medical role: β = 0.067, 95% CI: 0.004−0.130, P = 0.037; main effect of skin expertise: β = 0.073, 95% CI: 0.022−0.124, P = 0.005; Supplementary Table 25 ).

title: Divergent impacts of explainable AI for dermatological diagnosis on clinicians versus lay people
outcome: AI diagnostic performance by skin tone
effect: Primary model subgroup gaps: AUROC Δ = 0.091, weighted AUROC Δ = 0.192, balanced accuracy Δ = 0.056.
quote: For study 2, the primary five-class model achieved AUROC of 0.772 (0.782/0.691, Δ = 0.091), weighted AUROC of 0.753 (0.725/0.693, Δ = 0.192) and balanced accuracy of 0.478 on the four main diseases (0.487/0.431, Δ = 0.056), outperforming ERM (0.457, Δ = 0.144).

title: Improving sepsis best practice utility and clinical acceptance using an LLM-enhanced prediction system
outcome: Antibiotic administration delays following LLM augmentation of sepsis alerts
effect: Median BPA-to-antibiotic time decreased from 140.4 to 112.1 minutes; median ED-admission-to-antibiotic time decreased from 325.0 to 274.0 minutes.
quote: Importantly, this shift in BPA acknowledgement patterns was not associated with delays in sepsis management (Table 2 ), with median time from BPA firing to antibiotics decreasing from 140.4 to 112.1 minutes.

title: Improving sepsis best practice utility and clinical acceptance using an LLM-enhanced prediction system
outcome: Timeliness of sepsis treatment
effect: The median time from alert to antibiotic administration decreased from 140.4 to 112.1 minutes.
quote: Importantly, this shift in BPA acknowledgement patterns was not associated with delays in sepsis management (Table 2 ), with median time from BPA firing to antibiotics decreasing from 140.4 to 112.1 minutes.

title: Accuracy, Usefulness, and Impact Variability of ChatGPT4o for COPD Medication Management: A Modified Delphi Study
outcome: Consistency of ChatGPT-4o responses to identical COPD prompts entered simultaneously
effect: Simultaneous responses to identical prompts differed materially in accuracy and potential clinical impact; for two questions one response was rated more useful than the others; consensus in 40 of 45 ratings (88.9%).
quote: Simultaneous ChatGPT-4o responses to identical COPD prompts differed materially in accuracy and potential clinical impact.
