title: Can Artificial Intelligence Assess Distal Radius Fracture Stability?
outcome: Multimodal LLM agreement with surgeon consensus on fracture stability using radiographs
effect: Both models achieved overall accuracy 0.75 (95% CI, 0.56-0.94); ChatGPT moderate and Claude fair agreement; several criteria near chance and specificity limited.
quote: Performance across several criteria approached chance levels, and specificity was limited.

effect: Accuracy changed after vendor updates, improving from 88.0 to 93.7% with MCQ and 68.1 to 81.7% without MCQ; the changes were not all statistically significant, and drivers are opaque.
quote: GPT-4's performance improved across all question categories from round one to round two, most notably in management questions without MCQ options (+23.30%), though these differences were not statistically significant.

title: From prediction to practice: machine learning models and real-world interventions for magnetic resonance imaging appointment no-shows in a hospital setting
outcome: Data drift in appointment types and reasons after deployment
effect: Prostate appointments rose from 2%-3% to nearly 10%; 'None Given' reason (most predictive feature) fell from 13%-15% to 5%-6%, contributing to performance drop.
quote: This drop in performance can be explained in part by data drift—that is, changes in a feature’s distribution over time.

title: From prediction to practice: machine learning models and real-world interventions for magnetic resonance imaging appointment no-shows in a hospital setting
outcome: No-show rate with model-targeted phone reminders versus control
effect: No significant reduction: 21.9% intervention vs 22.0% control (P = .48) despite model identifying high-risk patients.
quote: Overall, the phone call trial showed no significant reduction in the no-show rate between the control (22.0%) and intervention (21.9%) groups ( P- value: .48), as shown in Table 2 .

title: From prediction to practice: machine learning models and real-world interventions for magnetic resonance imaging appointment no-shows in a hospital setting
outcome: Prospective predictive performance compared with retrospective validation
effect: Across 5882 appointments over 13 months, prospective AUROC was 0.61 and AUPRC 0.24, compared with validation AUROC 0.65 and AUPRC 0.29.
quote: On this dataset, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.61 and an AUPRC of 0.24, a reduction in performance when compared to the validation data performance (AUROC: 0.65, AUPRC: 0.29).

title: From prediction to practice: machine learning models and real-world interventions for magnetic resonance imaging appointment no-shows in a hospital setting
outcome: Prospective performance during 13-month silent live test versus retrospective validation
effect: Silent live test on 5882 appointments revealed AUROC 0.61 and AUPRC 0.24, down from held-out validation AUROC 0.65 and AUPRC 0.29.
quote: On this dataset, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.61 and an AUPRC of 0.24, a reduction in performance when compared to the validation data performance (AUROC: 0.65, AUPRC: 0.29).

title: From prediction to practice: machine learning models and real-world interventions for magnetic resonance imaging appointment no-shows in a hospital setting
outcome: Appointment no-show rates following risk-targeted reminder calls versus no reminders
effect: No-show rates were 21.9% for 274 intervention appointments versus 22.0% for 460 controls (P = .48). Only 158 (57.7%) answered; 116 (42.3%) were not reached.
quote: Overall, the phone call trial showed no significant reduction in the no-show rate between the control (22.0%) and intervention (21.9%) groups ( P- value: .48), as shown in Table 2 .

effect: Certified 4.99; ChatGPT-4o 4.89; DeepL Pro 4.43 (P<0.001 vs certified); Med_English2Spanish 3.32 (P<0.001). Variable equivalence; not suitable for clinical deployment without human review.

effect: Clinically reliable: 89.3% clinician-language vs 91.3% patient-language; cumulative OR 0.78 (95% CI 0.57-1.06; p=0.115); language-by-model interaction p=0.422. Some secondary scores higher for patient-language.
quote: Patient-language phrasing was not significantly associated with overall GCCS (cumulative odds ratio 0.78, 95% confidence interval 0.57-1.06; p = 0.115), and the language-by-model interaction was not significant (p = 0.422).

title: Artificial Intelligence Can Direct Patients Toward a Complaint-specific Musculoskeletal Provider
venue: Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons. Global research & reviews
outcome: Appropriateness of LLM-recommended musculoskeletal providers and hallucinated providers
effect: Appropriate: ChatGPT 17/17 (100%), Gemini 9/21 (43%), DeepSeek 4/10 (40%), P<0.001; 5 of 18 inappropriate recommendations were hallucinations, all from DeepSeek.
quote: Of the 18 inappropriate recommendations, 13 (72%) were real providers in unrelated specialties and 5 (28%) were hallucinations, all from DeepSeek.

title: Improved Readability and Translational Instability in LLM-Generated Radiology Reports
outcome: Model output variance and accuracy under baseline versus optimized structured prompts
effect: Optimized structured prompts significantly reduced output variance and improved translational accuracy, especially in DeepSeek-R1 and ChatGPT-4.0.
quote: Optimized structured prompting can substantially reduce the variability of model outputs and improve the accuracy of medical text translation.

title: Improved Readability and Translational Instability in LLM-Generated Radiology Reports
outcome: errors in AI-generated radiology reports
effect: All tested models omitted information and produced risk-averse, generalized clinical recommendations.
quote: Professional radiological evaluation revealed that all tested models exhibited inherent instability, omitted information, and tended to generate risk-averse, generalized clinical recommendations.

title: Improved Readability and Translational Instability in LLM-Generated Radiology Reports
outcome: model output instability
effect: All tested models exhibited inherent instability, with omitted information and generalized recommendations.
quote: Professional radiological evaluation revealed that all tested models exhibited inherent instability, omitted information, and tended to generate risk-averse, generalized clinical recommendations.

title: Improved Readability and Translational Instability in LLM-Generated Radiology Reports
outcome: radiology report readability
effect: LLMs significantly enhanced readability (P < 0.05); DeepSeek-R1 achieved the best performance.
quote: Overall, large language models significantly enhanced the readability of radiology reports (P < 0.05), with DeepSeek-R1 achieving the best performance.

title: Improved Readability and Translational Instability in LLM-Generated Radiology Reports
outcome: comprehension by demographic characteristics
effect: Self-reported comprehension was affected by demographic characteristics; no subgroup effect sizes reported.
quote: However, patients' self-reported comprehension of the reports was affected by demographic characteristics.

title: Performance of nine large language models on real-world polysomnography interpretation for obstructive sleep apnea: a multi-dimensional comparative analysis
venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy on real-world polysomnography reports versus expert consensus, by case complexity
effect: Fully correct diagnostic rates ranged from 75.0% to 86.3%; all models degraded on complex cases (11.8-25.7 percentage point decline); safety rates exceeded 88%.
quote: All models demonstrated significant performance degradation on complex cases (11.8-25.7 percentage point decline).

title: Theoretical Exploration of Error Thresholds for Clinical AI Decision Support in Nursing: Exploratory Simulation Study Grounded in Human-AI Reliance Data
outcome: Predicted human-AI team error by AI accuracy, clinician experience, and task complexity (overreliance)
effect: Simulated novice×high-complexity error rates of roughly 26% to 41% at AI accuracy 0.5-0.7; AI accuracy of 0.89 needed for error <10%.
quote: At the moderate accuracy levels currently reported for general-purpose LLMs on complex clinical tasks (approximately 0.5-0.7), the model predicts error rates of roughly 26% to 41% in this high-risk condition.
sample_unit: participants across 3 randomized experiments used for calibration (9 empirical data points)

title: Trial Files: Leveraging large language models to summarize practice-changing clinical trials for clinicians
outcome: LLM RCT summary accuracy against manual review reference across extracted fields
effect: Accuracy with prompt engineering vs manual review: 97.1% study phase, 92.2% blinding, 85.4% sample size, 97.9% population, 94.7% comparison groups, 92.7% primary outcome.
quote: The accuracy for reporting study information with prompt engineering, compared to manual review, was 97.1% for study phase, 92.2% for blinding, 85.4% for sample size, 97.9% for patient population, 94.7% for comparison groups, and 92.7% for primary outcome.
sample_unit: RCT abstracts (summaries) manually reviewed for accuracy

title: Iterative Multidisciplinary Development and Evaluation of a Patient-Facing Social Determinants of Health Chatbot Using Synthetic Data Simulation: Mixed Methods Study
outcome: Chatbot safety rating (recognition of health emergencies) across simulated cases, expert rater agreement
effect: Safety agreement=0.69% (95% CI 0.58-0.78), Fleiss κ=-0.04; domain focus agreement=0.51%, data completeness 0.59% (κ=0.18); other domains near ceiling (0.98-0.99).
quote: Lower performance was observed in domain focus and completeness (agreement=0.51%, 95% CI 0.40-0.61), completeness of data capture (agreement=0.59%, 95% CI 0.48-0.69; Fleiss κ=0.18), and safety (agreement=0.69%, 95% CI 0.58-0.78; Fleiss κ=-0.04), prompting targeted adaptations.

title: A Bilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Diagnostic Performance of Multimodal Large Language Models in Radiology (RadM-Bench): Evaluation Development and Validation
outcome: Model diagnostic score change from public teaching cases to real routine clinical cases
effect: Proprietary models declined from RadEdu to RealClin (O3 with images: 1.14 to 0.79); Chinese-centric open-source models improved (InternVL3-78B: 0.48 to 0.75). All models stayed below 1.5 on the 0-3 scale.
quote: Cross-dataset transfer diverged by model category: proprietary models declined from RadEdu to RealClin (eg, O3 with images: 1.14 to 0.79), whereas Chinese-centric open-source models improved (eg, InternVL3-78B: 0.48 to 0.75).

title: Patients' experiences and attitudes toward the use of real-time artificial intelligence-assisted colonoscopy
venue: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland
outcome: Patient views on how much information about AI should be provided
effect: Patients wanted information about AI proportional to the consequences; written information should be informative but concise, avoiding details that create confusion.
quote: If written information about AI is provided, it should be informative but concise, avoiding details that generate more confusion than clarity.

title: Sociodemographic bias in LLMs' clinical decision-making for dizziness
venue: Journal of vestibular research : equilibrium & orientation
outcome: LLM recommendation shifts versus neutral control when patient sociodemographic descriptors varied
effect: Descriptors changed recommendations; mental health referral lower for Black transgender women (-12.2 pp; 95% CI -14.0 to -10.3), Black homeless patients (-9.1 pp), homeless patients (-7.7 pp); low-income neuroimaging +4.0 pp.
quote: Referral likelihood was lower for Black transgender women (-12.2 pp; 95% CI -14.0 to -10.3), Black patients experiencing homelessness (-9.1 pp; -11.0 to -7.3), and patients experiencing homelessness (-7.7 pp; -9.5 to -5.9).

title: Sociodemographic bias in LLMs' clinical decision-making for dizziness
venue: Journal of vestibular research : equilibrium & orientation
outcome: LLM clinical recommendation differences across sociodemographic subgroups
effect: Sociodemographic descriptors influenced recommendations, largest for mental health referral in ambiguous cases; attenuated with clearer diagnostic information; other effects smaller.
quote: Sociodemographic descriptors influenced LLM recommendations, with the largest differences observed for mental health referral decisions in diagnostically ambiguous cases.

title: Sociodemographic bias in LLMs' clinical decision-making for dizziness
venue: Journal of vestibular research : equilibrium & orientation
outcome: Biased clinical recommendations by patient sociodemographic group in generative AI output
effect: LLM recommendations varied by descriptors, particularly under diagnostic uncertainty; referral lower for Black transgender women by 12.2 pp.
quote: LLM clinical recommendations varied by sociodemographic descriptors, particularly under diagnostic uncertainty.

title: LLM-assisted clinical coding audit through an interpretable coding pipeline
outcome: Error and undercoding rates in human-annotated reference standards (MDACE, CodiEsp)
effect: Audit found an estimated 76.3% undercoding rate in MDACE and a 29.7% error rate in CodiEsp; re-evaluating models on corrected datasets improved performance.
quote: The audit uncovered significant data quality issues, including an estimated 76.3% undercoding rate in MDACE and a 29.7% error rate in CodiEsp.

title: Adding artificial intelligence to the pulmonary embolism response team improves time to diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary embolism
venue: Journal of vascular surgery. Venous and lymphatic disorders
outcome: Time to diagnosis, anticoagulation, intervention and in-hospital mortality, pre-AI vs post-AI cohorts
effect: Time to diagnosis 72.5 to 40 min (P=.00005); intervention 1360 to 1224 min (P=.036); anticoagulation 76 vs 61.5 min (P=.824); two deaths, both pre-AI; underpowered for mortality.
quote: Time to diagnosis improved significantly from 72.5 (IQR, 44.5-93.3) to 40 (IQR, 28-68.2) minutes (P = .00005).

title: Large Language Models as Health Information Tools: Patient Use and Trust in Otolaryngology
outcome: Patient disclosure of LLM use to clinicians and concerns about accuracy
effect: 93.8% of LLM users did not disclose use to clinicians; 82.7% had accuracy concerns; 32.7% mostly or completely distrusted LLM information; 56.2% believed clinicians should be aware.
quote: Most users (93.8%) did not disclose LLM use, although 56.2% believed clinicians should be aware.

title: Large Language Models as Health Information Tools: Patient Use and Trust in Otolaryngology
outcome: Patient use of consumer LLM chatbots for health information before clinic visit
effect: 71.2% reported prior LLM use, and 28.6% used an LLM to learn about their condition before the visit; 93.8% did not disclose it to clinicians.
quote: Among 59 respondents (mean age 50.1 years; 53.4% female), 71.2% reported prior LLM use, and 28.6% used an LLM to learn about their condition before the visit.

title: Feasibility of LLM-assisted post-discharge tuberculosis care: A comparative study of medication counseling, patient education, and follow-up planning
outcome: LLM vs TB physician responses on precision, recall, F1 and subjective ratings
effect: Patient education: LLM precision 0.86 vs 0.50 (P<.001), recall 0.53 vs 0.14, F1 0.65 vs 0.22. No significant objective differences for medication counseling and follow-up planning (all P>.050). LLMs rated higher on suitability, understandability, empathy.
quote: Conversely, no statistically significant differences were observed in objective metrics for medication counseling and follow-up planning (all P > .050), although LLMs demonstrated a tendency toward broader but more discordant coverage.

title: Evaluating the efficacy of artificial intelligence in audiology: a head-to-head comparison of ChatGPT and Gemini on hearing aid management
outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs, measured by cosine similarity
effect: High semantic consistency (ChatGPT median 0.91; Gemini 0.93), no significant difference between models (overall p = 0.30), but repeatability was imperfect.
quote: In the objective assessment of repeatability via NLP algorithms, both models exhibited high semantic consistency (ChatGPT Median: 0.91; Gemini Median: 0.93), with no statistically significant differences observed between them in any category (overall p = 0.30).

title: Evaluating the efficacy of artificial intelligence in audiology: a head-to-head comparison of ChatGPT and Gemini on hearing aid management
outcome: Accuracy of LLM hearing aid answers against manufacturer manuals rated by audiologists
effect: Gemini showed significantly superior accuracy overall (p < 0.001), especially in Pairing (p = 0.03) and Before Using a Hearing Aid (p = 0.03); performance fluctuated with task complexity.
quote: Regarding medical and technical accuracy, rank-based analyses revealed that Gemini showed significantly superior overall performance (p < 0.001), specifically excelling in the "Pairing" (p = 0.03) and "Before Using a Hearing Aid" (p = 0.03) categories.

title: Validation and Comparison of 10-Year Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Models in Two Chinese Prospective Cohorts: The General Population and Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
outcome: Calibration (E/O ratio, Brier score) and discrimination of original versus locally recalibrated CVD risk models
effect: Recalibration markedly improved calibration and reduced Brier scores with little change in discrimination; original E/O 1.47-3.78 in general cohort and 0.32-2.70 in T2D cohort.
quote: Recalibration markedly improved calibration and reduced Brier scores, with little change in discrimination.

title: Validation and Comparison of 10-Year Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Models in Two Chinese Prospective Cohorts: The General Population and Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
outcome: Performance of existing risk models on local Chinese cohort data versus reference outcomes
effect: Original models were poorly calibrated, with systematic overprediction in the general population cohort (E/O 1.47-3.78) and heterogeneous miscalibration in the type 2 diabetes cohort (E/O 0.32-2.70).
quote: Original models were poorly calibrated, with systematic overprediction in the general population cohort (E/O 1.47-3.78) and heterogeneous miscalibration in the type 2 diabetes cohort (E/O 0.32-2.70).

title: Validation and Comparison of 10-Year Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Models in Two Chinese Prospective Cohorts: The General Population and Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
outcome: Discrimination of risk models in general population versus type 2 diabetes population
effect: Discrimination was higher in the general population cohort than in the type 2 diabetes cohort (C-statistic 0.723-0.778 vs. 0.584-0.629).
quote: Discrimination was higher in the general population cohort than in the type 2 diabetes cohort (C-statistic 0.723-0.778 vs. 0.584-0.629).

title: Validation and Comparison of 10-Year Cardiovascular Risk Prediction Models in Two Chinese Prospective Cohorts: The General Population and Patients With Type 2 Diabetes
outcome: Calibration despite discrimination
effect: C-statistic ranges were 0.723-0.778 vs. 0.584-0.629, while original models had substantial miscalibration.
quote: Widely used 10-year CVD risk models showed acceptable or modest discrimination but substantial miscalibration in Chinese populations, especially among adults with type 2 diabetes.

title: Conversational Large Language Models for Vestibular Diagnosis in Outpatient Clinics: Prospective Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
outcome: Prospective concordance of agent diagnosis with clinician final diagnosis while clinicians were blinded to agent output
effect: Agent matched the reference diagnosis in 140 of 176 (79.55%; 95% CI 72.8%-85.2%) patients, with clinicians blinded to agent output.
quote: The conversational agent matched the reference diagnosis in 140 of 176 (79.55%; 95% CI 72.8%-85.2%) patients.
sample_unit: outpatients with vertigo or dizziness (prospective clinical evaluation); 227 histories in history-based evaluation

title: Conversational Large Language Models for Vestibular Diagnosis in Outpatient Clinics: Prospective Multicenter Diagnostic Accuracy Study
outcome: LLM Top-1 accuracy compared with specialist panel majority vote on same vertigo histories
effect: Gemini-2.5-pro and o1 reached 69.6% Top-1 vs specialist majority vote 63.9%; no LLM significantly outperformed specialists (McNemar P>.10 for all models).
quote: no LLM significantly outperformed the specialist panel majority vote (63.9%, 95% CI 57.3%-70.1%; McNemar test, P>.10 for all models)
sample_unit: outpatients with vertigo or dizziness (prospective clinical evaluation); 227 histories in history-based evaluation

title: ImmunoResponse Predictor: a GUI for accurate response prediction to immunotherapy
outcome: Whether cohort-level applicability metric detects dataset shift relative to training data and tracks accuracy
effect: Applicability 74%, 76%, 71% with accuracy 69%, 83%, 86%; UNC-108 applicability 48% with accuracy 53%, flagged as shifted. Cosine distance alone was inconsistent (73% for UNC-108).
quote: In contrast, the UNC-108 cohort exhibited applicability below 60% and achieved a prediction accuracy of only 53%, indicating a substantial shift relative to the training data.
sample_unit: patients across four external test cohorts (PCD mUC 94, PCD mRCC 58, Moreno 11, UNC-108 89)

title: ImmunoResponse Predictor: a GUI for accurate response prediction to immunotherapy
outcome: Prediction performance variation across independent cohorts/sites
effect: Accuracy 69%, 83%, 86% in three cohorts but 53% in UNC-108; precision 24% in UNC-108.
quote: LogitDA with our signature (ours) demonstrated stable performance in the PCD(mUC), PCD(mRCC), and Moreno cohorts, but only moderate performance in the UNC-108 cohort.
sample_unit: patients across four external test cohorts (PCD mUC 94, PCD mRCC 58, Moreno 11, UNC-108 89)

title: ImmunoResponse Predictor: a GUI for accurate response prediction to immunotherapy
outcome: Asymmetric score cutoffs minimizing false negatives across cohorts
effect: FNR 0% (PCD mUC), 33% (PCD mRCC), 25% (Moreno), 27% (UNC-108); precision 41%, 40%, 100%, 24%.
quote: The associated false negative rates (FNRs; corresponding precisions) were 0% (41%) for PCD (mUC), 33% (40%) for PCD (mRCC), 25% (100%) for Moreno, and 27% (24%) for UNC-108 (see Table 1 for details).
sample_unit: patients across four external test cohorts (PCD mUC 94, PCD mRCC 58, Moreno 11, UNC-108 89)

title: ImmunoResponse Predictor: a GUI for accurate response prediction to immunotherapy
outcome: external-cohort prediction accuracy
effect: Accuracies were 0.69, 0.83, 0.86, and 0.53 across four independent cohorts.
quote: LogitDA achieved prediction accuracies of 0.69, 0.83, 0.86, and 0.53, with corresponding applicability estimates of 74%, 76%, 71%, and 48%, respectively, correctly identifying the UNC-108 cohort as one in which predictions warrant increased caution.
sample_unit: patients across four external test cohorts (PCD mUC 94, PCD mRCC 58, Moreno 11, UNC-108 89)

title: ImmunoResponse Predictor: a GUI for accurate response prediction to immunotherapy
outcome: out-of-distribution cohort flagging
effect: Applicability estimates were 74%, 76%, 71%, and 48%, flagging UNC-108 where accuracy was 0.53.
quote: LogitDA achieved prediction accuracies of 0.69, 0.83, 0.86, and 0.53, with corresponding applicability estimates of 74%, 76%, 71%, and 48%, respectively, correctly identifying the UNC-108 cohort as one in which predictions warrant increased caution.
sample_unit: patients across four external test cohorts (PCD mUC 94, PCD mRCC 58, Moreno 11, UNC-108 89)

title: ImmunoResponse Predictor: a GUI for accurate response prediction to immunotherapy
outcome: Prediction accuracy under distributional shift
effect: Accuracy was 53% in the UNC-108 cohort with applicability below 60%, compared to 69%-86% in cohorts with applicability above 70%, reflecting marked degradation from distributional shift.
quote: In contrast, the UNC-108 cohort exhibited applicability below 60% and achieved a prediction accuracy of only 53%, indicating a substantial shift relative to the training data.
sample_unit: patients across four external test cohorts (PCD mUC 94, PCD mRCC 58, Moreno 11, UNC-108 89)

title: Accuracy, Reliability, and Bloom's Taxonomy Performance of Seven Large Language Models on Microbiology Questions
venue: Advances in medical education and practice
outcome: Test-retest reliability (ICC) of LLM answers across three repeated sessions
effect: Claude ICC 0.966 (excellent) vs Gemini ICC 0.290 (poor); session-to-session fluctuations of up to 100 percentage points on individual topics.
quote: Test-retest reliability varied dramatically: Claude achieved excellent ICC (0.966), while Gemini exhibited poor reliability (ICC = 0.290), with session-to-session fluctuations of up to 100 percentage points on individual topics.
sample_unit: LLM responses (200 microbiology MCQs x 7 models x 3 sessions)

title: The Understandability and Readability of Online Patient Education Materials and ChatGPT Responses Regarding Xerostomia
outcome: Reading grade level and understandability of ChatGPT xerostomia patient education responses versus online sources
effect: ChatGPT mean FKGL 15.24, FRE 30.14, PEMAT 72.33; online sources FKGL 9.87, FRE 51.37, PEMAT 79.92. Both exceeded recommended reading levels.
quote: Both online PEM and ChatGPT responses on xerostomia exceeded recommended reading levels, with ChatGPT generating substantially less readable content.

title: Measuring Depression Severity With Clinical Global Impression-Severity Scale Scores From Clinical Notes Using Large Language Models: Validation Study
outcome: Model-human agreement across age, sex, race, and treatment location subgroups
effect: Model agreement did not significantly differ across age, sex, race, treatment location, or percentage of copy-forwarded text; lower for notes below median length (κ=0.72 vs 0.92; P=.003).
quote: Model agreement did not significantly differ across age, sex, race, treatment location, or the percentage of copy-forwarded text, but it was significantly lower for notes below the median note length than for notes at or above the median length (κ=0.72 vs 0.92; P=.003).

title: Measuring Depression Severity With Clinical Global Impression-Severity Scale Scores From Clinical Notes Using Large Language Models: Validation Study
outcome: Comparison of candidate LLMs and prompting strategies against psychiatrist ratings on the same notes
effect: GPT-4o zero-shot had highest agreement with average human ratings (κ=0.85, 95% CI 0.78-0.90); few-shot did not improve; Llama-4 zero-shot lower (κ=0.70, 95% CI 0.55-0.80).
quote: GPT-4o with zero-shot prompting demonstrated the highest agreement with average human ratings (κ=0.85, 95% CI 0.78-0.90), and few-shot prompting did not improve performance.

title: CONRep: Uncertainty-Aware Vision-Language Report Drafting Using Conformal Prediction
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Agreement with ground truth in conformal-prediction certain versus uncertain outputs
effect: Certain outputs had significantly higher AUROCs across multiple findings (P < 0.05) and greater semantic similarity to reference impressions (P < 0.001); an independent LLM evaluator agreed (P < 0.001).
quote: Across both pipelines, outputs classified as certain demonstrated significantly higher agreement with GT than uncertain outputs.

title: Prompt Configurations for Multimodal Large Language Models in Diagnosing and Staging Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: Multimodel Retrospective Observational Diagnostic Study
outcome: run-to-run grading stability
effect: SI exact agreement 0.44‐0.81, mean 0.65; mean absolute differences 0.22‐1.09 stages, mean 0.60.
quote: In contrast, SI input showed lower stability, with exact agreement of 0.44‐0.81 (mean 0.65, SD 0.16) and mean absolute differences of 0.22‐1.09 stages (mean 0.60, SD 0.27).

title: Prompt Configurations for Multimodal Large Language Models in Diagnosing and Staging Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: Multimodel Retrospective Observational Diagnostic Study
outcome: Stand-alone diagnostic performance of MLLMs for ONFH detection and grading
effect: Single-image detection AUC 0.50-0.58 (mean 0.55); detailed ARCO grading accuracy 0.22 with SI; authors conclude none should be used independently for clinical decision-making.
quote: Nevertheless, none of the evaluated models should currently be used independently for clinical decision-making.

title: Prompt Configurations for Multimodal Large Language Models in Diagnosing and Staging Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: Multimodel Retrospective Observational Diagnostic Study
outcome: MLLM performance compared with surgeons and commercial versus open-source models on same data
effect: Surgeons mean detailed grading accuracy 0.71 (SD 0.19) versus MLLM ID ARCO 0.56; no significant commercial versus open-source difference (P=.83).
quote: Consistent with the bootstrap analysis, no significant overall difference was found between commercial and open-source models, though some model-specific variations existed ( Figure 5 C,D).

title: Prompt Configurations for Multimodal Large Language Models in Diagnosing and Staging Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: Multimodel Retrospective Observational Diagnostic Study
outcome: detailed staging accuracy
effect: Mean detailed grading accuracy was 0.34 to 0.59 for Ficat, 0.22 to 0.56 for ARCO, and 0.19 to 0.49 for Steinberg.
quote: The mean detailed grading accuracy increased from 0.34 (SD 0.08) to 0.59 (SD 0.04) for Ficat, from 0.22 (SD 0.05) to 0.56 (SD 0.11) for ARCO, and from 0.19 (SD 0.05) to 0.49 (SD 0.05) for Steinberg.

title: Optimising Pharmacovigilance Efficiency with MLIT (Machine Learning for Intelligent Triage): A Tool for Statistical Safety Alerts
outcome: Prospective concordance between model predictions and reviewers' decisions on live alerts
effect: 92% of vaccine alerts closed in alignment with model's top-ranked prediction; 98% within top 3 predictions; comparable results for drug portfolio.
quote: In the prospective validation phase, 92% of vaccine alerts were closed in alignment with the model's top-ranked prediction, while 98% were closed within the top 3 predictions.

title: TrustEndo: A Conformal-Calibrated MLLM With Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Trustworthy Gastroscopic Diagnosis
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
outcome: Hallucination rate of diagnostic descriptions with retrieval-augmented, concept-grounded generation versus MLLM baselines
effect: Hallucination rate 7.8% versus 15-20% for baseline MLLMs; AP 40.9% versus 39.5% for best baseline.
quote: On LGLDD, Endo21, and HyperKvasir, TrustEndo achieves AP 40.9% (vs. 39.5% best MLLM baseline), hallucination rate 7.8% (vs. 15-20%), and ECE 0.038 (vs. 0.118+), with 95% empirical coverage on detection.

title: TrustEndo: A Conformal-Calibrated MLLM With Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Trustworthy Gastroscopic Diagnosis
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
outcome: Calibration (ECE) and coverage of confidence with conformal safety layer versus baselines
effect: ECE 0.038 versus 0.118+ for baselines, with 95% empirical coverage on detection.
quote: On LGLDD, Endo21, and HyperKvasir, TrustEndo achieves AP 40.9% (vs. 39.5% best MLLM baseline), hallucination rate 7.8% (vs. 15-20%), and ECE 0.038 (vs. 0.118+), with 95% empirical coverage on detection.
sample_unit: gastroscopic images (three datasets: LGLDD, Endo21, HyperKvasir)

title: Intelligent Framework for Adverse Drug Event Identification Using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: ADE identification F1/recall with retrieval-augmented prompts versus non-augmented and static-augmented prompts
effect: RAG raised GPT-4o L3 recall from 0.6419 (NAG) to 0.9241 (FDR P=.003); DeepSeek-V3 L3 F1 0.9638 with RAG vs 0.9022 NAG and 0.9441 SAG.
quote: However, under the SAG prompt, GPT-4o’s recall rate increased to 69.93%, and under the RAG prompt, it surged to 92.41%, representing an improvement of almost 30% (FDR P =.003).

title: Intelligent Framework for Adverse Drug Event Identification Using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: Inter-annotator agreement of reference standard built with blinded pharmacists and consensus adjudication
effect: Two blinded annotators reviewed 5535 notes; Cohen kappa=0.86, disagreements resolved by consensus discussion.
quote: Interrater reliability was assessed using Cohen κ based on 5535 clinical notes independently reviewed by 2 annotators, yielding a high agreement (Cohen κ=0.86).

title: Intelligent Framework for Adverse Drug Event Identification Using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: Accuracy of LLM ADE extraction against gold-standard reference
effect: Best DeepSeek-V3 RAG L3 F1 0.9638; but 15 notes misidentified by all three models, mostly commission errors (~80%); L1 exact-match recall only ~0.55-0.58.
quote: Notably, 15 critical records posed recognition challenges for all 3 models.

title: Intelligent Framework for Adverse Drug Event Identification Using Large Language Models and Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Development and Evaluation Study
outcome: Performance on uncurated real-world notes with ~4.6% ADE prevalence versus curated balanced set
effect: Real-world DeepSeek-V3 RAG L3 F1 0.8159 vs SAG 0.8134 (marginal), precision 0.7185, recall 0.9448, specificity 0.9821; NAG F1 0.6380.
quote: At the L3 level, RAG achieved an F 1 -score of 0.8159 (95% CI 0.7736‐0.8598), compared with 0.6380 (95% CI 0.5759‐0.6942) for NAG and 0.8134 (95% CI 0.7600‐0.8627) for SAG.

title: Comparative Performance of AI Models and Clinicians in Evidence-Based Cardiovascular Disease Management for People Living With HIV: Comparative Study
outcome: AI model versus clinician ratings on accuracy, completeness, readability, reliability for HIV-CVD guideline questions
effect: All AI models scored higher than clinicians across all dimensions (P<.001); AI mean 3.44-3.68 vs clinicians mean 1.78-2.05; DeepSeek-R1 best.

title: Nurse-Led Ambient AI Scribe for Patient Safety Incident Investigation Reports (Project NARRATE): Retrospective Pre-Post Comparative Document-Quality Study
outcome: WHO-aligned report completeness with workflow including visible missing-information cues
effect: Completeness 13.61 vs 11.81; cluster-adjusted difference 1.95 (95% CI 0.91-3.00; P<.001); persisted after deformatting (1.70, 95% CI 0.27-3.14). Bundled workflow, voluntary adopters; cue effect not isolated.

title: Nurse-Led Ambient AI Scribe for Patient Safety Incident Investigation Reports (Project NARRATE): Retrospective Pre-Post Comparative Document-Quality Study
outcome: Completeness and narrative quality of locally tailored ambient-scribe investigation reports
effect: Voluntary pre-post comparison: completeness adjusted difference 1.95 (95% CI 0.91-3.00; P<.001); adapted PDQI difference 0.53 (95% CI 0.37-0.69; P<.001). Results concern the bundled workflow; template-specific effects were not isolated.
quote: Unadjusted mean WHO total completeness was 11.81 (SD 3.39) for conventional reports and 13.61 (SD 2.54) for NARRATE reports; the unadjusted difference was 1.80 points, and the cluster-adjusted mean difference was 1.95 (95% CI 0.91-3.00; P<.001).

title: Nurse-Led Ambient AI Scribe for Patient Safety Incident Investigation Reports (Project NARRATE): Retrospective Pre-Post Comparative Document-Quality Study
outcome: adapted PDQI narrative quality
effect: The cluster-adjusted mean difference for the adapted PDQI mean score was 0.53 points higher for AI-supported reports (95% CI 0.37-0.69; P<.001).
quote: After accounting for multiple reports contributed by the same supervisor, the cluster-adjusted mean difference was 0.53 (95% CI 0.37‐0.69; P <.001) points.

title: AI Patient Support and 6-Month Medication Adherence in a Digital Obesity Program: A Retrospective Analysis
outcome: 6-month semaglutide adherence before vs after AI support agent, adjusted and matched
effect: Unadjusted adherence 53.2% vs 47.3% (p<0.001), but adjusted post-Junebot era had higher odds of attrition (OR 1.178; 95% CI 1.052-1.318); era-matched PSM OR 1.309 (p=0.038).
quote: Integrating an AI digital assistant did not independently improve medication adherence; programmatic costs, program pauses and initial tracking anxiety were stronger predictors of long-term retention.

title: Diagnostic performance and short-interval reproducibility of multimodal large language models in differentiating cholesteatoma from chronic otitis media using key-image temporal bone high-resolution computed tomography
outcome: Between-session reproducibility of LLM classifications on repeated runs one week apart
effect: Between-session reproducibility was fair for GPT-5 (κ: 0.360) and moderate for Gemini 2.5 Pro (κ: 0.485); inter-model agreement slight (κ: 0.035 at S1, 0.086 at S2).
quote: Between-session reproducibility was fair for GPT-5 (κ: 0.360) and moderate for Gemini 2.5 Pro (κ: 0.485), and inter-model agreement was slight at both sessions (κ: 0.035 at S1 and κ: 0.086 at S2).

title: Diagnostic performance and short-interval reproducibility of multimodal large language models in differentiating cholesteatoma from chronic otitis media using key-image temporal bone high-resolution computed tomography
outcome: Multimodal LLM diagnostic accuracy versus radiologist on same HRCT images
effect: Radiologist accuracy 96.0% (κ 0.921); GPT-5 43.6%/46.5% and Gemini 2.5 Pro 49.5%/47.5% in S1/S2, with specificity 1.9%-13.2%.
quote: The radiologist achieved an accuracy of 96.0% (95% CI: 90.3-98.4) with almost perfect agreement with the reference standard (κ: 0.921).

title: Determinants of Reader-LLM Interaction in Thoracic Radiology: Impact of Model Confidence and Reader Expertise
outcome: Reader adequate interaction and overreliance with versus without LLM assistance, by LLM accuracy and confidence
effect: Model confidence (OR 3.82) and reader expertise (OR 2.06) independently associated with adequate interaction; higher rationale quality increased acceptance of incorrect suggestions (OR 1.71) while reducing rejection of correct ones (OR 0.79).
quote: Higher rationale quality reduced rejection of correct suggestions (OR, 0.79 [95% CI: 0.67, 0.93]; P = .005) but increased acceptance of incorrect suggestions (OR, 1.71 [95% CI: 1.47, 1.99]; P < .001).
sample_unit: chest imaging cases (each read by 10 readers, 1000 reader-case pairs per session)

title: Determinants of Reader-LLM Interaction in Thoracic Radiology: Impact of Model Confidence and Reader Expertise
outcome: Reader acceptance of incorrect LLM suggestions (automation bias/overreliance)
effect: Higher rationale quality increased acceptance of incorrect suggestions (OR 1.71); higher reader expertise (OR 0.54) and reader confidence (OR 0.80) reduced acceptance of incorrect suggestions.
quote: Higher reader expertise (OR, 0.54 [95% CI: 0.41, 0.70]; P < .001) and reader confidence (OR, 0.80 [95% CI: 0.67, 0.94]; P = .007) were protective, reducing acceptance of incorrect suggestions.
sample_unit: chest imaging cases (each read by 10 readers, 1000 reader-case pairs per session)

title: Determinants of Reader-LLM Interaction in Thoracic Radiology: Impact of Model Confidence and Reader Expertise
outcome: Association of model confidence with readers' adequate acceptance or rejection of LLM suggestions
effect: Model confidence associated with adequate interaction (OR 3.82, 95% CI 1.58-9.25), with weaker effect among experts (OR 0.79).
quote: After multivariable adjustment, model confidence (odds ratio [OR], 3.82 [95% CI: 1.58, 9.25]; P = .003) and reader expertise (OR, 2.06 [95% CI: 1.38, 3.07]; P < .001) were independently associated with adequate interaction, with a weaker effect of confidence among experts (OR, 0.79 [95% CI: 0.67, 0.94]; P = .008).
sample_unit: chest imaging cases (each read by 10 readers, 1000 reader-case pairs per session)

title: Finite State Machine-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Generation Improves Expert-Rated Acceptability of a Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter Self-Management Chatbot: Single-Center Content Validation Study
outcome: Expert preference between fine-tuned model with and without RAG grounding
effect: Model 2 (FT+RAG) did not differ from model 1 (FT only) in expert preference after Bonferroni correction; adding FSM (model 3) was preferred in 34/43 (79.1%) scenarios.
quote: Pairwise McNemar tests showed model 3 was preferred significantly more often than model 1 and model 2 (both P<.001), while model 1 versus model 2 did not differ after Bonferroni correction.

title: Critical Care-Specific vs General-Purpose Large Language Models in Emergency Intensive Care Unit Diagnosis: Single-Center Retrospective Paired Comparative Study
outcome: Top-1 diagnostic accuracy of critical care-specific LLM versus general-purpose LLMs on same EICU data
effect: Final-stage top-1: Qiyuan 64.1% (118/184), GPT-5.1 59.2%, DeepSeek V3.1 57.1%, Qwen3-32B 51.6%; no significant gaps between Qiyuan and top 2 general models.
quote: Corrected pairwise comparisons (α=.0083) confirmed Qiyuan 3.0.1, GPT-5.1, and DeepSeek all outperformed Qwen3-32B significantly (all adjusted P<.008), while no statistical gaps were detected between Qiyuan 3.0.1 and the 2 top-performing general models.

title: Critical Care-Specific vs General-Purpose Large Language Models in Emergency Intensive Care Unit Diagnosis: Single-Center Retrospective Paired Comparative Study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of LLMs on real EICU clinical cases
effect: All models' top-1 accuracy stayed below 70%, with heterogeneous performance across core EICU diseases including sepsis, severe pneumonia, and gastrointestinal bleeding.
quote: Notably, all models' top-1 accuracy stayed below 70%, and stratified analysis revealed heterogeneous performance across core EICU diseases including sepsis, severe pneumonia, and gastrointestinal bleeding.

title: Benchmarking large language models for question answering on German clinical practice guidelines
outcome: LLM accuracy on German guideline questions with vs without RAG grounding
effect: RAG substantially improved accuracy across all tested models and most retrievers; GPT-5 with multilingual-e5-large reached 95%; gpt-oss-120b reached 90% with RAG.
quote: RAG integration substantially improved accuracy across all tested models and for most retrievers.

title: Development and Prospective Validation of a Machine Learning Tool for Predicting Multidrug-resistant Organism Infections in an Indian Critical Care Unit
venue: Indian journal of critical care medicine : peer-reviewed, official publication of Indian Society of Critical Care Medicine
outcome: Gap between training and test accuracy of random forest model
effect: Training accuracy 96.0% versus test-set accuracy 75.3%, indicating overfitting.
quote: While the performance discrepancy between training and testing indicates overfitting, the high specificity and sensitivity observed in the prospective pilot phase support its potential as a bedside aid for early antimicrobial stewardship (AMS).
sample_unit: patients (prospective validation cohort; 323 in retrospective development)

title: Leveraging large language models for information extraction from free-text liver MRI reports and assessment of clinical utility: a multicenter study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Report-level extraction success by center (site) for each LLM
effect: ChatGPT-4o varied across centers (Center 2 89.0% vs Center 4 78.0%, P=0.032); DeepSeek-V3 showed no significant difference across centers (P=0.114).
quote: Additionally, ChatGPT-4o exhibited significant variability across centers, particularly between Center 2 and Center 4 (89.0% vs. 78.0%, P=0.032), whereas DeepSeek-V3 showed no such difference.

title: Leveraging large language models for information extraction from free-text liver MRI reports and assessment of clinical utility: a multicenter study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Overestimation of report-level extraction accuracy owing to predominance of negative fields
effect: Report-level success fell from 85.4% to 75.9% (DeepSeek-V3) and from 83.3% to 73.4% (ChatGPT-4o) when only positive fields were assessed.
quote: In the sensitivity analysis ( Table S4 ), the report-level extraction success rates decreased to 75.9% (607/800) for DeepSeek-V3 and 73.4% (587/800) for ChatGPT-4o.

title: Leveraging large language models for information extraction from free-text liver MRI reports and assessment of clinical utility: a multicenter study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: macro F1 with local prompting
effect: Center-specific prompting improved F1 by 0.017-0.024 for DeepSeek-V3 and 0.014-0.026 for ChatGPT-4o versus global prompting.
quote: Center-specific prompting consistently outperformed global prompting (∆F1: 0.017-0.024 for DeepSeek-V3; 0.014-0.026 for ChatGPT-4o).

title: Swin-Qwen3: a three-stage vision-language framework for automated radiology report generation with multi-agent verification
outcome: Hallucination correction by the verifier stage and overall hallucination rate and factuality across one-, two-, three-stage variants
effect: Verifier corrected 85.6% of identified hallucinations, but the hallucination rate stayed 0.6116 (three-stage) vs 0.6109 (one/two-stage) and factuality was 0.843 vs 0.845.
quote: However, the clinical verifier demonstrated substantial effectiveness, correcting 85.6% of identified hallucinations.

title: From Promising Capabilities to Pervasive Bias: Assessing Large Language Models for Emergency Department Triage
outcome: LLM triage preference differences under counterfactual variation of patient sex and race
effect: LLMs showed sex-based differences that were more pronounced in certain racial groups, indicating intersectional bias. No numeric results are reported in the abstract.
quote: LLMs exhibit sex-based differences, and they are more pronounced in certain racial groups, suggesting that LLMs encode preferences that emerge in specific clinical contexts and combinations of characteristics.

title: From Promising Capabilities to Pervasive Bias: Assessing Large Language Models for Emergency Department Triage
outcome: Robustness of LLM versus conventional ML triage under distribution shift and missing data
effect: LLMs were more robust than traditional ML to distribution shifts and missing data. No numeric results are reported in the abstract.
quote: First, we demonstrate that LLMs exhibit superior robustness compared to traditional ML, which is promising due to their ability to provide explanatory rationales.

title: Postoperative Nocardia cyriacigeorgica infection after glioblastoma resection: correlating metagenomic next-generation sequencing with conventional microbiology
outcome: Consistency and correctness of multimodal AI outputs across systems and five repeated runs
effect: Outputs were discordant between three systems; one system was incorrect in a stable, reproducible way. Repeated queries were reproducible, but reproducibility did not ensure correctness.
quote: The artificial intelligence outputs were discordant between systems and, in one system, incorrect in a stable and reproducible way; this illustrates current limitations rather than clinical readiness and supports the need for prespecified, blinded, multi-case validation before clinical deployment.
sample_unit: AI queries (3 systems x 5 repeats) for a single case

title: ChatGPT-4o in delirium recognition: a pilot study
outcome: Reproducibility of delirium identification across repeated independent and consecutive sessions
effect: ChatGPT-4o identified delirium in 70% of cases in both independent sessions and 90% in consecutive-session run; agreement between independent sessions κ=0.76, but low agreement involving consecutive run, suggesting contextual priming.
quote: Agreement between independent ChatGPT-4o sessions was substantial (κ=0.76), while agreement involving the consecutive-session run was low, suggesting contextual priming.

title: ChatGPT-4o in delirium recognition: a pilot study
outcome: Delirium identification of ChatGPT-4o versus comparator model DeepSeek-V2 on same vignettes
effect: ChatGPT-4o identified delirium in 70% (independent sessions) and 90% (consecutive run) of cases, whereas DeepSeek-V2 identified 50%.
quote: ChatGPT-4o identified delirium in 70% of cases in both independent sessions and 90% in the consecutive-session run, whereas DeepSeek-V2 identified 50%.

title: Pediatric vs. Adult Pneumonia Detection: Quantifying Age-related Generalization Gaps in Zero-shot Multimodal Large Language Models
outcome: Pneumonia detection MCC by age subgroup (pediatric vs adult) for zero-shot multimodal LLMs versus CNN
effect: Pediatric MCC: GPT-5.2 0.484, Claude Opus 4.5 0.470, Gemini 2.5 Pro 0.272 vs CNN 0.799. Age-related ΔMCC larger for LLMs (+0.220 to +0.466) than CNN (+0.051).
quote: Age-related gains were larger for LLMs (ΔMCC +0.220 [95% CI 0.160-0.281] to +0.466 [0.407-0.525]) than for the CNN (ΔMCC +0.051 [0.005-0.098]), driven mainly by specificity increases.

title: Pediatric vs. Adult Pneumonia Detection: Quantifying Age-related Generalization Gaps in Zero-shot Multimodal Large Language Models
outcome: Comparison of zero-shot LLMs against domain-trained CNN baseline on same test sets
effect: CNN outperformed all LLMs in pediatrics (MCC 0.799 vs 0.484, 0.470, 0.272) and remained best in adults (MCC 0.850).
quote: In adults, all models improved, but the CNN remained best (MCC 0.850, 0.816-0.882).

title: AI-assisted rheumatology triage changes with referral framing
outcome: Change in AI triage concordance when patient race/ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and language barrier were varied
effect: Race or ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and language barrier produced no detectable effect, including in mixed-effects models accounting for repeated vignette use; framing cues (anxious, anchoring) did shift outputs.
quote: In contrast, race or ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and language barrier produced no detectable effect, including in mixed-effects models that accounted for repeated vignette use.
sample_unit: case variants (30 physician-authored rheumatology vignettes, each rephrased three times)

title: AI-assisted rheumatology triage changes with referral framing
outcome: Change in concordance with expert ground truth under framing perturbations
effect: Baseline concordance 0.869; clinician anchoring reduced concordance, significantly for acuity (dismissive anchor, vignette-level p = 0.01), mainly by downgrading urgency.
quote: Clinician anchoring in the referral note reduced concordance, consistently across models and rephrasings and significantly for acuity (dismissive anchor, vignette-level p = 0.01), mainly by downgrading urgency.
sample_unit: case variants (30 physician-authored rheumatology vignettes, each rephrased three times)

title: AI-assisted rheumatology triage changes with referral framing
outcome: Attribution of symptoms to psychological vs organic causes when patient described as anxious
effect: Models attributed symptoms to psychological causes 13.1% vs 4.5% at baseline; odds ratio 3.2 versus stoic framing.
quote: When patients were described as anxious, models attributed symptoms to psychological rather than organic causes nearly three times as often as at baseline (13.1% vs 4.5%; odds ratio 3.2 versus stoic framing), a shift that risks relabeling organic disease as functional.
sample_unit: case variants (30 physician-authored rheumatology vignettes, each rephrased three times)

title: Understanding of Preeclampsia Risk Factors in Large Language Models Compared with a Validated Competing-Risks Model
outcome: Agreement of LLM preeclampsia risk predictor effects with the validated FMF competing-risks model
effect: Composite scores 0.59 to 0.82; directionality preserved up to 90.9% in higher-scoring models; magnitude agreement limited (R2 0.44-0.59); lower-scoring models had frequent sign inconsistencies.
quote: Alignment between LLM outputs and the FMF model was heterogeneous, with composite scores ranging from 0.59 to 0.82.

title: Causal Uncertainty-Decomposed Ensemble Learning for Confounding-Aware Skin Cancer Detection in Dermoscopic Images
outcome: Accuracy and false-negative rates after deferring the most uncertain cases
effect: Deferring the 10% most uncertain cases raised non-deferred accuracy from 89.7% to 93.2% and reduced false-negative rates for melanoma, BCC and SCC in the non-deferred subset.
quote: Deferring the 10% most uncertain cases increased non-deferred accuracy from 89.7% to 93.2% and reduced false-negative rates for melanoma, BCC and SCC in the non-deferred subset.

title: Causal Uncertainty-Decomposed Ensemble Learning for Confounding-Aware Skin Cancer Detection in Dermoscopic Images
outcome: Relative performance drop under synthetic acquisition artifacts
effect: CUDE showed a relative performance drop of 5.0%, compared with 9.6% for the deep ensemble. Both models degraded under artifacts.
quote: Under the predefined synthetic artifact protocol, CUDE showed a relative performance drop of 5.0%, compared with 9.6% for the deep ensemble.

title: A Self-Controlled Benchmark of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models on Clinical Guideline Questions
outcome: Accuracy and hallucination rate with vs without guideline retrieval grounding
effect: Content-level hallucination fell from 42% to 4%; judge accuracy rose by pooled +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89%.
quote: On the judge, content-level hallucination fell from 42% to 4% and accuracy rose by a pooled +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); the accuracy gain persisted after adjustment for response length (+0.48, 95% CI 0.22-0.73), which retrieval shortened rather than lengthened.
sample_unit: evaluations (50 questions x 6 models x 3 repetitions)

title: A Self-Controlled Benchmark of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models on Clinical Guideline Questions
outcome: Retrieval recall and citation groundedness of a documented guideline RAG corpus
effect: Retrieval recall@5 was 92%; citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89% deterministically from retrieval logs.
quote: Deterministically from the retrieval logs, citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89% and retrieval recall@5 was 92%.
sample_unit: evaluations (50 questions x 6 models x 3 repetitions)

title: A Self-Controlled Benchmark of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models on Clinical Guideline Questions
outcome: Citation groundedness and auditability of answers with guideline retrieval
effect: Citation groundedness rose from 0% to 51-89%; hallucination and auditability gains were consistent across all models.
quote: The accuracy gain was large for weaker base models and small or non-significant for already-strong ones, whereas the hallucination and auditability gains were consistent across all models.
sample_unit: evaluations (50 questions x 6 models x 3 repetitions)

title: A Self-Controlled Benchmark of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models on Clinical Guideline Questions
outcome: Hallucination rate of standard LLMs without guideline access
effect: Content-level hallucination was 42% without retrieval, falling to 4% with retrieval; residual hallucination requires human oversight.
quote: On the judge, content-level hallucination fell from 42% to 4% and accuracy rose by a pooled +0.64 points (95% CI 0.47-0.80); the accuracy gain persisted after adjustment for response length (+0.48, 95% CI 0.22-0.73), which retrieval shortened rather than lengthened.
sample_unit: evaluations (50 questions x 6 models x 3 repetitions)

title: Evaluating Large Language Models for AI-Assisted Decision Support in Legal Capacity Assessment: A Comparative Study Using Interdisciplinary Medical Board Recommendations as the Expert Medical Reference Standard
outcome: Test-retest reliability of LLM categorical recommendations across repeated runs
effect: Temporal stability was high (κ = 0.87-0.95); agreement with IMBD recommendations ranged from κ = 0.60 to 0.73.
quote: Agreement with IMBD recommendations ranged from κ = 0.60 to 0.73, with high temporal stability (κ = 0.87-0.95); pairwise differences between the three models were not statistically significant after Holm correction.

title: Evaluation of Large Language Models in Generating Physical Exercise Rehabilitation Programs for Musculoskeletal Disorders Across Multiple Clinical Scenarios
outcome: Readability of LLM responses versus recommended reading levels across six indices
effect: Most responses exceeded the recommended reading levels across six readability indices (p < 0.05).
quote: The readability scores across six indices indicated that most responses exceeded the recommended reading levels (p < 0.05).

title: A Generalizable and Interpretable Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Integrating Conformal Uncertainty Quantification and Consensus-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence Across Multiple Cohorts
outcome: Conformal coverage under zero-shot transfer versus local recalibration on target-cohort sample
effect: Zero-shot coverage plateaued near 0.85 at alpha=0.05; recalibrating on 37 held-out TCGA samples restored nominal coverage (split-conformal 0.984, 0.973, 0.893 at alpha 0.05, 0.10, 0.20).
quote: In contrast, recalibrating the conformal layer on a held-out TCGA split (Regime 3; 37 calibration samples, all of the minority class), with the classifier still trained only on CPTAC and exposed to no TCGA label during training, restored nominal coverage at every level
sample_unit: tumor samples (140 CPTAC discovery, 150 TCGA external)
country: Not reported (public US cohorts CPTAC-PDAC and TCGA-PAAD; authors' future work references Turkey)

title: A Generalizable and Interpretable Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Integrating Conformal Uncertainty Quantification and Consensus-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence Across Multiple Cohorts
outcome: Discrimination of a CPTAC-trained classifier on an external, independent cohort versus internal cross-validation
effect: Internal nested CV AUROC ~0.96; external TCGA AUROC 0.913-0.938 (ensemble 0.961), with a small gap (0.959 to 0.938 for GNB) versus typical 5-15 point drops.
quote: First, the modest ΔAUROC of −0.021 for Gaussian Naïve Bayes between internal cross-validation and external evaluation (0.959 → 0.938) is among the smallest cross-cohort gaps reported in the PDAC subtype literature
sample_unit: tumor samples (140 CPTAC discovery, 150 TCGA external)
country: Not reported (public US cohorts CPTAC-PDAC and TCGA-PAAD; authors' future work references Turkey)

title: A Generalizable and Interpretable Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Integrating Conformal Uncertainty Quantification and Consensus-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence Across Multiple Cohorts
outcome: Dataset shift between development and external cohorts affecting performance and conformal validity
effect: Minimal batch effect on discrimination (cohort AUROC 0.58; 1.0% variance to cohort) but exchangeability violation caused ~10-point conformal undercoverage (~0.85 vs 0.95 target).
quote: All four conformal procedures converged to a coverage ceiling of approximately 0.85 at α = 0.05, despite targeting 0.95—a residual 10-percentage-point undercoverage.
sample_unit: tumor samples (140 CPTAC discovery, 150 TCGA external)
country: Not reported (public US cohorts CPTAC-PDAC and TCGA-PAAD; authors' future work references Turkey)

title: A Generalizable and Interpretable Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Integrating Conformal Uncertainty Quantification and Consensus-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence Across Multiple Cohorts
outcome: Reliability of reference-standard subtype labels (Moffitt vs PurIST agreement)
effect: Moffitt-PurIST agreement 78.6% (kappa 0.54) in CPTAC and 70.7% (kappa 0.42) in TCGA; labels derived from signature raise circularity concern.
quote: The Moffitt and PurIST subtype labels agreed in 78.6% of CPTAC samples (Cohen’s κ = 0.54, 95% CI 0.40–0.67) and 70.7% of TCGA samples (κ = 0.42, 0.30–0.54), corresponding to moderate agreement.
sample_unit: tumor samples (140 CPTAC discovery, 150 TCGA external)
country: Not reported (public US cohorts CPTAC-PDAC and TCGA-PAAD; authors' future work references Turkey)

title: A Generalizable and Interpretable Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Integrating Conformal Uncertainty Quantification and Consensus-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence Across Multiple Cohorts
outcome: abstention for uncertain tumors
effect: Abstention was 14.0%, 19.5%, 5.3%, and 0% across increasing Moffitt margin strata.
quote: Importantly, abstention behaved as theoretically expected with respect to the Moffitt label-assignment margin ( Supplementary Figure S2 ): samples with a margin below 0.25 had a 14.0% abstention rate, samples with a margin of 0.25–0.50 had a 19.5% rate, samples with a margin of 0.50–1.00 had a 5.3% rate, and samples with a margin above 1.0 had a 0% rate.
sample_unit: tumor samples (140 CPTAC discovery, 150 TCGA external)
country: Not reported (public US cohorts CPTAC-PDAC and TCGA-PAAD; authors' future work references Turkey)

title: A Generalizable and Interpretable Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Integrating Conformal Uncertainty Quantification and Consensus-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence Across Multiple Cohorts
outcome: Whether per-patient conformal uncertainty flags borderline tumors via abstention
effect: Abstention was 14.0% (margin <0.25), 19.5% (0.25-0.50), 5.3% (0.50-1.00), and 0% (>1.0), concentrating on borderline tumors that warrant manual review.
quote: That is, the conformal predictor abstained precisely on the biologically borderline tumors—providing a principled mechanism for flagging cases that warrant manual pathology review.
sample_unit: tumor samples (140 CPTAC discovery, 150 TCGA external)
country: Not reported (public US cohorts CPTAC-PDAC and TCGA-PAAD; authors' future work references Turkey)

title: A Generalizable and Interpretable Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Integrating Conformal Uncertainty Quantification and Consensus-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence Across Multiple Cohorts
outcome: Suitability for autonomous use versus decision-support given conformal undercoverage
effect: Even best procedure (CRC) reached only 85.3% coverage vs 95% target; authors do not recommend autonomous use and confine tool to decision support under expert oversight.
quote: However, because even CRC attains only 85.3% empirical coverage against the 0.95 target, we explicitly do not recommend any of these procedures for autonomous clinical use at α = 0.05.
sample_unit: tumor samples (140 CPTAC discovery, 150 TCGA external)
country: Not reported (public US cohorts CPTAC-PDAC and TCGA-PAAD; authors' future work references Turkey)

title: A Generalizable and Interpretable Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification of Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma Integrating Conformal Uncertainty Quantification and Consensus-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence Across Multiple Cohorts
outcome: uncertainty coverage
effect: At α=0.05, CRC coverage 0.853; split 0.847; weighted 0.847; CV+ 0.780, below 0.95 nominal.
quote: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) achieved the highest empirical coverage at α = 0.05 (0.853; abstention rate 0.0%; mean set size 1.000), followed by unweighted Mondrian split-conformal (0.847), weighted Mondrian (0.847), and CV+ (0.780).
sample_unit: tumor samples (140 CPTAC discovery, 150 TCGA external)
country: Not reported (public US cohorts CPTAC-PDAC and TCGA-PAAD; authors' future work references Turkey)

title: Large Language Models as Clinical Support Tools in Drug Information Services: Performance Comparison With Pharmacists
venue: Journal of the American College of Clinical Pharmacy : JACCP
outcome: Citation credibility of LLM responses to drug information questions
effect: Citation credibility fulfillment ranged 0.03-0.36 across seven LLMs, while concordance with pharmacist answers ranged 0.70-0.86.
quote: Concordance was more variable, ranging from 0.70-0.86, whereas citation credibility was consistently weak, ranging from 0.03-0.36.

title: Clinical transportability, calibration drift, and local updating of a B-mode ultrasound radiomics-clinical prediction model for occult high-volume central lymph node metastasis in cN0 papillary thyroid carcinoma: development, temporal validation, and external validation
outcome: Brier score and mean predicted risk in Center 3 before vs after intercept-only local updating
effect: Intercept-only updating aligned mean predicted risk with observed rate; Center 3 recalibrated mean risk changed to 23.5% and Brier score decreased from 0.138 to 0.121.
quote: The largest numeric change was observed in Center 3, where recalibrated mean predicted risk changed to 23.5% and Brier score decreased from 0.138 to 0.121 ( Figure 5 ; Table S4 ).

title: Clinical transportability, calibration drift, and local updating of a B-mode ultrasound radiomics-clinical prediction model for occult high-volume central lymph node metastasis in cN0 papillary thyroid carcinoma: development, temporal validation, and external validation
outcome: Center spectrum shift
effect: Event rates were 44.8%, 45.2%, 41.0%, and 23.5%; Center 3 had lower baseline risk.
quote: Event rates were 44.8%, 45.2%, 41.0%, and 23.5% in the development, temporal validation, Center 2, and Center 3 cohorts.

title: Clinical transportability, calibration drift, and local updating of a B-mode ultrasound radiomics-clinical prediction model for occult high-volume central lymph node metastasis in cN0 papillary thyroid carcinoma: development, temporal validation, and external validation
outcome: Performance variation across sites and ultrasound devices
effect: AUC stable across sites (0.823-0.874) but calibration and PPV varied by center; PPV 0.594 in Center 3 vs 0.877 in temporal cohort.
quote: Thus, the B-mode score accounted for most of the discriminative performance, and the clinical plus B-mode model did not show a consistent external AUC advantage over the B-mode score-only model.

title: Clinical transportability, calibration drift, and local updating of a B-mode ultrasound radiomics-clinical prediction model for occult high-volume central lymph node metastasis in cN0 papillary thyroid carcinoma: development, temporal validation, and external validation
outcome: Predictive values at local prevalence at fixed threshold
effect: At fixed threshold 0.565, PPV/NPV were 0.792/0.749, 0.877/0.774, 0.769/0.805 and 0.594/0.897 across cohorts, varying with local event rate.

title: Clinical transportability, calibration drift, and local updating of a B-mode ultrasound radiomics-clinical prediction model for occult high-volume central lymph node metastasis in cN0 papillary thyroid carcinoma: development, temporal validation, and external validation
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of locked model in temporal and external cohorts
effect: AUC 0.823 in development vs 0.874 temporal, 0.866 Center 2, 0.870 Center 3; calibration held except Center 3 (36.4% predicted vs 23.5% observed).
quote: The locked clinical plus B-mode score model had AUC values of 0.823, 0.874, 0.866, and 0.870, respectively.

title: Clinical transportability, calibration drift, and local updating of a B-mode ultrasound radiomics-clinical prediction model for occult high-volume central lymph node metastasis in cN0 papillary thyroid carcinoma: development, temporal validation, and external validation
outcome: External validation calibration drift
effect: Center 3 overestimated risk: 36.4% predicted vs. 23.5% observed; calibration intercept -0.902.
quote: Mean predicted risk aligned with observed risk in the development, temporal validation, and Center 2 cohorts but overestimated risk in Center 3 (36.4% predicted vs. 23.5% observed; calibration intercept, -0.902).

title: Clinical transportability, calibration drift, and local updating of a B-mode ultrasound radiomics-clinical prediction model for occult high-volume central lymph node metastasis in cN0 papillary thyroid carcinoma: development, temporal validation, and external validation

venue: Clinical & translational oncology : official publication of the Federation of Spanish Oncology Societies and of the National Cancer Institute of Mexico

title: A Multidisciplinary Team-Based Large Language Model Framework for Predicting Postoperative Neurological Complications in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: Model Development and Validation Study

title: Sequential vancomycin trough and dosing interval prediction in ICU patients using general purpose large language models: a head-to-head comparison of ChatGPT and GROK AI
outcome: Comparison of two LLMs on vancomycin trough and dosing interval prediction accuracy
effect: ChatGPT outperformed Grok for trough (MAE 4.07 vs 5.08 mg/L; ±2 mg/L accuracy 37.0% vs 29.0%); Grok better for interval (MAE 1.36 vs 1.61 h). Neither compared with pharmacist TDM.
quote: ChatGPT outperformed Grok in trough prediction (MAE 4.07 vs 5.08 mg/L; RMSE 5.55 vs 7.53 mg/L; ±2 mg/L accuracy 37.0% vs 29.0%), with greater advantage at T1/T2 and in renal dysfunction.

title: Large language models versus expert clinicians in optimizing Chinese patient education materials for temporomandibular disorders: a mixed-methods study integrating readability, accuracy, actionability, and cultural adaptability
outcome: Whether expert review corrects domain-specific errors in LLM-generated TCM and procedural content
effect: Expert-revised LLM texts improved accuracy from 3.23 to 4.49; TCM topics remained lowest across groups (Group C 3.8; Group D 4.0), and LLM TCM depth was limited.
quote: Critically, the human-AI collaboration model remediated these accuracy deficits, achieving accuracy equivalent to clinician-only texts.

title: Large language models versus expert clinicians in optimizing Chinese patient education materials for temporomandibular disorders: a mixed-methods study integrating readability, accuracy, actionability, and cultural adaptability
outcome: Actionability (PEMAT) of plain-language LLM-rewritten materials versus original and clinician-written materials
effect: LLM actionability 95.6% vs original 16.7% and clinician 46.7%; human-AI 95.6%; no human-written text reached the 70% threshold.
quote: All four LLM subgroups scored significantly higher than both A and C (all p ≤ 0.002): GPT-4 (80.0% ± 22.2%, 7/15 ≥ 70%), Claude Opus 4.6 (95.6% ± 11.3%, 13/15 ≥ 70%), DeepSeek-V2 (97.8% ± 8.6%, 14/15 ≥ 70%), Gemini 3.0 pro (95.6% ± 11.3%, 13/15 ≥ 70%).

outcome: Consistency of LLM output actionability and accuracy across prompt styles (empathetic, concise, authoritative)
effect: Accuracy showed borderline gradient across prompts (2.53, 2.67, 2.80; p=0.050); all below clinician 4.00; actionability robust under empathetic/authoritative prompts but attenuated under concise prompt.
quote: Accuracy scores showed a borderline-significant gradient across the three prompt conditions (Friedman χ 2 (2) = 6.00, p = 0.050): Prompt A (2.53 ± 0.61), Prompt B (2.67 ± 0.46), Prompt C (2.80 ± 0.40).
sample_unit: education topics (60 texts in four-group analysis)

title: Safety in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Evaluating Large Language Model Adherence to Antithrombotic Medication and Regional Anesthesia Guidelines
outcome: LLM adherence to 2025 ASRA antithrombotic hold/resumption guidelines in vignettes

title: Safety in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Evaluating Large Language Model Adherence to Antithrombotic Medication and Regional Anesthesia Guidelines

title: AI-ECG Detection of Structural Heart Disease in the Community Setting: Transportability and Spectrum Effects in the PREVUE-VALVE Study
venue: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
outcome: AI-ECG discrimination in community population versus hospital-based derivation cohort
effect: AUC 71% (95% CI 66%-76%) in PREVUE-VALVE vs 83% (95% CI 82%-83%) in hospital cohort; SHD prevalence 8% vs 43%; propensity matching attenuated but did not eliminate the difference.
quote: Consistent with these differences, model discrimination was lower in PREVUE-VALVE than in the hospital-based cohort (AUC: 71% [95% CI: 66%-76%] vs 83% [95% CI: 82%-83%]).
sample_unit: community-dwelling participants aged 65-85 with in-home ECG and echocardiography

title: AI-ECG Detection of Structural Heart Disease in the Community Setting: Transportability and Spectrum Effects in the PREVUE-VALVE Study
venue: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
outcome: AI-ECG performance in a new population compared to developer-reported hospital performance
effect: AUC fell to 71% in community cohort from 83% in hospital cohort; performance similar across external hospital cohorts, indicating disease spectrum drives the drop.
quote: Consistent with these differences, model discrimination was lower in PREVUE-VALVE than in the hospital-based cohort (AUC: 71% [95% CI: 66%-76%] vs 83% [95% CI: 82%-83%]).
sample_unit: community-dwelling participants aged 65-85 with in-home ECG and echocardiography

title: AI-ECG Detection of Structural Heart Disease in the Community Setting: Transportability and Spectrum Effects in the PREVUE-VALVE Study
venue: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

quote: In a community-dwelling population with lower disease prevalence and milder phenotypes, AI-ECG performance was attenuated relative to hospital-based cohorts, driven by differences in disease spectrum.
sample_unit: community-dwelling participants aged 65-85 with in-home ECG and echocardiography

title: Patient-Facing AI System for Symptom Guidance Using Simulated Encounters and Physician Review: Analytical Validation Study
outcome: Missed escalation (undertriage) and unnecessary escalation (overtriage) rates

quote: Overtriage met the prespecified criterion of less than 30%, whereas urgent and nonurgent undertriage did not meet their respective criteria of less than 5% and less than 15%, respectively.

title: Patient-Facing AI System for Symptom Guidance Using Simulated Encounters and Physician Review: Analytical Validation Study
outcome: Performance under simulated use conditions against prespecified criteria before live use

title: External validation of a machine learning-based web application for personalized testing of objective functioning using the five-repetition sit-to-stand test
outcome: Model prediction error of 5R-STS times on external healthy cohort versus observed

quote: In this external validation, the model demonstrated limited generalization including a systematic underestimation of slower test times and insufficient personalized ULN calibration.

title: External validation of a machine learning-based web application for personalized testing of objective functioning using the five-repetition sit-to-stand test
outcome: Performance differences across test setting and country compared with single-center development data

quote: Multivariable regression analyses showed that remote testing was independently associated with greater prediction bias and higher odds of personalized ULN exceedance compared with supervised testing (adjusted mean difference: - 0.90 s; adjusted OR: 10.7).
country: Multiple (including Germany and other countries; three largest national subgroups analyzed)

title: External validation of a machine learning-based web application for personalized testing of objective functioning using the five-repetition sit-to-stand test

quote: These findings indicate that external validity of models derived from single-center data can be limited, underscoring the importance of comprehensive external validation and, potentially, multicenter retraining before clinical implementation.
country: Multiple (including Germany and other countries; three largest national subgroups analyzed)

title: Multimodal Large Language Models and Dental Students in Radiographic Landmark Identification: A Novel Grid-Based Assessment

sample_unit: queries (200 dental radiographs, 12 landmarks, 3 repetitions; 10,800 API calls)

title: Multimodal Large Language Models and Dental Students in Radiographic Landmark Identification: A Novel Grid-Based Assessment

quote: Guided prompting produced heterogeneous effects, improving localisation of some landmarks while causing severe regression on others; most notably, GPT-5.4 directed the majority of lower-left canine apex predictions to the incorrect lower-right molar region, a prompt-resistant mislocalisation pattern absent in Gemini 3.1 Pro.
sample_unit: queries (200 dental radiographs, 12 landmarks, 3 repetitions; 10,800 API calls)

outcome: Documentation time and clinician burnout measured after AI scribe deployment
effect: Active note time decreased 26.2%; survey at 45 days showed most respondents reported reduced burnout; note length rose 28.8%. Coding accuracy and intensity were not measured.

title: Large-Scale Implementation of Ambient Artificial Intelligence Documentation and Its Effects on Electronic Health Record Efficiency and Clinician Well-Being

title: Large-scale AI-guided liver malignancy diagnosis: multicenter study and a single-arm trial

title: Artificial intelligence and the phantom pneumothorax: Clinical reasoning still matters
outcome: Whether clinician verification against clinical context caught a false-positive AI pneumothorax alert
effect: AI flagged right apical pneumothorax after left-sided pacemaker; team judged it discordant, CT excluded pneumothorax; no unnecessary intervention, uneventful recovery.
quote: The alert was immediately considered clinically discordant by the treating team, given the left-sided venous access, normal oxygen saturation, hemodynamic stability, and absence of respiratory symptoms.

title: Artificial intelligence and the phantom pneumothorax: Clinical reasoning still matters
outcome: Whether clinician retained final decision authority over AI-flagged finding
effect: Clinicians overrode false-positive AI alert using clinical reasoning and confirmatory CT; patient required no additional intervention.
quote: This case also emphasizes that AI should be regarded as a clinical decision-support tool rather than an autonomous diagnostic system and highlights the continuing importance of physician oversight in ensuring patient safety during AI-assisted post-procedural imaging interpretation.
