effect: Responses written at postgraduate reading level, substantially above recommended targets for patient-education materials.
quote: The models generated responses written at a postgraduate reading level, which is substantially higher than recommended targets for patient-education materials.

title: Decoding high-order clinical correlations: a knowledge-driven large language model framework for specialized medical decision-making
outcome: Exam score on 56 thoracic-surgery questions with versus without local knowledge base
effect: Removing the local knowledge base reduced the examination score by 11.8 percentage points; the knowledge-augmented DK-LLM showed an 11.8-point advantage.
quote: in the ablation analysis, removing the local knowledge base reduced the examination score by 11.8 percentage points.

title: Guideline-augmented large language models for contraindication screening in interventional spine care
outcome: Contraindication classification accuracy with versus without guideline retrieval-augmented generation
effect: Baseline accuracy 85.8% to 87.1% improved to 92.5% to 98.4% with RAG (all p < 0.05); weighted kappa rose from 0.885-0.913 to 0.949-0.990.
quote: Baseline accuracy ranged from 85.8% to 87.1% across models and improved to 92.5% to 98.4% with RAG (all p < 0.05).

title: Guideline-augmented large language models for contraindication screening in interventional spine care
outcome: LLM classification accuracy against guideline-derived ground truth, by contraindication type
effect: Absolute contraindication catch rates 99.0%-100.0% across all conditions; relative contraindication accuracy only 42.1%-56.1% at baseline, rising to 59.6%-93.0% with RAG.
quote: Relative contraindications showed the largest improvements with RAG, increasing from 42.1%-56.1% to 59.6%-93.0%.

title: Adoption, perceived value, and barriers to generative artificial intelligence in emergency medicine: A cross-sectional survey of Latin American clinicians
venue: International journal of critical illness and injury science
outcome: Proportion of respondents reporting existing institutional AI policies
effect: Only 7.4% reported existing institutional AI policies, despite 78.3% professional use of generative AI.
quote: Institutional AI governance was nearly absent, with only 7.4% reporting existing policies.

title: Adoption, perceived value, and barriers to generative artificial intelligence in emergency medicine: A cross-sectional survey of Latin American clinicians
venue: International journal of critical illness and injury science
outcome: Availability of structured AI training and interest in formal training
effect: 88.4% expressed interest in formal AI training; adoption occurred almost entirely without structured training.
quote: Despite this, 88.4% expressed interest in formal AI training and 65.6% supported integration into clinical guidelines.

title: Comparative evaluation of large language models for text-based diagnostic reasoning in fetal central nervous system MRI: A retrospective single-center diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Principal diagnosis matching against postnatal-confirmed diagnosis for LLM differential diagnoses
effect: Principal diagnosis matching: DeepSeek 66/85 (77.6%), Gemini 59/85 (69.4%), ChatGPT 52/85 (61.2%); Cochran's Q = 6.2553, P = .0438; no pairwise difference significant after Holm correction.
quote: DeepSeek achieved the highest principal diagnosis matching rate (66/85, 77.6%), followed by Gemini (59/85, 69.4%) and ChatGPT (52/85, 61.2%).

title: From zero-shot to fine-tuning: optimize large language models for error detection of ultrasound reports
outcome: Error detection performance of fine-tuned open-source LLMs versus proprietary LLMs and radiologists
effect: Fine-tuned Qwen3-14B reached accuracy 0.931 and Macro-F1 0.739, approaching senior radiologists (0.764) and outperforming most proprietary LLMs.
quote: Some fine-tuned open-source LLMs maintained performance despite smaller parameter sizes and outperformed most proprietary LLMs with vastly larger parameter counts.

title: Large language models for analyzing contrast-enhanced ultrasound reports of pancreatic cystic lesions
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Junior radiologist accuracy with versus without LLM assistance on CEUS report interpretation
effect: LLM guidance raised junior radiologists' accuracy to senior levels; overreliance was not assessed.
quote: LLM guidance elevated junior radiologists' accuracy to senior levels.
sample_unit: pathologically confirmed pancreatic cystic lesion CEUS reports

title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Repeat calibration testing after architectural model updates
effect: Repeat testing after updates detected regression: CalT6 accuracy 0.81 vs declared 0.92 (−11.96%), sensitivity −10.99%; subsequent CalT7 reached AUC 0.92, accuracy 0.90.
quote: Architectural updates (1st, 2nd, 5th, 6th) underwent repeat calibration testing ( Figure 4 , Tables 3,4 ).

title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Local performance vs developer-declared metrics
effect: CalT1 specificity 0.70 vs declared 0.88 (−20.45%); accuracy 0.77 vs 0.85 (−9.41%); CalT2 accuracy −12.94%.
quote: Subsequent calibration tests revealed initially subthreshold performance (AUC 0.83, accuracy 0.77, sensitivity 0.84, specificity 0.70), consistent with similar studies where early AI assessments uncover refinement needs ( 52 , 53 ).

title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Detection of incomplete mammogram processing during predeployment functional testing
effect: Functional testing identified incomplete processing in one out of four mammography studies, prompting developer refinement.
quote: Functional testing identified one critical noncompliance: one out of four mammography studies was processed incompletely.

title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Calibration tests against predefined AUC/accuracy thresholds before CMI implementation
effect: First two calibration tests failed thresholds (CalT1 accuracy 0.77; CalT2 AUC 0.78, accuracy 0.74), triggering developer updates; third test passed (AUC 0.84, accuracy 0.81) before implementation.
quote: The first two calibration tests failed to meet the predefined performance thresholds (0.80).

title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Automatically logged technical defect (analysis failure) rates during prospective monitoring
effect: Technical defects exceeded 10% in 1 of 25 months (11.10%); average defect rate decreased from 3.0% to 0.8%.
quote: Technical defect rates exceeded 10% in only 1 of 25 months (group B defects: 11.10%; Figure 3A ).

title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: Diagnostic performance following iterative error feedback, corrective updates, and repeat validation
effect: Across iterative testing, monitoring, and updates, AUC increased by 10.8% (from 0.83 to 0.92) and accuracy by 16.9% (from 0.77 to 0.90). Individual update effects could not be isolated.
quote: Over this time, AUC increased by 10.8% (from 0.83 to 0.92), accuracy by 16.9% (from 0.77 to 0.90), sensitivity by 4.8% (from 0.84 to 0.88), and specificity by 30.0% (from 0.70 to 0.91).

title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: meeting predefined local performance thresholds
effect: Evaluation on historical data against a 0.80 performance threshold prevented the clinical deployment of the algorithm during the first two tests until updates allowed the third test to successfully satisfy the criteria.
quote: The first two calibration tests failed to meet the predefined performance thresholds (0.80).

title: Implementation of an artificial intelligence-based system for mammography in the compulsory medical insurance program: results of a 3-year study
venue: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
outcome: technical error rates during monitoring
effect: Continuous technical and clinical monitoring over a 24-month period effectively tracked the system's operational stability, confirming that technical error rates exceeded the 10% threshold in only one observation period.
quote: The 24-month technical and clinical monitoring demonstrated stable AI system performance, with technical error rates remaining below threshold (<10%) in nearly all observation periods.

title: A two-stage evaluation of large language models for guideline-based Q&A and draft rehabilitation planning in stroke care
outcome: Repeated-generation score stability across three generations per question/case between models
effect: Repeated-generation score stability did not differ significantly between ChatGPT-o3 and DeepSeek.
quote: Repeated-generation score stability did not differ significantly between models.
sample_unit: de-identified stroke cases (Stage 2b); also 100 questions in Stage 1 and 20 guideline-derived questions in Stage 2a

title: A two-stage evaluation of large language models for guideline-based Q&A and draft rehabilitation planning in stroke care
outcome: Clinician-rated correctness, completeness, safety of LLM stroke Q&A and rehabilitation plans, and accuracy on 100 questions
effect: Stage 1 accuracy: DeepSeek 91%, ChatGPT-o3 90%, Gemini 85%, ChatGPT-4o 83%. ChatGPT-o3 outperformed DeepSeek on plan generation across all five domains; Q&A comparable.
quote: In Stage 1, DeepSeek achieved the highest accuracy (91%), followed by ChatGPT-o3 (90%), Gemini (85%), and ChatGPT-4o (83%).
sample_unit: de-identified stroke cases (Stage 2b); also 100 questions in Stage 1 and 20 guideline-derived questions in Stage 2a

title: A two-stage evaluation of large language models for guideline-based Q&A and draft rehabilitation planning in stroke care
outcome: Head-to-head comparison of candidate LLMs on the same questions and cases
effect: Four LLMs compared on 100 questions; top two compared on Q&A with no significant differences and on 60 cases where ChatGPT-o3 outperformed DeepSeek across all five domains.
quote: In Stage 2b, ChatGPT-o3 significantly outperformed DeepSeek across correctness, completeness, readability, helpfulness, and safety in the GEE analysis.
sample_unit: de-identified stroke cases (Stage 2b); also 100 questions in Stage 1 and 20 guideline-derived questions in Stage 2a

title: A two-stage evaluation of large language models for guideline-based Q&A and draft rehabilitation planning in stroke care
outcome: Readability of LLM stroke Q&A responses (Chinese LDU-TGP and English Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level)
effect: ChatGPT-o3 produced Q&A responses with higher recommended reading age and English FK Grade Level than DeepSeek; Chinese difference not significant after correction.
quote: ChatGPT-o3 generated clinical Q&A responses with a higher recommended reading age and English Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, whereas the difference in Chinese Reading Difficulty Score did not remain significant after correction.
sample_unit: de-identified stroke cases (Stage 2b); also 100 questions in Stage 1 and 20 guideline-derived questions in Stage 2a

title: Connecting Risk Prediction to Intervention: Evidence from a Randomized Trial Testing Patient Navigation and Education to Improve Postpartum Outcomes
venue: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
outcome: 30-day postpartum hospital use after navigation and education for patients flagged high-risk by the calculator
effect: Hospital use was 20.0% in the intervention group vs 16.4% in controls (RR 1.2, 95% CI 0.7-2.0). Estimates did not suggest reduced hospital use. Secondary outcomes were similar between groups.
quote: Incidence was 20.0% among intervention participants and 16.4% among control participants (risk ratio [95% confidence interval] = 1.2 [0.7-2.0]).

title: Connecting Risk Prediction to Intervention: Evidence from a Randomized Trial Testing Patient Navigation and Education to Improve Postpartum Outcomes
venue: American journal of obstetrics & gynecology MFM
outcome: Compatibility of model input definitions with local medical record data during real-time risk scoring
effect: Coordinators reported time-intensive abstraction, discrepancies between variable definitions in administrative data (model development) and medical records (recruitment), and missing data.
quote: Coordinators reported challenges to risk calculator use, including time-intensive abstraction, discrepancies between variable definitions in administrative data (model development) and medical records (recruitment), and missing data.

title: Safety and quality of public chatbots for lung cancer prognostic information: a comparative evaluation
outcome: Proportion of safe chatbot responses to patient lung cancer prognostic questions
effect: Safety differed across models (Cochran's Q = 14.089, p = 0.007); Gemini 48/53 (90.6%) safe versus DeepSeek 33/53 (62.3%) safe.
quote: Gemini generated the highest proportion of safe responses (48/53, 90.6%), whereas DeepSeek generated the lowest (33/53, 62.3%).

title: Safety, accuracy, empathic communication, information quality, and readability of five large language model interfaces answering public questions about interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome
outcome: Readability of LLM responses against patient-facing readability benchmarks
effect: Readability differed significantly across interfaces, but none met predefined patient-facing readability benchmarks.
quote: Readability differed significantly across interfaces, but none met predefined patient-facing readability benchmarks.

title: Safety, accuracy, empathic communication, information quality, and readability of five large language model interfaces answering public questions about interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome
outcome: Reading level of LLM answers versus patient-appropriate benchmarks
effect: None of the five interfaces met predefined patient-facing readability benchmarks across six readability indices.
quote: Readability differed significantly across interfaces, but none met predefined patient-facing readability benchmarks.

title: Safety, accuracy, empathic communication, information quality, and readability of five large language model interfaces answering public questions about interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome
outcome: Proportion of unsafe or inaccurate LLM responses to IC/BPS questions
effect: Unsafe responses occurred in all interfaces, ranging from 5.2% for ChatGPT to 8.6% for DeepSeek and Doubao, with no significant between-interface difference (Cochran Q = 1.000, p = 0.910).
quote: Unsafe responses occurred in all interfaces, ranging from 5.2% for ChatGPT to 8.6% for DeepSeek and Doubao, without a significant between-interface difference (Cochran Q = 1.000, p = 0.910).

title: Methylation profiling in CNS tumor diagnostics: a single-centre real-world experience from Central Europe
venue: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
outcome: Change in clinical utility after classifier pipeline version update
effect: Updating bioinformatic pipeline from v11b4 to v12.8 rescued multiple ambiguous entries, raising overall clinical utility from 81.1% to 84.1%.
quote: Updating bioinformatic pipelines from version 11b4 to 12.8 rescued multiple ambiguous entries, increasing overall clinical utility to 84.1%.

title: Methylation profiling in CNS tumor diagnostics: a single-centre real-world experience from Central Europe
venue: Virchows Archiv : an international journal of pathology
outcome: Clinical usefulness of classifier output when integrated with histomorphology and ancillary markers
effect: 52.7% of lower-confidence cases yielded meaningful clinical integration when supported by histomorphology and ancillary markers; discrepant or misleading classifications occurred in 1.9%.
quote: Crucially, over half (52.7%) of the lower-confidence cases yielded meaningful clinical integration when supported by histomorphology and ancillary genetic or immunohistochemical markers, demonstrating that rigid score cutoffs should not dictate assay failure.

title: Large language models answering structured questions on external cervical resorption: a comparative study
outcome: Reproducibility of LLM answer accuracy across user accounts and seven consecutive days
effect: No account-related variability (p = 0.654) and no temporal drift (p = 0.875); overall accuracy 90.8%.
quote: Accuracy remained stable across user accounts and evaluation days, with no evidence of account-related variability (p = 0.654) or temporal drift (p = 0.875).

title: Large language models answering structured questions on external cervical resorption: a comparative study
outcome: Error rates of document-grounded (RAG) versus base LLM configurations on ECR questions
effect: Configuration affected performance (p = 0.050); NotebookLM (RAG) 3.0% and Gemini (Base) 4.0% lowest error; Claude (Base) highest at 12.0%.
quote: Model configuration significantly influenced performance (p = 0.050), with NotebookLM and Gemini showing the lowest estimated error rates (3.0% and 4.0%, respectively), while Claude demonstrated the highest error rate (12.0%).

title: Performance, Failures, and Oversight of a Large Language Model Agent for Clinical Data Analysis: Evaluation Study
outcome: Errors in LLM agent analysis outputs and narrative summaries requiring verification
effect: Systematic execution errors emerged; of 17 narrative summaries, 8 were fully satisfactory; 2 runs produced clinically meaningful errors.
quote: Of 17 narrative summaries, 8 were fully satisfactory; 2 runs produced clinically meaningful errors.

title: Performance, Failures, and Oversight of a Large Language Model Agent for Clinical Data Analysis: Evaluation Study
outcome: Undisclosed agent actions such as postcrash rerun, detectable only via execution logs
effect: Result text accurately reflected execution logs in nearly all runs, though unit propagation and an undisclosed postcrash rerun were identified.
quote: Result text accurately reflected execution logs in nearly all runs, though unit propagation and an undisclosed postcrash rerun were identified.

title: Performance, Failures, and Oversight of a Large Language Model Agent for Clinical Data Analysis: Evaluation Study
outcome: Propagation of erroneous outputs across agent runs
effect: SAP quality did not predict code correctness, and within-mode errors propagated identically across independent repetitions.
quote: Systematic execution errors emerged: SAP quality did not predict code correctness, and within-mode errors propagated identically across independent repetitions.

title: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation versus long-context input for clinical reasoning over electronic health records
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Extraction and timeline task performance with targeted retrieval versus recent-notes long-context input
effect: For Imaging Procedures, RAG exceeded long-context performance by 0.17-9.83 F1 across models using <8K tokens; for Antibiotic Timelines, <8K retrieved tokens matched long-context (-3.26 to +3.24 Jaccard); Diagnosis Generation static.
quote: For Imaging Procedures, RAG strongly outperformed recent-note inputs and exceeded long-context performance (by 0.17-9.83 F1 across all models) using fewer than 8K tokens.

title: Evaluating retrieval-augmented generation versus long-context input for clinical reasoning over electronic health records
venue: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association : JAMIA
outcome: Effect of missing patient data in notes on task performance
effect: Error analysis found missing information in the clinical notes, often due to inter-hospital transfers, limited performance to some extent.
quote: Error analysis revealed that missing information in the clinical notes-often due to inter-hospital transfers-limited performance to some extent.

title: [Can ChatGPT Responses Be Improved by Incorporating S3 Clinical Practice Guidelines?]
outcome: Expert-rated accuracy of ChatGPT answers with vs without guideline PDF provided
effect: Accuracy improved with guideline PDF (1.77 vs. 1.26; p = 0.003); conciseness also improved (1.96 vs. 1.50; p = 0.004).
quote: Providing the guideline as a PDF together with the respective question resulted in a significant improvement in accuracy (1.77 vs. 1.26; p = 0.003) and conciseness (1.96 vs. 1.50; p = 0.004).

title: Impact of acoustic and informational noise on AI-generated clinical summaries
outcome: scribe robustness under realistic audio perturbations
effect: At 4.5 m from the consultation, all microphones omitted all facts.
quote: At 4.5 m from the consultation, for all microphones tested, all facts were omitted.

title: Impact of acoustic and informational noise on AI-generated clinical summaries
outcome: AI scribe omissions and hallucinations
effect: Under ideal audio, the CAIS produced around 0.5 hallucinations and one omission per consultation.
quote: We have observed that the commercial CAIS produces on average around 0.5 hallucinations and one omission per consultation under ideal audio conditions.

title: Impact of acoustic and informational noise on AI-generated clinical summaries
outcome: unreliable summaries from poor audio input
effect: +5 dB background noise led to degraded accuracy and incomplete clinical summaries.
quote: At this highest level of noise, the AI system struggled to isolate the clinician’s and patient’s speech, leading to degraded accuracy and incomplete clinical summaries.

title: Generative artificial intelligence in medicine: a mixed-methods survey of UK general practitioners
outcome: GP need for training and understanding of generative AI
effect: 80% of GPs expressed a need for more training in understanding generative AI tools; many reported lack of knowledge and experience.
quote: 80% of respondents expressed a need for more training in understanding these tools.

title: Generative artificial intelligence in medicine: a mixed-methods survey of UK general practitioners
outcome: GP use of unsanctioned non-medical-grade AI for clinical tasks
effect: One-fifth of GPs reported having used AI for clinical practice; a portion used non-medical grade technology for clinical tasks.
quote: Many GPs reported a lack of knowledge and experience with this technology, although a portion already used non-medical grade technology for clinical tasks, with the risks that this entails.

title: COPE: Chain-of-Thought Prediction Engine for open-source large language model-based stroke outcome prediction from clinical notes
outcome: Subgroup performance of stroke outcome prediction by sex, age, thrombectomy status, and summary length
effect: Consistent performance across sex and age, but higher error among older patients, those undergoing thrombectomy, and those with longer summaries.
quote: Subgroup analyses showed consistent performance across sex and age, with higher error among older patients, those undergoing thrombectomy and those with longer summaries.

title: Exposing the fragility of LLM reasoning through bias-inducing prompts: evidence from BiasMedQA
outcome: Model accuracy under unpublished bias-inducing prompt variations versus published prompts
effect: Gemini-2.5-Flash accuracy dropped from 80.0-88.6% to 47.4-86.1% with four unpublished bias-inducing prompts, exposing brittleness.
quote: The performance of Gemini-2.5-Flash dropped considerably when exposing it to four additional unpublished bias-inducing prompts (from 80.0-88.6% to 47.4-86.1%), hinting at potential contamination of its training data and exposing underlying brittleness.

title: Exposing the fragility of LLM reasoning through bias-inducing prompts: evidence from BiasMedQA
outcome: Gap between public benchmark performance and performance on unpublished prompts (possible contamination)
effect: Gemini-2.5-Flash fell from 80.0-88.6% on public BiasMedQA prompts to 47.4-86.1% on unpublished prompts, hinting at training data contamination.
quote: The performance of Gemini-2.5-Flash dropped considerably when exposing it to four additional unpublished bias-inducing prompts (from 80.0-88.6% to 47.4-86.1%), hinting at potential contamination of its training data and exposing underlying brittleness.

title: How data drift impacts the safety and interpretability of machine learning models predicting risk from blood glucose control
outcome: Whether combining covariate shift, multiple performance metrics and feature importance detects drift and safety risk
effect: Combined monitoring identified different drift types; single metrics missed risks (e.g., +20 mg/dL shift showed no AUROC/AP drop but significant sensitivity drop); simplistic drift detection could misidentify risk.
quote: This underlines the importance of using multiple methods and metrics to track drift and hence model safety.
sample_unit: adults with type 1 diabetes (REPLACE trial CGM data)

title: How data drift impacts the safety and interpretability of machine learning models predicting risk from blood glucose control
outcome: Effect of anomalous or shifted input data on model outputs and covariate shift detection
effect: Even 5% noise gave normalised JS divergence of 172 sigma; sensor noise and offsets degraded performance and changed output rates.
quote: Even a modest addition of 5% noise leads to a very significant covariate shift.
sample_unit: adults with type 1 diabetes (REPLACE trial CGM data)

title: How data drift impacts the safety and interpretability of machine learning models predicting risk from blood glucose control
outcome: Whether a single performance metric conceals poor performance under drift
effect: AUROC alone missed a significant sensitivity drop at +20 mg/dL shift; 'above range' AUROC rose while AP and sensitivity fell.
quote: This highlights the danger of using performance metrics alone to identify drift.
sample_unit: adults with type 1 diabetes (REPLACE trial CGM data)

title: How data drift impacts the safety and interpretability of machine learning models predicting risk from blood glucose control
outcome: Model performance under perturbed inputs (sensor noise, uniform offsets, reduced CGM use)
effect: Adding 5% Gaussian noise significantly lowered AUROC, AP and sensitivity, with specificity sharply declining and hypoglycaemia overpredicted; ±20 mg/dL shifts produced significant changes.
quote: Any addition of noise significantly lowers model performance as marked by AUROC, AP and sensitivity.
sample_unit: adults with type 1 diabetes (REPLACE trial CGM data)

title: How data drift impacts the safety and interpretability of machine learning models predicting risk from blood glucose control
outcome: Model performance when applied to unseen usage patterns, behaviours and sensor conditions
effect: Performance varied across glucose patterns; 'above range' users at elevated risk of false negatives, 'below range' had higher false-alarm rate, lowest CGM use (<0.1) significantly decreased performance.
quote: users who are ‘above range’ (3.2) despite only having a moderate covariate shift relative to baseline and no negative change in AUROC are at elevated risk of false negatives (ie, hypoglycaemia missed by the model).
sample_unit: adults with type 1 diabetes (REPLACE trial CGM data)

title: How data drift impacts the safety and interpretability of machine learning models predicting risk from blood glucose control
outcome: Explanation instability under sensor noise
effect: As Gaussian noise increased to 5%, 10%, and 20%, mean JS rose to 0.144, 0.209, and 0.251, with rate-of-change SD gaining importance.
quote: There is a strong correlation with the amplitude of added noise and the importance of ‘SD of rate of change’ features.
sample_unit: adults with type 1 diabetes (REPLACE trial CGM data)

title: How data drift impacts the safety and interpretability of machine learning models predicting risk from blood glucose control
outcome: Performance after sensor/device noise
effect: Gaussian sensor noise: mean JS 0.144 at 5%, 0.209 at 10%, 0.251 at 20%; performance degradation was significant with any added noise.
quote: For device and sensor changes, adding noise results in large covariate shifts, significant performance degradation and a change in the importance of rate of change (of CGM readings).
sample_unit: adults with type 1 diabetes (REPLACE trial CGM data)

title: How data drift impacts the safety and interpretability of machine learning models predicting risk from blood glucose control
outcome: hypoglycemia prediction performance under sensor calibration shift
effect: A +20 mg/dL shift showed no notable drop in AUROC or AP, but caused a significant drop in sensitivity.
quote: In particular, +20 mg/dL shows no notable drop in AUROC or AP; however, a significant drop in sensitivity.
sample_unit: adults with type 1 diabetes (REPLACE trial CGM data)

title: Importance of model governance in clinical AI models: case study on the relevance of data drift detection
outcome: Whether drift monitoring detects input distribution shifts and data quality problems in a deployed-style predictive model
effect: Univariate monitoring found respiratory rate shift from January 2022; multivariate PCA flagged three months, with data entry errors traced. Drift alerts did not coincide with the AUC dips in March 2020 and March 2021.
quote: In particular, multivariate monitoring surfaced data entry errors that were not detected by univariate methods and were absent from the training dataset, demonstrating how a comprehensive drift detection approach can uncover subtle or single-instance outliers.

title: Importance of model governance in clinical AI models: case study on the relevance of data drift detection
outcome: Whether input data monitoring detects anomalous values and data pipeline integrity issues
effect: PCA reconstruction error flagged data entry errors (saturation '955' instead of '95', incorrect heart rate) and an outlier length of stay; after pipeline modification, alerts for those months were removed.
quote: After modifying the data pipeline to guard against these types of data entry errors, the multivariate alerts for these months were removed.

title: Importance of model governance in clinical AI models: case study on the relevance of data drift detection
outcome: Temporal validation of model performance on later historical data
effect: XGBoost achieved AUC 0.82 and Brier score 0.158 in temporal validation (Jan 2020 to Oct 2022) after training on data through January 2020.
quote: The XGBoost model achieved an AUC of 0.82 and a Brier score of 0.158 during temporal validation from January 2020 to October 2022.

title: Importance of model governance in clinical AI models: case study on the relevance of data drift detection
outcome: Whether predefined drift and performance thresholds flag degradation
effect: AUC fell below the ±3 SD limit in March 2020 and March 2021, but drift detection did not detect those months; univariate drift alerts did not coincide with performance dips.
quote: First, while data drift detection was able to identify clinical shifts and data quality anomalies, it did not detect the months when the model performance was lower than expected.

title: Importance of model governance in clinical AI models: case study on the relevance of data drift detection
outcome: Monthly AUC monitoring against limits from cross-validation performance
effect: Temporal validation AUC 0.82 and Brier 0.158; monthly AUC dipped below the 3 SD limit twice (March 2020, March 2021), otherwise within limits.
quote: The AUC dipped slightly below our performance limit on two occasions: in March 2020 and March 2021.

title: Importance of model governance in clinical AI models: case study on the relevance of data drift detection
outcome: monthly performance versus outcomes
effect: Monthly AUC monitoring found two below-limit months, March 2020 and March 2021; otherwise within ±3 SD.
quote: The AUC dipped slightly below our performance limit on two occasions: in March 2020 and March 2021.

title: Development and prospective evaluation of a machine learning model to predict serious cardiac outcomes among paediatric cardiac inpatients
outcome: Prospective silent-trial performance versus retrospective validation performance (AUROC, PPV, NPV)
effect: AUROC 0.88 (95% CI 0.88 to 0.89) retrospective vs 0.82 (95% CI 0.79 to 0.83) in prospective silent trial; PPV 0.19 and NPV 0.97 at retrospective-selected threshold.
quote: The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.88 (95% CI 0.88 to 0.89) for retrospective and 0.82 (95% CI 0.79 to 0.83) for prospective silent trial phases.

title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
outcome: Agreement of live silent CDS with retrospective model; detection of problems before activation
effect: Silent pilot showed 96.8% raw agreement, Kappa 91.2% (95% CI 90.7–91.8%); uncovered monitoring data-capture flaw that would otherwise have been missed
quote: Without this prespecified quality check, we may have missed a major issue and attempted to correct calculation errors that were not actually occurring.

title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
outcome: Technical component analysis of CDS population capture, calculation, threshold, data capture
effect: No errors in population capture, risk calculation, threshold, or decision alignment; data capture for monitoring found to record overwritten values, not data used by CDS; corrected
quote: In the evaluation of the data capture for monitoring and transparency, we discovered that the ‘live care’ data that was recorded in the report were not what the CDS used for its calculations.

title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
outcome: CDS screening performance versus human standard-of-care screening
effect: CDS sensitivity 81.7% (77.1–85.8%) vs human 80.2% (75.4–84.4%); specificity 67.3% vs 67.4%; no notable difference
quote: There was no notable difference between human performance and the CDS given overlapping CIs.

title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
outcome: Silent mode CDS decisions versus original model and actual human decisions
effect: CDS sensitivity 81.7% vs in vitro model 82.0% vs human 80.2%; specificity 67.3% vs 67.3% vs 67.4%; raw agreement 96.8%, Kappa 91.2%
quote: We found 96.8% raw agreement and a Kappa of 91.2% (95% CI 90.7% to 91.8%).

title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
outcome: Differences between live input data and completed retrospective data
effect: Data differences affected about 13% of encounters, 96% from chief complaints; live vs completed-data model agreement 97.2%, Kappa 92.3%; sensitivity barely changed
quote: These data differences impacted about 13% of all encounters; 96% of all data differences were associated with the arrival chief complaints.

title: In vivo clinical effectiveness of artificial intelligence screening for acute coronary syndrome: testing real-world performance
