quote: Locally trained CatBoost models outperformed SafeNET (AUC-ROC, 0.92; F1, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.72-0.78) and demonstrated improved calibration (Brier 0.04 vs. 0.055).

title: Testing Transferability of a Mortality Risk Model for Interhospital Transfer Using Real-World Electronic Health Records: External Validation and Model Enhancement
outcome: external discrimination and calibration of SafeNET
effect: AUC-ROC was 0.87 (95% CI, 0.83-0.90), F1 was 0.73 (95% CI, 0.69-0.77), and Brier score was 0.055, closely approximating development-site results.
quote: These findings indicate that SafeNET maintained predictive performance for in-hospital mortality comparable to its originally reported results, despite substantial dataset shift and extensive missingness in our real-world EHR data.

title: AI adoption among French oncology pharmacists: A national survey
venue: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
outcome: Prevalence of shadow AI use and access to validated tools among oncology pharmacists
effect: 65.3% operated within a shadow AI framework; only 17.3% had access to fit-for-purpose validated tools; AI adoption 94.7%.
quote: However, 65.3% operated within a shadow AI framework, while only 17.3% had access to fit-for-purpose validated tools.

title: AI adoption among French oncology pharmacists: A national survey
venue: Journal of oncology pharmacy practice : official publication of the International Society of Oncology Pharmacy Practitioners
outcome: Unsanctioned generative AI use and patient data confidentiality concerns
effect: 65.3% used shadow AI; 62.5% concerned about patient data confidentiality (mean security concern score 3.21/4).
quote: However, 65.3% operated within a shadow AI framework, while only 17.3% had access to fit-for-purpose validated tools.

title: Large language models show high clinical safety but differences in completeness for reproductive counselling in women with inflammatory rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases: a comparative expert evaluation
outcome: Inter-rater agreement among ten expert raters of LLM responses
effect: Fleiss' kappa ranged from -0.043 to 0.059 (poor to slight); ICC moderate, range 0.259 to 0.692.
quote: Inter-rater agreement was poor to slight (Fleiss' kappa range: -0.043 to 0.059) and moderate for ICC (range: 0.259 to 0.692).

title: Agreement between artificial intelligence and periodontists in the detection of periodontal bone loss on panoramic radiographs
outcome: Agreement of AI bone level measurements with periodontist consensus at tooth level
effect: Across 2,037 teeth MAE was 5.08% points; mean bias 1.61%; wide limits of agreement, lowest agreement in lower molars (MAE 7.66; R²=0.26), so clinician oversight is needed.
quote: However, the limits of agreement, particularly in the molar regions, were too wide to support the use of AI-derived measurements for individual tooth-level assessment without clinician oversight.

title: GPT-4 improves sex-specificity in cardiovascular patient education but may perpetuate gender biases: A mixed-methods audit
outcome: Stereotyping and clinical knowledge gaps in GPT-4 sex-tailored cardiovascular patient education content
effect: Qualitative analysis found female symptoms framed as deviations from a male norm, erectile dysfunction frequently omitted from male-tailored content despite explicit prompting, and gendered stereotypes (e.g., "bottling up emotions") in both versions.
quote: However, qualitative analysis identified instances where outputs introduced content inconsistent with an equity-oriented framework: female-tailored content occasionally framed female symptoms as deviations from a male norm, male-tailored content frequently omitted erectile dysfunction as a CVD risk marker despite explicit prompting, and both versions at times reflected gendered social stereotypes (e.g., "bottling up emotions") rather than clinical evidence.

title: Development and Usability Assessment of a Health Education Conversational Agent for Patients With Gastric Cancer: Action Research Study
outcome: Answer accuracy and RAG knowledge hit rate across three alpha-testing rounds
effect: Accuracy 67% (37/55), 71% (44/62), 82% (31/38); RAG knowledge hit rates 86%, 98%, 100%; hit-rate differences significant (P<.01). No non-RAG comparator.
quote: The accuracy of the agent in 3 rounds was 67% (37/55), 71% (44/62), and 82% (31/38), respectively; RAG knowledge hit rates reached 86% (47/55), 98% (61/62), and 100% (38/38).
sample_unit: participants (44 patients, 13 nurses, 3 nursing managers, 2 surgeons, 1 psychologist, 1 dietitian)

title: Too agreeable to be accurate? Sycophancy and diagnostic instability of large language models in medical diagnosis
outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy stability after 'Are you sure?' challenge and specialty framing
effect: Baseline accuracy fell from 51.8% to 42.2% after 'Are you sure?' (AcFR 32.8%); correct-to-incorrect transitions (n=544) exceeded incorrect-to-correct (n=198). Specialty prompts changed accuracy by -1.8 to +2.8 points.
quote: Across all neutral model-case pairs, baseline accuracy decreased from 51.8% to 42.2% after 'Are you sure?' (AcFR = 32.8%).

title: Evaluating AI-assisted detection of fetal intracranial malformations in prenatal ultrasound practice: a multicentre, self-crossover, randomised controlled trial in China
outcome: Sonographer sensitivity and specificity for fetal intracranial malformations with vs without AI assistance in a randomised crossover trial
effect: Fetal-based sensitivity increased by 0·087 (95% CI 0·029 to 0·147; p superiority<0·0001); specificity non-inferior (difference 0·009, 95% CI -0·006 to 0·023). No AI-related adverse events reported.
quote: In the fetal-based analysis, sensitivity increased by 0·087 (95% CI 0·029 to 0·147; p<sub>superiority</sub><0·0001), with specificity meeting the non-inferiority criterion (difference 0·009, 95% CI -0·006 to 0·023; p<sub>non-inferiority</sub><0·0001).

title: Evaluating AI-assisted detection of fetal intracranial malformations in prenatal ultrasound practice: a multicentre, self-crossover, randomised controlled trial in China
outcome: Human-AI team performance compared with sonographers without AI in intended deployment mode
effect: Malformation-targeted sensitivity improved by 0·118 (95% CI 0·054 to 0·181; p superiority<0·0001); specificity non-inferior (difference 0·001, 95% CI -0·001 to 0·002).
quote: In the malformation-targeted analysis, sensitivity improved by 0·118 (95% CI 0·054 to 0·181; p<sub>superiority</sub><0·0001), and specificity was also non-inferior (difference 0·001, 95% CI -0·001 to 0·002; p<sub>non-inferiority</sub><0·0001).

title: Bridging semantics and clinical fidelity: a section-based assessment of a vision-language model (RadVLM) for chest x-ray report generation
outcome: Factual accuracy (RadGraph F1) of AI-generated chest x-ray report Findings versus reference reports
effect: Mean RadGraph F1 was 0.251 (95% CI, 0.245-0.257), indicating substantially imperfect structural correctness; BERTScore-F1 0.498; CheXbert cosine similarity 0.394.
quote: Mean RadGraph F1 was 0.251 (95% CI, 0.245-0.257), indicating substantially imperfect structural correctness.

title: Bridging semantics and clinical fidelity: a section-based assessment of a vision-language model (RadVLM) for chest x-ray report generation
outcome: Whether surface semantic similarity of Impressions reflects Findings-level entity-relation fidelity
effect: Weak positive association (coefficient 0.154; 95% CI 0.124-0.183), attenuating with longer Impressions; fluent Impressions gave little assurance that Findings were factually correct.
quote: A weak positive association existed between semantic similarity and entity-relation fidelity (coefficient 0.154; 95% CI, 0.124-0.183), and this association attenuated substantially with longer Impressions.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Large Language Models in Frontal Sinus Fracture Management: A Multidisciplinary Expert-Based Vignette Study
outcome: Proportion of LLM responses with at least one expert-recorded safety concern
effect: At least one safety concern was recorded in 45.2%, 41.1%, and 48.1% of individual assessments (ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek; P=0.255); majority consensus occurred for 35 of 90 responses.
quote: At least one safety concern was recorded in 45.2%, 41.1%, and 48.1% of individual assessments, respectively (P=0.255); majority consensus occurred for 35 of 90 responses and did not differ by model (P=0.056).
sample_unit: expert assessments (90 model-vignette responses rated by 9 clinicians)

title: Teaching Model Context Protocol, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and AI Agents to a Multidisciplinary Hospital Workforce: Single-Group Pre-Post Survey Study
outcome: Self-efficacy change in generative AI skills after an 8-week hospital workforce AI training program
effect: Large self-efficacy gains (MCP d=1.57; overall effect r=.574); satisfaction 4.03/5; job-specific competency stayed below the scale midpoint (knowledge-practice gap). Single-group pre-post, no comparator.
quote: This program suggests that transforming a multidisciplinary hospital workforce into AI-capable professionals is achievable through intensive, hands-on training centered on agent-level technologies, and that capstone projects with dedicated mentoring can serve as a pathway from classroom learning toward institutional AI adoption.

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Clinical Audiology (AUDIOLOGYBENCH): Benchmark Development and Validation Study
outcome: Critical-error rate on audiometric numerical interpretation (Q1) in case studies
effect: Q1 mean score 67.89 (SD 18.47) with a 35.4% (95/268) critical-error rate; errors shared across models.
quote: audiometric numerical interpretation (Q1) achieved a mean score of 67.89 (SD 18.47, 95% CI 65.68-70.10), with a 35.4% (95/268) critical-error rate

title: Evaluating Large Language Models in Clinical Audiology (AUDIOLOGYBENCH): Benchmark Development and Validation Study
outcome: Agreement between automated adjudicator and audiologist consensus reference standard on Q1 critical errors
effect: Adjudicator per-item labels diverged from human judgment (kappa=0.05; sensitivity 19/26, 73%; PPV 19/53, 36%), showing automated grading alone is unreliable.
quote: When 2 audiologists regraded all 80 model Q1 responses with the diagnostic images available, the adjudicator's per-item Q1 labels diverged from human judgment (κ=0.05; overflagging; sensitivity: 19/26, 73%; positive predictive value: 19/53, 36%)

title: Comparative analysis of AI enhancements to rules-based clinical triage chatbot: Convergent mixed-methods study
outcome: Triage accuracy of AI-enhanced chatbots versus existing rules-based chatbot on same vignettes
effect: Rules-based 71.8% (95% CI 56.2-83.5%) vs Dialogflow 30.8% (p = 0.002) and Gemini 41.0% (p = 0.031); Dialogflow, ChatGPT, Gemini statistically indistinguishable.
quote: The rules-based chatbot was most accurate (71.8%, 95% CI 56.2-83.5%), outperforming Dialogflow (30.8%, p = 0.002) and Gemini (41.0%, p = 0.031).

title: Comparative quality, accuracy, and readability of large language model responses to patient questions about robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty
outcome: Reading level of LLM patient-education responses versus recommended levels
effect: Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease differed significantly across models (p < 0.001); median responses across all models remained above recommended patient-education reading levels.
quote: Although Gemini 3 and DeepSeek demonstrated greater readability in selected comparisons, median responses across all models remained above recommended patient-education reading levels.

title: Simultaneous derivation, validation, and comparison of predictor hazard ratios for cardiovascular risk prediction equations in patients with diabetes from high versus non-high income countries: cohort study
outcome: Calibration (expected to observed ratio) after recalibration versus updating age coefficients in Chinese cohort
effect: Standard recalibration did not improve calibration (E/O 0.938 men, 0.809 women); replacing NZ age coefficients with Chinese ones improved it (E/O 1.027 men, 1.025 women).
quote: Replacing New Zealand age coefficients with Chinese coefficients noticeably improved calibration (expected to observed ratio 1.027 in men, 1.025 in women).

title: Simultaneous derivation, validation, and comparison of predictor hazard ratios for cardiovascular risk prediction equations in patients with diabetes from high versus non-high income countries: cohort study
outcome: Performance of NZ-derived equations when applied to a Chinese population with diabetes
effect: Applying the high-income-country equation to a non-high-income population may introduce systematic errors, driven by differing age effects (age HR women 1.61 NZ vs 2.51 China per 10 years).
quote: Applying a high income country derived CVD risk prediction equation to a population from a non-high income country with diabetes may introduce systematic errors, primarily driven by differing effect of age.

title: Simultaneous derivation, validation, and comparison of predictor hazard ratios for cardiovascular risk prediction equations in patients with diabetes from high versus non-high income countries: cohort study
outcome: cross-country calibration
effect: Standard recalibration E:O ratio: 0.938 in men, 0.809 in women.
quote: Standard recalibration of New Zealand equations did not improve calibration in the Chinese cohort (expected to observed ratio: 0.938 in men, 0.809 in women).

title: Simultaneous derivation, validation, and comparison of predictor hazard ratios for cardiovascular risk prediction equations in patients with diabetes from high versus non-high income countries: cohort study
outcome: predictor effect transportability
effect: Women age HR: 1.61 (1.51 to 1.71) in New Zealand, 2.51 (2.32 to 2.72) in China.
quote: Hazard ratios for most predictors were similar between New Zealand and Chinese equations but differed markedly for age (eg, women: 1.61, 95% confidence interval 1.51 to 1.71 per 10 years in New Zealand, 2.51 (2.32 to 2.72) per 10 years in China).

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Colonic Angiodysplasia Can Improve Endoscopic Reporting Consistency
outcome: CV model performance on external independent image datasets
effect: External validation of 3534 images from 239 procedures showed 94.5% accuracy, 84.4% sensitivity, and 95.9% specificity.
quote: External validation of 3534 images from 239 procedures showed 94.5% accuracy, 84.4% sensitivity, and 95.9% specificity.
sample_unit: images (external validation of CV model, from 239 procedures)

title: Comprehension of an AI-generated discharge letter versus a traditional discharge letter: two controlled quasi-experimental parallel-group studies
venue: International journal for quality in health care : journal of the International Society for Quality in Health Care
outcome: Comprehension of key discharge information: AI accessibility-optimised letter vs conventional letter
effect: Comprehension scores were higher with the AI letter in Study 1 (median 4 vs 2) and Study 2 (median 4 vs 3), both P<0.001. All secondary outcomes also improved; no gain for follow-up date identification.
quote: Participants receiving the AI-generated discharge letter achieved significantly higher comprehension scores in both studies (Study 1: median 4 vs. 2; Study 2: median 4 vs. 3; both P < 0.001).

title: Multimodal artificial intelligence-based decision support for stroke classification in medical emergency calls using call transcripts and patient health records: A retrospective diagnostic accuracy study
outcome: Stroke-class F1 of AI models versus EMCC operator baseline on same calls
effect: Multimodal model stroke F1 0.77 vs operator baseline 0.73 and transcript-only model; about 26 false alerts per 1,000 calls vs 36 for operators at assumed 1.2% prevalence.
quote: The multimodal classification model achieved a stroke-class F1-score of 0.77, exceeding that of both the transcript-only model and the operator baseline (0.73).

title: Optimizing deep learning-enhanced opportunistic osteoporosis screening from chest X-rays in Australia: Impact of follow-up and treatment adherence on clinical and economic outcomes
outcome: Clinical benefits from follow-up and adherence
effect: Optimizing follow-up and adherence could amplify clinical benefits by four- to five-fold.
quote: Optimizing follow-up and adherence could amplify clinical benefits by four- to five-fold.
sample_unit: simulated women aged ≥50 years undergoing chest radiography

title: Clinical usability of an explainable AI decision support tool and evaluation of multimodal models in NSCLC
outcome: Model performance drop in external validation versus test set
effect: External validation AUC ranged 0.55-0.72 versus up to 0.77 in the test set for CB-only models, attributed to population differences.
quote: Performance drop in external validation (EXVAL) likely reflects population differences (AUC range: 0.55-0.72).

title: Clinical usability of an explainable AI decision support tool and evaluation of multimodal models in NSCLC
outcome: Physician prediction accuracy with versus without XAI decision support tool
effect: Lung expert and nonexpert physicians improved their prediction when using the XAI ML CB-only tool; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: The clinical usability study showed that lung expert and nonexpert physicians improved their prediction with the explainable AI (XAI) ML CB-only based tool.

title: Multicenter evaluation of four large language models for automated spine imaging diagnosis
outcome: Cross-institutional recall variability of LLM diagnosis across three hospitals
effect: Cross-institutional validation demonstrated stable recall generalisability, with recall coefficients of variation ranging from 0.7% to 5.0%.
quote: Cross-institutional validation demonstrated stable recall generalisability, with recall coefficients of variation ranging from 0.7% to 5.0%.

title: Multicenter evaluation of four large language models for automated spine imaging diagnosis
outcome: Sensitivity of LLM diagnostic behaviour to input mode and prompt formulation
effect: Input mode and prompt formulation produced model-specific shifts in diagnostic behaviour across with-option and without-option modes.
quote: Input mode and prompt formulation also produced model-specific shifts in diagnostic behaviour.

title: Quality assurance for deep learning-based proton therapy planning in routine clinical use for oropharyngeal cancer
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Clinical goal achievement after planner manual adjustment of DL plans
effect: Clinical goal achievement rose from 91% to 93.6% (CTV therapeutic) and 78.2% to 88.5% (CTV elective); NTCPs significantly but slightly reduced (p < 0.001).
quote: Manual adjustments resulted in an increase of clinical goal achievement from 91% (sDLO, n = 71) to 93.6% (mDLO, n = 73) in CTV therapeutic and 78.2% (sDLO, n = 61) to 88.5% (mDLO, n = 69) in CTV elective ( Fig. 1 , Supplementary Table S4).

title: Quality assurance for deep learning-based proton therapy planning in routine clinical use for oropharyngeal cancer
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: Periodic benchmark of every fifth DL plan against blinded manual plans
effect: Manual plans met all clinical goals in 16/16 vs mDLO 14/16; mDLO had lower spinal cord (30.3 vs 33.2 Gy) and parotid dose (15.8 vs 16.9 Gy).
quote: All clinical goals were met in manual plans for all patients ( n = 16) in the benchmark cohort, while mDLO plans reached all clinical goals in 14/16 patients (Supplementary Table S4).

title: Quality assurance for deep learning-based proton therapy planning in routine clinical use for oropharyngeal cancer
venue: Physics and imaging in radiation oncology
outcome: clinical goal achievement
effect: increased from 91% to 93.6% in therapeutic volume and 78.2% to 88.5% in elective volume after manual adjustments
quote: Manual adjustments resulted in an increase of clinical goal achievement from 91% (sDLO, n = 71) to 93.6% (mDLO, n = 73) in CTV therapeutic and 78.2% (sDLO, n = 61) to 88.5% (mDLO, n = 69) in CTV elective ( Fig. 1 , Supplementary Table S4).

title: Ambient artificial intelligence scribe implementation in inpatient setting
outcome: Inpatient time in notes per day before vs after ambient AI scribe implementation
effect: Mean time in notes per day was unchanged, from 41.9 (SD 25.59) to 41.6 (SD 27.3) min (p = .77); overall ambient AI utilization was 3%.
quote: Mean time in notes (SD) per day was unchanged, from 41.9 (25.59) to 41.6 (27.3) min (p = .77).

title: Ambient artificial intelligence scribe implementation in inpatient setting
outcome: Fit of ambient scribe to inpatient workflows and note types; utilization by note type
effect: Utilization was low (3% overall; 12% of H&Ps, 2% of progress notes, 6% of consult notes). Physicians requested functionality to pull forward or add onto previously generated notes.
quote: Future development tailored to inpatient workflows is needed to increase adoption as organizations begin to expand ambient AI in this new clinical setting.

title: Depictions of Depression in Generative AI Video Models: Mixed Methods Study of OpenAI's Sora 2
outcome: Demographic and stereotyped patterns in generated depression videos (age, gender, isolation)
effect: 88% (323/367) of figures were aged 20-30 years and 98% (360/367) were alone; gender skewed male in app outputs (68%) and female in API outputs (59%); 94% seated figures, 93% downward gaze.
quote: Figures were predominantly young adults (323/367, 88% aged 20-30 years) and nearly always alone (360/367, 98%).

title: Locally Deployed Large Language Models for AI-Assisted Outpatient Prescription Review: Crossover Study
outcome: LLM hallucination rate with vs without knowledge augmentation from package inserts
effect: Hallucination rate fell from 19.7% (42/213) to 4.7% (10/213), absolute reduction 15.0 percentage points (relative 76.2%; P<.001)
quote: Knowledge augmentation reduced the model hallucination rate from 19.7% (42/213 prescriptions) to 4.7% (10/213), an absolute reduction of 15.0 percentage points (relative reduction 76.2%; P<.001).

title: Locally Deployed Large Language Models for AI-Assisted Outpatient Prescription Review: Crossover Study
outcome: Pharmacist review accuracy and sensitivity with vs without AI assistance
effect: Accuracy 97.2% (207/213) collaborative vs 82.6% (176/213) alone (P<.001); sensitivity 98% vs 55%; false-negative rate 45% to 2%
quote: Overall review accuracy was 97.2% (207/213, 95% CI 94.0%-98.7%) in the human-AI collaborative condition vs 82.6% (176/213, 95% CI 77.0%-87.1%) in the pharmacist-alone condition (P<.001).

title: Locally Deployed Large Language Models for AI-Assisted Outpatient Prescription Review: Crossover Study
outcome: Per-prescription review time
effect: 2.33 (SD 0.97) to 1.12 (SD 0.49) minutes; approximately 51.9% reduction; P<.001.
quote: Collaborative review reduced the mean per-prescription review time from 2.33 (SD 0.97) to 1.12 (SD 0.49) minutes (approximately 51.9% reduction; Wilcoxon signed-rank Z=-12.65; P<.001; r=0.87).

title: FairEnc: A Fair vision-language model with fair vision and text encoders for glaucoma detection
outcome: Demographic disparities (DPD, DEOdds) and diagnostic performance after fairness-aware pretraining for glaucoma detection
effect: FairEnc reduced demographic disparities measured by DPD and DEOdds while keeping strong diagnostic performance in zero-shot and linear probing; on FairFundus, performance stayed within a competitive range.
quote: Comprehensive experiments on the publicly available Harvard-FairVLMed dataset show that FairEnc reduces demographic disparities measured by DPD and DEOdds while achieving strong diagnostic performance under both zero-shot and linear probing evaluations.

title: Informal use of generative artificial intelligence by nursing interns during clinical placement: A multi-stakeholder interpretive description
outcome: Informal, unsanctioned generative AI use by nursing interns on personal devices amid lack of governance
effect: Interns used generative AI on personal devices during clinical placement while institutional governance had not kept pace; participants across all stakeholder groups called for tiered governance.
quote: Interns use it on personal devices, yet institutional governance has not kept pace.
sample_unit: interview participants (nursing interns, preceptors, head nurses, administrators, IT specialists, quality officer)

title: Informal use of generative artificial intelligence by nursing interns during clinical placement: A multi-stakeholder interpretive description
outcome: Presence of institutional AI rules governing intern use during placement
effect: Theme 1 identified multilevel discretionary rule-making in a policy vacuum, with a cross-stakeholder call for institutional frameworks.
quote: Five interconnected themes emerged: (1) multilevel discretionary rule-making in a policy vacuum; (2) a universally endorsed but unevenly enacted verification imperative; (3) intuitive risk stratification; (4) tensions between standardised AI outputs and embodied nursing care; and (5) a cross-stakeholder call for institutional frameworks.
sample_unit: interview participants (nursing interns, preceptors, head nurses, administrators, IT specialists, quality officer)

title: Informal use of generative artificial intelligence by nursing interns during clinical placement: A multi-stakeholder interpretive description
outcome: Whether staff verify AI outputs before acting on them
effect: Verification was universally endorsed by stakeholders but unevenly enacted in practice (qualitative theme; no numbers reported).
quote: Five interconnected themes emerged: (1) multilevel discretionary rule-making in a policy vacuum; (2) a universally endorsed but unevenly enacted verification imperative; (3) intuitive risk stratification; (4) tensions between standardised AI outputs and embodied nursing care; and (5) a cross-stakeholder call for institutional frameworks.
sample_unit: interview participants (nursing interns, preceptors, head nurses, administrators, IT specialists, quality officer)

title: Evaluation and Comparison of Large Language Model Responses to Frequently Asked Questions Regarding Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome: A Quality and Readability Assessment Study
outcome: Reading grade level of LLM patient education responses versus recommended sixth- to eighth-grade level
effect: Median Gunning Fog and Coleman-Liau scores for all four models exceeded the commonly recommended sixth- to eighth-grade reading level; Grok 4 produced the most difficult text.
quote: The median Gunning Fog and Coleman-Liau scores for all four models exceeded the commonly recommended sixth- to eighth-grade reading level for patient education.

title: Evaluation and Comparison of Large Language Model Responses to Frequently Asked Questions Regarding Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome: A Quality and Readability Assessment Study
outcome: Readability of LLM patient-oriented responses in plain language
effect: Readability differed significantly among models across all three indices; median Gunning Fog and Coleman-Liau exceeded the recommended sixth- to eighth-grade level for all four models.
quote: The median Gunning Fog and Coleman-Liau scores for all four models exceeded the commonly recommended sixth- to eighth-grade reading level for patient education.

title: Artificial Intelligence Integration in Radiology in Saudi Arabia: A Cross-Sectional Survey of Workforce Readiness and Implementation Challenges
outcome: Perceived barriers to AI integration in radiology, including insufficient staff training
effect: Insufficient staff training rated a major barrier (3.84 ± 0.77) and lack of technical expertise (3.82 ± 0.78); implementation readiness was lower (3.04 ± 0.79).
quote: Major barriers included implementation costs (3.98 ± 0.71), limited digital infrastructure (3.90 ± 0.75), insufficient staff training (3.84 ± 0.77), and lack of technical expertise (3.82 ± 0.78).
sample_unit: healthcare professionals involved in radiology services

title: Information Quality and Semantic Stability of AI Chatbot Responses to Complete Denture Questions: A Turkish-English Benchmarking Study
outcome: Semantic stability of chatbot responses across repeated runs, sessions, and paraphrased prompt variants
effect: Model significantly affected semantic stability (p<0.001; ηp2=0.820); stability differed across scheduled query sessions (p<0.001; ηp2=0.055), means 0.863, 0.874, 0.841 for morning, afternoon, evening.
quote: semantic stability differed across scheduled query sessions (p < 0.001; ηp2 = 0.055), with means of 0.863 ± 0.106, 0.874 ± 0.092, and 0.841 ± 0.140 for morning, afternoon, and evening sessions, respectively.
sample_unit: complete denture questions (submitted to 7 chatbots, repeated across sessions, in Turkish and English)

title: Information Quality and Semantic Stability of AI Chatbot Responses to Complete Denture Questions: A Turkish-English Benchmarking Study
outcome: Consistency of chatbot responses across semantically equivalent prompt variants and repeated queries
effect: AI model significantly affected embedding-based semantic stability (p<0.001; ηp2=0.820); Grok highest overall stability mean (0.952 ± 0.015); English showed higher similarity than Turkish conditions overall (p<0.001).
quote: English responses showed higher overall GQS than the original Turkish responses (3.96 ± 0.94 vs. 3.66 ± 1.23; p = 0.004) and higher embedding-based similarity than the Turkish conditions overall (p < 0.001).
sample_unit: complete denture questions (submitted to 7 chatbots, repeated across sessions, in Turkish and English)

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence as a First-Pass Reader in Fundus Photograph Screening: A Multireader Workflow Validation Study
outcome: fixed-threshold local sensitivity
effect: Target sensitivity 0.99; standalone sensitivity was 0.929 for AMD, 0.931 for DR, and 0.994 for RVO.
quote: A related consideration is that, as a standalone classifier, the AI system did not reach its prespecified operating target of 0.99 sensitivity for two of the three diseases, achieving a standalone sensitivity of 0.929 for AMD and 0.931 for DR, although it reached 0.994 for RVO.

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence as a First-Pass Reader in Fundus Photograph Screening: A Multireader Workflow Validation Study
outcome: Sensitivity/specificity of AI-human double reading versus human-human double reading, plus human reads per image
effect: DR/RVO: no significant difference (all p≥0.05). AMD: sensitivity 0.916 and 0.950 (p<0.001) vs 0.845, one combination 0.842 (p=0.742); human reads 1.02-1.11 vs 2.00-2.10 per image.
quote: Across AI-human combinations, sensitivity and specificity did not differ significantly from human-human reading (all p ≥ 0.05; specificity differences ≤0.001).

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence as a First-Pass Reader in Fundus Photograph Screening: A Multireader Workflow Validation Study
outcome: AI-human double reading compared with conventional human-human double reading on the same images
effect: Comparable accuracy for DR and RVO with about 46-49% fewer human reads; AMD sensitivity higher in two of three configurations, with lower specificity (≥0.978).
quote: Accordingly, human–human double reading required 2.00 to 2.10 human reads per image, whereas AI–human double reading required 1.02 to 1.11, corresponding to a 46% to 49% reduction in human reading events ( Table 2 ).

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence as a First-Pass Reader in Fundus Photograph Screening: A Multireader Workflow Validation Study
outcome: AI-human double-reading performance
effect: Human reads 1.02–1.11 vs 2.00–2.10; DR/RVO no significant loss; AMD sensitivity 0.842–0.950 vs 0.845, specificity ≥0.978.
quote: AI–human double reading with arbitration substantially reduced repeated human reading while preserving diagnostic reliability for DR and RVO and demonstrating reader-configuration-dependent performance for AMD.

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence as a First-Pass Reader in Fundus Photograph Screening: A Multireader Workflow Validation Study
outcome: standalone versus workflow specificity
effect: Standalone specificity was 0.925 for RVO and 0.938 for AMD, while workflow specificity was ≥0.978 across diseases.
quote: Although standalone AI specificity was as low as 0.925 for RVO and 0.938 for AMD, workflow specificity remained 0.978 or higher across all diseases.

title: Evaluating Artificial Intelligence as a First-Pass Reader in Fundus Photograph Screening: A Multireader Workflow Validation Study
outcome: AI false-negative correction
effect: False-negative correction: AMD 2–20/67 (3–30%); DR 17–20/37 (46–54%); RVO 0–1/2, despite human review/arbitration.
quote: Correction of standalone AI false negatives was less consistent (AMD, 2–20 of 67 [3–30%]; DR, 17–20 of 37 [46–54%]; RVO, 0–1 of 2) ( Table S3 ).

title: Comparison of OneChoice AI-Based Clinical Decision Support Recommendations with Infectious Disease Specialists and Non-Specialists for Empirical Urinary Tract Infection Therapy in Lima, Peru
outcome: Concordance of AI antimicrobial recommendations with physicians and blinded expert preference in discordant cases
effect: First-choice concordance was 50.9% and general concordance 62.5%. ID specialists showed higher concordance than non-ID physicians (72.9% vs. 57.8% general). The panel preferred the CDSS in 90.5-93.2% of discordant cases.
quote: Among discordant evaluations, the external panel judged the CDSS recommendation to be preferable in 90.5-93.2% of cases.
sample_unit: evaluations (by 194 physicians across 42 real UTI cases)

title: Cross-Domain Generalization of Deep Learning Architectures for Cephalometric Landmark Detection: A Dual-Dataset and Multi-Device Benchmark
outcome: Cross-dataset generalization drop in landmark error versus in-domain performance
effect: In-domain MRE 2.47-3.04 mm (Aariz) and 4.12-5.55 mm (ISBI); cross-dataset error rose 155-426%; single-dataset accuracy substantially overstates clinical generalizability.
quote: Single-dataset accuracy substantially overstates clinical generalizability, and the best in-domain architecture is not the most transferable, so in-domain leaderboards are an unreliable basis for selecting a model for clinical deployment; balanced multi-source training recovers most of the loss across the architectures tested.

title: Cross-Domain Generalization of Deep Learning Architectures for Cephalometric Landmark Detection: A Dual-Dataset and Multi-Device Benchmark
outcome: Device-specific performance shift under leave-one-device-out evaluation
effect: Leave-one-device-out revealed reproducible device-specific shift with held-out MRE 1.89-7.94 mm.
quote: Leave-one-device-out revealed reproducible device-specific shift (held-out MRE 1.89-7.94 mm).

title: Cross-Domain Generalization of Deep Learning Architectures for Cephalometric Landmark Detection: A Dual-Dataset and Multi-Device Benchmark
outcome: Performance degradation when test data differ from development data
effect: Cross-domain errors were 15-44x the 0.53 mm inter-observer band; Generalization Drop 155-426%; A-point, B-point, Nasion, Menton exceeded 2 mm threshold out-of-domain.
quote: A-point, B-point, Nasion, and Menton all exceeded the 2 mm clinical threshold out-of-domain, including points localized to sub-millimeter accuracy in-domain.

title: Cross-Domain Generalization of Deep Learning Architectures for Cephalometric Landmark Detection: A Dual-Dataset and Multi-Device Benchmark
outcome: Effect of balanced multi-source joint training on cross-domain error gap
effect: Balanced joint training reduced the cross-domain gap for all four architectures (both domains about 2.1-3.5 mm) without harming in-domain accuracy.
quote: Balanced joint training reduced the cross-domain gap for all four architectures (both domains ≈ 2.1-3.5 mm) without harming in-domain accuracy.

title: Cross-Domain Generalization of Deep Learning Architectures for Cephalometric Landmark Detection: A Dual-Dataset and Multi-Device Benchmark
outcome: Whether in-domain ranking of architectures predicts cross-domain ranking
effect: Best in-domain model (from-scratch heatmap CNN, 2.47 mm) showed the largest drop; in-domain ranking did not predict cross-domain ranking.
quote: The most accurate model in-domain (a from-scratch heatmap CNN, 2.47 mm) showed the largest drop, and every pretrained estimate fell below every from-scratch estimate (family means 248% vs. 380%): in-domain ranking did not predict cross-domain ranking.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Multimodal Large Language Models for Four-Class Benchmark of Oral Autoimmune Blistering Diseases: A Multicenter Paired Study
outcome: Calibration of model confidence (Brier score, expected calibration error)
effect: Claude had lower one-vs-rest Brier score (0.0468 vs. 0.0558), whereas Gemini had lower expected calibration error (0.083 vs. 0.251); calibration was metric-dependent.
quote: Calibration results were metric-dependent: Claude had a lower one-vs-rest Brier score (0.0468 vs. 0.0558), whereas Gemini had a lower expected calibration error (0.083 vs. 0.251).

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Multimodal Large Language Models for Four-Class Benchmark of Oral Autoimmune Blistering Diseases: A Multicenter Paired Study
outcome: Head-to-head diagnostic accuracy of two candidate multimodal LLMs on same cases
effect: Claude achieved higher accuracy than Gemini (92.0% vs. 86.0%, p = 0.012), kappa 0.893 vs. 0.813, macro-AUC 0.998 vs. 0.965.
quote: Claude achieved significantly higher diagnostic accuracy than Gemini (92.0% vs. 86.0%, p = 0.012), stronger agreement with the reference standard (κ = 0.893 vs. 0.813), and superior discrimination (macro-AUC 0.998 vs. 0.965).

title: Large Language Models in Perioperative Antithrombotic Management: A Blinded Scenario-Based Expert Evaluation
outcome: Expert-rated LLM performance on perioperative antithrombotic scenarios across models
effect: Overall expert-rated performance differed across models (Friedman χ2 = 28.75, p < 0.001; Kendall's W = 0.096); greater variability in discontinuation timing, anesthesia choice and clinical reasoning.
quote: Although all models performed well in drug discontinuation decisions, greater variability was observed in discontinuation timing, anesthesia choice and clinical reasoning.

title: Large Language Models in Perioperative Antithrombotic Management: A Blinded Scenario-Based Expert Evaluation
outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs
effect: Each scenario was queried only once, so fine-grained differences in model ordering are provisional; reproducibility was not tested.
quote: Because each scenario was queried only once, fine-grained differences in model ordering should be considered provisional.

title: External Validation of Clinical Risk Scores and Machine Learning Models for Predicting 30-Day Cardiovascular Risk After Noncardiac Surgery: The PERICARE Study
outcome: ML models' AUROC compared with established clinical risk scores (AUB-HAS2, RCRI) on external validation data
effect: No ML model showed statistically significant AUROC superiority over AUB-HAS2 (all p > 0.05), although several models modestly outperformed RCRI; Naive Bayes highest AUROC 0.738.
quote: However, in external validation, no ML model demonstrated statistically significant AUROC superiority over the AUB-HAS2 score (all p > 0.05), although several models modestly outperformed the RCRI.

title: External Validation of Clinical Risk Scores and Machine Learning Models for Predicting 30-Day Cardiovascular Risk After Noncardiac Surgery: The PERICARE Study
outcome: Model performance when externally validated at an independent site without refitting
effect: Absolute risk remained underestimated in external validation; Naive Bayes had poor calibration and threshold-dependent utility; no consistent best algorithm across metrics.
quote: Naive Bayes achieved the highest external discrimination (AUROC 0.738, 95% CI 0.668-0.804) but showed poor calibration and threshold-dependent clinical utility.

title: Prolonged Length of Stay After Lung Resection: A Prediction Model That Loses Accuracy Across Hospitals, with No Added Benefit from Blood Pressure Data
outcome: Baseline model AUROC across internal, temporal, and external (VitalDB) sites
effect: Baseline AUROC 0.714 internally, 0.719 temporally, 0.623 externally; external calibration slopes 0.570 and 0.534 versus about 1.11 temporally.
quote: Baseline-model AUROCs were 0.714 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.667-0.756) internally, 0.719 (0.640-0.788) temporally, and 0.623 (0.579-0.666) externally.
sample_unit: patients (536 development, 184 temporal validation, 626 external validation)

title: Prolonged Length of Stay After Lung Resection: A Prediction Model That Loses Accuracy Across Hospitals, with No Added Benefit from Blood Pressure Data
outcome: Discrimination and calibration of locally developed model when applied to a different cohort
effect: Similar discrimination locally (temporal AUROC 0.719) but external AUROC 0.623 and calibration slope about 0.55; limited transportability without updating.
quote: The baseline model retained similar discrimination locally but had limited unchanged external transportability.
sample_unit: patients (536 development, 184 temporal validation, 626 external validation)

title: LipoAssist: a structured GPT-4-based clinical workflow for preliminary lipedema assessment
outcome: Expert Likert ratings of diagnosis identification versus diagnostic-workup and surgical recommendations
effect: Most likely diagnosis scored 4.53 ± 0.51, but recommendations for further diagnostic evaluation scored 2.17 ± 0.83 and surgical necessity assessment 1.93 ± 0.64.
quote: Lower scores were recorded for recommendations regarding further diagnostic evaluation (2.17 ± 0.83) and assessment of surgical necessity (1.93 ± 0.64).

title: [Attention-based multi-task deep learning model for predicting the primary site of cervical metastatic squamous cell carcinoma with unknown primary]
venue: Zhonghua er bi yan hou tou jing wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of otorhinolaryngology head and neck surgery
outcome: Junior physician primary-site prediction accuracy with versus without model assistance in real-world CMSCCUP cohort
effect: Model achieved Micro-AUC 0.809 and Top-3 accuracy 88% in the real-world cohort (172 cases), significantly improving junior physicians' predictive accuracy (all P<0.001).
quote: In a real-world CMSCCUP cohort (172 cases, including 86 CMSCCUP patients and 86 normal controls), the model achieved a Micro-AUC of 0.809 against the gold standard and a Top-3 accuracy of 88%, significantly improving the predictive accuracy of junior physicians (all P<0.001).
sample_unit: patients with known-primary cervical lymph node metastases (training and test sets)

title: A clinically-oriented foundation model for intraoperative pathology
outcome: Pathologist workload and ancillary tests with versus without AI collaboration
effect: Human-AI collaboration reduced diagnostic workload by 35%, avoided 105 ancillary tests, and detected micrometastases with 87.5% accuracy.
quote: Human-AI collaboration further reduced diagnostic workload by 35%, avoided 105 ancillary tests and enhanced detection of micrometastases with 87.5% accuracy.

title: A clinically-oriented foundation model for intraoperative pathology
outcome: Generalization of model performance across institutions, tumor types, and anatomical sites
effect: Robust generalization across 6 institutions, 14 tumor types, and 24 anatomical sites, including previously unseen sites and rare cancers.
quote: The model demonstrated robust generalization across 6 institutions, 14 tumor types, and 24 anatomical sites-including previously unseen sites and rare cancers.

title: Retrospective comparison of three commercial artificial intelligence algorithms for detection of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in the emergency radiology department
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of three commercial AI algorithms versus radiologists on the same CT exams
effect: Aidoc performed best, with 90.3% sensitivity and 99.0% specificity; AI performance varied substantially, and only one system showed clinically relevant accuracy.
quote: Aidoc performed best, with 90.3% sensitivity and 99.0% specificity.

title: Retrospective comparison of three commercial artificial intelligence algorithms for detection of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in the emergency radiology department
outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of simulated combined human-AI reading versus AI alone
effect: Simulated combination of Aidoc with a human reader increased sensitivity to 96.0% while maintaining 99.4% specificity (P < 0.001), using an idealized logical OR model; overreliance was not assessed.
quote: A simulated mathematical combination of Aidoc with a human reader increased sensitivity to 96.0% while maintaining 99.4% specificity (P < 0.001), comparable to two radiologists.

title: Prospective Shadow-Mode Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Tool for Intracranial Aneurysm Detection on CT Angiography: Incremental Yield and Operational Impact
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Operational yield metrics (rEDR, gain-to-pain ratio, NNE) by care setting
effect: Favorable in inpatients (rEDR 78.3%, GPR 2.57, NNE 28.9) and emergency (rEDR 37.1%, GPR 1.0, NNE 85.3); unfavorable in outpatients (rEDR 14.1%, GPR 0.67, NNE 130.3).
quote: Operational metrics were most favorable in inpatients (rEDR 78.3%, GPR 2.57, NNE 28.9) and emergency (rEDR 37.1%, GPR 1.0, NNE 85.3) and were unfavorable in outpatients (rEDR 14.1%, GPR 0.67, NNE 130.3).

title: Prospective Shadow-Mode Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Tool for Intracranial Aneurysm Detection on CT Angiography: Incremental Yield and Operational Impact
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Prospective AI vs blinded radiologist performance in shadow mode on live CTAs
effect: Shadow mode on 3,856 CTAs yielded AI sensitivity 0.846 vs radiologist 0.718, similar specificity (0.987 vs 0.985), and revealed setting-specific variability in operational metrics before activation.
quote: Sensitivity of AI alone (0.846, 0.787-0.894) exceeded radiologist alone (0.718, 0.649-0.779), with similar specificity (radiologist: 0.985, 0.981-0.989; AI: 0.987, 0.983-0.991).

title: Prospective Shadow-Mode Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Tool for Intracranial Aneurysm Detection on CT Angiography: Incremental Yield and Operational Impact
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: Aneurysms detected by radiologists but missed by AI
effect: Radiologist-only aneurysms were mostly 3 to 5 mm (18 of 33, 54.5%); AI-alone sensitivity was 0.846, 0.787-0.894.
quote: Most AI-only aneurysms were <3 mm (31 of 55, 56.4%); radiologist-only were mostly 3 to 5 mm (18 of 33, 54.5%).

title: Prospective Shadow-Mode Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence Tool for Intracranial Aneurysm Detection on CT Angiography: Incremental Yield and Operational Impact
venue: Journal of the American College of Radiology : JACR
outcome: prospective evaluation in shadow-mode
effect: Shadow-mode testing identified variable setting-specific metrics, informing clinical deployment decisions.
quote: The AI tool demonstrated favorable operational performance, supporting clinical deployment in real-world practice, although setting-specific metrics were variable.

title: A Flexible-Horizon Clinical Decision Support Model for Dementia Early Detection and Risk Prediction in Secondary Care: A Responsible AI Approach
outcome: Flexible-horizon ML model versus Cox proportional hazards baseline: G-mean, sensitivity, specificity
effect: ML had higher G-mean at four of five horizons and higher specificity from 48 months; Cox had greater sensitivity from 48 months onwards.
quote: Compared with a Cox proportional hazards model, our flexible-horizon ML model achieved a higher G-mean at four of the five evaluated horizons and higher specificity from 48 months onwards, whereas Cox achieved greater sensitivity from 48 months onwards.

title: A Flexible-Horizon Clinical Decision Support Model for Dementia Early Detection and Risk Prediction in Secondary Care: A Responsible AI Approach
outcome: Model discrimination across sex, race and age subgroups (exploratory)
effect: Broadly similar balanced discrimination across sex, race and age groups, although sensitivity-specificity trade-offs varied.
quote: Exploratory subgroup analyses showed broadly similar balanced discrimination across sex, race and age groups, although sensitivity-specificity trade-offs varied.

title: Multi-site observational evaluation of Breast AI™-supported ultrasound risk stratification in breast cancer assessment pathways
outcome: Site-level variation in referral-associated malignancy rates across five facilities
effect: No statistically significant site-level differences in referral-associated malignancy rates (χ² = 1.67, p = 0.795).
quote: Referral-associated malignancy rates remained relatively consistent across participating healthcare sites, with no statistically significant site-level differences observed (χ² = 1.67, p = 0.795).

title: Evaluating an AI-assisted triage workflow for retinal diseases
outcome: Sensitivity for DR and AMD when AI-negative images skip clinician review versus human-only reading
effect: DR sensitivity fell 0.9168 to 0.8838 (diff -0.0330; p<0.001); AMD 0.8570 to 0.8445 (diff -0.0124; p=0.008); ophthalmologist review reduced to 7.3%-16.8% of images.
quote: For DR, mean sensitivity decreased from 0.9168 to 0.8838 (difference, -0.0330; 95% CI, -0.0495 to -0.0165; p < 0.001), whereas the increase in specificity did not reach statistical significance.

title: Evaluating an AI-assisted triage workflow for retinal diseases
outcome: AI-assisted negative-screening workflow versus human-only reading on same images: sensitivity, specificity, workload
effect: Workload cut to 7.3%-8.0% (DR), 11.7%-11.9% (RVO), 13.5%-16.8% (AMD); sensitivity lower for DR and AMD, unchanged for RVO; specificity not significantly changed.
quote: Thus, the MRMC analysis showed a significant sensitivity trade-off for DR and AMD, with no statistically significant specificity gain, while RVO performance was preserved.

title: Evaluating an AI-assisted triage workflow for retinal diseases
outcome: False negatives from out-of-distribution or atypical pathology outside the AI's target disease scope
effect: Composite false negatives included myopic chorioretinal atrophy, geographic atrophy, and treatment-altered DR; AI negatives were appropriate within scope but missed out-of-distribution pathology.
quote: While such classifications were appropriate within the algorithm’s defined scope, this discrepancy highlights a potential limitation of disease-specific AI models in negative-screening workflows, particularly when encountering out-of-distribution retinal pathologies.

title: Evaluating an AI-assisted triage workflow for retinal diseases
outcome: Generalizability of performance beyond single tertiary center and exclusion of ambiguous cases
effect: Discordant cases excluded (AMD 6.1%-11.6%); AMD full-cohort referral burden 19.6% versus 13.5%-16.8% in reader-agreed sets; results may overestimate performance.
quote: The primary AMD estimates should therefore be interpreted as results for reader-agreed cases rather than definitive performance in a full screening population containing ambiguous findings.

title: Evaluating an AI-assisted triage workflow for retinal diseases
outcome: Missed disease when AI-negative outputs substituted for diagnosis
effect: DR sensitivity decreased 0.9168 to 0.8838 (difference -0.0330; p < 0.001); AMD 0.8570 to 0.8445 (difference -0.0124; p = 0.008).
quote: AI-assisted negative-screening can reduce ophthalmologist workload across multiple retinal diseases, but with disease-specific safety trade-offs: because AI-negative images are not reviewed, reduced sensitivity for DR and AMD means a small proportion of true-positive cases would go undetected, potentially delaying diagnosis and treatment for sight-threatening disease.

title: Evaluating an AI-assisted triage workflow for retinal diseases
outcome: diagnostic sensitivity under AI-assisted negative-screening triage
effect: Sensitivity decreased for DR (0.9168 to 0.8838, p < 0.001) and AMD (0.8570 to 0.8445, p = 0.008), was unchanged for RVO (0.9807, p = 1.000), and decreased for composite disease (0.9122 to 0.9039, p < 0.001).
quote: AI-assisted negative-screening can reduce ophthalmologist workload across multiple retinal diseases, but with disease-specific safety trade-offs: because AI-negative images are not reviewed, reduced sensitivity for DR and AMD means a small proportion of true-positive cases would go undetected, potentially delaying diagnosis and treatment for sight-threatening disease.

title: Evaluation of a National Health Service Machine-Learning Model for Hypertension Case-Finding: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: Model sensitivity and specificity across demographic and deprivation subgroups
effect: Sensitivity higher in older adults and Black patients; specificity higher in younger adults, female and White patients. Higher deprivation had higher sensitivity but lower specificity. Overall sensitivity 62.7%, specificity 60.7%.
quote: Sensitivity was higher in older adults and Black patients; specificity was higher in younger adults, female patients, and White patients.

title: Evaluation of a National Health Service Machine-Learning Model for Hypertension Case-Finding: Retrospective Cohort Study
outcome: Performance of the ML model versus a more interpretable logistic regression model
effect: The ML model's performance was comparable with a more interpretable logistic regression model, so no gain from added complexity.
quote: The model's performance was comparable with a more interpretable logistic regression model.

title: Implementation of Artificial Intelligence-Powered Patient Simulation for Communication Training in a Telehealth Transitional Care Program
venue: Simulation in healthcare : journal of the Society for Simulation in Healthcare
outcome: Communication rubric scores during real telehealth patient encounters
effect: Rubric scores improved by 24% for inpatient, 19% for postoperative, and 37% for emergency department pathways (P < 0.001 for each), with sustained median shifts.
quote: Total rubric scores improved: inpatient by 24% (P < 0.001), postoperative by 19% (P < 0.001), and emergency department by 37% (P < 0.001).

title: On-premise medical AI agents for reliable clinical decision-making
outcome: Whether decision-time reliability signals identify cases to handle autonomously versus defer for review
effect: At a consistency threshold of 0.90, 49.4% of cases were retained at 98.9% diagnostic accuracy; remaining cases deferred for review.
quote: At a consistency threshold of 0.90, 49.4% of cases were retained at 98.9% diagnostic accuracy.

title: On-premise medical AI agents for reliable clinical decision-making
outcome: Discrimination of diagnostic correctness by internal-likelihood, language-based and behavioral-consistency uncertainty measures
effect: Diagnostic behavioral consistency gave the strongest discrimination of correctness (AUC = 0.860) and remained informative under stress testing (AUC = 0.875).
quote: Diagnostic behavioral consistency provided the strongest discrimination of correctness (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.860) and remained informative under stress testing (AUC = 0.875).

title: INFORMER-Interpretability-Founded Monitoring of Medical Image Deep Learning Models: Application to Chest X-ray Pathologies
venue: Journal of imaging informatics in medicine
outcome: Quality-control F1 under input-image noise levels 0.001-0.005 versus baseline
effect: Averaged across noise levels, under IxG-based evaluation, retrieval-based variant improved bootstrapped F1 by 21.92% and non-retrieval variant by 13.53% over baseline.
quote: Averaged across input-image noise levels of 0.001-0.005, under IxG-based evaluation, the proposed framework showed improvements in bootstrapped F1 over the baseline, with the retrieval-based variant achieving a 21.92% improvement and the corresponding non-retrieval variant achieving a 13.53% improvement.

title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Hospital Discharge Prediction
outcome: Inference-time optimization of discharge prediction
effect: Automated prompt optimization improved F1/sensitivity but reduced PPV/specificity; test-time scaling and expert prompt engineering showed minimal improvement.
quote: Automated prompt optimization had higher F1 score and sensitivity than the basic prompt on the hold-out test set, with lower PPV and specificity; test-time scaling and expert-led prompt engineering showed minimal improvement.
sample_unit: hospitalized inpatient encounters (validation n=860, test n=886)

title: Optimizing Large Language Models for Hospital Discharge Prediction
outcome: LLM error domains
effect: Operational workflows were the majority of LLM errors, rather than medical knowledge alone.
quote: Operational workflows, rather than medical knowledge alone, represented the majority of LLM errors.
sample_unit: hospitalized inpatient encounters (validation n=860, test n=886)

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence Chatbot to Generate Cochlear Implant Insurance Appeal Letter
outcome: Accuracy and relevance of citations in ChatGPT-generated appeal letters
effect: Of 96 citations, only 6 (6.3%) accurately referenced peer-reviewed sources; the rest were hallucinated (57.3%), erroneous (24%), or irrelevant (10%).
quote: Of the 96 citations, only six (6.3%) accurately referenced peerreviewed sources; the rest were hallucinated (57.3%), erroneous (24%), or irrelevant (10%).
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated appeal letters (87 total rater scores)

title: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence Chatbot to Generate Cochlear Implant Insurance Appeal Letter
outcome: Hallucinated benefits and incorrect content in AI-generated appeal letters
effect: 51.7% of responses contained hallucinated benefits; 79.3% only partially aligned with ACI Alliance guidelines.
quote: However, 51.7% contained hallucinated benefits.
sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated appeal letters (87 total rater scores)

title: Safety, accuracy, empathy, information quality, and readability of publicly accessible LLM-based chatbots for traumatic brain injury and concussion questions: a cross-sectional comparative study
outcome: Potentially harmful chatbot responses, including under-triage of TBI and concussion situations
effect: 27 of 325 responses were classified as potentially harmful, mainly due to under-triage, overly reassuring imaging advice, premature return-to-activity or driving guidance, and insufficient pediatric caution; safe response proportions were 89.2 to 95.4%.
quote: However, 27 responses were classified as potentially harmful, mainly because of under-triage, overly reassuring advice regarding imaging findings, premature return-to-activity or driving guidance, and insufficient pediatric caution.

title: An AI-Based Whole-Person Care Summarization Tool for Care Management Providers
outcome: Accuracy and demographic bias of AI patient summaries
effect: Reported high accuracy and minimal demographic bias; no numbers given in the abstract.
quote: The tool exhibits high accuracy and minimal demographic bias.

title: Large language models for tympanostomy patient education: readability and guideline adherence
venue: European archives of oto-rhino-laryngology : official journal of the European Federation of Oto-Rhino-Laryngological Societies (EUFOS) : affiliated with the German Society for Oto-Rhino-Laryngology - Head and Neck Surgery
outcome: Readability (FKGL) of LLM tympanostomy patient education outputs versus sixth-grade threshold
effect: All outputs exceeded the recommended sixth-grade reading threshold (mean FKGL 9.4 for long-form; 10.6 for layered), with no significant readability differences between prompt strategies.
quote: All outputs exceeded the recommended sixth-grade reading threshold (mean FKGL, 9.4 for long-form; 10.6 for layered), with no statistically significant readability differences between prompt strategies.

title: Accuracy and Safety of Large Language Models in Endometrial Cancer Decision Making: A Case-Based In Silico Benchmarking Study
outcome: Concordance of LLM recommendations with ESGO-ESTRO-ESP 2025 guideline-based reference standard
effect: Fully concordant recommendations in 65.7% Gemini, 2.9% ChatGPT, 8.6% Claude; median scores 2, 1, 0 (P < .001).
quote: Fully concordant recommendations were generated in 65.7% of cases by Gemini, 2.9% by ChatGPT, and 8.6% by Claude.

title: Accuracy and Safety of Large Language Models in Endometrial Cancer Decision Making: A Case-Based In Silico Benchmarking Study
outcome: Recognition of missing decisive information in vignettes
effect: Gemini identified need for additional data in 83.3% of cases versus 50.0% for both ChatGPT and Claude.
quote: In the subset of vignettes with intentionally missing decisive information, Gemini identified the need for additional data in 83.3% of cases, compared with 50.0% for both ChatGPT and Claude.

title: Accuracy and Safety of Large Language Models in Endometrial Cancer Decision Making: A Case-Based In Silico Benchmarking Study
outcome: Major safety issues in cancer management recommendations
effect: Major safety issues occurred in 22.9% Gemini, 48.6% ChatGPT, and 54.3% Claude responses.
quote: Major safety issues also differed across models (P = .007), occurring in 22.9% of Gemini responses, 48.6% of ChatGPT responses, and 54.3% of Claude responses.

title: Accuracy and Safety of Large Language Models in Endometrial Cancer Decision Making: A Case-Based In Silico Benchmarking Study
outcome: Effect of guideline-informed prompting on concordance in 12 cases
effect: Guideline-informed prompting significantly improved concordance for Gemini and Claude.
quote: In the post hoc subgroup analysis, guideline-informed prompting significantly improved concordance for Gemini and Claude.

title: Retrieve-Then-Verify for Evaluating Evidence Support and Hallucination in Large Language Model-Generated Medical Information: Empirical Study
outcome: Evidence support and hallucination rates of LLM-generated risk-of-bias claims against source trial reports
effect: Evidence support rates ranged from 60% to 65% across models, with conservative hallucination rates of 34%-37%, despite 90%-98% binary accuracy.
quote: However, evidence support rates across models ranged from only 60% to 65%, with conservative hallucination rates of 34%-37%.

title: Retrieve-Then-Verify for Evaluating Evidence Support and Hallucination in Large Language Model-Generated Medical Information: Empirical Study
outcome: LLM output accuracy against human reference standard RoB 2 annotations
effect: Binary accuracy 90%-98% across domains, but exact accuracy only 42%-71%; GPT-5 had perfect binary accuracy for overall risk-of-bias and quadratic kappa up to 0.81.
quote: Binary accuracy of AI-generated risk-of-bias judgments was high across domains (90%-98%), whereas exact accuracy was substantially lower (42%-71%), reflecting frequent disagreements in severity classification despite correct directional classification.

title: Large language models fail to reliably predict emergent catheterization laboratory activation from prehospital electrocardiograms
venue: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
outcome: Multimodal LLM diagnostic performance identifying ECGs warranting cath lab activation vs cardiology decisions
effect: Gemini sensitivity 95.3% but specificity 9.4%; ChatGPT and Claude sensitivity 68.1% and 67.2%, specificity 42.3% and 46.5%; ECG machine algorithm sensitivity 67.7%, specificity 64.2%.
quote: Multimodal LLM interpretation of prehospital ECGs demonstrated clinically unreliable performance for identifying ECGs warranting emergent cardiac catheterization laboratory activation when benchmarked against real-world cardiology activation decisions.

title: Large language models fail to reliably predict emergent catheterization laboratory activation from prehospital electrocardiograms
venue: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care
outcome: LLM performance compared against existing ECG machine algorithm on same ECGs
effect: ECG machine algorithm had sensitivity 67.7% and higher specificity (64.2%) than all LLMs; LLMs did not outperform the existing software.
quote: The ECG machine algorithm demonstrated more balanced performance, with sensitivity of 67.7% (95% CI 61.4-73.4) and higher specificity (64.2%) than all LLMs.

title: AI-assisted handheld echocardiography for hospital bedside cardiac triage: The prospective OPTIMUST implementation study
outcome: Feasibility of a prospective single-center AI handheld echo pilot with real users
effect: 206 of 287 attempts (71.8%) were analyzable. The study does not establish safety, diagnostic accuracy versus comprehensive echocardiography, or an independent effect of AI.
quote: A governed AI-enabled HUD pathway was feasible in a tertiary hospital and provided interpretable studies in 71.8% of attempts.

title: Clinical implementation and evaluation of an artificial intelligence-driven one-click automatic planning system for functional lung avoidance radiotherapy
outcome: Automatic FLART plan quality versus manual FLART and conventional plans, including blinded clinician review
effect: 87.9% of automatic plans clinically acceptable without modification; 68.7% rated comparable (38.4%) or superior (30.3%) to manual FLART plans; high-function lung mean dose reduced 15.1% versus manual ConvRT.
quote: Blinded reviews indicated that 87.9% of automatic FLART plans were clinically acceptable without modification, and 68.7% were rated as comparable (38.4%) or superior (30.3%) to manual FLART plans.

title: Assessing the accuracy and usability of artificial intelligence-based language models in responding to common periodontal patient questions
outcome: Usability of LLM responses for individuals with limited scientific literacy (5-point Likert)
effect: Usability for individuals with limited scientific literacy had the lowest mean score (3.80) among criteria, versus correlation with the question at 4.81.
quote: Among evaluated criteria, correlation had the highest mean score (4.81), whereas usability for individuals with limited scientific literacy had the lowest score (3.80).
sample_unit: questions (each administered to 10 LLMs in English and Persian)

title: Assessing the accuracy and usability of artificial intelligence-based language models in responding to common periodontal patient questions
outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility of LLM periodontal answers for lay patients
effect: Usability for limited scientific literacy scored lowest (3.80); the plain language summary says many explanations are too technical for the average person.
quote: second, many explanations are too technical and hard for the average person to understand.
sample_unit: questions (each administered to 10 LLMs in English and Persian)

title: Radiation Oncology Device Recalls (2015-2025): Software and Artificial Intelligence as Emerging Drivers of Postmarket Safety
outcome: Share of radiation oncology device recalls attributed to software root cause
effect: Software issues were the most common root cause (45%), exceeding 50% in 6 of 11 years; 68 AI-enabled RO devices recalled, 62 (91.18%) involving a single planning system.

title: Evaluating large language models for lay summaries of radiology reports using tailored prompting strategies and mixed-method assessment
